body.translated_text: // <s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s> //

body.text: 1 // nidānaparivartaḥ /
body.translated_text: 1 // <s>Nidānaparivarta</s> (Chapter of the Occasion) /

body.text: // om namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Oṃ, homage to all <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bodhisattva</s>s! //

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahāvyūhe kūṭāgāre sārdhaṃ pañcamātrairbodhisattvasahasraiḥ samantabhadramañjuśrībodhisattvapūrvaṃgamaiḥ / yaduta jñānottarajñāninā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / sattvottarajñāninā ca / asaṅgottarajñāninā ca / kusumottarajñāninā ca / sūryottarajñāninā ca / candrottarajñāninā ca / vimalottarajñāninā ca / vajrottarajñāninā ca / virajottarajñāninā ca / vairocanottarajñāninā
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, in a great adorned mansion, together with five thousand <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, led by <s>Samantabhadra</s> and <s>Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva</s>. Namely: with the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Jñānottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Sattvottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Asaṅgottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Kusumottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Sūryottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Candrottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Vimalottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Vajrottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Virajottarajñānin</s>, and <s>Vairocanottarajñānin</s>

jñānāvabhāsatejasā ca / samantaśrītejasā ca / samantaprabhatejasā ca / samantaprabhaśrītejasā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // dhāraṇīgarbheṇa ca / gaganagarbheṇa ca / padmagarbheṇa ca / ratnagarbheṇa body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Jyotirdhvaja</s>, and <s>Merudhvaja</s>, and <s>Ratnadhvaja</s>, and <s>Asaṅgadhvaja</s>, and <s>Kusumadhvaja</s>, and <s>Vimaladhvaja</s>, and <s>Sūryadhvaja</s>, and <s>Ruciradhvaja</s>, and <s>Virajadhvaja</s>, and <s>Vairocanadhvaja</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Ratnatejas</s>, and <s>Mahātejas</s>, and <s>Jñānavajratejas</s>, and <s>Vimalatejas</s>, and <s>Dharmasūryatejas</s>, and <s>Puṇyaparvatatejas</s>, and <s>Jñānāvabhāsatejas</s>, and <s>Samantaśrītejas</s>, and <s>Samantaprabhatejas</s>, and <s>Samantaprabhaśrītejas</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Dhāraṇīgarbha</s>, and <s>Gaganagarbha</s>, and <s>Padmagarbha</s>, and <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, and <s>Guṇaviśuddhigarbha</s>, and <s>Dharmasamudragarbha</s>, and <s>Vairocanagarbha</s>, and <s>Nābhigarbha</s>, and <s>Padmaśrīgarbha</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Sunetra</s>, and <s>Viśuddhannetra</s>, and <s>Vimalanetra</s>, and <s>Asaṅganetra</s>, and <s>Samantadarśananetra</s>, and <s>Suvilokitanetra</s>, and <s>Avalokitanetra</s>, and <s>Utpalanetra</s>, and <s>Vajranetra</s>, and <s>Ratnanetra</s>, and <s>Gagananetra</s>, and <s>Samantanetra</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Devamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsamaṇimukuṭa</s>, and <s>Bodhimaṇḍamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Digvairocanamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Sarvabuddhasaṃbhūtagarbhamaṇimukuṭa</s>, and <s>Sarvalokadhātūdgatamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Samantavairocanamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Anabhibhūtamukuṭa</s>, and <s>Sarvatathāgatasiṃhāsanasaṃpratiṣṭhitamaṇimukuṭa</s>, and <s>Samantadharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamukuṭa</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Brahmendracūḍa</s>, and <s>Nāgendracūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvabuddhanirmāṇapratibhāsacūḍa</s>, and <s>Bodhimaṇḍacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvapraṇidhānasāgaranirghoṣamaṇirājacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalapramuñcanamaṇiratna-nigarjitacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvākāśatalāsaṃbhedavijñaptimaṇiratnavibhūṣitacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvatathāgatavikurvitapratibhāsadhvajamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣacūḍa</s>, and <s>Sarvatryadhvanāmacakranirghoṣacūḍa</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Mahāprabha</s>, and <s>Vimalaprabha</s>, and <s>Vimalatejaḥprabha</s>, and <s>Ratnaprabha</s>, and <s>Virajaprabha</s>, and <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s>, and <s>Dharmaprabha</s>, and <s>Śāntiprabha</s>, and <s>Sūryaprabha</s>, and <s>Vikurvitaprabha</s>, and <s>Devaprabha</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Puṇyaketu</s>, and <s>Jñānaketu</s>, and <s>Dharmaketu</s>, and <s>Abhijñāketu</s>

ca / prabhāketunā / kusumaketunā ca / bodhiketunā ca / brahmaketunā ca / samantāvabhāsaketunā ca / maṇiketunā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // brahmaghoṣeṇa ca / sāgaraghoṣeṇa ca / dharaṇīnirnādaghoṣeṇa ca / lokendraghoṣeṇa ca / śailendrarājasaṃghaṭṭanaghoṣeṇa ca / sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaghoṣeṇa ca / sarvadharmadhātusāgaranigarjitaghoṣeṇa ca / sarvamāaramaṇḍalapramardanaghoṣeṇa ca / mahākaruṇānayameghanigarjitaghoṣeṇa ca / sarvajagadduḥkhapraśāntyāśvāsanaghoṣeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / dharmodgatena ca / viśeṣodgatena ca / jñānodgatena
ca / puṇyasumerūdgatena ca / guṇaprabhāvodgatena ca / yaśodgatena ca / samantāvabhāsodgatena ca / mahāmaitryudgatena ca / jñānasaṃbhārodgatena ca / tathāgatakulagotrodgatena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // prabhāśriyā ca / pravaraśriyā ca / samudgataśriyā ca / vairocanaśriyā ca / dharmaśriyā ca / candraśriyā ca / gaganaśriyā ca / ratnaśriyā ca / ketuśriyā ca / jñānaśriyā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // śailendrarājena ca / dharmendrarājena ca / jagadindrarājena ca / brahmendrarājena ca / gaṇendrarājena ca / devendrarājena ca / śāntendrarājena ca / acalendrarājena ca / ṛṣabhendrarājena ca / pravarendrarājena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // praśāntasvareṇa ca / asaṅgasvareṇa ca / dharaṇīnirghoṣasvareṇa ca / sāgaranigarjitasvareṇa ca / meghanirghoṣasvareṇa ca / dharmāvabhāsasvareṇa ca / gagananirghoṣasvareṇa ca / sarvasattvakuśalamūlanigarjitasvareṇa ca / pūrvapraṇidhānasaṃcodanasvareṇa ca / māramaṇḍalanirghoṣasvareṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // ratnabuddhinā ca / jñānabuddhinā ca / gaganabuddhinā ca / asaṅgabuddhinā ca / vimalabuddhinā ca / viśuddhabuddhinā ca / tryadhvāvabhāsabuddhinā ca / viśālabuddhinā ca / samantāvalokabuddhinā ca / dharmadhātunayāvabhāsabuddhinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena // evaṃpramukhaiḥ pañcamātrairbodhisattvasahasraiḥ sarvaiḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānābhiniryātairasaṅgagocaraiḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraspharaṇatayā / anantakāyādhiṣṭhānaiḥ sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇatayā / anāvaraṇacakṣurmaṇḍalaviśuddhaiḥ sarvabuddhavikurvitadarśanatayā / vijñaptiṣvapramāṇagataiḥ sarvatathāgatābhisaṃbodhimukhopasaṃkramaṇāpratiprasrabdhatayā / anantālokaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmasamudranayajñānāvabhāsapratilabdhatayā / anantakalpākṣīṇaguṇanirdeśaiḥ pratisaṃvidviśuddhyā / ākāśadhātuparamajñānagocaraviśuddhyanigṛhītairyathāśayajagadrūpakāyasaṃdarśanatayā / vitimirairniḥsattvanirjīvasattvadhātuparijñayā / gaganasamaprajñaiḥ sarvadharmadhāturaśmijālaspharaṇatayā / pañcabhiśca śrāvakamaharddhikaśataiḥ sarvaiḥ satyanayasvabhāvābhisaṃbuddhairbhūtakoṭipratyakṣagatairdharmaprakṛtyavatīrṇairbhavasamudroccalitaistathāgatagaganagocaraiḥ saṃyojanānuśayavāsanāvinivartitairasaṅgālayanilayairgaganaśāntavihāribhirbuddhakāṅkṣāvimativicikitsāsamucchinnaiḥ buddhajñānasamudrādhimuktipathāvatīrṇaiḥ // lokendraiśca pūrvajinakṛtādhikāraiḥ
sarvajagaddhitasukhapratipannairanadhīṣṭakalyāṇamitraiḥ
body.translated_text: and <s>Prabhāketu</s>, and <s>Kusumaketu</s>, and <s>Bodhiketu</s>, and <s>Brahmaketu</s>, and <s>Samantāvabhāsaketu</s>, and <s>Maṇiketu</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Brahmaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Sāgaraghoṣa</s>, and <s>Dharaṇīnirnādaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Lokendraghoṣa</s>, and <s>Śailendrarājasaṃghaṭṭanaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Sarvadharmadhātusāgaranigarjitaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Sarvamāramaṇḍalapramardanaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Mahākaruṇānayameghanigarjitaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Sarvajagadduḥkhapraśāntyāśvāsanaghoṣa</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. With <s>Dharmodgata</s>, and <s>Viśeṣodgata</s>, and <s>Jñānodgata</s>, and <s>Puṇyasumerūdgata</s>, and <s>Guṇaprabhāvodgata</s>, and <s>Yaśodgata</s>, and <s>Samantāvabhāsodgata</s>, and <s>Mahāmaitryudgata</s>, and <s>Jñānasaṃbhārodgata</s>, and <s>Tathāgatakulagotrodgata</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Prabhāśrī</s>, and <s>Pravaraśrī</s>, and <s>Samudgataśrī</s>, and <s>Vairocanaśrī</s>, and <s>Dharmaśrī</s>, and <s>Candraśrī</s>, and <s>Gaganaśrī</s>, and <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, and <s>Ketuśrī</s>, and <s>Jñānaśrī</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Śailendrarāja</s>, and <s>Dharmendrarāja</s>, and <s>Jagadindrarāja</s>, and <s>Brahmendrarāja</s>, and <s>Gaṇendrarāja</s>, and <s>Devendarāja</s>, and <s>Śāntendrarāja</s>, and <s>Acalendrarāja</s>, and <s>Ṛṣabhendrarāja</s>, and <s>Pravarendrarāja</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Praśāntasvara</s>, and <s>Asaṅgasvara</s>, and <s>Dharaṇīnirghoṣasvara</s>, and <s>Sāgaranigarjitasvara</s>, and <s>Meghanirghoṣasvara</s>, and <s>Dharmāvabhāsasvara</s>, and <s>Gagananirghoṣasvara</s>, and <s>Sarvasattvakuśalamūlanigarjitasvara</s>, and <s>Pūrvapraṇidhānasaṃcodanasvara</s>, and <s>Māramaṇḍalanirghoṣasvara</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // With <s>Ratnabuddhi</s>, and <s>Jñānabuddhi</s>, and <s>Gaganabuddhi</s>, and <s>Asaṅgabuddhi</s>, and <s>Vimalabuddhi</s>, and <s>Viśuddhabuddhi</s>, and <s>Tryadhvāvabhāsabuddhi</s>, and <s>Viśālabuddhi</s>, and <s>Samantāvalokabuddhi</s>, and <s>Dharmadhātunayāvabhāsabuddhi</s> the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. // Led by these, with five thousand <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, all having emerged through the practice and vows of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, of unobstructed range, pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; with the power to sustain infinite bodies, approaching all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; with purified vision-spheres free from obstruction, seeing the transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s; having entered immeasurable cognitions, unwearied in approaching the gates of the perfect awakening of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; with infinite light, having attained the illumination of the knowledge of the methods of the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; with inexhaustible exposition of qualities through infinite <s>kalpa</s>s, through the purification of analytical knowledge; unchecked by the supreme knowledge-range of the space-element, displaying form-bodies to beings according to their dispositions; free from darkness, through the complete knowledge of the realm of beings as devoid of self and devoid of life; with wisdom equal to space, pervading with the net of rays of all <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena); and with five hundred great <s>śrāvaka</s>s (hearers) of supernatural power, all fully awakened to the nature of the method of truth, having directly realized the ultimate point of reality, descended into the nature of <s>dharma</s>s, risen from the ocean of existence, whose range is the sky of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who have turned away from the latent tendencies of the fetters and proclivities, whose abode is in the non-clinging and unattached, who dwell in the peace of space, who have utterly cut off doubt, wavering, and perplexity regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, who have descended upon the path of devotion to the ocean of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // And with lords of the world who had previously performed service under former <s>Jina</s>s (Victors),

body.text: parasattvarakṣāpratipannaiḥ lokaviśeṣavartijñānasukhavatīrṇaiḥ sarvasattvāparityāgacittairbuddhaśāsanagocaraniryātaistathāgataśāsanarakṣāpratipannairbuddhavaṃśasaṃdhāraṇapraṇidhinirjātaistathāgatakulagotrasaṃbhavābhimukhaiḥ sarvajñatājñānābhilāṣibhiḥ //
body.translated_text: who were devoted to the welfare and happiness of all beings, who were unurged spiritual friends, who were devoted to the protection of other beings, who had descended into the knowledge and bliss of the special ways of the world, whose minds never abandoned any being, who had emerged into the range of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, who were devoted to guarding the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who were born from the vow to maintain the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s>, who faced the arising of the family and lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who longed for the knowledge of omniscience. //

body.text:
atha khalu teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saparivārāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca śrāvakamaharddhikānāṃ teṣāṃ ca lokendrāṇāṃ saparivārāṇāmetadabhavatna śakyaṃ sadevakenāpi lokena tathāgataviṣayaṃ tathāgatajñānagocaraṃ tathāgatādhiṣṭhānaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ tathāgatavaiśāradyaṃ tathāgatasamādhiṃ tathāgatavihāraṃ tathāgatādhipatyaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ tathāgatajñānamavagantuṃ vā avagāhituṃ vā adhimoktuṃ vā prajñātuṃ vā vijñātuṃ vā vicārayituṃ vā vibhāvayituṃ vā vibhājituṃ vā prabhāvayituṃ vā parasattvasaṃtāneṣu vā pratiṣṭhāpayitum, anyatra tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena tathāgatavikurvitena tathāgatānubhāvena tathāgatapūrvaprāṇidhānena pūrvabuddhasukṛtakuśalamūlatayā kalyāṇamitraparigraheṇa śraddhānayanajñānapariśuddhyā udārādhimuktyavabhāsapratilambhena bodhisattvādhyāśayapariśuddhyā adhyāśayasarvajñatāpraṇidhānaprasthānena / apyeva nāma bhagavānasmākaṃ yathāśayānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca sattvānāmāśaya vimātratayā adhimuktinānātvatayā pratibodhanānātvatayā vacanasaṃketanānātvaprāptānāṃ nānādhipateyabhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ nānendriyaviśuddhānāṃ nānāśayaprayogānāṃ nānācetanāviṣayāṇāṃ nānātathāgataguṇaniśritānāṃ nānādharmanirdeśadigabhimukhānāṃ pūrvasarvajñatāprasthānaṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvapraṇidhānābhinirhāraṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvapāramitāmaṇḍalaviśuddhiṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavikurvitaṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalābhinirhāraparipūriṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvayānābhinirhāravyūhāvabhāsaṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvamārgavyūhapariśuddhiṃ ca saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvaniryāṇanayasāgarābhinirhāravyūhānapi saṃdarśayet / pūrvabodhisattvasamudāgamavikurvitasāgaravyūhānapi saṃdarśayet / bodhisattvapūrvayogasamudrānapi saṃdarśayet / abhisaṃbodhimukhavikurvitasāgarānapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatadharmacakrapravartanavikurvitavṛṣabhitāmapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhivikurvitasāgarānapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasattvadhātuvinayopāyamukhānyapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasarvajñatādharmanagarādhipateyatāmapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasarvasattvamārgāvabhāsānapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasattvabhavanapraveśavikurvitānyapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasattvadakṣiṇāpratigrahāṃśca saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasarvasattvapuṇyadakṣiṇādeśanāprātihāryāṇyapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasarvasattvacittagatiṣu buddhapratibhāsavijñaptīrapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasattvavikurvitaprātihāryāṇyapi saṃdarśayet / tathāgatasarvasattvadeśanānuśāsanīprātihāryāṇyapi saṃdarśayet /
tathāgatasarvasattvācintyabuddhasamādhigocaravikurvitānyapi saṃdarśayediti //
body.translated_text: Then indeed, to those <s>bodhisattvas</s> together with their retinues, to those <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of great supernatural power, and to those lords of the world together with their retinues, this thought arose: 'It is not possible for the world, even including the gods, to comprehend, or to fathom, or to aspire toward, or to understand, or to cognize, or to investigate, or to contemplate, or to analyze, or to illuminate, or to establish in the continuities of other beings, the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the range of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge, the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the fearlessness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the abiding of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the sovereignty of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — except through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the miraculous transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the majestic power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the former vows of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through having roots of merit well-established by former <s>Buddhas</s>, through the embrace of spiritual friends, through the purification of knowledge born of faith, through the attainment of the radiance of noble aspiration, through the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s higher intention, and through the setting forth of the vow for omniscience arising from higher intention. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) show to us <s>bodhisattvas</s> according to our dispositions, and to all beings — who differ in the measure of their dispositions, in the variety of their aspirations, in the variety of their awakenings, who have attained various conventions of speech, who are established on various sovereign grounds, who are purified in various faculties, whose efforts arise from various dispositions, whose domains of volition are various, who rely on various qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and who face various directions of <s>Dharma</s> teaching — the former setting forth toward omniscience; and show the fulfillment of the former <s>bodhisattva</s> vows; and show the purification of the former <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) maṇḍala; and show the miraculous transformations of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>'s ascent through the stages; and show the complete fulfillment of the former <s>bodhisattva</s> practice-maṇḍala; and show the radiance of the array of the former <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle-fulfillment; and show the purification of the former <s>bodhisattva</s> path-array; and show the arrays of the ocean of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>'s method of liberation; and show the ocean-arrays of the miraculous transformations of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>'s attainment; and show the oceans of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice; and show the oceans of miraculous transformations that are gateways to <s>abhisaṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening); and show the supremacy of the miraculous transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma); and show the oceans of miraculous transformations in the purification of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-fields; and show the gateways to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s skillful means for disciplining the realm of beings; and show the sovereignty of the <s>Tathāgata</s> over the city of the <s>Dharma</s> of omniscience; and show the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s illumination of the paths of all beings; and show the miraculous transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s entering into the abodes of beings; and show the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s worthy recipients of beings' offerings; and show the miraculous displays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching of meritorious offerings for all beings; and show the <s>Buddha</s>-reflections and cognitions within the mental processes of all beings by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; and show the miraculous displays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s transformations of beings; and show the miraculous displays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching and instruction of all beings; and show the miraculous transformations within the range of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for all beings.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya mahākaruṇāśarīraṃ mahākaruṇāmukhaṃ mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamaṃ mahākaruṇādharmagaganayānugamaṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitaṃ nāma
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), knowing with his mind the mental deliberations of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, [arising from] the body of great compassion, the face of great compassion, preceded by great compassion, following the sky of the <s>Dharma</s> of great compassion, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called '<s>Siṃhavijṛmbhita</s>' (the Lion's Yawn),

samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma jagadvirocanavyūham / samanantarasamāpannasya ca bhagavato mahāvyūhaḥ kūṭāgāro 'nantamadhyavipulaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt / aparājitavajradharaṇītalavyūhaḥ sarvamaṇiratnarājajālasaṃsthitabhūmitalamanekaratnapuṣpābhikīrṇo mahāmaṇiratnasuvikīrṇo vaiḍūryastambhopaśobhito jagadvirocanamaṇirājasuvibhaktālaṃkāraḥ sarvaratnayamakasaṃghāto jāmbūnadamaṇiratnakūṭopaśobhitaḥ sarvaratnaniryūhatoraṇaharmyagavākṣāsaṃkhyeyavedikāviśuddhavyūhaḥ sarvalokendrasadṛśamaṇiratnavyūho jagatsāgaramaṇiratnavyūhaḥ sarvamaṇiratnasaṃchāditaḥ samucchritacchatradhvajapatākaḥ sarvadvāratoraṇavyūhamukhairdharmadhāturaśmijālapramuktaspharaṇavyūho bahiranabhilāpyaparṣanmaṇḍalabhūmitalavedikāvyūhaḥ samantadiksopānamaṇiratnakūṭaḥ paramasuvibhaktopaśobhitaḥ / sarvaṃ ca jetavanaṃ vipulāyāmavistāraṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / tānyapi ca buddhānubhāvena anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānibuddhakṣetrāṇi vipulāyāmavistārāṇi saṃsthitānyabhūvan / sarvaratnavicitravyūhāni anabhilāpyaratnacitrasaṃsthitabhūmitalāni asaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnaprākāraparikṣiptāni vividharatnatālapaṅktivyūhāni saṃsthitānyabhūvan / teṣu ca aparimāṇagandhodakanadyo 'nantāvartagandhodakaparipūrṇāḥ sarvaratnapuṣpaughakaluṣāḥ pradakṣiṇavāhinyaḥ sarvabuddhanirghoṣanigarjitavyūhāḥ samavatiṣṭhante sma / acintyāśca ratnapuṇḍarīkapaṅktayaḥ sarvaratnodgatapraphullapadmavyūhopaśobhitatalāśca ratnavṛkṣāḥ, acintyāśca vicitraratnakūṭāgārapaṅktayaḥ sarvamaṇiratnajālasaṃchannā asaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnaraśmijālāvabhāsavyūhā asaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnavimānasarvamaṇiratnavyūhāḥ sarvagandhakośapramuktāḥ sarvadhūpapaṭalavyūhāḥ saṃsthitā abhūvan / aparimāṇāśca ratnadhvajāḥ, evam vastradhvajāḥ patākādhvajā ratnapaṭṭadhvajāḥ puṣpadhvajā ābharaṇadhvajā mālyadhvajāḥ sarvaratnakiṅkiṇījāladhvajā maṇirājacchatradhvajāḥ samantāvabhāsaspharaṇamaṇiratnadhvajāḥ sarvatathāgatanāmacakranirghoṣamaṇiratnarājadhvajāḥ siṃhakāntamaṇiratnarājadhvajāḥ sarvatathāgatapūrvayoganigarjanamaṇiratnarājadhvajāḥ sarvadharmadhātupratibhāsadhvajā maṇiratnarājadhvajavyūhāḥ sarvadhvajālaṃkārasamantadiksuvibhaktavyūhāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante
sma / sarvāvacca jetavanamacintyadivyavimānameghagaganatalālaṃkāraṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / asaṃkhyeyasarvagandhavṛkṣameghasaṃchannālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyasarvavyūhasumerusaṃchannālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyavādyatūryameghasarvatathāgatastutisaṃgītimadhuranirghoṣālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyaratnapadmameghasaṃchannālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyaratnasiṃhāsanadivyamaṇiratnavastraprajñaptabodhisattvaniṣaṇṇatathāgatastutimeghamadhuranirghoṣālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyadevendrabimbasadṛśābhimukhamaṇivigrahameghālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyaśvetamuktijālameghālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyalohitamuktākūṭāgārameghasaṃchannālaṃkāram, anabhilāpyavajrasāramuktāmeghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tadacintyaṃ tathāgatakuśalamūlam, acintyastathāgataśukladharmopacayaḥ, acintyaṃ tathāgatabuddhavṛṣabhitādhiṣṭhānam, acintyaṃ tathāgatasarvalokadhātvekakāyaspharaṇavikurvitam, acintyaṃ sarvatathāgataikakāyapraveśasarvabuddhakṣetravyūhasamavasaraṇādhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśanam acintyaṃ tathāgatānāmekaparamāaṇurajasi sarvadharmadhātupratibhāsavijñaptisaṃdarśanam, acintyaṃ tathāgatānāmekaromakūpe
body.translated_text: the array that illuminates the world. And immediately upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s entering [this samādhi], the great arrayed pavilion stood vast, without center, immense. [It had] the array of the invincible <s>vajra</s> (diamond) ground-surface, a floor established upon a net of all jewel-gem-kings, strewn with many jewel-flowers, beautifully scattered with great gem-jewels, adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) pillars, beautifully divided and ornamented with world-illuminating gem-king-jewels, compacted with pairs of all kinds of gems, adorned with crests of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (finest gold) gem-jewels, with the pure array of innumerable balustrades of gem-jewel pinnacles, turrets, towers, and latticed windows, with arrays of gem-jewels resembling all lords of the world, with arrays of ocean-of-the-world gem-jewels, covered with all kinds of gem-jewels, with raised parasols, banners, and pennants, with array-entrances at all door-archways emitting nets of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (dharma-realm) rays spreading in arrays, with the array of ground-level balustrades of an indescribable assembly-maṇḍala outside, with gem-jewel crests of stairways in all directions, supremely well-divided and adorned. And the entire <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's grove) stood vast in length and breadth. And by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms and dust-particles of indescribable <s>Buddha</s>-fields stood vast in length and breadth, adorned with arrays variegated with all gems, with ground-surfaces established in indescribable gem-inlaid [patterns], surrounded by innumerable gem-jewel ramparts, with arrays of rows of various gem-jewel palm trees. And in those, rivers of immeasurable fragrant water, filled with endless whirlpools of fragrant water, turbid with floods of all gem-flowers, flowing clockwise, with arrays of the sounds and roars of all <s>Buddhas</s>, stood forth. And inconceivable rows of gem-lotuses, and gem-trees whose surfaces were adorned with arrays of fully-blooming lotuses rising from all gems, and inconceivable rows of variegated gem-jewel pavilions covered with all gem-jewel nets, with arrays of radiance from innumerable gem-jewel ray-nets, with innumerable gem-jewel aerial palaces and all gem-jewel arrays, releasing all fragrance-treasuries, with arrays of all incense-cloud layers, stood forth. And immeasurable gem-banners — likewise cloth-banners, pennant-banners, gem-silk banners, flower-banners, ornament-banners, garland-banners, banners with nets of all gem-bells, banners with gem-king parasols, gem-jewel banners of all-pervading radiance, gem-jewel-king banners resounding with the wheel of all <s>Tathāgata</s> names, banners of lion-beloved gem-jewel-kings, gem-jewel-king banners roaring with all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' former practices, banners of <s>dharmadhātu</s>-reflecting gem-jewel-king banner-arrays, arrays of all banner-ornaments beautifully divided in all directions — stood forth. And the entire <s>Jetavana</s> stood adorned with an inconceivable canopy of divine aerial palace-clouds in the sky — adorned with the covering of innumerable clouds of all fragrant trees, adorned with the covering of indescribable array-<s>Sumerus</s>, adorned with the sweet sounds of hymns to all <s>Tathāgatas</s> from indescribable clouds of musical instruments and drums, adorned with the covering of indescribable gem-lotus clouds, adorned with the sweet sounds of hymn-clouds to the <s>Tathāgata</s> from <s>bodhisattvas</s> seated on indescribable divine gem-jewel-cloth-appointed gem-lion-thrones, adorned with clouds of gem-forms resembling images of <s>Devendra</s> facing one another, adorned with indescribable nets of white pearl clouds, adorned with the covering of indescribable red-pearl pavilion clouds, adorned with the raining of indescribable adamantine-essence pearl-clouds. For what reason? For indeed inconceivable are the roots of merit of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s accumulation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment through the supremacy of <s>Buddha</s>-hood, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s miraculous transformation of pervading all world-realms with a single body, inconceivable is the displaying of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>' entering a single body and assembling the arrays of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields through empowerment, inconceivable is the displaying by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the reflection-cognition of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> in a single atom, inconceivable is the displaying by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in a single hair-pore

pūrvāntakoṭīgatasarvatathāgataparaṃparāsaṃdarśan, acintyaṃ tathāgatāmekaraśmimukhasarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥprasarāvabhāsanam, acintyaṃ tathāgatānāmekaromamukhasarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamaṃ nirmitameghasarvabuddhakṣetraspharaṇam, acintyaṃ tathāgatānāmekaromamukhasarvalokadhātusaṃvartavivartakalpasaṃdarśanaṃ ca / yathā ca jetavanamevaṃrūpayā buddhakṣetrapariśuddhyā pariśuddhaṃ saṃsthitam, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu dharmadhātuparamākāśadhātuparyavasānāḥ sarvalokadhātavaḥ pariśuddhāḥ saṃsthitā alaṃkṛtāḥ pratimaṇḍitāḥ tathāgatakāyaparisphuṭā jetavanasamavasaraṇā bodhisattvaparipūrṇāḥ tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrasuvyavasthitāḥ sarvavyūhameghabhipravarṣaṇāḥ, sarvaratnaprabhāvabhāsitāḥ sarvamaṇiratnameghapravarṣitālaṃkārāḥ, sarvakṣetravyūhameghasaṃchannālaṃkārāḥ, sarvadivyātmabhāvameghapravarṣitālaṃkārāḥ sarvapuṣpameghapravarṣitālaṃkārāḥ, supuṣpitakośaspharaṇālaṃkārāḥ, sarvavastrameghanānāraṅgaruciracīvaravarṣapramuktakośāḥ, sarvamālyadāmahāravyūhameghācchannadhārābhipravarṣaṇālaṃkārāḥ
sarvadiksamutthitanānāgandhadhūpameghapaṭalasarvajagaccharīrasadṛśasaṃsthānapravarṣāṇālaṃkārāḥ sarvaratnakusumajālameghācchannaratnajālasūkṣmacūrṇapravarṣaṇālaṃkārāḥ sarvaratnadhvajapatākāmeghadivyakanyāpāṇiparigṛhītagaganatalāvartanaparivartanālaṃkārāḥ sarvaratnapadmavicitraratnapatramaṇḍalordhvadaṇḍādhaḥkesaranibaddhatūryasaṃghaṭṭitamadhuranirghoṣālaṃkārāḥ sarvaratnabimbajālasiṃhapañjaranānāratnacitrahāramālyālaṃkārāḥ saṃsthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma //
body.translated_text: of the succession of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> going back to the beginningless past, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' illumination through the emission of a single ray-opening pervading the atoms of all world-realms, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-fields through emanation-clouds from a single hair-opening equal to the atoms of all world-realms, inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' displaying of the formation and dissolution of all world-realms over <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) from a single hair-opening. And just as <s>Jetavana</s> stood purified with such a purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field, so too in the ten directions, all world-realms extending to the ultimate bounds of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and the realm of space stood purified, adorned, embellished, pervaded by the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, assembled in <s>Jetavana</s>, filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, well-established as oceans of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s assembly-maṇḍalas, raining all array-clouds, illuminated by the radiance of all gems, adorned with raining clouds of all gem-jewels, adorned with coverings of all field-array clouds, adorned with raining clouds of all divine self-forms, adorned with raining clouds of all flower[-offerings], adorned with the spreading of fully-blossoming flower-treasuries, with treasuries releasing rains of beautifully-colored robes from all cloth-clouds, adorned with raining streams of covering clouds of all garland-wreath-necklace arrays, adorned with raining forms resembling the bodies of all beings from layers of clouds of various incense-fragrances rising from all directions, adorned with raining of fine powder from gem-net coverings of all gem-flower-net clouds, adorned with the revolving and turning in the sky held in the hands of divine maidens from clouds of all gem-banner-pennants, adorned with sweet sounds from instruments fastened to the lower filaments and upper stalks of maṇḍala-petals of variegated gem-petals of all gem-lotuses, adorned with necklaces and garlands of various gems in lion-lattices of nets of all gem-mirror-images — [all these] stood forth and were seen //

body.text: samanantarasamāpannasya bhagavata evaṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitaṃ tathāgatasamādhim, atha tāvadeva pūrvasyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa kanakameghapradīpadhvajāyā lokadhātorvairocanaśrītejorājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādvairocanapraṇidhānanābhiraśmiprabho nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrānto nānāvyūhameghairgaganatalamalaṃkurvan / yaduta divyapuṣpameghavarṣamabhipravarṣan, divyagandhameghavarṣaṃ pramuñcan, divyaratnapadmameghavarṣamabhiprakiran, divyamālyameghavarṣamavarsṛjan, divyaratnameghavarṣamabhipravarṣan, divyābharaṇameghavarṣamabhipravarṣan, divyaratnacchatrameghānabhinirharan, vicitranānāraṅgasūkṣmadivyavastrameghavarṣamabhipravarṣan, divyaratnadhvajapatākāmeghān gaganatale 'dhitiṣṭhan, ruciraiḥ sarvaratnameghavyūhairgaganatalaṃ spharan, yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya pūrvāṃ diśamupaniśritya samantavyūhamaṇiratnajālasaṃchannāni kūṭāgārāṇi dikprabhāsamaṇirājapadmagarbhāṇi ca siṃhāsanānyabhinirmāya nyaṣidatparyaṅkamābhujya cintārājamaṇiratnajālālaṃkārasaṃchannāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: Immediately after the Blessed One had entered this <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called the Lion's Yawn of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, thereupon in the eastern direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), from the world-system called <s>Kanakameghapradīpadhvajā</s> (Golden-Cloud-Lamp-Banner), from the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocanaśrītejorajas</s> (Splendor-King of <s>Vairocana</s>'s Glory), a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) named <s>Vairocanapraṇidhānanābhiraśmiprabha</s> (Radiance of the Rays from <s>Vairocana</s>'s Vow-Navel), together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having been permitted by that Blessed One, rising from that ocean of assembly circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, adorning the surface of the sky with various ornamental clouds — namely: raining showers of divine flower-clouds, releasing showers of divine fragrance-clouds, scattering showers of divine jewel-lotus-clouds, sending forth showers of divine garland-clouds, raining showers of divine gem-clouds, raining showers of divine ornament-clouds, producing divine jewel-parasol-clouds, raining showers of variegated multi-colored fine divine garment-clouds, establishing divine jewel-banner-and-flag-clouds upon the surface of the sky, pervading the sky-surface with beautiful arrays of all-jewel-clouds; and approaching the Blessed One, together with his retinue, having bowed to the Blessed One, settling in the eastern direction, having magically created mansions covered with nets of <s>samantavyūha</s> (universal-array) <s>maṇi</s>-jewels and lion-thrones with <s>dikprabhāsa</s> (direction-illuminating) jewel-king lotus-hearts, he sat down cross-legged, empowering the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with ornamental nets of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) jewel-king gems. //

body.text: dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa vajrasāgaragarbhāyā lokadhātoḥ samantāvabhāsaśrīgarbharājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrād duryodhanavīryavegarājo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaiḥ tena ca bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
body.translated_text: In the southern direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the world-system called <s>Vajrasāgaragarbhā</s> (Vajra-Ocean-Womb), from the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantāvabhāsaśrīgarbharāja</s> (King of the Womb of All-Illuminating Glory), a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Duryodhanavīryavegarāja</s> (King of the Force of Irresistible Heroic Energy), together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having been permitted by that Blessed One, rising from that ocean of assembly circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system

body.text: sarvagandhadāmajālāvanaddhān sarvalokasamudrānadhitiṣṭhan, sarvaratnahāradāmajālāvanaddhān sarvabuddhakṣetraprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, sarvapuṣpadāmahārajālāvanaddhān sarvabuddhakṣetravaṃśānadhitiṣṭhan, sarvamālyadāmahārajālāvanaddhān sarvabuddhakṣetraparivartānadhitiṣṭhan, sarvavajrahārādhastalapratiṣṭhānasaṃgṛhītāni sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanmaṇḍalānyadhitiṣṭhan, sarvamaṇiratnajālāvanaddhān sarvabuddhakṣetranayānadhitiṣṭhan, sarvavastradāmasamantaparigrahaparigṛhītān sarvalokadhātūnadhitiṣṭhan sarvaratnabimbahāradāmakalāpajālāvanaddhāni sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyabhinirharan, śrīraśmimaṇiratnahāradāmajālāvanaddhāni sarvakṣetrāṇyadhitiṣṭhan, sarvavyūharaśmyavabhāsavairocanamaṇirājadāmajālāvanaddhāni sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyadhitiṣṭhan, siṃhakāntamaṇiratnahāradāmajālapratiṣṭhānasaṃgṛhītān sarvalokadhātūnadhitiṣṭhan yena bhagavāstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya dakṣiṇāṃ diśamupaniśritya jagadvirocanamaṇikūṭāgārāṇi samantadigvirocanamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi ca siṃhāsanānyabhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya sarvaratnakusumajālālaṃkārasaṃchannāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: establishing all ocean-worlds bound with nets of garlands of all fragrances, establishing all expanses of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with nets of garlands of all jewel-necklaces, establishing all lineages of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with great nets of garlands of all flowers, establishing all revolutions of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with great nets of garlands of all wreaths, establishing all assembly circles of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> gathered upon foundations beneath all vajra-necklaces, establishing all courses of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with nets of all <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, establishing all world-systems encompassed by all-surrounding garment-garlands, producing all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with nets of clusters of all jewel-image-necklace-garlands, establishing all fields bound with nets of garlands of glorious-ray <s>maṇi</s>-jewel necklaces, establishing all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bound with nets of garlands of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-king jewels radiating all-ornament-rays, establishing all world-systems gathered upon foundations of nets of garlands of lion-beloved <s>maṇi</s>-jewel necklaces; approaching the Blessed One, together with his retinue, having bowed to the Blessed One, settling in the southern direction, having magically created mansions of <s>jagadvirocana</s> (world-illuminating) <s>maṇi</s> and lion-thrones with <s>samantadigvirocana</s> (all-direction-illuminating) <s>maṇi</s>-jewel lotus-hearts, he sat down cross-legged, empowering the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with ornamental nets of all-jewel-flower garlands. //

body.text: paścimāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa maṇisumerūvirocanadhvajapradīpāyā lokadhātordharmadhātujñānapradīpasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrātsamantaśrīsamudgatarājo nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrānto 'nabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairnānāvarṇagandhadhvajasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairvividhagandhakusumameghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairanekavarṇagandhasumerudhūpameghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairvicitravarṇagandhameghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvapariṣkārasadṛśavarṇaiḥ romatejaḥsaṃbhavamaṇirājasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairnānāprabhāmaṇḍalavyūhajyotirdhvajamaṇiratnasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairnānāvarṇavajragarbhamaṇirājanānāvyūhaviṣayasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvalokadhātupratibhāsaviṣayairjāmbūnadamaṇiratnasumerumeghai sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvaparvatadharmadhātupratibhāsamaṇirājasumerumeghaiḥ saṃchannaṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvatathāgatalakṣaṇapratibhāsamaṇirājasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuviṣayaṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvatathāgatapūrvayogapratibhāsasaṃdarśanabodhisattvacaryānirghoṣasvaramaṇirājasumerumeghaiḥ sarvadharmadhātugaganaṃ spharan, anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sarvatathāgatabodhimaṇḍapratibhāsamaṇirājasumerumeghairdaśa diśaḥ spharan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya paścimāṃ diśamupaniśritya
body.translated_text: In the western direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the world-system called <s>Maṇisumerūvirocanadhvajapradīpā</s> (Lamp-Banner of Jewel-<s>Sumeru</s> Illumination), from the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmadhātujñānapradīpa</s> (Lamp of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-Knowledge), a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Samantaśrīsamudgatarāja</s> (King Arisen from Universal Glory), together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible world-system-ocean <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having been permitted by that Blessed One, rising from that assembly circle, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) with clouds of various-colored fragrance-banner <s>Sumeru</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of diverse fragrant flowers equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of multi-colored fragrant <s>Sumeru</s>-incense equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of variegated-colored fragrances equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-king <s>Sumeru</s>s born from the radiance of body-hairs, colored like all adornments, equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-jewel <s>Sumeru</s>s of various radiance-circle-array light-banner gems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of <s>Sumeru</s>s of various-colored vajra-womb <s>maṇi</s>-king jewels of various ornamental realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with clouds of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (gold) <s>maṇi</s>-jewel <s>Sumeru</s>s reflecting all world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, establishing the sky-surface covered with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-king <s>Sumeru</s>s reflecting all mountains and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> realm with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-king <s>Sumeru</s>s reflecting the marks of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> sky with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-king <s>Sumeru</s>s whose sound proclaims <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct and reveals the past spiritual practices of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, pervading the ten directions with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-king <s>Sumeru</s>s reflecting the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of enlightenment) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>; approaching the Blessed One, together with his retinue, having bowed to the Blessed One, settling in the western direction

body.text: sarvagandharājaśarīramuktājālasaṃchāditān kūṭāgārān devendrapratibhāsadhvajamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi ca siṃhāsanānyabhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya suvarṇamaṇirājasaṃchāditāni cintārājamakuṭāvabaddhāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: having magically created mansions covered with nets of body-emitting all-fragrance-king jewels and lion-thrones with <s>Devendra</s>-reflecting banner <s>maṇi</s>-jewel lotus-hearts, he sat down cross-legged, empowering the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with golden <s>maṇi</s>-king [garments] and crowned with <s>cintāmaṇi</s>-king (wish-fulfilling jewel) diadems. //

body.text: uttarāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa ratnavastrāvabhāsadhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau dharmadhātugaganaśrīvairocanasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādasaṅgaśrīrājo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sarvaratnapaṭṭameghālaṃkāram gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, pītavarṇapītanirbhāsaratnavastrameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, nānāgandhaparivāsitamaṇivastrameghapravarṣitālaṃkāraṃ gananatalamadhitiṣṭhan, ādityadhvajamaṇirājavastrameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, kanakaśrījvalanamaṇiratnavastrameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, ratnajvalanamaṇirājavastrameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sarvajyotiḥpratibimbavicitramaṇivastrameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, pāṇḍukambalaśilāvabhāsamaṇiratnavastrameghadaśadikparisphuṭaṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, vairocanaśrījvalanāvabhāsamaṇirājavastrameghadaśadikparisphuṭaṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, avabhāsottaptavaddikkulavairocanamaṇirājavastrameghadaśadikparisphuṭaṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sāgaravyūhamaṇirājavastrameghasaṃchannaṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan yen bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya uttarāṃ diśamupaniśritya sāgarasaṃbhavamaṇirājakūṭāgāravaiḍūryapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya siṃhakrāntamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditāni jyotirdhvajamaṇicūḍāvabaddhāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: In the northern direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, in the world-system called <s>Ratnavastrāvabhāsadhvajā</s> (Banner of Jewel-Garment Illumination), from the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmadhātugaganaśrīvairocana</s> (<s>Vairocana</s> of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-Sky Glory), a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Asaṅgaśrīrāja</s> (King of Unattached Glory), together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible world-system-ocean <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having been permitted by that Blessed One, rising from that ocean of assembly circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system; establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of all-jewel-silk, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of yellow-colored, yellow-radiant jewel-garments, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-jewel garments perfumed with various fragrances showering down, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of sun-banner <s>maṇi</s>-king garments, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of golden-glory-blazing <s>maṇi</s>-jewel garments, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of jewel-blazing <s>maṇi</s>-king garments, establishing upon the sky-surface an ornament of clouds of variegated <s>maṇi</s>-garments reflecting all luminosities, establishing upon the sky-surface, pervading the ten directions, clouds of <s>pāṇḍukambalaśilā</s> (pale-blanket-stone) radiant <s>maṇi</s>-jewel garments, establishing upon the sky-surface, pervading the ten directions, clouds of <s>Vairocana</s>-glory-blazing radiant <s>maṇi</s>-king garments, establishing upon the sky-surface, pervading the ten directions, clouds of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-king garments illuminating the horizon-quarters as if heated by radiance, establishing upon the sky-surface covered with clouds of ocean-array <s>maṇi</s>-king garments; approaching the Blessed One, together with his retinue, having bowed to the Blessed One, settling in the northern direction, having magically created ocean-born <s>maṇi</s>-king mansions and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) lotus-heart lion-thrones, he sat down cross-legged, empowering the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with lion-stride <s>maṇi</s>-king nets and crowned with radiance-banner <s>maṇi</s> crests. //

body.text: uttarapūrvasyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa sarvamahāpṛthivīrājamaṇiraśmijālapramuktāyā lokadhātoranilambhacakṣuṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāddharmadhātusunirmitapraṇidhicandro nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / ratnakūṭāgāre meghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, gandhakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, dhūpakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, candanakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, kusumakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, maṇikūṭāgāramedhasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, vajrakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, kanakakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, vastrakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan, padmakūṭāgārameghasaṃchannān sarvalokadhātuprasarānadhitiṣṭhan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya uttarapūrvāṃ diśamupaniśritya sarvaratnadharmadhātvabhimukhadvāraśikharamahāmaṇiratnakūṭāgārān
body.translated_text: In the northeastern direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the world-system called <s>Sarvamahāpṛthivīrājamaṇiraśmijālapramuktā</s> (Released from the Net of Rays of the Great-Earth-King Jewel), from the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Anilambhacakṣus</s> (Ungraspable Eye), a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmadhātusunirmitapraṇidhicandra</s> (Moon of Vows Well-Fashioned from the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>), together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible world-system-ocean <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having been permitted by that Blessed One, rising from that ocean of assembly circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system; establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of jewel-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of fragrance-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of incense-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of sandalwood-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of flower-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of <s>maṇi</s>-jewel-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of vajra-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of gold-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of garment-mansions, establishing all expanses of world-systems covered with clouds of lotus-mansions; approaching the Blessed One, together with his retinue, having bowed to the Blessed One, settling in the northeastern direction, [having created] great <s>maṇi</s>-jewel mansions of all-jewel-<s>dharmadhātu</s>-facing door-pinnacles

body.text: atulyagandharājamaṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyasīdat paryaṅkamābhujya kusumarājajālasaṃchāditāni vicitrakośajālamaṇimakuṭāvabaddhāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: and incomparable fragrance-king <s>maṇi</s> lotus-heart lion-thrones, having magically created [these], he sat down cross-legged, empowering the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with nets of flower-king garlands, crowned with variegated treasure-chest-net <s>maṇi</s> diadems. //

body.text: pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa gandhameghavyūhadhvajāyā lokadhātornāgeśvararājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāddharmārciṣmattejorājo nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalanayasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / kanakavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, anantavarṇaratnaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, tathāgatorṇavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, vicitraratnavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, padmagarbhaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, ratnadrumaśākhāmaṇḍalamaṇirājavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, tathāgatoṣṇīṣavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvaṃ gaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, jāmbūnadakanakavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, ādityavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalameghaiḥ sarvaṃ gaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan, candrajyotiścakramaṇḍalavarṇameghaiḥ sarvagaganatalaṃ saṃchādayan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya purvadakṣiṇāṃ diśamupaniśritya virajovairocanamaṇiśrīkusumakūṭāgāran siṃhavajramaṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya ratnārcijvalanamaṇirājasaṃchāditāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: From the southeast direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Nāgeśvararāja</s> in the world-system called <s>Gandhameghavyūhadhvajā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmārciṣmattejoirāja</s>, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of inexpressible world-systems, authorized by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that ocean of assembly-circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. Covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of golden-hued radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of infinite-colored jewel-radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>ūrṇā</s>-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of variegated jewel-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of lotus-womb radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of jewel-tree-branch-circle-gem-king-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of <s>Jāmbūnada</s>-gold-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of sun-colored radiance-circles, covering the entire surface of the sky with clouds of moon-light-wheel-circle-colored [radiance] — approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking up position in the southeast direction, having magically created mansions of stainless <s>Vairocana</s>-gem-splendor-flower-peaks and lion-thrones with diamond-gem-lotus-womb [seats], he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with jewel-flame-blazing-gem-kings. //

body.text: dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa maṇisūryapratibhāsagarbhāyā lokadhātordharmacandrasamantajñānāvabhāsarājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvajo nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān kusumārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān sarvavādyārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya akāśadhātuvipulān maṇiratnārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromakūpebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān nānāgandhadhūpadhūpitaratnavastrārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān nāgavikurvitavidyudarcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān vairocanamaṇiratnārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān suvarṇajvalanaratnārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulān śrīgarbhamaṇirājajvalanārcimeghān pramuñcan, sarvaromavivarebhya ākāśadhātuvipulāṃstathāgatasmṛtisamudrasadṛśatryadhvatalāvabhāsanayanaratnārcimeghān pramuñcan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya dakṣiṇapaścimāṃ diśamupaniśritya samantadigabhimukharaśmijālabindusaddharmadhātuprabhāsamahāmaṇiratnakūṭāgārān
body.translated_text: From the southwest direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacandrasamantajñānāvabhāsarāja</s> in the world-system called <s>Maṇisūryapratibhāsagarbhā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvaja</s>, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of inexpressible world-systems, authorized by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that ocean of assembly-circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. Releasing from all hair-pores clouds of flower-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of all-music-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of gem-jewel-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of jewel-garment-flames perfumed with various incense-fragrances as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of <s>Nāga</s>-transformation-lightning-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of <s>Vairocana</s>-gem-jewel-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of gold-blazing-jewel-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of <s>Śrīgarbha</s>-gem-king-blazing-flames as vast as the realm of space, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of jewel-flames illuminating the surfaces of the three times, resembling the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s>-remembrance, as vast as the realm of space — approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking up position in the southwest direction, [having magically created] great gem-jewel mansions of radiance of rays-nets-drops of the true <s>Dharma</s>-realm shining in all directions,

body.text: gandhapradīpārcimaṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya vyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya vimalagarbhamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditāni sarvasattvaprasthānanirghoṣamaṇirājamakuṭāvabaddhani bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: and lion-thrones with fragrant-lamp-flame-gem-lotus-womb [seats], he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with stainless-womb-gem-king-nets, bound with crowns of gem-kings resounding with the sound of the setting-forth of all beings. //

body.text: paścimottarāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa vairocanaśrīpraṇidhigarbhāyā lokadhātoḥ samantavairocanaśrīmerurājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādvairocanapraṇidhijñānaketurnām bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptāṃstathāgatakāyapratibimbameghān niścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptabodhisattvakāyapratibimbameghān niścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalakāyapratibimbameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptabuddhanirmāṇacakrapratibimbakāyameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptatathāgatapūrvayogapratibimbakāyameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakāyapratibimbameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrat sarvatryadhvaprāptatathāgatakāyabodhimaṇḍavṛkṣarūpapratibimbameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptabuddhavikurvitapratibimbakāyameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptalokendrakāyapratibimbameghānniścārayan, sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvaśarīrāt sarvatryadhvaprāptapariśuddhabuddhakṣetrameghānniścārayan, kṣaṇe kṣaṇe sarvamākāśadhātuṃ spharan yen bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya paścimottarāṃ diśamupaniśritya samantadigvairocanamaṇirājagarbhakūṭāgārān jagadvirocanamaṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya ajitaprabhamuktājālasaṃchānnāni samantāvabhāsaprabhāmaṇimakuṭāvabaddhāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: From the northwest direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantavairocanaśrīmerurāja</s> in the world-system called <s>Vairocanaśrīpraṇidhigarbhā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vairocanapraṇidhijñānaketu</s>, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of inexpressible world-systems, authorized by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that assembly-circle, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. From all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-body reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-body reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circle-body reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of Buddha-emanation-wheel reflection-bodies reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s> former-practice reflection-bodies reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-body reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-body <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-tree form reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of Buddha-transformation reflection-bodies reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of world-lord-body reflections reaching all three times; from all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from his entire body, emanating clouds of completely purified <s>buddhakṣetras</s> reaching all three times, pervading the entire realm of space at every moment — approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking up position in the northwest direction, having magically created mansions of <s>Vairocana</s>-gem-king-womb [shining] in all directions and lion-thrones of world-illuminating-gem-lotus-womb [seats], he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with unconquered-radiance-pearl-nets, bound with crowns of universally-illuminating-radiance-gems. //

body.text: adhodiśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalavairocanāyā lokadhātorasaṅgajñānaketudhvajarājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāmī nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrādabhyudgamya yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ sarvajaganmantrasāgarasvaraniruktinirhāranirghoṣānniścārayan, sarvatryadhvabodhisattvaprasūtinayasāgarameghanirghoṣānnigarjan, sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānābhinirhāranayasāgaranirghoṣān pramuñcan, sarvabodhisattvapāramitāpariśuddhiparipurinayasāgarameghanirghoṣān
body.translated_text: From the nadir direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Asaṅgajñānaketudhvajarāja</s> in the world-system called <s>Sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalavirocanā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāmī</s>, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of inexpressible world-systems, authorized by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that ocean of assembly-circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. Emanating from all hair-pores the sounds of utterances expressing the ocean of mantras of all beings in all worlds; thundering with the sounds of clouds of the ocean of methods of the arising of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the three times; releasing the sounds of the ocean of methods of the production of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows; releasing the sounds of clouds of the ocean of methods for the purification and fulfillment of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>pāramitās</s>;

body.text: pramuñcan, sarvabodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalasarvakṣetraspharaṇanayasāgaranirghoṣān pramuñcan, sarvabodhisattvasamudāgamavikurvitanayasāgaranirghoṣān pramuñcan, sarvatathāgatabodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamārakalivikiraṇabodhivibudhyanayavikurvaṇanirghoṣasāgarān pramuñcan, sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravartanasūtrāntanayanāmasāgaranirghoṣameghānnigarjan, sarvajagadvinayakālacakravinayadharmanayopāyanirghoṣān pramuñcan, sarvajñānādhigamayathāpraṇidhikuśalamūlaviśeṣakālopāyadharmanayasāgaranirghoṣān pramuñcan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya adhodiśamupaniśritya sarvatathāgatavimānapratibhāsagarbhasarvaratnavicitrakośakūṭāgārān sarvaratnaviddhapadmasaṃdhāritagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya sarvabodhimaṇḍapratibhāsadhvajamaṇimakuṭacūḍāvabaddhāni sarvakṣetrāvabhāsamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: releasing the sounds of the ocean of methods of the circle of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct pervading all fields; releasing the sounds of the ocean of methods of the accomplishment and transformation of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; releasing oceans of the sounds of the transformation-methods of approaching the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, scattering <s>Māra</s>'s strife, and awakening to <s>Bodhi</s>; thundering with clouds of the ocean of sounds of the <s>sūtrānta</s>-methods of the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; releasing the sounds of the methods of the <s>Dharma</s> of the wheel of times for the discipline of all beings in the world; releasing the sounds of the ocean of methods of the <s>Dharma</s> of the special times and means of meritorious roots according to vows for the attainment of all knowledge — approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking up position in the nadir direction, having magically created mansions of all-jewel-variegated-treasure-womb reflecting all <s>Tathāgata</s> palaces and lion-thrones held by all-jewel-studded-lotus-womb [supports], he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies bound with crown-crests of all-<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-reflection-banner-gems, covered with gem-king-nets illuminating all fields. //

body.text: urdhvāyāṃ diśi anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa akṣayabuddhavaṃśanirdeśāyā lokadhātoḥ samantajñānamaṇḍalapratibhāsanirghoṣasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāddharmadhātupraṇidhitalanirbhedo nāma bodhisattvaḥ sārdhamanabhilāpyalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaistena bhagavatā anujñātaḥ tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāduccalitvā yena sahālokadhātustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanebhyaḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ sarvakāyāt sarvāṅgapratyaṅgebhyaḥ sarvavacanapathebhyaḥ sarvacīvaraparivārebhyaḥ sarvabodhisattvaparivārasya ātmano bhagavataśca vairocanasya pūrvāntakoṭīgatānāṃ ca atītānāgatānāṃ sarvatathāgatānāmaparāntakoṭīgatānāṃ ca anāgatānāṃ vyākṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ pratyutpannānāṃ ca daśasu dikṣu sarvakṣetraprasarapratiṣṭhitānāṃ sarvadānapāramitāpratisaṃyuktān pūrvayogasamudrān sarvapratigrāhakadeyavastrapratibimbāni ca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaromamukhasarvaśarīrāṅgapratyaṅgavacanapathasarvaśarīraparivāreṣu pratibhāsaprāptāni vijñāpayan, sarvaśīlapāramitāpratisaṃyuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvakṣāntipāramitāsaṃprayuktānāṃ ca aṅgapratyaṅgacchedena nidarśanasaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvabodhisattvavīryavegavikramasaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvatathāgatadhyānasāgaraparyeṣṭiniṣpattisaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvatathāgatadharmacakragatipariniṣpattidharmaparyeṣṭisaṃprayuktānapi sarvāstiparityāgamahāvyavasāyaśarīramukhabimbavijñāpanān pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvatathāgatadarśanaprītisarvabodhisattvamārgasarvajagadabhirocanasaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānasāgarābhinirhāramukhapariśuddhivyūhasaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, sarvabodhisattvabalapāramitāniṣpattivikramaviśuddhisaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan, vipulavipulaṃ dharmadhātuṃ sarvavikurvitameghaiḥ spharitvā sarvabodhisattvajñānamaṇḍalasaṃprayuktānapi pūrvayogasamudrān
body.translated_text: From the zenith direction, beyond oceans of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānamaṇḍalapratibhāsanirghoṣa</s> in the world-system called <s>Akṣayabuddhavaṃśanirdeśā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmadhātupraṇidhitalanirbheda</s>, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of inexpressible world-systems, authorized by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that ocean of assembly-circles, approached the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. From all marks and minor marks, from all hair-openings, from the entire body, from all limbs and minor limbs, from all paths of speech, from all garment-retinues, from his own entire <s>bodhisattva</s>-retinue's and from the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>'s, and from all <s>Tathāgatas</s> past and future who have reached the ultimate limit of the past, and from all <s>Tathāgatas</s> future who have reached the ultimate limit of the future, both those predicted and those not yet predicted, and from all <s>Tathāgatas</s> presently established throughout all field-expanses in the ten directions — making known the oceans of former practices connected with all <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), and the reflections of all recipients and gifts reaching their marks, minor marks, hair-openings, entire body, limbs, minor limbs, speech-paths, and all body-retinues; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with all <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with all <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), including demonstrations through the cutting of limbs and minor limbs, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the heroic energy, vigor, and valor of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the seeking and accomplishment of the ocean of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the seeking of the <s>Dharma</s> for the accomplishment of the course and perfection of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, making known through body-mouth-images the great resolve of complete renunciation of all existence, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the delight in seeing all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the path of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and the illumination of all beings, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the adornment of the purification of the gates of production of the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows, reached in reflection; displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the purification of the valor and accomplishment of the <s>bala-pāramitā</s> (perfection of power) of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, reached in reflection; having pervaded the vast, vast <s>dharmadhātu</s> with all transformation-clouds, displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the knowledge-circle of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>,

body.text:
pratibhāsaprāptān saṃdarśayan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya ūrdhvāṃ diśamupaniśritya sarvavajrendravicitravyūhakūṭāgāran vajrendradhārāsamantabhadrabodhisattvanīlapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanāni ca abhinirmāya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkamābhujya sarvaratnajvalanamaṇirājajālasaṃchannāni
tryadhvatathāgatanāmanirghoṣamaṇirājahārapralambacūḍāmaṇiratnamakuṭāvabaddhāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇyadhiṣṭhāya //
body.translated_text: reached in reflection — approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking up position in the zenith direction, having magically created mansions adorned with all variegated diamond-lord [jewels] and lion-thrones of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>'s diamond-lord-stream blue-lotus-womb [seats], he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies covered with all-jewel-blazing-gem-king-nets, bound with crowns of gem-jewel-necklace-pendants and crest-jewels resounding with the names of <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times. //

body.text: sarve ca te bodhisattvāḥ saparivārāḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaniryātāḥ sarvatathāgatapādamūlamukhoddarśanāya pariśuddhajñānacakṣuṣaḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasūtrāntanayanirghoṣasamudrasuśrotrasamavasaraṇāḥ sarvabodhisattvavaśitāpratilambhaparamapāramiprāptāḥ sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇakṣaṇakṣaṇasaṃdarśanavikurvitaniryātāḥ sarvalokadhātvekakāyaspharaṇaviṣayāḥ sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalābhyudgatavirocanakāyāḥ ekaparamāṇurajasi sarvalokadhātvekalokadhātupratibhāsasamavasaraṇasaṃdarśanaviṣayāḥ sarvajagatparipācanavinayakālāgamanapravaṇāḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakramedhasarvaromamukhanigarjanaviṣayāḥ māyopamasarvasattvadhātuparijñāpratilabdhāḥ pratibhāsopamasarvatathāgatāvatīrṇāḥ svapnopamasarvabhavagatyupapattijñānaniryātāḥ pratibimbopamasarvakarmavipākajñānaviśuddhāḥ marīcyupamasarvābhinirvṛttijñānābhijñāḥ nirmitopamasarvalokadhātuprasarāvatīrṇāḥ daśatathāgatabalajñānāvabhāsapratilabdhāḥ vaiśāradyarṣabhasiṃhanādaparākramāḥ akṣayapratisaṃvitsamudrāvatīrṇāḥ sarvajaganmantrasāgaradharmaniruktijñānapratilabdhāḥ asaṅgadharmadhātugaganajñānagocarāḥ sarvadharmānāvaraṇajñānapratilabdhāḥ sarvabodhisattvābhijñājñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhāḥ sarvamāramaṇḍalavikṣobhaṇavīryāḥ sarvatryadhvajñānabalapratiṣṭhānāḥ anāvaraṇasarvajñānapratilabdhāḥ anālayagaganagocarāḥ anāyūhasarvajñatābhūmigaganavīryāḥ sarvabhavānilambhajñānagocarāḥ sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarajñānaprasaritāḥ sarvalokadhātvasaṃbhedajñānamukhapraviṣṭāḥ sarvalokadhātvanyonyasamavasaraṇavikurvitaniryātāḥ sarvalokadhātu kulopapatyupapannakāyasaṃdarśakāḥ sarvalokadhātusūkṣmodāravipulasaṃkṣiptanānāsaṃsthānapratividdhāḥ sūkṣmārambaṇaviopulakṣetrasamavasaraṇajñānādhigatāḥ vipulālambanasūkṣmajñānānugatāḥ sarvabuddhaikacittakṣaṇavihārapratilabdhāḥ sarvatathāgatajñānaśarīrāḥ sarvadiksāgarāsaṃmohajñānapratilabdhāsarvadiksamudraikacittakṣaṇavikurvitaspharaṇāḥ / evaṃrūpāpramāṇasamanvāgatairbodhisattvaiḥ sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ paripūrṇamabhūt yadut tathāgatānāmadhiṣṭhānena //
body.translated_text: And all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, together with their retinues, had emerged through the practice and vows of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>; they possessed purified knowledge-eyes for appearing face to face at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they had assembled with well-trained ears for the ocean of sounds of the <s>sūtrānta</s>-methods of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they had attained the supreme <s>pāramitā</s> of the mastery of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; they had emerged through the transformative display of showing the approach to all <s>Tathāgatas</s> at every moment; their range was the pervading of all world-systems with a single body; their bodies were radiant, having arisen from all <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles; their range was the display of assembling all world-systems reflected within a single atom; they were inclined toward arriving at the proper time for the ripening and disciplining of all beings; their range was the thundering from all hair-openings of the wisdom-rain of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they had attained full comprehension of the realm of all beings as illusion-like; they had descended into all <s>Tathāgatas</s> as reflection-like; they had emerged with knowledge of all births and destinies as dream-like; they were purified in the knowledge of the ripening of all <s>karma</s> as mirror-image-like; they had direct knowledge of all production of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) as mirage-like; they had descended into the expansion of all world-systems as emanation-like; they had attained the illumination of the knowledge of the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers; they had the valor of a lion's roar of fearlessness; they had descended into the ocean of inexhaustible <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge); they had attained the knowledge of the linguistic expression of the <s>Dharma</s> of the ocean of mantras of all beings; the range of their knowledge was the unattached sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; they had attained knowledge of non-obstruction of all <s>dharma</s>s; they were purified in the knowledge-circle of the <s>abhijñā</s>s of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; their energy was the confounding of all <s>Māra</s>-circles; their foundation was the power of knowledge of all three times; they had attained unobstructed omniscience; the range of their course was the non-clinging sky; their energy was the effortless sky of the stage of omniscience; the range of their knowledge was non-attachment to all existences; they were extended in the knowledge of the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s; they had entered the gates of knowledge of the non-differentiation of all world-systems; they had emerged through transformative displays of the mutual assemblage of all world-systems; they displayed bodies born into the families and births of all world-systems; they had penetrated all world-systems in their subtle, gross, vast, contracted, and various configurations; they had attained the knowledge of the assemblage of vast fields within subtle objects; they had entered the subtle knowledge through vast objects; they had attained the abiding in a single mind-moment of all <s>Buddha</s>s; their bodies were the knowledge-body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they had attained knowledge of non-confusion in all oceans of directions; their transformative pervading of all oceans of directions was in a single mind-moment. Endowed with such immeasurable [qualities], the <s>bodhisattvas</s> completely filled the entire <s>Jetavana</s> — that is, through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //

body.text: na ca te mahāśrāvakāḥ śāriputramaudgalyāyanamahākāśyaparevatasubhūtyaniruddhanandikakapphiṇakātyāyanapūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputrapramukhā jetavane tathāgatavikurvitamadrākṣuḥ / na ca tān buddhavyūhān buddhavṛṣabhitāṃ buddhavikrīḍitaṃ buddhaprātihāryaṃ buddhādhipateyatāṃ buddhacaritavikurvitaṃ buddhaprabhāvaṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhimadrākṣuḥ / nāpi tamacintyaṃ bodhisattvaviṣayaṃ bodhisattvasamāgamaṃ bodhisattvasamavasaraṇaṃ bodhisattvasaṃnipātaṃ bodhisattvopasaṃkramaṇaṃ bodhisattvavikurvitaṃ
