body.translated_text: But those great <s>śrāvakas</s> — <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Nandika</s>, <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> and others foremost among them — did not see the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s transformative display in the <s>Jetavana</s>. Nor did they see those <s>Buddha</s>-arrays, the <s>Buddha</s>'s bull-like majesty, the <s>Buddha</s>'s playful display, the <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous feats, the <s>Buddha</s>'s sovereignty, the <s>Buddha</s>'s conduct-transformations, the <s>Buddha</s>'s might, the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, or the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field. Nor did they [see] that inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s>-domain, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-gathering, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-congregation, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-approach,

body.text:
bodhisattvaprātihāryaṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalaṃ bodhisattvadigavasthānaṃ bodhisattvasiṃhāsanavyūhaṃ bodhisattvabhavanaṃ bodhisattvavihāraṃ bodhisattvasamādhivikrīḍitaṃ bodhisattvavyavalokita bodhisattvavijṛmbhitaṃ bodhisattvavikramaṃ bodhisattvatathāgatapūjāṃ bodhisattvavyākaraṇaṃ bodhisattvavipākaṃ bodhisattvaparākramaṃ bodhisattvadharmakāyapariśuddhiṃ bodhisattvajñānakāyaparipūriṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhikāyavijñaptiṃ bodhisattvarūpakāyapariniṣpattiṃ bodhisattvalakṣaṇasaṃpatpariśuddhiṃ bodhisattvānantabalaprabhāmaṇḍalavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaraśmijālapramuñcanaṃ bodhisattvanirmitameghāvasṛjanaṃ bodhisattvadigjālaspharaṇaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalavikurvitamadrākṣuḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? kuśalamūlāsabhāgatayā / na hi taiḥ sarvabuddhavikurvitadarśanasaṃvartanīyāni kuśalamūlānyupacitāni / na ca teṣāṃ pūrvaṃ daśadiglokadhātuparyāpannāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhapariśuddhayaḥ saṃvarṇitāḥ / na ca teṣāṃ buddhairbhagavadbhirnānābuddhavikurvitāni saṃvarṇitāni / na ca taiḥ pūrvaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaradbhiranuttarāyāṃ saṃyaksaṃbodhau sattvāḥ pāramitāsu samādāpitāḥ / na ca tairbodhicittotpādaḥ parasaṃtāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ / na ca te tathāgatavaṃśasyānupacchedāya pratipannāḥ / na ca sarvasattvasaṃgrahāya prayuktāḥ / na ca tairbodhisattvāḥ pāramitāsu samādāpitāḥ / na ca taiḥ pūrvaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaradbhiḥ sarvajagadviśeṣavatījñānabhūmiradhyālambitā / na ca taiḥ
sarvajñatāsaṃvartanīyaṃ kuśalamūlamupacitam / na ca taistathāgatalokottarakuśalamūlapariniṣpannāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhivikurvitābhijñā jñātāḥ / na ca bodhisattvacakṣuṣpathavijñaptirasādhāraṇalokottarabodhyālambanakuśalamūlamahābodhisattvapraṇidhānasaṃbhavājñātāḥ / na ca tathāgatādhiṣṭhānaniryātamāyāgatadharmatā nirvṛttāḥ / svapnopamabodhisattvanānāsaṃjñāgrahādhiṣṭhānā mahābodhisattvaprītivegavivardhanāḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvajñānacakṣuṣpathavijñaptayo 'sādhāraṇāḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairjñātāḥ / tena te mahāśrāvakāḥ agrayugabhadrayugapramukhāstaṃ tathāgatavikurvitaṃ na paśyanti, na śṛṇvanti, na jānanti, na budhyanti, nāvataranti, nādhimucyante nādhigacchanti, na samanvāharanti, na vilokayanti, na nirīkṣante, na nidhyāyanti, nopnidhyāyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? buddhajñānagocaro 'sau, na śrāvakagocaraḥ / tena te mahāśrāvakāstatraiva jetavane sthitāstāni buddhavikurvitāni na paśyanti / na hi teṣāṃ tadbhāgāya kuśalamūlamasti, na ca teṣāṃ tajjñānacakṣurviśuddham, yena tāni buddhavikurvitāni paśyeyuḥ / na ca samādhiḥ saṃvidyate, yena parīttālambane vipulavikurvitādhiṣṭhānānyavatareyuḥ / nāṣṭau vimokṣāḥ saṃvidyate, na sā ṛddhiḥ, na sā vṛṣabhitā, na tadbalam, na tadādhipateyam, na tatsthānam, na saṃjñā, na cakṣurvikramaḥ saṃvidyate, yena tatsaṃjānīyurvā paśyeyurvā avatareyurvā adhigaccheyurvā sphareyurvā vyavalokayeyurvā anubhaveyurvā ākrameyurvā pareṣāṃ prabhāvayeyurvā deśayeyurvā sūcayeyurvā saṃvarṇayeyurvā saṃdarśayeyurvā upanāmayeyurvā upasaṃhareyurvā, tatra vā sattvāni samādāpayeyuḥ, niryojayeyuḥ pratiṣṭhāpayeyuḥ, tasyāṃ buddhavikurvitadharmatāyāṃ
body.translated_text: the <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformations, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-miracles, the <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly-circles, the <s>bodhisattva</s> directional positions, the <s>bodhisattva</s> lion-throne arrays, the <s>bodhisattva</s> mansions, the <s>bodhisattva</s> abodes, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>-play, the <s>bodhisattva</s> gazing, the <s>bodhisattva</s> expansion, the <s>bodhisattva</s> valor, the <s>bodhisattva</s> worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> predictions, the <s>bodhisattva</s> fruitions, the <s>bodhisattva</s> heroic exertion, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>dharmakāya</s>-purification, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>jñānakāya</s>-fulfillment, the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow-body manifestation, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>rūpakāya</s>-perfection, the <s>bodhisattva</s> mark-endowment purification, the <s>bodhisattva</s> infinite-power radiance-circle array, the <s>bodhisattva</s> ray-net emission, the <s>bodhisattva</s> emanation-cloud releasing, the <s>bodhisattva</s> directional-net pervading, or the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-circle transformations. For what reason? Due to the incompatibility of their roots of merit. For they had not accumulated roots of merit conducive to seeing all <s>Buddha</s>-transformations. Nor had the purifications of the quality-arrays of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields throughout the ten directions of world-systems been described to them. Nor had the various <s>Buddha</s>-transformations been described to them by the <s>Buddha</s>s, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Nor had they, while transmigrating in <s>saṃsāra</s>, established beings in the <s>pāramitās</s> with a view to supreme perfect awakening. Nor had they established the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> in the mental continua of others. Nor had they practiced for the uninterrupted continuation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage. Nor had they been engaged in embracing all beings. Nor had they established <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>pāramitās</s>. Nor had they, while transmigrating in <s>saṃsāra</s>, aspired to the stage of knowledge surpassing all beings. Nor had they accumulated roots of merit conducive to omniscience. Nor had they, through the perfected supramundane roots of merit of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, come to know the <s>abhijñā</s>-transformations of the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Nor had they known the manifesting of the <s>bodhisattva</s> eye-path, born from the uncommon supramundane <s>bodhi</s>-object roots of merit and the vows of the great <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Nor had the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature), arisen from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment, as if come from nowhere, been accomplished [by them]. The manifestations of the eye-path of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>'s knowledge, which augment the rapturous energy of the great <s>bodhisattvas</s>, which rest upon the empowerment of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s dream-like various perception-grasping — these uncommon [realities] were [not] known by all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Therefore those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, foremost pairs and supreme pairs, did not see, did not hear, did not know, did not understand, did not penetrate, did not have faith in, did not attain, did not apprehend, did not observe, did not examine, did not reflect upon, did not deeply reflect upon that <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformation. For what reason? That is the domain of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, not the domain of <s>śrāvakas</s>. Therefore those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, though standing right there in the <s>Jetavana</s>, did not see those <s>Buddha</s>-transformations. For they did not possess roots of merit for that purpose, nor was their knowledge-eye purified such that they could see those <s>Buddha</s>-transformations. Nor did they possess the <s>samādhi</s> by which they might penetrate the empowerments of vast transformative displays within a limited object. Nor did they possess the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), nor that <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), nor that majesty, nor that strength, nor that sovereignty, nor that station, nor that perception, nor that eye-valor by which they might cognize, see, penetrate, attain, pervade, observe, experience, enter, make manifest to others, teach, indicate, praise, demonstrate, present, or recapitulate those [displays], or by which they might establish, exhort, or confirm beings therein, in that nature of <s>Buddha</s>-transformation.

body.text:
sattvānniyojayeyuḥ / tatteṣāṃ jñānaṃ na saṃvidyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi te śrāvakayānena niryātāḥ, śrāvakamārgeṇa samudāgatāḥ, śrāvakacaryāmaṇḍalaparipūrṇāḥ śravākaphalapratiṣṭhitāḥ, satyāvabhāsajñānaniśritāḥ bhūtakoṭīpratiṣṭhitāḥ / atyantaśāntaniṣṭhāṃ gatāḥ mahākarūṇāvirahitacetasaḥ sarvalokanirapekṣaḥ ātmakāryapariprāptāḥ / te tatraiva jetavane saṃnipatitāḥ
saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ / bhagavataḥ purato vāmadakṣiṇapṛṣṭhato bhagavato 'bhimukhaṃ saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ / na ca tāni jetavane buddhavikurvitānyadrākṣuḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi śakyamasamārjitasarvajñatājñānairasamudānītasarvajñatājñānaiḥ asaṃprasthitasarvajñatājñānaiḥ apraṇihitasarvajñatājñānaiḥ anabhinirhṛtasarvajñatājñānaiḥ aparibhāvitasarvajñatājñānaiḥ apariśodhitasarvajñatājñānaiḥ tattathāgatasamādhivikurvitamavatartuṃ vā pratipattuṃ vā draṣṭumadhigantuṃ vā / tatkasya hetoḥ? abhijātabodhisattvacakṣuṣpathavijñeyaṃ hi tat, na śrāvakacakṣuṣpathavijñeyam / tena te mahāśrāvakāstatraiva jetavane sthitāstāni tathāgatavikurvitāni buddhādhiṣṭhānāni buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ bodhisattvasaṃnipātaṃ na paśyanti //
body.translated_text: they might engage beings [in the path]. But that knowledge does not exist in them. What is the reason? For they have emerged by the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Vehicle of Hearers), have come forth by the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-path, are complete in the sphere of <s>Śrāvaka</s>-conduct, are established in the fruit of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, are grounded in the knowledge of the illumination of the [Four Noble] Truths, are established at the ultimate point of reality. They have attained the goal of absolute peace, their minds are devoid of great compassion, they are indifferent to the entire world, they have accomplished their own task. They were assembled and seated right there in <s>Jetavana</s>, seated before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to his left, right, and behind, facing the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Yet they did not see those <s>Buddha</s>-transformations in <s>Jetavana</s>. What is the reason? For it is not possible for those who have not cultivated the knowledge of omniscience, who have not accumulated the knowledge of omniscience, who have not set forth toward the knowledge of omniscience, who have not aspired to the knowledge of omniscience, who have not produced the knowledge of omniscience, who have not developed the knowledge of omniscience, who have not purified the knowledge of omniscience — to enter into, understand, see, or realize that transformation arising from the <s>samādhi</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. What is the reason? For that is to be known by the vision-path of noble <s>bodhisattva</s>s, not by the vision-path of <s>śrāvaka</s>s. Therefore those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s, remaining right there in <s>Jetavana</s>, do not see those <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations, those <s>Buddha</s>-empowerments, those purifications of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, those assemblies of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma gaṅgāyā mahānadyā ubhayatastīre bahūni pretaśatasahasrāṇi samāgatāni kṣutpipāsāprapīḍitāni nagnāni nirvasanāni vidagdhagātracchavivarṇāni vātātapapariśuṣkāṇi kākasaṃghopadrutāni vṛkaśṛgālairvitrāsyamānāni tāṃ gaṅgāṃ mahānadīṃ na paśyanti / kecitpunaḥ śuṣkāṃ paśyanti nirudakāṃ bhasmaparipūrṇām, āvaraṇīyakarmāvṛtatvāt / evameva te sthavirā mahāśrāvakāstatraiva jetavane sthitāḥ tāni tathāgatavikurvitāni na paśyanti, nāvataranti, sarvajñatāvipakṣikāvidyāpaṭalanetraparyavanaddhatvāt, sarvajñatābhūmikuśalamūlāparigṛhītatvāt //
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, on both banks of the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>preta</s>s (hungry ghosts) have gathered — tormented by hunger and thirst, naked, without clothing, with bodies scorched and skin discolored, dried up by wind and sun, harassed by flocks of crows, terrified by wolves and jackals — they do not see that great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Some see it as dry, waterless, filled with ashes, because they are obscured by obstructive <s>karma</s>. Just so, those elder great <s>śrāvaka</s>s, remaining right there in <s>Jetavana</s>, do not see those <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations, do not enter into them, because their eyes are enveloped by the veil of ignorance that is adverse to omniscience, because they have not gathered the roots of merit belonging to the stage of omniscience. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma puruṣo mahatyahni vartamāne mahato janakāyasya madhye styānamiddhamavakrāmet / sa suptaḥ svapnāntaragatastatraiva pradeśe devanagaraṃ paśyet / sudarśanacakranilayaṃ sarvaṃ ca sumerutalaṃ savṛkṣaṃ sodyānamaṇḍalamapsaraḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrākīrṇaṃ devaputrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrādhyuṣitaṃ vicitradivyapuṣpābhikīrṇam / vividhadivyavastramuktāhāraratnābharaṇasrakpramuktakośāṃśca kalpavṛkṣān paśyet / nānāvidhadivyavādyasamīritamanojñamadhuranirghoṣāṃśca vādyavṛkṣān paśyet / anekavidhāṃśca ratikrīḍāvyūhān paśyet / madhurāṃśca divyāpsarogaṇasaṃgītivādyaśabdān śṛṇuyāt / tatrasthaṃ cātmānaṃ saṃjānīyāt / sarvāvantaṃ ca tatpradeśaṃ divyavyūhavibhūṣitaṃ paśyet / sa ca sarvo janakāyo na paśyet, na jānīyāt, na vilokayet, tatraiva pradeśe sthitaḥ san / tatkasya hetoḥ? tasyaiva hi puruṣasya svapnāntaragatasya taddarśanam, tatraiva ca pradeśe sthitasya tasya mahājanakāyasyādarśanam / evameva te bodhisattvāste ca lokendrā bodhyabhimukhā vipulena buddhādhiṣṭhānena svakuśalamūlasusamārjitatayā ca sarvajñatāpraṇidhānasvabhinirhṛtatayā ca sarvatathāgataguṇasupratipannatayā ca mahāvyūhabodhisattvamārgasupratiṣṭhitatayā ca sarvajñatājñānasarvākāradharmodgatasupariniṣpannatayā ca samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāviśeṣapraṇidhānaparipūriviśuddhyā
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, while a great day proceeds, a man in the midst of a great crowd of people might be overcome by sloth and torpor. Asleep, having entered a dream, in that very place he might see the city of the gods, the abode of the <s>Sudarśana</s> circle, the entire surface of <s>Sumeru</s>, with its trees and pleasure-gardens filled with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), inhabited by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of <s>devaputra</s>s (divine youths), strewn with various divine flowers. He might see wish-fulfilling trees with treasuries of various divine garments, pearl necklaces, gem ornaments, and garlands laid open. He might see music-trees producing sounds of charming and sweet melody stirred by various divine instruments. He might see manifold arrays of pleasure and play. He might hear the sweet sounds of singing and music of hosts of divine <s>apsaras</s>. He might recognize himself as being present there. He might see that entire region adorned with divine arrays. But that entire crowd of people would not see it, would not know it, would not behold it, though standing in that very place. What is the reason? For that vision belongs only to that man who has entered the dream, while for that great crowd of people standing in that very place, there is non-seeing. Just so, those <s>bodhisattva</s>s and those lords of the world, facing awakening, by the vast empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, by virtue of their own well-cultivated roots of merit, by virtue of having produced the vow for omniscience, by virtue of being well-devoted to all the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by virtue of being well-established on the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path of the great array, by virtue of having well-accomplished the arising of the <s>dharma</s> in all aspects of the knowledge of omniscience, by the purity of the fulfillment of the special vow of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>

body.text: ca sarvabodhisattvabhūmijñānamaṇḍalākramaṇatayā ca sarvabodhisattvasamādhivihāravikrīḍanatayā ca sarvabodhisattvajñānagocarāsaṅgavicāraṇatayā ca tāmacintyāṃ buddhavṛṣabhitāṃ buddhavikrīḍitaṃ paśyanti, avataranti, anubhavanti / te ca mahāśrāvakā agrayugabhadrayugapramukhā na paśyanti na jānanti bodhisattvacakṣurvirahitatvāt //
body.translated_text: and by virtue of treading the knowledge-sphere of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages, and by virtue of sporting in the <s>samādhi</s>-abode of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, and by virtue of wandering unobstructed in the knowledge-range of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s — they see, enter into, and experience that inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-magnificence and <s>Buddha</s>-play. But those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s, led by the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, do not see and do not know, being devoid of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-eye. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma himavati parvatarāje auṣadhyākarākīrṇe mantravidyauṣadhijñānagrahaṇasiddhavidyaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvauṣadhividhīn prajānan auṣadhigrahaṇakarma kuryāt / tatraiva ca śailendrābhirūḍhāḥ paśugaveḍakaṛkṣamṛgalubdhakāstadanye vā punarauṣadhyavidhijñāḥ puruṣāstamauṣadhirasavīryavipākaprabhāvopāyayogaṃ na prajānanti / evemeva te bodhisattvāstathāgatajñānaviṣayamavatīrṇā bodhisattvavikurvitaviṣayananiryātāstaṃ tathāgatasamādhivikurvitaviṣayaṃ prajānanti, te ca mahāśrāvakāagrayugabhadrayugapramukhāstatraiva jetavane viharantaḥ svakāryasaṃtuṣṭāḥ parakāryanirutsukā upekṣakā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāreṇa sukhasparśaṃ viharanti, taṃ ca tathāgatasamādhiviṣayavikurvitaviṣayaṃ na prajānanti //
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, on the king of mountains <s>Himavat</s>, filled with treasuries of medicinal herbs, a man accomplished in the knowledge of mantras, sciences, and herbs, knowing all the methods of herbs, might perform the work of gathering herbs. And right there, cattle-herders, sheep-herders, bears, deer, hunters, and other men who have climbed those mountain-peaks, being ignorant of the methods of herbs, do not know the method of the sap, potency, ripening, power, and application of those herbs. Just so, those <s>bodhisattva</s>s who have descended into the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge and have emerged into the domain of <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformations know that domain of the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. But those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s, led by the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, dwelling right there in <s>Jetavana</s>, content with their own task, without concern for the task of others, indifferent, dwell in the comfort of the pleasant abiding of the present <s>dharma</s>, and do not know that domain of the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī sarvaratnākarasamṛddhā nidhiśatasahasranicitā nānāvidhānantaratnaparipūrṇā / tatra ratnagotravidhijñānakṛtavidyaḥ puruṣo rantaparīkṣastatra paryavadātamatirvidhānatantrajñānaśilpasuśikṣito vipulapuṇyabalopastabdhaḥ tato yatheṣṭaṃ ratnānyādāaya ātmānaṃ samyak prīṇayet, mātāpitaraṃ samyakparicaret, putradāraṃ ca poṣayet / tadanyeṣāmapi sattvānāṃ vṛddhānāmāturāṇāṃ daridrāṇāṃ vinipatitānāmaśanavasanaviprahīṇānāṃ saṃvibhāgaṃ kuryāt / vividhāṃ ca artharatimanubhavet / ye tu punaste ratnākaranidhānāvidhijñāḥ sattvāḥ, akṛtapuṇyā apariśuddharatnajñānacakṣuṣasteṣāṃ ratnākarān ratnanidhīnna prajānanti, tatraiva ca vicaranti / na ca ratnāni gṛhṇanti / na ratnakāryāṇi kurvanti / evaṃ te bodhisattvā jetavane tatra acintye tathāgataviṣaye supariśuddhajñānacakṣuṣo 'cintyatathāgatajñānaviṣayāvatīrṇāstāni buddhavikurvitāni paśyanti / dharmanayasāgarāṃścāvataranti / samādhisamudrāṃśca niṣpādayanti / tathāgatapūjopasthāne ca prayujyante / sarvadharmaparigrahāya codyujyante / sarvasattvāṃśca saṃgṛhṇanti caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ / te ca mahāśrāvakāstāni tathāgatavikurvitāni taṃ ca mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇasaṃnipātaṃ na paśyanti na jānanti //
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, this great earth is rich with all gem-mines, stored with hundreds of thousands of treasuries, filled with various infinite gems. There, a man accomplished in the knowledge of the methods of gem-lore, skilled in gem-examination, of purified mind, well-trained in the knowledge and art of the method-treatises, supported by the power of vast merit — from there he might take gems as he wishes and properly satisfy himself, properly attend to his parents, support his wife and children. He might also share with other beings who are old, sick, destitute, fallen, and deprived of food and clothing. He might enjoy manifold pleasure in wealth. But those beings who are ignorant of the methods of gem-mines and treasuries, who have not performed merit, whose gem-knowledge-eye is not purified — they do not know the gem-mines and gem-treasuries, though they wander in that very place. They neither take the gems nor perform gem-tasks. Just so, those <s>bodhisattva</s>s in <s>Jetavana</s>, in that inconceivable domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with their well-purified knowledge-eye, having descended into the inconceivable domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, see those <s>Buddha</s>-transformations. They enter into the oceans of <s>dharma</s>-methods, accomplish the oceans of <s>samādhi</s>, apply themselves to the worship and service of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, strive for the comprehension of all <s>dharma</s>s, and gather all beings by the four means of attraction. But those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s do not see those <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations, nor that great assembly of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, nor do they know them. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma puruṣo dūṣyavastrābaddhābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ ratnadvīpamanuprāptaḥ syāt / sa tatra ratnadvīpe caṃkramet, tiṣṭhet, niṣīdet, śayyāṃ vā kalpayet, na ca taṃ ratnākaraṃ paśyet / na ratnavṛkṣān, na vastraratnāni, na gandharatnāni, na sarvaratnāni paśyet / nāpi tāni ratnāni parijānīyādviṣayato vā mūlyato vā paribhogato va / sa tāni ratnāni na parigṛhṇīyāt, na ca ratnakāryamanubhavet / anāvṛtacakṣuṣaḥ etatsarvaṃ paśyeyurvijānīyuḥ / evameva te bodhisattvā dharmaratnadvīpamanuprāptā anuttaraṃ tathāgataratnaṃ sarvalokālaṃkāraṃ saṃmukhībhūtaṃ jetavane sthitamacintyāni
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, a man might arrive at a jewel-island with both eyes bound by a dirty cloth. He might walk, stand, sit, or lie down on that jewel-island, yet he would not see that gem-mine, nor the gem-trees, nor the garment-gems, nor the fragrance-gems, nor any gems at all. He would not know those gems by their domain, value, or use. He would not gather those gems, nor experience the function of gems. But those with uncovered eyes would see all of this and know it. Just so, those <s>bodhisattva</s>s, having arrived at the island of <s>dharma</s>-gems, with the unsurpassed <s>Tathāgata</s>-gem — the ornament of the entire world — present before them, dwelling in <s>Jetavana</s>, displaying inconceivable

body.text: buddhavikurvitāni saṃdarśayamānaṃ paśyanti / te ca mahāśrāvakāstatraiva bhagavataḥ pādamūle tiṣṭhanti yāpayanti, na ca taṃ tathāgatasamādhiviṣayavikurvitaprātihāryaṃ paśyanti, na ca taṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvasaṃnipātaṃ mahāratnākaram / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi teṣāṃ sarvajñatāvipakṣāvidyādūṣyāvabaddhajñānacakṣuṣāṃ tadasaṅgabodhisattvajñānacakṣurna pariśuddham, na ca tairdharmadhātuparaṃparāpraveśo 'nubuddhaḥ, yena tadacintyatathāgatasamādhivṛṣabhitāvikurvitaprātihāryaṃ paśyeyuḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>-transformations, see them. But those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s remain and dwell right there at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, yet do not see that miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>samādhi</s>-domain-transformation, nor that great assembly of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, that great gem-mine. What is the reason? For their knowledge-eyes are bound by the dirty cloth of ignorance adverse to omniscience, and the unobstructed <s>bodhisattva</s> knowledge-eye is not purified in them, nor have they awakened to the successive entry into the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena), by which they might see that inconceivable miraculous display of the magnificent <s>samādhi</s>-transformation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma asti virajaḥprabhāsavatī nāma cakṣuḥpariśuddhiḥ, yā sarvatamondhakāreṇa sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati / tāṃ kaścitpuruṣaḥ pratilabheta / sa virajaḥprabhāsavatyā cakṣuḥpariśuddhyā samanvāgatastamondhakāraparyavanaddhāyāṃ rātryāmanekeṣāṃ prāṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saṃnipatītānāṃ vividhākalperyāpathānāṃ nimirāndhakāraparyākulanetrāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye 'nuvicaret, anucaṃkramet, tiṣṭhet, niṣīdet, nāneryāpathān, vā kalpayet / na ca te manuṣyāstaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyeyuḥ, na saṃjānīyuḥ vividhānīryāpathān kalpayamānam / sa ca puruṣastaṃ mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ paśyet nāneryāpathākalpavihāriṇaṃ nānādigabhimukhaṃ nānāsaṃsthānaṃ nānāvarṇaṃ nānāprāvaraṇam / evemeva tathāgataḥ sabodhisattvagaṇaparivāro viśuddhāsaṅgajñānacakṣuḥ sarvalokaṃ jānāti paśyati / mahābuddhasamādhivikurvitaprātihāryaṃ saṃdarśayati / na ca te mahāśrāvakāstaṃ tathāgatamahājñānasamādhivikurvitaprātihāryaṃ paśyanti, na ca taṃ mahābodhisattvasaṃnipātaparivāram //
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, there is a purification of vision called <s>Virajaḥprabhāsavatī</s> (Stainless and Radiant), which does not coexist with any darkness or obscurity. Some man might obtain it. That man, endowed with the <s>Virajaḥprabhāsavatī</s> purification of vision, in the pitch-dark night, might move about, walk, stand, sit, or assume various postures in the midst of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of assembled human beings — humans with eyes bewildered by the deep darkness, of various postures and appearances. But those human beings would not see that man, would not recognize him assuming his various postures. Yet that man would see that great crowd of people, dwelling in various postures, facing various directions, of various forms, various colors, various coverings. Just so, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, accompanied by his retinue of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with his purified, unobstructed knowledge-eye, knows and sees the entire world. He displays the miraculous display of the great <s>Buddha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-transformation. But those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s do not see that miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s great knowledge-<s>samādhi</s>-transformation, nor that retinue of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣurmahato janakāyasya madhye pṛthivīkṛtsnaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyeta, apkṛtsnaṃ vā, tejaḥkṛstnaṃ vā, vāyukṛtsnaṃ vā, nīlakṛtnraṃ vā, pītakṛtsnaṃ vā, lohitakṛtsnaṃ vā, avadātakṛtsnaṃ vā, devakṛtsnaṃ vā, vividhasattvakāryakṛtsnaṃ vā, sarvarutaravitakṛtsnaṃ vā, sarvālambanakṛtsnaṃ vā samādhiṃ samāpadyeta / na ca sa mahājanakāyastamapskandhaṃ paśyet, na ca taṃ jvalanālokaṃ na ca tadvividhakāyakṛtsnam yāvat taṃ sarvālambanakṛtsnaṃ na paśyet, anyatra tatsamādhisamāpattivihāraprāptebhyaḥ / evameva tathāgatasya tadacintyabuddhasamādhiviṣayavikurvitaṃ saṃdarśayataḥ ye mahāśrāvakā na paśyanti, te ca bodhisattvastathāgatamārgapratipannāstaṃ tathāgataviṣayamavataranti //
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the midst of a great crowd of people might enter the <s>samādhi</s> of the totality of earth, or the totality of water, or the totality of fire, or the totality of wind, or the totality of blue, or the totality of yellow, or the totality of red, or the totality of white, or the totality of the divine, or the totality of various activities for beings, or the totality of all sounds and cries, or the totality of all objects. But that great crowd of people would not see that mass of water, nor that blazing light, nor those various body-totalities, up to and including the totality of all objects — except for those who have attained the abode of that <s>samādhi</s> attainment. Just so, when the <s>Tathāgata</s> displays that inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-domain-transformation, those great <s>śrāvaka</s>s who do not see it, while those <s>bodhisattva</s>s who have entered the <s>Tathāgata</s>-path enter into that domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma añjanasiddhaḥ puruṣo netrayorañjitamātrayoḥ sarvajanakāyenādṛśyaśarīro bhavati / sa gacchan vā sthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā sarvajanakāyaṃ paśyati / evemeva tathāgato lokottarasarvajagadviṣayasamatikrāntaḥ sarvajñajñānaviṣayāvakrānto bodhisattvajñānacakṣurvijñeyaḥ / sa sarvajagat paśyati / te ca mahāśrāvakāstāni tathāgatavikurvitāni na paśyanti //
body.translated_text: Just as a man who has mastered the <s>añjana</s> (eye-ointment) <s>siddhi</s>, having merely anointed his eyes, becomes invisible in body to all people — he, whether walking, standing, or sitting, sees all people — even so the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having transcended all supramundane realms of all beings, having entered the domain of <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), is to be known through the wisdom-eye of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. He sees all beings, yet those great <s>śrāvakas</s> do not see those transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma puruṣasya sahajātā devatā nityānubaddhā / sā taṃ puruṣaṃ paśyati, sa ca puruṣastāṃ devatāṃ na paśyati / evameva tathāgataḥ sarvajñajñānaviṣayāvasthito mahānti buddhavikurvitāni saṃdarśayati mahato bodhisattvagaṇasaṃnipātasya madhye / te ca mahāśrāvakāstaṃ tathāgatavikurvitaprātihāryaṃ tacca bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalavikurvitaṃ na paśyanti na jānanti //
body.translated_text: Just as a deity born together with a man follows him constantly — she sees that man, but that man does not see that deity — even so the <s>Tathāgata</s>, abiding in the domain of <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), displays great <s>buddhavikurvita</s> (Buddha-transformations) in the midst of the great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Yet those great <s>śrāvakas</s> neither see nor know that miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s transformations, nor the transformations of that assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣuḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptaḥ saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno na saṃjānāti na vedayati, na ca ṣaḍindriyeṇa kiṃcitkāryamanubhavati, na ca parinirvṛtaḥ saḥ / sarvalokavyavahāraśca tasmin pradeśe pravartante / na ca tān saṃjānāti, na vedayati yaduta tasyā eva samāpatteradhiṣṭhānādhipatyena / evemeva te mahāśrāvakāstatraiva jetavane viharanti, ṣaḍindriyaṃ caiṣāmasti, na ca taṃ tathāgatasamādhivikurvitavṛṣabhitāprātihāryaṃ paśyanti, nāvataranti, na saṃjānanti, na vijānanti, na ca taṃ mahābodhisattvasaṃnipātam bodhisattvaprātihāryaṃ bodhisattvavikurvitamavataranti, na paśyanti na jānanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? gambhīro hi buddhaviṣayo vipulo 'prameyo durdṛśo duṣpratibodho duravagāhaḥ sarvalokasamatikrāntaḥ / acintyo buddhaviṣayo 'saṃhāryaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ / tena te mahāśrāvakāstatraiva jetavane bhagavataḥ pādamūlagatāstāni buddhavikurvitāni na paśyanti / taṃ ca mahābodhisattvasaṃnipātam tacca jetavanamacintyāsaṃkhyeyaviśuddhalokadhātuguṇavyūhasamavasaraṇaṃ na paśyanti na jānanti yathāpi tadabhājanībhūtatvāt //
body.translated_text: Just as a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has attained the supreme perfection of complete mastery over all mental states, having entered the cessation of perception and feeling, neither perceives nor feels, nor experiences any function through the six sense faculties, yet is not passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — and all worldly transactions continue in that place, yet he neither perceives nor feels them, precisely by the power and sovereignty of that attainment — even so those great <s>śrāvakas</s> dwell right there in <s>Jetavana</s>, and they possess six sense faculties, yet they do not see that miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>samādhi</s>-transformation and excellence, nor do they penetrate, perceive, or understand it, nor do they penetrate, see, or know that great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the miraculous display of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the transformations of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? Because the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> is profound, vast, immeasurable, difficult to see, difficult to awaken to, difficult to fathom, and transcends the entire world. The domain of the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable, not to be apprehended by all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Therefore those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, though dwelling right there at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, do not see those <s>Buddha</s>-transformations, and they neither see nor know that great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, nor that <s>Jetavana</s> adorned with the qualities and arrays of inconceivable, innumerable, pure world-realms — because they are unfit vessels for it.

body.text: atha khalu vairocanapraṇidhānābhiraścimaprabho bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vairocanapraṇidhānābhiraścimaprabhā</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Behold, of the Essence of Beings, the <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable;
At <s>Jetadhvaja</s> the <s>Jina</s> displays the <s>Buddha</s>-transformations. (1)
The empowerment of the Self-Arisen proceeds innumerably,
Whereby the world that does not know the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> is bewildered. (2)
Profound, immeasurable, inconceivable is the miraculous display

children.text: pravartate prātihāryaṃ yatra loko na gāhate // 3 //
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Dharma</s>-kings, which the world cannot fathom. (3)
The fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> are of infinite forms, beautifully adorned with marks,

children.text: alakṣaṇā hi te dharmā ye saṃbuddhaiḥ prabhāvitāḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Yet those <s>dharmas</s> which the <s>Buddhas</s> have revealed are without marks. (4)
The <s>Jina</s> displays transformations in the grove called <s>Jeta</s>,
Infinite, unfathomable, profound, and most difficult through paths of speech. (5)
The great assembly of great beings the <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not see —
Those who have come from inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of fields to behold the <s>Jina</s>. (6)
Endowed with <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows), whose conduct and domain are unattached,
The entire world cannot know their intention. (7)
All <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> and all <s>śrāvakas</s> whatsoever

children.text: na prajānanti te caryāṃ na caiṣāṃ cittagocaram // 8 //
children.translated_text: Do not comprehend their practice, nor is it within the range of their minds. (8)
The <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great wisdom, invincible, unconquered,
With heroic banners raised, unconfused, devoted to the stages of knowledge, (9)
Immeasurable, of great renown, they have entered <s>samādhi</s>;
Having pervaded the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, they display their transformations. (10)

body.text: atha khalu duryodhanavīryavegarājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Duryodhanavīryavegarāja</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Behold the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, treasures of merit, of great wisdom,
Who have reached the course of <s>bodhicaryā</s>, who bring safety to all the world! (11)
Intelligent, of infinite understanding, with well-concentrated minds,
Whose domain of knowledge is infinite, unfathomable, profound, and vast, (12)
In the great forest called <s>Jeta</s>, adorned with great arrays,
Filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the hermitage of the Perfectly Awakened One, (13)
Behold the many oceans — homeless, without abode —
Who have come from the ten directions and are seated on lotus seats, (14)
Without foundation, without elaboration, without clinging, without abode,
With unattached minds, free from dust, devoted to the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, (15)
Banners of knowledge, great heroes, with vajra-minds, unshakeable;
In <s>dharmas</s> that are without cessation, they display <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (16)
From innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of fields in the ten directions they have come,
Having approached the Fully Awakened One, free from the notion of duality. (17)
They behold this transformation of the Self-Arisen, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>,
By whose empowerment these <s>bodhisattvas</s> have assembled. (18)
Unconfused regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and the planes of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
The sons of the <s>Jina</s> have reached the far shore of distinctions that are mere conventions. (19)
The sages stand at the ultimate point of the indivisibility of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
And with inexhaustible words they expound the divisions of the <s>Dharma</s>. (20)

body.text: atha khalu samantaśrīsamudgatatejorājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaśrīsamudgatatejorāja</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Behold the vast maṇḍala of knowledge of the Essence of Beings;
Knowing the right and wrong time, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to living beings. (21)
Crusher of rival doctrines thronged with various heretics,
He displays transformations according to the dispositions of beings. (22)

children.text: na ca pradeśa saṃbuddho na ca buddho diśānugaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Fully Awakened One is not limited to a region, nor is the <s>Buddha</s> confined to a direction;
The great sage has not transgressed the immeasurable measures. (23)
Just as the sun, measurer of days, illuminates while traversing the sky,
So the Teacher, master of knowledge, is empowered through non-attachment in the three times. (24)
Just as on the full-moon night the orb of the moon shines,
So one beholds the Guide, complete with white (pure) <s>dharmas</s>. (25)
Just as here in the sky the orb of the sun travels
Yet does not remain here — such is the <s>Buddha</s>'s transformation. (26)
Just as space in all directions is unsupported in all fields,
So should the <s>Buddha</s>-transformation of the Light of the World be understood. (27)

children.text: yathā hi pṛthivī loke pratiṣṭhā sarvadehinām /
children.translated_text: Just as the earth in the world is the support of all embodied beings,
So stands the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of the Light of the World in the world. (28)
Just as the wind, unattached, swiftly blows through space,
So the nature of the <s>Buddha</s> operates in all world-realms. (29)
Just as all world-systems are established upon the mass of water,
So the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times are established upon the mass of knowledge. (30)

body.text: atha khalu asaṅgaśrīgarbharājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Asaṅgaśrīgarbharāja</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Just as a mountain peak, lofty, born of diamond,
So the <s>Buddha</s>, protector of all the world, has arisen in the world. (31)
Just as the water in the ocean is immeasurable and clear,
So the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> cuts through the thirst of the world. (32)
Just as Mount <s>Meru</s>, king of mountains, rises from the ocean waters,
So the Light of the World has arisen from the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>. (33)
Just as the ocean is full, a great mine of all jewels,
So is the knowledge of the Self-Arisen — inexhaustible, instantaneous awakening. (34)
Profound is the knowledge of the Guide, innumerable and immeasurable;
He displays the immeasurable and inconceivable by which the <s>Buddha</s> performs transformations. (35)
Just as a skilled magician displays the characteristics of illusion,
So the <s>Buddha</s>, master of knowledge, is the displayer of transformations. (36)
Just as a pure <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) fulfills desired aims,
So the <s>Jina</s> fulfills the vows of those whose intentions are pure. (37)
Just as the <s>Vairocana</s> gem illuminates, making things shine,
So <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), perfectly pure, illuminates the intentions of the world. (38)
Likewise the <s>digmukha</s> gem, octagonal, well-established,
So too the unattached Light illuminates the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. (39)
Like the radiance of water, of pure lustre, which clarifies turbid waters,
So the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> purifies the sense faculties of the world. (40)

body.text: atha khalu dharmadhātupraṇidhisunirmitacandrarājo bodhisattvo buddhadhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharmadhātupraṇidhisunirmitacandrarāja</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Just as by an <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) all directions are made of one color,
So the hue of <s>bodhi</s> makes the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> for all beings. (41)
In each and every one, that <s>Buddha</s> displays manifold transformations,
Immeasurable, purifying the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. (42)
That is exceedingly wondrous, profound, boundless, unapproachable,
Which the world cannot fathom — the domain of knowledge of the wise. (43)
And the arrays too, perfected, purified by the <s>Buddha</s>'s work,
Through the entry into the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' attainment. (44)
Inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-fields where the <s>Jina</s> displays,
Surrounded by <s>Buddhas</s> attended by the wise, filled on every side. (45)
The Teacher, master of all <s>dharmas</s>, has arisen, the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>,
Whose immeasurable miraculous display proceeds. (46)
Behold the manifold and immeasurable conduct of the steadfast ones,
The one of boundless splendor displays infinite transformations. (47)
The Lord of the World trains the true sons of the <s>Jina</s> in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>;
They become those whose domain of knowledge in all <s>dharmas</s> is unattached. (48)
By the empowerment of the Lord of Men, the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel turns,
Filled with hundreds of miraculous displays, purifying the entire world. (49)
In the domain of the Essence of Beings, purified by the maṇḍala of knowledge,
Of abundant wisdom, great <s>nāgas</s>, liberators of all the world. (50)

body.text: atha khalu dharmārciṣmattejorājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharmārciṣmattejorāja</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Those <s>śrāvakas</s> who are trained in the three times by the supreme sage,
They do not know the stepping forth and stepping down of the Fully Awakened One. (51)
Even those <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, in all three times without remainder,
Even they do not know the stepping forth and stepping down of the Protector. (52)

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ sarvasattvā hi vijñāsyanti vināyakam /
children.translated_text: How much less will all beings know the Guide,
They who are like dogs on a leash, enveloped in the darkness of ignorance? (53)
He is immeasurable by any measure; the <s>Jina</s> cannot be known;
The <s>Buddha</s> possessing unattached knowledge has transcended the path of speech. (54)
Steadfast, radiant as the full moon, beautifully adorned with marks,
He exhausts immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, presiding through his transformations. (55)
By method, contemplating the <s>Buddha</s> one-pointedly, well-concentrated,
the inexpressible one would exhaust inconceivable <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s> (billions of cosmic ages). // 56 //
Even a <s>Buddha</s> examining would not reach the limit of even a portion of the qualities
of the Self-Born One — for the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha) are indeed inconceivable. // 57 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca praṇidhistatra yeṣāṃ ca manaso ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those whose vows are directed there, and those whose minds delight therein —
all of those too, of such a domain, shall become exceedingly hard to perceive. // 58 //
Those of infinite merit and knowledge, of the vigor of great accumulations,
they indeed enter this method, established in the stainless mind of the wise. // 59 //
Vast are their vows, vast their mental discipline;
they shall attain vast <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), having reached the domain of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors). // 60 //

body.text: atha khalu sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvajarājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvajarāja</s> (King of the Knowledge-Banner that Scatters All <s>Māra</s>-Circles), by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, surveying the ten directions, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Because their body is unattached knowledge, the Self-Born Ones are bodiless;
their domain is inconceivable knowledge — they cannot be thought of. // 61 //
The <s>Buddha</s>-body has been purified by inconceivable, pure deeds;
it is unstained by the triple world, resplendent with marks and minor signs. // 62 //
He is all-illuminating in the world, purified in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality);
he is the gateway even to <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, the great mine of all knowledge. // 63 //
Free from dust, without conceptual elaboration, devoid of all attachment,
he has become the sun of the world, releasing rays of knowledge. // 64 //
He cuts off the terror of existence, he purifies the triple realm;
he is the accomplishment of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and likewise the mine of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. // 65 //
Displaying infinite forms, not dependent upon any form,
he shows even those inconceivable forms to all embodied beings. // 66 //

children.text: śakyaṃ na jñānaparyanto gantuṃ buddhasya kenacit /
children.translated_text: No one is able to reach the limit of the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge,
by whom <s>Buddha</s>-awakening — inconceivable — was purified in a single instant. // 67 //
Inexhaustible is the exposition of knowledge, unchanging by nature;
in a single instant, the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) of the three times are manifested therein. // 68 //
One of infinite deeds, possessed of wisdom, seeking awakening, should always contemplate;

children.text: cittamityapi yatrāsya citte cittaṃ na jāyate // 69 //
children.translated_text: [yet] even where there is 'mind' for him, no mind arises in [his] mind. // 69 //
Beyond all expression, profound, having abandoned the path of speech,
those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable, by which the Fully Awakened Ones are empowered. // 70 //

body.text: atha khalu vairocanapraṇidhānaketudhvajo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vairocanapraṇidhānaketudhvaja</s> (Banner of the Standard of <s>Vairocana</s>'s Vow), by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, surveying the ten directions, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Of unconfused mindfulness, pure, certain in the arising of <s>Dharma</s>,
those of inconceivable intellect, they are inexhaustible oceans of awakening. // 71 //
Their mind is determined here; for this is indeed the domain of their practice;
their knowledge here is unshakable; here they have cut off all doubt. // 72 //

children.text: khedo notpadyate teṣāṃ na teṣāṃ sīdate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Weariness does not arise in them; their mind does not flag;
their thought proceeds, devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. // 73 //
Faith arises in them, rooted at the base, arisen upward;
for their delight is in this knowledge, unsupported, without abode. // 74 //
Fulfilled with wholesome <s>dharmas</s> accumulated over <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>,
they all incline that [merit toward awakening] — these incomparable seekers of knowledge. // 75 //

children.text: vicaranti ca saṃsāre na ca saṃsāraniśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: They wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), yet they do not depend on <s>saṃsāra</s>;
certain in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, they delight in the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 76 //
Whatever worldly fortune arises in the realm of beings,

children.text: sarva prahīṇā dhīrāṇāṃ buddhasaṃpasthitā hi te // 77 //
children.translated_text: all is relinquished by the steadfast — for they are established in <s>Buddha</s>-fortune. // 77 //

children.text: vṛthā samāśrito lokaḥ sadā baddhaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: The world, relying upon the vain, always proceeds in bondage;
those of unattached conduct there are always devoted to the welfare of beings. // 78 //
Incomparable is their conduct, inconceivable to all embodied beings;
they contemplate the happiness of the world, by which suffering is turned back. // 79 //
Purified by the knowledge of awakening, they are compassionate toward all the world;
they have become the light of the world, the liberators of all the world. // 80 //

body.text: atha khalu sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāntarājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāntarāja</s> (King of the Valor of Knowledge that Scatters All Obstructions), by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, surveying the ten directions, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Rare is the word '<s>Buddha</s>' even in hundreds of <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>;
how much more rare the sight [of a <s>Buddha</s>], the supreme cutter of all doubt! // 81 //
He has been seen — the light of the world, who has gone to the course of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the sacred ford of the triple world, the purifier of all beings. // 82 //
For those beholding the form-body, the blameless essence of beings,
satiety does not arise even in myriads of <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>. // 83 //
Gazing upon the form-body of the lord of men, the sons of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: asaṅgāḥ svaṃ śubhaṃ bodhau nāmayanti parārthinaḥ // 84 //
children.translated_text: unattached, incline their own merit toward awakening, seeking the welfare of others. // 84 //
This form-body is the gateway to <s>Buddha</s>-awakening of the great sage;
from which emerge unattached, inexhaustible analytical knowledges. // 85 //
Having illuminated inconceivable, immeasurable beings, the great sage
introduces [them] to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) and prophesies supreme awakening. // 86 //
This field made of great merit, the arisen circle of knowledge,
illuminates the immeasurable world, augmenting the aggregate of merit. // 87 //
He cuts the net of suffering, he purifies the aggregate of knowledge;
there is no fear of evil destinies for those by whom the <s>Jina</s> has been approached here. // 88 //
A vast mind arises in those who behold the best of bipeds;
immeasurable power of wisdom arises, moon-radiant. // 89 //

children.text: bhavanti niyatā bodhau dṛṣṭvā buddhaṃ narottamam /
children.translated_text: They become determined toward awakening, having seen the <s>Buddha</s>, the best of men;
and the certainty arises in them: 'I shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>.' // 90 //

body.text:
atha khalu dharmadhātutalabhedajñānābhijñārājo bodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena
daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharmadhātutalabhedajñānābhijñārāja</s> (King of the Superknowledge of Wisdom that Penetrates the Ground of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>), by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, surveying the ten directions, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Having seen the sage, the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, endowed with infinite qualities,
the mind of those who dedicate [merit] is purified in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. // 91 //
<s>Tathāgatas</s> arise for the sake of all beings —
the greatly compassionate, the steadfast, the turners of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of <s>Dharma</s>). // 92 //
How can the <s>Buddhas</s> be repaid by all embodied beings,
those who are devoted to the welfare of beings, even in hundreds of <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>? // 93 //
Better to be cooked for <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s> in the most terrible lower realms,
than to not see the Teacher who turns away from all attachment. // 94 //
Whatever aggregate of suffering arises in the course of all beings' [existence],

children.text: utsoḍhavyaḥ sa nikhilo buddhānāṃ na tvadarśanam // 95 //
children.translated_text: all that must be endured — but not the failure to see the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 95 //
However many separate evil destinies there are in all this world,

children.text: varaṃ tatra ciraṃ vāso buddhānāmaśrutirna ca // 96 //
children.translated_text: better to dwell long there, than to not hear the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 96 //

children.text: ekaikatra varaṃ kalpān nivāso narake 'pi tān /
children.translated_text: Better to dwell even in hell for <s>kalpas</s>, one by one, in each,
than to remain far from the awakening obtained from the <s>Jinas</s>, standing elsewhere. // 97 //
For what reason is long dwelling in the evil destinies desired?
Because the sight of the lord of <s>Jinas</s> is the augmenter of knowledge. // 98 //
All sufferings are cut by seeing the <s>Jina</s>, lord of the world;
and there arises entry into knowledge, in the domain of the Fully Awakened. // 99 //
He destroys all obscurations — having seen the <s>Buddha</s>, the best of men;
he augments immeasurable merit, by which awakening is attained. // 100 //
The sight of the <s>Buddha</s> cuts doubts and uncertainties of beings
and fulfills aspirations, both worldly and supramundane. // 101 //

body.text: 2 samantabhadraḥ /
body.translated_text: 2. <s>Samantabhadra</s>.

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ vyavalokya bhūyasyā mātrayā vibhajan vistārayan deśayan uttānīkurvan saṃprakāśayan avabhāsayan prabhāsayan upadiśan dharmadhātunayena ākāśadhātusamatayā tryadhvasamatayā dharmadhātusamatayā sattvadhātusamatayā sarvalokadhātusamatayā sarvakarmavaṃśasamatayā sattvāśayasamatayā sattvādhimuktisamatayā dharmapratibhāsasamatayā sattvaparipākakālasamatayā sarvajagadindriyasamatayā ca, evaṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitaṃ tathāgatasamādhiṃ caiṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃprakāśayati sma daśabhirnirdeśapadaiḥ / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sarvadharmadhātuparyāpanneṣu buddhakṣetrapramāṇurajaḥsarvabuddhaparaṃparākṣetraparaṃparānirdeśaḥ / yaduta ākāśadhātuparameṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu aparāntakoṭīgatakalpatathāgataguṇānucaraṇanirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvabuddhakṣetratathāgatasamutpattyanantamadhyābhisaṃbodhimukhasamudrasaṃdarśananirdeśaḥ / yaduta ākāśadhātuparamabuddhakṣetratathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalabodhisattvasaṃghabodhimaṇḍābhimukhāvasthānanirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvatryadhvabuddhakāyasadṛśanirmāṇasarvaromamukhapramuñcanacittakṣaṇadharmadhātuspharaṇanirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvadiksamudreṣu sarvakṣetrasāgarasamatalādhiṣṭhānaikakāyaspharaṇaprabhāsanirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvārambaṇataleṣu buddhabhūmivikurvitasarvatryadhvasamavasaraṇadhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśananirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamatryadhvakṣetraparaṃparānānābuddhavikurvitakalpasāgarasaṃdarśananirdeśaḥ / yaduta sarvatryadhvabuddhapraṇidhānasāgarasarvaromanigarjanāparyantādhiṣṭhānabodhisattvasaṃbhavanirdeśaḥ / yaduta dharmadhātupramāṇabuddhasiṃhāsanabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāsaṃbhinnabodhimaṇḍālaṃkāranānādharmacakrapravartanāparāntādhiṣṭhānanirdeśaḥ / iti hi bho jinaputrā etān daśān pramukhān kṛtvā anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇūrajaḥsamān etasya siṃhavijṛmbhitasya samādhinirdeśananugacchāmi / api tu khalu punarbho jinaputrāḥ tathāgatajñānagocara eṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, surveying the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, further expounding, unfolding, teaching, making clear, illuminating, irradiating, and instructing, by the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, by the equality of the space-realm, by the equality of the three times, by the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, by the equality of the realm of beings, by the equality of all world-systems, by the equality of all lines of <s>karma</s>, by the equality of the dispositions of beings, by the equality of the inclinations of beings, by the equality of the reflection of <s>dharma</s>, by the equality of the time of maturing beings, and by the equality of the faculties of all beings in the world, thus elucidated this Lion's Yawn <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>samādhi</s> to those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> by ten expository points. Which ten? Namely: the exposition of all <s>Buddha</s>-field succession and the atoms contained in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> encompassed in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; namely: the exposition of following the qualities of <s>Tathāgatas</s> through <s>kalpas</s> reaching the furthest limit, in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> at the ultimate extent of the space-realm; namely: the exposition of displaying the ocean of gateways to the infinite, middleless <s>abhisaṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening) and arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>; namely: the exposition of the positioning of <s>bodhisattva</s> assemblies facing the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> in the assembly-circles of <s>Tathāgatas</s> in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> extending to the ultimate space-realm; namely: the exposition of pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in a single mind-moment, releasing from every hair-opening emanations resembling the bodies of all <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times; namely: the exposition of the radiance of pervading with a single body established equally in the oceans of all fields in all direction-oceans; namely: the exposition of displaying the empowerment of the convergence of all three times through the <s>Buddha</s>-ground transformations upon all bases; namely: the exposition of displaying the oceans of <s>kalpas</s> of various <s>Buddha</s>-transformations in successions of fields of the three times equal to the atoms of all fields; namely: the exposition of the arising of <s>bodhisattvas</s> through the empowerment of the limitless roaring from every hair [pore] of the ocean of vows of all <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times; namely: the exposition of the empowerment of the endlessness of the turning of the wheels of various <s>dharmas</s>, the unbroken <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-ornament, the <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly-circles, the <s>Buddha</s> lion-thrones of the measure of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Thus, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>, taking these ten as foremost, I follow the exposition of this Lion's Yawn <s>samādhi</s> equal to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. Moreover, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>, this is the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge. //

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattva etasyaiva siṃhavijṛmbhitasya tathāgatasamādherarthanirdeśaṃ dyotayamāno buddhādhiṣṭhānena tathāgatavadanaṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sarvāvantaṃ parṣanmaṇḍalasamudraṃ vyavalokya acintyabuddhaviṣayānantamadhyatathāgatasamādhivikurvitāni vyavalokya acintyajñānamāyāgatadharmatāṃ vyavalokya acintyatrayadhvabuddhasamatāṃ vyavalokya acintyānantamadhyasarvavākpathaniruktisarvadharmanayān vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, illuminating the meaning-exposition of this very Lion's Yawn <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>samādhi</s>, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, gazing upon the face of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, surveying the entire ocean of the assembly circle, beholding the transformations of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-domain of the infinite, middleless <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>samādhi</s>, beholding the reality of inconceivable knowledge as arrived at through illusion, beholding the equality of the inconceivable <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times, beholding the inconceivable, infinite, middleless methods of all speech-paths and linguistic expressions of all <s>dharmas</s>, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: In a single hair-pore, oceans of <s>Jina</s>-fields equal to the atoms of all fields,
there a <s>Buddha</s> sits upon a <s>Buddha</s>-throne, surrounded by assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // 1 //
In a single hair-pore, many oceans of fields; seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> upon a lotus-throne,

children.text: dharmadhātu vipulam karitvanā dṛśyate drumavareṣu nāyakaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: having pervaded the vast <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the Guide is seen at the best of trees. // 2 //
In a single hair-pore, <s>Jinas</s> seated equal to the atoms of all fields,
surrounded by assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, proclaim the practice of <s>Bhadracarī</s> (the Excellent Conduct). // 3 //
The <s>Jinas</s> seated in a single field, having pervaded all expanse of fields,

children.text: bodhisattva bahumegha akṣayā enti te daśadiśāṃ samantato // 4 //
children.translated_text: inexhaustible clouds of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> go forth to the ten directions on all sides. // 4 //
Equal to the atoms of <s>koṭis</s> of fields, radiant with the ocean of <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities,

children.text: utthihantu parṣāsu śāstuno dharmadhātu sphariṣu daśa diśaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: they rise in the assemblies of the Teacher, having pervaded the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions. // 5 //
Seeing the reflections of all fields, oceans of knowledge of the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), the <s>Jina</s>s (Victors),
they, established in the practice of <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Noble Conduct), approached the assembly of all <s>Buddha</s>s. // 6 //
Seated throughout the expanse of all fields, delighting in the practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>s,

children.text: dharmamegha śruṇamāna sūratā ekakṣetri cari kalpakoṭiyaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: listening to the <s>Dharmamegha</s> (Cloud of Dharma) with heroic resolve, having practiced in a single field for <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions) of <s>kalpa</s>s. // 7 //
<s>Bodhisattva</s>s wander in their spiritual journey, illuminating the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>-practice,
they descend into the ocean of vows — established in the range of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) stages. // 8 //
Born from the <s>Dharma</s> of various <s>Jina</s>s, they practice universally with auspicious wisdom,
they descend into the ocean of praise of the qualities of all <s>Buddha</s>s, into vast miraculous transformations. // 9 //
Having pervaded the good destiny of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality), resembling the atoms of all fields,

children.text: kāyamegha satataṃ pramuñcato dharmavarṣatu upetu bodhaye // 10 //
children.translated_text: constantly releasing clouds of bodies, may they rain <s>Dharma</s> and approach <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening). // 10 //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān bhūyasyā mātrayā teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmatraiva siṃhavijṛmbhite buddhasamādhau saṃniyojanārthaṃ bhrūvivarāntarādūrṇākośāddharmadhātusamantadvāravijñaptitryadhvāvabhāsaṃ nāma raśmiṃ niścārayitvā anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaraśmiparivārāṃ daśadiksarvalokadhātusamudreṣu sarvakṣetraprasarānavabhāsayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), to an even greater extent, for the purpose of engaging those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s in this very <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called '<s>Siṃhavijṛmbhita</s>' (the Lion's Yawn), emitting from the space between his eyebrows, from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (tuft of hair), a ray called '<s>Dharmadhātusamantadvāravijñaptitryadhvāvabhāsa</s>' (Illumination of the Three Times through the Cognition of the Universal Gateway of the Dharma Realm), accompanied by rays equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, illuminated the expanses of all fields in the oceans of all world-systems in the ten directions. //

body.text:
atha khalu ye te bodhisattva jetavane saṃnipatitāḥ, te paśyanti sma sarvadharmadhātugateṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ākāśadhātuparyavasāneṣu sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajontargateṣu buddhakṣetrasaṃgateṣu nānābaleṣu nānāviśuddheṣu nānāpratiṣṭhāneṣu nānāsaṃsthāneṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhimaṇḍavaragataṃ bodhisattvasiṃhāsananiṣaṇṇaṃ sarvalokendrasaṃpūjitaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyamāṇaṃ kvaciddharmacakraṃ pravartayantaṃ dharmadhātuspharaṇena svaramaṇḍalena samatānusṛtābhisaṃbhinnatryadhvatalasamatānugatasarvajagadasaṃbhinnasarvasattvasaṃjñāgatasamarutasarvajagaccitteṣu pratibhāsaprāptāni sarvasattvakāyeṣvabhimukhapralambasarvaparṣadupasaṃkramaṇarūpāṇi sarvakalpeṣu jñānāsaṃbhinnāni sarvakṣetreṣu sarvatra samatayā
body.translated_text: Then indeed those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who had assembled in <s>Jetavana</s> saw, in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields pervading the entire <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality), extending to the ultimate bounds of the realm of space, within field-assemblages contained within the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-field particles — in <s>Buddha</s>-fields of various powers, various purifications, various foundations, and various configurations — [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] seated at the supreme <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (Seat of Awakening) upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lion-throne, worshipped by all lords of the world, surrounded by hosts of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, awakening to unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (Complete Awakening); in some places turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), with a voice-sphere pervading the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, in assembly-circles as vast as inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields; in some places gone to the abode of <s>Deva</s>s (gods), in some places gone to the abode of <s>Nāga</s>s (serpent-beings), in some places gone to the abode of <s>Yakṣa</s>s, in some places gone to the abode of <s>Gandharva</s>s (celestial musicians), in some places gone to the abode of <s>Asura</s>s (anti-gods), in some places gone to the abode of <s>Garuḍa</s>s, in some places gone to the abode of <s>Kinnara</s>s, in some places gone to the abode of <s>Mahoraga</s>s (great serpents), in some places gone to the abode of lords of men, in some places in the human world — in villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals — teaching the <s>Dharma</s> through various miraculous transformations, in various deportments, in various forms of self-manifestation, through various <s>samādhi</s>-gateway cognitions, through various <s>samādhi</s> and <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge) powers, through various births in families and lineages, through various color-cognitions, through various radiance-circles, through various emissions of ray-nets, through various voice-spheres, through various assembly-circles, through various empowerments of speakers, through various empowerments of teaching, through various words and syllables, through various analytical languages — they saw [him] teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And as many as those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s were, they saw the profound <s>Buddha</s>-<s>samādhi</s> transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in each of those assembly-circles. In the supreme world-systems of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, extending to the ultimate bounds of the realm of space, in the establishments of the ten directions, in the convergences of infinite directional revolutions, in all oceans of directions, through various <s>Dharma</s>-direction gateways, through various direction-cognitions, through various directional convergences, through various directional parts, through various directional courses, through various directional oceans — namely in the eastern direction, southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, below, and above — in field-body directions, in being-body directions, in being-cognition directions, in past-limit directions, in present directions of the ten directions, in directions of the insertion and removal of subtle hair-tip openings along all paths of space, in directions of the succession of atoms of all fields, in directions of entering and descending into directions, in directions arising from various <s>karma</s>-formations, in directional paths of the cognition of infinite middle space-surfaces along a single hair-path —

yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukharūpasaṃdarśanavijñaptīni sarvabuddhadharmasaṃprakāśanasarvasattvavinayāpratiprasrabdhāni tathāgatavikurvitāni paśyanti sma / sarve te bhagavatā vairocanena pūrvakuśalacaryāsabhāgatayā caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ, darśanena śravaṇena anusmṛtyā paryupāsanena ca paripācitāḥ, pūrvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditāḥ, tatra tathāgateṣūpasaṃkramantaḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ, yathākuśalamūlasabhāgatayā sarvajñatāparipākopāyasuparigṛhītattvāttadacintyaṃ bhagavato vairocanasya samādhivikurvitamavataranti dharmadhātuvipulamākāśadhātuparyavasānam / keciddharmakāyamavataranti, kecidrūpakāyam, kecitpūrvaṃ bodhisattvasamudāgamam, kecit pāramitāparipūrim, keciccaryāmaṇḍalaviśuddhivyūham, kecidbodhisattvabhūmivikurvitam, kecidabhisaṃbodhivikurvitam, kicidbuddhavihārasamādhyasaṃbhedavikurvitam, kecittathāgatabalavaiśāradyajñānam, kecidbuddhapratisaṃvitsāgaramavataranti / evaṃpramukhān daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyaparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhavikurvitasamudrānavataranti / nānādhimuktibhirnānāpathairnānādvārairnānāpraveśairnānāvatārainārnānayairnānānugamairnānādigbhirnānābhājanairnānādeśairnānālokairnānādhigamairnānāsaṃbhārairnānāvikurvitairnānopāyairnānāsamādhibhiḥ tān buddhavikurvitasamudrānavataranti nānāsamādhyavatāraiḥ / yaduta samantadharmadhātuvyūhena bodhisattvasamādhinā avataranti / sarvatryadhvāsaṅgajñānaviṣayāvabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, dharmadhātutalāsaṃbhedajñānālokena bodhisattvasamādhinā, tathāgataviṣayatalapraveśena bodhisattvasamādhinā,
gaganatalāvabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, daśatathāgatabalākramaṇavivareṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, buddhacchambhitavyūhavikramavijṛmbhitena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmadhātunayāvartagarbheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmadhātvaṅganigarjanaspharaṇacandreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, samantavyūhadharmaprabheṇa ca bodhisattvasamādhinā te bodhisattvāstān bhagavato vairocanasya buddhavikurvitasamudrānavataranti / asaṅgapaṭṭadharmarājadhvajena ca bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvāvaraṇabuddhasamudravipaśyinā bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvalokagatyasaṃbhedakāyapratibhāsadhvajena bodhisattvasamādhinā, tathāgatakāyāsaṃbhedaviṣayapraveśena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvalokāvartyanupravartanakaruṇārgarbheṇa ca bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmapadapratiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitena ca bodhisattvasamādhinā, atyantaśāntapraśāntasamatāvabhāsamaṇḍalena bodhisattvasamādhinā, anilambhasunirmitasamantanirmāṇapratibhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvakṣetrasamantasamavasaraṇādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhakṣetrābhisaṃbodhyākāreṇābhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvajagadindrabalavivaraṇena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvajagadviśeṣāsaṅgamaṇḍalavivaraṇena, bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgatajanetrīsaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvasāgaraguṇapratipattyavatāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, aśeṣasarvārambaṇavikurvitābhinirhārāparāntādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgatapūrvayogasamudrāvatāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā,
body.translated_text: following the equality pervading the surface of the three times, unseparated from all worlds, entering the cognition of all beings' equal wind, reflected in the bodies of all beings — [these transformations] having forms of approaching and hanging down toward all assemblies face to face, inseparable from knowledge across all <s>kalpa</s>s, everywhere in all fields with complete equality — they saw the miraculous transformations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, cognitions displaying forms face to face according to the dispositions of beings, never ceasing from illuminating all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s and disciplining all beings. All of them had been gathered by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> through the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), by the affinity of former wholesome conduct. They had been matured through seeing, hearing, recollection, and attendance. They had previously generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s>. There, approaching those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, they were gathered by wholesome roots. Because they were well-embraced through the methods of ripening toward omniscience according to the affinity of their wholesome roots, they descended into that inconceivable <s>samādhi</s>-transformation of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> — vast as the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, extending to the ultimate bounds of the realm of space. Some descended into the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Truth-body), some into the <s>Rūpakāya</s> (Form-body), some into the former arising of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, some into the fulfillment of the <s>Pāramitā</s>s (Perfections), some into the purified array of the practice-<s>maṇḍala</s>, some into the miraculous transformations of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, some into the transformations of <s>Abhisaṃbodhi</s> (Complete Awakening), some into the unbroken <s>samādhi</s> transformations of the <s>Buddha</s>'s abiding, some into the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers and fearlessnesses, and some descended into the ocean of the <s>Buddha</s>'s analytical knowledges. Thus, beginning with these, they descended into oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-transformations equal in number to the atoms of ten inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Through various dispositions, various paths, various gateways, various entries, various descents, various methods, various courses, various directions, various receptacles, various lands, various lights, various attainments, various accumulations, various transformations, various skillful means, and various <s>samādhi</s>s — they descended into those oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-transformations through various <s>samādhi</s>-entries. Namely: they descended through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Universal Array of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Illumination of the Domain of Unobstructed Knowledge of the Three Times; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Light of Unbroken Knowledge of the Surface of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Entry into the Surface of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Domain; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Illumination of the Sky-Surface; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Opening of the Treading of the Ten <s>Tathāgata</s> Powers; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Stride-Display of the Array of <s>Buddha</s>-Majesty; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Womb of the Turning of the Method of All <s>Dharmadhātu</s>; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Moon of the Pervading Thunder of the Limbs of All <s>Dharmadhātu</s>; and through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Universal Array <s>Dharma</s>-Splendor — those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s descended into those oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-transformations of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>. And through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Unattached Silk Banner of the <s>Dharma</s> King; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> that Perceives the <s>Buddha</s>-Ocean of All Obstructions; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Banner of Body-Reflection Unbroken from All World-Destinies; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of Entry into the Domain of the Unbroken <s>Tathāgata</s>-Body; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Womb of Compassion Following All World-Revolutions; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> Empowered by the Empowerment of the Establishment of All <s>Dharma</s>-Words; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Maṇḍala of the Illumination of Utterly Peaceful Equanimity; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Reflection of Universal Emanation Ungraspable and Well-Fashioned; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Empowerment of Universal Convergence in All Fields; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Accomplishment of the Form of Awakening in All <s>Buddha</s>-Fields; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Revelation of the Power of All World-Lords; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Revelation of the Maṇḍala of Unattached Distinctions in All Worlds; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Empowerment of the Arising from the Mothers of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Entry into the Practice of the Qualities of All Oceans; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of the Empowerment of the Ultimate Accomplishment of All Objects of Transformation without Remainder; through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> of Descent into the Ocean of Former Yogic Practices of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s —
