aparāntasarvatathāgatavaṃśasaṃdhāraṇādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, pratyutpannadaśadiksarvakṣetrasāgarapariśuddhādhimuktyadhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhaikacittakṣaṇavihārāvabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvārambaṇāsaṅgakoṭipraveśena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvalokadhātvekabuddhakṣetrādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhakāyanirmāṇābhinirhāreṇa
bodhisattvasamādhinā, vajrendrasarvendriyasāgaraprativedhena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgataikaśarīragarbhādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, cittakṣaṇakoṭisarvadharmadhātunayānugamakṣaṇavihāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmadhātukṣetraprasaranirvṛtisaṃdarśanādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, adhamūrdhatalavihārādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhakṣetrasattvakāyāsaṃbhedādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvajñānāvartābhimukhasamavasaraṇena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇāparijñāprabhedena bodhisattvasamādhinā, tryadhvaikacittakṣaṇasaṃbhedamaṇḍalena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvacittakṣaṇadharmadhātunayaśarīragarbheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgatavaṃśānugamasiṃhena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvārambaṇadharmadhātumaticakṣurmaṇḍalena bodhisattvasamādhinā, daśabalākramavikramasamārambhena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvārambaṇasamantadarśanacakṣurmaṇḍalena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvavarṇamaṇḍalajadrocanābhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, acalāvartagarbheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, ekadharmasarvadharmasamavasaraṇanirdeśena bodhisattvasamādhinā, ekadharmavākpathaniruktipadaprabhedena bodhisattvasamādhinā te bodhisattvāstān bhagavato vairocanasya buddhavikurvitasamudrānavataranti / sarvabuddhadhvajādhiṣṭhānadharmanirdeśena bodhisattvasamādhinā, tryadhvakoṭyasaṅgavabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvakalpānugamāsaṃbhinnajñānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sūkṣmanayadaśabalāntargatena bodhisattvasamādhinā, anācchedyabodhisattvacaryāsarvakalpābhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadiksamantajavābhimukhameghena bodhisattvasamādhinā, abhisaṃbodhivikurvitaviṭhapanena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvavedayitāsparśakṣemadhvajena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvavyūhagaganālaṃkārābhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā,
kṣaṇakṣaṇajagadupanirmitabimbameghābhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, gaganavirajastathāgatacandraprabheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgatagaganādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmendriyavyūhaprabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmārthavivaraṇapradīpena bodhisattvasamādhinā, daśabalamaṇḍalāvabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, tryadhvabuddhaketudhvajena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhakagarbheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvakṣaṇakṣaṇārambhaniṣṭhena bodhisattvasamādhinā, akṣayapuṇyagarbheṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, anantabuddhadarśanavinayāvabhāsena bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvadharmavajrasiṃhapratiṣṭhānena bodhisattvasamādhina, sarvatathāgatanirmāṇasaṃdarśanasamantavijñaptyabhinirhāreṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvatathāgatadivasākramaṇāntinā bodhisattvasamādhinā, ekatryadhvasaṃtāpena bodhisattvasamādhinā, prakṛtiśāntasarvadharmasamantaprabhapramuktaghoṣasvareṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, sarvabuddhadarśanasīmāvatikrameṇa bodhisattvasamādhinā, niravaśeṣasarvadharmadhātupadmanalinīpratibuddhena
body.translated_text: by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowerment for maintaining the lineage of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the future; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowerment through purified devotion to the ocean of all fields in the ten directions of the present; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of illumination of the abiding in a single mind-moment of all <s>Buddha</s>s; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of entering the summit of non-attachment to all objects; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowering all world-realms as a single <s>Buddha</s>-field; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of producing the emanation of all <s>Buddha</s>-bodies; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of penetrating the ocean of all faculties with the diamond-lord; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowering the womb of a single body of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of abiding in moments following the method of all <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) in billions of mind-moments; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowerment for displaying the cessation and extension of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>-fields; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowerment for abiding from the lowest to the highest plane; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of empowering the non-differentiation of the bodies of beings in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of converging face-to-face with the vortex of all knowledge; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the distinction of full comprehension of the own-nature and characteristics of all <s>dharma</s>s; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the maṇḍala of unification of the three times in a single mind-moment; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the universally advancing transformation of <s>Padmaśrī</s>; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the superknowledge of the knowledge of the transformation of the bodies of all beings; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the superknowledge of the knowledge of the differentiation of the surfaces of all worlds; by the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> of the womb of the undifferentiated treasury of great compassion; At every mind-moment, by entering that pervades all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s, those <s>bodhisattva</s>s who have come into the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who have arrived at <s>Jetavana</s>, who are seated on lion-thrones of vast various-jewel-lotus-womb [seats] in world-realms as vast as the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who have emerged through the transformations of great knowledge-superknowledge, who have reached the stage of sharp knowledge-superknowledge, who are of universal knowledge-conduct, who are born in the family of the mine of wisdom, who face the knowledge of omniscience, who have the darkness-free eye of knowledge, who have attained the state of charioteers of beings, who follow the equality of all <s>Buddha</s>s, who always conduct the <s>dharma</s> without conceptualization, who have penetrated the object of all <s>dharma</s>s, whose object is the natural peace of all <s>dharma</s>s, who are supreme in the abode of the peace and <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all worlds, who are established in the diversity of all worlds, who go to all fields without a dwelling, whose ground of all <s>dharma</s>s is without establishment, who are established in the unconfined palace of non-elaboration, who are devoted to the ripening and discipline of all the world, who display the path of security for all beings, whose range is the palace of liberation through exalted knowledge, whose knowledge-bodies follow the summit of dispassion, who have risen from the ocean of all existences, who see the ultimate point of reality of all worlds, whose sphere is the illumination of wisdom of the ocean of <s>dharma</s>; who have well-composed minds of great compassion in the ocean-pervading realm of <s>samādhi</s>, who have well-penetrated the method of the <s>dharma</s> that is like an illusion, who have descended into all world-realms that are like a dream, who have penetrated the vision of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s that is like a reflection, whose cognitions of all sounds and cries are like an echo, who have penetrated the knowledge of the production of all <s>dharma</s>s that is like a magical creation, whose vows and domains are well-cultivated, who follow the skill of purification of the universal maṇḍala of knowledge, whose minds are utterly peaceful and tranquil, whose domain is the knowledge of the family of all <s>dhāraṇī</s>s, who have universal prowess through the power of unshakable <s>samādhi</s>, whose vision has reached the summit of the stability of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>

sarvadharmānilambhavihāraprāptānāṃ anantaprajñāsāgaravicāriṇāṃ jñānapāramitāpāraṃgatānāṃ prajñāpāramitābalādhānaprāptānām ṛddhipāramitāsarvajagatpāraṃgatānāṃ samādhipāramitāvaśagatānāṃ sarvatathāgatārthakauśalyāviparītajñānināṃ dharmakauśalyaprakāśanavidhijñānāṃ niruktijñānābhijñānāmakṣayapratibhānabaladharmameghānāṃ vaiśāradyarṣabhasiṃhanādinām anālayadharmāsamaratiratānāṃ vitimirasarvadharmaprasāritacakṣuṣāṃ sarvalokasaṃvittibhavajñānacandrāṇāṃ prajñāmaṇḍalasarvasatyanayavyavahāraraśmīnāṃ jñānavajrapuṇyacakravālānāṃ sarvaupamyaupamyasamatikrāntānāṃ sarvadharmendriyajñānāṅkuravirūḍhānāṃ śūradhvajānāṃ sarvamāradhvajapramardanavīryāṇāmanantajñānamaṇḍalatejasāṃ sarvajagadabhyudgatakāyānāṃ sarvadharmānāvaraṇaprajñānāṃ kṣayākṣayakoṭijñānavibuddhānāṃ samantakoṭyanugatabhūtakoṭipratiṣṭhānāṃ animittavyavaharaṇapratyavekṣajñānacakṣuṣāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryābhinirhāranimittakuśalānām advayajñānagocarāṇāṃ sarvalokagativipaśyakānām aniketasarvabuddhakṣetragatipratibhāsaprāptānāṃ sarvadharmāndhakāravigatānām atamojñānamaṇḍalapratipannānāṃ samantadigdharmāvabhāsaprayuktānāṃ sarvajadvareṇyapuṇyakṣetrānām amodhaśravaṇadarśanapraṇidhicandrāṇāṃ sarvalokābhyudgatapuṇyasumerūṇāṃ sarvaparapravādicakravinigrahaśūurāṇāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraghoṣasvaraśabdanirnādināṃ sarvabuddhakāyātṛptadarśanānāṃ sarvabuddhaśarīrapratibhāsavaśavartināṃ jagadvinayānukūlakāyādhiṣṭhānānāṃ sarvakṣetraprasaraikakāyaspharaṇānām abhisaṃskāravimaṇḍalapariśuddhānāmanāvaraṇagaganamahājñānayānapātrāṇāṃ jñānamaṇḍalasarvadharmadhātukāyaprabhāsanānāṃ sarvajagaduditajñānādityānāṃ sarvajagaducitayathāśayabalānāṃ sarvajagadāśayendriyapratividdhajñānānām anāvaraṇaviṣayasarvadharmopapannānām anupapattisarvadharmasvabhāvavijñaptānāṃ sūkṣmodārānyonyasamavasaraṇajñānasaṃvardhitavartināṃ gambhīrabuddhabhūmigatiniścitānāṃ gambhīrārthapadavyañjanavyavahārajñānānām akṣayapadavyañjanārthasūcakānāṃ sarvasūtrasāgaraikapadapraveśaprabhāṣamāṇānāṃ vipuladhāraṇījñānaśarīrādhiṣṭhānānām anantakalpasaṃdhāraṇānugatādhiṣṭhānānām ekacittakṣaṇānabhilāpyakalpasaṃvāsapratividdhajñānānām ekacittakṣaṇatryadhvajñānasarvalokābhijñānānāṃ sarvadharmadhāraṇyanantabuddhadharmasāgarapratibhāsānāṃ sarvajagajjñānopanāyikadharmacakrapravartanānivartyānāṃ buddhaviṣayajñānāvabhāsapratilabdhānāṃ sudarśanasamādhisadāsamāpannānām asaṅgakoṭīsarvadharmaprabhedajñānābhijñānāṃ
sarvadharmaviśeṣavimokṣaviṣayajñānavikrīḍitānāṃ sarvārambaṇaśubhavyūhādhiṣṭhānānāṃ daśadigdharmadhātudiganuśaraṇapraviṣṭānāṃ sarvadigvibhaṅgadharmadhātusamavasaraṇānāṃ susūkṣmodāraparamāṇurajobodhiṃ vibudhyatāṃ suvarṇaprakṛtisarvavarṇasaṃdarśakānāṃ ekadiksamavasaraṇānām ekarūpānantaguṇajñānasaṃvardhitajñānapuṇyagarbhāṇāṃ sarvabuddhastutastavitapraśastānām akṣīṇapadavyañjanaguṇavarṇanirdeśānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ jetavane saṃnipatitānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ tathāgataguṇasamudramavataratāṃ tathāgataraśmyavabhāsitānāṃ sarvaśarīrebhyaḥ tebhyaśca kūṭāgārebhyo bodhisattvaparibhogebhyaḥ tebhyaśca bodhisattvāsanebhyaḥ sarvasmājjetavanānmahāprītivegapratilābhadharmatayā acintyabodhisattvadharmāvabhāsapratilābhena prītivegasaṃbhavamahāvikurvitavyūhānniścaritvā

all directions, who are awakened to <s>bodhi</s> in the exceedingly subtle and gross atoms, who display all colors through the golden nature of one [reality], who assemble in a single direction, who are wombs of knowledge and merit augmented by the knowledge of infinite qualities in a single form, who are praised and extolled and commended by all <s>Buddha</s>s, who indicate qualities with inexhaustible words and syllables — [these] <s>bodhisattvas</s>, assembled and seated in <s>Jetavana</s>, illuminated by the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, penetrating the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities from all their bodies and from those mansions and from the <s>bodhisattva</s> accoutrements and from those <s>bodhisattva</s> seats and from the entire <s>Jetavana</s>, by the nature of attaining great rapturous energy and the inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-illumination-attainment, having sent forth great transformative array-displays born of rapturous energy,

body.text: sarvadharmadhātu spharanti sma / yaduta cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe vipularaśmijālameghāḥ sarvajagatsaṃtoṣaṇā niścaritvā daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvaratnamaṇighaṇṭāmegha niścaritvā sarvatryadhvatathāgataguṇavarṇanirdeśameghanirnādānanuravanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvajagadvādyameghaḥ sarvārambaṇebhyo niścaritvā sarvasattvakarmavipākamadhuravādyaghoṣasaṃprayuktā anuvaranto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānavicitrabodhisattvacaryāsaṃdarśanarūpameghā niścaritvā sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānarutaghoṣān nigarjanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavibhūṣitabodhisattvakāyameghā niścaritvā sarvakṣetreṣvanugatabuddhopādaparaṃparāmudīrayanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvatryadhvatathāgatasadṛśabodhimaṇḍameghā niścaritvā sarvatathāgatātisaṃbodhiniryāṇavyūhān saṃdarśayanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvārambaṇebhyaḥ sarvanāgendrakāyameghā niścaritvā sarvagandhavarṣāṇi pravarṣanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvajagadindrasadṛśakāyameghā niścaritvā samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāmudīrayanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / sarvārambaṇebhyaḥ sarvaratnamayasarvapariśuddhabuddhakṣetrapratibhāsameghā niścaritvā sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravartanāni darśayanto daśa diśaḥ spharanti sma / evaṃpramukhā anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā mahāvyūhavikurvitameghā niścaranti sma teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmadhiṣṭhānena acintyadharmasamudrāvabhāsapratilābhadharmatayā ca //
body.translated_text: pervaded all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s. Namely: at every mind-moment, vast ray-net-clouds, gladdening all beings, issued forth and pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of all jewel-gem bells issued forth and, resounding with the sounds of clouds proclaiming the quality-descriptions of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of music for all beings issued forth from all objects and, echoing with sweet musical sounds connected with the <s>karma</s>-ripening of all beings, pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of forms displaying the variegated <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of the vows of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> issued forth and, thundering with the sounds of the vow-utterances of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies adorned with marks and minor marks issued forth and, proclaiming the succession of the arising of <s>Buddha</s>s in all fields, pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of <s>Bodhimaṇḍas</s> (seats of awakening) resembling those of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times issued forth and, displaying the arrays of the emergence of the supreme perfect awakening of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, pervaded the ten directions. From all objects, clouds of all <s>Nāgendra</s> (great serpent-king) bodies issued forth and, raining showers of all fragrances, pervaded the ten directions. Clouds of bodies resembling all lords of the world issued forth and, proclaiming the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, pervaded the ten directions. From all objects, clouds of reflections of all completely purified <s>buddhakṣetras</s> made of all jewels issued forth and, displaying the turnings of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, pervaded the ten directions. Such and other great array-transformation-clouds, equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, issued forth through the empowerment of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and by the nature of attaining the illumination of the inconceivable ocean of <s>Dharma</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo buddhādhiṣṭhānena etānyeva sarvavikurvitāni saṃdarśayan daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva</s>, through the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, displaying these very transformations, surveying the ten directions, at that moment spoke these verses:

children.text: saṃprekṣato jetavane anantaṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ vipulaṃ pravṛttam /
children.translated_text: Beholding in <s>Jetavana</s> the infinite,

children.text: ārambaṇā sarvatu kāyameghā niścārya te sarvadiśaḥ spharanti // 11 //
children.translated_text: vast <s>Buddha</s>-empowerment set in motion — body-clouds from every object issue forth and pervade all directions. // 11 //

children.text: anantavarṇā vipulā viśuddhā vyūhā vicitrāḥ sugatātmajānām /
children.translated_text: Of infinite color, vast, and pure,

children.text: dṛśyanti sarvehi ta āsanebhyaḥ sārambaṇebhyaḥ pratibhāsaprāptāḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: the variegated arrays of the <s>Sugata</s>'s (Buddha's) sons are seen — from all their seats and from all objects, reached in reflection. // 12 //
Variously arrayed jewel-flame clouds pervade, being sent forth between fields,

children.text: romṇāṃ mukhebhyaḥ sugatātmajānāṃ rutāni bauddhāni nigarjamānāḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: from the hair-openings of the <s>Sugata</s>'s sons, thundering with sounds of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 13 //

body.text: brahmendrarūpaiḥ sadṛśātmabhāvāḥ praśāntaīryāpatha śuddhakāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: With forms resembling <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>, with peaceful deportment and pure bodies,

body.text: vṛkṣāṇa puṣpebhi viniścaritvā vrajanti dhyānāṅgamudīrayantaḥ // 14 //
body.translated_text: issuing forth from the flowers of the trees, they go proclaiming the limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). // 14 //

children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> resembling <s>Samantabhadra</s>, with limbs adorned with marks and minor marks,

children.text: acintyā asaṅkhyāḥ sugatasya romṇo adhiṣṭhitā nirmita niścaranti // 15 //
children.translated_text: inconceivable, innumerable, emanated and empowered, issue forth from the hairs of the <s>Sugata</s>. // 15 //
Of the <s>Sugata</s>'s sons arisen in the three times, those great oceans of quality-descriptions that stream forth —
those array-clouds of the oceans of virtues thunder upon those seated in <s>Jetavana</s>. // 16 //
Whatever great oceans of <s>karma</s> of the multitudes of beings in all directions,

children.text: śrūyanti te jetavane drumāṇāṃ kośāntarebhyo 'pi viniścarantaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: manifold and complete — they are heard issuing from within the sheaths of the trees of <s>Jetavana</s>. // 17 //

children.text: tryadhvasthitānāmiha yā jinanāṃ kṣetreṣu sarveṣvakhilā vikurvā /
children.translated_text: All the transformations of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) abiding in the three times in all fields —
from beneath the field, equal to the number of atoms, they shine forth, each in every object. // 18 //

children.text: ekaikaromṇi pravibhaktu citrā buddhā dikkṣetre samudrameghāḥ /
children.translated_text: In each single hair, distinctly variegated, <s>Buddha</s>-clouds, ocean-like, of the fields in the ten directions —

children.text: abhāsayanti jinādhivāsāṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ teṣu ca buddhameghāḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: they illuminate the dwellings of the <s>Jinas</s>, and in them, <s>Buddha</s>-clouds [appear] at every moment. // 19 //
Equal to beings, pervading all directions, ripening beings through skillful means,
from their radiances there issue forth ocean-clouds of fragrance-flames, flowers, and streams. // 20 //
Jewel-palace gems, immeasurable as space, adorned with all perfect arrays,

children.text: spharanti sarvāṇyapi sarvadikṣu kṣetrāṇi sarvāṇyatha bodhimaṇḍān // 21 //
children.translated_text: pervade all directions and all fields and all <s>Bodhimaṇḍas</s>. // 21 //
Those who have gone completely in all directions, the true sons of the <s>Sugatas</s> abiding in the three times,
through the modes of conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> have purified the fields of great healing herbs. // 22 //
Variegated arrays, purified by immeasurable beings through great oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s —
even these are seen through the connection of reflections, completely, in the sky of <s>Jetavana</s>. // 23 //

body.text:
atha khalu teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhasamādhyavabhāsitasaṃtānānāmekaikasya bodhisattvasya anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni mahākaruṇāmukhānyavakrāntāni / te bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvajagaddhitasaṃgrahāya pratipannāḥ / teṣāṃ tathā samāhitānāmekaikasmādromamukhādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā raśmayo niścaranti / ekaikasmācca raśmimukhādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvanirmāṇameghā niścaranti sma sarvalokendrasadṛśakāyāḥ sarvajaganmukhākāyāḥ sarvasattvaparipākānukūlakāyāḥ / niścaritvā sarvadikṣu dharmadhātuṃ spharitvā sattvān saṃbodhayanti paripācayanti vinayanti / anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairdevabhavanacyutisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvalokopapattisaṃdarśanamukhairbodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalasaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ svapnasaṃdarśanamukhaiścittasūcanāmakārṣuḥ / sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānaniryāṇamukhairlokadhātusaṃpannamukhairdānapāramitācaryāsaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvatathāgataguṇapratipattinivṛttimaṇḍalamukhaiḥ aṅgapratyaṅgacchedanākṣāntipāramitāsaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ mahābodhisattvavikurvitavīryapāramitāsaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattibuddhajñānamārgamaṇḍalālokaprabhāsasvaramukhaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmaparyeṣaṇāya ekaikasya dharmapadavyañjanasyārthāya asaṃkhyeyātmabhāvaparityāgasaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇasarvadharmaparipṛcchanamukhaiḥ yathākālayathāśayajagadupasaṃkramaṇopanāyikasarvajñatāparipūrakopāyanayasāgarālokavijñaptimukhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapuṇyajñānasaṃbhārasarvamāraparapravādyanavamṛdyabalaketusaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvaśilpajñānābhijñāvatījñānabhūmisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvajagadviśeṣajñānābhijñāvatījñānabhūmisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvasattvāśayaviśeṣajñānābhijñāvatījñānabhūmisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvasattvendriyapraveśaprayoganānākleśavāsanāsamuddhātajñānābhijñāvatījñānabhūmisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ sarvasattvanānākarmapratipattijñānābhijñāvatījñānabhūmisaṃdarśanamukhaiḥ / etatpramukhānanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ sattvaparipākavinayopāyasaṃgrahamukhaistairbodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvabhavaneṣūpasaṃkrāntāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / keciddevabhavaneṣu kecinnāgabhavaneṣu kecid yakṣabhavaneṣu kecidgandharvabhavaneṣu kecidasurabhavaneṣu kecidgaruḍabhavaneṣu kecitkinnarabhavaneṣu kecinmahoragabhavaneṣu kecidbrahmendrabhavaneṣu
kecinmanuṣyendrabhavaneṣu kecid yamanagareṣu kecit sarvapretālayeṣu kecit sarvanarakalokeṣu kecit sarvatiryagyonigatiṣu
body.translated_text: Then indeed, of those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s whose mental continua were illuminated by <s>Buddha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, each <s>Bodhisattva</s> had entered into gateways of great compassion equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. They were devoted to an even greater extent to embracing the welfare of all beings. While they were thus absorbed, from each of their hair-pores there issued rays equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And from each ray-opening there issued clouds of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-emanations equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields — with bodies resembling all lords of the world, with bodies facing all beings, with bodies suited to the ripening of all beings. Having issued forth and pervaded the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality) in all directions, they awakened, matured, and disciplined beings — through gateways displaying the passing away from divine abodes, through gateways displaying birth in all worlds, through gateways displaying the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct-circle, and through dream-display gateways, equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, they produced mental inspiration. Through gateways of the outpouring of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vows, through gateways of world-system accomplishment, through gateways displaying the practice of <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving), through gateways of the circle of the practice and cessation of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities, through gateways displaying the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) including the cutting of limbs and minor limbs, through gateways displaying the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Heroic Energy) through the transformations of great <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, through gateways of the light-voice of the illumination of the circle of the path of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge through the <s>dhyāna</s>s (meditations), liberations, <s>samādhi</s>s, and attainments of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, through gateways displaying the renunciation of innumerable self-existences for the sake of each <s>dharma</s>-word and its meaning in the quest for all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, through gateways of approaching all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and inquiring into all <s>dharma</s>s, through gateways of illumination-cognition of the ocean of methods leading to the approach of beings at the proper time and according to their dispositions for the fulfillment of omniscience, through gateways displaying the banner of power that cannot be trampled by any <s>Māra</s> or adversary through the accumulation of merit and knowledge of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, through gateways displaying the stage of knowledge transcending <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) in all crafts and sciences, through gateways displaying the stage of knowledge transcending <s>abhijñā</s> in the special knowledge of all beings, through gateways displaying the stage of knowledge transcending <s>abhijñā</s> in the special disposition-knowledge of all beings, through gateways displaying the stage of knowledge transcending <s>abhijñā</s> in the knowledge of the elimination of the latent tendencies of various afflictions through the application of entry into the faculties of all beings, through gateways displaying the stage of knowledge transcending <s>abhijñā</s> in the knowledge of the various <s>karma</s>-practices of all beings — through these and innumerable other gateways of means for ripening and disciplining beings, equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>s were seen approaching the abodes of all beings. Some in <s>Deva</s>-abodes, some in <s>Nāga</s>-abodes, some in <s>Yakṣa</s>-abodes, some in <s>Gandharva</s>-abodes, some in <s>Asura</s>-abodes, some in <s>Garuḍa</s>-abodes, some in <s>Kinnara</s>-abodes, some in <s>Mahoraga</s>-abodes, some in the abodes of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>, some in the abodes of human lords, some in the cities of <s>Yama</s>, some in the abodes of all <s>Preta</s>s (hungry ghosts), some in all <s>Naraka</s> (hell) worlds, some in all animal-realm destinies,

body.text: asaṃbhinnayā mahākaruṇayā asaṃbhinnena praṇidhānena asaṃbhinnena jñānena asaṃbhinnena sattvasaṃgrahaprayogena darśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ śravaṇavainayikānāmanusmṛtivainayikānāṃ svaramaṇḍalavainayikānāṃ nāmanadīnirghoṣavainayikānāṃ prabhāmaṇḍalavainayikānāṃ raśmijālapramuñcanavainayikānāṃ yathāśayānāaṃ sattvānāṃ paripākavinayārthaṃ jetavanānte bodhisattvā nānāvikurvitavyūhaiḥ sarvalokadhātusamudreṣu sarvasattvadhātuprasarān spharantaḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / na ca tathagatāpādamūlāduccalanti / kecit svabhavanakūṭāgārāsanaparivārā daśa diśaḥ spharantaḥ saṃdṛśyante, tathāgatapādamūlācca na calanti / kecinnirmitameghān pramuñcataḥ saṃdṛśyante sattvaparipākāya, tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalācca na calanti / kecicchramaṇarūpeṇa kecidbrāhmaṇarūpeṇa kecitsarvapratiliṅgākalpārohapariṇāharūpeṇa kecidvaidyarūpeṇa kecidvaṇigrūpeṇa kecicchrubhājīvarūpeṇa kecinnartakarūpeṇa keciddevalakarūpeṇa kecit sarvaśilpādhārarūpeṇa sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkrāntāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / kālavaśena kālamanuvartamānā anurūpakāyābhinirhārabhedena anurūpakāyavarṇasaṃsthānabhedena svarabhedena mantrabhedena īryāpathabhedena avasthānabhedena sarvajagadindrajālopamāyāṃ bodhisattvācaryāyāṃ sarvaśilpamaṇḍalaprabhāsanāyāṃ sarvajagajjñānoddyotanālokapradīpāyāṃ sarvasatyādhiṣṭhānavyūhāyāṃ sarvadharmāvabhāsanaprabhāyāṃ sarvadigyānavyavasthānaśodhanāyāṃ sarvadharmamaṇḍalapradīpāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ carantaḥ sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkrāntāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma sattvaparipākavinayāya //
body.translated_text: with unbroken great compassion, unbroken vows, unbroken knowledge, and unbroken application of the means of attracting beings — for the purpose of ripening and disciplining beings who are trainable through seeing, through hearing, through recollection, through voice-sphere, through the sound of name-rivers, through radiance-circles, through the emission of ray-nets, and according to the dispositions of beings — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>s were seen at the end of <s>Jetavana</s>, pervading the expanses of all beings in all oceans of world-systems with various arrays of miraculous transformations. Yet they did not move from the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Some were seen pervading the ten directions, surrounded by the retinues of their own mansion-pavilions and seats, yet they did not move from the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Some were seen releasing emanation-clouds for the ripening of beings, yet they did not move from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s assembly-circle. Some in the guise of <s>śramaṇa</s>s (ascetics), some in the guise of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, some in the form of various religious disguises and garbs, some in the guise of physicians, some in the guise of merchants, some in the guise of various artisans, some in the guise of dancers, some in the guise of temple-keepers, some in the form of masters of all crafts — they were seen approaching all villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals. Following the course of time, with corresponding forms of body-manifestation, with corresponding variations of body-color and configuration, with variations of voice, mantra, deportment, and station — practicing in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct that resembles the net of illusion of all world-lords, in the illumination of the circle of all crafts, in the lamp of light that illuminates the knowledge of all beings, in the array of the empowerment of all truths, in the radiance of the illumination of all <s>dharma</s>s, in the purification of the establishment of all directional courses, in the lamp of the circle of all <s>dharma</s>s — they were seen approaching all villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct for the purpose of ripening and disciplining beings. //

body.text: Kalyāṇamitrāṇi /
body.translated_text: <s>Kalyāṇamitrāṇi</s> (Spiritual Friends). /

body.text: 3 mañjuśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: 3. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. /

body.text:
atha khalu mañjuśrīrapi kumarabhūtaḥ pratiṣṭhānakūṭāgāragataḥ sārdhaṃ sabhāgacaritairbodhisattvaiḥ, nityānubaddhaiśca vajrapāṇibhiḥ, sarvalokabalakaraṇaprayuktābhiśca sarvabuddhopasthānapraṇidhānacittābhiḥ śarīrakāyikābhirdevatābhiḥ, pūrvapraṇidhānānubaddhābhiśca padakāyikābhirdevatābhiḥ, dharmaśravaṇābhimukhābhiśca pṛthivīdevatābhiḥ, mahākaruṇāprayuktābhiśca utsasarohradataḍāgodadhānanadīdevatābhiḥ, prajñālokabalaprabhāvabhāsābhiśca jvalanadevatābhiḥ, ābaddhamakuṭābhiśca vāyudevatābhiḥ, sarvadigavabhāsajñānābhiśca digdevatābhiḥ avidyāndhakāravidhamanaprayuktābhiśca rātridevatābhiḥ, tathāgatadivasābhinirhāraprayuktābhiśca divasadevatābhiḥ, sarvadharmadhātugaganapratimaṇḍalaprayuktābhiśca gaganadevatābhiḥ, sarvajagadbhavasamudrasaṃtāraṇaprayuktābhiśca sāgaradevatābhiḥ, sarvajñatāsaṃbhārasamārjanaprayuktābhiśca kuśalamūlakūṭāgārabhyudgatacittābhiḥ parvatadevatābhiḥ, sarvajagaccharīrālaṃkāraprayuktābhiśca sarvabuddhavarṇādhiṣṭhānapraṇidhānaprayuktābhirnadīdevatābhiḥ, sarvajagaccittanagaraparipālanaprayuktābhiśca nagaradevatābhiḥ, sarvadharmanagarapraṇidhānādhimuktaiśca nāgendraiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvasattvārakṣāpratipannaiśca yakṣendraiḥ, sarvasattvaprītivegavivardhanaprayuktaiśca gandharvendraiḥ, sarvapretagativinivartanaprayuktaiśca kumbhāṇḍendraiḥ, sarvasattvabhavasāgarābhyuddharaṇapraṇidhipratipannaiśca garuḍendraiḥ, sarvalokābhyudgatatathāgatakāyabalapariniṣpattipraṇidhānasaṃjātaiśca asurendraiḥ, tathāgatadarśanaprītilabdhaiśca praṇatakāyairmahoragendraiḥ, saṃsārodvignamānasaiśca ullokitavadanairdevaendraiḥ, mahāgauravapratilabdhaiśca
praṇataśarīrarbrahmendraiḥ, mahāgauravābhiṣṭutamahitam evaṃrūpayā bodhisattvavikramavyūhasaṃpadā mañjuśrīrbodhisattvaḥ svakādvihārānniṣkramya bhagavantamanekaśatakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya anekākārayā pūjayitvā bhagavato 'ntikādapakramya yena dakṣiṇāpathastena janapadacaryāṃ prakrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, being in the <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s> mansion, together with <s>Bodhisattva</s>s of kindred conduct, and with <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>s who were constantly in attendance, and with body-dwelling deities devoted to empowering all worlds and aspiring to attend all <s>Buddha</s>s, and with foot-dwelling deities bound by former vows, and with earth-deities inclined toward hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and with deities of springs, pools, ponds, reservoirs, and rivers devoted to great compassion, and with fire-deities radiant with the power and splendor of the light of wisdom, and with wind-deities with bound diadems, and with direction-deities possessing the knowledge of illuminating all directions, and with night-deities devoted to dispelling the darkness of ignorance, and with day-deities devoted to accomplishing the day of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and with sky-deities devoted to the reflected orb of the sky of all <s>Dharmadhātu</s>s, and with ocean-deities devoted to ferrying across the ocean of existence of all beings, and with mountain-deities whose minds had risen to the mansion of merit, devoted to gathering the accumulation of omniscience, and with river-deities devoted to adorning the bodies of all beings and devoted to the vow of empowering the color of all <s>Buddha</s>s, and with city-deities devoted to guarding the city of the minds of all beings, and with <s>Nāgendra</s>s (serpent lords) inclined to the vow for the city of all <s>dharma</s>s, and with <s>Yakṣendra</s>s (lords of yakṣas) devoted to protecting all beings, and with <s>Gandharvendra</s>s (lords of celestial musicians) devoted to augmenting the force of delight in all beings, and with <s>Kumbhāṇḍendra</s>s devoted to turning back all hungry-ghost destinies, and with <s>Garuḍendra</s>s whose vows were devoted to rescuing all beings from the ocean of existence, and with <s>Asurendra</s>s born from the vow for the accomplishment of the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-body transcending all worlds, and with <s>Mahoragendra</s>s (great serpent lords) with prostrate bodies, having obtained the delight of seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and with <s>Devendra</s>s (divine lords) with minds weary of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and gazing upward, and with <s>Brahmendra</s>s (lords of <s>Brahmā</s>) with prostrate bodies who had obtained great reverence — honored and lauded with such great reverence, endowed with such a splendor of the array of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-valor, <s>Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva</s> departed from his own dwelling, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> many hundreds of times, worshipped him in many ways, departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and set forth on a journey through the southern country toward <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu āyuṣmān śariputro buddhānubhāvena adrākṣīnmañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamanayā īdṛśyā bodhisattvavikurvitavyūhasaṃpadā jetavanānniṣkamya yena dakṣiṇā dik tenopasaṃkramamāṇam / dṛṣṭvā ca asyaitadabhavat - yannvahaṃ mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena sārdhaṃ janapadacaryāṃ prakrameyam / sa ṣaṣṭimātrairbhikṣubhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ svakādvihārānniṣkramya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantamavalokya bhagavatābhyanujñāto bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntikātprakramya yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopajagāma sārdhaṃ taiḥ ṣaṣṭibhirbhikṣubhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ, sārdhavihāribhirnavakairacirapravrajitaiḥ, yaduta sāgarabuddhinā ca bhikṣuṇā, mahāsudatena ca bhikṣuṇā, puṇyaprabheṇa ca mahāvatsena ca vibhudattena ca viśuddhacāriṇā ca devaśriyā ca indramatinā ca brahmottamena ca praśāntamatinā ca bhikṣuṇā / evaṃpramukhaiḥ ṣaṣṭibhirbhikṣubhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ / sarve ca te bhikṣavaḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikārā avaropitakuśalamūlā dūrānugatādhimuktayaḥ śraddhānayapariśuddhā mahācetanāsamudācārā
body.translated_text: Then indeed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, saw <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, departing from <s>Jetavana</s> toward the southern direction, endowed with such a splendor of the array of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-transformations. Having seen this, the thought occurred to him: 'Let me indeed set forth on the journey through the country together with <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince.' Surrounded and attended by sixty <s>bhikṣu</s>s (monks), he departed from his own dwelling, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, gazed upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, received permission from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and went to where <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince was, surrounded and attended by those sixty <s>bhikṣu</s>s — co-residents, novices, and recently ordained — namely: the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgarabuddhi</s>, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Mahāsudata</s>, and <s>Puṇyaprabha</s>, and <s>Mahāvatsa</s>, and <s>Vibhudatta</s>, and <s>Viśuddhacārin</s>, and <s>Devaśrī</s>, and <s>Indramati</s>, and <s>Brahmottama</s>, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Praśāntamati</s>. Led by these, surrounded and attended by sixty <s>bhikṣu</s>s. And all those <s>bhikṣu</s>s had performed service under former <s>Jina</s>s (Victors), had planted roots of merit, were of far-reaching inclinations, purified through the path of faith, of great aspiration and noble conduct,

body.text: buddhadigvilokanasamarthā dharmasvabhāvaprakṛtiniṣpatticetasaḥ parahitapariṇatabuddhayastathāgataguṇābhilāṣiṇo mañjuśrīdharmadeśanāvainayikāḥ //
body.translated_text: capable of gazing toward the direction of the <s>Buddha</s>, with minds attaining the true nature and natural arising of <s>dharma</s>s, with wisdom matured for the benefit of others, aspiring to the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, trainable through the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. //

body.text:
atha khalu āyuṣmān śāriputro gacchanneva mārgaṃ sarvāstān bhikṣūnavalokya sāgarabuddhiṃ bhikṣumāmantrayāmāsa - paśya sāgarabuddhe mañjuśriyo bodhisattvasya kāyapariśuddhimacintyāṃ sadevakena lokena, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavicitritāṃ prabhāmaṇḍalapariśuddhiṃ ca, aprameyasattvasaṃjananīraśmijālavyūhaṃ ca, aparimāṇasarvaduḥkhapraśamanaṃ parivārasaṃpadaṃ ca, pūrvakuśalamūlasuparigṛhītān mārgavyūhāṃśca gacchato 'ṣṭāpado mārgaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / mārgavikramavyūhāṃśca sarvadigmaṇḍalābhimukhān vartamānān puṇyasamyagvyūhāṃśca vāmadakṣiṇena mahānidhānānyudvelāni bhavanti / pūrvabuddhopasthānakuśalamūlaniṣyandaiśca sarvavṛkṣakośebhyo vyūhā nirgacchanti / sarvalokendrāḥ pūjāmeghānabhipravarṣantaḥ praṇamanti / daśabhyo digbhyaḥ sarvatathāgatorṇākośebhyo raśmijālamaṇḍalāni niścaritvā sarvabuddhadharmānnigarjamānān mūrdhni nipatanti / evaṃpramukhānāyuṣmān śāriputro mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya aparimāṇān mārgakramaṇaguṇavyūhāṃsteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃdarśayati, bhāṣate udīrayati prabhāvayati saṃvarṇayati vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti / yathā yathā svaviraḥ śāriputro mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya guṇānudīrayati, tathā tathā teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ cittāni viśuddhyanti prasīdanti, prītivegā vivardhante, harṣa utpadyate, saṃtānāni caiṣāṃ karmaṇyāni bhavanti, indriyāṇi prasīdanti, saumanasyaṃ vivardhate, daurmanasyaṃ prahīyate, cittamalo 'pagacchati, sarvāvaraṇāni vinivartante, buddhadarśanamabhimukhībhavati, buddhadharmeṣu cittāni pariṇamanti, bodhisattvendriyāṇi pariśuddhyante, bodhisattvaprasādavegā utpadyante, mahākaruṇā saṃbhavati, pāramitāmaṇḍalamavakrāmati, mahāpraṇidhānāni saṃjāyante, daśasu dikṣu buddhasamudrā ābhāsībhavanti / te evamudāraṃ sarvajñatāprasādavegaṃ pratilabdhā etadavocan - upanayatu upādhyāyo 'smānetasya satpuruṣasya sakāśam / atha khalu
āyuṣmān śāriputra trairbhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkramya etadavocat - ime mañjuśrīḥ bhikṣavaḥ tvaddarśanakāmāḥ / atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto mahatā bodhisattvavikurvitena sārdha parṣanmaṇḍalapramāṇena bhūmimaṇḍalena nāgāvalokitena pratyudāvṛtya tān bhikṣūnavalokayāmāsa / atha khalu te bhikṣavo mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirobhirabhivandya añjalīn pragṛhya etadavocan - anena vayaṃ satpuruṣa tvaddarśanakuśalamūlena yadapyasmākamanyatkuśalamūlaṃ tvaṃ jānīṣe, upādhyāyaśca, yacca bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya pratyakṣam, tena vayaṃ kuśalamūlena īdṛśā eva bhavem, yādṛśastvam / evaṃrūpaṃ ca kāyaṃ pratilabhema, evaṃrūpaṃ ghoṣam, evaṃrūpāṇi lakṣaṇāni, īdṛśāni vikurvitāni yādṛśāni tava //
body.translated_text: Then indeed, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, while going along the path, looking upon all those monks, addressed the monk <s>Sāgarabuddhi</s>: 'Behold, <s>Sāgarabuddhi</s>, the inconceivable bodily purity of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — [inconceivable] even to the world including the gods — the purity of his radiance-halo adorned with the marks and secondary signs, the array of ray-nets that generates immeasurable beings, the perfection of his retinue which allays all immeasurable suffering, and the path-arrays well-embraced by former roots of merit. As he walks, an eightfold path establishes itself; and the path-splendor arrays face all the circles of directions; and to the left and right, great treasures overflow as arrays of merit and right [action]; and from the treasure-chests of all trees, arrays issue forth through the outflow of roots of merit from attending upon former <s>Buddhas</s>; and all the lords of the world bow down, raining clouds of worship; and from the ten directions, from the shrine-treasuries of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, maṇḍalas of ray-nets issue forth and descend upon his head, roaring forth all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.' In this manner the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> displayed, spoke of, proclaimed, manifested, praised, expounded, analyzed, and made clear to those monks the immeasurable arrays of virtues attending the path-traversal of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Prince. As the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> proclaimed the virtues of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, so their minds became purified and serene, their waves of joy increased, delight arose, their continuities became pliant, their faculties became clear, their gladness increased, their dejection was abandoned, the defilement of mind departed, all obstructions were turned back, the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> drew near, their minds ripened in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, their <s>bodhisattva</s> faculties were purified, waves of <s>bodhisattva</s> faith arose, great compassion was born, they entered the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) maṇḍala, great vows arose, and oceans of <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions became radiant. Having obtained such a noble surge of faith toward omniscience, they said: 'May the preceptor lead us into the presence of this excellent being.' Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, together with those monks, approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince and said: 'These monks, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, wish to see you.' Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, with the great miraculous display of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, together with the ground-maṇḍala proportionate to the assembly, turned around with the gaze of a great serpent-king and looked upon those monks. Then those monks, bowing their heads at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, with palms joined together, said: 'By this root of merit of beholding you, O excellent being — and whatever other roots of merit are ours, which you know, and the preceptor knows, and which are witnessed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> — by those roots of merit, may we become just like you! May we obtain such a body, such a voice, such marks, and such miraculous transformations as yours!' //

body.text: evamukte ebhirbhikṣubhiḥ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastān bhikṣūnidamavocat - daśabhiraparikhedacittotpādaiḥ samanvāgato bhikṣavo mahāyānasaṃprasthitaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by those monks, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince said this to them: 'Endowed with ten unwearying mental aspirations, O monks, a son or daughter of good family who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle)

body.text: tathāgatabhūmimavakrāmati, prāgeva bodhisattvabhūmim / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sarvatathāgatadarśanaparyupāsanapūjopasthāneṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, sarvakuśalamūlopacayeṣvanivartyāparikhedacittotpādena, sarvadharmaparyeṣṭiṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, sarvabodhisattvapāramitāprayogeṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, sarvabodhisattvasamādhipariniṣpādaneṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, sarvādhvaparaṃparāvatāreṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, daśadiksarvabuddhakṣetrasamudraspharaṇapariśuddhiṣu aparikhedacittotpādena, sarvasattvadhātuparipākavinayeṣvaparikhedacittotpādena, sarvakṣetrakalpabodhisattvacaryānirhāreṣu aparikhedacittotpādena, sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamapāramitāprayogaikasattvaparipācanakrameṇa sarvasattvadhātuparipācanena, ekatathāgatabalapariniṣpādaneṣu aparikhedacittotpādena / ebhirbhikṣavo daśabhiraparikhedacittotpādaiḥ samanvāgataḥ śrāddhaḥ kulaputraḥ kuladuhitā vā saṃvartate sarvakuśalamūleṣu, vivartate sarvasaṃsāragatibhyaḥ, uccalati sarvalokavaṃśebhyaḥ, atikrāmati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmibhyaśca / saṃbhavati sarvatathāgatakulavaṃśeṣu, saṃpadyate bodhisattvapraṇidhāneṣu, viśudhyate sarvatathāgataguṇapratipattiṣu, pariśudhyate sarvabodhisattvacaryāsu, samudāgacchati sarvatathāgatabaleṣu, pramardati sarvamāraparapravādinaḥ, ākrāmati sarvabodhisattvabhūmīḥ, āsannībhavati tathāgatabhūmeḥ //
body.translated_text: enters the stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let alone the stage of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Which ten? Namely: with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the seeing, attending upon, worshipping, and serving of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; with an unwearying, irreversible mental aspiration toward the accumulation of all roots of merit; with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the investigation of all <s>dharmas</s>; with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the practice of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the accomplishment of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations); with an unwearying mental aspiration toward entering the succession of all time-periods; with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the purification of pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-field oceans in the ten directions; with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the maturation and discipline of the entire realm of beings; with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the fulfillment of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice throughout all field-<s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages); and with an unwearying mental aspiration toward the accomplishment of the powers of a single <s>Tathāgata</s> through the practice of <s>pāramitās</s> equal to the atoms in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, maturing each and every being in succession, and thus maturing the entire realm of beings. Endowed with these ten unwearying mental aspirations, O monks, a faithful son or daughter of good family progresses in all roots of merit, turns away from all states of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), rises above all worldly lineages, and transcends all stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones). One is born into the lineages of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arrives at the vows of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, is purified in the practice of all <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities, is fully purified in all <s>bodhisattva</s> practices, achieves all the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, vanquishes all <s>Māra</s>s and rival disputants, enters all the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, and draws near to the stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' //

body.text: atha khalu te bhikṣava imaṃ dharmanayaṃ śrutvā sarvabuddhavidarśanāsaṅgacakṣurviṣayaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratyalabhanta, yasyānubhāvāddaśadiganantāparyantalokadhātusthitāṃstathāgatān parṣanmaṇḍalānadrākṣuḥ / ye ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvajagatyupapannāḥ sattvāstānaśeṣānadrākṣuḥ / tāṃśca lokadhātūn nānāvibhaktitānapaśyan / yāni ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu paramāṇurajāṃsi, tānyapi gaṇanāyogena prajānanti sma / ye ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ nānāratnamayā bhavanavimānaparibhogāstānapi paśyanti sma / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ svarāṅgasamudrānaśrauṣuḥ / tāṃ ca dharmadeśanāṃ nānāpadavyañjananiruktimantranāmasaṃjñābhirājānanti sma / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ cittendriyāśayān vyavalokayanti sma / daśa ca pūrvāntāparāntajātiparivartānanusmaranti sma / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ daśadharmacakraniruktinirhārānavataranti sma / daśarddhivikurvitavihārān daśādeśanānayanirhārān daśānuśāstipadanirhārānavataranti sma / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ daśapratisaṃvinnayābhinirhārānavataranti sma / sahapratilambhādasya samādherdaśabodhicittāṅgasahasrāṇi pariniṣpādayanti sma / daśasamādhisahasrāṇyavakrāmanti sma / daśapāramitāṅgasahasrāṇi viśodhayanti sma / te mahāvabhāsapratilabdhā mahāprajñāmaṇḍalāvabhāsitā daśa bodhisattvābhijñāḥ pratilabhante sma / tān mṛdusūkṣmābhijñāṅkurapratilabdhān bodhicittotpādadṛḍhapratiṣṭhitān mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ samantabhadrāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ samādāpya pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / te samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpratiṣṭhitā mahāpraṇidhānasamudrānavatīrya abhinirharanti sma / te mahāpraṇidhānasāgarābhinirhṛtayā cittaviśuddhyā kāyaviśuddhiṃ pratilabhante sma / kāyaviśuddhyā kāyalaghutāṃ pratilabhante sma, yayā kāyaviśuddhyā
body.translated_text: Then those monks, having heard this <s>dharma</s>-method, attained the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called 'the unobstructed eye-domain for the vision of all <s>Buddhas</s>,' by whose power they beheld the <s>Tathāgatas</s> abiding in endless, boundless world-realms in the ten directions, and their assembly-maṇḍalas. They beheld without remainder all the beings born in those world-realms. They perceived those world-realms in their various distinctions. They cognized by means of calculation the atoms in those world-realms. They saw also the various jewel-wrought mansions, palaces, and enjoyments of those beings. They heard the oceans of vocal features of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. They understood that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching through its various words, syllables, etymologies, <s>mantras</s>, names, and designations. They observed the minds, faculties, and dispositions of those beings. They remembered ten previous and future births and life-turnings. They penetrated the ten modes of the etymological expression of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. They penetrated ten supernatural-power transformations, ten modes of instruction, and ten modes of admonishment. They penetrated the ten modes of analytical knowledge of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Simultaneously with obtaining this <s>samādhi</s>, they accomplished ten thousand limbs of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). They entered ten thousand <s>samādhis</s>. They purified ten thousand limbs of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). Having obtained great radiance, illuminated by the maṇḍala of great wisdom, they attained ten <s>bodhisattva</s> supernatural knowledges. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, [seeing them as] having obtained tender, subtle sprouts of supernatural knowledge and firmly established in the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, established them and engaged them in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. Established in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, they descended into and brought forth oceans of great vows. Through the mental purification brought forth from those great oceans of vows, they obtained bodily purification. Through bodily purification they obtained bodily lightness, by which bodily purification

body.text: kāyalaghutayā tānyabhijñāmukhāni vipulīkurvante, acyutāgāminīrabhijñāḥ pratilabhante sma, yenābhijñāpratilābhena mañjuśriyaśca kumārabhūtasya pādamūlānna calanti / daśasu ca dikṣu sarvatathāgatakāyameghānabhinirharanti sma sarvabuddhadharmapariniṣpattaye //
body.translated_text: and bodily lightness they expanded those gateways of supernatural knowledge. They attained unfailing and progressive supernatural knowledges, by which attainment of supernatural knowledge they did not move from the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, yet in the ten directions they brought forth clouds of the bodies of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the complete accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastān bhikṣūnanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpya anupūrveṇa janapadacaryāṃ caran yena dakṣiṇāpathe dhanyākaraṃ nāma mahānagaraṃ tenopajagāma / upetya dhanyākarasya mahānagarasya pūrveṇa vicitrasāradhvajavyūhaṃ nāma mahāvanaṣaṇḍaṃ pūrvabuddhādhyuṣitacaityaṃ tathāgatādhiṣṭhitaṃ sattvaparipākāya anantakṣetrānuravitanāmanirghoṣam, yatra bhagavatā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā aneke duṣkaraparityāgāḥ parityaktāḥ, yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe satatasamitaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ pūjāṃ pratyutsukāḥ, tatra vāsamupagataḥ sārdhaṃ saparivāreṇa / tatra mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto dharmadhātunayaprabhāsaṃ nāma sūtrāntaṃ prakāśayāmāsa daśasūtrāntakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraprasravam / tasya saṃprakāśayato mahāsamudrādanekāni nāgakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyupasaṃkrāntāni / te taṃ dharmanayaṃ śrutvā nāgagatiṃ vijugupsantastathāgataguṇān spṛhayanto nāgagatiṃ vivartya devamanuṣyopapattiṃ parigṛhṇanti sma / tatra daśa nāgasahasrāṇyavaivartikānyabhūvannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tasya taṃ dharmaṃ deśayataḥ kālāntareṇa anantamadhyasattvadhāturvinayaṃ gatastribhiryānaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, having established those monks in unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), gradually wandering through the countryside, approached the great city called <s>Dhanyākara</s> in the southern region. Having arrived, he took up residence at the eastern side of the great city of <s>Dhanyākara</s>, in a great forest-grove called <s>Vicitrasāradhvajavyūha</s> (Array of Wondrous Essential Banners), a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) formerly inhabited by <s>Buddhas</s>, empowered by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the maturation of beings, [a place] whose sound resounded through infinite fields — where formerly the <s>Bhagavān</s>, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, had accomplished many difficult renunciations, and in which spot of earth <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans were constantly eager to offer worship — together with his retinue. There <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince proclaimed the <s>sūtra</s> called '<s>Dharmadhātunayaprabhāsa</s>' (Radiance of the Method of the <s>Dharma</s>-Realm), which streams forth from ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousand <s>sūtras</s>. As he was teaching it, many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-kings) came from the great ocean. Having heard that <s>dharma</s>-method, disgusted with the <s>nāga</s> state of existence, longing for the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they turned away from the <s>nāga</s> destiny and took up rebirth among gods and humans. There ten thousand <s>nāgas</s> became irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. Through his teaching of that <s>Dharma</s> over time, the realm of beings without end or middle was disciplined by the three vehicles //

body.text: aśrauṣurdhanyākaramanuṣyāḥ - mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ idaṃ dhanyākaraṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ, ihaiva vicitrasāradhvajavyūhe caitye viharatīti / śrutvā ca punarupāsakopāsikā dārakadārikā mahāprajñopāsakaśreṣṭhipūrvaṃgamāḥ pratyekaṃ pañcaśataparivārā dhanyākarānnagarānniṣkramya yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / tatra mahāprajñopāsakaḥ sudattena copāsakena sārdhaṃ vasudattena ca puṇyaprabheṇa ca yaśodevena ca somaśrityā ca somanandinā ca sumatinā ca mahāmatinā ca rāhulabhadreṇa ca bhadraśriyā copāsakena sārdhametatpramukhaiḥ pañcabhirupāsakaśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkramya mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirasābhivandya mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdat //
body.translated_text: The people of <s>Dhanyākara</s> heard: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince has arrived at this city of <s>Dhanyākara</s> and is dwelling right here in the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Vicitrasāradhvajavyūha</s>.' Having heard this, lay men and lay women, boys and girls, led by the great lay devotee <s>Mahāprajña</s>, each with a retinue of five hundred, went forth from the city of <s>Dhanyākara</s> and approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince. There the lay devotee <s>Mahāprajña</s>, together with the lay devotee <s>Sudatta</s>, <s>Vasudatta</s>, <s>Puṇyaprabha</s>, <s>Yaśodeva</s>, <s>Somaśrī</s>, <s>Somanandī</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>, and the lay devotee <s>Bhadraśrī</s> — surrounded and attended by five hundred such lay devotees led by these — approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, bowed their heads at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, circumambulated <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince three times, and sat down to one side //

body.text: tatra mahāprajñā nāmopāsikā suprabhayā copāsikayā sārdhaṃ sugātrayā ca subhadrayā ca bhadraśriyā ca candraprabhāsayā ca ketuprabhayā ca śrībhadrayā ca sulocanayā copāsikayā sārdhametatpramukhaiḥ pañcabhirupāsikāśataiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkramya mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirasābhivandya mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdat //
body.translated_text: There, the lay-woman named <s>Mahāprajñā</s>, together with the lay-women <s>Suprabhā</s>, <s>Sugātrā</s>, <s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, <s>Candraprabhāsā</s>, <s>Ketuprabhā</s>, <s>Śrībhadrā</s>, and <s>Sulocanā</s>, at the head of five hundred lay-women, surrounded and preceded [by them], approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, bowed her head at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, circumambulated <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth three times, and sat down to one side. //

body.text: tatra sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ suvratena ca śreṣṭhidārakeṇa sārdhaṃ suśīlena ca svācāreṇa ca suvikrāmīṇā ca sucintinā ca sumatinā ca subuddhinā ca sunetreṇa ca subāhunā ca
body.translated_text: There, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, together with the merchant's sons <s>Suvrata</s>, <s>Suśīla</s>, <s>Svācāra</s>, <s>Suvikrāmin</s>, <s>Sucintin</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Subuddhi</s>, <s>Sunetra</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>,

body.text: suprabheṇa ca śreṣṭhidārakeṇa sārdhametatpramukhaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śreiṣṭhidārakaśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkramya mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirasābhivandya mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdat //
body.translated_text: and <s>Suprabha</s> the merchant's son, at the head of five hundred merchant's sons, surrounded and preceded [by them], approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, circumambulated <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth three times, and sat down to one side. //

body.text: tatra subhadrā dārikā mahāprajñasya gṛhapaterduhitā bhadrayā ca dārikayā sārdhamabhirāmavartayā ca dṛḍhamatyā ca śrībhadrayā ca brahmadattayā ca śrīprabhayā ca suprabhayā dārikayā sārdhametatpramukhaiḥ pañcabhirdārikāśataiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā yena mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastenopasaṃkramya mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirasābhivandya mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdat //
body.translated_text: There, the maiden <s>Subhadrā</s>, daughter of the householder <s>Mahāprajña</s>, together with the maidens <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Abhirāmavartā</s>, <s>Dṛḍhamatī</s>, <s>Śrībhadrā</s>, <s>Brahmadattā</s>, <s>Śrīprabhā</s>, and <s>Suprabhā</s>, at the head of five hundred maidens, surrounded and preceded [by them], approached <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, bowed her head at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, circumambulated <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth three times, and sat down to one side. //

body.text:
atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto dhanyākarānnagarāt tāḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇā viditvā yathāśayaṃ saṃdarśanādhipatyenābhibhūya mahāmaitryādhipatyena prahlādya mahākaruṇādhipatyena dharmadeśanāmabhinirhṛtya jñānādhipatyena cittāśayān pravicintya mahāpratisaṃvidā dharmamupadeṣṭukāmaḥ sudhanaṃ śreiṣṭhidārakamvalokayāmāsa / (sudhanaḥ khalu punaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kena kāraṇenocyate sudhana iti? sudhanasya khalu śreṣṭhidārakasya samanantarāvakrāntasya mātuḥ kukṣau tasmin gṛhe sapta ratnāṅkurāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ samantādgṛhasya suvibhaktāḥ / teṣāṃ ca ratnāṅkurāṇāmadhaḥ sapta mahānidhānāni, yataste ratnāṅkurāḥ samutpatya dharaṇitalamabhinirbhidya abhyudgatāḥ suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmagarbhasya musāaragalvasya saptamasya ratnasya / sa yadā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaiḥ paripūrṇo daśānāṃ māsānāmatyayājjātaḥ, tadā tāni sapta mahānidhānāni saptahastāyāmavistārodvedhapramāṇāni dharaṇitalādabhyudgamya vivṛttāni virocanti bhrājante sma / pañca ca bhājanaśatāni tasmin gṛhe prādurbhūtāni nānāratnamayāni, yaduta sarpibhājanāni tailabhājanāni madhubhājanāni navanītabhājanāni, pratyekaṃ ca sarvopakaraṇaparipūrṇāni / yaduta vajrabhājanāni sarvagandhaparipūrṇāni sugandhabhājanāni, nānāvastraparipūrṇāni śilābhājanāni, nānābhakṣyabhojyarasarasāgraparipūrṇāni maṇibhājanāni, nānāratnaparipūrṇāni suvarṇabhājanāni rūpyacūrṇaparipūrṇāni, rūpyabhājanāni suvarṇavarṇacūrṇaparipūrṇāni, suvarṇarūpyabhājanāni vaiḍūryamaṇiratnaparipūrṇāni, sphaṭikabhājanāni musāragalvaparipūrṇāni, musāragalvabhājanāni sphaṭikaratnaparipūrṇāni, aśmagarbhabhājanāni lohitamuktāparipūrṇāni, lohitamuktābhājanāni aśmagarbhaparipūrṇāni, jyotirdhvajamaṇīratnabhājanāni udakaprasādakamaṇīratnaparipūrṇāni, udakaprasādakamaṇīratnabhājanāni jyotirdhvajamaṇiratnaparipūrṇāni / etatpramukhāni
pañca ratnabhājanaśatāni sahajātasya khalu sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya gṛhe sarvakośakoṣṭhāgāreṣu dhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇavividharatnavarṣāṇyabhipravarṣitāni / tasya naimittikairbrāhmaṇairmātāpitṛbhyāṃ jñātivargeṇa ca vipulasamṛddhirasya jātamātrasya gṛhe prādurbhūteti sudhanaḥ sudhana iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam /) sudhanaḥ khalu śreṣṭhidārakaḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlaḥ
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, knowing that those men, women, boys, and girls had assembled and were seated at <s>Dhanyākara</s> city, having overcome [them] by the mastery of appropriate manifestation according to their dispositions, having gladdened [them] by the mastery of great loving-kindness, having produced a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching by the mastery of great compassion, having reflected upon [their] mental dispositions by the mastery of knowledge, wishing to teach the <s>Dharma</s> with great analytical knowledge, gazed upon <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son. (Now, why is <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son called '<s>Sudhana</s>' [Good Wealth]? Indeed, immediately upon <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son having entered his mother's womb, seven jewel-sprouts appeared in that house, well-distributed all around the house. And beneath those seven jewel-sprouts were seven great treasuries, from which those jewel-sprouts, having sprung up, breaking through the surface of the earth, emerged — [sprouts] of gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), and <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), the seventh gem. When he was born, complete in all limbs and members, after the passing of ten months, those seven great treasuries — each measuring seven cubits in length, breadth, and height — having risen from the earth's surface, stood open, shining, and gleaming. And five hundred vessels appeared in that house, made of various gems — namely vessels of clarified butter, vessels of oil, vessels of honey, vessels of fresh butter, each filled with every provision. Namely: vajra vessels filled with all fragrances, fine fragrance-vessels, stone vessels filled with various garments, gem vessels filled with various delicacies and foods of the finest flavors, golden vessels filled with various gems, silver vessels filled with gold-colored powder, silver vessels filled with golden powder, gold-and-silver vessels filled with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem-jewels, crystal vessels filled with <s>musāragalva</s>, <s>musāragalva</s> vessels filled with crystal gems, <s>aśmagarbha</s> vessels filled with red pearls, red-pearl vessels filled with <s>aśmagarbha</s>, radiance-banner gem-jewel vessels filled with water-clarifying gem-jewels, water-clarifying gem-jewel vessels filled with radiance-banner gem-jewels. At the head of these, five hundred gem-vessels — and in the house of <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, born simultaneously, in all treasuries and granaries, showers of wealth, grain, gold, fine gold, and various gems rained down. By the augur-brahmins, his parents, and his kinship group, since abundant prosperity appeared in his house at the very moment of his birth, the name '<s>Sudhana</s>, <s>Sudhana</s>' [Good Wealth] was given to him.) Now, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son had performed service under former <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), had planted roots of merit

body.text: udārādhimuktikaḥ kalyāṇamitrānugatāśayo 'navadyakāyavāṅmanaskarmasamudācāro bodhisattvamārgapariśodhanaprayuktaḥ sarvajñatābhimukho bhājanībhūto buddhadharmāṇāmāśayagamanapariśuddho 'saṅgabodhicittapariniṣpannaḥ //
body.translated_text: was of noble aspiration, of a disposition guided by spiritual friends, of blameless conduct in body, speech, and mind, devoted to the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path, facing omniscience, having become a vessel for the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, purified in his dispositional approach, with unattached <s>Bodhicitta</s> (aspiration for awakening) fully accomplished. //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamavalokya pratisaṃmodate sma, dharmaṃ cāsya deśayāmāsa - yaduta sarvabuddhadharmānārabhya sarvabuddhadharmasamudayāvāptimārabhya sarvabuddhānantatāmārabhya sarvabuddhaparaṃparāvatāramārabhya sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalaviśuddhimārabhya sarvabuddhadharmacakranirvāṇavyūhamārabhya sarvabuddharūpakāyalakṣaṇānuvyañjanaviśuddhimārabhya sarvabuddhadharmakāyapariniṣpattimārabhya sarvabuddhasarasvativyūhamārabhya sarvabuddhaprabhāmaṇḍalavyūhaviśuddhimārabhya sarvabuddhasamatāmārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, having gazed upon <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, received him with delight, and taught him the <s>Dharma</s> — namely: concerning all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, concerning the attainment of the arising of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, concerning the infinity of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the entry into the succession of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the purification of the assembly-circles of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the array of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>-turning and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the purification of the marks and minor signs of the form-body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the accomplishment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Truth-body) of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the array of the eloquence of all <s>Buddhas</s>, concerning the purification of the array of the radiance-circles of all <s>Buddhas</s>, and concerning the equality of all <s>Buddhas</s> — he taught the <s>Dharma</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ taṃ ca mahājanakāyaṃ dharmakathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣayitvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya pūrvakuśalamūlaṃ saṃsmārya dhanyākare mahānagare yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmadeśanādhiṣṭhānaṃ pratiprasrabhya prakrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth, having shown, established, inspired, and delighted <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son and that great multitude of people with his <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, having aroused in them the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, having reminded them of their former roots of merit, having relinquished the empowerment of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching for beings of various dispositions in the great city of <s>Dhanyākara</s>, departed. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya sakāśādidamevaṃrūpaṃ buddhaguṇamāhātmyaṃ śrutvā anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyabhilāṣaparamaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddho mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ gāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having heard from <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth such a description of the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities, with supreme longing for unsurpassed perfect awakening, following close behind, praised <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Eternal Youth with these verses:

children.text: tvatprabhāvata ahaṃ mahāmate bodhi prasthitu hitāya dehinām /
children.translated_text: Through your splendor, O great wise one, I have set forth toward <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) for the benefit of embodied beings;

children.text: tatra niścayu anantagocaro yo mamā bhavati taṃ śṛṇohi me // 1 //
children.translated_text: hear from me that determination of mine, of infinite domain. // 1 //
Planted with moats of the waters of delight, with ramparts raised high by pride and arrogance,
with doors fitted for the courses of all beings — that is the great city of the nature of the triple existence. // 2 //
Wrapped in the darkness of the night of delusion, scorched by the fire of desire and hatred,

children.text: māraīśvaravaśaṃgatāḥ sadā yatra bāla abudhā bhiniśritāḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: where the foolish, the unwise, always dwell, gone under the power of <s>Māra</s> the lord. // 3 //

body.text: tṛṣṇapāśanigaḍaiḥ sudāmitā māyaśāṭhiyakhilaiḥ khilīkṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: Well-fettered by the bonds and chains of craving, made rigid by the hardness of deceit and fraud,

body.text: saṃśayāvimatiandhalocanā mithyapṛthivīpathena prasthitāḥ // 4 //
body.translated_text: with eyes blinded by doubt and uncertainty, they have set forth on the path of the false earth. // 4 //

children.text: īrṣya mātsarya sadā sudāmitāḥ pretatiryannarakākṣaṇe gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ever well-fettered by envy and jealousy, gone to the ill-timed states of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), animals, and hells,
afflicted by birth, disease, old age, and death, they wander about, deluded by the wheel of destinies. // 5 //
For them, you — of the circle of pure compassion, emitter of rays and beams of knowledge,
arisen for the drying up of the ocean of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), having become a sun — illuminate me! // 6 //
With the full circle of the cultivation of loving-kindness, with rays of the moonlight of merit, bestowing happiness,
having risen above the dwellings of all beings, you shine like the full moon. // 7 //
Furnished with the treasury of all pure powers, you are connected with the sky of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>;
the jewel-wheel of <s>Dharma</s> goes before you — having become a sovereign, instruct me! // 8 //
With the valor of vows and aspirations for the vehicle of awakening, with vast merit and knowledge well-purified,
having set forth for the benefit of all beings — O caravan-leader, protect me! // 9 //
Armored with the armor of patience firm as diamond-essence, with arms extended by the sword of knowledge and compassion,
in the face of battle against <s>Māra</s>'s host — having become a hero, carry me forward! // 10 //
Seated upon the peak of the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Meru</s>, in the bliss of the <s>samādhi</s> of the supreme celestial lake,
crusher of the <s>asura</s> (anti-god) <s>Rāhu</s> of <s>kleśas</s> — having become <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), look upon me! // 11 //

body.text: tvaṃ pure tṛbhavabālaālaye kleśakarmavinaye viniścita /
body.translated_text: In the city that is the dwelling of the childish of the triple existence, you are resolute in the discipline of <s>kleśas</s> and <s>karma</s>;

body.text: hetubhūmigaticakrasaṃbhrame dīpabhūta gati darśayāhi me // 12 //
body.translated_text: in the confusion of the wheel of causes, grounds, and destinies — having become a lamp, show me the path! // 12 //

children.translated_text: Turning [beings] away from the paths leading to evil destinies, purifying the paths leading to good destinies,
crossing over the courses of all world-destinies — offer me the gateway to liberation! // 13 //
Bound together by the notions of permanence, self, and happiness, well-pressed down by the covering of false grasping,
with the sharp eye of the power of knowledge of truth — open quickly the door of liberation for me! // 14 //
Skilled in the paths of truth and non-falsity, expert in the methods of path-knowledge,
resolute in the discipline of all <s>Māra</s>'s courses — show me the path to <s>Bodhi</s>! // 15 //
Established on the ground and level of right view, nourished by the waters of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities,
raining flowers of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s> qualities — show me the path to <s>Bodhi</s>! // 16 //
The past <s>Jinas</s>, the future ones, and the present <s>Jinas</s>, the sun-[like ones], and those

children.text: sattvasārasugatān diśaṃ gatāṃstān pi darśayahi mārgadeśaka // 17 //
children.translated_text: who have gone to the directions — the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones), the essence of beings — show them too, O path-teacher! // 17 //
Skilled in the methods of the devices of <s>karma</s>, expert in the chariot-devices of the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>,
resolute in the methods of the vehicle of knowledge — show me the vehicle of awakening! // 18 //
The circle of aspirations and vow-wheels, established upon axles of patience-diamond and compassion,
adorned with arrow-shafts of faith and jewels of qualities — mount me upon the vehicle of awakening! // 19 //
With the pure circle of all <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, with the roof of loving-kindness at its peak, well-adorned,
with the auspicious bells and garlands of analytical knowledges — bring me the supreme vehicle! // 20 //
Adorned with the couch of the holy life, filled with the practices of the <s>samādhi</s> of women [as spiritual teachers],
resounding with the sound of the <s>Dharmadundubhi</s> (Drum of <s>Dharma</s>) — offer me the sovereignty of the vehicle! // 21 //
With the inexhaustible treasure of the four means of attraction, adorned with garlands of knowledge-jewel qualities,
restrained by the reins of modesty and excellent restraint — show me the supreme vehicle! // 22 //
With the radiance of the auspicious circle of the splendor of generosity, with the anointing of the sandalwood of morality and compassion,
firmly jointed with the bolts of patience — swiftly establish me upon the supreme vehicle! // 23 //
Never turning back from the discipline of all beings, raised up by the cage of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: prajñapāyasamayogavāha te dharmayāni pravare sthapehi me // 24 //
children.translated_text: with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) as yoked [horses] — place me upon the excellent <s>Dharma</s>-vehicle! // 24 //
Purifying the wheel of courses by the wheel of vows, firm with the great platform of <s>Dharma</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>,
well-made by the device of knowledge, well-established — mount me upon the <s>Dharma</s>-vehicle! // 25 //
That [vehicle] purified by the practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s> (Universal Good), with valor of deliberate consideration for beings,
with the exertion of auspicious conduct in all directions — offer me the vehicle of knowledge! // 26 //

body.text: tadṛḍhaṃ vajirasārasaṃsthitaṃ jñānamāryasukṛtaṃ suniṣṭhitam /
body.translated_text: That firm [vehicle], established with diamond-essence, well-made with noble knowledge, well-established,

body.text: sarvaāvaraṇasaṃprachedanaṃ bhadrayānamabhirohayāhi me // 27 //
body.translated_text: cutting through all obstructions — mount me upon the auspicious vehicle! // 27 //

children.translated_text: That vast, stainless [vehicle], equal to all beings, the refuge of all beings, bringing happiness,
vast as the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, illuminating — cause me to mount the vehicle of <s>Bodhi</s>! // 28 //
That which cuts asunder the aggregate of the suffering of [worldly] activity, which purifies the wheel of the dust of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
which crushes all <s>Māra</s>s and opposing teachers — cause me to mount the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>! // 29 //
That whose domain is the knowledge of all directions, which arrays the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
which fulfills the aspirations of all beings — cause me to ride the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>! // 30 //
That which is pure, sky-like, infinite, inexhaustible, stainless from [wrong] views, knowledge, darkness, and [wrong] views,
established for the benefit of all beings — cause me to mount the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>! // 31 //
That propelled with the speed of a great wind, sustaining the world by the power of the wind of vows,
establishing all in the city-ground of peace — cause me to mount the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>! // 32 //
That which is like a great immovable mountain of the earth, driven by the power and force of compassion's burden,
sustaining beings through the wealth of knowledge — cause me to mount the supreme vehicle! // 33 //
That [knowledge-sun] which, like the sun, sustains beings, embracing [all] with its vast radiance-circle,
brilliantly radiant with the purification of supreme <s>dhāraṇī</s> — show me the sun of knowledge! // 34 //

body.text: taddhyanekabahukalpaśikṣitaṃ sarvahetunayabhūmikovida /
body.translated_text: That which is trained through many and numerous <s>kalpa</s>s, O one skilled in the grounds of all causal methods,

body.text: jñānavajra dṛḍhamārya dehi me yena saṃskṛtapuraṃ vidāryate // 35 //
body.translated_text: give me, O Noble One, the firm vajra of knowledge, by which the city of the conditioned is sundered! // 35 //

children.translated_text: In that vast ocean of your knowledge, those of incomparable intelligence-oceans have been trained —
with wealth anointed by the qualities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — tell me well, O Noble One, what is it like? // 36 //
With that eye fully ascended, adorned with the crown of the king of knowledge,
with head bound by the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-turban — behold the city of the <s>Dharma</s>-king! // 37 //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto nāgāvalokitenāvalokya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya kalyāṇamitrāṇyanubadhnāsi / bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripraṣṭāvyāṃ manyase bodhisattvamārgaṃ paripūrayitukāmaḥ / eṣa hi kulaputra ādiḥ, eṣa niṣyandaḥ sarvajñatāpariniṣpattaye, yaduta kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ sevanaṃ bhajanaṃ paryupāsanam / tasmāttarhi kulaputra aparikhinnena te bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitraparyupāsanatāyai / sudhana āha - yadārya vistareṇa kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam? kathaṃ pratipattavyam? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā prārabhyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caritavyam? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrayitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā pariśodhayitavyā? katham bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā avatartavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā abhinirhartavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā anusartavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā adhyālambitavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā vistartavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvasya paripūrṇaṃ bhavati samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalam? atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sudhanaṃ śreiṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the princely youth, looking at the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> with a <s>Nāga</s>'s gaze, spoke thus to him: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You who have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening now seek to follow spiritual friends. You consider that the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct should be inquired about, wishing to fulfill the <s>bodhisattva</s> path.
