For this, O son of good family, is the beginning, this is the result of the accomplishment of omniscience — namely, attending upon, serving, and waiting upon spiritual friends. Therefore, O son of good family, you must be untiring in attending upon spiritual friends.' <s>Sudhana</s> said: 'O Noble One, explain in detail — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he practice? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> begin the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> carry out the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> fulfill the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> purify the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> enter the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> accomplish the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> follow the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> aspire to the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> expand the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How does the circle of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct become complete for a <s>bodhisattva</s>?' Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the princely youth, addressed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.text: sādhu śubhapuṇyasāgara yo hi tvamupāgato mama sakāśam /
children.translated_text: Excellent, O ocean of merit and virtue, who have come into my presence,
with a mind inclined to vast compassionate action, you seek the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>! // 38 //
For the liberation of all beings, you make vast vows and conduct, incomparable —
you shall become the protector of beings; this is the way of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. // 39 //

children.text: ye bodhisattva sudṛḍhā akhinnamanasaḥ saṃsāri te carim /
children.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are firmly resolute, with unwearied minds, conduct themselves in <s>saṃsāra</s> —
they attain the unconquered, unattached <s>Samantabhadra</s> [conduct]. // 40 //
O radiance of merit, banner of merit, mine of merit, ocean of merit, purity!

children.text: yastvaṃ samantabhadrāṃ praṇidhi si sacārikāṃ jagadartham // 41 //
children.translated_text: You who make the <s>Samantabhadra</s> vow together with its conduct, for the sake of beings — // 41 //
infinite and limitless, in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), you shall see the <s>Buddha</s>s in the ten directions of the world,
and their <s>Dharma</s>-clouds you shall retain by the power of mindfulness. // 42 //

children.text: sa tvaṃ jinan daśaddiśi paśyannapi yeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu /
children.translated_text: You, seeing the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) in the ten directions, in whatever <s>buddhakṣetras</s> they dwell —
the ocean of their vows you shall purify in the practice of <s>Bodhi</s>. // 43 //
Those who have descended into these oceans of method, standing on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage —
they become all-seeing, training under the Lords of the World. // 44 //
You, having practiced through many <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of all field-expanses,

children.text: caryāṃ samantabhadrāṃ spṛśiṣyasi śivāṃ prasara bodhim // 45 //
children.translated_text: shall touch the auspicious <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct — advance toward <s>Bodhi</s>! // 45 //
Through infinite, boundless oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, in all fields without remainder,
the vows of the supreme <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct must be fulfilled. // 46 //

children.text: prekṣasva sattvanayutān śrutvā tava praṇidhiprīti saṃjātā /
children.translated_text: Behold the myriads of beings in whom, upon hearing your vow, joy has arisen —
those who aspire to <s>Bodhi</s> through the knowledge of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. // 47 //

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta imā gāthā bhāṣitvā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittamutpādya bodhisattvacaryāṃ parigaveṣitavyāṃ manyase / durlabhāste kulaputra sattvā ye 'nuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittamutpādayanti / ataste durlabhatamāḥ sattvā ye 'nuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittamutpādya bodhisattvacaryāṃ parigaveṣante / tena hi kulaputra bhūtakalyāṇamitreṣu niścayaprāptena bodhisattvena bhavitavyaṃ sarvajñajñānapratilambhāya / aparikhinnamānasena bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitraparyeṣṭiṣu / atṛptena bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitradarśaneṣu / pradakṣiṇagrāhiṇā te bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṣu / apratihatena bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitropāyakauśalyacariteṣu / asti kulaputra ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe rāmāvarānto nāma janapadaḥ / tatra sugrīvo nāma parvataḥ / tatra meghaśrīrnāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ prayoktavyam / kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryā prārabhyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caritavyam? kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryā paripūrayitavyā? kathaṃ pariśodhayitavyā? kathamavatartavyā? kathamabhinirhartavyā? kathamanusartavyā? kathamadhyālambitavyā? kathaṃ vistārayitavyā? kathaṃ bodhisattvasya paripūrṇaṃ bhavati samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalam? sa te kulaputra kalyāṇamitraḥ samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalamupadekṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the princely youth, having spoken these verses, said this to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You who have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening and consider the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct worthy of investigation — rare are those beings, O son of good family, who generate the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Even rarer still are those beings who, having generated that mind, seek out the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. Therefore, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gained certainty regarding authentic spiritual friends must be [devoted] to attaining omniscient knowledge. You must be unwearied in mind in seeking spiritual friends. You must be insatiable in seeing spiritual friends. You must be receptive to the instructions of spiritual friends. You must not be obstructed in the practice of the skillful means of spiritual friends. There is, O son of good family, right here in the southern region a country called <s>Rāmāvarānta</s>. There is a mountain named <s>Sugrīva</s>. There dwells a monk named <s>Meghaśrī</s>. Approach him and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he apply himself? How should the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct be begun? How should one carry it out? How should it be fulfilled? How purified? How entered? How accomplished? How followed? How aspired to? How expanded? How does the circle of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct become complete for a <s>bodhisattva</s>? That spiritual friend, O son of good family, will instruct you in the circle of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct.' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pādau śirasābhivandya mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya anekaśatasahasrakṛtvo 'valokya kalyāṇamitrapremānugatacittaḥ kalyāṇamitrādarśanamasahamāno 'śrumukho rudan mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, delighted, elated, joyful, filled with gladness and mental happiness, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the princely youth, circumambulated <s>Mañjuśrī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him many hundreds of thousands of times, and with a mind following the love of a spiritual friend, unable to bear not seeing the spiritual friend, with tears streaming down his face, weeping, departed from the presence of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the princely youth. // 1 //

body.text: 4 Meghaśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: 4. <s>Meghaśrī</s> /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa yena rāmāvarānto janapadastenopajagāma / upetya rāmāvarānte janapade vicaran pūvakuśalamūlasaṃbhavo dārakarmādhiṣṭhānamanobhirucitān bhogān paribhuñjāno yena sugrīvaḥ parvatastenopasaṃkramya sugrīvaṃ parvatamadhiruhya meghaśriyaṃ bhikṣumanugaveṣamāṇaḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ niryayau / evaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ paścimāmuttarāmuttarapūrvāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāṃ paścimottarāmapi diśaṃ niryayau / meghaśriyaṃ bhikṣumanugaveṣamāṇaḥ ūrdhvato 'pyavalokayati sma, adhastādapi / sa saptāhasyātyayānmeghaśriyaṃ bhikṣumapaśyadanyatamasmin parvataśikharotsaṅge caṃkramyamāṇam / sa yena meghaśrīrbhikṣustenopasaṃkramya meghaśriyo bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya meghaśriyaṃ bhikṣuṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā etadavocat - yatkhalu āryo jānīyāt - mayā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jāne kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryā prārabdhavyā, kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caritavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvacaryā paripurayitavyā, kathaṃ pariśodhayitavyā, kathamavatartavyā, kathamabhinirhartavyā, kathamanusartavyā, kathamadhyālambitavyā, kathaṃ vistārayitavyā, kathaṃ bodhisattvasya paripūrṇaṃ bhavati samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ kathaṃ bodhisattvā niryānti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / evamukte meghaśrīrbhikṣuḥ sudhanaṃ śriṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripṛcchasi / duṣkaraṃ hi etat kulaputra paramaduṣkaraṃ yaduta bodhisattvacaryāparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvogocaraparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvaniryāṇaviśuddhiparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvamārgaviśuddhiparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvacaryāvaipulyaviśuddhiparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvābhijñānirhāraviśuddhiparimārgaṇaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvalokakṛpāpracārasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvayathāśayajagadanuvartanaṃ bodhisattvasaṃsāranirvāṇamukhasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtadoṣabhayānupalepavicāraparimārgaṇam / ahaṃ kulaputra adhimuktibalādhipateyatayā cakṣurmatiśraddhānayanaviśuddhayā
aparāṅmukhajñānālokāvabhāsena samantābhimukhāvalokanayā samantaviṣayāpratihatena darśanena sarvāvaraṇavigatena vipaśyinā kauśalyena samantacakṣurviṣayapariśuddhayā śarīraviśuddhyā sarvadiksrotaḥprasarābhimukhapraṇatena kayapraṇāmakauśalyena sarvabuddhadharmameghasaṃdhāranena ca dhāraṇībalena sarvadikkṣetrābhimukhāṃstathāgatān paśyāmi / yaduta pūrvasyāṃ diśi ekaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / dvāvapi, daśāpi, buddhaśatamapi, buddhasahasramapi, buddhaśatasahasramapi, buddhakoṭīmapi, buddhakoṭīśatamapi, buddhakoṭīsahasramapi, buddhakoṭiśatasahasramapi, buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasramapi, yāvadaparimāṇānaprameyānasaṃkhyeyānacintyānatulyānasamantānasīmāprāptānamāpyānanabhilāpyānapi
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, proceeded gradually to the region called <s>Rāmāvarānta</s>. Having arrived, wandering in the region of <s>Rāmāvarānta</s>, born of previous roots of merit, enjoying pleasures pleasing to the mind by the empowerment of youthful action, he approached <s>Sugrīva</s> mountain. Having climbed <s>Sugrīva</s> mountain and searching for the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Meghaśrī</s>, he went forth to the eastern direction. Likewise to the southern, western, northern, northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest directions he went forth. Searching for the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>, he also looked upward and downward. After the passing of seven days, he saw the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s> walking on the slope of a certain mountain peak. He approached the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>, circumambulated the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'May the Noble One know — I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how one should practice, how the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct should be undertaken, how one should engage in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct should be fulfilled, how it should be purified, how it should be entered, how it should be produced, how it should be followed, how it should be grasped, how it should be expanded, how the maṇḍala of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct becomes complete for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. And I have heard that the Noble One gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Let the Noble One tell me how <s>bodhisattva</s>s emerge toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.' Thus addressed, the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s> spoke to <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, thus: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you, having generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, inquire about the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. This is difficult indeed, son of good family, supremely difficult — namely, the seeking of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, the seeking of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-range, the seeking of the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-emergence, the seeking of the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path, the seeking of the purification of the vastness of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, the seeking of the purification of the production of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-superknowledges, the displaying of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation, the displaying of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s compassionate activity in the world, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s conforming to beings according to their dispositions, the displaying of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s gate of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and the seeking of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s investigation of the faults and dangers of the conditioned and unconditioned without defilement. I, son of good family, by the lordship of the power of devotion, by the purification of the eye of wisdom and faith, by the illumination of the light of knowledge that does not turn away, by the contemplation facing all directions universally, by unobstructed vision of the universal domain, by the skill of insight free from all obstructions, by the purification of the body through the purification of the universal eye-domain, by the skill of bodily bowing with the body inclining toward the streaming in all directions, and by the power of <s>dhāraṇī</s> for retaining the cloud of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s facing all directions and fields. In the eastern direction I see one <s>Tathāgata</s>; also two, also ten, also a hundred <s>Buddha</s>s, also a thousand, a hundred thousand, a <s>koṭi</s>, a hundred <s>koṭi</s>s, a thousand <s>koṭi</s>s, a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s>s, a <s>niyuta</s> hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>Buddha</s>s, up to immeasurable, incalculable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, universal, boundless, unfathomable, inexpressible

body.text:
tathagatān paśyāmi / jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi tathāgatān paśyāmi / cāturdvīpakalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, sāhasradvisāhasratrisāhasramahāsāhasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi tathāgatān paśyāmi / daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi tathāgatān paśyāmi / śatabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetrasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetrakoṭīparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetrakoṭīśataparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhākṣetrakoṭīsahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetrakoṭīśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi, yāvadanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi tathāgatān paśyāmi / yatha pūrvasyāṃ diśi, evaṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarāyāmuttarapūrvāyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ paścimottarāyāmadha ūrdhvaṃ diśi ekamapi tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi tathāgatān paśyāmi / ekaikasyāṃ diśi anuvilokayan nānāvarṇāṃstathāgatān paśyāmi nānāsaṃsthānān nānāvikurvitān nānāvṛṣabhitāvikrīḍitān vicitraparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhān anekavarṇānanekavarṇaraśmijālāvabhāsamuktān vividhabuddhakṣetraviśuddhibhavanavyūhān nānavidhāyuḥpramāṇaviśuddhān yathāśayajagadvijñāpanān vividhābhisaṃbodhiviśuddhimukhavikurvitān buddharṣabhasiṃhanādavinarditāṃstathāgatān paśyāmi / asyā ahaṃ kulaputra samantamukhasarvārambaṇavijñaptisamavasaraṇālokāyā
buddhānusmṛterlābhī / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmanantajñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhānāṃ caryā jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum, ye te samantāvabhāsamaṇḍalabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvatathāgatamaṇḍalasarvabuddhakṣetrabhavanaviśuddhivyūhābhimukhapaśyanatayā / ye te sarvajagatsamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā yathāśayajagadvijñaptitathāgatadarśanaviśuddhyā / ye te daśabalasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā daśatathāgatabalāpramāṇānusaraṇatayā / ye te dharmasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā dharmaśravaṇākārasarvatathāgatakāyameghāvalokanatayā / ye te digvirocanagarbhabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvadiksamudreṣvasaṃbhinnabuddhasamudrāvataraṇatayā / ye te dasadikpraveśabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sūkṣmāvalambanasarvatathāgatavikurvitavṛṣabhitāvataraṇatayā / ye te kalpasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā avarahitasarvakalpatathāgatadarśanavijñaptyā / ye te kālasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvakālatathāgatakāladarśanasaṃvāsāvijahanatayā / ye te kṣetrasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrābhyudgatānabhibhūtabuddhakāyadarśanavijñaptyā / ye te tryadhvasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāstryadhvatathāgatamaṇḍalasvacittāśayasamavasaraṇatayā / ye te ārambaṇasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvārambaṇatathāgataparaṃparāsamudāgamadarśanavijñaptyā / ye te śāntasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā ekakṣaṇasarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgataparinirvāṇavijñaptyā / ye te vigamasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā ekadivase sarvāvāseṣu sarvatathāgataprakramaṇavijñaptyā /
body.translated_text: <s>Tathāgata</s>s I see. I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of a four-continent world-system; equal to the atoms of a thousand-fold, two-thousand-fold, three-thousand-fold great thousand <s>Buddha</s>-field I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s. I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields; equal to the atoms of a hundred <s>Buddha</s>-fields, a thousand, a hundred thousand, a <s>koṭi</s>, a hundred <s>koṭi</s>s, a thousand <s>koṭi</s>s, a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s>s, a <s>niyuta</s> hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>Buddha</s>-field atoms, up to <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields I see. As in the eastern direction, so too in the southern, western, northern, northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest, nadir, and zenith directions I see even one <s>Tathāgata</s>, up to <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields I see. Gazing into each direction, I see <s>Tathāgata</s>s of various colors, various forms, various transformations, various magnificent displays, with variegated assembly-maṇḍala arrays, of many colors, releasing nets of rays of many colors, with various pure <s>Buddha</s>-field palace-arrays, of various purifications of lifespans, informing beings according to their dispositions, displaying various transformations through the gates of the purification of perfect awakening — <s>Tathāgata</s>s roaring the lion's roar of the <s>Buddha</s>-lord I see. I, son of good family, am the obtainer of this <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>) of the light of convergence of universal cognition regarding all objects of the universal gate. How could I know the conduct of <s>bodhisattva</s>s whose purification of the infinite maṇḍala of knowledge [is so vast], or speak of their qualities? Those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in universal illumination, through seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>-maṇḍalas facing the pure palace-arrays of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in all beings, through the purification of seeing <s>Tathāgata</s>s according to the dispositions and cognitions of beings; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in the ten powers, through following the immeasurable ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in the <s>Dharma</s>, through seeing the clouds of the bodies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the form of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> of the womb illuminating in [all] directions, through entering the undifferentiated ocean of <s>Buddha</s>s in the oceans of all directions; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> of entering the ten directions, through entering the magnificent transformations of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s by subtle observation; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in <s>kalpa</s>s, through the cognition of seeing <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all <s>kalpa</s>s without interruption; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in time, through never abandoning the dwelling of seeing <s>Tathāgata</s>s at all times; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in fields, through the cognition of seeing unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-bodies risen above all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in the three times, through the convergence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-maṇḍala of the three times in one's own mind and disposition; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in objects, through the cognition of seeing the successive arising of <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all objects; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in peace, through the cognition of the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all world-realms in a single moment; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in departure, through the cognition of the departure of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in a single day from all abodes;

body.text:
ye te vipulasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā ekaikatathāgatadharmadhātuparyaṅkaparisphuṭabuddhaśarīravijñaptyā / ye te sūkṣmasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā ekavālapathena anabhilāpyabuddhotpādārāgaṇāvataraṇatayā / ye te vyūhasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā ekakṣaṇe sarvalokadhātuṣu abhisaṃbodhivikurvitasaṃdarśanavijñaptyā / ye te kārya samāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvabuddhotpādadharmacakravikurvitajñānāvabhāsapratilābhatayā / ye te samāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ svacittāśayadarśanasarvatathāgatapratibhāsaprāptyā / ye te
karmasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāḥ sarvajagadyathopacitakarmapratibimbasaṃdarśanatayā / ye te vikurvitasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhā aśeṣasarvadharmadhātunalinīpadmaparisphuṭavipulabuddhavikurvitadarśanasamantadigabhimukhavijñaptyā / ye te gaganasamāropitabuddhānusmṛtimukhapratilabdhāstathāgatabimbamegharacitadharmadhātugaganālokanatayā //
body.translated_text: those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established vastly, through the cognition of the <s>Buddha</s>-body manifested on the <s>dharmadhātu</s>-throne of each <s>Tathāgata</s>; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established subtly, through entering inexpressible groves of <s>Buddha</s>-arising by a single hair-path; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in arrays, through the cognition of displaying the transformations of perfect awakening in all world-realms in a single moment; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in activity, through attaining the illumination of knowledge of the transformations of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>-arisings; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> [established in reflection], through the attainment of the reflection of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the vision of one's own mind and disposition; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in <s>karma</s>, through displaying reflected images according to the accumulated <s>karma</s> of all beings; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in transformations, through the universal cognition facing all directions of seeing the vast <s>Buddha</s>-transformations manifested on the lotus-pond of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s without remainder; those who have obtained the gate of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> established in space, through seeing the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> adorned with clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-images. //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe sāgaramukho nāma dikpratyuddeśaḥ / tatra sāgaramegho nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / sa te kulaputra kalyāṇamitraṃ paridīpayiṣyati / kuśalamūlasaṃbhārahetuṃ samavatārayiṣyati / vipulāṃ saṃbhārabhūmiṃ saṃjanayiṣyati / vipulaṃ kuśalamūlavegabalaṃ saṃvarṇayiṣyati / vipulaṃ bodhicittasaṃbhārahetuṃ janayiṣyati / vipulaṃ mahāyānāvabhāsahetumupastambhayiṣyati / vipulaṃ pāramitāsaṃbhārabalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyati / vipulaṃ caryāsāgarāvatāranayaṃ pariśodhayiṣyati / vipulaṃ praṇidhānamaṇḍalaṃ viśodhayiṣyati / vipulaṃ samantamukhaniryāṇavyūhaṃ saṃvardhayiṣyati / vipulaṃ mahākaruṇābalaṃ pravardhayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family — here in the southern region there is a place called <s>Sāgaramukha</s>. There dwells a <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Sāgaramegha</s>. Approach him and ask how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how one should practice. He, son of good family, will illuminate for you the spiritual friend. He will introduce you to the cause of accumulating roots of merit. He will generate in you the vast ground of accumulation. He will praise the vast power and momentum of roots of merit. He will generate the vast cause of accumulating the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). He will support the vast cause of illuminating the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). He will make manifest the vast power of accumulating the <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections). He will purify the vast method of entering the ocean of conduct. He will purify the vast maṇḍala of vows. He will increase the vast array of universal emergence. He will increase the vast power of great compassion. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako meghaśriyo bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya meghaśriyaṃ bhikṣumanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛty avalokya ca meghaśriyo bhikṣorantikāt prakrāntaḥ // 2 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>, circumambulated the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him, and departed from the presence of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Meghaśrī</s>. // 2 //

body.text: 5 Sāgarameghaḥ /
body.translated_text: 5 <s>Sāgaramegha</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastāṃ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīmanuvicintayan, taṃ lokamanusmaran, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ vicārayan, taṃ bodhisattvasamādhinayamanumārjan, taṃ bodhisattvasāgaranayamavalokayan, taṃ buddhamaṇḍalamabhimukhamadhimucyamānaḥ, taṃ buddhadarśanadiśamabhilaṣan, taṃ buddhasamudramanuvicintayan, tāṃ buddhaparaṃparāmanusmaran, taṃ buddhanayānugamamanugacchan, taṃ buddhagaganamanuvilokayan, anupūrveṇa yena sāgaramukhaṃ dikpratyuddeśo yena ca sāgaramegho bhikṣustenopasaṃkramya sāgarameghasya bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sāgarameghaṃ bhikṣumanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sāgarameghasya bhikṣoḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā etadavocat - ahamārya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthito 'nuttaraṃ jñānasāgaramavatartukāmaḥ / na ca jāne kathaṃ bodhisattvā vivartante lokavaṃśāt / āvartante tathāgatavaṃśe / uttaranti saṃsārasāgarāt / avataranti sarvajñajñānasāgaram / uccalanti bālapṛthagjanabhūmīḥ / saṃpadyante tathāgatakule / vivartante saṃsārasrotasaḥ / pravartante bodhisattvacaryāsrotasi, nivartante saṃsārasāgaragaticakrāt / āvartante bodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānacakram / pramardayanti sarvamāramaṇḍalam / dyotayanti sarvabuddhamaṇḍalaprabhavam / śoṣayanti tṛṣṇāsāgaram / vivardhayanti mahākaruṇātoyam / pithanti sarvākṣaṇāpāyadurgativinipātadvārāṇi / vivṛścanti svarganirvāṇadvāram, vinirbhindanti traidhātukanagarakapāṭam / vivṛṇvanti sarvajñatāpuradvārakapāṭam / vijahanti sarvopakaraṇatṛṣṇām / utpādayanti sarvajagatsaṃgrahapraṇidhim //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, reflecting upon that instruction of the spiritual friend, recollecting that world, contemplating that <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation, tracing that <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-method, surveying that <s>Bodhisattva</s>-ocean-method, inclining his mind toward that <s>Buddha</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, longing for that direction of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, reflecting upon that <s>Buddha</s>-ocean, recollecting that <s>Buddha</s>-succession, following that <s>Buddha</s>-method-course, gazing upon that <s>Buddha</s>-sky — gradually proceeded to the region called <s>Sāgaramukha</s> (Ocean-mouth), and to where the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgaramegha</s> (Ocean-cloud) was. Approaching the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgaramegha</s>, bowing his head at his feet, circumambulating the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgaramegha</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, standing before the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgaramegha</s> with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (Complete Awakening) and wish to descend into the unsurpassed ocean of knowledge. But I do not know: How do <s>Bodhisattva</s>s turn away from the lineage of the world? How do they turn toward the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? How do they cross over the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)? How do they descend into the ocean of omniscient knowledge? How do they rise above the stages of foolish ordinary beings? How do they achieve [birth in] the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? How do they turn away from the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>? How do they set in motion the current of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How do they turn back the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>-ocean destinies? How do they revolve the wheel of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct and vows? How do they crush the entire <s>Māra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>? How do they illuminate the source of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s? How do they dry up the ocean of craving? How do they augment the water of great compassion? How do they close the doors of all unfortunate destinies and downfalls? How do they open the door to heaven and <s>nirvāṇa</s>? How do they break open the gate of the city of the three realms? How do they open the gate-door of the city of omniscience? How do they abandon the craving for all possessions? How do they generate the vow to embrace all beings?' //

body.text: evamukte sāgaramegho bhikṣuḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yattvayā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na hi kulaputra anavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / samantamukhakuśalāvabhāsapratilabdhānāmupāyagarbhamārgasamādhijñānālokāvabhāsitānāṃ vipulapuṇyasāgarasaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārāṇāṃ sarvaśuklopacayāpratiprasrabdhānāṃ sarvakalyāṇamitropastabdhopāyāparikhinnānāṃ kāyajīvitanapekṣāṇāṃ sarvavastūdgrahavigatānāmanimnonnatapṛthivīsamacittānāmā prakṛtikṛpāsnehānugatānāṃ sarvabhavagatisaṃvāsābhimukhānāṃ tathāgataviṣayābhilāṣiṇāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / yaduta mahākaruṇācittaṃ sarvasattvaparitrāṇāya, mahāmaitrīcittam sarvajagatsamayogatāyai, sukhacittaṃ sarvajagadduḥkhaskandhavyupaśamanāya, hitacittaṃ sarvākuśaladharmavinivartanatāyai, dayācittaṃ sarvabhayārakṣāyai, asaṅgacittaṃ sarvāvaraṇavinivartanatāyai, vipulacittaṃ sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇatāyai, anantacittamākāśadhātusamavasaraṇasamatānugamāya, vimalacittaṃ sarvatathāgatadarśanavijñaptyai, viśuddhacittaṃ tryadhvāvaśeṣajñānaspharaṇatāyai, jñānacittaṃ sarvāvaraṇajñānavinivartanatāyai sarvajñajñāsāgarāvataraṇatāyai //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāgaramegha</s> said to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s>! For indeed, son of good family, the aspiration for awakening does not arise in beings who have not planted roots of merit — [but it arises] in those who have attained the illumination of universal wholesome radiance, who are illuminated by the light of knowledge of the <s>samādhi</s> of the path of the womb of skillful means, whose accumulations are gathered from the ocean of vast merit, who never relent in the accumulation of all that is wholesome, who are supported by the skillful means of all spiritual friends without weariness, who have no regard for body or life, who are free from grasping at any thing, whose minds are level like the earth — neither low nor high — who are pervaded by natural compassion and affection, who face the co-habitation of all existences and destinies, who long for the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — in such beings the aspiration for awakening arises. Namely: the mind of great compassion, for the protection of all beings; the mind of great loving-kindness, for the equal union with all the world; the mind of happiness, for the cessation of the mass of suffering of all the world; the mind of beneficence, for turning away from all unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s; the mind of sympathy, for protection from all fears; the unattached mind, for turning away from all obstructions; the vast mind, for pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>; the infinite mind, for following the equality of convergence in the realm of space; the stainless mind, for the cognition of seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; the purified mind, for pervading the knowledge of all three times without remainder; the knowledge-mind, for turning away from the knowledge of all obstructions and for descending into the ocean of omniscient knowledge.' //

body.text: ahaṃ kulaputra pūrṇāni dvādaśa varṣāṇi iha sāgaramukhe dikpratyuddeśe viharāmi imaṃ mahāsāgaramārambaṇīkṛtya āmukhīkṛtya, yaduta mahāsāgarasya vipulāpramāṇatāmanuvicintayan vimalaprasannatāṃ ca gambhīraduravagāhatāṃ ca anupūrvanimnasusthitāṃ ca anekaratnākaravicitratāṃ ca vāriskandhāpramāṇatāṃ ca acintyodāravarṇavimātratāṃ ca anantabhūtāṃ ca vicitrodārapraṇādhivāsanatāṃ
body.translated_text: Son of good family, I have dwelt here at the region called <s>Sāgaramukha</s> (Ocean-mouth) for fully twelve years, taking this great ocean as my object and focus — that is, reflecting upon the great ocean's vastness and immeasurability, and its stainless clarity, and its profound unfathomability, and its gradually-sloping well-established foundation, and its variegation with many jewel-mines, and the immeasurability of its mass of water, and its inconceivable, exalted, variegated color-measure, and its infinite creatures, and its variegated, exalted vow-habitation,

body.text:
ca mahāmeghapraticchannatāṃ ca antarāpurṇatāṃ ca anuvicintayan / tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ bhavati - asti na punaranyaḥ kaścidiha loke yo 'smānmanāsāgarādvipulataraśca vistīrṇataraśca apramāṇataraśca gambhīrataraśca vicitrataraśca / tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ yoniśaścintāmanasikāraprayuktasya mahāsāgarasyādhastānmahāpadmaṃ prādurabhūt / aparājitamaṇiratnendranīlamaṇivajradaṇḍaṃ mahāvaiḍūryamaṇiīratnāvataṃsakaṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇavimalavipulapatraṃ kālānusāricandanakalikāvyūham aśmagarbharatnakesaropetaṃ sāgaravipulavistīrṇapramāṇaṃ daśāsurendraśatasahasrasaṃdhāritadaṇḍagarbhaṃ daśamaṇiratnaśatasahasravicitraratnajālasaṃchannaṃ daśanāgendraśatasahasragandhodakameghābhipravarṣitaṃ daśagaruḍendraśatasahasramukhapralambitapaṭṭamaṇidāmahāraṃ daśakinnarendraśatasahasrahitacittasaṃprekṣitaṃ daśamahoragendraśatasahasramukhapraṇatopacāraṃ daśarākṣasendraśatasahasrapraṇatakāyābhipūjitaṃ daśagandharvendraśatasahasravicitratūryasaṃgītistutopacitaṃ daśadevendraśatasahasradivyapuṣpagandhamālyadhūpavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāmeghābhipravarṣitaṃ daśabrahmendraśatasahasramūrdhapraṇatopacāraṃ daśaśuddhāvāsakāyikādevatāśatasahasrakṛtāñjalipuṭanamaskṛtaṃ daśacakraparivartamanujendraśatasahasrasaptaratnapratyudgatābhipūjitaṃ daśasāgaradevatāśatasahasrābhyudgatanamaskṛtaṃ daśajyotīrasamaṇiratnaśatasahasraraśmivyūhāvabhāsitaṃ daśapuṇyaśuddhamaṇiratnaśatasahasrasuniścitavinyastopaśobhitaṃ daśavairocanamaṇiratnaśatasahasravimalagarbhaṃ daśaśrīmaṇiratnaśatasahasramahāśrīpratāpanaṃ daśavicitrakośamaṇiratnaśatasahasrānantāvabhāsitaṃ daśajambūdhvajamaṇiratnaśatasahasrasuparigṛhitasthitaprāptopaśobhitaṃ daśavajrasiṃhamaṇiratnaśatasahasrāparājitavyūhaṃ daśasūryagarbhamaṇiratnaśatasahasrodārottaptopacitaṃ daśaruciramaṇiratnaśatasahasravividhavarṇopacāraṃ daśacintārājamaṇiratnaśatasahasrākṣayavyūhaprabhojjvalitam / tacca mahāpadmaṃ tathāgatalokottarakuśalamūlanirjātaṃ bodhisattvāśayaṃsaṃprasthitaṃ sarvadigabhimukhavijñapanaṃ
mayāgatadharmaniryātaṃ nirāmagandhakarmasaṃbhutam araṇādharmatānayavyūhaṃ svapnasamadharmatāsamudācāram anabhisaṃskāradharmanayamudritam asaṅgadharmanayānugataṃ samantāddaśadikkuladharmadhātuspharaṇaṃ buddhaviṣayaprabhāvabhāsanākulam, yasya na śakyamasaṃkhyeyaiurapi kalpaśatasahasrairākāraguṇasaṃsthānavarṇavyūhaparyanto 'dhigantum / tacca mahāpadmaṃ tathāgatakāyaparyaṅkapariṣphuṭaṃ paripūrṇaṃ paśyāmi / taṃ ca tathāgatakāyamita upādāya yāvadbhavāgraparamaṃ paśyāmi / tasya ca tathāgatasya acintyamāsanavyūhaṃ paśyāmi / acintyaparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhān / acintiyān prabhāmaṇḍalavyūhān / acintyāṃ lakṣaṇasaṃpadamacintyāmanuvyañjanacitratāmacintyāṃ buddhavṛṣabhitām / acintyaṃ buddhavikurvitam / acintyāṃ tathāgatavarṇaviśuddhim / acintyāmavalokitamūrdhitām / acintyāṃ prabhūtajihvatāṃ paśyāmi / acintyān buddhasarasvatīvyūhān śṛṇomi / acintyāṃ balāpramāṇatām, acintyāṃ vaiśaradyavyūhaviśuddhim, acintyaṃ pratisaṃvidbalābhinirhāramanugacchāmi / acintyaṃ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāsamudāgamamanusmarāmi / acintyamabhisaṃbodhivikurvitaṃ paśyāmi / acintyaṃ dharmameghābhinigarjitam, acintyaṃ samantadarśanavijñaptyāśrayavyūhaṃ
body.translated_text: and its being covered by great clouds, and its inner fullness — reflecting upon all this. And, son of good family, this thought occurred to me: 'Is there perhaps anything else in this world that is vaster, more extensive, more immeasurable, deeper, more variegated than this great ocean?' And, son of good family, while I was thus engaged in thorough reflection and attention, from beneath the great ocean there appeared a great lotus — with a stalk of invincible <s>maṇi</s>-jewel, sapphire, and diamond; with a garland of great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; with vast, stainless petals of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (purest gold); with an array of buds of black <s>aloeswood</s> and sandalwood; with filaments of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (quartz) jewels; as vast in extent as the ocean; with its stalk-womb supported by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Asurendra</s>s (lords of anti-gods); covered with a jewel-net variegated with ten times a hundred thousand <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; showered upon with clouds of fragrant water from the mouths of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Nāgendra</s>s (serpent lords); adorned with jewel-silk-cord-garlands hanging from the mouths of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Garuḍendra</s>s (lords of Garuḍas); gazed upon with benevolent minds by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Kinnarendra</s>s (lords of Kinnaras); attended with prostrate-faced homage by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Mahoragendra</s>s; worshipped with prostrate bodies by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Rākṣasendra</s>s (lords of demons); honored with the music and songs of various instruments by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Gandharvendra</s>s; showered upon with clouds of divine flowers, fragrances, garlands, incense, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, and pennants by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Devendra</s>s; attended with crown-bowed homage by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Brahmendra</s>s; saluted with joined palms by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) deities; worshipped with the offering of the seven treasures by ten times a hundred thousand <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning) lords of men; saluted with rising homage by ten times a hundred thousand ocean-deities; illuminated with ray-arrays of ten times a hundred thousand luminous <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; adorned with well-placed arrangements of ten times a hundred thousand merit-purified <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; with stainless womb of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; blazing with great glory of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Śrī</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; infinitely illuminated by ten times a hundred thousand variegated-treasury <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; adorned with well-grasped stable <s>Jambūdhvaja</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, ten times a hundred thousand; of unconquered array with ten times a hundred thousand <s>Vajrasiṃha</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; resplendent with exalted, heated ten times a hundred thousand <s>Sūryagarbha</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; attended with various color-offerings of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Rucira</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels; blazing with the radiance of inexhaustible array of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Cintārāja</s> (wish-king) <s>maṇi</s>-jewels. And that great lotus was born from the supramundane roots of merit of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, set forth from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-aspiration, displaying cognition facing all directions, issuing the <s>Dharma</s> of attainment without foul-smelling <s>karma</s>-production, arrayed with the method of non-enmity <s>dharma</s>-nature, of the conduct of dream-like <s>dharma</s>-equality, sealed with the method of unconditioned <s>dharma</s>, following the method of unattached <s>dharma</s>, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions universally, filled with the radiance of the splendor of the <s>Buddha</s>-domain — whose boundary of form, qualities, configuration, color, and array cannot be reached even in innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpa</s>s. And I see that great lotus fully suffused with the cross-legged body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And I see that <s>Tathāgata</s>-body from here up to the highest plane of existence. And I see the inconceivable throne-array of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, and inconceivable assembly-circle arrays, and inconceivable radiance-circle arrays, and inconceivable perfection of marks, and inconceivable variegation of minor marks, and inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-majesty, and inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-transformations, and inconceivable <s>Tathāgata</s> color-purification, and inconceivable gazing majesty. And I see his inconceivable broad tongue. And I hear inconceivable arrays of the <s>Buddha</s>'s eloquence. And I follow his inconceivable immeasurability of powers, and inconceivable purification of the array of fearlessnesses, and inconceivable accomplishment of the power of analytical knowledges. And I remember inconceivable former <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct. And I see inconceivable <s>abhisaṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening) transformations. And inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>-cloud thundering, and inconceivable array of the support of the cognition of universal vision,

body.text: śṛṇomi / acintyāpramāṇāṃ vāmadakṣiṇena śarīravibhaktim, acintyaṃ sattvārthakāyapariprāptiṃ paśyāmi //
body.translated_text: I hear. And I see inconceivable, immeasurable division of his body into left and right, and inconceivable attainment of forms for the benefit of beings. //

body.text: sa ca me tathāgato dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya śirasaṃ parimārjya samantanetraṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvatathāgataviṣayaṃ bodhisattvacaryāprabhāvanaṃ sarvadharmadhātutalaprabhedāvabhāsanaṃ sarvadharmamaṇḍalasamavasaraṇāvabhāsanaṃ sarvakṣetramaṇḍalākāraviśuddhyālokaṃ sarvaparapravādimaṇḍalavikiraṇaṃ sarvamārakalipramardanaṃ sarvasattvadhātusaṃtoṣaṇaṃ sarvasattvacittagahanāvabhāsanaṃ sarvasattvayathāśayavijñāpanaṃ sarvasattvendriyacakraparivartaprabhāsanaṃ prakāśayati / taṃ cāhaṃ samantanetraṃ dharmaparyāyamudgṛhṇāmi saṃdhārayāmi pravartayāmi puanidhyāyāmi evaṃrūpeṇodgaheṇa, yasya likhyamānasya mahāsamudrāpskandhapramāṇā ca maṣiḥ, sumeruparvatarājamātrakalamasaṃcayaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet / na ca tasya dharmaparyāyasya ekaikasmātparivartādekaikasmāddharmadvārākaikasmāddharmanayādekaikasmāddharmayoneḥ ekaikasmāddharmapadaprabhedāt kṣaya upalabhyate, na ūnatvaṃ vā paryādānaṃ vā paryavasthānaṃ vā paryantaniṣṭhā vā //
body.translated_text: And that <s>Tathāgata</s>, extending his right hand, stroked my head and proclaimed to me a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) called '<s>Samantanetra</s>' (Universal Eye) — the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the illumination of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, the illumination of the analysis of the surface of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s, the illumination of the convergence of all <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s, the light illuminating the forms of all field-<s>maṇḍala</s>s, the scattering of all opposing doctrinal <s>maṇḍala</s>s, the crushing of all <s>Māra</s>-strife, the satisfying of the entire realm of beings, the illumination of the thicket of the minds of all beings, the cognition according to the dispositions of all beings, the illumination of the turning of the wheel of the faculties of all beings. And I take up, retain, set in motion, and deeply contemplate that <s>Samantanetra</s> discourse with such a manner of retention that, were it to be written down, the ink would be as vast as the great ocean's mass of water, and the pile of reed-pens as great as <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, would be exhausted — yet from that discourse, from each of its chapters, from each <s>dharma</s>-gateway, from each <s>dharma</s>-method, from each <s>dharma</s>-source, from each division of <s>dharma</s>-words, no exhaustion is found, nor diminution, nor consumption, nor constriction, nor a final limit. //

body.text: iti hi kulaputra pūrṇāni dvādaśa varṣāṇyahamimaṃ samantanetraṃ dharmaparyāyamudgṛhītavān / evaṃrūpeṇodgaheṇa yadekadivasena asaṃkhyeyan parivartān paryavāpnomi śrutodgahaṇadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartānavatarāmi śāntamukhadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān avatarāmi śāntamukhadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān samavasarāmi anantāvartadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān vibhāvayāmi praticinomi bhūmyavacāraṇānugamadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān paryādadāmi tejovatīdhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān abhinirharāmi padmavyūhadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān saṃprakāśayāmi svaraviviktadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān pratibhajāmi gaganagarbhadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān pravistarāmi jyotiṣakūṭadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / asaṃkhyeyān parivartān parisaṃsthāpayāmi sāgaragarbhadhāraṇyālokāvabhāsena / ye ca me kecit sattvā upasaṃkrāmanti pūrvasyāṃ diśi devā vā devendrā vā nāgā vā nāgendrā vā yakṣā vā yakṣendrā vā asurā vā asurendrā vā garuḍā vā garuḍendrā vā mahoragā vā mahoragendrā vā manuṣyā vā manuṣyendrā vā brahmāṇo vā brahmendrā vā, tān sarvānatraiva samantanetre tathāgatabodhisattvacaryāvabhāse dharmaparyāye pratiṣṭhāpayāmi niveśayāmi / sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāmeva samantanetraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ rocayāmi nirūpayāmi paridīpayāmi saṃvarṇayāmi saṃdarśayāmi vibhajāmi vistārayāmi uttānīkaromi vivarāmi pramuñcāmi avabhāsayāmi / yathā purvasyāṃ diśi, evaṃ dakṣiṇāyāḥ paścimāyā uttarāyā uttarapūrvāyāḥ purvadakṣiṇāyā dakṣiṇapaścimāyāḥ paścimottarāyā adha urdhvāyāśca diśaḥ ye kecit sattvā upasaṃkrāmanti - pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O son of good family, for a full twelve years I have mastered this <s>Samantanetra</s> (Universal Eye) <s>dharma</s>-discourse. With such mastery, in a single day I comprehend innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic power) of learning and retaining what is heard. I penetrate innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Śāntamukha</s> (Peaceful Gateway). I penetrate innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Śāntamukha</s>. I assemble innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Anantāvarta</s> (Infinite Turning). I illuminate and collect innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Bhūmyavacāraṇānugama</s> (Following the Traversal of the Stages). I master innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Tejovatī</s> (Possessing Splendor). I bring forth innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Padmavyūha</s> (Lotus Array). I proclaim innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Svaravivikta</s> (Distinct Voice). I distribute innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Gaganagarbha</s> (Womb of Space). I elaborate innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Jyotiṣakūṭa</s> (Peak of Light). I establish innumerable chapters through the radiance of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Sāgaragarbha</s> (Womb of the Ocean). And whatever beings approach me from the eastern direction — whether <s>devas</s> or <s>Devendras</s>, <s>nāgas</s> or <s>Nāgendras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s> or <s>Yakṣendras</s>, <s>asuras</s> or <s>Asurendras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s> or <s>Garuḍendras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s> or <s>Mahoragendras</s>, humans or lords of humans, <s>Brahmās</s> or <s>Brahmendras</s> — I establish and settle them all in this very <s>Samantanetra</s>, the <s>dharma</s>-discourse illuminating the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And for all of them I delight in, explain, illuminate, praise, display, analyze, expand, make plain, expound, release, and shed light upon this <s>Samantanetra</s> <s>dharma</s>-discourse. Just as in the eastern direction, so also in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, lower, and upper directions — whatever beings approach — as before //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra, ekaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryā jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktuṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsamudrāvatīrṇānāṃ pariśuddhapraṇidhyanugamena, sarvapraṇidhānasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvakalpasaṃvāsavyavacchedāya, sarvasattvasaṃsārāvatīrṇānāṃ yathāśayacaryānuvartanatāyaiḥ sarvajagaccittasāgarāvatīrṇānāmajñānavijñaptyā, sarvaguṇasāgarāvatīrṇānāmasaṅgadaśabalajñānāvalokasaṃjananatāyai, sarvasattvendriyasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ paripācanavinayakālānatikramaṇatāyai, sarvakṣetrasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvakṣetraviśuddhipraṇidhyabhinirhāreṇa, sarvabuddhasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ tathāgatapūjopasthānapraṇidhibalena, sarvadharmasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ jñānavijñaptyā, sarvaguṇasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ pratipatyanugamena, sarvajaganmantrasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvamantresu dharmacakrapravartanābhinirharaṇatāyai //
body.translated_text: This single <s>dharma</s>-discourse, O son of good family, is all I know. How could I know the practice or speak of the virtues of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — those who have descended into the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s> practices, through the pursuit of purified vows; who have descended into all oceans of vows, for the cutting off of cohabitation with all <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages); who have descended into the <s>saṃsāra</s> of all beings, for following their practice according to their dispositions; who have descended into the ocean of minds of all beings, for the notification of ignorance; who have descended into the ocean of all qualities, for generating the observation of the unattached ten powers of knowledge; who have descended into the ocean of faculties of all beings, for not overstepping the time of maturation and discipline; who have descended into the ocean of all fields, through the vow to accomplish the purification of all fields; who have descended into the ocean of all <s>Buddhas</s>, through the power of the vow to worship and serve the <s>Tathāgata</s>; who have descended into the ocean of all <s>dharmas</s>, through knowledge and cognition; who have descended into the ocean of all qualities, through following the practice; who have descended into the ocean of <s>mantras</s> of all beings, for accomplishing the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) in all <s>mantras</s> //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe itaḥ ṣaṣṭiyojanaiḥ sāgaratīraṃ nāma laṅkāpatham / tatra supratisthito nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha kathaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bodhisattvacaryā pariśodhayitavyā //
body.translated_text: Go, O son of good family. Right here in the southern region, sixty <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) from here, is the <s>Laṅkā</s>-path called <s>Sāgaratīra</s> (Ocean Shore). There dwells a monk named <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> (Well-Established). Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> purify the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sāgarameghasya bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sāgarameghaṃ bhikṣumanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya avalokya sāgarameghasya bhikṣorantikāt prakrāntaḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the monk <s>Sāgaramegha</s>, having circumambulated the monk <s>Sāgaramegha</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing [upon him], departed from the presence of the monk <s>Sāgaramegha</s> // 3 //

body.text: 6 Supratiṣṭhitaḥ /
body.translated_text: 6. <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastāṃ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanī taṃ ca samantanetraṃ dharmaparyāyamanusmaran, tacca tathāgatavikurvitamanuvicintayan, tāṃśca dharmapadavyañjanameghān dhārayan, tāṃśca dharmamukhasāgarānavataran, taṃ ca dharmavidhimanuvilokayan, tāṃśca dharmāvartanayānavagāhyamānaḥ, tacca dharmagaganaṃ samavasaran, tacca dharmamaṇḍalaṃ pariśodhayan, taṃ ca dharmaratnadvīpamanuvicārayan, anupūrveṇa yena sāgaratīraṃ laṅkāpathastenopasaṃkramya pūrvāṃ diśamavalokayāmāsa supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣordarśanakāmatayā / evaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ paścimāmuttarāmuttarapūrvāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāṃ paścimottarāmadha ūrdhvāṃ diśamavalokayāmāsa supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣordarśanakāmatayā / so 'paśyatsupratiṣṭhitaṃ bhikṣuṃ gaganatale caṃkramyamāṇamasaṃkhyeyadevatāśatasahasraparivṛtam, tacca gaganatalaṃ divyapuṣpameghābhikīrṇamadrākṣīdasaṃkhyeyadivyatūryameghanirghoṣam, asaṃkhyeyapaṭṭapatākālaṃkāraṃ devendraiḥ supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣoḥ pūjakarmaṇi / acintyakālāgurumeghonnatanigarjanaṃ ca gaganatalamapaśyat nāgendraiḥ / asaṃkhyeyadivyamanojñavacanopacārastutisarvavādyatūryasaṃgītinirghoṣāṃśca kinnarendraiḥ saṃprayojitān gaganatalādaśrauṣīt / acintyāṃśca sūkṣmasphuṭavastrameghān gaganatale prītimanobhirmahoragendraiḥ prahitān prasṛtānapaśyat supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣoḥ spṛhamāṇarūpaiḥ / acintyāṃśca maṇiratnameghān asurendragaganatalamadhiṣṭhitān acintyaguṇavyūhāvabhāsamapaśyat / acintyāṃśca garuḍendragaṇānudāramānavarūpabalasaṃsthānān garuḍendrakanyāparivārān avihiṃsāparamān prāñjalībhūtān gaganatale 'paśyat / acintyāni ca yakṣendraśatasahasrāṇi saparivārāṇi vikṛtaśarīrāṇi gaganatalagatānapaśyat supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣormaitryādhipateyatayā / acintyāni ca rākṣasendraśatasahasrāṇi saparivārāṇi gaganatale anuparivartamānāni supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣorārakṣāpratipannānyapaśyat / acintyāni ca brahmendraśatasahasrāṇi gaganatale kṛtāñjalipūṭāni abhipretamanojñavacanopacārastutipratyudāhāraprayuktānyapaśyat / acintyāni ca śuddhāvāsakāyikadevatāśatasahasrāṇi gaganatale vimānagatānyapaśyat supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣoḥ
pūjākarmaṇi //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, recollecting that instruction of the spiritual friend and that <s>Samantanetra</s> <s>dharma</s>-discourse, contemplating that miraculous transformation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, retaining those clouds of <s>dharma</s>-words and syllables, penetrating those oceans of <s>dharma</s>-gateways, observing that method of <s>dharma</s>, fathoming those vehicles of the mode of <s>dharma</s>-turning, assembling in that sky of <s>dharma</s>, purifying that maṇḍala of <s>dharma</s>, contemplating that jewel-island of <s>dharma</s>, gradually approached <s>Sāgaratīra</s>, the <s>Laṅkā</s>-path, and looked toward the eastern direction, desiring to see the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. Likewise he looked toward the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, lower, and upper directions, desiring to see the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. He saw the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> walking in the expanse of the sky, surrounded by innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>devatās</s> (divine beings). He beheld that expanse of the sky strewn with clouds of divine flowers, resounding with innumerable clouds of divine musical instruments, adorned with innumerable silk-and-pennant ornaments, by <s>Devendras</s> in the act of worshipping the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. He saw the expanse of the sky lofty with the roaring of inconceivable clouds of black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, [offered] by <s>Nāgendras</s> (serpent-kings). He heard from the expanse of the sky innumerable divine, delightful verbal praises and the sounds of all instruments, music, and song, produced by <s>Kinnarendras</s> (lords of <s>kinnaras</s>). He saw inconceivable clouds of fine, exquisite garments sent forth in the expanse of the sky with joyful minds by <s>Mahoragendras</s> (lords of great serpents), in forms expressing reverence for the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. He saw inconceivable clouds of gem-jewels established in the sky by <s>Asurendras</s> (lords of <s>asuras</s>), with the radiance of inconceivable arrays of virtues. He saw inconceivable hosts of <s>Garuḍendras</s> (eagle-kings), of noble, proud, powerful, and magnificent form, attended by <s>Garuḍendra</s> maidens, devoted to non-harm, with palms joined together, in the expanse of the sky. He saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣendras</s> (lords of <s>yakṣas</s>) with their retinues, of fearsome bodies, gone to the expanse of the sky, through the sovereignty of the loving-kindness of the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. He saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>Rākṣasendras</s> (lords of <s>rākṣasas</s>) with their retinues, revolving in the expanse of the sky, engaged in the protection of the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. He saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>Brahmendras</s> (lords of <s>Brahmā</s>s) with palms joined together in the expanse of the sky, engaged in offering the desirable, delightful verbal praises. He saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) <s>devatās</s> in their aerial palaces in the expanse of the sky, in the act of worshipping the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ supratiṣṭhitaṃ bhikṣuṃ gaganatale caṃkramyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ prāñjaliḥ supratiṣṭhitaṃ bhikṣuṃ namaskṛtya evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmā anveṣṭavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmāḥ samudānayitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmāḥ saṃhartavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmāḥ sevitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmā bhāvayitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmā anuvartitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmāḥ paripiṇḍayitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmāḥ paribhāvayitavyāḥ? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmā viśodhayitavyāḥ sarvabodhisattvakāryapariprāpaṇāya? kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmā anugantavyāḥ? śrutaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having seen the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> walking in the expanse of the sky, was pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, and with palms joined, bowing to the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>, spoke thus: 'I, O noble one, have generated the mind toward unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> seek the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> bring together the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> collect the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> cultivate the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> develop the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> follow the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> accumulate the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> cultivate the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> purify the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> for the accomplishment of all <s>bodhisattva</s> tasks? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> pursue the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? I have heard

body.text: ca ma āryo bodhisattvānāmavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena buddhadharmeṣu prayoktavyam, yathā prayujyamāno 'virahito bhavati buddhadarśanena, yathābhūtavipravāsāya avirahito bhavati bodhisattvadarśanena / sarvabodhisattvakuśalamūlaikadhyātāyai avirahito bhavati buddhadharmaiḥ / jñānānugamāyāvirahito bhavati sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānaiḥ / sarvabodhisattvakāryapariprāpaṇāya avirahito bhavati bodhisattvacaryayā / sarvakalpasaṃvāsāparikhedatāyai avirahito bhavati sarvabuddhakṣetraspharaṇena / sarvalokadhātupariśuddhaye avirahito bhavati buddhavikurvitadarśanena / sarvatathāgatavikurvitavijñaptyai avirahito bhavati saṃskṛtāvāsena / nirmitopamabodhisattvacaryāyāḥ sarvabhavagaticyutyupapattyāyatanasvaśarīrānugamanatāyai avirahito bhavati dharmaśravaṇena / sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanatāyai avirahito bhavati jñānālokena tryadhvajñānānugamānusaraṇatāyai //
body.translated_text: that the noble one gives instruction and guidance to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore let the noble one tell me: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> engage with the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, so that while engaging one is not separated from the vision of the <s>Buddha</s>, so that for the sake of not dwelling far from reality one is not separated from the vision of <s>bodhisattvas</s>? So that for the unification of all <s>bodhisattva</s> roots of merit one is not separated from the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? So that for the pursuit of knowledge one is not separated from all <s>bodhisattva</s> vows? So that for the accomplishment of all <s>bodhisattva</s> tasks one is not separated from <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? So that for unwearying cohabitation with all <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) one is not separated from the pervading of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields? So that for the purification of all world-realms one is not separated from the vision of <s>Buddha</s>-transformations? So that for the cognition of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations one is not separated from dwelling in the conditioned? So that for the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice resembling an emanation, for the pursuit of one's own body through the abodes, paths, deaths, and rebirths in all states of existence, one is not separated from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>? So that for receiving the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> one is not separated from the light of knowledge, for the pursuit and following of the knowledge of the three times? //

body.text: evamukte supratiṣṭhito bhikṣuḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya buddhadharmān sarvajñatādharmān svayaṃbhūdharmān paripṛcchasi / ahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgamukhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / etaṃ me kulaputra asaṅgamukhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamāyūhatā niryūhatā anusaratā vibhajatā vicinvatā pravicinvatā pratibhāsayatā prabhāsayatā asaṅgakoṭirnāma jñānālokaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya pratilambhānnāsti me sarvasattvacittacaritāvabhāseṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti sarvasattvacyutyupapattiparijñāsu saṅgaḥ / nāsti pūrvanivāsānusmṛtimukhāvatāreṣu saṅgaḥ / nāstyaparāntakalpasarvajagatsaṃvāseṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti pratyutpannādhvasarvajagadvijñaptiṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti sarvasattvarutamantrasaṃvṛtiparijñāneṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti sarvasattvasaṃśayacchedeṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti rātriṃdivakṣaṇamuhūrtakālasaṃjñāgatāvatāreṣu saṅgaḥ / nāsti daśadigbuddhakṣetresu aśarīraspharaṇatāsu saṅgaḥ, yaduta abhāvapratiṣṭhitānabhisaṃskāravipratilambhena / asyāhaṃ kulaputra anabhisaṃskārikāyā ṛddheranubhāvena iha gaganatale caṃkramāmi, tiṣṭhāmi, niṣīdāmi, niṣadyāmi, vividhānīryāpathān kalpayāmi, antadardhāmi prādurbhavāmi, dhūmāyāmi prajvalāmi / eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavāmi, bahudhā bhūtvaiko bhavāmi / āvirbhāvaṃ tirobhāvaṃ pratyanubhavāmi / tiraḥkuḍyaṃ tiraḥprākāramasajjan gacchāmi tadyathāpi nāma ākāśe / ākāśe 'pi paryaṅkena kramāmi tadyathāpi nāma pakṣī śakuniḥ / pṛthivyāmapi unmajjananimajjanaṃ karomi tadyathodake / udake 'pyasajjamāno gacchāmi tadyathā pṛthivyām / dhūmāyāmi prajvalāmi tadyathāpi nāma mahānagniskandhaḥ / pṛthivīmapi kampayāmi / imāvapi candrasūryau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau evaṃ mahaujasvinau pāṇinā saṃparimārjayāmi / yāvadbrahmalokaṃ kāye ca saṃvartayāmi / gandhadhūpapaṭalameghasaṃchannaṃ lokaṃ kṛtvā prajvalāmi / sarvaratnārcimeghasaṃchannaṃ lokaṃ kṛtvā sarvajagatsadṛśanirmitameghān pramuñcāmi / anantavarṇaprabhājālameghān pramuñcan samantāddiśo niryāmi - yaduta pūrvāṃ diśaṃ niryāmi,
body.translated_text: When this was said, the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You who have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening now inquire about the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> of omniscience, the <s>dharmas</s> of the Self-Born One. I, O son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called "Unobstructed Gateway" (<s>asaṅgamukha</s>). Through striving, endeavoring, following, analyzing, investigating, thoroughly investigating, reflecting upon, and illuminating this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation of the Unobstructed Gateway, I have attained the light of knowledge called "Unobstructed Summit" (<s>asaṅgakoṭi</s>), upon the attainment of which there is no attachment for me in illuminating the mental conduct of all beings. There is no attachment in the comprehensive knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of all beings. There is no attachment in entering the gateways of the recollection of past lives. There is no attachment in dwelling with all beings of the world in the future limit of <s>kalpas</s>. There is no attachment in the cognitions of all beings of the world in the present time. There is no attachment in the comprehensive knowledge of the conventional speech, sounds, and <s>mantras</s> of all beings. There is no attachment in cutting the doubts of all beings. There is no attachment in entering the designations of night, day, moment, and hour-time. There is no attachment in pervading the <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions without a body — namely, through the non-attainment of non-construction established in non-existence. By the power of this unconditioned <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), I walk in the sky, I stand, I sit, I recline, I assume various deportments, I vanish, I appear, I emit smoke, I blaze. Having become one, I become many; having become many, I become one. I experience appearance and disappearance. I pass through walls, through ramparts, without obstruction, just as through space. I walk cross-legged through space, just like a winged bird. I dive in and out of the earth as if in water. I walk upon water without sinking, as upon earth. I smoke and blaze like a great mass of fire. I cause the earth to tremble. These sun and moon, of such great supernatural power, of such great authority, of such great majesty — I wipe them with my hand. I extend my body up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world. Having covered the world with a layer of fragrance-incense clouds, I blaze. Having covered the world with clouds of all jewel-radiances, I release clouds of emanations resembling all beings of the world. Releasing clouds of nets of radiance of infinite colors, I go forth to all directions on all sides — namely, I go forth to the eastern direction,

body.text:
dakṣiṇāṃ paścimāmuttarāmuttarapūrvāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāṃ paścimottarāmadha urdhvāmapi diśaṃ niryāmi / ekaikena cittakṣeṇena pūrvasyāṃ diśi ekaṃ lokadhātumatikramāmi / dvāvapi daśāpi lokadhātuśatamapi lokadhātusahasramapi lokadhātuśatasahasramapi lokadhātukoṭīmapi lokadhātukoṭīśatamapi lokadhātukoṭīsahasramapi lokadhatukoṭīśatasahasramapi lokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasramapi, aparimāṇānapi lokadhātūnaprameyān, asaṃkhyeyānapi acintyānapi atulyānapi amāpyānapi asamantānapi aparyantānapi asīmāprāptānapi anabhilāpyānabhilāpyānapi lokadhātūnatikramāmi / ye ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, teṣu teṣu lokadhātusamudreṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātuprasareṣu, tāsu tāsu lokadhātudikṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātuparivarteṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātusamavasaraṇeṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātusaṃbhaveṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātunirdeśeṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātudvāreṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātukalpanirdeśeṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātvavatāreṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātubodhimaṇḍavyūheṣu, teṣu teṣu lokadhātuparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu ye buddhābhagavanto dharmaṃdeśayanti, teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmekaikaṃ tathāgatamanantabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kāyanānātvairekaikena kāyena anantabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ pūjāmeghaiḥ pravarṣannupasaṃkramāmi / upasaṃkramya pūjāṃ karomyapratiprasrabdhaḥ sarvapuṣpaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ sarvamālyaiḥ sarvavilepanaiḥ sarvavastraiḥ sarvadhvajaiḥ sarvapatākābhiḥ sarvavitānaiḥ sarvajālaiḥ sarvavigrahaiḥ / yacca te buddha bhagavanto bhāṣante deśayanti udīrayanti saṃprakāśayanti saṃvarṇayanti paridīpayanti upadiśanti nirdiśanti prabhāvayanti, tatsarvamājānāmi, udgṛhṇāmi / yā ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhistāṃ sarvāmanusmarāmi / yathā purvasyāṃ diśi,
evameva dakṣiṇāyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarāyāmuttarapūrvāyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ paścimottarāyāmadha ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi ekamapi lokadhātumatikramāmi / dvāvapi daśāpi lokadhātuśatamapi yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānapi lokadhātūnatikramāmi / ye ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, teṣu teṣu lokadhātusamudreṣu tāsu tāsu lokadhātuviśuddhiṣu, yāvat teṣu teṣu lokadhātuṣu parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu dharmaṃ deśayanti, tān sarvān paśyāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ pūjāṃ karomi sarvapuṣpairyāvatsarvaparigrahaiḥ / yacca te buddhā bhagavanto bhāṣante yāvatprabhāvayanti tatsarvamājānāmi udgṛhṇāmi / yā ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhistāṃ sarvāmanusmarāmi / yeṣāṃ ca sattvānāmābhāsamāgacchāmi, yaiḥ samāgacchāmi, te sarve niyatā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye ca sattvā mamābhāsamāgacchanti, sūkṣmā vā udārā vā hīnā vā praṇītā vā sukhitā vā duḥkhitā vā, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tatpramāṇāṃ kāyamadhitiṣṭhāmi paripākavinayakālānatikramaṇatāyai / ye ca sattvā māmupasaṃkrāmanti tān sarvānatraiva samantajave 'moghavikramaparyavasāne bodhisattvavimokṣe pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra samantajavaṃ tathāgatapūjopasthānaprayogaṃ
body.translated_text: the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, and also to the downward and upward directions. In a single mind-moment, in the eastern direction, I traverse one world-system — also two, also ten, also a hundred, also a thousand, also a hundred thousand, also a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), also a hundred <s>koṭis</s>, also a thousand <s>koṭis</s>, also a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s>, also a hundred thousand <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of world-systems, also immeasurable, incalculable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, immense, unbounded, limitless, and inexpressibly inexpressible world-systems I traverse. And in whatever world-systems the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, abide, dwell, and live — in those various world-system-oceans, in those world-system-expanses, in those world-system-directions, in those world-system-revolutions, in those world-system-convergences, in those world-system-arisings, in those world-system-expositions, in those world-system-gateways, in those world-system-<s>kalpa</s>-expositions, in those world-system-entries, in those world-system <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-arrays, in those world-system assembly-circles where the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s> — I approach each one of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with body-manifestations equal in number to the atoms of infinite <s>Buddha</s>-fields, each body raining clouds of worship equal in number to the atoms of infinite <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Having approached, I make unceasing worship with all flowers, all fragrances, all garlands, all ointments, all garments, all banners, all pennants, all canopies, all nets, and all forms. And whatever those <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, speak, teach, proclaim, elucidate, praise, illuminate, instruct, expound, and empower — all that I comprehend and grasp. And I recall all the purifications of the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Just as in the eastern direction, so too in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions, I traverse even one world-system — also two, also ten, also a hundred, up to inexpressibly inexpressible world-systems equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, I traverse. And in whatever world-systems the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, abide, dwell, and live — in those various world-system-oceans, in those world-system-purifications, up to where in those world-system assembly-circles they teach the <s>Dharma</s> — I see them all. And I make worship to those <s>Tathāgatas</s> with all flowers up to all provisions. And whatever those <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, speak up to empower — all that I comprehend and grasp. And I recall all the purifications of the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. And whatever beings come into the range of my radiance, whomever I meet — they all become determined toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. And whatever beings come into the range of my radiance, whether subtle or great, inferior or superior, happy or suffering — for all of them I empower a body of corresponding measure, so as not to miss the time for their ripening and discipline. And whatever beings approach me, I establish them all right here in this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called "Universal Speed of Unfailing Valor" (<s>samantajava amoghavikramaparyavasāna</s>). I, O son of good family, know this Universal Speed — the practice of worship and attendance upon <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

body.text: sarvasattvaparipākānukūlamasaṅgamukhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāśīlānāṃ mahāyānapratipattiśīlānāṃ bodhisattvamārgāvipravāsaśīlānāsaṅgaśīlānāṃ bodhisattvāśayagarbhāvipātanaśīlānāṃ bodhicittāparityāgaśīlānāṃ buddhadharmādhyālambanaśīlānāṃ sarvajñatāmanasikārāvipravasitaśīlānāṃ gaganasamaśīlānāṃ sarvalokāniśritaśīlānāmavinaṣṭaśīlāmanupahataśīlānāmakhaṇḍaśīlānāmacchidraśīlānāmaśabalaśīlānāmakalmāṣaśīlānāṃ viśuddhaśīlānāṃ virajonirmalaśīlānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryā jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation of the Unobstructed Gateway, conducive to the ripening of all beings. But how could I know or speak of the conduct or qualities of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> — whose nature is great compassion, whose nature is the practice of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, whose nature is never departing from the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, whose nature is unattached, whose nature is not letting fall the womb of <s>bodhisattva</s>-aspiration, whose nature is not abandoning <s>Bodhicitta</s>, whose nature is adherence to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, whose nature is not straying from the attention to omniscience, whose nature is equal to space, whose nature is not depending on any world, whose nature is unimpaired morality, whose nature is undamaged morality, whose nature is unbroken morality, whose nature is unperforated morality, whose nature is unspotted morality, whose nature is unstained morality, whose nature is pure morality, whose nature is morality free from dust and stain? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe vajrapuraṃ nāma dramiḍapaṭṭanam / tatra megho nāma dramiḍaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, katham pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, O son of good family! Right here in the southern region, there is a Dramiḍa settlement called <s>Vajrapura</s>. There dwells a Dramiḍa named <s>Megha</s>. Approach him and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he practice? //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreiṣṭhidārakaḥ supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya supratiṣṭhitaṃ bhikṣumanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣorantikāt prakrāntaḥ // 4 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>, circumambulated the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and departed from the presence of the monk <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>. // 4 //

body.text: 7 Meghaḥ /
body.translated_text: 7. <s>Megha</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreiṣṭhidārakastaṃ dharmālokamanusmaran dharmaprasādavegāviṣṭo buddhānugatasaṃjñāmanasikāraḥ triratnavaṃśānupacchedaprayuktaḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇyanusmaran tryadhvalokāvabhāsitacitto mahāpraṇidhānānugatamanaskāraḥ sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇayogaprasṛtaḥ sarvasaṃskṛtaratyaniśritacitto virāgavaṃśamudīrayan sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyaptiparamaḥ sarvalokadhātupariśuddhipraṇidhyanuccalitaḥ sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalāniśritavihārī anupūrveṇa vajrapuraṃ nāma dramiḍapaṭṭanamupasaṃkramya meghaṃ dramiḍaṃ paryeṣan adrākṣīt madhyenagaraṃ śṛṅgāṭake dharmasāṃkathyāya siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaṃ daśānāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ cakrākṣaraparivartavyūhaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamānam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, recollecting that light of <s>Dharma</s>, filled with the force of devotion to the <s>Dharma</s>, with his mind directed toward the perception of following the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the unbroken continuation of the lineage of the <s>Three Jewels</s>, recollecting spiritual friends, with his mind illuminated by the world of the three times, with his mental attention following great vows, engaged in the exertion of protecting the realm of all beings, with his mind not depending on delight in all that is conditioned, proclaiming the lineage of dispassion, supreme in the penetration of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, unwavering from the vow for the purification of all world-systems, dwelling without depending on the assembly-circles of all <s>Buddhas</s>, gradually approached the Dramiḍa settlement called <s>Vajrapura</s>, and searching for the Dramiḍa <s>Megha</s>, he saw him seated in the middle of the city, at a crossroads, upon a lion-throne, elucidating the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called '<s>Cakrākṣaraparivartavyūha</s>' (Array of the Cycle of Syllables) to ten thousand living beings. //
