body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako meghasya dramiḍasya pādau śirasābhivandya meghaṃ dramiḍamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ saṃyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam? kathaṃ pratipattavyam? kathaṃ bodhisattvasya bodhisattvabodhicittotpādo na praṇaśyati? sarvabhavagatiṣu kathamāśayo dṛḍhībhavatyaparikhedatayā? kathamadhyāśayaḥ pariśuddhyatyanavamardyatayā? kathaṃ mahākaruṇābalaṃ saṃjāyate aparikhedatayā? kathaṃ dhāraṇībalamākrāmati samantamukhaviśuddhatayā? kathaṃ prajñālokaḥ saṃjāyate sarvadharmavitimirālokaḥ sarvājñānatimirapaṭavikiraṇatayā? kathaṃ pratisaṃvidbalamākrāmati arthadharmaniruktipratibhānakauśalasvaramaṇḍalaparipūraye? kathaṃ smṛtibalamākrāmati sarvabuddhadharmacakrāsaṃbhinnasaṃdhāraṇatayā? kathaṃ gatibalaṃ viśudhyati sarvadharmadiggatyālokānugamanugamanatayā? kathaṃ bodhisattvasya samādhibalaṃ niṣpadyate sarvadharmārthaniścayaprabhedaparamatayā?
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the Dramiḍa <s>Megha</s>, circumambulated the Dramiḍa <s>Megha</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'O Noble One, I have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he practice? How does a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s generation of <s>Bodhicitta</s> not perish? In all courses of existence, how does his aspiration become firm through unwearied persistence? How does his higher intention become purified through indomitable resolve? How does the power of great compassion arise through tirelessness? How does the power of <s>dhāraṇī</s> develop through the purification of universal gateways? How does the light of wisdom arise — the light dispelling the darkness of all <s>dharmas</s>, scattering the thick darkness of all ignorance? How does the power of analytical knowledge develop, in the fulfillment of the vocal sphere of skill in meaning, <s>dharma</s>, etymology, and eloquence? How does the power of mindfulness develop, in the unbroken retention of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>? How is the power of course purified, in following the illumination of the directions and courses of all <s>dharmas</s>? How does a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s power of <s>samādhi</s> come to accomplishment, in the supreme penetration of the definite meanings of all <s>dharmas</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu megho dramiḍo bodhisattvagauraveṇa tataḥ siṃhāsanādutthāya avatīrya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ suvarṇapuṣparāśinā abhyavakirat / anarghaiśca maṇiratnairudāracandanacūrṇaiścābhiprākirat / nānācitraraṅgaraktaiśca anekairvastraśatasahasrairabhicchādayāmāsa / anekaiśca nānāvarṇai rucirairmanoramairgandhapuṣpairabhyavakīrya abhiprakīrya anyaiśca vividhaiḥ pūjāprakāraiḥ pūjayitvā satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / yena kulaputra anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam, sa sarvabuddhavaṃśasyānupacchedāya pratipanno bhavati virāgavaṃśasya yathāvadvijñāptaye 'bhiyuktaḥ, sarvakṣetravaṃśasya pariśuddhaye pratipannaḥ, sarvasattvavaṃśasya paripākavinayāya pratyupasthitaḥ, sarvadharmavaṃśasya yathāvannistīraṇāya prayuktaḥ, sarvakarmavaṃśasyāvirodhāya sthitaḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāvaṃśasya paripūraye prayuktaḥ, sarvapraṇidhānavaṃśasyāvyavacchedāya saṃprasthitaḥ, sarvatryadhvavaṃśasya jñānānugamāya pratipannaḥ, adhimuktivaṃśasya dṛḍhīkaraṇāyodyuktaḥ, sādhiṣṭhito bhavati sarvatathāgatamaṇḍalena samanvāhṛtaḥ, sarvabuddhaiḥ
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>, out of reverence for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, rising from that lion-throne and descending, prostrated with his entire body before the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, and showered <s>Sudhana</s> with heaps of golden flowers. He also scattered him with priceless gem-jewels and noble sandalwood powder. He covered him with many hundreds of thousands of garments dyed in various colorful hues. Having scattered and showered him with various kinds of beautiful, delightful, fragrant flowers of many colors, and having honored him with various other modes of worship, having respected, revered, esteemed, and worshipped him, he said this to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family, that you have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening! He who has generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening, O son of good family, has set forth for the uninterrupted continuation of the lineage of all <s>Buddha</s>s; he is devoted to the proper understanding of the lineage of dispassion; he has set forth for the purification of the lineage of all fields; he is present for the ripening and discipline of the lineage of all beings; he is engaged in the proper resolution of the lineage of all <s>dharma</s>s; he stands for the non-obstruction of the lineage of all <s>karma</s>; he is engaged in the fulfillment of the lineage of the conduct of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; he has set forth for the uninterrupted continuation of the lineage of all vows; he has set forth for the pursuit through knowledge of the lineage of all three times; he is striving for the strengthening of the lineage of faith. He is well-empowered, comprehended by the circle of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by all <s>Buddha</s>s

body.text:
samatānugataḥ, sarvabodhisattvairanumoditaḥ, sarvāryairabhinanditaḥ, sarvabrahmendraiḥ pūjitaḥ, sarvadevendrairārakṣitaḥ, sarvayakṣendrairapacitaḥ, sarvarākṣasendraiḥ, pratyudgataḥ, sarvanāgendrairabhiṣṭutaḥ, sarvakinnarendraiḥ saṃvarṇitaḥ, sarvalokendrairanveṣitaḥ, sarvalokadhātutrividhāpāyagatisamucchedāya sarvākṣaṇadurgatipathavinivartanatāyai sarvadāridryapathasamatikramāya devamanuṣyasaṃpatpratilābhāya kalyāṇamitrasaṃdarśanāvipravāsāya udārabuddhadharmaśravāvikārāya bodhicittāśayapariśodhanāya bodhicittahetusaṃbhavasamudayāya bodhisattvamārgāvabhāsapratilābhāya bodhisattvajñānānugamāya bodhisattvabhūmyavasthānāya / tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ bhavati - duṣkarakārakā bodhisattvā
durlabhadarśanaprādurbhāvā āśvāsakā lokasya / mātāpitṛbhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvānām / alaṃkārabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sadevakasya lokasya / pratiśaraṇabhūtā bodhisattvā duḥkhārditānām / layanabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvajagadārakṣāyai / prāṇabhūtā bodhisattvā vividhabhayopadravāṇām / vātamaṇḍalībhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvajagattryapāyaprapātasaṃdhāraṇatayā / dharaṇībhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvakuśalamūlavivardhanatayā / sāgarabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ akṣayapuṇyaratnakośagarbhatayā / ādityabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ jñānālokāvabhāsakaraṇatayā / sumerubhūtā bodhisattvāḥ kuśalamūlābhyudgatatayā / candrabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ bodhimaṇḍajñānacandrodāgamanatayā / śūrabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvamārasainyapramardanatayā / vīrabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ svayaṃbhūdharmanagarānuprāptaye / tejobhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvātmasnehaparyādānatayā / meghabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ vipuladharmameghābhisaṃpravarṣaṇatayā / vṛṣṭibhūtā bodhisattvāḥ śraddhādisattvendriyāṅkuravivardhanatayā / dāśabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ dharmasāgaratīrthapradarśanatayā / setubhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvasaṃsārasamudrasaṃtāraṇatayā / tīrthabhūtā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvābhigamanatayā //
body.translated_text: followed with equality, rejoiced in by all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, congratulated by all Noble Ones, worshipped by all <s>Brahmā</s>s and <s>Indra</s>s, protected by all <s>Devendra</s>s, honored by all <s>Yakṣendra</s>s, welcomed by all <s>Rākṣasendra</s>s, praised by all <s>Nāgendra</s>s, extolled by all <s>Kinnarendra</s>s, sought after by all <s>Lokendra</s>s — for the cutting off of the three lower destinies of evil in all world-systems, for the turning away from all unfortunate paths and inauspicious states, for the transcendence of all paths of poverty, for the attainment of divine and human prosperity, for never being separated from the sight of spiritual friends, for the hearing of the noble <s>Buddha-dharma</s> without distortion, for the purification of the disposition of <s>bodhicitta</s>, for the arising of the causes of <s>bodhicitta</s>, for the attainment of the illumination of the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, for the pursuit of <s>bodhisattva</s> knowledge, for establishment on the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages. This is my thought, O son of good family: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are doers of what is difficult to do, rare in their appearance and manifestation, comforters of the world. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like parents to all beings. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are ornaments of the world including its gods. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are refuges for those afflicted by suffering. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are shelters for the protection of all beings. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are life-breath for those beset by various dangers and calamities. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like a wind-circle, in that they hold beings back from the precipice of the three lower destinies. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like the earth, in that they cause the roots of merit of all beings to grow. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like the ocean, in that they are wombs of the inexhaustible treasure-store of merit-jewels. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like the sun, in that they produce the light of the illumination of knowledge. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like <s>Sumeru</s>, in that they rise above through roots of merit. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like the moon, in that the moon of knowledge rises at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening). <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like heroes, in that they crush the armies of all <s>Māra</s>s. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like warriors, for the attainment of the city of the Self-Born <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like fire, in that they consume the self-attachment of all beings. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like clouds, in that they pour down the vast <s>Dharma</s>-rain-clouds. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like rain, in that they cause the sprouts of the faculties of faith and the other spiritual faculties of beings to grow. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like ferrrymen, in that they show the fords of the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like bridges, in that they ferry all beings across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are like fords, in that all beings approach them. //

body.text: iti hi megho dramiḍaḥ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya purata ebhirvacanapadairbodhisattvān saṃvarṇya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya sādhukāramadāt / tasyemāṃ bodhisattvasaṃharṣaṇīṃ vācamudīrayato mukhadvārāttathārūpo 'rciḥskandho niścacāra, yenārciḥskandhena sāhasro lokadhātuḥ sphuṭo 'bhūt / ye ca sattvāstamavabhāsaṃ saṃjānanti sma, devamaharddhikā vā devā vā, nāgamaharddhikā vā nāgā vā, yakṣamaharddhikā vā yakṣā vā, gandharvamaharddhikā vā gandharvā vā, asuramaharddhikā vā asurā vā, garuḍamaharddhikā vā garuḍā vā, kinnaramaharddhikā vā kinnarā vā, mahoragamaharddhikā vā mahoragā vā, manuṣyamaharddhikā vā manuṣyā vā, amanuṣyamaharddhikā vā amanuṣyā vā, brahmamaharddhikā vā brahmāṇo vā, te tenāvabhāsenāvabhāsitāḥ santo meghasya dramiḍasyāntikamupasaṃkrāmantaḥ eteṣāṃ meghena dramiḍenādhiṣṭhitāśayānāṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭānāṃ hlāditakāyacittānām udāraprāmodyajātānāṃ mahāgauravasthitānāṃ nihatamāradhvajānāṃ māyāśāṭhyāpagatānāṃ viprasannendriyāṇāṃ megho dramiḍastameva cakrākṣaraparivartavyūhaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati pravedayati, praveśayati, nayati, anugamayati, yaṃ śrutvā sarve te 'vinivartanīyā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>, having praised <s>bodhisattvas</s> in front of the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> with these verbal expressions, gave his approval to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>. As he uttered these words encouraging the <s>bodhisattva</s>, from his mouth there issued forth a mass of radiance by which the thousandfold world-system was illuminated. And those beings who perceived that radiance — gods of great supernatural power or [ordinary] gods, <s>Nāga</s>s of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Nāga</s>s, <s>Yakṣas</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans of great supernatural power or [ordinary] humans, non-humans of great supernatural power or [ordinary] non-humans, <s>Brahmā</s>s of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Brahmā</s>s — they, illuminated by that radiance, approached the presence of <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>. To these beings, whose aspirations had been empowered by <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>, who stood with palms joined, whose bodies and minds were gladdened, who had attained noble delight, who stood with great reverence, whose <s>Māra</s>-banners had been cast down, who were free from deceit and guile, whose faculties were clear — <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s> illuminated, communicated, caused to enter, guided, and led them along that very <s>Dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on Dharma) called the <s>Cakrākṣaraparivartavyūha</s> (Array of the Wheel-Syllable Chapter) in detail. Having heard it, all of them became non-retrogressing from supreme perfect awakening.

body.text:
sa punarapi dharmāsane niṣadya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ahaṃ kulaputra sarasvatyā dhāraṇyālokasya lābhī / so 'hamekadvitrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau devānāṃ devamantrān prajānāmi / evaṃ nāgānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmamanuṣyāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmantrān prajānāmi / devānāṃ devamantranānātvam prajānāmi / evaṃ nāgānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmamanuṣyāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmamantranānātvaṃ prajānāmi / devānāṃ devamantraikatvam prajānāmi / evaṃ nāgānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmamanuṣyāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmamantraikatvaṃ prajānāmi / devānāṃ devamantrasaṃbhedaṃ prajānāmi / evaṃ nāgānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmamanuṣyāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmamantrasaṃbhedaṃ prajānāmi / tiryagyonigatānām sattvānāṃ sarvavyavahāramantrasaṃjñāḥ prajānāmi / nārakāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ mantrasaṃjñāḥ prajānāmi / yāmalaukikānāṃ sattvānām mantrasaṃjñāḥ prajānāmi / āryamantrasaṃjñāḥ prajānāmi / anāryamantrasaṃjñāḥ prajānāmi / bodhisattvamantrasattvāśayavāgniruktīḥ prajānāmi / tryadhvaprāptatathāgatasvarāṅgaghoṣasāgarān sarvasattvānāṃ kathārutamantrasaṃprayuktānavatarāmyadhimuñcāmi / cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe yathā ceha trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau sattvānāṃ sarvavyavahāraniruktimantrasaṃjñāsāgaramavatarāmi, tathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi lokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣu apramāṇeṣu asaṃkhyeyeṣu acintyeṣu atulyeṣu asamanteṣu asīmāprāpteṣu anabhilāpyanabhilāpyeṣu,
tathā dakṣiṇāyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarāyāmuttarapūrvāyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ paścimottarāyāmadha ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi lokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvapramāṇeṣu yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyeṣu sattvānāṃ sarvavyavahāraniruktimantrasaṃjñāsāgaramavatarāmi - yaduta devānāṃ devamantrān prajānāmi / yāvadbrahmaṇāṃ brahmamantrān prajānāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra, bodhisattvānāṃ sarasvatīdhāraṇyālokaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryā jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, ye te vividhasaṃjñāgatasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te vividhasarvajagatsaṃjñāmantrasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te vividhajagannāmanirdeśasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te vividhasarvajagadabhilāpyaprajñāptivyavahārasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te sarvapadānusaṃdhisāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te padaparamasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te sarvatryadhvārambaṇaikārambaṇavyavahārasamudrānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te padottaranirdeśasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te dvipadottaranirdeśasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te padaprabhedanirdeśasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te sarvadharmapadaprabhedavinayanirdeśasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te sarvajaganmantrasāgarānupraviṣṭāḥ / ye te sarvasvaramaṇḍalaviśuddhivyūhāvakrāntāḥ / ye te cakrākṣarakoṭīgatiprabhedaniryātāḥ //
body.translated_text: Sitting again on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat, he said this to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: 'I, O son of good family, am one who has attained the illumination of the <s>Sarasvatī dhāraṇī</s> (the dhāraṇī of [the goddess] Sarasvatī). I, in a single billion-fold great-thousandfold world-system, know the <s>mantra</s>s of the gods. Likewise I know the <s>mantra</s>s of <s>Nāga</s>s, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, non-humans, and the <s>Brahmā</s>-<s>mantra</s>s of <s>Brahmā</s>s. I know the diversity of divine <s>mantra</s>s of the gods. Likewise I know the diversity of the <s>Brahmā</s>-<s>mantra</s>s of the <s>Brahmā</s>s [and those of all intermediate classes]. I know the unity of the divine <s>mantra</s>s of the gods. Likewise I know the unity of the <s>Brahmā</s>-<s>mantra</s>s [and all others]. I know the analysis of the divine <s>mantra</s>s of the gods. Likewise I know the analysis of all [other] <s>mantra</s>s. I know the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of beings born in animal realms. I know the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of hell-beings. I know the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of beings in <s>Yama</s>'s world. I know the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of the Noble. I know the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of the ignoble. I know the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mantra</s>-expressions of beings' dispositions and speech. I enter and have faith in the oceans of voice-sounds and speech of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, connected with the conversational <s>mantra</s>-utterances of all beings. At every mind-moment, just as I enter the ocean of the <s>mantra</s>-conventions of all expressions and conventions of beings in this billion-fold great-thousandfold world-system, so too in the eastern direction, in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems, immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, boundless, limitless, inexpressibly inexpressible, and likewise in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, nadir, and zenith directions, in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems, immeasurable up to inexpressibly inexpressible, I enter the ocean of <s>mantra</s>-conventions of all expressions and conventions of beings — namely, I know the divine <s>mantra</s>s of the gods, up to I know the <s>Brahmā</s>-<s>mantra</s>s of the <s>Brahmā</s>s. This, O son of good family, is the illumination of the <s>Sarasvatī dhāraṇī</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> that I know. How could I know the conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s> or speak of their qualities — those who have entered the oceans of various perception-conventions, who have entered the oceans of <s>mantra</s>-conventions of all beings of various kinds, who have entered the oceans of the designation of names of various beings, who have entered the oceans of all expressible designations and conventions of various beings, who have entered the oceans of the connection of all words, who have entered the oceans of the ultimate meaning of words, who have entered the oceans of the convention of a single object among all objects of the three times, who have entered the oceans of the explanation of the meaning beyond words, who have entered the oceans of the explanation of the meaning beyond two words, who have entered the oceans of the analysis of words, who have entered the oceans of the explanation of the discipline through the analysis of the words of all <s>dharma</s>s, who have entered the oceans of <s>mantra</s>s of all beings, who have entered the purification-array of all sound-circles, who have emerged through the analysis of the courses of millions of wheel-syllables? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe vanavāsī nāma janapadaḥ / tatra muktako nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāmabhiyoktavyam, katham niryātavyam, kathaṃ cittaṃ nidhyātavyam /
body.translated_text: Go, O son of good family. Right here in the southern region is a country called <s>Vanavāsī</s>. There dwells a merchant named <s>Muktaka</s>. Approach him and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> apply himself in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he emerge? How should his mind be directed?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako meghasya dramiḍasya pādau śirasābhivandya dharmagauraveṇa kṛtvā mūlaṃ jātaśraddhālakṣaṇaṃ prarūpayamāṇaḥ kalyāṇamitrānugatāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan aśrumukho rudan meghaṃ dramiḍamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya praṇipatya meghasya dramiḍasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 5 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, bowing his head at the feet of <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>, showing the sign of faith born from the root of reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, seeing omniscience as following spiritual friends, with tears streaming from his face, weeping, circumambulated <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon him again and again, prostrating, and departed from the presence of <s>Megha</s> the <s>Dramiḍa</s>. // 5 //

body.text: 8 Muktakaḥ /
body.translated_text: 8. <s>Muktaka</s> /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastameva bodhisattvasarasvatīdhāraṇyālokavyūhamanuvicintayan, tameva bodhisattvamantranayasāgaramavataran, tameva bodhisattvacittavyavadānaviśuddhimanusmaran, tameva bodhisattvakuśalavāsanopasaṃhārābhinirhāramabhinirharan, tadeva bodhisattvaparipākamukhaṃ viśodhanayan, tadeva bodhisattvānāṃ sattvasaṃgrahajñānamuttāpayan, tāmeva bodhisattvāśayabalaviśuddhiṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ tadeva bodhisattvādhyāśayabalamupastambhayan, tameva bodhisattvādhimuktivaṃśaṃ pariśodhayan, tāmeva bodhisattvāśayacittakalyāṇatāṃ saṃbhāvayan, tameva bodhisattvavyavasāyamuttārayan, sudhanaḥ śreiṣṭhidārako dṛḍhapratijñāpraṇidhicittāparikhinnasaṃtānavyūho 'nivartyavikrāntavīryaḥ pratyudāvartyamanovyavasāyaḥ asaṃhāryaśraddhābalopetaḥ vajranārāyaṇābhedyacittaḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīpradakṣiṇagrāhī anupahataprajñāviṣayaḥ samantamukhaviśuddhayabhimukhaḥ apratihatajñānaviśuddhigocaraḥ samantanetrajñānanayālokaḥ samantabhūmidhāraṇyavabhāsapratilabdhaḥ dharmadhātutalabhedābhimukhacittaḥ samantatalāpratiṣṭhānavyūhaviśuddhisvabhāvavijñaptaḥ aniketāsamādvayagocaraparamaḥ sarvasaṃjñāvikramaṇajñānamukhaviśuddhaḥ sarvadikkulabhedadikpratyūhavyūhaḥ lokataladigbhedānivartyaḥ dharmataladigbhedāpratyudāvartyaḥ buddhadikkulabhedadarśanavijñaptiparamaḥ adhadikkulabhedānugatajñānī ruciradharmacakrasaṃbhṛtabuddhiḥ samantarucirajñānasamādhyākāralokāvabhāsitacittaḥ samantaviṣayabhūmyanugatamanaḥśarīraḥ tathāgatajñānavidyudavabhāsitasaṃtānaḥ sarvajñatormiprasādāvegasaṃjātaḥ buddhadharmaprasādavegāvirahitaḥ tathāgatādhiṣṭhānāvegāviṣṭaḥ sarvabuddhasvacittānugamālokāvabhāsitaḥ sarvalokadhātujālasvaśarīraspharaṇapraṇidhisamanvāgataḥ sarvadharmadhātusvakāyasamavasaraṇābhinirhāraparamo 'nupūrveṇa dvādaśabhirvarṣaistaṃ vanavāsijanapadamanuprāptaḥ / sa taṃ muktakaṃ śreṣṭhinaṃ parimārgamāṇo 'drākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ārya, labdhā me lābhāḥ, yasya meghakalyāṇamitrasamavadhānam / tatkasya hetoḥ? durlabhadarśanāni hi kalyāṇamitrāṇi
durlabhaprādurbhāvāni duḥpratyāgatāni durupasaṃkramaṇāni duḥparyupāsyāni / durāsadāni duḥsaṃvāsāni durabhisādhyāni duranubandhyāni kalyānamitrāṇi / tacca meghakalyāṇamitrasamavadhānaṃ jātam / mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / yaduta sarvabuddhārāgaṇatāyai sarvabuddhābhirādhanatāyai sarvabuddhadarśanatāyai sarvabuddhavijñaptaye sarvabuddhasamatānugamāya sarvabuddhapraṇidhyanugamāya sarvabuddhapraṇidhiparipūraye sarvabuddhasamudāgamajñānālokanatāyai sarvabuddhasvaśarīrābhinirharaṇatāyai sarvabuddhasamudāgamasvacaryābhinirharaṇatāyai sarvabuddhavikurvitapratyakṣābhijñatāyai sarvabuddhabalavaiśāradyapariśuddhaye sarvadharmadeśanāśravaṇāvitṛptatāyai sarvabuddhadharmadeśanāśravaṇodgrahaṇatāyai sarvabuddhadharmadeśanāsaṃdhāraṇatāyai sarvabuddhadharmadeśanāvibhajanatāyai sarvabuddhaśāsanasaṃdhāraṇatāyai sarvabuddhasattvaikatvatāyai sarvabodhisattvasabhāgatāyai sarvabodhisattvacaryāpariśuddhye sarvabodhisattvapāramitāparipūraye
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, reflecting on that very array of the illumination of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Sarasvatī</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>, entering that very ocean of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s mantra-method, recollecting that very purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s mental cultivation, producing that very production of the collection of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome impressions, purifying that very gate of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s ripening, generating that very knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s gathering of beings, strengthening that very purification of the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s disposition, supporting that very power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s superior disposition, purifying that very lineage of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s devotion, cultivating that very excellence of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s disposition and mind, raising that very resolve of the <s>bodhisattva</s> — <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, whose continuum-array was unwearied in the aspiration-mind of firm resolve, of irreversible advancing vigor, of mind-resolve that does not turn back, endowed with unshakable power of faith, whose mind was indestructible like diamond and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who received favorably the admonitions of all spiritual friends, whose domain of wisdom was unimpaired, who faced the purification of the universal gate, whose range was the unobstructed purification of knowledge, whose light was the method of the knowledge of the universal eye, who had attained the illumination of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the universal ground, whose mind faced the differentiation of the surface of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, who was cognized by the nature of the purification of the array of the non-established universal surface, whose supreme range was the non-dual without a dwelling, who was purified in the gate of knowledge of transcending all perceptions, whose array was the differentiation of the directions in all directions, who was irreversible in the differentiation of the directions of the world's surface, who did not turn back from the differentiation of the directions of the <s>dharma</s>'s surface, who was supreme in the cognition of seeing the differentiation of the directions of the <s>Buddha</s>, who followed the knowledge of the differentiation of the lower directions, whose intellect was nourished by the beautiful <s>Dharmacakra</s>, whose mind was illuminated by the light of the form of the beautiful universal knowledge-<s>samādhi</s>, whose mind-body followed the universal domain-ground, whose continuum was illuminated by the lightning of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, born of the surge of faith in the wave of omniscience, never without the surge of faith in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>, entered by the surge of <s>Tathāgata</s>-empowerment, illuminated by the light of following all <s>Buddha</s>s' own minds, endowed with the vow of pervading all world-realm-nets with his own body, supreme in the production of converging all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s in his own body — proceeded gradually and after twelve years arrived at the region of <s>Vanavāsī</s>. Searching for the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, he saw him. Having seen him, prostrating with his whole body, standing before him with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'Noble One, I have gained gains — for whom there has been an encounter with an excellent spiritual friend. What is the reason? For spiritual friends are difficult to see, difficult to appear, difficult to approach, difficult to visit, difficult to attend, difficult to reach, difficult to dwell with, difficult to accomplish, difficult to follow. And that encounter with an excellent spiritual friend has occurred. I, Noble One, have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening — that is, for the worship of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for the propitiation of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for the seeing of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for the cognition of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for following the equality of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for following the vows of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for the fulfillment of the vows of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for seeing the illumination of the knowledge of the arising of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for producing one's own body as all <s>Buddha</s>s, for producing one's own conduct of the arising of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for directly knowing the transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for the purification of the powers and fearlessnesses of all <s>Buddha</s>s, for insatiability in hearing the teaching of all <s>dharma</s>s, for receiving the teaching of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, for retaining the teaching of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, for analyzing the teaching of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, for maintaining all <s>Buddha</s>-teachings, for oneness with all <s>Buddha</s>-beings, for community with all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for the purification of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, for the fulfillment of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>pāramitā</s>s

body.text:
sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhyabhinirhāraviśuddhaye sarvabodhisattvabuddhādhiṣṭhānakośapratilābhitāyai sarvabodhisattvadharmanidhānakośākṣayajñānālokatāyai sarvabodhisattvanidhānakośānugamāya sarvabodhisattvāpramāṇakośābhinirharaṇatāyai sarvabodhisattvamahākaruṇānidhānakośasattvavinayaniṣṭhāparyantagamanatāyai sarvabodhisattvavikurvitanidhānakośavijñaptaye sarvabodhisattvavaśitānidhānakośasvacittavaśavartanatāyai sarvabodhisattvaviśuddhinidhānakośasarvākāravyūhatāyai / evaṃcitto 'hamārya ihopasaṃkrāntaḥ, evamabhiprāyaḥ evaṃmanorathaḥ evamabhinandyaḥ evamāśayaḥ evaṃnidhyaptiparamaḥ evaṃgocarābhimukhaḥ evanayānugamābhimukhaḥ evaṃviśuddhiparamaḥ evaṃvyūhābhiprāyaḥ evaṃpraṇatacittaḥ evaṃkalyāṇaprayogaḥ evamabhimukhendriyaḥ / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti, nayamupadiśati, anugamanamavabhāsayati, mārgamupadiśati, tīrthamavatārayati, dharmadvāraṃ vivṛṇoti, saṃśayān chinatti, kāṅkṣāṃ vinodayati, kathaṃkathāśalyamuddharati, vicikitsāmalamapakarṣayati,
cittagahanamavabhāsayati, cittamalamapaharati, cittasaṃtatiṃ prasādayati, cittakauṭilyamapanayati, cittatāpaṃ prahlādayati, vyāvartayati, saṃsāracittaṃ vinivartayati, akuśalebhyo vivartayati, narakebhyo vivecayati, niketanebhya uccālayati, anabhiniveśāt parimocayati, sarvasaṅgebhya āvarjayati, sarvajñatāyāmabhimukhīkaroti, dharmanagarānupraveśāya āvartayati, mahākaruṇāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati, mahāmaitryāṃ niyojayati, bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ praveśayati, samādhimukhabhavanatāyāṃ niveśayati, anugamamukheṣu sthāpayati, svabhāvanidhyaptau spharati, balānugamena vibhajati sarvajagatsamatānugamāya cittam / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam? kathamabhiyoktavyam? kathaṃ prayoktavyam? kathaṃ prayuktasya kṣipraṃ viśudhyati bodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalam?
body.translated_text: for the purification of the production of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows, for the attainment of the treasury of <s>Buddha</s>-empowerment of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for the inexhaustible knowledge-light of the treasury of the <s>dharma</s>-treasure of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for following the treasure-treasury of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for producing the immeasurable treasury of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for reaching the end of the discipline of beings through the treasury of the great compassion-store of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for the cognition of the transformation-treasure of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for the mastery of one's own mind through the mastery-treasure of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, for the array of all aspects through the purity-treasure of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. With such a mind, Noble One, I have come here, with such an intention, such a heart's desire, such delight, such a disposition, supreme in reflection, facing such a range, facing the following of such a method, supreme in such purification, with such an intent for arrays, with such a bowed mind, with such wholesome application, with such faculties directed forward. And I have heard that the Noble One gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattva</s>s, points out the method, illuminates the following, indicates the path, leads one down to the ford, opens the gate of <s>dharma</s>, cuts away doubts, dispels uncertainty, extracts the thorn of perplexity, removes the stain of wavering, illuminates the jungle of the mind, removes the stain of the mind, clarifies the continuum of the mind, removes the crookedness of the mind, refreshes the heat of the mind, turns one away, turns back the mind of <s>saṃsāra</s>, diverts from the unwholesome, separates from the hells, uproots from dwellings, liberates from attachment, turns one from all bonds, directs one toward omniscience, turns one for entering the city of <s>dharma</s>, establishes one in great compassion, engages one in great loving-kindness, leads one into <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, places one in the palace of <s>samādhi</s>-gates, establishes one in the gates of following, pervades one in the reflection on own-nature, analyzes by the following of powers, [and directs] the mind toward following the equality of all beings. Let the Noble One tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one apply oneself? How should one exert oneself? How does the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct-maṇḍala quickly become purified for one who exerts oneself?

body.text: atha khalu muktakaḥ śreṣṭhī tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrasamavasaraṇaṃ nāma anantāvartadhāraṇīmukhapūrvaṃgamaṃ bodhisattvasamādhimukhaṃ samāpadyata pūrvakuśalamūlabalādhānena tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena, mañjuśriyaśca kumārabhūtasya samanvāhareṇa jñānālokopasaṃhāreṇa ca / samanantarasamāpannasya ca muktakasya śreṣṭhinastathārūpā kāyapariśuddhiḥ saṃsthitā yayā kāyapariśuddhayā daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ saha buddhakṣetrapariśuddhayā saparṣanmaṇḍalāḥ saha prabhāviśuddhayā sapūrvacaryāsaṃvāsāḥ sabuddhavikurvitāḥ sapraṇidhānasaṃbhārāḥ sahacaryāniryāṇavyūhaviśuddhayā sābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanāḥ sahadharmacakroddayotanāḥ sasattvaparipākāḥ sadharmaniṣṭhāparyantāḥ sarvakāye 'ntargatāḥ anupraviṣṭāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / anyonyāsaṃbhinnā anyonyānāvaraṇā anyonyasuvibhaktā anyonyasuvyavasthitanānākalpasaṃsthānā yathāvadvijñaptā nānābuddhakṣetravyūhāḥ nānābodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalālaṃkārā nānābuddhavikurvitaṃ saṃdarśayantaḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / nānāyānanayavyavasthānā nānāpraṇidhānamukhaparidīpanāḥ kvacillokadhātau tuṣitabhavanopapannāḥ saṃdṛśyante / sarvabuddhakāryaṃ kurvantaḥ kvacittuṣitabhavanāccyavamānāḥ, kvacinmātuḥ kukṣigatāḥ vividhavikurvitāni
body.translated_text: Then the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, at that moment, entered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-gate called 'Convergence of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields,' preceded by the gate of the infinite-vortex-<s>dhāraṇī</s>, by the power of previous roots of merit, by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and by the blessing of the prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s> and the collection of the light of knowledge. And as soon as the merchant <s>Muktaka</s> had entered [that <s>samādhi</s>], such a purification of body was established that by that purification of body, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavān</s>s in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields — together with their <s>Buddha</s>-field purifications, with their assembly-maṇḍalas, with their purification of radiance, with their former conduct and dwelling, with their <s>Buddha</s>-transformations, with their accumulations of vows, with the purification of the array of the emergence of their conduct, with their displays of perfect awakening, with the dawning of their <s>Dharmacakra</s>s, with their ripening of beings, with the final end of their <s>dharma</s> — all appeared within his body, having entered in. Unmixed with one another, unobstructing one another, well-distinguished from one another, well-established in various <s>kalpa</s>-configurations — various <s>Buddha</s>-field arrays, various ornaments of <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly-maṇḍalas, displaying various <s>Buddha</s>-transformations were seen. Of various vehicle-method establishments, illuminating various gates of vows — in some world-realms they appeared as born in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, performing all <s>Buddha</s>-work; in some, descending from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven; in some, entering the mother's womb, displaying various transformations

body.text:
saṃdarśayantaḥ, kvacijjāyamānāḥ bālakrīḍāmupadarśayantaḥ, kvacidantaḥpuramadhyagatāḥ, kvacidabhiniṣkrāmantaḥ kvacidbodhimaṇḍavaragatāḥ mahāvyūhavikurvitamārasainyaparājayaṃ kurvantaḥ saṃdṛśyante / kvaciddevanāgayakṣagandharvaparivṛtā brahmendrairdharmacakrapravartanāyādhyeṣyamāṇāḥ, kvaciddharmacakraṃ pravartayantaḥ kvacitsarvasattvabhavanagatāḥ kvacitparinirvāyamāṇāḥ saṃdṛśyante / kvacillokadhātau tathāgatānāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ dhātuvibhaṅgāḥ saṃdṛśyante / kvacidbuddhakṣetradevamanuṣyāstathāgatacaityānyalaṃkurvantaḥ saṃdṛśyante / yacca te buddhā bhagavanto bhāṣante nānāsattvanikāyeṣu nānāsattvalokeṣu nānāsattvagatiṣu nānāsattvopapattiṣu nānāsattvasaṃnipāteṣu nānāsattvakuśalamūlaparivarteṣu nānāsattvagatiparivarteṣu nānāsattvāśayaparivarteṣu nānāsattvādhimuktiparivarteṣu nānāsattvendriyaparivarteṣu nānākālaparivarteṣu nānāsattvakarmasaṃbhedeṣu nānāsattvakarmavimātratāsu nānāsattvalokavibhāvanāsu nānāgaticaryāvicariteṣu sattvanayeṣu nānāśayaprayogeṣu sattvasamudreṣu nānendriyavimātratāviśuddheṣu nānākleśavāsanānuśayiteṣu sattvaprasareṣu vividhabuddhivikurvitasaṃdarśanairnānāniruktibhirnānāsvarāṅgarutanirhārairnānāsūtrāntanayodāhārairnānādhāraṇīmukhaparivartairnānāpratisaṃvinnayaprabhavairnānāsatyanāmasamudraparivartaiḥ
nānābuddharṣabhasiṃhanādanaiḥ nānāsattvakuśalamūladeśanāprātihāryasaṃdarśanaiḥ nānāmukhasmṛtinidarśanavikurvitaiḥ nānābodhisattvavyākaraṇasiṃhanādaiḥ nānātathāgatadharmacakravijṛmbhitaiḥ anantamadhyeṣu parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu anantasaṃbhedeṣvanyonyārambaṇeṣu nānāviśuddhaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu vipuleṣu sūkṣmaparṣanmaṇḍalasamavasaraṇeṣu yojanapramāṇeṣu daśayojanapramāṇeṣu yāvadanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātupramāṇeṣu parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu yatte buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ bhāṣante sarvasvarāṅgarutaghoṣānugāminyā tathāgatavācā, taṃ sarvaṃ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ śṛṇoti udgṛhṇāti saṃdhārayati pravartayati upanidhyāyati / tacca vikurvitaṃ paśyati, tāṃ ca acintyāṃ bodhisattvasamādhivṛṣabhitām //
body.translated_text: displaying [various wonders]; in some, being born and showing childhood play; in some, dwelling in the inner palace; in some, going forth [from home]; in some, gone to the excellent <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, performing the defeat of <s>Māra</s>'s armies through the great array-transformation; in some, surrounded by <s>deva</s>s, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, and <s>gandharva</s>s, being requested by <s>Brahma</s> and <s>Indra</s> to turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s>; in some, turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s>; in some, having gone to the abodes of all beings; in some, entering <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. In some world-realms, the distribution of relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s who have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> was seen. In some, the <s>deva</s>s and humans of <s>Buddha</s>-fields were seen adorning <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s>s (reliquary shrines). And whatever those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavān</s>s spoke among the various classes of beings, in the various worlds of beings, in the various destinies of beings, in the various births of beings, in the various assemblies of beings, in the various transformations of wholesome roots of beings, in the various transformations of the destinies of beings, in the various transformations of the dispositions of beings, in the various transformations of the devotions of beings, in the various transformations of the faculties of beings, in the various transformations of times, in the various differentiations of the <s>karma</s>s of beings, in the various measurements of the <s>karma</s>s of beings, in the various manifestations of the world of beings, in the various courses of conduct in the destinies of beings, in the ocean of beings of various applications of dispositions, in the various purifications of the measurements of the faculties of beings, in the various afflictions and latent tendencies of the extension of beings — with various displays of <s>Buddha</s>-wisdom-transformations, with various etymologies, with various productions of sounds, limbs, and cries, with various citations of <s>sūtrānta</s>-methods, with various turns of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gate methods, with various arising of analytical knowledge-methods, with various turns of the ocean of truth-names, with various lion's roars of the <s>Buddha</s>-lord, with various miraculous displays of teaching the roots of merit of beings, with various transformations of displaying recollection in various ways, with various lion's roars of the prediction of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with various expansions of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmacakra</s> — in infinite assembly-maṇḍalas, in infinite differentiations of mutual objects, in various purified assembly-maṇḍalas, vast, in subtle convergences of assembly-maṇḍalas, of one <s>yojana</s> extent, of ten <s>yojana</s>s, up to assembly-maṇḍalas of the extent of world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields — whatever those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavān</s>s spoke of <s>dharma</s> with the <s>Tathāgata</s>-voice that follows all sounds, limbs, cries, and utterances — all that <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, heard, received, retained, transmitted, and reflected upon. And he saw that transformation, and that inconceivable magnificence of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu muktakaḥ śreṣṭhī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānaṃstasmātsamādhervyūtthāya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgavyūhaṃ nāma tathāgatavimokṣamāyūhāmi niryūhāmi / tasya me kulaputra asaṅgavyūhaṃ tathāgatavimokṣamāyūhato niryūhataḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi jāmbūnadaprabhāsavatyāṃ lokadhātau tāreśvararājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ vairocanagarbhabodhisattvapramukhena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi sarvabalavegavatyāṃ lokadhātau samantagandhavitāno nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ cintārājabodhisattvapramukhena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, mindful and fully aware, rising from that <s>samādhi</s>, spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Son of good family, I cultivate and practice the <s>Tathāgata</s>-liberation called <s>Asaṅgavyūha</s> (Unattached Array). Son of good family, as I cultivate and practice this <s>Asaṅgavyūha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>-liberation, in the eastern direction, in the world-system called <s>Jāmbūnadaprabhāsavatī</s> (Radiance of Gold), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Tāreśvararāja</s> (Star-Lord King), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Vairocanagarbha Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the southern direction, in the world-system called <s>Sarvabalavegavatī</s> (Possessing All Power and Speed), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Samantagandhavitāna</s> (Canopy of Universal Fragrance), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Cintārāja Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision.

body.text:
ābhāsamāgacchati / paścimāyāṃ diśi sarvagandhaprabhāsavatyāṃ lokadhātau merupradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhamasaṅgacittabodhisattvapramukhena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / uttarāyāṃ diśi kāṣāyadhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau vajrapramardano nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ vajrapadavikrāmibodhisattvapramukhena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣaābhāsamāgacchati / uttarapūrvāyāṃ diśi sarvaratnarucirāyāṃ lokadhātau anilambhacakṣurvairocano nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhamanilambhasunirmitabodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi gandhārciḥprabhāsvarāyāṃ lokadhātau gandhapradīpo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ sarvadharmadhātutalabhedaketurājabodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi sūryakesaranirbhāsāyāṃ lokadhātau samantamukhajñānavirocanaghoṣo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ samantakusumārciḥpralambacūḍabodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / paścimottarāyāṃ diśi gandhālaṃkāraruciraśubhagarbhāyāṃ lokadhātāvapramāṇaguṇasāgaraprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhamasaṅgakāyaraśmitejomatibodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / aghodiśi ratnasiṃhāvabhāsajvalanāyāṃ lokadhātau dharmadhātuvidyotitaraśmirnām tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhaṃ dharmadhātvarcirvairocanasaṃbhavamatibodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati / ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi lakṣaṇaruciravairocanāyāṃ lokadhātāvapratihataguṇakīrtivimokṣaprabharājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārdhamasaṅgabalavīryamatibodhisattvapūrvaṃgamena sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalena
cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati //
body.translated_text: In the western direction, in the world-system called <s>Sarvagandhaprabhāsavatī</s> (Radiance of All Fragrance), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Merupradīparāja</s> (Lamp-King of <s>Meru</s>), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Asaṅgacitta Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the northern direction, in the world-system called <s>Kāṣāyadhvajā</s> (Ocher Banner), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Vajrapramardana</s> (Diamond Crusher), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Vajrapadavikrāmi Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the northeastern direction, in the world-system called <s>Sarvaratnarucirā</s> (Splendid with All Gems), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Anilambhacakṣurvairocana</s> (Ungraspable-Eye <s>Vairocana</s>), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Anilambhasunirmita Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the southeastern direction, in the world-system called <s>Gandhārciḥprabhāsvarā</s> (Brilliant with Fragrance-Flames), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Gandhapradīpa</s> (Fragrance-Lamp), together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly-circle led by <s>Sarvadharmadhātutalabhedaketurāja Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the southwestern direction, in the world-system called <s>Sūryakesaranirbhāsā</s> (Blazing with Sun-Filaments), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Samantamukhajñānavirocanaghoṣa</s> (Sound of Universal-Face Knowledge-Illumination), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Samantakusumārciḥpralambacūḍa Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the northwestern direction, in the world-system called <s>Gandhālaṃkāraruciraśubhagarbhā</s> (Womb of Beauty Adorned with Fragrance), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Apramāṇaguṇasāgaraprabha</s> (Radiance of the Ocean of Immeasurable Qualities), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Asaṅgakāyaraśmitejomati Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the nadir direction, in the world-system called <s>Ratnasiṃhāvabhāsajvalanā</s> (Blazing with Gem-Lion Illumination), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Dharmadhātuvidyotitaraśmi</s> (Ray Illuminated by the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Dharmadhātvarcirvairocanasaṃbhavamati Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. In the zenith direction, in the world-system called <s>Lakṣaṇaruciravairocanā</s> (Beautiful-Marked <s>Vairocana</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Apratihataguṇakīrtivimokṣaprabharāja</s> (King of the Radiance of Liberation whose Fame of Qualities is Unobstructed), together with the assembly-circle of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s led by <s>Asaṅgabalavīryamati Bodhisattva</s>, comes into the range of my vision. //

body.text: iti hi kulaputra, etān daśa tathāgatān pramukhān kṛtvā daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān paśyāmi / na ca te tathāgatā ihāgacchanti, na cāhaṃ tatra gacchāmi / yasyāṃ ca velāyāmicchāmi, tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvamitābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / candanavatyāṃ lokadhātau vajrābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / gandhavatyāṃ lokadhātau ratnābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / padmavatyāṃ lokadhātau ratnapadmābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / kanakavatyāṃ lokadhātau śāntābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / abhiratyāṃ lokadhātau akṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / supratiṣṭhāyāṃ lokadhātau siṃhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / ādarśamaṇḍalanibhāsāyāṃ lokadhātau candrabuddhiṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / ratnaśrīhaṃsacitrāyāṃ lokadhātau vairocanaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / iti hi kulaputra yasyāṃ yasyāṃ diśi yasyāṃ yasyāṃ lokadhātau yaṃ yameva tathāgataṃ draṣṭumākāṅkṣāmi, taṃ tameva tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / yasmin yasminnadhvani yasmin yasminnārambaṇe yasyāṃ yasyāṃ pūrvacayāyāṃ tathāgataṃ draṣṭumākāṅkṣāmi, yasmin yasmin vikurvitakāraṇe yasmin yasmin sattvavinayakāraṇe yaṃ yaṃ tathāgataṃ draṣṭumākāṅkṣāmi, taṃ tameva tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / na ca te tathāgatā ihāgacchanti, na cāhaṃ tatra gacchāmi / so 'haṃ kulaputra na kutaścidāgamanatāṃ tathāgatānāṃ prajānan, na kvacidgamanatāṃ svakāyasya prajānan, svapnopamavijñaptiṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prajānan, svapnasamavicāravijñaptiṃ svacittasya prajānan, pratibhāsasamavijñaptiṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prajānan, acchodakabhājanavijñaptiṃ ca svacittasya prajānan, māyākṛtarūpavijñaptiṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prajānan, māyopamavijñaptiṃ ca svacittasya prajānan, pratiśrutkāgirighoṣānuravaṇatāṃ ca tathāgataghoṣasya prajānan, pratiśrutkāsamavijñaptiṃ ca svacittasya prajānan, evamanugacchāmi
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, son of good family, taking these ten <s>Tathāgata</s>s as foremost, I see in the ten directions <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>s equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And those <s>Tathāgata</s>s do not come here, nor do I go there. And whenever I wish, at that very moment I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> in the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajrābha</s> in the world-system <s>Candanavatī</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnābha</s> in the world-system <s>Gandhavatī</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnapadmābha</s> in the world-system <s>Padmavatī</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śāntābha</s> in the world-system <s>Kanakavatī</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> in the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃha</s> in the world-system <s>Supratiṣṭhā</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrabuddhi</s> in the world-system <s>Ādarśamaṇḍalanibhāsā</s>. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s> in the world-system <s>Ratnaśrīhaṃsacitrā</s>. Thus indeed, son of good family, in whichever direction, in whichever world-system, whichever <s>Tathāgata</s> I wish to see, that very <s>Tathāgata</s> I see. In whichever time-period, in whichever object-domain, in whichever former conduct, in whichever transformative occasion, in whichever occasion of disciplining beings, whichever <s>Tathāgata</s> I wish to see, that very <s>Tathāgata</s> I see. And those <s>Tathāgata</s>s do not come here, nor do I go there. And I, son of good family, knowing the non-coming-from-anywhere of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and knowing the non-going-anywhere of my own body, and knowing the cognition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s as dream-like, and knowing the cognition of my own mind as dream-like reflection, and knowing the cognition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s as reflection-like, and knowing my own mind's cognition as [like] a clear water-vessel, and knowing the form-cognition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s as magically-created, and knowing my own mind's cognition as illusion-like, and knowing the <s>Tathāgata</s>s' voice as resounding like an echo from a mountain, and knowing my own mind's cognition as echo-like — thus I follow,

body.text:
evamanusmarāmi svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhadharma iti / svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvacaryā, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayaḥ, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānābhinirhāraḥ, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ
sarvajñatānagarānuprāptiḥ, svacittādhiṣṭhānamacintyabodhisattvavimokṣavikrīḍanatā, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhabodhyabhisaṃbodhaḥ, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ samantadharmadhātusamavasaraṇavṛṣabhitāvikurvitam, svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvakalpasūkṣmasamavasaraṇajñānamiti //
body.translated_text: thus I recollect: 'The empowerment of one's own mind — that is all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s for <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the ripening and disciplining of all beings. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the accomplishment of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vow outpourings. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the attainment of the city of omniscience. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the inconceivable sport of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the awakening to <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the transformative majesty of universal convergence in the entire <s>Dharmadhātu</s>. The empowerment of one's own mind — that is the knowledge of the subtle convergence of all <s>kalpa</s>s.' //

body.text: tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ bhavati - svacittamevopastambhayitavyaṃ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ / svacittameva pariṣyandayitavyaṃ dharmameghaiḥ / svacittameva pariśodhayitavyamārambaṇīyadharmebhyaḥ / svacitameva dṛḍhīkartavyaṃ vīryeṇa / svacittameva śamīkartavyaṃ kṣāntyā / svacitameva praṇayitavyaṃ jñānānugameṣu / svacittamevottāpayitavyaṃ prajñayā / svacittamevābhinirhartavyaṃ vaśitāśu / svacittamevavipulīkartavyaṃ buddhasamatāyām / svacittamevāvabhāsayitavyāṃ daśatathāgatabalaiḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgavyūhatathāgatavimokṣaṃ jānāmi āyūhāmi niryūhāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmasaṅgacittānāmasaṅgavihāragocarāṇāṃ pratyutpannasarvabuddhadharmasaṃmukhāvasthitasamādhipratilabdhānāmaparionirvāṇakoṭigatasaṃbodhimukhasamādhipratilabdhānāṃ tryadhvasamatānuprāptānāṃ samantatalasaṃbhedasamādhigocaravidhijñānāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrasuvibhaktaśarīrāṇāmasaṃbhinnabuddhaviṣayavihāriṇāṃ sarvadigabhimukhagocarāṇāmaparāṅbhukhajñānamaṇḍalavyavalokanānāṃ caryā jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, yeṣāmātmabhāvasarvalokadhātusaṃvartavivartāḥ prajñāyante / na caiṣāmātmani lokadhātuṣu vā dvayasaṃjñā pravartate //
body.translated_text: And, son of good family, this thought occurs to me: 'One's own mind alone must be supported by all roots of merit. One's own mind alone must be permeated by <s>Dharma</s>-clouds. One's own mind alone must be purified of objects [that cause attachment]. One's own mind alone must be made firm by heroic energy. One's own mind alone must be pacified by patience. One's own mind alone must be led into the paths of knowledge. One's own mind alone must be heated by wisdom. One's own mind alone must be brought to accomplishment in mastery. One's own mind alone must be made vast in the equality of the <s>Buddha</s>. One's own mind alone must be illuminated by the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' This, son of good family, is the <s>Asaṅgavyūha</s> (Unattached Array) <s>Tathāgata</s>-liberation that I know, cultivate, and practice. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the qualities, of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s of unattached mind, whose range is the abode of non-attachment, who have attained the <s>samādhi</s> of standing face to face with all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s of the present, who have attained the <s>samādhi</s> of the gateway of awakening reaching the limit of non-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, who have attained the equality of the three times, whose knowledge of the method of the <s>samādhi</s> whose range is the breaking of the universal surface, whose bodies are well-distributed in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who abide in the undifferentiated <s>Buddha</s>-domain, whose range faces all directions, who behold the unfailing knowledge-<s>maṇḍala</s> — [<s>Bodhisattva</s>s] in whose own bodies the formation and dissolution of all world-systems are perceived, yet in whom no perception of duality regarding themselves or the world-systems operates? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe milaspharaṇaṃ nāma jambūdvīpaśīrṣam / tatra sāradhvajo nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ prayoktavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here in <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region) to the place called <s>Milaspharaṇa</s>, the head of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. There dwells a <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Sāradhvaja</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should he practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako muktakasya śreṣṭhinaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya muktakaṃ śreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya muktakasya śreṣṭhino 'saṃkhyān guṇānudānayan upavicārayan, abhilaṣan, avijahan rudan paridevan kalyāṇamitrasnehajātaḥ kalyāṇamitrapratiśaraṇaḥ kalyāṇamitrārāgaṇābhimukhaḥ kalyāṇamitrajñānamavikopayan kalyāṇamitrādhīnāṃ sarvajñatāṃ samanupaśyan kalyāṇamitrānugatāśayaḥ kalyāṇamitropāyasādhyopacāraḥ kalyāṇamitracetanāvaśartī, mātṛsaṃjñī kalyāṇamitreṣu sarvāhitaparivarjanatayā, pitṛsaṃjñī kalyāṇamitreṣu sarvakuśaladharmasaṃjananatayā, muktakasya śreṣṭhino 'ntikātprakrāntaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, circumambulating the merchant <s>Muktaka</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon him again and again, lauding and reflecting upon the innumerable qualities of the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, longing [for him], not forsaking [him], weeping and lamenting — born of affection for the spiritual friend, taking refuge in the spiritual friend, facing the excellence of the spiritual friend, not allowing the knowledge of the spiritual friend to waver, seeing omniscience as dependent on the spiritual friend, with aspirations following the spiritual friend, with conduct accomplished by the skillful means of the spiritual friend, under the power of the spiritual friend's volition, perceiving spiritual friends as a mother through the avoidance of all harm, perceiving spiritual friends as a father through the generation of all wholesome <s>dharma</s>s — departed from the presence of the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>. // 6 //

body.text: 9 Sāradhvajaḥ /
body.translated_text: 9. <s>Sāradhvaja</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastāmeva muktakasya śreṣṭhino 'nuśāsanīmanuvicintayan, muktakasya śreṣṭhino 'vavāde pratipadyamāno 'cintyaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamanusmaran, acintyaṃ bodhisattvajñānālokamanusmaran, acintyaṃ dharmadhātupraveśāvatāramanugacchan, acintyaṃ bodhisattvasamavasaraṇanayamavataran, acintyaṃ tathāgatavikurvitamanupaśyan, acintyaṃ buddhakṣetrasamavasaraṇamadhimucyamānaḥ, acintyaṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānavyūhamanumārjan, acintyaṃ bodhisattvasamādhivimokṣavyavasthānavṛṣabhitāmavakalpayan, acintyāṃ lokadhātusaṃbhedānāvaraṇatāmavagāhamānaḥ, tasyāmacintyabodhisattvakarmadṛḍhādhyāśayatāyāṃ pratipadyamānaḥ, tadacintyabodhisattvakarmapraṇidhānasroto 'nukurvan, anupūrveṇa yena milaspharaṇaṃ jambūdvīpaśīrṣaṃ tenopasaṃkramya sāradhvajaṃ bhikṣuṃ parimārgayan apaśyadanyatarasminnāśrame caṃkramakoṭyāṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ samādhisamāpannamanuśvasantamanupraśvasantamaniñjamānamamanyamānamṛjukāyaṃ pratimukhasmṛtimacintyena samādhivikurvitena vikurvamāṇaṃ vāmadakṣiṇābhyāmūrdhvaṃ vā acintyāpramāṇānantakāyamavalokitamūrdhānamanekavarṇakāyāprameyavarṇavimātratāṃ cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe saṃdarśayamānam / tasya tathā samāpannasya gambhīrasya śāntasya nirunmiñjitasya nirālambasya romāñcordhvakāyasya sarvaromamukhebhyo 'cintyaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣavikurvitaṃ pravartayamānamapaśyat / yena vimokṣamukhavikurvitena sa cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharati anantanānāvikurvitavikalpaiḥ sarvasattvaparipākāya sarvatathāgatapūjāprayogāya sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanāya sarvasattvaduḥkhaskandhanivartanāya sarvadurgatimārgasamucchedāya sarvasattvasugatidvāravivaraṇāya sarvasattvakleśasaṃtāpapraśamanāya sarvasattvājñānāvaraṇavikiraṇāya sarvasattvasarvajñatāpratiṣṭhāpanāya //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, reflecting upon the very instruction of the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>, practicing in accordance with the merchant <s>Muktaka</s>'s counsel, recollecting the inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), recollecting the inconceivable light of <s>bodhisattva</s> knowledge, following the inconceivable entry into the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, entering the inconceivable method of <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly, beholding the inconceivable miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, aspiring to the inconceivable assembly of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, clearing away the inconceivable array of <s>Buddha</s>-empowerment, contemplating the inconceivable excellence of the establishment of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> and <s>vimokṣa</s>, plunging into the inconceivable unobstructed interpenetration of world-realms, practicing in that inconceivable firm resolution of <s>bodhisattva</s> action, following the stream of that inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> vow of action — proceeding gradually, he approached Milaspharaṇa, the summit of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and searching for the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, he saw him seated at the end of a walking-path in a certain hermitage, absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>, breathing in and breathing out, unmoving, without conceptual thought, with body erect, with mindfulness set before him, manifesting miraculous displays through inconceivable <s>samādhi</s> transformations, displaying at every mind-moment an inconceivable, immeasurable, infinite body-form visible to left and right and above, with head visible from all sides, with a body of many colors showing immeasurable variety of hues. He saw that one, thus absorbed — profound, peaceful, without agitation, without support, with hair standing on end throughout his body — emanating from every pore of his body the inconceivable miraculous display of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s>. Through that miraculous display of the gate of liberation, at every mind-moment he pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with infinite varieties of miraculous transformations, for the ripening of all beings, for the practice of worship of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, for the removal of the mass of suffering of all beings, for the cutting off of all paths to evil destinies, for the opening of the doors to happy destinies for all beings, for the pacification of the burning afflictions of all beings, for the dispelling of the obscurations of ignorance of all beings, and for establishing all beings in omniscience.

body.text: tasyādhaḥkramatalābhyāmasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān śreṣṭhigaṇān nānopasthānapratyupasthānān sarvalokadhātuparyāpannaśreṣṭhisadṛśarūpātirekaviṣayaprāvārān nānābhūṣaṇavibhūṣitaśarīrān vicitramaulicūḍāmaṇimakuṭadharān dārakabimbaparivārān niścaramāṇānapaśyat / brāhmaṇagṛhapatīṃśca sarvānnapānavidhibhiḥ sarvasāṅgopacāraiḥ sarvābharaṇaiḥ sarvavastraiḥ sarvapuṣpaiḥ sarvamālyaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ sarvavilepanaiḥ sarvakāmopacāraiḥ sarvaratnaiḥ sarvāyatanaiḥ sarvabhājanavidhibhiḥ sarvopakaraṇavidhibhiḥ daridrān sattvān saṃgṛhyamāṇān duḥkhitaṃ jagadāśvāsayamānān satvamanāṃsi paritoṣayamānān sattvāśayān viśodhayamānān sattvān bodhau paripācayamānān daśa diśaḥ spharitvā gacchato 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From the soles of both his feet, he saw issuing forth merchant assemblies equal in number to the atoms in innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, with various forms of service and attendance, wearing garments surpassing the appearance of all merchants throughout all world-realms, with bodies adorned with various ornaments, wearing diverse crests, diadems, jewels, and crowns, surrounded by retinues of young attendants. He saw them going forth pervading the ten directions, gathering poor beings with all manner of food and drink, with all forms of respectful service, with all ornaments, with all garments, with all flowers, with all garlands, with all fragrances, with all unguents, with all sensory pleasures, with all jewels, with all dwelling-places, with all manner of vessels, and with all manner of provisions, consoling the suffering world, gladdening the minds of beings, purifying the dispositions of beings, and ripening beings toward awakening.

body.text: jānumaṇḍalābhyāṃ niścaritvā kṣatriyapaṇḍitarūpān brāhmaṇapaṇḍitarūpān lokapaṇḍitarūpān vividhaśilpapaṇḍitarūpān manuṣyagatipaṇḍitarūpān laukikalokottarakriyāvidhijñānapaṭupaṇḍitarūpān lokācāryasaṃmatapaṇḍitarūpān anekākārakalpān anekākārasaṃsthānavyūhān manojñāni vacāṃsyudīrayato durmanasaḥ sattvān praharṣamāṇān dharmadhanaparihīṇān sattvānanugṛhyamāṇān duḥkhitān sattvān sukhayamānān vinipatitān sattvānabhyuddharamāṇān
body.translated_text: Issuing forth from both his knees, he saw figures in the form of <s>kṣatriya</s> scholars, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> scholars, worldly scholars, scholars skilled in various crafts, scholars learned in human conduct, scholars expert in knowledge of both mundane and supramundane procedures, and scholars esteemed as world-teachers — of manifold appearances and manifold configurations and arrays — uttering delightful words, gladdening beings who were dejected, assisting beings who had lost the wealth of <s>Dharma</s>, bringing happiness to suffering beings, uplifting beings who had fallen,

body.text: vipannayānapātrān sattvānāśvāsayamānān bhītān sattvān paritrāyamāṇān kuśalamūlaśabdamanuśrāvayamāṇān pāpavinivṛttiśabdamudīrayamāṇān kuśaladharmasamādāpane sattvān viniyojayamānān arthacaryāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān prītivegaṃ saṃjanayamānān priyavāditāsaṃgrahavastūnyudīrayamāṇān samānārthatāṃ ca lokasyopadarśayamānān daśa diśaḥ spharitvā gacchato 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: consoling beings whose vehicles had failed, rescuing beings who were frightened, causing them to hear the sound of wholesome roots, uttering the sound of turning away from evil, engaging beings in the undertaking of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, establishing beings in the practice of what is beneficial, generating a surge of joy, uttering the means of gathering through kind speech, and showing the world the state of shared purpose — going forth pervading the ten directions.

body.text: nābhimaṇḍalāt sarvasattvān sattvajagaccharīrasaṃsthānān ajinacīvaravalkaladharān daṇḍakāṣṭhakuṇḍikāgṛhītān nānārūpān kalpasaṃsthānān praśānteryāpathān ṛṣigaṇānniścaritvā uparyantarīkṣe buddhavarṇānudīrayamānān dharmaśabdaṃ saṃśrāvayamāṇān buddhaghoṣaṃ niścārayamāṇān bodhisattvasaṃghaṃ saṃdarśayamānān brahmacaryaṃ saṃpravarṇayamānān guptendriyatāyāṃ sattvānniyojayamānān niḥsvabhāvārthaṃ prarūpayamāṇān jñānārthe lokaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayamānān laukikaśāstravidhiṃ praṇayamānān sarvajñajñānaniryāṇamārgavidhiṃ pradarśayamānān anupūrvakriyāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān daśa diśaḥ spharitvā gacchato 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From the circle of his navel, he saw issuing forth hosts of sages equal in number to all beings, with bodily forms resembling the figures of the world of beings, wearing antelope skins, bark garments, and hides, carrying staffs, sticks, and water vessels, of various forms and configurations, with peaceful deportment — rising up into the sky above, uttering praises of the <s>Buddha</s>, causing the sound of <s>Dharma</s> to be heard, sending forth the proclamation of the <s>Buddha</s>, displaying the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, extolling the holy life, engaging beings in the restraint of the sense faculties, expounding the meaning of non-self-nature, establishing the world in the purpose of knowledge, setting forth the methods of worldly sciences, displaying the path and method leading to omniscient knowledge, and establishing beings in progressive practice — going forth pervading the ten directions.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ pārśvābhyāṃ sarvalokapravṛttisaṃkhyā acintyānekaśarīrasaṃsthānanāgakanyā niścaritvā acintyaṃ nāgavikurvitaṃ saṃdarśayamānāḥ acintyasugandhameghālaṃkāragaganatalamadhiṣṭhamānā acintyapuṣpameghālaṃkāraiḥ sarvagaganatalamalaṃkurvatīḥ acintyamālyameghālaṃkāraiḥ sarvamākāśadhātuṃ vyūhayamānā acintyaratnachatrameghālaṃkāraiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ saṃchādayamānā acintyaratnadhvajameghālaṃkāram acintyaratnapatākāmeghālaṃkāram acintyaratnapatākāvittaratnābharaṇameghavarṣāṃlaṃkāram acintyānantamahāmaṇiratnameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram acintyaratnahāravicitrakusumameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram acintyaratnāsanaparyaṅkaniṣaṇṇabodhisattvabuddhadharmameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram acintyadivyaratnābharaṇameghāpsarogaṇadharmasaṃgītirutaghoṣameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, acintyamuktajālālaṃkṛtaratnapadmordhvakesarasarvaratnarājacūrṇameghavarṣavikiraṇālaṃkāram, acintyaratnamakuṭameghasarvamaṇiratnavibhūṣitānantaraśmimeghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, acintyadevakāyameghapuṣpamālyacchatradhvajapatākālaṃkāram, acintyāpsaromeghonnatakāyakṛtāñjalipuṭasuvarṇapuṣpavikiraṇapramuktapuṭakośasarvatathāgataguṇavarṇastutimeghanigarjitapravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhamānāḥ sarvaratnavarṇairgandhakūṭameghairudāradhūpapaṭalameghaśca sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni saṃchādayamānāḥ, sarvalokadhātuprasarānalaṃkurvatīḥ sarvasattvāni praharṣayamāṇāḥ sarvabuddhān pūjayamānāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇāḥ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw, from both his sides, <s>nāga</s> maidens of inconceivable and manifold bodily forms equal in number to all the beings in the world issuing forth, displaying inconceivable miraculous <s>nāga</s> transformations, presiding over the vault of the sky with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of fragrance, adorning the entire sky with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of flowers, arraying the whole expanse of space with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of garlands, covering the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of jeweled parasols, with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of jeweled banners, with inconceivable cloud-ornaments of jeweled pennants, with inconceivable ornamental rains of clouds of jeweled pennant-streamers and jeweled adornments, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of infinite great maṇi-jewels, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of jeweled necklaces and variegated flowers, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s> teachings from those seated cross-legged on inconceivable jeweled thrones, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of celestial jeweled ornaments and choruses of <s>apsaras</s> singing songs of <s>Dharma</s>, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of jewel-dust of all jewel-kings upon the upraised filaments of jeweled lotuses adorned with nets of pearls, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of infinite rays adorned with all maṇi-jewels from clouds of jeweled crowns, with inconceivable ornaments of clouds of divine forms with flowers, garlands, parasols, banners, and pennants, with inconceivable ornamental showers of clouds of <s>apsaras</s> with raised bodies and palms joined, scattering golden flowers, releasing from their cupped hands thundering clouds of praise and glorification of the qualities of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — presiding over the vault of the sky, covering the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> with clouds of incense-peaks of all jewel-colors and clouds of magnificent incense-curtains, adorning the expanses of all world-realms, delighting all beings, worshipping all <s>Buddhas</s>, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every moment.

body.text: urastaḥ śrīvatsādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥ samānasurendrānniścaritvā acintyāsuramāyāvikurvitāni pradarśayamānān mahājaladharān saṃkṣobhayamāṇān lokadhātuśatasahasrāṇi saṃprakampayamānān sarvaśailendrarājānj saṃghaṭṭayamānān sarvadevabhavanāni saṃprakampayamānān
body.translated_text: From the <s>śrīvatsa</s> mark on his chest, he saw issuing forth lords of <s>asuras</s> equal in number to the atoms in innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, displaying inconceivable <s>asura</s> magical transformations, shaking the great ocean-bearers, causing hundreds of thousands of world-realms to tremble, striking together all the kings of mountains, causing all celestial palaces to quake,

body.text: sarvamāramaṇḍalāni jihmīkurvāṇān sarvamārasainyaṃ pramardayamānān sarvalokamadamānadarpān prabhañjayamānān praduṣṭacittānnivārya prasādayamānān vihiṃsācittān pratinivārayamāṇān sattvānāmakuśalān dharmānupaśamayamānān kleśaparvatān vikirayamāṇān raṇasaṃgrāmānupaśamayamānān vividhāsuramāyāvikurvitavikrīḍitaiḥ sattvān saṃvejayamānān pāpādudvejayamānān saṃsārāduntrāsayamānān sarvabhavagatibhya uccālya anikete niveśayamānān bodhicitte sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ viśodhayamānān bodhisattvān pāramitāsu pratiṣṭhāpayamānān bodhisattvabhūmiṣu avatārayamāṇān bodhisattvānāṃ buddhadharmanayāvabhāsaṃ janayamānān nānādharmanayavyavasthānaiścittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ //
body.translated_text: confounding all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, crushing all of <s>Māra</s>'s armies, shattering the pride, arrogance, and conceit of all the world, restraining and pacifying those with malicious minds, preventing those with harmful intent, causing the unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> of beings to subside, scattering the mountains of afflictions, pacifying battles and conflicts, alarming beings through various <s>asura</s> magical displays and feats, causing them to recoil from evil, terrifying them away from <s>saṃsāra</s>, uprooting them from all states of existence and establishing them in the homeless state, establishing beings in the thought of awakening, purifying the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, establishing <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), causing them to enter the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, generating for <s>bodhisattvas</s> the illumination of the method of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every mind-moment through various establishments of <s>Dharma</s>-methods — thus <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw.

body.text: pṛṣṭhavaṃśādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān śrāvakapratyekabuddhakāyānniścaritvā śrāvakapratyekabuddhavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmātmābhiniviṣṭānāṃ nirātmatāṃ niḥsattvatāmudīrayamāṇān śāśvatābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sarvasaṃskārānityatāṃ paridīpayamānān rāgacaritānāmaśubhāṃ bhāvanāṃ dveṣacaritānāṃ maitrīṃ mohacaritānāmidaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādamudīrayamāṇān samabhāgacaritānāṃ jñānaviṣayasaṃprayuktaṃ dharmanayabhidyotayamānān viṣayābhiratānāmanālayatāṃ kathayamānān śāntau niketāśayatānāṃ praṇidhiviśeṣamabhirocayamānān sarvadikparivartamukheṣu sarvadharmanayasāgaraparivartamukheṣu sarvasattvārthakriyāmabhidyotayato dharmadhātuṃ spharayamāṇānapaśyat sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the ridge of his back, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw issuing forth bodies of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> equal in number to the atoms in innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, proclaiming to those beings who were to be trained by <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> and who were attached to self — the selflessness and the absence of a being; illuminating for those attached to eternalism the impermanence of all conditioned things; proclaiming to those of lustful disposition the meditation on impurity, to those of hateful disposition loving-kindness, and to those of deluded disposition the conditioned co-arising of dependent origination; illuminating for those of balanced disposition the <s>Dharma</s>-method connected with the domain of knowledge; teaching non-attachment to those delighting in sense-objects; inspiring those inclined to rest in quiescence with the distinction of the vow; illuminating the activity for the benefit of all beings at all turning-points in every direction, at all turning-points in the ocean of all <s>Dharma</s>-methods — pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

body.text: aṃsakūṭābhyāmasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān yakṣarākṣasendrānniścaritvā nānāsaṃsthānavikṛtaśarīrān nānāvarṇārohapariṇāhān nāneryāpathavikalpān nānāyānābhirūḍhān nānāparivāraparivṛtān sattvadhātuparipālanaprayuktān nānāprabhāvabhāsaprayuktān nānāghoṣanirghoṣanigarjitān nānopāyābhinirhārairasaṃbhinnaiḥ samantadigvidiggaganaṃ spharamāṇān sarvasattvakuśalacaryārakṣāyai sarvāryamaṇḍalarakṣāyai sarvabodhisattvaparigrahāya sarvasamyagnatasamyakpratipannaparipālanāya vajrapāṇikarmaṇā sarvabuddhopasthānapūjāvidhānatāyai, vinipatitānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvāpāyagativinivartanatāyai, sarvalokasarvavyādhyādyupadravabhayopaśamanāya prayuktān sattvārthakriyālokaparipālanotsukān puṇyajñānasaṃbhāracakraṃ paripūrayamāṇān dharmacakramanupravartayamānān paravādicakraṃ nigṛhyamāṇān sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From the tops of both his shoulders, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw issuing forth lords of <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> equal in number to the atoms in innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields — with bodies of various distorted forms, of various colors, heights, and girths, with various modes of deportment, mounted upon various vehicles, surrounded by various retinues, engaged in the protection of the realm of beings, endowed with the radiance of various powers, with various sounds, resonances, and roars, pervading all directions, intermediate directions, and the sky with various unconfused skillful means — for the protection of the wholesome conduct of all beings, for the protection of all noble assemblies, for the care of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, for the safeguarding of all those who have rightly gone forth and rightly practice, for the service and worship of all <s>Buddhas</s> through the action of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, for turning back all beings who have fallen from all evil destinies, engaged in the pacification of all afflictions, diseases, calamities, and fears throughout the world, zealous for the benefit of beings and the protection of the world, fulfilling the wheel of merit and knowledge, turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, subduing the arguments of opponents, and pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>.
