body.text: udarādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kinnarendrān asaṃkhyeyakinnarendrakanyāśatasahasraparivārān asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca gandharvendrān asaṃkhyeyagandharvendrakanyāśatasahasraparivārān niścaritvā asaṃkhyeyadivyatūryaśatasahasrasaṃgītisaṃprabhaṇitadharmasvabhāvopasaṃhitāni buddhastotrāṇyudīrayamāṇān bodhicittaṃ paridīpayamānān bodhisattvacaryāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān sarvābhisaṃbodhimukhānyabhiṣṭavamānān sarvadharmacakramukhānyavagāhayamānān sarvavikurvitamukhānyabhirocayamānān sarvaparinirvāṇamukhāni paridīpayamānān sarvabuddhaśāsanamukhāni
body.translated_text: From his belly, having emanated <s>kinnara</s> lords equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, attended by retinues of innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>kinnara</s> lord maidens, and <s>gandharva</s> lords equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, attended by retinues of innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>gandharva</s> lord maidens, uttering praises of the <s>Buddha</s> accompanied by the singing of innumerable hundreds of thousands of divine musical instruments, endowed with the true nature of <s>Dharma</s>, illuminating <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), extolling the conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, praising all approaches to complete awakening, penetrating all approaches to the turning of the <s>Dharma</s> wheel, delighting in all approaches to miraculous transformations, illuminating all approaches to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, upholding all approaches to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching

body.text: saṃparigṛhyamāṇān sarvasattvamukhāni saṃpraharṣayamāṇān sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi pariśodhayamānān sarvadharmamukhāni abhidyotayamānān sarvāvaraṇamukhāni vinivartayamānān sarvakuśalamūlamukhāni saṃjayamānān dharmadhātuṃ spharayamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: gladdening all approaches to beings, purifying all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, illuminating all approaches to <s>Dharma</s>, turning back all approaches to obstruction, generating all approaches to roots of merit, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld.

body.text: mukhadvārādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān saptaratnacaturaṅgabalakāyaparivārān cakravartino niścaritvā mahātyāgaraśmivyūhān pramuñcamānān sarvaratnākarānutsṛjyamānān sarvamaṇiratnākarān viśrāṇayamānān daridrān sadhanīkurvāṇān prāṇivadhāllokaṃ vinivartayamānān maitrīcitte sattvān saṃniyojayamānān adattādānādvivecayamānān svalaṃkṛtāsaṃkhyeyakanyākoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pratipādayamānān kāmamithyācārādvicchandayamānān brahmacarye pratiṣṭhāpayamānān mṛṣāvādādvinivartayamānān asaṃvivādaparamatāyāṃ niyojayamānān, piśunavacanādvinivartayamānān paramasaṃgrahaprayuktaṃ ghoṣamudīrayamānān paruṣavacanāllokaṃ vinivartayamānān, manojñaślakṣṇāṃ vācamudīrayamāṇān, anarthādharmopasaṃhitādabaddhapralāpāt sattvān vinivartayamānān, gambhīrārthapadaprabhedaviniścaye saṃniyojayamānān, sarvavacanadoṣebhyo lokaṃ vinivartayamānān, karuṇābaddhavācamudīrayamāṇān, hṛdayamalaṃ loke 'paharaṇamāṇān, alpecchatāsaṃtuṣṭiparamatāyāṃ sattvānniyojayamānān, vyāpādāllokaṃ vinivartayamānān, parasaṃtatiprasādane saṃniyojayamānān, sarvadṛṣṭijālaṃ loke uddharamāṇān, sarvavimatiprakārān vikirayamāṇān, sarvasaṃdehakūṭān prapātayamānān, sarvasaṃśayavicikitsātimiramapanayamānān, dharmapravicayaṃ loke pravibhajamānān, idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādamudīrayamāṇān, svabhāvasatyanaye sattvānniyojayamānān, sarvāvaraṇāni vinivartayamānān, anāvaraṇanaye 'vatārayamāṇān, buddhārthanayamudyotayamānān, daśa diśo dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From the door of his mouth, having emanated <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning) kings equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, attended by fourfold armies equipped with the seven treasures, releasing arrays of rays of great generosity, pouring forth all mines of jewels, distributing all mines of gem-jewels, making the poor wealthy, turning the world away from the killing of living beings, establishing beings in the mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), separating them from taking what is not given, bestowing innumerable tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of beautifully adorned maidens, turning them away from desire for sexual misconduct, establishing them in <s>brahmacarya</s> (chaste conduct), turning them away from false speech, directing them toward the highest harmony free from quarrel, turning them away from divisive speech, uttering sounds engaged in the highest conciliation, turning the world away from harsh speech, uttering pleasant and gentle words, turning beings away from idle chatter connected with meaningless and unwholesome things, directing them toward the discernment of distinctions among words of profound meaning, turning the world away from all faults of speech, uttering words bound with compassion, removing the stain from the hearts of the world, directing beings toward the highest contentment with few desires, turning the world away from malice, directing them toward bringing joy to the minds of others, lifting the net of all wrong views from the world, scattering all varieties of doubt, toppling all peaks of uncertainty, dispelling the darkness of all hesitation and wavering, distributing the analysis of <s>Dharma</s> in the world, proclaiming <s>idaṃpratyayatā</s> (specific conditionality) and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), directing beings toward the method of the truth of intrinsic nature, turning back all obstructions, introducing them into the method of non-obstruction, illuminating the method of the <s>Buddha</s>'s purpose, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions — this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld.

body.text: nayanābhyāmasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni sūryamaṇḍalaśatasahasrāṇi niścaritvā sarvamahānirayānavabhāsamānāni, mahāndhakāraṃ loke vidhamanti, mohatimiraṃ sattvānāmapanayamānāni, śītanarakāpāyagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ śītaduḥkhaṃ praśamayamānāni, mṛṇmayeṣu kṣetreṣu avadātavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, suvarṇamayeṣu kṣetreṣu vaiḍūryavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, vaidūryamayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, rūpyamayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, suvarṇamayeṣu kṣetreṣu sphaṭikavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, sphaṭikamayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, suvarṇamayeṣu kṣetreṣu musāragalvavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, musāragalvamayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, lohitamuktāmayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, suvarṇaṃmayeṣu kṣetreṣu lohitamuktāvarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, aśmagarbhamayeṣu kṣetreṣu suvarṇavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, suvarṇamayeṣu kṣetreṣu aśmagarbhavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, indranīlamayeṣu kṣetreṣu sūryagarbhamaṇirājavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, sūryagarbhamaṇirājaśarīreṣu kṣetreṣu indranīlamaṇirājavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, lohitamuktāmayeṣu kṣetreṣu candrāṃśujālamaṇḍalagarbhamaṇirājavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, candrāṃśujālamaṇḍalagarbhamaṇirājaśarīreṣu
body.translated_text: From his eyes, having emanated hundreds of thousands of solar discs equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, illuminating all the great hells, dispelling the great darkness in the world, removing the darkness of delusion from beings, pacifying the suffering of cold for beings who have fallen into cold hells and lower realms, in realms made of earth releasing radiance of pure white color, in realms made of gold releasing radiance the color of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), in realms made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of silver releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of gold releasing radiance the color of <s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal), in realms made of <s>sphaṭika</s> releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of gold releasing radiance the color of <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), in realms made of <s>musāragalva</s> releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of red pearls releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of gold releasing radiance the color of red pearls, in realms made of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald) releasing radiance the color of gold, in realms made of gold releasing radiance the color of <s>aśmagarbha</s>, in realms made of <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) releasing radiance the color of the <s>sūryagarbha-maṇirāja</s> (sun-essence jewel-king), in realms with bodies made of the <s>sūryagarbha-maṇirāja</s> releasing radiance the color of the <s>indranīla-maṇirāja</s> (sapphire jewel-king), in realms made of red pearls releasing radiance the color of the <s>candrāṃśujāla-maṇḍalagarbha-maṇirāja</s> (jewel-king whose essence is the disc of the net of moon-rays), in realms with bodies made of the <s>candrāṃśujāla-maṇḍalagarbha-maṇirāja</s>

body.text: kṣetreṣu lohitamuktāvarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, ekaratnamayeṣu kṣetreṣu nānāratnavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, nānāratnamayeṣu kṣetreṣu ekaratnavarṇāṃ prabhāṃ pramuñcamānāni, evaṃ sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu aparimāṇasattvakāryaprayuktāni sarvasattvadharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānyapaśyat sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ //
body.translated_text: releasing radiance the color of red pearls, in realms made of a single jewel releasing radiance of the colors of various jewels, in realms made of various jewels releasing radiance the color of a single jewel — thus, engaged in immeasurable activities for the benefit of beings in all assemblies and circles of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of all beings — this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld.

body.text: bhrūvivarāntarādūrṇākośādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān śaśāṅkakāyānniścaritvā sarvadevendrānabhibhavamānān, kāmaratiṃ sarvaloke vinivartayamānān, buddhadarśanaratimanuvartayamānān, aparimāṇasattvavinayaprayuktān daśa diśo dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From the space between his brows, from the <s>ūrṇā</s>-tuft, having emanated moon-bodied beings equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, outshining all lords of the <s>devas</s>, turning away the delight in sensual pleasures throughout the world, cultivating delight in the vision of the <s>Buddha</s>, engaged in the discipline of immeasurable beings, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions — this he beheld.

body.text: lalāṭādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān mahābrahmaṇo niścaritvā praśānteryāpathān brahmaghoṣamudīrayamāṇān sarvabuddhānadhyeṣyamāṇān sarvabuddhānabhiṣṭavamānān sarvabodhisattvān praharṣayamāṇān aparimāṇasattvakāryaprayuktān daśa diśaḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From his forehead, having emanated great <s>Brahmā</s> beings equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, serene in deportment, uttering the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, entreating all <s>Buddhas</s>, praising all <s>Buddhas</s>, gladdening all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, engaged in activities for the benefit of immeasurable beings, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions — this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld.

body.text: śirasto 'saṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān bodhisattvānniścaritvā nānāvarṇasaṃsthānavibhūṣitaśarīratāṃ saṃdarśayamānān anuvyañjanavicitragātratāṃ prabhāvayamānān anantamadhyaprabhāmaṇḍalameghān pramuñcamānān sarvabuddhānāṃ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāmārabhya dāyakapratigrāhakavastuparityāgaprakārameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo niścārayamāṇān nānāpāramitāsaṃprayuktān pūrvayogasamudrān saṃdarśayamānān dānacaryāṃ lokasya saṃvarṇayamānān mātsaryamalaṃ vinivartayamānān sarvagrāhotsarge sattvānniyojayamānān, vicitrasarvaratnālaṃkārālaṃkṛtaṃ lokamadhitiṣṭhamānān, dānapāramitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpya pariṣkāravaśitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, sarvalakṣaṇaguṇān saṃvarṇayamānān, buddhalakṣaṇasaṃbhave hetumupadiśyamānānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā śīlapāramitāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvabuddhānāṃ śīlapāramitāsaṃprayuktān pūrvayogasamudrān sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvān sarvalokagativiṣayebhyo vimukhīkṛtya tathāgataviṣayābhimukhīkurvāṇān, kāmalokaṃ vijugupsamānān, viparyāsapaṭalaṃ loke vikiramāṇān, vitathaparikalpān praśamayitvā bodhisattvaśīle saṃniyojayamānān, mahākaruṇāśīlaṃ saṃvarṇayitvā tathāgataśīlapratilambhāya buddhamārgapratipattiśīle sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, svapnopamāṃ bhavagatiṃ sattvānāṃ prabhāvayitvā svapnavidhisamavasaraṇatāyai viṣayaparigrahakleśavaśitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścarya suvarṇavarṇacchavitāṃ loke 'bhidyotayamānān, akrodhānupāyāsatāyāmakhiladuṣṭāvinaṣṭāpratihatacittāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, sarvatiryagyonigatisamucchedāya sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ kṣāntipāramitāsaṃprayuktān tathāgatapūrvayogameghānniścārayamāṇān, kṣāntibale sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, dharmavaśitāyāṃ sattvānavabhāsayamānānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścarya anantabodhisattvavīryabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvajñatārambhāvivartyabalena
body.translated_text: From his head, having emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, displaying bodies adorned with various colors and forms, manifesting limbs beautified with the secondary marks, releasing clouds of light-halos of infinite extent, from all their pore-openings emitting clouds showing the manner of giving away substances by donors and recipients, beginning from the former <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of all <s>Buddhas</s>, displaying the oceans of former practices connected with the various <s>pāramitās</s>, extolling the practice of generosity to the world, turning back the stain of miserliness, directing beings toward relinquishing all grasping, presiding over a world adorned with ornaments of all kinds of jewels, having established beings in the <s>pāramitā</s> of giving, establishing them in mastery over requisites, extolling the qualities of all the marks, and pointing out the cause for the arising of the marks of a <s>Buddha</s> — this he beheld. And having emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, extolling the <s>pāramitā</s> of moral conduct, displaying from all their pore-openings the oceans of former practices connected with the <s>pāramitā</s> of moral conduct of all <s>Buddhas</s>, turning all beings away from the domains of all worldly destinies and directing them toward the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, inspiring disgust toward the realm of desire, scattering the veil of perversion in the world, pacifying false conceptualizations and directing them toward the moral conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, extolling the moral conduct of great compassion and establishing beings in the moral conduct of practice on the path to <s>Buddhahood</s> for the attainment of the moral conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, revealing the dream-like nature of the course of existence to beings and establishing them in mastery over the afflictions of grasping at sense-objects so that they may realize the dream-like nature of all phenomena — this he beheld. And having emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, illuminating golden-colored complexions in the world, establishing beings in a state free from anger and distress, with minds unimpaired, uncorrupted, and unobstructed, from all their pore-openings emitting clouds of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s former practices connected with the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience for the complete eradication of all animal-realm destinies, establishing beings in the power of patience, illuminating beings with mastery over <s>Dharma</s> — this he beheld. And having emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, displaying the infinite power of vigor of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, with the irreversible power of striving for omniscience

body.text:
sarvasattvaśrutasāgaraparyeṣṭiparikhedatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvatathāgatapūjopasthāne sattvānniyojayamānān, sarvaduḥkhaskandhavinivartanamahāvīryārambhe sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, vīryapāramitāpratisaṃyuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaśarīrānniścārayamāṇān,
bodhisattvavīryapāramitācaryāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, kausīdyaparvatān sattvānāṃ vikiramāṇān, vīryapāramitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, karmavaśitāyāṃ lokaṃ viniyojayamānān adhiṣṭhānaprayuktānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā bodhisattvānusmṛtipathe sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, sarvāvaraṇanivaraṇatimiraṃ vidhamamānān, sarvamadapramādāt sattvān vinivartayamānān, apramādadharme pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, stambhasaṃrambhamānadhvajānprapātayamānān, buddhadhyānāṅgasāgaramudīrayamānān, dhyānapāramitāṃ loke saṃvarṇayamānān, dhyānapāramitāpratisaṃyuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo niścārayamāṇān, cittavaśitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, kṣaṇe kṣaṇe dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā buddhadharmaparyeṣṭisaṃprayuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo niścārayamāṇān, sarvasvarāṅgasāgararūtaiḥ prajñāpāramitāmeghānnigarjamānān, samyagdṛṣṭividyutaṃ niścārayamāṇān, dharmasvabhāvarutaghoṣān ravamāṇān, ātmadṛṣṭiparvatakūṭānisattvānāṃ pradāryamāṇān, sarvadṛṣṭiśalyānyuddharamāṇān, kāṅkṣāvimatimativicikitsātimiraṃ vidhamamānān, adhimuktivaśitāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā sarvabuddhopāyakauśalyanayamaṇḍalaṃ prabhāvayamānān, upāyakauśalyapratisaṃyuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo niścārayamāṇān, upayakauśalyacaryāṃ loke prabhāvayamānān, mahāyānaniryāṇamabhidyotayamānān, sarvabuddhamaṇḍalaṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, saṃsāranirvāṇāsaṃbhinnāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, darśayamānān, bodhisattvopāyakauśalyapāramitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, sarvabodhisattvopapattivaśitāmaṇḍalaṃ loke nidarśayamānān, cittotpāde dharmadhātu spharamāṇānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā sarvatathāgatanāmasamudrameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo nigarjamānān, sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānapāramitāpariśuddhisaṃprayuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaromamukhamaṇḍalebhyaḥ pramuñcamānān, praṇidhānapāramitāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān,
sarvabodhisattvavaśitāsu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, aparāntakoṭyāviddhaṃ mahāpraṇidhānarathacakraṃ sarvadharmānusaraṇaṃ sarvakleśavinivartanamajñānaparvatavikiraṇaṃ loke prabhāvayamānān, nānāpraṇidhānavikurvitaiḥ cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvānniścaritvā bodhisattvabalamavabhāsayamānān, bodhisattvabalapariniṣpattirutaṃ pramuñcamānān, balapāramitāpariniṣpattisaṃbhavapūrvayogameghān sarvaromavivarebhyo niścārayamāṇān, sarvamāraparapravādyanavamṛdyabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvacakravālavajraparvataśarīropanipātātmabhedyabalaṃ prabhāvayamānān,
body.translated_text: praising the unwearying search through the ocean of learning of all beings, enjoining beings to the worship and attendance of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, establishing beings in the great heroic effort of turning away the aggregate of all suffering, releasing from all bodies clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the perfection of energy (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), displaying the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of the perfection of energy, scattering the mountains of laziness of beings, establishing beings in the perfection of energy, enjoining the world to the mastery of <s>karma</s> — [these bodhisattvas] empowered with spiritual resolve he saw. And he saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and establishing beings on the path of <s>bodhisattva</s>-recollection, dispelling the darkness of all obstructions and hindrances, turning beings away from all intoxication and heedlessness, establishing them in the <s>dharma</s> of heedfulness, casting down the banners of pride, arrogance, and conceit, proclaiming the ocean of the limbs of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), praising the perfection of <s>dhyāna</s> in the world, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the perfection of <s>dhyāna</s>, establishing beings in the mastery of mind, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> moment by moment. And he saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and releasing from all hair-pores clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the pursuit of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, thundering clouds of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) with the sounds of the ocean of all voice-limbs, producing the lightning of right view, sounding the voice-sounds of the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>, splitting the mountain-peaks of the view of self for beings, extracting all thorns of views, dispelling the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and perplexity, praising the mastery of aspiration, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every mind-moment. And he saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and empowering the maṇḍala of the method of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) of all <s>Buddhas</s>, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the perfection of skillful means, empowering the conduct of skillful means in the world, illuminating the emergence into the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, praising the maṇḍala of all <s>Buddhas</s>, praising and displaying the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct undivided between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, establishing beings in the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s perfection of skillful means, demonstrating in the world the maṇḍala of the mastery of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-rebirths, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at the generation of each mind-moment. And he saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and thundering from all hair-pore-maṇḍalas oceans of the names of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, releasing clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the purification of the perfection of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows (<s>praṇidhānapāramitā</s>), praising the perfection of vows, establishing beings in all <s>bodhisattva</s>-masteries, empowering in the world the great vow-chariot-wheel — reaching the ultimate future, following all <s>dharmas</s>, turning away all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), scattering the mountains of ignorance — pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every mind-moment with various vow-transformations. And he saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and illuminating the <s>bodhisattva</s>-power (<s>bala</s>), releasing the sound of the accomplishment of <s>bodhisattva</s>-power, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of former spiritual practice arising from the accomplishment of the perfection of power (<s>balapāramitā</s>), displaying the indomitable power against all <s>Māras</s> and opposing doctrines, empowering the power of the body's indestructibility even when struck by all <s>Cakravāla</s> vajra-mountains,

body.text: sarvakalpoddāhāgnisāgarasaṃvāsaśarīrānuddayotabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, gaganatale sarvalokadhātuprasarapāṇitalasaṃdhāraṇabalatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe ṛddhivaśitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān dharmadhātuspharaṇāpratiprasrabdhānapaśyat / asaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca bodhisattvān niścaritvā sattvānāṃ jñānamaṇḍalaṃ dyotayamānān, jñānaparimitāpariśuddhisaṃprayuktān pūrvayogameghān sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ pramuñcamānān, sarvabuddhaguṇajñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ loke prabhāvayamāṇān, sarvabuddhasaṃjñābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvapraṇidhyabhinirhārābhijñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ paridīpayamānān, sarvasattvasaṃgrahapraṇidhyabhinirhārajñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ vikhyāpayamānān, sarvasattvanairātmyāsvabhāvāvatārābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ vikhyāpayamānān, sarvasattvacittasāgaravyavalokanābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ prakāśayamānān, sarvasattvendriyavicayajñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ pravibhajamānān, sarvasattvāśayādhimuktivyavalokanajñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvasattvakarmasāgarāvatārābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ vivaramāṇān, sarvasattvapraṇidhānasāgarāvatārajñānābhijñāvatīṃ jñānabhūmiṃ saṃdarśyaṃ jñānapāramitāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: displaying the power of the body not being extinguished even while dwelling in the ocean of fire at the conflagration of all <s>kalpas</s>, displaying the power of holding all world-system-expanses in the palm of the hand upon the surface of the sky, establishing beings in the mastery of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) at every mind-moment, unceasingly pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. And <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> emerging and illuminating the knowledge-maṇḍala of beings, releasing from all hair-pores clouds of former spiritual practice connected with the purification of the perfection of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>), empowering in the world the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of all <s>Buddha</s>-quality-knowledge, displaying the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of the cognition of all <s>Buddhas</s>, illuminating the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of the accomplishment of all vow-productions, proclaiming the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of the gathering of all beings through vow-production, proclaiming the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of entering the non-self and intrinsic-nature-lessness of all beings, illuminating the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of observing the ocean of minds of all beings, analyzing the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of investigating the faculties of all beings, praising the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of observing the dispositions and aspirations of all beings, opening the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of entering the ocean of <s>karma</s> of all beings, and displaying the ground of knowledge endowed with superknowledge of entering the ocean of vows of all beings, establishing beings in the perfection of knowledge, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every mind-moment — this <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw. //

body.text: mūrdhata uṣṇīṣavivarādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatavigrahān varalakṣaṇānuvyañjanaviśuddhayalaṃkārān prataptajāmbūnadakanakaparvatanirbhāsān sarvadaśadikpratāpanāpramāṇadīptaprabhāmaṇḍaladharmadhātunayaspharaṇaghoṣān anantamadhyabuddhavikurvitasaṃdarśanān sarvajagadasaṃbhinnadharmameghānabhipravarṣamāṇān, yaduta bodhimaṇḍavaragatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samantadharmadhātutalabhedābhimukhajñānameghaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, abhiṣekaprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samantatalameghaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, mahādharmayauvarājyābhiṣiktānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samantamukhapraveśaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, kumārabhūtānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samantavyūhaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, avivartyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākarūṇādṛḍhakūṭaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, śuddhādhyāśayānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvabhedajñānavajraṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, pūrvayogasaṃpannānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samantajagatsaṃgrahavyūhaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, janmajānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tryadhvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalābhimukhavijñaptimeghaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, yogācārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvatalanirghoṣaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, ādikarmikāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇānayopāyagarbhameghasaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, prathamacittotpādikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pragraha kośopacayagarbhaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, udārādhimuktikānāṃ bodhisattvānāmakṣayavimokṣatathāgatapraṇidhipragrahakośaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, rūpāvacarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ samantatalākṣayakośaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, brahmakāyikānāṃ devānāmapramāṇanayasāgaranigarjitaghoṣaṃ
body.translated_text: From the crown of his head, from the aperture of the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance), [he saw emerging] <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, adorned with the purification of excellent marks and minor signs, radiant like mountains of heated <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, with immeasurable blazing radiance-circles pervading the ten directions, with sounds pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> by the method of [those circles], displaying the transformations of the infinite, middleless <s>Buddha</s>, raining <s>Dharma</s>-clouds undivided for all beings — namely: raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantadharmadhātutalabhedābhimukhajñānamegha</s>' (Knowledge-Cloud Facing the Penetration of the Surface of the Universal <s>Dharmadhātu</s>) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have reached the supreme <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantatalamegha</s>' (Universal Surface Cloud) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained consecration; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantamukhapraveśa</s>' (Entry through Universal Gateways) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> consecrated into the great <s>Dharma</s>-princedom; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantavyūha</s>' (Universal Array) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are Eternal Youths; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Mahākaruṇādṛḍhakūṭa</s>' (Firm Peak of Great Compassion) for non-retrogressing <s>bodhisattvas</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvabhedajñānavajra</s>' (Vajra of Knowledge Penetrating the Intrinsic Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> of purified higher intention; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantajagatsaṃgrahavyūha</s>' (Array of Universal Gathering of All Beings) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with former spiritual practice; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Tryadhvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalābhimukhavijñaptimegha</s>' (Cloud of Cognition Facing the Assembly-Circles of <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the Three Times) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who know births; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvatalanirghoṣa</s>' (Sound of the Surface of the Intrinsic Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are practitioners of yoga; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Mahākaruṇānayopāyagarbhameghasaṃbhava</s>' (Born from the Cloud-Womb of the Method of Great Compassion) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are beginners; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Pragrahakośopacayagarbha</s>' (Womb of the Accumulation of the Treasury of Embracing) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have first generated the mind; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Akṣayavimokṣatathāgatapraṇidhipragrahakośa</s>' (Treasury of Embracing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Vow of Inexhaustible Liberation) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> of noble aspiration; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Samantatalākṣayakośa</s>' (Inexhaustible Treasury of the Universal Surface) for beings of the form-realm; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Apramāṇanayasāgaranigarjitaghoṣa</s>' (Thundering Sound of the Ocean of Immeasurable Methods) for <s>Brahmakāyika</s> (Brahma-world) deities

body.text:
nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, vaśavartināṃ devānāṃ balasaṃbhavadharmopakaraṇākṣayakośaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, mārakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ citradhvajasarvajñatāsaṃbhārasaṃmārjanaghoṣaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, nirmāṇaratīnāṃ devānāṃ jñānaratnavicitradhuraṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, tuṣitānāṃ devānāṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhivicitradhvajaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, yāmānāṃ devānāṃ sarvatathāgatānusmṛtikośaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, śakradevendrabhavaneṣu tathāgatadarśanaprītivegasaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, yakṣendrabhavaneṣu dharmadhātugaganatathāgatavikurvitaspharaṇameghaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, gandharvendrabhavaneṣu sarvatathāgatadharmasaṃgītinirghoṣaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, asurendrabhavaneṣu jñānanayavajramaṇḍalaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, garuḍendrabhavaneṣu sarvatathāgatasaṃbhavopāyameghaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, kinnarendrabhavaneṣu sarvadharmameghasaṃgītinirghoṣaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, nāgendrabhavaneṣu
bodhisattvavikurvitanirghoṣabhavagatyudvegasaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, mahoragendrabhavaneṣu prītisāgaravivardhanavegaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, manuṣyalokeṣu sarvajagadviśeṣajñānaviṣayaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, narakalokeṣu sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhapraśāntanirghoṣāryamārgavacanādhārālaṃkāraṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, tiryagyoniṣu anavadyakarmapathapratipattinirghoṣatathāgatānusmṛtimeghamaṇḍalaśarīraṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, yāmalaukikeṣu sarvatathāgatapāramitānirnādasarvasattvatyāgacittasaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, vinipatiteṣu sattveṣu sarvaduḥkhopaśamapratilābhasamāśvāsanasvaranirghoṣaṃ nāma dharmameghavarṣamabhipravarṣamāṇān, sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Balasaṃbhavadharmopakaraṇākṣayakośa</s>' (Inexhaustible Treasury of <s>Dharma</s>-Equipment Born of Power) for <s>Vaśavartin</s> (sovereignty-wielding) deities; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Citradhvajasarvajñatāsaṃbhārasaṃmārjanaghoṣa</s>' (Sound of Cleansing the Accumulation of Omniscience of the Variegated Banner) for <s>Mārakāyika</s> deities; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Jñānaratnavicitradhura</s>' (Variegated Yoke of Knowledge-Jewels) for <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> (Delight-in-Creation) deities; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Bodhisattvapraṇidhivicitradhvaja</s>' (Variegated Banner of <s>Bodhisattva</s> Vows) for <s>Tuṣita</s> deities; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvatathāgatānusmṛtikośa</s>' (Treasury of the Recollection of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) for <s>Yāma</s> deities; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Tathāgatadarśanaprītivegasaṃbhava</s>' (Born of the Force of Joy of Seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>) in the abodes of <s>Śakra Devendra</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Dharmadhātugaganaтathāgatavikurvitaspharaṇamegha</s>' (Cloud of Pervading <s>Tathāgata</s>-Transformations in the Sky of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>) in the abodes of <s>Yakṣendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvatathāgatadharmasaṃgītinirghoṣa</s>' (Sound of the <s>Dharma</s>-Recital of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) in the abodes of <s>Gandharvendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Jñānanayavajramaṇḍala</s>' (Vajra-Maṇḍala of Knowledge-Method) in the abodes of <s>Asurendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvatathāgatasaṃbhavopāyamegha</s>' (Cloud of the Means of Arising of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) in the abodes of <s>Garuḍendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvadharmameghasaṃgītinirghoṣa</s>' (Sound of the Recital of Clouds of All <s>Dharmas</s>) in the abodes of <s>Kinnarendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Bodhisattvavikurvitanirghoṣabhavagatyudvegasaṃbhava</s>' (Born of the Alarm at Existential Courses through the Sound of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-Transformations) in the abodes of <s>Nāgendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Prītisāgaravivardhanavega</s>' (Force of Augmenting the Ocean of Joy) in the abodes of <s>Mahoragendras</s>; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvajagadviśeṣajñānaviṣaya</s>' (Domain of Distinctive Knowledge of All Beings) in the human worlds; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhapraśāntanirghoṣāryamārgavacanādhārālaṃkāra</s>' (Ornament of the Stream of Noble Path Words Sounding the Pacification of All <s>Saṃsāra</s>-Suffering) in the hell-worlds; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Anavadyakarmapathapratipattinirghoṣatathāgatānusmṛtimeghamaṇḍalaśarīra</s>' (Body of the Maṇḍala of the Cloud of <s>Tathāgata</s>-Recollection Sounding the Practice of Blameless <s>Karma</s>-Paths) in the animal realms; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvatathāgatapāramitānirnādasarvasattvatyāgacittasaṃbhava</s>' (Born of the Mind of Renunciation of All Beings from the Resounding of the <s>Pāramitās</s> of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) in <s>Yama</s>'s worlds; raining the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain called '<s>Sarvaduḥkhopaśamapratilābhasamāśvāsanasvaranirghoṣa</s>' (Sound of the Voice of Consolation and Attainment of the Subsiding of All Suffering) for beings who have fallen — pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw. //

body.text: sarvaromamukhebhyaśca ekaikasmādromavivarādasaṃkhyeyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni raśmijālamaṇḍalāni niścaritvā asaṃkhyeyabalarūpāvartavyūhān asaṃkhyeyavicitrakāryapratyupasthānāni daśa diśo dharmadhātuṃ spharamāṇānyapaśyat / yaduta kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalādvimaladānacaryāsarvasvaparityāgavikurvitamapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvatryadhvabodhisattvaśīlavratasamādānākalpamaṇḍalavikurvitamapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvabodhisattvakṣānticaryārūpatryadhvaprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ hastapādottamāṅgacchedādhivāsanavikurvitaṃ pāṇidaṇḍaśasraśarīropanipātādhivāsanavikurvitaṃ sarvaśarīrabhedanahṛdayanayanoddharaṇādhivāsanavikurvitapaśyat / yairapyanyaistryadhvaprāptabodhisattvavikalpitātmabhāvaiḥ sarvajñatādharmaparyeṣṭinidānaṃ sarvakāyikacaitasikaprapīḍitānyaṅgapratyaṅgacchedanāni mahākarūṇāprapīḍitairadhivāsitāni marṣitāni adhyupekṣitāni, tānyapi sarvabodhisattvakṣānticaryāvikurvitapratibimbarūpāṇyapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvabodhisattvavīryacaryādhimātratāvibhaktarūpāṇyatītānāgatapratyutpannāni bodhisattvavikurvitāni lokasaṃkampanasāgarasaṃkṣobhanasattvasaṃvejanasarvatīrthyasaṃtrāsanamāramaṇḍalavidrāvaṇadharmadigdyotanamahābodhisattvavikramavikurvitānyapaśyat /
body.translated_text: And from all the hair-pore openings, from each and every hair-pore, ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> equal in number to the atoms of innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields issued forth, pervading the ten directions and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> with innumerable arrays of powerful manifestations and innumerable wondrous displays of beneficial activity, and he beheld them. Namely, from certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the miraculous display of the stainless practice of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), the complete renunciation of all possessions. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the miraculous display of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the undertaking of <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) and vows of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the three times. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the miraculous display of the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) practice of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — the endurance of the cutting off of hands, feet, and head of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the form of <s>kṣānti</s>-practice across the three times, the endurance of the assault of sticks, swords, and weapons upon their bodies, and the endurance of the piercing, breaking, and tearing out of their entire bodies, hearts, and eyes. And whatever other bodily forms conceived by <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the three times — the cutting of limbs and minor limbs, all physical and mental torments endured for the sake of seeking the <s>Dharma</s> of omniscience, which were patiently endured, tolerated, and calmly accepted by those impelled by great compassion — all those too he beheld as reflections of the miraculous display of the <s>kṣānti</s>-practice of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the miraculous manifestations of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>' <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) practice, distinguished in their supreme forms across past, present, and future — the mighty miraculous displays of great <s>bodhisattva</s> valor that shake the world, agitate the oceans, stir sentient beings to urgency, terrify all non-Buddhist teachers, scatter the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, and illuminate the quarters with the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalād yāni sarvabodhisattvacaryānirūpaṇāni yānyātmabhāvopādānāni ye kulopapattiparigrahāya rūpakāya pariniṣpattaye ye kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīparigrahāḥ, yāni kalyāṇamitropadeśapratipattisthānāni, yāni tathāgatadhyānāṅgapariniṣpattyanurūpavihārabhavanavimānajanapadagirikandarāṇi,
yāni ṛṣiśarīrāṇi, yaistāni dhyānāṅgāni niṣpāditāni, yāni nṛpādhipatyāni, yāni naiṣkramyamukhāni, ye vratasamādānākalperyāpathāḥ, tatsarvaṃ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyat //
body.translated_text: From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s>, all the examinations of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice — the acquisitions of bodily forms, the embracing of family births for the perfection of the physical body, the receiving of instructions from spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), the places of practice according to the teachings of spiritual friends, the dwellings, palaces, mansions, countries, mountains, and caves suitable for the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) factors, the bodies of sages by whom those <s>dhyāna</s> factors were accomplished, the sovereign rulerships, the gateways to renunciation, the modes of conduct in undertaking vows and austerities — all this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld.

body.text: kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalāt prajñāpāramitācaryāvihārasarvadharmaparyeṣṭisaṃprayuktān kāyaparigrahānapaśyat / yaiḥ kāyairekaikaṃdharmapadaṃ sarvāstiparityāgitayā sarvasattvānāmantikātparyeṣitaṃ sarvopasthānaparicaryāsarvakalyāṇamitrasakāśātparyeṣitaṃ śraddhāgauravanirjātena ca kāyapramāṇena tathāgatasakāśātparyeṣitam, yathā caikatvaṃ dharmapadaṃ tathā sarvadharmapadāni prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni yāni sarvajagadupapattipratibhāsaiḥ kāyaiḥ paryeṣitāni, tatsarvaṃ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ ekaikasmādromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalādapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvabodhisattvaparipākopāyasattvagatisamudraprasaritān sarvasattvasaṃgrahaprayogānapaśyat / ekaikaṃ ca sattvaṃ sarvasattvakāyasadṛśairātmabhāvopacāramukhaiḥ pūrvātmabhāvopādānairupāyakauśalyacaryāprayuktaiḥ saṃgṛhyamāṇaṃ tata ekaikasmādromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalādapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalāt yā bhagavataḥ pūrvasarvakalpapraṇidhyabhinirhāracaryā sarvasattvaparipākapraṇidhyabhinirhāracaryā sarvakṣetrapariśuddhipraṇidhyabhinirhāracaryā, yāni ca sarvapraṇidhyabhinirhāramaṇḍalāni teṣu teṣu tathāgatapādamūleṣu abhinirhṛtāni sarvasaṃsāradoṣāṇāṃ tasya tasya saṃsāradoṣasya pratipakṣeṇa, tatsarvaṃ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastata ekaikasmādromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalādapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvabalapāramitācaryāsaṃprayuktān pūrvayogasamudrānapaśyat / kutaścidromamukharaśmijālamaṇḍalātsarvajñānacaryāvicārasaṃprayuktānajñānanidrāprasuptasattvaprabodhanaśarīrān pūrvayogasamudrānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the bodily forms connected with the practice of <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), dwelling in the quest for all <s>dharmas</s>. With those bodies, each single <s>Dharma</s>-word was sought from all beings through the complete renunciation of everything, sought from all spiritual friends through attendance and service, and sought from the <s>Tathāgata</s> with a body born of faith and reverence. And just as with one <s>Dharma</s>-word, so too all <s>Dharma</s>-words connected with <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> were sought through bodies reflecting the births of all beings in the world — all this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld from each and every hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍala</s>. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the means of maturing all <s>bodhisattva</s> practices extending into the ocean of destinies of beings, the applications for gathering all sentient beings. And he beheld from each hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍala</s> each individual being being gathered through skillful means connected with prior bodily form acquisitions resembling the bodies of all beings. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s former practice of aspiration-accomplishment across all <s>kalpas</s> — the aspiration-accomplishment practice for maturing all beings, the aspiration-accomplishment practice for purifying all fields, and the <s>maṇḍalas</s> of aspiration-accomplishment produced at the feet of each <s>Tathāgata</s> as antidotes to each of the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> — all this <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, beheld from each and every hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍala</s>. From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the oceans of former practices connected with the conduct of the perfection of all powers (<s>bala-pāramitā</s>). From certain hair-pore ray-net <s>maṇḍalas</s> he beheld the oceans of former practices connected with the investigation of the conduct of all knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>-practice) — the bodies that awaken beings who are asleep in the slumber of ignorance.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sāradhvajaṃ bhikṣuṃ tathā samāhitamupanidhyāyantamupaparīkṣamāṇaḥ, tatsamādhivimokṣamaṇḍalamanusmaran, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvasamādhivṛṣabhitāmanuvicintayan, tamacintyaṃ sattvārthanayasāgaramavataran, tadacintyaṃ samantasrotābhimukhavyūhābhisaṃskāramukhamanusaran, adhimucyamānaḥ, taddharmadhātuvyūhaviśuddhijñānamukhamavataran, tadbuddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ saṃpratīcchan, jñānaṃ nistīrayamāṇaḥ, tadbodhisattvavaśitābalaṃ saṃjanayan, tadbodhisattvapraṇidhibalaṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ, tadbodhisattvacaryābalaṃ vistārayan, sāradhvajasya bhikṣoḥ purataḥ ekamapi rātriṃdivasamatināmayati, dvāvapi, saptāpi rātriṃdivāni purato 'tināmayati, ardhamāsamapi, māsadvayamapi, yāvat ṣaḍapi māsān ṣaḍ vā rātriṃdivāni sāradhvajasya bhikṣoḥ purato 'tināmayati / tataḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ māsānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ ca rātriṃdivānāmatyayena sāradhvajo bhikṣustasmātsamādhervyutthitaḥ / sudhana āha - āścaryaṃ batedam, ārya, yāvadgambhīra eṣa
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, contemplating the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s> thus absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>, examining him closely, recollecting that <s>samādhi</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> <s>maṇḍala</s>, reflecting upon that inconceivable excellence of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, entering that inconceivable ocean of methods for the benefit of beings, following that inconceivable gateway of preparation for the array facing all currents, entering with faith, penetrating that gateway of knowledge of the purity of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> array, receiving that <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, crossing over in knowledge, generating that power of <s>bodhisattva</s> mastery, strengthening that power of <s>bodhisattva</s> aspiration, and expanding that power of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice — he passed before the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s> one day and night, then two, then seven days and nights, then half a month, two months, and up to six months and six days and nights before the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s>. Then, at the end of six months and six days and nights, the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s> arose from that <s>samādhi</s>. <s>Sudhana</s> said: 'How wonderful this is, Noble One! How profound is this

body.text:
samādhiḥ / yāvadvipulo yāvadapramāṇaviṣayo yāvadacintyavikurvitavyūhaḥ yāvadatulyālokaḥ yāvadasaṃkhyeyavyūhaḥ yāvadasaṃhāryagocaraḥ yāvadasaṃbhinnaviṣayaḥ yāvatsamadigvirocanaḥ yāvadapramāṇasattvārthaprayoga eṣa samādhiḥ, yatra hi nāma evaṃ sarvasattvānāmaparimāṇaduḥkhaskandhavyupaśamāya pratyupasthitaḥ, yaduta dāridryaduḥ khaskandhavyupaśamārthena pratyupasthitaḥ / narakagativyupacchedanārthena tiryagyonigatiparitrāṇārthena sarvākṣaṇagatidvārapithanārthena svargagatyupanayanārthena devamanuṣyaratisukhasaṃbhavārthena dhyānaviṣayaratyanubhavārthena saṃskṛtāvacarasukhasaṃvardhanārthena traidhātukaniḥsaraṇamukhasaṃdarśanārthena pratyupasthitaḥ / bodhicittasaṃbhavahetuparidīpanārthena pratyupasthitaḥ / puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasaṃbhavahetusaṃvardhanārthena vipulamahākaruṇāvegavivardhanārthena mahāpraṇidhānabalasaṃjananārthena bodhisattvamārgāvabhāsapratilambhārthena mahāpāramitāyānavyūhārthena mahāyānaviśeṣāvatārābhinirhārārthena samantabhadracaryājñānāvalokārthena bodhisattvabhūmijñānālokapratilābhārthena sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhicaryāniryāṇavyūhaviśuddhisamudāgamārthena
sarvajñaviṣayākramaṇādhiṣṭhānārthena pratyupasthitaḥ / ko nāma ārya eṣa samādhiḥ? āha - asti kulaputra, samantacakṣurupekṣāpratilabdhā nāma prajñāpāramitā / tadāloka eṣa samādhiḥ samantamukhaviśuddhivyūho nāma / etasya kulaputra samantacakṣurupekṣāpratilabdhaprajñāpāramitālokanirjātasya samantamukhaviśuddhivyūhasya samādheḥ subhāvitatvātsamantamukhaviśuddhivyūhapūrvaṃgamāni paripūrṇāni daśa samādhyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyājāyante / āha - etāvatparamaḥ ārya asya samādherviṣayaḥ? āha - etaṃ kulaputra samādhiṃ samāpannasya adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātuvijñaptiṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātvavatāreṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātuvikrameṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātupratimaṇḍaleṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātuparikarmasu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadhātupariśodhaneṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhadarśanavijñaptiṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhamāhātmyapratyavekṣāyām / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhavikurvitajñānatāyām / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhabalāvatārānugameṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhaguṇasamudrāvataraṇatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvabuddhadharmacakrapravartanāsaṃbhedajñānānugameṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhaparṣaṇḍalasamudrāvataraṇāvagāhanatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ daśadikpraveśānusaraṇatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhadharmadeśanānuvilokaneṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhadiganulokanatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ mahākaruṇādigavijahanatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ maitrīdikspharaṇatāsu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhadarśanadigavatārātṛptiṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvasattvasamudrāvatārānugameṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvasattvendriyasamudrajñānānugameṣu / adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvasattvendriyasaṃbhedajñāneṣu / etamahaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāvihāraṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ prajñāpāramitāvihārasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ dharmadhātuviṣayamativiśuddhānāṃ sarvadharmagatyanusṛtijñānināṃ vipulabuddhyapramāṇaviṣayaspharaṇānāṃ mahādhāraṇyavabhāsavaśavartināṃ sarvasamādhimaṇḍalālokasupariśuddhānāmabhijñāvikurvitavṛṣabhitāniryātānāmakṣayapratisaṃvitsāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ bhūmigarbhamadhuranirghoṣāṇāṃ sarvajagatpratiśaraṇabhūtānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryā jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum, gocaro vā nidarśayitum,
body.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s>! How vast, how immeasurable in scope, how inconceivable in its miraculous arrays, how incomparable in its radiance, how innumerable in its configurations, how indestructible in its domain, how undivided in its range, how illuminating in all directions, how immeasurable in its application for the benefit of beings is this <s>samādhi</s>, which stands ready for the pacification of the immeasurable mass of suffering of all sentient beings — namely, it stands ready for the pacification of the mass of suffering from poverty, for the cutting off of rebirth in the hells, for the rescue of those born in animal realms, for closing the doors to all unfortunate destinies, for leading beings to heavenly destinies, for producing the joys and happiness of gods and humans, for experiencing the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), for increasing the happiness within the conditioned realm, for revealing the gateway of escape from the triple world. It stands ready for illuminating the causes that give rise to <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), for increasing the causes that produce the accumulations of merit and knowledge, for intensifying the force of vast great compassion, for generating the power of great aspirations, for attaining the illumination of the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, for the adornment of the great <s>pāramitā</s> vehicle, for accomplishing entry into the distinction of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, for beholding the knowledge of the practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, for attaining the light of knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, for achieving the purity of the array leading to the fulfillment of the aspirations and practices of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and for the empowerment of entering the domain of omniscience.' 'What, Noble One, is the name of this <s>samādhi</s>?' He replied: 'Son of good family, there is the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> called "Attainment of Universal Vision and Equanimity." This <s>samādhi</s> is its illumination, called the "Array of Universal Gateway Purity." Son of good family, from the thorough cultivation of this <s>samādhi</s> — the Array of Universal Gateway Purity born from the light of the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> of Attainment of Universal Vision and Equanimity — there arise, preceded by the Array of Universal Gateway Purity, a full ten times innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s>.' He asked: 'Noble One, is this the ultimate scope of this <s>samādhi</s>?' He replied: 'Son of good family, for one who has entered this <s>samādhi</s>, there is mastery over the manifestations of world-realms, mastery over entry into world-realms, mastery over traversing world-realms, mastery over the adornment of world-realms, mastery over the preparation of world-realms, mastery over the purification of world-realms, mastery over the manifestation of seeing <s>Buddhas</s>, mastery over the contemplation of the <s>Buddha</s>'s majesty, mastery over the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous displays, mastery over following the entry into the <s>Buddha</s>'s powers, mastery over plunging into the ocean of <s>Buddha</s> qualities, mastery over receiving the cloud of <s>Buddha</s> <s>Dharma</s>, mastery over following the knowledge of the unbreakable turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Buddhas</s>, mastery over plunging into the ocean of <s>Buddha</s> assemblies, mastery over following entry into the ten directions, mastery over observing the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> teachings, mastery over gazing into the <s>Buddha</s>'s directions, mastery over not abandoning the direction of great compassion, mastery over pervading the directions with loving-kindness, mastery over insatiable entry into the directions of seeing <s>Buddhas</s>, mastery over following entry into the ocean of all beings, mastery over following the knowledge of the ocean of faculties of all beings, mastery over the knowledge of the distinctions among the faculties of all beings. This, son of good family, is the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> dwelling that I know. How could I know the conduct, speak of the qualities, demonstrate the domain,

body.text:
viṣayo vā prabhāvayitum, mahāpraṇidhānabalaṃ vā saṃvarṇayitum, niryāṇamukhaṃ vā avabhāsayitum, samudāgamo vā abhidyotayitum, mārgaṃ vā paridīpayitum,
samādhisroto va anusartum, cittaviṣayo vā jñātum, jñānaṃ vā samatā vā avagantum //
body.translated_text: display the scope, praise the power of great aspirations, illuminate the gateway of attainment, reveal the accomplishment, illumine the path, follow the current of <s>samādhi</s>, know the domain of mind, or comprehend the knowledge and equanimity of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have plunged into the ocean of inexhaustible analytical knowledge, who have descended into the ocean of the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> dwelling, whose <s>dharmadhātu</s> domain is supremely pure, who follow the knowledge of the course of all <s>dharmas</s>, whose vast wisdom pervades immeasurable domains, who command the radiance of great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, whose light of all <s>samādhi</s> <s>maṇḍalas</s> is thoroughly purified, who have attained excellence in miraculous displays of supernatural powers, who possess the sweet voice of the treasury of the stages, and who are the refuge of all the world?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe samudravetāḍī nāma pratyuddeśaḥ / tatra samantavyūhaṃ nāmodyānaṃ mahāprabhasya nagarasya pūrveṇa / tatra āśā nāmopāsikā prativasati suprabhasya manujendrasya bhāryā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ prayoktavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, here in the southern region there is a district called <s>Samudravetāḍī</s>. There is a garden called <s>Samantavyūha</s>, to the east of the great city of <s>Prabhāsa</s>. There dwells a lay-woman (<s>upāsikā</s>) named <s>Āśā</s>, the wife of the king <s>Suprabhasa</s>. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? How should one apply oneself?'

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ sāradhvajasya bhikṣorantikādāttasāraḥ upajīvitadharmā avatīrṇasamādhiviṣayo labdhālokāvabhāsitajñānaḥ samādhyavabhāsapratilabdhaḥ adhimuktiviśuddhayanugatadharmanayālokānugatacetanaḥ viśuddhimukhānugatāloko digālokaprasṛtajñānaḥ sāradhvajasya bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sāradhvajaṃ bhikṣumavalokya praṇipatya punaḥ punaravalokayan abhivilokayan nipatan praṇipatan namasyan avanaman manasikurvaṃścintayan bhāvayan pāribhāvayan udānamudānayan hākkāraṃ kurvan guṇānabhimukhīkurvan anugamayan anusmaran anusmārayan dṛḍhīkurvan avijahan manasā āgamayan upanibadhnan praṇidhiṃ samavasaran darśanamabhilaṣan svaranimittamudgṛhṇan dhārayan dhāraṇānugatacitto varṇasaṃsthānamanusmaran jñānaviśeṣamanuvicintayan samādhiviṣayaṃ samavataran praṇidhiviṣayamanuprabandhan gocaraviṣayaṃ vicārayan jñānāvabhāsaṃ saṃpratīcchan sāradhvajasya bhikṣorantikātprakrāntaḥ // 7 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, delighted, elated, joyful, filled with gladness and mental happiness, having taken the essence from the presence of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, sustained by the <s>Dharma</s>, having descended into the domain of <s>samādhi</s>, having attained knowledge illuminated by the light [of wisdom], having obtained the illumination of <s>samādhi</s>, with his mind following the light of the <s>dharma</s>-method through the purification of faith, with his light following the gateway of purification, with knowledge extending to the light of all directions — bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, prostrating, looking again and again, observing intently, bowing down, falling at his feet, paying homage, bending low, attending mentally, reflecting, cultivating, thoroughly cultivating, uttering exclamations of wonder, making exclamations, turning toward his virtues, following, remembering, recalling, making firm, not abandoning, mentally approaching, binding fast, assembling vows, longing for his sight, grasping the mark of his voice, retaining, with his mind following <s>dhāraṇī</s>, remembering the form and shape, contemplating the distinction of knowledge, entering the domain of <s>samādhi</s>, continuing the domain of vows, investigating the domain of the sphere [of knowledge], receiving the illumination of knowledge — departed from the presence of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sāradhvaja</s>. // 7 //

body.text: 10 āśā /

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kalyāṇamitraguṇārādhitaḥ kalyāṇamitrasaṃpreṣitaḥ kalyāṇamitradarśanāveśāviṣṭaḥ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṃ pratipadyamānaḥ kalyāṇavacanānyanusmaran, kalyāṇamiutrānugatapremā kalyāṇamitrāṇyākaraṃ buddhadarśanaṃ saṃpaśyan, kalyāṇamitrāṇi buddhadharmasaṃdarśakāni saṃpaśyan, kalyāṇamitrāṇyācāryāṇi sarvajñatādharmeṣu samanupaśyan, cakṣurbhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi buddhagaganālokanatāyai saṃpaśyan, anupūrveṇa yena samudravetālīpradeśe samantavyūhamudyānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / so 'paśyat samantavyūhamudyānaṃ sarvaratnaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ sarvaratnadrumapaṅktiṣu āviddhasamalaṃkṛtaṃ sarvaratnapaṅktirucirasūkṣmakusumareṇupramuktaṃ sarvaratnadrumasamalaṃkṛtaṃ sarvaratnadrumapuṣpavicitrakusumākīrṇaṃ sarvagandhadrumapaṅktisamantadigniścaritagandhaṃ sarvaratnamālādrumakośapramuktapralambanānāratnamālāvṛṣṭayabhipravarṣaṇaṃ sarvamaṇirājadrumamaṇiratnakṛtavicitrabhaktisaṃstīrṇopaśobhitatalaṃ sarvakalpapuṣpadrumanānāraṅgavastrapralambapracchannopacārasuvibhaktadeśaṃ sarvavādyadrumadivyātirekatūryamārutasamīritanirnāditamadhuranighoṣamanimnonnatapṛthivīsamatalāviddhaṃ sarvābharaṇavṛkṣakośapramuktābharaṇavikṛtavicitradhārābhipralambitopaśobhitavyūham / tasmin khalu punaḥ samantavyūhe mahodyāne daśa prāsādakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi sarvamahāmaṇiratnapratimaṇḍitaniryūhavyūhāni, daśa kūṭāgāraśatasahasrāṇi jāmbūnadakūṭakanakacchadanopetāni, daśa vimānaśatasahasrāṇi vairocanamaṇiratnopaśobhitagarbhāṇi, daśa puṣkariṇīśatasahasrāṇi sarvaratnamayāni ratneṣṭakānicitāni saptaratnavicitrasopānāni nānāmaṇiratnavedikāparivṛtāni divyacandanavāriniṣyandagandhāni suvarṇavālukāsaṃstīrṇadaśaprāsādakanakamaṇiratnākīrṇatalāni caturdikṣu vibhaktasopānāni aṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇāni haṃsakrauñcamayūrakokilakalaviṅkakuṇālanirnādarutamadhuranirghoṣāṇi ratnatālapaṅktiparivṛtāni suvarṇaghaṇṭājālasaṃchannamārutasamīritamanojñanirghoṣaśabdāni
uparimahāmaṇiratnavitānavitatāni nānāratnavṛkṣavāṭikāparivṛtāni ucchritacchatradhvajamaṇiratnajālodyotitāni daśa ca taḍāgaśatasahasrāṇi, kālānusāricandanakardamopacitāni sarvaratnamayavicitravarṇapadmasaṃchannāni mahāmaṇiratnapadmāvabhāsitavimalasalilāni / tasya codyānasya madhya vicitradhvajaṃ nāma mahāvimānaṃ sāgaragarbharatnapṛthivītalasaṃsthānaṃ vaidūryamaṇiratnastambhopaśobhitaṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇasamudgatakūṭaṃ jagadvirocanamaṇiratnagarbhavyūhaphalakabaddhamasaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnajālojjvalitatalamajitavatigandhamaṇirājanirdhūpitopacāramanuracitagandhamaṇirājasamīritagandhaṃ vibodhanagandhamaṇirājavidhamanatīkṣṇendriyavāsanam / tasmiṃśca vicitradhvaje mahāvimāne 'parimitānyāsanāni prajñaptāni - yaduta padmagarbhāṇi digrocanamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi vairocanamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi jagadrocanamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi citrakośamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi siṃhapañjaramaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi vimalamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi maṇiratnaracitapadmagarbhāṇi samantamukhamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi prabhāvyūhamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi sāgarapratiṣṭhānaviśuddhamaṇiratnavyūhasamantaraśmiprabhāsamaṇirājapadmagarbhāṇi
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, gladdened by the virtues of spiritual friends, sent forth by spiritual friends, possessed by the vision of spiritual friends, practicing the instructions of spiritual friends, remembering the words of good counsel, with love following spiritual friends, seeing spiritual friends as the vision of the <s>Buddha</s>, seeing spiritual friends as revealers of the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>, seeing spiritual friends as teachers in the <s>dharma</s>s of omniscience, seeing spiritual friends as eyes for beholding the sky of the <s>Buddha</s> — gradually approached the great park called <s>Samantavyūha</s> (Universal Array) in the region of <s>Samudravetālī</s>. He saw the <s>Samantavyūha</s> great park, enclosed by ramparts of all jewels, adorned with rows of all jewel-trees interspersed [with other trees], releasing fine, subtle flower-pollen from rows of all jewels, embellished with all jewel-trees, strewn with variegated blossoms from the flowers of all jewel-trees, with fragrance issuing in all directions from rows of all fragrant trees, raining down hanging garlands of various jewels released from the sheaths of all garland-trees, with ground adorned with variegated patterns made of gem-jewels from all gem-king trees, with areas well-divided and covered by hanging garments of various colors from all wish-fulfilling flower-trees, resounding with sweet sounds stirred by the wind from all music-trees producing surpassingly divine instrumental music, set on ground level and even, interspersed with no hollows or elevations, adorned with arrays of variegated ornament-streams hanging down released from the sheaths of all ornament-trees. In that <s>Samantavyūha</s> great park there were ten times a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of mansions, adorned with protruding turret-arrays of all great gem-jewels; ten times a hundred thousand pavilions with golden <s>jāmbūnada</s> pinnacles and golden canopies; ten times a hundred thousand aerial palaces with wombs adorned with <s>Vairocana</s> gem-jewels; ten times a hundred thousand lotus-pools made entirely of all jewels, paved with jewel-bricks, with staircases variegated with the seven jewels, surrounded by balustrades of various gem-jewels, fragrant with the flowing waters of divine sandalwood, with ground strewn with golden sand and scattered with golden gem-jewels from ten mansions, with staircases distributed on the four sides, filled with water possessing the eight qualities, resounding with sweet sounds of <s>haṃsas</s> (swans), <s>krauñcas</s> (curlews), peacocks, <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos), <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, and <s>kuṇālas</s>, surrounded by rows of jewel-palms, covered with golden bell-nets producing delightful sounds stirred by the wind, covered above with canopies of great gem-jewels, surrounded by groves of various jewel-trees, illuminated by raised parasol-banner-gem-jewel-nets; and ten times a hundred thousand reservoirs, filled with <s>kālānusāri</s> (finest black) sandalwood mud, covered with variegated-colored lotuses made entirely of all jewels, with stainless waters illuminated by great gem-jewel lotuses. In the center of that park was a great aerial palace called <s>Vicitradhvaja</s> (Variegated Banner), with its ground-level established on ocean-womb jewels, adorned with <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem-jewel pillars, with a pinnacle of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (finest) gold, with floor-panels bound with world-illuminating gem-jewel-womb arrays, blazing with innumerable gem-jewel nets, with approaches perfumed by invincible fragrance gem-kings, with fragrance stirred by well-placed fragrance gem-kings, with the habitation of those of keen faculties dispelled by awakening-fragrance gem-kings. In that <s>Vicitradhvaja</s> great aerial palace, innumerable seats were prepared — namely: lotus-womb [seats], direction-illuminating gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], <s>Vairocana</s> gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], world-illuminating gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], variegated-sheath gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], lion-lattice gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], stainless gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], gem-jewel-fashioned lotus-womb [seats], universal-face gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], radiance-array gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats], ocean-foundation pure gem-jewel-array universal-ray-radiance gem-king lotus-womb [seats],
