vajrasiṃhākrāntamaṇiratnapadmagarbhāṇi / tasya ca vicitradhvajasya mahāvimānasya aneke niryūhā acintyaratnamayā vicitraratnavyūhā acintyavarṇanirbhāsarucirasaṃsthānāḥ / tacca samantavyūhamudyānamupariṣṭāddaśabhirmahāvitānaśatasahasraiḥ saṃchannaṃ yaduta vastravitānairdrumalatāvitānaiḥ puṣpavitānairmālyavitānairgandhavitānairmaṇiratnavitānaiḥ suvarnavitānairābharaṇavitānaiḥ vajraprabhāsamaṇivitānairairāvaṇanāgarājavikurvitāpsarovitānaiḥ śakrābhilagnamaṇiratnavitānaiḥ
/ etatpramukhairdaśabhirvitānaśatasahasraiḥ saṃchannam / daśabhiśca mahāratnajālaśatasahasraiḥ saṃchannam / yaduta ratnagarbhakiṅkiṇījālaiḥ ratnacchatrajālaiḥ ratnabimbajālaiḥ sāgaragarbhamuktājālaiḥ nīlavaiḍūryamaṇiratnajālaiḥ siṃhalatājālaiḥ candrakāntamaṇiratnajālaiḥ gandhavigrahajālaiḥ rantamakuṭajālaiḥ rantahārajālaiḥ / etatpramukhairdaśabhirmahāmaṇiratnajālaśatasahasraiḥ saṃchannam / daśabhiśca mahāvabhāsaśatasahasrairavabhāsitam - yaduta jyotiraśmimaṇiratnāvabhāsena ādityagarbhamaṇiratnāvabhāsena candradhvajamaṇiratnāvabhāsena gandhapradhūpanārcimaṇiratnāvabhāsena śrīgarbhamaṇiratnavabhāsena padmagarbhamaṇiratnāvabhāsena jyotirdhvajamaṇiratnāvabhāsena mahāpradīpamaṇiratnāvabhāsena samantadigvairocanamaṇiratnāvabhāsena mahāgandhameghaniścaritavidyunmālāmaṇiratnāvabhāsena / etatpramukhairdaśabhirmahāmaṇiratnāvabhāsaśatasahasrairnityāvabhāsitaṃ tanmahodyānam / daśamahābharaṇameghaśatasahasrābhivarṣitālaṃkāraṃ ca tanmahodyānaṃ daśakālānusāricandanameghaśatasahasrābhigarjitaṃ daśadivyasamatikrāntamahāmālyadāmameghaśatasahasrābhipralambitopaśobhitaṃ daśadivyasamatikrāntanānāraṅgavicitravastrameghaśatasahasrābhipravarṣitaṃ daśadivyasamatikrāntābharaṇameghaśatasahasravibhūṣitaṃ daśadevaputraśatasahasradarśanakāmādhomukhapraṇatābhipravarṣitaṃ daśāpsaromeghaśatasahasrapūrvasabhāgacaritasvakasvakātmabhāvotsṛjanābhipravarṣitaṃ daśabodhisattvameghaśatasahasradharmaśravaṇatarṣopasaṃkrāntābhipravarṣitaṃ ca tanmahodyānam / yatra āśopāsikā kāñcanagarbhamahābhadrāsanopaviṣṭā sāgaragarbhamuktājālālaṃkṛtā avabaddhamakuṭā divyātirekakanakakeyūravalayabāhuvyūhā śrīkāyaraśmimaṇiratnavirājitabāhuḥ abhinīlavimalavilambamaṇikuṇḍalā mahāratnajālasaṃchannopaśobhitaśīrṣā siṃhamukhamaṇiratnakarṇacūḍakadhāraṇī cintārājamaṇiratnahārāvasaktakaṇṭhā sarvaratnajālasaṃchannaprabhojjvalitaśarīrā prāṇikoṭiniyutaśatasahasrapraṇatakāyā / tatra ye āśāyā upāsikāyāḥ sakāśamaparimāṇāḥ sattvāḥ pūrvasyā diśa āgacchanti,
mahābrahmāṇo vā brahmapurohitā vā brahmakāyikā vā vaśavartino vā paranirmitavaśavartikāyikā vā sunirmitā vā nirmāṇaratikāyikā vā saṃtuṣitā vā tuṣitakāyikā vā suyāmā vā suyāmakāyikā vā devendrā vā trāyastriṃśatkāyikā vā yakṣendrā vā yakṣā vā gandharvendrā vā gandharvā vā kumbhāṇḍendrā vā kumbhāṇḍā vā nāgendrā vā nāgā vā asurendrā vā asurā vā garuḍendrā vā garuḍā va kinnarendrā vā kinnarā vā mahoragendrā va mahoragā vā yamā vā yamakanyā vā, pretamaharddhikā vā pretā vā manuṣyendrā vā manusyā vā / evaṃ ye dakṣiṇāyā vā paścimāyā uttarāyā uttarapūrvāyā pūrvadakṣiṇāyā dakṣiṇapaścimāyāḥ paścimottarāyā adha
body.translated_text: vajra-lion-stride gem-jewel lotus-womb [seats]. And that <s>Vicitradhvaja</s> great aerial palace had many turrets, made of inconceivable jewels, of inconceivable variegated jewel-arrays, of inconceivable beautiful, charming configurations of various colors. And that <s>Samantavyūha</s> park was covered above by ten times a hundred thousand great canopies — namely: cloth canopies, tree-and-vine canopies, flower canopies, garland canopies, fragrance canopies, gem-jewel canopies, golden canopies, ornament canopies, vajra-radiance gem canopies, <s>Airāvaṇa</s> <s>Nāgarāja</s>-transformation-<s>apsaras</s> canopies, <s>Śakra</s>-pendant gem-jewel canopies — headed by these, covered with ten times a hundred thousand canopies. And covered with ten times a hundred thousand great jewel-nets — namely: jewel-womb bell-nets, jewel-parasol nets, jewel-image nets, ocean-womb pearl-nets, blue <s>vaidūrya</s> gem-jewel nets, lion-vine nets, moonstone gem-jewel nets, fragrance-form nets, jewel-crown nets, jewel-necklace nets — headed by these, covered with ten times a hundred thousand great gem-jewel nets. And illuminated by ten times a hundred thousand great radiances — namely: by the radiance of flame-ray gem-jewels, by the radiance of sun-womb gem-jewels, by the radiance of moon-banner gem-jewels, by the radiance of fragrance-incense-flame gem-jewels, by the radiance of splendor-womb gem-jewels, by the radiance of lotus-womb gem-jewels, by the radiance of light-banner gem-jewels, by the radiance of great-lamp gem-jewels, by the radiance of <s>Vairocana</s> gem-jewels illuminating all directions, by the radiance of great-fragrance-cloud-issuing-lightning-garland gem-jewels — headed by these, constantly illuminated by ten times a hundred thousand great gem-jewel radiances, that great park. And showered upon with ornaments by ten times a hundred thousand great ornament-clouds, and that great park was thundered upon by ten times a hundred thousand <s>kālānusāri</s> sandalwood clouds, adorned with hanging garlands surpassing divine [beauty] by ten times a hundred thousand garland-necklace clouds, showered upon with garments of various colors surpassing divine [beauty] by ten times a hundred thousand garment clouds, adorned with ornaments surpassing divine [beauty] by ten times a hundred thousand ornament clouds, showered upon by ten times a hundred thousand <s>devaputra</s>s (divine youths) bowing face-downward desiring to see, showered upon by ten times a hundred thousand <s>apsaras</s>-clouds casting forth their own bodies in accord with their former conduct, and showered upon by ten times a hundred thousand <s>bodhisattva</s>-clouds approaching with thirst for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, that great park. Where the laywoman <s>Āśā</s> sat upon a great golden-womb throne, adorned with ocean-womb pearl-nets, wearing a bound crown, with divine surpassing golden armlets, bracelets, and arm-arrays, with arms radiant with <s>Śrī</s>-body-ray gem-jewels, with dark-blue, stainless, hanging gem-earrings, with head adorned covered with great jewel-nets, bearing lion-face gem-jewel ear-ornaments, with neck adorned with <s>Cintārāja</s> (wish-king) gem-jewel necklaces, with body blazing with radiance covered with nets of all jewels, with hundreds of millions of billions of beings prostrating their bodies before her. And the immeasurable beings who came from the eastern direction to the presence of the laywoman <s>Āśā</s> — great <s>Brahmā</s>s or <s>Brahmapurohitas</s> or <s>Brahmakāyikas</s> or <s>Vaśavartins</s> or <s>Paranirmitavaśavartikāyikas</s> or <s>Sunirmitas</s> or <s>Nirmāṇaratikāyikas</s> or <s>Saṃtuṣitas</s> or <s>Tuṣitakāyikas</s> or <s>Suyāmas</s> or <s>Suyāmakāyikas</s> or <s>Devendras</s> or <s>Trāyastriṃśatkāyikas</s> or <s>Yakṣendras</s> or <s>Yakṣas</s> or <s>Gandharvendras</s> or <s>Gandharvas</s> or <s>Kumbhāṇḍendras</s> or <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s> or <s>Nāgendras</s> or <s>Nāgas</s> or <s>Asurendras</s> or <s>Asuras</s> or <s>Garuḍendras</s> or <s>Garuḍas</s> or <s>Kinnarendras</s> or <s>Kinnaras</s> or <s>Mahoragendras</s> or <s>Mahoragas</s> or <s>Yamas</s> or <s>Yama</s>-maidens or <s>Pretas</s> of great supernatural power or [ordinary] <s>Pretas</s> or lords of humans or humans. Likewise those who came from the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, lower,

body.text: ūrdhvāyā diśa āgacchati / mahābrahmāṇo va brahmapurohitā vā brahmakāyikā vā vaśavartino vā vaśavartikāyikā vā yāvanmanuṣyendrā vā manuṣyā vā āgacchanti nānāvyādhispṛṣṭā nānākleśaparyavasthitā vividhadṛṣṭigatābhiniviṣṭāḥ karmāvaraṇavṛtāḥ, te sahadarśanādāśāyā upāsikāyāḥ sarvavyādhyupaśāntā bhavati / vigatakleśamalacittā apagatadṛṣṭiśalyāḥ sarvāvaraṇaparvatavikīrṇā anāvaraṇaviśuddhimaṇḍalamavataranti / yatra viśuddhimaṇḍale sarvakuśalamūlānyuttapante, sarvendriyāṅkurā vivardhante, sarvajñajñānanayasāgarāḥ samavasaranti / sarvadhāraṇīmukhanayasamudrā āvartante / sarvasamādhimukhanayasamudrā abhimukhībhavanti / sarvapraṇidhānamukhāni saṃjāyante / sarvacaryāmukhāni pravartante / sarvaguṇābhinirhāramukhāni viśudhyante / cittavaipulyatāsarvābhijñāvatinayena pravartante / kāyāsaṅgatā sarvatrānugatā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: and upper directions — great <s>Brahmā</s>s or <s>Brahmapurohitas</s> or <s>Brahmakāyikas</s> or <s>Vaśavartins</s> or <s>Vaśavartikāyikas</s> up to lords of humans or humans — came afflicted by various diseases, beset by various <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), attached to the grip of various [wrong] views, veiled by <s>karma</s>-obstructions. They, immediately upon seeing the laywoman <s>Āśā</s>, had all diseases pacified, their minds purified of the stain of <s>kleśas</s>, the thorns of [wrong] views removed, the mountains of all obstructions scattered, and they entered the circle of unobstructed purification. In that circle of purification, all roots of merit are heated, all sprouts of faculties grow, all oceans of methods of omniscient knowledge assemble, all oceans of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateway methods revolve, all oceans of <s>samādhi</s>-gateway methods come face to face, all gateways of vows are born, all gateways of conduct set in motion, all gateways of quality-production are purified, [they] proceed by the method of the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) of the vast mind, and non-attachment of body, following everywhere, comes about. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantavyūhamudyānaṃ praviśya samantādanuvilokayan adrākṣīdāśāmupāsikāṃ bhadrāsane niṣaṇṇām / sa yena āśopāsikā tenopajagāma / upetya āśāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya āśopāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya etadavocat - mayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, entering the <s>Samantavyūha</s> (Universal Array) garden and looking all around, beheld the lay woman <s>Āśā</s> seated upon an auspicious seat. He approached the lay woman <s>Āśā</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the lay woman <s>Āśā</s>, circumambulated the lay woman <s>Āśā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and said: 'I, O noble lady, have generated the mind toward unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, or how one should conduct oneself. I have heard that the noble lady gives instruction and guidance to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore let the noble lady tell me: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, and how should one conduct oneself?' //

body.text: sā āha - ahaṃ kulaputra, aśokakṣemadhvajasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sāhaṃ kulaputra amoghadarśanā amoghaśravaṇā amoghaparyupāsanā amoghaikavāsasaṃvāsanā amoghānusmaraṇā / nāhaṃ kulaputra, anavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchāmi darśanavijñaptyā, nāparigṛhītakalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ nāsamanvāhṛtasamyaksaṃbuddhānām / mama kulaputra sahadarśanena sattvā avaivartikā bhavantyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / api tu khalu punarme kulaputra, pūrvasyāṃ diśi tathāgatā āgatya iha ratnāsane niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayanti / yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi, evaṃ daśabhyo digbhyaḥ / sāhaṃ kulaputra avirahitā tathāgatadarśanena, avirahitā dharmaśravaṇena, avirahitā bodhisattvasamavadhānena / yānyapīmāni kulaputra caturaśītiḥ prāṇikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi iha samantavyūhe mahodyāne prativasanti, sarvāṇyetānyavaivartikānyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ mama sabhāgacaritāni / ye 'pyanye kulaputra kecidiha sattvāḥ prativasanti, te 'pyavivartyāḥ save 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / avivartyasaṃghasamavasaraṇā mama sabhāgacaritā bodhisattvāḥ / āha - kiyaccirotpāditaṃ tvayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam? āha - ahaṃ kulaputra pūrvenivāsamanusmarāmi, dīpaṃkaraṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham / tasya me tathāgatasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇam / sa ca me tathāgataḥ pūjitaḥ, dharmadeśanā ca me tasyāntikādudgṛhītā / tasya pareṇa vimalo nāma tathāgato 'bhut /
body.translated_text: She replied: 'I, O son of good family, have obtained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Aśokakṣemadhvaja</s> (Banner of Sorrowless Security). I, O son of good family, am one whose seeing is never fruitless, whose hearing is never fruitless, whose attendance is never fruitless, whose cohabitation is never fruitless, whose recollection is never fruitless. I, O son of good family, do not come within the range of vision — through the cognition of seeing — of beings who have not planted roots of merit, nor of those who have not embraced spiritual friends, nor of those who are not blessed by perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>. O son of good family, merely by seeing me, beings become irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. Moreover, O son of good family, from the eastern direction <s>Tathāgatas</s> come and, sitting upon this jewel-seat, teach the <s>Dharma</s>. As from the eastern direction, so from all ten directions. I, O son of good family, am never separated from the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, never separated from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, never separated from the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. These eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousand beings, O son of good family, who dwell here in the great garden of <s>Samantavyūha</s> — all of them are irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, of similar conduct to mine. And whatever other beings, O son of good family, dwell here, they too are all irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. The <s>bodhisattvas</s> of similar conduct to mine assemble in an irreversible community.' He asked: 'How long ago, O noble lady, did you generate the mind toward unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?' She replied: 'I, O son of good family, recall my former abodes. [I recall] <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. Under that <s>Tathāgata</s> I practiced the holy life. That <s>Tathāgata</s> was worshipped by me, and the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching was learned by me in his presence. After him there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vimala</s>.

tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajitā, dharmacakraṃ ca me saṃdhāritam / tasya pareṇa keturnāma tathāgato 'bhūt / sa mayā ārāgitaḥ / tasya pareṇa meruśrīrnāma tathāgato 'bhūt / tasya pareṇa padmagarbho nāma tathāgato 'bhūt / tasya pareṇa vairocano nāma tathāgataḥ / tasya pareṇa samantacakṣurnām tathāgataḥ / tasya pareṇa brahmaśuddho nāma tathāgataḥ / tasya pareṇa vajranābhirnāma tathāgataḥ / tasya pareṇa varuṇadevo nāma tathāgato 'bhut / anena kulaputra paryāyeṇa jātiparaṃparayā kalpaparaṃparayā buddhaparaṃparāmavatarantī anusmaramāṇā tathāgatānarhato 'nantaryatayā ṣaṭtriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālukāsamāṃstathāgatānanusmarāmi, ye mayā ārāgitā upasthitāḥ pūjitā arcitāḥ yeṣāṃ mayā antikāddharmadeśanā śrutā, yeṣāṃ ca me śāsane brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇam / ata uttari kulaputra tathāgatāḥ prajānanti, yāvanto mayā tathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / apramāṇāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ prathamacittotpādenaiva sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇatayā, apramāṇāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ mahākarūṇānayena sarvajagadantargatatayā, apramāṇāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvā mahāpraṇidhānadaśadigdharmadhātutalaniṣṭhānugamanatayā, apramāṇāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvā mahāmaitryā sarvajagatspharaṇatayā, apramāṇāḥ kulaputra, bodhisattvā bodhisattvacaryayā sarvakṣetreṣu sarvakalpasamavasaraṇatayā, apramāṇāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ samādhibalena

body.translated_text: Under his dispensation I went forth, and the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) was upheld by me. After him there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ketu</s>. He was propitiated by me. After him there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Meruśrī</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmagarbha</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vairocana</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samantacakṣus</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Brahmaśuddha</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vajranābhi</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Varuṇadeva</s>. In this manner, O son of good family, descending through the succession of births, the succession of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages), the succession of <s>Buddhas</s>, recollecting [them], I recall <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, in unbroken succession, equal in number to the sands of thirty-six <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers — who were propitiated by me, attended, worshipped, and honored, from whose presence the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching was heard by me, and under whose dispensation the holy life was practiced by me. Beyond this, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> know how many <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. Immeasurable, O son of good family, are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who by their very first generation of the mind pervade the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the method of great compassion dwell within all beings; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through great vows pursue the ultimate ground of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through great loving-kindness pervade all beings; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through <s>bodhisattva</s> practice assemble in all fields throughout all <s>kalpas</s>; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the power of <s>samādhi</s> never turn back from the <s>bodhisattva</s> path; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the power of retention follow the method of <s>dhāraṇī</s> that upholds all beings; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the power of the light of knowledge uphold and follow the knowledge of the three times; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the power of supernatural knowledge accomplish the wheel of radiance-nets according to beings' dispositions in all fields; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through the power of analytical knowledge satisfy all beings with a single utterance; immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who through bodily purity pervade all <s>Buddha</s>-fields with their own bodies' //

na yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvacaryāvāsanānusaṃdhyavataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / naikalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvakleśasamudrāvataraṇāya, na yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvasarvakleśasamudrāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / naikalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvasarvakarmasamudrāvataraṇāya, na yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇūrajasamalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvasarvakarmasamudrāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / naikalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvasarvacaryāsamudrāvataraṇāya, na yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuparyāpannasarvasattvasarvacaryāsamudrāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / api tu aśeṣaniḥśeṣānavaśeṣasarvasattvadhātuparipākavinayāya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / anavaśeṣasarvabuddhārāgaṇābhirādhanapūjopasthānatāyai bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpadyate / anavaśeṣasarvalokadhātuparyāpannasarvabuddhavaṃśārāgaṇābhirādhanapūjopasthānatāyai
body.translated_text: nor up to the worship, propitiation, veneration, and service of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage contained in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for the purification of a single <s>Buddha</s>-field, nor up to the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible world-realms does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for maintaining the teaching of a single <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor up to maintaining the teaching of <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the measurement of the setting-forth and vow of a single <s>Buddha</s>, nor up to entering the measurement of the setting-forth and vow of <s>Buddha</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the array of a single <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field, nor up to entering the array of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the differentiation of the assembly-maṇḍala of a single <s>Buddha</s>, nor up to entering the differentiation of the assembly-maṇḍalas of <s>Buddha</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for maintaining the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of a single <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor up to maintaining the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the ocean of mind of a single being, nor up to entering the ocean of minds of beings equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for comprehending the faculty-wheel of a single being, nor up to comprehending the faculties of beings equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the ocean of faculties of a single being, nor up to entering the ocean of faculties of beings equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the succession of <s>kalpa</s>s of a single world-realm, nor up to entering the succession of <s>kalpa</s>s of world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the investigation of the impressions and conduct of all beings contained in a single world-realm, nor up to entering the investigation of the impressions and conduct of all beings contained in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the ocean of afflictions of all beings contained in a single world-realm, nor up to entering the ocean of all afflictions of all beings contained in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the ocean of all <s>karma</s> of all beings contained in a single world-realm, nor up to entering the ocean of all <s>karma</s> of all beings contained in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Not for entering the ocean of all conduct of all beings contained in a single world-realm, nor up to entering the ocean of all conduct of all beings contained in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields does the aspiration for awakening arise in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Rather, for the ripening and discipline of all beings contained in all world-realms without exception, without remainder, the aspiration for awakening arises in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. For the worship, propitiation, veneration, and service of all <s>Buddha</s>s without remainder, the aspiration for awakening arises in <s>bodhisattva</s>s. bodhisattvānāṃ praṇidhyabhilāṣo bhavati / anavaśeṣasarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanāya bodhisattvānāmāśayo dṛḍhībhavati / anavaśeṣasarvabuddhaśāsanasaṃdhāraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ prayogaḥ saṃbhavati / anavaśeṣasarvatathāgataprasthānapraṇidhivimātratānugamāya bodhisattvānāṃ cittavegāḥ prādurbhavanti / anavaśeṣasarvatathāgatasarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ vyavasāya utpadyate / anavaśeṣasarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāmabhilāṣaḥ prabhavati / anavaśeṣasarvajagaccittasāgarāvagāhanatāyai bodhisattvānāṃ prārthanā saṃjāyate / anavaśeṣasarvasattvendriyacakraparijñāyai bodhisattvānāmabhikāṅkṣotpadyate / anavaśeṣasarvasattvendriyasāgarāvataraṇatāyai bodhisattvānāmutsoḍhirājāyate / anavaśeṣasarvalokadhātukalpaparaṃparāvataraṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ chandaḥ saṃbhavati / anavaśeṣasarvasattvakleśavāsanānusaṃdhisamucchedāya bodhisattvānāṃ parākrama ājāyate / anavaśeṣasarvasattvakarmakleśasamudrocchoṣaṇāya bodhisattvānāṃ mahājñānasūrya udāgacchati / anavaśeṣasarvasattvacaryāparijñāyai bodhisattvānāṃ prajñālokaḥ prādurbhavati / anavaśeṣasarvasattvaduḥkhāgniskandhapraśamanāya bodhisattvānāṃ mahākarūṇāmeghaḥ samudāgacchati / saṃkṣepaeṇa kulaputra etatpramukhāni daśa bodhisattvacaryānayamukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi, yāni bodhisattvena samudānayitavyāni / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra sarvadharmasamavasaraṇā bodhisattvānāṃ caryā yaduta jñānānugamāya / sarvakṣetrasamavasaraṇā bodhisattvānāṃ caryā yaduta pariśodhanatāyai / tasyā mama kulaputra evaṃpraṇidheryanniṣṭhā kāma dhātuviśuddhiḥ, tanniṣṭhāni mama praṇidhānāni
bhavantu / yanniṣṭhā lokadhātuviśuddhiḥ, tanniṣṭhāni mama praṇidhānāni bhavantu / yā niṣṭhā sarvasattvakleśavāsanānusaṃdhyanuśayānām, tanniṣṭhāni mama praṇidhānāni bhavantu //
body.translated_text: the aspirational longing of <s>bodhisattva</s>s arises. For the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields without remainder, the disposition of <s>bodhisattva</s>s becomes firm. For maintaining the teaching of all <s>Buddha</s>s without remainder, the exertion of <s>bodhisattva</s>s comes into being. For following the measurement of the setting-forth and vows of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s without remainder, the surges of mind of <s>bodhisattva</s>s manifest. For entering the quality-arrays of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s without remainder, the resolve of <s>bodhisattva</s>s arises. For entering the ocean of assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s without remainder, the aspiration of <s>bodhisattva</s>s arises. For plunging into the ocean of minds of all beings in the world without remainder, the prayer of <s>bodhisattva</s>s is born. For comprehending the faculty-wheel of all beings without remainder, the longing of <s>bodhisattva</s>s arises. For entering the ocean of faculties of all beings without remainder, the endurance of <s>bodhisattva</s>s is born. For entering the succession of <s>kalpa</s>s of all world-realms without remainder, the desire of <s>bodhisattva</s>s comes into being. For completely cutting off the connections of the impressions of afflictions of all beings without remainder, the prowess of <s>bodhisattva</s>s is born. For drying up the ocean of <s>karma</s> and afflictions of all beings without remainder, the great sun of knowledge of <s>bodhisattva</s>s rises. For comprehending the conduct of all beings without remainder, the light of wisdom of <s>bodhisattva</s>s manifests. For pacifying the mass of fire of suffering of all beings without remainder, the great cloud of compassion of <s>bodhisattva</s>s arises. In brief, son of good family, led by these, there are innumerable hundreds of thousands of gates of methods of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct that a <s>bodhisattva</s> must bring together. Moreover, son of good family, the conduct of <s>bodhisattva</s>s converges with all <s>dharma</s>s — that is, for the following of knowledge. The conduct of <s>bodhisattva</s>s converges with all fields — that is, for purification. As for my vow, son of good family — whatever the end of the purification of the desire-realm, may my vows have that as their end. Whatever the end of the purification of the world-realm, may my vows have that as their end. Whatever the end of the impressions, connections, and latent tendencies of the afflictions of all beings, may my vows have that as their end. //

body.text: āha - ko nāma ārye eṣa vimokṣaḥ? āha - aśokakṣemadhvajo nāma kulaputra eṣa vimokṣaḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra, ekaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sāgarasamacittānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhadharmasaṃpratīcchanatayā, merukalpānāṃ dṛḍhādhyāśayatayā, sudarśanabhaiṣajyarājopamānāṃ sarvasattvakleśavyādhipramokṣaṇatayā, ādityakalpānāṃ sarvasattvāvidyāndhakāravidhamanatayā, dharaṇīsamacittānāṃ sarvasattvāśrayapratiṣṭhānabhūtatayā, mārūtasadṛśānāṃ sarvajagadarthakaraṇatayā, pradīpabhūtānāṃ sarvasattvajñānālokakaraṇatayā, meghopamānāṃ śāntanirghoṣayathāvaddharmapravarṣaṇatayā, candropamānāṃ puṇyaraśmijālapramocanatayā, śakropamānāṃ sarvajagadārakṣāpratipannatayā caryā jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, acintyā vā bodhisattvaśikṣāḥ prabhāvayitum, anantamadhyā vā bodhisattvapraṇidhivikalpāḥ saṃdarśayitum //
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Noble one, what is the name of this liberation?' She replied: 'Son of good family, this liberation is called <s>Aśokakṣemadhvaja</s> (Banner of Grief-free Security). This is the one <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation that I know, son of good family. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the qualities, of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s whose minds are like the ocean in receiving all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, who are like <s>Meru</s> in the firmness of their higher aspirations, who are like the healing king <s>Sudarśana</s> in liberating all beings from the diseases of afflictions, who are like the sun in dispelling the darkness of all beings' ignorance, whose minds are like the earth in being the true ground and support for all beings, who are like the wind in accomplishing the welfare of all the world, who are lamps in creating the light of knowledge for all beings, who are like clouds in raining the <s>Dharma</s> properly with peaceful sound, who are like the moon in releasing nets of rays of merit, who are like <s>Śakra</s> in being devoted to the protection of all the world — or to illuminate the inconceivable <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings, or to display the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vow-distinctions that are infinite and without middle? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe samudravetālyāṃ nālayurnāma janapadaḥ / tatra bhīṣmottaranirghoṣo nāma ṛṣiḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha / sa te kulaputra bodhisattvacaryāmupadekṣyati //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region), by the sea-cane thicket, is a country called <s>Nālayur</s>. There dwells a <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) named <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of Supreme Awe). Approach him and ask. He, son of good family, will instruct you in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidāraka āśāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya āśāmupāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya praṇipatya aśrumukho rudan bodhiparamadurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, kalyāṇamitradurārāgaṇatāmanuvicintayan, satpuruṣasamavadhānasudurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, bodhisattvendriyapratilābhadurabhisaṃbhavatāmanuvicintayan, bodhisattvāśayaviśuddhidurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, sabhāgamitrasamavadhānadurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, yathāvadbodhyabhimukhacittanidhyaptidurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, aviṣamadharmanayānuśāsanīprayogadurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, asaṃhāryacittakalyāṇatāyogasaṃjananadurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, sarvajñatāvegavivardhanadharmālokasudurlabhatāmanuvicintayan, āśāyā upāsikāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 8 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of the <s>upāsikā</s> (lay-woman) <s>Āśā</s>, circumambulating the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Āśā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, prostrating, with tear-streaked face, weeping — reflecting upon the supreme rarity of <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening), reflecting upon the rarity of the excellence of spiritual friends, reflecting upon the supreme rarity of the occasion of meeting good persons, reflecting upon the difficulty of attaining <s>Bodhisattva</s>-faculties, reflecting upon the rarity of the purification of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-aspiration, reflecting upon the rarity of the occasion of meeting a kindred spiritual friend, reflecting upon the rarity of attaining the true inclination of mind toward awakening, reflecting upon the rarity of the application of instruction in the undistorted <s>dharma</s>-method, reflecting upon the rarity of generating the yoga of goodness with an unshakeable mind, reflecting upon the supreme rarity of the light of <s>dharma</s> that augments the impetus toward omniscience — departed from the presence of the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Āśā</s>. // 8 //

body.text: 11 Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: 11. <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>. /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bodhisattvānuśāsanyanugatacitto bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhanānugatacitto bodhisattvapuṇyabalavivardhanacitto buddhadarśanavegāvabhāsitacitto dharmanidhānapratilābhasaṃjātacittavego mahāpraṇidhānābhinirhārapravardhitacittavegaḥ sarvadharmadigabhimukhacitto dharmasvabhāvāvabhāsitacittaḥ sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇacitto nirandhakāradharmadhātuvyavalokanacitto nārāyaṇavajraratnābhedyavimalāśayacittaḥ sarvamārabaladuryodhanadurdharṣaṇacitto 'nupūrveṇa yena nālayurjanapadaḥ tenopasaṃkramya bhīṣmottaranirghoṣamṛṣimanveṣate sma / tena ca samayena bhīṣmottaranirghoṣarṣiranyatamasminnāśramapade viharati sma asaṃkhyeyavicitradrumalatāvanaramaṇīye vividhavṛkṣapatrasaṃchanne sadāpraphullitavicitrapuṣpavṛkṣe sadāphalopacitaphalavṛkṣe nānāratnavṛkṣodāramaṇiphalakasaṃskṛtatale suvibhaktamahācandanadrume manojñāgaruvṛkṣasadāpramuktagandhopaśobhite caturdikṣuvibhaktagandhopaśobhite caturdikṣu vibhaktapāṭalīvṛkṣasamalaṃkṛte nyagrodhavṛkṣapādaparucirasaṃsthāne sadāpakvaphalajambūvṛkṣapravarṣaṇe navanalinīpadmotpalakumudopaśobhite / adrākṣītsudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bhīṣmottaranirghoṣamṛṣiṃ daśaṛṣisahasraparivṛtaṃ candanatalāvabaddhāyāṃ kuṭyāṃ jaṭāmakuṭadhāriṇamajinadarbhacīvaravalkalavasanaṃ tṛṇasaṃstaropaviṣṭam / dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa ṛṣistenopajagāma / upetya bhūtakalyāṇamitrapratilambanāśayakalyāṇamitrāyadvārāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, bhūtamārgopanayāya kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyadhīnāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, sarvajñatābhūmyupanayena kalyāṇamitradāsādhīnāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, daśabalajñānaratnadvīpopanayena kalyāṇamitrolkāvabhāsitāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, daśabalajñānālokasaṃjananatayā kalyāṇamitramārgāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, akṣuṇṇasarvajñatāpuraprāpaṇatayā kalyāṇamitrapradīpāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, samaviṣamasaṃdarśanatayā kalyāṇamitraṃ setuṃ sarvajñatāyāḥ saṃpaśyan, sarvaprapātabhayavigamanatayā kalyāṇamitracchatrāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, mahāmaitrībalāhlādasaṃjananatayā kalyāṇamitravegāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, mahākaruṇāsaṃjananatayā kalyāṇamitrādhīnāṃ sarvajñatādarśanaparipuṣṭiṃ saṃpaśyan, dharmasvabhāvanayāvabhāsanatayā sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya utthāya bhīṣmottaranirghoṣamṛṣiṃ
anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya prāñjalibhūtaḥ purataḥ sthitvā manojñopacāreṇa manojñāṃ vācamudīrayan evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, with a mind following the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-instruction, with a mind intent upon purifying the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, with a mind for augmenting the power of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-merit, with a mind illuminated by the impetus of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, with a mental impetus born from attaining the treasury of <s>Dharma</s>, with a mental impetus augmented by the accomplishment of great vows, with a mind facing all directions of <s>Dharma</s>, with a mind illuminated by the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>s, with a mind for scattering all obstructions, with a mind for beholding the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> free from darkness, with an aspiration-mind as indestructible as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s diamond-jewel, with a mind undaunted in conquering the forces of all <s>Māra</s>s — gradually proceeded to the country of <s>Nālayur</s> and searched for the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>. At that time, the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> was dwelling in a certain hermitage — delightful with innumerable variegated trees and creepers, covered with the leaves of various trees, with variegated flower-trees always in full bloom, with fruit-trees always laden with ripe fruit, with a ground-surface adorned with platforms of exalted <s>maṇi</s>-jewels from various gem-trees, with well-distributed great sandalwood trees, embellished with charming <s>aguru</s> (aloe) trees constantly releasing fragrance, adorned with <s>pāṭalī</s> (trumpet-flower) trees distributed in the four directions, with beautiful <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree formations, with <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) trees always raining ripe fruit, adorned with fresh water-lilies, lotuses, <s>utpala</s>s, and <s>kumuda</s>s. <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>, surrounded by ten thousand <s>ṛṣi</s>s, in a hut set upon a sandalwood platform, wearing matted locks bound in a topknot, clad in antelope-skin, <s>darbha</s>-grass robes, and bark garments, seated upon a grass-mat. Having seen him, he approached where the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> was. Having approached — seeing omniscience as dependent on the genuine aspiration of leaning upon spiritual friends, the gateway through the spiritual friend to omniscience; seeing omniscience as dependent on the instruction of the spiritual friend, for the guidance to the true path; seeing omniscience as dependent on the servitude to the spiritual friend, for the guidance to the stage of omniscience; seeing omniscience illuminated by the torch of the spiritual friend, for the guidance to the jewel-island of the knowledge of the ten powers; seeing omniscience as the path of the spiritual friend, for generating the light of the knowledge of the ten powers; seeing omniscience as the lamp of the spiritual friend, for the guidance to the unimpaired city of omniscience; seeing the spiritual friend as a bridge to omniscience, for showing the even and uneven; seeing omniscience as the umbrella of the spiritual friend, for the departure from the fear of all precipices; seeing omniscience as the impetus of the spiritual friend, for generating the delight of the power of great loving-kindness; seeing the nourishment of the vision of omniscience as dependent on the spiritual friend, for generating great compassion; seeing [all this] through the illumination of the method of the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>s — he prostrated with his entire body, rising, circumambulated the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before him with palms joined, and speaking in a delightful manner with delightful words, said thus: 'Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (Complete Awakening). But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how he should practice. And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and exhortation to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble one tell me: how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should he practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu bhīṣmottaranirghoṣaṛṣistāni daśa māṇavakasahasrāṇyanuvilokya evamāhaanena māṇavakāḥ kulaputreṇa anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / sarvasattvāścābhayenopanimantritāḥ / ayaṃ sa kulaputrāḥ sarvasattvahitasukhāya pratyupasthito jñānasāgarābhimukhaḥ
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>, looking upon those ten thousand young men, spoke thus: 'Young men, this son of good family has generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s> and has invited all beings with fearlessness. This son of good family, O sons of good family, stands ready for the happiness and welfare of all beings, facing the ocean of knowledge,

body.text: sarvatathāgatānāṃ dharmameghān dhātukāmaḥ sarvadharmanayasāgarānavagāhayitukāmaḥ mahājñānāloke 'vasthātukāmo mahākaruṇāmeghamupasthāpayitukāmo mahādharmavarṣamabhipravarṣayitukāmo mahājñānāloke candre udāgatya sarvakleśapratāpaṃ praśamayitukāmo sarvasattvakuśalamūlāni vardhayitukāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: desiring to uphold the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, desiring to plunge into the oceans of all <s>dharma</s>-methods, desiring to abide in the great light of knowledge, desiring to bring forth the cloud of great compassion, desiring to rain the great rain of <s>Dharma</s>, desiring to pacify the scorching heat of all afflictions like the moon risen in the great light of knowledge, desiring to augment the roots of merit of all beings.' //

body.text:
atha khalu tāni daśa māṇavakasahasrāṇi nānāvarṇaiḥ suruciraiḥ sugandhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamavakīrya abhyavakīrya abhivandya namaskṛtvā praṇipatya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya evaṃ vācamudīrayāmāsuḥ - eṣa trātā bhaviṣyati, sarvasattvānāṃ sarvanirayaduḥkhāni praśamayiṣyati / sarvatiryagyonigatiṃ vyavacchetsyati / sarvayamalokagatiṃ vinivartayiṣyati / sarvākṣaṇadvārakapāṭāni pithapayiṣyati / tṛṣṇāsamudramucchoṣayiṣyati / tṛṣṇābandhanaṃ chetsyati / duḥkhaskandhaṃ vinivartayiṣyati / avidyāndhakāraṃ vidhamayiṣyati / puṇyacakravālaṃ loke parisaṃsthāpayiṣyati / jñānaratnākaramupadarśayiṣyati / jñānasūryamudāgamiṣyati / dharmacakṣurviśodhayiṣyati / samaviṣamaṃ loke saṃprakāśayiṣyati / atha khalu bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa ṛṣiḥ tān māṇavakānevamāha - yena māṇavakā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ bhavati, sa bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran sarvasattvānāṃ sukhamutpādayati, anupūrveṇa ca sarvajñatāṃ pratilabhate / anena māṇavakāḥ kulaputreṇa anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / sa eṣa sarvabuddhaguṇabhūmiṃ paripūrayiṣyati / atha khalu bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa ṛṣiḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ahaṃ kulaputra aparājitadhvajasya bodhisattvasya vimokṣasya lābhī / sudhana āha - ka etasya ārya aparājitadhvajasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ? tato bhīṣmāttaranirghoṣaṛṣiḥ dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ śirasi parimārjya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā paryagṛhṇāt / samanantaraparigṛhītaśca sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bhīṣmottaranirghoṣeṇa ṛṣiṇā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā, atha tāvadeva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'paśyaddaśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi / teṣu ca daśabuddhakṣetraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ pādamūlagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānāti sma / tāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇyapaśyadasaṃkhyeyākāraviśuddhavyūhāni / teṣu ca tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānnānāvarṇavicitravyūhānapaśyat / teṣu ca parṣanmaṇḍalasamudreṣu tathāgataśarīrāṇi lakṣaṇānuvyañjanojjvalitopacitānyapaśyat / tebhyaśca dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇotyekapadavyañjanāparāṅbhukhām / tāni ca tathāgatadharmacakrāṇyanyonyāsaṃbhinnāni saṃdhārayati / tāṃśca dharmameghānnānāsattvāśayeṣu pravarṣaṇāṃ saṃpratīcchati / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ nānādhimuktibalaviśodhitaṃ
pūrvapraṇidhānasamudrānavatarati / tāṃśca nānāpraṇidhānasāgaraviśuddhān buddhasamudāgamasamudrānavatarati / tāṃśca yathāśayasarvasattvasahasrasaṃtoṣaṇavijñāpanān buddhavarṇānadrākṣīt / tāni ca buddharaśmijālāni nānāvirāgaviśuddhavyūhamaṇḍalānyapaśyat / tāni ca buddhabalānyanāvaraṇajñānālokānugamenāvatarati / sa kvacittathāgatapādamūle rātriṃdivaṃ saṃjānāti / kvacitsapta rātriṃdivāni, kvacidardhamāsam, kvacinmāsam,kvacitsaṃvatsaraṃ kvacidvarṣaśataṃ kvacidvarṣasahasraṃ kvacidvarṣaśatasahasraṃ kvacidvarṣakoṭiṃ
body.translated_text: Then indeed those ten thousand young men, showering and scattering the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> with flowers of various colors — beautiful and fragrant — bowing, saluting, prostrating, circumambulating, spoke these words: 'He shall become the Savior! He shall pacify the suffering of all hell-realms for all beings. He shall cut off the destinies of all animal-births. He shall turn back the course of the world of <s>Yama</s>. He shall close the gate-doors of all unfortunate destinies and downfalls. He shall dry up the ocean of craving. He shall cut the bonds of craving. He shall turn back the mass of suffering. He shall dispel the darkness of ignorance. He shall establish the <s>Cakravāla</s> (world-encircling mountain) of merit in the world. He shall reveal the jewel-mine of knowledge. He shall cause the sun of knowledge to rise. He shall purify the eye of <s>Dharma</s>. He shall illuminate the even and uneven in the world.' Then indeed the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> spoke thus to those young men: 'Young men, when one has generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, that one, practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, produces happiness for all beings and gradually attains omniscience. This son of good family, O sons of good family, has generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s>. He shall fulfill the entire ground of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities.' Then indeed the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Son of good family, I am the recipient of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Aparājitadhvaja</s> (Unconquered Banner).' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'Noble one, what is the domain of this <s>Aparājitadhvaja Bodhisattva</s>-liberation?' Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>, extending his right hand, stroked <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son on the head and grasped him with his right hand. And immediately upon being grasped by the right hand of the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he recognized himself as being present at the feet of <s>Tathāgata</s>s in those fields equal in number to the atoms of ten times a hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he saw those <s>Buddha</s>-fields adorned with innumerable purified array-forms. And in them he saw oceans of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles of various colors and variegated arrays. And in those oceans of assembly-circles he saw <s>Tathāgata</s>-bodies blazing and adorned with marks and minor marks. And from them he heard <s>Dharma</s>-teachings whose words and syllables were inexhaustible. And he retained those <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakra</s>s, undifferentiated from one another. And he received those <s>Dharma</s>-clouds raining upon the various dispositions of beings. And he descended into the oceans of former vows of those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, purified through the power of various higher aspirations. And he descended into the oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-attainment purified through various oceans of vows. And he saw those <s>Buddha</s>-colors, cognitions satisfying hundreds of thousands of all beings according to their dispositions. And he saw those <s>Buddha</s> ray-nets, <s>maṇḍala</s>s of arrays purified through various dispassions. And he descended into those <s>Buddha</s>-powers by following the light of unobstructed knowledge. And at some <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet he perceived a day and a night, at some seven days and nights, at some half a month, at some a month, at some a year, at some a hundred years, at some a thousand years, at some a hundred thousand years, at some a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of years,

body.text: kvacidvarṣakoṭīśataṃ kvacidvarṣakoṭisahasraṃ kvacidvarṣakoṭīśatasahasraṃ kvacidvarṣakoṭyayutaṃ kvacidvarṣakoṭīniyutaṃ kvacidardhakalpaṃ saṃjānāti / kvacitkalpaṃ kvacitkalpaśataṃ kvacitkalpasahasraṃ kvacitkalpaśatasahasraṃ kvacitkalpakoṭīṃ kvacitkalpakoṭīśataṃ kvacitkalpakoṭīsahasraṃ kvacitkalpakoṭīśatasahasraṃ kvacitkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraṃ kvacittathāgatapādamūle yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyān kalpān saṃjānāti / kvacittathāgatapādamūle jambūdvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān saṃjānāti / kvacidyāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān saṃjānāti aparājitadhvajabodhisattvavimokṣajñānāvabhāsito vairocanagarbhasamādhyavabhāsapratilabdhaḥ akṣayajñānavimokṣasamādhyanugataḥ samantadikpañjaradhāraṇīmukhāvalokapratilabdho vajramaṇḍaladhāraṇīmukhāvabhāsitacittaḥ suvibhaktajñānakūṭaviṣayasamādhivihārapratilabdhaḥ samantatalavyūhamārgaprajñāpāramitāvihāraviṣayo buddhagaganagarbhamaṇḍalasamādhyālokaprasṛtaḥ sarvabuddhadharmacakranemisamādhyavabhāsitacittaḥ tryadhvajñānaratnākṣayamaṇḍalasamādhyālokaprāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Sometimes he perceives a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of years, sometimes a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years, sometimes a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years, sometimes ten thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years, sometimes a <s>niyuta</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of years, sometimes half a <s>kalpa</s>. Sometimes a <s>kalpa</s>, sometimes a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a <s>niyuta</s> of hundred thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> he perceives up to inexpressibly inexpressible <s>kalpas</s>. Sometimes at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> he perceives <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Sometimes he perceives <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields — illuminated by the knowledge of the <s>Aparājitadhvaja</s> (Unconquered Banner) <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), having attained the illumination of the <s>Vairocanagarbha</s> (Womb of Vairocana) <s>samādhi</s>, following the <s>Akṣayajñānavimokṣa</s> (Inexhaustible Knowledge Liberation) <s>samādhi</s>, having attained the vision of the <s>Samantadikpañjara</s> (Universal Cage of Directions) <s>dhāraṇī</s> gate, his mind illuminated by the <s>Vajramaṇḍala</s> (Diamond Circle) <s>dhāraṇī</s> gate, having attained the <s>samādhi</s> abode in the domain of the <s>Suvibhaktajñānakūṭa</s> (Well-Divided Wisdom Peak), dwelling in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> path of the <s>Samantatala</s> (Universal Ground) display, extending into the light of the <s>Buddhagaganagarbhamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of the Womb of Buddha-Sky) <s>samādhi</s>, his mind illuminated by the <s>Sarvabuddhadharmacakranemi</s> (Rim of the Dharma-Wheel of All Buddhas) <s>samādhi</s>, having attained the light of the <s>Tryadhvajñānaratnākṣayamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of the Inexhaustible Jewel of Three-Time Wisdom) <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa ṛṣiḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ vyamuñcat / sa punarapi bhīṣmottaranirghoṣasya ṛṣeḥ purataḥ sthitamātmānaṃ saṃjānāti / taṃ bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa ṛṣirāha - smarasi kulaputra? āha - smarāmi ārya kalyāṇamitrādhiṣṭhānena / āha - etamahaṃ kulaputra aparājitadhvajaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvajagadviśeṣajñānābhijñāvatārasamādhipratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakālacakravaśavartināṃ buddhalakṣaṇajñānābhinirhārakuśalānāṃ tathāgatadivasāvakrāntivijñaptivyūhānāṃ tryadhvaviṣayaikalakṣaṇajñānasamavasaraṇānāṃ sarvalokadhātusuvibhaktakāyānāṃ sarvadharmadhātvavabhāsitajñānaśarīrāṇāṃ sarvasattvayathāśayābhimukhābhyutthitānāṃ yathāśayasattvacaryāvicārānukūlopacārāṇāṃ samantābhirucitarocanānām amalavipularucirajñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhānāṃ caryā jñātuṃ guṇā vā vaktuṃ praṇidhiviśeṣo vā sūcayituṃ kṣetrābhisaṃskāro vā jñātuṃ jñānaviṣayo avagāhituṃ samādhigocaro vā anusartuṃ ṛdvivikurvitaṃ vā avatarituṃ vimokṣavṛṣabhitāvikrīḍitaṃ vā anugantuṃ śarīravibhaktinimittaṃ vā udgrahītuṃ svaramaṇḍalaviśuddhirvā prabhāvayituṃ jñānāvabhāso vā nidarśayitum //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> released the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>. He again perceived himself standing before the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>. The <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> said to him — "Do you remember, son of good family?" He replied — "I remember, noble one, through the empowerment of the spiritual friend." He said — "I, son of good family, know this <s>Aparājitadhvaja</s> (Unconquered Banner) <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s>. But how could I know the conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the <s>samādhi</s> of entering the superknowledge of the distinctive wisdom of all beings, who are masters of the wheel of all times, who are skilled in manifesting the wisdom of the marks of a <s>Buddha</s>, who display the array of the manifestation of entry into the day of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who converge in the single-characteristic wisdom of the domain of the three times, who have well-distributed bodies throughout all world-realms, whose wisdom-bodies are illuminated by all <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), who arise facing the dispositions of all beings, whose conduct accords with and attends to the courses of beings according to their dispositions, who are universally delightful and brilliant, whose pure, stainless, vast, and resplendent wisdom-circles are purified — how could I know their conduct, or speak of their qualities, or indicate the distinction of their vows, or know their field-purification, or fathom the domain of their wisdom, or follow the range of their <s>samādhi</s>, or enter their miraculous transformations, or follow the play of their eminence in liberation, or grasp the signs of their body-distributions, or illuminate the purity of their voice-circles, or demonstrate the radiance of their wisdom?"

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe īṣāṇo nāma janapadaḥ / tatra jayoṣmāyatano nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: "Go, son of good family, here in the southern region there is a country called <s>Īṣāṇa</s>. There dwells a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s>. Approach him and ask — 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?'"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhīṣmottaranirghoṣasya ṛṣeḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhīṣmottaranirghoṣaṃ ṛṣimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya bhīṣmottaranirghoṣasya ṛṣerantikātprakrāntaḥ // 9 //
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, filled with gladness and happiness, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>, circumambulated the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa</s>. [9]

body.text: 12 jayoṣmāyatanaḥ /
body.translated_text: 12. <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s>

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'parājitadhvajabodhisattvavimokṣajñānāvabhāsitaḥ acintyabuddhaviṣayavikurvitapratyakṣavihārī acintyabodhisattvavimokṣapratyakṣajñānābhijñaḥ acintyabodhisattvasamādhijñānāvabhāsitacittaḥ sarvakālasamavasaraṇasamādhijñānāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ sarvasaṃjñāsaṃgatasamavasaraṇasamādhiviṣayāvabhāsitaḥ sarvajagadviśeṣavatijñānālokapratilabdhaḥ sarvatryadhvānugatagocaravihārābhimukhaḥ advayavikalpasamatānirdeśajñānaparamaḥ sarvārambaṇaprasaritajñānālokaḥ sattvaśraddhābhimukhakṣāntiviśuddhayadhimuktikośakuśalaḥ svabhāvadharmakṣāntiniścayajñānālokapratilabdhaḥ sarvatrānugatābhijñabodhisattvacaryāsvabhāvabhāvanāvirahitacittaḥ sarvajñatāvegāvivartyacitto daśabalajñānavidyudavabhāsapratilabdhaḥ dharmadhātunirghoṣābhilāṣāvitṛptacittaḥ sarvajñatāvihāragocarāvataraṇapratipatticittaḥ anantabodhisattvacaryāvyūhābhinirhāracitto 'nantabodhisattvamahāpraṇidhānamaṇḍalapariśodhanacittaḥ anantamadhyalokadhātujālākṣayānugamajñānābhimukhacittaḥ anantasattvasāgaraparipākavinayāsaṃkucitacittaḥ anantabodhisattvacaryāviṣayaṃ saṃpaśyan anantalokadhātugativimātratāṃ saṃpaśyan anantalokadhātuvibhaktivicitratāṃ saṃpaśyan ananta lokadhātusūkṣmodārārambaṇāntargatāṃ saṃpaśyan anantalokadhātupratiṣṭhānasaṃjñājālavicitritāṃ saṃpaśyan anantalokadhātuvyavahāraprajñaptisaṃvṛtivimātratāṃ saṃpaśyan anantasattvādhimuktivimātratāṃ saṃpaśyan anantasattvavibhaktivimātratāṃ saṃpaśyan anantasattvaparipākavinayānugamaṃ saṃpaśyan anantasattvadikkālasaṃjñāgatavicitratāṃ saṃpaśyan kalyāṇamitrāṇyabhimukhīkurvāṇo 'nupūrveṇa yena īṣāṇe janapade jayoṣmāyatano brāhmaṇaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / tena ca samayena jayoṣmāyatano brāhmaṇa ugraṃ tapaḥ tapyati sarvajñatāmārambaṇīkṛtya / tasya caturdiśaṃ mahānagniskandhaḥ parvatamātrojjvalitaḥ / abhyudgatamahāparvataprapātaḥ kṣuradhārāmārgaḥ saṃdṛśyate //
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>, illuminated by the knowledge of the <s>Aparājitadhvaja</s> <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s>, directly abiding in the inconceivable miraculous displays of the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, possessing superknowledge and direct wisdom of the inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s>, his mind illuminated by the inconceivable wisdom of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, having attained the illumination of the wisdom of the <s>samādhi</s> of the convergence of all times, illuminated by the domain of the <s>samādhi</s> of the convergence of all perceptions, having obtained the light of the distinctive wisdom of all beings, facing the abode and range that follows all three times, supreme in the wisdom of teaching the equality of non-dual discrimination, with the light of wisdom extending to all objects, skilled in the treasure of the resolution purified through faith directed toward beings, having obtained the light of definitive wisdom of the patient acceptance of the nature of phenomena, his mind never separated from the cultivation of the nature of the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of superknowledge following everywhere, his mind irreversible with the momentum toward omniscience, having obtained the flash-of-lightning illumination of the wisdom of the ten powers, his mind unsatisfied with longing for the sound of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, his mind set on the practice of entering the range of the abode of omniscience, his mind directed toward manifesting the array of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, his mind set on purifying the circle of infinite great <s>bodhisattva</s> vows, his mind facing the wisdom of following the inexhaustible net of infinite intermediate world-realms, his mind undaunted in ripening and disciplining the ocean of infinite beings, perceiving the infinite domain of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, perceiving the diversity of destinies in infinite world-realms, perceiving the variety of divisions of infinite world-realms, perceiving the entering into the subtle and vast objects of infinite world-realms, perceiving the variety of the net of notions of the foundations of infinite world-realms, perceiving the diversity of conventional designations and transactions of infinite world-realms, perceiving the diversity of the resolutions of infinite beings, perceiving the diversity of the distinctions of infinite beings, perceiving the following of the ripening and discipline of infinite beings, perceiving the variety of the notions of direction and time of infinite beings — approaching his spiritual friends, he gradually went to where the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s> was in the country of <s>Īṣāṇa</s>. At that time, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s> was performing fierce austerities, having taken omniscience as his object. In the four directions, a great mass of fire blazed, mountain-high. A razor-edged path with a great mountain precipice was visible.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako jayoṣmāyatanasya brāhmaṇasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam, śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / sa āha - gaccha kulaputra, etaṃ kṣuradhāramārgaṃ parvatamabhiruhya atra agnikhadāyāṃ prapata / evaṃ te bodhisattvacaryā pariśuddhiṃ gamiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s>, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus — "Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one should practice. And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the noble one tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?" He replied — "Go, son of good family, climb this mountain by the razor-edged path and cast yourself into this fire-pit. Thus your <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct will be purified."

body.text: atha khalu sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya etadabhavat - durlabhā aṣṭākṣaṇavinivṛttiḥ / durlabho mānuṣyapratilābhaḥ / durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpadviśuddhiḥ / durlabho buddhotpādaḥ / durlabhā avikalendriyatā / durlabho buddhadharmaśravaḥ / durlabhaṃ satpuruṣasamavadhānam / durlabhāni bhūtakalyāṇamitrāṇi / durlabho bhūtanayānuśāsanopasaṃhāraḥ / durlabhaṃ samyagjīvitaṃ manuṣyaloke / durlabhā dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ / mā haivāyaṃ māro bhaviṣyati mārādhiṣṭhito vā mārakāyiko vā kalyāṇamitrapratirūpako vā bodhisattvakhaṇḍako vā, yo mama kuśalamūlāntarāyāya pratipannaḥ, yo mama jīvitanirodhāya
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s> thought — "Rare is the freedom from the eight unfavorable conditions. Rare is the attainment of human birth. Rare is the purity of the opportune moment. Rare is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>. Rare is the completeness of the faculties. Rare is hearing the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>. Rare is the association with good people. Rare are true spiritual friends. Rare is the guidance of true teaching. Rare is right livelihood in the human world. Rare is the practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Could this be <s>Māra</s>, or one empowered by <s>Māra</s>, or a being of <s>Māra</s>'s host, or one disguised as a spiritual friend, or one who destroys <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who has set out to obstruct my roots of merit, who has arisen to end my life —

body.text: abhyutthitaḥ / mā haiva mamāntarāyaṃ kartukāmaḥ sarvajñatāyām / mā khalu māṃ viṣameṇa pathā praṇetukāmaḥ / mā khalu me dharmamukhāntarāyaṃ kartukāmo buddhadharmādhigamāya / tasyaivaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayuktasya daśa brahmasahasrāṇyuparyantarikṣe sthitvā evamāhuḥ - mā kulaputra evaṃ cetanāṃ dṛḍhīkārṣīḥ / eṣa kulaputra āryo vajrārciḥsamādhyavabhāsalabdhaḥ avivartyavīryo mahārambhottāraṇapratipannaḥ, sarvajagatsnehaparyādānāyābhyutthitaḥ, sarvadṛṣṭigatajāladālanāya prayuktaḥ, sarvakleśakarmakakṣanirdahanāya pratyupasthitaḥ, sarvākṣaṇajñānakāntārāvabhāsanāyodyuktaḥ, sarvasattvajarāmaraṇaprapātabhayavinivartanāya vyavasthitaḥ, tryadhvāndhakāravidhamanatāyai abhiyuktaḥ, sarvadharmaraśmipramuñcanatāyai pratipannaḥ / etasya hi kulaputra, pañcatapastapyamānasya yāvantaḥ kecidbrāhmaṇāḥ kartṛtvamīśvaratvaṃ sarvalokajyeṣṭhatvamātmani manyante vividhadṛṣṭigatābhiniviṣṭāḥ tasya asamogratapovratasamādānaprabhāveṇa sarve svabhavaneṣu na ramante / te dhyānaratimanāsvādayanto 'sya sakāśamupasaṃkrāmanti / tāneṣa āgatānṛddhayanubhāvenābhibhūya ugravratatapasā ca tebhyaḥ sarvadṛṣṭigatavinivartanāya sarvamānamadaprahāṇāya ca dharmaṃ deśayati / sarvajaganmahāmaitrīmahākarūṇāspharaṇatāyai bodhyāśayadṛḍhīkaraṇatāyai bodhicittotpādavipulakaraṇatāyai sarvabuddhasaṃdarśanābhimukhatāyai buddhasvaramaṇḍalapratilambhaparipūraṇāya sarvatrānuravaṇabuddhaghoṣāpratighātānāvaraṇatāyai ca dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: May he not wish to create obstacles for me on the path to omniscience. May he not wish to lead me along a wrong path. May he not wish to create obstacles to the gate of <s>Dharma</s> for my attainment of the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>." While he was thus engaged in reflection and mental attention, ten thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, standing in the sky above, spoke thus — "Do not, son of good family, hold firm to such an intention. This noble one, son of good family, has attained the illumination of the <s>Vajrārci</s> (Diamond Flame) <s>samādhi</s>, possesses irreversible vigor, has undertaken the great enterprise of deliverance, has arisen for the absorption of the attachment of all beings, is engaged in tearing apart the net of all wrong views, stands ready to burn the undergrowth of all afflictions and <s>karma</s>, is striving to illuminate the wilderness of the knowledge of all unfavorable conditions, is established for turning back beings from the precipice of old age and death, is devoted to dispelling the darkness of the three times, has undertaken to release the rays of all <s>Dharma</s>. For this one, son of good family, as he performs the five-fire austerity, all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who conceive of agency, lordship, and supremacy over the entire world in themselves, who are attached to various wrong views — through the power of his undertaking of incomparably fierce austerity and vows, none of them delight in their own abodes. They, not savoring the pleasure of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), approach him. Having overpowered those who come through his miraculous power, and through his fierce vows and austerity, he teaches them the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of all wrong views and for the relinquishing of all pride and arrogance. He teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the pervading of all beings with great loving-kindness and great compassion, for the strengthening of the aspiration toward awakening, for the expansion of the generation of the thought of awakening, for facing the vision of all <s>Buddhas</s>, for the fulfillment of attaining the voice-circle of the <s>Buddha</s>, and for the unobstructed and unimpeded resonance of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice everywhere."

body.text: daśa ca mārasahasrāṇyuparyantarīkṣe sthitvā divyairmaṇiratnairabhyavakīrya evamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra, pañcatapastapyato 'smādarciḥskandhādābhā niścaritvā asmadbhavanānyātmabhāvanābhavanābharaṇaparibhogāṃśca jihmīkurvanti / te vayaṃ saṃvegajātāḥ saparivārāḥ etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāma / upasaṃkrāntānāṃ caiṣā 'smākaṃ tathā dharmaṃ deśayati, yathā svacittapratilabdhā bodhāya cittamutpādya avinivartanīyā bhavāmo 'nuttarayāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Māras</s>, standing in the sky above, showered him with divine jewels and gems and spoke thus — "Son of good family, from the mass of flames of this one who performs the five-fire austerity, a radiance has emerged from us that makes our palaces, our personal forms, our dwelling ornaments, and our possessions crooked. We, filled with a sense of urgency, have come with our retinues to his presence. And when we have approached, he teaches us the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that, having generated the aspiration for awakening through our own mind's realization, we become irreversible in supreme perfect awakening."

body.text: daśa ca vaśavartidevarājasahasrāṇi divyaiḥ puṣpairabhyavakīrya evamāhuḥ - vayaṃ kulaputra, asya pañcatapastapyataḥ svabhavaneṣu ratiṃ na vindāmaḥ / te vayaṃ svasvajanaparivārā etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / sa eṣo 'smākamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ svacittavaśavartitāpratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayati / sarvakleśavaśitāpratilābhāya yathābhiprāyopapattivaśitāpratilābhāya sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhivaśitāpratilābhāya sarvasamāpattivaśavartitāpratilābhāya pariṣkāravaśitāvyūhapariśuddhaye yathābhiprāyavaśavartitāyai ca dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand kings of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods, showering him with divine flowers, spoke thus — "Son of good family, we find no pleasure in our own palaces while this one performs the five-fire austerity. We, together with our own people and retinues, have come to his presence. He teaches us the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of mastery over our own minds, for the attainment of mastery over all afflictions, for the attainment of mastery over rebirth according to one's wish, for the attainment of mastery over the purification of all obstructions of <s>karma</s>, for the attainment of mastery over all meditative attainments, for the purification of the array of mastery over requisites, and for mastery that operates according to one's wish."

body.text: daśa ca sunirmitadevarājasahasrāṇyuparyantarikṣe sthitvā divyasaṃgītaprayoganirnādamadhuranirghoṣeṇa pūjāṃ kṛtvā evamāhuḥ - etasya kulaputra pañcatapastapyata ebhyo 'gnikūṭebhyastadrūpā prabhā niścarati, yayā asmākamimāni vimānānyuttapyante, viśudhyanti, prabhāsvaratarāṇi bhavanti / imāni cābharaṇāni, imāścāpsarasaḥ, vayamapīdānīṃ sadevaputrāpsarogaṇaparivārā na kāmeṣu ratiṃ vindāmaḥ / na kāmasukhamabhinandāmaḥ / te vayaṃ prahlāditakāyacittāḥ etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / sa eṣo 'smākamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ cittaviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayati / cittaprabhāsvaratāyai cittakalyāṇatāyai cittakarmaṇyatāyai cittaprītisaṃjananatāyai daśabalajñānapratilābhaviśuddhaye
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Sunirmita</s> (Self-Created) divine kings, standing in the sky above, having made worship with sweet sounds of divine musical performances, spoke thus: 'O son of good family, as he performs the five-fire austerity, from these fire-mounds there issues forth a radiance by which our palaces are heated, purified, and become even more luminous. And these ornaments, and these <s>apsarases</s> — even we now, with our retinues of <s>devaputras</s> and hosts of <s>apsarases</s>, do not find delight in sensual pleasures. We do not rejoice in sensual happiness. We, with our bodies and minds gladdened, approach his presence. And he, when we have approached, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of our minds — for the luminosity of mind, for the wholesomeness of mind, for the pliancy of mind, for the generation of joy in mind, for the purification of attaining the knowledge of the ten powers,

body.text: mahādharmavegavivardhanatayai kāyaviśuddhaye apramāṇabuddhakāyābhinirharaṇatāyai vāgviśuddhaye tathāgataghoṣapratilābhāya cittaviśuddhaye sarvajñatāpratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: for the augmentation of the great <s>Dharma</s>-momentum, for the purification of body, for the production of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-bodies, for the purification of speech, for the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s voice, for the purification of mind, for the attainment of omniscience — he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.text: daśa ca saṃtuṣitadevarājasahasrāṇi sadevaputrāpsaragaṇoparivārāṇi uparyantarikṣe sthitvā sarvagandhacūrṇameghavarṣamabhipravṛṣya pūjayitvā namaskṛtya evamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra, pañcatapastapyamānasya asmākaṃ svabhavaneṣu ratirna bhavati / te vayamanabhiratāḥ santaḥ etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / tata eṣo 'smākamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ sarvaviṣayānavekṣatāyai dharmaṃ deśayati / saṃtuṣṭicittatāyai cittaparituṣṭitāyai kuśalamūlasaṃjananatāyai bodhicittotpādapratilābhāya yāvatsarvabuddhadharmaparipūraṇāya dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (<s>Tuṣita</s>) divine kings, with their retinues of <s>devaputras</s> and hosts of <s>apsarases</s>, standing in the sky above, having rained showers of clouds of all fragrant powders, having worshipped and paid homage, spoke thus: 'O son of good family, while he performs the five-fire austerity, delight does not arise in us in our own abodes. We, being without delight, approach his presence. Then he teaches us who have approached the <s>Dharma</s> for not regarding all sense-objects, for contentment of mind, for satisfaction of mind, for the generation of roots of merit, for the attainment of the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, up to for the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.text: daśa ca suyāmadevarājasahasrāṇi sadevaputrāpsarogaṇaparivārāṇi divyāni māndāravakusumavarṣāṇyabhipravṛṣya evamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra pañcatapastapyamānasya asmākaṃ divyasaṃgītiṣu ratirna bhavati / te vayamanabhiratā etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / tata eṣo 'smākamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ sarvakāmarativinivartanatāyai yāvatsarvabuddhadharmapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Suyāma</s> divine kings, with their retinues of <s>devaputras</s> and hosts of <s>apsarases</s>, having rained showers of divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers, spoke thus: 'O son of good family, while he performs the five-fire austerity, delight does not arise in us in divine musical performances. We, being without delight, approach his presence. Then he teaches us who have approached the <s>Dharma</s> for turning away from all sensual delight, up to for the attainment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.text: daśa ca śakradevendraśatasahasrāṇi pratyekaṃ dvātriṃśadbhirupendraiḥ sadevaputrāpsarogaṇaparivāraiḥ sārdhaṃ divyavastraratnābharaṇakusumameghavarṣamabhipravṛtya evamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra pañcatapastapyamānasya asmākaṃ sarvaśakrabhavanodyānakrīḍāvanadivyatūryatālopacārasaṃgītiparibhogeṣu ratirna bhavati / te vayamanabhiratā etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / tata eṣo 'smākamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ sarvakāmaratiprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayati / sarvamidamanityaṃ calaṃ vyayadharmamiti vācamudīrayati / sarvamadapramādasamucchedanāya dharmaṃ deśayati anuttarabodhicchandavivardhanatāyai / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra asya saṃprekṣitena imāni meruśikharāṇi saṃprakampitāni / te vayaṃ vyathitasaṃvignacittāḥ sarvajñatācittotpādanadṛḍhatayā sarvajñatājñāne praṇidhimabhinirharāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: And a hundred thousand <s>Śakra Devendra</s>s, each with thirty-two <s>Upendras</s> and their retinues of <s>devaputras</s> and hosts of <s>apsarases</s>, having rained showers of clouds of divine garments, jewels, ornaments, and flowers, having worshipped and paid homage, spoke thus: 'O son of good family, while he performs the five-fire austerity, a radiance issues forth from these fire-mounds by which our <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly-hall is illuminated. All the divine <s>devaputras</s>, their bodies pervaded by that radiance, do not find delight in divine music, nor in garlands, nor in ointments, nor in garments, nor in ornaments, nor in the five sensual pleasures; they approach his presence. Then he teaches us who have approached the <s>Dharma</s> — for the recollection of impermanence, for the fearful perception of the conditioned, for contemplating the reality of suffering, for the establishment of the mindfulness of the body upon one's own body, for the contemplation of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, for the examination of the dependent origination of all <s>dharmas</s>, for the non-clinging mind regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, for the non-attachment to all existences, for omniscient knowledge, for the attainment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.text: daśa ca nāgasahasrāṇi airāvatanandopanandanāgarājapramukhāni uparyantarikṣe gatāni divyakālānusāricandanameghairnāgakanyāsaṃgītinirnādamadhuranirghoṣairdivyagandhodakadhārāprasṛtapramuktairabhipravṛṣya evamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra pañcatapastapyata ebhyo mahāgniskandharāśibhya ābhāḥ pramuktāḥ sarvanāgabhavanānyavabhāsya vālikāvarṣasuparṇibhayānyapanayanti / krodhapravṛttiṃ caiṣāṃ praśamayitvā āśayaṃ prahlādya manaḥ prasādayanti / tata eṣo 'smākaṃ prasannacittānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, yaduta hīnanāgagativijugupsanatāyai sarvāvaraṇīyakarmaprahāṇāya / atyayaṃ deśayitvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādya sarvajñatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Nāga</s>s, headed by the <s>Nāgarājas</s> <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, and <s>Upananda</s>, gone to the sky above, having made worship with clouds of divine <s>kālānusāri</s> (finest black) sandalwood and sweet sounds of music-songs of <s>Nāga</s>-maidens, spoke thus: 'O son of good family, while he performs the five-fire austerity, a radiance issues forth from these fire-mounds which enters our abodes. Pervaded by that radiance, we <s>Nāgarājas</s>, together with our <s>Nāga</s>-maiden retinues, are freed from the three distresses of the <s>Nāga</s> state. And we delight in the bliss of <s>Dharma</s>. And we approach his presence. Then he teaches us who have approached the <s>Dharma</s> for the arising of faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the generation of the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, up to for the attainment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.text: daśa ca yakṣendrasahasrāṇi gaganatale sthitvā nānāvidhayā pūjayā pūjayitvā jayoṣmāyatanaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sudhanaṃ ca śreṣṭhidārakamevamāhuḥ - asya kulaputra pañcatapastapyamānasya asmatpārṣadānāṃ manuṣyeṣu maitraṃ cittaṃ saṃjāyate / sarvayakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍāśca maitracittā bhavanti / te maitracittā
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Yakṣendras</s>, standing on the surface of the sky, having worshipped with various forms of worship, spoke thus to the brāhmaṇa <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s> and to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'O son of good family, while he performs this five-fire austerity, a radiance issues forth from these fire-mounds which enters our abodes. We <s>Yakṣas</s>, pervaded by that radiance, and all our retinues of <s>Yakṣa</s>-maidens — we who are of violent nature, whose livelihood is violence, who are addicted to harming, who delight in killing, who are devoted to eating flesh — we abandon all that evil conduct, and with minds having set forth toward non-harm,

body.text: aviheṭhanapratipannā asmatsakāśamupasaṃkrāmanti - vayamapīdānīṃ maitryādhipatyenābhibhūtāḥ sveṣu sveṣu bhavaneṣu ratiṃ na vindāmaḥ / te vayaṃ sasvajanaparivārā etasya sakāśamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / tadasmākamupasaṃkrāntānāmasya śarīraniryātā prabhā avabhāsya sarvaśarīraṃ sukhena spharati / sa eṣo 'smākaṃ prīṇitakāyacittānāṃ tathā dharmaṃ deśayati, yadanekeṣāṃ yakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍakaṭapūtanānāṃ bodhāya cittānyutpadyante //
body.translated_text: we approach his presence practicing non-harm. Even now, we, overpowered by the sovereignty of loving-kindness, do not find delight in our respective abodes. We, with our bodies and minds gladdened, approach his presence. Then he teaches us who have approached the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of <s>Yakṣa</s>-conduct. And whatever beings encounter us, they all become established in the attainment of the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening and in the practice of non-harm toward all beings.' //

body.text: daśa ca gandharvendrasahasrāṇyuparyantarikṣe sthitvā evamāhuḥ - asmākamapi kulaputra svabhavaneṣu vasatāmasya pañcatapastapyata ebhyo 'gnikūṭebhya ābhā niścaritvā asmadbhavanānyavabhāsayati / te vayaṃ tayā prabhayā spṛṣṭā acintyasukhasamarpitā etasyāntikamupasaṃkramāmaḥ / upasaṃkrāntānāmeṣo 'smākaṃ tathā dharmaṃ deśayati, yadavivartyā bhavāmo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Gandharvendra</s>s, standing in the sky above, spoke thus: 'For us too, O son of good family, dwelling in our own abodes, as he performs the five-fire austerity, from these fire-mounds there is a radiance whose light illuminates us, pervaded by which, even hearing the sweet melodies of <s>Gandharva</s>-music delighting <s>Devendras</s>, we do not find satisfaction.
