ārye / āha - etatpramukhāni kulaputra strīṇāṃ daśāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi mama sabhāgacaritāni ekapraṇidhānāni ekakuśalamūlāni ekaniryāṇavyūhāni ekādhimuktipathaviśuddhāni mama sabhāgasmṛtiviśuddhāni sabhāgagativiśuddhāni sabhāgabudhyapramāṇāni sabhāgendriyapratilabdhāni sabhāgacittaspharaṇāni sabhāgagocaraviṣayāṇi sabhāgadharmanayāvatīrṇāni sabhāgārthaviniścatāni sabhāgadharmārthodyotanāni sabhāgarūpaviśuddhāni sabhāgabalāpramāṇāni, sabhāgavairyāparājitāni sabhāgadharmarutaghoṣāṇi, sabhāgasvaraviśuddhāni, sarvavyavahāreṣu sabhāgaguṇaviśuddhāni, apramāṇaguṇavarṇatayā sabhāgakarmaviśuddhāni, anavadyakarmavipākaviśuddhyā sabhāgamahāmaitrīspharaṇāni, sarvajagatparitrāṇatayā sabhāgamahākaruṇāspharaṇāni, sarvajagatparipācanākhedatayā sabhāgakāyakarmaviśuddhāni, yathāśayasarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇakāyasaṃdarśanatayā sabhāgavākkarmaviśuddhāni dharmadhātuniruktivyavahāreṣu, sabhāgopasaṃkramaṇāni sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu, sabhāganirjavanāni sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu, sarvabuddhapūjopasthānatāyai sabhāgapratyakṣajñānāni sarvadharmanayānugameṣu, sabhāgacaryāviśuddhāni sarvabodhisattvabhūmipratilābheṣu / etāni kulaputra daśastrīsahasrāṇi ekakṣaṇena daśa diśaḥ spharanti, yadutaikajātipratibaddhān bodhisattvān bhojanena pratipādanatāyai asyā eva piṭharikāyā bhojanamādāya / daśa diśaḥ spharanti asyā eva piṭharikāyā bhojanamādāya / daśa diśaḥ spharanti caramabhavikān sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikān piṇḍapātena pratipādanatāyai / spharitvā sarvapretagaṇān bhojanena saṃtarpayanti / sā ahaṃ kulaputra asyā eva piṭharikāyā devān devabhojanena saṃtarpayāmi / nāgānnāgabhojanena, yakṣān yakṣabhojanena, gandharvān gandharvabhojanena, asurānasurabhojanena, garuḍān garuḍabhojanena, kinnarān kinnarabhojanena, mahoragān mahoragabhojanena, manuṣyān manuṣyabhojanena, amanuṣyānamanuṣyabhojanena saṃtarpayāmi / āgamayasva kulaputra muhūrtaṃ yāvatpratyakṣo bhaviṣyasi
/ samantarabhaṣitā ceyaṃ vāk prabhūtayopāsikayā, atha tāvadeva aparimāṇāḥ sattvāḥ pūrveṇa gṛhadvāreṇa praviśanti sma yaduta prabhūtayopāsikayā pūrvapraṇidhānanimantritāḥ / evaṃ dakṣiṇena paścimeṇottareṇa gṛhadvāreṇa aparimāṇāḥ sattvāḥ praviśanti sma yaduta prabhūtayopāsikayā pūrvapraṇidhānanimantritāḥ / tān prabhūtopāsikā teṣvāsaneṣu niṣadya yathābhipretairbhojanairnānāsūpairnānārasairnānāvarṇairnānāgandhaiḥ saṃtarpayati, saṃpravārayati, saṃtoṣayati, saṃpraharṣayati, saṃpramodayati pariprīṇayati, āttamanaskān karoti / yathā nānābhojanaiḥ, evaṃ nānāpānavidhibhiḥ, nānārasāgraiḥ, nānāsanaiḥ, nānāśayanaiḥ nānāyānairnānāvastraiḥ nānāpuṣpairnānāmālyaiḥ nānāgandhairnānādhūpaiḥ nānāvilepanairnānācūrṇaiḥ nānābharaṇaiḥ nānāratnarathaiḥ nānāchatrairnānādhvajairnānāpatākābhiḥ nānāvidhopakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ saṃtarpayati, yāvadāttamanaskān karoti / devān devabhojanena saṃtarpayati / nāgān yakṣān gandharvānasurān garuḍān kinnarān mahoragān manuṣyānamanuṣyān tattadeva bhojanena saṃtarpayati yāvadāttamanaskān karoti / na ca sā piṭharikā hīyate, na parihīyate, nonībhavati, na kṣīyate, na paryādānaṃ gacchati, na sīmāmupaiti, na niṣṭhāṃ na paryantaṃ na pariniṣṭhāṃ gacchati //
body.translated_text: 'Noble one.' She replied: 'Led by these, son of good family, there are ten innumerable hundreds of thousands of women of kindred conduct with me — of a single vow, a single root of merit, a single outpouring-array, purified on a single path of higher aspiration, of kindred purification of mindfulness with me, of kindred purification of destiny, of kindred immeasurable awakening, of kindred attainment of faculties, of kindred pervading of mind, of kindred range and domain, of kindred descent into <s>dharma</s>-methods, of kindred determination of meaning, of kindred illumination of <s>dharma</s>-meaning, of kindred purification of form, of kindred immeasurability of power, of kindred unconquered heroic energy, of kindred sounds and voices of <s>dharma</s>, of kindred purification of voice, of kindred purification of qualities in all activities, of kindred purification of deeds through the description of immeasurable qualities, of kindred pervading of great loving-kindness through the purification of blameless <s>karma</s>-ripening, of kindred pervading of great compassion for the protection of all the world, of kindred purification of bodily deeds through unwearied ripening of all the world, of kindred purification of verbal deeds through displaying bodies that satisfy all beings according to their dispositions, of kindred purification in the conventions of the etymologies of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, of kindred approach to all <s>Buddha</s>-assembly-circles, of kindred swiftness in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields for the worship and service of all <s>Buddha</s>s, of kindred direct knowledge in following all <s>dharma</s>-methods, of kindred purification of conduct in the attainment of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages. And, son of good family, these ten thousand women pervade the ten directions in a single instant — taking food from this very food-vessel to provide nourishment to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s bound to their last birth. They pervade the ten directions, taking food from this very food-vessel. They pervade the ten directions to provide alms-food to those in their final existence, to all followers of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. Having pervaded, they satiate all hosts of <s>preta</s>s (hungry ghosts) with food. And I, son of good family, from this very food-vessel, satiate the <s>deva</s>s with <s>deva</s>-food, the <s>nāga</s>s with <s>nāga</s>-food, the <s>yakṣa</s>s with <s>yakṣa</s>-food, the <s>gandharva</s>s with <s>gandharva</s>-food, the <s>asura</s>s with <s>asura</s>-food, the <s>garuḍa</s>s with <s>garuḍa</s>-food, the <s>kinnara</s>s with <s>kinnara</s>-food, the <s>mahoraga</s>s with <s>mahoraga</s>-food, humans with human food, and non-humans with non-human food. Wait a moment, son of good family, and you shall witness this directly.' No sooner had this word been uttered by the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s>, than immediately innumerable beings entered through the eastern gate of the house — beings invited by the former vows of the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s>. Likewise through the southern, western, and northern gates of the house, innumerable beings entered — invited by the former vows of the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s>. The <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s> satiated, filled, satisfied, delighted, gladdened, pleased, and made happy those beings seated on those seats with foods according to their wishes — various curries, various flavors, various colors, various fragrances. Just as with various foods, so too with various kinds of drink, various finest flavors, various seats, various bedding, various vehicles, various garments, various flowers, various garlands, various fragrances, various incense, various unguents, various powders, various ornaments, various gem-chariots, various parasols, various banners, various pennants, and various kinds of special provisions — she satiated them, up to making them happy. She satiated <s>deva</s>s with <s>deva</s>-food, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kinnara</s>s, <s>mahoraga</s>s, humans, and non-humans — each with their own food — up to making them happy. And that food-vessel did not diminish, was not depleted, did not become less, was not exhausted, did not come to depletion, did not reach a limit, did not reach an end, a boundary, or a final completion. //

body.text: atha khalu prabhūtopāsikā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - etamahaṃ kulaputra akṣayavyūhapuṇyakośaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamakṣayapuṇyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāpuṇyasāgarākṣayatayā, gaganakalpānāṃ susaṃbhūtavipulapuṇyopacayatayā, cintārājamaṇiratnakalpānāṃ sarvajagatpraṇidhipūraṇatayā, mahāpuṇyacakravālānāṃ sarvajagatkuśalamūlārakṣaṇatayā, mahāpuṇyameghānāṃ sarvajagadratnapāṇyabhipravarṣaṇatayā, mahāpuṇyakośādhyakṣāṇāṃ dharmanagaradvāravivaraṇatayā, mahāpuṇyapradīpānāṃ sarvajagaddāridryāndhakāravidhamanatayā caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Son of good family, this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Akṣayavyūhapuṇyakośa</s> (Treasury of Merit of Inexhaustible Array) that I know. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the qualities, of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s of inexhaustible merit — by the inexhaustibility of their great ocean of merit, who are like space in the vastness of their well-accumulated merit, who are like <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems) in fulfilling the vows of all the world, who are great <s>Cakravāla</s>s (world-encircling mountains) of merit in protecting the roots of merit of all the world, who are great clouds of merit in raining the jewels of generosity upon all the world, who are great treasury-keepers of merit in opening the gates of the city of <s>Dharma</s>, who are great lamps of merit in dispelling the darkness of poverty of all the world?' //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe mahāsaṃbhavaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra vidvānnāṃ gṛhapatiḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here in <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region), to the city called <s>Mahāsaṃbhava</s>. There dwells a householder named <s>Vidvān</s> (the Learned). Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should he practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ prabhūtāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya prabhūtāmupāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya prabhūtāyā upāsikāyā darśanāvitṛpto 'ntikātprakrāntaḥ // 14 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s>, circumambulating the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, unsatiated in beholding the <s>upāsikā</s> <s>Prabhūtā</s>, departed from her presence. // 14 //

body.translated_text: 17. <s>Vidvān</s>. /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'kṣayavyūhapuṇyakośavimokṣāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ taṃ puṇyasāgaramanuvicintayan, tatpuṇyagaganamavalokayan, taṃ puṇyarāśimādadan, taṃ puṇyaparvatamabhirohan, taṃ puṇyanicayaṃ saṃgṛhṇan, taṃ puṇyaudhamavagāhayamānaḥ, tatpuṇyatīrthamavataran, taṃ puṇyamaṇḍalaṃ pariśodhayan, taṃ puṇyanidhiṃ saṃpaśyan, taṃ puṇyanayamanusmaran, tāṃ puṇyanetrīṃ samanvāharan, taṃ puṇyavaṃśaṃ pariśodhayan, anupūrveṇa yena mahāsaṃbhavaṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya vidvāṃsaṃ gṛhapatiṃ parimārgati, parigaveṣati, vyavalokayati kalyāṇamitrāṇyabhilaṣan / kalyāṇamitradarśanavāsitayā sataṃtyā, kalyāṇamitrādhiṣṭhānena āśayena, kalyāṇamitrānugatena prayogena, kalyāṇamitropacārāparikhinnena vīryeṇa, kalyāṇamitrādhīnaiḥ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ, kalyāṇamitraniyataiḥ sarvapuṇyasaṃbhāraiḥ, kalyāṇamitravivardhitairupāyakauśalyacaritaiḥ, aparapratyayena kalyāṇamitropacārakauśalyena, vivardhamānaiḥ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ, viśuddhayatā bodhisattvādhyāśayena, saṃvardhamānairbodhisattvendriyaiḥ, paripācyamānaiḥ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ, saṃvardhamānairmahāpraṇidhānābhinirhāraiḥ, vipulībhavantyā mahākaruṇayā, sarvajñatāyā āsannībhūtamātmānaṃ saṃpaśyan samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāyāḥ, sarvabuddhebhyo dharmāvabhāsaṃ saṃpratīcchan, vivardhamānena daśatathāgatabalāvabhāsena vidvāṃsaṃ gṛhapatiṃ parigaveṣamāṇo adrākṣīnmadhye nagarasya śṛṅgāṭake saptaratnavyomakoparyasaṃkhyeyaratnamaye vividhavajrendranīlaracitamaṇiratnapāde kāñcanasūtrajvālaśvete vimalagarbhamaṇiratnagarbhe pañcaratnaśatasamalaṃkṛtabimbe vicitradivyadūṣyaprajñapte ucchritadivyapaṭṭadhvajapatāke anekaratnajālasaṃchanne mahāratnavitānavitate mahāsuvarṇaratnapuṣpadāmābhipralambite bhadrāsane niṣaṇṇam,
vimalavaiḍūryadaṇḍena jāmbūnadakanakacchatreṇa dhriyatā haṃsarājanirmalacāmarasaṃvījyamānam, vividhagandhopacārapradhūpitaṃ vāmadakṣiṇena pañcabhistūryaśataiḥ pravādyadbhiḥ divyātirekamadhuranirghoṣairmahāsaṃbhavaṃ nagaraṃ paryāpannaiḥ sattvaprītisaṃjanārthaṃ divyakusumameghaiḥ pravarṣadbhirdivyamānuṣyarūpasamatikrāntaiḥ pariniṣpannabodhisattvāśayaiḥ divyātirekavibhūṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaiḥ kiṃkaropacaraṇapratikāribhiḥ pūrvakuśalamūlasabhāgacaritairdaśabhiḥ prāṇīsahasraiḥ parivṛtam / dṛṣṭvā ca sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena vidvān gṛhapatistenopajagāma / upetya viduṣo gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya vidvāṃsaṃ gṛhapatimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ahaṃ ārya sarvasattvānāmarthāya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃprasthito yaduta sarvasattvaduḥkhavyupaśamāya sarvasattvātyantasukhapratiṣṭhāpanāya sarvasattvasaṃsārasāgarābhyuddhāraṇatāyai sarvasattvadharmaratnadvīpasaṃprāpaṇatāyai sarvasattvatṛṣṇāsnehocchoṣaṇatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāsnehasaṃjananatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ kāmaratitṛṣṇāvinivartanatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ buddhajñānatṛṣṇotpādanatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ saṃsārāṭavīkāntārasamatikramaṇatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ buddhaguṇadharmārāmaratisaṃjananatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ traidhātukapurānniṣkramaṇatāyai sarvasattvānāṃ sarvajñatāpuropanayatāyai / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam,
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having attained the illumination of the <s>Akṣayavyūhapuṇyakośa</s> (Treasury of Merit of Inexhaustible Array) liberation, reflecting upon that ocean of merit, surveying that sky of merit, gathering that heap of merit, ascending that mountain of merit, collecting that accumulation of merit, plunging into that depth of merit, descending into that ford of merit, purifying that <s>maṇḍala</s> of merit, beholding that treasure of merit, recollecting that method of merit, tracing that guide of merit, purifying that lineage of merit — gradually proceeded to the city called <s>Mahāsaṃbhava</s> and searched for, sought, and looked about for the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, longing for spiritual friends — with a mind perfumed by seeing spiritual friends, with an aspiration empowered by the spiritual friend, with application following the spiritual friend, with heroic energy unwearied in attending upon the spiritual friend, with all roots of merit dependent on the spiritual friend, with all accumulations of merit determined by the spiritual friend, with skills in method augmented by the spiritual friend, with skill in attending upon the spiritual friend independent of others, with all roots of merit increasing, with a purified <s>Bodhisattva</s> higher aspiration, with <s>Bodhisattva</s>-faculties increasing, with all roots of merit being ripened, with great vow-accomplishments increasing, with great compassion becoming vast, seeing himself as drawing near to the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> and to omniscience, receiving the illumination of <s>Dharma</s> from all <s>Buddha</s>s, with the illumination of the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers increasing — while searching for the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, he saw him in the middle of the city, at a crossroads, seated upon a jeweled throne — in the sky made of the seven treasures, upon a seat of innumerable gems, with a pedestal fashioned of various diamond-sapphire-<s>maṇi</s>-jewels, white with blazing golden cords, with a womb of stainless-womb <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, with a mirror adorned with five hundred gems, spread with variegated divine cloth, with divine silk banners and pennants raised high, covered with many jewel-nets, with a great gem-canopy spread above, with great golden-gem-flower garlands hanging down. He was being shaded by a stainless <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-handled parasol of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, being fanned by spotless swan-king <s>cāmara</s>s (fly-whisks), perfumed with various incense-offerings. On his left and right, five hundred musical ensembles played, producing sounds of divine, surpassingly sweet melody. He was surrounded by ten thousand beings — who had performed kindred wholesome deeds in the past, endowed with <s>Bodhisattva</s>-aspiration, adorned with surpassingly divine ornaments, serving as attendants, performers of service, and helpers — who pervaded the city of <s>Mahāsaṃbhava</s>, raining divine flower-clouds for the purpose of generating the delight of beings, of forms surpassing divine and human beauty. Having seen him, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the householder <s>Vidvān</s>. Having approached, bowing his head at the feet of the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, circumambulating the householder <s>Vidvān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, standing before him with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect <s>Saṃbodhi</s> for the sake of all beings — namely: for the cessation of the suffering of all beings, for establishing all beings in ultimate happiness, for rescuing all beings from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for guiding all beings to the jewel-island of <s>Dharma</s>, for drying up the moisture of the craving of all beings, for generating the moisture of great compassion in all beings, for turning away the thirst for sensual delight in all beings, for generating the thirst for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge in all beings, for enabling all beings to cross beyond the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for generating in all beings the delight in the pleasure-gardens of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities and <s>dharma</s>s, for enabling all beings to depart from the city of the three realms, for guiding all beings to the city of omniscience. But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct,

body.text: kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ śikṣamāṇā bodhisattvāḥ pratiśaraṇabhūtā bhavanti sarvasattvānām //
body.translated_text: how he should practice. And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and exhortation to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble one tell me: how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How do <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, while training, become a refuge for all beings?' //

body.text:
evamukte vidvān gṛhapatiḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / durlabhāḥ kulaputra te sattvāḥ, ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ parimārgayamāṇā na tṛpyante kalyāṇamitradarśanena / na khidyante kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇeṣu / na paritapyante kalyāṇamitropacāreṣu / na daurmanasyamutpādayanti kalyāṇamitradurāsadatayā / na nivartante kalyāṇamitragaveṣaṇatayā / na vyāvartante kalyāṇamitratṛṣṇālālasahṛdayatvāt / na pratyudāvartante kalyāṇamitramukhāvalokena / na saṃsīdanti kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīpatheṣu / na khidyante kalyāṇamitropasthānaparicaryāsu / paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputra, imaṃ mama parivāram? āha - paśyāmi ārya / āha - sarva ete kulaputra mayā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditāḥ / mayaite janitāstathāgatakule / mayaite poṣitāḥ pāramitopasaṃhāraiḥ / mayaite saṃcaritāḥ sarvaśukladharmaiḥ / mayaite vivardhitā daśasu tathāgatabaleṣu / mayaite uccālitā lokavaṃśāt / mayaite pratiṣṭhāpitāstathāgatavaṃśe / mayaite vivartitā loke gaticakrāt / mayaite āvartitā dharmacakrapravartanatāyām / mayaite sattvāḥ tāritāstryadhvāpāyagatiprapātāt / mayaite pratiṣṭhāpitā dharmasamatānugamena / evaṃ hi kulaputra bodhisattvāstrātāro bhavanti sarvasattvānām / ahaṃ kulaputra manaḥkośasaṃbhavānāṃ puṇyānāṃ lābhī / so 'hamannārthibhyo 'nnaṃ dadāmi, pānārthibhyaḥ pānam, rasāgrārthibhyo rasāgram, khādyārthibhyaḥ khādyam, bhojyārthibhyo bhojyam, lehyārthibhyo lehyam, coṣyārthibhyaścoṣyam, vastrārthibhyo vastram, puṣpārthibhyaḥ puṣpam, mālyārthibhyo mālyam, gandhārthibhyo gandham, dhūpārthikebhyo dhūpam, vilepanārthibhyo vilepanam, cūrṇārthibhyaścūrṇam, ābharaṇavibhūṣaṇārthibhya ābharaṇavibhūṣaṇāni, ratnārthibhyo ratnāni, suvarṇārthibhyaḥ suvarṇam, rūpyārthibhyo rūpyam, muktārthibhyo muktām, pratiśrayārthibhyaḥ
pratiśrayam, āsanārthibhya āsanam, śayanārthibhyaḥ śayanam, glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārārthibhyo glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān, yānārthibhyo yānam, vāhanārthibhyo vāhanam, hastyaśvarathagogardabhamahiṣaiḍakārthibhyo hastyaśvarathagogardabhamahiṣaiḍakān, chatradhvajapatākārthibhyaśchatradhvajapatākāḥ, dāsīdāsārthibhyo dāsīdāsān, māṇavaparivārārthibhyo māṇavaparivāram, stryarthibhyaḥ striyaḥ, kumāryarthibhyaḥ, kumārīm, makuṭacūḍāmaṇyarthibhyo makuṭacūḍāmaṇīn, sacarmacūḍāmaṇyarthibhyo sacarmacūḍāmaṇīn, nīlavimalakeśamaṇḍalārthibhyo nīlavimalakeśamaṇḍalam, yāvadvividhasarvopakaraṇarthibhyo vividhasarvopakaraṇāni prayacchāmi / āgamaya kulaputra mūhūrtaṃ yāvatpratyakṣo bhaviṣyasi / samanantarabhāṣitāyāṃ cāsyāṃ vāci viduṣā gṛhapatinā, atha tāvadeva aparimāṇāḥ sattvā viduṣā gṛhapatinā pūrvapraṇidhānābhinimantritāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ / nānādigbhyo nānājanapadapradeśebhyo nānānagarebhyo nānānigamebhyo nānāpaṭṭanebhyo nānākarvaṭebhyo nānāsattvajātibhyo
body.translated_text: When this was said, the householder <s>Vidvān</s> (the Learned One) spoke thus to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: "Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You have generated the mind set upon unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Rare, O son of good family, are those beings who, having generated the mind set upon unsurpassed perfect awakening, while seeking in the practice of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, are never satiated by seeing spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>); who are never wearied in approaching spiritual friends; who are never distressed in serving spiritual friends; who do not give rise to despondency at the difficulty of reaching spiritual friends; who do not turn back from seeking spiritual friends; who do not turn away due to their hearts being filled with longing and thirst for spiritual friends; who do not retreat from gazing upon the faces of spiritual friends; who do not sink down upon the paths of instruction from spiritual friends; who are not exhausted in attending upon and serving spiritual friends. Do you see, O son of good family, this retinue of mine?" He said: "I see it, Noble One." He said: "All of these, O son of good family, have been established by me in the mind set upon unsurpassed perfect awakening. By me they have been born into the family of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. By me they have been nourished through the accumulation of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). By me they have been guided through all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. By me they have been made to grow in the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. By me they have been uprooted from the lineage of the world. By me they have been established in the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. By me they have been turned away from the wheel of destinies in the world. By me they have been turned toward the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma). By me these beings have been rescued from the precipice of the lower realms of the three times. By me they have been established through the practice of the equality of <s>Dharma</s>. Thus indeed, O son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> become the protectors of all beings. I, O son of good family, am the recipient of merits born from the treasury of the mind. Thus I give food to those who seek food, drink to those who seek drink, the finest flavors to those who seek the finest flavors, hard food to those who seek hard food, soft food to those who seek soft food, food to be licked to those who seek food to be licked, food to be sucked to those who seek food to be sucked, clothing to those who seek clothing, flowers to those who seek flowers, garlands to those who seek garlands, fragrance to those who seek fragrance, incense to those who seek incense, unguents to those who seek unguents, powders to those who seek powders, ornaments and adornments to those who seek ornaments and adornments, jewels to those who seek jewels, gold to those who seek gold, silver to those who seek silver, pearls to those who seek pearls, shelter to those who seek shelter, seats to those who seek seats, beds to those who seek beds, medicines and provisions for the sick to those who seek medicines and provisions for the sick, vehicles to those who seek vehicles, mounts to those who seek mounts, elephants, horses, chariots, cattle, donkeys, and buffalo to those who seek elephants, horses, chariots, cattle, donkeys, and buffalo, parasols, banners, and flags to those who seek parasols, banners, and flags, female and male servants to those who seek female and male servants, retinues of attendants to those who seek retinues of attendants, women to those who seek women, maidens to those who seek maidens, diadems and crest-jewels to those who seek diadems and crest-jewels, crest-jewels with leather to those who seek crest-jewels with leather, dark lustrous hair-circles to those who seek dark lustrous hair-circles, and all manner of various requisites to those who seek various requisites. Come, O son of good family, wait a moment, and you shall witness this directly." No sooner had these words been spoken by the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, than immeasurable beings, invited by the prior vows (<s>pūrvapraṇidhāna</s>) of the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, assembled together from various directions, from various regions and provinces, from various cities, from various towns, from various seaports, from various villages, from various classes of beings,

body.text: nānāsattvakulebhyo nānāsattvakulavimātratābhyo nānāgatiparivartebhyo nānāpratiṣṭhānasaṃjñānagatibhyo nānāyatanaviśuddhā nānāhārārthino nānāhārābhilāṣiṇo nānāśayā śucyannapānakāmā māṃsārthino vividhabhojanavimātratābhikāṅkṣiṇo vividhagativiśeṣopapatyāyatanasthitāḥ yaduta manuṣyeṣvodanakulmāṣasūpamatsyamāṃsādivividhakavalīkāhārārthinaḥ / yathā manuṣyeṣu, evaṃ sarvagativicāreṣu nānābhojanapānārthina upasaṃkrāntāḥ yaduta bodhisattvānubhāvena asaṅgatyāgadundubhinirghoṣeṇa bodhisattvapraṇidhinimantritāḥ / tamupasaṃkramya vidvāṃsaṃ gṛhapatiṃ yācante 'valokayanti nirīkṣante vijñāpayanti //
body.translated_text: from various families of beings, from various distinctions among families of beings, from various cycles of rebirth, from various states of awareness and destinations, purified through various sense-bases, desiring various kinds of nourishment, craving various foods, of various dispositions — those desiring pure food and drink, those seeking meat, those longing for various kinds of food in their diversity, those established in the abodes of various special destinies of rebirth — namely, among humans, those seeking various morsels of food such as rice, porridge, soup, fish, meat, and so forth. Just as among humans, so too from all the various courses of existence, those seeking various foods and drinks approached — invited by the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, by the resounding of the drum of unattached generosity (<s>asaṅgatyāgadundubhi</s>), summoned by the vows of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Having approached the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, they implored, gazed upon, looked toward, and made their wishes known.

body.text:
atha khalu vidvān gṛhapatistān yācanakān saṃnipatitān viditvā muhūrtamanuvicintya gaganatalamavalokayati sma / tasya tato gaganatalādvividhā bhojanapānavidhayo nānārasā nānāvarṇā nānāgandhā avalambya hastatale pratyatiṣṭhan / sa tānyādāya tān yathāsaṃnipatitān yācanakān nānādhimuktān yathābhipretairbhojanapānavidhibhiḥ sarvopakaraṇaviśaiṣaiḥ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati saṃtoṣayati saṃpraharṣayati saṃpramodayati pariprīṇayati, āttamanaskān karoti / uttare vai nānāmiṣeṇa saṃtarpya tebhyo dharmaṃ deśayet / yaduta vipulajñānasaṃbhāropacayahetuṃ paridīpayan, sarvadāridryāsaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, mahābhogatāsamudāgamasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, dharmajñānanayapratiulābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, vipulapuṇyasaṃbhāropacayahetuṃ paridīpayan, prītibhakṣabhojanapratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanopacitaśarīrapratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, anavamṛdyabalapariśuddhipratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, anantarāhāraprajñāpratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan, sarvamārabalapramardanāparyādattapuṇyabalapratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayan dharmaṃ deśayet / so 'nnārthina upasaṃkrāntān gaganatalānnānānnavidhīn gṛhītvā saṃtarpya tebhya āyurvarṇabalamukhapratibhānaṃ saṃpaśyan pratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayet / sa pānārthina upasaṃkrāntānnānāvidhaiḥ pānairudāraiḥ kalyāṇairanavadyairmanaḥsaṃpraharṣakaiḥ saṃtarpya tebhyaḥ saṃsāratṛṣṇārativinivartanatāyai buddhadharmaratitṛṣṇāsaṃjananatāyai dharmaṃ deśayet / rasarasāgrārthina upasaṃkrāntānnānāvidharasarasāgrairmadhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyaiḥ saṃtarpayāmāsa / uttare caiṣāṃ rasarasāgratāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayet / sa yānārthino nānādiksrotobhyāgatānnānāvidhayānadānaiḥ saṃgṛhya tebhyo mahāyānādhirohaṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayet / sa nānādigāgatān vastrārthina upasaṃkrāntān viditvā muhūrtaṃ vicintya gaganatalamullokayati sma / tasya tato gaganatalānnānāraṅgānyanekavarṇāni viśuddhāni nīlapītalohitāvadātamāñjiṣṭhasphaṭikavarṇāni
vividhāni vastrāṇyavalambya hastatale pratyatiṣṭhan / sa taistān yācanakān pratipādya tebhyo 'nuttaratathāgatahrayapatrāpyasuvarṇavarṇacchavitāpratilābhaviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayet / pratyekameva sarvopakaraṇavidhibhiryathāgatān yācanakān pratipādya tebhyo yathārhaṃ dharmaṃ deśayet //
body.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, knowing that those petitioners had assembled, reflected for a moment and gazed up at the vault of the sky. From that vault of the sky, various kinds of food and drink of various flavors, various colors, and various fragrances descended and came to rest upon his palm. Taking these, he satisfied, refreshed, delighted, gladdened, rejoiced, and gratified those petitioners who had assembled, of various dispositions, with foods, drinks, and all manner of requisites according to their wishes, making them content. Moreover, having satisfied them with various material gifts, he would teach them the <s>Dharma</s> — illuminating the cause for the accumulation of vast stores of wisdom (<s>jñānasaṃbhāra</s>), illuminating the cause for the non-arising of all poverty, illuminating the cause for the attainment of great prosperity, illuminating the cause for obtaining the method of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge, illuminating the cause for the accumulation of vast stores of merit (<s>puṇyasaṃbhāra</s>), illuminating the cause for obtaining food consisting of joy (<s>prītibhakṣa</s>), illuminating the cause for obtaining a body adorned with the marks and minor marks (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>), illuminating the cause for obtaining the purification of unassailable powers, illuminating the cause for obtaining uninterrupted wisdom of sustenance, illuminating the cause for obtaining the power of merit that crushes all the forces of <s>Māra</s> and is inexhaustible — thus he would teach the <s>Dharma</s>. To those who approached seeking food, he would take various kinds of food from the vault of the sky, satisfy them, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of long life, good complexion, strength, eloquence, and ready speech. To those who approached seeking drink, he would satisfy them with various noble, excellent, blameless, and mind-delighting drinks, and teach them the <s>Dharma</s> for turning away from the thirst and attachment to <s>saṃsāra</s> and for generating thirst and delight in the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. To those who approached seeking flavors and the finest flavors, he satisfied them with the finest flavors of various kinds — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent. Moreover, he would teach them the <s>Dharma</s> for obtaining the marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) through the excellence of flavors. To those who came from various directions seeking vehicles, he would embrace them with gifts of various vehicles and teach them the <s>Dharma</s> for mounting the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). Knowing that those who came from various directions seeking clothing had approached, he reflected for a moment and gazed up at the vault of the sky. From that vault of the sky, garments of various hues and many colors — pure blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored — various cloths descended and came to rest upon his palm. Having furnished those petitioners with these, he would teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification and attainment of the unsurpassed golden-hued complexion, the modesty and decorum of a <s>Tathāgata</s>. In the same manner, with all kinds of requisites, he would furnish those petitioners as they came and teach them the <s>Dharma</s> as was fitting.

body.text: atha khalu vidvān gṛhapatiḥ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya tamacintyaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaviṣayamupadarśya evamāha - etamahaṃ kulaputra manaḥkośasaṃbhavavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ pariṣkāravaśitāprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ratnapāṇinā pratilabdhānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, vikurvitaṃ vā nidarśayitum, ye te sarvalokadhātūnanavaśeṣaṃ pāṇinā saṃchādya buddhapūjāvidhānatāyai sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu nānāvarṇaratnameghān pravarṣanti / evaṃ nānāvarṇā bharaṇameghān nānāvarṇakūṭāgārameghān nānāvarṇavicitravastrameghān nānādivyatūryatālopacārasaṃgītimanojñāmadhuranirghoṣān nānāvarṇagandhameghān nānāvarṇadhūpamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāsarvopakaraṇameghān sarvākārasarvabuddhapūjāmeghān pravarṣanti / sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu sarvasattvabhavaneṣu yaduta sarvabuddhapūjopasthānatāyai sarvasattvadhātuparipākavinayāya ca //
body.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, having shown the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> that inconceivable domain of <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), spoke thus: "I know this liberation born from the treasury of the mind (<s>manaḥkośasaṃbhavavimokṣa</s>). How could I know the conduct, or speak of the virtues, or demonstrate the miraculous transformations of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery over provisions, who have obtained the jewel in their hand — those who, covering all world-realms entirely with their palm, rain down clouds of jewels of various colors upon all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Buddhas</s>? Likewise they rain down clouds of ornaments of various colors, clouds of pavilions of various colors, clouds of variegated garments of various colors, melodious and sweet sounds of various divine musical instruments and cymbals, clouds of fragrances of various colors, clouds of incense, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and all requisites of various colors, clouds of all forms of worship of all <s>Buddhas</s> — upon all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> and upon the dwellings of all beings, for the purpose of attending upon and worshipping all <s>Buddhas</s> and for the ripening and disciplining of the entire realm of beings."

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe siṃhapotaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra ratnacūḍo nāma dharmaśreṣṭhī prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: "Go, O son of good family, right here in the southern region there is a city called <s>Siṃhapota</s>. There dwells a chief merchant of the <s>Dharma</s> named <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the practice of a <s>bodhisattva</s>? How should one conduct oneself?'"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto viduṣi gṛhapatau dharmagauravācchiṣyabhāvamupadarśya tadadhiṣṭhānātsarvabuddhadharmān saṃpaśyan, tadadhīnāṃ sarvajñatāṃ saṃpaśyan, kalyāṇamitrānācchedyaprematāmupadarśayan, kalyāṇamitreṣvatyantājñācintyatāṃ saṃdarśayan, kalyāṇamitravaśavartitāmanuvartayan, kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīvacanaṃ śuśrūṣamāṇaḥ, kalyāṇamitraprabhavaṃ śraddhendriyaṃ nidhyāyan, kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyanupreṣitaḥ, kalyāṇamitrābhirādhanānuvartanacitto viduṣo gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya vidvāṃsaṃ gṛhapatimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya viduṣo gṛhapaterantikātprakrāntaḥ // 15 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, satisfied, elated, contented, joyful, filled with delight and gladness of mind, showing the attitude of a disciple out of reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> toward the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, beholding all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> through his empowerment, beholding omniscience as dependent upon him, displaying unbreakable love toward spiritual friends, showing inconceivable and supreme respect for spiritual friends, following the guidance of spiritual friends, listening attentively to the instructions of spiritual friends, contemplating the faculty of faith that arises from spiritual friends, sent forth by the instruction of spiritual friends, with a mind devoted to pleasing and following spiritual friends — he bowed his head at the feet of the householder <s>Vidvān</s>, circumambulated the householder <s>Vidvān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the householder <s>Vidvān</s>. [15]

body.text: 18 Ratnacūḍaḥ /
body.translated_text: [18. <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tatpuṇyatoyaṃ saṃbhāvayan, tatpuṇyakṣetraṃ saṃpaśyan, tatpuṇyasumeruṃ pariśodhayan, tatpuṇyatīrthamavagāhayamānaḥ, tatpuṇyakośaṃ vivṛṇvan, tatpuṇyanidhimavalokayan, tatpuṇyamaṇḍalaṃ pariśodhayan, tatpuṇyaskadhaṃ samādadat, tatpuṇyabalaṃ saṃjanayan, tatpuṇyavegaṃ vivardhayan, anupūrveṇa yena siṃhapotaṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya ratnacūḍaṃ dharmaśreṣṭhinaṃ parimārgamāṇo 'drākṣīdantarāpaṇamadhyagatam / tasya pādau śirasābhivandya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / tatsādhu me āryo bodhisattvamārgamupadiśatu, yenāhaṃ mārgeṇa sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāyām //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, honoring that merit-water, beholding that merit-field, purifying that merit-<s>Sumeru</s>, plunging into that merit-ford, opening that merit-treasury, gazing upon that merit-storehouse, purifying that merit-<s>maṇḍala</s>, gathering that merit-aggregate, generating that merit-power, augmenting that merit-impetus — gradually approached the city of <s>Siṃhapota</s> and, searching for <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant, saw him seated in the midst of the marketplace. He bowed his head at his feet, circumambulated him, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. May the noble one kindly teach me the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, by which path I may proceed toward omniscience.' //

body.text:
atha khalu ratnacūḍo dharmaśreṣṭhī sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ pāṇau gṛhītvā yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkramya tadgṛhamupadarśya evamāha - prekṣasva kulaputra mama niveśanam / so 'nuvilokayan adrākṣīttadgṛhaṃ śuddhaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayaṃ vipulamudviddhaṃ rūpyaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ sphaṭikaprāsādasukṛtopaśobhitaṃ vaiḍūryakūṭaśatasahasrapratimaṇḍitaṃ musāragalvasamucchritastambhaṃ suprajñaptaṃ lohitamuktāmayasiṃhāsanaṃ jyotīrasamaṇiratnasiṃhadhvajasamuchritaṃ vairocanamaṇiratnavitānavitataṃ cintāmaṇivicitrahemajālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnapratimaṇḍitavyūhaṃ śītajalāśmagarbhamayapuṣkariṇīsamupetaṃ sarvaratnadrumaparivṛtaṃ vipulaṃ vistīrṇaṃ daśapuramudviddhamaṣṭadvāram / sa tadgṛhaṃ praviśya samantādanuvilokayati sma / sa prathame pure 'nnapānavidhiparityāgamadrākṣīt / dvitīye pure sarvavastravidhiparityāgam / tṛtīye pure sarvaratnābharaṇālaṃkāraparityāgam / caturthe pure 'ntaḥpureparibhogaratimahāpṛthivīkalyāṇakanyāratnaparityāgamadrākṣīt / pañcame pure pañcamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dharmasaṃgītiratiprayuktānāṃ lokahitasukhacittaceṣṭānāṃ sarvaśāstrāṇyabhinirhārayatāṃ dhāraṇīnayaṃ ca samādhisamudraṃ ca samādhivyutthānaṃ ca samādhivyavacāraṃ ca jñānālokaṃ ca abhinirhārayatāṃ saṃnipātamadrākṣīt / ṣaṣṭhe pure prajñāpāramitāvihārapratilabdhānāṃ gambhīraprajñānāṃ sarvadharmapraśāntābhijñānāṃ bhūmisamādhidhāraṇīmukhagarbhasamantamukhaniryātānām anāvaraṇagocarāṇām advayasamudācārāṇāṃ dharmasaṃgītiṃ kurvatāṃ prajñāpāramitāparivartanamanusaratāṃ vibhajatāmuttānī kurvatāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃnipātamadrākṣīt imāni prajñāpāramitāmukhāni saṃgāyatām - yaduta śāntigarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, sarvajagajjñānasuvibhaktaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, acalāvartaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, virajaḥprabhāsaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, duryodhanagarbhaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, jagadrocanāmaṇḍalaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, anugamanayamaṇḍalaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, sāgaragarbhaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, samantacakṣurupekṣāpratilabdhaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, akṣayakośānugamaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, sarvadharmanayasāgaraṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, sarvajagatsāgarānugamaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham, asaṅgapratibhānaṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham,
dharmameghāvalambānupūrvābhilambhanilayaṃ
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant, taking the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> by the hand, approached his own dwelling and, showing him that house, spoke thus: 'Behold, son of good family, my dwelling!' He, looking all around, saw that house — pure, radiant, made of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, vast and lofty, enclosed by silver ramparts, beautifully embellished with crystal palaces, adorned with a hundred thousand <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) turrets, with pillars raised of coral, well-appointed with lion-thrones made of red pearls, with raised lion-banner poles of <s>jyotīrasa</s> gem-jewels, with canopies spread of <s>Vairocana</s> gem-jewels, covered with nets of golden <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems of variegated design, adorned with arrays of innumerable gem-jewels, furnished with pools made of cool water-crystal-womb stones, surrounded by rows of all jewel-trees, vast, extensive, rising to the height of ten cities, with eight gates. He entered that house and looked all around. In the first city he saw the gift-giving of food, drink, and provisions. In the second city, the gift-giving of all kinds of garments. In the third city, the gift-giving of all jewel-ornaments and adornments. In the fourth city, he saw the gift-giving of the inner palace's enjoyments, pleasures, great earth, auspicious maiden-jewels. In the fifth city, he saw an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the fifth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), engaged in the delight of <s>Dharma</s>-recitation, whose bodily and mental activities were for the welfare and happiness of the world, who were bringing forth all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), and who were bringing forth the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-method, the ocean of <s>samādhi</s>, the emergence from <s>samādhi</s>, the range of <s>samādhi</s>, and the light of knowledge. In the sixth city, he saw an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the dwelling in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), who possessed profound wisdom, who had superknowledge of the quiescence of all <s>dharmas</s>, who had emerged through the universal gateway of the womb of the <s>bhūmis</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, and <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, whose domain was unobstructed, whose conduct was non-dual, who were engaged in <s>Dharma</s>-recitation, following, analyzing, and elucidating the perfection of wisdom — reciting these gateways of the perfection of wisdom: namely, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Śāntigarbha</s> (Womb of Peace), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvajagajjñānasuvibhakta</s> (Well-Differentiated Knowledge of All Beings), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Acalāvarta</s> (Immovable Vortex), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Virajaḥprabhāsa</s> (Stainless Radiance), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Duryodhanagarbha</s> (Womb of Invincible Valor), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Jagadrocanāmaṇḍala</s> (Maṇḍala of World-Illumination), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Anugamanayamaṇḍala</s> (Maṇḍala of the Method of Following), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sāgaragarbha</s> (Ocean-Womb), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantacakṣūpekṣāpratilabdha</s> (Attained through Universal-Eye Equanimity), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Akṣayakośānugama</s> (Following the Inexhaustible Treasury), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvadharmanayasāgara</s> (Ocean of the Method of All Dharmas), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvajagatsāgarānugama</s> (Following the Ocean of All Beings), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Asaṅgapratibhāna</s> (Unattached Eloquence), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Dharmameghāvalambānupūrvābhilambhanilaya</s> (Abode of Successive Grasping Depending on Dharma-Clouds)

body.text: ca nāma prajñāpāramitāmukham / itīmāni prajñāpāramitāmukhāni pramukhaṃ kṛtvā paripūrṇāni daśa prajñāpāramitāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi, yāni tān bodhisattvānanabhilāpyavyūhasuvibhaktaparṣanmaṇḍalasthitān saṃgāyato 'drākṣīt / saptame pure pratiśrutkopamakṣāntipratilabdhānāmupāyajñānaviniścayaniryātānāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratyeṣakāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃnipātamadrākṣīt / aṣṭame pure 'cyutagāminyabhijñāpratilabdhānāṃ sarvalokadhātvanuvicaraṇānāṃ sarvaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsaprāptānāṃ sarvadharmadhātusuvibhaktaśarīrāṇāṃ sarvatathāgatapādamūlāsaṃbhinnaviṣayāṇāṃ sarvabuddhakāyasamavasaraṇānāṃ sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalapūrvagamakathāpuruṣāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃnipātamadrākṣīt / navame pure ekajātipratibaddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃnipātamadrākṣīt / daśame pure sarvatathāgatānāṃ saprathamopacittotpādacaryāniryāṇapraṇidhānasāgarān sarvabuddhadharmavikurvitaviṣayān sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanmaṇḍalān sarvabuddhadharmacakranirghoṣān sarvasattvavinayādhiṣṭhānavyūhānadrākṣīt //
body.translated_text: — headed by these, he saw a full ten innumerable hundred-thousands of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateways, which those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, stationed in the assembly-maṇḍala of the inexpressible well-differentiated array, were reciting. In the seventh city, he saw an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the endurance like an echo (<s>pratiśrutkopamakṣānti</s>), who had emerged through the decisiveness of the knowledge of skillful means, who were seekers of the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In the eighth city, he saw an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the superknowledge leading to the unfailing course (<s>acyutagāminī abhijñā</s>), who traversed all world-realms, who had attained reflection in all assembly-maṇḍalas, whose bodies were well-differentiated throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, whose domain was unbroken at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who assembled in the bodies of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who were heralds of the assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In the ninth city, he saw an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound to a single birth (<s>ekajātipratibaddha</s>). In the tenth city, he saw the oceans of the aggregate of practice, aspiration, and setting-forth from the first generation of the mind of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the domains of transformation of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the sounds of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>, and the arrays of the empowerment for the discipline of all beings. //

body.text: dṛṣṭvā ca ratnacūḍaṃ dharmaśreṣṭhinametadavocat - ārya, kutaste iyamevaṃrūpā saṃpadviśodhitā? kutra te kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yasya tava iyamīdṛśī vipākasaṃpat? sa āha - smarāmi kulaputra atīte 'dhvani buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa paratareṇa cakravicitre lokadhātāvanantaraśmidharmadhātusamalaṃkṛtadharmarājo nāma tathāgato loke udapādi, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / sa khalu punastathāgato jñānavairocanapramukhena śrāvakakoṭīśatena jñānasūryatejaḥpramukhena ca bodhisattvakoṭīśatasahasreṇa sārdhaṃ maṇidhvajavyūharājamahodyānadharaṇipraviṣṭo rājñā dharmeśvararājena abhinimantritaḥ / tasya me tathāgatasya nagarapraviṣṭasyāntarāpaṇamadhyagatasya tūryanādanirnāditaṃ kāritam / ekā ca gandhagulikā nidhūpitā tasya bhagavataḥ sabodhisattvaśrāvakasaṃghasya pūjākarmaṇe / tayā ca gandhagulikayā nidhūpitayā saptāhaṃ sarvajambudvīpo 'nantavarṇaiḥ sarvasattvakāyasadṛśairdhūpapaṭalameghaiḥ saṃchanno 'bhūt / tebhyaśca dhūpapaṭalameghebhya evaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścarati sma - aciantyastathāgatatryadhvavipulena skandhena samanvāgataḥ, sarvajñaḥ sarvāvaraṇavigataḥ sarvakleśavāsanāprahīṇaḥ, sarvatathāgatāvaropitā dakṣiṇā, apramāṇasarvajñātāphaladāyikā sarvajñatāsamavasaraṇā iti - yaduta asmatkuśalamūlaparipākārthamacintyasattvakuśalamūlavegasaṃjananārthaṃ ca / tebhyo dhūpapaṭalameghebhyo buddhādhiṣṭhānena ayamevaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścacāra / tacca me kulaputra tathāgatādhiṣṭhānaṃ saṃdarśanaprātihāryakuśalamūlaṃ triṣu sthāneṣu pariṇāmitam / katameṣu triṣu? yaduta atyantasarvadāridrayasamucchedāya saddharmaśravaṇāvirahitatāyai sarvabuddhabodhisattvakalyāṇamitradarśanaparipūraye ca / etamahaṃ kulaputra, apratihatapraṇidhimaṇḍalavyūhabodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamacintyāpramāṇaguṇaratnākarāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, ye te asaṃbhinnabuddhaśarīrasāgarāvatīrṇāḥ, ye te asaṃbhinnadharmameghasaṃpratīcchakāḥ, ye te asaṃbhinnaguṇasāgarapratipannāḥ, ye te samantabhadracaryājālavisṛtāḥ, ye te asaṃbhinnasamādhiviṣayāvatīrṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Having seen this, he spoke thus to <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant: 'Noble one, from where was this kind of magnificent attainment purified for you? Where were your roots of merit planted, that you have such a fruit of ripening?' He replied: 'I recall, son of good family, in the past, beyond a number of <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in the world-realm <s>Cakravicitra</s> (Variegated Wheel), a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Anantaraśmidharmādhātusamalaṃkṛtadharmarāja</s> (Dharma-King Adorned with the Dharmadhātu of Infinite Rays) arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of <s>devas</s> and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. That <s>Tathāgata</s>, together with a retinue of a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> headed by <s>Jñānavairocan</s>a and a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> headed by <s>Jñānasūryatejas</s>, entered the great park called <s>Maṇidhvajavyūharāja</s>, invited by King <s>Dharmeśvararāja</s>. For that <s>Tathāgata</s>, as he entered the city and was in the midst of the marketplace, I caused musical instruments to sound. And one single ball of incense was offered in worship for that <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>. And from that single ball of incense, when it was burned, for seven days all <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was covered with clouds of incense-masses of innumerable colors resembling the bodies of all beings. And from those clouds of incense-masses there issued forth this kind of sound: "Inconceivable is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowed with the vast aggregate of the three times, omniscient, free from all obstructions, with all <s>kleśa</s>-impressions abandoned, planted with the merit-offering of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, bestowing the fruit of immeasurable omniscience, assembling in omniscience" — that is, "for the ripening of our roots of merit and for generating the inconceivable impetus of the roots of merit of beings." From those clouds of incense-masses, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, this kind of sound issued forth. And that, son of good family, was a root of merit through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s display-miracle, which I dedicated to three things. Which three? Namely: to the utter cutting off of all poverty, to never being separated from hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, and to the fulfillment of seeing all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattva</s> spiritual friends. This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Apratihatapraṇidhimaṇḍalavyūha</s> (Array of the Maṇḍala of Unobstructed Vows) that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> of inconceivable, immeasurable quality-jewel-mines — those who have descended into the ocean of the undivided <s>Buddha</s>-body, who receive the undivided <s>Dharma</s>-clouds, who have entered the undivided ocean of qualities, who have cast forth the net of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-conduct, who have descended into the undivided domain of <s>samādhi</s>

body.text:
ye te asaṃbhinnasarvabodhisattvaikaghanakuśalamūlāḥ ye te asaṃbhinnatathāgatāvikalpavihāriṇaḥ, ye te asaṃbhinnatryadhvasamatāvatīrṇāḥ,ye te asaṃbhinnasarvakalpasaṃvāsāparikhinnāḥ,
ye te asaṃbhinnasamantacakṣurviṣayabhūmipratiṣṭhitāḥ //
body.translated_text: those whose roots of merit are of the undivided single mass of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those who dwell in the undivided non-conceptual abiding of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, those who have descended into the undivided equality of the three times, those who are unwearied in the undivided co-habitation of all <s>kalpas</s>, those who are established on the ground of the undivided domain of the universal eye? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe vetramūlako nāma janapadaḥ / tatra samantamukhe nagare samantanetro nāma gāndhikaḥ śreṣṭhī prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family; right here in <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region) is a country called <s>Vetramūlaka</s>. There, in the city of <s>Samantamukha</s>, dwells a perfumer-merchant named <s>Samantanetra</s> (Universal Eye). Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako ratnacūḍasya dharmaśreṣṭhinaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ratnacūḍaṃ dharmaśreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛutya punaḥ punaravalokya ratnacūḍasya dharmaśreṣṭhino 'ntikātprakrāntaḥ // 16 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant, circumambulating <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> the <s>Dharma</s>-merchant. // 16 //

body.text: 19 Samantanetraḥ /
body.translated_text: 19. <s>Samantanetra</s>. /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nantabuddhadarśanāvatīrṇo 'nantabodhisattvasamavadhānaprāpto 'nantabodhisattvamārganayāvabhāsito 'nantabodhisattvadharmanayābhiṣyanditaniścitacitto 'nantabodhisattvādhimuktipathaviśuddhiranantabodhisattvendriyāvabhāsapratilabdho 'nantabodhisattvāśayabalapratiṣṭhito 'nantabodhisattvacaryānugatacetāḥ anantabodhisattvapraṇidhānabalasaṃjāto 'nantabodhisattvāparājitadhvajo 'nantabodhisattvajñānālokaparivartī anantabodhisattvādharmāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ anupūrveṇa yena vetramūlako nāma janapadastenopasaṃkramya samantamukhaṃ nagaraṃ parimārgan samantadigvidikṣu deśapradeśopacāreṣu nimnonnatasamaviṣameṣu aparikhinnāśayo 'viśraman samānacitto 'vivartyavīryo 'paryādattacetano 'vismṛtakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanaḥsadākalyāṇamitrasamudācārahṛdayavāsanaḥ samantamukhavijñaptīndriyaḥ sarvapramādavigato visphāritakarṇacakṣuḥ sarvataḥ parigaveṣamāṇo 'drākṣītsamantamukhaṃ nagaram, madhye vetramūlasya janapadasya daśānāṃ paṭṭanasahasrāṇāṃ nigamaṃ supariniṣṭhitaṃ dṛḍhaprākāramudviddhamaṣṭacatvaropaśobhitam / tasya madhye samantanetraṃ gāndhikamadrākṣīt gāndhikavīthyāmupaviṣṭam / dṛṣṭvā ca yena samantanetro gāndhikastenopasaṃkramya samantanetrasya gāndhikasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / āha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvānāṃ vyādhīn prajānāmi vātasamutthānapi, pittasamutthānapi, śleṣmasamutthānapi, sabhāgakṣubhitānapi, paropakramitānapi, amanuṣyavaikārikānapi, viṣamaparopakramikānapi, vividhamantraśastravetālaprayogāgnisamutthānapi, udakasaṃkṣobhasamutthānapi, vividhabhayaṃsaṃtrāsasaṃbhavānapi / teṣāṃ ca sarvavyādhīnāṃ praśamaṃ prajānāmiyaduta snehanaṃ prajānāmi, vamanaṃ virecanamāsthāpanaṃ raktāvasecanaṃ nāsākarma karṣupariṇāhaṃ pariṣvedanamanulepanaṃ viṣapratighātaṃ bhūtagrahapratiṣedhaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ snapanaṃ saṃvāsanaṃ saṃvardhanaṃ varṇapariśodhanaṃ balasaṃjananaṃ prajānāmi / ye kulaputra
sattvā mamāntikamupasaṃkrāmanti daśabhyo digbhyaḥ, teṣāmahaṃ sarveṣāṃ vyādhīn praśamayāmi / vyādhipraśāntāṃśca susnātānuliptagātrān kṛtvā yathārhābharaṇavibhūṣitāṅgān yathārhavastrasaṃchāditaśarīrān vividhabhojanarasāgraiḥ saṃtarpya aparimitadhanasamṛddhān karomi / uttare caiṣāṃ rāgaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi aśubhopasaṃhāreṇa / doṣaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi mahāmaitrīsaṃvarṇanatayā / mohaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi dharmapravicayaprabhedapradarśanatayā / samabhāgacaryākleśaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / viśeṣaparijñānayamukhasaṃprakāśanatayā bodhicittasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / sarvabuddhaguṇadharmasaṃprayuktakathāsaṃprakāśanatayā mahākaruṇāsaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / aparimāṇasaṃsāraduḥkhasaṃprakāśanatayā aparimitaguṇapratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / vipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayasaṃvarṇanatayā mahāyānapraṇidhānasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / sarvasattvaparipākavinayasaṃdarśanatayā samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / sarvakṣetrasarvakalpasaṃvāsacaryājālapravistaraṇatayā
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having descended into the vision of infinite <s>Buddha</s>s, having attained the assembly of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, having been illuminated by the methods of the path of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, having his mind made resolute through the flow of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharma</s> methods, having attained the purification of the path of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s> aspiration and the illumination of the faculties of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, being established in the power of the intention of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with a mind following the conduct of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, born from the power of the vows of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, bearing the unconquered banner of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, revolving in the light of the knowledge of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s, having attained the illumination of the non-<s>Dharma</s> of infinite <s>bodhisattva</s>s — gradually approached the region called <s>Vetramūlaka</s> and searched for the city of <s>Samantamukha</s> in all directions and intermediate directions, in the vicinity of various places, on uneven and even ground, with unwearied intention, without rest, with an equanimous mind, with irreversible vigor, with an unexhausted mind, not forgetting the instructions of his spiritual friend, always carrying in his heart the conduct of his spiritual friend, with faculties alert in all directions, free from all heedlessness, with ears and eyes wide open, searching everywhere — he saw the city of <s>Samantamukha</s>, in the middle of the <s>Vetramūlaka</s> region, a well-established market town among ten thousand cities, with firm ramparts, lofty, adorned with eighty-four features. In its midst he saw the perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s> seated in the perfumers' street. Having seen him, he approached the perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s>, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: "Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one should practice." He replied: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family (<s>kulaputra</s>), that you have generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening. I, son of good family, know all the diseases of all beings — those arising from <s>vāta</s> (wind), those arising from <s>pitta</s> (bile), those arising from <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), those arising from combined disturbance, those caused by others' attacks, those caused by non-human beings (<s>amanuṣya</s>), those from irregular external harm, those arising from various applications of <s>mantra</s>s, weapons, <s>vetāla</s> practices, and fire, those arising from water disturbances, and those born from various fears and terrors. And I know the pacification of all these diseases — namely, I know oleation (<s>snehana</s>), emesis (<s>vamana</s>), purgation (<s>virecana</s>), enema (<s>āsthāpana</s>), bloodletting (<s>raktāvasecana</s>), nasal therapy (<s>nāsākarma</s>), compresses (<s>karṣupariṇāha</s>), sudation (<s>pariṣvedana</s>), anointing (<s>anulepana</s>), antidotes to poison (<s>viṣapratighāta</s>), warding off evil spirits (<s>bhūtagrahapratiṣedha</s>), nourishing therapy (<s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>), bathing (<s>snapana</s>), fumigation (<s>saṃvāsana</s>), growth therapy (<s>saṃvardhana</s>), purification of complexion (<s>varṇapariśodhana</s>), and generation of strength (<s>balasaṃjanana</s>). Those beings, son of good family, who approach me from the ten directions — I pacify all their diseases. Having pacified their diseases, I bathe and anoint their bodies, adorn their limbs with appropriate ornaments, clothe their bodies in appropriate garments, satisfy them with the finest food and drink, and make them endowed with immeasurable wealth and prosperity. Furthermore, I teach them the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of passion (<s>rāga</s>) through contemplation of the impure; I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of hatred (<s>doṣa</s>) through the praise of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>); I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of delusion (<s>moha</s>) through demonstrating the analysis of the <s>Dharma</s>; I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) of mixed conduct through illuminating the gateway of special comprehensive knowledge. I illuminate the cause for the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) through elucidating discourses connected with the qualities of all <s>Buddha</s>s. I illuminate the cause for the arising of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) through elucidating the sufferings of immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s>. I illuminate the cause for attaining immeasurable qualities through praising the accumulation of vast merit and knowledge. I illuminate the cause for the arising of <s>Mahāyāna</s> vows through demonstrating the ripening and discipline of all beings. I illuminate the cause for attaining the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> through the extensive spreading of the net of conduct dwelling in all realms and all eons,

body.text:
lakṣaṇānuvyañjanopacitabuddhaśarīrapratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / dānapāramitāsaṃvarṇanatayā sarvatragāminītathāgatapariśuddhipratilābhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / śīlapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā acintyatathāgatarūpavarṇaviśuddhisaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / kṣāntipāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā duryodhanatathāgataśarīrasaṃbhavahetuṃ paridīpayāmi / vīryapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā abhibhūtānabhibhūtatathāgatātmabhāvaviśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / dhyānapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā dharmaśarīraviśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / prajñāpāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā sarvajagadabhimukhabuddhātmabhāvaviśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / upāyakauśalyapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā sarvakalpakālajagaccittasaṃveśanaśarīraviśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / praṇidhānapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā sarvabuddhakṣetrābhyudgatātmabhāvaviśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / balapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā sarvajagadyathāśayasaṃtoṣaṇakāyapariśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi / jñānapāramitāsaṃprakāśanatayā paramaśubhadarśanakāyapariśuddhiṃ paridīpayāmi, yaduta sarvākuśaladharmavinivartanasaṃprakāśanatayā / evaṃ caitān dharmadānena saṃgṛhya anantadhanaratnopacayopastabdhān kṛtvā visarjayāmi / api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra sarvagandhadhūpavāsanānulepanayuktīḥ prajānāmi yaduta atulagandharājapramukhāḥ / sindhuvāritagandharājapramukhā
ajitāvatigandharājapramukhā vibodhanagandharājapramukhā aruṇavatigandharājapramukhāḥ kālānusārigandharājapramukhā uragasāracandanagandharājapramukhā meghāgarugandharājapramukhā akṣobhyendriyagandharājapramukhāḥ sarvagandhayuktīḥ prajānāmi / api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇasamantamukhabuddhadarśanapūjopasthānagandhabimbaṃ prajānāmi //
body.translated_text: I illuminate the cause for attaining a <s>Buddha</s> body endowed with the marks and minor characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>). By praising the <s>pāramitā</s> of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), I illuminate the cause for attaining the purity of the all-pervading <s>Tathāgata</s>. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), I illuminate the cause for the arising of the inconceivable purity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form and color. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), I illuminate the cause for the arising of the indomitable body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), I illuminate the purity of the unconquered and unconquerable self-nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), I illuminate the purity of the <s>Dharma</s> body. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), I illuminate the purity of the <s>Buddha</s>'s self-nature facing all worlds. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), I illuminate the purity of the body that enters the minds of all beings in all eons and times. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), I illuminate the purity of the self-nature arisen from all <s>Buddha</s> fields. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers (<s>bala</s>), I illuminate the purity of the body that satisfies all beings according to their dispositions. By elucidating the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), I illuminate the purity of the body of supremely auspicious appearance — namely, through elucidating the turning away from all unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s. Thus, having gathered them through this gift of <s>Dharma</s> and having established them with the accumulation of infinite wealth and jewels, I send them forth. Moreover, son of good family, I know all the preparations of incense, perfume, fumigation, and ointments — namely, those headed by the supreme <s>Atulagandharāja</s> (Incomparable King of Fragrances), those headed by <s>Sindhuvāritagandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Ajitāvatigandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Vibodhanagandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Aruṇavatigandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Kālānusārigandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Uragasāracandanagandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Meghāgarugandharāja</s>, those headed by <s>Akṣobhyendriyagandharāja</s> — I know all preparations of fragrances. Moreover, son of good family, I know the incense image (<s>gandhabimba</s>) of the worship and attendance upon the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Samantamukha</s> that satisfies all beings.

body.text: itaśca me kulaputra, sarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇātsamantamukhabuddhadarśanapūjopasthānagandhabimbātsarvābhiprāyāḥ paripūryante, yena sarvasattvaparitrāṇālaṃkārameghānadhitiṣṭhāmi / yaduta gandhavimānālaṃ kārameghān yāvatsarvākāratathāgatapūjopasthānālaṃkārameghānadhitiṣṭhāmi / yadāhaṃ kulaputra tathāgatān pūjayitukāmo bhavāmi, tadāhamitaḥ sarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇāt samantamukhabuddhadarśanapūjopasthānagandhabimbādaparimāṇān gandhakośakūṭāgārameghānniścārya daśadiksarvadharmadhātugateṣu sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu sarvagandhakośakūṭāgārameghālaṃkāraṃ sarvadharmadhātumadhitiṣṭhāmi / sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhabhavanameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhaprākārameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhaniryūhavyūhameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhatoraṇameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhagavākṣameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhaharmikameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhārdhacandrameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhacchatrameghālaṃkāraṃ samucchritagandhadhvajameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhapatākāmeghālaṃkāraṃ gandhavitānameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhavigrahajālameghālaṃkāraṃ gandhaprabhāmeghālaṃkāraṃ gandhāvabhāsavimalavyūhameghālaṃkāraṃ sarvagandhameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ sarvadharmadhātumadhitiṣṭhāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇaṃ samantamukhabuddhadarśanapūjopasthānagandhabimbaṃ dharmamukhaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bhaiṣajyarājakalpānāṃ bodhisattvānāmamoghadarśanānāmamoghaśravaṇānāmamoghasaṃvāsānāmamoghānusmṛtīnāmamoghānuvratānāmamoghanuvratānāmamoghanāmadheyagrahaṇānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena ca sarvasattvānāṃ sarvakleśāḥ praśamanti, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā vinivartante sarvāpāyagatibhyaḥ,
body.translated_text: And from this, son of good family, from the incense image of the worship and attendance upon the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Samantamukha</s> that satisfies all beings, all my aspirations are fulfilled, by which I project clouds of ornaments for the protection of all beings — namely, clouds of ornaments of incense palaces, up to clouds of ornaments for the worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all their aspects. When I, son of good family, wish to worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, then from this incense image of the worship and attendance upon the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Samantamukha</s> that satisfies all beings, I send forth immeasurable clouds of incense treasury mansions and project the adornment of clouds of all incense treasury mansions throughout the assemblies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in the ten directions — clouds of adornment purifying all <s>Buddha</s> fields, clouds of adornment of incense dwellings, clouds of adornment of incense ramparts, clouds of adornment of incense turret arrays, clouds of adornment of incense gateways, clouds of adornment of incense windows, clouds of adornment of incense balconies, clouds of adornment of incense half-moons, clouds of adornment of incense parasols, clouds of adornment of lofty incense banners, clouds of adornment of incense pennants, clouds of adornment of incense canopies, clouds of adornment of incense figure-nets, clouds of adornment of incense radiance, clouds of adornment of stainless arrays of incense splendor, adornment of raining all incense clouds — I project all this throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. This, son of good family, is the <s>Dharma</s> gateway I know — the incense image of the worship and attendance upon the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Samantamukha</s> that satisfies all beings. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattva</s>s who are like the king of medicines (<s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>), whose sight is never in vain, whose hearing is never in vain, whose company is never in vain, whose recollection is never in vain, whose following is never in vain, the taking of whose name is never in vain — by whose mere sight all the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) of all beings are pacified, by whose mere sight beings are turned away from all lower destinies (<s>apāya</s>),

body.text: yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā avakāśaṃ labhante buddhadharmeṣu, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvānāmupaśamanti sarvaduḥkhaskandhāḥ, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā vigatabhayā bhavanti sarvasaṃsāragatibhyaḥ, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā abhayaprāptā bhavanti sarvajñatādigupanayatayā, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā na pratipatanti jarāmaraṇaśvabhraprapāteṣu, yeṣāṃ sahadarśanena sattvā nirvṛtisukhaṃ pratilabhante dharmadhātusamatāsthānena //
body.translated_text: by whose mere sight beings gain access to the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, by whose mere sight all the masses of suffering of beings are pacified, by whose mere sight beings become free from fear of all the destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s>, by whose mere sight beings attain fearlessness through being led to omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), by whose mere sight beings do not fall into the precipice of old age and death, by whose mere sight beings attain the bliss of <s>nirvṛti</s> (final peace) through abiding in the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, idamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe tāladhvajaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra analo nāma rājā prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here in the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>) there is a city called <s>Tāladhvaja</s>. There dwells a king named <s>Anala</s>. Approach him and ask: "How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantanetrasya gāndhikaśreṣṭhinaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya samantanetraṃ gāndhikaṃ śreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya samantanetrasya gāndhikaśreṣṭhino 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 17 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the chief perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s>, circumambulated the chief perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the chief perfumer <s>Samantanetra</s>. [17]

body.text: 20 Analaḥ /
body.translated_text: [20 <s>Anala</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastāṃ kalyāṇamitraparaṃparāmanusmaran, tāni kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīmukhāni manasikurvan, parigṛhīto 'smi kalyāṇamitrairiti svacittaṃ saṃtoṣayan, kalyāṇamitrārakṣito 'smi na bhūyo vinivartiṣyāmi anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherityanuvicintayan pratyalabhata cittaprītim / cittaprasādaṃ cittaprāmodyaṃ cittatuṣṭiṃ cittapraharṣaḥ cittanandīṃ cittavyupaśamaṃ cittavipulatāṃ cittālaṃkāratāṃ cittāsaṅgatāṃ cittānāvaraṇatāṃ cittaviviktatāṃ cittasamavasaraṇatāṃ cittavaśitāṃ cittaiśvaryaṃ cittadharmānugamaṃ cittakṣetraspharaṇatāṃ buddhadarśanālaṃkāracittatāṃ daśabalamanasikārāvipravāsacittatāṃ pratyalabhata / so 'nupūrveṇa janapadena janapadaṃ grāmeṇa grāmaṃ deśena deśaṃ parimārgan yena tāladhvajaṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya paripṛcchati sma - kutrānalo rājeti / tamanyo janakāya etadavocat - eṣa kulaputra analo rājā arthakaraṇe siṃhāsanopaviṣṭo rājakāryaṃ karoti / janapadān praśāsti / nigrahītavyānnigṛhṇāti, pragrahītavyān pragṛhṇāti, aparādhitān daṇḍaṃ praṇayati / vivadatāṃ vivādaṃ chinatti / dīnānāśvāsayati / dṛptān damayati / prāṇivadhādvinivartayati / adattādānādvicchandayati / pariparigṛhītābhilāṣād vyupaśamayati / mṛṣāvādādvinivārayati / piśunayavacanādvivecayati / paruṣavacanādviramayati / saṃbhinnapralāpād vyāvartayati / abhidhyāyā viśleṣayati / vyāpādāddūrīkaroti mithādṛṣṭerviyojayati //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, remembering that succession of spiritual friends, attending to those gateways of the instructions of spiritual friends, gratifying his own mind [with the thought] 'I am embraced by spiritual friends,' reflecting 'I am protected by spiritual friends; I shall not turn back from unsurpassed perfect awakening' — he attained joy of mind, clarity of mind, delight of mind, satisfaction of mind, elation of mind, gladness of mind, tranquility of mind, vastness of mind, adornment of mind, non-attachment of mind, non-obstruction of mind, solitude of mind, convergence of mind, mastery of mind, sovereignty of mind, following the <s>Dharma</s> of mind, pervading fields with mind, the mind adorned with seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the mind of not departing from attention to the ten powers — he attained [all these]. Gradually, from region to region, village to village, country to country, searching, he approached the city called <s>Tāladhvaja</s> and inquired: 'Where is King <s>Anala</s>?' Another group of people said to him: 'This, O son of good family, is King <s>Anala</s>, seated on a lion-throne in the hall of justice, performing the business of kingship. He governs the provinces. He restrains those who should be restrained, and supports those who should be supported. He punishes those who have committed offenses. He settles the disputes of those who are in dispute. He consoles the wretched. He tames the arrogant. He turns [people] away from killing living beings. He dissuades [them] from taking what is not given. He pacifies [them] from the desire for the possessions of others. He prevents [them] from speaking falsehoods. He separates [them] from slanderous speech. He makes [them] desist from harsh speech. He diverts [them] from idle gossip. He disentangles [them] from covetousness. He distances [them] from malice. He separates [them] from wrong views.' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena analo rājā tenopajagāma / so 'drākṣīdanalaṃ rājānaṃ nārāyaṇavajramaṇivicitre asaṃkhyeyanānāvidhaprabhāsvaratnapāde anekaratnasuracitālaṃkārarucirabimbe, kāñcanasūtrajālaśvetasupariniṣṭhite, anekamaṇiratnadīpapradyotite, vaśirājamaṇiratnamayapadmagarbhe anekadivyaratnavastrasuprajñapte, vividhadivyagandhadhūpitopacāre ucchritaratnadhvajachatraśatasahasravirājite ratnapatākāśatasahasrodviddhopaśobhite vicitraratnapuṣpadāmakalāpābhipralambitojjvalite vividhadivyaratnavitānavitate mahāratnasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaṃ navaṃ daharaṃ taruṇamabhirūpaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyamabhinīlapradakṣiṇāvartakeśaṃ chatrākāramūrdhānamuṣṇīṣaśirasaṃ pṛthulalāṭamabhinīlaviśālagopakṣmanayanaṃ madhuronnatacārutuṅganāsāvaṃśaṃ hiṅgulukasuvarṇasuśliṣṭauṣṭhaṃ samavahitasuśuklapūrṇacatvāriṃśaddantaṃ siṃhahanuṃ paripūrṇopacitakapolaṃ suruciracāpāyatabhruvaṃ śaśāṅkavarṇorṇayā kṛtatilakamāyatapramuktapralambakarṇaṃ pūrṇacandrasaumyavadanaṃ kamburuciravṛttagrīvaṃ śrīvatsālaṃkṛtahṛdayaṃ siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaṃ citāntarāṃsaṃ susaṃvṛttoruskandhaṃ pralambabāhuṃ jālāvanaddhāṅgulicakrāṅkitahastapādaṃ mṛdutarūṇopacitapāṇipādaṃ saptotsadaṃ vajrasadṛśamadhyaṃ bṛhadṛjugātraṃ suvartitoruṃ kośagatabastiguhyam eṇeyajaṅghaṃ dirghāṅgulimāyatapādapārṣṇi vyāmaprabhaṃ suvarṇacchavimekaikapradakṣiṇordhvāṅgaromaṃ nyagrodharājaparimaṇḍalaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanopacitaśarīraṃ cintārājamaṇiratnamukuṭāvabaddhaśirasaṃ jāmbūnadakanakārdhacandraracitalalāṭālaṃkāramindranīlamaṇivimalanīlakuṇḍalapralambitakarṇamanardhyamaṇiratnahāraprabhāvabhāsitavimalavipulopacitavakṣasaṃ
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> approached King <s>Anala</s>. He saw King <s>Anala</s> seated on a lion-throne variegated with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-vajra jewels, in an incomparable assembly-hall arrayed with all jewels, with a body beautiful to behold, with the supreme mark of a great man — the long arms, the broad chest of a lion, with arms adorned and playing with divine supreme gem-jewel armlets and bracelets,

body.text:
divyottamamaṇikeyūrabalayavidaṣṭavikrīḍitabāhuṃ daśaratnaśalākāśatasuvibhaktena jāmbūnadakanakacchadanena jyotīrasamahāmaṇiratnasuviśuddhagarbheṇa ratnaghaṇṭāmālāniścaritamanojñamadhuraghoṣeṇa samantadiṅmahāmaṇiratnāvabhāsaprāptena
vimalavaiḍūryamaṇiratnadaṇḍena mahatā ratnacchatreṇa dhāryatā mahārājādhipatyaprāptamapratihataparacakraśāsanaṃ vigataparacakrabhayaiśvaryam / tasya samantāddaśāmātyasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni saṃniṣaṇṇāni rājakāryaprayuktānyapaśyat //
