body.translated_text: wearing ten jewel-rod-studded, well-divided, <s>jāmbūnada</s>-gold canopy-crowns with flame-radiance gem-jewel crests, with a moon-disc face shedding a gentle, pleasing radiance, with locks of deep-blue <s>vaidūrya</s>-colored hair, with a forehead bearing the mark of a <s>maṇi</s>-jewel, with eyes like the petals of a fully-blooming lotus — surrounded by ten thousand ministers, with ten thousand princes standing before him, guarded by ten thousand warriors, praised by ten thousand reciters of his fame, with ten thousand counselors deliberating on affairs, with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of brāhmaṇas, householders, merchants, caravan-leaders, ministers, commander-chiefs, city-lords, provincial governors, and frontier-officials.

body.text: daśa cāsya kāraṇāpurūṣasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni purata upasthāpitāni narakapālasadṛśāni yamapuruṣakalpāni vikṛtapadadhārīṇi raudravikṛtabhayasaṃjananāni raktanayanāni saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhatrivalībhṛkuṭīkṛtavadanāni asiparaśuśaktitomarabhuśuṇḍiśūlapraharaṇagṛhītāni viṣamavikṛtaduḥsaṃsthitavadanaśarīrāṇi meghavarṇāni bhīmarūpacaṇḍasvaranirghoṣāṇi durnirīkṣyatejāṃsi mahābhayakarāṇi prāṇiśatasahasrahṛdayasaṃtrāsasaṃjananāni nigṛhītavyasattvanigrahaprayuktāni apaśyat / tatra bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi corāṇāṃ parasvāpahāriṇā parasattvabhogavipralopināṃ panthamoṣakāṇāṃ grāmanagaranigamaghoṣadāhakānāṃ kulaghātakānāṃ saṃdhicchedakānāṃ kilbiṣakāriṇāṃ garadāyakānāṃ ḍāmarikānāṃ manuṣyaghātakānāṃ paradārasevināṃ mithyāpratipannānāṃ duṣṭacetasāmabhidhyālūnāṃ vividhapāpakrūrakarmakāriṇāṃ gāḍhapañcabandhanabaddhāni analasya rājño 'ntikamupanīyamānānyapaśyat / tebhyo 'nalaṃ rājānaṃ yathārhadaṇḍaṃ praṇayantamadrākṣīt / sa tatra rājño 'nalasyājñayā keṣāṃciddhastapādacchedaṃ keṣāṃcit karṇanāsācchedaṃ keṣāṃciccakṣurutpāṭanaṃ keṣāṃcidaṅgapratyaṅgaśīrṣacchedanaṃ keṣāṃcit sarvaśarīramagninā pradīpyamānāṃ kāṃścicchinnavikṛtataptakṣārodakapariṣicyamānaśarīrān, evamanekavidhāstīvrāḥ kharāḥ kaṭukā amanāpāḥ prāṇahāriṇīḥ kāraṇāḥ kāryamāṇā apaśyat / tasmiṃśca āghātane parvatapramāṇān karacaraṇanayanakarṇanāsāśiroṅgapratyaṅgarāśīnapaśyat / triyojanagambhīraṃ ca anekayojanāyāmavistīrṇaṃ śoṇitasaro 'drākṣīt / tatra ca aṅgapratyaṅgaśirovikalāni mṛtakalevaraśatasahasrāṇi vṛkaśṛgālāśvakākagṛdhraśyenakurarabhairavākīrṇāni bhakṣyamāṇāni apaśyat / kānicinnīlāni ca nīlavarṇāni vipūyakāni vyādhmātakāni vipaṭumakāni paramavikṛtabībhatsānyapaśyat / teṣāṃ ca vadhyānāṃ hanyamānānāṃ vividhāḥ kāraṇāḥ kāryamāṇānāṃ ghoramārtasvaraṃ krandatāṃ mahāntaṃ nirnādanirghoṣamaśrauṣīt mahāsaṃvegodvegasaṃjananaṃ tadyathā saṃghāte mahānarake //
body.translated_text: And ten thousand executioner-servants had gathered and were stationed before him — resembling the wardens of hell, like the agents of <s>Yama</s>, wearing deformed shoes, wearing garments of red [color], with terrifying faces, with red eyes blazing with anger, brandishing various weapons, with veins standing out on their frightful limbs, their bodies bound with iron chains, gnashing their teeth with sounds of fury, biting their lips, looking about with sidelong glances, their terrible shouts shaking the entire assembly. And they were cutting off the hands, feet, ears, noses, heads, and limbs of many hundreds of thousands of beings; they were tearing out eyes, piercing bodies, impaling [them], binding and chaining, tormenting with hot coals, pouring molten copper, hurling from precipices. There were sounds of lamentation from beings being beaten with clubs, cut with saws, having their flesh stripped by heated arrows, being dismembered limb by limb.

body.text: tasya tadatidārūṇabhairavakaraṃ paramavaiśasaṃ dṛṣṭvaivametadabhavat - ahaṃ ca sarvasattvahitasukhahetoranuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthito bodhisattvacaryāparimārgaṇatatparaḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇi paripṛcchāmi - kiṃ bodhisattvena kuśalaṃ kartavyam, kimakuśalaṃ parivarjayitavyamiti / ayaṃ ca analo rājā kuśaladharmaparihīṇo mahāsāvadyakarmakārī praduṣṭamanaḥsaṃkalpaḥ parasattvajīvitoparodhāya pratipannaḥ parasattvotpīḍanatatparaḥ paralokanirapekṣo durgatiprapātābhimukhaḥ / tatkṛto 'smādbodhisattvacaryāśravo bhaviṣyatīti? tasyaivaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayuktasya sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇābhimukhasya
body.translated_text: Having seen that extremely dreadful, terrifying, supremely horrific [sight], this thought arose in him: 'I, for the welfare and happiness of all beings, have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, and yet I now behold this king who, far from benefiting beings, is engaged in harming them, in oppressing them. It is not possible that he could illuminate me regarding any <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct! Let me go elsewhere — I should not be hindered from seeking spiritual friends!' Then, as if reading the thoughts of <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, whose mind was born of vast compassion,

body.text: vipulakarūṇāsaṃbhūtacetasa upari gaganatale devatā ityevamārocayāmāsuḥ na smarasi kulaputra jayoṣmāyatanasyarṣeḥ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīmiti? sa ūrdhvamukho gaganatalamavalokya evamāha - smarāmīti / devatāḥ prāhuḥ - mā tvaṃ kulaputra, kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṣu vicikitsāmutpādaya / samyak samena kalyāṇamitrāṇi praṇayanti na viṣameṇa / acintyaṃ hi kulaputra bodhisattvānāmupāyakauśalyacaryājñānam / acintyaṃ sarvasattvasaṃgrahajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvānugrahajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvanigrahajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvapragrahajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvasaṃgrahajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvapariśodhanajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvaparipālanajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvāvataraṇajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvaparipācanajñānam / acintyaṃ sattvavinayajñānam / gaccha kulaputra, paripṛccha enaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmiti //
body.translated_text: deities in the surface of the sky above proclaimed thus: 'Do you not remember, O son of good family, the instruction of the sage <s>Jayoṣmāyatana</s>, [your] spiritual friend? Did you not, trusting the instruction of the spiritual friend, throw your body into the great fire-mound, and having entered, did you not attain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable)? O son of good family, do not harbor wrong views regarding spiritual friends! Spiritual friends' [actions] are difficult to comprehend! Their conduct is difficult to comprehend! Their intentions are difficult to fathom! Their store of merit is difficult to conceive! The method of their skillful means is difficult to assess! Do not harbor wrong views, O son of good family, toward spiritual friends! Spiritual friends show the <s>bodhisattva</s> the path to the city of omniscience! Spiritual friends introduce the <s>bodhisattva</s> to the ocean of omniscient knowledge! They guide the <s>bodhisattva</s> toward the jewel-island of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>! They orient the <s>bodhisattva</s> toward the grounds of all virtues! They show the <s>bodhisattva</s> the terrifying current of <s>saṃsāra</s>! They illuminate for the <s>bodhisattva</s> the paths of all <s>Māra</s>-calamities! They establish the <s>bodhisattva</s> on the straight <s>bodhisattva</s>-path! They point out to the <s>bodhisattva</s> the courses to be followed! They teach the <s>bodhisattva</s> the methods leading to omniscience! They cause the <s>bodhisattva</s> to enter the ocean of methods of all qualities! The spiritual friend, O son of good family, shows you this skillful means! Do not harbor wrong views or wrong thoughts toward the spiritual friend, O son of good family!' //

body.text: atha sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako devatāvacanamupaśrutya yena analo rājā tenopajagāma / upetya analasya rājñaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya analaṃ rājānamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having heeded the words of the deities, approached King <s>Anala</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of King <s>Anala</s>, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'O Noble One, I have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how he should practice.' King <s>Anala</s> said to him: 'See, O son of good family, my royal punishment!' <s>Sudhana</s> said: 'I see, O Noble One.' Then King <s>Anala</s> said: 'Son of good family, look at those beings who are receiving punishments!' Thereupon <s>Sudhana</s> looked and saw all those beings — their hands were not being cut, nor their feet, nor ears, nor noses; their heads were not being cut off, their limbs were not being severed; they were not being impaled, not being burnt, not being split open, not being cast down. And he saw that all those executioners were <s>Yakṣas</s> magically created by King <s>Anala</s>. 'Son of good family, I do not even in thought produce the intention to harm a single being. Look, son of good family — I am compassionate even toward those who do harm. These, son of good family, are illusory displays of skillful means that I create through the power of my vow and the power of <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge, for the purpose of disciplining beings, not for harming them.' //

body.text: atha khalvanalo rājā rājakāryāṇi kṛtvā utthāya siṃhāsanāt sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇinā gṛhītvā tāladhvajaṃ rājadhānīṃ prāviśat / so 'nupūrveṇa svaṃ gṛhamanupraviśya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamantaḥpuraṃ praveśya bhadrāsane niṣadya evamāha - vyavalokayasva kulaputra imaṃ mama gṛhaparibhogamiti / sa vyavalokayannadrākṣīttadgṛhaṃ vipulaṃ vistīrṇaṃ saptaratnaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ vividhamaṇiratnaprāsādopaśobhitamanekaratnakūṭāgāraśatasahasrālaṃkṛtamacintyamaṇiratnaprabhājvālojjvalitatejasaṃ nānāmaṇiratnavividhavibhakticitravirājitalohitamuktāmayasamucchritastambhaṃ suprajñaptamusāragalvamayānekaratnaśatasahasravicitropaśobhitasiṃhāsanaṃ jyotīrasamaṇiratnasiṃhadhvajasamucchritaṃ vairocanaṃ maṇiratnavitānavitataṃ cintāmaṇivicitramahājālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyavicitramaṇiratnapratimaṇḍitaniryūhavyūhaṃ śītajalāśmagarbhamayapuṣkiriṇīsamupetaṃ sarvaratnadumayapaṅktiparivṛtam / daśa cāsya strīkoṭīparivāramadrākṣīt abhirūpāṇāṃ prāsādikānāṃ darśanīyānāṃ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatānāṃ sarvakalāvidhijñānāṃ pūrvotthāyinīnāṃ paścānnipātinīnāṃ maitracittānāṃ kiṃkaropacāvaravacanapratikāriṇīnām //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Anala</s>, having completed his royal duties, rose from the lion throne, took <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son by the right hand, and entered the royal capital <s>Tāladhvaja</s>. He gradually entered his own residence, led <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son into the inner palace, seated him on an excellent seat, and spoke thus: "Behold, O son of good family, this enjoyment of my household." Looking around, he saw that palace — vast, extensive, enclosed by walls of the seven precious substances, adorned with mansions of various jewels and gems, decorated with hundreds of thousands of pavilions of countless gems, blazing with the radiance and splendor of inconceivable jewel-light, with pillars raised high made of red pearls shining with variously arranged colorful patterns of diverse jewels and gems, with a well-appointed lion throne of coral adorned with hundreds of thousands of variegated precious substances, raised aloft with lion banners of luminous jewels, resplendent like <s>Vairocana</s>, spread with canopies of jewels and gems, covered with great nets variegated with <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), with projecting arrays decorated with innumerable variegated jewels, furnished with pools made of cool water-crystals, and surrounded by rows of trees made entirely of precious substances. And he saw his retinue of ten <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) women — beautiful, gracious, lovely to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious complexion, knowledgeable in all arts and sciences, rising early and retiring late, of loving disposition, responding to every word of service and attendance.

body.text: atha khalvanalo rājā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra, api tu pāpakāriṇāmevaṃrūpaḥ karmavipāko 'bhinirvartate? evaṃrūpā ātmabhāvasaṃpat, evaṃrūpā parivārasaṃpat, evaṃrūpā mahābhogasaṃpat, evaṃrūpā mahaiśvaryādhipatyasaṃpat? āha - no hīdamārya / so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra māyāgatasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / ime ca kulaputra
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Anala</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: "What do you think, O son of good family — does such a fruition of <s>karma</s> (action) arise for those who perform evil deeds? Such perfection of personal existence, such perfection of retinue, such perfection of great enjoyments, such perfection of great sovereignty and dominion?" He replied: "No indeed, O Noble One." He said: "I, O son of good family, am one who has attained the <s>Māyāgata</s> (Illusion-Arrived) <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation. And these, O son of good family —

body.text:
madviṣayavāsinaḥ sattvā yadbhūyasā prāṇātipātino 'dattādāyinaḥ kāmamithyācāriṇo mṛṣāvādinaḥ paiśunikāḥ pārūṣikāḥ saṃbhinnapralāpino 'bhidhyālambā vyāpannācittā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ pāpakarmāṇo raudrāścaṇḍāḥ sāhasikā vividhākuśalakarmakriyāparigatāḥ / te na śakyante 'nyathā pāpacaryāyā nivārayituṃ vinivartayitumanuśāsitum / so 'haṃ kulaputra eṣāṃ sattvānāṃ damanāya paripācanāya vinayena hite saṃniyojanārthaṃ mahākaruṇāṃ puraskṛtya nirmitairvadhyaghātakairnirmitān vadhyapuruṣān ghātayāmi / nirmitaiḥ kāraṇāpuruṣairnimitānakuśalakarmapathakāriṇo vividhāḥ kāraṇāḥ kārayāmi / hastapādakarṇanāsāṅgapratyaṅgaśīrṣacchedādhikārikāśca duḥkhāstīvrā vedanāḥ pratyanubhavamānān saṃdarśayāmi / tacca dṛṣṭvā ete madvijitavāsinaḥ sattvā labhante saṃvegam, jāyate bhayam, jāyate saṃtrāsaḥ, bhavati caiṣāṃ chambhitatvam, yaduta pāpakarmavyāpattivinivṛttaye / so 'haṃ kulaputra imān sattvānanenopāyenodvignottrastacittātmavivignamanaso viditvā daśabhyo 'kuśalebhyaḥ karmapathebhyo vinivartya daśakuśalakarmapathasamanvāgatān kṛtvā atyantaniṣṭhe yogakṣeme sarvaduḥkhopacchede sarvajñatāsukhe pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / nāhaṃ kulaputra kasyacit sattvasya viheṭhaṃ karomi kāyena vācā manasā va / āparāntikāvīcikadukhe saṃbhrāmayeyam / ahaṃ kulaputra tiryagyonigatasya saṃmūḍhasya antaśaḥ kuntapipīlikasya ekacittotpādenāpi duḥkhoparodhaṃ neccheyam, prāgeva kṣetrabhūtasya kuśalakarmapathavirohaṇasamarthasya manuṣyabhūtasya / svapnāntaragatasyāpi me kulaputra akuśaladharmasamudācāro notpadyate, kaḥ punarvādaḥ samanvāgataḥ / etasyāhaṃ kulaputra, māyāgatasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilabdhānāṃ
bodhisattvānāṃ māyāgatadharmasarvabhavagatyanubaddhānāṃ nirmitopamabodhisattvacaryāniryātānāṃ pratibhāsopamasarvalokavijñaptānāṃ svapnopamadharmatāpratividdhānām asaṅgamukhadharmadhātunayānusṛtānāmindrajālopamacaryājālānugatānāmanāvaraṇajñānagocaraviṣayāṇāṃ samantasamavasaraṇasamādhipathaniryātānām anantāvartadhāraṇīvaśavartināṃ buddhagocaraviṣayānubaddhānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: — the beings dwelling in my realm are for the most part killers of living beings, takers of what is not given, practitioners of sexual misconduct, speakers of falsehood, slanderers, speakers of harsh words, indulgers in idle talk, covetous, malicious in mind, holders of wrong views — doers of evil deeds, cruel, violent, reckless, engaged in various unwholesome activities. They cannot be restrained, turned back, or instructed away from evil conduct by any other means. Therefore I, O son of good family, for the taming and maturing of these beings, for the purpose of engaging them in what is beneficial through discipline, having placed great compassion at the forefront, cause manifested executioners to slay manifested criminals. Through manifested punishment officers, I cause various punishments to be inflicted upon those manifested perpetrators of unwholesome courses of action. I display them experiencing painful, intense sensations — the cutting off of hands, feet, ears, nose, limbs, minor limbs, and heads. Seeing that, these beings dwelling in my domain gain a sense of urgency; fear arises, terror arises, and they become paralyzed — all for the purpose of turning away from the calamity of evil deeds. Thus I, O son of good family, knowing these beings to be alarmed, frightened, agitated in mind, and distressed in heart through this skillful means, turn them away from the ten unwholesome courses of action, establish them in the ten wholesome courses of action, and finally establish them in the ultimate welfare and safety — the cessation of all suffering, the bliss of omniscience. I, O son of good family, do not harm any being whatsoever by body, speech, or mind. I would not cause even a moment of terror regarding the suffering of <s>Avīci</s> hell at the end of time. I, O son of good family, would not wish to cause the obstruction of happiness even by a single thought-moment for a being born in an animal womb, even the most confused, even an ant on a blade of grass — how much less for a human being who is a field of merit, capable of cultivating wholesome courses of action! Even in a dream, O son of good family, the practice of unwholesome states does not arise in me — how much less when fully conscious! I, O son of good family, am one who has attained this <s>Māyāgata</s> (Illusion-Arrived) <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena, who follow the <s>Māyāgata</s> dharma throughout all states of existence, who have emerged through conduct like that of emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who are known to all worlds as being like reflections, who have penetrated the nature of phenomena as being like dreams, who follow the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) through the gate of non-attachment, who pursue a net of conduct like <s>Indra</s>'s net of illusions, whose sphere of activity is the domain of unobstructed knowledge, who have emerged on the path of the <s>samādhi</s> of universal convergence, who command the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mystic retention) of infinite revolutions, and who follow the domain and sphere of activity of the <s>Buddhas</s>?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe suprabhaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra mahāprabho nāma rājā prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: "Go, O son of good family, here in this very southern direction there is a city called <s>Suprabhā</s>. There dwells a king named <s>Mahāprabha</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?'"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ analasya rājñaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya analaṃ rājānamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya analasya rājño 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 18 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of King <s>Anala</s>, circumambulating King <s>Anala</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of King <s>Anala</s>. [18]

body.text: 21 Mahāprabhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 21 <s>Mahāprabhaḥ</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastāṃ jñānamāyāmanusmaran, taṃ māyāgataṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamupanidhyāyan, tāṃ māyāgatadharmatāṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ, tāṃ karmamāyāsamatāṃ pratividhyan, tāṃ dharmamāyāsamatāmanuvicintayan, tāṃ dharmaparipākanirmāṇasamatāmanugacchan, tamacintyaṃ jñānasaṃbhavālokamanusaran, tamanantapraṇidhimāyāgatanirhāramabhinirharan, tāmasaṅgacaryānirmāṇadharmatāṃ viśodhayan, taṃ tryadhvamāyāgatalakṣaṇaṃ pravicinvan, anupūrveṇa janapadena janapadaṃ paripṛcchan parigaveṣamāṇo 'nuvilokayan, sarvadigvidikpathanimnasthalasamaviṣamajalājalapathaparvatagirikandaragrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣvaparikhinnacitto 'viśrāntaśarīro nikhilagaveṣī yena suprabhasya mahānagarasyopavicārastenopasaṃkramya paryapṛcchat - kva sa mahāprabho rājeti / tasya mahājanakāya upadarśayati - etatkulaputra suprabhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yatra mahāprabho rājā prativasati //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, recollecting that knowledge-illusion, contemplating that <s>Māyāgata</s> (Illusion-Arrived) <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation, examining that <s>Māyāgata</s> nature of phenomena, penetrating that equality of <s>karma</s> and illusion, reflecting upon that equality of dharma and illusion, following that equality of the emanations for the maturation of beings, pursuing that inconceivable illumination arising from knowledge, bringing forth that accomplishment arrived through the illusion of infinite aspiration, purifying that nature of emanation through unattached conduct, investigating that characteristic of the <s>Māyāgata</s> of the three times — journeying gradually from region to region, inquiring, searching, observing, with unwearied mind and unresting body, a tireless seeker through all directions and intermediate directions, along paths through lowlands, highlands, level and uneven terrain, waterways and dry-land routes, mountains, hills, caves, villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals — he approached the vicinity of the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s> and inquired: "Where is King <s>Mahāprabha</s>?" A great multitude of people showed him: "This, O son of good family, is the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s> where King <s>Mahāprabha</s> dwells."

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena suprabhaṃ mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramyādrākṣīt suprabhaṃ mahānagaram / dṛṣṭvā ca punastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāta evamanucintayāmāsa - kutra kalyāṇamitraḥ prativasati? adya taṃ drakṣyāmi kalyāṇamitram / tataṃ śroṣyāmi bodhisattvacaryāṃ bodhisattvaniryāṇamukhamacintyāṃ bodhisattvadharmatām acintyān bodhisattvaguṇagocarān acintyāṃ bodhisattvavṛṣabhitām acintyāṃ bodhisattvasamādhivihāritām acintyaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣavikrīḍitam acintyāṃ bodhisattvamahārambhanistāraṇaviśuddhim / evaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayukto yena suprabhaṃ mahānagaraṃ tenopajagāma / upetya suprabhaṃ mahānagaramavalokayāmāsa vicitradarśanīyaṃ saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ suvarṇasya rūpasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya ca, saptabhī ratnaparikhābhiḥ samantādanuparikṣiptaṃ gambhīrābhijātodakābhiḥ suvarṇavālikāsaṃstīrṇatalābhirdivyotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannābhiḥ kālānusāricandanakardamakaluṣodakābhiḥ, saptaratnamayatālapaṅktibhiḥ samantādanuparikṣiptam, saptabhirvajraratnaprākāraiḥ samantato 'nuparikṣiptam, yaduta siṃhakāntavajraprākāreṇa aparājitavajraprākāreṇa nirvedhavīryavajraprākāreṇa duryodhanavīryavajraprākāreṇa asaṅgavajradṛḍhaprākāreṇa vajrāṃśujālagarbhaprākāreṇa virajovarṇavyūhaprākāreṇa anuparikṣiptam / sarve ca vajraratnamahāprākārā asaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnapratyarpitā jāmbūnadakanakakṣoḍakaruciradantamālāracitā rajatamaṇiruciradantamālāracitā vaiḍūryamaṇiruciradantamālāracitāḥ sphaṭikamaṇiruciradantamālāracitā vidrumamaṇiruciradantamālāracitā lohitamuktāruciradantamālāracitāḥ sāgaragarbhamuktāmaṇiruciradantamālāracitāḥ / tasya ca mahānagarasya daśayojanāntarāṇyaṣṭau dvārāṇi vicitrāṇi darśanīyāni saptānāṃ ratnānām / tacca mahānagaraṃ vipulaṃ vistīrṇaṃ nānāṣṭāṅgasuvibhaktaṃ nīlavaiḍūryamayyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam / tasmiṃśca mahānagare daśa rathyākoṭyaḥ / ekaikasyāśca rathyāyā ubhayapārśvasaṃniviṣṭāni
nānāratnamayāni anekavividharatnavyūhapratimaṇḍitāni ucchritaratnacchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantīni sarvopakaraṇasamṛddhāni anekasattvaniyutādhyuṣitāni mahāgṛhaśatasahasrāṇi //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s> and saw that great city. Having seen it, he was delighted, elated, uplifted in spirit, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, and he reflected thus: "Where does my spiritual friend dwell? Today I shall see that spiritual friend. From him I shall hear the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, the gateway of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s emergence, the inconceivable nature of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the inconceivable domains of <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities, the inconceivable heroism of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the inconceivable <s>samādhi</s>-abiding of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the inconceivable play of the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation, the inconceivable purity of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s great undertaking and deliverance." Thus engaged in thought and mental attention, he proceeded toward the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s>. Approaching, he beheld the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s> — wondrous and beautiful to behold — made of the seven precious substances: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), and coral; entirely surrounded by seven moats of precious substances, with deep water of noble purity, their beds strewn with golden sand, covered with divine blue lotuses, lotuses, night-lotuses, and white lotuses, their waters scented with the mud of seasonally-fragrant sandalwood; entirely surrounded by rows of palm trees made of the seven precious substances; entirely enclosed by seven ramparts of <s>vajra</s> (diamond) gems — namely, the <s>siṃhakānta-vajra</s> rampart, the <s>aparājita-vajra</s> rampart, the <s>nirvedhavīrya-vajra</s> rampart, the <s>duryodhanavīrya-vajra</s> rampart, the <s>asaṅga-vajra-dṛḍha</s> rampart, the <s>vajrāṃśujālagarbha</s> rampart, and the <s>virajovarṇavyūha</s> rampart. All the great <s>vajra</s>-gem ramparts were studded with innumerable jewels, adorned with beautiful <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold cornices with lovely tooth-ornament garlands, adorned with beautiful silver-jewel tooth-ornament garlands, adorned with beautiful <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-jewel tooth-ornament garlands, adorned with beautiful crystal-jewel tooth-ornament garlands, adorned with beautiful coral-jewel tooth-ornament garlands, adorned with beautiful red-pearl tooth-ornament garlands, and adorned with beautiful ocean-pearl jewel tooth-ornament garlands. That great city had eight gates at intervals of ten <s>yojanas</s>, wondrous and beautiful, made of the seven precious substances. That great city was vast, extensive, well-divided into eight sections, established upon ground made of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s>. In that great city there were ten <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) streets. On both sides of each street were hundreds of thousands of great mansions made of various precious substances, decorated with arrays of many diverse jewels, with raised parasols, banners, flags, and victory pennants of precious substances, replete with all requisites, and inhabited by many millions of beings.

body.text: tacca mahānagaramasaṃkhyeyasuvarṇamaṇiratnaprāsādopaśobhitaṃ vaiḍūryamaṇijālasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyajāmbūnadakanakakūṭāgāraṃ lohitamuktājālasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyarūpyakūṭāgāraṃ vicitraratnakośamaṇijālasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyavaiḍūryakūṭāgāraṃ vipulagarbhamaṇirājasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyasphaṭikakūṭāgāram ādityagarbhamaṇirājasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyajagadrocanāmaṇiratnakūṭāgāraṃ śrīraśmimaṇirājasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyendranīlaratnakūṭāgāraṃ jyotīraśmimaṇirājasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyajagatsāgaramaṇirājakūṭāgāraṃ aparājitadhvajamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyavajrakūṭāgāraṃ divyamāndāravakusumajālasaṃchāditācintyavyūhāsaṃkhyeyakālānusāricandanakūṭāgāraṃ vividhadivyakusumajālasaṃchāditācintyaratnavyūhāsaṃkhyeyātulagandharājakūṭāgāramanekaratnakhoṭakapratimaṇḍitaṃ saptaratnavedikāparivṛtaṃ ratnatālapaṅktiparikṣiptam / sarve ca te ratnakhoṭakā ratnajālāścānyonyaratnasūtravinibaddhāḥ / sarvāṇi tāni ratnasūtrāṇi suvarṇaghaṇṭāmālopaśobhitāni / sarvāśca tāḥ suvarṇaghaṇṭāmālā vicitraratnadāmakalāpopanibaddhāḥ / sarve ca te ratnasūtradāmakalāpā ratnakiṅkiṇījālābhipralambitāḥ / sarvaṃ ca taṃ mahānagaramasaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnajālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyaratnakiṅkiṇījālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyadivyagandhajālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyadivyavicitrapuṣpajālasaṃcchannamasaṃkhyeyaratnabimbajālasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyavajravitānasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyaratnavitānasaṃchannamasaṃkhyeyaratnacchatravitānasaṃcchannam asaṃkhyeyaratnakūṭāgāravitānasaṃchannam asaṃkhyeyaratnavastravitānasaṃcchannam asaṃkhyeyaratnapuṣpamālāvitānasaṃcchannamutsṛjananānāratnadhvajapatākam //
body.translated_text: That great city was adorned with innumerable gold-gem-jewel palaces: innumerable mansions of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold covered with nets of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) gems in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of silver covered with nets of red pearls in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> covered with nets of variegated gem-treasury jewels in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of crystal covered with king-gems of vast womb in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of world-illuminating gem-jewels covered with sun-womb king-gems in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) jewels covered with <s>Śrīraśmi</s> king-gems in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of world-ocean king-gems covered with <s>Jyotīraśmi</s> king-gems in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of diamond covered with nets of unconquered-banner king-gems in inconceivable gem-arrays; innumerable mansions of <s>kālānusāri</s> sandalwood covered with nets of divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers in inconceivable arrays; innumerable mansions of incomparable fragrance-king covered with nets of various divine flowers in inconceivable gem-arrays — decorated with numerous gem-spires, surrounded by railings of the seven gems, encircled by rows of gem-palms. All those gem-spires and gem-nets were bound together by mutual gem-threads. All those gem-threads were adorned with garlands of golden bells. All those golden bell-garlands were tied with bundles of variegated gem-wreaths. All those gem-thread wreath-bundles hung with nets of gem-bells. The entire great city was covered with innumerable nets of gem-jewels, innumerable nets of gem-bells, innumerable nets of divine fragrances, innumerable nets of divine variegated flowers, innumerable nets of gem-images, innumerable diamond canopies, innumerable gem canopies, innumerable gem-parasol canopies, innumerable gem-mansion canopies, innumerable gem-garment canopies, innumerable gem-flower-garland canopies, releasing various gem-banner-flags. //

body.text: tasya ca suprabhasya mahānagarasya madhye rājño mahāprabhasya gṛhaṃ māpitamabhūt / samantāccaturyojanaṃ parikṣepeṇa saptaratnamayaṃ saptabhirnānāratnamayībhirvedikābhiḥ parivṛtaṃ saptabhī ratnakiṅkiṇījālaiḥ manojñamadhuranirghoṣaiḥ samantādanuracitaṃ saptaratnamayībhiḥ saptatālapaṅktibhiranuparikṣiptamacintyanānāratnamayakūṭāgāravyūhaśatasahasrasamalaṃkṛtaṃ divyotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchāditasalilābhiraṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇābhiḥ suvarṇavālikāsaṃstīrṇatalābhiḥ sarvaratnapuṣpaphalavṛkṣapratimaṇḍitābhiḥ caturdikṣu suvibhaktaratneṣṭakānicitasopānābhiranekaratnamayībhiḥ puṣkariṇībhirupaśobhitaṃ divyamadhuramanojñanānāśakunigaṇakūjitamamarapatibhavanapratispardhi / madhye cāsya jagadrocanamaṇiratnakūṭāgāraḥ saṃsthitaḥ, citro darśanīyo 'saṃkhyeyamaṇiratnācintyavyūhavirājito rājñā mahāprabheṇa saddharmagañjaḥ sthāpitaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the middle of that great city of <s>Suprabha</s>, the palace of King <s>Mahāprabha</s> had been constructed — four <s>yojana</s>s in extent on all sides, made of the seven gems, surrounded by seven railings of various gems, adorned all around by seven nets of gem-bells with charming sweet sounds, encircled by seven rows of palms of the seven gems, decorated with hundreds of thousands of inconceivable mansion-arrays of various gems, beautified by pools filled with water endowed with the eight qualities, whose surfaces were strewn with golden sand, decorated with trees of all gem-flowers and fruits, with well-apportioned stairs of gem-bricks piled in the four directions, of many gems — [all] rivaling the palace of the lord of the immortals, filled with the sweet and charming cooing of hosts of various birds. In its center stood the mansion of world-illuminating gem-jewels — magnificent, beautiful to behold, shining with innumerable gem-jewel inconceivable arrays — where King <s>Mahāprabha</s> had established the Treasury of the True <s>Dharma</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako ratnaparikhāsvananunītacitto ratnaprākāreṣvavismayamāno ratnatālapaṅktiṣvarajyamāno ratnaghaṇṭākiṅkiṇījālaghoṣamanāsvādayan divyavādyarutasaṃgītimadhuranirghoṣeṣvasaktacittaḥ nānāvicitraratnavimānakūṭāgāraparibhogānamanasikurvan pramuditeṣu naranārīgaṇeṣu dharmārāmaratirato rūpaśabdagandharasasparśarativiviktacetā dharmanidhyaptiparamo yathābhigatasattvakalyāṇamitranirantaraparipṛcchanatayā anupūrveṇa yena nagaraśṛṅgāṭakaṃ tenopajagāma / upetya samantādanuvilokayan adrākṣīnmahāprabhaṃ rājānaṃ madhye nagaraśṛṅgāṭakasya caityagṛhasya nātidūre
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, his mind drawn forward by the sound of the gem-moats, marveling at the gem-ramparts, delighting in the rows of gem-palms, savoring the sounds of the gem-bell-nets, his mind absorbed in the sweet sounds of the melodies of divine musical instruments, not attending to the enjoyment of the various magnificent gem-mansion-palaces, delighting among the joyful crowds of men and women in the pleasure-garden of the <s>Dharma</s>, his mind detached from the enjoyment of form, sound, smell, taste, and touch, supreme in the reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>, through his uninterrupted questioning of the spiritual friends of beings he had encountered — proceeded gradually to the crossroads of the city. Having arrived, looking all around, he saw King <s>Mahāprabha</s> in the middle of the city crossroads, not far from the <s>caitya</s>-hall

body.text:
mahāvyūhe bhadrāsane nīlavaiḍūryamaṇiratnapāde śvetavaiḍūryamaye siṃhapratiṣṭhite jāmbūnadasuvarṇasūtraśvetajāle divyātirekavicitraratnavastrasuprajñaptopacāre asaṃkhyeyaratnabimbaracitālaṃkāre acintyamaṇiratnavyūhajālasaṃchādite divyaratnanānābhaktivicitrajāmbūnadakanakapaṭṭavitānavitate cintārājamaṇiratnapadmagarbhe mahādharmāsane paryaṅkena niṣaṇṇam / dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīram / vicitrāśītyanuvyañjanopaśobhitagātram / kanakaparvatamiva nānāratnavinyāsavirājitam / ādityamaṇḍalamiva dīptatejasam / pūrṇacandramaṇḍalamiva saumyadarśanam / brahmāṇamiva brahmaparṣadivirocamānam / sāgaramiva gambhīradharmānantaguṇaratnanicayam / mahāmeghamiva varṣasvabhāvanirghoṣam / gaganamiva dharmanayajyotirgaṇapratimaṇḍitam / sumerumiva cāturvarṇasattvasāgaracittapratibhāsaprāptam / ratnadvīpamiva vividhajñānaratnākīrṇatalam / purataścāsya anekān suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajataratnarāśīn, nānāratnadivyavastraratnarāśīn, vividhadivyaratnābharaṇarāśīn, nānābhakṣyabhojyarāśīn, vividharasāgraviśeṣanicayān, nānāvyūhaviṣayasthāpitānapaśyat / anekāni ca divyaratharatnakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, anekāni divyatūryakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, anekāni divyagandhaprākārakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, anekān glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān, anekān sarvopakaraṇaviśeṣarāśīn, kalpikānanavadyān
yathābhiprāyasattvaparibhogāya / anekāni ca gośatasahasrāṇi suvarṇaśṛṅgakhurāṇi kaṃsadohāni daridrāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃgrahāya sthāpitānyapaśyat / anekāni ca kanyākoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi abhirūpāṇi prāsādikāni darśanīyāni sarvābharaṇavibhūṣitāni divyāmbaradharāṇi divyoragasāracandanānuliptagātrāṇi catuḥṣaṣṭikalāvidhijñāni sarvakāmacaryopacārakuśalāni sthāpitānyapaśyat / yathā cāsya puratastathā sarvarathyācatvaraśṛṅgāṭakadvāravīthimukheṣu ekaikasyāṃ rathyāyāmubhayorantaryorviṃśativyomakakoṭīḥ sarvopakaraṇaparipūrṇaiḥ sthāpitā yaduta sattvasaṃgrahāya sattvaparigrahāya sattvaprītisaṃjananāya sattvaprāmodyotpādanāya sattvamanaḥsaṃprasādanāya sattvacittaprahlādanāya sattvakleśavyupaśamāya sarvadharmasvabhāvārthasaṃniyojanāya sattvasarvajñatāsamānārthokaraṇāya sattvaparadrohacittavinivartanāya sarvakāyavāgduścaritavinivartanāya sattvadṛṣṭiśalyasamuddharaṇāya sattvakarmapathapariśuddhaye //
body.translated_text: seated cross-legged upon a great array, a noble seat with feet of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem-jewels, made of white <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, established on lions, with a white net of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold threads, with a well-prepared arrangement of surpassingly divine variegated gem-garments, with ornaments composed of innumerable gem-images, covered with nets of inconceivable gem-jewel arrays, with a canopy of variegated <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold sheets of various designs of divine gems, in a lotus-womb of <s>Cintārāja</s> (wish-fulfilling king) gem-jewels, upon a great <s>Dharma</s>-seat. His body was adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs beautified by eighty variegated subsidiary marks. Like a golden mountain shining with the arrangement of various gems. Blazing with splendor like the solar disc. Of gentle appearance like the full moon. Shining in <s>Brahmā</s>'s assembly like <s>Brahmā</s> himself. Like the ocean — a deep accumulation of infinite qualities of <s>dharma</s>-gems. Like a great cloud — of a nature sounding forth rain. Like space — adorned with the constellations of <s>dharma</s>-method lights. Like <s>Sumeru</s> — having attained the reflection in the minds of the ocean of beings of the four classes. Like a gem-island — its surface strewn with various knowledge-gems. And before him [<s>Sudhana</s>] saw many heaps of gold, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, <s>jātarūpa</s>, silver, and jewels; heaps of various gem-divine garments and jewels; heaps of various divine gem-ornaments; heaps of various foods and provisions; piles of the finest special flavors; [all] arranged in various array-domains. And innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s of divine chariot-gems, innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s of divine musical instruments, innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s of divine fragrance-walls, numerous medicinal provisions for the sick, numerous heaps of all special implements — faultless, for the enjoyment of beings according to their wishes. And he saw many hundreds of thousands of cows established for the support of poor beings — with golden horns and hooves, milked into bronze [vessels]. And he saw many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of maidens — beautiful, graceful, lovely, adorned with all ornaments, wearing divine garments, their bodies anointed with divine <s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood, skilled in the sixty-four arts, accomplished in all ways of serving desires — [all] established [for giving]. And as before him, so at every road, square, crossroads, gate, and lane-entrance, on both sides of each road, twenty <s>koṭi</s>s of aerial storehouses fully equipped with all provisions were established — namely, for the gathering of beings, the caring for beings, the generating of joy in beings, the producing of delight in beings, the clarifying of the minds of beings, the refreshing of the hearts of beings, the pacification of the afflictions of beings, the engagement in the meaning of the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s, the making of all beings equal in the purpose of omniscience, the turning back of beings' minds of hostility toward others, the turning back of all misconduct of body and speech, the extraction of the thorn of wrong views from beings, and the purification of the paths of <s>karma</s> of beings. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahāprabhasya rājñaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya mahāprabhaṃ rājānamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / āha - ahaṃ kulaputra mahāmaitrīdhvajāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ pariśodhayāmi, paripūrayāmi / eṣā ca me kulaputra mahāmaitrīdhvajā bodhisattvacaryā anekeṣāṃ buddhaśatānāmanekeṣāṃ buddhasahasrāṇāmanekeṣāṃ buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyānāṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, prostrated with his whole body before King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, circumambulated King <s>Mahāprabha</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'Noble One, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how one should practice. And I have heard that the Noble One gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Let the Noble One tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice?' He replied: 'I, son of good family, purify and fulfill the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of the great banner of loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrīdhvaja</s>). This great banner of loving-kindness, my <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, son of good family, has been [perfected] under many hundreds of <s>Buddha</s>s, many thousands, many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands, up to inexpressibly inexpressible

body.text:
buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantikāt paripṛṣṭā paripraśnīkṛtā viśodhitā vyūhitā vilokitā vicāritā anugaveṣitā paryanviṣṭā vicitritā vipulīkṛtā / so 'haṃ kulaputra asyāṃ mahāmaitrīdhvajāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ sthitvā dharmeṇa rājyamanuśāsāmi / dharmeṇa lokamanugṛhṇāmi / dharmeṇa lokamanuvicarāmi / dharmeṇa sattvān praṇayāmi / dharmeṇa sattveṣu pratipadye / dharmamaṇḍale sattvānāvartayāmi / dharmanayaṃ sattvānāmupasaṃharāmi / dharmeṇa sattvān paribhāvayāmi / dharmapratipattau sattvān niyojayāmi / dharmasvabhāvanidhyaptau sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / maitracittatāyāṃ mahāmaitryādhipatye maitrībale hitacittatāyāṃ sukhacittatāyāṃ dayācittatāyāmanugrahacittatāyāṃ sattvānugrahacittatāyāṃ sattvaparigrahānutsargacittatāyāṃ sarvaduḥkhavinivartanapraṇidhyanupacchedacittatāyāmatyantasukhapratiṣṭhāpanasamudācārān pratiprasrabdhaye sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / āśrayaṃ caiṣāṃ prahlādayāmi / prasrabdhisukhasaṃjananatayā cittalatāṃ caiṣāṃ vyāvartayāmi / saṃsāraratiprasaṅgāccittasaṃtatiṃ caiṣāṃ pariṇāmayāmi / dharmārāmaratyāṃ viśodhayāmi / sarvākuśaladharmebhyaḥ pariśodhayāmi / sarvākuśaladharmebhyo vinivartayāmi / saṃsārasrotasa āvartayāmi / dharmadhātunayasamudreṣu cittāvidyāṃ caiṣāṃ nirdahāmi sarvabhavagatyupapattivyavacchedāya / cittārciṣāśayaṃ caiṣāṃ saṃjanayāmi sarvajñatāphalapratilābhāya
/ cittasāgaraṃ caiṣāṃ prasādayāmi asaṃhāryaśraddhābalasaṃjananāya / evamāhaṃ kulaputra maitrīdhvajāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ sthitvā dharmeṇa lokamanuśāsāmi / na khalu kulaputra madvijitavāsinaḥ sattvā mamāntikādbhayaṃ trāsaṃ chambhitatvaṃ romaharṣaṇaṃ vā nirgacchanti / ye ca kulaputra daridrāḥ sattvā vividhopakaraṇavikalā māmupasaṃkrāmanti annārthino vā pānārthino vā vastrārthino vā yāvat sarvārthino vā, tānahaṃ pūrvaparicitāneva vivṛtān rājakośān gṛhṇīdhvamityapyanujānāmi yasyārthe yūyaṃ pāpakaṃ karma ārabhetha prāṇivadhaṃ vā adattādānaṃ vā kāmamithyācāraṃ vā mṛṣāvādaṃ vā paiśunyaṃ vā pāruṣyaṃ vā saṃbhinnapralāpaṃ vā abhidhyāṃ vā vyāpādaṃ vā mithyādṛṣṭiṃ vā tadanyāni vā vividhāni dṛṣṭikṛtānyabhiniviśetha / ataḥ tasmāt suprabhānmahānagarānnagaradvārebhyo vīthirathyāmukhacatvaraśṛṅgāṭakebhyo yo yenārthī sa taṃ gṛhṇātu, pūrvadattameva yattanmayeti / ye khalu punaḥ kulaputra suprabhamahānagarābhyantaranivāsinaḥ sattvāḥ, sarve te bodhisattvā mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ / teṣāṃ yathāśayapariśuddhyā idaṃ suprabhaṃ mahānagaramābhāsamāgacchati, yaduta keṣāṃcit parīttaṃ keṣāṃcidvipulaṃ keṣācinmṛttikātalaṃ keṣācidvaiḍūryamaṇiratnasaṃstṛtatalaṃ keṣācinmṛttikāprākāraṃ keṣāṃcidaparājitavastradhvajavastraratnamahāprākāraparikṣiptaṃ keṣāṃcidākīrṇaśarkarakaṭhallamutkūlanikūlaṃ śvabhraprapātabahulam, keṣāṃcidanekamahāmaṇiratnasaṃstṛtatalaṃ kṛtopacāraṃ samapāṇitalajātam, keṣāṃcidasaṃkhyeyaratnabhavanavimānaprāsādakūṭāgāraharmyatalaniryūhagavākṣajālārdhacandrasiṃhapañjaramaṇivicitradarśanīyamābhāsamāgacchati / bahirnagaranivāsināmapi śuddhāśayānāṃ kṛtakuśalamūlānāṃ paryupāsitabahubuddhotpādānāṃ sarvajñatābhimukhānāṃ sarvajñatāpratiśaraṇānāṃ ratnamayamābhāsamāgacchati / ye mayā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caratā caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ, madanyeṣāṃ mṛṇmayābhāsamāgacchati /
body.translated_text: inquired about, questioned, purified, arrayed, contemplated, deliberated upon, sought out, investigated, elaborated, and expanded from the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavats</s>. Thus I, O son of good family, established in this <s>Mahāmaitrīdhvaja</s> (Great Loving-Kindness Banner) <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, govern the kingdom through <s>Dharma</s>, benefit the world through <s>Dharma</s>, move through the world through <s>Dharma</s>, guide beings through <s>Dharma</s>, engage with beings through <s>Dharma</s>, turn beings toward the circle of <s>Dharma</s>, present to beings the method of <s>Dharma</s>, nurture beings through <s>Dharma</s>, yoke beings to the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, and establish beings in the contemplation of the intrinsic nature of <s>Dharma</s>. Through a mind of loving-kindness, through the sovereignty of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), through the power of <s>maitrī</s>, through a mind of benevolence, through a mind of happiness, through a mind of compassion, through a mind of grace, through a mind intent on benefiting beings, through a mind that does not abandon its embrace of beings, through a mind whose vow to turn back all suffering is unbroken — I establish beings in the tranquility of conduct that leads to the attainment of ultimate happiness. I refresh their very basis of support. Through generating the bliss of tranquility, I redirect the creeping vine of their minds. I transform their mental continuum away from attachment to <s>saṃsāra</s>. I purify them in the delight of the garden of <s>Dharma</s>. I cleanse them of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. I turn them away from all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. I turn them back from the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>. In the oceans of the methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), I burn away the ignorance in their minds for the sake of cutting off all states of existence, destinies, and rebirths. I generate in them a disposition of mental radiance for the sake of obtaining the fruit of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). I clarify the ocean of their minds for the sake of generating the power of unshakable faith. Thus do I, O son of good family, established in the <s>Maitrīdhvaja</s> (Loving-Kindness Banner) <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, govern the world through <s>Dharma</s>. Indeed, O son of good family, the beings dwelling in my realm do not experience fear, terror, paralysis, or hair-raising dread from me. And, O son of good family, those beings who are poor, lacking in various requisites, who come to me seeking food, or drink, or clothing, or indeed anything at all — I permit them, saying: 'Take from the royal treasuries which have already been opened for you, for whatever purpose you might otherwise undertake evil <s>karma</s> — whether killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, slander, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill will, wrong views, or would cling to various other view-fabricated things. Therefore, from the great city of <s>Suprabha</s>, from the city gates, from the streets, highways, crossroads, intersections, and public squares — let each person take whatever they need, for it is already given by me.' And, O son of good family, all the beings dwelling within the great city of <s>Suprabha</s> are <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). According to the purity of their respective dispositions, this great city of <s>Suprabha</s> appears to them differently — namely, to some it appears small, to some vast; to some the ground is of earth, to some it is paved with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), gems, and jewels; to some the rampart is of earth, to some it appears encircled by great ramparts adorned with banners, cloths, and jewels of unconquerable fabric; to some it appears rough with gravel, stones, and uneven terrain, full of pits and precipices; to some the ground is paved with innumerable great gems and jewels, well-maintained, smooth as the palm of a hand; to some it appears resplendent with countless jeweled houses, mansions, palaces, tiered pavilions, terraces, projecting balconies, latticed windows, half-moon ornaments, lion-throne enclosures, all wonderfully adorned with gems. Even to those dwelling outside the city, whose dispositions are pure, who have cultivated roots of merit, who have attended upon many Buddha-arisings, who face toward <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), who take refuge in <s>sarvajñatā</s> — to them it appears as made of jewels. To those whom I formerly gathered through the four means of attraction while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, but who are different from me, it appears as made of clay.

body.text:
yadā ca kulaputra madvijatavāsinaḥ sattvā deśapradeśeṣu grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu pañcakaṣāye loke kālasvabhāvasaṃkṣobhitān daśākuśalānāṃ karmapathānapyācaritumicchanti, tadāhaṃ teṣāmanugrahāya mahāmaitrīpūrvaṃgamaṃ lokendriyāvartaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ
samāpadye / samanantarasamāpannasya ca me kulaputra imaṃ samādhim, atha teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tāni bhayāni te upasargāḥ tāni vairāṇi te vigrahavivādāḥ te cittasaṃkṣobhāḥ tāni vihiṃsācittāni praśamanti vyupaśamanti nivartante nirudhyante tadyathāpi tadasyaiva mahāmaitrīpūrvaṃgamasya lokendriyāvartasya bodhisattvasamādhidharmatāpratilābhena / api tu kulaputra, āgamaya muhūrtaṃ yāvat pratyakṣībhaviṣyasi //
body.translated_text: When, O son of good family, the beings dwelling in my realm, in various regions and districts, in villages, cities, market towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, in this world afflicted by the five corruptions, wish to practice the ten unwholesome courses of action due to the disturbances of time's nature — then, for their benefit, I enter the <s>bodhisattva samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s> (Turning of the World's Faculties), preceded by great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). And, O son of good family, immediately upon my entering this <s>samādhi</s>, those fears of those beings, those calamities, those enmities, those quarrels and disputes, those mental agitations, those intentions to harm — all subside, are pacified, cease, and are extinguished, precisely through the attainment of the nature of this <s>bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s>, preceded by great <s>maitrī</s>. But, O son of good family, wait a moment and you shall witness this directly.

body.text: atha khalu mahāprabho rājā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāmaitrīpūrvaṃgamaṃ lokendriyāvartaṃ bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / samanantarasamāpannasya ca rājño mahāprabhasya imaṃ mahāmaitrīpūrvaṅgamaṃ lokendriyāvartaṃ bodhisattvasamādhim, atha tāvadeva suprabhaṃ mahānagaraṃ sadeśapradeśaṃ sagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīparivāraṃ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitam / tasya pracalataste 'pi ratnaprākārā ratnaprāsādā ratnagarbhāṇi ratnagṛhāṇi, ratnabhavanāni ratnavimānāni ratnakūṭāgārāṇi ratnaniryūhā ratnaharmyāṇi ratnagavākṣāḥ ratnavedikāḥ ratnatoraṇāni ratnārdhacandrā ratnasiṃhapañcarāṇi ratnakhoṭakāni ratnabimbāni ratnavitānāni ratnasūtrakiṅkiṇījālāni ratnaghaṇṭāḥ ratnadhvajāḥ ratnapatākāḥ ratnatālāḥ saṃpracalitāḥ saṃpragarjitāḥ saṃghaṭṭitāḥ / te ca saṃghadṛmānā valgu manojñaṃ śravaṇīyaṃ śabdamanuravanto yena rājā mahāprabhaḥ, tenāvanamanti sma, praṇamanti sma / ye ca te suprabhasya mahānagarābhyantaravāsinaḥ, sarve te prītiprāmodyaparisphuṭacetaso yena mahāprabho rājā tenābhimukhāḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇamanti sma / ye cāsya vijitavāsinaḥ sattvāḥ sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu, te 'pi sarve prahlāditakāyacittāḥ prītiprāmodyajātāḥ yena rājā mahāprabhastenābhimukhāḥ praṇemuḥ / ye ca tiryagyonigatāḥ sattvāḥ, te 'pi sarve anyonyamaitracittā hitacittā yena rājā mahāprabhastenābhipraṇatāḥ / yāni ca parvataśikharāṇi tadanye cāpyunnatāḥ pṛthivīpradeśāḥ, te 'pi sarve yena rājā mahāprabhastenābhinatāḥ / ye ca puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛkṣāḥ patravṛkṣā bījagrāmabhūtagrāmaśasyatṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo vā, te 'pi sarve yena mahāprabho rājā tenābhinatāḥ / yāni cāsya vijite sarvotsasarohradataḍāgaprasravaṇanadīpuṣkariṇyudapānāni, tānyapi sarvāṇi yena rājā mahāprabhastenābhimukhaṃ vegaṃ prāmuñcan //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Mahāprabha</s> at that very moment entered the <s>bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s> (Turning of the World's Faculties), preceded by great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). And immediately upon King <s>Mahāprabha</s>'s entering this <s>bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s>, preceded by great <s>maitrī</s>, at that very moment the great city of <s>Suprabha</s>, together with its surrounding regions and districts, together with its attendant villages, cities, market towns, settlements, kingdoms, and royal capitals, trembled and quaked in six ways. As it shook, those jeweled ramparts, jeweled palaces, jeweled treasure-chambers, jeweled houses, jeweled mansions, jeweled aerial pavilions, jeweled tiered halls, jeweled projecting balconies, jeweled terraces, jeweled latticed windows, jeweled balustrades, jeweled archways, jeweled half-moon ornaments, jeweled lion-throne enclosures, jeweled pinnacles, jeweled images, jeweled canopies, jeweled strings of tinkling bells, jeweled bells, jeweled banners, jeweled pennants, and jeweled palm-leaf ornaments — all trembled, resounded, and clashed together. And as they struck together, they produced a beautiful, delightful, pleasing sound, and they bowed and inclined toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And all the beings dwelling within the great city of <s>Suprabha</s>, their minds suffused with joy and delight, bowed with their entire bodies facing toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And the beings dwelling in his realm, in all the villages, cities, market towns, settlements, kingdoms, and royal capitals — they too, with bodies and minds refreshed, filled with joy and delight, bowed facing toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And the beings born in animal realms — they too all became of loving mind and benevolent intent toward one another, and bowed toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And the mountain peaks and all other elevated areas of the earth — they too all inclined toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And the flowering trees, fruit trees, leafy trees, seed-plants, plant-life, crops, grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest lords — they too all bent toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And all the springs, pools, lakes, reservoirs, waterfalls, rivers, lotus ponds, and wells in his realm — they all released their currents flowing toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>.

body.text: daśa ca nāgarājasahasrāṇi mahākālāgarudhūpapaṭalagandhodakameghairvicitravidyullatājvālāvabhāsitairabhigarjadbhiḥ sūkṣmābhirgandhodakadhārābhiścaturdiśamabhiprāvarṣan / daśa ca devaputrasahasrāṇi śakrasuyāmasaṃtuṣitasunirmitavaśavartidevarājapramukhāni antarikṣe gatāni, divyatūryameghakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃpravāditodārapramuktanirghoṣālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyāpsarogaṇadivyasaṃgītimeghanirnādamanojñamadhuranirghoṣālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyavicitraratnapuṣpameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram,
body.translated_text: And ten thousand <s>Nāga</s> kings rained down from all four directions with clouds of water fragrant with great black <s>agaru</s> (aloeswood) incense, illuminated by blazing flashes of wondrous lightning, thundering mightily, releasing fine streams of fragrant water. And ten thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), led by the divine kings <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, and <s>Vaśavartin</s>, stationed in the sky, adorned with the resounding tones issuing from hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of celestial musical instrument-clouds magnificently played, adorned with the delightful, sweet-sounding tones of the songs of countless hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) reverberating like cloud-thunder, adorned with showers of clouds of countless varieties of celestial jewel-flowers,

body.text:
asaṃkhyeyanānāvarṇadivyagandhapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavicitramālyameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyanānāvarṇadivyacūrṇameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavicitrābharaṇameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavastravicitravimalasūkṣmanānāvarṇameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnanānāvicitracchatrameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyasiṃhakāntaratnadhvajameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnaprabhājvālojjvalitaratnapatākāmeghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhyatiṣṭhan mahāprabhasya rājñaḥ pūjākarmaṇe / airāvaṇaśca mahānāgarājā sarvaṃ gaganatalamasaṃkhyeyadivyanānāratnapadmameghasaṃchannamadhyatiṣṭhadasaṃkhyeyadivyamaṇiratnahārābhipralambitam, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnapaṭṭadāmakalāpābhipralambitam, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavicitramālāguṇābhipralambitālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavicitrābharaṇamālābhipralambitālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyavicitraratnakusumadāmābhipralambitālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyanānāvarṇadivyagandharājasarvadikspharaṇagandhameghasaṃchāditālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyaratnavastranānāvarṇameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyadhūpabimbapaṭalameghapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram, asaṃkhyeyadivyanānāvarṇacūrṇameghasūkṣmapravarṣaṇālaṃkāram,
asaṃkhyeyāpsarogaṇadivyatūryasaṃgītimadhuramanojñanirghoṣasaṃprayuktastutimeghasaṃchāditābhipravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ sarvagaganatalamadhyatiṣṭhat acintyanāgendravṛṣabhitāvikurvitaprabhāvena / asaṃkhyeyāni ca rākṣasendraśatasahasrāṇi jaladharanivāsīni cāturdvīpikalokadhātvadhiṣṭhānadharaṇitalanivāsīni ca māṃsarudhirabhakṣāṇi jalacaramṛgapaśupakṣigavāśvagajagardabhanaranārīgaṇojohārīṇi praduṣṭamanaḥsaṃkalpāni nityaṃ jagadviheṭhāvihiṃsāpratipannāni sarvāṇi paramamaitrahitacittāni suprasannamukhavarṇāni sarvajagadavihiṃsāviheṭhāparamāṇi paralokasāpekṣāṇi kṛtāñjalipuṭāni paramaprīticittāni yena rājā mahāprabhastenābhipraṇatānyabhūvan, atulyaṃ ca kāyikacaitasikamudāraṃ sukhaṃ pratyanubhavanti sma / anekāni ca yakṣakumbhāṇḍapiśācabhūtādhipatiśatasahasrāṇi paramamaitrahitacittāni suprasannamukhavarṇāni sarvajagadavihiṃsāviheṭhāparamāṇi paralokasāpekṣāṇi kṛtāñjalipuṭāni paramaprīticittāni yena rājā mahāprabhaḥ, tenābhipraṇatānyabhūvan, atulyaṃ ca kāyikacaitasikamudāraṃ sukhaṃ pratyanubhavanti sma / evaṃ sarvāvatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvasattvānāṃ sarvabhayopadravopasargavairavigrahavivādāścittasaṃkṣobhāvihiṃsācittāni praśāmyanti vyupaśāmyanti vinivartante nirudhyante pratyudāvartante / yathā cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau, evaṃ sarvasyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau yāvaddaśasu dikṣu daśalokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣu sarvasattvānāṃ sarvabhayopadravopasargavairavigrahavivādāścittasaṃkṣobhāḥ pāpavihiṃsācittāni praśāntānyabhūvan / vyupaśāntāni vinivṛttāni niruddhāni pratyudāvartānyabhūvan, yaduta mahāmaitrīpūrvaṃgamasya lokendriyāvartasya bodhisattvasamādherdharmatāpratilambhena //
body.translated_text: an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine fragrances of various colors, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine garlands variegated with jewels, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine powders of various colors, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine ornamental jewelry variegated with jewels, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of pure, fine, many-colored divine garments variegated with jewels, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine parasols variegated with various jewels, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine banners of lion-beloved jewels, an ornament of raining innumerable clouds of divine jewel-pennants blazing with radiant jewel-flames — all pervading the sky for the worship of King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. And <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, the great <s>nāga</s>-king, pervaded the entire sky covered with innumerable clouds of divine lotus-jewels of various kinds, adorned with hanging innumerable necklaces of divine <s>maṇi</s>-gems, adorned with hanging innumerable festoons and clusters of divine jewel-ribbons, adorned with hanging innumerable garlands and strings of divine jewels variegated in design, adorned with hanging innumerable garland-chains of divine ornamental jewelry variegated with jewels, adorned with hanging innumerable wreaths of divine flower-jewels variegated in design, adorned and covered with innumerable clouds of the king of divine fragrances of various colors pervading all directions, adorned with raining innumerable clouds of many-colored divine jewel-garments, adorned with raining innumerable clouds of masses of divine incense-orbs, adorned with raining innumerable fine clouds of divine powders of various colors, adorned and covered with raining innumerable clouds of praise combined with the sweet and delightful sounds of divine music performed by hosts of <s>apsaras</s>es — all pervading the entire sky through the miraculous power of the inconceivable lordly bull among <s>nāga</s>-lords. And innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>rākṣasa</s>-lords, dwelling in clouds and dwelling on the surface of the earth in the four-continent world-system, who feed on flesh and blood, who carry off aquatic creatures, deer, cattle, birds, cows, horses, elephants, donkeys, and groups of men and women, who are of corrupt mental intentions, who are always engaged in tormenting and harming the world — all of them became supremely benevolent and compassionate in mind, with serene and clear countenances, devoted to non-harming and non-tormenting of all beings, mindful of the next world, with palms joined in reverence, with minds of supreme joy — they all bowed down toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, and experienced incomparable, magnificent physical and mental happiness. And many hundreds of thousands of lords of <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>s, <s>piśāca</s>s, and <s>bhūta</s>s, with supremely benevolent and compassionate minds, with serene and clear countenances, devoted to non-harming and non-tormenting of all beings, mindful of the next world, with palms joined in reverence, with minds of supreme joy — they all bowed down toward King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, and experienced incomparable, magnificent physical and mental happiness. Thus, in the entire four-continent world-system, all fears, calamities, afflictions, enmities, conflicts, and disputes of all beings, as well as mental agitations and thoughts of harm, became pacified, thoroughly pacified, ceased, were extinguished, and turned back. Just as in the four-continent world-system, so too in the entire great trichiliocosm, and extending to ten directions across hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s and <s>niyuta</s>s of ten world-systems, all fears, calamities, afflictions, enmities, conflicts, and disputes of all beings, as well as evil thoughts of harm, became pacified, thoroughly pacified, ceased, extinguished, and turned back — through the attainment of the nature of reality in the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s> (Whirlpool of the World's Faculties), which has great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) as its forerunner.

body.text: atha khalu mahāprabho rājā tasmātsamādhervyūtthāya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - etamahaṃ kulaputra, mahāmaitrīdhvajaṃ bodhisattvacaryājñānālokamukhaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāmaitryapramāṇacchatrāṇāṃ sarvalokadhātusukhāśayaspharaṇatayā, sarvajagatparivārāṇāmabhinnaparivāratayā,
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, having arisen from that <s>samādhi</s>, spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: "I, son of good family, know this entrance to the illumination of knowledge of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice called the Banner of Great <s>Maitrī</s> (Loving-Kindness). How could I comprehend the practice of <s>bodhisattva</s>s who possess the immeasurable canopy of great <s>maitrī</s>, who pervade all world-systems with the intention of happiness, who have undivided retinues of all beings,

body.text: sarvajagatparitrāṇaprasṛtānāṃ hinotkṛṣṭamadhyamasamaprayogatayā, dharaṇisamamaitracittānāṃ sarvajagatsaṃdhāraṇapratipannatayā, pūrṇacandramaṇḍalasamānānāṃ sarvajagatsamaprasṛtapuṇyajñānaraśmīnāmādityamaṇḍalasamānānāṃ sarvajñeyajñānālokāvabhāsanatayā, mahāpradīpakalpānāṃ sarvasattvacittagahanāndhakāravidhamanatayā, udakaprasādakamaṇiratnasadṛśānāṃ sarvasattvacittasaromāyāśāṭyakāluṣyāpanayanatayā, cintārājamaṇiratnasadṛśānāṃ sarvajagadabhiprāyapraṇidhiparipūraṇatayā, mahāmārutasadṛśānāṃ sarvajagatsamādhisamāpattibhavanasarvajñatāmahāpuraparisaṃsthāpanatayā caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, puṇyaparvato vā tulayitum, guṇajyotirgaṇagaganaṃ vā avalokayitum, mahāpraṇidhivāyumaṇḍalaṃ vā paricchettum, dharmasamatābalaṃ vā pramātum, mahāyānavyūhavarṇān vā paridīpayitum, samantabhadracaryānayaviśeṣān vā vaktum, mahābodhisattvasamādhibhāvanādvāraṃ vā vivaritum, mahākaruṇāmeghān vā saṃvarṇayitum //
body.translated_text: who extend protection to all beings equally through inferior, superior, middling, and equal application, whose minds of <s>maitrī</s> are like the earth in sustaining all beings, who are like the orb of the full moon with rays of merit and knowledge extending equally to all beings, who are like the orb of the sun in illuminating all knowable things with the light of knowledge, who are like great lamps in dispelling the darkness of the dense thickets of all beings' minds, who are like the water-purifying <s>maṇi</s>-gem in removing the impurity, deception, and crookedness of all beings' minds, who are like the wish-fulfilling <s>cintāmaṇi</s>-gem in fulfilling all the aspirations and vows of all beings, who are like the great wind in establishing all beings in the great city of omniscience through the abode of all <s>samādhi</s>s and attainments — how could I know their practice, or speak of their qualities, or weigh their mountain of merit, or survey their sky of constellations of qualities, or delimit the sphere of wind of their great vows, or measure the strength of their equality of <s>dharma</s>, or illuminate the ornamental displays of the great vehicle, or speak of the distinctive methods of <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s practice, or open the door of meditation on the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, or describe the clouds of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion)?"

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe sthirā nāma rājadhānī / tatra acalā nāmopāsikā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: "Go, son of good family! Here in this southern region there is a royal capital called <s>Sthirā</s> (Steadfast). There dwells a lay-woman named <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? How should one conduct oneself?'"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahāprabhasya rājñaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya mahāprabhaṃ rājānamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya mahāprabhasya rājño 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 19 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having bowed his head at the feet of King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, having circumambulated King <s>Mahāprabha</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing back again and again, departed from the presence of King <s>Mahāprabha</s>. [19]

body.text:
22 Acalā /
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ suprabhānmahānagarānniṣkramya muhūrtaṃ mārgamanusṛtya mahāprabhasya rājño 'nuśāsanīmanuvicintayan, taṃ mahāmaitrīdhvajaṃ bodhisattvacaryānayamanusmaran, taṃ lokendriyāvartamahāsamādhimukhālokaṃ paribhāvayan, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvakāyaviśuddhyalaṃkārasiṃhāsanavyūhavimātratāmabhinirharamāṇaḥ, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhipuṇyādhipateyabalatāmanubṛṃhayan, tamacintyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sattvaparipākajñānanayaṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ, tāmacintyāmasādhāraṇāṃ bodhisattvaparibhogamāhātmyatāmanuvicintayan, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvādhimātratāṃ nimittīkurvan, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sattvaparipākaviśuddhimanusmaran, tāmacintyāṃ bodhisattvaparivārasaṃpatpariśuddhimavakalpayan, tamacintyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sattvakāryanidhyānālokanayamadhimucyamānaḥ pratilebhe cittaprītiprasādavegaṃ cittapraharṣaṃ cittotplavaṃ cittanandīṃ cittānāvilatāṃ cittaprabhāsvaratāṃ cittadṛḍhatāṃ cittavipulatāṃ cittāparyādanatām / sa evaṃ kalyāṇamitrānusmṛtimanasikāraprayukto 'śrūṇi pravartayan anuvicintayāmāsa - aho batedaṃ kalyāṇamitradarśanaṃ sarvaguṇaratnākarabhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāpariśodhanaparipūraṇaṃ sarvabodhisattvasmṛtiviśuddhikaraṃ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīmaṇḍalapariśodhanaṃ sarvabodhisattvasamādhyālokasaṃjananaṃ sarvabuddhadarśanapratilābhasaṃbhāvanaṃ sarvabuddhadharmameghasaṃpravarṣaṇaṃ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhinayasūcanamacintyaprajñājñānālokasaṃjananaṃ dṛḍhabodhisattvendriyāṅkuravivardhanam / paritrāyakā mama kalyāṇamitrāḥ sarvadurgatiprapātagatibhyaḥ / praṇetāro mama kalyāṇamitrā dharmasamatānayānugamena / darśayitāro mama kalyāṇamitrā mārgasamaviṣatāyāḥ / paridīpakāni mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi mahāyānasya / avavādakāni mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāyām / deśayitṝṇi mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvajñatānagaramārgasya / praveśayitṝṇi
mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvajñatāpuram / avatārakāṇi mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi dharmadhātunayasāgare / ālokakarāṇi mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi tryadhvajñeyasāgaranayasya / darśayitṝṇi mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvārthamaṇḍalagaṇasya / vivardhayitāro mama kalyāṇamitrāḥ sarvaśukladharmāṇām //
body.translated_text: [22 <s>Acalā</s>] Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having departed from the great city of <s>Suprabhā</s>, traveled the path for a short while, contemplating the instruction of King <s>Mahāprabha</s>, recollecting that method of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice called the Banner of Great <s>Maitrī</s>, reflecting upon the illumination of the great <s>samādhi</s> entrance called <s>Lokendriyāvarta</s> (Whirlpool of the World's Faculties), bringing forth that inconceivable array of lion-thrones adorned with the purity of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s body of immeasurable extent, augmenting that inconceivable sovereignty of the power of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s merit from vows, strengthening that inconceivable method of knowledge for maturing beings possessed by <s>bodhisattva</s>s, contemplating that inconceivable and extraordinary greatness of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s enjoyments, taking as a sign that inconceivable superabundance of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, recollecting that inconceivable purity in the maturation of beings by <s>bodhisattva</s>s, conceiving that inconceivable purity of the prosperity of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s retinue, being convinced of that inconceivable method of illuminating contemplation of the welfare of beings by <s>bodhisattva</s>s — he attained a surge of mental joy and serenity, mental delight, mental elation, mental bliss, mental clarity, mental luminosity, mental firmness, mental expansiveness, and mental inexhaustibility. Thus engaged in mindful attention recollecting spiritual friends, shedding tears, he reflected: "Oh, how wonderful is the sight of spiritual friends — it is an ocean of all quality-jewels, it perfects and fulfills all <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, it purifies the mindfulness of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, it purifies the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-maṇḍala of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, it generates the light of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>s, it enables the attainment and encounter of seeing all <s>Buddha</s>s, it rains down the cloud of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, it indicates the methods of all <s>bodhisattva</s> vows, it generates the light of inconceivable <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge, it nurtures the firm sprouts of all <s>bodhisattva</s> faculties. My spiritual friends are protectors from all evil destinies and precipitous falls. My spiritual friends are guides through conformity with the method of equality of <s>dharma</s>. My spiritual friends are revealers of the path free from poison. My spiritual friends are illuminators of the great vehicle. My spiritual friends are instructors in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. My spiritual friends are teachers of the path to the city of omniscience. My spiritual friends are those who cause entry into the city of omniscience. My spiritual friends are those who cause descent into the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). My spiritual friends are makers of light regarding the method of the ocean of what is knowable in the three times. My spiritual friends are revealers of all assemblies of the maṇḍala of purposes. My spiritual friends are increasers of all wholesome qualities."

body.text: tasyaivaṃ rudataḥ krandataḥ paridevamānasya gagatalagatā devagaṇāḥ sadānubaddhāśca saṃcodakā buddhadūtā bodhisattvadevatā evamāhu - kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīpratipannasya kulaputra bodhisattvasya buddhā bhagavanto 'bhirādhitacittā bhavanti / kalyāṇamitravacanāvilomasthāyino bodhisattvasya sarvajñatā āsannībhavati / kalyāṇamitravacanāvicikitsakasya bodhisattvasya āsannībhavanti kalyāṇamitrāṇi / kalyāṇamitramanasikārāvirahitasya bodhisattvasya sarvārthā abhimukhībhavanti / gaccha kulaputra, yena sthirāyāṃ rājadhānyāmacalopāsikā / tataḥ śroṣyasi bodhisattvacaryām / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastataḥ samādhijñānālokād vyutthāya anupūrveṇa yena sthirā rājadhānī tenopasaṃkramya acalāmupāsikāṃ parimārgati parigaveṣate / tasya
body.translated_text: As he wept, cried, and lamented thus, the hosts of <s>deva</s>s stationed in the sky, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> deities who were constantly accompanying and urging him on as messengers of the <s>Buddha</s>, spoke thus: "Son of good family, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> follows the instruction of spiritual friends, the blessed <s>Buddha</s>s become pleased in mind toward him. For a <s>bodhisattva</s> who stands in accord with the words of spiritual friends, omniscience draws near. For a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has no doubt regarding the words of spiritual friends, spiritual friends draw near. For a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose mind is never separated from the recollection of spiritual friends, all purposes come face to face. Go, son of good family, to the lay-woman <s>Acalā</s> in the royal capital of <s>Sthirā</s>. From her you will hear of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice." Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having arisen from that <s>samādhi</s> and illumination of knowledge, traveling gradually arrived at the royal capital of <s>Sthirā</s>, and began searching and seeking for the lay-woman <s>Acalā</s>. His

body.text: mahājanakāya upadarśayati - eṣā kulaputra acalopāsikā svaniveśane mātāpitṛsabhāginī kumārabhūtā svajñātigaṇaparivṛtā mahato janakāyasya dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: a great multitude of people pointed out to him: "This, son of good family, is the lay-woman <s>Acalā</s>, who in her own dwelling, sharing with her mother and father, still in her youth, surrounded by her own kinfolk, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to a great multitude of people."

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahāprītiprasādaprāmodyaparisphuṭacetā yena acalāyā upāsikāyā niveśanaṃ tenopajagāma / upetya acalāyā upāsikāyā niveśanadvāre sthito 'paśyat sarvaṃ taṃ niveśanaṃ suvarṇavarṇayā ābhayā sphuṭamavabhāsitaṃ kāyacittaprahlādinyā / samanantaraspṛṣṭasya ca sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya tayā prabhayā, sarvavedayitaiśvaryadhvajasamādhipramukhāni śāntipradeśasamādhipramukhāni sarvajagaddhitasamādhipramukhāni samantacakṣurupekṣāvatīsamādhipramukhāni tathāgatakośasamādhipramukhāni pañcamātrāṇi samādhimukhaśatānyavakrāntāni saṃbhūtāni sūkṣmāṇi mṛdūni / tadyathāpi nāma taddivasārdhakrāntasya garbhasya vijñānam, evaṃ tāni samādhimukhāni sūkṣmāṇi mṛdūnyājātāni / tathārūpaṃ ca gandhamajighrat yo na devānāṃ na devakanyānāṃ na nāgānāṃ na nāgakanyānāṃ na yakṣāṇāṃ na yakṣakanyānāṃ na gandharvāṇāṃ na gandharvakanyānāṃ nāsurāṇāṃ nāsurakanyānāṃ na garuḍānāṃ na garūḍakanyānāṃ na kinnarāṇāṃ na kinnarakanyānāṃ na mahoragāṇāṃ na mahoragakanyānāṃ na manuṣyāṇāṃ na manuṣyakanyānām / na sā strī daśadiśi loke saṃvidyate, yā tasyā rūpeṇa samā, kutaḥ punaruttari / na sa varṇāvabhāso 'sti daśadiśi loke sthāpayitvā tathāgatavarṇāvabhāsam, abhiṣekaprāptabodhisattvavarṇāvabhāsaṃ ca, yastasyā varṇāvabhāsena samaḥ, kutaḥ punaruttari / nāsti tadātmabhāvārohapariṇāhasaṃsthānaṃ daśadiśi loke sthāpayitvā tathāgatātmabhāvārohapariṇāhasaṃsthānam, abhiṣekaprāptabodhisattvātmabhāvārohapariṇāhasaṃsthānaṃ ca, yattasyā ātmabhāvārohapariṇāhasaṃsthānena samam, kutaḥ punaruttari / nāsti sa prabhāvyūho daśadiśi loke sthāpayitvā tathāgataprabhāvyūham, abhiṣekaprāptabodhisattvacaryāprabhāvyūhaṃ ca, yastasyāḥ prabhāvyūhena samaḥ, kutaḥ punaruttari / nāsti sa gandho daśadiśi loke devabhavaneṣu vā nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyabhavaneṣu vā yastasyā mukhakośavisṛtagandhena samaḥ, kutaḥ punaruttari / nāsti sa bhavanavyūhaparibhogo daśadiśi loke sthāpayitvā tathāgataparibhogam, abhiṣekaprāptabodhisattvaparibhogaṃ ca, yastasyā bhavanavyūhaparibhogena samaḥ, kutaḥ punaruttari / nāsti sā parivārasaṃpat daśadiśi loke sthāpayitvā tathāgataparivārasaṃpadam, abhiṣekaprāptabodhisattvaparivārasaṃpadaṃ ca, yā tasyāḥ parivārasaṃpadā samā, kutaḥ punaruttari / na sa sattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate daśadiśi
loke yaḥ samartho 'calāmupāsikāṃ rāgacittena prekṣitum / na sa sattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate daśadiśi loke yaḥ acalāyā upāsikāyāḥ sahadarśanena kleśo na vyupaśamaṃ gacchet / tadyathāpi nāma daśa śatasahasravaśavartino mahābrahmāṇaḥ kāmāvacarāḥ kleśānna samudācaranti, evameva sahadarśanena acalāyā upāsikāyāḥ sattvānāṃ kleśā na samudācaranti /
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, his mind pervaded with great joy, serenity, and delight, approached the dwelling of the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>. Having arrived, standing at the doorway of the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>'s dwelling, he saw that entire dwelling clearly illuminated by a golden radiance that gladdened body and mind. And as soon as <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son was touched by that radiance, five hundred <s>samādhi</s> gateways arose in him — subtle and gentle — headed by the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Banner of Sovereignty over All Sensations,' headed by the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Abode of Peace,' headed by the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Welfare of All Beings,' headed by the <s>samādhi</s> called 'All-seeing Equanimity,' and headed by the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Treasury of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Just as the consciousness of an embryo that has entered the womb only half a day ago is subtle and gentle, so too those <s>samādhi</s> gateways arose subtle and gentle. And he smelled a fragrance such as belongs neither to <s>deva</s>s nor <s>deva</s> maidens, neither to <s>nāga</s>s nor <s>nāga</s> maidens, neither to <s>yakṣa</s>s nor <s>yakṣa</s> maidens, neither to <s>gandharva</s>s nor <s>gandharva</s> maidens, neither to <s>asura</s>s nor <s>asura</s> maidens, neither to <s>garuḍa</s>s nor <s>garuḍa</s> maidens, neither to <s>kiṃnara</s>s nor <s>kiṃnara</s> maidens, neither to <s>mahoraga</s>s nor <s>mahoraga</s> maidens, neither to humans nor human maidens. There is no woman found in the world in the ten directions who is equal to her in beauty, let alone superior. There is no radiance of form in the world in the ten directions — except the radiance of a <s>Tathāgata</s> and the radiance of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained consecration — that is equal to her radiance of form, let alone superior. There is no bodily stature, height, circumference, or shape in the world in the ten directions — except that of a <s>Tathāgata</s> and that of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained consecration — that is equal to her bodily stature, height, circumference, and shape, let alone superior.
