There is no array of radiant splendor in the world in the ten directions — except the array of radiant splendor of a <s>Tathāgata</s> and the array of radiant splendor of the practice of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained consecration — that is equal to her array of radiant splendor, let alone superior. There is no fragrance in the world in the ten directions, whether in the abodes of <s>deva</s>s or in the abodes of <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, <s>mahoraga</s>s, humans, or non-humans, that is equal to the fragrance emanating from her mouth, let alone superior. There is no enjoyment of dwelling arrays in the world in the ten directions — except the enjoyment of a <s>Tathāgata</s> and the enjoyment of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained consecration — that is equal to her enjoyment of dwelling arrays, let alone superior. There is no retinue wealth in the world in the ten directions — except the retinue wealth of a <s>Tathāgata</s> and the retinue wealth of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained consecration — that is equal to her retinue wealth, let alone superior. There is no being found among the assemblies of beings in the world in the ten directions who is able to look upon the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> with a mind of lust. There is no being found among the assemblies of beings in the world in the ten directions whose <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions) would not be pacified upon seeing the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>. Just as ten hundred thousand sovereign <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s of the desire realm do not give rise to afflictions, even so upon seeing the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, the afflictions of beings do not arise.

body.text: na sa sattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate daśadiśi loke yo acalāyā upāsikāyāḥ sahadarśanena tṛptimāpadyeta sthāpayitvā prajñātṛptān //
body.translated_text: There is no being found among the assemblies of beings in the world in the ten directions who, upon seeing the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, would become satiated — except those who are satiated by wisdom.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'calāyā upāsikāyā acintyāṃ kāyādhipateyatām, acintyaṃ rūpavarṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāham, acintyaṃ ca sarvakṣititalanagaramahāparvatāpratihataṃ raśmijālavyūhaṃ dṛṣṭvā acintyaṃ sattvārthakaraṇaṃ ca sarvaromakūpavisṛtaṃ gandhamāghrāya aparyantāṃ ca parivārasaṃpadamavalokya asaṃhāryaṃ ca bhavanavimānavyūhasaṃpadamudvīkṣya aparimāṇāṃśca guṇasamudrānavagāhya acalāmupāsikāmanayā gāthayā abhyaṣṭauṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, with palms joined, having beheld the inconceivable sovereignty over her body, the inconceivable beauty of form, color, shape, height, and circumference, the inconceivable array of a net of rays unobstructed by all surfaces of the earth, cities, and great mountains, and having smelled the inconceivable fragrance emanating from all hair-pores that benefits beings, and having surveyed her boundless retinue wealth, and having gazed upon her indestructible splendor of dwelling palaces, and having plunged into her immeasurable oceans of virtues, praised the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> with this verse:

children.text: śīlaṃ sadā yadamalaṃ parirakṣitaṃ te kṣāntiryataḥ suvipulā paribhāvitā ca /
children.translated_text: Your morality is always stainless and well-guarded, and your patience has been cultivated vast and wide,

children.text: vīryaṃ ca vajramiva yaddṛḍhamāsthitaṃ te tenodgatā jagati bhāsyacalendrakalpā // 1 //
children.translated_text: And your vigor, firm as a vajra, has been steadfastly maintained — by these you have risen in the world, resplendent like <s>Acalā</s>, the queen. // 1 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'calāmupāsikāmanayā gāthayā abhiṣṭutya evamāhamayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having praised the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> with this verse, spoke thus: "Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, how one should conduct oneself. And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and guidance to <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Therefore, may the noble one tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, how should one conduct oneself?"

body.text: atha khalvacalopāsikā snigdhayā bodhisattvavācā manojñayā premaṇīyayā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ pratisaṃmodya evamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ahaṃ kulaputra duryodhanajñānagarbhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī, dṛḍhasamādānabodhisattvacaryāmukhe ca anuśikṣāmi / sarvadharmasamatābhūmidhāraṇīmukhasya ca lābhinī, dṛḍhasamādānabodhisattvacaryāmukhe ca anuśikṣāmi / sarvadharmasamatābhūmidhāraṇīmukhasya ca lābhinī, sarvadharmatattvodyotanaṃ ca me pratibhānajñānālokamukhamavakrāntam, dharmaparyeṣṭayaparikhedavyūhaṃ ca me samādhimukhaṃ pratilabdham / āha - ka etasya ārye duryodhanajñānagarbhasya bodhisattvavimokṣamukhasya viṣayaḥ, dṛḍhasamādānabodhisattvacaryāmukhasya ca sarvadharmasamatābhūmidhāraṇamukhasya ca sarvadharmatattvodyotanapratibhānālokamukhasya ca dharmaparyeṣṭyaparikhedavyūhasamādhimukhasya ca viṣayaḥ? āha - duradhimokṣaṃ kulaputra idaṃ sthānam / āha - vada ārye, buddhānubhāvena kalyāṇamitraparigraheṇa ca adhimokṣye avatariṣyāmi vijñāsyāmi vicārayiṣyāmi anusariṣyāmi nidhyāsyāmi upanidhyāsyāmi pratyavekṣiṣye vibhāvayiṣyāmi, na virodhayiṣyāmi, na vikalpayiṣyāmi, na samāropayiṣyāmi, samīkariṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Then the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, having greeted the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> with an affectionate, pleasing, and endearing <s>bodhisattva</s> voice, spoke thus: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening! I, son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Duryodhana-jñāna-garbha</s> (Womb of Invincible Knowledge), and I train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice gateway of firm resolution. I have also attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway called 'Ground of Equality of All <s>Dharma</s>s,' and I train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice gateway of firm resolution. I have also attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway called 'Ground of Equality of All <s>Dharma</s>s,' and the gateway of the light of <s>pratibhāna</s> (inspired eloquence) called 'Illumination of the True Nature of All <s>Dharma</s>s' has been entered by me, and the <s>samādhi</s> gateway called 'Array of Unwearied Seeking of the <s>Dharma</s>' has been attained by me." He asked: "Noble one, what is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation gateway called <s>Duryodhana-jñāna-garbha</s>, and of the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice gateway of firm resolution, and of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway of the Ground of Equality of All <s>Dharma</s>s, and of the gateway of the light of <s>pratibhāna</s> called 'Illumination of the True Nature of All <s>Dharma</s>s,' and of the <s>samādhi</s> gateway called 'Array of Unwearied Seeking of the <s>Dharma</s>'?" She replied: "This matter is difficult to have faith in, son of good family." He said: "Speak, noble one! By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>s and by the support of spiritual friends, I shall have faith, I shall enter into it, I shall understand, I shall investigate, I shall follow, I shall contemplate, I shall deeply reflect, I shall examine, I shall make it clear — I shall not oppose it, I shall not conceptually elaborate it, I shall not superimpose upon it, I shall make it equal."

body.text: atha khalu acalopāsikā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāhabhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra, atīte 'dhvani vimalaprabhe kalpe pralambabāhurnāma tathāgato loke udapādi / ahaṃ ca rājño vidyuddattasyaikā
body.translated_text: Then the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> spoke thus to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: "Formerly, son of good family, in the past, in the <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) called <s>Vimalaprabha</s> (Stainless Radiance), a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Pralambabāhu</s> (Long-armed) arose in the world. And I was a

body.text: duhitā abhūvam / tayā me rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ pihiteṣu rājapuradvāreṣu, suptayormātāpitroḥ, saṃprasupteṣu naranārīgaṇeṣu, vyupaśānteṣu tūryatālāvacaranirghoṣeṣu, śayiteṣu sabhāgacariteṣu pañcasu kanyāśateṣu, śayanatalagatayā gaganatalagatāṃ jyotirgaṇavatīṃ rajanīṃ prekṣantyā uparyantarikṣe sa bhagavān pralambabāhustathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sumeruriva acalendrānekadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaparivāro 'cintyāsaṃkhyeyabodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sarvadigapratihataraśmijālaspharaṇakāyo dṛṣṭaḥ / tasya ca tathāgatasya sarvaromavivarebhyastathārūpo gandhaḥ pravāti, yenāsmi prahlāditakāyacittā praharṣitamānasā / śayanatalādutthāya daśanakhakṛtakarapuṭāñjalirdharaṇitalapratiṣṭhitā taṃ bhagavantaṃ pralambabāhuṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ namaskṛtvā mūrdhnā namasya avalokayamānā paryantaṃ nādhigacchāmi / vāmadakṣiṇataḥ pramāṇaṃ nopaimi / lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasaṃpadamanuvicintayamānā tṛptiṃ nāpnomi / tasyā mama kulaputra etadabhavat - kīdṛśaṃ karma kṛtvā iyamīdṛśī kāyasaṃpat pratilabhyate? lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasaṃpadā jāyate? prabhāvyūhasaṃpatsaṃbhavati? parivārasaṃpadabhinirvartate? manomayabhavanaparibhogasaṃpatprādurbhavati? puṇyasaṃpadutpadyate? jñānasaṃpadviśuddhyate? acintyasamādhivikurvitasaṃpatsamudāgacchati? dhāraṇīsaṃpatpariniṣpadyate? pratibhānasaṃpadvaśībhavati?
body.translated_text: daughter of King <s>Vidyuddatta</s>. On a certain night, when all was quiet, when the palace gates were shut, when my mother and father were asleep, when the assemblies of men and women had fallen into deep sleep, when the sounds of musical instruments, cymbals, and chanting had ceased, when the five hundred maidens who shared my quarters were lying on their beds — as I lay upon my couch gazing at the night sky filled with stars above, I beheld in the sky that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhat</s> Perfectly Awakened One <s>Pralambabāhu</s>, like <s>Sumeru</s>, the immovable lord of mountains, surrounded by innumerable <s>deva</s>s, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>mahoraga</s>s, attended by an inconceivable and incalculable host of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, his body pervading all directions with an unobstructed net of rays. And from every hair-pore of that <s>Tathāgata</s> there wafted such a fragrance that my body and mind were gladdened and my spirit was filled with joy. Rising from my couch, with palms joined with fingers interlaced, standing upon the ground, having bowed my head to that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhat</s> Perfectly Awakened One <s>Pralambabāhu</s>, gazing upon him, I could find no limit. To his left and right I could not ascertain his measure. Contemplating the perfection of his <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks) and <s>anuvyañjana</s>s (minor marks), I could not be satisfied. Then, son of good family, this thought arose in me: 'What kind of <s>karma</s> must one perform to obtain such perfection of body? To be born with such perfection of major and minor marks? For such splendor of radiant arrays to arise? For such retinue wealth to be produced? For such enjoyment of mind-made dwelling palaces to manifest? For such merit to be generated? For such wisdom to be purified? For such inconceivable <s>samādhi</s> miracles to be accomplished? For such <s>dhāraṇī</s> to be perfected? For such <s>pratibhāna</s> (inspired eloquence) to come under one's mastery?'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra sa bhagavān pralambabāhustathāgato mamādhyāṃśayaṃ viditvā evamāha - duryodhanacittaṃ te dārike utpādayitavyaṃ sarvakleśanirghātāya / aparājitacittaṃ sarvābhiniveśanirvedāya / asaṃkucitacittaṃ gambhīradharmanayānugamāya / akṣobhyacittaṃ viṣayāśayasattvasāgarāvartaprapāteṣu / asaṃmūḍhacittaṃ sarvabhavagatyupapattyāyataneṣu / avitṛptacittaṃ sarvabuddhadarśanābhilāṣāpratiprasrabdhaye / asaṃtuṣṭicittaṃ sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratyeṣaṇāya / nidhyapticittaṃ sarvabuddhadharmanayālokānugamāya / saṃghāraṇācittaṃ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrāṇām / asaṃpramohacittamantaśaḥ saṃketakṛte, kimuta tathāgatavadanavinirgatajñāne / vibhājanacittaṃ ca te dārike utpādayitavyaṃ yathāśayasarvasattvadharmaratnasaṃvibhajanāya /
body.translated_text: Then, son of good family, that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Pralambabāhu</s>, knowing my intention, spoke thus: 'You should generate, O maiden, an invincible mind (<s>duryodhana-citta</s>) for the eradication of all <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions); an unconquerable mind for turning away from all attachments; an unshrinking mind for following the profound way of the <s>Dharma</s>; an unshakeable mind amid the whirlpools and abysses of the ocean of sense-objects, inclinations, and beings; an unconfused mind in all states of existence, destinies, births, and sense-bases; an unsatiated mind so that the longing to see all <s>Buddha</s>s never relaxes; a mind of discontent for the sake of seeking the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; a mind of contemplation for following the light of the <s>Dharma</s>-way of all <s>Buddha</s>s; a mind of gathering for all the <s>Dharma</s>-wheels of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; an undeluded mind even regarding a mere hint, how much more so regarding the wisdom issuing from the mouth of a <s>Tathāgata</s>; and you should generate, O maiden, a mind of sharing for distributing the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings according to their dispositions.'

body.text: sāhaṃ kulaputra tasya bhagavataḥ pralambabāhostathāgasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādimāni evaṃrūpāṇi dharmanayānuśāsanīmukhāni śrutvā sarvajñajñānamabhikāṅkṣamāṇā daśabalabhāvamabhiprārthayamānā buddhasarasvatīmabhilaṣantī buddhaprabhāvyūhaṃ pariśodhayitukāmā buddhaśarīrasaṃpadaṃ pariniṣpādayitukāmā buddhalakṣaṇānuvyañjanaviśuddhimabhikāṅkṣamāṇā buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalasaṃpadamabhiprārthayamānā buddhakṣetraviśuddhimabhilaṣantī buddheryāpathasaṃpadamabhikāṅkṣamāṇā buddhāyuḥpramāṇasaṃpadamabhinandantī sarvakleśasarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhābhedyacittamutpādaditavatī duryodhanavajramiva sarvaparvatāyudhabalaiḥ / nābhijānāmi kulaputra tata upādāya etena cittotpādena jambudvīpaḥ paramāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kalpairapi kāmān paribhoktum, kaḥ punarvādo dvayadvayasamāpattyā / nābhijānāmi kulaputra tata upādāya ekapratighacittamutpādayituṃ svabāndhaveṣu, prāgevānaparādhiṣu tadanyeṣu sattveṣu / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya ekacittotpādamadhyātmadṛṣṭisahagatamutpādayitum,
body.translated_text: I, O son of good family, having heard from that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Pralambabāhu</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, these kinds of <s>dharma</s>-method instructional teachings, aspiring to omniscient knowledge, seeking the state of the Ten Powers, longing for the eloquence of a Buddha, wishing to purify the splendid array of a Buddha's radiance, wishing to perfect the excellence of a Buddha's body, aspiring to the purity of the marks and secondary characteristics of a Buddha, seeking the excellence of a Buddha's assembly circle, longing for the purity of a Buddha-field, aspiring to the excellence of a Buddha's deportment, rejoicing in the excellence of the measure of a Buddha's lifespan — I generated a mind unbreakable by all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, like an invincible <s>vajra</s> against all mountains, weapons, and forces. I do not recall, O son of good family, from that time onward, with this generation of mind, indulging in sense pleasures even for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of dust of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, let alone through the union of couples. I do not recall, O son of good family, from that time onward, generating even a single thought of hostility toward my own relatives, much less toward other beings who have committed no offense. I do not recall from that time onward generating even a single thought accompanied by the view of a self,

body.text:
prāgeva tadanyeṣūpakaraṇeṣu mamakārābhiniveśam / nābhijānāmi cittasaṃmohaṃ nānyatvasaṃjñāmavyākṛtacittatāṃ vā cyutyupapattigarbhasaṃvāseṣvapi, prāgeva samanvāharamāṇā / nābhijānāmi tāvadbhiḥ kalpairekabuddhadarśanamapi vismartum / antaśaḥ svapnadarśanavijñaptimapi, prāgeva daśabodhisattvacakṣuḥpratibhāsaprāpteṣu / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya sarvatathāgatadharmameghān saṃpratīcchamānā ekadharmapadavyañjanamapi manasā vismartum, antaśaḥ saṃjñākṛtamapi, prāgeva tathāgatavadanakośaviniḥsṛtam / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya tāvato dharmasāgarān pibantī ekapadamapyanidhyātamavilokitam, antaśo laukikeṣu dharmeṣu / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya tāvatāṃ dharmanayasāgarāṇāmekadharmanayadvāramapi yatra mayā na samādhirabhinirhṛtaḥ, antaśo laukikaśilpajñānanayeṣvapi / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya tāvatāṃ tathāgatānāṃ dharmacakraṃ saṃdhārayamāṇā yathāsaṃdhāritādekapadavyañjanamapyanusraṣṭam, antaśo 'nvayajñānānugamanenāpi anyatra sattvavinayavaśāt / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya tāvatāṃ buddhadarśanasamudrāṇāmekapraṇidhānamapi yanmayā na sarvasattvasāgaraviśuddhaye 'bhinirhṛtam, antaśo nirmāṇabuddhapraṇidhivicāreṣvapi / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya tāvatāṃ buddhasamudrāṇāṃ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāsamudrādekabodhisattvacaryāmapi, yā mayā na svacaryāpariśuddhye
'bhinirhṛtā / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya ekasattvamapi cakṣuravabhāsamāgataṃ yo mayānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau na samādāpitaḥ / nābhijānāmi tata upādāya ekacittotpādamapi śrāvakapratyekabuddhamanasikārapratisaṃyuktamabhinirhartum / nābhijānāmi kulaputra tata upādāya jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kalpairekapadavyañjane 'pi saṃśayamutpādayituṃ dvayasaṃjñāṃ vā vikalpasaṃjñāṃ vā nānātvasaṃjñāṃ vā agrahasaṃjñāṃ vā hīnapraṇītasaṃjñāṃ vā anunayapratighasaṃjñāṃ vā utpādayitum //
body.translated_text: much less attachment or clinging to possessiveness regarding other possessions. I do not recall mental confusion, nor perception of otherness, nor an indeterminate state of mind even during death, rebirth, or dwelling in the womb, much less while being mindful. I do not recall forgetting even a single vision of a Buddha during all those <s>kalpas</s>, not even a cognition arising in a dream vision, much less when the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> eyes have manifested their illumination. I do not recall from that time onward, while receiving the <s>dharma</s>-cloud of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, mentally forgetting even a single word or syllable of <s>dharma</s>, not even one formed by mere perception, much less one that has issued from the treasury of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s mouth. I do not recall from that time onward, while drinking such oceans of <s>dharma</s>, leaving even a single word uncontemplated or unexamined, not even regarding worldly teachings. I do not recall from that time onward, regarding such oceans of <s>dharma</s>-method, even a single <s>dharma</s>-method gate in which I have not produced <s>samādhi</s>, not even regarding worldly arts and knowledge-methods. I do not recall from that time onward, while upholding the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of dharma) of so many <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having released even a single word or syllable from what was upheld, not even through the process of inferential knowledge, except for the sake of disciplining beings. I do not recall from that time onward, regarding such oceans of Buddha-visions, even a single <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vow) that I have not produced for the purification of the entire ocean of beings, not even in the deliberations regarding <s>Nirmāṇa</s>-Buddha vows. I do not recall from that time onward, regarding the oceans of prior <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct of so many oceans of Buddhas, even a single <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice that I have not produced for the purification of my own conduct. I do not recall from that time onward even a single being who has come within the range of my sight whom I have not established in supreme perfect enlightenment. I do not recall from that time onward producing even a single thought connected with the mental activity of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. I do not recall, O son of good family, from that time onward, for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of dust of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, generating even a doubt regarding a single word or syllable, nor generating a perception of duality, nor a perception of discrimination, nor a perception of multiplicity, nor a perception of non-apprehension, nor a perception of inferior and superior, nor a perception of attraction and aversion.

body.text: sāhaṃ kulaputra tataḥ paścādavirahitā abhūvaṃ buddhotpādaiḥ / avirahitā buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ / avirahitā bodhisattvaiḥ / avirahitā bhūtakalyāṇamitraiḥ / avirahitā buddhapraṇidhānaśraveṇa / avirahitā bodhisattvacaryāśraveṇa / avirahitā bodhisattvapāramitānayaśraveṇa / avirahitā bodhisattvabhūmijñānālokanayaśraveṇa / avirahitā bodhisattvadhāraṇīsamādhyakṣayakoṣanidhānaśravaṇapratilābhena / avirahitā anantamadhyalokadhātujālapraveśāvatāranayaśraveṇa / avirahitā anantamadhyasattvadhātusaṃbhavahetuśravaṇapratilābhena / avirahitā sarvajagatkleśajālamaṇḍalaparyādānajñānālokena / avirahitā sarvasattvakuśalamūlasaṃbhavahetujñānapratilābhena / avirahitā sarvasattvayathāśayakāyasaṃdarśanena / avirahitā sarvasattvājñāpanasvaramaṇḍalaviśuddhyā / etaṃ ca me kulaputra duryodhanajñānagarbhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣasukham, etacca sarvadharmaparyeṣṭyaparikhedavyūhaṃ samādhimukhaṃ samāpannāyāḥ, etacca dṛḍhasamādānabodhicaryāmukhaṃ pravicinvantyāḥ / etacca sarvadharmasamatābhūmidhāraṇīmukham / etacca sarvadharmatalodyotanapratibhāvajñānālokamukhaṃ vyavacārayantyā acintyāni prātihāryāṇi bhavanti / icchasi tvaṃ kulaputra, pratyakṣo bhavitum? āha - icchāmyārye //
body.translated_text: I, O son of good family, from that time onward was never without the arising of Buddhas, never without Blessed Buddhas, never without <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, never without true spiritual friends, never without hearing the vows of Buddhas, never without hearing the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, never without hearing the <s>Pāramitā</s>-method teachings of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, never without hearing the knowledge-illumination teachings of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, never without obtaining the hearing of the inexhaustible treasury of <s>Dhāraṇī</s> and <s>Samādhi</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, never without hearing the method of entering into the net of infinite, beginningless world-realms, never without obtaining the hearing of the causes of arising of the infinite, beginningless realm of beings, never without the light of knowledge that completely exhausts the circle of the net of afflictions of all beings, never without obtaining the knowledge of the causes of arising of the roots of virtue of all beings, never without displaying bodies according to the dispositions of all beings, never without the purity of the sphere of voice that instructs all beings. And this, O son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) bliss called '<s>Duryodhana-jñāna-garbha</s>' (Invincible Knowledge Treasury), and this is the <s>samādhi</s> gateway called the array of unwearied seeking of all <s>dharmas</s>, entered by me; and this is the gateway of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct with firm resolution that I investigate; and this is the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway of the ground of equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; and while I practice this gateway of the light of knowledge of insight illuminating the ground of all <s>dharmas</s>, inconceivable miracles occur. Do you wish, O son of good family, to witness this directly? He said: I do wish it, O noble lady.

body.text: atha khalu acalopāsikā yathāniṣaṇṇaiva duryodhanajñānagarbhabodhisattvavimokṣamukhapūrvaṃgamāni sarvadharmaparyeṣṭyaparikhedavyūhasamādhimukhapūrvaṃgamāni amoghamaṇḍalavyūhasamādhimukhapūrvaṃgamāni daśabalajñānamaṇḍalābhimukhasamādhimukhapūrvaṃgamāni buddhavaṃśākṣayakośasamādhivimokṣamukhapūrvaṃgamāni ca daśa samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇi vyavalokayati anuvicārayati anusarati nidhyapayati / samanantarasamāpannāyāṃ ca acalāyāmupāsikāyām, apaśyat sudhanaḥ śreiṣṭhidārako daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyaparamāṇurajaḥsamān lokadhātūn ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampamānān, pariśuddhavaiḍūryamayān saṃsthitān / ekaikasmiṃśca lokadhātau koṭīśate cāturmahādvīpakānāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ koṭīśataṃ tathāgatānāmapaśyat / kāṃścittuṣitavarabhavanagatān, kāṃścid yāvatparinirvāyamāṇānapaśyat yaduta anāvaraṇatvātpariśuddhavaiḍūryamayalokadhātūnām / ekaikaṃ ca tathāgataṃ sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaraśmijālaprabhāmaṇḍalam, ekaikaṃ ca tathāgataṃ suvibhaktaparṣanmaṇḍalasamudramapaśyat / ekaisya ca tathāgatasya sarvadharmacakrodyotanaṃ sarvasattvaśrotravijñapanaṃ svaramaṇḍalamaśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, seated just as she was, surveyed, contemplated, followed, and meditated upon one hundred thousand <s>samādhi</s> gateways preceded by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> gateway called '<s>Duryodhana-jñāna-garbha</s>' (Invincible Knowledge Treasury), preceded by the <s>samādhi</s> gateway called the array of unwearied seeking of all <s>dharmas</s>, preceded by the <s>samādhi</s> gateway called the array of infallible <s>maṇḍala</s>, preceded by the <s>samādhi</s> gateway facing the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the knowledge of the Ten Powers, and preceded by the <s>samādhi</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> gateway of the inexhaustible treasury of the lineage of Buddhas. And as soon as the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> entered <s>samādhi</s>, the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s> saw in the ten directions, in world-realms equal to the inexpressible atoms of dust of ten Buddha-fields, the ground trembling in six ways, established as made of pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). And in each world-realm he saw hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of world-systems of four great continents, and hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Some he saw dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, some he saw up to entering <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — because of the unobstructedness of the pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made world-realms. And he saw each <s>Tathāgata</s> with a radiance-halo of a net of rays pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and he saw each <s>Tathāgata</s> with a well-arranged ocean of assembly circles. And he heard the sphere of voice of each <s>Tathāgata</s> illuminating the turning of the wheel of all <s>dharma</s> and making known to the ears of all beings.

body.text: atha khalvacalopāsikā tataḥ samādhervyutthāya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - dṛṣṭaṃ te kulaputra, śrutaṃ vijñātam? āha - dṛṣṭamārye, śrutaṃ vijñātam / āha - evamahaṃ kulaputra, dṛḍhasamādānāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāmanuśikṣamāṇā sarvadharmaparyeṣṭyaparikhedavyūhasamādhisamāpannā duryodhanajñānagarbhabodhisattvavimokṣamukhapratiṣṭhitā sarvadharmasamatābhūmidhāraṇyanugamena sarvadharmatalodyotanapratibhānajñānālokakauśalyena sarvasattvān subhāṣitena saṃtoṣayāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamacintyāprameyaguṇasamanvāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum? ye te dvijarṣabhā iva gaganatale 'niketacāriṇaḥ / ye te mahāgaruḍendrā iva sattvasāgaramavagāhante paripakvabodhisattvoddharaṇatāyai / ye te vaṇija iva sarvajñatāratnadvīpe 'nuvicaranti daśabalajñānaratnābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ / ye te balavatkaivartā iva saṃsārasāgare 'nuvicaranti ruciradharmacakramaṇḍalajālahastāḥ tṛṣṇodbhavasattvaparipācanābhyuddharaṇatāyai / ye te 'surendrā iva tribhuvanapuraṃ spharitvā vicaranti kleśāsurasaṃkṣobhodvṛttasaṃśamanatāyai / ye te dinakaramaṇḍalamiva dharmadhātugaganatale samudāgacchanti sattvatṛṣṇāsalilakleśapaṅkocchoṣaṇatāyai / ye te pūrṇacandramaṇḍalamiva jñānanabhasyudāgacchanti vineyamanaḥkumudavibodhanatāyai / ye te dharaṇitalamivānunayapratighonnāmāvanāmaviṣame samā loke saṃtiṣṭhante sarvajagatkuśalendriyāṅkuraprarohaṇavivardhanatāyai / ye te māruta ivāsaṅgasarvadigvicāriṇaḥ sarvasattvakleśadṛṣṭidrumalatāvanārāmonmūlanatāyai / ye te cakravartina iva loke vicaranti catuḥsaṃgrahavastupariṣkāropakaraṇasarvajagatsaṃgrahaṇatāyai / gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe 'mitatosale janapade tosalaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra sarvagāmī nāma parivrājakaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, rising from that <s>samādhi</s>, spoke thus to the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>: Did you see, O son of good family? Did you hear and understand? He said: I saw, O noble lady; I heard and understood. She said: Thus I, O son of good family, training in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct with firm resolution, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> of the array of unwearied seeking of all <s>dharmas</s>, established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> gateway called '<s>Duryodhana-jñāna-garbha</s>' (Invincible Knowledge Treasury), through following the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the ground of equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, through skill in the light of knowledge of insight illuminating the ground of all <s>dharmas</s>, I satisfy all beings with well-spoken words. How could I know the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with inconceivable, immeasurable qualities, or speak of their virtues? They who, like kings of birds, wander without abode in the sky. They who, like great <s>Garuḍa</s> lords, plunge into the ocean of beings to rescue <s>Bodhisattvas</s> ripe for liberation. They who, like merchants, travel to the jewel-island of omniscience, seeking the jewel of the knowledge of the Ten Powers. They who, like mighty fishermen, move through the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> with nets of the splendid <s>dharmacakra</s> <s>maṇḍala</s> in hand, for the sake of ripening and rescuing beings born from craving. They who, like <s>Asura</s> lords, pervade and traverse the triple world-city, for the pacification of the agitation caused by the <s>Asuras</s> of affliction. They who, like the orb of the sun, rise in the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, for drying up the water of craving and the mud of afflictions of beings. They who, like the full orb of the moon, rise in the firmament of knowledge, for awakening the water-lilies of the minds of those to be trained. They who, like the surface of the earth, stand level in the world which is uneven through the ups and downs of attraction and aversion, for the sprouting and growth of the shoots of the wholesome faculties of all beings. They who, like the wind, move unattached in all directions, for uprooting the pleasure gardens of forest-creepers and trees of afflictions and views of all beings. They who, like <s>Cakravartins</s>, move through the world for gathering all beings through the equipment and provisions of the four means of attraction. Go, O son of good family, right here in the southern region, to a country called <s>Amitatasala</s>, to a city called <s>Tosala</s>. There dwells a wandering ascetic named <s>Sarvagāmī</s>. Approach him and ask: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sughanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'calāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya acalāmupāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya acalāyā upāsikāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 20 //
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>, bowing his head at the feet of the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>, circumambulating the lay woman <s>Acalā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the lay woman <s>Acalā</s>. [20]

body.text: 23 Sarvagāmī /
body.translated_text: [23 <s>Sarvagāmī</s>]

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'calāmupāsikāmāmukhīkṛtya acalāyā upāsikāyā anuśāsanīmanusmaran, yadacalayopāsikayā darśitaṃ śrāvitaṃ deśitaṃ saṃvarṇitaṃ yojitaṃ vibhaktaṃ prabhāvitaṃ visṛtaṃ tatsaṃbhāvayan, anusaran, anuvicintayan avataran bhāvayan nigamayan nidhyāyan avabhāsayan samīkurvan anupūrveṇa deśena deśaṃ janapadena janapadamanucaṃkraman anuvicaran yenāmitatosalo janapadastenopajagāma / upetya tosalaṃ nagaraṃ parimārgan parigaveṣamāṇo 'nupūrveṇa tosalaṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ / sūryāstaṃgamanakāle sa tosalaṃ nagaramanupraviśya madhye nagaraśṛṅgāṭakasya sthitvā vīthīmukhena vīthīmukhaṃ catvareṇa catvaraṃ rathyayā rathyāṃ sarvagāminaṃ parivrājakaṃ parigaveṣamāṇo vyavacārayan adrākṣīdrātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ tosalasya nagarasyottare digbhāge sulabhaṃ nāma parvatam / tasya śikhare vividhatṛṇagulmauṣadhivanārāmaracite mahāvabhāsaprāptaṃ bhāskaramivoditam / tasya tamavabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā udāraprītivegasaṃjātasya etadabhavat - asaṃśayamahamatra parvataśikhare kalyāṇamitraṃ drakṣyāmīti / sa tasmānnagarādabhiniṣkramya yena sulabhaḥ parvataḥ, tenopetya sulabhaṃ parvatamabhiruhya yena tanmahāvabhāsaṃ parvataśikharaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmannadrākṣīddūrata eva sarvagāminaṃ parivrājakaṃ mahābrahmātirekavarṇaṃ śriyā dedīpyamānaṃ daśabhirbrahmasahasraiḥ parivṛtaṃ caṃkrame caṃkramyamāṇam / sa tasya pādau śirasābhivandya tamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / āha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitaḥ / ahaṃ kulaputra sarvagāmī sarvatrānugatāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ sthitaḥ samantamukhavyavacāraṇālokena samādhimukhena abhāvapratiṣṭhitayā āryānabhisaṃskārikayā samantadharmadhātutalabhedena ca prajñāpāramitājñānālokamukhena samanvāgataḥ / so 'haṃ kulaputra sarvasattvabhājanalokavyavacāreṣu sarvasattvagativyavacāreṣu sarvasattvacyutimukheṣu sarvasattvopapattimukheṣu sarvabhavagatisaṃbhedeṣu vividhopapattyāyatanavicitre lokasaṃniveśe vicitravarṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānāvidhopapattisaṃyojanānāṃ nānāprayogāṇāṃ vicitrādhimuktānāṃ yaduta devagatiparyāpannānāṃ nāgagatiparyāpannānāṃ yakṣagatiparyāpannānāṃ gandharvagatiparyāpannānāmasuragatiparyāpannānāṃ garuḍagatiparyāpannānāṃ kinnaragatiparyāpannānāṃ
mahoragagatiparyāpannānāṃ narakagatiparyāpannānāṃ tiryagyonigatiparyāpannānāṃ yamalokagatiparyāpannānāṃ manuṣyagatiparyāpannānāmanuṣyagatiparyāpannānāṃ vividhadṛṣṭigatiniśritānāṃ śrāvakayānādhimuktānāṃ pratyekabuddhayānādhimuktānāṃ mahāyānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ karomi vividhairupāyairvividhairjñānanayaprayogaiḥ / yaduta keṣāṃcitsattvānāṃ vividhalaukikaśilpaśikṣaṇatayā arthaṃ karomi sarvaśilpajñānabhedavatīdhāraṇyālokena /
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, turning away from the lay devotee <s>Acalā</s>, recalling the instructions of the lay devotee <s>Acalā</s>, contemplating what had been shown, proclaimed, taught, praised, applied, analyzed, manifested, and set forth by the lay devotee <s>Acalā</s>, following it, reflecting upon it, entering into it, cultivating it, concluding it, meditating upon it, illuminating it, and perfecting it, wandering gradually from region to region, from country to country, he arrived at the country of <s>Amitatosala</s>. Having arrived, searching and seeking, he gradually reached the city of <s>Tosala</s>. At the time of sunset, he entered the city of <s>Tosala</s>, and standing in the middle of the city crossroads, searching from lane to lane, from square to square, from street to street for the wandering ascetic <s>Sarvagāmin</s>, when the night had become calm, he saw on the northern side of the city of <s>Tosala</s> a mountain called <s>Sulabha</s>. On its peak, adorned with various grasses, shrubs, herbs, forests, and gardens, a great radiance had appeared, like a risen sun. Seeing that radiance, filled with a surge of great joy, this thought arose in him: "Without doubt, on that mountain peak I shall see a spiritual friend." He went forth from that city, approached Mount <s>Sulabha</s>, ascended it, and proceeding toward that mountain peak of great radiance, he saw from afar the wandering ascetic <s>Sarvagāmin</s>, surpassing the great <s>Brahmā</s> in splendor, blazing with glory, surrounded by ten thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, walking in meditation on a walking path. He bowed his head at his feet, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before him with palms joined, spoke thus: "Noble one, I have generated the mind set upon unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one should practice. And I have heard that the noble one gives counsel and instruction to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore may the noble one tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?" He replied: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you have set out toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. I, son of good family, <s>Sarvagāmin</s>, am established in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct that follows everywhere, endowed with the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) gateway of universal illumination, through the noble unconditioned wisdom established in non-existence, and through the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) knowledge-light gateway that penetrates the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). I, son of good family, benefit beings of various forms, colors, configurations, heights, and girths, beings with various kinds of birth-connections, various endeavors, and various aspirations — those belonging to the realm of <s>devas</s> (gods), those belonging to the realm of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), those belonging to the realm of <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), those belonging to the realm of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), those belonging to the realm of <s>asuras</s> (titans), those belonging to the realm of <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), those belonging to the realm of <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), those belonging to the realm of <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), those belonging to the realm of hells, those belonging to the realm of animals, those belonging to the realm of <s>Yama</s>, those belonging to the realm of humans, those belonging to the realm of non-humans, those attached to various wrong views, those inclined toward the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (vehicle of hearers), those inclined toward the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (vehicle of solitary realizers), and those inclined toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle) — in all the activities of sentient and material worlds, in all the courses of beings' destinies, in all the doors of beings' deaths, in all the doors of beings' rebirths, in all the divisions of states of existence, in the varied abodes of diverse rebirths, I benefit them through various skillful means and various applications of knowledge-methods. That is to say, for some beings I render service through training in various worldly arts and crafts, by means of the illumination of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) that encompasses all branches of craft-knowledge.

body.text: keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ catuḥsaṃgrahavastuprayogeṇa arthaṃ karomi yaduta sarvajñajñānopanayanāya / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ pāramitāsaṃvarṇanatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta sarvajñatāpariṇāmajñānanayālokasaṃjananatayā / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ bodhicittasaṃvarṇanatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta bodhibījāvipraṇāśopastambhasaṃjananatayā / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ sarvākārabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvarṇanatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanasarvasattvaparipākapraṇidhisaṃjananatāyai / keṣāṃcit sattvānāmudvegasaṃjananatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta duścaritavipākaniṣyandanarakagatiduḥkhavedanānubhavasaṃdarśanatayā / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ mahāprītisaṃjananatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta sarvatathāgatāvaropitadakṣiṇāniyatasarvajñatāphalaparyavasāne 'bhyudīraṇatayā / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ sarvatathāgataguṇavarṇasaṃprakāśanatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta buddhaguṇaśarīrābhilāṣasarvajñatāpraṇidhisaṃjananatāyai / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ buddhamāhātmyasūcanayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta avivartyānābhogāpratiprasrabdhabuddhakāryānuṣṭhānasaktabuddhakāyapratilambhābhilāṣasaṃjananatāyai / keṣāṃcit sattvānāṃ buddhādhipateyatāsaṃdarśanatayā arthaṃ karomi yaduta anabhibhūtabuddhātmabhāvasaṃpatpratilābhābhilāṣasaṃjananatāyai /
body.translated_text: For some beings I render service through the application of the four means of attraction, namely for leading them toward omniscient knowledge. For some beings I render service by praising the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), namely by generating the light of the knowledge-method of dedication to omniscience. For some beings I render service by praising <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), namely by generating the support for the non-destruction of the seed of awakening. For some beings I render service by praising the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in all its aspects, namely for generating the aspiration to purify all <s>Buddha</s>-fields and ripen all beings. For some beings I render service by generating a sense of urgency, namely by showing the experience of suffering in the hells as the maturation and outflow of misconduct. For some beings I render service by generating great joy, namely by proclaiming that the merit planted with all <s>Tathāgatas</s> will certainly culminate in the fruit of omniscience. For some beings I render service by illuminating the qualities and glory of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, namely for generating the aspiration toward omniscience and desire for the body endowed with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. For some beings I render service by indicating the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>, namely for generating the desire to obtain the <s>Buddha</s>-body that is irreversible, effortless, and unrelenting in carrying out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>. For some beings I render service by showing the sovereignty of the <s>Buddha</s>, namely for generating the desire to attain the perfection of an unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-body.

body.text: api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra, iha nagare tosale sarvarathyāsu sarvacatvareṣu sarvaśṛṅgāṭakeṣu sarvavīthīmukheṣu sarvagṛheṣu sarvaśreṇiṣu sarvakuleṣu sarvakulaparivarteṣu yathāsaṃnipatitānāṃ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāṃ yathāśayānāṃ yathāprayogāṇāṃ yathādhipateyānāṃ yathāvyavacārāṇāṃ tatsabhāgāni ātmabhāvārohapariṇāhasaṃsthānāni abhinirhṛtya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / na ca te sattvā avabudhyante kenedaṃ deśitam, kuto vāyamiti / anyatra śrutvā tathatvāya pratipadyante / ye 'pīme kulaputra jambudvīpe ṣaṇṇavatiyo pāṣaṇḍā vividhadṛṣṭigatābhiniviṣṭāḥ, tatrāpyahaṃ sarvatrānugacchāmi vividhadṛṣṭigatasaktānāṃ sattvānāṃ paripācanatāyai / yathā ca kulaputra ahamiha tosale nagare sattvānāmarthaṃ karomi, evaṃ jambudvīpe sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu sattvānāmarthaṃ karomi / yathā jambudvīpe, tathā sarvatra cāturdvīpake lokadhātau, evaṃ sāhasre dvisāhasre trisāhasre mahāsāhasre lokadhātau, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu, aparimāṇeṣu lokadhātuṣu, sarvasattvapatheṣu sarvasattvapratiṣṭhāneṣu sarvasattvaniketeṣu sarvasattvanilayasaṃjñāgateṣu sarvasattvaparivarteṣu sarvasattvasamavasaraṇeṣu sarvasattvasamudreṣu sarvasattvavaṃśeṣu sarvasattvadikṣu sarvasattvavidikṣu sarvasattvavidhiṣu yathāśayādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ karomi / vividhairupāyai rvividhairnayairvividhairdvārairvividhābhiryuktibhirvividhaiḥ saṃprayogaiḥ vividhairupāyanayairvividhābhiḥ kriyābhirvividharūpavarṇasaṃdarśanasaṃprasādanatayā vividhavākpathodīraṇatayā sattvānāmarthaṃ karomi / etāmahaṃ kulaputra sarvagāminīṃ sarvatrānugatāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajaganmayaśarīrāṇāṃ svakāyasarvakāyāsaṃbhedasamādhipratilabdhānāṃ sarvabhavagatyanusṛtavipulanirmāṇacakrāṇāṃ sarvalokopapattisvaśarīrānuvicāriṇāṃ sarvajagannayanarocanaruciranirmāṇacakraparamāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, in this city of <s>Tosala</s>, in all the streets, all the squares, all the crossroads, all the lanes, all the houses, all the guilds, all the families, and all the family gatherings, I manifest bodily forms corresponding in height, girth, and shape to those of the men, women, boys, and girls assembled there, according to their dispositions, endeavors, inclinations, and activities, and I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Yet those beings do not understand by whom this was taught or where it came from — they simply hear it and practice accordingly. Furthermore, son of good family, whatever ninety-six heterodox sects exist in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, attached to various wrong views, I follow among them all for the sake of ripening beings attached to various wrong views. And just as I benefit beings here in the city of <s>Tosala</s>, son of good family, so too I benefit beings in all villages, cities, towns, countries, kingdoms, and capitals throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. As in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, so everywhere in the four-continent world system, likewise in the thousand-fold, two-thousand-fold, and three-thousand great thousand world systems, and in the ten directions in immeasurable world systems — in all the paths of beings, all the abodes of beings, all the dwellings of beings, all the places where beings conceive of a home, all the assemblies of beings, all the congregations of beings, all the oceans of beings, all the lineages of beings, in all the directions and intermediate directions of beings, in all the modes of beings — I benefit beings according to their dispositions and aspirations, through various skillful means, various methods, various gateways, various devices, various applications, various approaches, various actions, by displaying various forms and colors to inspire faith, and by uttering various modes of speech. This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of <s>Sarvagāmin</s> ('the one who goes everywhere'), following everywhere, that I know. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> whose bodies encompass all worlds, who have attained the <s>samādhi</s> of non-differentiation between their own body and all bodies, who possess vast emanation-wheels that follow all courses of existence, whose own bodies pervade all rebirths in all worlds, who are supreme in emanation-wheels that delight and beautify the eyes of all the world,

body.text:
sarvajagajjātikulajanmopapattipradarśakānāṃ sarvakalpasaṃvāsāpratihatapraṇidhicakrāṇāmindrajālatalopamacaryāvyūhāvabhāsapratilabdhānāṃ sarvajagadarthakriyānupalesaṃvāsaparamāṇāṃ tryadhvajagattalasamatānugatānāṃ nairātmyavatījñānadhātupratibhāsitāparyantamahākaruṇāgarbhāṇāṃ
sarvajagatkuśalādhānābhimukhānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: who display the birth, family, origin, and rebirth in all the world, whose vow-wheels are unobstructed throughout all eons, who have attained the illumination of conduct-arrays like the net of <s>Indra</s>, who are supreme in dwelling without attachment for the sake of all the world, who follow the equality of the world-ground across the three times, whose boundless great compassion-womb is reflected in the knowledge-realm of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), and who are directed toward establishing virtue in all the world — how could I know their conduct or describe their qualities?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe pṛthurāṣṭraṃ nāma janapadaḥ / tatrotpalabhūtirnāma gāndhikaśreṣṭhī prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here in the southern region there is a country called <s>Pṛthurāṣṭra</s>. There dwells a perfume merchant named <s>Utpalabhūti</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?'

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvagāminaḥ parivrājakasya pādau śirasābhivandya sarvagāminaṃ parivrājakamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sarvagāminaḥ parivrājakasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 21 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the wandering ascetic <s>Sarvagāmin</s>, circumambulated the wandering ascetic <s>Sarvagāmin</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the wandering ascetic <s>Sarvagāmin</s>. [21]

body.text: 24 Utpalabhūtiḥ /
body.translated_text: [24 <s>Utpalabhūti</s>]

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'napekṣaḥ kāye jīvite ca, anapekṣaḥ sarvabhavabhogaparigrahopādānābhiniveśanāpattiṣu, anapekṣaḥ sarvasattvadeśaratiṣu, anapekṣaḥ sarvarūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyeṣu, anapekṣaḥ sarvaparivāropabhogaparibhogeṣu, anapekṣaḥ sarvarājyaiśvaryādhipatyasukheṣu, sāpekṣaḥ sarvasattvaparipācanavinayapariśuddhiṣu anuttarabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhyabhinirharaṇatayā, sāpekṣaḥ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānaparicaryāvitṛptatayā, sāpekṣaḥ sarvadharmeṣu svabhāvaparijñānānugamāya, sāpekṣa sarvabodhisattvaguṇeṣu sarvaguṇasāgareṣu pratipattyacyavanatāyai, sāpekṣaḥ sarvabodhisattvamahāpraṇidhāneṣu sarvakalpānavaśeṣabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsanatāyai, sāpekṣaḥ sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāvatāreṣu, sāpekṣaḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhimukheṣu ekaikasamādhimukhasarvabodhisattvasamādhyasaṃkhyeyāvataraṇavikurvaṇatāyai, sāpekṣaḥ sarvadharmajñānālokacakreṣu sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasaṃpratīcchanātṛptatāyai sarvakalyāṇamitrākarān sarvakalyāṇamitrasaṃbhavane, tāṃśca anyāṃśca sarvabodhisattvaguṇān saṃpaśyan anupūrveṇa yena pṛthurāṣṭraṃ janapadastenopasaṃkramya utpalabhūtiṃ gāndhikaśreṣṭhinaṃ parimārgan parigaveṣamāṇo 'drākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca punaryenotpalabhūtirgāndhikaśreṣṭhī tenopajagāma / upetya utpalabhūtergāndhikaśreṣṭhinaḥ pādau sirasābhivandya utpalabhūtiṃ gāndhikaśreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya utpalabhūtergāndhikaśreṣṭhinaḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ahamārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitaḥ sarvabuddhasamajñānamākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ sarvabuddhapūrṇapraṇidhānamaṇḍalaṃ paripūrayitukāmaḥ sarvabuddharūpakāyaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ sarvabuddhadharmakāyaṃ pariniṣpādayitukāmaḥ sarvabuddhadharmajñānakāyaṃ parijñātukāmaḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalaṃ pariśodhayitukāmaḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhimaṇḍalamavabhāsayitukāmaḥ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīmaṇḍalaṃ saṃsthāpayitukāmaḥ sarvāvaraṇamaṇḍalaṃ vikaritukāmaḥ sarvakṣetramaṇḍalamanuvicaritukāmaḥ / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / kathaṃ pratipadyamāno bodhisattvo niryāti sarvajñatāyām? āha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ahaṃ kulaputra sarvagandhān prajānāmi / sarvagandhayogān sarvadhūpān sarvadhūpayogān prajānāmi / sarvānulepanāni sarvānulepanayogān
sarvacūrṇān sarvacūrṇayogān sarvagandhānulepanacūrṇākarān prajānāmi / devagandhānapi prajānāmi / nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyagandhānapi prajānāmi / vividhānapi gandhān prajānāmi / vyādhipraśamanagandhānapi, daurmanasyāpahāragandhānapi, laukikaprītisaṃjananagandhānapi, kleśojjvālanagandhānapi, kleśapraśamanagandhānapi, vividhasaṃskṛtaratisukhasaṃjananagandhānapi, sarvasaṃskṛtodvegasaṃjananagandhānapi, madapramādāpahāragandhānapi, buddhamanasikārasamudācārasaṃbhavagandhānapi, dharmanayānugamagandhānapi, āryopabhogyagandhānapi, sarvabodhisattvagandhavimātratāmapi, sarvabodhisattvabhūmivyavasthānagandhānapi
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, without regard for body or life, without regard for the acquisitions, clinging, attachments, and misfortunes of all existences, without regard for the delights of all beings in [their] lands, without regard for all forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles, without regard for all retinues, enjoyments, and possessions, without regard for the happiness of all sovereignty, dominion, and rulership — but with regard for the purification of the ripening and discipline of all beings through the accomplishment of the purification of unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-fields; with regard for the insatiability in the worship, attendance, and service of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; with regard for following the comprehension of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; with regard for non-falling from the practice in all <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities and all oceans of qualities; with regard for dwelling in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct without remainder throughout all <s>kalpas</s> in all great <s>bodhisattva</s> vows; with regard for descending into the oceans of assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; with regard for the transformation of descending into innumerable <s>samādhis</s> of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> through each <s>samādhi</s>-gateway in all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>-gateways; with regard for the insatiability in receiving the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> through all wheels of the light of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge; [with regard for] the mines of all spiritual friends and the arising of all spiritual friends — beholding these and other qualities of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, he gradually approached the country of <s>Pṛthurāṣṭra</s> and, searching and seeking for <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant, saw him. Having seen him, he approached where <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant was. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant, circumambulated <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), aspiring to the equal knowledge of all <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to fulfill the maṇḍala of the complete vows of all <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to behold the form-body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to perfect the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) of all <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to comprehend the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge-body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to purify the maṇḍala of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, wishing to illuminate the maṇḍala of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>, wishing to establish the maṇḍala of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, wishing to scatter the maṇḍala of all obstructions, wishing to traverse the maṇḍala of all fields. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. How, by practicing, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> proceed toward omniscience?' He replied: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening! I, son of good family, know all fragrances. I know all fragrance-compositions, all incenses, all incense-compositions. I know all ointments, all ointment-compositions, all powders, all powder-compositions, and the sources of all fragrance-ointments and powders. I know also divine fragrances. I know also the fragrances of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans. I know also various fragrances: fragrances that pacify diseases, fragrances that remove grief, fragrances that generate worldly joy, fragrances that inflame <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), fragrances that pacify <s>kleśas</s>, fragrances that generate the pleasure and happiness of various conditioned things, fragrances that generate revulsion toward all conditioned things, fragrances that remove intoxication and heedlessness, fragrances that arise from the practice of <s>Buddha</s>-mindfulness, fragrances that follow the method of <s>dharma</s>, fragrances fit for the use of noble ones, and also the various measures of fragrances of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and also the fragrances that mark the stages of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>

body.text: prajānāmi / sarvāṃśca tānahaṃ gandhānākārato 'pi prajānāmi / saṃbhavato 'pi utpādato 'pi prādurbhāvato 'pi pariniṣpattito 'pi pariśuddhito 'pi parihārato 'pi prayogato 'pi paribhogato 'pi viṣayato 'pi prabhāvato 'pi dharmato 'pi mūlato 'pi prajānāmi //
body.translated_text: I know. And all those fragrances I know by their form, by their origin, by their production, by their manifestation, by their perfection, by their purification, by their decline, by their application, by their use, by their domain, by their potency, by their nature, and by their root. //

body.text: asti kulaputra manuṣyaloke nāgasaṃkṣobhasaṃbhavahastigarbho nāma gandhaḥ, yasya tilamātrā gulikā sakalaṃ pṛthurāṣṭraṃ janapadaṃ mahāgandhaghanābhrajālasaṃchannaṃ kṛtvā saptāhaṃ sūkṣmagandhodakadhārāvarṣamabhipravarṣati / tatra yeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ śarīre vā cīvare vā gandhodakadhārā nipatanti, te sarve suvarṇavarṇakusumavicitritā bhavanti / yeṣu ca bhavanavimānakūṭāgāreṣu nipatanti, te sarve suvarṇavarṇakusumavicitritā bhavanti / ye 'pi sattvāsteṣāṃ gandhameghajālānāṃ mārutasamīritānāmantarbhavanagatā gandhaṃ jighranti, te sarve saptāhamudāraprītiprāmodyaparisphuṭā bhavanti, anekavidhāni ca kāyikacaitasikāni sukhasaumanasyāni pratyanubhavanti / na caiṣāṃ śarīre vyādhirutpadyate dhātusaṃkṣobhajo vā aparaparikramiko vā / nāpi caitasikaṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyamutpadyate, na samudācarati bhayaṃ vā trāsaṃ vā cchambhitattvaṃ vā manaḥsaṃkṣobho vā vyāpādo vā / sarve ca te sattvā anyonyaṃ maitracittā bhavanti harṣaprītisaṃjātāḥ / teṣāmahaṃ kulaputra harṣaprītisaṃjātānāmāśayaviśuddhimārabhya tathā dharmaṃ deśayāmi, yathā niyatā bhavanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: There is, son of good family, in the human world, a fragrance called <s>Nāgasaṃkṣobhasaṃbhavahastigarbha</s> (Elephant-Womb Born of the Agitation of <s>Nāgas</s>), a sesame-sized pellet of which, having covered the entire country of <s>Pṛthurāṣṭra</s> with a great net of dense fragrance-clouds, rains a shower of fine fragrant water-streams for seven days. Therein, whatever beings have those fragrant water-streams fall upon their bodies or garments, they all become adorned with golden-colored flowers. And whatever palace-mansions and turret-chambers they fall upon, they all become adorned with golden-colored flowers. And whatever beings, dwelling within their abodes, smell the fragrance of those nets of fragrance-clouds stirred by the wind, they all for seven days are pervaded with sublime joy and delight, and experience manifold bodily and mental pleasures and happiness. And no disease arises in their bodies, whether born of humoral imbalance or from other external causes. Nor does mental suffering or grief arise in them; neither fear, nor terror, nor trembling, nor mental agitation, nor hostility arises. And all those beings become friendly-minded toward one another, born of gladness and joy. For those beings, son of good family, who are born of gladness and joy, beginning from the purification of their disposition, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that they become destined for unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: asti kulaputra malayaparvatasaṃbhavaṃ gośīrṣaṃ nāma candanam, yenānuliptagātro agnikhadāyāmapi prapatito na dahyate / asti kulaputra sāgarakacchasaṃbhavo aparājito nāma gandhaḥ, yenānuliptāyā bheryāḥ śaṅkhasya vā nirghoṣeṇa sarvaparacakraṃ parājayaṃ gacchati / asti kulaputra anavataptahṛdatīrasaṃbhavaṃ padmagarbhaṃ nāma kālāgaru, yasya tilamātrā gulikā sakalaṃ jambudvīpaṃ gandhena spharati / ye ca sattvāstaṃ gandhaṃ jighranti, te sarve pāpavijugupsanasaṃvaracittaṃ pratilabhante / asti kulaputra himavatparvatarājasaṃbhavā aruṇavatī nāma gandhajātiḥ, yasyā gandhamāghrāya sattvā viraktacittā bhavanti / teṣāmahaṃ tathā dharmaṃ deśayāmi, yadvirajomaṇḍalaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhante / asti kulaputra rākṣasalokasaṃbhavā sāgaragarbhā nāma gandhajātiḥ, yā rājñaścakravartinaḥ paribhogāyotpadyate, yayā dhūpitamātrayā caturaṅgo balakāyo rājñaścakravartino gaganatale pratiṣṭhate / asti kulaputra, sudharmadevasabhāsaṃbhavā śobhanavyūhā nāma gandhajātiḥ, yayā dhūpitamātrayā devā buddhagandhasmṛtiṃ pratilabhante / asti kulaputra suyāmadevarājabhavane śuddhakośānāṃ gandhajātiḥ, yayā dhūpitayā sarve suyāmadevaputrāḥ suyāmadevarājasakāśamupasaṃkrāmanti / teṣāmupasaṃkrāntānāṃ suyāmo devarājo dhārmīṃ kathāṃ kathayati / asti kulaputra tuṣitabhavane sindhuvāritā nāma gandhajātiḥ, yā dharmāsananiṣaṇṇasya ekajātipratibaddhasya bodhisattvasya purato dhūpitā mahāgandhameghena sakalaṃ dharmadhātuṃ spharitvā sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣvanekākāravyūhaṃ mahādharmameghavarṣaṃ pravarṣati / asti kulaputra sunirmitadevarājabhavane manoharā nāma gandhajātiḥ, yā sunirmitadevarājabhavane pradhūpitā saptāhamacintyadharmameghavarṣaṃ pravarṣati / etāmahaṃ
body.translated_text: There is, son of good family, a sandalwood called <s>Gośīrṣa</s> (Cow-Head), born on <s>Malaya</s> mountain, with which one whose body is anointed, even if fallen into a fire-pit, is not burned. There is, son of good family, a fragrance called <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquered), born on the shore of the ocean, with which when a drum or conch is anointed, by its sound all enemy armies are defeated. There is, son of good family, a black <s>aguru</s> (aloe) called <s>Padmagarbha</s> (Lotus-Womb), born on the shores of Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, a sesame-sized pellet of which pervades all <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with its fragrance; and whatever beings smell that fragrance, they all attain the mind of restraint through revulsion toward evil. There is, son of good family, a fragrance-species called <s>Aruṇavatī</s> (Dawn-Light), born on the <s>Himavat</s> king of mountains, upon smelling whose fragrance beings become dispassionate in mind; for them I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that they attain the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Virajomaṇḍala</s> (Circle of the Stainless). There is, son of good family, a fragrance-species called <s>Sāgaragarbhā</s> (Ocean-Womb), born in the world of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, which arises for the use of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, by merely burning which the four-fold army of the <s>Cakravartin</s> king stands upon the surface of the sky. There is, son of good family, a fragrance-species called <s>Śobhanavyūhā</s> (Beautiful Array), born in the <s>Sudharmā</s> divine assembly-hall, by merely burning which the <s>devas</s> attain the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>-fragrance. There is, son of good family, in the palace of the <s>Suyāma</s> divine king, a fragrance-species called <s>Śuddhakośa</s> (Pure Treasury), by burning which all the <s>Suyāma devaputras</s> approach the presence of the <s>Suyāma</s> divine king; and when they have approached, the <s>Suyāma</s> divine king speaks a <s>Dharma</s>-discourse to them. There is, son of good family, in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, a fragrance-species called <s>Sindhuvāritā</s>, which, when burned before a <s>bodhisattva</s> bound to a single birth seated upon the <s>dharma</s>-seat, having pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with a great fragrance-cloud, rains a great <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain of manifold arrays in the assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. There is, son of good family, in the palace of the <s>Sunirmita</s> divine king, a fragrance-species called <s>Manoharā</s> (Mind-Captivating), which, when burned in the palace of the <s>Sunirmita</s> divine king, rains for seven days an inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>-cloud-rain. This

body.text:
kulaputra gandhayuktiṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ nirāmagandhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakāmoccalitānāṃ kleśamārapāśavipramuktānāṃ sarvabhavagativyativṛttānāṃ jñānamāyāgatarūpavicāriṇāṃ sarvalokānupaliptānāmasaṅgaśīlānāmanāvaraṇajñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhānāmapratihatajñānagocaraviṣayāṇāṃ sarvālayaniketāniśritānāṃ sarvabhavālayaniketacāriṇāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, śīlacaryāviśuddhimukhaṃ
vā paridīpayitum, anavadyacaraṇaṃ vā prabhāvayitum, avyāpādakāyavāṅbhanaḥsamudācāro vā deśayitum //
body.translated_text: fragrance-science, son of good family, I know. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the qualities, of <s>bodhisattvas</s> whose fragrance is free from impurity, who are displaced from all desires, who are freed from the snares of <s>Māra</s> [born of] <s>kleśas</s>, who have transcended all courses of existence, who move in forms attained through the magical illusion of knowledge, who are unstained by all worlds, whose conduct is unattached, whose maṇḍala of unobstructed knowledge is purified, whose domain of unimpeded knowledge-range is [boundless], who are unsupported by all abodes and dwellings, who move in the abodes and dwellings of all existences — or illuminate the gateway of the purification of their conduct and discipline, or reveal their blameless practice, or display their conduct of body, speech, and mind free from hostility? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe kūṭāgāraṃ nāma nagaram / tatra vairo nāma dāśaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family; right here in <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region) is a city called <s>Kūṭāgāra</s> (Turret-Chamber). There dwells a mariner named <s>Vaira</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidāraka utpalabhūtergāndhikaśreṣṭhinaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya utpalabhūtiṃ gāndhikaśreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya utpalabhūtergāndhikaśreṣṭhino 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 22 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant, circumambulating <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Utpalabhūti</s> the perfumer-merchant. // 22 //

body.text: 25 Vairaḥ /
body.translated_text: 25. <s>Vaira</s>. /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kūṭāgāranagarābhimukhaṃ mārgaṃ pratipadyamāno 'nuvicaran, mārganimnatāṃ mārgonnatatāṃ mārgasamatāṃ mārgaviṣamatāṃ mārgasarajaskatāṃ mārgavirajaskatāṃ mārgakṣematāṃ mārgagahanatāṃ mārgānāvaraṇatāṃ mārgakuṭilatāṃ mārgarjukatāmanuvilokya evaṃ cittamutpādayāmāsa - idaṃ khalu me tasya kalyāṇamitrasyopasaṃkramaṇaṃ bodhisattvamārgapratipattihetubhūtaṃ sattvānugrahazñānamārgapratipattihetubhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati / pāramitāmārgapratipattihetubhūtaṃ sarvasattvānugrahajñānamārgapratipattihetubhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati / sarvasattvānunayapratighonnāmāvanāmaprapātavinivṛttaye sarvasattvaviṣamamatipratinivāraṇatāyai sarvasattvakleśarajaḥpraśamanāya, sarvasattvavividhākuśaladṛṣṭisthāṇukaṇṭakaśarkarakaṭhallāpanayanāya, anāvaraṇadharmadhātuparamatāyaiḥ, akṣuṇṇasarvajñatāpuropanayanāya hetubhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? kalyāṇamitrākarāḥ sarvakuśaladharmāḥ / kalyāṇamitrādhīnā sarvajñatā / sa evaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayukto durāsadasamudācāro 'nupūrveṇa yena kūṭāgāraṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya vairaṃ dāśaṃ parimārgan parigaveṣamāṇo 'drākṣīnmahānagaramukhe sāgarāvatāratīre vairaṃ dāśaṃ vaṇikūśatasahasrairanekaiśca prāṇiśatasahasrairvicitrāṃ kathāṃ śrotukāmaiḥ parivṛtaṃ samudrakathāsaṃprakāśanatayā buddhaguṇasamudrān sattvānāmārocayamānam / dṛṣṭvā ca yena vairo dāśaḥ, tenopajagāma / upetya vairasya dāśasya pādau śirasābhivandya vairaṃ dāśamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vairasya dāśasya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāhamayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / āha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya mahājñānapratilambhasaṃbhavahetuṃ paripṛcchasi / vividhasaṃsāraduḥkhasamudācārasaṃbhavahetuṃ sarvajñatādvīpādhiṣṭhānagamanasaṃbhavahetum abhedyamahāyānasaṃbhavahetuṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipātabhayavigamamārgapratipattisaṃbhavahetuṃ vividhaśāntasamādhimukhāvartanayādhigamajñānamārgasaṃbhavahetuṃ sarvatragāminībodhisattvacaryāvicārapraṇidhirathacakrāparāhatamārgasaṃbhavahetuṃ sarvatejaūrmivyūhabodhisattvacaryāsvabhāvanayamārgasaṃbhavaviśuddhihetuṃ sarvadharmadiṅbhukhāparāntamārgasaṃbhavaviśuddhihetuṃ sarvajñatāsāgarāvatāramārgasaṃbhavaviśuddhihetuṃ paripṛcchasi / ahaṃ kulaputra iha
mahāsāgaratīrakūṭāgāre mahānagare prativasāmi mahākaruṇādhvajāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ pariśodhayan / so 'haṃ kulaputra jambudvīpe daridrān sattvānavalokya eṣāmarthāya tathā tapastapyāmi, yaduta abhiprāyameṣāṃ paripūrayiṣyāmi / lokāmiṣasaṃgrahaṃ kariṣyāmi / dharmasaṃbhogena cainān saṃtoṣayiṣyāmi puṇyasaṃbhāramārgameṣāmupadekṣyāmi / jñānasaṃbhāraṃ saṃjanayiṣyāmi / kuśalamūlabalaṃ saṃvardhayiṣyāmi / bodhicittamutpādayiṣyāmi / bodhyāśayaṃ viśodyayiṣyāmi / mahākaruṇābalamupastambhayiṣyāmi / saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ vyupaśamayiṣyāmi / saṃsāracaryāparikhedabalamupastambhayiṣyāmi / sattvasāgarasaṃgrahaṇe cainānniyojayiṣyāmi / guṇasāgarapratipattimukhe ca pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, setting out on the road toward the city of <s>Kūṭāgāra</s> and traveling along it, observed the lowness of the path, the elevation of the path, the evenness of the path, the unevenness of the path, the dustiness of the path, the dustlessness of the path, the safety of the path, the density of the path, the unobstructedness of the path, the crookedness of the path, and the straightness of the path, and generated this thought: "This approach of mine to that <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend) will become the cause for entering the path of <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, the cause for entering the path of knowledge that benefits beings. It will become the cause for entering the path of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the cause for entering the path of knowledge that benefits all beings. It will become the cause for turning back all beings from the precipice of attraction and aversion, for preventing the crooked thoughts of all beings, for pacifying the dust of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of all beings, for removing the stumps, thorns, gravel, and pebbles of the various unwholesome views of all beings, for attaining the supreme unobstructed <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), and for approaching the unimpaired city of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). Why is that? All wholesome <s>dharmas</s> originate from the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>. <s>Sarvajñatā</s> depends on the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>." Thus engaged in reflection and mental attention, with conduct difficult to attain, he gradually approached the city of <s>Kūṭāgāra</s>, and while searching and seeking the fisherman <s>Vaira</s>, he saw at the gate of the great city, on the shore where one descends into the ocean, the fisherman <s>Vaira</s> surrounded by hundreds of thousands of merchants and many hundreds of thousands of living beings who wished to hear wondrous stories, proclaiming to beings the ocean of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities by way of telling ocean stories. Having seen him, he approached the fisherman <s>Vaira</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the fisherman <s>Vaira</s>, circumambulated the fisherman <s>Vaira</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before the fisherman <s>Vaira</s> with palms joined, he said: "Noble one, I have generated the mind of supreme perfect <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one should practice. I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, may the noble one tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?" He replied: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you, having generated the mind of supreme perfect <s>bodhi</s>, ask about the cause for the arising of the attainment of great knowledge, the cause for the arising of the path to the island of <s>sarvajñatā</s> beyond the arising of various <s>saṃsāra</s> sufferings, the cause for the arising of the indestructible <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), the cause for the arising of the path that removes the fear of falling into the grounds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the cause for the arising of the knowledge-path for attaining entry into various peaceful <s>samādhi</s> gates, the cause for the arising of the path whose chariot-wheel of the vow of investigating the all-pervading <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct is unimpeded, the cause for the purification of the arising of the path of mastering the nature of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct adorned with the splendor of all radiant energies, the cause for the purification of the arising of the path to the farthest reaches of all <s>dharmas</s> in every direction, the cause for the purification of the arising of the path of descent into the ocean of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. I, son of good family, dwell here in the great city of <s>Kūṭāgāra</s> on the shore of the great ocean, purifying the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct whose banner is great compassion. I, son of good family, observing the poor beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, practice austerities for their sake, thinking: I shall fulfill their aspirations. I shall gather them through worldly goods. I shall satisfy them with the enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s>. I shall show them the path of accumulating merit. I shall generate in them the accumulation of knowledge. I shall increase the power of their wholesome roots. I shall cause them to generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). I shall purify their aspiration for <s>bodhi</s>. I shall strengthen the power of great compassion. I shall pacify the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. I shall strengthen the power of unwearying conduct in <s>saṃsāra</s>. I shall engage them in gathering the ocean of beings. And I shall establish them at the gate of practicing the ocean of qualities.

body.text: dharmasāgarajñānālokaṃ caiṣāmupasaṃhariṣyāmi / sarvabuddhasāgaraṃ caiṣāmabhimukhamāvartayayiṣyāmi / sarvajñatāsāgare cainānavatārayiṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: I shall bring to them the light of knowledge of the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>. I shall turn toward them the entire ocean of all <s>Buddhas</s>. And I shall cause them to descend into the ocean of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).

body.text: evaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayukto 'haṃ kulaputra iha sāgaratīrakūṭāgāranagare pravicarāmi / evaṃ jagaddhitasukhaprayukto 'haṃ kulaputra sarvamahāsāgararatnadvīpān prajānāmi / sarvaratnākarān sarvaratnagotrāṇi sarvaratnamūlaṃ prajānāmi / sarvanāgabhavanāni sarvanāgasaṃkṣobhān sarvayakṣabhavanāni sarvayakṣasaṃkṣobhān sarvarākṣasabhavanāni sarvarākṣasabhayapraśamanāni sarvabhūtabhavanāni sarvabhūtāntarāyavyupaśamanāni prajānāmi / sarvāvantaṃ saṃbhavāvartaparivarjanaṃ mahormiveśaparihāramudakavarṇavimātratāṃ prajānāmi / candrādityajyotirgrahagaṇaparivartanaṃ rātriṃdivakṣaṇalavamūhūrtaṃ prajānāmi / gamanāgamanaviśeṣatāṃ kṣemākṣematāṃ yānapātrayantrakriyādṛḍhatāṃ yānaparihāraṃ yānavāhanaṃ mārutasaṃgrahaṇaṃ mārutotpādanaṃ yānāvartanaṃ yānaparivartanaṃ yānasaṃsthāpanaṃ yānasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ prajānāmi / so 'haṃ kulaputra evaṃjñānasamanvāgataḥ satataṃ sattvārthakāryaprayukto vaṇiggaṇaṃ dṛḍhena yānena kṣemeṇa śivenābhayena yathāpraharṣaṃ pramodayan dhārmyā kathayā yathābhiprāyeṇa ratnadvīpamupanayāmi / sarvaratnasamṛddhiṃ caiṣāṃ kṛtvā punarjambūdvīpamupanayāmi / na ca mama kulaputra kadācit kiṃcid yānapātraṃ vipannapūrvam / yeṣāṃ ca sattvānāmahaṃ kulaputra cakṣuṣāmābhāsamāgacchāmi, ye ca sattvā mama dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇvanti, teṣāṃ sarvasaṃsārasāgarasaṃsīdanabhayāni vigacchanti, sarvajñatāsāgarāvatārajñānaṃ cāmukhībhavati / tṛṣṇāsāgarocchoṣaṇatāyai ca pratipadyante, tryadhvasāgarajñānālokaṃ ca pratilabhante / sarvasattvaduḥkhasāgarakṣayāya cābhyutsahante / sarvasattvacittasāgarakāluṣyaprasādanatāyai ca prayujyante / sarvakṣetrasāgaraviśuddhaye vīryamārabhante / sarvadiksāgaraspharaṇatāyai ca na vinivartante / sarvajagadindriyasāgarasaṃbhedaṃ ca pratividhyanti / sarvasattvacaryāsāgaraṃ cānuvartante / yathāśayajagatsāgarapratibhāsaprāptāśca bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Thus engaged in reflection and mental attention, I, son of good family, wander here in the city of <s>Kūṭāgāra</s> on the ocean shore. Thus devoted to the welfare and happiness of the world, I, son of good family, know all the jewel-islands of the great ocean, all the jewel-mines, all the jewel-veins, all the jewel-sources. I know all the <s>Nāga</s> dwellings, all the disturbances of <s>Nāgas</s>, all the <s>Yakṣa</s> dwellings, all the disturbances of <s>Yakṣas</s>, all the <s>Rākṣasa</s> dwellings, all the means of pacifying the fear of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, all the <s>Bhūta</s> dwellings, and all the means of removing the obstacles of <s>Bhūtas</s>. I know the avoidance of all whirlpools and currents, the evasion of great waves, and the diversity of water colors. I know the revolutions of the moon, sun, luminaries, and constellations, the divisions of night and day into moments, instants, and <s>muhūrtas</s> (hours). I know the distinctions of going and coming, safety and danger, the soundness of vessels, boats, and mechanical devices, the management of vessels, the steering of vessels, the gathering of winds, the generation of winds, the turning of vessels, the maneuvering of vessels, the anchoring of vessels, and the dispatching of vessels. I, son of good family, endowed with such knowledge and constantly devoted to the welfare of beings, delight the company of merchants with a sturdy, safe, auspicious, and fearless vessel according to their wishes, and with <s>Dharma</s> discourse I guide them according to their aspirations to the jewel-island. Having provided them with the abundance of all jewels, I bring them back to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. And never, son of good family, has any vessel of mine ever been wrecked. Those beings who come within the range of my sight, son of good family, and those beings who hear my teaching of <s>Dharma</s> — for them all fears of sinking in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> vanish, and knowledge of descent into the ocean of <s>sarvajñatā</s> becomes manifest. They set forth toward the drying up of the ocean of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and they obtain the light of knowledge of the ocean of the three times. They become capable of exhausting the ocean of suffering of all beings. They engage in purifying the turbidity of the ocean of minds of all beings. They undertake effort for the purification of the ocean of all realms. They do not turn back from pervading the ocean of all directions. They penetrate the diversity of the ocean of faculties of all beings in the world. They follow the ocean of conduct of all beings. And they attain the reflection in the ocean of the world according to dispositions.

body.text: etasya ahaṃ kulaputra mahākarūṇādhvajasya amoghadarśanaśravaṇaṃ saṃvāsānusmṛtirnāma nadīnirghoṣasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasaṃsārasāgaravicāriṇāṃ sarvakleśāsāgarānupaliptānāṃ sarvadṛṣṭigatasāgarasaṃgrahagrāhabhayavigatānāṃ sarvadharmasāgarasvabhāvajalavicāriṇāṃ sarvajagatsāgarasvabhāvatalavicāriṇāṃ sarvajagatsāgarasaṃgrahavastusaṃgrahaṇajālānāṃ sarvajñatāsāgarasaṃvāsināṃ sarvasattvābhiniveśasāgaranirmathanānāṃ sarvakālasāgarasaṃbhinnavihāriṇāṃ sarvajagatsāgaraparipākatattvābhijñānāṃ sarvajagatsāgaravinayakālānatikrāntānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, have obtained this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Unfailing Seeing, Hearing, Dwelling Together, and Recollection, the Sound of the River,' which belongs to the banner of great compassion.
