How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who traverse the ocean of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, who are unstained by the ocean of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), who are free from the fear of the crocodiles of grasping in the ocean of all views, who traverse the waters of the essential nature of the ocean of all <s>dharmas</s>, who traverse the depths of the essential nature of the ocean of the entire world, who possess nets of gathering through the means of gathering the ocean of the entire world, who dwell in the ocean of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, who churn the ocean of attachment of all beings, who abide having penetrated the ocean of all times, who have direct knowledge of the truth of the ripening of the ocean of the entire world, and who never miss the time of disciplining the ocean of the entire world?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe nandihāraṃ nāma nagaram / tatra jayottamo nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, here in the southern region there is a city called <s>Nandihāra</s>. There dwells a merchant named <s>Jayottama</s>. Approach him and ask: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vairasya dāśasya pādau śirasābhivandya vairaṃ dāśamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya aśrumukho rudan kalyāṇamitradarśanābhilāṣāvitṛpto vairasya dāśasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 23 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the fisherman <s>Vaira</s>, circumambulated the fisherman <s>Vaira</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing back again and again, weeping with tear-streaked face, unsatisfied in his longing to see the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend), and departed from the presence of the fisherman <s>Vaira</s>. [23]

body.text: 26 Jayottamaḥ /
body.translated_text: [26 <s>Jayottama</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahāmaitryapramāṇasattvadhātuspharaṇacitto mahākaruṇāsnehābhiṣyanditasaṃtāno vipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāravyūhopacitaḥ sarvakleśarajastamomalapaṅkāpagato dharmasamatānugamo nimnonnatasarvajñatāmārgaprasṛtaḥ aparimāṇākuśaladharmāvatāramukhoddhṛtaḥ sarvākuśalābhedyadṛḍhavīryabalaparākramaḥ acintyabodhisattvasamādhivipulaprasrabdhimukhasamarpitaḥ prajñābhāskaratejovabhāsavidhūtaniravaśeṣāvidyāndhakāraḥ sukhaśītalopāyamāruteritajñānakusumāvakīrṇo mahāpraṇidhānasamudraniryāṇajñānanayānukūlaḥ apratihatadharmadhātuspharaṇajñānaḥ akṣuṇṇasarvajñatāpurapraveśābhimukhaḥ bodhisattvamārgamabhikāṅkṣamāṇo yena nandihāraṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya jayottamaṃ śreṣṭhinaṃ parimārgan parigaveṣamāṇo 'drākṣīt pūrveṇa nadihārasya nagarasya paryante vicitradhvajāyāmaśokavanikāyāmanekagṛhapatisahasraparivṛtaṃ vividhāni nagarakāryāṇi pariniṣṭhāpayantaṃ tadāgamya ca dhārmīṃ kathāṃ kathayantam, sarvāhaṃkārasamudyotāya, sarvamamakārotsargāya, sarvaparigrahaparityāgāya, sarvavastugrahaṇapratinisargāya, sarvābhiniveśanirdāraṇāya, sarvatṛṣṇābandhanacchedanāya, sarvadṛṣṭigatakapāṭanirbhedanāya, sarvasaṃśayavimativicikitsātimiravidhamanāya, māyāśāṭhyakāluṣyāpanayanāya, īrṣyāmātsaryamalasaṃśodhanāya, cittasaraḥprasādanāya, anāvilacittatāyāṃ sattvapratiṣṭhāpanatāyai, anāvilaśraddhābalotpādanatayā buddhadarśanābhirocanatāyai, bodhisattvabalodbhāvanatayā buddhadharmasaṃpratīcchanatāyai, bodhisattvacaryāsūcanatayā bodhisattvasamādhibalajananatāyai, bodhisattvaprajñābalasaṃdarśanatayā bodhisattvasmṛtibalaviśuddhyuttāraṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayamānaṃ yaduta bodhicittotpādābhirocanāya //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, whose mind pervaded the realm of beings with the immeasurable quality of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), whose continuum was moistened with the affection of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), who was enriched by the adornment of vast accumulations of merit and knowledge, who had removed all the mud and mire of the dust and darkness of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), who followed the equality of <s>Dharma</s> and proceeded on the path of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) through high and low, who was lifted up from the entrance into immeasurable unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, whose vigor, strength, and valor were firm and impenetrable by all that is unwholesome, who was established in the vast tranquility of inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>, whose darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) was entirely dispelled by the radiant splendor of the sun of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), who was strewn with the blossoms of knowledge stirred by the gentle, cool breeze of skillful means, who was in accord with the method of the knowledge flowing from the ocean of great vows, whose knowledge of pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) was unimpeded, who faced the approach to the unimpaired city of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, longing for the <s>bodhisattva</s> path — approached the city of <s>Nandihāra</s>, and while searching and seeking the merchant <s>Jayottama</s>, he saw him on the eastern outskirts of the city of <s>Nandihāra</s>, in a beautiful <s>aśoka</s> grove adorned with various banners, surrounded by many thousands of householders, bringing to completion various affairs of the city. And having come there, <s>Jayottama</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> — for the dispelling of all sense of self, for the relinquishing of all sense of 'mine,' for the abandonment of all possessiveness, for the giving up of grasping at all things, for the breaking through of all attachment, for the cutting of all bonds of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), for the breaking open of the bolts of all wrong views, for the dispelling of the darkness of all doubt, uncertainty, and hesitation, for the removal of deceit, dishonesty, and impurity, for the cleansing of the stain of envy and miserliness, for the clarifying of the lake of the mind, for establishing beings in purity of mind, for inspiring the sight of the <s>Buddhas</s> through generating the power of unclouded faith, for receiving the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s> through producing the strength of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, for generating the power of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> through revealing <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, and for purifying and elevating the power of <s>bodhisattva</s> mindfulness through displaying the power of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>prajñā</s> — that is, for inspiring the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening).

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastatkathāparyavasānamāgamayitvā jayottamasya śreṣṭhinaḥ pādayoḥ praṇipatya suciramabhināmya dharmagauravapratilabdhenāśayena evaṃ vācamudīrayāmāsasudhano 'smi, sudhano 'smi ārya, bodhisattvacaryāṃ parimārgāmi / tadvadatu me āryo yathāhaṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣeyam / yathā śikṣamāṇaḥ sarvasattvaparipākavinayakāyeṣvabhimukho bhaveyam / sarvabuddhadarśanaṃ na vijahyām / sarvabuddhadharmaṃ śṛṇuyām / sarvabuddhadharmameghān saṃdhārayeyam / sarvabuddhadharmanayeṣu pratipadyeyam / sarvalokadhātuṣu bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ careyam / sarvakalpasaṃvāseṣu bodhisattvacaryayā na parikhidyeyam / sarvatathāgatavikurvitānyājānīyām / sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānāni saṃpratīccheyam / sarvatathāgatabaleṣu ca avabhāsaṃ pratilabdho bhaveyam //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, having waited for the conclusion of that discourse, prostrated at the feet of the merchant <s>Jayottama</s>, bowed long, and with a disposition gained through reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, uttered these words: 'I am <s>Sudhana</s>, I am <s>Sudhana</s>, Noble One, seeking the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. Let the Noble One tell me how I might train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — how, training thus, I might face the bodies for the ripening and discipline of all beings; how I might never abandon the seeing of all <s>Buddha</s>s; how I might hear all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; how I might retain the clouds of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; how I might practice the methods of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; how I might walk the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct in all world-realms; how I might not be wearied by the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct through all <s>kalpa</s>s of dwelling; how I might know all <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations; how I might receive all <s>Buddha</s>-empowerments; and how I might attain illumination in the powers of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' //

body.text: atha khalu jayottamaḥ śreṣṭhī sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ahaṃ kulaputra sarvagāminībodhisattvacaryāmukhaṃ pariśodhayāmi yaduta abhāvapratiṣṭhitānabhisaṃskāravipratilābhabalena / so 'hamiha sarvagāminībodhisattvacaryāpariśuddhimukhe sthitvā sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvatridaśadevalokeṣu sarvayāmabhavaneṣu sarvatuṣitadevalokeṣu sarvanirmāṇaratidevalokeṣu sarvaparanirmitavaśavartidevalokeṣu
body.translated_text: Then the merchant <s>Jayottama</s> spoke to <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, thus: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. I, son of good family, purify the gate of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct that goes everywhere (<s>sarvagāminī</s>) — that is, by the power of obtaining the absence of fabrication established in non-existence. And I, standing in this gate of the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct that goes everywhere, in the entire three-thousand-fold great thousand world-realm, in all the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heavens, in all the <s>Yāma</s> abodes, in all the <s>Tuṣita</s> heavens, in all the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> heavens, in all the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heavens

body.text:
sarvamārabhavaneṣu sarvakāmādhātuṣu devanikāyāntargateṣu sarvadevabhavaneṣu sarvanāgalokeṣu sarvanāgabhavaneṣu, sarvayakṣalokeṣu sarvayakṣabhavaneṣu, sarvarākṣasalokeṣu sarvarākṣasabhavaneṣu, sarvakumbhāṇḍalokeṣu sarvakumbhāṇḍabhavaneṣu, sarvapretalokeṣu sarvapretabhavaneṣu, sarvagandharvalokeṣu sarvagandharvabhavaneṣu, sarvāsuralokeṣu sarvāsurabhavaneṣu, sarvagaruḍalokeṣu sarvagaruḍabhavaneṣu, sarvakinnaralokeṣu sarvakinnarabhavaneṣu, sarvamahoragalokeṣu sarvamahoragabhavaneṣu, sarvamanuṣyalokeṣu sarvamanuṣyabhavaneṣu, sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu sarvakāmadhātvantargatāsu sarvasattvagatiṣu dharmaṃ deśayāmi / adharmaṃ pratijahāmi / vivādaṃ praśamayāmi / vigrahaṃ vyāvartayāmi / kalahaṃ vyupaśamayāmi / yuddhaṃ nivārayāmi / raṇamupaśamayāmi / vairamuparamayāmi / bandhanāni cchinadmi / cārakāṇi bhinadmi / bhayāni vinivartayāmi / akuśalakarmābhisaṃskārān samucchinadmi / prāṇivadhāt sattvān vinivārayāmi / adattādānāt kāmamithyācārāt mṛṣāvādāt paiśunyāt pārūṣyāt saṃbhinnapralāpādabhidhyāyā vyāpādāt mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sattvānnivārayāmi / sarvakāryebhyaḥ sattvān vinivārayāmi / sarvadharmakuśaladharmakriyāsvanuvartayāmi / sarvasattvān sarvaśilpāni śikṣayāmi / lokahitāvahāni sarvaśāstrāṇi dyotayāmi, prakalpayāmi, prakāśayāmi, prabhāvayāmi lokapraharṣaṇatāyai / sattvaparipākāya sarvapāṣaṇḍānanuvartayāmi / uttarijñānaviśeṣasūcanatāyai sarvadṛṣṭigatavinivartanatāyai
sarvabuddhadharmārocanatāyai yāvadbrahmaloke 'pi sarvarūpadhātukān devānabhibhūya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / yathā ceha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau, tathā daśasu dikṣu daśānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu dharmaṃ deśayāmi / buddhadharmān deśayāmi / bodhisattvadharmān śrāvakadharmān pratyekabuddhadharmān deśayāmi / narakān deśayāmi / narakagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ deśayāmi / nairayikasattvakāraṇāṃ deśayāmi / tiryagyoniṃ deśayāmi / tiryagyonigatisaṃbhedaṃ tiyagyonigatigāminīṃ pratipadaṃ tiryagyonyupapattiduḥkhaṃ deśayāmi / yamalokaṃ deśayāmi, yamalokagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ yamalokaduḥkhaṃ deśayāmi / svargalokaṃ deśayāmi, svargalokagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ svargalokaratyupacāraparibhogaṃ deśayāmi / manuṣyalokaṃ deśayāmi, manuṣyalokagatigāminīṃ pratipadaṃ manuṣyalokasukhaduḥkhānubhavavaicitryaṃ deśayāmi / iti hi kulaputra lokadharmaṃ deśayāmi / lokasamudayaṃ lokāstaṃgamanaṃ lokādīnavaṃ lokaniḥsaraṇamapi deśayāmi, yaduta bodhisattvamārgasaṃprakāśanatāyai saṃsāradoṣavinivartanatāyai sarvajñatāguṇasaṃdarśanatāyai bhavagatisaṃmohaduḥkhasaṃpraśamanatāyai anāvaraṇadharmatārocanatāyai lokapravṛttikriyāparidīpanatāyai sarvalokapravṛttisukhaduḥkhasūcanatāyai sarvajagatpratiṣṭhāsaṃjñāgatavibhāvanatāyai anālayatathāgatadharmābhidyotanatāyai sarvakarmakleśacakravyāvartanatāyai tathāgatadharmacakrapravartanasūcanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvagāminībodhisattvacaryāviśuddhimukhamavabhāsapratiṣṭhitānabhisaṃskāravimalavyūhaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvābhijñānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakṣetratalamāyāgatajñānaśarīraspharaṇānāṃ samantacakṣurjñānabhūmipratilabdhānāṃ sarvavākpatharutavijñaptiparamaśrotrāṇāṃ tryadhvaspharaṇadharmamukhālokavaśitāprāptānāṃ sarvadharmasamavasaraṇajñānavaśitādhipativīrapuruṣāṇāmacintyāpramāṇayathāśayasattvavijñapanāsaṃbhinnasvaramaṇḍalaprabhūtaruciratanujihvānāṃ
body.translated_text: in all the abodes of <s>Māra</s>, in all the heavenly hosts within the desire-realm, in all heavenly abodes, in all <s>Nāga</s>-worlds and <s>Nāga</s>-abodes, in all <s>Yakṣa</s>-worlds and <s>Yakṣa</s>-abodes, in all <s>Rākṣasa</s>-worlds and <s>Rākṣasa</s>-abodes, in all <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>-worlds and <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>-abodes, in all <s>Preta</s>-worlds and <s>Preta</s>-abodes, in all <s>Gandharva</s>-worlds and <s>Gandharva</s>-abodes, in all <s>Asura</s>-worlds and <s>Asura</s>-abodes, in all <s>Garuḍa</s>-worlds and <s>Garuḍa</s>-abodes, in all <s>Kinnara</s>-worlds and <s>Kinnara</s>-abodes, in all <s>Mahoraga</s>-worlds and <s>Mahoraga</s>-abodes, in all human worlds and human abodes, in all villages, cities, towns, provinces, kingdoms, and royal capitals, in all the destinies of beings within the desire-realm — I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. I reject what is against the <s>Dharma</s>. I pacify disputes. I avert quarrels. I calm conflicts. I prevent wars. I pacify battles. I cease enmity. I sever bonds. I break prisons. I turn back fears. I completely eradicate unwholesome <s>karma</s>-formations. I restrain beings from the killing of living creatures, from taking what is not given, from sexual misconduct, from false speech, from slander, from harsh speech, from idle chatter, from covetousness, from malice, from wrong views. I restrain beings from all [harmful] deeds. I lead them to engage in all <s>dharma</s>-wholesome-<s>dharma</s> activities. I teach all beings all arts. I illumine, arrange, make clear, and make manifest all treatises that benefit the world, for the delight of the world. For the ripening of beings I conform to all [philosophical] schools. For the sake of indicating the special excellence of higher knowledge, for turning back all views, for proclaiming all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, up to and including the <s>Brahma</s>-world I teach the <s>Dharma</s>, surpassing all the gods of the form-realm. And as here in the three-thousand-fold great thousand world-realm, so in the ten directions, in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of ten inexpressible <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. I teach <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. I teach the hells, the path leading to the hells, the causes of hellish beings. I teach the animal realm, the differentiation of animal destinies, the path leading to animal destinies, the suffering of birth in the animal realm. I teach the world of <s>Yama</s>, the path leading to the world of <s>Yama</s>, the suffering of the world of <s>Yama</s>. I teach the heavenly world, the path leading to the heavenly world, the delight, enjoyment, and use of the heavenly world. I teach the human world, the path leading to the human destiny, the diversity of experience of happiness and suffering in the human world. Thus, son of good family, I teach the worldly <s>dharma</s>. I also teach the arising of the world, the cessation of the world, the danger of the world, and the escape from the world — namely, for the illumination of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path, for turning back the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for displaying the qualities of omniscience, for the pacification of the suffering and delusion of the destinies of existence, for proclaiming the nature of <s>dharma</s> free from obstruction, for illuminating the activity and operations of the world, for indicating the happiness and suffering of the operations of the entire world, for manifesting the conceptions of the establishment of all beings, for illuminating the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dharma</s> that is free from attachment, for turning back the wheel of all <s>karma</s> and afflictions, and for indicating the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. This, son of good family, is the gate of purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct that goes everywhere, the stainless array of illumination established in the absence of fabrication, that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattva</s>s who possess all superknowledges, whose knowledge-bodies of illusion-like nature pervade the surfaces of all fields, who have attained the ground of the universal eye of knowledge, whose ears are supreme in the cognition of all utterances of spoken words, who have attained the mastery of the light of the gate of <s>dharma</s> pervading the three times, who are heroes and lords of the mastery of the knowledge of the convergence of all <s>dharma</s>s, whose subtle tongues produce the beautiful sphere of voice indistinguishably informing beings according to their dispositions in inconceivable and immeasurable ways

body.text:
nānābhiprāyasattvasamudraruciravarṇasaṃsthānasarvabodhisattvasamamāyopamaśarīrāṇāṃ
sarvatathāgatādvayākalpācintyaśarīraparamāṇāṃ sarvatryadhvānusṛtajñānakāyānāṃ gaganatalavipulāpramāṇagocaraviṣayāṇāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: whose bodies are like illusions, equal to all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, of beautiful color and form resembling the ocean of beings of various dispositions, whose bodies are supreme in the inconceivable non-dual nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, whose knowledge-bodies follow all three times, whose range and domain are as vast and immeasurable as the surface of space — to know their conduct or speak of their qualities? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe śroṇāparānteṣu janapadeṣu kaliṅgavanaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra siṃhavijṛmbhitā nāma bhikṣuṇī prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family — here in the southern region, in the province of <s>Śroṇāparānta</s>, there is a city named <s>Kaliṅgavana</s>. There dwells a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) named <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>. Approach her and ask — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice? //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako jayottamasya śreṣṭhinaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya jayottamaṃ śreṣṭhinamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya jayottamasya śreṣṭhino 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 24 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the merchant <s>Jayottama</s>, circumambulated the merchant <s>Jayottama</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, looked back at him again and again, and departed from the presence of the merchant <s>Jayottama</s>. //

body.text: 27 Siṃhavijṛmbhitā /
body.translated_text: 27 <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa yena śroṇāparānte janapade kaliṅgavanaṃ nāma nagaram, tenopajagāma / upetya siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ nāma bhikṣuṇīṃ paryeṣamāṇaḥ pratisattvaṃ paripṛcchan yato yataḥ paryaṭati, tena tenaiva anekāni kumāraśatāni anekāni kumārikāśatāni rathyācatvaraśṛṅgāṭakebhyaḥ saṃbhūya anubadhnanti sma / anekāni ca puruṣaśatāni anekāni ca strīśatānyarocayāmāsuḥ - eṣā kulaputra siṃhavijṛmbhitā bhikṣuṇī ihaiva kaliṅgavane nagare jayaprabhānupradatte sūryaprabhe mahodyāne prativasati aparimāṇānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya dharmaṃ prakāśayamānā //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, proceeded gradually to the city named <s>Kaliṅgavana</s> in the province of <s>Śroṇāparānta</s>. Having arrived, searching for the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, asking each person, wherever he went, many hundreds of boys and many hundreds of girls would gather from the roads, squares, and crossroads and follow him. And many hundreds of men and many hundreds of women told him: 'This <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, son of good family, dwells here in the city of <s>Kaliṅgavana</s>, in the great garden called <s>Sūryaprabha</s>, granted by <s>Jayaprabha</s>, illuminating the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of immeasurable beings.' //

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena tatsūryaprabhaṃ mahodyānaṃ tenopasaṃkramya samantādanuvicaran anuvilokayan adrākṣīttasmin mahodyāne candrodgatān nāma vṛkṣān kūṭāgārasaṃchannānarcirvarṇārcirnirbhāsān samantādyojanamābhayā spharamāṇān, saṃpracchadanāmāṃśca patravṛkṣān chatrākārān saṃsthānaparṇacchadanān nīlavaidūryavarṇapayodāvabhāsān, kusumakośanāmāṃśca puṣpavṛkṣān himavatparvatarājaramaṇīyavicitrasaṃsthānān nānāvarṇākṣayakusumaughapravarṣaṇān tridaśapuropaśobhanapārijātakakovidārasadṛśān, sadāpakvānanupamasvāduphalanicitanāmāṃśca suphalavṛkṣān suvarṇameruśikharasaṃsthānān sadāphalasaṃpannān, vairocanakośanāmnaśca maṇirājavṛkṣānanupamamaṇiratnarājasaṃsthānān divyaratnasragmālābharaṇacintārājamaṇiratnapramuktakośasamṛddhidharān asaṃkhyeyavarṇamaṇiratnākārān, prasādananāmāṃśca vastravṛkṣān nānāvarṇadivyaratnavastrakośapramuktapralambopaśobhitān, pramodananāmnaśca vādyavṛkṣān divyātirekatūryamanojñamadhuranirghoṣān, samantaśubhavyūhanāmnaśca gandhavṛkṣān sarvadigapratihatasarvākāramanojñagandhābhipramodanānadrākṣīt / utsasarastaḍāgapuṣkiriṇīśca saptaratneṣṭakānicitāścaturdikṣu vibhaktaratnasopānāḥ kālānusāricandanaparidigdhavividharatnavedikāparivṛtāḥ, nīlavaidūryamaṇirājakṛtatalasaṃsthānāḥ, jāmbūnadakanakavālikāstīrṇatalāḥ, manojñadivyagandhāṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇāḥ, vicitravarṇadivyagandhasparśaratnotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchāditasalilāḥ, divyātirekamanojñarūpanānāśakunigaṇamadhuranirghoṣanikūjitāḥ, vividhadivyaratnasuruciradrumapaṅkiparikṣepopaśobhitāḥ / sarveṣu ca teṣu nānāratnavṛkṣamūleṣu vicitramanojñarūpāṇi ratnasiṃhāsanāni prajñaptāni acintyānekavividharatnavyūhāni, nānādivyaratnavastraprajñaptopacārāṇi, sarvākāradivyagandhadhūpanirdhūpitāni, divyātikrāntaratnapaṭṭābhipralambitavicitraratnavitānavitatāni, nānāratnavicitrajāmbūnadakanakajālasaṃchannāni, ratnakiṅkiṇījālamanojñamadhuranirghoṣāṇi,
anekadivyaratnāsanaśatasahasraparivārāṇyapaśyat / sa kvacidratnavṛkṣamūle ratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptamapaśyat / kvacidgandharājamaṇiratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvacinnāgavyūhamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvacidratnasiṃhaskandhamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvacidvairocanamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvaciddigvirocanamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam,
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, approached that great garden called <s>Sūryaprabha</s>, and wandering and looking around on all sides, he saw in that great garden trees called <s>Candrodgata</s> (Moon-risen) — covered with mansions, blazing with flames of light, radiating splendor for a <s>yojana</s> all around. And canopy-trees called <s>Saṃpracchada</s> — parasol-shaped with leaf-canopies of foliage, with the appearance of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-colored rain-clouds. And flower-trees called <s>Kusumakośa</s> — of beautiful and various forms like <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, raining forth torrents of imperishable flowers of various colors, resembling the <s>Pārijātaka</s> and <s>Kovidāra</s> trees adorning the city of the thirty [gods]. And fruit-trees called <s>Sadāpakva</s> (Ever-ripe) — of the form of the golden peak of <s>Meru</s>, always laden with fruit of incomparable sweetness. And gem-king-trees called <s>Vairocanakośa</s> — of the form of incomparable gem-jewel-kings, bearing the abundance of treasuries releasing divine gem-garland-ornaments and wish-fulfilling king-gem-jewels, of innumerable colors and gem-jewel forms. And garment-trees called <s>Prasādana</s> — adorned with hanging treasuries of various-colored divine gem-garments. And music-trees called <s>Pramodana</s> — producing surpassingly divine charming sweet sounds. And fragrance-trees called <s>Samantaśubhavyūha</s> — gladdening all directions with unobstructed fragrance of every kind. He saw springs, lakes, ponds, and pools — piled with bricks of the seven gems, with gem-stairs apportioned in the four directions, surrounded by various gem-railings anointed with <s>kālānusāri</s> sandalwood, their floors made of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem-kings, their surfaces strewn with <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold sand, filled with water endowed with the eight qualities of charming divine fragrance, their waters covered with <s>utpala</s>s, lotuses, <s>kumuda</s>s, and <s>puṇḍarīka</s>s of variegated colors and divine fragrance and touch, resounding with the sweet cries of flocks of birds surpassingly divine in form, beautified by encircling rows of various divine gem-trees of fine beauty. At the roots of all those various gem-trees, he saw beautiful charming gem lion-thrones arranged — of inconceivable manifold various gem-arrays, with preparations of various divine gem-garments, perfumed with all kinds of divine fragrant incense, canopied with surpassingly divine gem-sheet hangings of variegated gem-canopies, covered with nets of various gem-adorned <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, sounding sweetly with charming gem-bell nets, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of divine gem-seats. In some places at the roots of gem-trees he saw a lion-throne of gem-lotus-womb; in some, a lion-throne of fragrance-king-gem-jewel-lotus-womb; in some, a lion-throne of <s>Nāga</s>-array-king-gem-lotus-womb; in some, a lion-throne of gem-lion-shoulder-king-gem-lotus-womb; in some, a lion-throne of <s>Vairocana</s>-king-gem-lotus-womb; in some, a lion-throne of direction-illuminating-king-gem-lotus-womb

body.text:
kvacidindravajramaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvacijjagadrocanamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanam, kvacidratnavṛkṣamūle sitābhamaṇirājapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptamapaśyat / sarvāvacca tanmahodyānaṃ nānāratnākīrṇatalaṃ mahāsāgaramiva ratnadvīpākīrṇamapaśyat nīlavaiḍūryarājakhacitasarvaratnapratyarpitakācilindikasukhasaṃsparśabhūmibhāgaṃ caraṇanikṣepotkṣeponnāmāvanāmavigataṃ vajraratnarājamayasukhasaṃsparśamanojñagandhanalinasaṃstīrṇatalaṃ haṃsakrauñcamayūrakuṇālakalaviṅkakokilajīvaṃjīvakarutanirnādamadhuranirghoṣaṃ divyaratnacandanadrumavanasuracitapraviṣṭavyūhopaśobhitaṃ vicitraratnapuṣpamegharatnakusumākṣayadhārābhipravarṣitaṃ miśrakāvanaprativiśiṣṭaṃ suracitanānāratnakūṭāgārātulagandharājasatatapradhūpitopacāraṃ sudharmadevasabhāprativiśiṣṭavyūhaṃ upariṣṭāddivyātirekavicitraratnajālasaṃchannaṃ muktāmaṇipuṣpahārakalāpapralambitopaśobhitadeśaṃ samantādratnakiṅkiṇīvicitravinyāsojjvalitasuvarṇajālapariṣkṛtaṃ vividhavādyavṛkṣaratnatālakiṅkiṇījālamārutasamīritamadhuramanojñaśabdanirghoṣaṃ vaśavartidevarājapramukhāpsaraḥsaṃgītirutaparamaramaṇīyanirghoṣaṃ vicitravarṇadivyakalpadūṣyameghābhipravarṣaṇavirājitaṃ mahāsāgaramivānantavarṇāvabhāsamasecanakadarśanamacintyāsaṃkhyeyaratnavyūhakūṭāgāraśatasahasrapratimaṇḍitaṃ tridaśendrapuramiva sudarśanaṃ sarvākāranānāratnabhaktipratimaṇḍitaṃ supariṇatacchatravinyāsasamantaśubhadarśanaṃ mahendralokamiva citrakūṭopaśobhitaṃ sadāpramuktamanojñamahāprabhāvabhāsaṃ jagadrocanamaṇiratnarājaprabhājvalitamiva
mahābrahmavihāramasaṃkhyeyalokadhātvadhiṣṭhānākāśakośavipulāpramāṇāvakāśaṃ tatsūryaprabhaṃ mahodyānamapaśyat siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyā mahatā acintyarddhiprabhāvabalādhānena //
body.translated_text: In some places he saw an <s>Indravajramaṇirājapadmagarbha</s> (Indra-Vajra Jewel-King Lotus-Womb) lion-throne, in some places a <s>Jagadrocanamaṇirājapadmagarbha</s> (World-Illuminating Jewel-King Lotus-Womb) lion-throne, and in some places, at the foot of jewel-trees, a <s>Sitābhamaṇirājapadmagarbha</s> (White-Lustre Jewel-King Lotus-Womb) lion-throne set in place. And he saw that entire great garden with its ground strewn with various jewels, like a great ocean scattered with jewel-islands — its ground-surface inlaid with blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) king-gems and set with all manner of precious stones forming smooth crystal tiles pleasant to touch, yielding neither to the stepping down nor lifting up nor bending nor straightening of the feet; its floor spread with lotuses of delightful fragrance made of the king of <s>vajra</s> (diamond) gems, pleasant to touch; resounding with the sweet cries of geese, herons, peacocks, <s>kuṇāla</s> birds, <s>kalaviṅka</s> sparrows, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds; adorned with beautifully arranged groves of divine jewel-and-sandalwood trees entering into elaborate configurations; rained upon by clouds of variegated jewel-flowers showering inexhaustible streams of gem-blossoms, surpassing the <s>Miśrakāvana</s> grove; its precincts perpetually perfumed by incomparable king-of-fragrances from beautifully fashioned pavilions of various jewels; its array surpassing the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly-hall of the gods; covered above with canopies of extraordinary and variegated divine jewel-nets; its spaces adorned with hanging garlands and clusters of pearl-gem flowers; adorned on all sides with golden nets blazing with variously arranged jewel-bells; resounding with sweet and delightful sounds from jewel cymbals and bell-nets on musical trees stirred by the wind; resounding with supremely enchanting songs led by <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) headed by <s>Vaśavartī</s>, king of the gods; made radiant by showers of clouds of divine <s>kalpa</s>-silks of variegated colors; a sight as inexhaustible as a great ocean with its infinite play of colors, adorned with hundreds of thousands of pavilions of inconceivable and innumerable jewel-arrays; beautiful to behold like the city of <s>Tridaśendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), adorned with decorative patterns of all varieties of jewels; lovely in every direction with the arrangement of well-formed parasols, like the world of <s>Mahendra</s> adorned with <s>Citrakūṭa</s> peak; perpetually emitting a splendid radiance of delightful great power, as if blazing with the light of the <s>Jagadrocanamaṇiratnarāja</s> (World-Illuminating Jewel-King); vast as the abode of <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, with immeasurable space like a treasury of the sky sustaining innumerable world-realms. He saw that great garden, radiant as the sun, manifested through the great and inconceivable power of miraculous might of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ imānevamapramāṇācintyaguṇasamuditān mahodyānavyūhān bodhisattvakarmavipākapariniṣpannān lokottaravipulakuśalamūlanirjātānacintyabuddhapūjopasthānaniṣyandasaṃbhavān sarvalokagatānavaśeṣakuśalamūlāsaṃhāryān māyāgatadharmasvabhāvanirvṛttān vimalavipulaśubhapuṇyavipākasaṃbhūtān siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrvasukṛtasucaritaniṣyandabalādhānasaṃbhūtānasādhāraṇān saśrāvakapratyekabuddhairasaṃhāryān sarvatīrthyaparapravādibhiranavamardyān sarvamārapathasamudācārairanavalokyān sarvabālapṛthagjanaiḥ samantādanuvilokayannadrākṣīt / sarveṣu ca teṣu nānāratnavṛkṣamūlagateṣu mahāsiṃhāsaneṣu siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ saṃniṣaṇṇāṃ mahāparivāraparivṛtāṃ prāsādikenātmabhāvena praśānteryāpathāṃ śāntendriyāṃ śāntamanasaṃ suguptāṃ jitendriyāṃ nāgamiva sudāntāṃ hradamiva acchānāvilaviprasannacittāṃ cintāmaṇirājamiva sarvakāmapradāṃ padmamiva vāriṇānupaliptāṃ lokadharmaiḥ, siṃha iva vigatabhayaromaharṣāṃ vaiśāradyaviśuddhyā, mahācalendrarājamivāprakampāṃ śīlaviśuddhyā, manoharagandharājamiva jagaccittaprahlādanakarīṃ himacandanamiva kleśaparidāhapraśamanakarīṃ sudarśanabhaiṣajyarājamiva sarvajagadduḥkhavyupaśamanakarīṃ varuṇapāśamivāmoghadarśanāṃ tathāgataprabhāmiva kāyacittaprasrabdhisukhasaṃjananīṃ mahābrahmāṇamiva vigatarāgadoṣamohaparyutthānām udakaprasādakamaṇiratnarājamiva kleśāvilasattvacittaprahlādanakarīṃ sukṣetramiva kuśalamūlavivardhanīm / teṣu cāsanaparivāreṣu vicitrāṃ parṣadaṃ saṃniṣaṇṇāmadrākṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, gazing all around, beheld these arrays of the great garden endowed with immeasurable and inconceivable virtues — produced as the fruition of <s>bodhisattva</s> deeds, born from vast and world-transcending roots of merit, arisen from the overflow of inconceivable worship and service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, not to be appropriated by the residual merit of all worldly beings, established in the nature of <s>dharmas</s> that are like illusions, born from the ripening of stainless, vast, and auspicious merit — the uncommon attainments born from the power of the overflow of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>'s former wholesome and virtuous deeds, not to be undone even by <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), not to be crushed by all the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) and proponents of other doctrines, not to be perceived by the conduct of all <s>Māra</s>-paths, and not visible to all foolish ordinary beings who looked at them from every direction. And upon all those great lion-thrones situated at the feet of various jewel-trees, he beheld the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> seated, surrounded by a great retinue, with an inspiring physical form, of tranquil deportment, with senses calmed, with mind at peace, well-guarded, with senses mastered, well-tamed like an elephant, with a mind clear, pure, and unsullied like a lake, granting all wishes like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) king, unstained by worldly conditions like a lotus by water, free from the bristling of fear like a lion through the purity of her fearlessness, unshakeable like the great king of mountains through the purity of her moral conduct, gladdening the minds of the world like a delightful king-of-fragrances, cooling the burning of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) like Himalayan sandalwood, alleviating the suffering of all beings like the <s>Sudarśana</s> (Fair-to-See) king of medicines, unerring in her gaze like the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>, generating the bliss of bodily and mental tranquility like the radiance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, free from the arising of passion, hatred, and delusion like <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, gladdening the minds of beings muddied by <s>kleśas</s> like the water-clarifying jewel-king, and nurturing roots of merit like a fertile field. And among those surrounding seats, he beheld a varied assembly seated.

body.text:
sa kvacidāsanaparivāre maheśvaradevaputrapramukhānāṃ śuddhāvāsakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmakṣayavimokṣasaṃbhedaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ prakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre rucirabrahmapramukhānāṃ brahmakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ samantatalabhedaṃ nāma svaramaṇḍalaviśuddhiṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre vaśavartidevarājapramukhānāṃ paranirmitavaśavartidevarājapramukhānāṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ bodhisattvāśayaviśuddhivaśitāvyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre sunirmitadevarājapramukhānāṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ sarvadharmaśubhavyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre saṃtuṣitadevarājapramukhānāṃ tuṣitakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ svacittakośāvartaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre suyāmadevarājapramukhānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmanantavyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre śakradevarājapramukhānāṃ trāyastriṃśakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmudvegamukhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre sāgaranāgarājapramukhānāṃ śataraśminandopanandamanasyairāvatānavataptaprabhṛtīnāṃ nāgarājñāṃ sanāgakanyānāṃ nāgakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ buddhaviṣayaprabhāvyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre vaiśravaṇamahārājapramukhānāṃ yakṣendrāṇāṃ sayakṣakanyāyakṣakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ jagatparitrāṇakośaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre dhṛtarāṣṭragandharvarājapramukhānāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ sagandharvakanyāgandharvakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmakṣayapraharṣaṇaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre rāhvasurendrapramukhānāmasurendrāṇāṃ sāsurakanyāsurakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ dharmadhātujñānayavegavyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre mahāvegadhārigaruḍendrapramukhānāṃ garuḍendrāṇāṃ sagaruḍakanyāgarūḍakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ bhavasāgarasaṃtrāsaviṣayaṃ
nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre drumakinnararājapramukhānāṃ kinnarendrāṇāṃ sakinnarakanyākinnarakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ buddhacaryāvabhāsaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre bhṛkuṭīmukhamahoragendrapramukhānāṃ mahoragendrāṇāṃ samahoragakanyāmahoragakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ buddhaprītisaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre 'nekeṣāṃ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāśatasahasrāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: In one seat-assembly, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding to the divine sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) gods, headed by <s>Maheśvara</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> (dharma-gate) called '<s>Akṣayavimokṣasaṃbheda</s>' (Inexhaustible Liberation Analysis). In another seat-assembly, he saw her revealing to the divine sons of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, headed by <s>Rucirabrahmā</s>, a purification of the sphere of vocal tones called '<s>Samantatalabheda</s>' (Universal Ground Analysis). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the divine sons of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (Those Who Control Others' Emanations) gods, together with divine maidens and retinues, headed by <s>Vaśavartī</s> king of the gods, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Bodhisattvāśayaviśuddhivaśitāvyūha</s>' (Array of Mastery through Purification of Bodhisattva Intention). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the divine sons of the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> (Delighting in Emanation) gods, together with divine maidens and retinues, headed by <s>Sunirmita</s> king of the gods, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Sarvadharmaśubhavyūha</s>' (Auspicious Array of All Dharmas). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the divine sons of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, together with divine maidens and retinues, headed by <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> king of the gods, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Svacittakośāvarta</s>' (Whirlpool Treasury of One's Own Mind). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the divine sons headed by <s>Suyāma</s> king of the gods, together with divine maidens and retinues, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Anantavyūha</s>' (Infinite Array). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the divine sons of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, together with divine maidens and retinues, headed by <s>Śakra</s> king of the gods, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Udvegamukha</s>' (Gateway of Urgency). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>nāga</s>-kings — <s>Śataraśmi</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Upananda</s>, <s>Manasvin</s>, <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Anavataptā</s>, and others — together with <s>nāga</s>-maidens and <s>nāga</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Sāgara</s> <s>nāga</s>-king, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Buddhaviṣayaprabhāvyūha</s>' (Array of the Light of the Buddha's Domain). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>yakṣa</s>-lords, together with <s>yakṣa</s>-maidens and <s>yakṣa</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the great king, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Jagatparitrāṇakośa</s>' (Treasury of World Protection). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>gandharvas</s>, together with <s>gandharva</s>-maidens and <s>gandharva</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> king of the <s>gandharvas</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Akṣayapraharṣaṇa</s>' (Inexhaustible Delight). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>asura</s>-lords, together with <s>asura</s>-maidens and <s>asura</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Rāhu</s> lord of the <s>asuras</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Dharmadhātujñānayavegavyūha</s>' (Array of the Swift Force of Knowledge of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>garuḍa</s>-lords, together with <s>garuḍa</s>-maidens and <s>garuḍa</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Mahāvegadhārin</s> lord of the <s>garuḍas</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Bhavasāgarasaṃtrāsaviṣaya</s>' (Domain of Terror at the Ocean of Existence). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>kinnara</s>-lords, together with <s>kinnara</s>-maidens and <s>kinnara</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Druma</s> king of the <s>kinnaras</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Buddhacaryāvabhāsa</s>' (Illumination of the Buddha's Conduct). In another seat-assembly, he saw her expounding to the <s>mahoraga</s>-lords, together with <s>mahoraga</s>-maidens and <s>mahoraga</s>-prince retinues, headed by <s>Bhṛkuṭīmukha</s> lord of the <s>mahoragas</s>, a <s>dharmamukha</s> called '<s>Buddhaprītisaṃbhava</s>' (Arising of Delight in the Buddha). In another seat-assembly, before hundreds of thousands of men, women, boys, and girls

saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ jñānaviśeṣagamanaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre nityaujoharadrumarājarākṣasendrapramukhānāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ sarākṣasakanyārākṣasakumāraparivārāṇāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ kṛpāsaṃbhavaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre śrāvakayānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ jñānaviśeṣaprabhāvaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāpaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre pratyekabuddhayānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmudārabuddhaguṇāvabhāsaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre mahāyānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ samantamukhaṃ nāma samādhijñānālokamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre prathamacittotpādikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ sarvabuddhapraṇidhikūṭaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre dvitīyabhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ virajomaṇḍalaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre tṛtīyabhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ praśāntavyūhaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre caturthībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ sarvajñatāvegaviṣayasaṃbhavaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre pañcamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ cittalatākusumagarbhaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānamapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre
ṣaṣṭhībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ vairocanagarbhaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre saptamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ samantabhūmyalaṃkāraṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre aṣṭamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ dharmadhātupañjarasuvibhaktaśarīraviṣayaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre navamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmanilambhabalanilayavyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre daśamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmanāvaraṇamaṇḍalaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / kvacidāsanaparivāre saṃniṣaṇṇasya vajrapāṇiparṣanmaṇḍalasya siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ jñānavajranārāyaṇavyūhaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāmapaśyat / iti hi yāvatyaḥ sarvopapattyāyatanasaṃbhedeṣu sattvaprajñaptayaḥ sattvagatayaḥ, tāsu ye sattvāḥ paripakvā vainayikā bhājanībhūtāḥ, teṣāṃ tasmin mahodyāne samavasṛtya pratyekamāsanaparivārasaṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ nānāśayānāṃ nānādhimuktānāṃ niyatāśayānāṃ ghanarasaśraddhānāṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ
body.translated_text: seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Jñānaviśeṣagamana</s> (Entering Distinguished Knowledge). In another seat-assembly, to the <s>rākṣasa</s>-lords headed by <s>Nityaujoharadrumarājarākṣasendra</s>, together with their retinues of <s>rākṣasa</s> maidens and <s>rākṣasa</s> youths, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Kṛpāsaṃbhava</s> (Arising of Compassion). In another seat-assembly, to beings inclined toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Jñānaviśeṣaprabhāva</s> (Power of Distinguished Knowledge). In another seat-assembly, to beings inclined toward the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Udārabuddhaguṇāvabhāsa</s> (Illumination of Sublime Buddha-Qualities). In another seat-assembly, to beings inclined toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge-light-gate called <s>Samantamukha</s> (Universal Gateway). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had just generated the first aspiration-mind, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Sarvabuddhapraṇidhikūṭa</s> (Summit of All Buddha-Vows). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the second <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Virajomaṇḍala</s> (Stainless Maṇḍala). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the third <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Praśāntavyūha</s> (Array of Tranquility). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the fourth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Sarvajñatāvegaviṣayasaṃbhava</s> (Arising in the Domain of the Impetus of Omniscience). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the fifth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Cittalatākusumagarbha</s> (Womb of Mind-Creeper Blossoms). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the sixth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Vairocanagarbha</s> (Womb of Vairocana). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Samantabhūmyalaṃkāra</s> (Ornament of All Stages). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Dharmadhātupañjarasuvibhaktaśarīraviṣaya</s> (Domain of the Body Well-Differentiated in the Cage of the Dharmadhātu). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the ninth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Anilambhabalanilayavyūha</s> (Array of the Abode of Ungraspable Power). In another seat-assembly, to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the tenth <s>bhūmi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>samādhi</s>-gate called <s>Anāvaraṇamaṇḍala</s> (Unobstructed Maṇḍala). In another seat-assembly, to the assembly-maṇḍala of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, seated, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> expounding the <s>dharma</s>-gate called <s>Jñānavajranārāyaṇavyūha</s> (Array of the Diamond-Nārāyaṇa of Knowledge). Thus, as many as are the designations and destinies of beings in the divisions of all places of rebirth — among them, those beings who were ripened, disciplinable, and fit vessels, having assembled in that great park, each seated in their respective seat-assembly, of various dispositions and inclinations, of determined aspirations, of dense and mature faith — he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>

body.text:
tathā tathā dharmaṃ deśayamānāmapaśyat, yatsarve niyatā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi tatsiṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ samantacakṣurupekṣāvatīpramukhāni sarvabuddhadharmanirdeśapramukhāni dharmadhātutalaprabhedapramukhāni sarvāvaraṇamaṇḍalavikiraṇapramukhāni sarvajagatkuśalacittasaṃbhavapramukhāni viśeṣavativyūhapramukhāni asaṅganayagarbhapramukhāni dharmadhātumaṇḍalapramukhāni cittakośapramukhāni samantarucitābhinirhāragarbhapramukhāni daśaprajñāpāramitāmukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyavakrāntāni / ye ca tatsūryaprabhaṃ mahodyānaṃ bodhisattvāstadanye vā sattvāḥ praviśanti siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyā darśanāya dharmaśravaṇāya, sarve te siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā
bhikṣuṇyāḥ prathamaṃ kuśalamūladharmasamudāneṣu niyojitā yāvadanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheravivartyāḥ kṛtāḥ //
body.translated_text: teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to each in such a way that all became determined for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). For what reason? Because the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> had entered innumerable hundreds of thousands of the ten <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateways — headed by <s>Samantacakṣūpekṣāvatī</s> (Endowed with Universal-Eye Equanimity), headed by the exposition of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, headed by the penetration of the ground of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, headed by the scattering of all maṇḍalas of obstruction, headed by the arising of wholesome minds in all beings, headed by <s>Viśeṣavatīvyūha</s> (Array Endowed with Distinction), headed by <s>Asaṅganayagarbha</s> (Womb of the Method of Non-Attachment), headed by <s>Dharmadhātumaṇḍala</s> (Maṇḍala of the Dharmadhātu), headed by <s>Cittakośa</s> (Treasury of Mind), headed by <s>Samantarucitābhinirhāragarbha</s> (Womb of Universally Delightful Accomplishment). And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> or other beings who entered the great park called <s>Sūryaprabha</s> (Sunlight) to see the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> and to hear the <s>Dharma</s> — all of them were first engaged by the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> in wholesome-root-<s>dharma</s>-collections, up to being made irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyā imāmevaṃrūpāmudyānasaṃpadaṃ vihārasaṃpadaṃ caṃkramasaṃpadaṃ paribhogasaṃpadaṃ śayyāsanasaṃpadaṃ parṣanmaṇḍalasaṃpadamādhipateyasaṃpadamṛddhivikurvitasaṃpadaṃ sarasvatīvyūhasaṃpadaṃ dṛṣṭvā acintyaṃ ca dharmanayaṃ śrutvā vipuladharmameghābhiṣyanditacittaḥ siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyā abhimukhamāśayaviśuddhisaṃpadaṃ saṃpraṇīto 'nekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkariṣyāmīti / atha siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ sarvaṃ tanmahodyānaṃ saparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhamudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭamavabhāsitam / anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā evaṃ saṃjānāti - pradakṣiṇīkurvaṃśca samantādabhimukhaṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmadrākṣīt / sa purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārye, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having seen this kind of park-attainment, dwelling-attainment, walkway-attainment, enjoyment-attainment, bedding-and-seat-attainment, assembly-maṇḍala-attainment, sovereignty-attainment, supernatural-display-attainment, and eloquence-array-attainment of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, and having heard that inconceivable <s>dharma</s>-method, his mind moistened by vast <s>Dharma</s>-clouds, drawn toward the attainment of purity of aspiration face-to-face with the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, [he thought:] 'I shall circumambulate her many hundreds of thousands of times.' Then, from the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, that entire great park together with its assembly-maṇḍala-array was illuminated by a magnificent radiance. Having circumambulated many hundreds of thousands of times, he perceived thus — while circumambulating, he saw the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s> facing him from all directions. Standing before her with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how he should practice. And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and exhortation to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the noble one tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should he practice?' //

body.text: sā avocat - ahaṃ kulaputra sarvamanyanāsamuddhātitasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / āha - ka etasya ārye sarvamanyanāsamuddhātitasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ? āha - eṣa kulaputra tryadhvagatavyūhaikacittakṣaṇakoṭivijñaptisvabhāvo jñānālokaḥ / āha - ka etasya ārye jñānālokasya viṣayaḥ? āha - etanmama kulaputra jñānālokamukhamāyūhatyā niryūhatyāḥ sarvadharmopapanno nāma samādhirājāyate, yasya samādheḥ sahapratilābhena manomayaiḥ kāyaiḥ sarvāsu daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣvekajātipratibaddhānāṃ tuṣitabhavanagatānāṃ sarvabodhisattvānāmekaikasya bodhisattvasya anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥ samairātmabhāvairanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamābhiḥ pūjāvimātrābhiḥ pūjāprayogāyopasaṃkramāmi, yaduta devaindrakāyairnāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyendrakāyaiḥ puṣpameghaparigṛhītairgandhameghaparigṛhītairdhūpameghaparigṛhītairmālyameghaparigṛhītairvilepanameghaparigṛhītaiścūrṇameghaparigṛhītairvastrameghaparigṛhītaiśchatrameghaparigṛhītairdhvajameghaparigṛhītaiḥ patākāmeghaparigṛhītai ratnābharaṇameghaparigṛhītai ratnajālavyūhameghaparigṛhītai ratnavitānavyūhameghaparigṛhītai ratnapradīpavyūhameghaparigṛhītai ratnāsanavyūhameghaparigṛhītaiḥ pūjāprayogāya
body.translated_text: She replied: 'I, son of good family, am one who has attained the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Sarvamanyanāsamuddhātita</s> (Transcending All Wrong Conceptualization). He asked: 'What is the domain of this <s>Sarvamanyanāsamuddhātita bodhisattva</s>-liberation, noble one?' She replied: 'This, son of good family, is the light of knowledge whose nature is the manifestation of <s>koṭi</s>s of single-mind-moments of the array of the three times.' He asked: 'What is the domain of this light of knowledge, noble one?' She replied: 'This light-of-knowledge gateway of mine, son of good family, when drawn forth and extended, gives rise to the <s>samādhi</s>-king called <s>Sarvadharmopapanna</s> (Endowed with All Dharmas). Upon attaining this <s>samādhi</s>, with mind-made bodies in all ten directions, in all world-realms, I approach each and every <s>bodhisattva</s> bound to their last birth dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven — approaching each one with bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, with worship-offerings equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields — for the purpose of worship and service. That is to say, with bodies of <s>deva</s>-lords, <s>nāga</s>-, <s>yakṣa</s>-, <s>gandharva</s>-, <s>asura</s>-, <s>garuḍa</s>-, <s>kinnara</s>-, <s>mahoraga</s>-, human, and non-human lords, bearing clouds of flowers, clouds of fragrances, clouds of incense, clouds of garlands, clouds of unguents, clouds of powders, clouds of garments, clouds of parasols, clouds of banners, clouds of pennants, clouds of gem-ornaments, clouds of gem-net-arrays, clouds of gem-canopy-arrays, clouds of gem-lamp-arrays, clouds of gem-seat-arrays — for the purpose of worship and service

body.text:
upasaṃkramāmi / yathā tuṣitabhavanagatānāmekajātipratibaddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pūjāprayogāyopasaṃkramāmi, evaṃ kukṣigatānāṃ jāyamānānāmantaḥpuramadhyagatānāmabhiniṣkramatāṃ bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkramatāṃ bodhimaṇḍavaragatānāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvadharmacakraṃpravartayatāmevaṃ devabhavanagatānāṃ nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyabhavanagatānāṃ yāvatsarvajagaccittāśayān saṃtoṣayitvā parinirvāyamāṇāmevaṃrūpairmanomayairātmabhāvairevaṃrūpāṃ pūjāṃ kurvāṇānāṃ sarvatathāgatānāmupasaṃkramāmi / ye ca sattvā mamedaṃ buddhapūjopasthānakarma prajānanti, te sarve niyatā bhavanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye ca sattvā māmupasaṃkrāmanti, teṣāmahaṃ sarveṣāmetāmeva prajñāpāramitāvavādānuśāsanīṃ dadāmi / ahaṃ kulaputra jñānacakṣuṣā sarvasattvān paśyāmi / na ca sattvasaṃjñāmutpādayāmi, na manye / sarvajaganmantrasaṃjñāmudrāṃ śṛṇomi, na ca manye sarvavākpathānabhiniviṣṭatvāt / sarvatathāgatān paśyāmi, na ca manye dharmaśarīraparijñānatvāt / sarvatathāgatadharmacakrāṇi ca saṃghārayāmi, na ca manye dharmasvabhāvānubuddhatvāt / praticittakṣaṇaṃ
sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharāmi, na ca manye māyāgatadharmatāvabuddhatvāt / etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvamanyanāsamuddhātitaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmanantamadhyadharmadhātvavatīrṇānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, ye te sarvadharmamanyanāvihāriṇaśca ekaparyaṅkena ca sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti / ye te svakāyāntargatāni sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi saṃdarśayanti, ekakṣaṇena ca sarvatathāgatānupasaṃkrāmanti / yeṣāmātmabhāve sarvabuddhavikurvitāni pravartante / ye ekaromnā bahvanabhilāpyānabhilāpyāni buddhakṣetrāṇyabhūtkṣipanti / ye te svaromavivare 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyalokadhātusaṃvartavivartakalpānādarśayanti / ye ekakṣaṇenānabhilāpyānabhilāpyakalpasaṃvāsasamatāṃ samavasaranti / ye ekakṣaṇena anabhilāpyānabhilāpyān kalpān saṃsaranti /
body.translated_text: I approach them. Just as I approach <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound to their last birth dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven for the purpose of worship and service, so too do I approach those in the womb, those being born, those in the inner palace, those going forth, those approaching the seat of awakening, those seated at the excellent seat of awakening, those who have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> — likewise those dwelling in <s>deva</s>-abodes, <s>nāga</s>-, <s>yakṣa</s>-, <s>gandharva</s>-, <s>asura</s>-, <s>garuḍa</s>-, <s>kinnara</s>-, <s>mahoraga</s>-, human, and non-human abodes — up to those who, having satisfied the minds and dispositions of all beings, are entering <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — I approach all such <s>Tathāgatas</s> with such mind-made bodies, performing such worship. And those beings who know of my practice of <s>Buddha</s>-worship and attendance — they all become determined for unsurpassed perfect awakening. And those beings who approach me — to all of them I give this very instruction and exhortation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). I, son of good family, see all beings with the eye of knowledge, yet I do not generate the perception of 'being,' nor do I conceptualize. I hear the <s>mantra</s>-seal-signs of all the world, yet I do not conceptualize, because I do not fixate on any path of speech. I see all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, yet I do not conceptualize, because of the thorough understanding of the <s>Dharma</s>-body. I gather together the <s>Dharmacakras</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, yet I do not conceptualize, because of awakening to the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>. In each mind-moment I pervade the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, yet I do not conceptualize, because of awakening to the illusion-like nature of reality. This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Sarvamanyanāsamuddhātita</s> (Transcending All Wrong Conceptualization) that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who dwell without conceptualization of any <s>dharma</s> in the boundless, middleway-less <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and who with a single cross-legged posture pervade the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>? Who display within their own bodies all <s>Buddha</s>-fields? Who in a single instant approach all <s>Tathāgatas</s>? In whose bodies all <s>Buddha</s>-transformations proceed? Who with a single hair-pore cast away many inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields? Who in the opening of their hair-pores display inexpressibly inexpressible world-realm formation-and-dissolution <s>kalpas</s>? Who in a single instant enter into the equality of dwelling through inexpressibly inexpressible <s>kalpas</s>? Who in a single instant wander through <s>saṃsāra</s> for inexpressibly inexpressible <s>kalpas</s>? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe durge janapade ratnavyūhaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra vasumitrā nāma bhāgavatī prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, noble son, right here in the southern region, in the land of <s>Durga</s>, there is a city called <s>Ratnavyūha</s> (Array of Jewels). There dwells a <s>bhāgavatī</s> (holy woman) named <s>Vasumitrā</s>. Approach her and ask: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, and how should one proceed?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya siṃhavijṛmbhitāṃ bhikṣuṇīmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya siṃhavijṛmbhitāyā bhikṣuṇyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 25 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>, circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, and departed from the presence of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitā</s>. [25]

body.text: 28 Vasumitrā /
body.translated_text: [Chapter 28: <s>Vasumitrā</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastayā mahāprajñāvidyutāvabhāsitacittaḥ, taṃ sarvajñajñānālokaṃ nidhyāyan, taṃ dharmatāsvabhāvabalāvabhāsaṃ samanupaśyamānaḥ, sarvasattvarutavijñaptikośaṃ dhāraṇīnayaṃ dṛḍhīkurvan, taṃ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasaṃdhāraṇaṃ dhāraṇīnayaṃ vipulīkurvan, taṃ sarvajagaccharaṇaṃ mahākaruṇābalamupastambhayan, taṃ sarvadharmanayālokamukhasamutthānaṃ sarvajñatāvegaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ, tāṃ vipuladharmadhātumaṇḍalaspharaṇapraṇidhipariśuddhimanuvartamānaḥ, taṃ sarvadharmadigavabhāsajñānālokamuttāpayamānaḥ, tatsarvadharmadaśadiglokadhātuvyūhaspharaṇamabhijñānabalaṃ nirharan, taṃ sarvabodhisattvakarmasmṛtyupādānārambhanistīraṇapraṇidhiṃ paripūrayan anupūrveṇa yena durge janapade ratnavyūhaṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrānto vasumitrāṃ bhāgavatīṃ parimārgan / tatra ye puruṣā vasumitrāyā bhāgavatyā guṇānabhijñā jñānagocarāvidhijñāśca, teṣāmetadabhavat - kimasya evaṃ śāntadāntendriyasya evaṃ saṃprajānasya evamabhrāntasya evamavikṣiptamānasasya evaṃ yugamātraprekṣiṇaḥ evaṃ vedanābhiraparyādattacittasya evamanimittagrāhiṇaḥ sarvarūpagateṣu utkṣiptacakṣuṣaḥ evamavyagramānasasya gambhīraceṣṭasyābhirūpasya sāgarakalpasya akṣobhyānabalīnacittasya vasumitrayā bhāgavatyā kāryam? na hīdṛśā rāgaratā bhavanti, na viparyastacittāḥ / nedṛśānāmaśubhasaṃjñā samudācarati / nedṛśāḥ kāmadāsā bhavanti / nedṛśāḥ strīvaśagā bhavanti / nedṛśā māragocare caranti / nedṛśā māraviṣayaṃ niṣevante / nedṛśāḥ kāmapaṅke saṃsīdanti / nedṛśā mārapāśairbadhyante / nākāryakāriṇo bhavanti / ye punarvasumitrāyā bhāgavatyā guṇaviśeṣābhijñā jñānagocarapratyakṣā vā, te evamāhuḥ - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, sulabdhāste lābhāḥ, yastvaṃ vasumitrāṃ bhāgavatīṃ paripraṣṭavyāṃ manyase / niyamena tvaṃ buddhatvaṃ prārthayase / niyamena tvaṃ sarvasattvapratiśaraṇamātmānaṃ kartukāmaḥ / niyamena tvaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ rāgaśalyamuddhartukāmaḥ / niyamena tvaṃ śubhasaṃjñāṃ vikaritukāmaḥ / eṣā kulaputra vasumitrā bhāgavatī nagaraśṛṅgāṭakasyottareṇa svagṛhe tiṣṭhati //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, his mind illuminated by the lightning flash of her great <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), contemplating that light of omniscient knowledge, beholding that radiance of the power of the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), strengthening the <s>dhāraṇī</s> method that is the treasury of comprehension of the speech of all beings, expanding the <s>dhāraṇī</s> method that upholds the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of the Dharma) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, sustaining the power of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) that is the refuge of all the world, examining that momentum toward omniscience arising from the gateway of illumination of all approaches to the <s>Dharma</s>, following that purification of the <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow) that pervades the vast maṇḍala of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), intensifying that light of knowledge that illuminates all directions of the <s>Dharma</s>, bringing forth that power of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) that pervades the ornamental arrays of world-realms in all ten directions of the <s>Dharma</s>, and fulfilling the <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow) that undertakes, sustains, initiates, and completes the recollection of the deeds of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — he gradually approached the city of <s>Ratnavyūha</s> in the land of <s>Durga</s>, searching for the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>. There, those men who were acquainted with the virtues of the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s> and who knew the scope of her knowledge, thought thus: what business could one so serene, with tamed faculties, so clearly comprehending, so unconfused, with undistracted mind, gazing only a yoke's length ahead, whose mind is not overwhelmed by feelings, who grasps no outward signs, whose eyes are uplifted beyond all forms, whose mind is unagitated, whose conduct is profound, who is handsome, who is like the ocean, whose mind is unshakable and unwavering — what business could such a one have with the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>? For such persons are not those who delight in passion, nor are they of perverted mind. Impure perception does not arise in such persons. Such persons are not slaves of desire. Such persons are not subject to women's power. Such persons do not move in <s>Māra</s>'s domain. Such persons do not resort to <s>Māra</s>'s territory. Such persons do not sink in the mire of sensual desire. Such persons are not bound by <s>Māra</s>'s snares. They do not perform improper deeds. But those who knew the special virtues of the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s> and who had direct knowledge of the scope of her wisdom, they said: Excellent, excellent, noble son! Your gains are well obtained, that you think to question the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>. Surely you aspire to Buddhahood. Surely you wish to make yourself a refuge for all beings. Surely you wish to extract the thorn of passion from all beings. Surely you wish to dispel the perception of the attractive. This <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>, noble son, dwells in her own home to the north of the city crossroads.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidāraka idaṃ vacanamupaśrutya tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto yena vasumitrāyā bhāgavatyā niveśanam, tenopasaṃkramya tadgṛhamadrākṣīdvipulaṃ ca vistīrṇaṃ ca daśaratnaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ daśaratnatālapaṅktiparivṛttam / daśabhiḥ parikhābhirgandhodakābhirdivyaratnotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchāditasalilābhiḥ aṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇābhiḥ kanakavālikāsaṃstīrṇatalābhiḥ manoharagandhalulitasugandhīkṛtodakābhiḥ anekaratnaprākāropaśobhitābhiḥ samantādanuparikṣiptam, sarvaratnamayabhavanavimānakūṭāgārasuvibhaktodviddhaniryūhatoraṇagavākṣajālārdhacandrasiṃhapañjaravicitrajyotirdhvajamaṇiratnojjvalitatejasam, asaṃkhyeyavividharatnaprākāropaśobhitaṃ vaiḍūryakhacitaratnahārasaṃskṛtatalaṃ sarvadivyasubhagandhavāsitopacāraṃ mahākālāgarudhūpadhūpitasugandhaṃ sarvānulepanaviliptopacāraṃ sarvaratnakhoṭakaracitaprākāraṃ vividharatnapratyarpitajāmbūnadajālasaṃchāditakūṭaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having heard these words, delighted, elated, joyful, gladdened, filled with happiness and mental ease, approached the dwelling of the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>. He beheld that residence — vast and extensive, enclosed by walls of ten kinds of jewels, surrounded by rows of palm trees of ten kinds of jewels, encircled on all sides by ten moats filled with fragrant water, covered with divine jeweled <s>utpala</s> lotuses, <s>padma</s> lotuses, <s>kumuda</s> water-lilies, and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> white lotuses, brimming with water possessing the eight excellent qualities, with floors strewn with golden sand, with waters made fragrant by delightful perfumes, adorned with walls of many jewels — with mansions, palaces, pavilions, and multi-storied halls all made of every kind of jewel, well-proportioned and soaring, with arched gateways, lattice windows, half-moon ornaments, lion-cages, shining with the radiance of varied luminous banners, jewels, and gems, adorned with innumerable walls of various gems, with floors inlaid with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) and strung with jeweled garlands, with surroundings perfumed with all divine and auspicious fragrances, fumigated with the sweet scent of the finest <s>kālāgaru</s> (dark aloe) incense, its surroundings anointed with all kinds of unguents, with enclosing walls fashioned from blocks of every jewel, with pinnacles covered by nets of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (refined gold) set with various gems

body.text:
kanakaghaṇṭājālaśatasahasravāteritapramuktamadhuramanojñanirghoṣaṃ sarvaratnapuṣpameghaprasṛtaprakīrṇaratnakusumālaṃkāraṃ sarvaratnavicitradhvajopaśobhitadvāraṃ nānāmaṇiratnaprabhājvālālokāparyantanirdeśaṃ prabhūtamaṇivicitradrumaśākhāvajraśilāprakaṭanidhiśatasahasranicayākṣayakośaṃ daśamahodyānapratimaṇḍitam / sa tatrāpaśyadvasumitrāṃ bhāgavatīmabhirūpāṃ prāsādikāṃ darśanīyāṃ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatāṃ suvarṇavarṇacchavimabhinīlakeśīṃ suvibhaktasamāṅgapratyaṅgaśarīrāṃ sarvakāmadhātukadevamanuṣyātikrāntavarṇarūpasaṃsthānaśobhāṃ brahmātirekasvarāṃ sarvasattvarutamantravidhijñāṃ sarvasvaravyūhopetakāntasvarāṃ cakrākṣaravyūhavimokṣakauśalyānugatāṃ sarvaśilpaśāstrakauśalaniryātāṃ dharmajñānamāyākauśalasuśikṣitāṃ sarvākārabodhisattvopāyanayapratilabdhāṃ vicitraratnābharaṇavibhūṣitāṃ manojñakāyāṃ sarvaratnamayaprabhāsvarajālasaṃchāditaśarīrām asaṃkhyeyadivyamaṇiratnābharaṇavyūhapratimaṇḍitojjvaladehāṃ cintārājamahāmaṇiratnābaddhamakuṭāṃ
vajraratnavicitrasiṃhakāntamaṇiratnopaśobhitamadhyavaiḍūryamaṇihārāvasaktakaṇṭhāmabhinnakuśalamūlacaryāsabhāgaikapraṇidhānamanāpamahāparivārāmakṣayapuṇyajñānamahānidhānakośām / tayā ca sarvaṃ tadgṛhaṃ sarvaratnabhavanavimānavyūhaṃ svaśarīraniryātayā premaṇīyayā kāyaprahlādasukhasaṃjananyā cittaudbilyaprītikaraṇyā udārayā prabhayā sphuṭabhavabhāsitamapaśyat //
body.translated_text: with hundreds of thousands of nets of golden bells stirred by the wind releasing sweet and pleasing sounds, with ornaments of jewel-flowers scattered and streaming from clouds of every kind of jewel-blossom, with doorways adorned by banners of variegated jewels, with radiance extending boundlessly from the brilliance of diverse gems and jewels, with inexhaustible treasuries of hundreds of thousands of deposits displayed on diamond rock-faces amid the branches of trees richly adorned with jewels, and embellished with ten great gardens. There he beheld the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s> — beautiful, gracious, lovely to behold, endowed with the supreme excellence of auspicious complexion, with a golden-hued skin and dark-blue hair, with a body of well-proportioned limbs and members, surpassing in the beauty of her form, figure, and splendor all the gods and humans of the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), with a voice surpassing <s>Brahmā</s>'s, knowing the methods and mantras of the speech of all beings, endowed with a pleasing voice furnished with all varieties of vocal display, skilled in the liberation through the array of syllabic wheels, accomplished in all arts and sciences, well-trained in the skillful means of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge and <s>māyā</s> (magical display), having attained the methods of skillful means of the <s>bodhisattva</s> in all their aspects, adorned with ornaments of variegated jewels, with a captivating body, her form canopied by nets of radiant light made of every kind of jewel, her body blazing with the ornamental array of innumerable divine gems and jewel-adornments, wearing a crown bound with the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), the great king of jewels, her neck hung with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem garlands set in the center of splendid lion-shaped ornaments of <s>vajra</s> (diamond) and variegated jewels, attended by a great retinue united in aspiration through practices sharing the same roots of merit, a treasury of inexhaustible stores of merit and knowledge. And he saw that her entire dwelling with all its arrays of jewel-mansions and palaces was suffused with a radiance emanating from her own body — a radiance that was lovely, that generated bodily delight and ease, that produced mental joy and gladness, that was magnificent and that illuminated the entire abode.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vasumitrāyā bhāgavatyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārye, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / sā avocat - mayā kulaputra virāga koṭīgato nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ / sāhaṃ kulaputra devānāmapsarorūpavarṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhātirekaprabhāsvaraviśuddhyā yathāśayādhimuktānāmābhāsamāgacchāmi / evaṃ nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāṃ kanyārūpavarṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhātirekaprabhāsvaraviśuddhā yathāśayādhimuktānāmābhāsamāgacchāmi / ye ca sattvā māmupasaṃkrāmanti rāgaparyavasthitacetasaḥ, teṣāmahaṃ kulaputra sarveṣāṃ rāgavirāgatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / te ca taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, asaṅgaviṣayaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecinmama sahadarśanena rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, prāmodyaratiṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecidālapanamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, asaṅgasvarakośaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecitpāṇigrahamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, sarvabuddhakṣetrānugamanapratiṣṭhānaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecidekāvāsamātrakeṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, visaṃyogālokaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecitprekṣitamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, praśāntākāravyūhaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecidvijṛmbhitamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, parapravādivikṣobhaṇaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvāsamādhiṃ pratilabhante /
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bhāgavatī</s> <s>Vasumitrā</s>, stood before her with palms joined, and spoke thus: O Noble Lady, I have set forth the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening, yet I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, nor how one should proceed. I have heard that the Noble Lady gives instruction and guidance to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the Noble Lady tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, and how should one proceed? She replied: Noble son, I have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Virāgakoṭīgata</s> (Having Reached the Pinnacle of Dispassion). Noble son, I appear to beings in the form surpassing in radiance, purity, figure, stature, and girth the <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) of the gods, according to their dispositions and inclinations. Likewise, I appear in the form of a maiden surpassing in radiance, purity, figure, stature, and girth the maidens of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, according to their dispositions and inclinations. Those beings who approach me with minds overwhelmed by passion — to all of them, noble son, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of dispassion from passion. And having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, they attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called <s>Asaṅgaviṣaya</s> (Realm of Non-attachment). Some, merely by seeing me, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Prāmodyarati</s> (Delight of Joy). Some, merely through conversation, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Asaṅgasvarakośa</s> (Treasury of Unattached Voice). Some, merely through the clasping of hands, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvabuddhakṣetrānugamanapratiṣṭhāna</s> (Establishment in Following All Buddha-fields). Some, merely through dwelling together, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Visaṃyogāloka</s> (Light of Liberation). Some, merely through a gaze, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Praśāntākāravyūha</s> (Array of Tranquil Forms). Some, merely through an embrace, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Parapravādivikṣobhaṇa</s> (Overturning Rival Doctrines).

body.text:
kecinnimīlanamatreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, buddhaviṣayālokaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / kecidāliṅganamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, sarvajagatsaṃgrahāparityāgagarbhaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante
/ kecitparicumbanamātreṇa rāgavirāgatāmanuprāpnuvanti, sarvajagatpuṇyakośasaṃsparśanaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / ye kecitsattvā mamāntikamupasaṃkrāmanti, sarvāṃstānahamatraiva virāgakoṭīgate asaṅgasarvajñatābhūmyabhimukhe bodhisattvavimokṣe pratiṣṭhāpayāmi //
body.translated_text: Some, merely through the closing of their eyes, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Buddhaviṣayāloka</s> (Light of the Buddha's Domain).
