Some, merely through an embrace, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvajagatsaṃgrahāparityāgagarbha</s> (Womb of Non-abandonment of the Embrace of All the World). Some, merely through a kiss, attain dispassion from passion and gain the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvajagatpuṇyakośasaṃsparśana</s> (Touching the Treasury of Merit of All the World). Whatever beings approach me, I establish all of them right here in the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Virāgakoṭīgata</s> (Having Reached the Pinnacle of Dispassion), which faces the stage of unattached omniscience.

body.text: āha - kutra tvayā ārye kuśalamūlamavaropitam, kīdṛśaṃ ca karmopacitam, yasyāstaveyamīdṛśī saṃpat? āha - smarāmi kulaputra, atīte 'dhvani atyuccagāmī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān / tasya kulaputra atyuccagāminastathāgatasya sattvānāmanukampārthaṃ sumukhāṃ nāma rājadhānīṃ praviśataḥ indrakīlamākrāmataḥ sarvaṃ tannagaraṃ prākampata / vipulavistīrṇaṃ ca anekaratnamayaṃ saṃsthitamabhūt anekaratnaprabhāvyūhaṃ vividharatnapuṣpābhikīrṇaṃ nānādivyatūryapramuktanirghoṣam / udārāprameyadevakāyameghapracchannaṃ ca antarīkṣaṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / ahaṃ ca kulaputra tena samayena sumatirnāma śreṣṭhibhāryā abhūvam / tato me buddhaprātihāryasaṃcoditayā svāminā sārdhaṃ pradhāvitvā tasya tathāgatasya vīthīmukhamupasaṃkrāntasya udāraprasādajātayā ekā ratnakākaṇiḥ pratipāditā / tadā ca mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastasya bhagavato 'tyuccagāminastathāgatasyopasthānako 'bhūt / tenāhamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditā / etamahaṃ kulaputra virāgakoṭīgataṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamanantopāyajñānakauśalapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vipulākṣayapuṇyakośānāmaparājitajñānaviṣayāṇāṃ caryāṃ jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum //

gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe śubhapāraṃgamaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra veṣṭhilo nāma gṛhapatiścandanapīṭhaṃ tathāgatacaityaṃ pūjayati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vasumitrāyā bhāgavatyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya vasumitrāṃ bhāgavatīmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya vasumitrāyā bhāgavatyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 26 //
29 Veṣṭhilaḥ /

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena śubhapāraṃgame nagare veṣṭhilasya gṛhapaterniveśanaṃ tenopajagāma / upetya veṣṭhilasya gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / so 'vocat - āhaṃ kulaputra aparyādattakoṭīgatasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / na mama kulaputra saṃtānāttathāgataḥ parinirvṛto na parinirvāti na parinirvāsyati sarvalokadhātuṣu atyantaparinirvāṇena anyatra vainayikasattvavaśamupādāya / so 'haṃ kulaputra candanapīṭhasya tathāgatacaityasya dvāramuddhāṭayāmi / tacca me caityadvāramuddhāṭayato 'kṣayabuddhavaṃśavyūho nāma bodhisattvasamādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / etaṃ cāhaṃ kulaputra samādhiṃ cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe samāpadye / sarvatra cittakṣaṇe anekākāraviśeṣatāmadhigacchāmi //

āha - ka etasya ārya samādherviṣayaḥ? āha - etaṃ mama kulaputra samādhiṃ samāpannasya asmin lokadhātuvaṃśe buddhaparaṃparayā kāśyapapramukhāḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ kanakamunikrakucchandaviśvabhukaśikhivipaśyitiṣyapuṣyayaśottarapadmottarapramukhāḥ sarvatathāgatā abhimukhā bhavanti / buddhadarśanānusaṃdhau buddhaparaṃparānupacchedena cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe buddhaśataṃ paśyāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena buddhasahasramavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena buddhaśatasahasramavatarāmi / evaṃ buddhakoṭīṃ buddhakoṭīśataṃ buddhakoṭīsahasraṃ buddhakoṭīśatasahasraṃ buddhakoṭyayutaṃ buddhakoṭīniyutaṃ buddhakoṭīkaṅkaraṃ buddhakoṭībimbaram / tadanantareṇa cittena yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhotpādaparaṃparāmavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatānavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatānavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prathamacittotpādasaṃbhāraparaṃparāmavatarāmi /

prathamacittotpādapratilambhavikurvitamavatarāmi / praṇidhānavimātratābhinirhāraviśuddhimavatarāmi / caryāviśuddhimavatarāmi pāramitāparipūrimavatarāmi / sarvabodhisattvabhūmisamudāgamamavatarāmi / kṣāntipratilambhaviśuddhimavatarāmi / mārakalivikiraṇavinarditamavatarāmi / abhisaṃbodhivikurvitavyūhamavatarāmi / buddhakṣetraviśuddhivimātratāmavatarāmi / sattvaparipākavimātratāmavatarāmi / parṣatsaṃnipātavimātratāmavatarāmi / prabhāmaṇḍalavimātratāmavatarāmi / dharmacakrapravartanavṛṣabhitāmavatarāmi / buddhavikurvitaprātihāryamavatarāmi / suvibhaktāṃ saṃbhinnāṃ caiṣāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ smarāmi, saṃdhārayāmi, smṛtyā codgṛhṇāmi / gatyā pravicinomi / bhaktyā pravibhajāmi / buddhyānugacchāmi / prajñayā prakāśayāmi / anāgatabuddhaparaṃparāṃ ca maitreyapramukhānavatarāmi / ekacittakṣaṇe buddhaśatamavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena buddhasahasramavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥ samāṃstathāgatānavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prathamacittotpādasaṃbhāraparaṃparāmavatarāmi / yāvatsuvibhaktāṃ saṃbhinnāṃ caiṣāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ smarāmi, saṃdhārayāmi, smṛtyā codgṛhṇāmi / gatyā pravicinomi
/ matyā pravibhajāmi / buddhyā anugacchāmi / prajñayā prakāśayāmi / yathā ceha lokadhātuvaṃśe pūrvāntāparāntaparyāpannānāṃ buddhaparaṃparāṃ paśyāmi, avatarāmi, tathā daśasu dikṣu anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu atītānāgateṣu lokadhātuvaṃśeṣu sarvatathāgataparaṃparāmavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ prathamacittotpādasaṃbhāraparaṃparāmavatarāmi / tāṃ ca buddhaparaṃparāvatāramavyavacchinnāṃ niṣṭhāmavatarāmi / atulaṃ śraddhāgamanīyaṃ bodhisattvavīryavyavasāyagamyaṃ bodhisattvavīryavegavivardhanamasaṃhāryaṃ sarvalokena sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaistadviṣayānavakrāntaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ pratyutpannānāṃ ca daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu vairocanapramukhānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ paraṃparāmavatarāmi / ekacittakṣaṇe buddhaśataṃ paśyāmi avatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena buddhasahasramavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatānavatarāmi / yaṃ ca yadā tathāgataṃ draṣṭumākāṅkṣāmi, taṃ tadā paśyāmi / yacca taibuddhairbhagavadbhirbhāṣitaṃ bhāṣante bhāṣiṣyante, tatsarva śṛṇomi / śrutvā codgṛhṇāmi / smṛtyā saṃdhārayāmi / gatyā pravicinomi / matyā pravibhajāmi / buddhyā anugacchāmi / prajñayā prakāśayāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra aparinirvāṇakoṭīgataṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ tryadhvaikakṣaṇajñānapratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kṣaṇakoṭīsamādhivyūhavihāriṇāṃ tathāgatadivasāvakrāntānāṃ sarvakalpavikalpasamatānugatānāṃ sarvabuddhasamatāsamādhyanubaddhānāmātmasattvabuddhādvayavihāriṇāṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaradharmavyūhamaṇḍalānāṃ jñānayantralokajālaspharaṇānāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmamudrāvikopitavihāriṇāṃ sarvadharmadhātuvijñapanajñānaviṣayāṇāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmadeśanāvijñaptijñānaviṣayāṇāṃ caryāṃ jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum //

gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe potalako nāma parvataḥ / tatra avalokiteśvaro nāma bodhisattvaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / tasyāṃ velāyāmime gāthe abhāṣata -

children.text: gaccho hi sūdhana śirījalarājamadhye girirājapotalaki śobhani śūrabhāge /
tasmiṃśca parvatavare viharāti dhīro avalokiteśvaru vidū jagato hitāya /
taṃ gaccha pṛccha sudhanā guṇa nāyakānāṃ deśiṣyate vipulaśobhi nayapraveśam // 2 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako veṣṭhilasya gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya veṣṭhilaṃ gṛhapatimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ
30 Avalokiteśvaraḥ /

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako veṣṭhilasya gṛhapateranuśāsanīmanuvicintayan, taṃ bodhisattvādhimuktikośaṃ nigamayan, tadbodhisattvānusmṛtibalamanusmaran, taṃ buddhanetraparaṃparābalaṃ saṃdhārayan, taṃ buddhānantaryānusaṃdhimanugacchan, taṃ buddhanāmaśrotrānugamamanusmaran, taṃ buddhadharmadeśanānayamanulomayan, taṃ buddhadharmasamudāgamavyūhamavataran, tadbuddhābhisaṃbodhivinarditamadhimucyamānaḥ, tadacintyaṃ tathāgatakarmābhimukhīkurvan anupūrveṇa yena potalakaḥ parvatastenopasaṃkramya potalakaṃ parvatamabhiruhya avalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ parimārgan parigaveṣamāṇo 'drākṣīdavalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ paścimadikparvatotsaṅge utsasaraḥprasravaṇopaśobhite nīlataruṇakuṇḍalakajātamṛduśādvalatale mahāvanavivare vajraratnaśilāyāṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā upaviṣṭaṃ nānāratnaśilātalaniṣaṇṇāparimāṇabodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānaṃ sarvajagatsaṃgrahaviṣayaṃ mahāmaitrīmahākarūṇāmukhodyotaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayantam / dṛṣṭvā ca punastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ praharṣitavikasitānimiṣanayanaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ kalyāṇamitraprasādavegānugatāvikṣiptacetāḥ kalyāṇamitreṣu sakalabuddhadarśanasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitraprabhavasarvadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrādhīnasarvaguṇapratipattisaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrasamavadhānadurlabhasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrodbhavadaśabalajñānaratnapratilābhasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrasamudbhavākṣayajñānālokasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrāśrayasaṃvardhitapuṇyapravālasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrasaṃprakāśitasarvajñatādvārasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitroddeśitamahājñānasāgarāvatārasaṃjñī kalyāṇamitrasaṃjanitasarvajñatāsaṃbhārasamudayasaṃjñī yena avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvastenābhijagāma //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, reflecting on the instruction of the householder <s>Veṣṭhila</s>, assimilating that treasury of <s>bodhisattva</s> resolute faith, remembering the power of that <s>bodhisattva</s>-recollection, retaining that power of the succession of the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, following that continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>'s uninterrupted [transmission], remembering that following of the hearing of the <s>Buddha</s>'s name, conforming to that method of teaching the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>, entering that array of the complete attainment of the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>, developing faith in that proclamation of the <s>Buddha</s>'s perfect awakening, turning toward that inconceivable activity of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — gradually approached the mountain <s>Potalaka</s>, and ascending Mount <s>Potalaka</s>, searching and seeking the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, he saw the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> on the western slope of the mountain, in a great forest clearing on a vajra-jewel rock, beautified by springs and flowing streams, on soft green grass with young curling shoots, seated cross-legged, surrounded by an immeasurable assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> seated on various jewel-rock surfaces, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, illuminating the <s>dharma</s>-discourse called 'The Illumination of the Gateway of Great Loving-kindness and Great Compassion' concerning the domain of gathering all beings. Having seen him, joyful, elated, glad, delighted, filled with joy and mental happiness, with eyes wide open and unwinking in delight, with palms joined, with mind following the force of devotion to the spiritual friend without distraction, perceiving spiritual friends as the vision of all <s>Buddhas</s>, perceiving them as the source of all <s>Dharma</s>-clouds, perceiving the attainment of all qualities as dependent on spiritual friends, perceiving the encounter with spiritual friends as rare, perceiving them as the source of obtaining the jewel of the knowledge of the ten powers, perceiving them as the source of inexhaustible light of knowledge, perceiving the sprouts of merit as nourished through reliance on spiritual friends, perceiving them as illuminators of all gateways to omniscience, perceiving them as guides to entering the ocean of great knowledge, perceiving them as producers of the accumulation of the equipment for omniscience — he approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ dūrata eva āgacchantamavalokya āmantrayāmāsa - ehi / svāgataṃ te anupamodārācintyamahāyānasaṃprasthitā jātamūlakavividhaduḥkhopadrutāpratiśaraṇasarvajagatparitrāṇāśayā sarvalokātikrāntānupamāprameyā sarvabuddhadharmādhyakṣatābhilāṣin mahākarūṇāvegāviṣṭa sarvajagatparitrāṇamate samantabhadradarśanacaryābhimukha mahāpraṇidhānamaṇḍalapariśodhanacitta sarvabuddhadharmameghasaṃdhāraṇābhilaṣitakuśalamūlopacayātṛptāśayakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīsamyakpravṛttamañjuśrījñānasāgarasaṃbhūta guṇakamalākara buddhādhiṣṭhānapratilābhābhimukhaḥ samādhyālokavegapratilabdha sarvabuddhadharmameghasaṃdhāraṇābhilaṣitacitta buddhadarśanaprītiprasādavegapraharṣitamānasa acintyāpramāṇasucaritavegābhiṣyanditacetaḥ guṇapratipattivegaviśuddhapuṇyajñānakośa svayamabhijñāmukhasarvajñajñānamātravegaparasaṃdarśābhiprāya mahākaruṇāvegavipannamūlatathāgatajñānālokavega saṃdhāraṇamate //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, seeing the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> approaching from afar, addressed him: 'Come! Welcome to you, who have set forth upon the inconceivable <s>Mahāyāna</s> with rejoicing, with the intention of rescuing all beings who are without refuge and afflicted by various sufferings rooted in birth, [whose aspiration is] surpassing, incomparable, and immeasurable beyond all worlds, who aspire to the mastery of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, who are seized by the force of great compassion, whose intention is the rescue of all beings, who face the conduct of the vision of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, whose mind is set on the purification of the maṇḍala of the great vow, who aspire to hold the clouds of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, whose intention is insatiable in accumulating roots of merit, who rightly follow the instruction of spiritual friends, who are born from the ocean of the knowledge of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who are a mine of the lotuses of virtues, who face the attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, who have obtained the force of the light of <s>samādhi</s>, whose mind aspires to hold the clouds of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, whose mind is delighted by the joy and devotion of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, whose mind overflows with the force of inconceivable and immeasurable good conduct, whose treasury of merit and knowledge is purified by the force of the practice of qualities, whose intention is to demonstrate to others the mere force of omniscient knowledge through the gateway of one's own superknowledge, whose force is that of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s light of knowledge rooted in the force of great compassion — O you of the intention of holding [all this]!' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvastenopasaṃkramya avalokiteśvara bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandya avalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, circumambulated the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> many hundreds of thousands of times

body.text: pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: and standing before him with palms joined, spoke thus: 'O Noble One, I have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how he should practice. And I have heard that the Noble One gives counsel and instruction to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the Noble One tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should he practice?' //

body.text:
atha khalu avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo jāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇaṃ vicitrāprameyaprabhājālavāhavyūhameghapramuñcanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavisṛtavividhavimalāmitakāyacittaprahlādasaṃjananaraśmipratānasaṃkusumitaṃ pāṇiṃ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpya evamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yena te anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ahaṃ kulaputra mahākaruṇāmukhāvilambaṃ nāma bodhisattvacaryāmukhaṃ prajānāmi / etacca kulaputra mahākaruṇāmukhāvilambaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmukhaṃ sarvajagadasaṃbhinnasattvaparipākavinayanapravṛttaṃ samantamukhasrotavijñaptisattvasaṃgrahavinayaparyupasthānam / so 'haṃ kulaputra mahākaruṇāmukhāvilambabodhisattvacaryāmukhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ ca pādamulānna vicalāmi, sarvasattvakāryeṣu ca abhimukhastiṣṭhāmi / dānenāpi sattvān saṃgṛhṇāmi / priyavāditayā arthakriyayā samānārthatayāpi sattvān saṃgṛhṇāmi / rūpakāyavidarśanenāpi sattvān paripācayāmi / acintyavarṇasaṃsthānarūpadarśanaviśuddhyā raśmijālotsargeṇāpi sattvān prahlādya paripācayāmi / yathāśayaghoṣodāhāreṇāpi yathābhimateryāpathasaṃdarśanenāpi vividhādhimuktisabhāgadharmadeśanayāpi nānārūpavikurvitenāpi kuśaladharmopacayapravṛttasattvacittasaṃcodanayāpi āśayānurūpavicitrāparimāṇanirmāṇasaṃdarśanenāpi nānājātyupapannasattvasabhāgarūpasaṃdarśanenāpi ekāvāsanivāsenāpi sattvān saṃgṛhṇāmi paripācayāmi / tena mayā kulaputra idaṃ mahākaruṇāmukhāvilambaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmukhaṃ pariśodhayatā sarvajagatpratiśaraṇapraṇidhirutpāditaḥ, yaduta sarvasattvaprapātabhayavigamāya sarvasattvasaṃtrāsakabhayapraśamanāya sarvasattvasaṃmohabhayavinivartanāya sarvasattvabandhanabhayasamucchedāya sarvasattvajīvitoparodhopakramabhayavyāvartanāya sarvasattvopakaraṇavaikalyabhayāpanayanāya sarvasattvajīvikābhayavyupaśamanāya / sarvasattvāślokabhayasamatikramaṇāya sarvasattvasāṃsārikabhayopaśamanāya sarvasattvaparṣacchāradyabhayavigamāya sarvasattvamaraṇabhayavyatikramāya sarvasattvadurgatibhayavinivartanāya sarvasattvatamondhakāraviṣamagatyapratyudāvartyāvabhāsakaraṇāya sarvasattvaviṣabhāgasamavadhānabhayātyantavigamāya sarvasattvapriyaviprayogabhayanirodhāya sarvasattvāpriyasaṃvāsabhayāpanayanāya sarvasattvakāyaparipīḍābhayasaṃyogāya sarvasattvacittaparipīḍanabhayanirmokṣaṇāya sarvasattvaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsasamatikramāya
sarvajagatpratiśaraṇapraṇidhyabhinirhāraḥ kṛtaḥ / anusmṛtimukhaṃ ca me sarvaloke 'dhiṣṭhitaṃ sarvasattvabhayavyupaśamanāya / svanāmacakraṃ me sarvaloke 'bhivijñaptaṃ sarvasattvabhayavigamāya / sarvajagadanantākṛtibhedaśamatho me kāye 'dhiṣṭhito yathākālajagatprativijñaptaye / so 'haṃ kulaputra, anenopāyena sattvān sarvabhayebhyaḥ parimocya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya avivartyān karomi buddhadharmapratilābhāya / etamahaṃ kulaputra mahākaruṇāmukhāvilambasya
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, extending his right arm — of the color of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, releasing clouds of arrays of immeasurable, variegated radiance-net streams — and placing his hand, blooming with rays spreading forth from the marks and minor marks that generate joy and refreshment of body and mind for immeasurable beings in manifold stainless ways, upon the head of the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, spoke thus: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family, that you have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening! I, son of good family, know the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-gateway called "The Pendant of the Gateway of Great Compassion" (<s>Mahākaruṇāmukhāvilamba</s>). And this <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-gateway called the Pendant of the Gateway of Great Compassion operates for the ripening and disciplining of all beings without distinction, and serves for the gathering and disciplining of beings through universal streams of communication in all directions. I, son of good family, established in this <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-gateway of the Pendant of the Gateway of Great Compassion, do not depart from the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and I stand face to face with the tasks of all beings. I gather beings through generosity. I gather beings through kind speech, beneficial action, and joint endeavor. I ripen beings through the display of a visible body. I delight and ripen beings through the purity of vision of forms of inconceivable colors and configurations, and through the emission of nets of rays. I also gather and ripen beings through the utterance of sounds according to their dispositions, through the display of deportment according to their wishes, through teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in accord with their various resolute faiths, through various magical transformations, through stimulating the minds of beings engaged in the accumulation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through the display of variegated and immeasurable emanations according to their dispositions, through the display of forms similar to beings born in various births, and through dwelling together [with them]. By me, son of good family, in purifying this <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-gateway of the Pendant of the Gateway of Great Compassion, the vow of being the refuge of all beings has been generated — namely: for the removal of the fear of falling for all beings, for the pacification of the fear of terror for all beings, for the averting of the fear of delusion for all beings, for the cutting off of the fear of bondage for all beings, for the averting of the fear of attempts upon the life of all beings, for the removal of the fear of lacking requisites for all beings, for the pacification of the fear concerning livelihood for all beings, for the transcending of the fear of ill-repute for all beings, for the pacification of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> for all beings, for the removal of the fear of assemblies for all beings, for the transcending of the fear of death for all beings, for the averting of the fear of bad destinies for all beings, for illuminating and turning back all beings from the dangerous paths of darkness and gloom, for the complete removal of the fear of encountering hostile conditions for all beings, for the cessation of the fear of separation from the beloved for all beings, for the removal of the fear of association with the unloved for all beings, for the release from the fear of bodily affliction for all beings, for the liberation from the fear of mental affliction for all beings, for the transcending of suffering, grief, and distress for all beings — the accomplishment of the vow of being the refuge of all beings has been made. And the gateway of recollection has been established by me in all worlds for the pacification of the fear of all beings. The wheel of my name has been made known in all worlds for the removal of the fear of all beings. The pacification of the infinite varieties of forms of all beings has been established in my body for the communication [with beings] at the appropriate time. Thus, son of good family, by this method I liberate beings from all fears, generate in them the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, and make them irreversible for the attainment of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. I, son of good family, have attained this

body.text: bodhisattvacaryāmukhasya lābhī / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ samantabhadrāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhapraṇidhānamaṇḍalaviśuddhānāṃ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāgatiṃgatānāṃ kuśaladharmābhisaṃskārāvyavacchinnasrotānāṃ sarvabodhisattvasamādhiśrotrasadāsamāhitānāṃ sarvakalpasaṃvāsacaryāvivartyasrotānāṃ sarvatra adhvanayānugatasrotānāṃ sarvalokadhātvāvartaparivartasrotakuśalānāṃ sarvasattvākuśalacittavyupaśamakarasrotānāṃ sarvasattvakuśalacittasaṃvardhanasrotānāṃ sarvasattvasaṃsārasrotovinivartikarasrotānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct-gateway of the Pendant of the Gateway of Great Compassion. How could I know or express the conduct or qualities of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of <s>Samantabhadra</s> — those who have purified the maṇḍala of the vows of all <s>Buddhas</s>, who have reached the course of the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, whose stream of constructing wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is uninterrupted, who are always concentrated in the stream of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>, whose stream of conduct dwelling in all <s>kalpas</s> is irreversible, whose stream follows all times everywhere, who are skilled in the turning and revolving stream of all world-realms, whose stream pacifies the unwholesome minds of all beings, whose stream increases the wholesome minds of all beings, whose stream turns back all beings from the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>?' //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here the following is said —

children.text: kṛtvā pradakṣiṇu stavitva ca gauraveṇa prakānta dakṣiṇapathaṃ sudhanaḥ sudāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated and praised with reverence, <s>Sudhana</s>, the well-disciplined, departed toward the southern region.
He sees <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the sage dwelling in compassion, abiding in a cave on the jewel-mountain. // 1 //

children.text: vajrāmaye giritaṭe maṇiratnacitre siṃhāsane padumagarbhi niṣaṇṇa dhīro /
children.translated_text: On a vajra mountain-slope adorned with <s>maṇi</s>-jewels and gems, the steadfast one sits on a lotus-womb lion-throne.
Surrounded by gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and sons of the <s>Jina</s>, he teaches them the <s>Dharma</s>. // 2 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvopajāta atulā sudhanasya prīti upagamya vandati kramau guṇasāgarasya /
children.translated_text: Having seen him, incomparable joy arose in <s>Sudhana</s>; approaching, he bows at the feet of that ocean of virtues.

children.text: ovāca dehi mama ārya kṛpāṃ janitvā śikṣāṃ tu ahu labhe ima bhadracaryām // 3 //
children.translated_text: He said: 'O Noble One, having generated compassion, grant me the training that I may obtain this excellent conduct!' // 3 //

children.text: bāhuṃ praṇamya vimalaṃ śatapuṇyacitraṃ prabhameghajāla vipulaṃ śubha muñcamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Extending his stainless arm, adorned with a hundred merits, releasing vast and auspicious clouds of radiance-nets,

children.text: mūrdhni sthihitva sudhanasya viśuddhasattvo avalokiteśvaru vidū vacanaṃ bhaṇāti // 4 //
children.translated_text: placing it upon the head of <s>Sudhana</s>, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the pure-hearted wise one, speaks these words: // 4 //

children.text: ekaṃ vimokṣamukha jānami buddhaputra sarvajināna karuṇāghanajñānagarbham /
children.translated_text: 'I know one gateway of liberation, O son of the <s>Buddha</s> — the womb of the dense knowledge of compassion of all the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: saṃbhūta sarvajagatrāyaṇasaṃgrahāya sarvatra vartati mamāpyatha ātmaprema // 5 //
children.translated_text: arisen for the rescue and gathering of all beings; everywhere it operates, and [in it] there is also self-cherishing for me.' // 5 //

children.text: trāyāmi sarvajanatāṃ vyasanairanekaiḥ ye gāḍhabandhanagatāriṣu hastaprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I rescue all people from manifold calamities — those who have fallen into the hands of enemies, trapped in tight bonds,

children.text: gātreṣu viddha tatha cārakasaṃniruddhā mucyanti bandhanagatā mama nāma śrutvā // 6 //
children.translated_text: wounded in their limbs and imprisoned by guards — the bound are freed upon hearing my name.' // 6 //

children.text: utsṛṣṭaḥ vadhya nṛpatīna kṛtāparādhāḥ kṣiptā iṣu na ca kramanti śarīri teṣām /
children.translated_text: 'Those condemned to death by kings, who have committed offenses — arrows shot at them do not penetrate their bodies;

children.text: chidyanti śastra parivartati tīkṣṇa dhārā ye nāmadheyu mama tatra anusmaranti // 7 //
children.translated_text: weapons break and sharp blades turn away for those who there remember my name.' // 7 //

children.text: rājāna madhyagata ye ca vivādaprāptā vijinanti sarvaripavo 'tha śubhe labhante /
children.translated_text: 'Those who have come before kings and are embroiled in disputes — they defeat all enemies and obtain auspiciousness;

children.text: vardhanti sarva yaśa mitrakule dhanāni bhontī adharṣiya smaritvana mahya nāma // 8 //
children.translated_text: all their fame, kinsmen, and wealth increase; they become invincible by remembering my name.' // 8 //
'Those entering forests [beset by] fear of robbers, fear of enemies, filled with lions, leopards, yaks, deer, and serpents —

children.text: gacchanti nirbhaya jinitvana sarvaśatrūn ye nāmadheyu mama kecidanusmaranti // 9 //
children.translated_text: they go fearlessly, conquering all foes, those who remember my name.' // 9 //

children.text: kṣiptā manāgiritaṭītu praduṣṭacittairaṅgārakarṣu jvalitā api co vadhārtham /
children.translated_text: 'Those cast from mountain-cliffs by those of hostile intent, and those set ablaze in pits of coals for the purpose of execution —

children.text: padmāṅkurā jalanidhi jvalanā bhavanti ye nāmadheyu mama kecidanusmaranti // 10 //
children.translated_text: lotus-sprouts [appear in] the ocean, and fires become [cool] for those who remember my name.' // 10 //

children.text: prakṣipta sāgarajale na marenti tatra nadyāṃ na cohyati na dahyati cāgnimadhye /
children.translated_text: When cast into ocean waters, they do not die there; they are not swept away in rivers, nor are they burned in the midst of fire,

children.text: sarve anartha na bhavantyapi cārthasiddhiḥ nāmaṃ mamā anusmaritva muhūrtakaṃ pi // 11 //
children.translated_text: All misfortunes do not arise, and there is success in all aims, by recollecting my name even for a single moment. [11]

children.text: haḍidaṇḍabandhanigaḍāśca tathā kudaṇḍā avamānanā tatha vimānana ṭhambhanāśca /
children.translated_text: Fetters, beatings, bonds, shackles, and also stocks, humiliation, contempt, and paralysis,

children.text: ākrośatāḍanavibhartsanatarjanāśca mama nāmadheyu smaramāṇa labhanti mokṣam // 12 //
children.translated_text: Abuse, striking, reproach, and threats — those who remember my name attain liberation from all these. [12]

children.text: ye vairiṇo vivarachidragaveṣiṇaśca nityapraduṣṭamana ye ca avarṇavādī /
children.translated_text: Those who are enemies, seeking gaps and openings, whose minds are always hostile, and who speak slander —

children.text: sahadarśanena tada maitramanā bhavanti bheṣyanti varṇi śruta mahya smaritva nāma // 13 //
children.translated_text: Upon seeing them, they become friendly-minded; they will become praisers, having heard and recollected my name. [13]

body.text: vetālamantratha kakhorda sadā prayuktā ghātārtha teṣa ripavaḥ stimitā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vetāla</s> (zombie) spells and <s>kakhorda</s> (malevolent sorcery), always employed for the purpose of killing — their enemies become paralyzed,

body.text: teṣa śarīri na kramanti viṣā aśeṣā ye nāmadheṣu mama kecidanusmaranti // 14 //
body.translated_text: And no poisons whatsoever enter their bodies — those who recollect my name in any way. [14]

children.translated_text: By <s>Nāga</s> lords, troops of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Pūtanas</s>, mischief-makers with fierce minds,

children.text: ojoharairbhayakaraiḥ supināntare 'pi śāmyanti sarvi mama nāma anusmaritvā // 15 //
children.translated_text: By vitality-stealers and fear-makers — even in dreams, all are pacified by recollecting my name. [15]
There is no separation from mother, father, friends, relatives, and kinsmen, nor is there the encounter with the unpleasant,

children.text: na dhanakṣayo nāpi upaiti daridrabhāvaṃ nāmaṃ mamā anusaritva muhūrtakaṃ pi // 16 //
children.translated_text: There is no loss of wealth, nor does one approach the state of poverty, by recollecting my name even for a single moment. [16]

children.text: na ca gacchati cyuta ito narakaṃ avīciṃ na tiraścayoni na ca preta na cākṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: Having fallen from here, one does not go to <s>Avīci</s> hell, nor to animal births, nor to the realm of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), nor to unfavorable conditions,

children.text: deve manuṣya upapadyati śuddhasattvo yo nāmadheyu mama kecidanusmaranti // 17 //
children.translated_text: One of pure being is reborn among <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans — those who recollect my name in any way. [17]

children.text: na ca andhakāṇabadhirā na pi carcigātrā na ca raudra khañjā atha cāṭaka prekṣaṇīyā /
children.translated_text: They are not blind, one-eyed, deaf, nor leprous of body, not fierce, not lame, but rather handsome and pleasant to behold,

children.text: sarvendriyairavikalā bahukalpakoṭyo bhontī narā mama smaritvana nāmadheyam // 18 //
children.translated_text: With all sense faculties intact for many millions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), people become so by having recollected my name. [18]

children.text: avalokiteti mama te sugatiṃ vajranti yo puṣpamuṣṭi mama okirate śarīre /
children.translated_text: Saying '<s>Avalokita</s>!' they go to a good destiny; whoever scatters a handful of flowers upon my body,

children.text: dhūpāṃśca dhūpayati yaśca dadāti chatraṃ vistārikai puja karoti prasannacitto
children.translated_text: And whoever offers incense, and whoever gives a parasol, and whoever with a joyful mind performs extensive worship —

children.text: mama buddhakṣetri sa ca bheṣyati dakṣiṇīyaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: In my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), that one will become worthy of offerings. [19]

children.text: upapadyate itu cyavitvana śuddhasattvo buddhāna saṃmukha daśaddiśi lokadhātau /
children.translated_text: Having departed from here, one of pure being is reborn face to face with <s>Buddhas</s> in world-systems of the ten directions,

children.text: buddhāṃśca paśyati śṛṇoti ca teṣa dharmaṃ ye nāmadheyu mama kecidanusmaranti // 20 //
children.translated_text: And sees <s>Buddhas</s> and hears their <s>Dharma</s> — those who recollect my name in any way. [20]

children.text: ete tathānya kṣayituṃ nimituṃ na śakyā yāvaccupāyi ahu sattva vinemi loke /
children.translated_text: These and other such things cannot be exhausted or measured, for as long as I, through skillful means, guide beings in the world,

children.text: eko vimokṣa mama bhāvitu buddhaputra nāhaṃ guṇān guṇadharāṇa vijāni sarvān // 21 //
children.translated_text: Even a single liberation of mine, O son of the <s>Buddha</s>, has been cultivated — yet I do not know all the virtues of those who possess virtues. [21]

children.text: aṣṭāpadākṛtu daśaddiśi lokadhātau kalyāṇamitra samupāsita sūdhanena /
children.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> has attended upon spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) in world-systems of the ten directions, arranged like an eightfold pattern,

children.text: na ca tṛptu dharma śruṇamāṇu jinaurasānāṃ kasmānna prīti bhavati śruṇamāna dharmam // 22 //
children.translated_text: And is never satiated hearing the <s>Dharma</s> of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) — how could one not feel joy when hearing the <s>Dharma</s>? [22]

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena ananyagāmī nāma bodhisattvaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaganatalenāgatya sahāyā lokadhātoścakravālaśikhare pratyaṣṭhāt / samantarapratiṣṭhāpitau ca ananyagāminā bodhisattvena sahāyā lokadhātoścakravālaśikhare pādau, tatkṣaṇādiyaṃ sahālokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prākampata, anekaratnamayī ca saṃsthitābhūt / tathārūpā ca ananyagāminā bodhisattvena kāyāt prabhā pramuktā, yayā prabhayā sarvacandrasūryaprabhā paryādattāḥ, sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālānāmagnimaṇijyotiṣāṃ ca prabhā jihmīkṛtāḥ, sarvamahānarakāścāvabhāsitāḥ, sarvatiryagyoniyamalokagatigahanaṃ cāvabhāsitam, sarvāpāyaduḥkhāni ca tadanantaraṃ praśāntāni / sarvasattvānāṃ ca kleśā na bādhante / vividhaśokaśalyaduḥkhāni ca prasrabdhāni / sarvaṃ cedaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarvaratnameghairabhipravarṣan sarvapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvyūhasarvapūjāmeghairabhipravarṣan bhagavantamupasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa cāsyāśrayaḥ sarvasattvabhavanapratibhāsaprāpto yathāśayasattvasaṃtoṣaṇābhimukhaḥ / tasmiṃśca potalake parvate 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasyāntikamupasaṃkrāntaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma //
body.translated_text: Then at that time, a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Ananyagāmī</s> came from the eastern direction through the sky and stood upon the peak of the <s>Cakravāla</s> (world-encircling mountain) of the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. And when <s>Ananyagāmī</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> placed his feet upon the peak of the <s>Cakravāla</s> of the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, at that very instant this <s>Sahā</s> world-system trembled and shook in six ways, and became made of many kinds of jewels. And from the body of <s>Ananyagāmī</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, such a radiance was released that by that radiance all the light of the moon and sun was overcome, the lights of all <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, and of fires, jewels, and luminaries were outshone, all the great hells were illuminated, the dense thicket of animal births and the realm of <s>Yama</s> was illuminated, and immediately all sufferings of the lower realms were pacified. The afflictions of all beings no longer troubled them. Various sorrows, thorns, and sufferings subsided. And this entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) was showered with clouds of all jewels, clouds of all flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and arrays of all worship-offerings, and he approached the Blessed One. His very presence was capable of reflecting the abodes of all beings, and was directed toward satisfying beings according to their dispositions. And he was seen approaching the presence of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> on <s>Potalaka</s> mountain.

body.text: atha khalu avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputra ananyagāminaṃ bodhisattvamiha parṣanmaṇḍale saṃprāptam? āha - paśyāmi ārya / āha - etaṃ kulaputra ananyagāminaṃ bodhisattvamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> addressed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son thus: 'Do you see, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s> who has arrived in this assembly?' He said: 'I see him, Noble One.' He said: 'Go to this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s>, O son of good family, and ask him: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? How should one conduct oneself?'

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandya avalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 28 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, circumambulated <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>. [28]

body.text: 31 Ananyagāmī /
body.translated_text: [Chapter 31: <s>Ananyagāmī</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya jñānagāthālabdhacitto 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasyāvitṛpto darśanena vāṇīmaprativahan yena ananyagāmī bodhisattvastenopasaṃkramya ananyagāmino bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, his mind inspired by the wisdom-verses of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, unsatisfied with merely seeing <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, carrying his words in his heart, approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s>, stood before him with palms joined together, and spoke thus: 'I, Noble One, have generated the aspiration for supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, how one should conduct oneself. And I have heard that the Noble One gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the Noble One tell me: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? How should one conduct oneself?'

body.text:
so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra samantamukhanirjavanasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / āha - katamasya tvayā ārya tathāgatasya pādamūlādeṣa samantamukhanirjavano nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ? kiyaddūre vā sa ito lokadhātuḥ? kiyacciroccalito vāsi tato lokadhātoḥ? āha - durvijñeyametatkulaputra sthānaṃ sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikayā prajayā - yaduta bodhisattvaparākramī bodhisattvavīryānivartyatā bodhisattvavīryasaṃhāryatā / nedaṃ kulaputra śakyaṃ kalyāṇamitrāparigṛhītairbuddhāsamanvāhṛtairanupacitakuśalamūlairapariśuddhāśayairapratilabdhabodhisattvendriyaiḥ prajñācakṣuvirahitaiḥ śrotuṃ vā saṃdhārayituṃ vā adhimoktuṃ vā avatarituṃ vā / āha - vadatu me āryaḥ / adhimokṣyāmi śraddhāsyāmi buddhānubhāvena kalyāṇamitraparigraheṇa ca / so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra pūrvasyāṃ diśi śrīgarbhavatyā lokadhātorāgacchāmi samantaśrīsaṃbhavasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt / tasya me kulaputra samantaśrīsaṃbhavasya tathāgatasya pādamūlādeṣa samantamukhanirjavano nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tataśca me kulaputra śrīgarbhavatyā lokadhātoruccalitasya anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ kalpāḥ kṣīṇāḥ / ekaikena ca cittotpādena anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān padavyavahārān vyatikramāmi / ekaikena ca padavyavahāreṇa anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramāmi / sarvāṇi ca tāni buddhakṣetrāṇi avirahitāni tathāgataiḥ / avatarāmi sarvāṃśca tān buddhān bhagavataḥ / anuttarayā manomayyā anabhisaṃskāradharmadhātumudrāmudritayā tathāgatānujñātayā sarvabodhisattvapraharṣasaṃjananyā tathāgataṃ pūjayāmi / yāvataśca tāsu lokadhātuṣu sattvasamudrān paśyāmi, sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ cittasāgarānavatarāmi, sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāmindriyacakraṃ parijñāya yathāśayādhimuktito rūpakāyaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / dharmaghoṣamudīrayāmi / prabhāmaṇḍalamutsṛjāmi / vividhopakaraṇasaṃpadamupasaṃharāmi / svakāyaṃ caiṣāmadhitiṣṭhāmi, yaduta paripākavinayaprayogāpratiprasrabdhaye / yathā ca pūrvasyā diśo niryāmi, evaṃ dakṣiṇāyāḥ paścimāyāḥ uttarāyā uttarapūrvāyāḥ pūrvadakṣiṇāyā dakṣiṇapaścimāyāḥ
paścimottarāyā adha
body.translated_text: He replied: 'I, O son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>samantamukhanirjavana</s> (universal unimpeded emergence in all directions).' He said: 'At the feet of which <s>Tathāgata</s>, Noble One, did you attain this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>samantamukhanirjavana</s>? And how far away is that world-system from here? And how long ago did you depart from that world-system?' He replied: 'This matter is difficult to comprehend, O son of good family, for the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, with its ascetics and brahmins — namely, the heroic exertion of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, the irreversibility of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vigor, the indefatigability of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s energy. This, O son of good family, cannot be heard, retained, accepted with faith, or penetrated by those who are not guided by spiritual friends, not blessed by <s>Buddhas</s>, who have not accumulated roots of merit, whose intentions are impure, who have not attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> faculties, and who lack the eye of wisdom.' He said: 'May the Noble One speak! I will have faith, I will believe, through the power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and through the guidance of spiritual friends.' He replied: 'I, O son of good family, come from the eastern direction, from a world-system called <s>Śrīgarbhavatī</s>, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantaśrīsaṃbhava</s>. At the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantaśrīsaṃbhava</s>, O son of good family, I attained this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>samantamukhanirjavana</s>. Since my departure from that world-system <s>Śrīgarbhavatī</s>, O son of good family, <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s> have elapsed. And with each single arising of thought, I traverse paths equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And with each single step, I pass through <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And all those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are not devoid of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I enter all of them and approach all those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. With supreme, mind-made worship, stamped with the seal of the unconditioned <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), authorized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, generating joy in all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, I worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And however many oceans of beings I see in those world-systems, I enter the mind-oceans of all of them, and having fully comprehended the circle of faculties of all of them, I display a physical form according to their dispositions and inclinations. I utter the voice of the <s>Dharma</s>. I release a halo of radiance. I provide various kinds of material assistance. And I establish my own body for them, so that the effort of ripening and disciplining them is not relaxed. And just as I go forth in the eastern direction, so too I go forth in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, and downward directions —

body.text: ūrdhvāyā diśo niryāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra samantamukhanirjavanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvatrānugatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samatādigabhimukhānāmasaṃbhinnajñānaviṣayāṇāṃ sarvadharmadhātusuvibhaktaśarīrāṇāṃ yathāśayādhimuktasarvasattvānuvicāriṇāṃ sarvakṣetraspharaṇakāyānāṃ sarvadharmayathānugatānāṃ tryadhvapathasamatānuprāptānāṃ sarvadikpathasamatānusaraṇānāṃ sarvajagatpathavirocanānāṃ tathāgatapathāvikalpānāmasaṅgasarvapathānugatānāmanālayapathapratiṣṭhitānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: — and the upward direction. This, O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>samantamukhanirjavana</s> that I know. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the virtues, of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who follow everything everywhere, who face the depths of equality, whose domains of knowledge are undivided, whose bodies are well-distributed throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> (realms of reality), who examine all beings according to their dispositions and inclinations, whose bodies pervade all fields, who follow all phenomena as they truly are, who have attained equality on the path of the three times, who follow the equality of the path in all directions, who illuminate the path of all worlds, who are free from conceptualization on the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who follow all paths without attachment, and who are established on the path of non-attachment?'

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe dvāravatī nāma nagarī / tatra mahādevo devaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha kathaṃ - bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Go, O son of good family, to the city called <s>Dvāravatī</s>, right here in the southern region. There dwells the god <s>Mahādeva</s>. Approach him and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice? How should one conduct oneself?'

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nanyagāmino bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandya ananyagāminaṃ bodhisattvamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya ananyagāmino bodhisattvasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 29 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s>, circumambulated the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ananyagāmī</s>. [29]

body.text: 32 Mahādevaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Chapter 32: <s>Mahādeva</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vipulabodhisattvacaryānugatacitto 'nanyagāmino bodhisattvasya jñānagocaraṃ spṛhayamāṇarūpo mahābhijñābhinirhāraviṣayaguṇaviśeṣadarśī dṛḍhavīryasaṃnāhapraharṣaprāpto 'cintyavimokṣavikrīḍitānugatāśayaḥ bodhisattvaguṇabhūmau pratipadyamānaḥ samādhibhūmiṃ vicārayamāṇo dhāraṇībhūmau pratiṣṭhamānaḥ praṇidhānabhūmimavataran pratisaṃvidbhūmāvanuśikṣamāṇobalabhūmiṃ niṣpādayamāno 'nupūrveṇa yena dvāravatī nagarī tenopasaṃkramya mahādevaṃ paryapṛcchat / tasya mahājanakāya ārocayāmāsa - eṣa kulaputra mahādevo nagaraśṛṅgāṭake devāgāre audārikeṇātmabhāvena sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena mahādevastenopasaṃkramya mahādevasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, his mind intent upon the vast <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, longing for the domain of knowledge of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who goes nowhere else, perceiving the special qualities of the sphere of the manifestation of great supernatural powers, having attained the joy of donning the armor of firm vigor, his disposition following the play of inconceivable liberations, progressing on the ground of <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities, exploring the ground of <s>samādhi</s>, established on the ground of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, entering the ground of aspiration, training on the ground of analytical knowledge, accomplishing the ground of powers — gradually approached the city of <s>Dvāravatī</s> and inquired about <s>Mahādeva</s>. A great multitude of people informed him: "This, O son of good family, is <s>Mahādeva</s>, who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings with an enormous bodily form in the temple at the city crossroads." Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, approached <s>Mahādeva</s>, bowed his head at <s>Mahādeva</s>'s feet, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke thus: "O noble one, I have generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one should practice. I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and guidance to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, may the noble one tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?"

body.text: atha khalu mahādevo devaścaturdiśaṃ caturaḥ pāṇīn prasārya caturbhyo mahāsamudrebhyaḥ paramaśīghrajavena vāryānīya svamukhaṃ prakṣālya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ suvarṇapuṣpairabhyavakīrya evamāha - sudurlabhadarśanā hi kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ, paramadurlabhaśravaṇā āścaryaprādurbhāvā loke 'gratvāt paramapuruṣapuṇḍarīkā jagatrtrātāraḥ, pratiśaraṇabhūtā lokasya, pratiṣṭhānabhūtā jagataḥ, mahāvabhāsakarāḥ sattvānām, kṣemapathadarśakāḥ saṃmūḍhamārgāṇām, nāyakabhūtā dharmanayāvataraṇatāyai, pariṇāyakabhūtāḥ sarvajñatāpuropanayanatāyai / tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ bhavati - durdṛṣṭighātanaṃ nāmadheyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yena nirmalacittānāṃ svakāyapratibhāsaṃ darśayati / viśuddhakāyakarmaṇāmabhimukhā bhavanti / vacanadoṣavivarjitānāṃ sarasvatyālokamavakrāmayanti / viśuddhāśayānāṃ sarvakālamabhimukhāstiṣṭhanti / ahaṃ kulaputra meghajālasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / āha - ka etasya ārya meghajālasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, extending his four arms in the four directions, bringing water from the four great oceans with supreme swiftness, washing his own face, and scattering golden flowers upon <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, spoke thus: "<s>Bodhisattvas</s> are indeed rarely seen, O son of good family — supremely rare to hear of, wondrous in their appearance, foremost in the world, supreme lotus-like beings among men, protectors of the world, a refuge for beings, a foundation for the world, great illuminators for sentient beings, guides showing the safe path to those who have lost their way, leaders for entering into the method of the <s>Dharma</s>, guides for leading toward omniscience. This is my thought, O son of good family — the very name of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is 'destroyer of wrong views,' for they show the reflection of their own body to those of pure mind. They turn face-to-face toward those whose bodily actions are purified. They cause the light of <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) to descend upon those free from faults of speech. They always stand face-to-face before those of pure intention. I, O son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Meghajāla</s> (Cloud Net)." He asked: "What is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Meghajāla</s>, O noble one?"

body.text: atha khalu mahādevoḥ devaḥ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya purato mahāparvatamātraṃ suvarṇarāśimupadarśya rūpyarāśiṃ vaiḍūryarāśiṃ sphaṭikarāśiṃ musāragalvarāśiṃ aśmagarbharāśiṃ jyotirasamaṇiratnarāśiṃ vimalagarbhamaṇiratnarāśiṃ vairocanamaṇiratnarāśiṃ samantadigabhimukhamaṇiratnarāśiṃ cūḍāmaṇiratnamakuṭarāśiṃ vicitramaṇiratnarāśiṃ keyūrarāśiṃ kuṇḍalavibhūṣaṇarāśiṃ valayarāśiṃ mekhalarāśiṃ nūpūrarāśiṃ vividhamaṇiratnarāśiṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgavibhūṣaṇarāśiṃ cintārājamaṇiratnarāśiṃ sarvapuṣpāṇi sarvagandhān sarvadhūpān sarvamālyāni sarvavilepanāni sarvacūrṇāni sarvavastrāṇi sarvacchatrāṇi sarvadhvajān sarvapatākāḥ sarvatūryāṇi sarvatālāvacarān sarvakāmaviṣayān /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, displayed before <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son heaps as large as great mountains — a heap of gold, a heap of silver, a heap of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), a heap of crystal, a heap of <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), a heap of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), a heap of <s>jyotirasā</s> jewels, a heap of <s>vimalagarbha</s> jewels, a heap of <s>vairocana</s> jewels, a heap of jewels facing all directions, a heap of crest-jewel diadems, a heap of variegated jewels, a heap of armlets, a heap of earring ornaments, a heap of bracelets, a heap of girdles, a heap of anklets, a heap of various jewels, a heap of ornaments for all major and minor limbs, a heap of wish-fulfilling king jewels, all flowers, all fragrances, all incenses, all garlands, all ointments, all powders, all garments, all parasols, all banners, all pennants, all musical instruments, all cymbals, and all objects of desire.

body.text:
asaṃkhyeyāni ca kanyākoṭīśatasahasrāṇyupadarśya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - itaṃ kulaputra gṛhītvā dānāni dehi, puṇyāni kuru, tathāgatān pūjaya, sattvān dānena saṃgrahavastunā saṃgṛhya tyāgapāramitāyāṃ niyojaya, dānena lokaṃ śikṣaya / duṣkaraparityāgatāṃ pradarśaya / yathaivāhaṃ kulaputra tavopakaraṇavidhimupasaṃharāmi, evamaparimāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ dānacetanāniruddhānāṃ tyāgavāsitāṃ saṃtatiṃ karomi / buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu bodhisattvakalyāṇamitreṣu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayitvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayāmi / api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra kāmaratipramattānāṃ sattvānāṃ viṣayaparibhogaparigṛddhānāṃ tān viṣayānaśubhānadhitiṣṭhāmi / krodhāviṣṭānāṃ mānamadadarpagarvitānāṃ vigrahavainayikānāṃ raudrarākṣasavikṛtabhayānantaśarīrān māṃsarudhirabhakṣānātmabhāvānupadarśya taṃ sarvaṃ stambhasaṃrambhamupadarśayāmi / kusīdanyastaprayogān sattvānagnyudakarājacauropasargabhayasaṃdarśanenodvejya vīryārambhe niyojayāmi / evaṃ taistairupāyaiḥ sarvākuśalacaryābhyo vinivartya sarvakuśaladharmapratipattau saṃniyojayāmi / sarvapāramitāvipakṣanirghātāya sarvapāramitāsaṃbhāropacayāya sarvāvaraṇaparvataprapātapathasamatikramaṇāya anāvaraṇadharmāvatārāya ca / etamahaṃ kulaputra meghajālaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamindrakalpānāṃ
bodhisattvānāṃ kleśāsurapramardakānāṃ vārikalpānāṃ sarvajagadduḥkhāgniskandhanirvāpayitṝṇāṃ tejaḥskandhakalpānāṃ sarvajagattṛṣṇāsalilasaṃśoṣaṇakarāṇāṃ vāyukalpānāṃ sarvagrāhābhiniveśaparvatavikiraṇānāṃ vajrakalpānāṃ dṛḍhātmasaṃjñāśailanirdāraṇānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: And displaying innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of maidens, he said this to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: "Take these, O son of good family, give gifts, make merit, worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, gather beings through the means of attraction beginning with generosity, engage them in the perfection of giving, train the world through generosity. Demonstrate the abandonment of what is difficult to abandon. Just as I, O son of good family, provide these resources for you, so too for immeasurable beings whose intention to give has not ceased, I make their continuity infused with renunciation. Having planted roots of merit in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> and in <s>bodhisattva</s> spiritual friends, I establish them in supreme perfect awakening. Moreover, O son of good family, for beings intoxicated by sensual pleasures and attached to the enjoyment of sense objects, I make those sense objects appear repulsive. For those possessed by anger, pride, intoxication, arrogance, and conceit, for those inclined to conflict, I display terrifying <s>rākṣasa</s>-like bodies of fearsome, boundless form, feeding on flesh and blood, and I show them all that obstinacy and violence. For lazy beings engaged in wrong endeavors, I rouse them to exertion by showing them the dangers of fire, water, kings, and thieves. Thus, by various such skillful means, I turn them away from all unwholesome conduct and engage them in the practice of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — for the destruction of all that opposes the perfections, for the accumulation of provisions for all perfections, for crossing over the precipitous path of the mountains of all obscurations, and for entering the unobstructed <s>Dharma</s>. This, O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Meghajāla</s> (Cloud Net) that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are like <s>Indra</s>, crushing the <s>asuras</s> (demons) of the afflictions, who are like water, extinguishing the mass of flames of all the world's suffering, who are like a mass of fire, drying up the waters of craving of all the world, who are like wind, scattering the mountains of all grasping and attachment, who are like <s>vajra</s> (diamond), splitting the rocks of the firm notion of self?"

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva jambudvīpe magadhaviṣaye bodhimaṇḍe sthāvarā nāma pṛthvīdevatā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: "Go, O son of good family. Here in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the region of <s>Magadha</s>, at the seat of awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>), there dwells an earth goddess named <s>Sthāvarā</s>. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should one practice?'"

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahādevasya pādau śirasābhivandya mahādevaṃ devamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya mahādevasya devasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 30 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at <s>Mahādeva</s>'s feet, circumambulated <s>Mahādeva</s> the god many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of <s>Mahādeva</s> the god. [30]

body.text: 33 Sthāvarā /
body.translated_text: [33 <s>Sthāvarā</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa yena magadhaviṣaye bodhimaṇḍe sthāvarā pṛthvīdevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / daśapṛthivīdevatāśatasahasrāṇi anyonyamevaṃ vācamudīrayāmāsuḥ - ayaṃ sa āgacchati, yaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇabhūto bhaviṣyati / ayaṃ sa tathāgatagarbha āgacchati, yaḥ sarvasattvānāmavidyāṇḍakośaṃ nirbhetsyati / ayaṃ sa dharmarājakulodita āgacchati, yo 'saṅgavaravimaladharmarājapaṭṭamābandhiṣyati / ayaṃ sa jñānanārāyaṇavajrapraharaṇaśūra āgacchati, yaḥ sarvaparapravādicakraṃ pramardiṣyati / atha tāni sthāvarāpramukhāni daśapṛthivīdevatāśatasahasrāṇi mahāpṛthivīcālaṃ kṛtvā gambhīrajaladharanirnādaṃ janayitvā sarvaṃ trisāhasraṃ lokadhātumudāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya sarvaratnābharaṇālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitaśarīrāṇi vidyullatākalāpā iva gaganatale lambamānāḥ, prarohadbhiḥ sarvavṛkṣāṅkuraiḥ, praphulladbhiḥ sarvapuṣpavṛkṣaiḥ, pravarṣadbhiḥ sarvanadīsrotobhiḥ, unnamadbhiḥ sarvotsasarohradataḍāgaiḥ, pravarṣadbhirmahāgandhodakavarṣaiḥ, pravāyadbhiḥ kusumaughotkarapravāhibhirmahāvātaiḥ, pravādayadbhiḥ tūryakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ, prasaradbhiḥ divyavimānābharaṇamakuṭaiḥ, praṇadadbhiḥ govṛṣagajavyāghramṛgendraiḥ, pragarjadbhiḥ devāsuroragabhūtādhipatibhiḥ, saṃghaṭṭamānairmahāśailendraiḥ utplavadbhiḥ, nidhicayakoṭīśatasahasraiḥ unnamadbhiḥ, dharaṇītalādabhyudgatāni //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, gradually approached <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess at the seat of awakening in the region of <s>Magadha</s>. Ten hundreds of thousands of earth goddesses called out to one another thus: "He is coming — he who will become a refuge for all beings! He is coming, that embryo of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, who will crack open the shell of ignorance of all beings! He is coming, that one born in the family of the <s>Dharma</s> king, who will bind upon himself the turban of the unattached, supreme, stainless <s>Dharma</s> king! He is coming, that hero whose weapon is the <s>vajra</s> of knowledge like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who will crush the armies of all rival teachers!" Then those ten hundreds of thousands of earth goddesses, led by <s>Sthāvarā</s>, caused the great earth to tremble, produced the deep rumbling of thunderclouds, illuminated the entire trichiliocosm with a magnificent radiance, their bodies adorned with all jeweled ornaments, hanging in the sky like clusters of lightning streaks — with all tree sprouts sprouting forth, with all flower trees blossoming, with all river currents flowing, with all springs, pools, and ponds rising, with great rains of fragrant water pouring down, with great winds blowing forth cascades of flowers, with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of musical instruments sounding, with divine pavilions, ornaments, and diadems spreading forth, with bulls, elephants, tigers, and lords of beasts bellowing, with the lords of gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s> thundering, with the great mountain kings colliding and leaping up, with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of treasure hoards rising up from the surface of the earth.

body.text: atha sthāvarā pṛthivīdevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - svāgataṃ te kulaputra / ayaṃ sa pṛthivīpradeśo yatra te sthitvā kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yatrāhaṃ pratyakṣā / kimicchasi tadvipākaphalaikadeśaṃ draṣṭum? atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sthāvarāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sthāvarāṃ pṛthivīdevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sthāvarāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - icchāmyārye //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: "Welcome, O son of good family! This is the very spot of earth where, standing, you planted roots of merit, and where I was present as witness. Do you wish to see even a portion of the fruit of that ripening?" Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess, circumambulated <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess with palms joined, and spoke thus: "I wish to, O noble one."

body.text: atha khalu sthāvarā pṛthivīdevatā pādatalābhyāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ parāhatya asaṃkhyeyamaṇiratnanidhānakoṭīśatasahasrapratimaṇḍitāmupadarśya evamāha - imāni kulaputra maṇiratnanidhānakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tavānugāmīni, tava purojavāni, tava yathecchopabhogyāni, tava puṇyavipākanirjātāni, tava puṇyabalarakṣitāni / tebhyastvaṃ gṛhītvā yatkārthaṃ tatkuruṣva / api tvahaṃ kulaputra jñānaduryodhanagarbhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sā ahametena bodhisattvavimokṣeṇa samanvāgatā dīpaṃkaratathāgatamupādāya bodhisattvasya nityānubaddhā satatamārakṣāpratipannā / tataḥ prabhṛti ahaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya cittacaritaṃ vyavacārayāmi, jñānaviṣayamavagāhayāmi, sarvapraṇidhānamaṇḍalamavatarāmi, bodhisattvacaryāviśuddhimanugacchāmi, sarvasamādhinayamanusarāmi, sarvabodhisattvābhijñācittavipulatāṃ spharāmi / sarvabodhisattvabalādhipateyatāṃ sarvabodhisattvāsaṃhāryatāṃ sarvakṣetrajālaspharaṇatāṃ sarvatathāgatavyākaraṇasaṃpratīcchanatāṃ sarvakālābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanatāṃ sarvadharmacakrapravartananayaṃ sarvasūtrāntasaṃprabhāṣaṇadharmameghanayaṃ mahādharmāvalokāvabhāsanayaṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sthāvarā</s> the earth goddess struck the great earth with the soles of her feet, displaying it adorned with innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of jewel treasure hoards, and spoke thus: "These hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of jewel treasure hoards, O son of good family, follow you, go before you, are for your enjoyment as you wish, are born from the ripening of your merit, and are protected by the power of your merit. Take from them and do whatever purpose you wish. Moreover, O son of good family, I have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Jñānaduryodhanagarbha</s> (Womb of Invincible Knowledge). Endowed with this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation, beginning from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, I have always followed the <s>bodhisattva</s>, constantly engaged in protecting him. From that time onward, O son of good family, I examine the mental conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, I enter into the domain of his knowledge, I enter into the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of all his aspirations, I follow the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, I follow all methods of <s>samādhi</s>, I pervade the vastness of the minds and supernatural knowledge of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The sovereign mastery of the powers of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the indestructibility of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the pervading of all networks of <s>buddha</s>-fields, the receiving of the prophecies of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the displaying of awakening at all times, the method of turning the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, the method of the cloud of <s>Dharma</s> that expounds all <s>sūtras</s>, the method of the radiance of beholding the great <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: sarvasattvaparipācanavinayajñānanayaṃ sarvabuddhavikurvitasaṃdarśananayaṃ ca anugacchāmi saṃdhārayāmi saṃpratīcchāmi //
body.translated_text: the method of the knowledge of maturing and disciplining all beings, and the method of displaying the miraculous transformations of all <s>Buddhas</s> — I follow, retain, and receive all of these.

body.text: eṣa ca me kulaputra jñānaduryodhanagarbho bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa paratareṇa candradhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau sunetrasya tathāgatasyāntikātpratilabdhaḥ avabhāsavyūhe kalpe / sā ahaṃ kulaputra imaṃ jñānaduryodhanagarbhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamāyūhantī niryūhantī saṃvardhayantī vipulīkurvāṇā avirahitābhūvaṃ tathāgatadarśanena yāvad bhadrakalpāt / atra ca mayā anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā ārāgitāḥ / sarveṣā ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ bodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇavikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭam / sarveṣāṃ ca ahaṃ teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ kuśalamūleṣu sākṣībhūtā / etamahaṃ kulaputra jñānaduryodhanagarbhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvatathāgatānubaddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhakathānudhāriṇāṃ sarvatathāgatajñānagahanapraviṣṭānāṃ cittakṣaṇadharmadhātuspharaṇānujavānāṃ tathāgatasamatāśarīrāṇāṃ sarvabuddhāśayavimalagarbhāṇāṃ sadābhinirhṛtasarvabuddhotpādānāmasaṃbhinnasarvabuddhakāyadūtānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: And this, O son of good family, is my bodhisattva liberation called <s>Jñānaduryodhanagarbha</s> (Womb of Invincible Wisdom), which I obtained from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sunetra</s> in the world-system called <s>Candradhvajā</s>, in the <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Avabhāsavyūha</s> (Array of Radiance), beyond and far beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>. I, O son of good family, while striving for, developing, cultivating, and expanding this <s>Jñānaduryodhanagarbha</s> bodhisattva liberation, was never separated from the sight of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> throughout the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon). And here I have pleased <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible buddha-fields. And I have witnessed the miraculous displays of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> approaching the seat of enlightenment. And I have been a witness to the roots of merit of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This, O son of good family, is the <s>Jñānaduryodhanagarbha</s> bodhisattva liberation that I know. How could I know the conduct or describe the virtues of bodhisattvas who follow all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who uphold the teachings of all Buddhas, who have entered the depths of the wisdom of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whose swiftness matches the spreading of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in each moment of mind, whose bodies are the equality of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whose wombs are purified by the intentions of all Buddhas, who constantly manifest the arising of all Buddhas, and who are undivided emissaries of the bodies of all Buddhas?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, idamihaiva jambudvīpe magadhaviṣaye kapilavastu nāma nagaram / tatra vāsantī nāma rātridevatā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, O son of good family, here in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the region of <s>Magadha</s>, there is a great city called <s>Kapilavastu</s>. There dwells a night-goddess named <s>Vāsantī</s>. Approach her and ask: How should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct? How should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sthāvarāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sthāvarāṃ pṛthivīdevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sthāvarāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 31 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the earth-goddess <s>Sthāvarā</s>, having circumambulated the earth-goddess <s>Sthāvarā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing back at her again and again, departed from the presence of the earth-goddess <s>Sthāvarā</s>. [31]

body.text: 34 Vāsantī /
body.translated_text: [34 <s>Vāsantī</s>]

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ tāṃ sthāvarāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyā anuśāsanīmanusmaran, taṃ duryodhanagarbhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamanusmaran, tāṃ bodhisattvasamādhibhāvanāṃ vipulīkurvan, taṃ bodhisattvadharmanayamanuvicintayan, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣavikrīḍitaṃ vicārayan, tāṃ bodhisattvavimokṣajñānasūkṣmādiṃ saṃvyavalokayan, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣajñānasāgaramavataran, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣajñānasaṃbhedamadhimucyamānaḥ, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣānantajñānābhisaṃskāramanugacchan, taṃ bodhisattvavimokṣajñānasamudramavagāhamānaḥ / sa kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa praviśya madhye nagaraśṛṅgāṭakasya asthāt / acirāstamite sūrye sarvabodhisattvānuśāsanīṣu pradakṣiṇagrāhī vāsantyā rātridevatāyā darśanaparitṛṣitaḥ kalyāṇamitreṣu buddhajñānapratilambhaniścitabuddhiḥ samantajñānacakṣurviṣayaśarīrādhiṣṭhānaḥ sarvadigabhimukhena kalyāṇamitradarśanacittena udārādhimuktijñānagarbhasaṃjñāgatacetāḥ sarvārambaṇaprasṛtajñānacakṣuḥ sarvadharmadhātunayajñānasāgaraprasaraspharaṇānugatena samāṃdhicakṣuṣā sarvadigjñeyasāgaraṃ vyavalokayan, mahājñānacakṣuḥprasṛtāvahitāśayo 'drākṣīdvāsantīṃ rātridevatāṃ kapilavastuno mahānagarasyordhvaṃ gaganatale vicitrānupamamaṇikūṭāgāre sarvavaragandhapadmagarbhamahāratnasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇām, suvarṇavarṇena kāyenābhinīlamṛdubahukeśīmabhinīlanetrāmabhirūpāṃ prāsādikāṃ darśanīyāṃ sarvābharaṇālaṃkāravibhūṣitaśarīrāṃ raktavarāmbaranivasanāṃ candramaṇḍalālaṃkṛtabrahmajaṭāmakuṭadhāriṇīṃ sarvatārāgrahanakṣatrajyotirgaṇapratibhāsasaṃdarśanaśarīrām / yāvantaśca tayā vipule sattvadhātau akṣaṇāpāyadurgativinipātebhyaḥ sattvāḥ parimocitāḥ, tānapi tasyā romavivaragatānadrākṣīt / yāvantaḥ svargaloke pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, yāvantaḥ śrāvakapratyekabodhau sarvajñatāyāṃ ca paripācitāḥ, tānapi tasyāḥ sarvaromavivaragatānapaśyat / yairnānopāyaiḥ paripācitāḥ kāyābhinirhārai rūpābhinirhārairvarṇābhinirhāraiḥ, tānapi tasyā romavivaragatānadrākṣīt / yairghoṣābhinirhāraiḥ
svarāṅgābhinirhārairvividhamantradharmanayasaprayogaiḥ paripācitāḥ, tānapi tasyā romamukhebhyo 'nuravamāṇānaśrauṣīt / yaiḥ kālābhinirhāraiḥ, yairyathāśayādhimuktasattvānuvartanaiḥ, yābhirbodhisattvacaryābhirbodhisattvavikramairbodhisattvasamādhivikurvitamukhairbodhisattvavṛṣabhitābhirbodhisattvavihārairbodhisattvāvalokitairbodhisattvavilokitairbodhisattvavikurvābhirbodhisattvamahāpuruṣasiṃhavijṛmbhitaiḥ, yairbodhisattvavimokṣavikrīḍitaistayā sattvāḥ paripācitāḥ, tānyapi tasyā romavivaragatāni prajānīte sma //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> approached the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, recalling the instruction of the earth-goddess <s>Sthāvarā</s>, recalling the <s>Duryodhanagarbha</s> bodhisattva liberation, expanding the cultivation of bodhisattva <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), contemplating the method of bodhisattva <s>dharma</s>, reflecting on the play of bodhisattva liberation, examining the subtle beginnings of bodhisattva liberation-wisdom, plunging into the ocean of bodhisattva liberation-wisdom, resolving upon the penetration of bodhisattva liberation-wisdom, following the infinite mental formations of bodhisattva liberation-wisdom, and immersing himself in the ocean of bodhisattva liberation-wisdom. Having circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, he entered through the eastern gate and stood in the middle of the city crossroads. Shortly after sunset, embracing all the instructions of the bodhisattvas, thirsting for the sight of the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>, with a mind of firm resolve to attain Buddha-wisdom through spiritual friends, with a body empowered by the domain of the eye of omniscient wisdom, with a mind turned toward every direction seeking the sight of spiritual friends, with thoughts imbued with the womb of noble resolve and wisdom, with the eye of wisdom extending to all objects, surveying the ocean of the knowable in every direction with the eye of <s>samādhi</s> pervaded by the flow and spread of the ocean of wisdom of all <s>dharmadhātu</s> methods — with the great eye of wisdom extended and his mind attentive, he beheld the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> above the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the sky, seated upon a great jeweled lion-throne in the womb of the finest fragrant lotuses, within a jeweled pavilion of variegated and incomparable gems. She had a body of golden hue, with soft and abundant dark-blue hair, dark-blue eyes, beautiful, graceful, and lovely to behold, her body adorned with all manner of ornaments and decorations, clothed in excellent red garments, wearing a crown with a <s>Brahma</s>-topknot adorned with a moon-disc, her body reflecting the radiance of all the stars, planets, constellations, and luminous hosts. And all those beings whom she had liberated from the misfortunes, evil destinies, and woeful states of existence in the vast realm of beings — he saw them within the pores of her body. All those whom she had established in the heavenly worlds, and all those whom she had matured in the paths of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers), and omniscience — he saw them also within every pore of her body. By whatever various skillful means she had matured them — through manifestations of bodies, forms, and colors — he saw them within the pores of her body. By whatever manifestations of sounds, vocal characteristics, and various applications of <s>mantra</s> and <s>dharma</s> methods she had matured them — he heard them resounding from the openings of her pores. By whatever manifestations of time, by whatever ways of adapting to the dispositions and aspirations of beings, by whatever bodhisattva practices, bodhisattva powers, manifestations of bodhisattva <s>samādhi</s> transformations, bodhisattva heroic deeds, bodhisattva abodes, bodhisattva gazes, bodhisattva glances, bodhisattva miraculous powers, and bodhisattva lion-stretches of great beings she had matured beings — he perceived all of these within the pores of her body.

body.text: sa tān nānopāyasaṃprayuktān dharmanayasāgarān dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto vāsantyā rātridevatāyāḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya utthāya vāsantīṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vāsantyā rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā khalu devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam /
body.translated_text: Having seen and heard those ocean-like <s>dharma</s> methods connected with various skillful means, <s>Sudhana</s> was delighted, elated, joyful, glad, filled with happiness and mental ease. He prostrated with his entire body before the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>, rose, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> with palms joined, spoke thus: O goddess, I have generated the aspiration for supreme perfect enlightenment.

body.text: so 'haṃ kalyāṇamitrādhiṣṭhānān sarvabuddhaguṇān saṃpaśyan kalyāṇamitrāśritamātmānaṃ karomi / darśaya me devate sarvajñatāmārgaṃ yatra pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo niryāti daśabalabhūmau //
body.translated_text: And I, relying on the empowerment of spiritual friends, behold all the qualities of the Buddhas and make myself dependent upon spiritual friends. Show me, O goddess, the path to omniscience, established upon which a bodhisattva advances to the stage of the Ten Powers.

body.text: evamukte vāsantī rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamevaṃ kalyāṇamitrāveśāviṣṭaḥ kalyāṇamitravacanāni śuśrūṣuḥ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyāṃ pratipadyase / niyamena tvaṃ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṃ pratipadyamānaḥ āsannībhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / viṣamamatiṣu sattveṣu maitracittā, akuśalakarmapathapratipanneṣu karuṇacittā, kuśalakarmapathapratipanneṣu muditacittā / samaviṣamamatiṣu sattveṣūpekṣācittā, saṃkliṣṭeṣu viśodhanacittā, viṣamagateṣu samyakpratipannacittā, hīnādhimuktikeṣu udārādhimuktisaṃjananacittā, hīnendriyeṣu mahāvīryavegavivardhanacittā, saṃsārābhirateṣu saṃsāragaticakravinivartanacittā, śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānābhimukheṣu sattveṣu sarvajñatāmārgapratiṣṭhāpanacittā / evaṃ cittamanasikāraprayuktā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra anena sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukhena bodhisattvavimokṣeṇa samanvāgatā //
