body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> spoke to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> as follows: Excellent, excellent, O son of good family, that you, thus inspired and possessed by spiritual friends, eager to hear the words of spiritual friends, practice according to the instructions of spiritual friends. Assuredly, practicing the instructions of spiritual friends, you will draw near to supreme perfect enlightenment. I, O son of good family, have attained the bodhisattva liberation called <s>Sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukha</s> (Gateway of Taming the World through the Radiance of <s>Dharma</s> that Dispels the Darkness of All Beings). Toward beings of uneven minds I have a mind of loving-kindness; toward those following unwholesome paths of action, a mind of compassion; toward those following wholesome paths of action, a mind of sympathetic joy; toward beings of even and uneven minds, a mind of equanimity; toward the defiled, a mind of purification; toward those gone astray, a mind of right guidance; toward those of inferior aspirations, a mind that generates noble aspirations; toward those of weak faculties, a mind that increases great vigor and energy; toward those delighting in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), a mind that turns back the wheel of <s>saṃsāric</s> destinies; toward beings inclined toward the vehicles of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, a mind that establishes them on the path to omniscience. Thus, O son of good family, engaged in such mental attention and intention, I am endowed with this bodhisattva liberation, the Gateway of Taming the World through the Radiance of <s>Dharma</s> that Dispels the Darkness of All Beings.

body.text: ye sattvā andhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrau parikrānteṣu manuṣyeṣu bhūtasaṃghānucaritāyāṃ taskaragaṇasaṃkīrṇāyāṃ viṣamacāritrasattvadikcaritāyāṃ kālābhrameghajālasaṃchannāyāṃ dhūmarajomalasamākulāyāṃ viṣamavātavṛṣṭisaṃkṣobhitāyāṃ candrādityajyotirgaṇarahitāyāṃ cakṣuṣkāryāparākramāyāṃ rātrau sāgaragatā bhavanti, sthalagatā vā parvatagatā vā aṭavīkāntāragatā vā vanāntaragatā vā deśāntaragatā vā grāmāntaragatā vā digantaragatā vā vidigantaragatā vā mārgāntaragatā vā mahāsāgaragatā vā vipannayānapātrā bhavanti, sthalagatā vā vihanyante, parvatagatā vā mahāprapāteṣu prapatanti, mahāṭavīkāntāragatā vā annapānavirahitā bhavanti, vanagahanavetrajālairavasaktā vā anayavyasanamāpadyante, deśāntaragatā vā taskarairhanyante, grāmāntaragatā vā viṣamacāritrā vinaśyanti, digantaragatā vā saṃmuhyanti, vidigantaragatā vā vimuhyanti, mārgāntaragatā vā vilayamāpadyante, teṣāmahaṃ kulaputra sattvānāṃ nānopāyamukhairlayanabhūtā bhavāmi - yaduta sāgaragatānāṃ kālikāvātameghavikiraṇatāyai kaluṣodakātikramaṇatāyai viṣamavātamaṇḍalīvikiraṇatāyai mahormivegavyupaśamanatāyai āvartabhayavimocanatāyai digudyotanatāyai samyagudakapathapratipādanatāyai tīradarśanatāyai / ratnadvīpopanayanāya mārgaṃ saṃdarśayāmi saṃgrāhakarūpeṇa sārthavāhakarūpeṇa / kasyacidrājarūpeṇa jagarājarūpeṇa kūrmarājarūpeṇa asurarājarūpeṇa garuḍarājarūpeṇa kinnararājarūpeṇa mahoragarāgarājarūpeṇa sāgaradevatārūpeṇa kaivartarūpeṇa pratiśaraṇabhūtā bhavāmi / tacca kuśalamūlamevaṃ pariṇāmayāmi - sarvasattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇabhūtā bhaveyaṃ sarvaduḥkhaskandhavinivartanatāyai / sthalagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ mohāndhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrau veṇukaṇṭakaśarkarakaṭhallākīrṇāyāṃ ghoraviṣoragasaṃkīrṇāyāṃ nimnonnataviṣamapracārāyāṃ rajoreṇusamuddhatāyāṃ viṣamavātavṛṣṭisaṃkṣobhitāyāṃ
body.translated_text: Those beings who in the dark and gloomy night — when people have withdrawn, when hosts of spirits roam, when bands of thieves abound, when creatures of evil conduct wander about, when dense masses of dark clouds cover the sky, when smoke, dust, and grime fill the air, when harsh winds and rain disturb everything, when the moon, sun, and luminous hosts are absent, when the eyes can accomplish nothing — find themselves upon the ocean, or upon land, or upon mountains, or in the wilderness of desolate forests, or within dense woods, or in foreign lands, or between villages, or between the cardinal directions, or between the intermediate directions, or between roads, or upon the great ocean; and those whose vessels and boats are wrecked, or those on land who are struck down, or those on mountains who fall into great precipices, or those lost in great wilderness-deserts who are deprived of food and drink, or those caught in the tangles of forest undergrowth and cane-thickets who fall into calamity and misfortune, or those in foreign lands who are slain by thieves, or those between villages who perish through evil conduct, or those between the directions who become bewildered, or those between the intermediate directions who become confused, or those between roads who fall into destruction — for all these beings, O son of good family, I become a refuge through various skillful gateways: namely, for those upon the ocean, to dispel the dark storm-clouds and winds, to cross over turbid waters, to scatter the circles of hostile winds, to calm the force of great waves, to liberate from the terror of whirlpools, to illuminate the directions, to guide rightly upon the water-path, and to show the shore. I show the way to the jewel-island, appearing in the form of a guide, in the form of a caravan-leader. For some I appear in the form of a king, in the form of a serpent-king, in the form of a turtle-king, in the form of an <s>Asura</s>-king, in the form of a <s>Garuḍa</s>-king, in the form of a <s>Kinnara</s>-king, in the form of a great <s>Mahoraga</s>-king, in the form of an ocean-deity, in the form of a fisherman — becoming a refuge. And I dedicate those roots of merit thus: May I become a refuge for all beings, for the turning back of all masses of suffering. For beings on land, in the dark and gloomy night of delusion, on ground strewn with bamboo, thorns, gravel, and rocks, infested with terrible venomous serpents, with uneven and rough terrain, with dust and sand swirling up, disturbed by harsh winds and rain —

body.text:
śītoṣṇaduḥkhasaṃsparśāyāṃ vyālamṛgendrasābhiśaṅkāyāṃ vadhakataskaragaṇānuvicaritāyāṃ dharaṇyāṃ diksaṃmūḍhānāṃ sattvānāmādityarūpeṇa udgatacandrarūpeṇa maholkāpātarūpeṇa vidyunmālāniścāraṇarūpeṇa ratnābhārūpeṇa grahamaṇḍalarūpeṇa nakṣatrajyotirgaṇavimānaprabhārūpeṇa devarūpeṇa bodhisattvarūpeṇa sattvānāṃ trāṇabhūtā bhavāmi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - anena kuśalamūlena sarvasattvānāṃ trāṇaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvakleśāndhakāravidhamanatāyai / parvataprapātagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ maraṇabhayabhītānāṃ jīvitapratilambhāya yaśaskāmatāvaśagatānāṃ kīrtiśabdadhvajakāmānāṃ bhogārthikānāṃ
lobhāviṣṭānāmupakaraṇaparyeṣṭyabhiyuktānāṃ lokasaṃpattyabhilāṣaparamāṇāṃ putrabhāryāsnehavinibaddhānāṃ dṛṣṭigatagahanapranaṣṭānāṃ vividhaduḥkhabhayopadrutānāṃ nānopāyamukhaiḥ śaraṇabhūtā bhavāmi - yaduta giriguhāsaṃsthānābhinirhāreṇa phalamūlabhojanābhinirhāreṇa jalapathodapānābhinirhāreṇa śītoṣṇapratipakṣābhinirhāreṇa samyakpathanidarśanena kalaviṅkarūtanirghoṣeṇa mayūrarājanikūjaghoṣeṇa auṣadhijvalanāvabhāsarūpeṇa parvatadevatāprabhārūpeṇa / giriguhādarivivaragatānāṃ vividhaduḥkhopadrutānāṃ timirāndhakāravinivartanatāyai samapṛthivītalābhinirhāreṇa śaraṇabhūtā bhavāmi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - yathā ahameṣāṃ parvatagatānāṃ sattvānāmārakṣāṃ karomi, evamahameṣāṃ saṃsāraparvatagiriprapātapatitānāṃ jarāmaraṇagrahābhiniviṣṭānāṃ śaraṇabhūtā bhaveyam / vanagahanajālasaṃsaktakānāmapyahaṃ sattvānāṃ tamondhakārāyāṃ rātrau vipulaviṣayavṛkṣavividhopasthānāṃ vividhatṛṇodakakaṇṭakadrumalatoparuddhamārgāṇāṃ nānādrumalatāvanagahanaprāptānāṃ śārdūlanaditanirghoṣasaṃtrastahṛdayānāṃ kāryāparipūrisamākulacittānāṃ vividhabhayopadravopasṛṣṭānāṃ vanagahananiḥsaraṇadiśamaprajānatāṃ samyaggamanapathasaṃdarśayitrī bhavāmi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - anena kuśalamūlena vividhadṛṣṭigahanagatān sattvāṃstṛṣṇājālasaṃsaktān vicitrasaṃsāraduḥkhabhayopadrutān sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ parimocayeyam / aṭavīkāntāragatānāmapyahaṃ sattvānāmandhakāraprāptānāṃ nānopāyamukhaiḥ sukhaṃ saṃjanayya mārgaṃ saṃdarśya etānabhayakṣeme pratiṣṭhāpya evaṃ cittamutpādayāmi - anena kuśalamūlena saṃsāraṭavīkāntāraprāptān sattvān durgatipathapratipannān sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ parimocya atyantayogakṣeme sarvajñatāmārge pratiṣṭhāpayeyam / deśajanapadāviṣṭānapyahaṃ kulaputra sattvānabhiniveśādhikārikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavamānān vividhairudbadhyamānopāyaistato janapadābhiniveśāduccālya evaṃ cittamutpādayāmi - anena kuśalamūlena sarvasattvān skandhālayābhiniveśāduccālya anālayasarvajñajñāne pratiṣṭhāpayeyam / grāmagatānapyahaṃ kulaputra sattvān gṛhaniketabandhanabaddhānandhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrau vividhagṛhāpadduḥkhitān nānodvegamukhairudbadhya saṃjanitasaṃvegacittān dhanadānena saṃgṛhya samyak prīṇayitvā anikete dharme pratiṣṭhāpya
evaṃ cittamutpādayāmi - anena kuśalamūlena sarvasattvān svāyatanagrāmasaṃniśritān saṃsāragativiṣayagocarāduccālya sarvajñatāgocare pratiṣṭhāpayeyam //
body.translated_text: On the earth afflicted by the touch of cold and heat suffering, threatened by serpents and lords of beasts, roamed by groups of murderers and thieves, for beings who have lost their sense of direction, I become a refuge in the form of the sun, in the form of the risen moon, in the form of a great meteor fall, in the form of emanating garlands of lightning, in the form of the radiance of jewels, in the form of planetary circles, in the form of the light of celestial chariots bearing hosts of stars and luminaries, in the form of a <s>deva</s> (god), in the form of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I become a refuge for all beings, for the dispelling of the darkness of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). For beings who have fallen from mountain precipices, terrified by the fear of death, for the recovery of their lives; for those overcome by desire for fame, longing for renown, glory, and banners; for those seeking wealth, possessed by greed, engaged in the pursuit of material goods; for those whose supreme desire is worldly prosperity; for those bound by affection for sons and wives; for those lost in the thicket of wrong views; for those beset by various sufferings and fears — through manifold skillful means I become a refuge: namely, by manifesting mountain caves as shelters, by manifesting fruits and roots as food, by manifesting water sources and wells, by manifesting antidotes to cold and heat, by showing the correct path, by the sound of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird's call, by the cooing sound of the king of peacocks, by the luminous form of blazing medicinal herbs, by the radiance of mountain deities. For those who have entered mountain caves, crevices, and chasms, afflicted by various sufferings, for the removal of gloom and darkness, I become a refuge by manifesting level ground. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'Just as I provide protection for these beings who are on the mountains, so may I become a refuge for those who have fallen from the mountain precipices of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who are seized by the demons of old age and death.' For beings entangled in the net of dense forests too, on a night of darkness and gloom, amid vast trees of sensory objects with various attendants, whose paths are blocked by diverse grasses, water, thorns, trees, and creepers, who have entered the dense tangles of various trees and vines, whose hearts are terrified by the roaring sounds of tigers, whose minds are agitated by the incompletion of their tasks, who are beset by various fears and calamities, who do not know the direction of escape from the dense forest — I become one who shows them the correct path. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I liberate from all sufferings those beings who have entered the thicket of various wrong views, who are entangled in the net of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), who are beset by the sufferings and fears of the manifold <s>saṃsāra</s>.' For beings who have entered the wilderness too, who have fallen into darkness, having generated comfort for them through various skillful means, having shown them the path, having established them in safety and security, I generate the aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I liberate from all sufferings those beings who have entered the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who have taken the paths of evil destinies, and establish them on the path of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), in ultimate safety and security.' O son of good family, for beings who are attached to countries and provinces, who experience the suffering arising from clinging, whom I rouse from that attachment to their provinces through various means of arousing urgency, I generate the aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I dislodge all beings from clinging to the abode of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and establish them in the knowledge of <s>sarvajña</s> (the omniscient one), which is without abode.' O son of good family, for beings who dwell in villages, bound by the fetters of homes and dwellings, on a night of darkness and gloom, suffering from various domestic misfortunes, whom I rouse through manifold means of creating urgency, and whose minds I cause to feel spiritual urgency, whom I gather through the gift of wealth, whom I properly gratify and establish in the <s>dharma</s> that is without fixed abode, I generate the aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I dislodge all beings who are dependent on the village of their own sense-bases from the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s> courses and sensory fields, and establish them in the domain of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).'

body.text:
ye ca kulaputra andhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrāvekaikaśaḥ pūrvādidigvidikṣu sarvadiksaṃmūḍhā bhavanti, sameṣu pṛthivīpradeśeṣu viṣamaprapātasaṃjñinaḥ, unnateṣvavanatasaṃjñinaḥ, avanateṣūnnatasaṃjñinaḥ, teṣāmahaṃ digmārgadeśasaṃmūḍhānāṃ nānāvidhairupāyairavabhāsaṃ kṛtvā niṣkramitukāmānāṃ dvāraṃ saṃdarśayāmi / gantukāmānāṃ mārgaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / taritukāmānāṃ tīrthaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / praveṣṭukāmānāṃ bhavanaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / vilokayitukāmānāṃ diśaḥ saṃdarśayāmi / nimnonnate pṛthivītalaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / samaviṣamān pṛthivīpradeśān vividhāni ca rūpagatāni saṃdarśayāmi / mārgākrāntānāṃ grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṃ saṃdarśayāmi / gharmatṛṣārtānāmutsasarohradataḍāgapuṣkariṇīnadīvanodyānārāmaramaṇīyāni saṃdarśayāmi / priyaviprayogotkaṇṭhitānāṃ mātāpitṛputradāramitrāmātyajñātisālohitān vividhāni ca manāpāni rūpagatāni saṃdarśayāmi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - yathāhameṣāṃ sattvānāmandhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrau timiropahatanetrāṇāṃ diksaṃmūḍhānāmālokaṃ karomi, avabhāsaṃ janayāmi vividharūpagatavijñaptaye, evamevāhaṃ dīrghasaṃsārarātrāvupapannānāṃ sarvadiksaṃmūḍhānāmavidyāndhakāraprāptānāmajñānapaṭalāvanaddhajñānacakṣuṣāṃ saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyastānām anitye nityasaṃjñināṃ duḥkheduḥkhasaṃjñināṃ anātmani ātmasaṃjñinām aśubhe śubhasaṃjñināṃ dṛḍhātmasattvajīvapoṣapudgalagrahasaṃniśritānāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanasaṃniśritānāṃ hetuphalasaṃmūḍhānāmakuśalakarmapathadikpratipannānāṃ prāṇātipātināmadattādāyināṃ kāmamithyācāriṇāṃ mṛṣāvādināṃ paiśunyānāṃ pāruṣikāṇāmasaṃbhinnapralāpināmabhidhyālūnāṃ vyāpannacittānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭigatānāmamātṛjñānāmapitṛjñānāmaśrāmaṇyānāmabrāhmaṇyānāmanindyajñānāmapuruṣajñānānāmadharmarāgaraktānāṃ viṣamalābhābhibhūtānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭidharmaparītānāṃ tathāgatānabhyākhyāyikānāṃ dharmacakrāntavādapratipannānāṃ māradhvajadharāṇāṃ bodhisattvaghātināṃ mahāyānavidveṣikāṇāṃ bodhicittavicchindikānāṃ
bodhisattvavivarṇakānāṃ mātṛghātadrohiṇāmanapakāravairiṇāmāryāpavādakānāmasatpuruṣādharmasamācāragocarāṇāṃ staupikasāṃghikavastudrohiṇāṃ mātāpitṛvipratipannānāmānantaryakarmakāriṇāṃ mahāprapātābhimukhānāṃ sattvānāṃ mahāprajñālokena avidyāndhakāraṃ vidhūya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpya samantabhadreṇa mahāyānena daśabalajñānabhūmimārgaṃ saṃdarśayeyam / tathāgatabhūmimapi tathāgataviṣayamapi sarvajñajñānanayasāgaramapi buddhajñānagocaramapi buddhaviṣayamapi daśabalapariniṣpattimapi buddhadhāraṇībalamapi sarvabuddhaikaśarīratāmapi saṃdarśayeyam / saṃdarśya cainān sarvabuddhasamatājñāne pratiṣṭhāpayeyam //
body.translated_text: O son of good family, for those who on a dark and gloomy night, one by one, have become completely confused about direction in the eastern and other cardinal and intermediate directions; who on level ground perceive precipitous drops, who on elevated ground perceive depressions, who on low ground perceive elevations — for those confused about direction, path, and region, having created illumination through various means, I show the door to those wishing to go out, I show the path to those wishing to travel, I show the ford to those wishing to cross, I show the dwelling to those wishing to enter, I show the directions to those wishing to look around, I show the terrain both low and high, I show even and uneven regions of the earth and various forms and destinations, I show villages, cities, market towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals to those traveling on the road, I show springs, lakes, ponds, reservoirs, lotus pools, rivers, forests, gardens, parks, and delightful places to those tormented by heat and thirst, I show mothers, fathers, sons, wives, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen, and various pleasing forms and destinations to those anguished by separation from loved ones. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'Just as I create light for these beings on the dark and gloomy night, whose eyes are impaired by darkness, who have lost their sense of direction, and produce illumination for the cognition of various forms and destinations — even so may I, for those born into the long night of <s>saṃsāra</s>, completely confused about direction, plunged into the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), whose eye of knowledge is covered by the film of <s>ajñāna</s> (nescience), who are perverted in perception, thought, and view — perceiving permanence in the impermanent, suffering in suffering, self in what is without self, purity in what is impure; who cling to firm grasping of self, being, life-force, nourisher, and person; who depend on the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); who are confused about cause and effect; who have taken the direction of unwholesome courses of action; who kill living beings, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsehood, engage in slander, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter; who are covetous, of malicious mind, who hold wrong views; who do not honor mothers, who do not honor fathers, who do not honor ascetics, who do not honor brahmins, who do not honor the venerable, who do not honor the worthy; who are attached to unrighteous desires, who are overwhelmed by unjust gains, who are surrounded by the doctrines of wrong views, who slander the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who follow doctrines opposed to the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), who bear the banner of <s>Māra</s>, who harm <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who despise the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who destroy the <s>bodhicitta</s> (aspiration for awakening), who disparage <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who harbor enmity against mothers, who are hostile without cause, who slander the noble ones, whose conduct follows the ways of the wicked, who betray <s>stūpa</s> and <s>saṃgha</s> property, who have turned against their parents, who commit the deeds of immediate retribution, who face the great precipice — for these beings, may I, with the great light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), dispel the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), inspire them toward supreme perfect awakening, and through the great vehicle of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, show them the path to the stage of the knowledge of the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten Powers). May I also show them the stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the ocean of the method of <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), the scope of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, the perfection of the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten Powers), the power of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>, and the unity of all <s>Buddhas</s> in one body. And having shown them these, may I establish them in the knowledge of equality with all <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: glānānāmapyahaṃ kulaputra sattvānāṃ dīrghavyādhiparikhinnānāṃ durbalaśarīrāṇāṃ jīrṇānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ jarābhibhūtānāmanāthānāṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ ca daridrāṇāṃ vilayagatānāṃ videśaprāptānāṃ vidikpratipannānāṃ bandhanagatānāṃ kāraṇāprāptānām aparādhināṃ rājabandhotsṛṣṭānāṃ jīvitoparodhabhayaparitrāṇāya avatiṣṭhāmi / sāhaṃ kulaputra glānānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvopāyairvyādhyapanayanāya pratipadyāmi / jīrṇānāṃ jarābhibhūtānāmupasthānaparicaryopakaraṇāvighātaiḥ saṃgrahaṃ karomi / anāthānāṃ sattvānāṃ sānāthyaṃ karomi / kṛpaṇadaridrāṇāṃ dhanakanakaskandhena saṃgrahaṃ karomi
body.translated_text: O son of good family, for beings who are ill, exhausted by long illness, with weakened bodies; for the aged, the old, those overcome by old age; for the helpless, the wretched, the destitute; for those who have fallen into ruin, who have reached foreign lands, who have gone in the wrong direction; for those in bondage, those who have come to trial, offenders, those condemned by the king — I stand ready for the protection of their lives from the fear of death. O son of good family, I apply myself to the removal of illness for sick beings through every means. For the aged who are overcome by old age, I give support through unhindered provision of nursing, attendance, and supplies. For helpless beings, I provide protection. For the wretched and destitute, I give support through heaps of wealth and gold.

body.text: vinipātagatānāṃ samānārthatayā saṃgrahaṃ karomi / videśaprāptānāṃ svadeśamupanayāmi / vidikpratipannānāṃ samyagdiśamupanayāmi / bandhanagatān bandhanebhyo vipramokṣayāmi / kāraṇāprāptānāṃ kāraṇāduḥkhebhyo vipramokṣayāmi / aparādhino rājavadhyotsṛṣṭān jīvitāśvāsaprāptān karomi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - yathāhameṣāṃ sattvānāṃ vividhabhayopadravaparitrāṇe pratiśaraṇaṃ bhavāmi, evamahametānanuttareṇa dharmasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhya sarvakleśebhyaḥ parimocayeyam / jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ samatikrāmayeyam / sarvadurgativinipātabhayebhyaḥ parimocayeyam / kalyāṇamitraparigrahe pratiṣṭhāpayeyam / dharmaratnadānasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhṇīyām / anavadye karmaṇi niyojayeyam / tathāgataśarīraviśuddhaye samādāpayeyam / atyantājarāmaraṇadhātuprativedhe pratiṣṭhāpayeyam //
body.translated_text: For those who have fallen into ruin, I give support by sharing their purpose. For those who have reached foreign lands, I lead them back to their own land. For those who have gone in the wrong direction, I lead them to the right direction. Those in bondage I release from their bonds. For those who have come to trial, I release them from the sufferings of prosecution. Those offenders condemned by the king I cause to gain the breath of life. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'Just as I become a refuge for these beings in protection from various fears and calamities, even so, having gathered them through the supreme gathering of the <s>Dharma</s>, may I liberate them from all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), cause them to transcend birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, liberate them from the fears of all evil destinies and downfalls, establish them in the care of spiritual friends, gather them through the gift of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, engage them in blameless action, inspire them toward the purification of the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and establish them in the realization of the realm of ultimate freedom from old age and death.'

body.text: mithyāmāgārgatipannānāmapyahaṃ kulaputra sattvānāṃ vividhadṛṣṭigatagahanābhiniviṣṭānāṃ mithyāsaṃkalpagocarāṇāṃ viṣamakāyavāṅbhanaskarmasamudācāriṇāmasaṃvṛtacāriṇāṃ nānāvratatapaḥsaṃniśritānāmasamyaksaṃbuddhe samyaksaṃbuddhasaṃjñināṃ samyaksaṃbuddhe ca asamyaksaṃbuddhasaṃjñināṃ śarīrātāpanaparitāpanaprayuktānām utsasarohradataḍāganadīparvataprasravaṇadigvidikpraṇāmaparāyaṇānāṃ pāpamitravaśagatānāṃ nānopāyamukhaiḥ pratiśaraṇabhūtā bhavāmi / tata etān pāpakād dṛṣṭigatāt sarvadurgatiprapātapathādvinivartayāmi / laukikāyāṃ ca samyagdṛṣṭau pratiṣṭhāpya divyamānuṣikāyāṃ saṃpattau saṃniyojayāmi / evaṃ ca cittamutpādayāmi - yathāhametān sattvānevaṃrūpādviṣamapratipattiduḥkhātparimocayāmi, evamahaṃ sarvasattvānārye lokottare pāramitāmārge pratiṣṭhāpya sarvajñatāyāmavaivartyān kṛtvā samantabhadreṇa mahāpraṇidhānena sarvajñatāyāmupanayeyam / na ca bodhisattvabhūmeruccaleyamavinivartya sarvasattvadhātum //
body.translated_text: O son of good family, for beings who have entered the path of wrong courses, who are plunged into the thicket of various wrong views, whose domain is wrong intention, who engage in crooked conduct of body, speech, and mind, who are of unrestrained conduct, who resort to various vows and austerities, who perceive a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> as not perfectly awakened and one not perfectly awakened as a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, who are devoted to tormenting and burning the body, who are given to bowing down to springs, lakes, ponds, rivers, mountain streams, and the cardinal and intermediate directions, who are under the power of evil friends — I become a refuge through manifold skillful means. From those evil wrong views, from all the paths leading to the precipice of evil destinies, I turn them back. Having established them in mundane right view, I engage them in divine and human prosperity. And thus I generate the aspiration: 'Just as I liberate these beings from such suffering of wrong practice, so may I establish all beings on the noble, supramundane path of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), make them irreversible in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), and through the great vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, guide them toward <s>sarvajñatā</s>. And may I not waver from the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage until I have turned back every single being.'

body.text: atha khalu vāsantī rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣadiśaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānā buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, at that moment, the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>, displaying even more extensively this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation-door called 'the means of training the world through the radiance of <s>Dharma</s> that scatters the darkness of all beings,' surveyed the ten directions through the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, and addressed the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: For the sake of dispelling the darkness of delusion and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), for the generation of the radiance of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: kālamavekṣya jagatsukhanetā eṣa vimokṣanayo mama śāntaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: observing the right time, the guide to the happiness of the world — this is my peaceful liberation-method. [verse 1]

children.text: maitri mamā vipulā suviśuddhā kalpa ananta subhāvita pūrve /
children.translated_text: My <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is vast and perfectly pure, cultivated through innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) in the past,

children.text: apāya pharitva prabhāsami lokaṃ eta nayottara sudhana sudhīrā // 2 //
children.translated_text: Having pervaded the unfortunate realms, I illuminate the world — this is the supreme method, O <s>Sudhana</s>, O wise one! // 2 //

body.text: karuṇasamudra mamāmita loke saṃbhavu yatra triyadhvajinānām /
body.translated_text: My ocean of compassion is boundless in the world, arising wherever the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) of the three times [appear];

body.text: yena jagasya dukhaṃ praśamemī eta nayottara sudhana sudhīrā // 3 //
body.translated_text: by which I pacify the suffering of beings — this is the supreme method, O <s>Sudhana</s>, O wise one! // 3 //

children.text: lokasukhānyabhinirharamāṇā saṃskṛta ārya sukhāni ca yāni /
children.translated_text: Bringing forth the happiness of the world, and whatever noble pleasures of the conditioned there are,

children.text: prīti udagra pramodami tena otara eta nayaṃ jinaputra // 4 //
children.translated_text: I rejoice with exalted joy and delight thereby — descend into this method, O son of the <s>Jina</s>! // 4 //
Ever turned away from the faults of the conditioned, and from the fruits of <s>śrāvaka</s>-knowledge and liberation,

children.text: buddhabalaṃ pariśodhayamānā otara eta nayaṃ jinaputra // 5 //
children.translated_text: purifying the powers of the <s>Buddha</s> — descend into this method, O son of the <s>Jina</s>! // 5 //

children.text: cakṣu mamā vipulaṃ pariśuddhaṃ yena daśaddiśi paśyami kṣetrā /
children.translated_text: My eye is vast and purified, by which I see the fields in the ten directions,

children.text: teṣu ca kṣetrataleṣu svayaṃbhūn paśyami bodhidrumendraniṣaṇṇān // 6 //
children.translated_text: and upon those field-surfaces I see the Self-Arisen Ones seated beneath the kings of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees. // 6 //
Adorned with marks, the <s>Buddha</s>-bodies, releasing rays of various and variegated splendor,
with hair-pores releasing oceans of rays — I see thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> with their assemblies. // 7 //

children.text: teṣu ca kṣetrapatheṣu ya sattvāḥ sarvacyutīupapattimukheṣu /
children.translated_text: In those field-paths, whatever beings [dwell], at the gateways of all deaths and rebirths,

children.text: paśyami te gatisāgari bālāḥ saṃsaramāṇa svakarmanubhonti // 8 //
children.translated_text: I see them — childish ones in the ocean of destinies, wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, experiencing the fruits of their own <s>karma</s>. // 8 //

children.text: srotasamudra mamātiviśuddho yatra samosari śabda aśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: My ocean of hearing is supremely pure, wherein all sounds converge without remainder;

children.text: sarvajagasya ya mantrasamudrā sarva śruṇitva dharemi smṛtīye // 9 //
children.translated_text: whatever are the oceans of sacred speech of all beings — hearing all, I retain them in mindfulness. // 9 //
Adorned with sounds in all voice-forms, etymologies, and utterances, incomparable,

children.text: yo hi pravartati cakru jinānāṃ taṃ ca śruṇitva dharemi smṛtīye // 10 //
children.translated_text: whatever wheel the <s>Jinas</s> set turning — hearing it, I retain it in mindfulness. // 10 //

body.text: ghrāṇabalaṃ vipulaṃ suviśuddhaṃ dharmasamudranayeṣu asaṅgam /
body.translated_text: My power of smell is vast, well-purified, unattached in the methods of the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: sarvavimokṣavihārapraveśaṃ otara eta nayaṃ jinaputra // 11 //
body.translated_text: entering the abode of all liberations — descend into this method, O son of the <s>Jina</s>! // 11 //

children.text: jihva mamā vipula suprabhūtā tāmratanū ratanābha viśuddhā /
children.translated_text: My tongue is vast, most abundant, copper-bodied, jewel-radiant, purified,

children.text: yāya jñapemi yathāśaya sattvān otara eta nayaṃ jinaputra // 12 //
children.translated_text: by which I make known to beings according to their dispositions — descend into this method, O son of the <s>Jina</s>! // 12 //
My <s>Dharma</s>-body is supremely purified, established universally throughout all three times;
my form-body beings shall see according to their dispositions, through the power of their aspiration. // 13 //
My mind is unattached, free from outflows; my voice-sound is like the roar of thunder-clouds;

children.text: tatra samosari sarvanarendrān no ca vikalpana vidyati mahyam // 14 //
children.translated_text: therein converge all lords of humans, yet no conceptual distinction exists for me. // 14 //

children.text: kṣetrataleṣu acintiya sattvāḥ teṣa prajānami cittasamudrān /
children.translated_text: In the field-surfaces, inconceivable beings — I know the oceans of their minds;

children.text: indriyaāśaya jānami teṣāṃ no ca vikalpana vidyati mahyam // 15 //
children.translated_text: I know their faculties and dispositions, yet no conceptual distinction exists for me. // 15 //

children.text: ṛddhi mamo vipulā susamāptā kampayi kṣetra acintiyāya /
children.translated_text: My supernatural power is vast, well-accomplished; I cause inconceivable fields to tremble;

children.text: kāyaprabhāya prabhāvatu yeno sarva sudurdama sattva damemi // 16 //
children.translated_text: by the splendor of my bodily radiance, I tame all beings difficult to tame. // 16 //

children.text: puṇya mamo vipulaṃ pariśuddhaṃ akṣayakoṣa samantaviyūham /
children.translated_text: My merit is vast, purified, an inexhaustible treasury of universal array,

children.text: yena pravartayi pūja jinānāṃ bhoti ca sarvajagatyupajīvyam // 17 //
children.translated_text: by which I set in motion the worship of the <s>Jinas</s>, and it becomes the sustenance of all the world. // 17 //

children.text: prajña mamo vipulā suviśuddhā yāya prajānami dharmasamudrān /
children.translated_text: My wisdom is vast, well-purified, by which I comprehend the oceans of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: saṃśaya chindami sarvajanānāṃ otara eta nayaṃ jinaputra // 18 //
children.translated_text: I cut the doubts of all people — descend into this method, O son of the <s>Jina</s>! // 18 //

children.text: buddhasamudra ahaṃ avatīrṇā sarvi triyadhvi nayottaramānā /
children.translated_text: I have descended into the ocean of <s>Buddhas</s>, leading [beings] to the supreme method in all three times;

children.text: teṣu ca otaramī praṇidhānaṃ eṣa nayo atulaḥ susamāptaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: and into them I descend with vows — this method is incomparable, well-accomplished. // 19 //

children.text: sarvaraje ahu kṣetrasamudrān paśyami caiva triyadhvapraveśān /
children.translated_text: In all atoms I see the oceans of fields, and I see the entries into the three times;

children.text: tatra ca paśyami buddhasamudrā teṣa samantatalaṃ nayabhūmim // 20 //
children.translated_text: and therein I see the oceans of <s>Buddhas</s>, and their universal surface — the ground of method. // 20 //

children.text: paśya virocana bodhivibuddhaṃ sarvadiśāsu spharitvana kṣetrā /
children.translated_text: Behold <s>Vairocana</s>, awakened to <s>Bodhi</s>, having pervaded the fields in all directions,
upon the kings of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees on every atom-path, releasing the ultimate <s>Dharma</s>. // 21 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vāsantīṃ rātridevatāmetadavocat - kiyacciraṃ saṃprasthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? kiyacciraṃ pratilabdhaśca te 'yaṃ vimokṣaḥ, yasya pratilambhāttvamevaṃrūpayā sattvārthakriyayā pratyupasthitā? evamukte vāsantī rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - bhūtapūrvaṃ jinaputra atīte 'dhvani sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa praśāntaprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūtpañcabuddhakoṭīśataprabhavaḥ / tatra ratnaśrīsaṃbhavā nāma lokadhāturabhūt / tasyāṃ khalu punarlokadhātau ratnacandrapradīpaprabhā nāma madhyamā cāturdvīpikā / tasyāṃ padmaprabhā nāma rājadhānī / tatra rājadhānyāṃ sudharmatīrtho nāma rājābhūt dhārmiko dharmarājā cakravartī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / sa tāmakaṇṭakāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ sasāgaragiriparyantāṃ dharmeṇābhinirjitya adhyāvasati sma //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son spoke thus to the night goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>: 'How long ago, O goddess, did you set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening? And how long ago did you obtain this liberation, upon obtaining which you are present with this kind of activity for the welfare of beings?' Thus addressed, the night goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Once upon a time, son of the <s>Jina</s>, in the past, beyond a number of <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, in [a world-realm called] <s>Praśāntaprabha</s> (Tranquil Radiance),

body.text: tasya sudharmatīrthasya rājño dharmamaticandrā nāma bhāryābhūt / sā rātryāḥ pūrve yāme madanamattā ratikrīḍāpariśrāntā madhyame yāme 'ntaḥpuramadhyagatā prasuptā / atha tasyāḥ padmaprabhāyā rājadhānyāḥ pūrveṇa śamathaśrīsaṃbhave mahāvanaṣaṇḍe sarvadharmanigarjitarājo nāma tathāgataḥ sarvavyūhaprabhāmaṇirājaśarīre sarvabuddhavikurvitaprabhave mahābodhivṛkṣe 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / tenāsau sarvo ratnaśrīsaṃbhavo lokadhāturanekavarṇayā udārayā prabhayā sphuṭāvabhāsito 'bhūt / tasyāṃ ca padmaprabhayāṃ rājadhānyāṃ suviśuddhacandrābhā nāma rātridevatā abhūt / sā tāṃ dharmamaticandrāṃ rājabhāryāmupasaṃkramya ābharaṇasaṃghaṭṭanaśabdena prabodhya evamāha - yatkhalu rājapatni jānīyāḥ - śamathaśrīsaṃbhave mahāvanaṣaṇḍe sarvadharmanigarjitarājo nāma tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / sā tasyā rājabhāryāyāḥ purato vistareṇa buddhaguṇavarṇaṃ buddhavikurvitaṃ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaṃ ca saṃprakāśayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: there was a king of that <s>Sudharmatīrtha</s> whose wife was named <s>Dharmamaticandā</s>. She, in the first watch of the night, wearied by intoxicated play and amorous sport, in the middle watch fell asleep in the interior of the palace. Then, to the east of the royal capital <s>Padmaprabhā</s>, in the great forest-grove called <s>Śamathaśrīsaṃbhava</s> (Born of the Glory of Tranquility), a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja</s> (King of the Roaring of All Dharmas), at the great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree called <s>Sarvavyūhaprabhāmaṇirājaśarīra</s> (Body of the King of Jewels of the Radiance of Universal Array), at <s>Sarvabuddhavikurvitaprabhava</s> (Arising from the Transformations of All Buddhas), attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: sā khalu punaḥ kulaputra rājabhāryā tathāgataprabhāvabhāsitādhyāśayenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitā / tasya tathāgatasya sabodhisattvaśrāvakasaṃghasya mahāntaṃ pūjāsatkāramakārṣīt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena dharmamaticandrā nāma rājabhāryā abhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena dharmamaticandrā nāma rājabhāryā abhūvam //
body.translated_text: That queen, son of good family, with her higher aspiration illuminated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s splendor, set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. She performed great worship and honor for that <s>Tathāgata</s> together with his assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>. What do you think, son of good family — was that queen named <s>Dharmamaticandrā</s> at that time someone other [than me]? It should not be seen thus. I was at that time that queen named <s>Dharmamaticandrā</s>. //

body.text: sā ahaṃ kulaputra tenābhilāṣikeṇa cittotpādena tena ca tathāgatāvaropitena kuśalamūlena sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kalpairna jātu durgatiṣūpapannā / na narake, na tiryagyonau preteṣu vā, na jātu hīnakuleṣūpapannā / na jātvindriyavikalābhūvam / na jātu duḥkhitābhūvan / sadā ahaṃ deveṣu devamāhātmyaṃ pratilabhya manuṣyeṣu ca manuṣyamāhātmyaṃ na jātu kalyāṇamitravirahitā abhūvaṃ yaduta buddhabodhisattvaiḥ / na jātu viṣameṣu kāleṣūpapannā / sā khalvahaṃ kulaputra buddhānubuddheṣu kuśalamūlānyavaropayamāṇā sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān sukhena śamena kṣemeṇa mārgeṇa āgatā / na ca tāvanme bodhisattvendriyāṇi pariniṣpannāni //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, through that aspirational mind-generation and through that root of merit planted under that <s>Tathāgata</s>, for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, was never born in unfortunate destinies — not in hell, not in the animal realm or the <s>preta</s> realm; I was never born in low families; I was never deficient in faculties; I was never afflicted. Always, among <s>devas</s> I obtained divine greatness, and among humans I obtained human greatness. I was never separated from spiritual friends — that is, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: teṣāṃ sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāmatikrāntānāmito bhadrakalpātpūrvaṃ daśānāṃ kalpasahasrāṇāṃ prathamastena kālena aśokavirajo nāma kalpo 'bhūt rajovimalatejaḥśrīnāmni lokadhātau / sa khalu punaḥ kulaputra rajovimalatejaḥśrīrlokadhātuḥ kliṣṭaviśuddho 'bhūt pañcabuddhotpādaśataprabhavaḥ / teṣāṃ khalu punaḥ pañcānāṃ buddhaśatānāṃ prathamaḥ sumerudhvajāyatanaśāntanetraśrīrnāma tathāgato loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / ahaṃ ca prajñāvabhāsaśrīrnāma śreṣṭhidārikā abhūvaṃ vighuṣṭakīrteḥ śreṣṭhino duhitā abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā / sā ca suviśuddhacandrābhā rātridevatā praṇidhānavaśena virajovatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau vicitradhvajāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ viśuddhanetrābhā nāma rātridevatā abhūt / tayā me rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ śayitayormātāpitrostadgṛhaṃ kampayitvā udāreṇāvabhāsena svarūpaṃ saṃdarśya buddhaguṇavarṇaṃ bhāṣitvā sa tathāgataḥ prathamasaptāhābhisaṃbuddho bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaḥ saṃdarśitaḥ / sā ahaṃ sārdhaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ mahatā ca jñātisaṃghena tāṃ suviśuddhacandrābhāṃ rātridevatāṃ puraskṛtya tasya tathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkrāntā / tato mayā tasya tathāgatasya udārāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā sahadarśanena jagadvinayabuddhadarśanaprabhavo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tryadhvatalajñānāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśca nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya pratilambhānmayā te sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ kalpā anusmṛtāḥ / tacca me bodhicittamāmukhībhūtam / tayā me tasya tathāgatasyāntikāddharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā eṣa sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukho nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya pratilambhāddaśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃllokadhātūn kāyena spharāmi / ye
body.translated_text: After those <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s> had passed, before this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Auspicious Aeon), at the beginning of ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>, at that time there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Aśokaviraja</s> (Sorrowless and Stainless) in a world-realm named <s>Rajovimalatejaḥśrī</s> (Glory of the Radiance of Stainless Dust). That world-realm <s>Rajovimalatejaḥśrī</s>, son of good family, was of impure-pure [nature], the source of five hundred <s>Buddha</s>-arisings. Of those five hundred <s>Buddhas</s>, the first was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sumerudhvajāyatanaśāntanetraśrī</s> (Glory of the Peaceful Eye of the Abode of the Sumeru-Banner) who arose in the world.

body.text: ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatāḥ, te sarve mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / teṣāṃ ca pādamūlagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānāmi / ye ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvā upapannāḥ, te 'pi sarve mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / teṣāṃ ca rutavimātratāsaṃketaṃ prajānāmi / cittāśayendriyādhimuktīśca prajānāmi / pūrvāntakalyāṇamitreṣu ca paripākaṃ prajānāmi / yathāśayasaṃtoṣaṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kāyamādarśayāmi //
body.translated_text: and whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s> [dwell] in those world-realms, they all come within the range of my vision. And I recognize myself as being present at their feet. And whatever beings are born in those world-realms, they all come within the range of my vision. And I comprehend the signs of their various utterances. And I comprehend their minds, dispositions, faculties, and aspirations. And I comprehend the ripening [they have received] from spiritual friends in the past. And I display my body to them in a way that satisfies them according to their dispositions. //

body.text: sa ca me vimokṣaḥ praticittakṣaṇaṃ vivardhate / tadvimokṣacittānantareṇa cittena lokadhātuśataparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi kāyena spharāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena lokadhātusahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi kāyena spharāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena lokadhātuśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi kāyena spharāmi / evaṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi kāyena spharāmi / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tathāgatāḥ, sarve te mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / teṣāṃ ca pādamūlagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānāmi / yā ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā, tāṃ sarvāmudgṛhṇāmi, dhārayāmi saṃpradhārayāmi upadhārayāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ pūrvayogasamudrān praṇidhānasamudrānavatarāmi / yā ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ, tāmapi ca sarvāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhaye 'bhinirhārāmi / ye ca sattvāsteṣu lokadhātusamudreṣūpapannāḥ, te 'pi sarve mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / yatpramāṇāśca teṣāṃ sattvānāmāśayendriyādhimuktibhedāḥ, tatpramāṇabhedaṃ kāyamadhitiṣṭhāmi yaduta eṣāṃ paripākavinayamupādāya / evaṃ praticittakṣaṇameṣa vimokṣo vivardhate dharmadhātuprasaraspharaṇavivardhanayogena / etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvatamovikiraṇadharmāvabhāsajagadvinayamukhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamanantamadhyasamantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhiniryātānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dharmadhātusāgaranayaprasarapraveśavaśavartināṃ sarvabodhisattvasamudāgamajñānavajraketusamādhivikrīḍitānāṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatavaṃśasaṃdhāraṇamahāpraṇidhānaniryātānāṃ sarvalokadhātuprasaracittakṣaṇapariśodhanamahāpuṇyasāgarapariniṣpannānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmadhātuparipākavinayajñānavaśavartināṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvasarvāvaraṇamahāndhakāravidhamanajñānādityacakṣuṣāṃ sarvasattvadhātumahāyānavijñapanavikramāṇāṃ sarvajagatkāṅkṣāvimativicikitsātimiravidhamanamaticandrāṇāṃ sarvabhavasamudrābhiniveśoccalanaviśuddhaghoṣasvaramaṇḍalānāṃ sarvadharmadhāturajaḥpathi vikurvitasaṃdarśanavaśavartināṃ tryadhvatalajñānamaṇḍalāsaṃbhinnānāṃ caryāṃ jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum, gocaro vā avatartum, vimokṣavikrīḍitaṃ vā saṃdarśayitum //
body.translated_text: And that liberation of mine expands with each moment of thought. With the mind-moment immediately following that liberation-mind, I pervade with my body <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) equal in number to the atoms of a hundred world-systems. With the next mind-moment, I pervade with my body buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of a thousand world-systems. With the next mind-moment, I pervade with my body buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of a hundred thousand world-systems. Thus, with each successive mind-moment, I pervade with my body buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible world-systems. And all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in those buddha-fields come within the range of my vision. I perceive myself as present at the feet of each of them. Whatever <s>Dharma</s> teachings those blessed Buddhas give, I grasp them all, retain them, thoroughly retain them, and firmly retain them. I enter into the oceans of former spiritual practices and the oceans of vows of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Whatever purification of buddha-fields those <s>Tathāgatas</s> have achieved, all that I also bring to fulfillment for the purification of buddha-fields. And all the beings born in those oceans of world-systems also come within the range of my vision. To the extent that there are distinctions in the dispositions, faculties, and resolute inclinations of those beings, to that same extent I manifest diverse forms of my body for the sake of their maturation and discipline. Thus, with each mind-moment, this liberation expands through the method of extending and pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). This, O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'the gateway of disciplining the world through the radiance of <s>Dharma</s> that dispels the darkness of all beings,' which I know. How could I possibly know the conduct, speak of the qualities, enter the domain, or display the playful manifestation of liberation of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have gone forth through the vows of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> Bodhisattva that is infinite and without middle, who are masters of entering the expanse of the methods of the ocean of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, who sport in the <s>vajraketu</s> (diamond-banner) <s>samādhi</s> of the knowledge of the accomplishment of all bodhisattvas, who have gone forth through the great vows of maintaining the lineage of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in all world-systems, who have perfected the great ocean of merit of purifying all world-system expanses in each mind-moment, who in each mind-moment are masters of the knowledge of maturing and disciplining all beings throughout the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, who possess the sun-eye of knowledge that dispels the great darkness of all obstructions of all beings in all world-systems, who exert themselves in making known the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to the entire realm of beings, who are moons of wisdom dispelling the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and hesitation of all the world, who possess a sphere of voice of pure resonance that removes attachment to all oceans of existence, who are masters of displaying magical transformations throughout all the dust-paths of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and whose maṇḍala of knowledge-ground of the three times is undivided?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva magadhaviṣaye bodhimaṇḍe samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā nāma rātridevatā prativasati, yayā ahamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditā, punaḥ punaśca saṃcoditā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family — here in this very region of <s>Magadha</s>, at the site of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), there dwells a night-goddess named <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>, by whom I was first inspired to generate the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment, and by whom I was again and again urged onward. Approach her and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vāsantīṃ rātridevatāmābhigārthābhirabhyaṣṭauṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, praised the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> with these verses of praise:

children.text: paśyami kāyu tavādya viśuddhaṃ lakṣaṇacitritu meru yathaiva /
children.translated_text: I behold your body today, pure, adorned with the marks of excellence, like <s>Meru</s> itself,
Risen above the world, illuminating the world, like <s>Mañjuśrī</s> in glorious form. (22)
Your <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) is supremely pure, equal throughout all three times, free from conceptual elaboration,

children.text: yatra samosari loka aśeṣaḥ saṃbhavate 'tha vibhoti asaṅgam // 23 //
children.translated_text: Wherein the entire world converges — it arises and shines forth, unattached. (23)
I behold in all the expanses of the realms of existence your body manifested and distributed,

children.text: romamukheṣu ca paśyami tubhyaṃ tārakasaṃgha sajyotiṣacandrān // 24 //
children.translated_text: And in your hair-pores I see hosts of stars together with the luminous moons. (24)

children.text: cittu tavā vipulaṃ suviśuddhaṃ yena sphuṭaṃ gaganaṃ va diśāsu /
children.translated_text: Your mind is vast and perfectly pure, by which it pervades space itself in all directions,

children.text: yatra samosari sarvanarendrā jñānamakalpamalaṃ varu tubhyam // 25 //
children.translated_text: Wherein all the lords of beings converge — your excellent knowledge is unconditioned and stainless. (25)

children.text: kṣetrarajopama megha vicitrā niścariṣū tava romamukheṣu /
children.translated_text: Wondrous clouds, numerous as atoms of the fields, issue forth from your hair-pores,

children.text: te ca pharanti daśaddiśi buddhān sarvaviyūha pravarṣayamāṇāḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: And they pervade the Buddhas in the ten directions, raining down all manner of ornamental arrays. (26)

children.text: sarvajagopama kāya anantā niścariṣū tava romamukheṣu /
children.translated_text: Infinite bodies, numerous as all the beings of the world, issue forth from your hair-pores,

children.text: te ca daśaddiśi loku pharitvā nānaupāya viśodhayi sattvān // 27 //
children.translated_text: And having pervaded the world in the ten directions, they purify beings through various skillful means. (27)
In your hair-pores I see inconceivable fields, resplendent with various ornamental arrays,

children.text: ye tvaya śodhita sattvagatīṣu teṣa yathāśayasaṃbhuta sarvān // 28 //
children.translated_text: Which you have purified in the realms of beings — all of them manifested according to their aspirations. (28)

body.text: lābha sulabdha sujīvitu teṣāṃ ye tava nāma śṛṇonti udagrāḥ /
body.translated_text: Well-gained is the gain, well-lived is the life of those who hear your name with joy,

body.text: ye 'tha ca darśanameṣi narāṇāṃ bodhipathābhimukhāśca bhavanti // 29 //
body.translated_text: And those to whom you appear — they become oriented toward the path of enlightenment. (29)

children.text: kalpa acintiya vāsu apāye darśanahetu tavotsahitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the sake of beholding you, one should endure dwelling in the lower realms for inconceivable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: yatti śraveṇa praharṣitacittā darśanamātra śamesi ca kleśān // 30 //
children.translated_text: For by merely hearing of you, minds are filled with delight, and by merely seeing you, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are pacified. (30)
If bodies as numerous as the atoms of thousands of fields were to exist for as many <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: varṇa bhaṇettava romamukhasya varṇakṣayo 'sya bhavenna kadācit // 31 //
children.translated_text: And were to describe the qualities of even a single hair-pore of yours, the description of its qualities would never be exhausted. (31)

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vāsantīṃ rātridevatāmābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya vāsantyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya vāsantīṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya avitṛpta eva kalyāṇamitraparyupāsanena vāsantyā rātridevatāyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 32 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, having praised the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> with these verses, bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing at her again and again, still unsatisfied with attending upon his spiritual friend, departed from the presence of the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>. (32)

body.text: 35 Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā /
body.translated_text: [35 <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>]

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vāsantyā rātridevatāyāḥ prathamasthānabodhisattvacittamaṇḍalapariśuddhimanugacchan, bodhigarbhasaṃbhavamanuvicārayan, bodhisattvapraṇidhānasāgaramavataran, bodhisattvapāramitāmārgaṃ pariśodhayan, bodhisattvabhūmimaṇḍalamavakrāmayan, bodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalaṃ pravistaran, bodhisattvaniryāṇasāgaramanusmaran, sarvajñatāvabhāsamahāsāgaramanuvilokayan, sarvajagatparitrāṇapravaṇabodhisattvamahākaruṇāmeghaṃ vipulīkurvan, vāsantyā rātridevatāyāḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānamaṇḍalaṃ sarvakṣetreṣvaparāntādhiṣṭhānamabhinirharan, yena samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā nāma rātridevatā, tenopasaṃkramya samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya devate, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvo bodhisattvacaryābhūmau carati, kathaṃ niryāti, kathaṃ pariniṣpadyate? āha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya bodhisattvabhūminiryāṇapariniṣpattiṃ pṛcchasi / daśabhiḥ kulaputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ pariniṣpannā bhavanti bodhisattvacaryāyām / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sarvatathāgatasaṃmukhībhāvadarśanasamādhipratilambhaviśuddhyā, sarvabuddhalakṣaṇavicitratānantakāyavyavalokanacakṣurviśuddhayā, anantamadhyatathāgatavarṇasamudravijñaptyavatāreṇa, apramāṇabuddhadharmāvabhāsamaṇḍalasamudrasarvadharmadhātupramāṇāvataraṇatayā, sarvatathāgataromavivarasarvasattvopamaraśmisamudranānāsattvārthaniścaritāvataraṇatayā, ekaikaromavivarasarvaratnavarṇārciḥsamudradarśanatayā, praticittakṣaṇaṃ buddhanirmitasamudrasarvadharmadhātuprasaraspharaṇasatvavinayādhiṣṭhānāvataraṇatayā, sarvasattvasvarāṅgasamudrasaṃprayuktatathāgatanirghoṣasarvatryadhvagatadharmacakranirnāda - nirghoṣasarvasūtrāntameghanigarjitanirghoṣamaṇḍalāvataraṇatayā,
anantamadhyabuddhanāmasamudrāvataraṇatayā, acintyabuddhavikurvitasaṃdarśanasattvavinayāvaraṇatayā / ebhiḥ kulaputra daśabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ pariniṣpannā bhavanti bodhisattvacaryāyām //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, following the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s initial stage mind-maṇḍala as taught by the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s>, contemplating the arising of the essence of enlightenment, entering the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> vows, purifying the path of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), entering the maṇḍala of <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, expanding the maṇḍala of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, recollecting the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> progress, contemplating the great ocean of radiance of omniscience, expanding the great cloud of compassion of the <s>bodhisattva</s> inclined toward the rescue of all the world, and bringing forth in all fields the maṇḍala of the vows of <s>Samantabhadra</s> Bodhisattva's conduct as taught by the night-goddess <s>Vāsantī</s> and its empowerment reaching to the furthest end — approached the night-goddess named <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s> with palms joined, and spoke thus: O noble goddess, I have generated the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment, yet I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> moves on the stages of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how one progresses, how one reaches perfection? She replied: Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you, having generated the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment, ask about the progress and perfection of the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages. Son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with ten qualities become perfected in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. Which ten? Namely: through the purification of attaining the <s>samādhi</s> of seeing face-to-face all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; through the purification of the eye that beholds the infinite bodies adorned with all the marks and signs of the Buddhas; through entering the understanding of the ocean of praises of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who are infinite and without middle; through entering the measure of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> as the maṇḍala-ocean of radiance of immeasurable Buddha-qualities; through entering the emanation of oceans of rays from every hair-pore of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, rays equal in number to all beings, issuing forth for the benefit of various beings; through seeing the ocean of rays of light of all jewel-colors from each and every hair-pore; through entering the empowerment of discipline of beings through the ocean of Buddha-emanations pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> at each mind-moment; through entering the maṇḍala of the resounding proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheels of all three times, united with the ocean of voices and limbs of all beings, the thundering of the clouds of all <s>sūtrāntas</s>; through entering the ocean of names of Buddhas who are infinite and without middle; and through entering the discipline of beings by displaying inconceivable Buddha-transformations. Son of good family, endowed with these ten qualities, <s>bodhisattvas</s> become perfected in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct.

body.text: ahaṃ khalu kulaputra śāntadhyānasukhasamantavikramasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / tasyā mama kulaputra tryadhvaprāptāḥ sarvatathāgatāścakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhimavatarāmi / parṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānapi, anantamadhyasamādhivikurvitasamudrānapi, pūrvayogasamudrānapi, nāmasamudrānapyavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ dharmacakrapravartanavimātratāmavatarāmi / tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanānātvamapi, svarāṅgavimātratāmapi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmanantadharmadhātuśarīratāmavatarāmi / na ca tāṃstathāgatān bhāvato 'bhiniviśāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? agatikā hi te tathāgatāḥ, sarvalokagatiniruddhatvāt / anāgatikā hi te tathāgatāḥ,
body.translated_text: I, O son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Śāntadhyānasukhasamantavikrama</s> (Peaceful Meditation-Bliss Universal Valor). All <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times come within the range of my vision. I enter into the purification of the buddha-fields of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, into the oceans of their assembly-maṇḍalas, into the oceans of their infinite and immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>-transformations, into the oceans of their former spiritual practices, and into the oceans of their names. I enter into the diversity of the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and also into the diversity of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' lifespans and the diversity of their vocal qualities. I enter into the nature of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> as having bodies that are the infinite <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Yet I do not grasp those <s>Tathāgatas</s> as truly existent. For what reason? For those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are without going, since all worldly destinations are ceased. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are without coming, since

body.text: svabhāvāsaṃbhūtatvāt / anutpannā hi te tathāgatāḥ, anutpādadharmatāsamaśarīratvāt / aniruddhā hi te tathāgatāḥ, anutpādalakṣaṇatvāt / asatyā hi te tathāgatāḥ, māyāgatadharmadarśanavijñaptyā / amṛṣā hi te tathāgatāḥ, sarvajagadarthasamutpannatvāt / asaṃkrāntā hi te tathāgatāḥ, cyutyupapattivyativṛttatvāt / avinaṣṭā hi te tathāgatāḥ, dharmaprakṛtyavināśadharmatayā / ekalakṣaṇā hi te tathāgatāḥ, sarvavākpathasamatikrāntatvāt / alakṣaṇā hi te tathāgatāḥ, dharmalakṣaṇasvabhāvaparyavasānatvāt //
body.translated_text: they are unoriginated in their own nature. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are unborn, since their bodies are equal to the nature of non-arising. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are unceasing, since they bear the mark of non-arising. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are unreal, since they are understood through seeing phenomena as illusory in nature. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are not false, since they arise for the benefit of all the world. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are without transference, since they have transcended passing away and rebirth. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are indestructible, since the essential nature of <s>Dharma</s> is by nature indestructible. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> bear a single mark, since they have transcended all paths of speech. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are markless, since they culminate in the own-nature of the marks of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra evaṃ sarvatathāgatānavataramāṇā etaṃ śāntadhyānasukhasamantavikramaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ tathāgatadhyānamaṇḍalāvabhāsena vipulīkaromi, pravistarāmi avatarāmi anugacchāmi samīkaromi abhinirharāmi samatalīkaromi praveśayāmi vivardhayāmi nidhyāyāmi upanidhyāyāmi ākārayāmi gocarīkaromi dṛḍhīkaromi avabhāsayāmi prabhāsayāmi vyūhayāmi vibhajāmi saṃbhārayāmi saṃbhāvayāmi / tatra ca sarvasaṃkalpāsamudācārāyāṃ mahākaruṇāyāṃ sthitvā sarvasattvaparitrāṇasamudācāracittaikāgratāyai prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ bhāvayāmi sarvamanaskarmavyupaśamāya jñānabalaparākramasarvasattvasaṃgrahaprītisukhacittaikāgratāyai / dvitīyadhyānaṃ bhāvayāmi saṃsāravipannopekṣāsarvasattvasvabhāvaviśuddhyāyatanatāyai / tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ bhāvayāmi sarvasattvakleśaduḥkhasaṃtāpapraśamanatāyai / caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ bhāvayāmi sarvajñatāpraṇidhimaṇḍalavipulīkaraṇatāyai sarvasamādhisāgarābhinirhārakauśalyatāyai sarvabodhisattvavimokṣasāgaranayāvataraṇatāyai sarvabodhisattvavikrīḍitajñānābhijñatāyai sarvabodhisattvacaryāvikurvitābhinirharaṇatāyai samantamukhadharmadhātupraveśajñānanayaṃ pariśodhayamānā / evaṃ śāntadhyānamukhasamantavikramaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayāmi //
body.translated_text: Moreover, I, son of good family, thus entering all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, expand this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the universal advance through the bliss of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) by the illumination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dhyāna</s>-maṇḍala — I extend it, enter it, follow it, equalize it, produce it, make it even, cause it to enter, increase it, reflect on it, contemplate it, form it, make it my range, strengthen it, illumine it, make it radiant, array it, analyze it, accumulate it, cultivate it. And standing in great compassion free from all conceptual activity, I cultivate the first <s>dhyāna</s> for one-pointedness of mind in the conduct of protecting all beings, for the pacification of all mental activity. I cultivate the second <s>dhyāna</s> for one-pointedness of mind in the joy and happiness of gathering all beings through the prowess of the power of knowledge. I cultivate the third <s>dhyāna</s> for the base of the purification of the own-nature of all beings through equanimity toward the misfortunes of <s>saṃsāra</s>. I cultivate the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> for the pacification of the affliction-suffering-torment of all beings; for the expansion of the maṇḍala of the vow for omniscience; for the skill of producing the ocean of all <s>samādhi</s>s; for entering the method of the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberations; for the superknowledge of the playful knowledge of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s; for producing the transformations of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — purifying the method of knowledge of entry into the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the universal gate. Thus I cultivate this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the universal advance through the gate of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s>. //

body.text: sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra etaṃ vimokṣaṃ bhāvayamānā nānopāyaiḥ sattvān paripācayāmi yaduta rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ ratipramattānāṃ sattvānāmaśubhasaṃjñāṃ saṃjanayāmi / aratisaṃjñāṃ parikhedasaṃjñāmuparodhasaṃjñāṃ bandhanasaṃjñāṃ rākṣasīsaṃjñāmanityasaṃjñāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñāmanātmasaṃjñāmasvāmikasaṃjñāmaparādhīnasaṃjñāṃ jarāmaraṇasaṃjñām / sarvakāmaviṣayaparibhogeṣvanabhiratisaṃjñāṃ saṃjanayāmi / te ca sattvāstaccittaṃ paribhāvayantaḥ sarvakāmaratiṣvanabhiratā dharmārāmaratiṃ pravārayamāṇā agārādanāgārikaṃ niṣkrāmanti / teṣāmahamaraṇyagatānāṃ dharmeṣvānulomikīṃ śraddhāṃ janayāmi / ārtabhīṣaṇodārasvararavaśabdānantardhāpayāmi / rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ buddhadharmagambhīratāṃ saṃdarśayāmi / prahāṇānukūlaṃ ca pratyayamupasaṃharāmi / niṣkramatāṃ ca agāradvāraṃ vivṛṇomi / mārgaṃ saṃdarśayāmi / ālokaṃ karomi / tamondhakāraṃ vidhamāmi / bhayamantardhāpayāmi / naiṣkramyaṃ saṃvarṇayāmi / buddhavarṇaṃ bhāṣayāmi / dharmavarṇaṃ saṃghavarṇaṃ kalyāṇamitravarṇaṃ bhāṣāmi / kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇaṃ saṃvarṇayāmi //
body.translated_text: Moreover, I, son of good family, cultivating this liberation, ripen beings by various means — namely, when the night is peaceful, for beings intoxicated with pleasure, I generate the perception of the impure, the perception of weariness, the perception of disgust, the perception of obstruction, the perception of bondage, the perception of <s>rākṣasī</s>s (she-demons), the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of ownerlessness, the perception of non-mastery, the perception of old age and death. I generate in them the perception of dissatisfaction with all enjoyments of sense-pleasures. And those beings, cultivating that mind, becoming disenchanted with all sensual delights, letting flow the delight of the pleasure-garden of <s>Dharma</s>, go forth from the household life to homelessness. For those who have gone to the forest, I generate faith conforming to the <s>dharma</s>s. I make terrifying, frightening, and noble sounds disappear. When the night is peaceful, I display the profundity of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>. I provide conditions favorable to abandonment. For those going forth, I open the door of the house. I show the path. I create light. I dispel darkness and obscurity. I make fear disappear. I praise the going forth. I speak in praise of the <s>Buddha</s>, in praise of the <s>Dharma</s>, in praise of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, in praise of spiritual friends. I praise the approaching of spiritual friends. //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra vimokṣaṃ bhāvayamānā sattvānāmadharmarāgaraktānāmadharmarāgasaṃkalpānantardhāpayāmi / viṣamalobhābhibhūtānāṃ mithyāsaṃkalpagocarāṇāṃ tān saṃkalpāṃstān manasikārānantardhāpayāmi /
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, cultivating this liberation, make disappear the unwholesome desire-intentions of beings inflamed by unwholesome desire. For those overwhelmed by crooked greed, whose range is wrong intentions, I make those intentions and those mental activities disappear.

body.text: anutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya utpannānāṃ ca pāpakānāṃ saṃkalpānāmantardhānāya pratyayamupasaṃharāmi / anutpannānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ saṃkalpānāṃ pāramitāsaṃprayuktānāṃ caryāsaṃprayuktānāṃ sarvajñatājñānaniryāṇapraṇidhānābhinirhārasaṃprayuktānāṃ maitrīnayasaṃprayuktānāṃ sarvasattvamahākarūṇāspharaṇasaṃprayuktānāṃ vividhadivyamānuṣyasukhopadhānajananasaṃprayuktānāṃ saṃkalpānāmutpādāya utpannānāṃ ca vividhanayapratyayamupasaṃharāmi / yāvatsarvajñatānulomikānāṃ sarvasaṃkalpānāṃ pratyayamupasaṃharāmi //
body.translated_text: I provide conditions for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, and for the disappearance of arisen evil intentions. I provide conditions of various methods for the arising of unarisen wholesome-root intentions — those connected with the <s>pāramitā</s>s, those connected with conduct, those connected with the production of the vow for the emergence of omniscience-knowledge, those connected with the method of loving-kindness, those connected with pervading all beings with great compassion, those connected with generating the provision of various divine and human happiness — for the arising of unarisen intentions. I provide conditions for all intentions conforming to omniscience. //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra śāntadhyānasukhasamantavikramaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaniryātānāṃ bodhisattvānāmanantākāradharmadhātujñānapratilabdhānāṃ sarvakuśalamūlasaṃvardhitacittānāṃ sarvatathāgatajñānabalacittāvabhāsapratilabdhānāṃ sarvatathāgataviṣayasaṃvasitacittānāṃ sarvasaṃvāsānāvaraṇacittānāṃ paripūrṇasarvajñatāpraṇidhicittānāṃ sarvakṣetrasāgarāvatīrṇacittānāṃ sarvabuddhasāgaradarśanaprasṛtacittānāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanacittānāṃ sarvāvidyāndhakāravidhamanakarāṇāṃ saṃsāraratitṛṣṇākṣayāntakaraṇamārgasarvajñatābhāsasaṃjananacittānāṃ caryāṃ jñātum, guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the universal advance through the bliss of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s> that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattva</s>s who have emerged through the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, who have attained the knowledge of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of infinite aspects, whose minds are nourished by all wholesome roots, whose minds have attained the illumination of the power of the knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, whose minds have dwelt in the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, whose minds are unobstructed in all dwellings, whose minds have fulfilled the vow for omniscience, whose minds have descended into the ocean of all fields, whose minds are extended in seeing the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>s, whose minds receive the cloud of <s>dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, who are rays dispelling the darkness of all ignorance, whose minds generate the light of omniscience on the path that makes an end of the extinction of craving for delight in <s>saṃsāra</s> — to know their conduct or speak of their qualities? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva mamānantaraṃ vairocanabodhimaṇḍe pradakṣiṇena pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā nāma rātridevatā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvakarmasu prayoktavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family — here, immediately next to me, in the <s>Vairocana</s> <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, circumambulating to the right, dwells a night-goddess named <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>. Approach her and ask — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> exert himself in <s>bodhisattva</s>-activities? //

body.text: atha khalu samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva śāntadhyānasukhasamantavikramaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>, at that moment, while displaying to an even greater degree this very <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the universal advance through the bliss of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s>, addressed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, in verses:

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>s, supreme in all times, are to be faced with a mind of devotion;

children.text: teṣu cakṣu vipulaṃ viśudhyate yena otariṣu buddhasāgarān // 1 //
children.translated_text: in them the vast eye becomes purified, by which one enters the oceans of <s>Buddha</s>s. // 1 //

children.text: paśyahī jinaśarīru nirmalaṃ lakṣaṇehi samalaṃkṛtaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: See the stainless body of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), adorned with marks, auspicious;

children.text: tacca paśyahi jine vikurvitaṃ dharmadhātupharaṇaṃ pratikṣaṇam // 2 //
children.translated_text: and see the transformations of the <s>Jina</s>, pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every moment. // 2 //
This <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone), <s>Vairocana</s> (Illuminator), is perfectly awakened upon the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree seat;

children.text: dharmadhātu vipulaṃ spharitvanā cakru vartayi jage yathāśayam // 3 //
children.translated_text: having pervaded the vast <s>dharmadhātu</s>, he turns the wheel in the world according to dispositions. // 3 //

children.text: buddhiyā jinu svabhāvadharmatāṃ niḥśarīra supraśānta advayām /
children.translated_text: Understand the <s>Jina</s>'s own-nature <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) — bodiless, supremely peaceful, non-dual;

children.text: rūpakāyu śubhalakṣaṇaiścitaṃ darśayī jagu pharitva śeṣataḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: he displays the form-body, adorned with auspicious marks, pervading the world without remainder. // 4 //

children.text: buddhakāyu vipulo acintiyo dharmadhātu phari yenaśeṣato /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>-body is vast and inconceivable; it pervades the <s>dharmadhātu</s> without remainder;

children.text: so ca dṛśyati samantataḥ samaṃ sarva darśayi samantato jinān // 5 //
children.translated_text: and it is seen equally from all sides — he shows <s>Jina</s>s universally in all [directions]. // 5 //
Equal to the atoms of all fields, dwelling in the radiance-maṇḍala of the <s>Buddha</s>-body,
displaying to one another beautiful colors — pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every moment. // 6 //
Vast, inconceivable clouds of rays, inexhaustible, issue from the pores of the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: te spharitva jaga sarvaśeṣato kleśatāpa śamayanti prāṇinām // 7 //
children.translated_text: pervading all beings without remainder, they pacify the torment of afflictions. // 7 //
Inexhaustible oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-emanations issue from the pore-maṇḍala of the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: dharmadhātu vipulaṃ spharitvanā durgatīdukha śamenti prāṇinām // 8 //
children.translated_text: pervading the vast <s>dharmadhātu</s>, they pacify the suffering of bad destinies for beings. // 8 //
The sweet <s>Buddha</s>-voice thunders, radiant with the ocean of beautiful sounds, limbs, and cries;

children.text: dharmavarṣa vipula pravarṣaṇo bodhiāśayu janeti prāṇinām // 9 //
children.translated_text: raining forth a vast rain of <s>Dharma</s>, it generates the disposition for awakening in beings. // 9 //

children.text: saṃgṛhīta anena pūrvato kalpasāgara caritva cārikām /
children.translated_text: Gathered by this one in the past, having wandered the pilgrimage through oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s,
they see the <s>Jina</s> <s>Vairocana</s> shining — whose mark is the reflection in all fields. // 10 //
The <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen in the entire world, standing equally face-to-face with all beings;

children.text: anyamanya adhimuktigocaraste na śakyamapi sarvi jānitum // 11 //
children.translated_text: yet the ranges of mutual devotions [of beings] cannot all be known. // 11 //
The excellent <s>bodhisattva</s>s, without remainder, have entered a single pore of the <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: tadvimokṣanaya ye acintiyāste na śakyamapi sarvi jānitum // 12 //
children.translated_text: those inconceivable methods of liberation — they all cannot be known. // 12 //

children.text: eṣa devata mamā anantaraṃ lokanāthabhimukhā pramodate /
children.translated_text: This goddess, next to me, delights in facing the Lord of the World;

children.text: jyotirarcinayaneti nāmato eta pṛccha katha bodhicārikām // 13 //
children.translated_text: named <s>Jyotirarcinetra</s> (Fire-light-eyed) — ask her about the conduct of awakening. // 13 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhāyā rātridevatāyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 33 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, looked back at her again and again, and departed from the presence of the night-goddess <s>Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā</s>. // 33 //

body.text: 36 Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā /
body.translated_text: 36 <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyāveśāviṣṭaḥ kalyāṇamitravacanapratipattisaṃbhūtacittaḥ kalyāṇamitravaidyeṣvāturasaṃjñāsamudācāracittaḥ kalyāṇamitradarśanamanasikārāvikṣiptacittaḥ kalyāṇamitradarśanasarvāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇāvakāśapratilabdhacittaḥ kalyāṇamitradarśanena sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇamahākaruṇānayasāgarāvataraṇapratilabdhacittaḥ kalyāṇamitradarśanena dharmadhātunayasāgarajñānāvabhāsapratilabdhacitto yena pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā nāma rātridevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, entered by the entry into the admonition of the spiritual friend, his mind arisen from the practice of the words of the spiritual friend, his mind generating the perception of illness toward the medicines of the spiritual friend, his mind undistracted from the mental attention of seeing the spiritual friend, his mind having gained the space of scattering the mountains of all obstructions through seeing the spiritual friend, his mind having gained entry into the ocean of the method of great compassion for the protection of the entire realm of beings through seeing the spiritual friend, his mind having gained the illumination of the knowledge of the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> through seeing the spiritual friend — approached the night-goddess named <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>. //
