body.text: atha khalu pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā rātridevatā sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya bhūyasyā mātrayā kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇakuśalamūlasaṃbhārasaṃbhavaparipākamupādāya mahāsaṃbhārasaṃbhavakalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / mahāvikramaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / duravataraṇavīryakarmakalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / suciravilagnaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / anantamadhyadikpraveśaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / dīrghādhvasaṃvasanasaṃbhavaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / anantakāryasaṃpūrṇavijñaptisaṃbhavaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / anantamadhyamārgavyūhasaṃbhārakramaṇaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / samantamukhavikramasaṃbhavaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat / anuccalanāgamanavikramaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇamadhyatiṣṭhat //
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>, to an even greater degree, taking up the ripening of the accumulation of wholesome roots of approaching the spiritual friend for <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that arises from the great accumulation; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend of great advance; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend of the vigorous action that is difficult to enter; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that is long-attached; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend of entry into infinite middle directions; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that arises from dwelling together over long roads; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that arises from the cognition fulfilling infinite tasks; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that courses through the accumulation of the infinite middle path-arrays; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend that arises from the advance of the universal gate; empowered the approaching of the spiritual friend of the advance of coming without moving. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvajñatāsaṃbhāravīryaparākrameṇa kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, mahāpraṇidhānasāgarābhinirhāravikrameṇa kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, ekasattvārthamaparāntakalpāparyantaduḥkhānubhavavyavasitena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, ekaparamāṇurajasi sarvadharmadhātvanucaraṇavilambavikrameṇa mahāvīryakavacavarmaṇā kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, sarvadiksamudraprasarānujavanena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, ekavālapathe aparāntakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvasanena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, bodhisattvacaryāprāptasya praticittakṣaṇaṃ sakalasarvajñatājñānapratiṣṭhānena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, tryadhvaprāptasarvatathāgatavikurvitavyūhamārgākramaṇavyavasitena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, sarvadharmadhātunayasrotaḥprasṛtamārgākrameṇa kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena, sarvadharmadhātunayārambaṇānuccalitena sakaladharmadhātuspharaṇena kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena yena pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā rātridevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, with the approach to spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) characterized by heroic exertion in accumulating provisions for omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), with the approach to spiritual friends characterized by the power of bringing forth an ocean of great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>), with the approach to spiritual friends resolved to endure suffering until the end of future kalpas for the sake of even a single being, with the approach to spiritual friends wearing the armor of great heroic effort that traverses the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> in a single atom of dust, with the approach to spiritual friends that follows the expanse of oceans in all directions, with the approach to spiritual friends that dwells in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct for future kalpas on a single hair-tip path, with the approach to spiritual friends that establishes complete omniscient knowledge at every mind-moment for one who has attained <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, with the approach to spiritual friends resolved to tread the path of the miraculous display-arrays of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, with the approach to spiritual friends that treads the path flowing from the stream of methods of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, with the approach to spiritual friends that pervades the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> without wavering from the support of the methods of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> — approached the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>.

body.text: so 'paśyat pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāṃ rātridevatāṃ bhagavataḥ parṣanmaṇḍale puṣpagarbhasiṃhāsananiṣaṇṇāṃ samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvajaṃ bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpannām / tasyāścāpaśyat sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ sarvasattvābhirocanāṃ sarvasattvābhirucitāṃ sarvasattvadarśanānukūlāṃ sarvasattvapriyadarśanavividhadānādipāramitācaryābhidyotanameghānniścaramāṇan yaduta sarvasattvayathāśayavijñaptisamarutadānacaryāsaṃdarśanameghān sarvasattvānugrahāvigrahāya sarvavastvanavekṣaṇatāyai sarvasattvasamaprayogāparityāgitāyai sarvasattvasamacittatāyai sarvasattvāvimānanāparityāgatāyai ādhyātmikabāhyasarvavastuparityāgitāyai
body.translated_text: He beheld the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> seated upon a flower-core lion-throne in the assembly circle of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Samantabhadra</s>-joy-vast-pure-velocity-banner.' And from every hair-pore of her body he beheld clouds issuing forth that illuminated the practice of various <s>dāna</s> (giving) and other <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) practices — delightful to all beings, conforming to the sight of all beings, and pleasing to behold for all beings — namely, clouds displaying the practice of giving that matched the speech and aspirations of all beings, for the benefit and non-harm of all beings, for non-attachment to any possessions, for not abandoning equal effort toward all beings, for equanimity of mind toward all beings, for not abandoning non-contempt toward all beings, for the relinquishment of all internal and external possessions,

body.text: mahāduṣkaraparityāgasaṃdarśanatāyai sarvaloke yathāśayasattvadānacaryāsaṃdarśanatāyai tryadhvaprāptabodhisattvācintyaduṣkaracaryāparityāganirmāṇameghānniścaritvā daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuprasaraparyāpannānāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ vijñaptimāgacchato 'paśyat yadutācintyabodhisattvavṛṣabhitāvikurvitapratilābhena //
body.translated_text: for displaying the relinquishment of great and difficult sacrifices, for displaying the practice of giving to beings according to their aspirations throughout all worlds — and having issued forth clouds of miraculous emanations displaying the inconceivable difficult conduct and relinquishment of <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the three times, he beheld them reaching the cognition of all beings in all world-realms pervading the ten directions, through the attainment of the miraculous powers of inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> excellence.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ sarvasattvasamāpannānaupapattinirmāṇakāyameghānniścaritvā sarvalokadhātuparyāpannān sarvasattvān spharitvā abhimukhaṃ sarvavratasamādānākampyatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān sattvadhātusamaṃ nānātapovratamaṇḍalamudyotayamānān sarvasarvalokaniśrayatāṃ sarvaviṣayānavekṣatāṃsarvasaṃsārasaṃvāsavimukhatāṃ divyamānuṣasaṃpattivipattisukhasamavasaraṇatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān aśubhamaṇḍalamudyotayamānān, śubhasaṃjñāviparyāsaṃ loke vinivartayamānān, anityacalavyayapariṇāmadharmatāṃ paridīpayamānān, duḥkhānātmasarvasaṃskāradharmatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, tathāgataviṣayasaṃvāsāvipravāsatāṃ rocayamānān, atyantatathāgataśīlapariśuddhaye sattvān samādāpayamānān, sarvasattvayathāśayarutaśīlacaryāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvasaṃtoṣaṇaśīlasugandhikatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having issued forth clouds of emanation-bodies born into the same states of existence as all beings, and having pervaded all beings throughout all world-realms, he beheld them displaying face-to-face the unshakability of undertaking all vows, illuminating maṇḍalas of various ascetic practices equal to the realm of beings, displaying non-reliance on all worldly things, non-regard for all sense objects, aversion to dwelling in all <s>saṃsāra</s>, equanimity toward the fortune and misfortune and happiness of divine and human states, illuminating the maṇḍala of the impure (<s>aśubha</s>), turning back the perversion of the perception of the pure (<s>śubha</s>) in the world, illuminating the nature of impermanence, instability, decay, and transformation, displaying the nature of suffering and non-self in all conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāra</s>), proclaiming the inseparability from dwelling in the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, urging beings toward the ultimate purification of <s>Tathāgata</s> morality (<s>śīla</s>), displaying the practice of moral conduct in speech according to the aspirations of all beings, displaying the fragrance of morality that satisfies all beings — he beheld them maturing all beings.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca sarvasattvadhātusamāpannān nānāvarṇātmabhāvanirmāṇameghānniścaritvā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgacchedādhivāsanatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvakāyotpīḍanopakramaṇādhivāsanatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvāsatyavacanākrośaparibhāṣaṇakutsanapaṃsanatāḍanatarjanādhivāsanatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvākṣobhyatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān sarvasattvasatkārānunnāmāvanāmatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvanirabhimānatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvadharmasvabhāvakṣāntyakṣayatākṣayajñānatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvasarvakleśaprahāṇāya kṣānticaryāṃ saṃdarśayamānān sarvasattvānāṃ, visaṃsthitadurvarṇāśrayaśarīratāṃ vyāvartayamānān sarvasattvānāmanuttarāṃ tathāgatavarṇaviśuddhiṃ saṃvarṇayamānān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having issued forth clouds of emanation-bodies of various colors equal to the entire realm of beings, he beheld them displaying the endurance of the cutting of all limbs and minor limbs for all beings, displaying the endurance of oppression and assault upon the bodies of all beings, displaying the endurance of false speech, reviling, abuse, reproach, censure, beating, and threats from all beings, displaying imperturbability toward all beings, displaying neither elation nor dejection at honor or dishonor from all beings, displaying freedom from pride toward all beings, displaying the inexhaustible knowledge of patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, displaying the practice of patience for the abandonment of all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of all beings, turning beings away from bodies of ugly form and ill-complexioned support, praising the unsurpassed purification of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s radiance for all beings — he beheld them maturing beings.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca sarvasattvasamānnānāvarṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhān nānopapattikasattvakāyanirmāṇameghānniścārya yathāśayān sattvān spharitvā sarvajñatāmahāsaṃbhāravīryaparākramatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvamārakalivikiraṇavīryatāṃ bodhyārambhākṣobhyāvivartyavīryatāṃ sarvasattvasaṃsārasāgarottāraṇavīryatāṃ sarvākṣaṇāpāyadurgativinipātapathavinivartanavīryatāmajñānaparvatavikiraṇavīryatāṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāparikhedavīryatāṃ sarvabuddhadharmacakrasaṃpratīcchanasaṃdhāraṇavīryatāṃ sarvāvaraṇaparvatanirbhedanavikiraṇavīryatāṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayāparikhedavīryatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanavīryatāmanuttarāṃ tathāgatavīryaviśuddhiṃ saṃdarśayamānān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having sent forth clouds of emanation-bodies of beings born in various states with various colors, forms, heights, and proportions equal to all beings, and having pervaded beings according to their aspirations, he beheld them displaying heroic exertion in the great accumulation of provisions for omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), displaying the power to scatter all <s>Māra</s>'s conflicts, the power of unshakable and irreversible vigor in the undertaking of enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>), the power of vigor to ferry all beings across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the power of vigor to turn beings back from the paths of inopportune births, evil destinies, and woeful states, the power of vigor to scatter the mountains of ignorance, the power of unwearying vigor in worshipping and attending all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the power of vigor to receive and retain the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel turning of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the power of vigor to penetrate and scatter the mountains of all obstructions (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), the power of unwearying vigor in maturing and disciplining all beings, the power of vigor to purify all <s>Buddha</s>-fields — displaying the unsurpassed purification of <s>Tathāgata</s> vigor — he beheld them maturing beings.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca nānāvarṇasaṃsthānān vividhātmabhāvanirmāṇameghānniścaritvā nānopāyaiḥ sattvānāṃ prītiṃ saṃjanayamānān, daurmanasyaṃ vinivartayamānān, sarvakāmaratiṃ vijugupsamānān, hrīdharmatāṃ loke prabhāvayamānān, guptendriyatāyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, anuttarabrahmacaryaṃ
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having issued forth clouds of emanation-bodies of various colors and forms, he beheld them generating delight in beings through various means, turning back despondency, inspiring disgust for all sensual pleasures (<s>kāma</s>), manifesting the quality of moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) in the world, establishing beings in the guarding of the sense-faculties, praising the unsurpassed holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>),

body.text: saṃvarṇayamānān, sabhayaṃ kāmalokamāraviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, vigatakāmaratīnāmapi sarvalokakāmarativiṣayaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, dharmārāmaratyāṃ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānān, anupūrvadhyānasamādhisamāpattisukhānyabhinirharamāṇān, sarvasattvasarvakleśanidhyapticittatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvabodhisattvasamādhisamudravikurvaṇatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, bodhisattvābhijñāvikurvitavṛṣabhitāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sattvānāṃ prītiṃ saṃjanayamānān, prāmodyamutpādayamānān, daurmanasyaṃ vyāvartayamānān, cittakalyatāmāvahayamānān, cittakarmaṇyatāṃ kurvāṇān, āśayaṃ viśodhayamānān, indriyāṇyuttāpayamānān, kāyasukhaṃ saṃjanayamānān, dharmaprītivegaṃ vivardhayamānān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: displaying the fearful realm of <s>Māra</s> of the desire-world (<s>kāmaloka</s>), displaying the domain of sensual pleasure in all worlds even to those free from attachment to sensual pleasures, establishing beings in delight in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>, producing in sequence the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment), praising the state of mind intent on abandoning all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of all beings, displaying the miraculous powers of the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>, displaying the excellence of <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and miraculous powers, generating delight in beings, producing joy, turning back despondency, bringing about well-being of mind, making the mind pliant, purifying their disposition, kindling their faculties, generating bodily happiness, increasing the force of delight in the <s>Dharma</s> — he beheld them maturing beings.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca sarvopapattisadṛśaśarīrānnānākāyameghānniścaritvā sarvakṣetragatasarvasattvābhimukhābhirucitadarśanatāyai sarvakalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇāparikhedatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvācāryagurukalyāṇamitropasthānaparicaryāparikhedatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravartanasaṃpratīcchanasaṃdhāraṇāparikhedavīryatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvadharmamukhasamudrān pravicinvānān, sarvabuddhasamudrāvatāraṇanayaṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvadharmalakṣaṇasvabhāvanayamabhidyotayamānān, sarvadharmān, samādhidvāraṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvadṛṣṭiparvatanirbhedanaṃ prajñāvajraṃ saṃdarśayamānān, anekacittakṣaṇasamāyogena sarvasattvāvidyāndhakāravidhamanaprajñādityamaṇḍalodāgamaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvaprītisaṃjananatayā sarvajñatāyāṃ sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having issued forth clouds of various body-emanations with forms resembling all states of existence, for the purpose of appearing in a manner pleasing and face-to-face to all beings in all fields, he beheld them displaying unwearying approach to all spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), displaying unwearying attendance and service to all teachers, elders, and spiritual friends, displaying unwearying vigorous reception and retention of the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, investigating all oceans of <s>Dharma</s> gates, praising the method of entering all <s>Buddha</s>-oceans, illuminating the method of the intrinsic nature and characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>, displaying all <s>dharmas</s> as a gateway to <s>samādhi</s>, displaying the vajra of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that penetrates the mountains of wrong views of all beings, displaying the arising of the sun-maṇḍala of the wisdom that dispels the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) of all beings through the conjunction of countless mind-moments — he beheld them maturing beings in omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) through generating delight in all beings.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca sarvajagatsamānudārācintyanānāvarṇavikalpasaṃsthān ātmabhāvanirmāṇameghānniścaritvā yathāśayādhimuktasarvasattvābhimukhasthitān nānārutamantrasaṃskāranirdeśaiḥ sarvalaukikapuṇyābhijñatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvalaukikakṛtyapracārataśca sarvatraidhātukasaṃbhavasaṃdarśanataśca sarvatraidhātukaniḥsaraṇadiksaṃvarṇanataśca sarvadṛṣṭikāntāragahananiḥsaraṇadiksaṃdarśanataśca sarvajñatāmārgaviśeṣatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipathasamatikramaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, saṃskārāsaṃskārānunayapratighānunaye 'pratighānunayatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, saṃsāranirvāṇasukhāsaṃniśritatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, tuṣitabhavanavāsādiparaṃparāgamanāpratiprasrabdhiṃ saṃdarśayamānān, bodhimaṇḍaprasthānābhisaṃbodhāpratiprasrabdhiṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvajñatāyāṃ sattvān paridīpayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore, having issued forth clouds of emanation-bodies of various inconceivable colors, distinctions, and forms equal to all the world — standing face-to-face with all beings according to their aspirations and dispositions — he beheld them displaying, through teachings of various verbal formulas (<s>mantra</s>) and expressions, expertise in all worldly merits, and praising the distinction of the path to omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) through displaying all worldly activities, displaying the arising in all three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>), praising the direction of escape from all three realms, and displaying the direction of escape from the thickets and wilderness of all wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), displaying the transcendence of the paths and stages of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, displaying freedom from attraction and aversion toward both conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, displaying non-reliance on the happiness of either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>, displaying the unrelenting continuity from dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven onward, displaying the unrelenting progress toward the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) and full awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhi</s>) — he beheld them illuminating beings toward omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>).

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānātmabhāvanirmāṇameghānniścaritvā sarvasattvalokābhimukhasthitān samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvadharmadhātuviśuddhiniṣṭhāpraṇidhānavaiśeṣikatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvalokadhātusamudrapariśuddhiṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāpratiprasrabdhiṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmanayasāgarāvatārāpratiprasrabdhiṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ tathāgatabalapraveśāpratiprasrabdhatāṃ
body.translated_text: From every hair-pore — from each single hair-pore — having issued forth clouds of emanation-bodies equal in number to the atoms and dust-particles of all fields, standing face-to-face with all beings in the world, he beheld them praising the vows and conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, praising the distinction of the vow for the ultimate purification of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, praising the purification of all oceans of world-realms at every mind-moment, praising the unrelenting worship and attendance of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, praising the unrelenting entry into the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmas</s> at every mind-moment, praising the unrelenting entry into the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> at every mind-moment,

body.text: saṃvarṇayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvalokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamasarvadharmadhātunayasāgarāvataraṇāpratiprasrabdhīḥ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvakṣetreṣvaparāntādhiṣṭhānakalpasaṃvāsasarvajñatāmārgaviśuddhisaṃprakāśanāpratiprasrabdhatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ tathāgatabalapraveśāpratiprasrabdhatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvatryadhvanayasāgarāvatārāpratiprasrabdhatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, bodhisattvasarvakṣetrarddhivikurvitasaṃdarśanāpratiprasrabdhatāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, bodhisattvapraṇidhānacaryāsaṃdarśanena sarvasattvān sarvajñatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: praising the unrelenting descent into the ocean of methods of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> equal to the atoms and dust-particles of the ocean of all world-realms at every mind-moment, praising the unrelenting manifestation of the purification of the path to omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) through dwelling for future kalpas in all fields through sovereign power, displaying the unrelenting entry into the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> at every mind-moment, displaying the unrelenting entry into the ocean of methods of all three times, displaying the unrelenting manifestation of the miraculous powers and transformations of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all fields — he beheld them establishing all beings in omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) through the display of <s>bodhisattva</s> vow-conduct.

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvajagaccittasamān kāyanirmāṇameghānniścaritvā sarvasattvābhimukhasthitānaparyantaṃ sarvajñatāsaṃbhārabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, abhedyāparyādattāvināśadharmasarvajñatācittabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, avivartyāpratyudāvartyādhiṣṭhānāpratiprasrabdhamanuttarasarvabodhisattvacaryāsamudāgamabalaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasaṃsāradoṣānanulepabalatāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃvarṇayamānān, sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇabalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvakleśamalānanulepakleśabalatāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvakarmāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇabalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvakalpasaṃvāsabodhisattvacaryāparikhedamahākaruṇābalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvabuddhakṣetrasaṃprakampanasaṃkṣobhaṇasarvasattvasaṃpraharṣaṇabalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvamāraparapravādigaṇapramardanabalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃdarśayamānān, mahādharmacakrapravartanajñānabalaṃ loke prabhāvayamānān, sarvasattvān sarvajñatāyāṃ paridīpayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: And from all hair-pores, from each single hair-pore, sending forth clouds of body-emanations equal to the minds of all beings, standing face-to-face with all beings without limit — he saw them displaying the power of the equipment for omniscience, displaying the power of the mind of omniscience whose nature is indestructible, unappropriated, and imperishable, displaying the power of accomplishing all supreme <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct that is irreversible, unturnable, sustained, and unrelaxed, praising the strength of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in being unstained by all the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, displaying the power of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in scattering all the <s>maṇḍalas</s> of <s>Māra</s>, displaying the strength of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in being unstained by the impurities of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), displaying the power of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in scattering the mountains of all <s>karma</s>-obstructions, displaying the power of the great compassion of <s>bodhisattvas</s> that is unwearied in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct throughout the dwelling of all <s>kalpas</s>, displaying the power of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in shaking, agitating, and delighting all beings in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, displaying the power of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in crushing all the hosts of <s>Māra</s> and proponents of rival doctrines, manifesting in the world the power of knowledge in turning the great <s>Dharmacakra</s> — he saw them illuminating all beings toward omniscience. //

body.text: sarvaromavivarebhyaśca ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvajagaccittasamādānānantavarṇakāyanirmāṇasamudremeghānniścaritvā daśadiganantasattvadhātuspharaṇān yathāśayādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryājñānavikramaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvadhātusamudrāvataraṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvacittasamudrāvataraṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvendriyasāgaraparijñājñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvacaryāsamudrāvataraṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvasattvaparipākavinayakālānatikramaṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvadharmadhātvānuravaṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmadhātujñānanayasāgaraspharaṇajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvalokadhātusamudrasaṃvartavivartajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvalokadhātupratiṣṭhānasaṃsthānavyūhavikalpajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, sarvatathāgatapūjāvikurvitopasaṃkramaṇapūjopasthānadharmacakrameghasaṃpratīcchanajñānaṃ saṃdarśayamānān, evaṃ jñānapāramitācaryāsaṃdarśanena sattvānāṃ prītiṃ saṃjanayamānānapaśyat / cittaṃ prasādayamānān prāmodyamutpādayamānān harṣaṃ saṃjanayamānān daurmanasyaṃ vinivartayamānān cittaṃ viśodhayamānān cittakalyatāmāvartayamānān, indriyāṇyuttāpayamānān adhimuktibalaṃ saṃjanayamānān sarvajñatāyāmavaivartyān kurvāṇānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: And from all hair-pores, from each single hair-pore, sending forth ocean-clouds of body-emanations of infinite colors equal to the mental undertakings of all beings, pervading the infinite being-realms in the ten directions — he saw them displaying the heroic advance of the knowledge of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct to beings according to their dispositions and inclinations, displaying the knowledge of descending into the ocean of all being-realms, displaying the knowledge of descending into the ocean of the minds of all beings, displaying the knowledge of thorough comprehension of the ocean of the faculties of all beings, displaying the knowledge of descending into the ocean of the conduct of all beings, displaying the knowledge of not transgressing the proper time for ripening and disciplining all beings, displaying the knowledge of consonance with all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, displaying the knowledge of pervading the ocean of methods of knowledge of all <s>dharmadhātus</s> in each mind-moment, displaying the knowledge of the formation and dissolution of all world-realm oceans, displaying the knowledge of discriminating the foundations, configurations, and arrays of all world-realms, displaying the knowledge of approaching, worshipping, serving, and receiving the clouds of <s>Dharmacakra</s>s of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> through miraculous displays of worship and attendance. Thus, through the display of the conduct of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge, he saw them generating delight in beings — gladdening their minds, producing joy, generating happiness, turning back dejection, purifying the mind, bringing about mental fitness, heating up the faculties, generating the power of resolute faith — he saw them making them irreversible from omniscience. //

body.text: yathā ca pāramitācaryāsaṃdarśanena loke sattvān paripākaṃ vrajato 'paśyat, tathā sarvabodhisattvadharmanigarjanena ye ca pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ prathamacittotpādasaṃbhārāḥ
body.translated_text: And just as he saw her ripening beings in the world through the display of the conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s>, so too through the proclamation of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — those that are the equipment of the first generation of the aspiration-mind of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>

body.text:
kalyāṇamitrārāgaṇaprayogāḥ tathāgatapādamūlopasaṃkramaṇapūjopasthānaprayogāḥ kuśaladharmacaryābhiyogaprayogāḥ, ye ca dānapāramitācaryāduṣkaraparityāgāḥ, śīlapāramitāpariśodhanaprayogāḥ, mahārājyaiśvaryaparivārabhogādhipatyaparityāgābhiniṣkramaṇaprayogāḥ, ye loke duṣkaracaryāmahāvratatapomaṇḍalakṣāntinirhārāḥ, yā bodhisattvavratasamādānaprayogākampyatā, ye bodhisattvadṛḍhasamādānadharmasamudrāḥ sarvasattvadhātuduṣkṛtadurbhāṣitaduścintitādhivāsanaprayogāḥ, kāyikacaitasikapīḍādhivāasanaprayogāḥ, yā sarvakarmāvipraṇāśadharmatākṣāntiḥ sarvadharmādhimuktikṣāntiḥ sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyānakṣāntiḥ, yat sarvajñatārambhaprayogavīryam, yat sarvabuddhadharmapariniṣpādanavīryam, yāḥ sarvavīryapāramitācaryāḥ ye dhyānapāramitāsaṃbhārāḥ dhyānapāramitābhiyogāḥ dhyānapāramitāpariniṣpattiviśuddhicaryāḥ, yāni bodhisattvasamādhipratilābhavikurvitāni, ye samādhimukhasamudrāvatārāḥ, yāni dhyānapāramitācaritāni, ye prajñāpāramitāsaṃbhārāḥ, ye bodhisattvamahāprajñādityamaṇḍalaviśodhananayāḥ, ye mahāprajñāmeghasaṃbhavāḥ, ye prajñānidhānasaṃbhārāḥ, ye mahāprajñāmahāsāgaravyavacāraṇanayaprayogāḥ, ye mahopāyakauśalyanayaprayogāḥ, ye mahopāyakauśalyapariśuddhisaṃprayuktāḥ pūrvayogāḥ, yāni bodhisattvamahāpraṇidhipāramitāśarīrāṇi, yā mahāpraṇidhipāramitāpariniṣpattayaḥ, yāni mahāpraṇidhānapāramitācaritāni, ye mahāpraṇidhānapāramitāsaṃprayuktāḥ pūrvayogāḥ, ye balapāramitāpratilābhamahāsaṃbhārāḥ, ye balapāramitāpratyayāḥ , ye balapāramitānayamahāsāgarāḥ, ye balapāramitānirdeśāḥ,
ye balapāramitāsaṃprayuktāḥ pūrvayogāḥ, ye jñānapāramitānayāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāprayogāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāviśuddhinayāḥ, yā jñānapāramitādiśaḥ, ye jñānapāramitānugamāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāprasarāḥ, yāni jñānapāramitānayasamavasaraṇāni, ye jñānapāramitāvijñaptinayāḥ, yāni jñānapāramitāprasarānusaraṇāni, yāni jñānapāramitāspharaṇāni, ye jñānapāramitāpravistarāḥ, ye jñānapāramitākāyāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāsamudranayāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāpariniṣpattisaṃprayuktāḥ pūrvayogāḥ, ye jñānapāramitācaryāprakārapravicayapraveśasaṃbhavasamudāgamāḥ, ye jñānapāramitāsamavasaraṇanayasaṃprayuktā dharmādharmasaṃgrahadharmajñānānugamāḥ karmajñānānugamāḥ kṣetrajñānānugamāḥ kalpajñānānugamāḥ tryadhvajñānānugamāḥ buddhotpādajñānānugamā buddhajñānānugamā bodhisattvajñānānugamā bodhisattvacittasaṃbhavajñānānugamā bodhisattvavyavasthānajñānānugamā bodhisattvasaṃbhavajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvaprasthānajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvapraṇidhijñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmacakrajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmapravicayajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmasāgaranayajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmasamudrajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmaparivartajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmanidhānajñānānugamāḥ, bodhisattvadharmagatijñānānugamāḥ, ye pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā yāvadanantamadhyārambaṇajñānapāramitāsaṃprayuktā bodhisattvadharmāḥ, tānasyāḥ sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikaromavivaravisṛtanānāvarṇasattvakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / yaduta akaniṣṭhasudarśanasudṛśātapobṛhacchuddhāvāsadevasadṛśakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat /
body.translated_text: — the efforts of attending upon hosts of spiritual friends, the efforts of approaching, worshipping, and serving at the feet of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the efforts of applying oneself to the practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; the difficult renunciations in the conduct of the <s>pāramitā</s> of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>); the efforts of purifying the <s>pāramitā</s> of moral conduct (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>); the efforts of going forth through renunciation of great kingship, sovereignty, retinue, enjoyments, and dominion; the accomplishments of patience through the <s>maṇḍala</s> of austerities and great vows of difficult conduct in the world; the unshakeability in undertaking <s>bodhisattva</s> vows; the oceans of <s>dharma</s> of firm <s>bodhisattva</s> undertaking — the efforts of enduring the evil deeds, evil speech, and evil thoughts of all being-realms, the efforts of enduring bodily and mental affliction; the patience of the non-destruction of all <s>karma</s>, the patience of resolute faith in all <s>dharmas</s>, the patience of contemplation of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; the vigor of initial effort toward omniscience; the vigor of accomplishing all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities; the various conducts of the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor; the equipment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), the application to the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation, the purification-conduct of the accomplishment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation; the miraculous transformations of attaining <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>; the descents into the oceans of <s>samādhi</s>-gateways; the practices of the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation; the equipment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>); the methods of purifying the great sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s great wisdom; the arisings of the clouds of great wisdom; the equipment of the treasury of wisdom; the efforts of the method of navigating the great ocean of great wisdom; the efforts of the method of great skillful means (<s>mahopāyakauśalya</s>); the former practices connected with the purification of great skillful means; the embodiments of the <s>pāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhi</s>); the accomplishments of the <s>pāramitā</s> of great vows; the practices of the <s>pāramitā</s> of great vows; the former practices connected with the <s>pāramitā</s> of great vows; the great equipment for attaining the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers (<s>balapāramitā</s>); the conditions for the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers; the great oceans of the method of the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers; the expositions of the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers; the former practices connected with the <s>pāramitā</s> of powers; the methods of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>); the applications of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the methods of purification of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the directions of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the followings of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the extensions of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the convergences of the method of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the manifestation-methods of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the pursuings of the extensions of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the pervaddings of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the elaborations of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the embodiments of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the ocean-methods of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the former practices connected with the accomplishment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the arisings through entering, investigating, and analyzing the various aspects of the conduct of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge; the followings of the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s> collection connected with the method of convergence of the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge — the followings of <s>karma</s>-knowledge, field-knowledge, <s>kalpa</s>-knowledge, three-times-knowledge, <s>Buddha</s>-arising-knowledge, <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-mind-arising-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-establishment-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-arising-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-setting-forth-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-vow-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>Dharmacakra</s>-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-investigation-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-ocean-method-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-ocean-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-revolution-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-treasury-knowledge, <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>-course-knowledge; the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s> connected with the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge up to the boundless and middleway-less — all the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> — he saw them ripening beings through the emission from her hair-pores, from each single hair-pore, of clouds of being-bodies of various colors. That is to say, he saw them ripening beings through the emission of clouds of bodies resembling those of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods

body.text:
evaṃ bṛhatphalapuṇyaprasavānabhrakadevasadṛśakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / śubhakṛtsnāpramāṇaśubhaparīttaśubhadevasadṛśakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānāpaśyat / ābhāsvarāpramāṇābhaparīttābhadevasadṛśakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / mahābrahmabrahmapurohitabrahmapārṣadadevasadṛśakāyameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāpsarogaṇasadevaputravaśavartidevarājasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāpsarogaṇasadevaputrasunirmitadevarājasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāpsarogaṇasadevaputrasaṃtuṣitadevarājasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāpsarogaṇasadevaputrasuyāmadevarājasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāpsarogaṇasadevaputraśakradevarājasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / dhṛtarāṣṭragandharvarājagandharvaputragandharvakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat /
virūḍhakakumbhāṇḍarājakumbhāṇḍaputrakumbhāṇḍakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / virūpākṣanāgarājanāgaputranāgakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / vaiśravaṇamahāyakṣarājayakṣaputrayakṣakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / drumakinnararājakinnaraputrakinnarakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sumatimahoragendramahoragaputramahoragakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / mahābalavegasthāmagaruḍendragaruḍaputragaruḍakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / rāhvasurendrāsuraputrāsurakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / yamadharmarājayamaputrayamakanyāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sarvamanuṣyendranaranārīdārakadārikāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / evaṃ sarvagatiparyāpannasarvasattvasadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddharṣisadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / vāyvaptejaḥskandhadevatāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / sāgaranadīparvatavanaspatyauṣadhivṛkṣapṛthivīdevatāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / udyānanagarabodhimaṇḍarātridivasagaganadikpādagāminīśarīrakāyikadevatāsadṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat / evaṃ yāvadvajrapāṇisādṛśātmabhāvameghaniścaritān daśa diśaḥ spharitvā dharmadhātunayaprasareṣu sarvasattvasaṃmukhībhāvasthitān sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: Thus, she saw beings being matured through the emanation of body-form clouds resembling the gods of <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit), <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> (Merit-Born), and <s>Anabhraka</s> (Cloudless) heavens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of body-form clouds resembling the gods of <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Universal Beauty), <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> (Immeasurable Beauty), and <s>Parīttaśubha</s> (Limited Beauty) heavens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of body-form clouds resembling the gods of <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant), <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Immeasurable Light), and <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Light) heavens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of body-form clouds resembling the gods of <s>Mahābrahma</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, and <s>Brahmapārṣada</s> heavens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Vaśavartin</s> (Controlling) god-kings together with their hosts of <s>apsaras</s> and <s>devaputras</s>; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Sunirmita</s> (Well-Fashioned) god-kings together with their hosts of <s>apsaras</s> and <s>devaputras</s>; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (<s>Tuṣita</s>) god-kings together with their hosts of <s>apsaras</s> and <s>devaputras</s>; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Suyāma</s> (<s>Yāma</s>) god-kings together with their hosts of <s>apsaras</s> and <s>devaputras</s>; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Śakra</s>, king of gods, together with his hosts of <s>apsaras</s> and <s>devaputras</s>; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, king of <s>gandharvas</s>, together with <s>gandharva</s> sons and <s>gandharva</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, king of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, together with <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> sons and <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, king of <s>nāgas</s>, together with <s>nāga</s> sons and <s>nāga</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, great king of <s>yakṣas</s>, together with <s>yakṣa</s> sons and <s>yakṣa</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Druma</s>, king of <s>kinnaras</s>, together with <s>kinnara</s> sons and <s>kinnara</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Sumati</s>, lord of <s>mahoragas</s>, together with <s>mahoraga</s> sons and <s>mahoraga</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Mahābalavegasthāma</s>, lord of <s>garuḍas</s>, together with <s>garuḍa</s> sons and <s>garuḍa</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Rāhu</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>, together with <s>asura</s> sons and <s>asura</s> maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>Yama</s>, king of <s>dharma</s>, together with <s>Yama</s>'s sons and <s>Yama</s>'s maidens; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling all human lords, men and women, boys and girls; thus she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling all beings included in every destiny; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), and <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers); she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling deities of the wind-element, water-element, and fire-element; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling deities of oceans, rivers, mountains, trees, medicinal herbs, vegetation, and earth; she saw beings being matured through the emanation of self-form clouds resembling deities of gardens, cities, <s>bodhimaṇḍas</s> (seats of awakening), night, day, sky, directions, walking, and the body — thus, extending in all ten directions as far as self-form clouds resembling <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, pervading the expanse of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) methods, she saw beings being matured while standing face-to-face before all beings.

body.text: ye ca pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ prathamacittotpādasaṃbhāramukhāḥ pūrvajanmasamudāgatakuśalacittaparaṃparāvyavacchedanayāḥ, yāni ca bodhicittotpādapraśaṃsāparaṃparānantaryāṇi
body.translated_text: And those which are the gates of the accumulation of first thought-generation of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> (She Who Illumines the World with Joyful Eyes), the methods of unbroken succession of wholesome mind-streams gathered from former births, and which are the unbroken successions of praise for the generation of the thought of awakening

body.text: cyutyupapattiparigrahaparaṃparānantaryāṇi ātmabhāvaparigrahaparaṃparānantaryāṇi nāmacakraparaṃparānantaryāṇi kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇaparaṃparānantaryāṇi buddhotpādārāgaṇaparaṃparānantaryāṇi, dharmapadavyañjanodgrahaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvamārgapratipatticittaparaṃparānantaryāṇi samādhipratilābhaparaṃparānantaryāṇi samādhipratilābhādbuddhadarśanaparaṃparānantaryāṇi kṣetradarśanacakṣuspharaṇaparaṃparānantaryāṇi kalpaparaṃparājñānacakrānantaryāṇi dharmadhātuprativedhajñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi sattvadhātuvyavalokanajñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi dharmadhātunayasāgarāvataraṇaparaṃparācyutyupapattijñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi divyaśrotrapariśuddhipratyavekṣaṇajñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi sarvasattvadhātucittavyavalokanasarasvatyavakrāntimukhaparaṃparānantaryāṇi prathamadivyacakṣuravakrāntimukhaparaṃparānantaryāṇi prathamadivyaśrotravijñaptiparaṃparānantaryāṇi prathamaparasattvacittajñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi prathamātmaparasattvapūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānaparaṃparānantaryāṇi prathamābhāvapratiṣṭhānābhisaṃskārarddhipratilābhapratyayaparaṃparānantaryāṇi maharddhivikramadikspharaṇaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvavimokṣapratilābhaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvavimokṣasāgarācintyanayāvatāraparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvavikurvitaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvavikramaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvākramaparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvasaṃjñāgataparaṃparānantaryāṇi bodhisattvamārgāvatāraparaṃparānantaryāṇi, yāvad yāni pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā bodhisattvasusūkṣmajñānapraveśaparaṃparānantaryāṇi, tāni asyāḥ sarvaromavivarebhyo nirmāṇakāyameghānniścaritvā sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayamānānapaśyat / saṃprakāśayamānān dyotayamānān saṃdarśayamānān udīrayamānān pravibhajamānān pravistaramānān gaṇayato nirdiśyamānān vijñāpayamānān upasaṃharamāṇānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: the unbroken successions of transmigration and rebirth, the unbroken successions of assuming bodily forms, the unbroken successions of the wheel of names, the unbroken successions of approaching spiritual friends, the unbroken successions of devotion to the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the unbroken successions of grasping the words and syllables of the <s>Dharma</s>, the unbroken successions of the mind of practice on the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, the unbroken successions of attaining <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the unbroken successions of seeing <s>Buddhas</s> through attaining <s>samādhi</s>, the unbroken successions of the expansion of the eye that sees <s>buddha-fields</s>, the unbroken successions of the wheel of knowledge of the succession of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), the unbroken successions of the knowledge of penetrating the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), the unbroken successions of the knowledge of observing the realm of beings, the unbroken successions of knowledge of transmigration and rebirth through entering the ocean of methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the unbroken successions of the knowledge of reviewing the purification of the divine ear, the unbroken successions of the gate of entering <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) through observing the minds of all realms of beings, the unbroken successions of the gate of entering the first divine eye, the unbroken successions of communication through the first divine ear, the unbroken successions of the first knowledge of other beings' minds, the unbroken successions of the first knowledge of recollecting one's own and others' former abodes, the unbroken successions of the conditions for attaining the first supernatural power established in non-existence and mental formations, the unbroken successions of the expansion of great supernatural power and prowess in all directions, the unbroken successions of attaining <s>bodhisattva</s> liberations, the unbroken successions of entering the inconceivable methods of the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> liberations, the unbroken successions of <s>bodhisattva</s> miraculous transformations, the unbroken successions of <s>bodhisattva</s> heroic deeds, the unbroken successions of <s>bodhisattva</s> approaches, the unbroken successions of <s>bodhisattva</s> conceptual attainments, the unbroken successions of entering the <s>bodhisattva</s> path — as far as all the unbroken successions of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>'s entry into the most subtle <s>bodhisattva</s> knowledge — she saw all these emanating clouds of transformation bodies from each of her pores, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, illuminating, radiating, displaying, proclaiming, analyzing, elaborating, enumerating, expounding, explaining, and summarizing.

body.text: keṣāṃcidvātamaṇḍalīsaṃkṣobhanirghoṣarutena deśayamānānapaśyat / keṣāṃcidapskandhasaṃkacchananirnādarutena, keṣāṃcijjvalanārcinigarjitarutena, keṣāṃcit sāgaragarjitanirghoṣarutena, keṣāṃcit pṛthivīsaṃkampananirnādarutena, keṣāṃcinmahāparvatarājasaṃghaṭṭanasaṃharṣaṇanirghoṣanirnādarutena, keṣāṃciddevanagarasaṃkampanamadhuranirnādanirghoṣarutena, keṣāṃciddivyavimānasaṃghaṭṭanarutena, keṣāṃciddevendrarutena, keṣāṃcinnāgendrarutena, keṣāṃcidyakṣendrarutena, keṣāṃcidgandhavendrarutena, keṣāṃcidasurendrarutena, keṣāṃcidgaruḍendrarutena, keṣāṃcinmahoragarutena, keṣāṃciddevarutena, keṣāṃcitkinnarendrarutena, keṣāṃcinmanuṣyendrarutena, keṣāṃcidbrahmendrarutena, keṣāṃcidapsaraḥsaṃgītirutena, keṣāṃciddivyatūryasaṃpravādanarutena, keṣāṃcinmaṇirājanirghoṣarutena, keṣāṃcit sarvasattvakāyanānārutaiḥ pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā vimokṣaviṣayaṃ sattvānāṃ prabhāvayamānānapaśyat / evaṃ bodhisattvātmabhāvameghairnānābodhisattvarutaistathāgatanirmāṇakāyameghaistathāgatarutavimātratāsvarāṅganayaiḥ pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā vimokṣaviṣayaṃ saprathamacittotpādasaṃbhavaniṣpattisamudāgamaṃ savimokṣavikrīḍitaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ vijñapyamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: She saw them teaching some through the sound of the roar of wind-circles churning; some through the sound of water-masses crashing together; some through the sound of blazing flames thundering; some through the sound of ocean thunder roaring; some through the sound of the earth shaking and resounding; some through the sound of great mountain kings colliding and grinding together; some through the sweet resounding sound of divine cities trembling; some through the sound of divine palaces striking together; some through the sound of <s>Indra</s>, lord of gods; some through the sound of the lord of <s>nāgas</s>; some through the sound of the lord of <s>yakṣas</s>; some through the sound of the lord of <s>gandharvas</s>; some through the sound of the lord of <s>asuras</s>; some through the sound of the lord of <s>garuḍas</s>; some through the sound of <s>mahoragas</s>; some through the sound of gods; some through the sound of the lord of <s>kinnaras</s>; some through the sound of the lord of humans; some through the sound of the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>s; some through the song of <s>apsaras</s>; some through the sound of divine musical instruments playing; some through the resounding sound of the king of jewels; some through all the various sounds of the bodies of all beings — she saw the domain of liberation of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> being made manifest to beings. Thus, through <s>bodhisattva</s> self-form clouds, through various <s>bodhisattva</s> sounds, through <s>Tathāgata</s> transformation-body clouds, and through the methods of the immeasurable tones of <s>Tathāgata</s> voices, she saw the domain of liberation of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> being made known to all beings, together with the arising, accomplishment, and attainment of her first generation of the thought of awakening, and together with the play of her liberation.

body.text: tasyā ekaikena nirmāṇarūpameghena praticittakṣaṇamanabhilāpyānabhilāpyāni daśadiśi loke buddhakṣetrāṇi viśodhyamānānapaśyat / anantamadhyān sattvasamudrān sarvāpāyaduḥkhebhyo
body.translated_text: Through each single one of her emanated form-clouds, at every moment of thought, she saw inexpressibly inexpressible <s>buddha-fields</s> in the worlds of the ten directions being purified; she saw infinite and boundless oceans of beings being liberated from all the sufferings of the lower realms

body.text: vimocyamānānapaśyat / anantamadhyaṃ sattvadhātuṃ devamanuṣyasaṃpattau pratiṣṭhāpyamānānapaśyat / anantamadhyān sattvasamudrān saṃsārasāgarāduccālyamānānapaśyat / anantamadhyān sattvasamudrān śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpyamānānapaśyat / praticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyān sattvasamudrān daśabhūmāvāvartamānān sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ paśyati sma, śṛṇoti vyavacārayati avacarati pratividhyati nidhyāyati anugacchati anusarati anupraviśati samatayādhitiṣṭhati yaduta pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā acintyasamantabhadraprītivipuladhvajabodhisattvavimokṣavikurvitavṛṣabhitānubhāvena pūrvasabhāgacaritatvāttathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitatvādacintyakuśalamūlaparipākena samantabhadrāyāśca bodhisattvacaryāyā bhājanībhūtatvāt //
body.translated_text: she saw infinite and boundless realms of beings being established in the prosperity of gods and humans; she saw infinite and boundless oceans of beings being lifted out of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence); she saw infinite and boundless oceans of beings being established on the grounds of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones); at every moment of thought, the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s> saw infinite and boundless oceans of beings being turned upon the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) — he heard, investigated, entered into, penetrated, contemplated, followed, pursued, entered, and abided in equanimity — all through the power and majesty of the inconceivable <s>Samantabhadra</s>-joy-vast-banner <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation-play of the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>, because of his similar previous conduct, because of being sustained by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, through the ripening of inconceivable roots of merit, and because of being a vessel for the practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahābodhisattvaprītivegasāgarāvabhāsapratilabdho daśadiktathāgatādhiṣṭhitaḥ pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāṃ rātridevatāmābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭauṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then the young merchant <s>Sudhana</s>, having obtained the illumination of the ocean of joy of the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, sustained by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the ten directions, standing with palms joined before the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s>, praised the night-goddess <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> with these fitting verses:

children.translated_text: You who are well-trained for immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) in the profound <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones),

children.text: daśadiśi loki anupūrvaṃ rūpa yathāśayaṃ jagu pharitvā // 1 //
children.translated_text: pervading the world in the ten directions successively with forms according to beings' dispositions. //1//
Knowing the world to be without self, without protector, illusory, unconscious, and constantly wandering,

children.text: ṛddhyā anekavidha kāyaiśvarya vidarśatva jagu vinesi // 2 //
children.translated_text: through manifold supernatural powers and bodily sovereignty you display and guide the world. //2//
Utterly free from affliction, perfectly peaceful, with a <s>Dharma</s>-body purified in non-duality,
the entire world dependent on duality — you guide it through the thunder of emanation-clouds. //3//

children.text: na ca skandhaāyatanadhātau niśrayu tubhya vidyati kadācit /
children.translated_text: You never have any reliance upon the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), or <s>dhātus</s> (elements),
yet with complete and perfect forms of sovereign splendor and thundering proclamations you guide the world. //4//
Liberated inwardly and outwardly, risen above the ocean born of duality,
you display reflections in the infinite destinies within the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). //5//

children.text: na ca tubhya iñjana kadācinmanyana syandanā na ca prapañcā /
children.translated_text: Never is there any movement for you, nor conceptualization, nor mental flow, nor proliferation,
yet you show the true nature of <s>dharmas</s> to the childish beings delighting in proliferation in the world, and guide them. //6//
With one-pointed mind for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), through dwelling in the ocean of all <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations),
for the purpose of worship you release from your pores clouds of emanations in all directions for the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones). //7//
At every moment you enter the infinite approaches to the powers of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
and you display all the methods of gathering beings, each through its own appropriate entrance. //8//
Having surveyed the ocean of existence, variegated by <s>karma</s>, with manifold forms,
you teach the unobstructed path in the <s>dharmas</s> and purify beings. //9//
Your form is adorned with various marks, purified by the practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>,

children.text: sattvānāmāśayavaśā tvaṃ devata rūpu darśayasi loke // 10 //
children.translated_text: According to the dispositions of beings, O goddess, you display forms in the world. // 10 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāṃ rātridevatāmābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya etadavocat - kiyacciraṃ saṃsthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? kiyaccirapratilabdhaścāyaṃ tvayā devate samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvajo bodhisattvavimokṣa iti //
body.translated_text: Then the youth <s>Sudhana</s>, having praised the night-deity <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> with these verses expressing her nature, spoke thus: "How long have you been established, O goddess, in supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)? And how long ago did you, O goddess, attain this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>) called <s>Samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvaja</s> (Banner of the Vast Pure Force of Samantabhadra's Joy)?"

body.text: atha khalu pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the night-deity <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā</s> addressed the youth <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: I remember past times, many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) beyond those equal to the dust-atoms of world-systems,
A world-system called <s>Maṇiprabhasukhābha</s> (Radiance of Jewel-light and Happiness), and there was an aeon called <s>Praśāntaghoṣa</s> (Tranquil Sound). // 11 //
It was complete with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of ten-thousand four-continent world-systems,
The central four-continent system was wonderfully adorned, measuring as great as <s>Maṇiparvata</s> (Jewel Mountain). // 12 //
It was complete with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of ten-thousand royal capitals,
The central royal capital was delightful, called <s>Gandhadhvajā Maṇiprabhāsā</s> (Fragrance-Banner, Jewel-Radiance). // 13 //
In that city there was a lord of the people, a sovereign <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), of beautiful form,
Endowed with the thirty-two marks, his body adorned with the secondary characteristics. // 14 //
He was born miraculously in a lotus womb, his body of golden color and excellent radiance,

children.text: jambudhvajaṃ sakalu sarva spharati prabhāya so gaganacārī // 15 //
children.translated_text: He pervaded the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (Rose-apple continent) with his splendor, that sky-traveler. // 15 //
His sons were a full thousand, heroic, of excellent limbs and form,

children.text: koṭī amātya paripūrṇā paṇḍita dakṣa viddha medhāvī // 16 //
children.translated_text: A full <s>koṭi</s> of ministers, learned, skilled, knowledgeable, and wise. // 16 //
Ten full <s>koṭis</s> of women, resembling <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), skilled in the arts of love,

children.text: tāḥ sniogdhacitta hitacittā maitramanā upasthihiṣu rājñaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: They were affectionate-minded, benevolent-minded, with friendly hearts, attending upon the king. // 17 //
And that great king of the earth, up to the boundaries of the surrounding <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains,

children.text: catvāra dvīpa susamṛddhā dharmabalena āvasati sarvān // 18 //
children.translated_text: Ruled over all four prosperous continents by the power of <s>dharma</s>. // 18 //
I was the chief queen of the <s>cakravartin</s>, with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, with a graceful body,
Of pure radiance and golden color, I pervaded a thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) with my splendor. // 19 //

children.text: astaṃ gate dinakararaśmi svapiti nṛpe saputraparivāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the rays of the sun had set, the king slept with his sons and retinue,
When the sound of music had subsided, having gone to bed, I was happily asleep. // 20 //

children.text: rātrimadhyamaki yāme buddha utpannu bhū śirisamudraḥ /
children.translated_text: In the middle watch of the night, a <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śirīsamudra</s> (Ocean of Glory) arose in the world,

children.text: tasmin vikurvita anantā darśi jino daśaddiśi pharitvā // 21 //
children.translated_text: He displayed infinite transformations, the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) was seen pervading the ten directions. // 21 //
Those oceans of radiance, honored by <s>Śrī</s> (Glory), equal to the dust-atoms of all world-systems,

children.text: nānāvikurvitaśarīrān yehi pharī diśo daśa aśeṣāḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: With variously transformed bodies, by which he pervaded the ten directions completely. // 22 //

children.text: pṛthivī prakampita saśailā ghoṣa nigarji te jina utpanno /
children.translated_text: The earth trembled with its mountains, a sound thundered forth: "The <s>Jina</s> has arisen!"

children.text: devāsurā manujanāgāḥ sarvi praharṣi te jina utpannaḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>asuras</s> (titans), humans, and <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) — all rejoiced that the <s>Jina</s> had arisen. // 23 //
Oceans of emanations issued from every pore of the <s>Buddha</s>'s body,

children.text: te co daśaddiśi pharitvā loki yathāśaye bhaṇiṣu dharmam // 24 //
children.translated_text: And they, pervading the ten directions, taught the <s>dharma</s> in the world according to beings' dispositions. // 24 //

children.text: tāṃśco vikurvita anantān supini jino nidarśi mama sarvān /
children.translated_text: All those infinite transformations the <s>Jina</s> displayed to me in a dream,

children.text: gambhīra garjita śruṇitvā prīti mamā abhūṣi supinānte // 25 //
children.translated_text: Having heard the profound roar, joy arose in me at the end of the dream. // 25 //

children.text: daśa rātridevatasahasrā upari mama sthitā nabhatalasmin /
children.translated_text: Ten thousand night-deities stood above me in the sky,

children.text: varṇānudīryanta jinasya divyarutena māṃ bhaṇi prabodhya // 26 //
children.translated_text: Proclaiming the virtues of the <s>Jina</s> with divine voices, they spoke to awaken me: // 26 //

children.text: uttiṣṭha devamatibhārye eṣa jinopapanna tava rājye /
children.translated_text: "Arise, O queen of the <s>Deva</s>-king! A <s>Jina</s> has appeared in your kingdom!

children.text: kalpāna sāgaraśatebhi durlabha saṃpaśyan sukhi viśuddho // 27 //
children.translated_text: Difficult to encounter in hundreds of oceans of <s>kalpas</s>, behold the Blissful, Pure One!" // 27 //

children.text: ahu prītisaṃbhuta vibuddhā paśyami ābha nirmala viśuddhām /
children.translated_text: I, born of joy, awakened and saw a radiance, pure and stainless,
Gazing upon this radiance with my eyes, I beheld the <s>Buddha</s> at the king of <s>bodhi</s>-trees. // 28 //
Adorned with the thirty-two marks, oceans of rays streaming from his pores,

children.text: abhyudgato yatha sumeru dakṣiṇavāmato jina samantāt // 29 //
children.translated_text: He rose up like <s>Sumeru</s>, the <s>Jina</s> resplendent on all sides, right and left. // 29 //
Having seen him, in my joyful mind this thought arose: "May I become like this!"

children.text: praṇidhiśca me kṛtu udāro buddhavikurvitaṃ vipula dṛṣṭvā // 30 //
children.translated_text: And I made a noble <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow), having beheld the vast transformations of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 30 //

children.text: pratibodhitaḥ sa maya rājā istrigaṇaśca yo 'sya parivāram /
children.translated_text: I awakened the king and the host of women who were his retinue,

children.text: buddhaprabhā vipula dṛṣṭvā sarvi abhūṣi prīṇitaśarīrāḥ // 31 //
children.translated_text: Having seen the vast radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>, all became filled with joy in body. // 31 //
I approached the presence of the <s>Jina</s> together with my lord, with ten thousand vehicles,
Surrounded by many <s>koṭis</s> and tens of thousands of living beings, with his entire army. // 32 //

children.text: pūjā kṛtā mayi jinasyo varṣasahasra viṃśati anūnā /
children.translated_text: Worship was performed by me to the <s>Jina</s> for a full twenty thousand years,

children.text: niryātitā ratana sapto pṛthivī sasāgarā ca sugatasya // 33 //
children.translated_text: The seven treasures and the earth with its oceans were offered to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). // 33 //
Oceans of <s>sūtras</s> (discourses), clouds of virtues, oceans of <s>praṇidhis</s> (vows), arrays of origination,
All the manifestations of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — he taught according to the dispositions of beings in the world. // 34 //

children.text: sā rātridevata hitārthaṃ bodhayi māṃ tadā karuṇajātā /
children.translated_text: That night-deity, for my benefit, compassion-born, awakened me at that time,

children.text: tasyāṃ mama spṛha utpannā īdṛśa bhūtva bodhayi pramattān // 35 //
children.translated_text: A longing arose in me toward her: "Having become like this, may I awaken the heedless!" // 35 //
This was my first aspiration-mind (<s>praṇidhicitta</s>) that arose toward supreme, foremost awakening,
Though I was traversing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the oceans of existence did not overwhelm me. // 36 //

children.text: daśa buddhakoṭinayutāni ye mama pūjitā janiya śraddhām /
children.translated_text: Ten <s>koṭi</s>-tens of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshiped by me, having generated faith,
While wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> among gods and humans, still craving the pleasures of sensory enjoyments. // 37 //
The first <s>Jina</s> was <s>Śirīsamudra</s> (Ocean of Glory), immediately after him was <s>Guṇapradīpa</s> (Lamp of Virtues),
The third <s>Jina</s> was <s>Ratanaketu</s> (Jewel-Banner), the fourth <s>Buddha</s> was <s>Gaganaprajña</s> (Sky-Wisdom). // 38 //

children.text: jina pañcamaḥ kusumagarbhaḥ ṣaṣṭhu jino asaṅgamaticandraḥ /
children.translated_text: The fifth <s>Jina</s> was <s>Kusumagarbha</s> (Flower-Womb), the sixth <s>Jina</s> was <s>Asaṅgamaticandra</s> (Moon of Unattached Mind),
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmadhātusvaraketu</s> (Banner of the Voice of the Dharma-realm), and the fourth was <s>Dharmasamudragarjana</s> (Roar of the Dharma-Ocean). // 48 //
<s>Racanārciparvatapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Mountain of Ornamental Flames) was the ninth, and the tenth there was <s>Dvipadendu</s> (Moon of the Two-footed Ones),
The tenth was <s>Tryadhvaprabhaghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Radiance of Three Times) — they were all worshiped by me with joy. // 40 //

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā sarvi ta pūjitā naravarendrā /
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those lords among men were worshiped,

children.text: na ca tāva labdha maya cakṣuryeni mamottari nayasamudram // 41 //
children.translated_text: But I had not yet attained the eye by which I might enter the ocean of higher guidance. // 41 //
After that, in all directions, there was a world-system of beings called <s>Sarvaratnābha</s> (Radiance of All Jewels),

children.text: kalpaśca devaśirināmā tatra utpanna buddha śatapañca // 42 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>kalpa</s> was named <s>Devaśirī</s> (Divine Glory); there five hundred <s>Buddhas</s> arose. // 42 //
The first was <s>Śaśimaṇḍalābha</s> (Radiance of the Moon's Orb), the second was <s>Bhāskarapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Sun),
The third <s>Buddha</s> was <s>Jyotidhvaja</s> (Light-Banner), and immediately after him was <s>Maṇisumeru</s> (Jewel-Sumeru). // 43 //
<s>Kusumārcisāgarapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Ocean of Flower-Flames), <s>Jvalanaśirīṣa</s> (Blazing Glory), <s>Devaśirigarbha</s> (Womb of Divine Glory),
<s>Obhāsarāja</s> (King of Radiance), <s>Prabhaketu</s> (Radiance-Banner), and the tenth was <s>Samantajñānaprabharāja</s> (King of the Radiance of Universal Knowledge). // 44 //

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā sarvi ta pūjitā maya narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those lords among men were worshiped by me,
While I delighted in the abode of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), with an understanding of abode in the non-abiding <s>dharma</s>. // 45 //
After that, there came forth a world-system named <s>Dharmapradīpameghaśirī</s> (Glory of the Cloud of the Lamp of Dharma),

children.text: atra lokadhātu suvicitraḥ kalpa tadāsi brahmaprabhanāmā // 46 //
children.translated_text: Here in this wonderfully adorned world-system, the <s>kalpa</s> then was named <s>Brahmaprabha</s> (Radiance of Brahmā). // 46 //

children.text: tasmin jinā aparimāṇāḥ te maya pūjitāḥ saparivārāḥ /
children.translated_text: In that aeon, immeasurable <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) were worshiped by me together with their retinues,

children.text: sarveṣa teṣa sugatānāṃ dharma śruto mi gauravi janitvā // 47 //
children.translated_text: I heard the <s>dharma</s> of all those <s>Sugatas</s>, having generated reverence. // 47 //
The first <s>Jina</s> was <s>Ratanameru</s> (Jewel-Meru), immediately after him was <s>Guṇasamudra</s> (Ocean of Virtues),
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmadhātusvaraketu</s> (Banner of the Voice of the Dharma-realm), and the fourth was <s>Dharmasamudragarjana</s> (Roar of the Dharma-Ocean). // 48 //
<s>Dharmadhvaja</s> (Dharma-Banner), <s>Dharaṇiteja</s> (Splendor of the Earth), <s>Dharmabalaprabha</s> (Radiance of Dharma-Power), <s>Gaganabuddhi</s> (Sky-Intellect),
<s>Dharmārcimeruśikharābha</s> (Radiance of the Peak of the Mountain of Dharma-Flames), and the last among them was named <s>Meghaśirī</s> (Cloud-Glory). // 49 //

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā sarvi ta pūjitā maya narendrā /
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those lords among men were worshiped by me,

children.text: na ca meṣa dharmata vibuddhā yenima otari jinasamudrān // 50 //
children.translated_text: But I had not yet awakened to the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, by which I might enter the ocean of the <s>Jinas</s>. // 50 //
After that there was a <s>Sugata</s> named <s>Sūryapradīpaketuśirī</s> (Glory of the Banner of the Lamp of the Sun),

children.text: kṣetrā sa buddhamati nāmnā tatra abhūcca somaśirikalpaḥ // 51 //
children.translated_text: His world-system was called <s>Buddhamati</s> (Buddha-Mind), and there the <s>kalpa</s> was called <s>Somaśirī</s> (Moon-Glory). // 51 //
In that aeon, eighty tens of thousands of the Ten-Powered Ones were worshiped by me,
With various, infinite, and vast offerings of many delightful kinds. // 52 //
The first was <s>Gandharvarāja</s> (King of the <s>Gandharvas</s>), the second was <s>Buddhadrumarāja</s> (King of the Buddha-Tree),
The third <s>Jina</s> was <s>Guṇasumeru</s> (Virtue-Sumeru), and immediately after him was <s>Ratananetra</s> (Jewel-Eye). // 53 //
<s>Vairocanaprabhaviyūha</s> (Array of <s>Vairocana</s>'s Radiance), <s>Dharmasamudratejaśirī</s> (Glory of the Splendor of the Dharma-Ocean) <s>Buddha</s>,
<s>Lokendratejaśiribhadra</s> (Auspicious Glory of the Splendor of the Lord of the World), and the last was <s>Sarvadharmaprabharāja</s> (King of the Radiance of All Dharmas). // 54 //

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā pūjita te mayā sugata sarve /
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those <s>Sugatas</s> were worshiped by me,

children.text: na tu tāva labdha maya jñānaṃ saddharmasamudra yenavatareyam // 55 //
children.translated_text: But I had not yet attained the knowledge by which I might enter the ocean of the true <s>dharma</s>. // 55 //
After that, there was a supremely pure world-system called <s>Vajramaṇiabhedyadṛḍhateja</s> (Indestructible Firm Splendor of the Diamond-Jewel),
A world-system called <s>Samantaprabhamegha</s> (Cloud of Universal Radiance), wonderfully arrayed in manifold configurations. // 56 //
In which there were many pure beings, of excellent faculties, with <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) diminished,
The <s>kalpa</s> was called <s>Praśāntamatiteja</s> (Tranquil Mind-Splendor), an array of a thousand <s>Buddhas</s> arising therein. // 57 //
The first <s>Jina</s> was <s>Vajiranābhi</s> (Diamond-Navel), the second was <s>Asaṅgabaladhārī</s> (Bearer of Unattached Power),
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsa</s> (Reflection of the Dharma-realm), and <s>Sarvadiśapradīpaprabharāja</s> (King of the Radiance of the Lamp of All Directions). // 58 //

children.text: jinu pañcamaḥ karuṇatejā ṣaṣṭha abhū jino vratasamudraḥ /
children.translated_text: The fifth <s>Jina</s> was <s>Karuṇāteja</s> (Splendor of Compassion), the sixth <s>Jina</s> was <s>Vratasamudra</s> (Ocean of Vows),
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Kṣāntimaṇḍalapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Circle of Patience), the eighth was <s>Dharmamaṇḍalaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of the Dharma-Circle). // 59 //
<s>Obhāsasāgaraviyūha</s> (Array of the Ocean of Radiance), and the last among them was <s>Praśāntaprabharāja</s> (King of Tranquil Radiance),

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā sarvi ta pūjitā maya narendrā // 60 //
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those lords among men were worshiped by me. // 60 //

children.text: na ca meṣa dharmata vibuddhā gaganasamā svabhāvapariśuddhā /
children.translated_text: But I had not yet awakened to the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, equal to space, pure in intrinsic nature,
Abiding in which I might wander, journeying through all the expanses of world-systems. // 61 //
After that, there was a delightful world-system named <s>Gandhapradīpameghaśirī</s> (Glory of the Cloud of the Lamp of Fragrance),
A world-system both defiled and pure, and the <s>kalpa</s> then was called <s>Susaṃbhava</s> (Good Arising). // 62 //
There arose <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Jinas</s> there, by whom that ten-<s>kalpa</s> period was adorned,

children.text: te nāyakā bhaṇiya dharmā so maya dhārita smṛtibalena // 63 //
children.translated_text: Those leaders taught the <s>dharma</s>, which I retained by the power of mindfulness. // 63 //
The first <s>Jina</s> was <s>Vipulakīrti</s> (Vast Renown), then <s>Dharmasamudravegaśirirāja</s> (King of the Glory of the Force of the Dharma-Ocean),
<s>Dharmendrarāja</s> (King of the Lord of Dharma), <s>Guṇaghoṣa</s> (Sound of Virtues), <s>Dharmaśirī</s> (Dharma-Glory), and <s>Devamakuṭa</s> (Diadem of the Gods). // 64 //
The seventh among them was named <s>Jñānārcitejaśirī</s> (Glory of the Splendor of the Flame of Knowledge), then the lord of the two-footed ones,
The eighth <s>Jina</s> was <s>Gaganaghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Sky), the ninth was <s>Samantasaṃbhavapradīpa</s> (Lamp of Universal Arising). // 65 //
And the last <s>Buddha</s> among them was named <s>Ūrṇaśirīprabhāsamati</s> (Mind of the Radiance of the Glory of the <s>Ūrṇā</s>),

children.text: te sarvi pūjita narendrā mārgu na caiṣa śodhitu asaṅgaḥ // 66 //
children.translated_text: All those lords among men were worshiped, yet the unobstructed path had not yet been purified. // 66 //
After that, with excellent arrays, bodies established in jewel-adorned configurations,
The last world-system was well-divided, named <s>Ratnadhvajāgramati</s> (Supreme Mind of the Jewel-Banner). // 67 //

children.text: sārocayaśca tada kalpastatra utpanna buddha śatapañca /
children.translated_text: And the <s>kalpa</s> then was called <s>Sārocaya</s> (Excellent Gathering); there five hundred <s>Buddhas</s> arose,

children.text: te sarvi satkṛta svayaṃbhū eta vimokṣa samabhilaṣatyā // 68 //
children.translated_text: All those Self-Arisen Ones were honored by me, as I aspired for this liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>). // 68 //
The first was named <s>Guṇamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of Virtues), then <s>Śāntanirghoṣa</s> (Peaceful Sound) and <s>Sāgaraśirī</s> (Ocean-Glory),
<s>Ādityateja</s> (Splendor of the Sun), <s>Girirāja</s> (King of Mountains), <s>Lakṣaṇameru</s> (Mark-Meru), <s>Megharutaghoṣa</s> (Sound of Thunder-Clouds). // 69 //
<s>Dharmendrarāja</s> (King of the Lord of Dharma), <s>Guṇarāja</s> (King of Virtues), <s>Puṇyasumeru</s> (Merit-Sumeru), <s>Śāntaprabharāja</s> (King of Tranquil Radiance),

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā sarvi ti pūjitā maya narendrāḥ // 70 //
children.translated_text: With these ten as the foremost, all those lords among men were worshiped by me. // 70 //

children.text: mārgu viśodhitu jinānāṃ yatra samosarī jina aśeṣā /
children.translated_text: The path of the <s>Jinas</s> was purified, where the <s>Jinas</s> without exception entered,

children.text: na ca tāva labdha maya kṣāntiryā imamotare nayu jinānām // 71 //
children.translated_text: But I had not yet attained the <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) by which I might enter this guidance of the <s>Jinas</s>. // 71 //
After that, there was a world-system of beautiful radiance named <s>Śāntanirghoṣahāramati</s> (Mind of the Necklace of Peaceful Sound),
Here this world-system was pure, inhabited by beings of few <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // 72 //
The <s>kalpa</s> was named <s>Sukhābhirati</s> (Delight in Happiness), in which there were eighty tens of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: te sarvi pūjitā maya narendrā mārgu viśodhito jinavarāṇām // 73 //
children.translated_text: All those lords among men were worshiped by me, the path of the excellent <s>Jinas</s> was purified. // 73 //
The first <s>Jina</s> was <s>Kusumarāśi</s> (Heap of Flowers), then <s>Sāgaragarbha</s> (Ocean-Womb) and <s>Saṃbhavagiri</s> (Mountain of Arising),
<s>Devendracūḍa</s>, <s>Maṇigarbha</s>, <s>Kāñcanaparvata</s>, <s>Ratanarāśi</s>, // 74 //

children.text: dharmadhvajo 'tha vacanaśrīḥ paścimu teṣu jñānamati buddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmadhvaja</s>, then <s>Vacanaśrī</s>; the last among them was the Buddha <s>Jñānamati</s>,

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā pūjita te mayā suranarendrāḥ // 75 //
children.translated_text: Having made these ten foremost, those lords of gods and men were worshipped by me. // 75 //
After that there was a field called <s>Sunirmitadhvajapradīpa</s> (Well-Fashioned Banner Lamp),
the <s>kalpa</s> was named <s>Sahasraśiri</s> (Thousand-Splendored); there were <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of Buddhas therein. // 76 //
<s>Śāntadhvaja</s> (Peaceful Banner), <s>Śamathaketu</s> (Tranquility Emblem), <s>Śāntapradīpa</s> (Peaceful Lamp), <s>Meghaśirirāja</s> (Cloud-Glory King),
<s>Obhāsayantaprabharāja</s> (King of Illuminating Radiance), <s>Meghavilambita</s> (Cloud-Suspended), <s>Suriyateja</s> (Sun-Splendored), // 77 //
<s>Dharmapradīpaśiri</s> (Dharma-Lamp Glory), <s>Meruarciśiri</s> (Meru-Flame Glory), and <s>Devaśirigarbha</s> (Essence of Divine Glory),
