children.text: teṣāṃ ca paścimaku āsīt siṃhavinardito vidupradīpaḥ // 78 //
children.translated_text: and the last among them was <s>Siṃhavinardita Vidupradīpa</s> (Lion's Roar, Lamp of the Wise). // 78 //

children.text: etān daśa pramukha kṛtvā pūjita te mayā sugatacandrā /
children.translated_text: Having made these ten foremost, those <s>Sugata</s>-moons were worshipped by me,

children.text: na ca tāva labdha maya kṣāntiryā imamotare nayasamudram // 79 //
children.translated_text: yet I had not attained the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) that would enable entry into this ocean of methods. // 79 //
After that there was a field named <s>Samantābhaśiri</s> (Universal Radiance-Glory),
the <s>kalpa</s> was <s>Anālayaviyūha</s> (Non-Attachment Array); there were twenty-six <s>nayutas</s> of Buddhas therein. // 80 //
The first was <s>Samantaguṇamegha</s> (Cloud of Universal Virtues), immediately after him was <s>Gaganacitta</s> (Sky-Mind),
the Buddha <s>Susaṃbhavaviyūha</s> (Excellent Arising Array), <s>Garjitadharmasāgaranirghoṣa</s> (Thunder-Sound of the Dharma Ocean). // 81 //
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmadhātusvaraghoṣa</s> (Voice-Sound of the Dharma-Realm), <s>Nirmitameghasusvaraśiri</s> (Glory of the Beautiful Voice of Emanated Clouds),
the Buddha <s>Samantadiśateja</s> (Splendor in All Directions), and <s>Dharmasamudrasaṃbhavaruta</s> (Sound Arising from the Dharma Ocean). // 82 //
<s>Guṇasāgara</s> (Ocean of Virtues), <s>Giripradīpa</s> (Mountain Lamp), the ninth was <s>Jinasūrya</s> (Conqueror Sun),
and the last among them, whom I delighted, was <s>Ratanaśirīpradīpaguṇaketu</s> (Jewel-Glory Lamp Virtue-Banner). // 83 //
When that lord of bipeds, <s>Ratanaśiripradīpaguṇaketu</s>, went forth into renunciation,
I was the goddess <s>Śaśivakrā</s>; having worshipped the lord of men as he went forth, // 84 //
he proclaimed to me the <s>Anālayaviyūha Praṇidhisamudrasaṃbhavaviyūha</s> (Non-Attachment Array, Ocean of Vows Arising Array)

children.text: sūtraṃ nigarjasu narendraḥ śrutva mi dhāritaṃ smṛtibalena // 85 //
children.translated_text: <s>sūtra</s>; having heard it, I retained it by the power of mindfulness. // 85 //
I attained the vast <s>cakṣuḥśānta-samādhi</s> (eye-of-peace concentration) and the power of <s>dhāraṇī</s>,
and I behold oceans of <s>Jinas</s> and successions of <s>kṣetras</s> (fields) moment by moment. // 86 //

children.text: jātaṃ hi me karuṇagarbhā maitrinayaṃ samantaprabhamegham /
children.translated_text: There arose in me a womb of compassion, the method of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), a cloud of universal radiance,
a <s>bodhicitta</s> (thought of awakening) like the sky, of immeasurable and vast radiance equal to the power of the Buddhas. // 87 //
Having seen the world in its inversions, attached to notions of permanence, pleasure, and purity,
covered by the darkness of delusion, substance, and ignorance, afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), holding to false perceptions, // 88 //
wandering in the thicket of wrong views, subject to craving, performing uneven <s>karma</s>,
taking on manifold forms in the various realms of existence, painted by the variety of <s>karma</s>, arising again and again, // 89 //
those who, through the openings of death in all realms of existence, are reborn through various births,
experience the affliction of birth, old age, and death, both physical and mental. // 90 //
Then, for the welfare and happiness of those beings, the supreme <s>citta</s> (aspiration) arose in me,
wherever the <s>Daśabalas</s> (Ten-Powered Ones) arise, extending into all fields. // 91 //
Then arose a cloud of <s>praṇidhi</s> (vows), whose womb inclines toward the happiness of all beings,
with infinite arising of the accumulations, following the ocean-methods of the path. // 92 //
A cloud of setting forth with vast radiance, with the force of clear-faced entry into all paths,
releasing vast clouds of <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) throughout the expanse of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma). // 93 //
The progression through the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) with vast momentum, within the ocean-methods of all three times,
moving unattached through the <s>bhūmis</s>, reaching all the <s>Jinas</s> in a single instant. // 94 //

children.text: api cāpyahaṃ sugataputra carya samantabhadra avakrāntā /
children.translated_text: Moreover, O son of the <s>Sugata</s>, I have entered the practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>,
and I descend into the ocean-methods of the ten levels of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // 95 //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena viśāṃpatirnāma rājābhūccakravartī buddhavaṃśānupacchedāya sthitaḥ? na khalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ tena kālena tena samayena viśāṃpatirnāma rājā abhūccakravartī buddhavaṃśānupacchedāya pratipannaḥ / yayā cāhaṃ rātridevatayā prabodhitā, sā samantabhadreṇa bodhisattvena nirmitā / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena bhadramatirnāma cakravartibhāryā abhūt strīratnam? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena bhadramatirnāma
body.translated_text: What do you think, son of good family? Could it be that the one who was the king named <s>Viśāṃpati</s>, the <s>Cakravartin</s> who upheld the unbroken lineage of the Buddhas at that time, was someone else? You should not see it so, son of good family. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> <s>Kumārabhūta</s> was the king named <s>Viśāṃpati</s>, the <s>Cakravartin</s> who practiced to preserve the unbroken lineage of the Buddhas at that time. And the <s>rātridevatā</s> (night-goddess) by whom I was awakened was an emanation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. What do you think, son of good family? Could it be that the one who was the <s>Cakravartin</s>'s wife named <s>Bhadramatī</s>, the jewel among women, at that time was someone else? You should not see it so. I myself was the <s>Cakravartin</s>'s wife named <s>Bhadramatī</s>,

body.text: cakravartibhāryā abhūvaṃ strīratnam / sāhaṃ tayā rātridevatayā pratibodhyaṃ buddhadarśane samādāpitā / iyaccirotpāditaṃ me kulaputra anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / sāhaṃ tena cittotpādena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān na jātu durgativinipāteṣu upapannā / satatasamitaṃ devamanuṣyagatiparāyaṇā / sarvatra ca avirahitā tathāgatadarśanenābhūvam / yāvanme bhagavato ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketostathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sahadarśanādayaṃ samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvajo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya pratilābhādahamevaṃrūpeṇa sarvasattvaparipākavinayārthena pratyupasthitā //
body.translated_text: the jewel among women, at that time. And by that <s>rātridevatā</s> (night-goddess) I was awakened and inspired to behold the Buddhas. It has been this long, son of good family, since I first generated the <s>citta</s> (aspiration) toward supreme perfect awakening. With that generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, throughout <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), I was never once reborn in the lower realms of misfortune. I was constantly destined for the realms of gods and humans. Everywhere I was never separated from beholding the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Until, upon first seeing the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu</s>, I attained this <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Samantabhadra-prīti-vipula-vimala-vega-dhvaja</s> (Banner of the Vast, Pure, Swift Joy of Samantabhadra), upon attaining which I am present in this manner for the purpose of ripening and disciplining all beings.

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvajaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvajñatāprasthānamahāvegasāgarapratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaprasthānamukheṣu pratikṣaṇaṃ mahāpraṇidhānasāgarāvatārāpratiprasrabdhānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvapraṇidhānasāgaranayeṣu aparāntakalpacaryāmaṇḍalābhinirhārakuśalānām, ekaikasyāṃ ca caryāyāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamakāyābhinirhārakuśalānām, ekaikena ca kāyena sarvadharmadhātunayasāgaraspharaṇanām, ekaikasmiṃśca dharmadhātunayasāgare sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu yathāśayasattvakāyavijñapticaryāsaṃdarśanakuśalānām, ekaikasmiṃśca kṣetraparamāṇurajasyanantamadhyatathāgatasamudrāvataraṇakuśalānām, ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya dharmadhātuspharaṇaparamatathāgatavikurvitāvataraṇakuśalānām, ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya dharmadhātuspharaṇaparamatathāgatavikurvitāvataraṇakuśalānām, ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya pūrvāntakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃbhārasaṃbhavasamudāgamāvatārakuśalānām, ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya vimaladharmacakrasaṃpratyeṣaṇasaṃdhāraṇakuśalānāṃ sarvatryadhvatathāgatavikurvitanayasāgarāvataraṇakuśalānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, know this <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Samantabhadra-prīti-vipula-vimala-vega-dhvaja</s>. But how could I describe the conduct and virtues of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, at every moment at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, have attained the great ocean-force of setting forth toward omniscience at every entrance of all settings-forth; who at every moment in every ocean-method of great vows never relax; who at every mind-moment in all the ocean-methods of vows are skilled in accomplishing the maṇḍala of practice for future <s>kalpas</s>; who in each and every practice are skilled in manifesting bodies equal in number to the atoms of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>; who with each and every body pervade the ocean-methods of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>; who in each and every ocean-method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> are skilled in displaying conduct through bodily manifestation according to the dispositions of beings in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>; who in each and every atom of a <s>kṣetra</s> are skilled in entering the ocean of infinite, boundless <s>Tathāgatas</s>; who are skilled in entering the supreme <s>Tathāgata</s> transformations pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>; who are skilled in entering the arising and accomplishment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice-accumulations of the past <s>kalpas</s> of each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>; who are skilled in seeking, comprehending, and retaining the stainless <s>Dharmacakra</s> of each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>; and who are skilled in entering the ocean-methods of the transformative displays of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of all three times?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamanantaraṃ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī nāma rātridevatā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalamavataritavyam, kathaṃ pariśodhayitavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in this very assembly of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, there dwells a <s>rātridevatā</s> (night-goddess) named <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s> (Glory of the Strength that Protects All Beings). Approach her and ask: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> enter the maṇḍala of <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice? How should it be purified?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 34 //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana</s> (Joyful-Eyed World-Illuminator), circumambulated the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon her again and again, and departed from the presence of the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana</s>. // 34 //

body.text: 37 Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: [37. <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>]

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakoḥ tat pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ samantabhadraprītivipulavimalavegadhvajaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamadhimucyamāno 'vataran, adhigacchan praviśan prasaran spharamāṇo 'nugacchan anusaran pratilabhamāno bhāvayan paribhāvayan kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṃ pratipadyamāno 'vavādānuśāsanīnirdeśānantaryatāyai pramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ saṃpreṣaṇānuśāsanīmanusmaran, kalyāṇamitradarśanānugatena sarvendriyamaṇḍalena samantadigabhimukhena kalyāṇamitradarśanapratilābhasamudācāreṇa sarvamānavigatena kalyāṇamitragaveṣaṇamanasikāreṇa mahāsaṃbhārasaṃbhavavyavasitena kalyāṇamitrārāgaṇavikrameṇa kalyāṇamitraikotībhāvagataiḥ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ kalyāṇamitrasarvopāyakauśalyacariteṣvabhedyāśayapratipannaḥ kalyāṇamitrasaṃniśrayasaṃvardhanamahāvīryavegasāgarasaṃjātaḥ sarvakalpakalyāṇamitrasamatānugatasaṃvāsapraṇidhānaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyā antikamupasaṃkrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, entering into, penetrating, comprehending, pervading, following, pursuing, attaining, cultivating, and thoroughly developing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation called <s>Samantabhadra-prīti-vipula-vimala-vega-dhvaja</s> of the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana</s>, practicing the instruction of the spiritual friend, for the sake of uninterrupted exposition of the admonitions and instructions, recollecting the directive instruction of the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana</s>, with all his faculties turned toward all directions through the pursuit of seeing the spiritual friend, with all pride abandoned through the disposition of seeking the spiritual friend, with his mind resolved through the great accumulation arising from earnest seeking of the spiritual friend, with all roots of virtue directed single-pointedly toward the spiritual friend, proceeding with unbreakable intention in all the skillful means and conduct of the spiritual friend, having generated the great ocean-force of vigor that increases reliance upon the spiritual friend, with a vow to abide in equality with the spiritual friend throughout all <s>kalpas</s>, he approached the presence of the <s>rātridevatā</s> <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>.

body.text: tasyopasaṃkrāmataḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī rātridevatā sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśanānantabodhisattvavimokṣavṛṣabhitāsaṃdarśanārthaṃ vicitralakṣaṇānuvyañjanaparaniṣpannakāyaṃ saṃdarśya ūrṇakośātsamantajñānārciḥpradīpavimalajyotidhvajaṃ nāma raśmiṃ prāmuñcadanantamadhyaraśmiparivāram / sa sarvalokamavabhāsya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhni nipatya sarvaśarīramanuspharati sma / samanantaraspṛṣṭaśca sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastena raśminā, atha tāvadeva atyantavirajomaṇḍalaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratyalabhata, yasya pratilābhātpramuditanayanajagadvirocanāyā rātridevatāyāḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyaśca rātridevatāyā mārgāntare yatpṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ tatra yāvanti tejaḥparamāṇurajāṃsi vā apsu paramāṇurajāṃsi vā pṛthivīparamāṇurajāṃsi vā vajraparamāṇurajāṃsi vā vividhamahāmaṇiratnarajaḥparamāṇurajāṃsi vā puṣpagandhacūrṇaparamāṇurajāṃsi vā ratnavyūhaparamāṇurajāṃsi vā sarvārambaṇaparamāṇurajāṃsi vā, teṣu sarveṣu paramāṇurajaḥsu ekaikasmin paramāṇurajasi buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān lokadhātūn saṃvartamānān vivartamānāṃścāpaśyat / sāpskandhān satejaḥskandhān savāyuskandhān sapṛthivīskandhān samalokadhātusattvān sādhiṣṭhānān nānāsaṃsthānān saṃpratiṣṭhānān nānāpṛthivītalavyūhān nānāparvataparivārān nānānadītaḍāgavyūhān nānāsāgaraparisaṃsthānān nānādivyavibhaktibhavanavyūhān nānāvṛkṣasaṃsthānān nānāgaganālaṃkārān, sadevanagarabhavanālaṃkārān sanāganagarabhavanālaṃkārān sayakṣanagarabhavanālaṃkārān sagandharvanagarabhavanālaṃkārān sāsuranagarabhavanālaṃkārān sagaruḍanagarabhavanālaṃkārān, sakinnaranagarabhavanālaṃkārān, samahoraganagarabhavanālaṃkārān, samanuṣyanagarabhavanālaṃkārān, sasarvadigvidigvyavasthānasarvasattvanagarabhavanālaṃkārān, sanarakalokagativiṣayān, satiryagyonilokaviṣayān, sayamalokaviṣayān, samanuṣyagativyavacāracyutyupapattiviṣayān, nānopapattyabhisaṃbhinnān, anantagatibhedasamavasaraṇān / teṣu ca lokadhātuṣu vimātratāmadrākṣīt / yaduta kāṃścillokadhātūna saṃkliṣṭānapaśyat / kāṃścitpariśuddhān, kāṃścidekāntasaṃkliṣṭān,

kāṃścidgatipariśuddhān, kāṃścitsaṃkliṣṭaviśuddhān,
kāṃścidviśuddhasaṃkliṣṭān, kāṃścidekāntapariśuddhān, kāṃścitsamatalapraveśān, kāṃścidavamūrdhapratiṣṭhānān, kāṃścidvyatyastasaṃsthānān, teṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvagatiṣu sarvasattvopapattiṣu samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāṃ prativineyasattvasarvasattvābhimukhāmapaśyat / sarvalokāsaṃbhinnadarśanatayā yathāyuḥpramāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhimuktigocarāṇāṃ yathātmabhāvānāṃ yathātmavacanaprajñaptiniruktisaṃskāravyavahārāṇāṃ yathāprayogānāṃ yathādhipateyānāṃ paripākavinayamupādāya sarvasattvāsaṃbhinnasaṃmukhāvasthitāmapaśyat //

yaduta nānānarakagatiparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāṃ vividhanarakaduḥkhabhayavinivartanatāyai, nānātiryagyonyupapannānāṃ sattvānāmanyonyasaṃbhakṣaṇabhayavinivartanatāyai, yamalokagatiparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣutpipāsādiduḥkhabhayavinivartanatāyai, nāgalokagatiparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvanāgaduḥkhabhayavinivartanatāyai, sarvakāmadhātuparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvakāmadhātukaduḥkhabhayavinivartanatāyai, manuṣyalokagatiparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāmandhakāratamisrāyāṃ rātrau sarvāndhakārabhayavinivartanatāyai, avarṇāyaśokīrtiśabdaślokābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvāyaśokīrtibhayavinivartanatāyai, parṣacchāradyabhayaniviṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ parṣacchāradyabhayavinivartanatāyai, maraṇabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ maraṇabhayavinivartanatāyai, durgatiprapātabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ durgatiprapātabhayavinivartanāyai, ājīvikābhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāmājīvikābhayavinivartanatāyai, kuśalamūlavipraṇāśabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlavipraṇāśabhayavinivartanatāyai, bodhicittasaṃmoṣaṇabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhicittasaṃmoṣaṇabhayavinivartanatāyai, pāpamitrasamavadhānabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ pāpamitrasamavadhānabhayavinivartanatāyai, kalyāṇamitravipravāsabhayabhītānāṃ kalyāṇamitravipravāsabhayavinivartanatāyai, śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmiprapātabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmiprapātabhayavinivartanatāyai, vividhasaṃsārasaṃvāsaduḥkhabhayabhītānāṃ vividhasaṃsāraduḥkhabhayavinivartanatāyai, visabhāgasarvasamavadhānabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ visabhāgasarvasamavadhānabhayavinivartanatāyai, viṣamakālopapattibhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ viṣamakālopapattibhayavinivartanatāyai, viṣamakulopapattibhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ viṣamakulopapattibhayavinivartanatāyai, pāpakarmādhyāpattibhayabhītānāṃ
pāpakarmādhyāpattibhayavinivartanatāyai, karmakleśāvaraṇabhayabhītānāṃ karmakleśāvaraṇabhayavinivartanatāyai, vividhasaṃjñāgataniketabandhanabhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ vividhasaṃjñāgataniketabhayavinivartanatāyai sarvasattvānāmasaṃbhinnasaṃmukhāvasthitāmapaśyat //

yaduta aṇḍajānāṃ sattvānāṃ jarāyujānāṃ saṃsvedajānāmupapādukānāṃ rūpiṇāmarūpiṇāṃ saṃjñināṃ naivasaṃjñināṃ nāsaṃjñināṃ sarvasattvaparitrāṇapraṇidhānabalābhinirhṛtatvāt, vipulabodhisattvasamādhivegavikramabalena bodhisattvamahābhijñābalaparākrameṇa samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhyabhinirhābalena mahākaruṇānayasāgaravegasaṃjātatvāt, sarvajagadapraṇihitamahāmaitrīspharaṇatāyai

sarvasattvasukhasamudayaprītivegavivardhanatāyai sarvasattvasaṃgrahajñānaprayogatāyai vipulabodhisattvavimokṣavikurvitavṛṣabhitāsamanvāgatatvāt, sarvakṣetrapariśodhanābhimukhīmapaśyat / sarvadharmajñānānubodhābhimukhīṃ sarvabuddhapūjopasthānābhimukhīṃ sarvatathāgataśāsanasaṃdhāraṇābhimukhīṃ sarvakuśalopacayābhimukhīṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāvivardhanābhimukhīṃ sarvasattvacittānāvaraṇābhimukhasthitāṃ sarvasattvendriyaparipācanābhimukhasthitāṃ sarvasattvādhimuktisamudraviśodhanābhimukhīṃ sarvasattvāvaraṇīyadharmavinivartanābhimukhīṃ sarvasattvājñānāndhakāravidhamanābhimukhīṃ sarvakuśalāparyayābhimukhīmapaśyat sarvajñajñānālokasaṃjananatāyai //

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyā idamacintyaṃ sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśanabodhisattvavimokṣavṛṣabhitāvikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā praharṣajāto mahāprītivegasāgarapratilabdhaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya ūrdhvaṃ vadanamavalokayāmāsa / atha khalu samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī rātrīdevatā tāṃ bodhisattvarūpalakṣaṇaviśuddhisaṃpadamantardhāpya rātridevatārūpeṇa sarvavikurvitāni pravartayamānā adhyatiṣṭhat / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -

children.text: dṛṣṭo mayā vipulakāyu tavā varalakṣaṇo ratanaābharaṇa /
raśmīmukhe rucirapadmasthitāḥ tava nirmitā jagi sameti duḥkham // 3 //
puṣpā pravarṣanta samantamukhaṃ spharati dharmadhātugata sarvajinān // 4 //
tava sūryameghapaṭalā vipulā sada niścaranti vadanādvimalāḥ /
tava candrajyotiṣaprabhā vimalā nayanebhi megha sada niścariṣu /
te co daśaddiśi spharitva jagaṃ dyotanti loki timiropahatā // 7 //
tava kāyu dṛśyati hi dikprasaraiḥ sarvajagābhimukha prītikaraḥ /
yada preṣitastava sakāśamahaṃ samupasthito guṇa vicintayatā /
tada raśmimaṇḍala śubhā vimalā bhrumukhāntarātu tava niścariṣu // 10 //
obhāsayan diśa samudraśatānāloka loki vipulāṃ janiya /
nānāvikurvita vidarśya bahūnastaṃgatā mama śarīri tadā // 11 //
yada raśmiṇḍala mamā nipatī tada saukhyamadbhutamudāramabhūt /
okrānta dhāraṇi samādhiśatā paśyāmi dikṣu ca jinānamitā // 12 //
kramavikrame yada dharā kramataḥ paramāṇusaṃkhyanayu jñātu mayā /
rajasi sthitā pṛthaganekavidhā nekāntakliṣṭa bahu kṣetraśatā /
saṃkliṣṭaśuddha puna kṣetra bahūn alpaṃ sukhaṃ vipula yatra duḥkha /
samudenti yeṣu jina kāruṇika jinaśrāvakā api pratyekajināḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: in which arise the compassionate <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), <s>śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Jina</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Buddhas). // 15 //
Purified-impure again are the field-methods, richly fashioned with many <s>bodhisattva</s>-arrangements;

children.text: naranārimaṇḍita sudarśanīyāḥ jinavaṃśu yatra sthihatī ruciraḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: adorned with men and women, beautiful to behold — where the resplendent lineage of <s>Jinas</s> abides. // 16 //

children.text: kṣetrasamudra vipula vimalā rajasi sthitā samatalānugatā /
children.translated_text: Vast, stainless oceans of fields, situated upon atoms, following the even surface,

children.text: vairocane caritā hi purā pariśodhitā vipulakalpaśataiḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: practiced formerly by <s>Vairocana</s>, purified through vast hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>. // 17 //
In all expanses of fields, <s>Jinas</s> are seen, seated beneath the best of trees;

children.text: bodhi vibuddhyayu vikurvayato cakraṃ pravartyaṃ vinayanti jagat // 18 //
children.translated_text: having awakened to <s>Bodhi</s>, performing transformations, turning the wheel, they discipline the world. // 18 //

children.text: paśyāmi tvāmanugatāmapi tāṃ vairocanasya viṣaye vipule /
children.translated_text: I see you too, following that [path], in the vast domain of <s>Vairocana</s>,

children.text: pūjā sahasranayutaiḥ amitaiḥ sarvān jinān samabhipūjayantī // 19 //
children.translated_text: worshipping all <s>Jinas</s> with innumerable thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of acts of worship. // 19 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ imā gāthā bhāṣitvā samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmetadavocat - āścaryaṃ devate, yāvadbhambhīro 'yaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ / kiṃ nāma ayaṃ vimokṣaḥ? kiyaccirapratilabdhaścāyaṃ tvayā? kathaṃ ca pratipadyamāno bodhisattvaḥ imaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pariśodhayati? āha - durabhisaṃbhavaṃ kulaputra etatsthānaṃ sadevakena lokena saśrāvakapratyekabuddhena / tatkasya hetoḥ? samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānānugatānāṃ hi bodhisattvānāmeṣa gocaro mahākaruṇāgarbhāṇāṃ sarvajagatparitrāṇapratipannānāṃ sarvākṣaṇāpāyadurgatipathaviśodhanapratipannānāṃ sarvakṣetrānuttarabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhipratipannānāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetratathāgatavaṃśānupacchedapratipannānāṃ sarvabuddhaśāsanasaṃdhāraṇapratipannānāṃ sarvakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsasaṃvasanamahāpraṇidhānasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvadharmasāgaravitimirajñānālokaviśodhanapratipannānāmekakṣaṇena sarvatryadhvanayasāgarajñānālokavihārapratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmeṣa viṣayaḥ / atha ca punastathāgatādhiṣṭhānena nirdekṣyāmi -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having spoken these verses, said to the night goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>: 'How wondrous, O goddess, how profound is this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation! What is the name of this liberation? And how long ago did you obtain it? And how, by practicing, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> purify this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation?' She replied: 'This state, son of good family, is difficult to attain for the world with its <s>devas</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. And why? For this is the domain of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who follow the practice and vows of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> — those whose womb is great compassion, who are devoted to the protection of all beings, who are devoted to the purification of all unfortunate destinies, bad courses, and inopportune paths, who are devoted to the purification of all fields into unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who are devoted to the unbroken continuity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who are devoted to upholding the teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>, who have descended into the ocean of great vows for dwelling in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct throughout all <s>kalpas</s> without remainder, who are devoted to the purification of the light of knowledge dispelling the darkness of the ocean of all <s>dharmas</s>, who in a single moment have attained the abode of the light of knowledge of the ocean of all methods of the three times — this is the domain of such <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And yet, by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, I shall explain:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa vairocanatejaḥśriyāṃ lokadhātau virajomaṇḍalo nāma kalpo 'bhūt sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamabuddhotpādaprabhavaḥ / sā khalu punarvairocanatejaḥśrīlokadhātuḥ sarvaratnameghavyūhā vajramayavimānabhavanapratimaṇḍitābhūt //
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, son of good family, in the past, beyond a number of <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in the world-realm <s>Vairocanatejaḥśrī</s> (Glory of the Radiance of <s>Vairocana</s>), there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Virajomaṇḍala</s> (Stainless Circle), the source of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. That world-realm <s>Vairocanatejaḥśrī</s> was arrayed with clouds of all jewels, adorned with mansions and palaces made of vajra (diamond). //

body.text: atha sā lokadhātuḥ sarvavimalaprabhamaṇirājasāgarapratiṣṭhitā sarvagandharājamaṇiratnaśarīrā samantaparimaṇḍalaviśuddhasaṃkliṣṭā sarvābharaṇameghavitānasaṃchāditā sarvavyūhamaṇicakravālasahasraparikṣiptā cāturdvīpikakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrasuracitavyūhā / kācittatra cāturdvīpikā saṃkliṣṭāsaṃkliṣṭakarmaṇāṃ sattvānāmāvāsaḥ, kācitsaṃkliṣṭaviśuddhavyāmiśrakarmaṇāṃ sattvānāmāvāsaḥ, kācidviśuddhasaṃkliṣṭānāṃ sattvānāmāvāsaḥ uttaptakuśalamūlānāmalpasāvadyānām, kācidekāntapariśuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmāvāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: That world-realm was established upon the ocean of <s>Sarvavimalaprabhamaṇirāja</s> (King of All Stainless Radiance Gems), with a body of <s>Sarvagandhārājamaṇiratna</s> (Gem-Jewels of the King of All Fragrances), universally circular, of purified-impure [nature], covered with canopies of clouds of all ornaments, enclosed by thousands of <s>Cakravāla</s>s (world-encircling mountains) of all array-gems, richly fashioned with arrangements of <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of four-continent systems. Some of those four-continent systems were the abode of beings of impure-not-impure <s>karma</s>; some were the abode of beings of mixed impure-and-pure <s>karma</s>; some were the abode of beings of pure-impure [nature] with heated roots of merit and few offenses; some were the abode of entirely purified <s>bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: tasyāḥ khalu punarvairocanaśriyo lokadhātoḥ pūrveṇa cakravālānusaṃdhau ratnakusumapradīpadhvajā nāma cāturdvīpikā bhūmiśuddhisaṃkliṣṭā akṛṣṭoptaśāliparibhogā pūrvakarmavipākābhinirvṛttakūṭāgārabhavanavimānaparibhogā samantāt kalpavṛkṣasaṃchāditā nānāgandhavṛkṣasadāpramuktakośagandhameghā vividhamālyavṛkṣasadāpravarṣitamālyameghā vicitrapuṣpavṛkṣā acintyavarṇagandhapuṣpavarṣaughapramuktā nānāvarṇacūrṇavṛkṣasadāpramuktakośasarvagandharatnarājacūrṇavarṣābhipravṛṣṭā vividharatnavṛkṣamahāmaṇiratnakośavisṛtavarṇāvabhāṣitā divyavādyavṛkṣasarvavādyameghavātasamīritagaganatalapramuktamadhuranirghoṣā candrasūryarātriṃdivāsukhaprabhavā maṇiratnasamantāvabhāsasamabhūmibhāgā //
body.translated_text: To the east of that world-realm <s>Vairocanatejaḥśrī</s>, at the juncture of the <s>Cakravāla</s>, there was a four-continent system called <s>Ratnakusumapradīpadhvajā</s> (Banner of the Lamp of Jewel-Flowers), of earth-purified-impure [nature], with unharvested self-growing rice for sustenance, with turret-palaces and mansions produced by the ripening of former <s>karma</s> for habitations, covered all around with wishing-trees, with fragrance-clouds constantly released from the sheaths of various fragrance-trees, with garland-clouds constantly rained from various garland-trees, with variegated flower-trees releasing torrents of flower-rain of inconceivable colors and fragrances, with various-colored powder-trees constantly releasing showers of all fragrance-jewel-king powders from their sheaths, with various jewel-trees whose great gem-jewel sheaths released variegated radiance, with divine music-trees from which sweet sounds were released to the surface of the sky stirred by the wind of all music-clouds, with pleasant light arising day and night from moon, sun, and gem-jewels universally illuminating the even ground-surface. //

body.text: tasyāṃ khalu cāturdvīpikāyāṃ daśa rājadhānīkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan / ekaikā ca rājadhānī samantānnadīsahasraparikṣiptā / sarvāśca tā nadyo vicitradivāpuṣpaughasaṃkaravāhinyo divyatūryasaṃgītimanojñamadhuranirghoṣāḥ sarvaratnadrumatīrasuruciravyūhāḥ nānāratnapratimaṇḍitāḥ nausaṃcāriṇyo yathecchāvividhasukhaparibhogyāḥ / ekaikasyāṃ ca nadyantarikāyāṃ daśa nagarakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsthitānyabhūvan / ekaikaṃ ca nagaraṃ daśagrāmakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāram / sarve te grāmanagaranigamā anekadivyodyānabhavanavimānakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivārā abhūvan / tasyāṃ khalu punaścāturdvīpikāyāṃ jambudvīpasya madhye ratnakusumapradīpā nāma madhyamā rājadhānyabhūt, ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ākīrṇabahujanadevamanuṣyā ca daśakuśalakarmapathasamāttānāṃ sattvānāmālayaḥ / tasyāṃ khalu punā ratnakusumapradīpāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍo nāma rāja abhūta cakravartī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ aupapādukaḥ padmagarbhe dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaśarīro dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / pūrṇaṃ cāsya sahasramabhūt putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānāṃ sarvākārasuparipūrṇavarāṅgānām / daśa cāsya strīkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyantaḥpuramabhūt sarvāsāṃ cakravartisabhāgakuśalamūlasaṃbhavānāṃ sabhāgacaritānāṃ saharatnakāyālaṃkārāṇāṃ kalyāṇacittānāṃ devakanyānirviśeṣasadṛśarūpāṇāṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇakāyānāṃ nānādivyagandharomakūpapramuktagātrāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: In that four-continent system there were ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of royal capitals. Each royal capital was surrounded by thousands of rivers on all sides. All those rivers carried torrents of variegated divine flowers, resounded with delightful sweet sounds of divine music-recitals, had shores beautifully arrayed with all jewel-trees, adorned with various gems, navigable by boats, and enjoyable with various pleasures as desired. Between each pair of rivers there were established ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of cities. Each city had a retinue of ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of villages. All those villages, cities, and market-towns had retinues of innumerable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of divine parks, mansions, and palaces. In the center of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in that four-continent system, there was a central royal capital called <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s> (Lamp of Jewel-Flowers) — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, densely populated with many <s>devas</s> and humans, the abode of beings who had undertaken the ten wholesome <s>karma</s>-paths. In that royal capital <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s> there was a king named <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s> (Crest of the Glory of the Lotus-Womb of <s>Vairocana</s> Jewels), a <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), lord of four continents, spontaneously born upon a lotus-womb, with a body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, righteous, a <s>dharma</s>-king, endowed with the seven jewels. He had a full thousand sons — heroic, brave, valiant, of excellent form, crushers of enemy armies, with limbs well-proportioned in every way. He had ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of women in the inner palace, all born from the same class of roots of merit as the <s>Cakravartin</s>, of similar conduct, with bodies adorned with the same jewel-ornaments, of virtuous minds, with forms comparable to divine maidens, with bodies of the color of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, with limbs releasing various divine fragrances from their hair-pores

body.text: divyagandhavimalaprabhāpramuñcanaśarīrāṇām / daśa cāsya amātyakoṭyo 'bhūvan pariṇāyakaratnapramukhāḥ //
body.translated_text: with bodies releasing the stainless radiance of divine fragrance. He had ten <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, headed by the minister-jewel. //

body.text: tasya khalu vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍasya rājñaścakravartinaḥ saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā nāma bhāryā abhūt strīratnam, abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā / abhinīlakeśī abhinīlanetrā suvarṇavarṇacchavirbrahmasvarā satatapramuktaprabhāśarīrā samantādyojanasahasramanekavarṇayā divyagandhaprabhayā spharati sma / tasyāśca saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrāyā rājabhāryāyāpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīrnāma cakravartiduhitā abhūt, sarvāṅgasaṃpūrṇā abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā sarvalokātṛptadarśanā / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra rājñaścakravartino darśanena na kaścit tṛpyati, evameva tasyāḥ padmabhadrābhirāminetraśriyaścakravartiduhiturna kaściddarśanena tṛptimāpadyate sthāpayitvā prajñātṛptān / tena ca kālena tena samayena amitāyuṣaḥ sattvā abhūvan na niyatāyuṣaḥ, nāsti antareṇa kālakriyā / tena ca kālena sattvānāṃ saṃsthānanānātvamapi prajñāyate sma / varṇanānātvamapi svaranānātvamapi nāmadheyanānātvamapi kulanānātvamapi āyuṣpramāṇanānātvamapi ārohapariṇāhavimātratāmapi utsāhabalaparākramasthāmavimātratāmapi manāpāmanāpakaraṇīyavimātratāmapi udārahīnādhimuktinānātvamapi prajñāyate sma / tatra ye sattvāḥ suvarṇā abhūvannudārādhimuktikāḥ saṃpūrṇagātrā abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ, ta evaṃ vācamabhāṣanta - ahaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa suvarṇatarastvatsakāśāditi / evaṃ ye sattvāḥ susaṃsthitaśarīrā abhūvan, te duḥsaṃsthitaśarīrān sarvānavamanyante sma / te tena anyonyāvamānanāsamuditena akuśalamūlena āyuḥpramāṇādapi parihīyante sma, varṇādapi balādapi saukhyādapi parihīyante sma //
body.translated_text: That <s>Cakravartin</s> King <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s> had a wife named <s>Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā</s>, the woman-jewel — beautiful, graceful, lovely to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious color. She had dark-blue hair, dark-blue eyes, skin the color of gold, a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, a body constantly releasing radiance, pervading a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in all directions with divine fragrance-radiance of many colors. That queen <s>Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā</s> had a <s>Cakravartin</s>-daughter named <s>Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrī</s> (Glory of the Eye Charming with the Auspicious Lotus), complete in all limbs, beautiful, graceful, lovely to behold — one whose sight no one in the entire world could be satiated with. Just as, son of good family, no one is satiated with the sight of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, even so no one could be satiated with the sight of that <s>Cakravartin</s>-daughter <s>Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrī</s>, except those satiated by wisdom. At that time, beings were of immeasurable lifespan, not of fixed lifespan; there was no untimely death. At that time, among beings there was diversity of bodily configuration, diversity of color, diversity of voice, diversity of name, diversity of family, diversity of lifespan-measure, diversity of height and girth, diversity of energy, strength, and valor, diversity of what is pleasing and displeasing to be done, and diversity of exalted and lowly aspirations. Among those beings, whoever were of golden [hue], of exalted aspiration, of complete limbs, beautiful and lovely — they would speak thus: 'I, sir, am more golden than you!' Thus those beings who were well-formed in body looked down upon all who were ill-formed in body. Through that unwholesome root arisen from mutual contempt, they declined even in lifespan, and declined also in color, strength, and happiness. //

body.text: tasyāṃ khalu ratnakusumapradīpāyāṃ rājadhānyāmuttareṇa samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvajo nāma bodhimaṇḍavṛkṣo 'bhūt sarvatathāgatabodhimaṇḍavyūhapratikṣaṇadarśanaḥ abhedyavajramaṇirājasāramūlaḥ sarvamaṇiratnanicitavipulodviddhaskandhaḥ sarvaratnamayaskandhaśākhāpatrapalāśapuṣpaphalaḥ saṃpannaḥ samantasuvibhaktaḥ samabhāgābhipralambaracitaśākhaḥ samantaspharaṇākṣayatāvyūho nānāratnārcividyutsamantabhadrapramuktāvabhāsaḥ sarvatathāgataviṣayavikurvitanirghoṣānuravitaḥ //
body.translated_text: To the north of that royal capital <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s> there was a <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-tree called <s>Samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja</s> (Banner of the Sound of <s>Dharma</s>-Cloud-Rain Illuminating Everything) — displaying at every moment the array of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with roots of the essence of indestructible vajra gem-kings, with a vast lofty trunk encrusted with all gem-jewels, with trunk, branches, leaves, foliage, flowers, and fruits all made of all jewels, complete, universally well-differentiated, with evenly proportioned gracefully hanging branches, with an array of inexhaustible universal pervading, illuminated with radiance of various gem-arc-lightning universally releasing the light of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, resounding with the sounds of transformations of the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //

body.text: tasya khalu bodhimaṇḍasya purato ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣaṃ nāma gandhodakasaro 'bhūddaśaratnadrumakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāram / sarve ca te ratnavṛkṣā bodhivṛkṣasaṃsthānā abhūvan / tasya khalu punā ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣasya mahāgandhodakasarasaḥ sarvamaṇiratnasuvibhaktanicitāni kūlānyabhūvan, sarvaratnahārapralambitāni viśuddharatnamayasarvabhavanavyūhopaśobhitāni viśuddhasarvābharaṇavyūhasamalaṃkṛtāni / sarvaśca bodhimaṇḍo 'pramāṇaiḥ padmagarbhairacintyavyūhamahāmaṇiratnakūṭāgāraiḥ samantātparivṛto 'bhūt / tasya khalu punā ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣasya gandhodakasarasaḥ madhyāt sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitameghavyūhaṃ nāma mahāratnarājapadmaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: Before that <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> there was a great fragrant-water lake called <s>Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>-Roaring Lightning of Jewel-Flowers), with a retinue of ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of jewel-trees. All those jewel-trees were in the form of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees. That great fragrant-water lake had banks well-differentiated and encrusted with all gem-jewels, hung with garlands of all jewels, embellished with the arrays of all dwellings made of pure jewels, adorned with arrays of all pure ornaments. The entire <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> was surrounded on all sides by immeasurable lotus-wombs and inconceivably arrayed great gem-jewel turret-chambers. From the center of that fragrant-water lake <s>Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa</s> there appeared a great jewel-king lotus called <s>Sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitameghavyūha</s> (Cloud-Array Illuminated by the Leaf-Joints of the Domain of All <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the Three Times). //

body.text:
tatra mahāpadme samantajñānārciśrīguṇaketudhvajo nāma tathāgataḥ prādurbabhūva teṣāṃ sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ prathamakalpikaḥ, yena tasmin kalpe sarvaprathamamanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā / so 'nekavarṣasahasrāṇi dharmaśravaṇena sattvān paripācya daśavarṣasahasraṃ raśmyavabhāsavikurvitena paripācayāmāsa tatra daśabhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgataḥ prādurbhaviṣyatīti / yattataḥ sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitaraśmimeghavyūhamahāratnarājapadmāt sarvasattvavirajaḥpradīpā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā raśmyā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ saṃjānanti sma - daśabhirvarṣasahasraistathāgata utpatsyata iti, navabhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattato mahābodhivṛkṣādvirajovatīśrīgarbhā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā raśmyā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ sarvarūpāṇi sūkṣmāṇyapaśyan - aṣṭābhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvasattvakarmavipākanirghoṣā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā raśmyā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ svakasvakān karmasamudrānavataranti sma, karmasmṛtijñānaṃ ca pratyalabhanta - saptabhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhavanirghoṣā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā raśmyā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ paripūrṇā avikalasarvendriyāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante sma - ṣaḍbhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣādacintyabuddhaviṣayanidarśananirghoṣā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ udārātiśayatayā vikurvanti sma - pañcabhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhinigarjitapratibhāsavijñāpanā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ sarvākārāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhimadrākṣuḥ caturbhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvatathāgataviṣayāsaṃbhedapradīpā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ tasya tathāgatasya sarvatrānugatavikurvitamavataranti sma - tribhirvarṣasahasraiḥ sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣātsarvajagadabhimukhapradīpā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ tathāgatamabhimukhamadhimucyāpaśyan - dvābhyāṃ varṣasahasrābhyāṃ sa tathāgata utpasyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt tryadhvajñānavidyutpradīpā nāma raśmirniścacāra satathāgatapūrvayoganirghoṣā nāma, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ tasya tathāgatasya pūrvayogasamudrānavakalpayāmāsuravataranti
sma - varṣasahasreṇa sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattato mahābodhivṛkṣādvitimirajñānatathāgatapradīpā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ samantacakṣuṣkatāṃ pratyalabhanta sarvatathāgatavikurvitabuddhakṣetrasarvasattvadarśanatāyai - varṣaśatena sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvajagadbuddhadarśanavipākakuśalamūlasaṃbhavā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ tathāgatotpādasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhanta - saptāhena sa tathāgata utpatsyata iti / yattata eva mahābodhivṛkṣāt sarvasattvapraharṣaprītiprāmodyasamudayanirghoṣā nāma raśmirniścacāra, yayā te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ buddhadarśanamahāprītivegasaṃjātā abhūvan / iti hi kulaputra ebhirevaṃrūpairapramāṇaiḥ raśmiparipācananayairdaśavarṣasahasrāṇi sattvān paripācya saptame divase pūrṇe
body.translated_text: In that great lotus, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samantajñānārciśrīguṇaketudhvaja</s> appeared — the first-of-the-<s>kalpa</s> among those <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, by whom unsurpassed perfect awakening was first attained in that <s>kalpa</s>. He ripened beings through hearing the <s>Dharma</s> for many thousands of years, and for ten thousand years ripened them through the transformation of ray-illumination. [It was announced that] in ten thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> would appear. From that great gem-king lotus of the array of ray-cloud illuminating the leaf-joints of the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the three times, a ray named 'Stainless Lamp of All Beings' issued forth, by which ray those beings, touched by it, knew: 'In ten thousand years the <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' [Then:] 'In nine thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named <s>Virajovatīśrīgarbhā</s> (Stainless Splendor-Womb) issued forth, by which ray those beings, touched by it, saw all subtle forms — 'In eight thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Sound of the Ripening of the <s>Karma</s> of All Beings' issued forth, by which ray those beings, touched by it, entered their own respective oceans of <s>karma</s> and attained the knowledge of <s>karma</s>-recollection — 'In seven thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Sound of the Arising of All Wholesome Roots' issued forth, by which ray those beings, touched by it, stood complete with all faculties intact — 'In six thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Sound Displaying the Inconceivable Domain of the <s>Buddha</s>' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, performed transformations of surpassing excellence — 'In five thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Cognition of the Reflected Sound of the Purification of All <s>Buddha</s>-Fields' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, saw the complete purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in all aspects — 'In four thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Lamp of the Non-differentiation of the Domain of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, entered the everywhere-following transformations of that <s>Tathāgata</s> — 'In three thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Lamp Facing All Beings' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, saw that <s>Tathāgata</s> face-to-face with devotion — 'In two thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Lightning-Lamp of the Knowledge of the Three Times' and also named 'Sound of the Former Practice of that <s>Tathāgata</s>' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, conceived and entered the oceans of the former practice of that <s>Tathāgata</s> — 'In one thousand years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Darkness-free Knowledge <s>Tathāgata</s>-Lamp' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, attained the state of the universal eye for seeing all beings in all <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformation-<s>Buddha</s>-fields — 'In one hundred years that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Arising of the Wholesome Root of the Ripening of <s>Buddha</s>-Vision of All Beings' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, attained the perception of the arising of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — 'In seven days that <s>Tathāgata</s> will arise.' From that very great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a ray named 'Sound of the Arising of Delight, Joy, and Gladness of All Beings' issued forth, by which those beings, touched by it, were born with the great surge of joy of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>. Thus, son of good family, by such immeasurable methods of ray-ripening, having ripened beings for ten thousand years, when the seventh day was complete

body.text: sarvaṃ taṃ lokadhātumapramāṇaiḥ saṃkampananayaiḥ saṃkampya ekāntapariśuddhāmadhyatiṣṭhat yāvaddaśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ / tāmapi sarvāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ tatra buddhakṣetranānāvidhācintyavyūhān saṃdarśayāmāsa / atha paścime saptāhe ye tatra lokadhātau sattvā buddhadarśanaparipakvāḥ, te sarve bodhimaṇḍābhimukhāḥ sthitā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: having caused the entire world-realm to tremble by immeasurable methods of trembling, he established it in absolute purity, even as far as the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the ten directions. And at every mind-moment he displayed there the various inconceivable arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Then in the last seven days, all beings in that world-realm who had been ripened by seeing the <s>Buddha</s> stood facing the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu tasmin lokadhātau sarvacakravālebhya sarvasumerubhyaḥ sarvaparvatebhyaḥ sarvanadībhyaḥ sarvasāgarebhyaḥ sarvavṛkṣebhyaḥ sarvapṛthivītalebhyaḥ sarvanagarebhyaḥ sarvaprākārebhyaḥ sarvabhavanebhyaḥ sarvavimānebhyaḥ sarvavastrābharaṇaparibhogebhyaḥ sarvavādyavṛkṣebhyaḥ sarvatūryasaṃgītibhyaḥ sarvanirmāṇavyūhebhyaḥ ekaikasmādārambaṇāt sarvatathāgataviṣayaprabhavaṃ nigarjamānāḥ sarvagandhadhūpameghānnirścārya sarvaratnārcimeghān sarvagandhadhūpārcigarbhān sarvagandhamaṇivigrahameghān sarvamaṇivastraratnābharaṇameghān sarvaratnapuṣpasumerumeghān sarvacūrṇameghān sarvatathāgataraśmimeghān vidyotayamānāḥ sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalameghānniścārayamāṇāḥ sarvavādyatūryameghān saṃghaṭṭayamānāḥ sarvatathāgatapraṇidhānanirghoṣameghān pramuñcayamānāḥ sarvatathāgatasvarāṅgarutasamudrameghān nigarjayamānāḥ sarvatathāgatalakṣaṇānuvyañjanavicitrapratibhāsameghān nidarśayamānāḥ acintyāni tathāgatotpādapūrvanimittāni saṃdarśya tasya sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhidyotitaraśmimeghavyūhamahāratnarājapadmasya bodhau daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā mahāratnarājapadmaparivārāḥ samavatiṣṭhanta / teṣāṃ ca mahāratnarājapadmaparivārāṇāṃ mahāratnapadmānāṃ kesarakarṇikāsu daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni mahāmaṇiratnagarbhāṇi siṃhāsanāni prādurabhūvan / teṣu ca maṇiratnagarbheṣvāsaneṣu daśabuddhakṣetraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvāḥ paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇāḥ prādurbabhūvuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then in that world-realm, from all <s>Cakravāla</s>s, all <s>Sumeru</s>s, all mountains, all rivers, all oceans, all trees, all surfaces of the earth, all cities, all ramparts, all dwellings, all mansions, all garments, ornaments, and enjoyments, all music-trees, all musical ensembles, all arrays of emanations — from each and every object, thundering forth the arising of the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, releasing clouds of all fragrant incense, illuminating clouds of all gem-flame, clouds of all fragrant incense-flame-wombs, clouds of all fragrant gem-embodiment, clouds of all gem-garment-jewel-ornaments, clouds of all gem-flower-<s>Sumeru</s>, clouds of all powders, clouds of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-rays, emitting clouds of all <s>Tathāgata</s> radiance-maṇḍalas, producing the sound of clouds of all musical instruments, releasing clouds of the sound of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-vows, thundering forth clouds of the ocean of sounds, limbs, and cries of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, displaying clouds of the variegated reflections of the marks and subsidiary marks of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — having displayed the inconceivable auspicious omens of the arising of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, great gem-king-lotus companions equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared around the <s>Bodhi</s> of that great gem-king-lotus of the array of ray-cloud illuminating the leaf-joints of the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the three times. And on the filament-pistils of those great gem-king-lotus companions, great gem-jewel-womb lion-thrones equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared. And on those gem-jewel-womb seats, <s>bodhisattva</s>s equal in number to the atoms of a hundred thousand times ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared, seated cross-legged. //

body.text: samanantarābhisaṃbuddhasya tasya bhagavataḥ samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurājñaḥ tathāgatasya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim, atha tāvadeva daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātutathāgatā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayāmāsuḥ / tena tato lokadhātoraprameyāḥ sattvāḥ sarvadurgativinipātebhyo vinivartitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ svargopapattipratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ śrāvakabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ pratyekabodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā vegaprabhāniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā vimalaparākramadhvajāyāṃ bodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ dharmaprabhāvanābhavananiryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā indriyapariśuddhiprabhāvanāniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ balasamatāsamudācārānugamaniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā dharmanagarābhimukhaviṣayayānasaṃbhavaniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ sarvatrānugatarddhyabhisaṃbhinnanayayānananiryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ caryāprayogasamavasaraṇanayaniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ samādhiprasthānanayaniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ sarvārambaṇaviṣayapariśuddhimaṇḍalanayaniryāṇāyāṃ bodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā bodhisattvabodhau cittamutpāditāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvā bodhisattvamārge
body.translated_text: Immediately upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>'s attaining unsurpassed perfect awakening, at that very moment the <s>Tathāgata</s>s of all world-realms in the ten directions, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> face-to-face according to the dispositions of beings. By that [turning], immeasurable beings of that world-realm were turned back from all the downfalls of bad destinies. Immeasurable beings were established in rebirth in the heavens. Immeasurable beings were established on the stage of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>. Immeasurable beings were ripened for <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>. Immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening of the emergence of the power of speed-radiance. Immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening of the banner of stainless prowess. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the palace of the manifestation of the <s>Dharma</s>. Immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening of the emergence of the manifestation of the purification of faculties. Immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening of the emergence of following the conduct of equality of powers. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the vehicle arising from the domain facing the city of <s>Dharma</s>. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the vehicle of the everywhere-following method of supernatural powers. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the method of convergence of the application of conduct. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the method of the setting-forth of <s>samādhi</s>. Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening of the emergence of the maṇḍala-method of the purification of the domain of all objects. Immeasurable beings generated the aspiration for the awakening of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Immeasurable beings were established on the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path

body.text: pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ pāramitāmārgaviśuddhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evaṃ tasya tathāgatasya acintyena buddhavṛṣabhitāvikurvitena dharmacakraṃ pravartayataḥ praticittakṣaṇamanantāprameyāḥ sattvā dvitīyāyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ pañcabhyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ saptamyāmaṣṭabhyāṃ navamyām, aprameyāḥ sattvā daśabhyāṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ praṇidhānavaiśeṣikāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāmavatāritāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaviśuddhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evaṃ tasya tathāgatasya acintyena buddhavṛṣabhitāvikurvitena dharmacakraṃ pravartayataḥ praticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyasattvadhāturvinayamagamat / tasmiṃśca lokadhātau sarvasattvā yathāśayāstasya tathāgatasya nānātmabhāvopāyakauśalyapramuktāṃ dharmadeśanāmājānanti sma //
body.translated_text: Immeasurable beings were established in the purification of the path of the <s>pāramitā</s>s. Immeasurable beings were established on the first <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage. Thus, as that <s>Tathāgata</s> turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> through the inconceivable magnificent <s>Buddha</s>-transformation, at every mind-moment infinite and immeasurable beings were established on the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth — immeasurable beings were established on the tenth stage. Immeasurable beings were led into the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct distinguished by vows. Immeasurable beings were established in the purification of the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>. Thus, as that <s>Tathāgata</s> turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> through the inconceivable magnificent <s>Buddha</s>-transformation, at every mind-moment, the discipline of the infinite, boundless realm of beings was accomplished. And all beings in that world-realm, according to their dispositions, understood the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> released through the skill in means of that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s various self-manifestations. //

body.text: tasyāṃ khalu punā ratnakusumapradīpāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ rūpavarṇaviṣayaparibhogamadamattānāṃ sattvānāmanyonyamavamanyamānānāṃ vinayavaśaṃ samupādāya samantabhadro bodhisattva udāravarṇarūpagatamabhinirmāya tāṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ / tasyodārayā prabhayā sarvā sā rājadhānyavabhāsitā / yā ca tasyā rājadhānyāḥ prabhā, yā ca rājñaścakravartino vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍasya svaśarīraniryātā prabhā, yā ca strīratnasya prabhā, yā ca ratnavṛkṣāṇāṃ prabhā, yā ca mahāmaṇiratnasya prabhā, yā ca candrasūryagrahanakṣatrajyotiṣāṃ prabhā, yā ca sarvajambudvīpe prabhā, sā ca sarvā na prajñāyate sma / tadyathāpi nāma āditye udite vigate 'ndhakāre na candragrahanakṣatrajyotiṣāṃ nāgnerna maṇīnāṃ prabhā prajñāyate sma, evameva samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya prabhayābhibhūtāḥ tatra jambudvīpe sarvaprabhā na prajñāyate sma / tadyathāpi nāma jāmbūnadakanakabimbasya purato maṣivigraho na śobhate na bhāsate na tapati na virocate, evameva samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya purataḥ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ rūpakāyā na śobhante, na bhāsante, na tapanti, na virocante //
body.translated_text: Now, in that royal capital <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s> (Jewel-Flower-Lamp), in order to take hold of the discipline of beings intoxicated and maddened by the enjoyment of the objects of form and color, who were mutually despising one another, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> magically created a sublime form of color and appearance and arrived at that royal capital. By his sublime radiance, that entire royal capital was illuminated. Whatever radiance belonged to that royal capital, whatever radiance issued from the body of the <s>cakravartin</s> king <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s>, whatever radiance of the woman-jewel, whatever radiance of the jewel-trees, whatever radiance of the great <s>maṇi</s>-jewel, whatever radiance of the moon, sun, planets, stars, and luminaries, whatever radiance in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — all of that was no longer perceived. Just as when the sun has risen and darkness has departed, the radiance of the moon, planets, stars, luminaries, fire, and gems is no longer perceived — even so, overpowered by the radiance of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, all radiance in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was no longer perceived. Just as an ink-figure does not shine, does not gleam, does not glow, does not radiate before an image of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold — even so, before the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the form-bodies of those beings did not shine, did not gleam, did not glow, did not radiate. //

body.text: teṣāmetadabhavat - ko 'nvayaṃ bhaviṣyati devo vā brahmā vā, yasya purato vayaṃ na śobhāmahe, na bhāsāmahe, na tapāmo na virocāmahe kāyena vā prabhayā vā śubhayā vā varṇena vā tejasā vā? na cāsya śaknumo nimittamudgrahītum //
body.translated_text: This thought arose in them: 'Who could this be — a <s>deva</s> or a <s>Brahmā</s> — before whom we do not shine, do not gleam, do not glow, do not radiate, neither in body, nor radiance, nor beauty, nor color, nor splendor? And we cannot grasp his distinguishing mark.' //

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvaḥ tasyā ratnakusumapradīpāyā rājadhānyā madhye vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍasya rājñaścakravartino vimānasyoparyantarikṣe sthitvā taṃ vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍaṃ rājānaṃ cakravartinametadavocat - yat khalu mahārāja jānīyāḥ - tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpannaḥ / ihaiva tava vijite samantadharmāvabhāsadharmameghanirghoṣadhvajabodhimaṇḍe viharati //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, standing in the sky above the palace of the <s>cakravartin</s> king <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s>, in the middle of that royal capital <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s>, spoke thus to that <s>cakravartin</s> king <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s>: 'Know this, great king — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, has arisen in the world! Right here in your domain, he dwells at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Samantadharmāvabhāsadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja</s> (Banner of the Thunder of the Dharma-Cloud Illuminating All Dharmas).' //

body.text: atha khalu samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā rājaduhitā samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya rūpakāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā prabhāvikurvitamābharaṇanirghoṣaṃ ca śrutvā mahāprītiprāmodyavegajātā tasyāṃ velāyāmevaṃ cittamutpādayāmāsa - yanme kiṃcidupacitakuśalamūlaṃ tenāhamīdṛśaṃ kāyaṃ pratilabheyam /
body.translated_text: Then indeed the princess <s>Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā</s>, having seen the form-body of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> and having heard the sound of his ornaments, was seized by a great surge of joy and delight, and at that moment generated this aspiration-mind: 'By whatever wholesome roots have been accumulated by me, may I obtain such a body as this!

body.text: īdṛśamalaṃkāram, īdṛśāni lakṣaṇāni, īdṛśamīryāpatham, īdṛśīmṛddhim / yathā anenāndhakārāyāṃ rātrau sattvānāmavabhāsaṃ saṃjanayya buddhotpādaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ, tathāhamapi sattvānāmajñānāndhakāraṃ vidhūya mahājñānālokaṃ kuryām / yatra yatra cotpadyeyam, sarvatrāvirahitā syāmanena kalyāṇamitreṇa //
body.translated_text: Such ornaments, such marks, such deportment, such supernatural power! Just as this one, in the dark night, has generated illumination for beings and has proclaimed the arising of the <s>Buddha</s>, so may I too, having dispelled the darkness of ignorance in beings, create the great light of knowledge! And wherever I may be reborn, may I never be separated from this spiritual friend!' //

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍaścakravartī sādha caturaṅgena balakāyena, sārdhaṃ saptabhī ratnaiḥ, sārdhaṃ strīgaṇaparivāreṇa, sārdhaṃ putrāmātyanaigamairjānapadaiḥ, mahatyā rājarddhyā, mahatā rājānubhāvena tasyā ratnakusumapradīpāyā rājadhānyā uccālya yojanamūrdhvaṃ vihāyasyabhyudgamya sarvaṃ jambudvīpaṃ sarvāvatīṃ cāturdvīpikalokadhātuṃ mahāvabhāsena spharitvā sarvasattvānāṃ buddhadarśanasamādāpanārthaṃ sarvaratnaparvateṣu pratibhāsaṃ saṃdarśya sarvacāturdvīpikalokadhātuparyāpannānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā tadbuddhadarśanaṃ gāthābhigītena saṃvarṇayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then indeed, son of good family, the <s>cakravartin</s> king <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s>, together with his fourfold army, together with the seven treasures, together with his retinue of women, together with his sons, ministers, townsfolk, and countryfolk, with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, rising up from that royal capital <s>Ratnakusumapradīpā</s> one <s>yojana</s> into the sky, pervading all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and the entire four-continent world-realm with a great radiance, displaying reflections on all jewel-mountains for the purpose of inspiring all beings to see the <s>Buddha</s>, standing face-to-face with all beings throughout the entire four-continent world-realm — praised that vision of the <s>Buddha</s> with verses sung aloud:

children.translated_text: A <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world, the savior of all embodied beings;
let all arise and go to behold the guide of the world! // 20 //
Only after <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> do <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise;
they proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> for the welfare of all embodied beings. // 21 //
Having seen the world perverted, enveloped in the darkness of ignorance,
afflicted by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, generating great compassion, // 22 //
innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> has the course of awakening been practiced,
for the ripening of beings, for the pacification of all suffering. // 23 //
He renounced hands, feet, ears, noses, and heads,
through <s>kalpas</s> of infinite extent, to obtain the nectar of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. // 24 //
Rare through <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> are the guides of the world;
not in vain is hearing them, seeing them, attending upon them. // 25 //
Seated on the seat of awakening, this best of speakers is seen,
having conquered <s>Māra</s> together with his armies, fully awakened to the supreme awakening. // 26 //
Behold the <s>Buddha</s>-body, the <s>maṇḍala</s> of infinite rays,
issuing forth in various colors, it delights the world. // 27 //
Innumerable clouds of rays issue forth from the pores of the <s>Buddha</s>;
beings illuminated by them attain incomparable joy. // 28 //
Each with their own mind, worship the Guide;
generating great vigor, come, let us go to his presence! // 29 //

body.text: atha khalu rājā vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍaścābhirgāthābhiḥ svavijitavāsinaḥ sarvān sattvān saṃcodya daśabhirvividhapūjāmeghasahasraiścakravartikuśalamūlapariniṣpannaiḥ samantāvabhāsadharmameghanirghoṣadhvajaṃ bodhimaṇḍaṃ samantādabhipravarṣan yena sa bhagavān samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurājastathāgataḥ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ sarvaratnacchatrameghasaṃchāditamākāśaṃ kurvan, sarvapuṣpavitānameghavitatamākāśaṃ kurvan, sarvavastrameghasaṃchāditālaṃkāramākāśaṃ kurvan, sarvaratnakiṅkiṇījālameghairgaganamalaṃkurvan, sarvagandhasāgaranirdhūpitagandhārcimeghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sarvaratnāsanamaṇiratnavastraprajñaptaviracanameghālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sarvaratnadhvajameghocchritālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhān, sarvabhavanavimānameghasaṃchannālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sarvapuṣpameghasaṃchannālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan, sarvapūjāvyūhameghābhipravarṣaṇālaṃkāraṃ gaganatalamadhitiṣṭhan / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ samantajñānaratnarciśrīguṇaketurājasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tasya bhagavataḥ purataḥ samantadigvidyotitamahāmaṇiratnapadmagarbhāsane nyaṣīdat //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the king <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa</s>, having urged all beings dwelling in his domain with these verses, raining upon the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Samantāvabhāsadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja</s> from all sides with ten thousand clouds of various worship-offerings accomplished through the <s>cakravartin</s>'s wholesome roots — making the sky covered with clouds of all jewel-parasols, making the sky spread with clouds of all flower-canopies, making the sky covered with clouds of all garment-ornaments, adorning the sky with clouds of all jewel-bell-nets, establishing the adornment of clouds of fragrance-flame-rays from all oceans of fragrance upon the surface of the sky, establishing the adornment of clouds of all jewel-seat-gem-jewel-garment-prepared arrangements upon the surface of the sky, establishing the adornment of clouds of all jewel-banner raised high upon the surface of the sky, establishing the adornment of clouds covered with all dwelling-palace-clouds upon the surface of the sky, establishing the adornment of clouds covered with all flower-clouds upon the surface of the sky, establishing the adornment of clouds raining all worship-array-clouds upon the surface of the sky — he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before the <s>Bhagavān</s> upon a great <s>maṇi</s>-jewel lotus-womb seat illuminated in all directions. //

body.text: atha khalu samantajñānaratnārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā cakravartiduhitā svānyābharaṇāni kāyānnirmucya tairābharaṇaistaṃ bhagavantaṃ samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurājānaṃ tathāgatamabhyavakirat / atha tānyābharaṇāni tasya bhagavataḥ upari mūrdhasaṃdhau mahāmaṇiratnābharaṇacchatraṃ saṃsthitamabhūvan vicitramaṇiratnajālaparikṣiptaṃ nāgendrakāyaparigṛhītaṃ sarvābharaṇaśarīrasusaṃsthitaparimaṇḍalaṃ daśābharaṇacchatramaṇḍalaparivāritamekāntapariśuddhaṃ kūṭāgārasaṃsthānavicitravyūhaṃ sarvaratnābharaṇameghasaṃchāditaṃ sarvamaṇirājadrumavyūhasaṃchannaṃ sarvagandhasāgaramaṇirājasamalaṃkṛtam / tasya madhye dharmadhātuprabhavasarvaratnamaṇiśākhāpralambaṃ nāma mahābodhivṛkṣamadrākṣīt anantamadhyavyūhanirdeśaṃ pradakṣiṇanānāvyūhasaṃdarśanam / tatra vairocanaṃ nāma tathāgatamadrākṣīt anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ sarvaiḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaniryātaiḥ nānābodhisattvairacintyavyūhāsaṃbhinnavihāribhiḥ, sarvalokendrāṃśca tadabhimukhānadrākṣīt / tasya bhagavato vairocanasyānantamadhyaṃ buddhavikurvitamadrākṣīt, pūrvabodhisattvacaryākalpaparaṃparāṃ ca avatarati sma / tasyāśca lokadhātoḥ saṃvartavivartakalpānavatarati sma / tatra lokadhātāvatītāṃ buddhavaṃśaparaṃparāmavatarati sma / tasyāṃ ca lokadhātau samantabhadrabodhisattvamadrākṣīt / sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu buddhapūjāprayuktasarvasattvaparipākavinayābhimukhaṃ cādrākṣīt / sarvabodhisattvāṃśca samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya kāye pratibhāsaprāptān, ātmānaṃ ca tatraivānugatamadrākṣīt sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu / samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya kāyapratibhāsaprāptasarvabodhisattvapādamūleṣu sarvasattvabhavaneṣu, tāsu ca lokadhātuṣvekaikasmin lokadhātau buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān lokadhātūnadrākṣīt / sasaṃdhivyūhān, sapratiṣṭhānān, sasaṃsthānān, saśarīrān, sanānāvyūhapariśuddhān, nānāvyūhameghaparisaṃchannān, nānākalpanāmasaṃkhyeyān, nānātathāgatavaṃśanirdeśān, nānātryadhvanayāvatārān, nānādikprasarapraveśān, nānādharmadhātuprasaraparyāpannān
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>cakravartin</s>'s daughter <s>Samantajñānaratnārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā</s>, removing her own ornaments from her body, scattered those ornaments upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja</s>. Then those ornaments came to rest above the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s crown-junction as a great <s>maṇi</s>-jewel-ornament parasol — encircled by a net of variegated <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, supported by <s>nāgendra</s> (serpent-king) bodies, well-formed and circular with the bodies of all ornaments well-arranged, surrounded by a circle of ten ornament-parasol-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, absolutely pure, of the configuration of a multi-storied pavilion with variegated array, covered with clouds of all jewel-ornaments, concealed by arrays of all <s>maṇi</s>-king trees, adorned with all fragrance-ocean <s>maṇi</s>-kings. In its center, she saw a great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree named <s>Dharmadhātuprabhavasarvaratnamaṇiśākhāpralamba</s> (Hanging Branches of All Jewel-Gems Arising from the Dharmadhātu), displaying an array that is boundless and without middle, showing variegated arrays in circumambulation. There she saw a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vairocana</s>, surrounded and attended by <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of inexpressibly many <s>Buddha</s>-fields — all having emerged through the vows and conduct of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> of various kinds dwelling in inconceivable arrays. And she saw all the lords of the world facing toward him. She saw the boundless and middleway-less <s>Buddha</s>-transformations of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>. And she descended into the succession of <s>kalpas</s> of his former <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. And she descended into the formation-and-dissolution <s>kalpas</s> of that world-realm. There she descended into the succession of <s>Buddha</s>-lineages of that world-realm's past. And in that world-realm she saw the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. And she saw him engaged in <s>Buddha</s>-worship at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, facing the ripening and disciplining of all beings. And she saw all <s>bodhisattvas</s> reflected in the body of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, and she saw herself there too, following at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, at the feet of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> reflected in the body of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, in all the abodes of beings. And in those world-realms, in each single world-realm, she saw world-realms equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields — with their juncture-arrays, with their foundations, with their configurations, with their embodiments, purified with variegated arrays, covered with clouds of variegated arrays, with innumerable <s>kalpas</s> of various names, with displays of various <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineages, with descents into methods of the various three times, with entries extending in various directions, encompassed in the extensions of various <s>dharmadhātus</s>

body.text:
nānādharmadhātutalapraveśān, nānākāśatalavyavasthānān, nānābodhigaṇḍavyūhān, nānātathāgatavikurvitaprabhān, nānābuddhasiṃhāsanavyūhān, nānātathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrān nānātathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalaparivartān nānātathāgatopāyakauśalyaparidīpanān, nānātathāgatadharmacakrapravartananayān, nānātathāgatasvarāṅgarutanirghoṣamuktān
nānāmantranayasāgaranirdeśān nānāsūtrāntameghānuravamāṇānadrākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca bhūyasyā mātrayā mahāprītiprasādavegān pratyalabhata //
body.translated_text: with entries into various grounds of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, with establishments on various surfaces of space, with various <s>Bodhi</s>-<s>gaṇḍa</s>-arrays, with radiance of various <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations, with various <s>Tathāgata</s> lion-throne arrays, with oceans of various <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, with revolvings of various <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, with illuminations of the skillful means of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with methods of turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, releasing the voices, limbs, sounds, and proclamations of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with expositions of oceans of various <s>mantra</s>-methods, resounding with clouds of various <s>sūtra</s>-discourses — she saw [all this]. And having seen, she gained surges of great joy and faith to an even greater degree. //

body.text: tasyā mahāprītivegasaṃjātāyāḥ sa bhagavān samantajñānaratnārciḥśrīguṇaketurājastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣaṃ nāma sūtrāntaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamasūtrāntaparivāram / tasyāstaṃ sūtrāntaṃ śrutvā daśa samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇyavakrāntāni mṛdūni sukhasaṃsparśanāni / tadyathāpi nāma taddivasāvakrāntasya garbhasya mātuḥ kukṣau vijñānam, tadyathāpi nāma sattvānāṃ karmābhinirhāram, tadyathāpi nāma taddivasāvaruptasya sālakalyāṇavṛkṣasya bījāṅkurahetuḥ, evameva te samādhayo mṛdavaḥ kamanīyāḥ / yaduta sarvatathāgatābhimukhavijñāpano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvakṣetraprasarānugatāvabhāso nāma samādhiḥ / sarvatryadhvanayāvatārapraveśo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvabuddhapraṇidhānasāgaravijñāpano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhapratipīḍitasarvaniryāṇanirghoṣavijñāpano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvatamondhakāravidhamanapraṇidhānavyūho nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvaduḥkhavipramokṣapraṇidhivilambo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvasukhaniṣpattisaṃbhavo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvaparipākavinayāparikhedagarbho nāma samādhiḥ / sarvabodhisattvamārgāvataraṇadhvajo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇasaṃbhavavyūho nāma samādhiḥ / evaṃpramukhāni asyā daśa samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇyavakrāntāni //
body.translated_text: For her, who had been born of that great surge of joy, that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciḥśrīguṇaketurāja</s> revealed a <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>), attended by a retinue of <s>sūtrāntas</s> equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Having heard that <s>sūtrānta</s>, she entered ten hundred-thousands of <s>samādhi</s>-gateways — tender and of blissful touch. Just as the consciousness of an embryo conceived that very day [rests] in the mother's womb, just as the production of <s>karma</s> of beings [is subtle], just as the seed-sprout-cause of a <s>śāla</s>-tree planted that very day [is tender] — even so those <s>samādhis</s> were tender and lovely. Namely: the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatābhimukhavijñāpana</s> (Cognition Facing All <s>Tathāgatas</s>); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvakṣetraprasarānugatāvabhāsa</s> (Radiance Following the Expanse of All Fields); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvatryadhvanayāvatārapraveśa</s> (Entry into Descent through the Methods of All Three Times); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvabuddhapraṇidhānasāgaravijñāpana</s> (Cognition of the Ocean of Vows of All <s>Buddhas</s>); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhapratipīḍitasarvaniryāṇanirghoṣavijñāpana</s> (Cognition of the Sound of All Deliverances for Those Oppressed by the Suffering of All <s>Saṃsāra</s>); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasattvatamondhakāravidhamanapraṇidhānavyūha</s> (Array of the Vow to Dispel the Darkness and Gloom of All Beings); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasattvaduḥkhavipramokṣapraṇidhivilamba</s> (Suspended Vow of the Liberation from the Suffering of All Beings); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasattvasukhaniṣpattisaṃbhava</s> (Arising of the Accomplishment of the Happiness of All Beings); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasattvaparipākavinayāparikhedagarbha</s> (Womb of Unwearied Ripening and Discipline of All Beings); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvabodhisattvamārgāvataraṇadhvaja</s> (Banner of Descending into the Path of All <s>Bodhisattvas</s>); the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇasaṃbhavavyūha</s> (Array of the Arising of Ascending the Stages of All <s>Bodhisattvas</s>) — headed by these, ten hundred-thousands of <s>samādhi</s>-gateways were entered by her. //
