body.text: sā sūkṣmasamāhitacittā aniñjanacittā praharṣitacittā samāśvāsitacittā anābhāsacittā kalyāṇamitreṣvanugatacittā gambhīrasarvajñatārambaṇacittā maitrānugamanasāgaraprasṛtacittā sarvābhiniveśoccalitacittā sarvalokaviṣayāsaṃvāsacittā tathāgataviṣayāvataraṇacittā sarvabuddharūpavarṇasāgarāvabhāsitacittā akṣubhitacittā anīritacittā apratihatacittā abhinnacittā anunnatacittā anavanatacittā akhinnacittā anivartyacittā asaṃsīdanacittā sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyapticittā sarvadharmasvabhāvanayasāgarānugatacittā sarvadharmapravicayanayānugatacittā sarvasattvasamudrāvataraṇacittā sarvajagatparitrāṇacittā vipulabuddhasamudrāvabhāsasaṃjātacittā, sarvatathāgatapraṇidhānasāgarāvataraṇacittā sarvāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇacittā vipulapuṇyasaṃbhārasamudānayanacittā daśatathāgatabalapratilābhābhimukhacittā sarvabodhisattvaviṣayāvabhāsapratilabdhacittā sarvabodhisattvasaṃbhārasaṃvartanacittā sarvadiksamudraspharaṇacittā samantabhadramahāpraṇidhānādhyālambanatāyai, daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ praṇidhānasamudraiḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ pūrvapraṇidhānaṃ svabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhaye 'bhinirharati sma, yaduta sarvasattvaparipākavinayāya dharmadhātunayasamudraprasaraparijñāyai dharmadhātunayasamudrāvataraṇatāyai sarvabuddhakṣetreṣvaparāntakalpabodhisattvacaryāvataraṇatāyai sarvabodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalāparāntakalpasaṃvāsanatāyai sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇatāyai sarvakalyāṇamitrārāgaṇatāyai
body.translated_text: She, with subtly concentrated mind, unmoved mind, delighted mind, consoled mind, non-appearing mind, mind following spiritual friends, mind with the deep support of omniscience, mind extended in the ocean of following loving-kindness, mind displaced from all clinging, mind not dwelling in the domain of all worlds, mind descending into the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, mind illuminated by the ocean of form-colors of all <s>Buddhas</s>, unagitated mind, unstirred mind, unobstructed mind, undivided mind, un-exalted mind, un-depressed mind, unwearied mind, unreturning mind, unsinking mind, mind contemplating the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, mind following the ocean of the method of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, mind following the method of investigating all <s>dharmas</s>, mind descending into the ocean of all beings, mind protecting all the world, mind arisen from the illumination of the vast ocean of <s>Buddhas</s>, mind descending into the ocean of vows of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, mind scattering the mountains of all obstructions, mind gathering the vast accumulation of merit, mind facing the attainment of the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, mind having attained the illumination of the domain of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, mind accumulating the provisions of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, mind pervading the ocean of all directions — for the support of the great vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, she brought forth the former vow of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the purification of her own <s>Buddha</s>-field through oceans of vows equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields — namely, for the ripening and discipline of all beings, for comprehending the ocean-expanse of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>-method, for descending into the ocean of <s>dharmadhātu</s>-methods, for descending into <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct for the ultimate future <s>kalpas</s> in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, for dwelling in the maṇḍala of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct throughout ultimate future <s>kalpas</s>, for approaching all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the non-separation from all spiritual friends

body.text: sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānaparipūraṇatāyai praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvajñajñānavirohaṇavibodhanabodhisattvacaryānupacchedanatāyai / evaṃpramukhairdaśabuddhakṣetrapramāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ praṇidhānābhinirhāramukhasamudraiḥ samantabhadrāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ praṇidhimabhinirharati sma tasyāḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhyabhinirhārāya //
body.translated_text: for the fulfillment of the worship and service of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the uninterrupted <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of awakening and growing the sprout of omniscient knowledge at every mind-moment — headed by these, through oceans of gateways of bringing forth vows equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields, she brought forth the vow for the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, for the accomplishment of the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: sa bhagavān samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurājastathāgataḥ pūrvakuśalamūlāni saṃcodayati udyotayati saṃdarśayati vivṛṇoti vibhajati saṃprakāśayati sārīkaroti avipraṇāśatāyai, vipulīkaroti mahāspharaṇatāyai, sthāpayati sarvajñatāpramāṇīkaraṇatāyai, yaduta prathamacittotpādamupādāya tathāgatapūrvapraṇidhisamudrāsaṃkhyeyapratilābhāya //
body.translated_text: That <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja</s> stimulated, illuminated, displayed, opened, analyzed, revealed, and made substantial [her] former roots of merit for their non-destruction; made them vast for their great pervading; and established them for making [them] immeasurable through omniscience — that is, beginning from the first generation of the mind, for the attainment of the innumerable ocean of former vows of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani tataḥ pareṇa daśame kalpe maṇisūryacandravidyotitaprabhāyāṃ lokadhātau candradhvajaśrīketoḥ tathāgatasya pravacane samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrayā dārikayā samantabhadrabodhisattvasamādāpitayā pralugnastathāgatavigrahaḥ padmaniṣaṇṇaḥ pratisaṃskāritaḥ / pratisaṃskārya citritaḥ / citrayitvā ratnapratimaṇḍitaḥ kṛtaḥ / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ samantabhadrabodhisattvakalyāṇamitramāgamya / sā tena kuśalamūlena avinipātadharmiṇī sadā devendrakuleṣu manuṣyendrakuleṣu copapannā, sarvatra cābhirūpābhūt prāsādikā darśanīyā paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā / sadā ca avirahitābhūttathāgatadarśanena samantabhadrabodhisattvena / tenaiva ca kalyāṇamitreṇa tasyāṃ tasyāṃ jātau paripācitā saṃcoditā smāritā / etarhi ca punastayā samantabhadro bodhisattva ārāgito 'tyantāvirāgaṇatayā //
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, son of good family, in the past, beyond that, in the tenth <s>kalpa</s>, in the world-realm <s>Maṇisūryacandravidyotitaprabhā</s> (Radiance Illuminated by the Sun, Moon, and Gem), in the dispensation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candradhvajaśrīketu</s> (Banner-Crest of the Glory of the Moon), by the maiden <s>Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā</s>, who had been inspired by <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, a dilapidated image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated upon a lotus was restored. Having restored it, it was painted. Having painted it, it was adorned with jewels. The aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening was generated through coming to the spiritual friend <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>. She, through that root of merit, became one whose nature was not to fall [into lower realms], and was always born in the families of <s>Devendras</s> and human kings, and everywhere she was beautiful, graceful, lovely to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious color. She was always never separated from the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and from <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>. Through that very spiritual friend, in each and every birth she was ripened, stimulated, and reminded. And even now, <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> has been pleased by her through utter non-separation. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍo nāma rājacakravartī? na khalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / maitreyaḥ sa bodhisattvaḥ tena kālena tena samayena vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍo nāma rājābhūccakravartī / syātkhalu punaste kulaputra evam - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā nāma rājabhāryābhūt? na khalu evaṃ draṣṭavyam / iyaṃ praśāntarutasāgaravatī nāma rātridevatā, yā mamānantaraṃ saṃniṣaṇṇā / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā nāma rājaduhitā abhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā nāma rājaduhitā abhūvam / yanme dārikābhūtayā indradhvajaketostathāgatasya pravacane pralugnastathāgatavigrahaḥ padmodgataḥ pratisaṃskāritaḥ, sa me heturabhūt yāvadanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / yadā cāsmi samantabhadreṇa bodhisattvena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā, sa me kulaputra prathamacittotpādo bodhāya abhūt / yadā ca sa me bhagavān samantajñānārciḥśrīguṇaketurājaḥ tathāgata upasaṃkramya ābharaṇairavakīrṇaḥ, tathāgatavikurvitaprātihāryaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā dharmaśca me tasya bhagavato 'ntikācchrutaḥ, tadā mayaiṣa sarvalokābhimuikhajagadvinayanidarśano bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ / sarve ca te sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā ārāgitā abhirādhitāḥ,
body.translated_text: What do you think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍa</s> someone else? You should not see it so, son of good family. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> was at that time the <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍa</s>. And you might think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the queen named <s>Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā</s> someone else? It should not be seen thus. It was this night goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>, who is seated next to me. And what do you think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the princess named <s>Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā</s> someone else? It should not be seen thus. I myself at that time was the princess named <s>Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā</s>. The act I performed as a maiden — restoring the dilapidated image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that had emerged from a lotus, in the dispensation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indradhvajaketu</s> — that was my cause, all the way up to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And when I was inspired by <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> to [aspire for] unsurpassed perfect awakening, that, son of good family, was my first generation of the mind toward awakening. And when I approached that <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānārciḥśrīguṇaketurāja</s> and was showered with ornaments, and beheld the miraculous display of <s>Tathāgata</s>-transformations, and heard the <s>Dharma</s> in the presence of that <s>Bhagavān</s> — then I obtained this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the display of disciplining all the world facing all beings. And all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s> were pleased, propitiated

body.text: sarvopakaraṇapūjāsatkāreṇa ca satkṛtāḥ / yaśca taistathāgatairdharmo bhāṣitaḥ, sa me sarvaṃ śrutaḥ / teṣāṃ cāsmi tathāgatānāmavavādānuśāsanīṣu pratipannā / teṣu ca me tathāgateṣu tīvraṃ gauravaṃ pratilabdhaṃ yathārūpeṇa gauraveṇa ekacittakṣaṇe tān sarvāṃstathāgatāṃstāni bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāni tāni ca sarvāṇi buddhakṣetrāṇi paśyāmi //
body.translated_text: and honored with the worship of all requisites. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> was spoken by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, all of it was heard by me. And I practiced according to the admonitions and instructions of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And I obtained such intense reverence toward those <s>Tathāgatas</s> that by such reverence, in a single mind-moment, I behold all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, all those <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly-maṇḍalas, and all those <s>Buddha</s>-fields. //

body.text: tasyāṃ ca vairocanaśriyāṃ lokadhātau saṃvṛttāyāṃ tatra ca virajomaṇḍale kalpe nirgate 'nantare maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā nāma lokadhāturmahāprabhaśca nāma kalpo 'bhūt / tatra pañca buddhaśatānyutpannāni / tāni mayā sarvāṇyārāgitāni / tasmiṃśca khalu mahāprabhe kalpe mahākaruṇameghadhvajo nāma tathāgataḥ prāthamakalpiko 'bhūt / sa mayā rātridevatābhūtayā abhiniṣkrāman pūjitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vajranārāyaṇaketurnāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / sa mayā cakravartibhūtayā pūjitaḥ / tena ca me sarvabuddhotpādasaṃbhavo nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśito daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamasūtrāntaparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutaḥ udgṛhītaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jvalanārciḥparvataśrīvyūho nāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / sa me śreṣṭhiduhitṛbhūtayā pūjitaḥ / tena ca me tryadhvāvabhāsagarbho nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśito jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamasūtrāntaparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutaḥ udgṛhītaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sarvadharmasamudrābhyudgatavegarājo nāma tathāgato loka udapādi / sa mayā asurarājabhūtayā pūjitaḥ / tena ca me sarvadharmadhātutalajñānabhedo nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ pañcasūtrāntaśataparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutaḥ udgṛhītaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ gambhīradharmaśrīsamudraprabho nāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / sa me nāgendrakanyābhūtayā pūjitaścintārājamaṇiratnameghavarṣamabhipravarṣantyā / tena ca me prītisāgaravivardhanavego nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśito daśasūtrāntakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutvodgṛhītaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnaśikharārciḥparvatapradīpo nāma tathāgataḥ utpannaḥ / sa ca me sāgaradevatābhūtayā ratnapadmameghavarṣairupasaṃkramya pūjitaḥ / tena ca me dharmadhātusāgaranayaprabho nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśito daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamasūtrāntaparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutvodgṛhītaḥ, smṛtyā ca saṃdhāritaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśrīrnāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / sa me pañcābhijñaṛṣibhūtayā maharddhivikurvitena ṣaṣṭiṛṣisahasraparivṛtayā upasaṃkramaya gandhapuṣpaśikharameghānabhipravarṣantyā pūjitaḥ / tena ca me anālayadharmapradīpo nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ ṣaṣṭisūtrāntasahasraparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutvodgṛhītaḥ, tasyānantaraṃ vairocanaśrīgarbho nāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / ahaṃ ca samatārthasaṃbhavā nāma pṛthivīdevatā abhuvam / sā ahamaprameyapṛthivīdevatāparivārā sarvaratnadrumakośebhyo ratnapuṣpameghavarṣāṇyutsṛjamānā sarvaratnahārameghān pravarṣamāṇā upasaṃkrāntā tasya tathāgatasya pūjākarmaṇe / tena ca me sarvatathāgatasaṃbhavajñānākaragarbho nāma sūtrāntaḥ saṃprakāśito 'prameyasūtrāntaparivāraḥ / sa ca me śrutvā dhārito na vipraṇāśitaḥ /
body.translated_text: When that <s>Vairocanaśrī</s> world-realm had come to an end and when that <s>Virajomaṇḍala</s> kalpa had passed, next there arose a world-realm called <s>Maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā</s> and a kalpa called <s>Mahāprabha</s>. There five hundred Buddhas arose, and I worshipped them all. In that <s>Mahāprabha</s> kalpa, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahākaruṇameghadhvaja</s> was the first of the kalpa. I worshipped him as a night-goddess when he went forth. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vajranārāyaṇaketu</s>. I worshipped him having become a <s>cakravartin</s>. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Sarvabuddhotpādasaṃbhava</s>, accompanied by <s>sūtrāntas</s> equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields. I heard and retained it. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jvalanārciḥparvataśrīvyūha</s>. I worshipped him having become a merchant's daughter. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Tryadhvāvabhāsagarbha</s>, accompanied by <s>sūtrāntas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. I heard and retained it. After him the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvadharmasamudrābhyudgatavegarāja</s> appeared in the world. I worshipped him having become an <s>asura</s> king. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Sarvadharmadhātutalajñānabheda</s>, accompanied by five hundred <s>sūtrāntas</s>. I heard and retained it. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Gambhīradharmaśrīsamudraprabha</s>. I worshipped him having become a <s>nāgendra</s> princess, raining down showers of wish-fulfilling jewel-gem clouds. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Prītisāgaravivardhanavega</s>, accompanied by ten million hundred thousand <s>sūtrāntas</s>. I heard and retained it. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaśikharārciḥparvatapradīpa</s>. I approached and worshipped him having become an ocean deity, with showers of jewel-lotus clouds. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Dharmadhātusāgaranayaprabha</s>, accompanied by <s>sūtrāntas</s> equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields. I heard and retained it, and held it in memory. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśrī</s>. I worshipped him having become a <s>ṛṣi</s> with the five supernatural powers, approaching with great miraculous transformations, surrounded by sixty thousand <s>ṛṣis</s>, raining down clouds of fragrant flower-peaks. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Anālayadharmapradīpa</s>, accompanied by sixty thousand <s>sūtrāntas</s>. I heard and retained it. After him arose the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vairocanaśrīgarbha</s>. I became an earth deity named <s>Samatārthasaṃbhavā</s>. Accompanied by immeasurable earth deities, releasing showers of jewel-flower clouds from all jewel-tree treasuries, raining down clouds of jewel-garlands, I approached for the worship of that <s>Tathāgata</s>. He illuminated for me the <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatasaṃbhavajñānākaragarbha</s>, accompanied by immeasurable <s>sūtrāntas</s>. I heard and retained it and did not let it be lost.

body.text: teṣāṃ khalu kulaputra pañcānāṃ buddhaśatānāṃ sarvapaścimo dharmadhātugaganapūrṇaratnaśikharaśrīpradīpo nāma tathāgato loka udapādi / ahaṃ ca tena kālena abhirāmaśrīvakrā nāma
body.translated_text: The very last of those five hundred Buddhas, O son of good family, was the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmadhātugaganapūrṇaratnaśikharaśrīpradīpa</s> who appeared in the world. At that time I was a dancer girl named <s>Abhirāmaśrīvakrā</s>

body.text: naṭadārikā abhūvam / sā ahaṃ tasya tathāgatasya nagarapraveśasamaye nāṭake pravṛtte buddhānubhāvena ūrdhvaṃ gaganatale sthitvā gāthāsahasreṇa taṃ tathāgatamabhiṣṭuvantī upasaṃkrāntā / tena ca me dharmadhātuvidyotitavyūhaṃ nāma raśmimūrṇakośādutsṛjya sarvakāyo 'vabhāsitaḥ / tayā ca me raśmyā samanantaraspṛṣṭayā dharmadhātunayāvartagarbho nāma vimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ //
body.translated_text: . When that <s>Tathāgata</s> entered the city and a dance performance was underway, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s> I stood aloft in the sky and approached, praising that <s>Tathāgata</s> with a thousand verses. He then released from his <s>ūrṇā</s>-tuft a radiance called <s>Dharmadhātuvidyotitavyūha</s>, which illuminated my entire body. The moment that ray touched me, I attained the <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) called <s>Dharmadhātunayāvartagarbha</s>.

body.text: iti hi kulaputra etān pramukhān kṛtvā yāni tatra maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhāyāṃ lokadhātau mahāprabhe kalpe pañca buddhaśatānyutpannāni, tāni mayā sarvāṇyārāgitāni, pūjā ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ kṛtā / yaśca me taistathāgatairdharmo deśitaḥ, taṃ sarvaṃ smarāmi / ekapadavyañjanamapi me tato dharmanayānna vipramuṣitam / ekaikasya ca me tathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkrāmantyā aparimāṇānāṃ sattvānāmarthaḥ kṛto buddhadharmasaṃvarṇanatayā / ekaikasya ca me tathāgatasya antikāt tryadhvajñānagarbhadharmadhātuvipulo nāma dharmadhātuśarīrasāgaraḥ sarvajñatāvidyudavabhāsaḥ pratilabdhaḥ sarvasamantabhadracaryāsaṃvāsasamavasaraṇaḥ / etarhyapi me kulaputra praticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyāstathāgatā ābhāsamāgacchanti / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sahadarśanāt sarvajñatāvidyudavabhāsā āśaye 'vakrāntā apratilabdhapūrvā adṛṣṭapūrvāḥ / na ca samantabhadrāyā bodhisattvacaryāyā uccalāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? anantamadhyanirdeśa eṣa sarvajñatāvidyudavabhāsapratilambhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O son of good family, taking these as foremost, all five hundred Buddhas that arose in the world-realm <s>Maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā</s> during the <s>Mahāprabha</s> kalpa were worshipped by me, and I performed worship for those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Whatever <s>Dharma</s> was taught to me by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I remember it all. Not even a single word or syllable of those <s>Dharma</s>-methods has been lost to me. And as I approached each <s>Tathāgata</s>, I brought benefit to immeasurable beings through the praising of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s>. From each <s>Tathāgata</s> I attained the <s>dharmadhātu</s>-body-ocean called <s>Tryadhvajñānagarbhadharmadhātuvipula</s>, vast as the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, illuminated by the lightning-flash of omniscience, an assembly-ground for dwelling in all <s>Samantabhadra</s>-practice. Even now, O son of good family, at every moment of thought, <s>Tathāgatas</s> without middle or end come into my vision. Upon seeing all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, lightning-flashes of omniscience, never before attained, never before seen, enter into my intention. Yet I do not deviate from the <s>bodhisattva</s>-practice of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. Why is that? Because this attainment of the lightning-flash of omniscience is an exposition without end or middle.

body.text: atha khalu samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tameva sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā pradarśayamānā buddhādhiṣṭhānena sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>, at that moment, further displaying that very <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) called 'the demonstration of the disciplining of the world facing all realms,' by the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, addressed the youth <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.text: śṛṇu sūdhanā vacanametu mamā gambhīra durdṛśa durāvagaham /
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Sudhana</s>, to this my word, profound, hard to see, hard to comprehend,
the method of distinguishing all three times, the all-pervading radiance of the <s>dharma</s>-light <s>maṇḍala</s>. // 30 //

children.text: yatha saṃbhuta prathama cittu mamā bodhāya buddhaguṇaprārthanayā /
children.translated_text: How my first thought arose toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), through aspiration for the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: yatha bodhivimokṣu ayu labdhu maṃyā etaṃ śṛṇohi pravibhāganayam // 31 //
children.translated_text: how this <s>bodhi</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) was attained by me — hear this method of detailed exposition! // 31 //
Beyond a number of kalpas equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields before this,
there was a vast, stainless world-realm here called <s>Vairocanadhvajapradīpaśrī</s>. // 32 //

children.text: kalpo abhū virajamaṇḍalu yo acchinnu yatra jinavaṃśu abhūt /
children.translated_text: There was a kalpa called <s>Virajamaṇḍala</s>, uninterrupted, in which a lineage of <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) existed;
in it arose <s>Daśabalas</s> (Possessors of Ten Powers), free from affliction, equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. // 33 //
In that kalpa, <s>Samantaratanārciśrī</s> was the first <s>Sugata</s>, then <s>Guṇaketurāja</s>,

children.text: dharmadhvajaḥ śirisumeru jino guṇakeśarīśvaru caturtha jinaḥ // 34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmadhvaja</s>, <s>Śrīsumeru</s> the <s>Jina</s>, and <s>Guṇakeśarīśvara</s> the fourth <s>Jina</s>. // 34 //
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Śāntirāja</s>, <s>Samitāyuratha</s>, <s>Yaśaparvata</s>, <s>Guṇasumeruśrī</s>,

children.text: jinabhāskaraḥ śaśimukho bhagavānete daśa prathama atra naye // 35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jinabhāskara</s>, and the Blessed One <s>Śaśimukha</s> — these are the first ten in this sequence. // 35 //
<s>Gaganālaya</s> the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Samataprabha</s>, <s>Diśasaṃbhava</s>, <s>Smṛtisamudramukha</s>,
<s>Abhyudgatā</s> the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Sumeruśrī</s>, and the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Dharmārciparvataśrī</s>, // 36 //

children.text: padmodgato navamu kāruṇiko jinu dharmadhātukusumo daśamaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Padmodgata</s> the ninth, <s>Kāruṇika</s> the <s>Jina</s>, and <s>Dharmadhātukusuma</s> the tenth —

children.text: buddhosamudra paridīpayato eṣā daśā dvitiya atra naye // 37 //
children.translated_text: illuminating the ocean of Buddhas, this is the second decade in this sequence. // 37 //
<s>Prabhaketurājamati</s>, <s>Jñānamati</s>, <s>Citrārtha</s>, <s>Indraśrī</s>, <s>Devamati</s>,
the <s>Jina</s> <s>Vegarājamati</s>, <s>Jñānaśrī</s>, <s>Avabhāsarāja</s>, <s>Prabhaketuśrī</s>, // 38 //

children.text: vikrāntadevagati nāma jino tatha dharmadhātupadumo daśamaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Vikrāntadevagati</s>, and <s>Dharmadhātupaduma</s> the tenth —

children.text: evaṃ nayaṃ vipula darśayato tṛtiyā daśā bhavati atra naye // 39 //
children.translated_text: thus displaying the vast method, this is the third decade in this sequence. // 39 //
The Blessed One <s>Ratnārciparvataśrī</s>, then <s>Guṇasamudraśrī</s>,
<s>Dharmaprabha</s>, <s>Padumagarbhaśrī</s>, and the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Gaticandranetranayanaḥ</s>, // 40 //
<s>Gandhaprabha</s>, <s>Maṇisumeruśrī</s>, <s>Gandharvakāyu</s>, <s>Prabharāja</s>,
<s>Maṇigarbharāja</s>, <s>Śrītejavatī</s> — the tenth <s>Jina</s> is <s>Praśamarūpagati</s>. // 41 //
Then the <s>Jina</s> <s>Vipulabuddhi</s>, <s>Ratanaprabha</s>, <s>Gaganameghaśrī</s>,

children.text: varalakṣaṇaḥ śiri babhūva jino bratamaṇḍalaśca svaśarīraprabhaḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Varalakṣaṇa</s>, the <s>Jina</s> <s>Śrī</s> arose, <s>Bratamaṇḍala</s> with the radiance of his own body, // 42 //
<s>Nārāyaṇavrata</s>, <s>Sumeruśrī</s>, <s>Guṇacakravālaśrīrāja</s> the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: aparājitavratadhvajo bhagavān drumaparvato daśamu teṣa jinaḥ // 43 //
children.translated_text: the Blessed One <s>Aparājitavratadhvaja</s>, and <s>Drumaparvata</s> the tenth of those <s>Jinas</s>. // 43 //
The <s>Jina</s> <s>Sālendrarājaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Lokendrakāyapratibhāsaprabha</s>,
the Blessed One <s>Abhyudgataprabhaśrī</s>, <s>Virajaprabha</s>, <s>Dharaṇitejaśrī</s>, // 44 //
<s>Gambhīradharmaguṇarājaśrī</s> the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Dharmasāgaranirghoṣamati</s>,
<s>Merudhvaja</s>, <s>Śrīprabhāsamati</s> — the tenth <s>Jina</s> is <s>Ratanarājaśrī</s>. // 45 //
<s>Brahmaprabha</s>, the <s>Jina</s> <s>Gaganaghoṣa</s>, and <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsaśrī</s>,
the Blessed One <s>Ālokamaṇḍalaprabha</s>, <s>Daśabhedajñānaprabhaketumatī</s>, // 46 //
<s>Gaganapradīpa</s>, <s>Abhirāmaśrī</s>, the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Vairocanaprabhaśrī</s>,
<s>Puṇyaprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Śāntaśrī</s> — the tenth is <s>Mahākaruṇameghaśrī</s>. // 47 //
<s>Tathatāprabha</s>, <s>Balaprabhāsamati</s>, the <s>Jina</s> <s>Sarvajagābhimukharūpa</s>,

children.text: abhyudgatābhu abhu tatra jinastadanantaraṃ samaśarīru jinaḥ // 48 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhyudgatābha</s> the <s>Jina</s> arose there, then the <s>Jina</s> <s>Samaśarīra</s>, // 48 //
then <s>Dharmodgata</s> the <s>Sugata</s> arose, after him <s>Anilavegaśrī</s>,
<s>Śūradhvaja</s>, <s>Ratanagātraśrī</s> — the tenth is <s>Tryadhvapratibhāsaprabha</s>. // 49 //
<s>Praṇidhānasāgaraprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Vajrāśaya</s>, <s>Giriśrī</s> the second,
the third <s>Jina</s> <s>Harisumeruśrī</s>, <s>Smṛtiketurājaśrī</s>, <s>Dharmamati</s>, // 50 //
<s>Prajñāpradīpa</s>, <s>Prabhaketuśrī</s>, then the <s>Jina</s> <s>Vipulabuddhi</s>,
the <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmadhātunayajñānagati</s>, <s>Dharmasamudramatijñānaśrī</s>, // 51 //
<s>Dharmadhara</s>, <s>Ratanadānaśrī</s>, the <s>Jina</s> <s>Guṇacakravālaśrīmegha</s>,
<s>Kṣāntipradīpaśrī</s>, <s>Tejavatī</s>, <s>Vegaprabha</s>, the <s>Jina</s> <s>Śamathaghoṣa</s>, // 52 //
<s>Śāntidhvaja</s>, <s>Jagapradīpaśrī</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Mahāpraṇidhivegaśrī</s>,
the Blessed One <s>Aparājitadhvajabala</s>, and the <s>Jina</s> <s>Jñānārcisāgaraśrī</s>. // 53 //
<s>Dharmeśvara</s> the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Asaṅgamati</s>, <s>Jagamantrasāgaranirghoṣamati</s>,
<s>Sarvasvarāṅgarutaghoṣaśrī</s>, <s>Vaśavartiyajñayaśayaṣṭimati</s>, // 54 //
the Blessed One <s>Diśadeśāmukhajaga</s>, <s>Sattvāśayassamaśarīriśrī</s>,
the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Parārthasavihāraśrī</s>, and the auspicious <s>Jina</s> <s>Prakṛtīśarīraśrī</s>. // 55 //

children.text: ete jinā pramukha tatra abhūdupapadyi ye jina pradīpakarāḥ /
children.translated_text: These <s>Jinas</s> were the foremost who arose there; those <s>Jinas</s> who arose were lamps of light,
worshipped during kalpas equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, in the ocean-method of the <s>Jinas</s>. // 56 //
During kalpas equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, whatever <s>Jinas</s> arose,

children.text: te sarvi pūjita mayā sugatā etaṃ vimokṣanayamotariyā // 57 //
children.translated_text: all those <s>Sugatas</s> were worshipped by me, through crossing over by this method of liberation. // 57 //

children.text: kalpānananta ahu cīrṇa purā etaṃ vimokṣanayu bhāvayatī /
children.translated_text: For innumerable kalpas I have practiced this in the past, cultivating this method of liberation;

children.text: tvamapi śruṇitva pratipadya laghu pratilapsyase nayamimaṃ nacirāt // 58 //
children.translated_text: you too, having heard and entered upon it swiftly, will attain this method before long. // 58 //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamanantamadhyabodhisattvacaryāsāgaranānādhimuktisaṃvāsānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ nānāśayaśarīrāṇāṃ vividhendriyasāgarapariniṣpannānāṃ vicitrabodhisattvapraṇidhānasupratividdhānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśana</s> (Display of the Discipline of the World Facing All Worlds) that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the boundless and middleway-less ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, who dwell in various resolute faiths, whose bodies are of various dispositions, who are accomplished in the ocean of manifold faculties, who are penetrated by variegated <s>bodhisattva</s> vows? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva bodhimaṇḍe praśāntarutasāgaravatī nāma rātridevatā, yā mamānantaraṃ jyotirdhvajamaṇirājapratimaṇḍitagarbhe padmāsane niṣaṇṇā daśarātridevatāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasraparivārā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> is a night-goddess named <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> (Possessing an Ocean of Peaceful Sounds), who sits right next to me on a lotus-seat adorned with the <s>Jyotirdhvajamaṇirāja</s> (King of Light-Banner Gems), surrounded by ten innumerable hundreds of thousands of night-goddesses. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should he practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokyaṃ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 35 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>, circumambulating the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s>. // 35 //

body.text: 38 Praśāntarutasāgaravatī /
body.translated_text: 38. <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāstaṃ sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayan avataran adhimucyamāno 'vagāhayamāno vipulīkurvāṇaḥ spharan prasaran vaśīkurvan avabhāsayamānaḥ samavasaran yena praśāntarutasāgaravatī rātridevatā tenopasaṃkramya praśāntarutasāgaravatyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya praśāntarutasāgaravatīṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praśāntarutasāgaravatyā rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ahamārye devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitaḥ / so 'haṃ kalyāṇamitrasaṃniśrayeṇa bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvacaryāmavataran bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ pratipadyamāno bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ niryātumicchāmi / tadvadasva me ārye devate kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, cultivating, descending into, resolving upon, plunging into, expanding, pervading, extending, mastering, illuminating, and converging in that <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī</s> called <s>Sarvalokābhimukhajagadvinayanidarśana</s> (Display of the Discipline of the World Facing All Worlds) — approached the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>. Having bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>, having circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, standing before her with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'Noble goddess, I have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. And I, relying on the spiritual friend, training in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, descending into <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, practicing <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, established in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, wish to emerge toward omniscience. May the noble goddess tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should he practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu praśāntarutasāgaravatī rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvaṃ kalyāṇamitrasaṃniśrayeṇa bodhisattvacaryāsāgaraṃ parimārgasi / ahaṃ kulaputra vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sudhana āha - kiṃkarmāsi devate, kiṃviṣayāsi, kiṃprayogā kiṃvyavacārā? ka etasya vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ? sā avocat - ahaṃ kulaputra cittāśayasāgarapariśuddhisamatāpratipannā sarvalokarajomalavimalābhedyavyūhasaṃpratipannā avaivartyāpratyudāvartyārambhacittā ratnaparvataguṇālaṃkārākampyacittā apratiṣṭhitānālayacittā sarvajagatparitrāṇābhimukhacittā sarvabuddhasamudradarśanāvitṛptacittā sarvabodhisattvabalāśayaviśuddhacittā mahājñānāvabhāsavyūhasmṛtisāgarasaṃvāsacittā sarvasattvaśokakāntārasamatikramaṇāya pratipannā, sarvasattvaduḥkhadaurmanasyavinivartanāyābhiyuktā, sarvasattvānāṃ nāmarūpaśabdagandharasasparśasamudācāravinivartanāya pratipannā, sarvasattvānāṃ priyāpriyaviprayogasaṃprayogaduḥkhavyupaśamāya pratipannā, sarvasattvānāṃ viṣayapratyayasaṃbhavasaṃmohaduḥkhavinivartanaprayuktā, vinipatitasarvasattvapratiśaraṇabhūtā sarvasattvasaṃsārasaṃvāsaduḥkhaniḥsaraṇasaṃdarśanābhiyuktā, sarvasattvānāṃ jātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsavinivartanāya pratipannā, sarvasattvānāmanuttaratathāgatasukhapariniṣpattaye pratipannā, sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ sukhopasthānena tuṣṭiṃ vindāmi, teṣāṃ ca dhārmikīṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidadhāmi / anupūrveṇa ca tān sarvajñatāyāṃ paripācayāmi / yaduta mahābhavanavimānagatānāṃ sattvānāmanabhiratiṃ saṃjanayāmi / tāni tāni ca daurmanasyāni vyapanayāmi / sarvābhiniveśavyavacchedāya sarvadharmasvabhāvaparijñāyai ca dharmaṃ deśayāmi / mātāpitṛbhrātṛbhaginījñātisālohitasamavadhānagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ cirakālasaṃjātasnehānāṃ buddhabodhisattvasamavadhānapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / bhāryāputrasamavadhānagatānāṃ
body.translated_text: Then indeed the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Well done, well done, son of good family, that you, relying on the spiritual friend, seek the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct! I, son of good family, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūha</s> (Array of Mind-Moments Arising from the Surge of Vast Joy).' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'What is your activity, goddess? What is your domain? What is your practice? What is your course of conduct? What is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called Array of Mind-Moments Arising from the Surge of Vast Joy?' She replied: 'I, son of good family, have entered the equality of the purification of the ocean of mental dispositions, have entered the stainless, indestructible array of the dust-impurity of all worlds. My mind is of irreversible and unturnable initial effort. My mind is unshakeable like a jewel-mountain of quality-ornaments. My mind is without foundation and without abode. My mind faces the protection of all beings. My mind is unsatiated in seeing the ocean of all <s>Buddhas</s>. My mind is purified in the aspiration of the power of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. My mind dwells in the ocean of recollection of the array of the illumination of great knowledge. I am engaged in crossing all beings beyond the wilderness of grief. I am devoted to turning back the suffering and dejection of all beings. I am engaged in turning back the operations of name, form, sound, smell, taste, and touch in all beings. I am engaged in the pacification of the suffering of separation from the beloved and association with the unloved for all beings. I am devoted to turning back the suffering of the delusion arising from conditions of sense-objects for all beings. I am a refuge for all beings who have fallen. I am devoted to showing the way out of the suffering of dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s> for all beings. I am engaged in turning back birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress for all beings. I am engaged in accomplishing unsurpassed <s>Tathāgata</s>-happiness for all beings. I find satisfaction in providing comfort and happiness to beings dwelling in all villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, and I provide them with righteous protection, defense, and guardianship. And gradually I ripen them toward omniscience. That is to say: for beings dwelling in great mansions and palaces, I generate disenchantment; I dispel their various dejections; I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the cutting off of all attachments and for the thorough understanding of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. For beings gathered with mothers, fathers, brothers, sisters, relatives, and kinsmen, who have developed long-standing affection, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of gathering with <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. For those gathered with

sattvānāṃ sarvasaṃsāraratitṛṣṇāprahāṇāya sarvasattvasamacittatāyai mahākaruṇāpratilābhāya
dharmaṃ deśayāmi / antarāpaṇamadhyagatānāṃ sattvānāmāryasaṃghatathāgatadarśanasamavadhānasamavasaraṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / bhogamadamattānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣāntipāramitāparipūraṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / nṛttagītavādyābhiratānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmārāmaratyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / viṣayaratigṛddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgataviṣayasamavasaraṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / krodhāviṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣāntipāramitāpratiṣṭhāpanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / kusīdānāṃ sattvānāṃ vīryapāramitāpariśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / vibhrāntacittānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgatadhyānapāramitāpratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / dṛṣṭikṛtagahanapraskannānāṃ sattvānāmavidyāndhakārapatitānāṃ dṛṣṭikṛtagahanāvidyāndhakāravinivartanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / duṣprajñānāṃ sattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāpratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / traidhātukābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃsāraduḥkhaniḥsaraṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / hīnādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgatabodhipraṇidhānaparipūraye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ātmahitaprayuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvasattvahitāvahanapraṇidhānaparipūraye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / durbalādhyāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvabalapāramitāviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / avidyātamondhakāracetasāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvajñānapāramitāviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / virūpakāyānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgatarūpakāyaviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / visaṃsthitaśarīrāṇāṃ sattvānāmanuttaradharmakāyaviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / durvarṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ sūkṣmatathāgatasuvarṇavarṇacchavitāyai kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśaśarīratāviśuddhaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāmatyantatathāgatasukhapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sukhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvajñatāsukhapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / glānānāmāturāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ pratibhāsopamabodhisattvakāyapariniṣpattaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / vicitraratiprasaktānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryāratipratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / daridrāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvadharmanidhānakośapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / udyānagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhadharmaparyeṣṭyabhiyogāhetutāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / mārgagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvajñatāmārgapratipattaye dharmaṃ deśayāmi / grāmagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvatraidhātukaniḥsaraṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / janapadapradeśagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabodhimārgasamatikramāya tathāgatabhūmipratiṣṭhāpanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / nagaragatānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmarājanagarāvabhāsanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / vidiggatānāṃ sattvānāṃ tryadhvasamatājñānapratilābhāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / diggatānāṃ
sattvānāṃ sarvadharmajñānābhijñatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekāntarāgacaritānāṃ sattvānāmaśubhamukhena sarvasaṃsāraratitṛṣṇāvinivartanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / doṣacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ mahāmaitrīnayasāgarāvataraṇatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāti / mohacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvadharmamukhasamudrapravicayajñānābhijñatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / samabhāgacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvayānapraṇidhānanayasāgaravaiśeṣikatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / saṃsāraviṣayaratyāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃsāraviṣayarativinivartanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhaspṛṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhānupakliṣṭatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi /
body.translated_text: wives and sons, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of craving and thirst for delight in all <s>saṃsāra</s>, for generating equal-mindedness toward all beings, and for the attainment of great compassion. For beings in the midst of the marketplace, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the convergence in the gathering and meeting of the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> and the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For beings intoxicated and maddened by wealth, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>). For beings delighting in dance, song, and music, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for delight in the pleasure-garden of <s>Dharma</s>. For beings greedy and attached to sense-pleasures, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for convergence in the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For beings possessed by anger, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for establishing them in the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience. For lazy beings, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>). For beings of distracted mind, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). For beings fallen into the thicket of fabricated views, fallen into the darkness of ignorance, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for turning back from the thicket of fabricated views and the darkness of ignorance. For beings of poor wisdom, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). For beings attached to the three realms, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for escape from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For beings of inferior aspiration, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the fulfillment of the vow for <s>Tathāgata</s>-awakening. For beings devoted to their own welfare alone, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the fulfillment of the vow to bring about the welfare of all beings. For beings of weak aspiration, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> of powers (<s>balapāramitā</s>). For beings whose minds are in the darkness of ignorance, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>). For beings of ugly body, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form-body. For beings of ill-proportioned body, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-body. For beings of ugly complexion, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification into the subtle golden complexion of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the body pleasant to touch like <s>kācilindika</s> silk. For suffering beings, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the ultimate happiness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For happy beings, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the happiness of omniscience. For sick and ailing beings, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the accomplishment of a <s>bodhisattva</s>-body like a reflection. For beings attached to variegated pleasures, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of delight in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. For poor beings, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s treasury-store of <s>Dharma</s>. For beings gone to parks, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> as a cause for the effort and application of seeking <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. For beings on the road, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for entering the path to omniscience. For beings in villages, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for escape from the entire three realms. For beings in the provinces, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for transcending the path of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and for establishing them on the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage. For beings in cities, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for illuminating the city of the <s>Dharma</s>-King. For beings gone to the intermediate directions, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the attainment of the knowledge of the equality of the three times. For beings gone to the cardinal directions, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the superknowledge of the knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>. For beings exclusively given to passion, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> through the gateway of the impure for turning back from craving for delight in all <s>saṃsāra</s>. For beings of hateful conduct, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for descending into the ocean of the method of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). For beings of deluded conduct, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the superknowledge of the knowledge of investigating the ocean of all <s>dharma</s>-gateways. For beings of balanced conduct, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the distinction of the ocean of the method of vows for all vehicles. For beings whose disposition delights in the pleasures of <s>saṃsāra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for turning back from delight in the pleasures of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For beings touched by the suffering of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for being unafflicted by the suffering of all <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: tathāgatavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmanutpādapadasaṃprakāśanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / skandhaniketāśayānāṃ sattvānāmanālayadharmagocaravihāratāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / saṃlīnāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ mārgavyūhaviśeṣasaṃprakāśanatāyai dharmaṃ deśayāmi / adhimānaprāptānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvadharmasamatākṣāntiṃ saṃprakāśayāmi / māyāśāṭhyaviṣayāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvāśayapariśuddhiṃ saṃprakāśayāmi //
body.translated_text: For beings who are to be disciplined by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for illuminating the stage of non-arising. For beings whose disposition is attachment to the aggregates, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for dwelling in the domain of <s>dharmas</s> that are without abode. For beings of contracted disposition, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for illuminating the distinction of path-arrays. For beings who have attained conceit, I illuminate the patience of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. For beings whose disposition is the domain of deceit and crookedness, I illuminate the purification of <s>bodhisattva</s>-disposition. //

body.text: evamahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvān dharmadānena saṃgṛhya sarvaduḥkhadurgatipathebhyo vinivartayamānā devamanuṣyasaṃpattisukhāni saṃdarśayamānā traidhātukāduccālayamānā sarvajñatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayamānā vividhairupāyamukhaiḥ paripācayamānā mahāprītivegasamudrāvabhāsapratilabdhā modāmi, pramodāmi, āttamanaskā bhavāmi / api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra sarvadigvidikṣu bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānavalokayamānā nānāpraṇidhānacaritānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ nānākāyaviśuddhānāṃ nānāprabhāmaṇḍalavyūhānāmanantavarṇaraśmiprabhāmaṇḍalaṃ pramuñcamānānāṃ nānāsarvajñatānayasāgaraprasṛtajñānālokānāṃ nānāsamādhisamudrāvatīrṇānāṃ nānāvikurvitaviṣayāṇāṃ nānāsvarāṅgarutasāgaranirghoṣāṇāṃ nānābharaṇavibhūṣitaśarīrāṇāṃ nānātathāgatanayāvatīrṇānāṃ nānākṣetrasamudraprasaraprasṛtaśarīrāṇāṃ nānābuddhasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ nānāpratisaṃvinnayasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ nānātathāgatavimokṣajñānaviṣayāvabhāsitānāṃ nānājñānasāgarāvabhāsapratilabdhānāṃ nānāsamādhisamudranayavihāriṇāṃ nānādharmavimokṣavinayavikrīḍitaviṣayāṇāṃ nānāsarvajñatādvārābhimukhānāṃ nānādharmadhātugaganavyūhānāṃ nānāvyūhameghagaganaspharaṇānāṃ nānāparṣanmaṇḍalasamudravyavalokayitṝṇāṃ nānāprītivegalokadhātusaṃnipatitānāṃ nānābuddhakṣetraprasarānusṛtānāṃ nānādiksāgarasaṃnipatitānāṃ tathāgatasaṃpreṣitānāṃ nānātathāgatapādamūloccalitānāṃ nānābodhisattvagaṇaparivārāṇāṃ nānāvyūhameghapravarṣaṇānāṃ nānātathāgatanayāvatīrṇānāṃ nānātathāgatadharmasāgaravicārāṇāṃ nānājñānasamudrāvatīrṇānāṃ nānāvyūhagarbhāvabhāsananiṣaṇṇānāṃ nānāprītivegasamudrān saṃjanayāmi / te nānāprītivegasamudrasaṃjātāstathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānavataranti paśyanti vicārayanti / teṣāṃ tathāgatabalāpramāṇatāmanuvicintayatāṃ mahāprītivegasamudrāḥ saṃbhavanti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>kulaputra</s> (son of good family), having gathered all beings through the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, turning them away from all paths of suffering and misfortune, showing them the happiness and prosperity of <s>devas</s> and humans, raising them out of the triple world, establishing them in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), and maturing them through various gates of skillful means, having attained the radiance of oceans of great torrents of joy, I rejoice, I am delighted, I am elated. Moreover, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the oceans of assemblies of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all directions and intermediate quarters — <s>bodhisattvas</s> of various conduct and aspirations, of various purities of body, of various arrays of radiance-<s>maṇḍalas</s> releasing infinite multicolored rays and radiance-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, of various lights of knowledge extending into oceans of approaches to <s>sarvajñatā</s>, immersed in various oceans of <s>samādhi</s>, of various domains of miraculous display, of various ocean-sounds of voices, limbs, and cries, of various bodies adorned with ornaments, entered into various approaches of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, of various bodies extending through oceans of fields, immersed in various oceans of <s>Buddhas</s>, immersed in various oceans of approaches to analytical knowledge, illuminated by the domains of knowledge and liberation of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having attained the radiance of various oceans of knowledge, abiding in various approaches to oceans of <s>samādhi</s>, of various domains of sport in <s>Dharma</s>-liberation and discipline, facing various gates of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, of various arrays of the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, pervading the sky with various clouds of arrays, beholding various oceans of assembly-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, gathered in <s>lokadhātus</s> through various torrents of joy, following the extension of various <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, gathered from various oceans of directions, sent by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arisen from the feet of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, surrounded by various retinues of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, raining various clouds of arrays, entered into the approaches of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, investigating the ocean of <s>Dharma</s> of various <s>Tathāgatas</s>, immersed in various oceans of knowledge, seated in the illumination of various array-treasures — I generate various oceans of torrents of joy. They, born from those various oceans of torrents of joy, enter into the oceans of assemblies of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, behold them, and investigate them. As they contemplate the immeasurability of the powers of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, great oceans of torrents of joy arise in them.

body.text: api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya lakṣaṇapratimaṇḍitāmacintyāṃ rūpakāyapariśuddhimavataramāṇā labhāmi udāraprītiprasādaprāmodyam / praticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyavarṇasamudrasaṃdarśanadharmadhātuvipulaṃ prabhāsamaṇḍalamavalokayamānā cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>kulaputra</s>, as I enter into the inconceivable purity of the form-body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, adorned with the marks, I obtain sublime joy, serenity, and delight. Beholding a radiance-<s>maṇḍala</s> vast as the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, displaying infinite oceans of colors at every moment of mind, at each moment of mind I attain great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyādekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān mahāraśmisamudrān niścaramāṇān, ekaikāṃ ca raśmimanantabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaraśmisamudraparivārāṃ sarvabuddhadharmadhātuspharaṇāṃ sarvasattvaduḥkhāni praśamayamānāṃ dṛṣṭvā cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, seeing great oceans of rays issuing forth from each and every pore of the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, equal in number to the atoms of infinite and boundless <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, each ray accompanied by an ocean of rays equal in number to the atoms of infinite <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmadhātus</s>, pacifying the sufferings of all beings — at each moment of mind I attain great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya uttamāṅgādaṃsakūṭābhyāṃ ca praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvaratnārciḥparvatameghān niścaramāṇān sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, seeing clouds of mountains of all jewel-flames issuing from the crown of the head and from both shoulders of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> at every moment of mind, equal in number to the atoms of all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, pervading all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyādekaikasmādromavivarāt praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamavarṇān nānāgandharaśmimeghānniścaramāṇān sarvabuddhakṣetraspharaṇān dṛṣṭvā udārān prītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, seeing various clouds of fragrant rays issuing from each and every pore of the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> at every moment of mind, of colors equal in number to the atoms of all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, pervading all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, I attain sublime oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayāmānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmāllakṣaṇātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān lakṣaṇamaṇḍitāṃstathāgatavigrahameghān niścaramāṇān sarvalokadhātusamudraspharaṇān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing at every moment of mind from each mark clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms adorned with the marks, equal in number to the atoms of all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth and pervading all oceans of <s>lokadhātus</s>, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyādekaikasmādanuvyañjanātpraticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānaśītyanuvyañjanojjvalāṃstathāgatanirmitakāyameghān niścaramāṇān sarvabuddhakṣetrasamudraspharaṇān sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣanigarjanān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, seeing from each secondary mark of the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanation-bodies radiant with the eighty secondary marks, equal in number to the atoms of all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth and pervading all oceans of <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, resounding with the thundering proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhavikurvitameghān saprathamacittotpādān saṣaṭpāramitāmārgaviśuddhivyūhān sabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavikurvitān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing at every moment of mind from each pore clouds of <s>Buddha</s>-miracles equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, complete with the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, with arrays of purification through the path of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, with the miraculous displays of ascending through the <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyātpraticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān devendrakāyameghān niścaramāṇān sarvalokadhātuspharaṇān sadevendravikurvitān devendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, seeing from each pore of the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Devendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth and pervading all <s>lokadhātus</s>, with the miraculous displays of <s>Devendra</s>, standing face to face before beings who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Devendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyāt praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānnāgendrakāyameghān sanāgendravikurvitān nāgendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhāmi //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Nāgendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, with the miraculous displays of <s>Nāgendra</s>, standing face to face before beings who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Nāgendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra tasya bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān yakṣendrakāyameghān sayakṣendravikurvitān sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇān yakṣendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Yakṣendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, with the miraculous displays of <s>Yakṣendra</s>, pervading all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, standing face to face before beings who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Yakṣendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān gandharvendrakāyameghān sagandharvendravikurvitān sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇān gandharvendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Gandharvendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, with the miraculous displays of <s>Gandharvendra</s>, pervading all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, standing face to face before beings who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Gandharvendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānasurendrakāyameghānniścaramāṇān sāsurendravikurvitānasurendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā sarvadharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Asurendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Asurendra</s>, standing face to face before beings throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Asurendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān garuḍendrakāyameghānniścaramāṇān sagaruḍendravikurvitān garuḍendrakāyasaṃdarśanavainayikānāṃ sarvadharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Garuḍendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Garuḍendra</s>, standing face to face before beings throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Garuḍendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromakūpādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kinnarendrakāyameghān niścaramāṇān sakinnarendravikurvitān kinnarendrakāyasaṃdarśanavinayānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Kinnarendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Kinnarendra</s>, standing face to face before beings throughout the <s>dharmadhātu</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Kinnarendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān mahoragendrakāyameghān niścaramāṇān samahoragendravikurvitān mahoragendrakāyasaṃdarśanavineyānāṃ sarvadharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Mahoragendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Mahoragendra</s>, standing face to face before beings throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Mahoragendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān manuṣyendrakāyameghānniścarataḥ samanuṣyendravikurvitān manuṣyendrakāyasaṃdarśanavineyānāṃ sarvadharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā dharmāṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Manuṣyendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Manuṣyendra</s> (lord of humans), standing face to face before beings throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Manuṣyendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> — seeing this, I attain sublime great oceans of torrents of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya kāyaṃ vyavalokayamānā praticittakṣaṇamekaikasmādromavivarādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān brahmendrakāyameghānniścarataḥ sabrahmendravikurvitān brahmendrakāyasaṃdarśanavineyānāṃ sarvadharmadhātugatānāṃ sattvānāmabhimukhaṃ sthitvā brahmasvararutanirghoṣeṇa dharmaṃ deśayamānān dṛṣṭvā udārān dharmadhātuvipulāṃścittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe sarvajñatāsahagatān mahāprītivegasamudrān pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, gazing upon the body of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, seeing from each pore at every moment of mind clouds of <s>Brahmendra</s>-bodies equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, issuing forth, with the miraculous displays of <s>Brahmendra</s>, standing face to face before beings throughout all <s>dharmadhātus</s> who are to be trained through the appearance of the body of <s>Brahmendra</s> and teaching them the <s>Dharma</s> with the sound of <s>Brahma</s>-voice — seeing this, at each moment of mind I attain great oceans of torrents of joy, vast as the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, accompanied by <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).

body.text: na ca pratilabdhapūrvān pratilabhe / nādhigatapūrvānadhigacchāmi / nāvatīrṇapūrvānavatarāmi / na sphūṭapūrvān spharāmi / na dṛṣṭapūrvān paśyāmi / na ca śrutapūrvān śṛṇomi / tatkasya hetoḥ? kiṃcāpi dharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇaparijñeyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, ekalakṣaṇāstrayadhvapathāvatārāḥ punaranantamadhyanirdeśāḥ sarvadharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: Yet I do not attain what has not been attained before; I do not reach what has not been reached before; I do not enter what has not been entered before; I do not pervade what has not been pervaded before; I do not see what has not been seen before; I do not hear what has not been heard before. For what reason? Although all <s>dharmas</s> are to be fully known through their own-nature and characteristics, all <s>dharmas</s> are of one characteristic with entry into the path of the three times, and yet all <s>dharmas</s> are of infinite, boundless exposition.

body.text: ayamasya kulaputra vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhasya bodhisattvavimokṣanayasamudrasyāvabhāsaḥ / api tu anantamadhyaḥ khalveṣa vimokṣo dharmadhātunayasamudrāvatāraṇatvāt / akṣaya
body.translated_text: This, O <s>kulaputra</s>, is the radiance of the ocean of approaches to <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), the array of mind-moments generating vast torrents of joy. Moreover, this liberation is truly infinite and boundless, because it enters the ocean of approaches to the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Inexhaustible

body.text: eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādāsaṃbhinnatvāt / aparyanta eṣa vimokṣo bodhisattvacakṣurvijñeyatvāt / atula eṣa vimokṣo 'saṃbhinnadharmadhātunayatalaspharaṇatvāt / samantamukha eṣa vimokṣa ekārambaṇasarvavikurvitasamavasaraṇatvāt / amogha eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvadharmaśarīrādvayasamudācāratvāt / anutpanna eṣa vimokṣo māyopamasamudācāratvāt / pratibhāsopama eṣa vimokṣo sarvajñatāpraṇidhānapratibhāsasaṃbhūtatvāt / nirmitopama eṣa vimokṣo bodhisattvacaryāsunirmitatvāt / mahāpṛthivīsadṛśa eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvajagatpratiśaraṇatvāt / apskandhopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvajaganmahākaruṇābhiṣyandanatayā / tejaḥskandhopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvasattvatṛṣṇāsnehaparyādānatayā / vāyuskandhopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvasattvasarvajñatāpratiṣṭhāpanatayā / sāgaropama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvajagadguṇālaṃkārālayatvāt / meruparvatarājopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvadharmajñānaratnasamudrābhyudgatatvāt / vyūhanayavātamaṇḍalasadṛśa eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvadharmavimokṣavidhivyūhanatayā / gaganopama eṣa vimokṣastradhvaprāptasarvatathāgatavikurvitāvakāśatvāt / mahāmeghopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvasattvābhimukhadharmameghābhipravarṣaṇatvāt / ādityopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvasattvājñānatamondhakāravidhamanatayā / candropama eṣa vimokṣo mahāpuṇyajñānasamudrasusamārjitatvāt / tathāgatopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvatrānugatatvāt / svacchāyopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ karmadharmasunirmitatvāt / pratiśrutkopama eṣa vimokṣo yathādhimuktasarvadharmanirghoṣanigarjanatayā / pratibhāsopama eṣa vimokṣo yathāśayasarvasattvavijñāpanatayā / drumarājopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvabuddhavikurvitasaṃkusumitatvāt / vajropama eṣa vimokṣo 'bhedyadharmatvāt / cintārājamaṇiratnopama eṣa vimokṣo 'nantamadhyavikurvitasamudrābhinirharaṇatayā / vimalagarbhamaṇirājopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvatryadhvatathāgatavikurvitavijñaptyanāvaraṇatayā / nandidhvajamaṇiratnopama eṣa vimokṣaḥ sarvabuddhadharmacakrasamatānirghoṣatvāt / evamaparimāṇopamopanyāsānugamanirdeśo batāyaṃ kulaputra vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūho bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: This liberation is inseparable from the arising of the mind of omniscience. This liberation is boundless, because it is to be known by the <s>bodhisattva</s>-eye. This liberation is immeasurable, because it pervades the ground of the method of the undivided <s>dharmadhātu</s>. This liberation is of universal gate, because all transformations converge in a single object. This liberation is unfailing, because it operates through the non-duality of the body of all <s>dharma</s>s. This liberation is unborn, because it operates like an illusion. This liberation is like a reflection, because it arises from the reflection of the vow for omniscience. This liberation is like a creation, because it is well-created by <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. This liberation is like the great earth, because it is the refuge of all the world. This liberation is like a mass of water, because it floods all the world with great compassion. This liberation is like a mass of fire, because it exhausts the moisture of craving of all beings. This liberation is like a mass of wind, because it establishes all beings in omniscience. This liberation is like the ocean, because it is the repository of the ornaments of qualities of all the world. This liberation is like <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, because it rises above the ocean of the gem of knowledge of all <s>dharma</s>s. This liberation is like the wind-maṇḍala of the method of array, because it arrays the method of the liberation of all <s>dharma</s>s. This liberation is like space, because it is the room for the transformations of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s attained in the three times. This liberation is like a great cloud, because it rains forth clouds of <s>Dharma</s> facing all beings. This liberation is like the sun, because it dispels the darkness of ignorance of all beings. This liberation is like the moon, because it is well-gathered from the ocean of great merit and knowledge. This liberation is like a <s>Tathāgata</s>, because it follows everywhere. This liberation is like one's own shadow, because it is well-created by the <s>dharma</s> of <s>karma</s>. This liberation is like an echo, because it thunders forth the sound of all <s>dharma</s>s according to the dispositions [of beings]. This liberation is like a reflection, because it informs all beings according to their intentions. This liberation is like the king of trees, because it blossoms with the transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s. This liberation is like a <s>vajra</s> (diamond/thunderbolt), because its <s>dharma</s> is indestructible. This liberation is like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> wish-fulfilling jewel, because it brings forth an ocean of transformations without end or middle. This liberation is like a stainless-womb gem-king, because it is unobstructed in making known the transformations of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the three times. This liberation is like a <s>nandidhvaja</s> (joy-banner) gem-jewel, because it sounds forth the equality of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>s. Thus, son of good family, this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation — the array of mind-moments arising from the surge of vast delight — is to be taught through the approach of immeasurable similes. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ praśāntarutasāgaravatīṃ rātridevatāmetadavocat - kathaṃ pratipadyamānasya devate bodhisattvasya ayamevaṃrūpo vimokṣaḥ saṃpadyate? āha - daśeme kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsaṃbhārā mahāvitānadharmā mahāvisphārā mahādyutayo mahāvabhāsā mahāprabhāvabhāsā mahābhāgā mahāvibhāgā mahāsaṃbhavā mahāvibhavāḥ, yeṣu pratipadyamānānāṃ bodhisattvānāmayamevaṃrūpo vimokṣaḥ saṃpadyate / katame daśa? yaduta dānaṃ bodhisattvasya yathāśayasarvasattvasamudrasaṃtoṣaṇaprasṛtaṃ mahāvitānadharmaḥ / śīlaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvatathāgataguṇasamudrāvatārapratipattiprasṛtaṃ mahāvitānadharmaḥ / kṣāntirbodhisattvasya sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyaptiprasṛtaṃ mahāvitānadharmaḥ / vīryaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvajñatāsamārambhāvivartyaprasṛtaṃ mahāvitānadharmaḥ / dhyānaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvasattvakleśapratāpapraśamanaprasṛtaṃ mahāvitānadharmaḥ / prajñā bodhisattvasya sarvadharmasamudraprajñāprasṛtā mahāvitānadharmaḥ / upāyo bodhisattvasya sarvasattvasamudraparipākavinayaprasṛto
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, spoke to the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> thus: 'How, goddess, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing [this path] accomplish this kind of liberation?' She replied: 'There are, son of good family, ten great provisions for <s>bodhisattva</s>s — great canopy-<s>dharma</s>s, great expansions, great radiances, great illuminations, great splendor-illuminations, great fortunes, great distinctions, great arisings, great powers — through practicing which <s>bodhisattva</s>s accomplish this kind of liberation. What are the ten? Namely: the generosity (<s>dāna</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the satisfaction of the ocean of all beings according to their intentions, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the practice of entering the ocean of qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the contemplation of the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to irreversible exertion for omniscience, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the pacification of the torment of afflictions of all beings, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the wisdom of the ocean of all <s>dharma</s>s, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the ripening and discipline of the ocean of all beings, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>.

body.text: mahāvitānadharmaḥ / praṇidhānaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvakṣetrasamudraprasṛtamaparāntakoṭīgatakalpasarvakṣetrabodhisattvacaryāvataraṇatāyai mahāvitānadharmaḥ / balaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvadharmadhātunayasamudraprasṛtaṃ sarvakṣetreṣu pratikṣaṇamabhisaṃbodhidarśanāpratiprasrabdhaye mahāvitānadharmaḥ / jñānaṃ bodhisattvasya tathāgatabalaprasṛtaṃ tryadhvasarvadharmānāvaraṇajñānavijñaptaye mahāvitānadharmaḥ / ime kulaputra daśa bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsaṃbhārāṃ mahāvitānadharmāḥ, yeṣu pratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāmayamevaṃrūpo vimokṣaḥ saṃpadyate, viśudhyati saṃbhavati saṃvardhate samudeti prādurbhavati saṃvartate sārībhavati vipulībhavati pariniṣpadyate saṃtiṣṭhate //
body.translated_text: The vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the ocean of all fields for entry into the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of all fields throughout <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The power (<s>bala</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of all <s>dharma</s>s, for the unrelenting display of awakening in all fields at every mind-moment, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. The knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, extending to the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for making known the unobstructed knowledge of all <s>dharma</s>s of the three times, is a great canopy-<s>dharma</s>. These, son of good family, are the ten great provisions for <s>bodhisattva</s>s, the great canopy-<s>dharma</s>s. For <s>bodhisattva</s>s established in these, this kind of liberation is accomplished — it is purified, it arises, it grows, it springs forth, it appears, it develops, it becomes essential, it becomes vast, it is perfected, it abides.' //

body.text: sudhana āha - kiyacciraṃ saṃprasthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? sā avocat - asti kulaputra asya kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkārasya lokadhātusamudrasya pūrveṇa daśalokadhātusamudrasahasrāṇyatikramya pareṇa sarvaratnavimalaprabhāvyūho nāma lokadhātusamudraḥ / tasya madhye sarvatathāgataprabhāpraṇidhinirghoṣo nāma lokadhātuvaṃśaḥ / tasya madhye kanakavimalaprabhāvyūho nāma lokadhātuḥ sarvaratnameghavicitra adholokadhātau sarvaratnahārajālasāgarapratiṣṭhitaḥ sarvagandhavajramaṇirājavyūhaśarīraḥ kūṭāgārapariṇāhasaṃsthāno viśuddho 'saṃkliṣṭaḥ divyavimānabhavanameghasaṃchāditaḥ / tatra samantāvabhāsadhvajo nāma kalpaḥ / tasmin lokadhātau sarvaratnagarbhavicitrābho nāma bodhimaṇḍo 'bhūt / tatra bhagavānavivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣo nāma tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena tasmin bodhivṛkṣe puṇyapradīpasaṃpatketuprabhā nāma bodhimaṇḍadevatā abhūvam / tayā me tasya tathāgatasya abhisaṃbodhivikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / tasya ca me tathāgatasya sahadarśanena tathāgataguṇasamudrāvabhāso nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātau samantasaṃpūrṇaśrīgarbhāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe dharmadrumaparvatatejo nāma tathāgato 'bhisaṃbuddhaḥ / ahaṃ ca tataścyutvā tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe jñānaśrīpuṇyaprabhā nāma rātridevatā abhūvam / tayā me tasya bhagavato dharmadrumaparvatatejastathāgatasya dharmacakrapravartanavikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvajagatsaṃdarśanasamatāvabhāsaviṣayo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena sarvadharmabhūmisaṃvardhanasthāno nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe ratnaraśmipradīpadhvajarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ, tasya me sahadarśanena samantavṛkṣaprabhamegho nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe guṇasumeruprabhatejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena buddhasamudrāvabhāso nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe dharmameghanirghoṣarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena
