dharmasāgarapradīpo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe jñānolkāvabhāsarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgito devakanyābhūtayā / tasya me sahadarśanena sarvasattvaduḥkhapraśamanapratibhāsapradīpo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe
body.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> said: 'How long ago, goddess, did you set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening?' She replied: 'There is, son of good family, to the east of this ocean of world-realms called <s>Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra</s>, beyond ten thousand oceans of world-realms, an ocean of world-realms called <s>Sarvaratnavimalaprabhāvyūha</s>. In its midst is a succession of world-realms called <s>Samantāvabhāsadhvaja</s>. In its midst is a world-realm called <s>Kanakavimalaprabhāvyūha</s> — variegated with clouds of all gem-jewels, established below in an ocean of nets of garlands of all gems, with a body of arrays of <s>vajra</s>-kings of all fragrances, of the extent and shape of a mansion, purified and undefiled, covered with clouds of divine mansions and dwellings. There the <s>kalpa</s> is called <s>Samantāvabhāsadhvaja</s>. In that world-realm there was a <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Sarvaratnagarbhavicitrābha</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Avivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣa</s>, attained unsurpassed perfect awakening. And I at that time, in that era, was a <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-goddess named <s>Puṇyapradīpasaṃpatketuprabhā</s> at that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree. Upon seeing the transformation of that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s awakening, I generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. And upon seeing that <s>Tathāgata</s>, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Illumination of the Ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s>-Qualities.' Immediately afterward, in that very world-realm, in the royal capital <s>Samantasaṃpūrṇaśrīgarbhā</s>, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmadrumaparvatateja</s> attained awakening. And I, having passed from there, became a night-goddess named <s>Jñānaśrīpuṇyaprabhā</s> at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. Upon seeing the transformation of the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmadrumaparvatateja</s>, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Illumination of the Equality of Showing All the World.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣarāja</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Ground for the Growth of the Stage of All <s>Dharma</s>s.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaraśmipradīpadhvajarāja</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Cloud of the Radiance of the Universal Tree.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Guṇasumeruprabhateja</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Illumination of the Ocean of <s>Buddha</s>s.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmameghanirghoṣarāja</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Lamp of the Ocean of <s>Dharma</s>.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānolkāvabhāsarāja</s> was honored — when I was a divine maiden. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Lamp of the Reflection of the Pacification of the Suffering of All Beings.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>,

body.text:
dharmavikurvitavegadhvajaśrīrnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena tryadhvatathāgatasaṃprasthānāvabhāsagarbho nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe dharmapradīpavikramajñānasiṃho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena sarvalokāpratihatajñānacakraprabhatejo
nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe jñānabalaparvatatejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya me sahadarśanena tryadhvasarvasattvacaryendriyaprabhāso nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / iti hi kulaputra tasmin samaye mayā kanakavimalaprabhe lokadhātau tasmin samantāvabhāsadhvajakalpe daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ tathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / keciddevendrabhūtayā kecinnāgendrabhūtayā kecidyakṣendrabhūtayā kecidgandharvendrabhūtayā kecidasurendrabhūtayā kecidgaruḍendrabhūtayā kecitkinnarendrabhūtayā kecinmahoragendrabhūtayā kecinmanuṣyendrabhūtayā kecidbrahmendrabhūyatā keciddevabhūtayā kecinmanuṣyabhūtayā kecitstrībhūtayā kecitpuruṣabhūtayā keciddārakabhūtayā keciddārikābhūtayā ārāgitāḥ / sarve ca me tathāgatāḥ pūjitā yathāsaṃprāptaiḥ pūjāpariṣkāraiḥ / sarve ca te tathāgatā upasthitāḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā śrutā //
body.translated_text: a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmavikurvitavegadhvajaśrī</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Womb of the Illumination of the Setting-Forth of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the Three Times.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmapradīpavikramajñānasiṃha</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Radiance and Splendor of the Wheel of Unobstructed Knowledge of All Worlds.' Immediately afterward, at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānabalaparvatateja</s> was honored. Upon seeing him, I attained a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Illumination of the Faculties and Conduct of All Beings of the Three Times.' Thus, son of good family, at that time, in the world-realm <s>Kanakavimalaprabhā</s>, in the <s>kalpa</s> <s>Samantāvabhāsadhvaja</s>, I honored <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields — some as a lord of gods, some as a lord of <s>Nāga</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Yakṣa</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Gandharva</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Asura</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Garuḍa</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Kinnara</s>s, some as a lord of <s>Mahoraga</s>s, some as a lord of humans, some as a lord of <s>Brahmā</s>s, some as a god, some as a human, some as a woman, some as a man, some as a boy, some as a girl — I honored them. And all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s were worshipped by me with whatever offerings were at hand. And all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s were served. And the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s was heard by me. //

body.text: sā ahaṃ tataścyutvā tasminneva lokadhātau buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān bodhisattvacaryāṃ caritvā tataścyutvā iha kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāre lokadhātusamudre asmin sahālokadhātāvupapannā / tayā me bhagavān krukucchandastathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya ca me sahadarśanena sarvāndhakāravirajapratibhāso nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ kanakamunistathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasya ca me sahadarśanena sarvakṣetrasāgarāvabhāsānugataspharaṇo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ kāśyapastathāgataḥ ārāgitaḥ / tasya ca me sahadarśanena sarvasattvamantrasamudranigarjanasvaranirghoṣo nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tasyānantaramayaṃ bhagavān vairocanastathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tadbodhimaṇḍe tathāgatābhisaṃbodhivikurvitamukhasamudrān praticittakṣaṇe saṃdarśayamānān dṛṣṭvā mayā eṣa vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūho bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya sahapratilambhāddaśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparamāṇurajaḥsamān / sarvadharmadhātunayasamudrānavatīrṇā / teṣu ca sarvadharmadhātunayasamudrāntargateṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu yāni sarvaparamāṇurajāṃsi, teṣu ekaikasmin paramāṇurajasi daśānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyavatīrya paśyāmi / teṣu ca sarvakṣetreṣvekaikasmin buddhakṣetre bhagavantaṃ vairocanaṃ bodhimaṇḍavaragataṃ praticittakṣaṇamabhisaṃbodhivikurvitaṃ saṃdarśayamānānekaikena ca abhisaṃbodhivikurvitena sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarān spharantaṃ paśyāmi / teṣāṃ ca sarvatathāgatānāmekaikasya ca tathāgatasya pādamūlagatamātmānaṃ saṃjāne / ye ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu te tathāgatā bodhimaṇḍagatā dharmaṃ deśayanti, taṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇomi / ye ca teṣāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ nirmāṇasamudrāḥ sarvaromavivarebhyo niścarya dharmameghasamudrān nigarjamānān nānāvikurvitāni saṃdarśayamānān
body.translated_text: Having fallen from there, I practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct in that very world-realm for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and then, falling from there, I was reborn here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm within the ocean of world-realms called <s>Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra</s>. By me the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krukucchanda</s>, was worshipped. And upon seeing him, I attained the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvāndhakāravirajapratibhāsa</s> (Radiance Free from All Darkness). After that, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kanakamuni</s> was worshipped. And upon seeing him, I attained the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvakṣetrasāgarāvabhāsānugataspharaṇa</s> (Pervading Radiance Following the Illumination of All Field-Oceans). After that, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> was worshipped. And upon seeing him, I attained the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasattvamantrasamudranigarjanasvaranirghoṣa</s> (Resounding Voice Thundering the Ocean of All Beings' <s>Mantras</s>). After that, this <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, was worshipped. Having seen at that <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> the ocean-gateways of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s enlightenment-transformations being displayed at each moment of thought, I attained this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūha</s> (Array of Thought-Moments Arising from the Force of Vast Joy). Upon attaining it, I descended into oceans of methods of all <s>dharmadhātus</s> equal in number to ten inexpressibly-inexpressible atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And in all the <s>Buddha</s>-fields contained within those oceans of methods of all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, however many atoms there are — in each single atom I enter and see <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to ten inexpressible atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And in all those fields, in each single <s>Buddha</s>-field, I see the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> seated at the supreme <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, displaying enlightenment-transformations at each moment of thought, and with each enlightenment-transformation pervading all the oceans of methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. And I perceive myself present at the feet of each and every one of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> those <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach while seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> in those world-realms, I hear all of it. And the oceans of emanations of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, issuing forth from every hair-pore, thundering clouds of <s>Dharma</s>-rain, displaying various transformations

body.text:
sarvadharmadhātudiksamudrāntargateṣu kṣetrasamudreṣu sarvalokadhātuvaṃśeṣu sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu sarvasattvaprasareṣu nānāgatyupapanneṣu sattvāśayavaśena nānāsaṃjñāgatairdharmacakraṃ pravartayanti, taṃ sarvaṃ saṃdhārayāmi, pratipadye, nidhyāyāmi / sarvārthapadavyañjanodgrahavegavikramayā dhāraṇyā udgṛhṇāmi sarvadharmamaṇḍalaviśuddhigarbhānugamayā prajñayā pariśodhayāmi / sarvadharmasāgarapravicayābhijñayā gatyānugacchāmi / tryadhvavipulayā buddhyā spharāmi / tathāgatasamatānugāminyā prajñayā sāmīkaromi / sarvadharmanayānabhinirharāmi / sarvadharmamegheṣu sūtrāntameghānabhinirharāmi / sarvasūtrāntamegheṣu dharmasamudrān parisaṃsthāpayāmi / sarvadharmasamudreṣu dharmaparivartān samavasarāmi / sarvadharmaparivarteṣu dharmameghān saṃjāne / sarvadharmamegheṣu dharmormīn saṃjanayāmi / sarvadharmormiṣu
dharmaprītivegasāgarān pratilabhe / sarvadharmaprītivegasāgareṣu bhūmipratilambhavegānabhinirharāmi / sarvabhūmivegeṣu samādhisamudravegānabhinirharāmi / sarvasamādhisamudramegheṣu buddhadarśanasamudrān pratilabhe / sarvabuddhadarśanasamudreṣvavabhāsasamudrān pratilabhe / sarvāvabhāsasamudreṣu tryadhvajñānamaṇḍalabhūmīḥ parisaṃsthāpayāmi anantamadhyadiksāgaraspharaṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvāntacaryāsamudrāvataraṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvayogasamudrajñānāvabhāsayogena, aprameyatathāgatajñānālokapratilambhayogena, aprameyatathāgataśīlamaṇḍalapariśuddhyavabhāsayogena, aprameyatathāgatakṣāntibhūmipariśodhanayogena, aprameyatathāgatamahāvīryavegavivardhanavikramajñānāvabhāsapratilambhayogena, aprameyatathāgatadhyānamaṇḍaladhyānāgamasamudrapariśuddhiprayogāvabhāsapratilambhayogena, aprameyatathāgataprajñāpāramitānayasāgarapariśuddhivijñaptyavabhāsayogena, aprameyatathāgatopāyakauśalyapāramitānayasamudrāvataraṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatapraṇidhānapāramitānayasamudrāvataraṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatapuṇyajñānabalapāramitāsaṃvardhanasaṃvasanajñānapratilambhayogena, aprameyatathāgatajñānapāramitānayasāgaravicārapralambhayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇajñānāvabhāsapratilambhayogena, aprameyatathāgatabhūmyākramaṇasaṃdhivikurvitakalpasāgarasaṃvasanayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvabodhisattvabhūmimaṇḍalākramaṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatabodhisattvabhūmisaṃvasanayogena, aprameyatathāgatabodhisattvabhūmipariśodhanayogena, aprameyatathāgatajñānasāgaravicāraṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatajñānāvabhāsapratilābhayogena, aprameyatathāgatabodhisattvabhūtāśeṣapūrvabuddhadarśanānubandhavijñaptiyogena, aprameyatathāgatabodhisattvabhūtāśeṣapūrvabuddhasamudradarśanakalpasamudrasaṃvāsayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvabodhisattvabhūtāśeṣakṣetrasamudraspharaṇakāyābhinirhārajñānāvabhāsapratilābhayogena, aprameyatathāgatavipulapūrvabodhisattvacaryānavaśeṣadharmadhātuspharaṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatapūrvabodhisattvacaryānānopāyasukhasarvasattvaparipācanavinayasaṃdarśanayogena, aprameyatathāgatasarvadiksamudrānavaśeṣaprabhāprasaraspharaṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatasattvābhimukhavikurvitasaṃdarśanayogena, aprameyatathāgatabhūmyākramaṇajñānāvabhāsayogena, aprameyatathāgatābhisaṃbodhivikurvaṇajñānāvabhāsapratilābhayogena, aprameyatathāgatadharmacakrapravartanasarvadharmameghānavaśeṣasaṃpratīcchanasaṃdhāraṇayogena, aprameyatathāgatalakṣaṇasamudravijñaptijñānāvabhāsapratilābhayogena,
aprameyatathāgatakāyasamudrasamudācāravijñaptyavabhāsapratilābhayogena, aprameyatathāgatavipulaviṣayajñānāvabhāsapratilābhayogena /
body.translated_text: turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> with various modes of perception according to the dispositions of beings born in various destinies, in all world-realm lineages, in all world-realm extensions, in all being-extensions, in field-oceans contained within all directions of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — all of that I retain, I comprehend, I contemplate. With <s>dhāraṇī</s> possessing the power and vigor to grasp all meanings, words, syllables, and expressions, I retain it; with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that follows the womb of purification of all <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍalas</s>, I purify it; with <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge) investigating the ocean of all <s>dharmas</s>, I follow its course; with <s>buddhi</s> (intelligence) vast across the three times, I pervade it; with <s>prajñā</s> following the equality of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I equalize it. I bring forth methods of all <s>dharmas</s>; within all <s>dharma</s>-clouds I bring forth clouds of <s>sūtra</s>-discourses; within all <s>sūtra</s>-discourse clouds I establish oceans of <s>Dharma</s>; within all <s>Dharma</s>-oceans I enter into <s>Dharma</s>-chapters; within all <s>Dharma</s>-chapters I perceive <s>Dharma</s>-clouds; within all <s>Dharma</s>-clouds I generate <s>Dharma</s>-waves; within all <s>Dharma</s>-waves I attain oceans of the force of <s>Dharma</s>-joy; within all oceans of the force of <s>Dharma</s>-joy I bring forth the forces of attaining the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages); within all forces of the <s>bhūmis</s> I bring forth the forces of oceans of <s>samādhi</s>; within all oceans of <s>samādhi</s>-clouds I attain oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-vision; within all oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-vision I attain oceans of radiance; within all oceans of radiance I establish the grounds of the <s>jñāna</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> (knowledge-circle) of the three times — by means of pervading the oceans of directions that are endless and without middle, by means of entering the oceans of past conduct of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the illumination of knowledge of the oceans of former practice of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the light of knowledge of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the illumination of the purification of the <s>śīla</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> (moral discipline circle) of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of purifying the ground of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of the knowledge of vigor in the growth of the force of great <s>vīrya</s> (heroic effort) of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of the practice of purifying the ocean of <s>dhyāna</s>-attainments in the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the illumination of consciousness purifying the ocean of methods of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of entering the ocean of methods of the perfection of skillful means of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of entering the ocean of methods of the perfection of <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows) of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the knowledge of cultivating and dwelling in the perfection of the power of merit and knowledge of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of investigating the ocean of methods of the perfection of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of ascending the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of dwelling in the ocean of <s>kalpas</s> of the transformations at the junctures of ascending the <s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of ascending the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of dwelling on the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of purifying the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of investigating the ocean of knowledge of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the consciousness following the vision of all past <s>Buddhas</s> without remainder while being <s>bodhisattvas</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of dwelling in the ocean of <s>kalpas</s> of seeing oceans of past <s>Buddhas</s> without remainder while being <s>bodhisattvas</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of producing bodies pervading all field-oceans without remainder while being <s>bodhisattvas</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the vast former <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s> pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> without remainder, by means of displaying the ripening and disciplining of all beings through various skillful and joyful means in the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the radiance-extension pervading all directional oceans without remainder of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of displaying transformations facing all beings of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of the illumination of knowledge of ascending the <s>bhūmis</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of the enlightenment-transformations of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of receiving and retaining without remainder all <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of consciousness of the ocean of marks of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of consciousness of the conduct of the ocean of bodies of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by means of attaining the illumination of knowledge of the vast domain of immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ prathamacittotpādamādāya yāvatsaddharmāntardhānaṃ sarvamavatarāmi //
body.translated_text: And of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, at each moment of thought, beginning from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> up to the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, I enter into all of it. //

body.text: yatpunarevaṃ vadasi - kiyaccirapratilabdhastvayāyaṃ vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūho bodhisattvavimokṣa iti / yanmayā vibuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ buddhakalpānāṃ pareṇa kanakavimalaprabhāyāṃ lokadhātau puṇyapradīpasaṃpatsamantaketuprabhā bodhivṛkṣadevatā abhūt, tayā avaivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣasya tathāgatasya dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya tān vibuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān bodhisattvacaryāṃ caritvā iha sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvupapadya krakucchandapramukhāḥ śākyamuniparyavasānā bhadrakalpikāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / anāgatāṃśca sarvānārāgayiṣyāmi / yatheha lokadhātau, tathā sarvalokadhātuṣvanāgatān buddhavaṃśānārāgayiṣyāmi, pūjayiṣyāmi / adyāpi hi kulaputra sā kanakavimalaprabhā lokadhātustiṣṭhati acchinnabuddhavaṃśaḥ / tasmāttarhi kulaputra iha naye mahatā bodhisattvavikrameṇa prayoktavyam //
body.translated_text: As for your question — 'How long ago did you attain this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūha</s> (Array of Thought-Moments Arising from the Force of Vast Joy)?' — Beyond <s>kalpas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> equal in number to the atoms of illuminated <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in the world-realm called <s>Kanakavimalaprabhā</s> (Pure Golden Radiance), I was a <s>Bodhi</s>-tree goddess named <s>Puṇyapradīpasaṃpatsamantaketuprabhā</s> (Radiance of the Banner of the Attainment of the Lamp of Merit in All Directions). Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Avaivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣa</s> (Irreversible Sound of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>), I generated the thought of supreme perfect enlightenment, and having practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct for those <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of illuminated <s>Buddha</s>-fields, I was reborn here in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, and I worshipped the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of this Fortunate <s>Kalpa</s> (<s>Bhadrakalpa</s>), beginning with <s>Krakucchanda</s> and ending with <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And I shall worship all the future ones as well. Just as in this world-realm, so too in all world-realms I shall worship and honor the future <s>Buddha</s>-lineages. Indeed, O noble son, that world-realm <s>Kanakavimalaprabhā</s> still exists even now, with an unbroken <s>Buddha</s>-lineage. Therefore, O noble son, one should exert oneself in this method with great <s>bodhisattva</s>-vigor. //

body.text: atha khalu praśāntarutasāgaravatī rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā pradarśayamānā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>, at that moment, while demonstrating to an even greater degree this very <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūha</s>, addressed the youth <s>Sudhana</s> in verses —

children.text: śṛṇu sūdhanā vacanametu mamā yathayaṃ vimokṣa pratilabdhu śubham /
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Sudhana</s>, to this my word, how this auspicious liberation was attained;

children.text: śrutvā ca prītibalu saṃjaniyā etaṃ vimokṣanayamotarahi // 1 //
children.translated_text: and having heard, generating the power of joy, descend into this method of liberation. // 1 //

children.text: bahu kalpasāgara purā caritā cittāśayaṃ svaku viśodhayati /
children.translated_text: For many oceans of <s>kalpas</s> in the past I practiced, purifying my own mental disposition;
generating vast force of <s>adhimukti</s> (devoted faith), facing the city of omniscient knowledge. // 2 //

children.text: śrutvā triyadhvaparamā sugatānadhimukti teṣu vipulāṃ janiya /
children.translated_text: Having heard of the supreme <s>Sugatas</s> of the three times, generating vast <s>adhimukti</s> toward them,

children.text: sarvaiḥ sukhaiḥ saparivāra mayā te upasthitāḥ sabahukalpaśatān // 3 //
children.translated_text: with all comforts, together with retinues, I attended them for many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>. // 3 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mayā purimakāḥ sugatāḥ saṃpūjitā janahitāya caran /
children.translated_text: Having seen the <s>Sugatas</s> of former times, I worshipped them, acting for the benefit of beings;

children.text: dharmaśca me nirupamo 'yu śrutaḥ prītibalaṃ vipulaṃ saṃjaniyā // 4 //
children.translated_text: and the incomparable <s>Dharma</s> was heard by me, generating vast power of joy. // 4 //

children.text: mātā pitā gurujanaḥ satataṃ maya satkṛtā hitasukhena tadā /
children.translated_text: Mother, father, and elders were always honored by me with benefit and happiness then;
attendance was rendered with a stance of reverence, while descending into this method of liberation. // 5 //

body.text:
jīrṇāturā dhanavihīna narā vikalendriyā dukhi anātha bahū /
te me sukhe sthapiya maitramanā sudhanā sanātha kṛta jātiśatān // 6 // rājāgnitaskarajalaprabhavā siṃhadvipā hi paraśatrubhayāt /

children.translated_text: from manifold fears of those caught in the ocean of existence, I rescued them while wandering in the past. // 7 //

body.translated_text: The aged, the sick, the destitute, those with impaired faculties, the suffering, the shelterless — many such people I established in happiness with a mind of loving-kindness, O <s>Sudhana</s>, making them protected for hundreds of births. // 6 // From dangers arising from kings, fire, thieves, floods, lions, elephants, and enemies,

children.text: kleśapratāpita sadā tribhave karmaiḥ prabhāvita tathā aśubhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those always scorched by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in the three realms of existence, impelled by unwholesome <s>karmas</s>,
fallen into the precipice of <s>saṃsāra</s>'s mountain — I rescued beings in the courses of existence. // 8 //
Those fierce, unceasing, harsh, and numerous fears of suffering and evil destinies' precipice,

children.text: jātījarāmaraṇarogabhayā loke mayā śamita te nikhilā // 9 //
children.translated_text: the fears of birth, old age, death, and disease in the world — all of them were pacified by me entirely. // 9 //
The pacification of the intense suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the generation of all happiness for beings,
the generation of the ultimate bliss of <s>Buddhahood</s> — this is my vow until the final <s>kalpa</s>. // 10 //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ bodhisattvānāmādhyātmikabāhyaniravaśeṣaduḥkhavipramuktānāṃ sarvakalpasaṃjñāgatajñānapratilabdhānāṃ sarvalokadhātusamudrasaṃbhavavibhavajñānavakuśalānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: This, O noble son, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūha</s> (Array of Thought-Moments Arising from the Force of Vast Joy) that I know. How could I know the conduct, or speak of the qualities, of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have descended into the oceans of methods of all <s>dharmadhātus</s>, who are freed from all internal and external suffering without remainder, who have attained knowledge transcending all concepts of <s>kalpas</s>, who are skilled in the knowledge of the arising and dissolution of all world-realm oceans? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva bodhimaṇḍe bhagavato vairocanasya parṣanmaṇḍale sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrīrnāma rātridevatā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, <s>kulaputra</s> (son of good family), here in this very <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), in the assembly-circle of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, there is a night-goddess named <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>. Approach her and ask: How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ praśāntarutasāgaravatīṃ rātridevatāmābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, addressed the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> with these fitting verses (<s>gāthās</s>):

children.translated_text: Instructed by a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend), I have come into your presence, O <s>Devī</s> (goddess);

children.text: paśyāmi te āsanu saṃniṣaṇṇā anantamadhyena samucchrayeṇa // 11 //
children.translated_text: I behold you seated upon your throne, with an infinite, boundless elevation. // 11 //
Not by those whose domain is the marks of color, form, and characteristics, not by those attached to existence, nor by those who grasp at the notion of being,

children.text: na hīnasattvairviparītadarśibhiḥ śakyastava jñātumayaṃ hi gocaraḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: not by inferior beings of perverted views can this domain of yours be known. // 12 //

children.text: jñātuṃ na lokena sahadevakena tvadvarṇarūpasya nimitta śakyam /
children.translated_text: The marks of your color and form cannot be known by the world together with its gods,

children.text: kalpānanantān samudīkṣatāpi tathā hi te rūpamanantadarśanam // 13 //
children.translated_text: even if they were to gaze upon it for infinite <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), for your form is of infinite appearance. // 13 //

children.text: skandhālayāduccalitāsi devi pratiṣṭhitā nāyataneṣu ca tvam /
children.translated_text: You have risen beyond the abode of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), O <s>Devī</s>, nor are you established in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases);

children.text: lokavyatītā ca vitīrṇakāṅkṣā saṃdṛśyase loki vikurvamāṇā // 14 //
children.translated_text: you have transcended the world and gone beyond doubt, yet you are seen manifesting in the world through miraculous transformations. // 14 //
You have attained the immovable, you are faultless and unattached; your supreme <s>jñānacakṣus</s> (wisdom-eye) has been purified,
by which you behold in the realm of dust <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as all dust-particles, manifesting their miraculous transformations. // 15 //

children.text: kāyo hi te dharmaśarīragarbhaḥ cittaṃ ca te jñānamayaṃ asaṅgam /
children.translated_text: Your body is the womb of the <s>Dharma</s>-body, and your mind is made of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), unattached;
you are illuminated with the radiance of universal light, and you generate infinite illumination in the world. // 16 //

children.text: cittādanantaṃ samudeti karma vicitritaḥ karmaṇa sarvalokaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the mind arises infinite <s>karma</s> (action), and by <s>karma</s> the entire world is diversified;

children.text: cittasvabhāvaṃ ca jagadviditvā jagatsamān darśayasi svakāyān // 17 //
children.translated_text: having understood the nature of mind as the nature of the world, you display your own bodies equal to the world. // 17 //

children.text: svapnopamaṃ lokamimaṃ viditvā buddhāṃśca sarvān pratibhāsakalpān /
children.translated_text: Having understood this world to be dream-like, and all <s>Buddhas</s> to be like reflections,
and all <s>dharmas</s> to be like echoes without remainder, unattached you move through the world. // 18 //

children.text: tryadhvasthitasyāpi janasya devi pratikṣaṇaṃ darśayasi svakāyam /
children.translated_text: Even for beings abiding in the three times, O <s>Devī</s>, you display your own body at every moment;

children.text: dvayapravṛttirna ca te 'sti citte dharmaṃ vadasyeva ca sarvadikṣu // 19 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no dualistic activity in your mind, and you teach the <s>Dharma</s> in all directions. // 19 //
Infinite are the great oceans of dust-particles, and likewise immeasurable are the great oceans of beings;
infinite and boundless are the oceans of <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas) — this is the domain of the conduct of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). // 20 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ praśāntarutasāgaravatīṃ rātridevatāmābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya praśāntarutasāgaravatyā rātridevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 36 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, having praised the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s> with these verses, having circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>. // 36 //

body.text: 39 Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: 39. <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastaṃ vipulaprītivegasaṃbhavacittakṣaṇavyūhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayan saṃbhāvayan praśāntarutasāgaravatyā rātridevatāyā avavādānuśāsanīmanusmaran, nigamayan, ekaikapadavyañjanānekanayāpramāṇāśayaṃ dharmatānayajñānamanusmaran, smṛtāvupanibadhnan, matyā pravicinvan, gatyā anugacchan, buddhyā vipulīkurvan, kāyena spṛṣṭvā viharan, avataran, anupraviśan, anupūrveṇa yena sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī rātridevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / so 'paśyat sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāṃ sarvanagarabhavanaprabhāsamaṇirājagarbhamahāpadmāsane niṣaṇṇāmanabhilāpyarātridevatāparivārāṃ sarvadiksattvajagadabhimukhenakāyena sarvajagadrūpasamena kāyena sarvasattvābhimukhena kāyena sarvajagadanuliptena kāyena sarvajagatsamaśarīreṇa kāyena sarvajagadabhyudgatena kāyena sarvajagatparipākavinayākūlena kāyena samantadiṅnigarjanena kāyena sarvajagadasaṃkrāntena kāyena sarvāvaraṇātyantasamuddhāṭitena kāyena tathāgatasvabhāvena kāyena sarvajagadvinayaniṣṭhāparyavasānena kāyena //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, contemplating and cultivating that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) called the array of mind-moments born from the surge of vast joy, recalling the admonishment and instruction of the night-goddess <s>Praśāntarutasāgaravatī</s>, comprehending it, reflecting upon each word and syllable having manifold methods and immeasurable intentions, recalling the knowledge of the way of the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, binding it in memory, investigating with discernment, following with his gait, expanding with his intellect, dwelling having touched it with his body, entering and penetrating into it, gradually approached the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>. He beheld the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> seated upon the great lotus throne whose womb was the radiant jewel-king of all city-dwellings, surrounded by an inexpressible retinue of night-goddesses, with a body facing all beings in all directions, with a body equal in form to the entire world, with a body facing all beings, with a body anointed by the entire world, with a body of equal form to the entire world, with a body surpassing the entire world, with a body filled with the purpose of maturing and disciplining the entire world, with a body resounding in all directions, with a body untransferred from the entire world, with a body from which all obstructions are utterly removed, with a body of the nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and with a body whose culmination and conclusion is the discipline of the entire world.

body.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ahaṃ khalu devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitaḥ / tadvadasva me devate kathaṃ bodhisattvo bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ carannupakārībhūto bhavati sattvānām / kathaṃ ca sattvānanuttareṇa saṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhṇāti / kathaṃ bodhisattvastathāgatānujñāto bodhisattvakarmaṇi prayukto bhavati, yathāprayuktasya bodhisattvasya āsanno bhavati dharmarājaḥ / evamukte sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvaṃ sarvajagatparipākavinayaniṣṭhāgamanatāyai sarvatathāgatavaṃśasaṃdhāraṇaprayoganiṣṭhāgamanatāyai sarvadikprasaraspharaṇajñānaprayogatāyai sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarāvataraṇābhimukhatāyai ākāśasamatalānantajñānajñeyaspharaṇatāyai sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapratīcchanasaṃdhāraṇatāyai yathāśayasarvajagatsamudradharmameghābhipravarṣaṇacaryānayaṃ paripṛcchasi / ahaṃ kulaputra manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra anena vimokṣeṇa samanvāgatā asaṅgamahādharmabhāṇakapaṭṭabaddhādhyālambanaprayogā sarvatathāgatadharmakośaviśrāṇanapraṇidhānā mahākaruṇāmaitrībalapratilabdhā sarvasattvabodhicittapratiṣṭhāpanatāyai sarvasattvārthakriyāsaṃprasthitā apratiprasrabdhabodhicittakuśalamūlasaṃbhāropacayāya sarvajagatsārathibhūmisaṃprasthitā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvajñatāmārgapratiṣṭhāpanatāyai, sarvaloke dharmameghadharmasūryasaṃbhavaprayogā aprameyakuśalamūlaprabhavasarvalokāvabhāsanatāyai, sarvajagatsamacittaprasṛtāpratipraśrabdhā sarvajagatkuśalamūlābhisaṃskārasaṃmārjanaprayogavijñānatāyai, viśuddhacittaprayogā sarvakuśalakarmapathapradakṣiṇakarmāntatayā sarvasattvasārthavāhatvāya saṃprasthitā sarvākuśalakarmapathaprahīṇā
body.translated_text: Having seen her, delighted, exultant, elated, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, he bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> with palms joined, and spoke thus: I, O <s>Devī</s>, have set forth toward supreme perfect <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Therefore, tell me, O <s>Devī</s>, how a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct becomes a benefactor of beings; how he gathers beings with the supreme means of attraction; how a <s>bodhisattva</s> authorized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> becomes engaged in the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s work, so that for the <s>bodhisattva</s> thus engaged, the <s>Dharma</s>-king becomes near. Thus addressed, the night-goddess <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> spoke to <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, as follows: Excellent! Excellent! O <s>kulaputra</s>, that you, for the sake of attaining the culmination of maturing and disciplining the entire world, for the sake of attaining the culmination of the endeavor to maintain the lineage of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the sake of the application of knowledge spreading in all directions, for the sake of being directed toward entering the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in all its aspects, for the sake of pervading the infinite field of knowledge and the knowable equal to the expanse of space, for the sake of receiving and maintaining the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, ask about the method of the conduct of raining the cloud of <s>Dharma</s> upon the ocean of the entire world according to their dispositions. I, O <s>kulaputra</s>, have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> called 'entry into the deep miraculous display of pleasing sounds.' And I, O <s>kulaputra</s>, endowed with this <s>vimokṣa</s>, am engaged in the application of relying upon and supporting the unattached great <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, with the vow of dispensing the treasure of the <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, empowered by the strength of great compassion and loving-kindness, set forth for the sake of establishing all beings in <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), set forth for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all beings, for the accumulation of the provisions of wholesome roots of unrelenting <s>bodhicitta</s>, set forth upon the ground of being the charioteer of all the world for the sake of establishing all beings on the path to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), engaged in the application of producing the cloud of <s>Dharma</s> and the sun of <s>Dharma</s> in all worlds for the sake of illuminating all worlds through the arising of immeasurable wholesome roots, extended with equal mind toward the entire world without relaxation, for the sake of knowing the application of sweeping away and purifying the wholesome roots of the entire world, engaged with the application of purified mind, set forth for the sake of being the caravan-leader of all beings through the completion of the auspicious path of all wholesome <s>karma</s>, having abandoned all unwholesome paths of <s>karma</s>,

body.text:
sarvasattvakuśaladharmapratiṣṭhāpanakarmaprayogā sarvasattvakṣemagatisaṃpradarśanaprayogā sarvasattvayānavyūhapūrvaṃgamasaṃprasthitā sarvakuśaladharmacakracaraṇasarvasattvapratiṣṭhāpanaprayogā sarvakalyāṇamitrābhedyopacaraṇābhirādhanasaṃprasthitā sarvasattvatathāgataśāsanapratiṣṭhāpanaprayogā dharmadānapūrvaṃgamasarvaśukladharmasamārambhaprayogā sarvajñatācittotpādābhijātadṛḍhābhedyāśayā vajranārāyaṇagarbhadṛḍhabuddhabalārambaṇavipulacittamaṇḍalā kalyāṇamitramupaniśritya viharāmi / sarvakleśakarmāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇacittā sarvajñatāsaṃbhārasamārambhā sarvaśukladharmasamarjanaprayogā anantamadhyasarvajñatābhimukhārambaṇacetanāprayogaprayuktā
//
body.translated_text: engaged in the application of establishing all beings in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, engaged in the application of showing the way to safety and well-being for all beings, set forth with the array of vehicles for all beings as the foremost, engaged in the application of establishing all beings through the turning of the wheel of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, set forth with indestructible attendance upon and devotion to all <s>kalyāṇamitras</s> (spiritual friends), engaged in the application of establishing all beings in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, engaged in the undertaking of all pure <s>dharmas</s> with the gift of <s>Dharma</s> as the foremost, with the intention born of the generation of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> that is firm and indestructible, with the vast circle of mind that is firm as <s>vajra</s> (diamond) and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in its core, relying upon the power of the <s>Buddha</s> as its support — thus I dwell having relied upon a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>. With a mind intent on scattering the mountains of obstructions from afflictions and <s>karma</s>, with the undertaking of accumulating provisions for <s>sarvajñatā</s>, with the application of cultivating all pure <s>dharmas</s>, engaged in the application of intention and effort directed toward the infinite and boundless approach to <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra evaṃrūpaṃ sarvasattvavijñāpanaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ pariśodhayamānā kuśalamūlopacayasaṃbhārapratyupasthitāṃ daśabhirākārairdharmadhātuṃ vyavalokayāmi anugacchāmi prasarāmi / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta aprameyaṃ dharmadhātumanugacchāmi vipulajñānālokapratilābhena / anantamadhyadharmadhātumanugacchāmi sarvatathāgatavikurvitavijñaptaye / aparyantadharmadhātumanugacchāmi sarvabuddhakṣetrākramaṇatathāgatapūjopasthānaparipūraye / asīmāprāptaṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi sarvalokadhātusamudreṣu bodhisattvacaryāsaṃdarśanatāyai / avyavacchinnaṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi asaṃbhinnatathāgatajñānamaṇḍalāvataraṇatāyai / ekotībhāvagataṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi yathāśayasarvasattvavijñapanatathāgatasvaramaṇḍalāvataraṇatāyai / svabhāvavimalaṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi sarvajagadvinayaniṣṭhāgatapūrvapraṇidhānaniṣṭhāvataraṇatāyai / sarvajagatsamatānugataṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāprasarapraveśāya / ekālaṃkāraṃ sarvadharmadhātumavatarāmi samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāvikurvitālaṃkārāvataraṇatāyai / avināśanaṃ dharmadhātumavatarāmi sarvakuśaladharmadhātuspharaṇaviśuddhyavināśadharmatāyai / ebhirahaṃ kulaputra daśabhirākāraiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ vyavalokayāmi anugacchāmi prasarāmi sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhāropacayāya buddhamāhātmyāvataraṇatāyai acintyabuddhaviṣayānugamāya //
body.translated_text: And I, O <s>kulaputra</s>, while purifying such a method — a gateway of the light of <s>Dharma</s> for instructing all beings — with the provisions of accumulated wholesome roots made ready, contemplate, follow, and pervade the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in ten aspects. Which ten? Namely: I follow the immeasurable <s>dharmadhātu</s> through the attainment of the light of vast <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom); I follow the infinite and boundless <s>dharmadhātu</s> for the sake of making known the miraculous displays of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; I follow the limitless <s>dharmadhātu</s> for the fulfillment of traversing all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) and worshiping and attending upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; I enter the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that has reached no boundary for the sake of displaying the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in all ocean-worlds; I enter the uninterrupted <s>dharmadhātu</s> for the sake of entering the unbroken <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge; I enter the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that has gone to a state of unity for the sake of entering the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s voice that instructs all beings according to their dispositions; I enter the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that is pure in its own nature for the sake of entering into the prior vows that have reached the culmination of disciplining the entire world; I enter the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that pervades the equality of the entire world for the sake of entering the extension of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>; I enter the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that is one single ornament for the sake of entering the ornament of miraculous displays of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>; I enter the indestructible <s>dharmadhātu</s> for the sake of the purity and indestructibility of pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. By these ten aspects, O <s>kulaputra</s>, I contemplate, follow, and pervade the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, for the accumulation of provisions of all wholesome roots, for entering the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>, and for following the inconceivable domain of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra ahamevaṃ tathāgatamāhātmyānugatairmanasikārairdaśabhirdhāraṇīmaṇḍalaparivartasahasraiḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sarvadharmasamudrasamavasaraṇena ca nāmnā dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvadharmādhiṣṭhānena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvatathāgatasmṛtipradīpena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvasattvakarmasamudrapradīpagarbheṇa ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvayānanayasamudravimalasamavasaraṇena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvatathāgatanāmacakrāvartanirghoṣeṇa ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / tryadhvabuddhapūrvanirvāṇapraṇidhānasāgaranirdeśasamavasaraṇena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvadharmābhimukhāvartavegena ca dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / sarvajñatāveśaprabheṇa ca nāmnā dhāraṇīmaṇḍalena / etāni ca kulaputra daśa dhāraṇīmaṇḍalāni pramukhaṃ kṛtvā daśabhirdhāraṇīmaṇḍalaparivartasahasraiḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, with mental reflections that follow the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through ten thousand revolutions of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍalas</s>. Which ten? Namely: through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the confluence of the ocean of all <s>dharmas</s>'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the empowerment of all <s>dharmas</s>'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the reception of the cloud of all <s>dharmas</s>'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the lamp of the recollection of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the womb of the lamp of the ocean of <s>karma</s> of all beings'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the pure confluence of the ocean of all vehicle-methods'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the resounding turning of the name-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the confluence of the exposition of the ocean of prior <s>nirvāṇa</s>-vows of <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times'; through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the turning force directed toward all <s>dharmas</s>'; and through the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called 'the splendor of the entry into <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' With these ten <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍalas</s> as the foremost, O <s>kulaputra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through ten thousand revolutions of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>maṇḍalas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra śrutamayyā prajñayā sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi, cintāmayyā bhāvanāmayyā prajñayā sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi bhavaparivartamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>kulaputra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) born of learning, through <s>prajñā</s> born of reflection, and through <s>prajñā</s> born of cultivation. Beginning from even a single turning of existence, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings.

body.text: sarvabhavasamudraparivartānapyārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekasyāpi tathāgatasya nāmacakrasamudramārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi lokadhātusamudramārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvalokadhātusamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi buddhavyākaraṇasamudrāmārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvatathāgatavyākaraṇasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudramārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi tathāgatadharmacakramārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi sūtrāntamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasamavasaraṇānapi sūtrāntamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasaṃnipātamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi sarvajñatācittamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvabodhicittāṅgasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / ekamapi yānamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / sarvayānaniryāṇasamudrānapyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayāmi / etatpramukhairahaṃ kulaputra anabhilāpyairdeśanānayābhinirhāraiḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi / evamahaṃ kulaputraṃ dharmadhātunayāsaṃbhinnāṃstathāgatasamudrānavataramāṇā sarvasattvānāṃ dharmadeśanayā anuttaradharmasaṃgrahaṃ kurvāṇā samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāparāntakoṭīgatān kalpasamudrān saṃvasamānā etanmanojñarūtagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayāmi ekaikacittakṣaṇavivardhanena vimokṣaviṣayabhāvanānayena / ekaikena ca vimokṣaviṣayabhāvanānayena praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharāmi //
body.translated_text: Beginning from the revolutions of all oceans of existence, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Beginning from the ocean of name-wheels of even a single <s>Tathāgata</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single ocean of world-realms, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of world-realms, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single ocean of <s>Buddha</s>-prophecies, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of <s>Tathāgata</s>-prophecies, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakras</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single <s>sūtrānta</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from the convergences of all <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakra</s> oceans, from a single <s>sūtrānta</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single gathering of a <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circle, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single thought of omniscience, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of limbs of the thought of awakening, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from even a single vehicle, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Beginning from all oceans of vehicle-departures, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. With these as foremost, O son of good family, through inexpressible methods of teaching-accomplishment, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Thus, O son of good family, descending into oceans of <s>Tathāgatas</s> undivided from the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, accomplishing the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-gathering through the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> to all beings, dwelling through oceans of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) extending to the ultimate limit of <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, I cultivate this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entrance into the Deep Miraculous Display of Delightful Speech,' through the method of cultivating the domain of liberation that increases with each and every mind-moment. And through each method of cultivating the domain of liberation, at every mind-moment I pervade the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> //

body.text: sudhana āha - āścaryaṃ devate yāvadgambhīra eṣa bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ / kiyaccirapratilabdhaḥ tvayāyamārye bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ? āha - bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani lokadhātuparivartaparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpāṇāṃ pareṇa dharmārcinagarameghā nāma lokadhāturabhūt cāturdvīpalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamagandhamaṇisumerujālapratiṣṭhitā sarvatathāgatapūrvapraṇidhāṇanirghoṣapadmasaṃdhivyūhā sarvasattvakarmasamudrasaṃbhūtamaṇirājasāgaraśarīrā mahāpadmasaṃsthānā viśuddhasaṃkliṣṭā sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamapuṣpacakravālaparivṛtā sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamagandhamaṇisumervabhyudgatālaṃkārā sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamamahācāturdvīpikālaṃkārā / ekaikasyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāmanabhilāpyānabhilāpyanagarakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan //
body.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> said: 'How wonderful, O goddess, how profound is this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation! How long ago, O noble lady, did you attain this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation?' She replied: 'Long ago, O son of good family, in the past, beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of a world-realm revolution, there was a world-realm called <s>Dharmārcinagarameghā</s> (Cloud-City of Dharma Flames), established upon a net of fragrant jewel <s>Sumerus</s> equal in number to atoms of four-continent world-realms, arrayed with lotus-joint displays of the sounds of the prior vows of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with a body of jewel-king oceans born from the oceans of karma of all beings, in the form of a great lotus, both pure and defiled, surrounded by flower <s>Cakravāḷas</s> equal in number to atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, adorned with ornaments of fragrant jewel <s>Sumerus</s> surpassing <s>Sumeru</s> equal in number to atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, adorned with great four-continent systems equal in number to atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. In each four-continent system there were inexpressibly inexpressible <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundreds of thousands of cities //'

body.text: tasyāṃ khalu kulaputra lokadhātau vimalaprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūt sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamatathāgataprabhavaḥ / tasyāṃ ca dharmārcinagarameghāyāṃ lokadhātau madhyamā vicitradhvajā nāma cāturdvīpikābhūt / tasyā madhye samantaratnakusumaprabhā nāma rājadhānyabhūt / tasyā rājadhānyā nātidūre dharmarājabhavanapratibhāso nāma bodhimaṇḍo 'bhūt / tatra bodhimaṇḍe sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājo nāma tathāgata udapādi teṣāṃ sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ prathamakalpikaḥ / tena ca samayena vimalavakrabhānuprabho nāma rājā abhūt cakravartī / tena tasya bhagavataḥ sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājñastathāgatasyāntikāt sarvadharmasāgaro nāma sūtrānta udgṛhītaḥ / udgṛhya ca dharmacakramanupravartitam / parinirvṛtasya ca pravrajitvāśāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam /
body.translated_text: In that world-realm, O son of good family, there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Vimalaprabha</s> (Pure Radiance), producing <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. In that world-realm of <s>Dharmārcinagarameghā</s>, the central four-continent system was called <s>Vicitradhvajā</s> (Variegated Banner). In its midst was a royal capital called <s>Samantaratnakusumaprabhā</s> (Radiance of Universal Jewel Flowers). Not far from that royal capital was a <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) called <s>Dharmarājabhavanapratihhāsa</s> (Reflection of the Palace of the Dharma King). At that <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s> (King of Radiance of the Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas) arose in the world, the first of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. At that time there was a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), named <s>Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha</s> (Radiance of the Sun of a Pure Face). From that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s>, he received and retained a <s>sūtrānta</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasāgara</s> (Ocean of All Dharmas). Having received it, he turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma). After [the Tathāgata's] <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having gone forth, he upheld the teaching

body.text: śāsanāntardhānakāle ca sahasradhā bhinne śāsane daśanayaśatabhinnāyāṃ dharmadeśanāyāmanantarakalpakaṣāye pratyupasthite sarvakarmakleśāvaraṇāvṛtānāṃ sattvānāṃ kalahavigrahavivādamāpannānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ ca buddhaśāsanaguṇānarthikānāṃ viṣayaratiparāyaṇānāṃ rājacaurakathābhiratānāṃ strījanapadasamudrakathābhiratānāṃ lokāyatamantrābhiratānāmudvegasaṃjananārthaṃ dhārmika utkāsaḥ kṛto 'bhūt - aho bateyamanekakalpasamudānītā mahādharmolkā antardhāsyatīti saṃvegajananīyā kathā kṛtā / sa ūrdhvaṃ gaganatale saptatālamātramabhyudgamya anantavarṇānarcimeghānniścārya nānāvarṇān mahāraśmijālavyūhān kāyādutsṛjya anekavarṇayā prabhayā loke kleśatāpaṃ śamayitvā anantamadhyān sattvān bodhau pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / tacca tathāgataśāsanaṃ punarjvālayitvā ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇyasthāt //
body.translated_text: At the time of the disappearance of the teaching, when the teaching had been split a thousandfold, when the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse had been divided into ten hundred methods, when the defilement of the subsequent <s>kalpa</s> was at hand — for the sake of arousing urgency in beings covered by the obstructions of all karma and defilements, beings who had fallen into quarrel, conflict, and dispute, and in monks who had no interest in the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, who were devoted to sensory pleasures, who delighted in tales of kings and thieves, who delighted in tales of women, countries, and oceans, who delighted in worldly spells — a righteous cry was raised: 'Alas! This great torch of <s>Dharma</s>, accumulated over countless <s>kalpas</s>, will disappear!' — a tale arousing urgency was told. Rising upward into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, sending forth clouds of rays of countless colors, releasing from his body arrays of great nets of rays of various colors, pacifying the burning of defilements in the world with light of many colors, he established beings of infinite extent in awakening. And having rekindled that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, it endured for sixty thousand years //

body.text: tena ca samayena dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā nāma bhikṣuṇyabhūt tasyaiva vimalacakrabhānuprabhasya cakravartino duhitā bhikṣuṇīśatasahasraparivārā / sā taṃ saṃvegaśabdaṃ śrutvā tacca mahāprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā saparivārā bodhāya cittamutpādayāmāsa / tacca bhikṣuṇīśatasahasramanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvavaivartikamabhūt / tathāgatasaṃmukhībhāvasamavasaraṇaṃ ca nāma samādhiṃ pratyalabhata / sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirmāṇaprabhaṃ ca nāma dhāraṇī sarvadharmasāgaranayapraveśāṃ ca nāma prajñāpāramitāṃ pratyalabhata / dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā ca bhikṣuṇī sarvatathāgataśāsanasaṃbhavāvabhāsapradīpaṃ ca nāma samādhim, etaṃ ca manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ ca bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ sūkṣmamṛdukaṃ pratyalabhata, yatpratilābhādasya sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājasya tathāgatasya tatsarvaṃ vikurvitamāmukhībhūtam //
body.translated_text: At that time there was a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) named <s>Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā</s> (Radiance of the Creation of the Dharma Wheel), the daughter of that very <s>cakravartin</s> <s>Vimalacakrabhānuprabha</s>, attended by a hundred thousand <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. She, hearing that sound of urgency and seeing that great miraculous display, together with her retinue generated the mind toward awakening. And that hundred thousand <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> became irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. And she attained a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Tathāgatasaṃmukhībhāvasamavasaraṇa</s> (Convergence of Being Face-to-Face with the Tathāgata). She also attained a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirmāṇaprabha</s> (Radiance of the Creation of the Dharma Wheel of All Tathāgatas) and a <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranayapraveśa</s> (Entrance into the Method of the Ocean of All Dharmas). And the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā</s> attained in subtle and tender form a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgataśāsanasaṃbhavāvabhāsapradīpa</s> (Lamp Illuminating the Origin of All Tathāgatas' Teaching) and this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entrance into the Deep Miraculous Display of Delightful Speech,' upon attaining which all that miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s> became manifest to her //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vimalavaktrabhānuprabho nāma rājābhūccakravartī yena tatsarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājñastathāgatasya śāsane pravrajitvā dharmacakramanupravartitam, parinirvṛttasya ca śāsanāntardhānakālasamaye śāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam, mahādharmolkā ca jvalitā? na khalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / samantabhadro bodhisattvaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vimalavaktrabhānuprabho nāma rājā abhūccakravartī / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena vimalavaktrabhānuprabhasya rājñaścakravartino dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā nāma duhitā bhikṣuṇyabhūdbhikṣuṇīśatasahasraparivārā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā nāma bhikṣuṇyabhūvam? mayā tattasya sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājñastathāgatasya śāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam / tacca bhikṣuṇīśatasahasraṃ sarvamavaivartikaṃ kṛtamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tathāgatasaṃmukhībhāvasamavasaraṇe ca samādhau pratiṣṭhāpitam / sarvatathāgatadharmacakravajraprabhāyāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ sarvadharmasāgaranayapraveśāyāṃ ca prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam //
body.translated_text: What do you think, O son of good family? Was that king, the <s>cakravartin</s> named <s>Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha</s>, at that time someone else — he who, having gone forth under the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s>, turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, and at the time of the disappearance of the teaching after [the Tathāgata's] <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, upheld the teaching and kindled the great torch of <s>Dharma</s>? You should not see it so, O son of good family. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> was at that time the king, the <s>cakravartin</s> named <s>Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha</s>. What do you think, O son of good family? Was someone else the daughter of the king, the <s>cakravartin</s> <s>Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha</s>, at that time — the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā</s>, attended by a hundred thousand <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>? It should not be seen so. I myself was at that time the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā</s>. By me, at that time, the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s> was upheld. And that hundred thousand <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were all made irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. They were established in the <s>samādhi</s> of convergence of being face-to-face with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakravajraprabhā</s> (Vajra Radiance of the Dharma Wheel of All Tathāgatas) and in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranayapraveśa</s> //

body.text: tasya ca mayā tathāgatasyānantaraṃ vimaladharmaparvatajñānaśikharābho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ maṇḍalāvabhāsaprabhacūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmabhāskaraśrīmegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmasāgaranirdeśaghoṣo nāma tathāgata
body.translated_text: After that <s>Tathāgata</s>, I propitiated a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vimaladharmaparvatajñānaśikharābha</s> (Splendor of the Peak of Knowledge of the Mountain of Pure Dharma). After him, I propitiated a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Maṇḍalāvabhāsaprabhacūḍa</s> (Crest of the Radiance Illuminating the Maṇḍala). After him, I propitiated a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmabhāskaraśrīmegha</s> (Cloud of the Glory of the Sun of Dharma). After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmasāgaranirdeśaghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Exposition of the Ocean of Dharma)

body.text: ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmādityajñānamaṇḍalapradīpo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmakusumaketudhvajamegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmārciḥparvataketurājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmanayagambhīraśrīcandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmajñānasaṃbhavasamantapratibhāsagarbho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānākaracūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ śailendraśrīgarbharājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantamukhajñānabhadramerurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sarvadharmavīryavegadhvajo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmaratnakusumaśrīmegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ śāntiprabhagambhīrakūṭo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ raśminetrapratibhāsaprabhacandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānārciśrīsāgaro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantajñānabhadramaṇḍalo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ adhaūrdhvadigjñānāvabhāso nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ raśmisaṃkusumitapradīpo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānasiṃhaketudhvajarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantasūryāvabhāsaprabharājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnalakṣaṇavibhūṣitamerurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sūryavikramasamantapratibhāso nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmajālavibuddhaśrīcandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmapadmapraphullitaśrīmegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ lakṣaṇasūryacakrasamantaprabho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantāvabhāsadharmaśrīghoṣo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vaiśāradyavajranārāyaṇasiṃho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantajñānadhvajaśūro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmapadmaphullagātro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ guṇakusumaśrīsāgaro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmadhanaśikharābhaskandho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānaśikharārcimegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantadharmadvāravahanaśikharābho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ bodhimaṇḍavibuddhaśrīcandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmolkājvalanaśrīcandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantapratibhāsacūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmameghadhvajapradīpo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vajrasāgaradhvajamegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ yaśaḥparvataśrīmegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ, tasyānantaraṃ candanaśrīcandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantaśrīkusumatejābhonāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sarvasattvāvabhāsatejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ guṇapadmaśrīgarbho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ gandhārciravabhāsarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ hetupadmo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ lakṣaṇaparvatavairocano nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantavighuṣṭakīrtidhvajo nāma tathāgata
body.translated_text: was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmādityajñānamaṇḍalapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Maṇḍala of Dharma-Sun Knowledge) was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmakusumaketudhvajamegha</s> (Cloud of the Banner-Crest of Dharma-Flowers) was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmārciḥparvataketurāja</s> (King of the Crest of the Mountain of Dharma-Flame) was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmanayagambhīraśrīcandra</s> (Moon of the Glory of the Profound Dharma-Method) was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmajñānasaṃbhavasamantapratibhāsagarbha</s> (Womb of Universal Reflection Born of Dharma-Knowledge) was propitiated. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānākaracūḍa</s> (Crest of the Mine of Knowledge) was propitiated. body.text: iti hi kulaputra etadbuddhaśataṃ pramukhaṃ kṛtvā tasmin vimalābhe kalpe sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā utpannā abhūvan / teṣāṃ punaḥ kulaputra sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sarvapaścimo dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'bhūt / te khalu mayā kulaputra sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatāḥ sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharājapūrvaṃgamā dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparājapaścimāḥ sarve pūjitāḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca me tathāgatānāmupasthānaṃ kṛtam / sarveṣāṃ ca dharmadeśanā śrutā / sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāmahaṃ tathāgatānāṃ śāsane pravrajitā / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ śāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam / sarveṣāṃ ca mayā teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantikādeṣa manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśo bodhisattvavimokṣo vividhaiḥ pratilābhanayaiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca mayā teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantikādanantamadhyāḥ sattvasāgarāḥ paripācitāḥ / tato 'rvāgbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu yāvantastathāgatā utpannāḥ, sarve te mayā tathāgatāḥ dharmapratipattyā pūjitāḥ / sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra tata upādāya saṃsārarātrigateṣu sattveṣu ajñānanidrāprasupteṣu jāgarmi, cittanagaraṃ caiṣāṃ paripālayāmi, traidhātukanagarāccainānuccālya sarvajñatādharmanagare pratiṣṭhāpayāmi //
body.translated_text: Thus, son of good family, headed by this hundred of <s>Buddhas</s>, in that <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Vimalābha</s> (Stainless Splendor), <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s> arose. Of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, son of good family, the very last was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja</s> (King of the Lamp of Knowledge Like the City of the Dharmadhātu). Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, son of good family, beginning with <s>Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja</s> and ending with <s>Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja</s> — all were worshipped by me. I performed attendance for all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of all was heard by me. In the dispensation of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I went forth [from the household life]. The teaching of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> was upheld by me. And from all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I obtained this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of entry into the transformations of the profound, sweet-voiced — by various methods of attainment. And in the presence of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, infinite and middleless oceans of beings were ripened by me. And after that, whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s> arose in <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to [their] atoms — all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were worshipped by me through the practice of <s>Dharma</s>. And I, son of good family, from that time onward, keep watch over beings who have gone to the night of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who are asleep in the slumber of ignorance; I guard the city of their minds; and having dislodged them from the city of the three realms, I establish them in the <s>Dharma</s>-city of omniscience. //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ lokasaṃbhinnapralāpavinivartanamadvayabhaṇitāviniyojanaṃ satyapratiṣṭhāpanaparyavasānaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmavipratibaddhasarvavākpathasvabhāvajñānānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmābhisaṃbodhivaśavartināṃ sarvasattvavacanarutaghoṣasāgarāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvamantrasamudrasaṃskārakuśalānāṃ sarvadharmasaṃkhyānāmasamudranayavidhijñānāṃ sarvadharmasamavasaraṇadhāraṇīsamudravaśavartināṃ sarvasattvayathāśayadharmameghābhinirhārakuśalānāṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayacaryāparyavasānānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, sarvasattvasaṃgrahapratipattirvā jñātum, anuttaro bodhisattvakarmasamārambhaprayogo vā bodhisattvasūkṣmajñānānugamo vā bodhisattvadharmanidhānakośavibhaktavṛṣabhitā bodhisattvakarmasāṃkathyasiṃhāsanākramaṇaṃ vā jñātum / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi te satpuruṣāḥ sarvadharmabhūmimaṇḍaladhāraṇyavakrāntāḥ //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, know this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entry into the Profound Magical Display of Pleasing Sounds' (<s>Manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśa</s>) — which turns [beings] away from the confused prattle of the world, which directs them toward non-dual speech, and which culminates in establishing them in truth. How could I know the conduct or express the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> whose nature is the unobstructed knowledge of all paths of speech, who at every mind-moment are masters of the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, who have descended into the ocean of the sounds, utterances, and voices of all beings, who are skilled in the construction of all <s>mantra</s>-oceans, who possess the knowledge of the methods of the ocean of the enumeration of all <s>dharmas</s>, who are masters of the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-ocean of the convergence of all <s>dharmas</s>, who are skilled in producing clouds of <s>Dharma</s> according to the dispositions of all beings, whose conduct culminates in the ripening and disciplining of all beings — or know their practice of gathering all beings, or know the supreme undertaking of <s>bodhisattva</s> activity, or the following of the subtle knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, or the eminence of the differentiated treasury of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-storehouse, or the ascending of the lion-throne of the discourse on <s>bodhisattva</s> activity? For what reason? Because those noble beings have entered the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the ground-maṇḍala of all <s>dharmas</s>. //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva bhagavato vairocanasya pādamūle sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā nāma rātridevatā saṃnipatitā, yā mamānantaraṃ saṃniṣaṇṇā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvāḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣante, kathaṃ ca pratipadyamānāḥ sarvasattvān sarvajñatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family; here at the feet of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, there is gathered a night-deity named <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> (She of Pleasant Dwelling Where All Trees Blossom), who is seated next to me. Approach her and ask: 'How do <s>bodhisattvas</s> train in omniscience, and how, while practicing, do they establish all beings in omniscience?' //

body.text: atha khalu sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>, at that moment, further demonstrating this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entry into the Profound Magical Display of Pleasing Sounds,' addressed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: The liberation of the sons of the <s>Jina</s> is profound and hard to perceive — an entry into the universal ground that has the character of space.
They descend upon all the <s>Jinas</s> abiding in the three times, and upon the expanse of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, endless and without middle. // 1 //
Attaining infinite methods of liberation born from the accumulation of [meritorious] provisions, inconceivable and immeasurable in their nature as <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: saṃvardhanāmapi samanta asaṅgavegam avagāha maitriṣu triyadhvanayaṣpatheṣu // 2 //
children.translated_text: and also increasing them everywhere with unobstructed force, they plunge into loving-kindness along the paths of the three times. // 2 //

children.text: iti buddhakṣetraparivartarajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānamādigatamāsa purā hi kṣetram /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the past, beyond [kalpas] equal to the dust-atoms of the revolutions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, there was formerly a field —

children.text: dharmārcimeghanagaraḥ śirilokadhātu kalpo babhūva vimalābha mahāprabhaśca // 3 //
children.translated_text: the world-realm called <s>Dharmārcimeghanagara</s> (City of Dharma-Flame-Clouds), Glorious, and the <s>kalpa</s> was called <s>Vimalābha Mahāprabha</s> (Stainless-Radiance Great-Splendor). // 3 //

children.text: tatraiva kalpi jinavaṃśi anūpachinne buddhāḥ sumeruparamāṇusamā upannāḥ /
children.translated_text: In that very <s>kalpa</s>, in an unbroken succession of <s>Jinas</s>, <s>Buddhas</s> arose equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>.

children.text: dharmasamudraprabhagarjitarāja buddhaḥ purvaṃgamaḥ prathamakalpika āsi teṣām // 4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Dharmasamudraprabhagarjitarāja</s> (King of the Roar of the Radiance of the Ocean of Dharma) was the first of them, at the beginning of that <s>kalpa</s>. // 4 //

children.text: jinu dharmameghanagarābhapradīparājo yaḥ sarvapaścimu abhūtsugatāna teṣām /
children.translated_text: The <s>Jina</s> <s>Dharmameghanagarābhapradīparāja</s> (Lamp-King of the Radiance of the City of Dharma-Clouds) was the last of those <s>Sugatas</s>.

children.text: te sarvi pūjita mayā upasaṃkramitvā dharmaśca teṣa mi śruto janayitva prītim // 5 //
children.translated_text: All of them were worshipped by me, having approached them, and their <s>Dharma</s> was heard by me, generating joy. // 5 //

children.text: dṛṣṭo mayā prathamu kāñcanavarṇaraśmiḥ dharmaḥ samudraprabhagarjitaghoṣarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: The first [Buddha] I saw was of golden radiance — <s>Dharmasamudraprabhagarjitaghoṣarāja</s> (King of the Sound of the Roar of the Radiance of the Ocean of Dharma),

children.text: dvātriṃśallakṣaṇavicitritu merukalpo dṛṣṭvā ca me matirabhūtsugato bhaveyam // 6 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the thirty-two marks, like <s>Sumeru</s> in <s>kalpa</s>-[splendor]; and having seen him, the thought arose in me: 'May I become a <s>Sugata</s>!' // 6 //

children.text: sahadarśanena mama tasya tathāgatasya prādurbabhūva balavajjinacittamādyam /
children.translated_text: At the very sight of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, there first arose in me, strong as vajra, the mind of a <s>Jina</s>,
stainless as the realm of space, of the nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), through the conditions for the arising of the expanse of omniscience. // 7 //

body.text: yena triyadhvagata sarvi sphuṭāḥ samantāt buddhāśca tatsutasamudravṛtā aśeṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: By which all [<s>Jinas</s>] abiding in the three times are manifest everywhere, and <s>Buddhas</s> together with their oceanic assemblies of sons without remainder,

body.text: kṣetrārṇavā api samudra sarve āsan kṛpāmṛtamahodadhi saṃbhaveta // 8 //
body.translated_text: and oceans of fields too — all became oceans; from the great ocean of the nectar of compassion it would arise. // 8 //

children.text: kāyena sarvi spharaṇārthamaśeṣa kṣetrā kāyaṃ yathāśayajagadvinidarśanāya /
