children.translated_text: For the purpose of pervading all fields without exception with [this] body, for demonstrating the body to beings according to their dispositions,

children.text: kṣetrāṇyaśeṣamavabhāsanakampanāya pākāya caiva jagatāṃ janitaṃ mano me // 9 //
children.translated_text: for illuminating and shaking all fields without exception, and for the ripening of beings — this mind was generated in me. // 9 //

children.text: dvitīye yajjinasya upasaṃkramaṇe 'pi dṛṣṭāḥ kṣetrārṇaveṣu daśasu sthita ye jinendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: When I approached the second <s>Jina</s>, I saw the <s>Jinendras</s> abiding in the ocean of fields in the ten [directions],

children.text: kṣetrāḥ samudraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kṣetrārṇaveṣu jina paścimake mi dṛṣṭāḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: in oceans of fields equal to the atoms of oceanic dust-particles — the <s>Jinas</s> in the last of those field-oceans were seen by me. // 10 //

children.text: sarvāntakṣetraparivartarajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu ye jina upanna jagatpradīpāḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>kalpas</s> equal to the dust-particles of the revolutions of all ultimate fields, whatever <s>Jinas</s> arose as lamps of the world,

children.text: te sarvi pūjita mayā upasaṃkramitvā evaṃ vimokṣanayasāgaru śodhayeyam // 11 //
children.translated_text: all of them were worshipped by me, having approached them — thus I would purify the ocean of methods of liberation. // 11 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratilabdhaḥ anantamadhyasamādhimukhasamudrāvatīrṇo vipuladhāraṇīmukhasamudrasaṃbhūtacetā bodhisattvamahābhijñāvabhāsapratilabdho mahāprītisaṃvitsāgarāvatīrṇo vipulaprītivegasāgaravivardhitacetāḥ sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entry into the Profound Magical Display of Pleasing Sounds,' having descended into the ocean of gateways of infinite <s>samādhis</s>, with a mind born from the ocean of vast <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, having attained the radiance of the great superknowledge of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having descended into the ocean of great joy and understanding, with a mind expanded by the ocean of the force of vast joy — praised the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> with appropriate verses:

children.text: prajñā hi te vipula dharmasamudracārī cīrṇā ca me bhavasamudra anantamadhyān /
children.translated_text: Your wisdom is vast, ranging through the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>, and you have traversed the oceans of existence, endless and without middle.

children.text: dīrghāyu nirjvara sujñānaśarīragarbhe tvaṃ devi rocasi imāṃ pariṣāmupetya // 12 //
children.translated_text: O long-lived one, free from affliction, with a body that is a womb of excellent knowledge, you, O goddess, shine having come to this assembly. // 12 //
Having awakened to the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, luminous as space, you descend into the methods of all three times without attachment.

children.text: ārambaṇāni tulayasyapi cāvikalpā cittakṣaṇena api tāni acintiyāni // 13 //
children.translated_text: You weigh even the objects of support without conceptual elaboration — and those too are inconceivable in a single mind-moment. // 13 //
With the eye of knowledge you perceive the nature of <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of beings; with compassion you descend into the infinite oceans of beings.

children.text: buddhyā vimokṣa sugabhīra vigāhamānā sarvān vinesi paripācayase 'prameyān // 14 //
children.translated_text: Plunging into the supremely profound liberation with wisdom, you discipline and ripen immeasurable [beings]. // 14 //

body.text: tvaṃ dharmamaṇḍalavicāranaye vidhijñā dharmasvabhāvaprativedhanaye vibuddhā /
body.translated_text: You are skilled in the method of investigating the maṇḍala of <s>Dharma</s>; you are awakened to the method of penetrating the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: sarvāryamārgamamalaṃ paribhāvayantī niryātyase jagadaśeṣa viśodhayantī // 15 //
body.translated_text: Cultivating the stainless noble path, you go forth purifying the world without remainder. // 15 //

children.translated_text: You, O goddess, are the supreme, unconquerable charioteer of beings, receiving the stainless knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: tvaṃ dharmadhātugata sarvi spharitva sattvān dharmaṃ prakāśya bhaya sarvi śamesi loke // 16 //
children.translated_text: Pervading all beings who abide in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>, you pacify all fears in the world. // 16 //
By the method of the path of the vow of <s>Vairocana</s>, O goddess, you shall go forth, endowed with unattached, vast, stainless wisdom.

children.text: sarvatra jinabalaṃ pratipadyamānā saṃpaśyase jinavikurvita sarvakṣetraiḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: Attaining the power of the <s>Jina</s> everywhere, you behold the magical displays of the <s>Jinas</s> in all fields. // 17 //

children.text: cittaṃ durāsadu tavā gaganaprakāśaṃ sarve kileśamali nirmalamādiśuddham /
children.translated_text: Your mind is invincible, luminous as space; all the stains of defilement are stainless [in it], pure from the beginning.

children.text: yasmin samosari triyadhvaga sarvakṣetrā buddhāśca sātmajagaṇāḥ saha sarvasattvaiḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: In it converge all fields abiding in the three times, and <s>Buddhas</s> with their assemblies of sons, together with all beings. // 18 //
Night and day, moments, fractions, seasons, fortnights, months, years, and <s>kalpas</s> together with their perishable and conceptual [divisions],

children.text: kalpārṇavānapi sanāmasamudrasaṃkhyān saṃjñodadhīn jagatāṃ vidarśayasi kṣaṇena // 19 //
children.translated_text: and even oceans of <s>kalpas</s> with their numerical ocean-designations and the oceans of concepts of beings — you display [all these] in a single instant. // 19 //

children.text: diśatāsu yāvata tu sattvacyutopapādā ye rūpiṇāmapi ca saṃjñiasaṃjñināṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The deaths and rebirths of beings in the ten directions, of those with form, and of those with and without perception —

children.text: vyavahārasatyanaya otaramāṇā teṣāṃ mārgaṃ vidarśya varabodhipathe praṇesi // 20 //
children.translated_text: descending into the method of conventional truth regarding them, showing the path, you guide them to the supreme way of <s>bodhi</s>. // 20 //
You have come forth from the cluster of the net of the vow of <s>Vairocana</s>, and from the exaltation common to all <s>Sugatas</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ dharmakāyapariśuddha asaṅgacittā rūpaṃ vidarśayami loki yathāśayānām // 21 //
children.translated_text: You, with a <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) that is pure, with an unattached mind — 'I display forms in the world according to beings' dispositions.' // 21 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyo rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyaṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśriyo rātridevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 37 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having praised the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> with appropriate verses, bowed his head at the feet of the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>, circumambulated the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the night-deity <s>Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī</s>. // 37 //

body.text: 40 Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā /
body.translated_text: 40. <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako manojñarutagambhīravikurvitapraveśaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā prabhāvayamānaḥ saṃbhāvayamāno vipulīkurvan yena sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā rātridevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / so 'paśyat sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsāṃ rātridevatāṃ ratnadrumāṅkuragarbhe siṃhāsane sarvagandharatnadrumaśākhe kūṭāgāre saṃniṣaṇṇāṃ daśarātridevatāsahasraparivārām //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, further magnifying, honoring, and expanding the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Entry into the Profound Magical Display of Pleasing Sounds,' approached the night-deity <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s>. He saw the night-deity <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> seated on a lion-throne within a jewel-tree-sprout womb, in an aerial palace with branches of trees of all fragrant jewels, surrounded by ten thousand night-deities. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārye devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caritavyam, kathaṃ śikṣitavyam / tadvadasva me devate, kathaṃ bodhisattvā bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caranti, kathaṃ śikṣante, kathaṃ caritvā kathaṃ śikṣitvā niryānti sarvajñatāyām //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the night-deity <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s>, stood before her with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'O Noble Goddess, I have generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> practice in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how should he train? Tell me, O goddess, how do <s>bodhisattvas</s> practice in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, how do they train, and having practiced and trained, how do they go forth to omniscience?' //

body.text: evamukte sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - mama kulaputra anubhāvena sahe lokadhātau ādityāstaṃgamanakāle padmāni praphullāni sugandhībhavanti / sarve nagaranārīgaṇāścodyānagatā ratikrīḍāprayuktā gṛhagamanāya matimutpādayanti / pathotpathagatāḥ sattvā rātristhāne cetanābahulāḥ sarvajagatpālanābhimukhā bhavanti / darīgahanaguhāśrayāḥ sattvā darīgahanaguhāsu praviśanti / vṛkṣālayāśrayāḥ sattvā vṛkṣālayāśrayābhimukhā bhavanti / vilāśrayāḥ sattvā bilānyanupraviśanti / grāmanagaranigamajanapadāśrayāḥ sattvā grāmanagaranigamajanapadānanupraviśanti / udakāśrayāḥ sattvā jalamavataranti / anyadigjanapadagatāḥ sattvāḥ svajanapadadikcetanāmutpādayanti rātrau sukhasparśavihārāya //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the night-deity <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> said to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: 'By my power, son of good family, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, at the time of sunset, lotuses bloom and become fragrant. All the companies of women in the cities who are engaged in play and amusement in the parks generate the intention to return home. Beings on roads and byways become attentive to [the coming of] night and turn toward the protection of all beings. Beings who dwell in ravines, thickets, and caves enter their ravines, thickets, and caves. Beings who dwell in tree-hollows turn toward their tree-hollow abodes. Beings who dwell in burrows enter their burrows. Beings who dwell in villages, cities, towns, and districts enter their villages, cities, towns, and districts. Beings who dwell in water enter the water. Beings who have gone to other regions and lands generate the intention toward their own homeland during the night, for the purpose of dwelling in the comfort of ease.' //

body.text: api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra naranārīgaṇānāṃ daharāṇāṃ taruṇānāṃ yauvanamadamattānāṃ nṛtyagītavādyaratipramattānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāmaguṇapramuktānāṃ jātijarāmaraṇamahāndhakārabhayapratipakṣāya kuśalamūlasaṃjānābhiyogaṃ saṃvarṇayāmi / matsariṇaḥ sattvān dāne saṃniyojayāmi / duḥśīlān sattvān śīle pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / vyāpannacittānāṃ sattvānāṃ maitrīṃ saṃvarṇayāmi / kṣubhitacittān sattvān kṣāntau pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / kusīdān sattvān bodhisattvavīryārambhe pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / vibhrāntacittān sattvān dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / duḥprajñān sattvān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ niyojayāmi / hīnayānādhimuktān sattvān mahāyān pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / traidhātukābhiniviṣṭān sattvān bhavagatiniṣṭhāmaṇḍalacāriṇo bodhisattvapraṇidhānapāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / āvaraṇavaśagatān sattvān karmakleśaprapīḍitān puṇyajñānabalaparihīṇān bodhisattvabalapāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / ajñānatamovanaddhān sattvān ahaṃkāramamakāravidyāndhakāraprāptān bodhisattvajñānapāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmi //
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, for groups of men and women — young, youthful, intoxicated and maddened by the pride of youth, heedless in their delight in dance, song, and music, released into the qualities of sense-desire — I praise the effort of generating wholesome roots as an antidote to the great darkness and fear of birth, old age, and death. I engage miserly beings in generosity. I establish immoral beings in moral conduct. I praise loving-kindness to beings of corrupted mind. I establish agitated beings in patience. I establish lazy beings in the initial effort of <s>bodhisattva</s>-vigor. I establish distracted beings in <s>dhyāna</s>s (meditations). I engage beings of poor wisdom in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). I establish beings inclined toward the inferior vehicle in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). I establish beings attached to the three realms — those who course in the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the finality of the destinies of existence — in the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> of vows (<s>praṇidhānapāramitā</s>). I establish beings who have fallen under the power of obstructions, afflicted by <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), deficient in the power of merit and knowledge, in the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> of powers (<s>balapāramitā</s>). I establish beings bound in the darkness of ignorance, those who have fallen into the darkness of ego-grasping and possessiveness, in the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>). //

body.text: api tu khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra vipulaprītisaṃbhavasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sudhana āha - ka etasya devate vipulaprītisaṃbhavatuṣṭyavabhāsasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, I have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītisaṃbhavasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsa</s> (Illumination of the Satisfaction Arising from Vast Joy).' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'What is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called Illumination of the Satisfaction Arising from Vast Joy, goddess?'

body.text: viṣayaḥ? āha - tathāgatapuṇyasattvaṃsaṃgrahajñānopāyāvabhāsa eṣa kulaputra vimokṣaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yatkiṃcit kulaputra sattvāḥ sukhamanubhavanti, sarvaṃ tattathāgatapuṇyaprabhāvena tathāgatānuśāsanīpathena tathāgatavacanapratipattyā tathāgatānuśikṣaṇena tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena tathāgatajñānamārgapratipattyā tathāgatabhāgakuśalamūlāvaropaṇena tathāgatadharmadeśanāniṣyandena tathāgatajñānasūryāvabhāsena / tathāgatagotraśuklakarmamaṇḍalaprabhayā hi kulaputra sattvānāṃ sukhāni saṃbhavanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kulaputra ahametaṃ vipulaprītisaṃbhavasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣamavatarantī bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūrvabodhisattvacaryāsamudraṃ samanusmarantī avatarantī avagāhayamānā evaṃ jānāmi, evamanugacchāmi - yathā bhagavataḥ pūrvabodhisattvabhūmimadhyālambamānasya sattvānahaṃkāramamakārābhiniviṣṭānavidyāndhakāraprāptān dṛṣṭigahanakāntārapraviṣṭāṃstṛṣṇāvaśaṃgatān rāgabandhanabaddhān doṣapratighacetaso mohākulasaṃtānānīrṣyāmātsaryaparyavanaddhān kleśasamākulacittān mahatsaṃsāraduḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavataḥ saṃsāradāridryaduḥkhaprapīḍitān buddhadarśanavimukhān sattvān dṛṣṭvā mahākaruṇācittaṃ prādurabhavat / sarvasattvānāmarthaṃ sarvajagadupakaraṇaratnasaṃgrahaparigrahacittaṃ sarvasattvasaṃsāropakaraṇasaṃbhavacittaṃ sarvavastvāgrahavigatacittaṃ sarvaviṣayālubdhacittaṃ sarvaratiṣvanadhyavasitacittaṃ sarvaparibhogeṣvagṛddhacittaṃ sarvadāneṣu vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇacittaṃ sarvalokasaṃpattiṣvaspṛhaṇācittaṃ hetupratyayasaṃmūḍhacittaṃ suparyeṣitayathāvaddharmanidhyapticittaṃ sarvasattvārthapratiśaraṇatābhinirharaṇacittaṃ prādurabhavat //
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This liberation, son of good family, is the illumination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge of the method of gathering beings through merit. For what reason? Because whatever happiness beings experience, son of good family, all of that is through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s merit, through the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s instruction, through the practice of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s words, through training under the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment, through the practice of the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge, through the planting of wholesome roots that belong to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s portion, through the overflow of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching of <s>Dharma</s>, through the illumination of the sun of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. For through the radiance of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of pure <s>karma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage, son of good family, the happiness of beings arises. For what reason? For thus, son of good family, as I enter this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called Illumination of the Satisfaction Arising from Vast Joy, recollecting and descending into and plunging into the ocean of the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, I know thus, I follow thus: how the <s>Bhagavān</s>, while dwelling on the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage, seeing beings ensnared by ego-grasping and possessiveness, fallen into the darkness of ignorance, entered into the thicket-wilderness of views, gone under the power of craving, bound by the bonds of passion, of minds marked by hatred and aversion, of mental continuums confused by delusion, enveloped by jealousy and miserliness, of minds bewildered by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), experiencing great suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, oppressed by the suffering of the poverty of <s>saṃsāra</s>, turned away from the vision of the <s>Buddha</s> — seeing such beings, the mind of great compassion arose in him. For the sake of all beings, the mind of gathering the jewel-collections of all worldly requisites arose, the mind arising from the requisites of <s>saṃsāra</s> for all beings arose, the mind free from grasping at any object arose, the mind ungreedy for any sense-object arose, the mind not fixated on any pleasure arose, the mind uncovetous of any enjoyment arose, the mind not expecting the ripening of any gift arose, the mind without longing for any worldly prosperity arose, the mind confused about causes and conditions arose, the mind contemplating <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are through well-sought contemplation arose, the mind accomplishing the refuge for the welfare of all beings arose. //

body.text: sa evaṃ yathābhūtasarvadharmasvabhāvāvatīrṇacetāḥ sarvasattvadhātau mahāmaitrīsamatāpratipannaḥ sarvajaganmahākaruṇāmeghaspharaṇaprayogaḥ sarvasattvalokasaṃchādanamahādharmacchatramaṇḍalaḥ sarvasattvakleśaparvatavinirbhedanamahājñānavajrapraharaṇaḥ sarvajagatsukhasaṃbhavatuṣṭivegasaṃvardhitacetāḥ sarvasattvātyantasukhābhinirhārapraṇidhānacetā yathāśayābhiprāyasarvasattvavastvabhipravarṣaṇacetāḥ sarvasattvāparityāgasamaprayogacetā āryadhanasarvasattvasaṃtarpaṇacetāḥ paramadaśabalajñānaratnapratilambhacetā bodhisattvamahābhijñābalādhānaprāpto vividhabodhisattvamahāvikurvitameghena dharmadhātuparamākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvasattvadhātuṃ spharitvā sarvasattvābhimukhasthitaḥ sarvākārasarvārambaṇamahāmeghaṃ pravartayan sarvaratnābharaṇamahāmeghavarṣaṃ cābhipravarṣan, yaduta sarvasattvānāṃ yathānukūlaparibhogāya anantavastuvimātratāparityāgamaprameyopakaraṇavaimātracāritraṃ nānāvidhasarvadānasaṃgrahaprayogamanekavidhavastu parityāgasamudācāramanabhilāpyopakaraṇajātavyūhābhisaṃskāraṃ nānālakṣaṇadānasaṃbhāravicitraṃ yathāśayasattvasaṃtoṣaṇamanantatyāgavidhimanugacchan yathāśayasattvasaṃtarpaṇābhinirhāraṃ sarvavastutyāgavisarjanamavicchinnasarvajagatsaṃskāraduḥkhaparitrāṇaprayogaṃ sarvasattvapratikārāpratikāṅkṣī sarvajagatsamatāsamudāgatacetāḥ sarvajagaccittaratnaṃ pariśodhayamānaḥ sarvabuddhaikaghanakuśalamūlasamudrasaṃbhūtaṃ sarvajagadyathāśayopakaraṇavarṣaṃsaṃgrahaprayogaṃ sarvajagatsarvajñatāpuṇyasamudrevagaṃ vivardhayan praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvasattvaparipākavinayaparaṃparāviśuddhaye
body.translated_text: He, with a mind thus descended into the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are, having entered the equality of great loving-kindness toward the entire realm of beings, engaged in the effort of pervading all beings with clouds of great compassion, a <s>maṇḍala</s> of the great <s>Dharma</s>-umbrella covering all the world of beings, a great knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-weapon for penetrating the mountains of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) of all beings, with a mind augmented by the surge of satisfaction arising from the happiness of all beings, with the mind of a vow for accomplishing the ultimate happiness of all beings, with a mind raining objects upon all beings according to their dispositions and intentions, with a mind of equal effort in not abandoning any being, with a mind of satiating all beings with noble wealth, with a mind for the attainment of the supreme jewel of the knowledge of the ten powers — having attained the establishment of the power of <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledge, having pervaded the entire realm of beings, to the ultimate limit of the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, through the cloud of manifold great <s>bodhisattva</s> miraculous transformations, standing face-to-face with all beings, setting in motion the great cloud of all aspects and all objects, and raining the great cloud-rain of all jewel-ornaments — that is, for the enjoyment of all beings according to their inclinations, following the renunciation of immeasurable and boundless objects, the conduct of immeasurable provisions, the practice of giving-up various kinds of objects in manifold ways, the preparation of arrays of inexpressible kinds of provisions, variegated with the equipment of various kinds of generosity, the method of satisfying beings according to their dispositions through boundless methods of giving, the accomplishment of satisfying beings according to their dispositions, the relinquishing of all possessions, the effort of uninterrupted protection from the <s>saṃskāra</s>-suffering of all beings, expecting no return from any being, with a mind arisen from the equality toward all beings, purifying the mind-jewel of all beings, increasing the momentum of the merit-ocean of omniscience for all beings through the practice of gathering provisions of rain according to the dispositions of all beings, born from the ocean of wholesome roots of the single dense mass of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the purification of the succession of ripening and discipline of all beings without remainder at each mind-moment

body.text:
'bhinirharati sma / praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvakṣetraparaṃparānupakliṣṭānuttarabuddhakṣetrālaṃkāraviśuddhavyūhapratimaṇḍalaparipūraye praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvadharmanayasāgarakaraṇaviśuddhaye praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣākāśadhātutalaspharaṇajñānanayaparipūraye praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasattvādhyavataraṇajñānanayaviśuddhaye praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvajagadvinayajñānanayāvabhāsapratilambhāya praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvakāladharmacakrapravartanābhivartyatāyai praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvajñajñānādhiṣṭhānakauśalasaṃdarśanasarvajagadupakārībhūtatvāya praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvalokadhātusaṃkhyāpracāreṣu sarvalokadhātusamudrābhyudgateṣu sarvalokadhātusamudrasamavasaraṇeṣu nānālokadhātuprasaranirdeśeṣu nānālokadhātuvaṃśavyavasthānasaṃdhivyūheṣu nānāpratiṣṭhānānekaśarīranirdeśeṣu nānāvyūhakalpavimātratānirdeśeṣu saṃkliṣṭaviśuddhasaṃkliṣṭaikāntapariśuddhavipulamahadgatāpramāṇasaṃkṣiptasūkṣmodārasamatalavyatyastordhvamūrdhadigvidigmukhanānādiksamudrasamavasaraṇeṣu nānāmukhanirdeśāntadvārasaṃsthānavimātratāvyūheṣu
sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran bodhisattvanyāmamavakramya nānābodhisattvacaryāvikurvitaspharaṇatāyai praticittakṣaṇamanavaśeṣasarvatryadhvabuddhakāyaparasattvacittāśayavijñaptaye sarvajagatsarvajñatāpuṇyasamudravegaṃ vivardhayannaminirharanti sma //
body.translated_text: he accomplished [this]. At each mind-moment, for the fulfillment of the adornment-array-<s>maṇḍala</s> of unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-field purification unafflicted throughout the succession of all fields without remainder; at each mind-moment, for the purification of making the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmas</s> without remainder; at each mind-moment, for the fulfillment of the knowledge-method of pervading the surface of space without remainder; at each mind-moment, for the purification of the knowledge-method of descending into all beings without remainder; at each mind-moment, for the attainment of the illumination of the knowledge-method of disciplining all beings without remainder; at each mind-moment, for the unceasing turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> at all times without remainder; at each mind-moment, for becoming a benefactor of all beings without remainder through displaying the skill in the empowerment of omniscient knowledge; at each mind-moment, in the immeasurable world-realm oceans without remainder — in the emergences from all world-realm oceans, in the convergences of all world-realm oceans, in the displays of the extensions of various world-realms, in the juncture-arrays of the establishments of various world-realm lineages, in the displays of the various foundations and manifold embodiments, in the displays of the immeasurability of various array-<s>kalpas</s>, in the impure, pure, impure-pure, entirely pure, vast, great, immeasurable, contracted, subtle, sublime, equal, inverted, upward, downward, directional, intermediate-directional, and facing — in the convergences of various ocean-directions, in the arrays of the immeasurability of configurations and positions of various gateway-displays — practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct in the extensions of all world-realms, entering the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, for the pervading with the miraculous transformations of various <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts; at each mind-moment, for the manifestation to the minds of all beings of the <s>Buddha</s>-bodies of all the three times without remainder — increasing the momentum of the merit-ocean of omniscience for all beings, he accomplished [all this]. //

body.text: evaṃ hi kulaputra bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāṃ caran puṇyajñānasaṃbhāravirahite lokasaṃniveśe akṛtajñasattvaparipūrṇe ajñānatamovanaddhe ahaṃkāramamakārābhiniviṣṭe avidyāndhakāratimirāvṛte ayoniśovitarkaprasṛte dṛṣṭigahanakāntārapraskandhe hetuphalasaṃmūḍhe karmakleśavaśagate mahāsaṃsārakāntāraduḥkhapātālamadhyaprapatite vividhadāridryaduḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavati mahākaruṇāṃ saṃjanayya vipulān pāramitācaryāmeghānabhinirhṛtya kuśalamūladṛḍhapratiṣṭhānaṃ saṃvarṇayan sarvasattvānāṃ saṃsāradāridryaduḥkhaṃ vinivartayan mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāramabhirocayan hetumaṇḍaladiśamabhidyotayan karmadharmāvirodhadiśaṃ prabhāvayan buddhadharmamaṇḍalasamudāgamadiśamavabhāsayan sarvasattvādhimuktidiśaṃ prabhāsayan sarvasattvakṣetrasaṃbhavadiśaṃ saṃdarśayan sarvatathāgatavaṃśānupacchedadiśamanubadhnan sarvabuddhaśāsanadiśaṃ saṃdhārayan sarvākuśaladharmadiśaṃ vinivartayan sarvajñatāsaṃbhāradiśaṃ saṃvarṇayan sarvasattvadhātuṃ spharitvā mahāntaṃ pāramitāmeghamabhinirhṛtya yathāśayasattvasaṃtoṣaṇamatyantadharmasaṃgrahe sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / sarvajñatāsaṃbhāre samādāpayati sma / mahābodhisattvapāramitāsvavatārayāmāsa / sarvāryadhanapratilambhairupastambhayāmāsa / sarvajñatāprītivegaiḥ kuśalamūlasamudrān sattvānāṃ vivardhayāmāsa / sarvatathāgatavikurvitamukheṣu cainānavatārya atyantamupadhiśeṣasukhasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhya tathāgatamāhātmyābhimukhān kṛtvā bodhisattvasaṃgrahajñāne pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, son of good family, the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, while practicing the former <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, in a worldly domain devoid of the equipment of merit and knowledge, filled with ungrateful beings, bound in the darkness of ignorance, ensnared by ego-grasping and possessiveness, enveloped in the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), gone forth in improper mental constructions, fallen into the thicket-wilderness of views, confused about cause and effect, gone under the power of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, fallen into the abyss of the great wilderness of suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, experiencing the suffering of various kinds of poverty — generating great compassion, bringing forth vast clouds of <s>pāramitā</s>-conduct, praising the firm establishment in wholesome roots, turning back the suffering of the poverty of <s>saṃsāra</s> for all beings, inspiring the great accumulation of merit and knowledge, illuminating the direction of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of causes, manifesting the direction of the non-contradiction of <s>karma</s> and <s>dharma</s>, illuminating the direction of the accomplishment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, illuminating the direction of the dispositions of all beings, displaying the direction of the arising of the fields of all beings, following the direction of the uninterrupted lineage of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, upholding the direction of the teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>, turning back the direction of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, praising the direction of the equipment for omniscience — having pervaded the entire realm of beings, having brought forth the great cloud of <s>pāramitā</s>s, satisfying beings according to their dispositions, he established beings in the ultimate <s>Dharma</s>-gathering. He inspired them in the equipment for omniscience. He caused them to descend into the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitā</s>s. He supported them through the attainment of all noble wealth. He augmented the oceans of wholesome roots of beings through the surges of joy of omniscience. Having caused them to descend into the gateways of the miraculous transformations of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having gathered them through the ultimate gathering of residual happiness, having turned them face-to-face with the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he established them in the knowledge of <s>bodhisattva</s>-gathering. //

body.text: sudhana āha - kiyacciraṃ saṃprasthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? āha - durabhisaṃbhavaṃ kulaputra etatsthānaṃ durvijñeya duradhimocaṃ duravataraṃ duḥpravyāhāraṃ duradhigamam / na śakyaṃ sadevakena lokenāvatarituṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiśca, anyatra tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena
body.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'How long ago, goddess, did you set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening?' She replied: 'This matter, son of good family, is difficult to attain, difficult to know, difficult to resolve, difficult to descend into, difficult to express, difficult to comprehend. It cannot be descended into by the world together with its <s>devas</s>, nor by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — except through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: kalyāṇamitraparigraheṇa vipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropastabdhacittatayā āśayaviśuddhyā adīnākliṣṭāvakrānupahatāsaṃkucitānandhakāracittatayā samantāvabhāsajñānālokāvabhāsacittatayā sarvasattvahitasukhādhānapariṇatacittatayā sarvamāramaṇḍalakleśadurdharṣacittatayā sarvajñatājñānapratilambhāvakāśacittatayā sarvasaṃsārasukhānabhilāṣibhistathāgatasukhādhyālambanaiḥ sarvasattvaduḥkhadaurmanasyapraśamanapratipannaistathāgataguṇasamudrāvatārapratipattyabhimukhaiḥ sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyaptigaganagocaraiḥ udārādhimuktipathaviśuddhaiḥ saṃsārasrotovimukhaiḥ sarvatathāgatajñānasamudrābhimukhaiḥ sarvanagaragamananiścitaiḥ tathāgataviṣayākramaṇavīryaiḥ buddhabhūmigativikrāntaiḥ sarvajñatābalapariniṣpattyabhimukhaiḥ daśabalapratilambhaparyavasānaiḥ sattvaiḥ śakyametatsthānamavataritumadhimoktumudgahītumanusartuṃ vijñātum / tatkasya hetoḥ? tattathāgatajñānaviṣayaṃ hi kulaputra etatsthānamanākrāntaṃ sarvabodhisattvaiḥ / prāgeva anyaiḥ sarvasattvaiḥ / atha ca punastathāgatādhiṣṭhānena nirdekṣyāmi ājāneyānāṃ sattvānāmāśayasamyagviśuddhaye, kuśalamūlacaritānāṃ sattvānāmadhyāśayavaśitāyai, tava ca adhyāśayaparipṛcchāvyākaraṇadharmatāpravartanāpratilambhāya //
body.translated_text: by the embrace of the spiritual friend, with minds supported by vast provisions of merit and knowledge, with purity of intention, with minds that are neither depressed, nor afflicted, nor crooked, nor impaired, nor contracted, nor dark, with minds illuminated by the light of the knowledge of universal illumination, with minds directed toward the establishment of the welfare and happiness of all beings, with minds invincible against all hosts of <s>Māra</s> and afflictions, with minds open to the attainment of the knowledge of omniscience — by beings who do not long for the pleasures of <s>saṃsāra</s> but rely upon the happiness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who have set out to pacify the suffering and mental distress of all beings, who face the practice of entering the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities, whose range is the sky of contemplation of the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s, who are purified on the path of noble aspiration, who have turned away from the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who face the ocean of knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, who are resolved to go to all cities, whose vigor treads the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who stride on the path to the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, who face the perfection of the power of omniscience, whose culmination is the attainment of the ten powers — by such beings alone can this matter be entered into, believed, grasped, followed, and understood. And why? Because this matter, son of good family, is the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, untrodden by all <s>bodhisattva</s>s — how much less by other beings. Yet by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> I shall teach it — for the complete purification of the intentions of noble beings, for the mastery over the deep intentions of beings who have practiced wholesome roots, and for your attainment of the turning of the <s>dharmatā</s> that is the answer to the inquiry of your deep intention. //

body.text: atha khalu sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānā tryadhvaprāptatathāgataviṣayaṃ vyavalokya imā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s>, at that moment, to an even greater degree displaying this very meaning, having surveyed the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>s attained in the three times, spoke these verses:

children.text: gambhīru bauddho viṣayo anantā yaṃ pṛcchasi tvaṃ khalu buddhaputra /
children.translated_text: Profound is the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, infinite — what you ask, O son of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: acintiyakṣetrarajopamānaiḥ kalpairna śakyaṃ sa hi sarva vaktum // 1 //
children.translated_text: cannot be fully told even in <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of inconceivable fields. // 1 //

children.text: na lubdhasattvairna ca duṣṭacittaiḥ śakyaṃ na mohāndhatamovṛtaiśca /
children.translated_text: Not by greedy beings, nor by those of malicious mind, nor by those enveloped in the darkness of delusion,

children.text: na mrakṣamānopahatāśayaiśca vijānituṃ śānta jināna dharmatā // 2 //
children.translated_text: nor by those whose intentions are impaired by concealment and pride — can the peaceful <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Jina</s>s be known. // 2 //
Not by those who follow in the power of envy and miserliness, nor by those whose intentions are defiled by deceit and illusion,

children.text: na kleśakarmāvaraṇāvṛtaiśca śakyo hyayaṃ jānitu buddhagocara // 3 //
children.translated_text: nor by those covered by the obscurations of afflictions and <s>karma</s> — can this domain of the <s>Buddha</s> be known. // 3 //
Not by those established in the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, nor by those who rely on the view of a real self,

children.text: na dṛṣṭisaṃjñāviparītacittaiḥ śakyā iyaṃ jānitu buddhabhūmiḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: nor by those whose minds are distorted by wrong views and perceptions — can this stage of the <s>Buddha</s> be known. // 4 //

body.text: durjñeya śānto viṣayo jinānāṃ svabhāvato nirmalanirvikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: Hard to know is the peaceful domain of the <s>Jina</s>s, by its own-nature stainless and free from conceptual elaboration;

body.text: saṃsārasaktaina bhavāśritaiśca śakyaṃ samājñātumayaṃ hi dharmaḥ // 5 //
body.translated_text: by those attached to <s>saṃsāra</s>, who cling to existence — this <s>dharma</s> cannot be fully known. // 5 //

children.translated_text: Those who are born in the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-families, who are empowered by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
who bear the family-lineage of the <s>Dharma</s>-kings — for those sages, this is indeed the domain. // 6 //
Those whose minds are satisfied by the ocean of white <s>dharma</s>s, who are well-embraced by spiritual friends,

children.text: munerbalārambaṇacittameghāḥ kṣāntiṃ labhante ta idaṃ niśāmya // 7 //
children.translated_text: whose mind-clouds rest upon the power of the Sage — they attain patience upon hearing this. // 7 //
Those whose deep intentions are stainless and free from conceptual elaboration, like [the sky] in all directions of space,
whose darkness is dispelled, whose clouds are lamps of wisdom — for those stainless ones, this is the domain. // 8 //
Those who pervade the oceans of beings throughout all three times with an intention of compassion,

children.text: aśeṣasattvānugatā ca maitrī naye jinānāṃ ta ihāvatīrṇāḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: whose loving-kindness follows all beings without remainder — they have descended into the method of the <s>Jina</s>s. // 9 //

children.text: anāgrahā ye khalu hṛṣṭacittāḥ sarvāstidānābhiratāḥ sadaiva /
children.translated_text: Those who are without grasping, whose minds are joyful, who always delight in the giving of everything,
who act equally toward all beings — for those without grasping, this is the stage. // 10 //
Those whose minds are unafflicted, whose conduct is blameless, whose minds are thoroughly purified of remorse,
who are engaged in the practice of the <s>Buddha</s>'s instruction — for those stainless ones, this is the domain. // 11 //
Those whose minds are unshakable, whose minds are unwavering, whose minds are bound to the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>,
whose minds are unobstructed even in the oceans of <s>karma</s> — for those inexhaustible ones, this is the liberation. // 12 //

body.text: ye 'khinnacittā 'vinivartacittā pauruṣyavīryādhipateyayuktāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those whose minds are unwearied, whose minds never turn back, who are endowed with the sovereignty of manly vigor,

body.text: sarvajñasaṃbhāri anantavīryāsteṣāmayaṃ gocaru suvratānām // 13 //
body.translated_text: whose vigor for the provisions of omniscience is infinite — for those of excellent vows, this is the domain. // 13 //

children.translated_text: Those whose minds are peaceful and concentrated, who have attained utter peace, free from fever,
who course in the ocean of the limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> of omniscience — for those who have attained tranquility, this is the method. // 14 //
Those whose minds are freed from all attachments, whose minds have penetrated the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: gatiṃ gatā ye jinadharmadhātau prajñāpradīpāna nayeṣa teṣām // 15 //
children.translated_text: who have gone to the destination of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the <s>Jina</s>s — for those with lamps of wisdom, this is the method. // 15 //
Those whose minds have penetrated the own-nature of beings, who are without craving in the ocean of existence,
who are moons reflecting the minds of beings — for those knowers of the path, this is the liberation. // 16 //
Of those oceans of <s>Jina</s>s abiding in the three times, those born from the ocean of the lineage of vows,
who practice conduct unto the furthest limit in all fields — for those of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, this is the method. // 17 //
Those who, by the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, have descended into all the oceans of beings,
through all <s>kalpa</s>s of formation and dissolution — for those beyond reckoning, this is the liberation. // 18 //
Those who see <s>Buddha</s>s, equal in number to the atoms of fields in all directions, at the roots of the king of trees,

children.text: vibuddhya bodhiṃ vinayanta sarvān asaṅganetrāna nayeṣa teṣām // 19 //
children.translated_text: awakening to <s>Bodhi</s> and disciplining all — for those with unattached eyes, this is the method. // 19 //
You have come through the great ocean of <s>kalpa</s>s, attending upon spiritual friends,

children.text: dharmārthiko dharmagaveṣyakhinnaḥ śrutvā ca taṃ dhārayituṃ samarthaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, unwearied in searching for the <s>Dharma</s> — and having heard, you are able to retain it. // 20 //
For the purification of your intention, by the inconceivable power of the Sage's empowerment,
the immeasurable domain of <s>Vairocana</s> proceeds from my words, unattached. // 21 //

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani lokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa parataraṃ maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocano nāma lokadhātusamudro 'bhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ kulaputra maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocanalokadhātusamudre jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorājo nāma tathāgato 'bhūt / tena khalu punaḥ kulaputra jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorājonāmnā tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sa maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocano lokadhātusamudraḥ pariśodhitaḥ / tasmin lokadhātusamudre pṛthivīparvataparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuprasaranirdeśaḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca lokadhātuprasare lokadhātuvaṃśaparamāṇurajaḥsamā lokadhātunirdeśāḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca lokavaṃśe lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ kalpasaṃkhyānirdeśāḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca kalpe 'neke 'nantarakalpanirdeśāḥ / ekaikasmiṃścānantarakalpe 'nekalokadhātunānākaraṇanirdeśāḥ / tathāgatotpādā vividhavikurvitanirdeśāḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca tathāgatotpāde lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ sūtrāntasaṃprakāśanirdeśāḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca sūtrānte lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvavyākaraṇanirdeśāḥ anantamadhyasattvavinayanirdeśā nānāyānanayaiḥ pravartitā nānāvikurvitaprātihāryavinayatāḥ //
body.translated_text: In the past, son of good family, in a former time, beyond <s>kalpa</s>s equal in number to the atoms of oceans of world-realms, there was an ocean of world-realms called <s>Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana</s>. In that ocean of world-realms, son of good family, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorāja</s>. By that <s>Tathāgata</s>, son of good family, while formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, that ocean of world-realms <s>Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana</s> had been purified. In that ocean of world-realms, the teaching of the extent of world-realms is equal to the atoms of the earth-mountains. In each extent of world-realms, the teachings of world-realms in the successions of world-realms are equal to the atoms of those world-realms. In each succession of worlds, the enumeration of <s>kalpa</s>s is equal to the atoms of those world-realms. In each <s>kalpa</s>, there are many intermediate <s>kalpa</s> teachings. In each intermediate <s>kalpa</s>, there are teachings of the various transformations of many world-realms — the arisings of <s>Tathāgata</s>s with their various transformation-teachings. In each arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, the exposition of <s>sūtra</s>s is equal to the atoms of world-realms. In each <s>sūtra</s>, the predictions of <s>bodhisattva</s>s are equal to the atoms of world-realms — teachings of the discipline of beings without end or middle, set in motion through various methods of vehicles, disciplines through various miracles and transformations. //

body.text: tasmin khalu punarmaṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocane lokadhātusamudre samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūho nāma madhyamo lokadhātuvaṃśo 'bhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ kulaputra samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūhe madhyame lokadhātuvaṃśe sarvaratnavarṇasamantaprabhāsaśrīrnāma lokadhāturabhūt / sarvatathāgatabodhimaṇḍapratibhāsamaṇirājo lokadhātusaṃdhivyūhaḥ sarvaratnakusumasāgarapratiṣṭhitaḥ sarvatathāgatanirmāṇanirbhāsanidarśanamaṇirājaśarīro devanagarasaṃsthāno viśuddhasaṃkliṣṭaḥ / tasmin punarlokadhātau sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamāścāturdvīpakā lokadhātavo 'bhūvan / teṣāṃ ca sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ cāturdvīpakānāṃ sarvaratnaśikharadhvajo nāma madhyamaścāturdvīpako 'bhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ sarvaratnaśikharadhvaje cāturdvīpake lokadhātau aprameyayojanaśatasahasrāyāmavistārāścatvāro dvīpā abhūvan / ekaikasmiṃśca dvīpake daśa mahānagarasahasrāṇyabhūvan / tasmiṃśca khalu punaḥ cāturdvīpake jambudvīpakasya madhye ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā nāma rājadhānyabhūddaśanagarasahasraparivārā / tasmin khalu punarjambudvīpe daśa varṣasahasrāṇi manuṣyāṇāmāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt / tasyāṃ khalu punā ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo nāma rājābhūccakravartī / rājñaḥ khalu punaḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya pañcāmātyaśatānyabhūvan / ṣaṣṭiḥ strīsahasrāṇyantaḥpuramabhūt / sapta putraśatānyabhūvan sarveṣāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ sudarśanānāṃ mahātejasāṃ mahābalānām / tasya khalu punaḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājñaḥ sarvo jambudvīpa ekacchatro 'bhūnnihataparacakrapratyarthikaḥ //
body.translated_text: In that ocean of world-realms <s>Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana</s>, there was a middle succession of world-realms called <s>Samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūha</s>. In that middle succession of world-realms, son of good family, there was a world-realm called <s>Sarvaratnavarṇasamantaprabhāsaśrī</s> — its world-realm joint-array was a gem-king reflecting the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, established in an ocean of flowers of all gem-jewels, with a body of gem-kings displaying the emanation-reflections of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, of the shape of a divine city, purified and undefiled. In that world-realm there were four-continent worlds equal in number to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>. Among those four-continent worlds equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, the middle one was called <s>Sarvaratnaśikharadhvaja</s>. In that four-continent world-realm there were four continents of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>yojana</s>s in length and breadth. In each continent there were ten thousand great cities. In the middle of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> of that four-continent world there was a royal capital called <s>Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā</s>, surrounded by ten thousand cities. In that <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the lifespan of humans was ten thousand years. In that royal capital <s>Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā</s>, there was a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch) named <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>. That king had five hundred ministers. His inner palace had sixty thousand women. He had seven hundred sons — all of them heroes, champions, of fine limbs and form, handsome, of great splendor and great strength. That king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> held all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> under a single umbrella, having defeated enemy forces and rivals. //

body.text: tena ca samayena lokadhātāvantarakalpakṣaye pratyupasthite pañcasu kaṣāyeṣu loke prādurbhūteṣu daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣvantarhiteṣu daśākuśalakarmapathavartinaḥ sattvā yadbhūyasā durgatigāmino 'bhūvan / te daśākuśalakarmapathasamādānahetoḥ parīttāyuṣo 'bhūvan alpabhogā virūpā vivarṇā duḥsaṃsthitaśarīrā alpasukhasamudācārā duḥkhavedanāsamudācārabahulā anyonyavisaṃvādavacanaśīlā anyonyabhedapratipannāḥ paruṣavacanasamudācārāḥ prakīrṇavacaso viṣayalobhābhibhūtāḥ praduṣṭamanaḥsaṃkalpā vividhadṛṣṭigahanakāntārapraviṣṭāḥ / teṣāmadharmarāgaraktānāṃ viṣamalobhābhibhūtānāṃ mithyādharmaparigatānāṃ na devaḥ kāle vāridhārā udasṛjat yena pṛthivyāṃ bījagrāmāḥ sasyagrāmā viroheyuḥ //
body.translated_text: At that time, as the intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of destruction was approaching in that world-realm, the five degenerations (<s>kaṣāya</s>s) had appeared in the world, the ten wholesome courses of action had disappeared, and beings following the ten unwholesome courses of action had for the most part become destined for bad rebirths. Due to their undertaking of the ten unwholesome courses of action, they had short lifespans, few possessions, were ugly, discolored, with misshapen bodies, with little experience of happiness, with predominantly painful sensations, habituated to speech of mutual deception, disposed toward mutual discord, given to harsh words, with scattered speech, overpowered by craving for sense-objects, with malicious mental intentions, having entered the dense thicket of various wrong views. For those who were inflamed with unlawful desire, overpowered by uneven greed, possessed of wrong <s>dharma</s>, the gods did not release streams of rain in due season, by which seed-crops and grain-crops on the earth might grow. //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ sattvāḥ śuṣkeṣu tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanodyānadrumeṣu nānāvyādhispṛṣṭā digvidiśo vidhāvanti sma aparāyaṇāḥ / te samāgamya sarva eva yena ratnasālavyūhameghapradīparājadhānī tenopasaṃkramya tāṃ samantādanuparivārya kecidūrdhvabāhavaḥ, kecitkṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ, kecit saṃkampitaśarīrāḥ, kecidabhyudgatāṅgāḥ, kecidadhomukhaṃ prapatitāḥ, kecitsarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatitāḥ, keciddharaṇitalajānupratiṣṭhitāḥ, kecidgaganatalābhinatabāhavaḥ, kecinnagnā nirvasanāḥ, kecidvikṛtavadananayanāḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño 'bhimukhaṃ mahāntamārtasvaramutkrośamakārṣuḥ - upadrutāḥ sma / devāpasṛṣṭāḥ sma / kṣutpipāsāduḥkhaprapīḍitāḥ sma / vividhabhayopataptāḥ sma / trāṇavirahitāḥ sma / deva aśaraṇā aparāyaṇāḥ sma / duḥkhapañjaragatāḥ sma jīvitoparodhaprāptā maraṇābhimukhāḥ / iti nānāvidhān pralāpān pralapanto nānāsvarāṅgairnānāvacanairnānāvikṛtavaktranayanā vividhasaṃjñāvacanavyāhāranimantrapadairnānārthasūcakavacanapadairutkrośamakārṣuḥ / ye ca tasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāḥ kṣutpipāsāprapīḍitā nirābharaṇagātrā nagnanirvasanā duṣṭavivarṇā rūkṣaparuṣagātrā duḥkhitā durmanaso 'nāttamanaskāḥ, te cāpi sattvā duḥkhānabhilāṣiṇo duḥkhabhayanirviṇṇāḥ / te sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaṃ rājānaṃ mahājñānapuruṣaṃ pratiśaraṇabhūtaṃ śaraṇamupāgatāḥ sarvasukhapratilambhasaṃjñayā sarvapriyasamavadhānapratilambhasaṃjñayā jīvitāśāparigatanidhānapratilambhasaṃjñayā tīrthasaṃdarśanasaṃjñayā mahāpathapratipattisaṃjñayā mahāyānapātrasaṃjñayā mahājñānaratnadvīpasaṃjñayā mahārthapratilambhasaṃjñayā svargasarvaratisukhapratilambhasaṃjñayā //
body.translated_text: Then indeed, those beings — with grasses, shrubs, herbs, forests, gardens, and trees dried up, afflicted by various diseases — ran in all directions without refuge. They all gathered together and approached the royal capital <s>Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpa</s>, surrounding it on all sides. Some with arms raised upward, some with palms joined together, some with bodies trembling, some with limbs outstretched, some fallen face-down, some prostrated with their entire bodies, some with knees set upon the ground, some with arms bowed toward the sky, some naked and unclothed, some with distorted faces and eyes — they raised a great cry of anguish before King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>: 'We are afflicted! We are abandoned by the gods! We are oppressed by the suffering of hunger and thirst! We are tormented by manifold fears! We are bereft of protection! O lord, we are without shelter, without refuge! We are trapped in a cage of suffering, our lives obstructed, facing death!' Thus lamenting with various kinds of lamentations, with diverse voices and gestures, with diverse words, with distorted faces and eyes, with various signals and utterances and invocations, with words indicating various meanings, they raised their cry. And the women, men, boys, and girls in that royal capital — oppressed by hunger and thirst, their bodies devoid of ornaments, naked and unclothed, wretched and discolored, with rough and coarse bodies, miserable, despondent, and dejected — those beings too, not desiring suffering, were distressed by the fear of suffering. They approached King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, a man of great knowledge, who had become their refuge, seeking refuge with the perception of obtaining all happiness, with the perception of obtaining the fulfillment of all that is dear, with the perception of obtaining a treasure encompassed by the hope of life, with the perception of seeing a holy crossing, with the perception of entering upon the great path, with the perception of being a vessel of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), with the perception of an island of the jewel of great knowledge, with the perception of obtaining great benefit, with the perception of obtaining heavenly bliss and all delight.

body.text: aśrauṣīdrājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaḥ tasya mahataḥ samantādyācanakasamūhasya taṃ mahāntamārtasvaramutkrośanaśabdam / śrutvā ca asya daśa mahākaruṇāmukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyavakrāman / sa mahākaruṇānayacetanānidhyapticitto muhūrtamekāgratāmanubhūya daśa mahākaruṇopasaṃhitāni vacanapadānyudīrayāmāsa / katamāni daśa? aho bata anālambanāḥ sattvā mahāsaṃsāraprapātaprapatitāḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ saṃsāramahāprapātaprapatitānāṃ sattvānāṃ layanabhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ tathāgatalayanabhūmipratiṣṭhāpanatayā / aho bata atrāṇāḥ sattvā nānākleśopadravopadrutāḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ vividhakleśabhayopadrutānāṃ sattvānāmatrāṇānāṃ
body.translated_text: King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> heard that great sound of anguished crying from the multitude of supplicants gathered all around. And upon hearing it, innumerable hundreds of thousands of aspects of his ten great compassions arose. With a mind intent upon the disposition of the conduct of great compassion, having experienced one-pointed concentration for a moment, he uttered ten words accompanied by great compassion. What are the ten? 'Alas, beings without support have fallen into the great precipice of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)! When will it come to pass that we shall become a place of rest for beings who have fallen into the great precipice of <s>saṃsāra</s>, by establishing them on the ground of rest of a <s>Tathāgata</s>? Alas, beings without protection are afflicted by the attacks of various <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements)! When will it come to pass that we, for beings without protection who are afflicted by the attacks of various defilements, shall become

body.text: trāṇabhūtā bhaviṣyāmo 'navadyakarmāntapratiṣṭhāpanatayā / aho bata aśaraṇāḥ sattvā loke jarāmaraṇabhayāviṣṭāḥ / katā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayamaśaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ śaraṇabhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasaṃsārabhayavinivartanatayā / aho bata aparāyaṇāḥ sattvā vividhalokabhayopadrutāḥ / katā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ vividhalokabhayopadrutānāmaparāyaṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmo 'tyantayogakṣeme sarvajñatāmārge pratiṣṭhāpanatayā / aho bata avidyāndhakāraprāptaḥ sarvalokovimatisaṃśayatimirāvṛtaḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayamulkābhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasattvānāmavidyāndhakāravidhamanatayā / aho bata ālokavirahitāḥ sattvāḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ mahājñānālokakarā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ vitimirajñānamukhasaṃdarśanatayā / aho bata jñānajyotirvirahitaḥ sarvasattvadhāturīrṣyāmātsaryamāyāśāṭhyakāluṣāśayaḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayamanuttarajñānapradyotakarā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasattvānāmatyantapariśuddhipratipratiṣṭhāpanatayā / aho bata nāyakavirahitaḥ sarvaloko mahāsaṃsārasāgaraviṣamasrotaḥprapannaḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ nāyakabhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ karmasamudranayāvataraṇatayā / aho bata vināyakavirahitaḥ sarvaloko durvinītaḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ vināyakabhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvākāraparipākavinayatathāgatādhiṣṭhānakālānatikramaṇena / aho bata apariṇāyakaḥ sarvaloko jātyandhabhūtaḥ / kadā tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ pariṇāyakabhūtā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvaṃsattvānāmanāvaraṇasarvajñajñānanayāvataraṇatayā //
body.translated_text: a protection, by establishing them in blameless conduct? Alas, beings without shelter are seized by the fear of old age and death in the world! When will it come to pass that we shall become a shelter for beings without shelter, by turning back the fear of all <s>saṃsāra</s>? Alas, beings without refuge are afflicted by the fears of various worlds! When will it come to pass that we shall become a refuge for beings without refuge who are afflicted by the fears of various worlds, by establishing them on the path of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) in absolute safety? Alas, the entire world has fallen into the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), covered by the gloom of doubt and wrong views! When will it come to pass that we shall become torchbearers, by dispelling the darkness of ignorance for all beings? Alas, beings are deprived of light! When will it come to pass that we shall become makers of the great light of knowledge, by showing all beings the face of knowledge free from darkness? Alas, the entire realm of beings is devoid of the light of knowledge, its dispositions tainted by envy, jealousy, deceit, fraud, and impurity! When will it come to pass that we shall become producers of the radiance of unsurpassed knowledge, by establishing all beings in absolute purity? Alas, the entire world is without a leader, having entered the treacherous currents of the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>! When will it come to pass that we shall become leaders for all beings, by navigating the ocean of <s>karma</s> (action)? Alas, the entire world is without a guide, undisciplined! When will it come to pass that we shall become guides for all beings, by ripening and disciplining them in every way, without letting the appointed time of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment pass? Alas, the entire world is without a conductor, born blind! When will it come to pass that we shall become conductors for all beings, by leading them into the unobstructed knowledge of omniscience?

body.text: sa imāni daśa mahākaruṇopasaṃhitāni vacanapadānyudīrya tasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇamakārṣīt / mahātyāgadundubhinirghoṣaṃ ca akārayat - sarvajagat saṃtarpayiṣyāmaḥ, yasya yenārthastasmai tadanupradāsyāma iti / tena sarvajambudvīpe sarvarājadhānīṣu sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadapattaneṣu sarvopakaraṇakośā vivṛtāḥ / sarvaśṛṅgāṭakarathyācatvareṣu vividhopakaraṇavidhayaḥ sthāpitāḥ / sarvajagadupajīvyāḥ suprativihitāḥ / sarvakośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi vivṛtāni / mahāratnanidhānanicayā nidarśitāḥ / anekanānāvidharatnarāśayaḥ sthāpitāḥ / annapānavastrayānapuṣpamālyagandhavilepanacūrṇanānāgandhavarṇacīvararatnakośā vivṛtāḥ / śayanāsanavasanabhavanavimānagṛhāṇyalaṃkṛtāni sarvadhanakanakasamṛddhāni jyotirdhvajamāṇirājavinyāsavidhūtāndhakārāṇi / sa teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ yathābhilaṣitasarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇārthaṃ teṣu gṛheṣu pratyekamātmabhāvasadṛśamupādāya kāyamabhinirmāya sthāpayāmāsa / sarvasattvasarvavyādhipraśamanāya ca vaidyabhaiṣajyopasthāyakavividhajīvitopakaraṇapratyayasaṃpadamupasthāpayāmāsa / yathārhavividhopakaraṇapūrṇāni ca nānāratnavicitrabhājanānyupasthāpayāmāsa - yaduta vajramaṇibhājanāni nānāgandhamaṇiratnaparipūrṇāni, nānāgandharatnabhājanāni vividhodāravicitravarṇaraṅgavastraparipūrṇāni, yānayugyāni subahūni nānākārasaṃsthānāni vicitraratnapratimaṇḍitāni ājāneyāśvagajagoyuktāni / vividhāṃśca rathān rājārhān sarvaratnābharaṇaparibhogāṃśca sarvāsanavidhīṃśca nānāratnavicitrān vividhavitānavitatān
body.translated_text: Having uttered these ten words accompanied by great compassion, he caused bells to be sounded in proclamation throughout that royal capital. And he had the drum of the great gift resound: 'We shall satisfy the entire world; whatever anyone needs, that we shall bestow upon them.' Thereupon, throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in all royal capitals, in all villages, towns, market-towns, districts, and cities, all treasuries of provisions were opened. At all crossroads, thoroughfares, and squares, various kinds of provisions were arranged. Everything was well-prepared for the sustenance of the entire world. All treasuries and granaries were opened. Great heaps of jewel-treasures were displayed. Numerous and diverse piles of gems were set forth. Storehouses of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, flowers, garlands, fragrances, unguents, powders, various perfumes, colored robes, and jewels were opened. Bedchambers, seats, garments, dwellings, mansions, and houses were adorned, replete with all wealth and gold, their darkness dispelled by arrays of luminous banners and jewel-kings. For the purpose of fulfilling all the wishes and intentions of those beings, in each of those houses he fashioned and placed an emanated body resembling his own form. And for the alleviation of all diseases of all beings, he provided physicians, medicines, attendants, and the resources of various means of sustaining life. And he arranged vessels filled with various provisions as appropriate, adorned with diverse gems — namely, <s>vajra</s>-jewel vessels filled with various fragrant gem-treasures, vessels of fragrant jewels filled with diverse excellent and variegated colored fabrics, and very many yoked vehicles of various shapes and forms, adorned with variegated gems, yoked with thoroughbred horses, elephants, and oxen. And various royal chariots, and enjoyments of all jewel-ornaments, and all manner of seats variegated with diverse gems, spread with diverse canopies,

body.text: ratnakiṅkiṇījālāvanaddhān ucchritacchatradhvajapatākopaśobhitān sarvajanapadapradeśeṣu sthāpayāpāsa / grāmanagaranigamajanapadapradānāni coddhoṣayāmāsa / nānāvidhodyānaramyārāmatapovanaparibhogānapi sarvagṛhakalatraputradārakaparityāgānapi anardhyasarvaratnaparityāgānapi svahṛdayamajjāntraguṇavṛkkamedamāṃsarudhiracchavicarmakaracaraṇabāhukarṇanāsānayanajihvādantoṣṭhaśīrṣaparityāgānapi yāvatsarvabāhyādhyātmikasarvākāraparityāgānapyuddhoṣayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: hung with nets of jeweled bells, adorned with raised parasols, banners, and pennants — he placed throughout all the districts and regions of the land. And he proclaimed gifts of villages, towns, market-towns, and districts. He also proclaimed the enjoyment of various delightful gardens, groves, and ascetic forests, and also the relinquishment of all households, wives, and children, and also the relinquishment of all priceless jewels, and also the relinquishment of one's own heart, marrow, entrails, sinews, kidneys, fat, flesh, blood, skin, hide, hands, feet, arms, ears, nose, eyes, tongue, teeth, lips, and head — even the relinquishment of all external and internal possessions of every kind.

body.text:
sa tamevaṃrūpamupakaraṇaparityāgavidhiṃ pratyupasthāpya mahāyajñavāṭaṃ kārayāmāsa, yastasyā ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpāyā rājadhānyāḥ pūrveṇa maṇiśikharatejonāmno nagaradvārasya purataḥ samavipulāyāmaḥ paramavistīrṇadharaṇītalapraveśo nimnonnataviśuddhasamatalo 'pagataśvabhraprapātaḥ sarvasthāṇukaṇṭakāpagataḥ utsannaśarkarākaṭhallaḥ sarvaratnadhātusaṃcayaḥ sarvaratnamayamaṇiratnarājasaṃstīrṇatalaḥ anekamaṇiratnavyuhopaśobhito nānāratnakusumābhikīrṇaḥ sarvacūrṇasugandharājasamākulaḥ sarvagandhadhūpaparidhūpito ratnārciḥpradīpaḥ tejaḥśrīsarvagandhadhūpapaṭalameghagaganasaṃchāditālaṃkāraḥ sarvaratnadrumapaṅktisuvibhaktopaśobhito nānābhavanavimānakūṭāgārasamalaṃkṛtaḥ ucchritacchatradhvajapatāko nānāratnapaṭṭapralambavidyotito vividharatnakusumajālasaṃchannaḥ sarvagandharājaratnajālacchatramaṇḍalaḥ suvarṇajālaratnaghaṇṭānirghoṣo nānāratnavirājitavitānavitataḥ sarvagandharājacūrṇavikīrṇaḥ sarvaratnakusumaprakīrṇābhirāmaḥ tūryakoṭīniyutaśatasahasramanojñarutaghoṣanirnāditaḥ sarvaratnavicitrālaṃkāravyūhasupariśuddho bodhisattvakarmavipākābhinirvṛttaḥ / tasya madhye mahāsiṃhāsanamabhinirvṛttaṃ daśaratnanicitavicitrabhūmitalasaṃsthānaṃ daśaratnanānāvedikāparivāravirājitaṃ daśamaṇidrumaśākhāvedikāntarasuvibhaktopaśobhitavyūham abhedyavajracakradharaṇītalasupratiṣṭhitapādaṃ sarvaratnabimbavigrahasaṃdhāritāsanacakram, anekaratnamayaniryūhaśatālaṃkṛtaṃ nānāratnabhaktivicitravyūhapratimaṇḍitaṃ samantasuvibhaktaratnadhvajasamucchritaṃ nānāratnapatākāpralambitavicitravyūhaṃ ratnakiṅkiṇījālapariṣkṛtaṃ nānādivyamaṇivicitrahemajālavitataṃ vividharatnakusumajālamahāmaṇirājajālavicitravastraratnajālayathārhasaṃchāditopaśobhitavyūhaṃ anekagandhamaṇivigrahapāṇimaṇḍalagandhameghapramuktamacintyavarṇagandhamaṇirājavistṛtamanojñanānāsaṃsthānasarvagandhapaṭalameghapramuktaṃ sarvadivyagandhadhūpapradhūpitopacāraṃ divyātirekasukhasaṃsparśānekavarṇamaṇiratnavastraprajñaptamanekadivyatūryasaṃgītiśatasahasraṃ samantāt saṃpravāditamanojñamadhuranirghoṣaṃ
nānāratnasopānapaṅktipatākāsuvibhaktavedikāpratimaṇḍitavyūhamanekamaṇiratnapratyarpitavividhavikurvitamaṇibimbavigrahavidyotitaprabhāsam yatra sa rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgato viśuddhamahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdho vairocanamaṇiratnanirbhāsakeśamakuṭaḥ abhedyanārāyaṇavajrasaṃhananakāyo gūḍhadṛḍhapārśvanibaddhasaṃdhiḥ sarvāṅgaparipūrṇaḥ samantabhadraḥ samantaprāsādikaḥ samantaśobhanaḥ sarvākāravaropeto mahādharmarājakaroditaḥ sarvapariṣkāravaśitāpratilabdho dharmavaśitāsuviśuddhaḥ svacittavaśavartī apratihatavacanamaṇḍalaḥ akopyajñānasamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: Having prepared such a method of renouncing provisions, he had a great sacrificial ground (<s>mahāyajñavāṭa</s>) constructed, which was to the east of that royal city called <s>Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā</s>, in front of the city gate named <s>Maṇiśikharateja</s>, of even and extensive length, with supremely vast ground surface, with level ground purified of unevenness, free from chasms and precipices, cleared of all stumps and thorns, free from gravel and pebbles, an accumulation of all jewel-ores, with its ground spread with king-gems made of all jewels, adorned with arrays of many jewel-gems, strewn with various jewel-flowers, filled with all the finest fragrant powders, perfumed with all incense, illuminated by jewel-flame lamps, with ornaments canopied by clouds of radiance and splendor and all fragrant incense spreading across the sky, beautified by well-arranged rows of all jewel-trees, decorated with various mansions, palaces, and pinnacled dwellings, with raised parasols, banners, and flags, brilliant with hanging silk-banners of various jewels, covered with nets of diverse jewel-flowers, canopied with circles of nets of jewels of the king of all fragrances, resounding with golden nets and jewel-bells, spread with canopies shining with various jewels, strewn with powder of the king of all fragrances, delightful with scattered flowers of all jewels, resounding with the pleasant and beautiful sounds of tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of musical instruments, supremely pure with arrays of variegated ornaments of all jewels, produced by the ripening of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s actions. In its midst was established a great lion-throne (<s>mahāsiṃhāsana</s>), resting on a ground-surface variegated with ten kinds of jewels, resplendent with surrounding balustrades of ten kinds of jewels, beautifully adorned with arrays well-arranged between the branches and balustrades of trees of ten kinds of gems, with feet firmly established on indestructible <s>vajra</s>-wheel ground, with seat-wheels supported by images made of all jewels, adorned with hundreds of projections made of many jewels, decorated with arrays variegated with designs of various jewels, with well-arranged jewel-banners raised on all sides, with variegated arrays hanging with flags of various jewels, adorned with nets of jewel-bells, spread with nets of golden filigree variegated with various divine gems, with arrays beautifully canopied as befitting with nets of diverse jewel-flowers, nets of great king-gems, nets of variegated cloth-jewels, emitting clouds of fragrance from hand-circles of bodies of many fragrance-gems, releasing clouds of all fragrance of pleasant and various forms spread with inconceivable colored fragrance-gem-kings, with offerings perfumed with all divine incense, furnished with coverings of jewel-cloths of many-colored gem-jewels with a touch of divine and surpassing happiness,

body.text: supratiṣṭhāpitadharmaṃsamyakprayogo 'nantaguṇavarṇanirdeśaḥ / tasya khalu punaḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño mahāsiṃhāsananiṣaṇṇasyopari mūrdhasaṃdhāvantarikṣe mahācchatramaṇḍalaṃ prādurbabhūva vicitrodviddhamaṇiratnadaṇḍaṃ mahāmahāmaṇikośagarbhaṃsarvaratnaśalākāśatasahasrasamyagvitatamanekārciḥśrītejojjvalitavyūhaṃ jāmbūnadakanakaprabhāsvaraviśuddhacchadanaṃ nānāratnabhakticitrahemajālātyantavyūhacchadanopetaṃ vividhamuktāhārābhipralambitaṃ samantānnānāratnajālasaṃchāditaṃ ratnakiṅkiṇījālasuvarṇamaṇighaṇṭāratnasūtradāmopanibaddhābhipralambitaṃ mahāmaṇiratnahārasamantābhipralambitavyūhaṃ divyamadhuramanojñapramuktaśabdopacāraṃ sarvasattvakuśalakarmapathasaṃcodanaghaṇṭāvisṛtanirghoṣam / sa khalu rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo ratnavālavyajanaiḥ saṃvījyamānaḥ śakradevendrātirekeṇa tejasā jvālayannupaśobhate sma / tasya samanantaraniṣaṇṇasya tasmin siṃhāsane sarvo janakāyo 'bhimukhaḥ prāñjaliḥ sthito 'bhūttameva rājānaṃ namasyan //
body.translated_text: one whose practice was well-established in <s>Dharma</s>, whose exposition described infinite qualities. Above the head of that king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, who was seated on the great lion-throne, in the space above his crown, a great parasol-circle appeared, with a shaft studded with variegated gem-jewels, with a core of a great treasury of supreme gems, well-spread with a hundred thousand spokes of all jewel-rods, with arrays blazing with the splendor and radiance of many flames, with a covering bright and pure as the radiance of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, furnished with canopies of utterly elaborate designs of golden nets of various jewels, hung with pendants of diverse pearl-garlands, covered on all sides with nets of various jewels, bound and suspended with strings of jewel-threads and golden gem-bells in nets of jewel-bells, with arrays of great gem-jewel garlands hanging all around, with offerings of sweet and pleasing divine sounds emanating, resounding with the sound of bells that urge all beings onto the path of wholesome action. That king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, being fanned with jewel-handled fly-whisks, shone resplendently with a radiance surpassing that of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. As soon as he was seated on that lion-throne, all the people stood facing him, with palms joined, paying homage to that very king.

body.text: atha khalu sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño 'saṃkhyeyeṣu prāṇikoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu nānāyācanakeṣu nānāvastuparigrāhakeṣu nānopakaraṇādhimukteṣu nānājātiṣu nānāgatiparyāpanneṣu nānābhilāṣacitteṣu nānāśayābhiprāyeṣu nānādiksaṃnipatiteṣu nānāviṣayaparibhogopacāreṣu nānāparibhogābhilāṣitacetaneṣu nānābhiprāyakalpeṣu nānāmanuṣyanikāyeṣu nānākulopapatyupapanneṣu nānājanapadasamāgateṣu nānaniruktivacanamantrasaṃskāreṣu nānāsvaramaṇḍalapramocakeṣu nānavastuvyañjaneṣu nānāvacanapadānyudīrayatsu, tamekaṃ mahāpuṇyasumerumullokayamāneṣu ayamevaiko mahājñānapuruṣa iti niścitacetaneṣu, mahāpuṇyopastabdho mahāpuruṣacandro mahātyāgāśayapratilabdha ityunmukheṣu, bodhisattvapraṇidhicetanānipatiteṣu bodhisattvapraṇidhicetanānirmiteṣu taṃ mahāntaṃ yācanakasaṃnipātaṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ yācanakānāmantike 'bhūccittaprema cittaprītiḥ cittaprasādaḥ / kalyāṇamitradarśanasaṃjñā suvipulā mahākaruṇavegāḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ / aparāntakalpasarvayācanakasaṃtarpaṇāvivartyavīryavegāḥ prādurabhavan / sarvajagatsamaprayogaparityāgacittaspharaṇameghāḥ samabhavan //
body.translated_text: Then, when innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of beings had assembled before King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> — supplicants of various kinds, acceptors of various goods, devoted to various provisions, of various births, belonging to various destinies, with minds of various desires, of various dispositions and intentions, assembled from various directions, accustomed to the enjoyment of various sense-objects, with minds longing for the enjoyment of various things, of various intentions and imaginations, belonging to various classes of humans, born into various families, come from various countries, endowed with various linguistic conventions and grammatical formations, releasing various vocal expressions, indicating various objects through words, uttering various verbal phrases — gazing upon that one great <s>Sumeru</s> of merit, with minds certain that 'This alone is a great being of wisdom,' standing with upturned faces thinking 'He is supported by great merit, he is a moon among great beings, he has attained the disposition of great generosity' — those who had fallen into the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vow-intention, those who were fashioned by the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vow-intention — seeing that great assembly of supplicants, there arose in him love of heart, joy of heart, and serenity of heart toward those supplicants. Vast surges of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) arose. Surges of indefatigable energy to satisfy all supplicants until the end of future <s>kalpas</s> appeared. Clouds of mind-expansion of equal and universal renunciation for the benefit of all the world arose.

body.text: sa khalu punaḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo rājā teṣāṃ yācanakānāṃ sahadarśanena āttamanaskataro 'bhūt na trisāhasracakravartirājyapratilambhena asīmāprāptakalpaparyavasānena, na śakratvādhipatyāsanapratilambhena bahukalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparyavasānena, na suyāmadevarājādhipatyāsanapratilambhena bahukalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparyavasānena, na saṃtuṣitadevarājādhipatyāsanapratilambhena bahukalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparyavasānena, na sunirmitadevarājaiśvaryādhipatyāsanapratilambhena aprameyakalpāvasānena, na vaśavartidevarājādhipatyāsanapratilambhena, sumukhāpsaramanoharadevakanyopasthānena acintyakalpaparyavasānena, na brahmāsanenānabhilāpyakalpabrahmavihārasukhāvasānena, na ābhāsvaradevasukhena anantakalpāvasānena, na śubhakṛtsnadevasukhena atulyakalpākṣīṇena, na śuddhāvāsadevaśāntavimokṣasukhavihāreṇa aparyantakalpāvasānena / tadyathā kulaputra puruṣasyaikāntatṛṣṇācaritasya matāpitṛbhrātṛbhaginīmitramātyajñātisālohitaputraduhitṛbhāryācirakālaviprayuktasya
body.translated_text: That king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> was more delighted by the mere sight of those supplicants than by obtaining the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s> over the three-thousandfold world-system lasting until the end of a boundless <s>kalpa</s>, or by obtaining the throne of lordship of <s>Śakra</s> lasting for many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or by obtaining the throne of lordship as king of the <s>Suyāma</s> gods lasting for many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or by obtaining the throne of lordship as king of the <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (Tuṣita) gods lasting for many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or by obtaining the throne of sovereignty and lordship as king of the <s>Sunirmita</s> gods lasting for immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, or by obtaining the throne of lordship as king of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods attended by the captivating divine maidens <s>Sumukhāpsaras</s> lasting for inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>, or by the seat of <s>Brahmā</s> with the happiness of <s>brahmavihāra</s> (divine abiding) lasting for inexpressible <s>kalpas</s>, or by the happiness of the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods lasting for infinite <s>kalpas</s>, or by the happiness of the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods lasting for incomparable and inexhaustible <s>kalpas</s>, or by the peaceful liberation-happiness of dwelling among the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods lasting for boundless <s>kalpas</s>. O son of good family, just as a man of exclusively craving disposition who has been long separated from his parents, brothers, sisters, friends, ministers, relatives, kinsmen, sons, daughters, and wife,

body.text:
aṭavīkāntāravipranaṣṭasya taddarśanakāmasya teṣāṃ samavadhānena mahatī prītiradhyavasānamutpadyate taddarśanāvitṛptatayā, evameva kulaputra rājñaḥ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya teṣāṃ yācanakānāṃ sahadarśanena mahāprītivegāḥ saṃjātāḥ / cittatuṣṭisukhamavakrāntam / mahāṃścittodagratāvegaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / mahāprābhodyaharṣavegaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ / buddhabodhādudāraśraddhādhimuktivegabalaṃ saṃvardhitam / mūlajātā śraddhā sarvajñatāyāṃ vivardhitā / sarvabuddhadharmādhyāśayaviśuddhibalamabhivivardhitam / bodhisattvendriyakarmaṇyatā saṃbhūtā / cittaharṣaparipūrṇamahāprasādavega udapadyata / vipulacittaudbilyavegena kalyāṇamitrendriyāśayatā mṛdubhūtā / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasya sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājñaḥ sarvajñatārambaṇaprayuktakasya sarvajñatādharmatāpratiśaraṇasya sarvajñatāmārgadvārābhimukhasya sarvajagatsaṃtarpaṇamanasikāraprayuktasya sarvabuddhaguṇasamudrānavatārapratipattyabhimukhasya sarvamārakarmakleśāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇaprayuktasya sarvatathāgatānuśāsanīpradakṣiṇagrāhitāvasthitasya sarvakuśalamūlasamudrasamantamukhasamārjanābhiyogagarbhasya sarvābhiniveśoccalitasaṃtānasya sarvalokaviṣayānabhiniviṣṭasya sarvadharmasvabhāvagaganagocarasya teṣu sarvayācanakeṣvekaputrakasaṃjñā udapadyata,
mātāpitṛsaṃjñā dakṣiṇīyasaṃjñā kalyāṇamitrasaṃjñā durlabhasaṃjñā duṣkarakārakasaṃjñā bahukarasaṃjñāparamopakārakasaṃjñā bodhimārgopastambhasaṃjñā ācāryasaṃjñā śāstṛsaṃjñā udapadyata / sa tān sarvayācanakān yathāgatān yathāsaṃprāptān yathākālasaṃnipatitān yathādigdeśasthitān yathāvastuyācanakān yathārucīn yathābhiprāyān yathābhikāṅkṣiṇo yathābhilāṣiṇo yathāvastuparyeṣakān saṃtarpayāmāsa apratihatena mahāmaitrīmaṇḍalena yācanakajanāparāṅbhukhatayā mahātyāgaraśminā sarvasattvasamaprayogena tyāgamukhena / so 'nnamannārthikebhyaḥ prādāt / pānaṃ pānārthikebhyo vastraṃ vastrārthikebhyaḥ puṣpāṇi puṣpārthikebhyaḥ prādāt / evaṃ gandhadhūpamālyavilepanacūrṇa cīvaracchatradhvajapatākāratnābharaṇāsanaśayanabhavanavimānavihārārāmodyānatapovanāni hayagajarathapattivāhanayugyayānānyapi hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatānyapi prādāt / svagṛhavimānāntaḥpuraparivārānapi, sarvakośānapi vivṛtya vibhajya arthikebhyaḥ prādāt yasya yenārthaḥ sa taṃ gṛhṇātu iti / janapadānapi janapadārthikebhyaḥ prādāt / grāmānapi grāmārthibhyo nagarāṇyapi nagarārthibhyaḥ prādāt / sa tān sarvayācanakān sarvāstiparityāgatayā sarvasattveṣu samapratipannaḥ sarvavastuparityāgairabhicchādayāmāsa //
body.translated_text:
of one lost in a wilderness who desires to see it, upon seeing them a great joy and determination arises due to insatiable delight in beholding them — in just this way, O son of good family, upon seeing those supplicants, great surges of joy arose in King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>. The happiness of mental satisfaction was attained. A great surge of mental elation manifested. A great surge of exuberant joy arose. The force of noble faith and aspiration from <s>buddhabodhi</s> (buddha-awakening) was augmented. The root-born faith in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) was increased. The power of purification of aspiration toward all <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas was greatly augmented. The readiness of <s>bodhisattva</s> faculties arose.
