A surge of great serenity filled with mental delight arose. Through the vast surge of mental buoyancy, the disposition of faculties toward spiritual friends became softened. For what reason? Because that King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, who was engaged with <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) as his object, who had <s>sarvajñatā</s>-dharmatā as his refuge, who faced the gateway of the path to <s>sarvajñatā</s>, who was engaged in the mental attention of satisfying all beings, who faced the practice of entering the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, who was engaged in scattering the mountains of all <s>Māra</s>-deeds and <s>kleśa</s>-obstructions, who stood firmly in respectfully receiving the instructions of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who was pregnant with the exertion of sweeping together the universal ocean of all roots of merit, whose continuum was freed from all attachments, who was not attached to the domains of any world, whose range was the sky of the intrinsic nature of all dharmas — toward all those supplicants the perception of them as an only child arose,
the perception of them as mother and father, the perception of them as worthy of offerings, the perception of them as spiritual friends, the perception of them as rare, the perception of them as doers of difficult deeds, the perception of them as greatly beneficial, the perception of them as supremely helpful, the perception of them as supports on the path to awakening, the perception of them as teachers, the perception of them as masters arose. He satisfied all those supplicants — however they had come, however they had arrived, however they had assembled at the proper time, however they stood in various directions and places, whatever goods they sought, whatever their tastes, whatever their intentions, whatever their desires, whatever their longings, whatever things they were seeking — with an unobstructed great circle of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), with the radiance of great generosity that never turned away from the supplicant people, through the gateway of giving with equal effort toward all beings. He gave food to those seeking food, drink to those seeking drink, clothing to those seeking clothing, flowers to those seeking flowers. Likewise he gave incense, fragrance, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, jewels, ornaments, seats, beds, dwellings, palaces, monasteries, parks, gardens, hermitages, horses, elephants, chariots, infantry, vehicles, yokes, conveyances, as well as gold, silver, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch shells, crystal, coral, refined gold, and silver. He also gave his own household, palace, inner quarters, retinue, and all his treasuries, opening and distributing them to the seekers, saying 'Let whoever needs whatever take it.' He gave provinces to those seeking provinces, villages to those seeking villages, cities to those seeking cities. He covered all those supplicants with the relinquishment of all possessions, acting equally toward all beings, showering them with the giving up of all things.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena ratnaprabhā nāma śreṣṭhidārikā ṣaṣṭikanyāparivārā tasminneva mahāyajñavāṭe saṃnipatitābhūt, abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā, suvarṇavarṇacchavirabhinīlakeśyabhinīlanetrā manojñagandhā brahmasvarā suvastrā svalaṃkṛtā smṛtimatigatihrīdhṛtyapatrāpyeryācaryāsaṃpannā, guruṣu sagauravā, paramasaṃprajanyacāriṇī gambhīraceṣṭā meghāsaṃpannā dharmāṇāṃ grahaṇacāraṇapratibodhiṣu pūrvasukṛtakuśalamūlā dharmābhiṣyanditaprasannasaṃtānā
body.translated_text: At that time, a merchant's daughter named <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> (Jewel Radiance), accompanied by sixty maidens, had assembled at that very great sacrificial ground. She was beautiful, graceful, lovely to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious complexion, golden-skinned, with deep blue hair and deep blue eyes, of pleasing fragrance, with a <s>Brahmā</s>-like voice, well-clothed, well-adorned, possessed of mindfulness, intelligence, deportment, modesty, steadfastness, moral shame, and dignified conduct, respectful toward elders, practicing supreme clear comprehension, of profound bearing, possessed of <s>megha</s>-like qualities, with roots of merit from previous good deeds in the apprehension, practice, and awakening of dharmas, whose continuum was purified by the flow of <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: viśuddhakalyāṇāśayā udārādhimuktigaganagocaparahitapariṇatacittā buddhadarśanadigabhimukhā sarvajñajñānābhilāṣiṇī / sā khalu ratnaprabhā śreṣṭhidārikā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño mahāsiṃhāsanasya pradakṣiṇena nātidūre sthitābhūt prāñjalistaṃ rājānaṃ namasyantī, na ca kiṃcidgṛhṇāti / ekāntasthitā caivaṃ cittamutpādayāmāsa - sulabdhā me lābhā, yadahamevaṃrūpasya kalyāṇamitrasya darśanasamavadhānapratilābhinīti / sā tasya sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño 'ntikekalyāṇamitrasaṃjñāmanukampakasaṃjñāmanugrāhakasaṃjñāṃ buddhasaṃjñāmutpādya māyāśāṭhyāpagatena cittena paramodāraprītiprasādaprāmodyavegapratilabdhā svānyābharaṇāni kāyādavamucya yena rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaḥ, tenābhimukhamakṣaipsīt / tāni tasya siṃhāsanavedikāmadhye adhaḥ pṛthivīmaṇḍale pratiṣṭhitānyabhūvan / sā tānyābharaṇāni pravikīrya evaṃ praṇidhimutpādayāmāsa - yathaiṣa rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo 'nāthānāṃ sattvānāmandhakāraprāptānāṃ pratiśaraṇabhūtaḥ, tathāhamapyanāgate 'dhvani bhaveyam / yāmeṣa dharmatāṃ jānāti, tāmahamati jānīyām / yena yānenaiṣa niryāsyati, tenāhamapi niryāyām / yasminneva mārgapratipannaḥ, tatrāhamapi pratipadyeyam / yathāyamasecanako rūpeṇākṣayabhogo 'nantaparicāro durgharṣo 'parājito 'navamṛdyaḥ, tathāhamapi bhaveyam / yatra yatra cāsyopapattirbhavet, ahamapi tatra tatropapadyeyamiti //
body.translated_text: of purified and virtuous aspiration, with a mind dedicated to the welfare of others whose range was the sky of noble aspiration, facing the direction of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, longing for the knowledge of <s>sarvajña</s> (the omniscient one). That merchant's daughter <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> stood not too far from King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>'s great lion throne, to the right of it, with palms joined, paying homage to that king, and she did not take anything. Standing apart, she generated this thought: 'What good fortune is mine, that I have obtained the sight and presence of such a spiritual friend!' Having generated toward that King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> the perception of a spiritual friend, the perception of one who is compassionate, the perception of one who bestows grace, and the perception of a <s>Buddha</s>, with a mind free from deceit and fraud, having attained the force of supremely noble joy, faith, and gladness, she removed her own ornaments from her body and cast them toward King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>. They came to rest below on the surface of the earth within the platform of his lion throne. Having scattered those ornaments, she generated this aspiration: 'Just as this King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> has become a refuge for protectorless beings who have fallen into darkness, may I also become such in the future. Whatever <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of things) he knows, may I know it even more. By whatever vehicle he will set forth, may I also set forth by that. On whatever path he has entered, may I also enter upon it. Just as he is of incomparable beauty, of inexhaustible enjoyment, of infinite retinue, invincible, unconquered, and unassailable, may I also become so. And wherever he may be reborn, may I also be reborn there.'

body.text: tāmevaṃcittamanasikāraprayuktāmājñāya rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo 'valokya evamāha - gṛhāṇa dārike, yena te 'rthaḥ / ahaṃ khalu dārike sarvāstiparityāgī sarvasattvasaṃtarpaṇāya pratipannaḥ / sā khalu samanvāhṛtā tena rājñā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣeṇeti bhūyasyā mātrayā prasādaṃ pratyalabhata / sā prasannacittā udāravipulakuśalamūlavegasaṃjātā rājānaṃ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāmābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Knowing her to be engaged in such mental attention, King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> looked upon her and spoke thus: 'Take, O maiden, whatever you need. I am one who has relinquished all possessions for the satisfaction of all beings.' Having been thus attended to by King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, she obtained faith to an even greater degree. With a serene mind, born of a surge of vast and noble roots of merit, she at that time praised King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> with these verses:

children.text: pūrve iyaṃ sālaviyūhameghā anopapanne tvayi rājasiṃha /
children.translated_text: Previously, this <s>Sālaviyūhameghā</s> (Array of Śāla-tree Clouds),

children.text: nirābhiramyā hatateja āsīt pretālayo vā yatha bhīṣaṇīyā // 22 //
children.translated_text: before your arising, O lion among kings, was joyless, bereft of splendor, and terrifying like an abode of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts). // 22 //
People were killers of living beings, takers of what was not given, and unrestrained,

children.text: mṛṣāmabhāṣan paruṣāṃ ca vācaṃ piśunāmabaddhāṃ giramapyavocan // 23 //
children.translated_text: they spoke falsehood and harsh words, and uttered slanderous and incoherent speech. // 23 //
With covetous minds toward the words and thoughts of others, with malicious minds toward other persons,
resorting to evil ways through wrong views, they fall into the lower realms through wrong conduct. // 24 //
For those people who practiced <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), enveloped in the darkness of ignorance and delusion,
who held perverted views and saw things wrongly, the sky-god did not rain for many years. // 25 //

children.text: avarṣi deve ca vinaṣṭabījāḥ sasyā na rohanti na caiva vṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the sky-god did not rain, the seeds were destroyed; crops did not grow, nor did trees,
the lakes and ponds, river currents were dried up, as were the herbs and all the forest trees. // 26 //

children.text: nadyo viśuṣkā abhavannaśeṣā udyāna sarve aṭavīprakāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: The rivers dried up entirely without exception, all the gardens and forests became barren,
the earth was filled with white bones before your arising, O one of most pure eyes. // 27 //

children.text: yadā hi te yācakasaṃdhisaṃbhute saṃtarpitā yācanakāstu sarve /
children.translated_text: When, O you who were born from the meeting of supplicants, all the supplicants were satisfied,

children.text: utpadya meghena tadā caturdiśaṃ saṃtarpitā nimnasthalā ca sarve // 28 //
children.translated_text: then clouds arose in the four directions and all the lowlands and highlands were nourished. // 28 //

children.text: bhūyo na corā na bhaṭā na dhūrtā na hanyate kaścana cāpi vadhyate /
children.translated_text: No more were there thieves, nor soldiers, nor rogues; no one was killed or put to death,

children.text: na cāpyanāthā maraṇaṃ vrajanti nātho bhavān sarvajagatyanāthe // 29 //
children.translated_text: nor did the protectorless go to their death — you became the protector of the entire world that lacked a protector. // 29 //
Those people who delighted in killing living beings, having slain others, drank their blood,

children.text: khādanti māṃsāni parasparaṃ ye te tvatpradānairbhuta maitracittāḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: and those who ate each other's flesh — through your gifts they became endowed with minds of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). // 30 //

children.text: ekaḥ śatānto hi sahasrasaṃkhyāṅganā tadā cīvarasaṃvṛtābhūt /
children.translated_text: Where one man had a hundred or a thousand women, at that time they were clothed in robes,

children.text: saṃchādya kāyaṃ tṛṇaparṇacīvaraiḥ pretāḥ kṣudhārtā iva te 'viśaṃstadā // 31 //
children.translated_text: covering their bodies with garments of grass and leaves, afflicted by hunger like <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) they entered then. // 31 //
Rice appeared unsown and uncultivated, and <s>kalpa</s>-trees (wish-fulfilling trees) released their treasures,

children.text: dṛśyanti nāryastu narāśca paṇḍitā jāto yadā tvaṃ jagato 'sya nāthaḥ // 32 //
children.translated_text: women and wise men are seen when you, O lord of this world, were born. // 32 //
Those who formerly, standing on wrong paths, had accumulated provisions month by month and half-month,

children.text: svalaṃkṛtāstvadya mahārhavastrāḥ krīḍanti devā iva nandanasthāḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: now well-adorned and wearing precious garments, they play like gods in <s>Nandana</s> (the divine garden). // 33 //

children.text: kāmeṣu mithyāviṣamapravṛttā adharmarāgeṇa narā hi raktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those men who were wrongly and crookedly engaged in sensual pleasures, stained by unrighteous passion,

children.text: nāryaḥ kumāryaḥ svaparābhiguptā viṣaṃ śayanti sma purā prasajya // 34 //
children.translated_text: women and maidens, guarded by themselves and others, formerly drank poison in despair. // 34 //
Seeing those of form equal to the finest <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), well-clothed and well-adorned,
other women with bodies anointed with sandalwood — now they are content with their own wives, like those in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven. // 35 //

children.text: mṛṣāṃ ca rūkṣāṃ piśunāmabaddhāṃ purā giraṃ śāṭhyavaśādavocan /
children.translated_text: Formerly, under the power of deceit, they spoke false, harsh, slanderous, and incoherent words,

children.text: caturvidhāṃ vācamimāṃ prahāya dharmaṃ carantyadya kudṛṣṭimuktāḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned these four kinds of speech, they now practice <s>Dharma</s>, freed from wrong views. // 36 //
Neither the delightful sound of musical instruments, nor these divine songs,

children.text: sabrahmaghoṣāḥ kalaviṅkaghoṣā rutasya tubhyaṃ padavīṃ spṛśanti // 37 //
children.translated_text: neither the sounds of <s>Brahmā</s> nor the songs of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow-cuckoo) bird can match the quality of your voice. // 37 //

children.text: chatraṃ hi te tiṣṭhati mūrdhasaṃdhau ratnaiścitaṃ kāñcanajālachatram /
children.translated_text: A parasol stands upon the crown of your head, a golden-netted parasol studded with jewels,
with a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) handle, a sheath of <s>śirī</s> (glory), surrounded on all sides by a net of fine jewels. // 38 //
The sounds arising from its bells surpass all musical tones in the world without exception,
resounding like the voices of <s>Buddhas</s>, proclaiming the peaceful sound of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // 39 //

children.text: ye śrutva sattvāḥ śamayanti kleśān aśeṣadikkṣetraparaṃparāsu /
children.translated_text: Hearing which, beings pacify their <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in endless successions of world-realms in every direction,
the name-wheel of the ocean of the wise one, of the oceans of <s>Sugatas</s> (well-gone ones) across oceans of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages). // 40 //
From the beginning, through successions of world-realms, uninterrupted is his name,

children.text: tavānubhāvena ca dikṣvaśeṣaṃ saddharmacakrāṇi ravanti ghaṇṭāḥ // 41 //
children.translated_text: and by your power, in all directions without exception, the bells resound the wheels of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // 41 //
The bell-sound, unattached to lethargy, pervading <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent), resounds throughout,
proclaiming to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the lord of gods, and the lords of the world their respective ritual duties. // 42 //

children.text: śrutvā ca te ghaṇṭarutāṃ nṛdevāḥ svakasvakāṃ karmanidhānakośān /
children.translated_text: Having heard the sound of those bells, the god-kings, understanding their respective treasuries of <s>karma</s> (deeds),

children.text: vivarjya pāpaṃ śubhamācaranti sarve pratiṣṭhanti ca buddhabodhau // 43 //
children.translated_text: abandoning evil, practice virtue, and all become established in <s>buddhabodhi</s> (buddha-awakening). // 43 //

children.text: jyotiḥprabhaste nṛpatiḥ pitābhūt padmaprabhā tanmahiṣī ca mātā /
children.translated_text: The king <s>Jyotiḥprabha</s> (Light Radiance) was your father, and Queen <s>Padmaprabhā</s> (Lotus Radiance) was your mother,

children.text: abhyutsade pañcakaṣāyakāle ka dharmarājyaṃ pratilabdhavān saḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: he who obtained the kingdom of <s>Dharma</s> when he arose in the age of the five degenerations. // 44 //
A vast garden belonged to him, adorned with arrays of blossoming flowers and jeweled lamps,
beautified with five hundred lotus ponds and surrounded by hundreds of trees. // 45 //
Each of them had a palace, rising with a thousand pillars on beautiful shores,
adorned with a thousand arrays together with platforms, illuminated all around by nets and half-moons. // 46 //

children.text: vavarṣa devo na yadā bahūni varṣāṇyadharme balavatyapūrṇe /
children.translated_text: When the god did not rain for many years, while unrighteousness prevailed and [the land was] unfulfilled,

children.text: jalaṃ tadā puṣkiriṇīṣvaśeṣā drumāḥ sapatracchavayaśca śuṣkāḥ // 47 //
children.translated_text: then the water in the lotus-pools [dried up], all the trees with their leaves and colors became withered. // 47 //
Seven nights before your birth, wondrous portents appeared,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayā yāni nirīkṣya sattvāstrātā hi naḥ saṃbhavitetyavocan // 48 //
children.translated_text: seeing which, beings said without doubt, 'Indeed, our savior is being born!' // 48 //
Then in the depths of midnight, O king, the earth-bearer shook with a sixfold trembling,
and even in the blameless lotus-pool, a radiance equal to the sun appeared in the center. // 49 //
Five hundred lotus-pools became filled with water possessing the eight excellent qualities,
trees grew with well-formed branches, resplendent, endowed with flowers and fruits. // 50 //
Those lotus-pools, filled with water, refreshed that entire grove as well,
and from the streams flowing forth from them, <s>Jambudhvaja</s> (Rose-Apple Banner) became filled with water. // 51 //
Trees, herbs, crops, and grasses grew; trees became laden with fruits and flowers,

children.text: bījāni yāvanti ca bhūtadhātryāṃ sarvāṇyarohanta jalāplutāni // 52 //
children.translated_text: and whatever seeds were in the earth, all of them sprouted, bathed in water. // 52 //
Whatever region of the earth was flooded with water, all of it became level at that time,

children.text: nimnonnatāścaiva mahīpradeśāḥ sarve samā eva tadā babhūvuḥ // 53 //
children.translated_text: and the low and elevated regions of the earth all became perfectly even then. // 53 //
Pits, precipices, and uneven places became level in an instant at that time;
thorns, pebbles, and the like disappeared, and veins of precious gems arose. // 54 //
The throngs of men and women who were nearby and afflicted by thirst drank the waters,
and they exclaimed: 'This experience of happiness — oh! whose generous giving is this today?' // 55 //
The lord of the earth, <s>Jyotiḥprabha</s> (Radiance of Light), together with his son, his wives, and his retinue of ministers,
accompanied by thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of people, set forth on a grand excursion to the park. // 56 //

children.text: aninditā puṣkiriṇī surabhyā yā madhyamā gandhajalābhipūrṇā /
children.translated_text: The blameless lotus-pool called <s>Surabhyā</s>, the central one, filled with fragrant water —
in that pool the king stood with his queen, having ascended a pavilion, a holy ford of <s>Dharma</s>. // 57 //

children.text: saptabhyabhūdyā rajanī jalasya samudbhavāṃ tatra sameva rātre /
children.translated_text: On the seventh night after the water's arising, on that very same night,

children.text: punaḥ saśailā savimānamālā cacāla sarvā dharaṇī tathaiva // 58 //
children.translated_text: again the entire earth with its mountains and garlands of palaces trembled just as before. // 58 //
And from the center of <s>Aninditā</s> (the Blameless One), a great lotus of a thousand petals arose,
spreading with the radiance of a thousand suns, a mass of clouds, and the splendor of the summit of great <s>Sumeru</s>. // 59 //
That [lotus] had a <s>vajra</s> (diamond) stalk, a womb of auspicious being, jewel-lord petals, vast and pure,
with a seed-cup of most precious <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, and rich with filaments blazing with the king of fragrances. // 60 //
In that seed-cup, O Lord, you were born, seated in cross-legged posture, rising up,
you shone with a body adorned with [the thirty-two] marks, worshipped by hundreds of <s>devas</s> (gods). // 61 //
The king, descending from the roof of the pavilion, took you in his arms with a delighted mind,

children.text: devyai dadau vācamuvāca caivaṃ sutastavāyaṃ bhava tuṣṭacittā // 62 //
children.translated_text: and gave you to the queen, speaking these words: 'This is your son — be joyful in heart!' // 62 //
Multitudes of treasure troves appeared; trees released their stores,
and the sky resounded with musical instruments when you, the Lord of the World, were born. // 63 //
All the beings in <s>Jambudhvaja</s> became joyful, turning their faces toward you,
and with palms joined together they said, 'Oh! A protector for this unprotected people!' // 64 //

children.text: prabhā śarīrāttava niścaritvā prabhāsayāmāsa mahīṃ samantāt /
children.translated_text: A radiance issuing forth from your body illuminated the earth in all directions,

children.text: tamondhakāraṃ jagatāṃ ca hatvā vyādhīnaśeṣān śamayāṃbabhūva // 65 //
children.translated_text: and having dispelled the darkness of gloom from the worlds, it quelled all diseases without remainder. // 65 //
The hosts of <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s> who were tormenting [beings] all departed,
and venomous serpents of great poison, intent on killing beings, no longer roamed at that time. // 66 //

children.text: alābhaninde ayaśo 'tha duḥkhaṃ yā ītayo vyādhirupadravāśca /
children.translated_text: Loss, blame, disgrace, suffering, calamities, diseases, and afflictions —

children.text: śamaṃ samāsādya hitaṃ jagāma loke pramodastu samudbabhūva // 67 //
children.translated_text: all came to peace and went to welfare; and joy arose in the world. // 67 //
All beings in the world at that time regarded each other with the feeling of a mother,
with minds of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), free from enmity, without harmfulness, and with the disposition toward the path of omniscience. // 68 //
The evil destinies were turned back by the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), and the great highway to heaven was opened,
and you made manifest the path to omniscience, accomplishing the vast purpose of the world. // 69 //
The supreme gain for us is seeing you, who are like a great ocean of giving;
a protector of the unprotected has been born in the world — you are the wondrous guide after the long disappearance [of the Dharma]. // 70 //

body.text: atha khalu ratnaprabhā śreṣṭhidārikā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaṃ rājānamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya saṃvarṇya saṃpraśasya anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇipatya ekānte prāñjaliḥ sthitābhūnnamasyantī / atha khalu rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo ratnaprabhāṃ śreṣṭhidārikāmavalokya evamāha - sādhu sādhu dārike, yā tvaṃ parasattvaguṇaviśeṣajñānābhijñāmavatīrṇā / durlabhāste dārike sattvāḥ sarvaloke, ye parasattvaguṇānadhimucyante / na śakyaṃ dārike tamovṛtairakṛtajñasattvaiḥ buddhivipannaiḥ kṣubhitacittairlulitasaṃtānaistamaścetobhiḥ prakṛtivinaṣṭāśayaiḥ pratipatticyutaiḥ parasattvaguṇaviśeṣānabhijñairbodhisattvaguṇā avatārituṃ tathāgataguṇā vā kalpayituṃ sarvaguṇajñānaviśeṣābhijñā vā anuprāptum / asaṃśayaṃ tvaṃ dārike bodhau
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's daughter <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> (Jewel-Radiance), having praised, extolled, and lauded the king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Canopy-Maṇḍala Resounding with All Dharmas) with these verses, having circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times and bowed down, stood to one side with palms joined in reverence. Then the king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, looking at the merchant's daughter <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, spoke thus: 'Well done, well done, O maiden, that you have descended into the special knowledge of the qualities of other beings! Rare, O maiden, are those beings in the entire world who have faith in the qualities of other beings. It is not possible, O maiden, for beings who are covered in darkness, ungrateful, whose wisdom is impaired, whose minds are agitated, whose mental continuity is disturbed, whose thoughts are darkened, whose dispositions are corrupted by nature, who have fallen from practice, who lack the special knowledge of the qualities of other beings — it is not possible for them to fathom the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, or to conceive the qualities of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, or to attain the special knowledge of all qualities. Without doubt, O maiden, you have set forth toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

body.text: saṃprasthitā, yā tvamevaṃrūpān bodhisattvaguṇānavatarasi / udārasattvābhijñatayā jambudvīpe 'mogho 'smākaṃ sattvasaṃgrahavikramo yeṣāṃ no vijite tvamevaṃrūpajñānasamanvāgatā utpannā / atha khalu rājā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo 'nardhaṃ mahāmaṇiratnaṃ jyotiḥprabhamaṇiratnavicitraṃ ca anarghaṃ vastraratnaṃ svena pāṇinā ādāya ratnaprabhāyāḥ śreṣṭhidārikāyāḥ prādāt / tatparivārasya ca sarvāsāṃ dārikāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ nānāvastraratnāni prādāt, evaṃ cāvocat - pratigṛhāṇa dārike tvamida vastraratnam, parigṛhyātmanā paribhuṅkṣva / atha khalu ratnaprabhā śreṣṭhidārikā saparivārā ubhābhyāṃ jānubhyāṃ dharaṇitale praṇipatya tadvastraratnaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ parigṛhya mūrdhni kṛtvā pratyavasṛtya tadvastraratnaṃ prāvṛtavatī / tatparivārāśca sarvā dārikāḥ pratyekaṃ svāni vastraratnāni prāvṛtavatyaḥ / sā tadvastraratnaṃ prāvṛtya rājānaṃ sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣaṃ pradakṣiṇamakarot sārdhaṃ svena dārikāparivāreṇa / tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ teṣu vastraratneṣu sarvanakṣatrajyotirbimbāni vidyotamānānyadarśan / tāṃ janakāyo dṛṣṭvā evamāha - śobhanastavāyaṃ dārike kanyāparivāraḥ / rātridevateva jyotirgaṇapratimaṇḍitā tvamābhiḥ parivṛtā atīva bhrājase //
body.translated_text: you who fathom such qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Through the special knowledge of noble beings, our effort in gathering beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> has not been in vain, since in our domain you have arisen endowed with such knowledge.' Then the king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, taking in his own hand a priceless great jewel-gem, variegated with <s>jyotiḥprabha</s> (light-radiance) jewels, and a priceless cloth-jewel, gave them to the merchant's daughter <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>. And to all the maidens of her retinue he gave individually various cloth-jewels, and spoke thus: 'Accept, O maiden, this cloth-jewel; having accepted it, enjoy it yourself.' Then the merchant's daughter <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> with her retinue, kneeling on both knees on the ground, bowed down, received that cloth-jewel in both hands, placed it upon her head, withdrew, and wrapped herself in that cloth-jewel. And all the maidens of her retinue individually wrapped themselves in their own cloth-jewels. Having wrapped herself in that cloth-jewel, she circumambulated the king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> together with her retinue of maidens. In all those cloth-jewels, the luminous orbs of all the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations) appeared shining. And the crowd of people, seeing them, spoke thus: 'Beautiful, O maiden, is this retinue of maidens of yours. Like a goddess of the night adorned with a host of stars, you shine exceedingly, surrounded by them.' //

body.text: atha khalu sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājābhūt sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo nāma? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ayaṃ sa bhagavān vairocanastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastena kālena tena samayena rājā abhūt sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣo nāma / syātkhalu punaste kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena padmaprabhā nāma devyabhūdrājño jyotiṣprabhasya bhāryā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājño mātā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / iyaṃ sā māyādevī tena kālena padmaprabhā nāma rājabhāryā abhūt, yayā sa upapādukaḥ kumāraḥ utsaṅge pratigṛhītaḥ / syātkhalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jyotiṣprabho nāma rājā abhūtsarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣasya rājñaḥ pitā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / śuddhodanaḥ sa rājā tena kālena jyotiṣprabho nāma rājā abhūt / syātkhalu punaste kulaputra evam - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena ratnaprabhā nāma śreṣṭhidārikā abhūt / na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena ratnaprabhā nāma śreṣṭhidārikā abhūvam / syātkhalu punaste kulaputra evam - anye tena kālena tena samayena sattvā abhūvan, ye tatra jambudvīpe upapannāḥ rājñā sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣeṇa caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ime te bodhisattvāḥ sarve ihaiva bhagavataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalasamavasṛtā ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau avaivartyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / kecitprathamāyāṃ bhūmau, kecid dvitīyāyāṃ kecitṛtīyāyāṃ keciccaturthyāṃ bhūmau kecitpañcamyāṃ kecitṣaṭhyāṃ kecitsaptamyāṃ kecidaṣṭabhyāṃ kecinnavamyāṃ keciddaśamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / ye nānāpraṇidhānavimātratābhirnānāsarvajñatāprasthānairnānāsaṃbhārairnānāsamudrāgamairnānāniryāṇairnānāmārgavyūhaśuddhibhirnānāvikurvitavṛṣabhitābhirvividhamārgavyūhaiḥ
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> (Blissful Dwelling of All Trees in Full Bloom) spoke thus to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>: 'What do you think, O son of good family — was someone else the king named <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> at that time? It should not be seen so. The Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly and Completely Awakened One, was at that time the king named <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>. And do you think, O son of good family, that someone else was at that time the queen named <s>Padmaprabhā</s> (Lotus-Radiance), the wife of king <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s> and the mother of king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>? It should not be seen so. It was <s>Māyādevī</s> who at that time was the queen named <s>Padmaprabhā</s>, she who received that spontaneously-born prince in her lap. And do you think, O son of good family, that someone else was at that time the king named <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s>, the father of king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>? It should not be seen so. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> was at that time the king named <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s>. And do you think, O son of good family, that someone else was at that time the merchant's daughter named <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>? It should not be seen so. I myself was at that time the merchant's daughter named <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>. And do you think, O son of good family, that at that time there were other beings who were born in that <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and gathered by the king <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s> through the four means of gathering? It should not be seen so. All those <s>bodhisattvas</s> are assembled right here in the assembly-circle of the Blessed One — those who were established on the irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. Some were established on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), some on the second, some on the third, some on the fourth <s>bhūmi</s>, some on the fifth, some on the sixth, some on the seventh, some on the eighth, some on the ninth, and some on the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>bhūmi</s>. They, through various differences of <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows), through various settings forth toward omniscience, through various accumulations, through various ocean-entrances, through various outgoing activities, through various purifications of path-arrays, through various miraculous-display excellences, through manifold path-arrays,

body.text: samudāgatā nānāvimokṣavihārairiha parṣanmaṇḍale nānādharmavimānavihārānāvasanto viharanti //
body.translated_text: having arrived, dwell in this assembly-circle, abiding in various <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) dwellings, in various <s>Dharma</s>-palace dwellings. //

body.text: atha khalu sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva vipulaprītisaṃbhavanidhānasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the night-goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s>, at that moment, further revealing this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation — the illumination of satisfaction born from vast joy, the treasure-store — addressed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> in verses:

children.text: cakṣurmamā jinasutā vipulaṃ yeno vilokayami sarvadiśaḥ /
children.translated_text: My eye, O son of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), is vast, by which I behold all directions,

children.text: kṣetrodadhīn bahuvidhān vipulān sattvārṇavānapi ca saṃsarataḥ // 71 //
children.translated_text: the manifold vast oceans of <s>kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), and the oceans of beings as they transmigrate. // 71 //
In all the expanses of <s>kṣetras</s>, the <s>Jinas</s> seated at the <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, free from defilement,
pervading the ten directions with miraculous powers continuously, they discipline beings through utterances of <s>Dharma</s>. // 72 //
My ocean of hearing is supremely pure, by which I hear all sounds without remainder;
all the <s>dharmas</s> spoken by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) without exception — I hear them all with a mind full of delight. // 73 //
My knowledge is non-dual and unattached, extending into the domain of the minds of other beings;
the vast ocean of minds of the world — I enter into all of it in a single mind-moment. // 74 //
By the power of my recollection and <s>samādhi</s> of the past, I perceive those oceans of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages);
the hundreds of many oceans of previous births — both my own and those of [all] beings. // 75 //
In an instant I know completely the <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of the oceans of <s>kṣetras</s>;

children.text: sattvān gatiṣvapi ca saṃsarato buddhān vikurvitagaṇaiśca saha // 76 //
children.translated_text: and beings wandering in the destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s> together with their hosts of emanations. // 76 //

body.text: tacca smarāmi khalu lokavidāṃ teṣāṃ yathā prathamakaḥ praṇidhiḥ /
body.translated_text: And I recall indeed the knowers of the world — what their first vow was,

body.text: prasthānasaṃbhavanayairvipulaiḥ samudāgatāścarimupetya ca yāḥ // 77 //
body.translated_text: and by what vast methods of setting-forth and arising they came, having reached the final [stage]. // 77 //

children.translated_text: And whatever passages to the consecration-stage there are, for those endowed with the supreme stream of qualities and unsurpassed <s>samādhis</s>,
and the vast and manifold methods of awakening to <s>Bodhi</s> — I descend into all of them in a single mind-moment. // 78 //
By whatever methods and domains the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) turned the supreme wheel in the world,

children.text: yā nirvṛtīparimāṇaguṇā dharmasthiterapi ca yo niyamaḥ // 79 //
children.translated_text: and whatever qualities are measures of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and whatever is the determination of the abiding of <s>Dharma</s> — // 79 //

children.text: ye yānasāgaranayā vimalā ye caiva sattvavinayā vipulāḥ /
children.translated_text: whatever stainless ocean-methods of vehicles, and whatever vast disciplines of beings
have been displayed to the world by those immeasurable ones — I descend into each separately by various methods. // 80 //
A treasury of joy, a lord of abundant satisfaction — this indeed is the method of liberation,

children.text: mama bhāvito vipula kalpaśatānyetaṃ tvamapyavatarāśu nayam // 81 //
children.translated_text: cultivated by me for vast hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> — descend quickly into this method, you too! // 81 //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra vipulaprītisaṃbhavanidhānasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu sarvajñatāprasthānapraṇidhisamudrāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvatathāgatapūrvapraṇidhānasāgarābhinirhārapraṇidhiparipūrṇānāmekabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇasarvabodhisattvabhūmisāgarākramaṇavikrāntajñānānāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsamudraikaikacaryāsamavasaraṇapraṇidhānacaryāpariśuddhānāmekaikasmin bodhisattvavimokṣe sarvabodhisattvavimokṣasāgarasamavasaraṇavihāravaśavartināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vipulaprītisaṃbhavanidhānasaṃtuṣṭyavabhāsa</s> (Illumination of the Satisfaction that is a Treasury Arising from Vast Joy) that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have descended into the ocean of vows of setting forth toward omniscience at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who are fulfilled in the vow of bringing forth the ocean of former vows of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who through ascending a single <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage possess the valorous knowledge of ascending the ocean of stages of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who are purified in vow-conduct through converging in each and every conduct of the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts, who in each and every <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation command the abode of converging in the ocean of liberations of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva bodhimaṇḍe sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā nāma rātridevatā bhagavataḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sattvāḥ paripācayitavyāḥ, kathaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi pariśodhitavyāni, kathaṃ sarvatathāgatā ārādhayitavyā atyantatārādhanatayā, kathaṃ bodhisattvena sarvabuddhadharmeṣu prayoktavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here at this <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a night goddess named <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> (Radiance of the Energy of the Vow to Protect All the World) has approached the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> ripen beings for unsurpassed perfect awakening? How should all <s>Buddha</s>-fields be purified? How should all <s>Tathāgatas</s> be propitiated with ultimate propitiation? How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> exert oneself in all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsāṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsāyā rātridevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 38 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of the night goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> (Blissful Dwelling in the Blossoming of All Trees), circumambulating the night goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the night goddess <s>Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā</s>. // 38 //

body.text: 41 Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā /
body.translated_text: 41. <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā rātridevatā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / so 'drākṣītsarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāṃ rātridevatāṃ tasminnevaṃ parṣanmaṇḍale sarvajagadbhavanapratibhāsamaṇirājagarbhāsananiṣaṇṇāṃ dharmadhātunayapratibhāsamaṇijālasaṃchāditaśarīrāṃ sarvacandrasūryajyotirgrahatārānakṣatrapratibhāsasaṃdarśanakāyāṃ yathāśayasattvacakṣurvijñaptisaṃdarśanakāyāṃ sarvasattvakāyasaṃsthānasadṛśasvaśarīravijñapanakāyām anantamadhyavarṇasamudrodāravijñaptisaṃdarśanakāyāṃ sarveryāpathavihāranayasaṃdarśanakāyāṃ samantamukhābhimukhavijñapanakāyāṃ sarvadigabhimukhasattvaparipācanābhimukhakāyāṃ samantadharmameghanigarjitavividhavikurvitasarvadikspharaṇasarvajagadabhimukhakāyāṃ sarvakālajagadarthābhimukhagaganapralambakāyāṃ sarvatathāgatakramatalapraṇipatitakāyāṃ sarvasattvakuśalamūlopacayasukhapūrvaṃgamakāyāṃ sarvatathāgatābhimukhadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanasaṃdhāraṇapraṇidhisiddhiparipūrṇacetoparāṅmukhasmṛtisaṃdhāraṇakāyām anantamadhyāvabhāsasarvadikspharaṇaśarīrāṃ sarvajagattamovikiraṇadharmapradīpālokasamantapramuktāvabhāsasaṃdarśanakāyāṃ māyāgatadharmanirmalajñānaśarīranidarśanakāyāṃ vigatatamorajodharmaśarīranidarśanakāyāṃ māyāgatadharmatānirjātakāyāṃ dharmatāprativibuddhāndhakāracittāṃ samamukhajñānālokāvabhāsapratilabdhān atyantanirjvaraniḥsaṃtāpamanaḥśarīrāṃ dharmakāyābhedyasāravatīdhātuniryātām apratiṣṭhitatathāgatādhiṣṭhānaprakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭasvabhāvanirmaladharmatāśarīraviśuddhakāyām / sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mūrdhnā praṇamya buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān darśananayānanusmaramāṇo 'ntaradharaṇitale praṇipatya suciramatināmayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the night goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>. He saw the night goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> seated in that very assembly-maṇḍala upon a seat with a womb of gem-kings reflecting all world-dwellings, with a body covered by a net of gems reflecting the methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, with a body displaying the reflections of all moons, suns, luminaries, planets, stars, and constellations, with a body displaying cognitions to the eyes of beings according to their dispositions, with a body manifesting her own form resembling the bodily configurations of all beings, with a body displaying infinite and middleless sublime cognitions of the ocean of colors, with a body displaying the methods of all deportments and abodes, with a body of cognition facing universal gateways, with a body facing in all directions toward the ripening of beings, with a body facing all the world through the pervading of all directions with various transformations of the thunder of universal <s>Dharma</s>-clouds, with a body hanging in the sky facing the welfare of the world at all times, with a body prostrating at the sole-surfaces of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with a body led by the happiness of accumulating the roots of merit of all beings, with a body of mind turned toward the fulfillment of vows for receiving and upholding the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds facing all <s>Tathāgatas</s> and of memory-retention of non-distraction, with a body pervading all directions with infinite and middleless illumination, with a body displaying the universal release of the light of the <s>Dharma</s>-lamp dispelling the darkness of all the world, with a body displaying the stainless knowledge-body of the <s>dharma</s> attained through illusion, with a body displaying the <s>dharma</s>-body free from darkness and dust, with a body born from the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) attained through illusion, with a mind whose darkness has been awakened to <s>dharmatā</s>, having attained the illumination of equal-face knowledge-light, with a body and mind utterly free from fever and torment, arisen from the element of the essence of the indestructible <s>Dharmakāya</s>, with a body purified of the <s>dharmatā</s>-body whose intrinsic nature is primordially undefiled through the non-abiding empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having seen her, bowing his head, recollecting methods of seeing equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, prostrating upon the surface of the ground, he paid homage for a very long time. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tasmāddharaṇitalādutthāya prāñjalībhūtaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ kāyaṃ nirīkṣamāṇo daśa saṃjñāviśuddhīḥ pratilabhate sma, yāsāṃ pratilābhāt sarvakalyāṇamitrasabhāgatāṃ pratyalabhata / katamā daśa? yaduta - kalyāṇamitreṣu svacittasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvajñatāsamārambhavīryasarvālambanasaṃvāsāya / svakarmavipākaviśuddhisvabhāvasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata kalyāṇamitrārāgaṇavipulakuśalamūlasamudāgamārāgaṇatāyai / bodhisattvacaryālaṃkārasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvapraṇidhānālaṃkāracaryāsaṃvasanatāyai / sarvabuddhadharmābhiniṣpādanasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīpathapratipattaye / sparśopapattisaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvabuddhaviṣayānuttaradharmavihārāvabhāsasaṃdarśanatāyai / ekaniryāṇasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata samantabhadrayānaniryāṇapraṇidhānacaryāviśuddhaye / sarvajñapuṇyasāgarākarasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvaśukladharmasamārjanavivardhanatāyai / suparipūrṇakuśaladharmaparipūraṇasaṃvardhanaparipālanasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata buddhabodhau sarvajñajñānavīryavegasaṃvardhanatāyai / sarvakuśalamūlaparipūrisaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata sarvasattvasarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇatāyai / sarvārthasaṃsādhakasaṃjñāṃ pratyalabhata kalyāṇamitreṣu sarvabodhisattvakarmavaśavartitāpratiṣṭhāpanāya / imā daśa saṃjñāviśuddhīḥ pratilabhate sma, yāsāṃ pratilābhāt sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyā buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvasabhāgatāḥ pratyalabhata /
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having risen from that ground-surface, standing with palms joined, gazing upon the body of the night goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>, obtained ten purifications of perception, upon obtaining which he attained equality with all spiritual friends. Which ten? Namely: he obtained the perception of his own mind toward spiritual friends — for dwelling in the support of the energy of the endeavor toward omniscience in all conditions. He obtained the perception of the purification of the intrinsic nature of his own <s>karma</s>-ripening — for the attainment of the vast root of merit arising from non-separation from spiritual friends. He obtained the perception of the adornment of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — for dwelling in the conduct of the adornment of all vows. He obtained the perception of accomplishing all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — for practicing the path of the instructions of all spiritual friends. He obtained the perception of rebirth through contact — for displaying the illumination of the unsurpassed <s>dharma</s>-abode of the domain of all <s>Buddhas</s>. He obtained the perception of a single emergence — for the purification of the conduct of the vow of emergence through the vehicle of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. He obtained the perception of the mine of the ocean of merit of the Omniscient One — for the cleansing and augmenting of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. He obtained the perception of the well-fulfilled fulfillment, augmenting, and guarding of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — for augmenting the force of the energy of omniscient knowledge in <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. He obtained the perception of the fulfillment of all roots of merit — for the fulfillment of all intentions of all beings. He obtained the perception of accomplishing all purposes — for establishing among spiritual friends the mastery of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>karma</s>. These ten purifications of perception he obtained, upon obtaining which he attained equality with the night goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> in <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields.

body.text:
yaduta smṛtisabhāgatāṃ daśadiksarvatathāgatatryadhvānusmṛtinayeṣu, matisabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmasāgaranayāsaṃbhedaviniściteṣu, gatisabhāgatāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmacakramaṇḍalagatyanugatāsaṃbhedavibhāganayakauśalyeṣu, bodhisabhāgatāmākāśasamabuddhyā sarvatryadhvanayasāgarāvabhāsapratilābhāya, indriyaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvendriyasāgarajñānāvabhāsapratilābhāya, cittaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ sarvākārasattvasaṃgrahavyūhabodhisattvamārgaguṇapratipatyalaṃkāramārgapratipattaye, gocarasabhāgatāṃ tathāgatajñānagocarāvabhāsapratilābhāya, nayānugamasabhāgatāṃ sarvākārasarvajñatānayasamudrāvatārapathāvabhāsapratilābhāya, arthaprativedhasabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvajñānaprativedhapratilābhāya, dharmavihārasabhāgatāṃ
sarvāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇatāyai, rūpakāyaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ yathāśayajagadvimātratāsaṃdarśanalakṣaṇānuvyañjanavicitraśarīraviśuddhipratilābhāya, balasabhāgatāṃ bodhisattvabalapariniṣpattisarvajñatārambaṇavivardhanatāyai, sarvadharmanayasamudreṣu vaiśāradyasabhāgatāṃ cittāśayagaganapariśuddhaye, vīryasabhāgatāṃ sarvakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsāparikhedapratilābhāya, pratibhānasabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmānāvaraṇajñānālokapratilābhāya, anabhibhūtasabhāgatāṃ sarvajagadabhyudgatātmabhāvapariśuddhaye, adīnālīnavacanasabhāgatāṃ sarvaparṣanmaṇḍalābhirādhanapariśuddhaye, ghoṣasabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmanayasamudrarutagarjanatāyai, svarāṅgaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ sarvajagadvacanavijñaptivyavahāranayasamudreṣu, guṇaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ tathāgatānuśāsanīguṇapratipattiviśuddhiṣu, buddhadharmakarmavaṃśāvirodhanasabhāgatāmanavadyakarmavipākaviśuddhaye, dharmayajñabhūmipratiṣṭhāpanasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhotpādadharmacakrapravartanatāyai, brahmacaryaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ sarvatathāgataviṣayajñānasaṃvasanatāyai, mahāmaitrīsabhāgatāṃ nānāmaitrīnayapratikṣaṇasarvasattvasāgaraspharaṇatāyai, mahākaruṇānayasamudrāvatārasabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇadharmameghābhipravarṣaṇatāyai, kāyakarmasabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvaparipācanopāyopacārasabhāgatāyai, vākkarmaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmavyavahārābhilāṣeṣu, manaskarmasabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvacitteṣu sarvajñatārambaṇopasaṃharaṇatāyai, vividhasarvavyūhapratimaṇḍanasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇatāyai, upasaṃkramaṇasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhotpādasamudreṣu, dharmacakrādhyeṣaṇasabhāgatāṃ sarvatathāgateṣu, pūjopasthānasabhāgatāṃ sarvatathāgatāśeṣakālasarvapūjopasthānatāyai, sarvasattvaparipākavinayasabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvadhātau, ālokapratilābhasabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvadharmanayeṣu, samādhipratilābhasabhāgatāṃ sarvasamādhinayasamudreṣu, samantaspharaṇasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrasamudrabodhisattvacaryāvikurvitaspharaṇatāyai, bodhisattvavihārasabhāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvavikurvitanayasamudreṣu, parivārasabhāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāseṣu, praveśasabhāgatāṃ sarvalokadhātususūkṣmapraveśeṣu, cittavibhaktisabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetravaipulyeṣu,
anugamavaimātratāsabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrasamudrāvatāravimātratānugameṣu, samantanayaprasaraspharaṇasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetravibhaktyanantajñānavijñaptiṣu, abhyudgatasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu, avaivartyasabhāgatāṃ sarvadikspharaṇasamavasaraṇādhiṣṭhānāvivartyatāyai, andhakāravidhamanasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhabodhimaṇḍavibudhyanajñānamaṇḍalāvabhāsapratilābhāya,
body.translated_text: namely, conformity of mindfulness (<s>smṛti-sabhāgatā</s>) in the methods of recollecting all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times in the ten directions, conformity of intellect (<s>mati-sabhāgatā</s>) in the definitive analyses that are undivided in the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of progress (<s>gati-sabhāgatā</s>) in skillfulness regarding the methods of undivided classification following the course of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, conformity of awakening (<s>bodhi-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the ocean of methods of all three times through a wisdom equal to space, conformity of purity of faculties (<s>indriya-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the knowledge of the ocean of faculties of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conformity of purity of mind (<s>citta-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) for the practice of the path of adornment and the qualities of the <s>bodhisattva</s> path in the array of gathering beings in all aspects, conformity of domain (<s>gocara-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge, conformity of following methods (<s>nayānugama-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the path of entry into the ocean of methods of omniscience in all aspects, conformity of penetration of meaning (<s>artha-prativedha-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the penetration of knowledge of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of abiding in <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharma-vihāra-sabhāgatā</s>) for the scattering of the mountains of all obstructions, conformity of purity of the form-body (<s>rūpakāya-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the purity of a variegated body endowed with marks and minor signs manifesting the diversity of beings according to their dispositions, conformity of powers (<s>bala-sabhāgatā</s>) for the increase of the support of omniscience through the perfection of <s>bodhisattva</s> powers, conformity of fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmas</s> for the purification of the sky of mental intention, conformity of vigor (<s>vīrya-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining unwearied dwelling in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct throughout all <s>kalpas</s>, conformity of eloquence (<s>pratibhāna-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the light of unobstructed knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of being unconquerable (<s>anabhibhūta-sabhāgatā</s>) for the purification of a self-nature surpassing all the world, conformity of undepressed and unlethargic speech (<s>adīnālīna-vacana-sabhāgatā</s>) for the purification of delighting all assemblies, conformity of voice (<s>ghoṣa-sabhāgatā</s>) for the roaring sound of the ocean of methods of all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of purity of vocal limbs (<s>svarāṅga-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of methods of verbal communication and designation for all the world, conformity of purity of qualities (<s>guṇa-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in the purification of the practice of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> instruction, conformity of non-contradiction with the lineage of <s>Buddha-dharma</s> action (<s>buddha-dharma-karma-vaṃśā-virodhana-sabhāgatā</s>) for the purification of blameless <s>karma</s>-fruition, conformity of establishing the ground of <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice (<s>dharma-yajña-bhūmi-pratiṣṭhāpana-sabhāgatā</s>) for the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel at the arising of all <s>Buddhas</s>, conformity of purity of the holy life (<s>brahmacarya-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) for dwelling in the knowledge of the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, conformity of great loving-kindness (<s>mahā-maitrī-sabhāgatā</s>) for pervading the ocean of all beings at every moment through various methods of loving-kindness, conformity of entry into the ocean of methods of great compassion (<s>mahā-karuṇā-naya-samudra-avatāra-sabhāgatā</s>) for raining down <s>Dharma</s>-clouds for the protection of the entire realm of beings, conformity of bodily action (<s>kāya-karma-sabhāgatā</s>) for conformity with skillful means of ripening all beings, conformity of purity of verbal action (<s>vāk-karma-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in all pursuits of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, conformity of mental action (<s>manas-karma-sabhāgatā</s>) for directing the support of omniscience into the minds of all beings, conformity of adorning with various arrays (<s>vividha-sarva-vyūha-pratimaṇḍana-sabhāgatā</s>) for approaching all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of approaching (<s>upasaṃkramaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, conformity of requesting the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel (<s>dharma-cakra-adhyeṣaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) before all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, conformity of worship and attendance (<s>pūjā-upasthāna-sabhāgatā</s>) for worship and attendance upon all <s>Tathāgatas</s> at all times without exception, conformity of ripening and disciplining all beings (<s>sarva-sattva-paripāka-vinaya-sabhāgatā</s>) in the entire realm of beings, conformity of attaining illumination (<s>āloka-pratilābha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the methods of <s>Dharma</s> for all beings, conformity of attaining <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhi-pratilābha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of methods of all <s>samādhis</s>, conformity of pervading everywhere (<s>samanta-spharaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) for pervading through the miraculous displays of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding (<s>bodhisattva-vihāra-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of methods of miraculous displays of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conformity of retinue (<s>parivāra-sabhāgatā</s>) in dwelling with the conduct of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conformity of entry (<s>praveśa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the subtle entries into all world-realms, conformity of mind-differentiation (<s>citta-vibhakti-sabhāgatā</s>) in the vastness of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of following the diversity of entry (<s>anugama-vaimātratā-sabhāgatā</s>) in following the diversity of entry into the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of universal pervading extension of methods (<s>samanta-naya-prasara-spharaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the infinite knowledge-communications of the differentiation of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of being exalted (<s>abhyudgata-sabhāgatā</s>) in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of irreversibility (<s>avaivartyā-sabhāgatā</s>) for irreversibility from the empowerment of assembling the pervasion in all directions, conformity of dispelling darkness (<s>andhakāra-vidhamana-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge of awakening at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>,

body.text:
anuprāptisabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalasamudreṣu, sarvabuddhakṣetrakāyajālaspharaṇasabhāgatāmanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetratathāgatapūjopasthānaprayogeṣu, jñānapratyakṣasabhāgatāṃ tatra dharmanayasamudrānuprabandheṣu, pratipattisabhāgatāmanulomasarvadharmanayanasaṃmukhaprayogeṣu, eṣaṇasabhāgatāṃ tīvradharmacchandārambhaviśuddhaye, viśuddhisabhāgatāṃ kāyavāṅbhanaskarmabuddhaguṇālaṃkārasamādāneṣu, sumanaḥsabhāgatāmaviṣamakalpacittamaṇḍalasarvadharmajñānamaṇḍalapariśuddhaye, vīryārambhasabhāgatāṃ sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhārasamārambhanistīraṇaprayogeṣu, caryāvyūhasabhāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāpariniṣpattiṣu, asaṅgavihārasabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmanimittaprativedheṣu, upāyakauśalyanayasabhāgatāṃ tatra tatra dharmavihārajñānavikurvaṇatāsu, āyatanaviśuddhisabhāgatāṃ yathāśayasattvāviṣamadarśanasamādāneṣu, bodhisattvasamādhimukhapratilābhasabhāgatāṃ sarvadharmavibhāvanāpratilābheṣu, adhiṣṭhānasabhāgatāṃ sarvatathāgataveśeṣu, bhūmyākramaṇasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvabhūmipratilābheṣu, pratiṣṭhānasabhāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvavyavasthāneṣu, ādeśanasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhavyākaraṇeṣu, samādhisabhāgatāṃ ekakṣaṇe sarvasamādhisāgaranayeṣu, samādhivyavasthānasabhāgatāṃ nānālakṣaṇabuddhakāryeṣu, anusmṛtisabhāgatāṃ sarvānusmṛtyārambaṇanayasamudreṣu, bodhisattvacaraṇasabhāgatāṃ bodhisattvakāryāparāntakoṭīgatakalpavyavasāyeṣu, prasādasabhāgatāmaprameyabuddhajñānādhimuktiprītivegasamudravivardhanatāyai, vivardhanasabhāgatāṃ sarvāvaraṇaparvatānāmavivartyajñānasabhāgatāṃ buddhajñānānantasaṃbhārasaṃbhavāya, upapattisabhāgatāṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayakāleṣu, vihārasabhāgatāṃ sarvajñatānayamukheṣu, viṣayasabhāgatāṃ dharmadhātunayavṛṣabhitāviṣayapraveśeṣu, anālayasabhāgatāṃ sarvālayasamuddhātitacittatāyai, sarvadharmanirdeśasabhāgatāṃ dharmasamatājñānāvatāreṣu, abhiyogasabhāgatāṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānasvaśarīrasaṃpratīcchanatāyai, abhijñāsabhāgatāṃ sarvalokajñāpanapratipattinayeṣu,
anabhisaṃskārarddhipratilābhasabhāgatāṃ sarvadikkṣetrasāgarāvatāreṣu, dhāraṇibhūmisabhāgatāṃ sarvadhāraṇīsamudrāvabhāsapratilābhāya, sarvabuddhadharmacakrasaṃdhyavatārasabhāgatāṃ sarvasūtrāntadharmaparyāyeṣu, gambhīradharmapraveśasabhāgatāṃ gaganatalopamasarvadharmanayāvatāreṣu, avabhāsasabhāgatāṃ sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu, abhirocanasabhāgatāṃ yathāśayajagadvijñaptiṃsaṃdarśaneṣu, prakampanasabhāgatāṃ kṣetrādhiṣṭhānavikurvitasattvadarśaneṣu, amoghacaraṇasabhāgatāṃ darśanaśravaṇānusmṛtisattvavinayeṣu, niryāṇasabhāgatāṃ pratyalabhata sarvapraṇidhānasamudranayapariniṣpattidaśabalajñānānubodhāya / iti hi sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ prasannacittaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāṃ rātridevatāmavalokayan āsāṃ daśānāṃ saṃjñāviśuddhīnāṃ pratilābhādetatpramukhān buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ sabhāgatanayān pratilabhate sma //
body.translated_text: conformity of attainment (<s>anuprāpti-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of assemblies of all <s>Buddhas</s>, conformity of pervading with the body-net of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields (<s>sarva-buddha-kṣetra-kāya-jāla-spharaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the practices of worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, conformity of direct knowledge (<s>jñāna-pratyakṣa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the continuing streams of the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>-methods therein, conformity of practice (<s>pratipatti-sabhāgatā</s>) in the practices facing all methods of <s>Dharma</s>-analysis in conformity, conformity of seeking (<s>eṣaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) for the purification of intense <s>Dharma</s>-desire and undertaking, conformity of purification (<s>viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in the undertakings of adorning body, speech, and mind with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, conformity of good mind (<s>sumanas-sabhāgatā</s>) for the purification of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> through an impartial mind-<s>maṇḍala</s> of even <s>kalpas</s>, conformity of vigor-undertaking (<s>vīrya-ārambha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the practices of undertaking the accomplishment and completion of the accumulation of all roots of merit, conformity of conduct-array (<s>caryā-vyūha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the perfection of all <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, conformity of unattached abiding (<s>asaṅga-vihāra-sabhāgatā</s>) in the penetration of the marks of all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of methods of skill in means (<s>upāya-kauśalya-naya-sabhāgatā</s>) in the various miraculous transformations of knowledge of <s>Dharma</s>-abiding, conformity of purity of sense-bases (<s>āyatana-viśuddhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in the undertakings of impartially perceiving beings according to their dispositions, conformity of attaining the gate of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> (<s>bodhisattva-samādhi-mukha-pratilābha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the attainment of discerning all <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna-sabhāgatā</s>) in the guises of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, conformity of ascending the stages (<s>bhūmi-ākramaṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in attaining all the stages of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conformity of establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhāna-sabhāgatā</s>) in the stations of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conformity of prophecy (<s>ādeśana-sabhāgatā</s>) in the predictions of all <s>Buddhas</s>, conformity of <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhi-sabhāgatā</s>) in the methods of the ocean of all <s>samādhis</s> in a single instant, conformity of <s>samādhi</s>-establishment (<s>samādhi-vyavasthāna-sabhāgatā</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>-activities of various characteristics, conformity of recollection (<s>anusmṛti-sabhāgatā</s>) in the ocean of methods of all recollection-supports, conformity of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct (<s>bodhisattva-caraṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the <s>bodhisattva</s> activities extending to the final limit of <s>kalpas</s>, conformity of faith (<s>prasāda-sabhāgatā</s>) for the increase of the ocean of torrents of joy from faith in the immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, conformity of increase (<s>vardhana-sabhāgatā</s>) — irreversible knowledge-conformity for the scattering of the mountains of all obstructions — for the arising of the inexhaustible accumulation of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, conformity of birth (<s>upapatti-sabhāgatā</s>) at the times of ripening and disciplining all beings, conformity of abiding (<s>vihāra-sabhāgatā</s>) in the gateways of methods of omniscience, conformity of domain (<s>viṣaya-sabhāgatā</s>) in the entry into the domain of the preeminence of methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, conformity of non-attachment (<s>anālaya-sabhāgatā</s>) for a mind-state that has transcended all attachment, conformity of teaching all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarva-dharma-nirdeśa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the entry into the knowledge of the equality of <s>dharmas</s>, conformity of application (<s>abhiyoga-sabhāgatā</s>) for receiving in one's own body the empowerment of all <s>Buddhas</s>, conformity of higher knowledge (<s>abhijñā-sabhāgatā</s>) in the methods of practice of making known to all the world, conformity of attaining effortless supernatural power (<s>anabhisaṃskāra-ṛddhi-pratilābha-sabhāgatā</s>) in the entry into the ocean of fields in all directions, conformity of the stage of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (<s>dhāraṇī-bhūmi-sabhāgatā</s>) for attaining the illumination of the ocean of all <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, conformity of entering the junctures of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>sarva-buddha-dharma-cakra-saṃdhy-avatāra-sabhāgatā</s>) in all <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, conformity of entering the profound <s>Dharma</s> (<s>gambhīra-dharma-praveśa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the entry into all methods of <s>dharmas</s> like the surface of the sky, conformity of illumination (<s>avabhāsa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the extensions of all world-realms, conformity of shining forth (<s>abhirocana-sabhāgatā</s>) in the manifestations of communicating to the world according to their dispositions, conformity of causing trembling (<s>prakampana-sabhāgatā</s>) in the miraculous displays of field-empowerment and showing to beings, conformity of unfailing conduct (<s>amogha-caraṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) in the disciplining of beings through seeing, hearing, and recollection, conformity of going forth (<s>niryāṇa-sabhāgatā</s>) — she attained [these] for the awakening to the knowledge of the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten Powers) through the perfection of the ocean of methods of all <s>praṇidhānas</s> (vows). Thus indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, with a clear mind, gazing upon <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> the night-goddess, through the attainment of these ten purifications of perception, obtained conformity-methods of that night-goddess equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, headed by these.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyā buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamadarśanatayā avatīrṇo 'nantamadhyakalyāṇamitrasaṃjñāviśuddhipratilabdho buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamasabhāgatānayāvatīrṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having descended through the vision equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields of <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> the night-goddess, having attained the purification of the perception of spiritual friends that is infinite and without middle, having entered the conformity-methods equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields,

body.text: ekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya yena sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā rātridevatā, tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: having draped his robe over one shoulder and bowing with joined palms toward <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> the night-goddess, at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: yathā svacitte vaśitā mamāsti chandaśca bodhau sudṛḍho 'nivartyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as I have mastery over my own mind, and my aspiration toward awakening is firm and irreversible,

children.text: tvadīyacitte 'pi hi me tathaiva svataiva devyadya dṛḍhopajātā // 1 //
children.translated_text: so too in your mind, O goddess, such firm [resolve] has arisen in me spontaneously. // 1 //
All sins without remainder have been purified, a radiant auspicious fruition has been obtained,
and through the vision of you who are beautiful to behold, imperishable wholesome <s>dharmas</s> have been accumulated by me. // 2 //

children.text: cittaṃ guṇaughaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ me pṛthagvidhaiḥ sattvahitapravṛttaiḥ /
children.translated_text: My mind has been adorned with floods of virtues of various kinds, engaged in the welfare of beings,
adorned with which I have practiced the conduct in all fields for <s>kalpas</s> extending to the final limit. // 3 //

children.text: nidarśitā te khalu sarvadharmān niṣpattirārye madanugrahāya /
children.translated_text: You have shown me, O noble one, the accomplishment of all <s>dharmas</s> for my benefit,
for my welfare, with the intention of grace, bestow upon me the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-instruction. // 4 //
The path of falling into lower realms has been reversed, the pure path to heaven has been shown,
and the path to omniscience has been displayed by you — the vehicle followed by all the <s>Sugatas</s> without exception. // 5 //
In your presence, an incomparable and wondrous perception of going forth has arisen supremely in me today,
immaculate like space, immeasurable — the pure gateway of the <s>Dharma</s> of omniscience. // 6 //
The immeasurable perception of being a source of all the wholesome [qualities] of omniscience has arisen in me today in your presence,

children.text: puṇyārṇavā me gaganapramāṇāḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ cetasi codbhavanti // 7 //
children.translated_text: and oceans of merit, vast as the sky, arise in my mind at every moment. // 7 //

body.text: unnehi me pāramitābhirārye puṇyairacintyaiśca vivardhayasva /
body.translated_text: Lift me up with the <s>pāramitās</s>, O noble one, and cause me to grow with inconceivable merits,

body.text: saṃvardhitaḥ sarvaguṇaiḥ śubhaiśca sarvajñapaṭṭaṃ nacireṇa lapsye // 8 //
body.translated_text: and nourished by all auspicious qualities, I shall before long attain the throne of the Omniscient One. // 8 //

children.translated_text: In spiritual friends I always have the perception of fulfilling the path to omniscience,
and for this reason all my wholesome [merit], having been honored, shall quickly bear fruit. // 9 //

children.text: sarve yato 'rthāḥ prabhavanti cāsmāt siddhaśca kalyāṇaguṇairupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since all aims arise from this [spiritual friend], and [one becomes] accomplished, endowed with auspicious qualities,
having pleased this one of infinite renown, I shall proclaim the path to omniscience to the world. // 10 //

children.text: ācāryabhūtā mi guṇāprameye sarvajñadharmeṣu mama praṇetrī /
children.translated_text: You are my teacher in immeasurable qualities, my guide in the <s>dharmas</s> of the Omniscient One,

children.text: na kalpakoṭīnayutairasaṃkhyaiḥ śakyaṃ mayā te pratikartumārye // 11 //
children.translated_text: not even in innumerable myriads of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> would it be possible for me to repay you, O noble one. // 11 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ imā gāthā bhāṣitvā sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāṃ rātridevatāmetadavocat - saṃdarśitastvayā devate mamāyamacintyo bodhisattvavimokṣaviṣayaḥ / vadasva me devate - ko nāmāyaṃ vimokṣaḥ? kiyacciraṃ saṃprasthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? kiyaccireṇa vā tvamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having spoken these verses, said this to the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>: 'You have shown me, goddess, this inconceivable domain of <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation. Tell me, goddess — what is the name of this liberation? How long ago, goddess, did you set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening? And how long until you will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening?'

body.text: evamukte sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā rātridevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sarvasattvaparipākasaṃcodanakuśalasaṃbhavo nāma kulaputra ayaṃ vimokṣaḥ / ahaṃ kulaputra anena vimokṣeṇa samanvāgatā sarvadharmasvabhāvavasamatāmanubuddhya sarvadharmaprakṛtimavatīrya anālayaṃ dharmaṃ niśritya sarvalokoccālitā suvibhaktarūpatāṃ dharmāṇāmavatīrya avisabhāgavarṇā avaivartavarṇā avikalpavarṇā anīlavarṇā apītavarṇā alohitavarṇā anavadātavarṇā dharmatāmavatīrya anekavarṇavibhaktirūpātmabhāvā nānātvavarṇā avisabhāgā anānātvā avaimātryā avikalpā anīlā apītā alohitā anavadātavarṇā, anekavarṇā aprameyavarṇā viśuddhavarṇā sarvavyūhapramuñcanavarṇā samantadarśanavarṇā sarvajagatsadṛśavarṇā sarvalokābhimukhātirekavarṇā samantāvabhāsapratibhāsavarṇā apratikūladarśanavarṇā lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasuviśodhitavarṇā anavadyacaraṇaprabhāsavarṇā mahābalavikramasaṃdarśanavarṇā durāsadagambhīravarṇā sarvalokāparyādattavarṇā kṣaṇakṣaṇavicitravarṇā nānāvarṇameghasaṃdarśanavarṇā nānārūpasaṃsthānavarṇā aprameyavikurvitasaṃdarśanavarṇā suruciravacanavarṇā sarvasurūpacittavarṇā sarvasattvaparipākānukūlavarṇā yathāśayavaineyābhimukhopanītakuśalavarṇā apratihatasamantaprabhāsavarṇā acchānāvilaviprasannaprabhāsvaravarṇā abhedyakāyopacayopaśobhitavarṇā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> said this to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'This liberation is called <s>sarvasattvaparipākasaṃcodanakuśalasaṃbhava</s> (the arising of skill in urging the maturation of all beings), son of good family. I, son of good family, being endowed with this liberation, having awakened to the equality of the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, having descended into the fundamental nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, relying on the <s>dharma</s> of non-attachment, transcending all worlds, having descended into the well-distinguished form-nature of <s>dharmas</s> — of non-disparate appearance, of irreversible appearance, of non-conceptual appearance, of non-blue appearance, of non-yellow appearance, of non-red appearance, of non-white appearance — having descended into <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of reality), with a self-nature of manifold appearances distinguished in form, of diverse appearances, non-disparate, non-diverse, non-discordant, non-conceptual, non-blue, non-yellow, non-red, non-white in appearance, of manifold appearances, of immeasurable appearances, of purified appearances, of appearances releasing all arrays, of appearances seeing in all directions, of appearances resembling all worlds, of appearances surpassing all that faces all worlds, of appearances illuminating and reflecting in all directions, of appearances whose sight is never adverse, of appearances well-purified in marks and secondary characteristics, of appearances radiant with faultless conduct, of appearances displaying great power and valor, of appearances profound and difficult to approach, of appearances not exhausted by all worlds, of appearances variegated at every moment, of appearances displaying clouds of diverse colors, of appearances in diverse forms and shapes, of appearances displaying immeasurable transformations, of appearances with beautiful speech, of appearances with minds devoted to all beautiful forms, of appearances favorable to the maturation of all beings, of appearances whose wholesome qualities are brought forth facing those to be guided according to their dispositions, of appearances with unobstructed radiance pervading all directions, of appearances clear, unclouded, serene, and luminous, of appearances adorned with an indestructible bodily form

acintyadharmanayaprabhāvanavarṇā abhibhūranabhibhūtasarvābhibhavanavarṇā atamastimiravarṇā sarvāndhakāravidhamanavarṇā sarvaśuklasusamārjitavarṇā mahātmagunasamudravarṇā pūrvagurugauravasusamārjitavarṇā adhyāśayagaganapariśuddhivarapravarottamaviśālavarṇā anācchedyākṣayaguṇasamudraprabhāvanavarṇā sarvalokābhiniśritāsaṃbhedavarṇā asaṅgasarvadikspharaṇavarṇā anabhilāpyakṣetrasamudracittakṣaṇaprasarānekavividhavarṇasamudrasaṃdarśanavarṇā sarvasattvamahāprītivegavivardhanavarṇā sarvasattvasāgarasaṃgrahavarṇā sarvaromavivarāśeṣabuddhaguṇasamudrameghanigarjanavarṇā sarvasattvāśayādhimuktisāgaraviśodhitavarṇā sarvadharmārthaviniścayasaṃdarśanavarṇā nānāvarṇaraśmijālavabhāsavarṇā gaganapramāṇavimalaprabhāvarṇā viśuddhamaṇirājavimalarajaḥprabhāniśritavarṇā nirmaladharmatāpratibhāsavarṇā atulavarṇanayasamudravicitrapratibhāsavarṇā samantadigavabhāsavarṇā yathākālajagatsaṃdarśanābhinnavarṇā praśamadamadiksaṃbhavavarṇā sarvakleśapraśamanavarṇā sarvajagatpuṇyakṣetraprabhāvanavarṇā sarvanayapraśamanavarṇā amoghajagatspharaṇavarṇā mahājñānavikramaprabhāvanavarṇā asaṅgakāyasamantaspharaṇavarṇā samantādvarakāyāmoghajagatsaṃdarśanavarṇā mahāmaitrīsamudrasamudāgamavarṇā mahāpuṇyasumerusamudāgamavarṇā sarvajagadaniśritasarvalokagatipratibhāsaprāptavarṇā mahājñānabalaviśodhanavarṇā sarvalokānusmṛtisaṃvasanavarṇā sarvaratnābhavarṇā vairocanagarbhanidarśanavarṇā sarvajagatprasādānurūpavarṇā sarvajñatākārābhimukhavarṇā prahasitanayanajagatprasādavarṇā
sarvaratnavyūhāgrāvabhāsavarṇā anāgṛhābhāsasarvajagatparāṅmukhavarṇā aniyatābhiniviṣṭavarṇā adhiṣṭhānavikurvitavṛṣabhitāsaṃdarśanavarṇā sarvavividhavikurvitavṛṣabhitāsaṃdarśanavarṇā tathāgatakuśalamūlāvabhāsanavarṇā anavadyasarvadharmadhātunayasāgaraprasṛtavarṇā sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalopasaṃkramaṇapratibhāsaprāptavarṇā vividhavarṇasamudraniṣpādanavarṇā sucaritaniṣyandasaṃbhūtavarṇā yathāvaināyikopanāyikavarṇā sarvalokātṛptadarśanavarṇā vicitraprabhāsvarāvabhāsanavarṇā sarvatryadhvavarṇā samudrasaṃdarśanavarṇā sarvavarṇaraśmisamudrapramuñcanavarṇā anabhilāpyavarṇā prabhāmaṇḍalasamudranānārthavimātratāsaṃdarśanavarṇā sarvagandhāvasasarvajagatsamatikrāntavarṇā ekaikaromavivarānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥ samasūryamaṇḍalameghasaṃdarśanavarṇā vimalacandramaṇḍalavigrahameghādhiṣṭhānavarṇā anantarucirapuṣpasumerumeghasaṃpramuñcanavarṇā nānābhinirhāramālyadrumameghasarvālaṃkāramālyavarṣapramuñcanavarṇā sarvaratnapadmameghasaṃdarśanavarṇā sarvagandhadhūpapaṭalavigrahameghasarvadharmadhātuspharaṇavarṇā praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvacūrṇakośameghānadhiṣṭhāya daśasu dikṣu sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarān spharitvā darśanavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ śravaṇavaineyānāmanusmṛtivaineyānāṃ dharmacakranirmāṇābhinirhāravaineyānāṃ pratyupasthitaparipākakālavaineyānāṃ rūpakāyasaṃdarśanavaineyānāṃ pratyupāsanavaineyānāmanubodhanavaineyānāṃ vividhavikurvitaprātihāryasaṃdarśanavaineyānāmacintyavikurvitaprātihāryavijñaptisaṃdarśanavaineyānāṃ sattvānāmāśayavaśena kālavaśena akuśalakarmavivartanavaśena kuśalakarmasaṃbhavapratiṣṭhāpanavaśena pūrvamahāpraṇidhānābhinirhāravaśena sarvajñatāvegavaśena bodhisattvavimokṣavipulavikurvitapratilābhadharmavaśena sarvajagatparitrāṇasvabhinirhṛtamahākaruṇābalasaṃbhavavaśena mahāmaitrīsāgaraviśuddhisaṃjananāśayavaśena pravartayāmi tathāgatādhiṣṭhānasupratīcchitatvāt //
body.translated_text: of appearances manifesting inconceivable methods of <s>dharma</s>, of appearances overcoming all yet neither overpowering nor overpowered, of appearances free from darkness and obscurity, of appearances dispelling all blindness, of appearances well-cleansed in complete whiteness, of appearances like an ocean of the qualities of great beings, of appearances well-polished through former reverence for teachers, of appearances vast, supreme, and excellent through the purification of the sky of aspiration, of appearances manifesting an unbreakable and inexhaustible ocean of qualities, of appearances unsevered from reliance on all worlds, of appearances pervading all directions without attachment, of appearances displaying an ocean of manifold and various colors spreading through mind-moments across an inexpressible ocean of fields, of appearances increasing the force of great joy in all beings, of appearances gathering the ocean of all beings, of appearances in which from each hair-pore resounds a cloud from the ocean of qualities of all <s>Buddhas</s>, of appearances purified through the ocean of dispositions and inclinations of all beings, of appearances displaying the ascertainment of the meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>, of appearances illuminated by nets of rays of diverse colors, of appearances with a radiance as vast as space and
