stainless, of appearances grounded in the stainless dust-free radiance of the king of pure jewels, of appearances reflecting the stainless <s>dharmatā</s>, of appearances with variegated reflections from an incomparable ocean of methods of appearance, of appearances illuminating all directions, of appearances undivided in the display of the world at the proper time, of appearances arising from the direction of tranquility and self-control, of appearances pacifying all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), of appearances manifesting all worlds as fields of merit, of appearances pacifying all methods, of appearances pervading all worlds unfailingly, of appearances manifesting the valor of great knowledge, of appearances with an unattached body pervading in all directions, of appearances displaying all worlds unfailingly with a body open in all directions, of appearances arising from the ocean of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), of appearances arising from the <s>Sumeru</s> of great merit, of appearances that have attained the reflection of all worldly destinies without relying on any world, of appearances purified by the power of great knowledge, of appearances dwelling in the recollection of all worlds, of appearances having the luster of all jewels, of appearances revealing the womb of <s>Vairocana</s>, of appearances conforming to the faith of all worlds, of appearances facing the form of omniscience, of appearances that gladden all worlds with smiling eyes, of appearances illuminated by the foremost array of all jewels, of appearances turning away from all worldly affairs with ungraspable radiance, of appearances not fixedly attached, of appearances displaying the excellence of empowered transformations, of appearances displaying the excellence of all manner of transformations, of appearances illuminating the wholesome roots of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, of appearances extending into the faultless ocean of methods throughout the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), of appearances that have attained the reflection of entering the assembly-circles of all <s>Buddhas</s>, of appearances producing an ocean of diverse colors, of appearances born from the outflow of good conduct, of appearances guiding according to those to be trained, of appearances whose sight never satiates all worlds, of appearances illuminated with variegated radiance, of appearances displaying the ocean of all three times and all colors, of appearances releasing an ocean of rays of all colors, of inexpressible appearances, of appearances displaying the diversity of manifold meanings through an ocean of radiance-circles, of appearances surpassing all worlds with all fragrances and garments — I display from each hair-pore clouds of sun-circles equal to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, empowered clouds with forms of stainless moon-circles, releasing clouds of infinite beautiful flowers like <s>Sumeru</s>, releasing showers of all ornamental garlands from clouds of garland-trees of various miraculous creations, displaying clouds of lotus-seats of all jewels, pervading all the oceans of methods throughout the <s>dharmadhātu</s> by empowering clouds of all incense, fragrance, and smoke formations, and releasing clouds of all powder-caskets at every mind-moment — I set this in motion for the sake of beings to be guided by seeing, by hearing, by recollection, by the miraculous creation of <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of <s>dharma</s>) emanations, for those whose time of maturation is at hand, for those to be guided by displaying the form-body, for those to be guided by attendance, for those to be guided by awakening, for those to be guided by displaying various miraculous feats, for those to be guided by the display of inconceivable miraculous transformations — according to the dispositions of beings, according to the times, according to the power of turning away from unwholesome <s>karma</s>, according to the power of establishing beings in the arising of wholesome <s>karma</s>, according to the power of accomplishing former great <s>praṇidhānas</s> (vows), according to the impetus of omniscience, according to the power of attaining vast transformations of <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation, according to the power arising from the strength of great compassion brought forth for the protection of all worlds, and according to the aspiration born from the purification of the ocean of great <s>maitrī</s> — because the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is well-received.

body.text: evamahaṃ kulaputra asmin sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayakuśalamūlasaṃcodanabodhisattvavimokṣe pratiṣṭhāya avibhaktarūpadharmatāmavatīrya anantamadhyakāyavarṇasaṃsthānatāṃ saṃdarśayitvā ekaikasmāccaryākāyādanantamadhyān varṇasamudrālokavijñaptyā ekaikasmāccaryāvarṇādanantamadhyān raśmimeghānavasṛjya buddhakṣetrapratibhāsān darśayitvā ekaikasmiṃśca buddhakṣetre anantamadhyāmekaikasmādreśmaranantamadhyān tathāgatotpādān saṃdarśayitvā ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya anantamadhyāni vikurvitāni saṃdarśayamānā pūrvakāṇi kuśalamūlāni saṃcodayāmi / anavaropitāni ca kuśalamūlanyavaropayāmi / avaropitāni ca vipulīkaromi / vipulīkṛtāni ca kuśalamūlāni vivardhayāmi / praticittakṣaṇaṃ ca anantamadhyaṃ sattvadhātumanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau avivartyabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpayāmi //
body.translated_text: Thus I, son of good family, having become established in this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation of urging the maturation of all beings according to their dispositions through wholesome roots, having descended into the <s>dharmatā</s> of undifferentiated form, having displayed an endless and boundless array of bodily appearances and forms, from each wondrous body through the illumination and notification of endless and boundless oceans of appearances, from each wondrous appearance releasing endless and boundless clouds of rays displaying reflections of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and in each <s>Buddha</s>-field from each ray displaying endless and boundless arisings of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and displaying endless and boundless transformations of each <s>Tathāgata</s> — I urge forth the wholesome roots already planted. Those wholesome roots not yet planted, I cause to be planted. Those already planted, I cause to expand. Those wholesome roots already expanded, I cause to grow further. And at every mind-moment, I establish endless and boundless realms of beings on the stage of non-regression toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text:
yatpunaḥ kulaputra evaṃ vadasi - kiyaccirasaṃprasthitāsi devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? kiyanti kalpaśatānyupādāya bodhisattvacārikāṃ carasi? ityetadapi te 'rthaṃ nirdekṣyāmi buddhānubhāvena / akalpāvikalpaparikalpaviṣayaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ jñānamaṇḍalam / na tatra saṃsāradīrghatā vā saṃsārahrasvatā vā prabhāvyate prajñāyate / kalpasaṃkliṣṭatā vā kalpaviśuddhatā vā kalpaparīttatā vā kalpamahadgatatā vā kalpabahutvaṃ vā kalpanānātvaṃ vā kalpanānākaraṇaṃ vā kalpavimātratā vā prabhāvyate prajñāyate vā / tatkasya hetoḥ? prakṛtisvabhāvapariśuddhaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ jñānamaṇḍalaṃ sarvasaṃjñājālanirmuktaṃ sarvāvaraṇaparvatasamatikrāntamāśaye udeti / tacca sarvasattvānāṃ yathāśayaparipākakālavaineyānāmavabhāsaṃ karoti / tadyathā kulaputra sūryamaṇḍale rātriṃdivaṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate, na saṃvasati / astaṃgamite sūryamaṇḍale rātriḥ prajñāyate prabhāvyate / udāgate ca sūryamaṇḍale divasaḥ prajñāyate prabhāvyate / evameva kulaputra avikalpe bodhisattvajñānamaṇḍale sarvakalpavikalpaparikalpā na saṃvidyante / sarvasaṃsārasaṃvasanasaṃjñāgatāni sarvādhvānaśca saṃvidyante / atha ca punarbodhisattvāśayoditā vikalpajñānamaṇḍalaprabhena sarvasattvaparipākakālavaśena kalpasaṃvāsasaṃsārasaṃjñāgatagaṇanāsaṃkhyā prabhāvyate / avikalpajñānamaṇḍale pūrvāntāparāntakalpasaṃvāsasaṃjñāgatasaṃkhyā prabhāvyate / tadyathā kulaputra sūryamaṇḍalaṃ gaganatalagataṃ sarvaratnaparvateṣu sarvaratnadrumeṣu sarvaratnarājeṣu sarvaratnākareṣu sarvasāgareṣu sarvotsasaraḥsu sarvasvacchajalabhājaneṣu sarvajagaccitteṣu ca pratibhāsaprāptaṃ vijñāyate / sattvānāṃ cābhimukhaṃ samudāgacchati / sarvaratnaparamāṇurajaḥsu ca sūryamaṇḍalaṃ pratibhāsaprāptaṃ dṛśyate / na ca punastatsūryamaṇḍalaṃ ratnaparvateṣu saṃbhavati, na ratnadrumeṣu yāvanna paramāṇurajaḥsvanupraviśati / na maṇisphareṣvantargataṃ bhavati / na ratnākareṣvanugacchati / na sāgareṣvavatarati / na sarvodakabhājaneṣvanupraviśati / sarvatra cāntargataṃ dṛśyate / evameva kulaputra bodhisattvo mahāsattva uccalito bhavasamudrādudgatastathāgatadharmadhātugagane dharmasvabhāvagaganagocaravihārī śāntagagananilayaḥ sarvabhavagatyupapattiṣu saṃdṛśyate sarvasattvasadṛśaiḥ kāyaiḥ sattvānāṃ paripākavinayamupādāya / na ca saṃsāradoṣairlipyate, na cyutyupapattiduḥkhairupatapyate,
na ca kalpavikalpaiḥ saṃvasati, na cāsya kalpe dīrghasaṃjñā bhavati na hrasvasaṃjñā / tatkasya hetoḥ?
body.translated_text: As for what you further say, son of good family — 'How long ago, goddess, did you set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening? For how many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have you been practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct?' — I shall explain this meaning to you as well, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>. The <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of knowledge of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, son of good family, is beyond the domain of <s>kalpas</s>, non-conceptualization, and conceptualization. There neither the length of <s>saṃsāra</s> nor the brevity of <s>saṃsāra</s> becomes manifest or is discerned, neither the defilement of <s>kalpas</s> nor the purity of <s>kalpas</s>, neither the smallness of <s>kalpas</s> nor the vastness of <s>kalpas</s>, neither the multiplicity of <s>kalpas</s> nor the diversity of <s>kalpas</s>, neither the differentiation of <s>kalpas</s> nor the discordance of <s>kalpas</s> becomes manifest or is discerned. Why is that? Because, son of good family, the <s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is by its own intrinsic nature primordially pure, freed from the net of all conceptualizations, having transcended all mountains of obstruction — it arises in aspiration. And it illuminates all beings who are to be matured and guided at the proper time according to their dispositions. Just as, son of good family, in the disc of the sun, the count of nights and days is not found and does not dwell therein — when the sun-disc has set, night is discerned and becomes manifest; when the sun-disc has risen, day is discerned and becomes manifest — even so, son of good family, in the non-conceptual <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>bodhisattva</s> knowledge, all conceptualizations and discriminations regarding <s>kalpas</s> are not found, yet all perceptions pertaining to the succession of <s>saṃsāra</s> dwelling-periods and all time-periods are found. And yet again, through the light of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of discriminating knowledge arisen from the <s>bodhisattva's</s> aspiration, by the power of the time of maturation of all beings, the enumeration of perceptions pertaining to <s>saṃsāra</s> dwelling-periods and <s>kalpa</s>-periods becomes manifest. In the non-conceptual <s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge, the count of perceptions pertaining to past and future <s>kalpa</s>-periods becomes manifest. Just as, son of good family, the sun-disc abiding in the expanse of the sky is perceived as having attained reflection in all jewel-mountains, all jewel-trees, all jewel-kings, all jewel-mines, all oceans, all springs and lakes, all vessels of clear water, and in the minds of all beings — and it comes forth facing all beings, and the sun-disc is seen as having attained reflection in all atoms of jewels — yet that sun-disc does not arise in the jewel-mountains, nor in the jewel-trees, nor does it enter even into the atoms, nor is it contained within the jewel-spheres, nor does it follow into the jewel-mines, nor does it descend into the oceans, nor does it enter into all water-vessels, yet it is seen as having entered everywhere — even so, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being), having risen above the ocean of existence, having ascended into the sky of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>dharmadhātu</s>, dwelling in the domain of the sky of the inherent nature of <s>dharma</s>, abiding in the peaceful sky, appears in all states of existence, destinies, and rebirths with bodies resembling all beings, for the sake of maturing and training beings — yet is not stained by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is not tormented by the sufferings of death and rebirth, does not dwell with conceptualizations about <s>kalpas</s>, and regarding <s>kalpas</s> has neither the perception of long nor the perception of short. Why is that?

body.text: tathā hi bodhisattvo 'tyantamaviparyastasaṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsamatikrāntaḥ, svapnopamasarvalokayathābhūtajñānadarśī māyopamasarvalokāvatīrṇo niḥsattvavatīdhātujñānapratilabdho yathābhūtadharmadarśī suvipulakaruṇāmaṇḍalamahāpraṇidhānavaśena sarvasattvābhimukhaḥ saṃdṛśyate paripākavinayamupādāya //
body.translated_text: For indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> has utterly transcended the perversions of perception, mind, and view — he is one who sees all the world as it truly is, as being like a dream, one who has descended into all the world as being like an illusion, one who has attained the knowledge of the realm as being devoid of beings, one who sees <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are, yet who appears face-to-face with all beings by the power of the great vow of his vast and extensive <s>maṇḍala</s> of compassion, undertaking their ripening and discipline. //

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra mahānadyādiṣu yānapātraṃ satatasamitaṃ sattvasaṃtāraṇāya prayuktamapratiprasrabdhaṃ bhavati, yāvajjīvaṃ na cāsya apārime tīre 'bhiniveśo bhavati na pārime, na codakamadhye saṃtiṣṭhate, evameva kulaputra bodhisattvo mahāpāramitāyānapātrabalena saṃsāranadīsrotasaḥ sarvasattvasaṃtāraṇāya pratipanno bhavati / na cāsya apārime tīre utrtrāso bhavati, na pārime tīre kṣemasaṃjñā / atha ca punaḥ satatasamitaṃ sattvasaṃtāraṇāya pratipanno bhavati / aparimitasarvakalpavyavasitena bodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsena ca kalpavimātratāmabhiniviśate / na kalpātikramaṇadīrghasaṃjñāyāmabhiniviṣṭo bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ carati //
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, a ferry-vessel on a great river is constantly engaged in carrying beings across, without ceasing — it remains for a lifetime, and it has no attachment to the near shore nor to the far shore, and it does not stop in the middle of the water — even so, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, by the power of the ferry-vessel of the great <s>pāramitā</s>s, is engaged in carrying all beings across the river-current of <s>saṃsāra</s>. He has no fear of the near shore, no perception of security at the far shore. And yet he is constantly and continually engaged in carrying beings across. Through his dwelling in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct throughout unlimited and all-<s>kalpa</s>-determined [time], he enters into the immeasurability of <s>kalpas</s>. He does not dwell in the perception of the long duration of the passing of <s>kalpas</s> as he practices the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. //

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra dharmadhātuvipulamākāśadhātugaganamaṇḍalaṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu saṃvartamāneṣu vivartamāneṣu vyativṛtteṣu vā avikalpaṃ prakṛtiviśuddhamasaṃkliṣṭamanāvṛtamakhinnamadīrghamanavatīrṇamaparāntakālaṃ sarvakṣetrāṇi dhārayamāṇam, evameva kulaputra bodhisattva āśayajñānagaganatalamaṇḍalaṃ mahāpraṇidhānavātamaṇḍalīparivṛtaṃ sarvadurgatiprapātebhyaḥ sattvān saṃdhārayamāṇaḥ na parikhidyate, sugatipathamupanayamāno na paritrasyati, sarvajñatāpatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayamāno nāvasīdati, sarvakleśairnākulībhavati, saṃsāradoṣairnopalipyate //
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, the sky-<s>maṇḍala</s>, vast as the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, in all world-realms — whether they are forming, dissolving, or have already passed — remains undifferentiated, pure by nature, undefiled, uncovered, unbroken, neither long nor short, unentered, without a final end, bearing all fields — even so, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s sky-surface-<s>maṇḍala</s> of the knowledge of aspiration, surrounded by the wind-<s>maṇḍala</s> of great vows, while bearing beings from all the precipices of bad destinies is not wearied, while leading them to the path of good destinies is not frightened, while establishing them on the paths of omniscience does not sink down, is not bewildered by any <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), and is not stained by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra māyāgatanivṛttasya puruṣasya sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaparipūrṇasya daśa śarīrasthā dharmā na saṃvidyante / katame daśa? yaduta āsaritaṃ vā niḥsaritaṃ vā, śītaṃ voṣṇaṃ vā, kṣudhā vā pipāsā vā, harṣo vā manyuvṛtabhāvo vā, jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaṃ vā pīḍā vā na saṃvidyate / evameva kulaputra bodhisattvasya jñānamāyāgataniryātarūpasyāsaṃbhinnadharmadhātukāyasya sarvabhavagatiṣūpapannasya sarvasattvaparipākāya sarvakalpān saṃvasamānasya daśa dharmā na saṃvidyante / katame daśa? yaduta saṃsārābhilāṣo vā saṃsārabhavagatyupapattinirvedo vā viṣayaratyanunayo vā pratighātacittatā vā upabhoktukāmatā vā sarvakleśaparitāpo vā duḥkhavedanānubhāvo vā viṣayagatyupapattibhayaṃ vā bhavābhilāṣo vā abhiniveśo vā / api tu khalu kulaputra nirdekṣyāmi buddhānubhāvena anāgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ vipulabodhisattvapraṇidhānabalavivardhanatāyai //
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, for a person produced and returned from illusion, complete in all limbs and members, ten bodily conditions are not found — which ten? Namely: coming in or going out, cold or heat, hunger or thirst, happiness or the state of anger, and birth, old age, sickness, and death, or affliction — are not found. Even so, son of good family, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> — whose form is produced and issued from the illusion of knowledge, whose body is the undivided <s>dharmadhātu</s>, who is born in all states of existence and destinies, who dwells through all <s>kalpas</s> for the ripening of all beings — ten <s>dharmas</s> are not found. Which ten? Namely: longing for <s>saṃsāra</s>, or weariness with the births, existences, destinies, and rebirths of <s>saṃsāra</s>, or delight in sense-objects, or a mind of aversion, or the wish to enjoy, or the burning of any <s>kleśa</s>, or the experience of painful sensation, or the fear of the destinies of sense-objects and their births, or longing for existence, or attachment. But indeed, son of good family, I shall declare — by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment and for the augmentation of the power of the vast <s>bodhisattva</s> vows of future <s>bodhisattvas</s>: //

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani lokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ pareṇa paratareṇa yadāsīt - tena kālena tena samayena ratnaprabhā nāma lokadhātuḥ / tasyāṃ khalu punaḥ kulaputra ratnaprabhāyāṃ lokadhātau suprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ suprabhe kalpe daśa buddhasahasrāṇyupapadyante sma / teṣāṃ khalu kulaputra daśānāṃ buddhasahasrāṇāṃ prāthamakalpiko dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān, yena sarvaprathamamanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā / sa khalu punaḥ kulaputra tathāgato madhye
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, son of good family, in the past, beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of oceans of world-realms and far, far beyond — at that time there was a world-realm called <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> (Jewel-Radiance). In that world-realm <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, son of good family, there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Suprabha</s> (Well-Radiant). In that <s>kalpa</s> <s>Suprabha</s>, ten thousand <s>Buddhas</s> arose. Of those ten thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, son of good family, the first-of-the-<s>kalpa</s> was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja</s> (King of the Sky-Lamp of the Sound of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>) — an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, who arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of <s>devas</s> and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s> — by whom unsurpassed perfect awakening was first fully awakened. That <s>Tathāgata</s>, son of good family, in the middle

body.text: cāturdvīpakasya rativyūhāyā rājadhānyā nātidūre upapannaḥ / tasyāḥ khalu punā rativyūhāyā rājadhānyāḥ pūrveṇa suprabhaṃ nāma vanaṣaṇḍamabhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ suprabhe vanaṣaṇḍe ratnakusumamegho nāma bodhimaṇḍo 'bhūt / tasmin khalu ratnakusumameghe bodhimaṇḍe vairocanamaṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsanaṃ prādurabhūt, yatra sa bhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīrājastathāgato niṣadya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / tena ca samayena manuṣyāṇāṃ daśa varṣasahasrāṇi āyuḥ pramāṇamabhūt / atha prāṇātipātiṣu sarveṣu loke prādurbhūteṣu adattādāyiṣu kāmamithyācāriṣu mṛṣāvādiṣu paiśunikeṣu pāruṣikeṣu saṃbhinnapralāpiṣu abhidhyāluṣu vyāpannacitteṣu mithyādṛṣṭiṣu, evaṃ daśasvakuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu vipulībhūteṣu supratiṣṭhiteṣu sa bhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājastathāgataḥ paripūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ bodhimaṇḍagato bodhisattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa lokendrāṇāṃ ca pūrvajinakṛtādhikārāṇāṃ jambudvīpakānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ kuśalamūlaparipācanāya //
body.translated_text: of the four-continent world, not far from the royal capital called <s>Rativyūhā</s> (Array of Delight), arose. To the east of that royal capital <s>Rativyūhā</s> there was a forest-grove called <s>Suprabha</s> (Well-Radiant). In that forest-grove <s>Suprabha</s> there was a <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Ratnakusumamegha</s> (Cloud of Jewel-Flowers). In that <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> <s>Ratnakusumamegha</s> there appeared a <s>Vairocanamaṇipadmagarbha</s> (Vairocana Jewel-Lotus-Womb) lion-throne, where that <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīrāja</s>, having sat down, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. At that time, the lifespan of human beings was ten thousand years. Then, when killing of living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, speaking falsehood, slander, harsh speech, idle gossip, covetousness, malicious mind, and wrong views — when these ten unwholesome courses of action had become widespread and well-established in the world — that <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s>, dwelling at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> for a full thousand years, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>bodhisattvas</s>, to the lords of the world who had performed former service under the <s>Jinas</s>, and for the ripening of the wholesome roots of the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. //

body.text: tena ca samayena tasyāṃ rativyūhāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ jayaprabho nāma rājā abhūt / tena adattādāyināṃ puruṣāṇāṃ caurāṇāṃ kilbiṣakāriṇāṃ prāṇātipātināṃ kāmamithyācāriṇāṃ mṛṣāvādināṃ paiśunikānāṃ pāruṣikāṇāṃ saṃbhinnapralāpināṃ abhidhyālūnāṃ vyāpannacittānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭikānāmadharmarāgaraktānāṃ viṣamalobhābhibhūtānāṃ mithyādharmaparigatānāṃ kṛtapāpānāṃ kṛtaraudrāṇāmakṛtapuṇyānāmakṛtabhayabhīrutrāṇānāmamātṛjñānāmapitṛjñānāmaśrāmaṇyānāmabrāhmaṇyānāmamanāryajñānāmaparādhināmanekāni śatasahasrāṇi cārake prakṣiptānyabhūvan damanārthāya / rājñaḥ khalu punaḥ jayaprabhasya vijitāvī nāma putro 'bhūdabhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgato 'ṣṭaviṃśatibhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇairupetaḥ / atha sa sarasvatisaṃgītiprāsādābhirūḍho mahāstrīgaṇaparivāraparivṛtaḥ teṣāṃ cārakāvaruddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ vividhagāḍhabandhanabaddhānāṃ bhairavamutkrośaśabdamaśrauṣīt / śrutvā ca punarudvignaḥ saṃvignacitto mahākaruṇāsaṃjātaḥ tasmātprāsādādavatīrya taccārake praviśya adrākṣīttāṃścārakagahanaprakṣiptān sattvān nānāhaḍinigaḍakaṭakakuṇḍalaśṛṅkhalākhalīnabandhanabaddhān parasparaśarīravinibaddhān mahāndhakāraprakṣiptān dhūmatimirāvṛtān viṣamavātopahataśarīrān dhamanīsaṃtatagātrān kṣutpipāsāparipīḍitān nagnān nirvasanān pāṃśurajaḥsaṃmrakṣitaśarīrāṃśca keśābhicchāditakāyān urunigaḍabandhanabaddhān vividhāḥ kāraṇāḥ kāryamāṇān duḥkhavedanāmanubhavamānānanekavidhān kāraṇān paridevavipralāpān pramuñcamānān / sa tān dṛṣṭvā mahatkāruṇyamutpādya udārakaruṇāśayasaṃjātaḥ parahitādhāno 'dbhutacetāścārakagahanagatān sattvān samāśvāsayāmāsa bandhanavipramokṣāya / sa teṣāṃ sattvānāmabhayaṃ datvā yena rājā jayaprabhastenopasaṃkramya evamāhayatkhalu devo jānīyāt - mayā bandhanāgārabandhanagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāruṇyādabhayaṃ dattam / te mucyeran / atha jayaprabheṇa rājñā sarvāṇi pañcāmātyaśatāni saṃnipātya paripṛṣṭāniyuṣmākaṃ kathaṃ bhavati? ta āhuḥ - ete rājakośavilopino rājño vadhāya parākrāntāḥ / rājño 'ntaḥpure parākramanto gṛhītāḥ / vadhārhā hyete / vadha evaiṣāṃ daṇḍo bandhanagatānāṃ vā maraṇam / yo 'pyeṣāmanugrahāya pratipadyate, so 'pi rājño 'parādhī //
body.translated_text: At that time, in that royal capital <s>Rativyūhā</s>, there was a king named <s>Jayaprabha</s> (Victory-Radiance). By him, many hundreds of thousands of men — thieves, takers of what is not given, criminals, killers of living beings, practitioners of sexual misconduct, speakers of falsehood, slanderers, speakers of harsh words, indulgers in idle gossip, the covetous, the malicious-minded, holders of wrong views, those inflamed by unlawful desire, overpowered by uneven greed, possessed of wrong <s>dharma</s>, doers of evil, doers of cruelty, without merit, without having created refuge from fear, ungrateful toward mother, ungrateful toward father, not respecting <s>śramaṇas</s>, not respecting <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, not knowing what is noble, offenders — had been cast into prison for the purpose of taming. Now, King <s>Jayaprabha</s> had a son named <s>Vijitāvin</s> (Victorious) — handsome, inspiring, lovely to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious complexion, possessing twenty-eight marks of a great being. Then he, having ascended the palace of musical recitals, surrounded by a great retinue of women, heard the terrifying cries and shouts of those beings imprisoned and confined. Having heard them, alarmed and agitated in mind, great compassion having arisen, he descended from that palace, entered that prison, and saw those beings cast into the depths of the prison — bound with various fetters, shackles, iron rings, chains, and constraints, their bodies bound together, cast into great darkness, enveloped in smoke and gloom, their bodies afflicted by noxious winds, their limbs stretched by sinews, tormented by hunger and thirst, naked, without garments, their bodies smeared with dust and dirt, their bodies covered with hair, bound with thigh-shackles and fetters, subjected to various tortures, experiencing painful sensations, releasing various cries of lamentation and wailing. Having seen them, generating great pity, with a sublime disposition of compassion arisen, intent on the welfare of others, with a wondrous mind, he consoled those beings gone into the depths of the prison and sought to free them from bondage. Having given fearlessness to those beings, he approached King <s>Jayaprabha</s> and spoke thus: 'May the lord know: I, out of compassion, have given fearlessness to the beings confined in the prison. May they be released!' Then King <s>Jayaprabha</s>, having summoned all five hundred ministers, asked them: 'What is your opinion?' They said: 'These are plunderers of the royal treasury, those who attempted to slay the king, those who were caught trespassing in the king's inner palace. They deserve execution. Execution alone is their punishment — or death in prison. And whoever undertakes to show them favor is also an offender against the king.' //

body.text: atha khalu sa vijitāvī rājaputro mahākaruṇāparipīḍitastānamātyān provācatathāstu yathā yūyaṃ vadatha / tadathotsṛjatainānaparādhinaḥ puruṣān / ahameṣāmathārya sarvaduḥkhavedanāḥ saṃsoḍhumutsahe / yad yuṣmābhireṣāṃ karaṇīyaṃ tanmama kuruta / ahameṣāṃ bandhanavipramokṣāya vividhakāraṇāparigataḥ kāyajīvitaṃ parityajāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? yadyahametān sattvānasmādbandhanānna śaknomi mocayitum, tatkathaṃ śakyaṃ traidhātukabandhanāgāragatān sattvāṃstṛṣṇāpāśavinibaddhān avidyāgahanagatān mohāndhakāraprakṣiptān dāridryaduḥkhaprapīḍitān gambhīragahanadurgatipratipannān visaṃsthitavivarṇaśarīrān nirastasarvendriyaprayogān vibhrāntamānasān aniḥsaraṇadarśinaḥ ālokavirahitāṃstāṃstraidhātukābhiniviṣṭān puṇyajñānasaṃbhāravikalān jñānāyatanaparibhraṣṭān nānākleśamalinacittān duḥkhapañjaraprakṣiptān māravaśagatān jātijarāramaṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaprapīḍitān parimocayitum //
body.translated_text: Then indeed that prince <s>Vijitāvin</s>, overwhelmed by great compassion, spoke to those ministers: 'So be it, as you say. Then release these offending men. I am prepared to endure all their painful sensations on their behalf. Whatever punishment you would inflict upon them, inflict it upon me. I renounce my bodily life for the liberation of these from bondage, taking upon myself their various tortures. For what reason? If I cannot free these beings from this bondage, then how could I free beings confined in the prison of the three realms, bound by the noose of craving, gone into the thicket of ignorance, cast into the darkness of delusion, oppressed by the suffering of poverty, fallen into the deep thicket of bad destinies, with ill-proportioned and discolored bodies, with all their faculties' efforts cast away, with bewildered minds, seeing no way of escape, devoid of light, attached to the three realms, deficient in the equipment of merit and knowledge, fallen from the abode of knowledge, with minds defiled by various <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), cast into the cage of suffering, gone under the power of <s>Māra</s>, oppressed by birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress?' //

body.text: atha khalu vijitāvī rājakumārastān sarvān bandhanagatān sattvāṃstasmādbandhanāgārātparimocayati sma ātmaparityāgena sarvaparivāreṇa sarvadhanaskandhena / sa tān parimocya yatteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhopadhānaṃ tadutsṛjya na vinivartayate sma / atha tāni pañcāmātyaśatānyūrdhvabāhūni utkrośamānāni jayaprabhaṃ rājānamupasaṃkramya evamāhuḥ - yatkhalu devo jānīyāt - vijitāvinaḥ kumārasya cchandenāyaṃ rājakośo vilupyate / asmākamapi sarveṣāṃ jīvite saṃśayaḥ / yadi devo vijitāvino rājakumārasya nigrahaṇaṃ ca kariṣyati, devasya nacireṇa jīvitaṃ na bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the prince <s>Vijitāvin</s> freed all those beings confined in bondage from that prison — through the renunciation of himself, of all his retinue, of all his wealth. Having freed them, he released whatever was the basis of suffering for those beings, and did not turn back. Then those five hundred ministers, raising their arms, crying out, approached King <s>Jayaprabha</s> and spoke thus: 'May the lord know: by the will of Prince <s>Vijitāvin</s>, the royal treasury is being plundered! All our lives are in danger. If the lord does not restrain Prince <s>Vijitāvin</s>, the lord's life will not last long.' //

body.text: atha khalu jayaprabho rājā kupito vijitāvinaṃ rājakumāraṃ saha tairaparādhibhiḥ puruṣairvadhāyotsṛṣṭavān / tasya mātā janetrī tacchrutvā udvignā strīsahasraparivṛtā pramuktakeśī nirābharaṇagātrī svamukhaṃ vyālupya urastāḍayantī pāṃśvavakīrṇaśiraskā krandamānā ārtasvaraṃ rudantī rājānamupasaṃkramya saparivārā caraṇayornipatya evaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa - pramuñca deva vijitāvinaṃ rājakumāram / dehi deva kumārasya jīvitam / atha rājā vijitāvinaṃ kumāraṃ saṃmukhaṃ sthāpayitvā evamāhaṃ - utsṛja kumāra etānaparādhino manuṣyān / yadi notsrakṣyasi, tadeṣāmarthāya vadhamupagamiṣyasīti / sa vadhamabhyupagatavānasaṃlīnena cittena asaṃkucitena sarvajñatārambaṇaprayuktena parahitapariṇatena mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamena / tasya janetryā rājā jayaprabho 'rdhamāsaṃ yācito darśanāya-ardhamāsaṃ kumāro dānaṃ dadātu yasya yenārthaḥ / tato yathākāmaṃ karaṇīyaḥ / bhavatu tattatheti rājñānujñatām / atha tasyā rativyūhāyā rājadhānyā uttareṇa pūrvayajñavāṭaprakṛtaṃ sūryaprabhaṃ nāma mahodyānam / tatra kumāro 'bhiniṣkramya yasya yenārthaḥ tasya tatprādāt / tena nirargalaṃ yajñaṃ yajatā ardhamāsaṃ vividhā dānavidhayo dattāḥ / annamannārthibhyaḥ pānavastrapuṣpamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāratnābharaṇavividhavibhūṣaṇasarvopakaraṇaviṣayastadarthibhyo nisṛṣṭaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed King <s>Jayaprabha</s>, enraged, condemned Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> to death along with those offenders. His mother, having heard this, was distressed; surrounded by a thousand women, with hair disheveled, her limbs stripped of ornaments, scratching her own face, beating her breast, her head covered with dust, wailing, crying out in a voice of anguish, she approached the king and, together with her retinue, fell at his feet and implored him thus: 'Release, O Lord, Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s>! Grant the prince his life!' Then the king, having placed Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> before him, spoke thus: 'Release, O prince, these offending men! If you will not release them, you will undergo execution on their behalf.' He accepted execution with an unshrinking mind, uncontracted, engaged in the aspiration for omniscience, dedicated to the welfare of others, preceded by great compassion. His mother entreated King <s>Jayaprabha</s> for half a month for a meeting — 'Let the prince give gifts for half a month to whoever has need of whatever; after that, do with him as you wish.' 'So be it,' the king consented. Now, to the north of the royal capital <s>Rativyūhā</s>, there was a great park called <s>Sūryaprabha</s>, previously prepared as a sacrificial ground. There the prince went forth and gave to each whatever they needed. By him, performing an unrestricted sacrifice for half a month, various kinds of gifts were given — food to those who sought food; drink, clothing, flowers, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, jewel-ornaments, various adornments, and all provisions to those who sought them. //

body.text: tataḥ paścime divase sarvajanakāyaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ / rājāmātyastrīgaṇaśreṣṭhigṛhapatinaigamajanapadāḥ
body.translated_text: Then on the last day, the entire populace assembled — the king, ministers, women's guilds, merchants, householders, townspeople, and country-folk

body.text: sarvapāṣaṇḍāśca saṃnipatitāḥ / sa ca bhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājastathāgataḥ sattvaparipākavinayakālamāgamayya taṃ yajñavāṭamupasaṃkrānto devendragaṇaparivṛto nāgendragaṇaparivṛto nāgendrasaṃpūjito yakṣendrakāyābhinato gandharvendrābhiṣṭuto 'surendrapraṇataśarīraścūḍāmaṇivibhūṣitaprasannacitto garuḍendrapūjāvidhibhirabhiprakīrṇaḥ prītimanobhiḥ kinnarendaiḥ paripūjitaḥ stutisaṃgītisaṃcodito mahoragendrasaṃprekṣitāvalokitavadanaḥ / adrākṣīt sa mahājanakāyo vijitāvī ca rājakumārastaṃ bhagavantaṃ dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ guptaṃ jitendriyaṃ nāgamiva sudāntaṃ hradamivācchaṃ viprasannamanāvilaṃ mahatā buddhavikurvitaprātihāryeṇa mahatyā buddhavṛṣabhitayā virocayamānaṃ buddhādhipateyenābhibhavantaṃ buddhamāhātmyatayā prabhāsayamānaṃ mahābuddhalakṣaṇānuvyañjanavibhūṣaṇopaśobhitakāyaṃ sarvalokaṃ buddhaprabhāmaṇḍalāvabhāsena spharamāṇaṃ buddharaśmibhiravabhāsayamānaṃ sarvaromavivarebhyo gandharatnārciścakrāṇi pramuñcamānaṃ buddhakṣetraprakampanena sarvalokaṃ saṃkampayamānaṃ sarvavyūhameghapravarṣaṇena buddhavikrameṇa sarvasattvakleśaprajahanena buddheryāpathena sarvasattvaprītivegavivardhanena buddhadarśanaprabhāvenopasaṃkramamāṇam / dṛṣṭvā ca bhagavato 'ntike cittamabhiprasādayāmāsuḥ //
body.translated_text: and all the sectarians assembled. And that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s> (Lamp-King of the Sky-Cloud of the Sound of the Dharma-Wheel), knowing the time for the ripening and disciplining of beings had come, approached that sacrificial ground — surrounded by hosts of <s>Devendras</s>, surrounded by hosts of <s>Nāgendras</s>, worshipped by <s>Nāgendras</s>, bowed to in body by <s>Yakṣendras</s>, praised by <s>Gandharvendras</s>, with body prostrated to by <s>Asurendras</s>, with a serene mind adorned with crest-jewel ornaments, showered with worship-rites by <s>Garuḍendras</s>, worshipped by <s>Kinnarendras</s> with joyful minds, attended by chants and hymns, gazed upon with faces looked to by <s>Mahoragendras</s>. That great assembly of people and Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> saw that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhat</s> Perfectly Awakened One <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s>, approaching from afar — pleasing, beautiful to behold, with senses at peace, with mind at peace, controlled, with senses mastered, well-tamed like a <s>nāga</s>, clear like a lake, with mind serene and untroubled — shining with the great miraculous display of the <s>Buddha</s>'s magical power, overwhelming with the great eminence of the <s>Buddha</s>, illuminating with the majesty of the <s>Buddha</s>, with body adorned and beautified by the great marks and minor marks of a <s>Buddha</s>, pervading all the world with the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>'s halo of light, illuminating with the rays of the <s>Buddha</s>, releasing wheels of fragrant jewel-flames from all the hair-pores, shaking the entire world with the trembling of the <s>Buddha</s>-field, raining down clouds of all arrays with the prowess of the <s>Buddha</s>, destroying the defilements of all beings with the deportment of the <s>Buddha</s>, increasing the force of joy of all beings with the splendor of the <s>Buddha</s>'s appearance — approaching. And having seen him, they generated serene faith in the presence of the Blessed One. //

body.text: atha khalu vijitāvī rājakumāraḥ sa ca mahān janakāyastaṃ bhagavantaṃ dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājaṃ tathāgataṃ dūrādeva pratyudgamya prasannacittaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya pādau śirasābhivandya anekavidhayā pūjayā saṃpūjya evaṃ vācamabhāṣata - ehi bhagavan, ehi sugata / samanvāhṛtāḥ smaḥ tathāgatena, anuparigṛhītāḥ smaḥ sugatena / atha khalu vijitāvī rājakumārastasya bhagavato 'grāsanamupadarśayan evamāha - niṣīdatu bhagavān / idamāsanaṃ prajñaptam / tato bhagavata upasaṃkrāmatastadāsanaṃ śucigarbhaśarīrakāyikābhirdevatābhirbuddhānubhāvena gandhamaṇirājapadmagarbhamadhiṣṭhitam / nyaṣīdadbhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājastathāgatastatrāsane, āsanaparivāreṣu ca bodhisattvāḥ / tasya sahadarśanena tasyāṃ parṣadi sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvavyādhayaḥ praśāntāḥ, sarvāvaraṇanivaraṇavigatāścāryadharmāṇāṃ bhājanībhūtāḥ saṃsthitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> and that great assembly of people went out to meet that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s> from afar, and with serene minds, prostrating with their whole bodies, bowing their heads at his feet, worshipping with manifold forms of worship, spoke these words: 'Come, O Blessed One! Come, O <s>Sugata</s>! We have been remembered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; we have been embraced by the <s>Sugata</s>!' Then Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s>, showing the foremost seat to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'Let the Blessed One be seated! This seat has been prepared.' Then, as the Blessed One approached, that seat was consecrated by deities of pure womb-bodies through the power of the <s>Buddha</s> with a fragrant jewel-king lotus-womb. The Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s> sat upon that seat, and the <s>bodhisattvas</s> upon the surrounding seats. At the very sight of him, all diseases of all beings in that assembly were pacified, all obstructions and hindrances departed, and they became fit vessels for the wondrous <s>dharmas</s> and remained so. //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājastathāgatastān sattvān bhājanabhūtān viditvā anupūrveṇa kathāmakārṣīt / yaduta hetumaṇḍalaprabhāsaṃ nāma sūtrāntaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa / svarāṅgasahasrasaṃprayuktaṃ ca vadanāntarāt sarvadharmāṅgasaṃprayuktaṃ sarvajaganmantrasāgaraniruktinirnādanirghoṣaṃ niścārayāmāsa / atha tāvadeva tataḥ parṣado 'śītīnāṃ prāṇiniyutānāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurutpannam / bahubhiśca prāṇiniyutairaśaikṣabhūmiranuprāptā / daśa ca prāṇisahasrāṇi mahāyāne vinītāni, yaduta samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāmahāpraṇidhānaparipūrinaye 'vatāritāni / evaṃ tasya bhagavato mahābuddhavikurvitena dharmacakraṃ pravartayamānasya daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ sattvā mahāyāne vinayamagaman / anantamadhyāśca sattvā daśadiśi loke nānābuddhakṣetraprasarasamavasaraṇeṣvapāyabhūmiṃ vinivartayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s>, knowing those beings had become fit vessels, gave a gradual discourse — namely, he illuminated the <s>sūtrānta</s> called '<s>Hetumaṇḍalaprabhāsa</s>' (Illumination of the Maṇḍala of Causes). And from his mouth he emitted the resounding, proclaiming voice of the ocean of <s>mantras</s> of all beings, connected with a thousand musical limbs, connected with the limbs of all <s>dharmas</s>, in all languages. Then immediately, from that assembly, in eighty <s>niyutas</s> of beings the pure, stainless <s>dharma</s>-eye arose regarding <s>dharmas</s>. And many <s>niyutas</s> of beings attained the stage of no-more-training. And ten thousand beings were established in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — namely, they were led into the method of fulfilling the great vow of the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. Thus, as the Blessed One turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel with the great miraculous display of the <s>Buddha</s>, beings equal to the atoms of a hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions were established in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And infinite, innumerable beings in the ten directions of the world, in the convergences of the expanses of various <s>Buddha</s>-fields, were turned back from the realm of bad destinies.

body.text: gaṇanāsamatikrāntāśca sattvāḥ svargopapattipathe pratiṣṭhāpitā abhūvan / vijitāvī ca rājakumāra imaṃ sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratyalabhata //
body.translated_text: And beings beyond counting were established on the path of rebirth in heaven. And Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> attained the <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Arising from the Root of Merit of Stimulating [Beings] According to the Dispositions for the Ripening of All Beings' (<s>Sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhava</s>). //

body.text: syātkhalu punaste kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vijitāvī rājakumāro 'bhūt, yena tatsvakāyajīvitaṃ parityajya sarvadhanaskandhaparivāraṃ parityajya sarvamānuṣyakaṃ ca jīvalokasukhaṃ parityajya te bandhanagatāḥ sattvāḥ tasmādbandhanāt parimokṣitāḥ? sa ca nirargalo mahāyajño yaṣṭaḥ? sa ca bhagavān dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ārāgitaḥ? tasya ca tathāgatasya sahadarśanenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam? eṣa ca sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ? na khalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena vijitāvī nāma rājakumāro 'bhūvam / mayā tadvijitāvīrājakumārabhūtena mahākaruṇāprapīḍitena sarvajagaddhitapratipannena traidhātukāniśritena vipākāpratikāṅkṣiṇā yaśaskīrtināmānabhinandinā ātmānamanutkarṣayatā paramapaṃsayatā sarvavastvanabhiniviṣṭena bhavasaṃjñoccalitena traidhātukānabhinandinā lokaviṣayasukhavimukhena tathāgataviṣayāvimukhena bodhyāśayaviśuddhena adhyāśayavajrapariniṣpannena sarvajaganmahāmaitrīprayogena sarvajaganmahākaruṇāduḥkhavyupaśamasaṃprayuktena tathāgatabalādhyāśayamadhyālambatā bodhisattvamārgaṃ pariśodhayatā mahāyānavyūhaniryāṇapathamalaṃkurvatā sarvajñatāmārgamabhivilokayatā imānyevaṃ duṣkarāṇi kṛtāni / evaṃ cirapratilabdhaḥ kulaputra mayaiṣa sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Do you perhaps think, son of good family, that Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s> at that time and on that occasion was someone else — he who, abandoning his own body and life, abandoning all his wealth, possessions, and retinue, abandoning all human worldly happiness, liberated those beings from their bondage while himself condemned to execution? And that unrestricted great sacrifice was offered? And that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhat</s> Perfectly Awakened One <s>Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja</s> was pleased? And at the very sight of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening was generated? And this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Arising from the Root of Merit of Stimulating [Beings] According to the Dispositions for the Ripening of All Beings' was attained? You should not see it thus, son of good family! I myself was at that time and on that occasion Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s>. By me, being that Prince <s>Vijitāvī</s>, pressed by great compassion, engaged in the welfare of all beings, not relying on the three realms, not expecting karmic fruition, not delighting in fame, glory, or renown, not exalting myself, not disparaging others, not clinging to any possession, with the notion of existence dislodged, not delighting in the three realms, averse to worldly pleasures, not averse to the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with purified aspiration for awakening, with resolute intention perfected like vajra, with the practice of great loving-kindness toward all beings, engaged in pacifying the suffering of all beings through great compassion, with resolute intention relying on the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s ten powers, purifying the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, adorning the path of going forth through the array of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, gazing upon the path to omniscience — these difficult deeds were performed. Thus, son of good family, this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Arising from the Root of Merit of Stimulating [Beings] According to the Dispositions for the Ripening of All Beings' was attained by me long ago. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyāni tāni tena samayena pañcāmātyaśatānyabhūvan, yaiḥ sa rājā jayaprabho vitathaṃ vijñāpya mama vadhāyodyojitaḥ? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / imāni tāni pañca puruṣaśatāni yāni devadattena bhagavato vadhāyodyojitāni / tāni ca bhagavatā vinīya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāni - bhaviṣyatyanāgate 'dhvani sumeruparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kalpaiḥ ekasmin suprabhanāmadheye kalpe pañca buddhaśatāni nānābuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāni nānājanmakulagotrasaṃbhavāni nānāmātāpitṛvyapadeśāni nānājanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanāni nānābhiniṣkramaṇavikurvitāni nānābodhivṛkṣaprabhāsaṃdarśanāni nānābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamukhāni nānāmārabhaṅgasaṃdarśanāni nānābhisaṃbodhivikurvitasaṃdarśanāni nānādharmacakrapravartananayanāmaniruktīni nānāsūtrāntanayanirdeśāni nānāvākpatharutodāhārāṇi nānāparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhāni nānāprabhāmaṇḍalaprabhāvyūhapramuñcanāni nānāyuḥpramāṇāni nānāśāsanādhiṣṭhānāni nānāśāsanavijñaptīni nānānāmadheyāni mahākaruṇāśarīrāṇi, yeṣāṃ prāthamakalpiko mahākāruṇiko nāma tathāgato ratnaprabhāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / tasyāmeva lokadhātau dvitīyaḥ sarvajagaddhitapraṇidhānacandro nāma tathāgata utpatsyate / tṛtīyo mahākaruṇāsiṃho
body.translated_text: Do you perhaps think, son of good family, that those five hundred ministers at that time and on that occasion were others — they who, by deceiving the king <s>Jayaprabha</s> with falsehoods, had me condemned to death? You should not see it thus! These are those very five hundred men who were incited by <s>Devadatta</s> to [attempt] the murder of the Blessed One. And they were disciplined by the Blessed One and given the prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening: 'In the future, after <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of <s>Sumeru</s>, in a single <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Suprabha</s>, five hundred <s>Buddhas</s> will arise — with various <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities and arrays, born in various birth-families and lineages, with various designations of mothers and fathers, displaying various birth-miracles, with various miracles of going forth, displaying various radiances of <s>bodhi</s>-trees, with various modes of approaching the seat of awakening, displaying various defeats of <s>Māra</s>, displaying various miracles of perfect awakening, with various methods and languages of turning the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, with various <s>sūtrānta</s> method-teachings, with various utterances of speech-paths, with various arrays of assembly-maṇḍalas, releasing various arrays of radiance-halo-splendors, with various life-spans, with various establishments of teachings, with various communications of the teaching, with various names, with bodies of great compassion — of whom the first in that <s>kalpa</s> will be the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahākāruṇika</s> (The Greatly Compassionate), who will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening in the world-realm <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>. In that very world-realm, the second <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvajagaddhitapraṇidhānacandra</s> (Moon of the Vow for the Welfare of All Beings) will arise. The third

body.text: nāma tathāgata utpatsyate / caturthaḥ sarvalokahitaiṣī nāma tathāgata utpatsyate / yāvatsarvapaścimo vaidyarājo nāma tathāgata utpatsyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahākaruṇāsiṃha</s> (Lion of Great Compassion) will arise. The fourth <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvalokahitaiṣī</s> (Desirer of the Welfare of All Worlds) will arise. Up to the very last, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vaidyarāja</s> (King of Physicians) will arise.' //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anye te tena kālena tena samayena aparādhinaḥ puruṣā rājakilbiṣakāriṇo 'bhūvan ye te mayā vadhyaghātavaśagatāḥ svakāyajīvitaṃ parityajya tato bandhanāt parimokṣitāḥ? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ime te krakucchandapūrvagamā bhadrakalpikāstathāgatāḥ / tadanyāni ca daśaḥ bodhisattvāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi yairbhagavato 'nantabalavighuṣṭanirnāditaśrīsaṃbhavamatestathāgatasya darśanena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam, yānyetarhi daśasu dikṣu bodhicaryāṃ caranti / ime ca sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayanti vipulīkurvanti //
body.translated_text: Do you perhaps think, son of good family, that those offending men, those royal criminals, whom I liberated from that bondage by abandoning my own body and life while being condemned to execution — were they others at that time? You should not see it thus! These are those <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the Auspicious <s>Kalpa</s> (<s>Bhadrakalpa</s>), beginning with <s>Krakucchanda</s>. And there are also ten <s>asaṃkhyeya</s> hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who, upon seeing the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Anantabalavighuṣṭanirnāditaśrīsaṃbhavamati</s>, generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — they who now practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in the ten directions. And they cultivate and expand this <s>bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Arising from the Root of Merit of Stimulating [Beings] According to the Dispositions for the Ripening of All Beings.' //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jayaprabho nāma rājā abhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / satyakaḥ sa mahāvādī tena kālena tena samayena jayaprabho nāma rājā abhūt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājaparivāro 'bhūdantaḥpurastryāgāradauvārikapārṣadyā vā anuyātrikā vā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / imāni tāni ṣaṣṭirnigranthasahasrāṇi, yāni satyakena mahāvādinā bhagavataḥ sakāśamupanītāni, vādidhvajadhāraṇatayā bhagavato vādāyopasaṃkrāntāni / tāni ca sarvāṇi bhagavatā vyākṛtānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / nānābuddhakṣetravyūhairnānākalpairnānānāmadheyaistathāgatāṃ loke utpatsyante //

sa khalu punaḥ kulaputra vijitāvī rājakumāro mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñātastān bandhanagatān sattvān parimocya sphītāṃ vasumatīṃ dhanakanakaratnasamṛddhāmapahāya putradāraṃ cotsṛjya tasya bhagavato dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājasya tathāgatasyāntike prāvrajat / pravrajitvā pañca varṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryamacarat / etasminnantare daśa samādhimukhasahasrāṇi saṃniṣpādayāmāsa / daśa ca dhāraṇīmukhasahasrāṇi pratyalabhata / daśa ca abhijñānayasahasrāṇyavakrāntāni / daśa bodhisattvamahānidhānasahasrāṇi pratilabhate sma / daśa cāsya sarvajñatāvegasahasrāṇyājātāni / daśa cānena kṣāntimukhasahasrāṇi pariśodhitāni / daśa cittanidhyaptisahasrāṇyabhinirhṛtāni / daśa ca bodhisattvabalaśarīrāṇi saṃvardhitāni / daśa ca bodhisattvajñānamukhasahasrāṇyavakrāntāni / daśa cāsya prajñāpāramitānayasahasrāṇyājātāni / daśa ca buddhasahasradarśanadiṅbhukhasahasrāṇyāmukhībhūtāni / daśa ca anena bodhisattvapraṇidhānasahasrāṇyabhinirhṛtāni / sa evaṃ dharmasamanvāgataḥ praticittakṣaṇe daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇyākrāmati sma / ekaikasyāṃ ca lokadhātau cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe daśa buddhasahasrāṇi pūrvāntāparāntato 'nusmarati sma / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ daśa buddhanirmāṇasamudrasahasrāṇi daśadikprasṛtānyavataranti sma / cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe daśa buddhakṣetrasahasraparyāpannān sarvasattvānadrākṣīt / nānāgatyupapannāṃścyavata

upapadyamānān hīnān praṇītān sugatān durgatān suvarṇān durvarṇān yathākāmopagatān / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ cyutyupapattīravatarati sma / cittaparivartān cittacaritāni cintānantaryatāmāśayanānātvamindriyasāgarānapi prayogaprasarānapi karmāvasānamapi paripākavinayakālamapi avatarati sma //

sa khalu punaḥ kulaputra vijitāvī rājakumārastataścyutvā tatraiva jambudvīpe rativyūhāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ tasminneva rājakule upapadya cakravartirājyaiścaryaṃ pratyalabhata / tena cakravartirājabhūtena tasya bhagavato dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparājasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasyānantaraṃ dharmagaganābhyudgataśrīrājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva bodhimaṇḍe śakrabhūtena devendragarbho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tatraiva lokadhātau suyāmadevarājabhūtena dharaṇīśrīparvatatejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātau saṃtuṣitadevarājabhūtena dharmacakraprabhanirghoṣarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātau sunirmitadevarājabhūtena gaganakāntarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātau vaśavartidevarājabhūtenānavamardabalaketurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātāvasurendrabhūtena sarvadharmanigarjitarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva lokadhātau brahmendrabhūtena dharmacakranirmāṇasamantapratibhāsanirghoṣo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / iti hi kulaputra etāṃstathāgatān pramukhān kṛtvā tasyāmeva ratnaprabhāyāṃ lokadhātau tasminneva suprabhe kalpe daśa buddhasahasrāṇyudapadyanta / sarve ca te tathāgatā vijitāvinā rājakumāreṇārāgitāḥ / tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputra suprabhasya mahākalpasyānantaraṃ suraśmirnāma kalpo 'bhūt / tasmiṃśca suraśmikalpe daśa buddhasahasrāṇyupapadyanta / ahaṃ ca tasmin kalpe mahāmatirnāma rājā abhūvam / tena me rājabhūtena lakṣaṇaśrīparvato nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe gṛhapatibhūtena saṃvṛtaskandho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe amātyabhūtena vimalavatso nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe 'surendrabhūtena veśadhārī nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe vṛkṣadevatābhūtena lakṣaṇasumerurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe sārthavāhabhūtena vimalabāhurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe nagaradevatābhūten siṃhavikrāntagāmī nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe vaiśravaṇabhūtena devendracūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe gandharvarājabhūtena dharmodgatakīrtināma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ tasminneva kalpe kumbhāṇḍendrabhūtena avabhāsamakuṭī nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ //
iti hi kulaputra mayaitān daśa tathāgatān pramukhān kṛtvā tatra suraśmikalpe ṣaṣṭirbuddhakoṭya ārāgitāḥ / nānopapattikāyikayā sarve ca me tathāgatāḥ pūjitāḥ / ekaikaṃ

ca tathāgatamupasaṃkrāmantyā anantamadhyaḥ sattvadhāturanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācitaḥ / ekaikaṃ ca tathāgatamupasaṃkrāmantyā nānāsamādhimukhāni pratilabdhāni / nānādhāraṇīmukhāni nānābhinirhāranayā nānāpratisaṃvinnayābhinirhārā nānāsarvajñatānayānugamā nānādharmālokamukhapratilābhanayā nānājñānanayānugamavicārā nānādiksamudrapraveśāvabhāsā nānākṣetrasamudrāvatārapraveśāvabhāsā nānātathāgatadarśanasamudravijñaptyavabhāsāḥ pratilabdhāḥ, avakrāntā viśuddhāḥ saṃvardhitāḥ prasṛtāḥ pratisṛtāḥ / yathā ca tatra suraśmikalpe tathāgatā ārāgitāḥ, tathā sarvatralokadhātusamudraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu ye kecittathāgatā upapadyante, ye 'pi tadanyebhyo lokadhātubhya āgatya tathāgatā dharmaṃ deśayamāsuḥ, teṣāṃ mayā sarveṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantikāddharmadeśanā śrutā, śrutvā ca saṃdhāritā / sarve ca mayā te tathāgatā ārāgitā abhirādhitāḥ / teṣāṃ ca me buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantikādeṣa sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdho nānāpratilābhanayanānāvimokṣanayamukhaiḥ //
atha khalu sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā rātridevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetaṃ vimokṣanayaṃ paridīpayantī saṃdarśayamānā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -

children.text: acintyametaṃ paramaṃ vimokṣaṃ māṃ pṛcchasi tvaṃ khalu yatprapītaḥ /
sarvānatikramya babhūva ramyā ratnaprabhā yā khalu lokadhātuḥ // 13 //
ārāgitāste khalu me munīndrā vimokṣametaṃ paribhāvayantyā // 14 //

body.text: jayaprabho 'syāṃ nṛpatirbabhūva dharmeṇa yastānanuśāsti sattvān /
putro 'sya nāmnā vijitāvirāsīt prāsādiko lakṣaṇacitritāṅgaḥ // 16 //

children.text: vadhāya sṛṣṭāni nṛpeṇa tena tadā sahasrāṇyaparādhināṃ hi /
dṛṣṭvā kumāraḥ kṛpayā parītastān vipramokṣāya nṛpaṃ yayāce // 17 //
śrutvā nṛpo 'mātyagaṇaṃ tadānīmāhūya teṣāṃ nikhilaṃ tadāha /
te procurenaṃ praṇipatya sarve tvaddhātanāyaiṣa nṛpa prayogaḥ // 18 //
śrutvā vadhotsṛṣṭamathāsya mātā sāntaḥpurārtā nṛpatiṃ yayāce /
muñcārdhamāsaṃ nṛpate kumāraṃ dātuṃ pradānānyakhilāni loke // 20 //
dattābhyanujñaśca nṛpeṇa tena prādātsa dānāni yathocitāni /
pāṣaṇḍināṃ yasya yadīpsitaṃ tat tasmai dadāti sma vadhāya sajjaḥ /
muktārtanādātha vinirjagāma sā rājadhānyā janatā samagrā // 22 //
pakvāni jñātvā jagadindriyāṇi taṃ yajñavāṭaṃ kṛpayā jagāma // 23 //

body.text: upetya tasyāṃ pariṣadyathāsau tathāgatavyūhavikurvitena

children.text: anantamadhyāṃ janatāṃ vinīya sa vyākaroti sma tadāgrabodhau /
ārāgya buddhaṃ vipulaṃ ca tasmai vidhāya pūjāṃ mudito babhāṣe /
dvīpo bhaveyaṃ jagatāṃ vinetā trāṇaṃ śaraṇyaśca parāyaṇaṃ ca // 26 //
sa prāvrajattasya muneḥ samīpe saṃbodhimārgaṃ parimārgamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He went forth in the presence of that Sage, seeking the path of awakening,

children.text: dharmasvabhāvaṃ suparīkṣamāṇo yatra sthitaḥ kalpaśatāni cīrṇaḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: thoroughly examining the own-nature of <s>dharma</s> — and abiding there, he practiced for hundreds of <s>kalpa</s>s. // 27 //
Having compassion for the entire mass of beings who had fallen, protectorless, into the ocean of suffering,

children.text: saṃbodhimārgaṃ paribhāvayitvā labhate tadānīṃ sa vimokṣametam // 28 //
children.translated_text: having cultivated the path of awakening, he then obtained this liberation. // 28 //

children.text: ye tatra kalpe sugatā babhūvurārāgya tānapyakhilān prasannaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Sugata</s>s arose in that <s>kalpa</s>, toward all of them without exception he was devoted;

children.text: pūjāṃ ca teṣāmakarodudārāṃ saṃdhārayāmāsa ca dharmacakram // 29 //
children.translated_text: he made noble offerings to them and upheld the <s>Dharmacakra</s>. // 29 //
In the subsequent great oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, in all those [<s>kalpa</s>s] equal to the atoms of oceans of fields,
whatever <s>Jina</s>s arose at that time — he honored and worshipped them all. // 30 //

children.text: ahaṃ sa āsaṃ vijitāvināmā dṛṣṭvā narāṃścārakabandhanasthān /
children.translated_text: I was that [king] named <s>Vijitāvin</s>; and having seen humans standing in prison-bonds,

children.text: tadvipramokṣāya visṛjya dehaṃ labdho mamāyaṃ hi tadā vimokṣaḥ // 31 //
children.translated_text: for their release I gave up my body — and thus was this liberation obtained by me at that time. // 31 //
Which was cultivated through great oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, equal to the atoms of oceans of fields,
and at every mind-moment it was increased — by infinite and middleless, incomparable methods. // 32 //

children.text: dṛṣṭāśca me kecana ye munīndrāḥ prāptaśca yaṃ me nikhileṣvavāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seen by me were certain lords of sages, and attained was that which was attained by me in all [those encounters],
and through the faces of methods, again and again — this liberation of mine was displayed. // 33 //
In the inconceivable truth of their liberation I have trained for many <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>kalpa</s>s,
established therein by the <s>Jina</s>s, simultaneously drinking the clouds of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the liberated. // 34 //

children.text: kṣetrāṇi sarvāṇyapi sarvadikṣu spharanti kāyena asajjamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: They pervade all fields in all directions with their bodies, unattached,
and at every mind-moment they enter inconceivable successions of world-realms on field-paths, proclaimed in the three times. // 35 //
They stand face-to-face with each and every one of the oceans of <s>Jina</s>s of the three times without remainder,

children.text: vidarśayantyeva ca te jineṣu svakāyameghān pratibimbabhūtāḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: and they display cloud-bodies of their own among the <s>Jina</s>s, like reflections. // 36 //
Approaching in all directions, they shine forth before all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,

children.text: vyūhānaśeṣānabhivarṣamāṇāḥ pūjāṃ prakurvanti ca te jinānām // 37 //
children.translated_text: raining forth all manner of arrays without remainder, and they make offerings to the <s>Jina</s>s. // 37 //
They ask <s>Buddha</s>s equal to oceans in number — vast and infinite oceans of questions,
and they retain the immeasurable <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of the <s>Jina</s>s that rain forth. // 38 //

body.text: sarvāsvaśeṣāsu ca dikṣu yānti cakṣuṣpathe te jinamaṇḍaleṣu /
body.translated_text: In all directions without remainder they go, within the range of sight, in the maṇḍalas of <s>Jina</s>s,

body.text: anekarūpāsanasaṃniṣaṇṇā nānāvikurvāmupadarśayantaḥ // 39 //
body.translated_text: seated on seats of various forms, displaying various transformations. // 39 //

children.translated_text: With bodies of infinite colors, they pervade all directions a thousandfold,
and they display forms of infinite middle, each of single height. // 40 //
From each and every pore-opening they release innumerable great oceans of rays,
and they pacify the burning of the fire of afflictions of all beings by various means. // 41 //
Abiding there, releasing clouds of emanation-bodies from each and every hair-pore,
having pervaded all directions with those wondrous [emanations], they discipline beings with rains of the <s>Dharma</s>-water. // 42 //
This entry into the method is of inconceivable form, the refuge of all sons of the <s>Jina</s>s,

children.text: yatra pratiṣṭhāya caranti caryāṃ kṣetreṣu sarveṣvaparāntakalpān // 43 //
children.translated_text: abiding in which they practice the conduct in all fields for <s>kalpa</s>s unto the furthest limit. // 43 //
Proclaiming the <s>Dharma</s> according to dispositions, they turn [beings] back from the net of views,
and having established beings in heavenly bliss and liberation, they display the stage of omniscience. // 44 //
In all births in the world without exception, with bodies of infinite colors, inconceivable,
they proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> according to dispositions — they whose forms are reflections of all beings. // 45 //
These and other immeasurable, inconceivable [qualities] equal to the atoms of oceans of fields,

children.text: acchambhi te varṇamahāsamudrān vimokṣametaṃ pratilabhya śāntam // 46 //
children.translated_text: fearlessly [they proclaim] great oceans of qualities — having obtained this peaceful liberation. // 46 //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvalokagatisamatikrāntānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvalokopapattipratibhāsaprāptānāṃ
body.translated_text: This, son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation arising from the wholesome root of the prompting according to the dispositions of the ripening of all beings, that I know. How could I know the conduct of <s>bodhisattva</s>s who have surpassed all worldly destinies, who have attained reflection in all worldly births,

body.text: sarvajñajñānāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇaprayuktānāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇapratividdhānāṃ sarvakleśāvaraṇāndhakāravidhamanaprayuktānāṃ sarvadharmapravicāraṇābhinirhārakuśalamūlānāṃ nirātmadharmajñānapratyakṣāṇāṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayāpratiprasrabdhānāmadvayadharmadhātunayasupratibiddhānāṃ sarvavākpathanayasāgarānuprasṛtabuddhīnāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇasamudrān vā avatartuṃ jñānavikramo parijñātuṃ cintāvasthānaṃ vā prajñātuṃ samādhivaśitā vādhigantuṃ vimokṣavikurvitaṃ vā samājñātum //
body.translated_text: who are engaged in scattering the mountains of obscurations to omniscient knowledge, who have penetrated the own-nature and characteristics of all <s>dharma</s>s, who are engaged in dispelling the darkness of all obscurations of afflictions, who possess wholesome roots of the accomplishment of the investigation of all <s>dharma</s>s, who directly perceive the knowledge of the selflessness of <s>dharma</s>s, who are unrelenting in the ripening and discipline of all beings, who have well penetrated the method of the non-dual <s>dharmadhātu</s>, whose intellects follow the ocean of the method of all paths of speech — to know their conduct, or fathom their oceans of qualities, or comprehend their stride of knowledge, or understand their ground of thought, or attain their mastery over <s>samādhi</s>, or fully understand their transformations of liberation? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva jambudvīpe lumbinīvane sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīrnāma lumbinīvanadevatā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvā jātā bhavanti tathāgatakule? kathamālokakarā bhavanti lokānām? kathamaparāntakoṭīgatān kalpān bodhisattvasaṃcārikāṃ caranto na parikhidyante?
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family — here in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, dwells a <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess named <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>. Approach her and ask — how are <s>bodhisattva</s>s born in the family of <s>Tathāgata</s>s? How do they become light-makers for the worlds? How do they practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-pilgrimage through <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit without becoming wearied?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāṃ rātridevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvya vanditvā namaskṛtya prāñjalīkṛto 'valokayamānaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 39 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>, circumambulated the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, saluted her, paid homage to her, and standing with palms joined, gazing back at her, departed from the presence of the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>. // 39 //

body.text: 42 Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: 42 <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāyā rātridevatāyāstāmanuśāsanīmanusmaran taṃ sarvasattvaparipākayathāśayasaṃcodanakuśalamūlasaṃbhavabodhisattvavimokṣaṃ paribhāvayan vipulīkurvan anupūrveṇa yena lumbinīvanaṃ tenopajagāma / upetya lumbinīvanaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyaṃ lumbinīvanadevatāṃ parigaveṣamāṇo 'paśyatsutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyaṃ lumbinīdevatāṃ lumbinīvaneṣu sarvaratnadrumaśākhāmaṇḍalakūṭāgāre maṇipadmagarbhasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇāṃ viṃśatyā vanadevatāniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtāṃ puraskṛtāṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānāṃ sarvabodhisattvajanmasamudranirdeśaṃ nāma sūtrāntaṃ saṃprakāśayamānāṃ tathāgatagotrābhijātānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ guṇasamudravegavivardhanām / dṛṣṭvā ca yena sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīrlumbinīvanadevatā tenopajagāma / upetya sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīlumbinīvanadevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā devate anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvā jātā bhavanti tathāgatakule, kathaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ carantaḥ sattvānāmālokakarā bhavantīti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, recollecting the admonition of the night-goddess <s>Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā</s>, contemplating and expanding that <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation arising from the wholesome root of the prompting according to the dispositions of the ripening of all beings, proceeded gradually to <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. Having arrived, he circumambulated <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, and searching for the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, he saw the <s>Lumbinī</s> goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> seated in the <s>Lumbinī</s> groves upon a <s>maṇi</s>-lotus-womb lion-throne in a mansion of canopy-maṇḍalas of branches of all gem-trees, surrounded and attended by twenty <s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of grove-goddesses, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, expounding a <s>sūtra</s> called 'The Teaching of the Ocean of All <s>Bodhisattva</s> Births,' increasing the momentum of the ocean of qualities of <s>bodhisattva</s>s born in the lineage of <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Having seen her, he approached the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, and standing before her with palms joined, he spoke thus: 'I, goddess, have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how <s>bodhisattva</s>s are born in the family of <s>Tathāgata</s>s, how <s>bodhisattva</s>s practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-pilgrimage become light-makers for beings.' //

body.text: evamukte sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīrlumbinīvanadevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - daśemāni kulaputra bodhisattvajanmāni yaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā jātā bhavanti tathāgatakuleṣu / niryātā bodhisattvāḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ bodhisattvakuśalairvivardhante, na vitiṣṭhante na viṣīdanti na vivartante na pratiprasrabhyante na parikhidyante na saṃsīdanti na muhyanti nāvalīyante na paritrasyanti na praṇaśyanti / anugacchanti sarvajñatādiganugamam / anusmaranti dharmadhātunayam / paripākaprāptā bhavanti buddhabodhau / vipulīkurvanti bodhicittotpādam / vivardhante sarvapāramitābhiḥ / vivartante sarvalokagatibhyaḥ / saṃvartante tathāgatabhūmau / uttāpayanti jñānābhijñatāḥ / āmukhībhavanti buddhadharmeṣu / anugatārthā bhavanti sarvajñatāviṣaye / katamāni daśa? yaduta - sarvabuddhopasthānapraṇidhiprayogagarbhaṃ nāma prathamaṃ bodhisattvajanma / bodhicittāṅgapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma / dharmanayanidhyaptiprayogābhimukhasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma / tryadhvalokādhyāśayaviśuddhigarbhaṃ nāma caturthaṃ bodhisattvajanma / samantāvabhāsaprabhāgarbhaṃ nāma pañcamaṃ bodhisattvajanma / sarvatathāgatakulagotrasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ bodhisattvajanma / buddhabalāvabhāsālokālaṃkāragarbhaṃ nāma saptamaṃ bodhisattvajanma / samantajñānamukhavyavacāraṇapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāmāṣṭamaṃ bodhisattvajanma / dharmadhātunirmāṇavyūhagarbhaṃ nāma navamaṃ bodhisattvajanma / tathāgatabhūmyākramaṇavegagarbhaṃ nāma daśamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> spoke to <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, thus: 'There are, son of good family, ten <s>bodhisattva</s> births, endowed with which <s>bodhisattva</s>s are born in the families of <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Having come forth, <s>bodhisattva</s>s increase in <s>bodhisattva</s>-wholesome [qualities] by circumambulating — they do not regress, do not decline, do not turn back, do not relax, do not become wearied, do not sink, do not become confused, do not shrink, do not become frightened, do not perish. They follow the path leading to omniscience in all directions. They recollect the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. They become ripe for the awakening of <s>Buddha</s>s. They expand the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>. They grow through all <s>pāramitā</s>s. They turn away from all worldly destinies. They develop on the stage of <s>Tathāgata</s>s. They bring forth the superknowledges of knowledge. They become face-to-face with <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. They become accomplished in the domain of omniscience. What are the ten? Namely — the first <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Effort of the Vow of Attending All <s>Buddha</s>s'; the second <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Arising from the Perfection of the Limbs of <s>Bodhicitta</s>'; the third <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Arising Facing the Effort of Contemplation of the Method of <s>Dharma</s>'; the fourth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Purification of the Deep Intention toward the World of the Three Times'; the fifth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Radiance of Universal Illumination'; the sixth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Arising from the Family-Lineage of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s'; the seventh <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Ornament of the Light of the Illumination of the Power of <s>Buddha</s>s'; the eighth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Arising from the Perfection of the Practice of the Gate of Universal Knowledge'; the ninth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Array of Emanation of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>'; the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Momentum of Treading the Stage of <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' //

body.text: tatra kulaputra katamatsarvabuddhopasthānapraṇidhiprayogagarbhaṃ nāma prathamaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ ādita eva buddhopasthānāya prapūjyate sarvabuddhān bhagavataḥ satkurvan gurukurvan mānayan pūjayan upatiṣṭhan ārāgayan avirāgayan tathāgatadarśanāvitṛpto buddhasatkāraprayuktabuddhaprītivegavivardhitacetāstathāgatadarśanaprasādavegasaṃjātaḥ / anivartayā śraddhayā
body.translated_text: Therein, son of good family, what is the first <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Effort of the Vow of Attending All <s>Buddha</s>s'? Here, son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> from the very beginning worships all <s>Buddha</s>s, the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, for the purpose of attending the <s>Buddha</s> — honoring, venerating, respecting, worshipping, serving, gratifying, not becoming dissatisfied — insatiable in seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with a mind increased by the momentum of the delight of the <s>Buddha</s> engaged in honoring the <s>Buddha</s>, born from the surge of the serenity of seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>. With irreversible faith,

body.text: puṇyaṃ samārjayan atṛptaḥ sarvatathāgatapūjāsaṃbhārasamudānayanaprayukto 'pratiprasrabdhaprayogo bhavati / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhapūjopasthānapraṇidhiprayogagarbhaṃ nāma prathamaṃ bodhisattvajanma sarvajñatāsaṃbhārakuśalamūlasaṃbhavasamārjanatāyai saṃvartate //
body.translated_text: gathering merit, insatiable, engaged in assembling the ocean of provisions for the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with unrelenting effort — this, son of good family, is the first <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called 'Womb of the Effort of the Vow of Attending and Worshipping All <s>Buddha</s>s,' which develops for the gathering of wholesome roots that are provisions for omniscience. //

body.text: tatra kulaputra katamadbodhicittāṅgapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayati / yaduta mahākaruṇācittaṃ sarvasattvaparitrāṇāya / sarvabuddhārāgaṇacittamatyantābhirādhanatāyai / sarvabuddhadharmaparyeṣṭicittaṃ sarvavastvanapekṣatāyai / mahāprasthānacittaṃ sarvajñatābhimukhatāyai / mahāmaitrīcittaṃ sarvajagatsaṃgrahaprayogaspharaṇatāyai / sarvajagadaparityāgacittaṃ sarvajñatāsaṃnāhadṛḍhatāyai / aśāṭhyāmāyācittaṃ yathābhūtajñānāvabhāsapratilābhatāyai / yathāvādītathākāricittaṃ bodhisattvamārgapratipadyanatāyai / sarvabuddhāvisaṃvādanacittaṃ sarvatathāgatapraṇidhyanupālanatāyai / sarvajñatāmahāpraṇidhānacittamaparāntakoṭīgatasarvasattvaparipākavinayāpratiprasrabdhaye / etatpramukhairbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhicittāṅgasaṃbhārairabhiniṣpannaḥ sa bodhisattvo jāto bhavati tathāgatakule / idaṃ kulaputra bodhicittāṅgapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ dharmanayanidhyaptiprayoganetryabhimukhasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ sarvadharmanayasaṃbhavantighyaptimukhacetāḥ sarvajñatāmārgākārapratipūryabhimukhapariṇatacetāḥ anavadyakarmasamudācārasaṃkalpacetāḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhinayasāgarapariśuddhyabhimukhacetāḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇapratipattipariniṣpannacetāḥ sarvabodhisattvamārgāṅgavyūhābhinirhāracetā vipulasarvajñatārambaṇasaṃbhavakalpoddāhajvalanakalpāpratiprasrabdhavīryacetāḥ sarvajagatparipākavinayaprasthānānantamadhyabodhisattvacaryābhinirhāracetāḥ sarvācāraśikṣāsupratipannabodhisattvaguṇapariniṣpattiṣu sarvabhāvavibhāvanayānubhāvanayapraviṣṭacetā bhavati / idaṃ kulaputra dharmanayanidhyaptiyoganetryabhimukhasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ tryadhvalokādhyāśayaviśuddhigarbhaṃ nāma caturthaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ pariśuddho bhavatyadhyāśayadhātau / avabhāsaprāpto bhavati buddhabodhau / avatīrṇo bhavati bodhisattvanayasamudreṣu / sāro bhavati dṛḍhādhyāśayavajradhātusaṃgṛhītacetāḥ / vimukhībhavati sarvabhavagatyupapattiṣu / abhimukhībhavati sarvatathāgatavikurvitapariniṣpattiṣu / viśeṣagāminīprāpto bhavati bodhisattvatīkṣṇendriyatāvivardhanatāyai / kalyāṇacitto bhavatyadhyāśayaprabhāsvaratāyai / acalo bhavati dṛḍhamahāpraṇidhānavivardhanatāyai / sarvatathāgatasamanvāhṛto bhavati sarvāvaraṇaparvatavikiraṇatāyai / pratiśaraṇabhūto bhavati sarvajagadupajīvyaḥ / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ tryadhvalokādhyāśayaviśuddhigarbhaṃ nāma caturthaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ samantāvabhāsaprabhāgarbhaṃ nāma pañcamaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ prayogasaṃpanno bhavati sarvajagatparipākavinayapratipannaḥ / sarvavastusaṃjño ccalito bhavati pramuktatyāgaḥ / atyantaviśuddho bhavati anantaśīlaḥ tathāgataviṣayasaṃvasanaḥ / kṣāntisaṃpanno bhavati sarvabuddhadharmakṣāntyavabhāsapratilabdhaḥ / mahāvīryo bhavati sarvata udāraniḥśaraṇapratipannaḥ / dhyānapramukto bhavati samantamukhasamādhijñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhaḥ / prajñāvīryaprabho bhavati sarvadharmāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ / asaṅgacakṣurbhavati buddhadarśanasamudravijñaptyavatīrṇaḥ / sarvadharmatattvavibhutvaprabhāvito bhavati sarvalokaṃ paritoṣayitvā / suprayukto bhavati yathāvaddharmanayapratilābheṣu / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ samantāvabhāsaprabhāgarbhaṃ nāma pañcamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //
