tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ sarvatathāgatakulagotrasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvo jāto bhavati tathāgatakule 'nujāto bhavati, tathāgatavaṃśe niṣpanno bhavati sarvabuddhadharmanayamukheṣu, viśuddho bhavatyatītānāgatapratyutpannatathāgatamahāpraṇidhāneṣu / ekadhanakuśalamūlo bhavati sarvatathāgatakuśalamūleṣu / ekaśarīro bhavati sarvabuddhaiḥ / lokottaragāmī śukladharmaiḥ / mahātmadharmavihārī bhavati buddhādhiṣṭhānadarśanasamādhau / sattvaviśuddhidharmapratipanno bhavati yathākāle / apratiprasrabdhapratibhāno bhavati buddhadharmaparipṛcchāsu / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ sarvatathāgatakulagotrasaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatabalāvabhāsālokālaṃkāragarbhaṃ nāma saptamaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvo buddhabalapraveśāvabhāse na nivartate buddhakṣetragamaneṣu / na pratyudāvartate nānābodhisattvaguṇasamudropasthānāya / na paritrasyati sarvadharmamāyāgatayathābhūtajñānena / svapnopamaṃ sarvalokaṃ pratividhyati / pratibhāsopamaṃ sarvarūpavijñaptyadhiṣṭhānamabhinirharati / nirmitopamābhijñāvikurvitavaśitāprāpto bhavati / chāyopamaṃ sarvabhavagatyupapattiṣu mukhaṃ saṃdarśayati / pratiśrutkopamāni sarvatathāgatadharmacakrāṇi prajānāti / dharmadhātunayanirdeśaparamapāramitāprāpto bhavati nānārthopāyanayanirdeśaprayuktaḥ / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatabalāvabhāsālokālaṃkāragarbhaṃ nāma saptamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ samantajñānamukhavyavacārapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāmāṣṭamaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ kumārabhūta eva bodhisattvavyavasthānavyavasthito bhavati, yatra pratiṣṭhāya sarvajñajñānanayaṃ vyavacārayati / ekaikatra jñānanayamukhe 'prameyāḥ kalpāḥ kṣayaṃ vrajeyuraprameyaṃ bodhisattvagocaraṃ nirdiśataḥ / sarvabodhisattvasamādhiṣu ca vaśī bhavati paramapāramitāprāptaḥ / praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvacittakṣaṇeṣu daśadiganabhilāpyabuddhakṣetragatānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ pādamūleṣūpapadyate / asaṃbhinnaiścārambaṇairasaṃbhinnān samādhīn samāpadyate / asaṃbhinneṣu ca dharmeṣu asaṃbhinnajñānavaśitāṃ saṃdarśayati / aparyantāni cārambaṇāni anārambaṇe dhātāvavakrāmati / parīttaiścārambaṇairanantanirdeśabhūmimavatarati / aprameyāṃ ca dharmatāṃ parīttāṃ mahadgatāṃ vā pratividhyati / vijñaptisamaṃ ca sarvalokamavatarati / sarvadharmārambaṇāni
sarvavijñaptipathāṃśca bhāvanayā anugacchati / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ samantajñānamukhavyavacāraṇapariniṣpattisaṃbhavagarbhaṃ nāmāṣṭamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ dharmadhātunirmāṇavyūhagarbhaṃ nāma bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvaḥ sarvatra cittakṣaṇe nānāvyūhāni buddhakṣetrāṇi adhitiṣṭhati / sattvanirmāṇe vaiśāradyaparamapāramitāprāptaśca bhavati / buddhanirmāṇakauśalyaprāptaśca bhavati / dharmanirmāṇavaiśāradyaviśuddhaśca bhavati / asaṅgavaradharmadhātugocaraśca bhavati / yathāśayasarvakāyavijñaptyadhiṣṭhānakuśalaśca bhavati / acintyasattvavinayakauśalyagataśca bhavati / nānācaryābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśakaśca bhavati / anāvaraṇasarvajñatāmārgābhinirhārakuśalaśca bhavati / tadanantaraṃ dharmacakrapravartanakauśalyaṃ saṃdarśayati / anantamadhyasattvavinayopāyābhinirhārakuśalaśca bhavati / kālaprāpte sattvavinaye sadāsamāhitaśca bhavati vairocanajñānagarbhakośaḥ / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ dharmadhātunirmāṇavyūhagarbhaṃ nāma navamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

tatra kulaputra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatabhūmyākramaṇavegagarbhaṃ nāma daśamaṃ bodhisattvajanma? iha kulaputra bodhisattvo vivikto bhavati sarvatryadhvatathāgataikībhāvaviṣaye / sarvalokadhātvānantaryaviṣayaṃ cāvatarati / sarvasattvānāṃ pūrvāntāparāntacyutyupapattiṣu cittānantaryotpādaṃ jānāti / sarvabodhisattvānāṃ caryājñānānantaryaviṣayaṃ prajānāti / atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ ca sarvabuddhānāmabhisaṃbodhānantaryaṃ prajānāti / sarvadharmāṇāṃ copakārakauśalyānantaryaṃ prajānāti / sarvakalpasaṃvartavivartakalpānāṃ ca pūrvāntāparāntapratyuatpannānāṃ sanāmnāṃ sopadeśānāmānantaryaṃ prajānāti / yathāparipāciteṣu ca sattveṣu yathākālaprāpteṣu abhisaṃbodhivyūhavibuddhyanaviṣayasaṃdarśanādhiṣṭhānajñānamabhinirharati / sarvabuddhotpādeṣu cābhisaṃbodhyupanayanadharmacakrapravartanakauśalyanayānantaryatāṃ saṃdarśayati anantasattvadhātuvinayopāyābhinirhārakauśalyena / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatabhūmyākramaṇavegagarbhaṃ nāma daśamaṃ bodhisattvajanma //

imāni kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ daśa bodhisattvajanmāni yeṣu bodhisattvā jāyante upapadyante samarjayanti saṃvardhayanti pratipūrayanti saṃbhavanti parisaṃbhavanti pariniṣpadyante / sarvakṣetraniravaśeṣānubodhāyaikavyūhālaṃkārasamudācārānadhitiṣṭhanti / sattvadhātunayāpratiprasrambhaṇāya aparāntakoṭīgatakalpādhiṣṭhānānadhitiṣṭhante / sarvadharmasamudranānārambaṇānekavicitranānāparaṃparānirdeśānantadharmaparaṃparāsroto 'bhisaṃbudhyante / acintyāṃ buddhavṛṣabhitāṃ dharmadhātuparamākāśadhātuparyavasānāṃ saṃdarśayanti / aprameyasattvacaryānānātvasamudreṣu paripākavinayasaṃgṛhīteṣu dharmacakrapravartanaṃ saṃdarśayanti / sarvalokadhātūn buddhotpādāvirahitānadhitiṣṭhanti / sarvadharmameghānanabhilāpyasvarāṅgasamudraviśuddhiṃ sarvārambaṇeṣu pravartamānāṃ vijñapayanti / aprameyavihāritāyāmanāvaraṇagatiṃ gatāḥ sarvadharmaruciravyūhāni bodhisattvamaṇḍalāni prabhāvayanti / yathāśayādhimuktiṣu
body.translated_text: These, O <s>kulaputra</s> (son of good family), are the ten births of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, in which <s>bodhisattva</s>s are born, arise, are generated, are nurtured, are fulfilled, come into being, fully come into being, and are perfected. They sustain the practices of the single array-ornament for the awakening of all fields without remainder. They sustain the empowerments of <s>kalpa</s>s extending to the furthest limit for the unflagging method of the realm of beings. They awaken to the endless successions of <s>dharma</s> — the manifold and variegated expositions of diverse objects in the ocean of all <s>dharma</s>s, with their various continuing streams. They display the inconceivable excellence of a <s>Buddha</s>, extending to the ultimate limit of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) and the expanse of space. They display the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) within the immeasurable oceans of the diversity of beings' conduct, encompassed by ripening and discipline. They sustain all world-realms as never devoid of the arising of <s>Buddha</s>s. They make known the purity of the ocean of inexpressible voices and limbs of all <s>dharma</s>-clouds, operating in all objects. Having gone to unobstructed movement in immeasurable abiding, they illuminate the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s (assemblies) with splendid arrays of all <s>dharma</s>s. In accordance with the dispositions and inclinations of

body.text: sattveṣu aprameyabuddhabhūmyanugatasarvalokapariniṣpādanārthamanantamadhyaṃ dharmakoṣaṃ saṃprakāśayanti //
body.translated_text: beings, they illuminate the endless and boundless treasury of <s>dharma</s> for the purpose of accomplishing the perfection of all worlds, following the immeasurable stages of a <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīrlumbinīvanadevatā tasyāṃ velāyāmetameva bodhisattvajanmārthamabhidyotayantī buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess, at that time, illuminating this very meaning of <s>bodhisattva</s>-birth, by the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed the ten directions and addressed <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, in verses:

children.text: adhyāśayena vimalena anāvilena paśyanti ye jina na jātu bhavanti tṛptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who see the <s>Jina</s>s (Victorious Ones) with a stainless and unclouded deep intention are never satiated;

children.text: sarvān jināna aparāntaviyūhameghān praṇidhyenti te prathamajanmasthitāḥ sumedhāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: they aspire to the clouds of arrays at the furthest limit of all <s>Jina</s>s — those of excellent wisdom, established in the first birth. // 1 //

children.text: sarvatriyadhvagamaśeṣa spharitva lokaṃ kṣetrāṇi sarva tatha dharma tathaiva buddhān /
children.translated_text: Having pervaded the world throughout the entire three times without remainder, all fields, all <s>dharma</s>s, and likewise all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the mind that is an array of vows for the liberation of beings — this is said to be the second birth of those beyond conception. // 2 //

children.text: ye dharmamegha pibamāna na jātu tṛptāḥ nidhyaptimānasa triyadhvaasaṅgakāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, drinking the <s>dharma</s>-clouds, are never satiated, whose minds are intent, whose bodies are unattached across the three times,

children.text: ākāśadhātuvimalā samacittakāyāḥ janmaṃ tṛtīyamidamapratimaṃ hi teṣām // 3 //
children.translated_text: whose minds and bodies are pure as the expanse of space — this is their third birth, incomparable indeed. // 3 //
Those who descend into the ocean of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) with deep intentions firm as <s>vajra</s> (diamond) and like <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: sarvajñatānayasamudra viśāhamānāḥ teṣāṃ caturthamiha janma nararṣabhāṇām // 4 //
children.translated_text: bearing the ocean of the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) — this here is the fourth birth of those bulls among men. // 4 //

children.text: ye maitrayā daśasu dikṣu jagatspharitvā abhinirharantyamalapāramitāsamudrān /
children.translated_text: Those who, with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), pervade beings in the ten directions and bring forth the ocean of stainless <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections),

children.text: paripācayanti jagu dharmaprabhābhiranta imu janmu pañcamu mahāpuruṣāṇa teṣām // 5 //
children.translated_text: and ripen beings endlessly with the radiance of <s>dharma</s> — this is the fifth birth of those great beings. // 5 //
Those who have penetrated the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>, whose minds are unattached, born in the incomparable <s>Buddha</s>-family of the three times,

children.text: ye dharmadhātunayasāgaramotaranti ṣaṣṭhaṃ idaṃ vipula janma vidūna teṣām // 6 //
children.translated_text: who descend into the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this is the sixth birth, the vast birth of those wise ones. // 6 //

body.text: ye dharmakāya pariśuddha asaṅgacittāḥ kṣetrāṇyaśeṣatu spharitva svakaiḥ śarīraiḥ /
body.translated_text: Those whose <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body) is pure, whose minds are unattached, who pervade all fields without remainder with their own bodies,

body.text: niḥśeṣabuddhabalatānugamapraviṣṭā janmātha saptamamacintyamidaṃ budhānām // 7 //
body.translated_text: having entered the complete following of all <s>Buddha</s>-powers — this then is the seventh birth, inconceivable, of the wise. // 7 //

children.translated_text: Those who follow mastery in the method of the ocean of knowledge, who practice the gateway of the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s>,

children.text: sarvaṃ samādhinayasāgara otaranti janmāṣṭamaṃ matamidaṃ tathatāśrayāṇām // 8 //
children.translated_text: who descend into the entire ocean of the method of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) — this is considered the eighth birth of those who rely on <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). // 8 //
Those who purify the expanse of <s>dharma</s>-fields, who are engaged in the ripening of all beings,

children.text: bauddhā vikurvitaviyūha vidarśayanti teṣāmidaṃ navamu janma mahāśayānām // 9 //
children.translated_text: who display the arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-transformations — this is the ninth birth of those of great intention. // 9 //

children.text: ye te yathābala jināna tathā praviṣṭāḥ sarvajñatāvipulavegavivardhamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have entered in accordance with the power of the <s>Jina</s>s, growing in the vast momentum of <s>sarvajñatā</s>,
who are unattached in the methods of penetrating the ground of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this is the tenth birth of those born from the <s>Jina</s>s' breast. // 10 //

body.text: ebhiḥ kulaputra bodhisattvo daśabhirjanmabhistathāgatakule jāta evamālokakaro bhavati sarvasattvānām / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra ahamaprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / āha - ka etasya devate aprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ? āha - ahaṃ kulaputra sarvabodhisattvajanmasaṃdarśanopasaṃkramaṇapraṇidhānapariniṣpannā / sā khalvahaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya vipulaṃ janmasamudramavatarāmi / yaduta asyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau bodhisattvajanma avataramāṇā bhāgavatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāmiha jambudvīpe lumbinīvane bodhisattvajanmasaṃdarśane pūrvapraṇidhānopapannā / sā ahamiha bodhisattvajanmānusmṛtiṃ bhāvayamānā viharāmi / tasyā mameha viharantyā varṣaśatena bhagavāṃstuṣitabhavanāccyaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: By these ten births, O <s>kulaputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> born in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s> becomes such a bringer of light for all beings. Moreover, son of good family, I have attained the <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) of displaying the transformations of <s>bodhisattva</s>-birth in all objects throughout immeasurable <s>kalpa</s>s. He said: 'What, O goddess, is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> of displaying the transformations of <s>bodhisattva</s>-birth in all objects throughout immeasurable <s>kalpa</s>s?' She replied: 'I, son of good family, have perfected the vow to approach and witness all <s>bodhisattva</s>-births. And I, son of good family, descend into the vast ocean of births of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>. That is to say, having descended into this birth of the <s>bodhisattva</s> in this great trichiliocosm, I have arisen by prior vow in the four-continent world, here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, to witness the <s>bodhisattva</s>-birth. And I dwell here cultivating the recollection of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s birth. And while I dwell here, in one hundred years the <s>Bhagavān</s> will descend from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven.'

body.text: athāsmin lumbinīvane daśa pūrvanimittāni prādurbabhūvuḥ / katamāni daśa? yaduta - sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvana samaṃ saṃsthitamapagatanimnonnataviṣamamapagataśvabhraprapātam / idaṃ prathamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaḥ sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvanamutpasannaśarkarakaṭhallamapagatasthāṇukaṇṭakaṃ vajrapṛthivītalasaṃsthānamanekaratnābhikīrṇaṃ samavasthitam / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaḥ sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvanaṃ sarvaratnadrumaśālatālapaṅktisuvibhaktālaṃkāraṃ samavāsthiṣata / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaḥ sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvanaṃ divyasamatikrāntagandhāṅkuraprarūḍhaṃ sarvacūrṇakośasaṃbhūtaṃ sarvadhvajameghapaṭalamaṇḍalajātaṃ gandhamaṇivigrahavṛkṣamūlaparisaṃsthāpitālaṃkāraṃ samavāsthiṣata / idaṃ caturthaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaḥ sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvanaṃ vividhadivyapuṣpamālyābharaṇakośanirvṛttasarvālaṃkāraparipūrṇaṃ samavāsthiṣata / idaṃ pañcamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt /
body.translated_text: Then in this <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, ten preliminary signs appeared. What are the ten? Namely — this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove became level and even, with all hollows, elevations, and unevenness gone, free from chasms and precipices. This was the first preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, with gravel and pebbles vanished, free from stumps and thorns, established on a ground of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), strewn with numerous gems, remained so established. This was the second preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove remained arrayed with well-ordered rows of trees, <s>śāla</s>-trees, and palm trees of all gems. This was the third preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove remained established with sprouts of fragrance surpassing divine fragrances, produced from all repositories of powders, adorned with canopies of clouds of all banners and ornaments set at the roots of trees with bodies of fragrant gems. This was the fourth preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove remained fully adorned with repositories of various divine flowers, garlands, and ornaments. This was the fifth preliminary sign that appeared.

body.text:
punaḥ sarvasminniha lumbinīvane sarvavṛkṣeṣu mahāmaṇiratnakośā abhinirvṛttāḥ / idaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaḥ sarvasminniha lumbinīvane sarvanalinīṣu sarvāṇi jalajaratnapuṣpāṇi śuṅgībhūtāni dharaṇitalādabhyudgamya vārisamudgatāni samavāsthiṣanta / idaṃ saptamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaryāvanta iha lokadhātau kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāśca devaputrā nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā lokendrajagadindrā vā, te 'pyasmin lumbinīvane sarve kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sthitā abhūvan / idamaṣṭamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punaryāvanta iha cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau devakanyā vā nāgakanyā vā yakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragakanyā vā, tāḥ sarvāḥ pramuditamānasāḥ sarvapūjāvidhiparigṛhītahastāḥ plakṣaśākhābhimukhāḥ praṇatakāyāḥ sthitā abhūvan / idaṃ navamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / punardaśabhyo digbhyaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ nābhimaṇḍalebhyo niścaramāṇā bodhisattvajanmavikurvitapradīpā
nāma raśmayo niścaritvā sarvamidaṃ lumbinīvanamavabhāsya tiṣṭhanti sma / teṣu ca sarvaraśmimukhamaṇḍaleṣu teṣāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ janmavikurvitāni pratibhāsaprāptāni saṃdṛśyante sma / saṃprasavavikurvitāḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇāśca buddhasvarasaṃprayuktāstebhyo raśmimukhamaṇḍalebhyo niścaramāṇāḥ śrūyante sma / idaṃ daśamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / imāni daśa pūrvanimittāni prādurbhūtāni bodhisattvajanmakālasamaye pratyupasthite, yeṣāṃ prādurbhāvādvitarkamabhavat sarvalokendrāṇāṃ bodhisattvo janiṣyata iti / sā khalu punarahaṃ kulaputra eṣāṃ daśānāṃ pūrvanimittānāṃ darśanādacintyaṃ prītivegaṃ pratilabhe //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, in this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, great repositories of gem-jewels appeared in all the trees. This was the sixth preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, in this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, in all the lotus ponds, all water-born gem-flowers, having budded, rose up from the surface of the earth and stood emerging from the water. This was the seventh preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, as many as there are gods of the desire-realm and form-realm in this world-realm, <s>devaputra</s>s, <s>Nāga</s>s, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Asura</s>s, <s>Garuḍa</s>s, <s>Kinnara</s>s, <s>Mahoraga</s>s, lords of the world, and lords of beings — they all stood in this <s>Lumbinī</s> grove with palms joined together. This was the eighth preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, as many as there are divine maidens, <s>Nāga</s>-maidens, <s>Yakṣa</s>-, <s>Gandharva</s>-, <s>Asura</s>-, <s>Garuḍa</s>-, <s>Kinnara</s>-, and <s>Mahoraga</s>-maidens in this four-continent world-realm — they all stood with joyful minds, holding in their hands all manner of offerings, with bodies bowed toward the <s>Plakṣa</s> branch. This was the ninth preliminary sign that appeared. Furthermore, from the navel-circles of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the ten directions, rays of light called 'Lamp of the Transformation of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-Birth' issued forth, illuminated this entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, and remained. And in all those radiant circles, the birth-transformations of all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s appeared reflected and were seen. And the qualities of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, connected with the birth-transformations, joined with the voice of the <s>Buddha</s>, were heard issuing from those radiant circles. This was the tenth preliminary sign that appeared. These ten preliminary signs appeared when the time of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s birth was at hand, from the appearance of which there arose the thought in all the lords of the world: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> is about to be born.' And I, son of good family, upon seeing these ten preliminary signs, attained an inconceivable rush of joy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra māyādevyāḥ kapilavastuno mahānagarānniṣkramantyā iha lumbinīvane daśa mahāvabhāsapūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan, yeṣāṃ prādurbhāvādaprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvajñatādharmālokaprītivegā vivardhitāḥ / katame daśa? yaduta - dharaṇītalagateṣu sarvaratnakūṭāgāragarbheṣvavabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / sarvagandhakusumamukuleṣvavabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / aśeṣaratnapadmamukuleṣu vikasamāneṣu sarvapatrebhyo 'vabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, madhuraśca sujātajātaśabda ebhyo niścarati sma / yaśca daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvānāṃ prathamacittotpādāvabhāsaḥ, sa idaṃ lumbinīvanamavabhāsya abhyuditaḥ / yacca daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇāvabhāsavikurvitam, tadiha lumbinīvane prādurabhūt / yaśca daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvānāṃ sarvapāramitāpariniṣpattijñānādhigamālokāvabhāsaḥ, sa iha lumbinīvane prādurbabhūva / yaśca daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvānāṃ sarvapraṇidhānavaśitājñānālokāvabhāsaḥ, sa iha lumbinīvane prādurbabhūva / yaśca daśasu dikṣu sarvabodhisattvānāṃ paripākavinayajñānālokāvabhāsaḥ, sa iha lumbinīvane prādurbabhūva / yaśca daśasu dikṣu sarvabodhisattvānāṃ dharmadhātunayajñānādhigamālokāvabhāsaḥ, sa iha lumbinīvane prādurbabhūva / yaśca daśasu dikṣu sarvabodhisattvānāṃ buddhavikurvitajanmābhiniṣkramaṇabodhivibudhyanajñānādhigamālokāvabhāsaḥ, sa iha lumbinīvane prādurbabhūva / imāni daśa mahāvabhāsanimittāni prādurbabhūvuḥ, yairanantamadhyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ cittāśayagahanāndhakārāṇyavabhāsitāni //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, when <s>Māyādevī</s> departed from the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and came to this <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, ten great radiance-preliminary signs appeared, from the appearance of which rushes of joy in the light of the <s>dharma</s> of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) were increased for immeasurable beings. What are the ten? Namely — a radiance appeared in all the gem-mansions resting on the surface of the earth. A radiance appeared in all the buds of fragrant flowers. In all the gem-lotus buds as they were opening, a radiance appeared from every petal, and from these issued a sweet and beautiful sound of birth. And that radiance of the first arising of the thought of awakening of <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions illuminated this <s>Lumbinī</s> grove and arose. And the transformation-radiance of the ascending of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages by <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And the radiance of the light of the knowledge attained through the perfection of all <s>pāramitā</s>s by <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And the radiance of the light of the knowledge of mastery over all vows by <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And the radiance of the light of the knowledge of ripening and disciplining by all <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And the radiance of the light of the attainment of the knowledge of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> by all <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And the radiance of the light of the attainment of the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>-transformation, birth, going-forth, and awakening to <s>Bodhi</s> by all <s>bodhisattva</s>s in the ten directions appeared here in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. These ten great radiance-signs appeared, by which the darkness of the depths of the mental dispositions of limitless and boundless <s>bodhisattva</s>s was illuminated.

body.text: tatra kulaputra māyāyā devyāḥ plakṣadrumanilayagatāyāḥ saṃnipatitānāṃ sarvalokendrāṇāṃ sarvakāmadhātukānāṃ ca devaputrāṇāṃ sāpsarogaṇadevakanyāparivārāṇāṃ saṃnipatitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca rūpāvacarāṇāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ nirāmagandhānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāṇāṃ saparivārāṇāṃ saṃnipatitānāṃ bodhisattvapūjāsaṃprayuktānāṃ māyādevyāstejasā śriyā varṇena rūpeṇa sarvapūjāvyūhāḥ kāyāścāvabhāsitā babhūvuḥ, asyāṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau yāḥ prabhāḥ, tā api sarvā grastāścābhibhūtāścābhūvan / sarvaromavivaravisṛtāśca māyādevyāḥ prabhāvabhāsāstadanyābhiḥ prabhābhiranupahatā anāvṛtā apravyāhṛtā asaṅgāḥ sarvadiśaḥ spharitvā sarvāṇi nairayikāṇi duḥkhāni sarvāṇi tairyagyonikāni duḥkhāni sarvāṇi ca yāmalaukikāni duḥkhāni sarvabhavagatiparyāpannānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni saṃkleśāṃśca praśamayitvā tiṣṭhanti bhāsante tapanti virocante sma / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya lumbinīvane prathamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: There, son of good family, when <s>Māyādevī</s> had gone to the abode of the <s>Plakṣa</s> tree, the bodies and all offerings-arrays of all the assembled lords of the worlds, all the <s>devaputra</s>s (divine sons) of the entire <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) attended by hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> and divine maidens, all the assembled <s>devaputra</s>s of the <s>Rūpāvacara</s> (form realm) who are free from impure odors, and all the assembled <s>Deva</s>s, <s>Nāga</s>s, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Asura</s>s, <s>Garuḍa</s>s, <s>Kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>Mahoraga</s>s with their retinues — all engaged in the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — were illuminated by the splendor, glory, radiance, and beauty of <s>Māyādevī</s>. And whatever radiances existed in this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-realm, all of those were swallowed up and overpowered. And the radiant lights emitted from every pore of <s>Māyādevī</s>, unimpaired, unobstructed, unobscured, and unhindered by those other radiances, having pervaded all directions, pacified all the sufferings of hell-beings, all the sufferings of the animal realm, all the sufferings of <s>Yama</s>'s world, and all the sufferings and defilements of beings caught in all states of existence and destinies — they stood, shone, blazed, and radiated brilliantly. This, son of good family, is the first birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s> (Lumbini grove). //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra yasmin samaye māyāyā devyāḥ kukṣau sarvāvatīyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrā lokadhāturantargatā pratibhāsaprāptā saṃdṛśyate sma, tasyāṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau koṭīśatacāturdvīpikānāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ sarve jambudvīpeṣu nānānāmadheyāsu rājadhānīṣu nānānāmadheyeṣu vanaṣaṇḍeṣu nānāvṛkṣamūleṣu māyādevī upagatā evameva saṃdṛśyate sma sarvalokendraparivṛtā bodhisattvajanmapratyupasthānā acintyena bodhisattvajananījñānavikurvitena / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya lumbinīvane dvitīyaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, at that time when the entirety of this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-realm contained within the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s> appeared as having attained a reflected image, in that billion-fold world-realm, in all the <s>Jambudvīpa</s>s of hundreds of <s>koṭi</s>s of four-continent worlds, in royal capitals of various names, in forest groves of various names, at the bases of various trees, <s>Māyādevī</s> was seen in just this same way — surrounded by all the lords of the worlds, attending the birth of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the inconceivable miraculous transformation of the knowledge of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother. This, son of good family, is the second birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra māyāyā devyāḥ sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromamukhādyāvanto bhagavatā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā tathāgatā ārāgitāḥ satkṛtā gurukṛtā mānitā pūjitāḥ, te sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / yaśca taistathāgatairdharmo deśitaḥ, sa sarvastebhyo romavivarebhyo buddhasvarāṅgasaṃprayukto nikhilena śrūyate sma / tadyathāpi nāma vārirāśe rajasi kanakaparamāṇurajasi vā ādarśamaṇḍale vā svacche suprasanne vā udake gaganamaṇḍalamādityacandrajyotigrahagaṇapratimaṇḍitaṃ gambhīrameghapaṭalanigarjitanirghoṣapratibhāsaprāptaṃ saṃdṛśyate sma, evameva kulaputra māyāyā devyāḥ sarvaromamukhamaṇḍaleṣu pūrvatathāgatavikurvitāni saṃdṛśyante sma sarvadharmadeśanānirghoṣāṇi / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya lumbinīvane tṛtīyaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, from every pore of <s>Māyādevī</s>, from each single hair-opening, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s who had been previously honored, venerated, esteemed, respected, and worshipped by the Blessed One while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — all of them became visible. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> was taught by those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, all of that was heard in its entirety from those hair-openings, accompanied by the voice-limbs of a <s>Buddha</s>. Just as in an ocean of dust particles, or in dust of golden atoms, or in a mirror-disc, or in clear and pellucid water, the vault of the sky adorned with the reflected images of the sun, moon, and constellations of stars is seen, and the deep rumbling sound of cloud-masses appears as a reflected image — even so, son of good family, in the circle of every hair-opening of <s>Māyādevī</s>, the miraculous displays of the former <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the sounds of all <s>Dharma</s>-teachings became visible. This, son of good family, is the third birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra māyāyā devyāḥ sarvakāyātsarvaromamukhamaṇḍalebhya ekaikasmādromavivarādyāvatsu sarvakṣetreṣu yāvatsu lokadhātusamudreṣu yāvatsu lokadhātuvaṃśeṣu yāvatsu lokadhātusaṃjñāgateṣu bhagavān bodhisattvacārikāmakārṣīt / yatpratiṣṭhāneṣu kṣetreṣu yatsaṃsthāneṣu yadvyūheṣu yaccharīreṣu yatparvatālaṃkāreṣu yadgrāmanagaranigamajanapadapaṭṭanālaṃkāreṣu yadudyānanadīhṛdataḍāgasāgarālaṃkāreṣu yadgaganameghālaṃkāreṣu yatsattvanilayeṣu yadyānanirdeśeṣu yatkalpanāmasaṃkhyāsu yadbuddhotpādaprabhaveṣu yadviśuddhiparameṣu yathāyuḥpramāṇasattveṣu yathālokajanmopapattiṣu yathāsattvasamavadhāneṣu yathākalyāṇamitrasaṃniśrayeṣu yathākuśaladharmaprayogeṣu yathādharmapratipatyabhiyogeṣu
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, from the entire body of <s>Māyādevī</s>, from the circles of all hair-openings, from each single pore — in whatever fields, in whatever oceans of world-realms, in whatever successions of world-realms, in whatever designations of world-realms the Blessed One had practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct; in whatever foundations of fields, in whatever configurations, in whatever arrays, in whatever bodies, in whatever mountain-ornaments, in whatever ornaments of villages, cities, towns, districts, and market-towns, in whatever ornaments of gardens, rivers, lakes, ponds, and oceans, in whatever ornaments of sky and clouds, in whatever abodes of beings, in whatever teachings of vehicles, in whatever enumerations of <s>kalpa</s>-names, in whatever manifestations of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, in whatever supreme purities, among beings of whatever lifespan, in whatever births and rebirths of beings in worlds, in whatever assemblages of beings, in whatever reliances upon spiritual friends, in whatever applications to wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, in whatever zealous practices of <s>Dharma</s>-practice,

body.text: buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvacārikāmacaran, te sarve buddhakṣetraprasarā māyāyā devyāḥ sarvaromamukhebhyaḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / yāvadbhiśca kāyairbhagavān pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāmakārṣīdavivartyasthānaprāptaḥ, yairākārairyairvihārairyaiḥ paribhogairyaiḥ sukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedībhiryeṣu jātiparivarteṣu, tatsarvamekaikasmin romavivare saṃdṛśyate sma / sarveṣu ca teṣu tāsu tāsūpapattiṣu māyādevī bodhisattvasya jananī babhūva / sarve ca te bodhisattvakāyā māyāyā devyā romavivareṣu vikurvitapratibhāsaprāptāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / idaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya lumbinīvane caturthaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields where he practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — all those extents of <s>Buddha</s>-fields became visible from every hair-opening of <s>Māyādevī</s>. And with however many bodies the Blessed One had formerly practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, having reached the stage of non-retrogression — in whatever forms, in whatever modes of life, in whatever enjoyments, in whatever experiences of pleasure and pain, in whatever turns of birth — all of that became visible in each single pore. And in all those various rebirths, <s>Māyādevī</s> had been the mother of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And all those bodies of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> appeared visible as reflected images in the pores of <s>Māyādevī</s>. This, son of good family, is the fourth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra yāvadbhiḥ kāyairbhagavān pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāmacarat yadvarṇairyatsaṃsthānairyadākārairyatparibhogairyatsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedībhiryajjātiparivartaiḥ, te sarve māyāyā devyāḥ kāye sarvaromamukheṣu pratibhāsaprāptāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya pañcamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, with however many bodies the Blessed One had formerly practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — of whatever complexions, whatever configurations, whatever forms, whatever enjoyments, whatever experiences of pleasure and pain, whatever turns of birth — all of those appeared visible as reflected images in every hair-opening on the body of <s>Māyādevī</s>. This, son of good family, is the fifth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra yāvanto bhagavatā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ caratā duṣkaraparityāgāḥ parityaktāḥ, hastapādaparityāgā vā karṇanāsāparityāgā vā jihvādaṃṣṭrāparityāgā vā nayanottamāṅgaparityāgā vā māṃsaśoṇitaparityāgā vā asthimajjāparityāgā vā vakṣohṛdayaparityāgā vā chavicarmaparityāgā vā bāhyādhyātmikavastuparityāgā vā putraduhitṛbhāryāparityāgā vā ātmabhāvaparityāgā vā bhogaratnaparityāgā vā grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīparityāgā vā dhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāraparityāgā vā maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajataparityāgā vā vividharatnābharaṇaparityāgā vā śayyāsanaparityāgā vā gṛhavimānaparityāgā vā sarvopabhogaparityāgā vā, te ca dāyakabodhisattvavigrahakāyai rūpaiḥ parityajanti sma / te ca pratigrāhakāyai rūpaiḥ pratigṛhṇanti sma / tāni ca deśavastūni yāni parityaktāni, te ca deśapradeśāḥ, te ca bodhisattvaparivārāḥ, sarve te māyāyā devyāḥ sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ pratibhāsaprāptāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya ṣaṣṭhaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, however many difficult renunciations were made by the Blessed One while formerly practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — whether the giving up of hands and feet, or of ears and nose, or of tongue and teeth, or of eyes and head, or of flesh and blood, or of bones and marrow, or of chest and heart, or of outer skin and inner skin, or of external and internal possessions, or of sons, daughters, and wives, or of one's own body, or of enjoyments and jewels, or of villages, cities, towns, districts, countries, and royal capitals, or of wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries, or of gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, gold, and silver, or of various jewel-ornaments, or of beds and seats, or of houses and palaces, or of all enjoyments — the donor <s>Bodhisattva</s> gave them away in those bodily forms, and the recipients accepted them in their respective forms. And those lands and places where the gifts were made, and those regions and districts, and those retinues of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — all of these appeared as reflected images from every pore of <s>Māyādevī</s>. This, son of good family, is the sixth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra ....................... lumbinīvanaṣaṇḍe samavasṛtā abhijātajagadvijñānā prādurabhavat / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya saptamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, [...lacuna...] having assembled in the grove of <s>Lumbinīvana</s>, the noble knowledge of the world manifested. This, son of good family, is the seventh birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra yāvantaḥ sarvadevendrabhavanavyūhaparibhogasamatikrāntāḥ sarvanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyendrabhavanavyūhaparibhogasamatikrāntāḥ sarvabodhisattvaparibhogāḥ, yaduta sarvamaṇirājakūṭāgāraparibhogā vā maṇirājavimānaparibhogā vā maṇirājajālaparibhogā vā maṇirājavigrahaparibhogā vā maṇirājabimbaparibhogā vā maṇirājavyūhā vā sarvābharaṇaparibhogā vā sarvagandharājaparibhogā vā śubhāpratikūlasarvārambaṇaparibhogā vā, te sarve māyāyā devyāḥ kukṣeranyonyāsaṃbhinnā niścaritvā iha lumbinīvane samantavyūhāḥ samavāsthiṣanta / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasyāṣṭamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, all the enjoyments of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that surpassed the palace-array-enjoyments of all lords of <s>Deva</s>s, that surpassed the palace-array-enjoyments of all lords of <s>Nāga</s>s, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Asura</s>s, <s>Garuḍa</s>s, <s>Kiṃnara</s>s, <s>Mahoraga</s>s, and human lords — namely, enjoyments of pinnacled mansions of all jewel-kings, or enjoyments of palaces of jewel-kings, or enjoyments of nets of jewel-kings, or enjoyments of bodies of jewel-kings, or enjoyments of images of jewel-kings, or arrays of jewel-kings, or enjoyments of all ornaments, or enjoyments of all kings of fragrances, or enjoyments of all beautiful and agreeable objects — all of these, issuing forth from the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s> without mutual interference, stood arrayed on all sides here in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. This, son of good family, is the eighth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra māyāyā devyāḥ kukṣeḥ prathamataraṃ daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā bhagavato vairocanasya sadṛśarūpavarṇasaṃsthānāḥ sadṛśalakṣaṇānuvyañjanālaṃkārāḥ sadṛśaprabhāḥ sadṛśaraśmipramuñcanāḥ sadṛśaliṅgalīlāḥ sadṛśavikramāḥ sadṛśavirocanavikurvitāḥ sadṛśaparivārāḥ sadṛśavyūhā niścaranti sma bhagavato varṇasamudrānudīrayamāṇāḥ / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya navamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, from the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s>, before all else, <s>Bodhisattva</s>s equal in number to the atoms of ten inexpressible <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields emerged — resembling Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> in form, complexion, and configuration; resembling him in the marks and minor characteristics of adornment; resembling him in radiance; resembling him in the emission of rays; resembling him in bearing and grace; resembling him in might; resembling him in miracles of illumination; resembling him in retinue; resembling him in array — proclaiming oceans of praise of the Blessed One. This, son of good family, is the ninth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvasya janmakālasamaye pravṛtte māyāyā devyāḥ purastādadho vajratalānmahāpṛthivīmabhinirbhidya sarvaratnavyūhagarbhaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnapadmamabhyudgatamabhūdaparājitamahāvajramaṇirājagarbhasarvamaṇirājakesararaśmivyūhaṃ daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamapatrapaṅktisuvibhaktaṃ vividhamaṇirājapatramaṇḍalaṃ cintāmaṇirājaviśuddhakarṇikaṃ sarvaratnavarṇāprameyakesarapaṅktivyūham, asaṃkhyeyamaṇirājaratnavyūhajālasaṃchannamabhedyanārāyaṇavajramaṇirājendrakūṭasaṃchāditaṃ sarvadevendrakāyaparivṛtaṃ sarvanāgendragandhameghābhipravarṣitaṃ divyapuṣpapāṇipuṭaprayuktasarvayakṣendraparivṛtaṃ sarvagandharvendrapūrvabuddhotpādasthānamadhurarutasaṃgītinirghoṣasaṃprayuktastutimeghāviṣkṛtaṃ nihatamānamadadarpasarvāsurendrapraṇataśarīranamaskṛtaṃ sarvagaruḍendrābhipralambitaratnapaṭṭagaganameghālaṃkārabodhisattvagaṇasaṃcodanasaṃgītisaṃprayuktaiḥ prītimanobhiḥ sarvakinnarendraiḥ saṃprekṣitaṃ sarvamahoragendraprītisaṃbhavaprayuktanayaruciranirghoṣavyūhameghābhipravarṣitam / idaṃ kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya daśamaṃ janmavikurvitam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, son of good family, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth-occasion commenced, before <s>Māyādevī</s>, breaking through the great earth from the <s>vajra</s>-base below, there arose a great <s>maṇi</s>-jewel lotus called <s>Sarvaratnavyūhagarbha</s> (Womb of the Array of All Jewels) — with <s>Aparājitamahāvajramaṇirājagarbha</s> (Womb of the Invincible Great Vajra Jewel-King) radiance-array filaments of all jewel-kings, with rows of petals equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields well-arranged, with a petal-circle of various jewel-kings, with a pistil purified of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) kings, with an array of immeasurable filament-rows of the colors of all jewels, covered by a canopy-net of countless jewel-king-gem arrays, roofed by an indestructible <s>Nārāyaṇa-vajra-maṇi</s>-king pinnacle, surrounded by the bodies of all lords of <s>Deva</s>s, showered by clouds of fragrance from all lords of <s>Nāga</s>s, surrounded by all lords of <s>Yakṣa</s>s with hands full of divine flowers, displaying clouds of hymns accompanied by sweet melodious sounds of all lords of <s>Gandharva</s>s singing of the sites of former <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, saluted with bowed bodies and homage by all lords of <s>Asura</s>s whose pride, intoxication, and arrogance had been vanquished, gazed upon with joyful minds by all lords of <s>Kiṃnara</s>s engaged in songs encouraging the assembly of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s amid the sky-cloud ornaments of jewel-cloths suspended by all lords of <s>Garuḍa</s>s, and showered with clouds of melodious arrays of delightful eye-pleasing sounds arising from the joy of all lords of <s>Mahoraga</s>s. This, son of good family, is the tenth birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. //

body.text: imāni kulaputra lumbinīvane bodhisattvasya daśa janmavikurvitāni prādurabhūvan / tataḥ paścādbodhisattvo 'cintyāpramāṇaprabhāsecanakadarśano māyāyā devyāḥ kukṣerabhyudgataḥ sūryamaṇḍalamiva gaganatalāt, vidyutkalāpa iva meghasaṃghātāt, sāṃdhya iva mahāghanaḥ śailaśikharāntarāt, mahāpradīpa iva tamo 'ndhakārāt / ityevaṃ bodhisattvo māyāyā devyāḥ kukṣerabhiniṣkramaṇaṃ saṃdarśayāmāsa māyāgatarūpavijñaptisaṃdarśanadharmatayā anāgatadharmatayā anutpādānirodhalokavijñaptisaṃdarśanadharmatayā //
body.translated_text: These, son of good family, are the ten birth-transformations of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that manifested in <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. Thereafter, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, displaying an inconceivable, immeasurable, radiance-anointing vision, emerged from the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s> — like the orb of the sun from the vault of the sky, like a flash of lightning from a mass of clouds, like twilight glow from a great dense mountain peak, like a great lamp from the darkness of gloom. Thus did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> display his emergence from the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s>, by the nature of displaying the perception of form through the manner of <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), by the nature of the unarisen, by the nature of displaying the perception of a world that is unproduced and unceased. //

body.text: ityevamahaṃ kulaputra bhagavato vairocanasya janmavikurvitasamudrānavatarāmi iha lumbinīvane viharamāṇā / yathā cāhaṃ kulaputra syāṃ bhāgavatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ bhagavato vairocanasya janmavikurvitasamudrānavatarāmi, tathā sarvāvatyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvacāturdvīpikāsu koṭīśatajambudvīpānāṃ sarvatra bhagavato vairocanasya janmavikurvitānyavatarāmi / yathā cāhaṃ kulaputra asyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvacāturdvīpikāsu koṭīśatajambudvīpānāṃ bhagavato vairocanasya koṭīśataṃ janmavikurvitānāmavatarāmi, evaṃ sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparyāpannaparamāṇurajontargateṣu sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥpraveśajñānānugateṣu praticittakṣaṇamekaikena cittapraveśena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni bhagavato vairocanasya janmavikurvitānyavatarāmi / tadanantareṇa cittena buddhakṣetrasahasraparamāṇurajontargateṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ekaikatra buddhatatsamānyeva bodhisattvajanmavikurvitānyavatarāmi / etena nayena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajontargateṣu
body.translated_text: Thus, O son of good family, I descend into the ocean of birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> while dwelling here in <s>Lumbinī</s> grove. And just as I, O son of good family, descend into the ocean of birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> in this blessed <s>cāturdvīpikā</s> (four-continent world-system), so too throughout the entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (triple-thousand great-thousand) world-realm, in all four-continent world-systems, in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Jambudvīpas</s>, everywhere I descend into the birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>. And just as I, O son of good family, in this triple-thousand great-thousand world-realm descend into hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> across all four-continent world-systems and hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Jambudvīpas</s>, so too within the atoms contained in all triple-thousand great-thousand world-realms, guided by the knowledge of entering all atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, at every mind-moment, with each single entry of mind, I descend into birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. With the immediately subsequent mind, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields contained within the atoms of thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in each and every one I descend into <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles equal in number to those very <s>Buddhas</s>. By this method, within <s>Buddha</s>-fields contained in the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields

body.text: buddhakṣetreṣvekaikasmin buddhakṣetre sarvāṇi bodhisattvajanmavikurvitānyavatarāmi, na ca paryantamupaimi / sarvaparamāṇurajaḥsu ekaikasmin paramāṇurajasi buddhakṣetraparaṃparāṇāṃ na ca paryantamupaimi sarvakṣetreṣvekaikasmin buddhakṣetre buddhasattvajanmaparaṃparāṇām / yathā ceha lokadhātau sarvāṇi bodhisattvajanmavikurvitānyavatarāmi, tathā daśasu dikṣu anantamadhyāsu lokadhātuṣu sarvaparamāṇurajaḥsu praticittakṣaṇamekaikena cittapraveśena sarvākārāṇi sarvabodhisattvajanmavikurvitānyavatarāmyapratiprasrabdhyadhiṣṭhānayogena //
body.translated_text: in each and every <s>Buddha</s>-field I descend into all <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles, and I reach no limit. In all atoms, in each single atom, I reach no limit of the successions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields; in all fields, in each single <s>Buddha</s>-field, I reach no limit of the successions of <s>bodhisattva</s> births. And just as in this world-realm I descend into all <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles, so too in the ten directions, in infinite and middleless world-realms, in all atoms, at every mind-moment, with each single entry of mind, I descend into all forms of all <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles through the yoga of unrelenting empowerment. //

body.text: evamukte sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyaṃ lumbinīvanadevatāmevamāha kiyaccirapratilabdhastvayāyaṃ devate aprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitaṃ saṃdarśayamāno bodhisattvajanmavimokṣaḥ? āha - bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani buddhakṣetrakoṭīparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa parataramīśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān samantaratnāyāṃ lokadhātau samāpadyate kalpe 'śītibuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraprabhave / tasyāṃ khalu kulaputra samantaratnāyāṃ lokadhātau vicitravyūhaprabhā nāma madhyamā cāturdvīpikābhūt / tasyāṃ khalu cāturdvīpikāyāṃ madhye jambudvīpasya meruviśuddhavyūhadhvajā nāma rājadhānyabhūt / tasyāṃ khalu rājadhānyāṃ ratnārcinetraprabho nāma rājā abhūt / rājñaḥ khalu kulaputra ratnārcinetraprabhasya rājñaḥ suharṣitaprabheśvarā nāma bhāryābhūt / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra asyāṃ bhāgavatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāmiha jambudvīpe māyādevī bhagavato vairocanasya janetrī, evameva kulaputra tena kālena tena samayena tasyāṃ vicitravyūhaprabhāyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ jambudvīpe suharṣitaprabheśvarā nāma tasya bhagavata īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajasya tathāgatasya mātā abhūt / yathā teṣāmaśītibuddhakoṭīniyutānāṃ pūrvaṃgamasya prāthamakalpikasya bhagavata īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajasya tathāgatasya mātā abhūt / sā khalu kulaputra suharṣitaprabheśvarā devī bodhisattvasya janmakālasamaye viṃśatyā strīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍalaṃ nāma mahodyānaṃ niryayau, yatra tamīśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajaṃ kumāraṃ janayāmāsa acintyena bodhisattvavikurvitena / tena khalu punaḥ samayena suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍalasya nāma mahodyānasya madhye śubharatnavicitrakūṭaṃ nāma kūṭāgāramabhūt / tasmin kūṭāgāre sarvakāmaṃdadavṛkṣaśākhāmadhyālambatayā suharṣitaprabheśvarāyā devyāḥ sa bhagavānīśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajastathāgato janitaḥ / tena khalu samayena tasya bhagavato janmakāle vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā nāma dhātrī pratyupasthitābhūt / jātamātraṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ lokendrā vicitrasurabhimanojñadivyapuṣpotkarodgāribhiḥ paramasurabhigandhodakakalaśairvisnāpya tadarhābhiśca acintyāsaṃkhyeyābhiruttamābhiḥ pūjābhirabhipūjya tasyā vimalasaṃbhavaprabhāyā dhātryā aṅke prāyacchan / parigṛhītamātre ca tasmin bodhisattve tayā dhātryā ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāmaṃse ca, tatkṣaṇameva sā dhātrī mahāprītiprāmodyavegapratilabdhā samantacakṣurviṣayaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratyalabhata, yasya samādheḥ
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son said to <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess, thus: 'How long ago, O goddess, did you attain this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation that displays immeasurable <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles initiating all <s>kalpas</s>?' She replied: 'Long ago, O son of good family, in the past age, beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s> (Banner of Unconquered Lordly Qualities) arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>, appearing in the world-realm called <s>Samantaratnā</s>, in a <s>kalpa</s> that gave rise to eighty <s>koṭi</s> <s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. In that world-realm <s>Samantaratnā</s>, O son of good family, there was a central <s>cāturdvīpikā</s> called <s>Vicitravyūhaprabhā</s> (Splendor of Marvelous Arrays). In the middle of that four-continent world-system, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, there was a royal capital called <s>Meruviśuddhavyūhadhvajā</s> (Banner of the Pure Array of Meru). In that royal capital there was a king named <s>Ratnārcinetraprabha</s> (Radiance of Jewel-Flame Eyes). That king <s>Ratnārcinetraprabha</s>, O son of good family, had a queen named <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s> (Sovereign Lady of Joyful Radiance). Just as, O son of good family, in this blessed four-continent world-system, here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Māyādevī</s> is the mother of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, even so, at that time and on that occasion, in that four-continent world-system <s>Vicitravyūhaprabhā</s>, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the queen <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s> was the mother of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s>. She was the mother of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s>, who was the forerunner and the first of the <s>kalpa</s> among those eighty <s>koṭi</s> <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. That queen <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s>, O son of good family, at the time of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s birth, went forth with twenty <s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of women to a great park called <s>Suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of Golden Flower Radiance), where she gave birth to the prince <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s> through an inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformation. At that time, in the midst of the great park <s>Suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍala</s>, there was a pavilion called <s>Śubharatnavicitrakūṭa</s> (Peak of Auspicious Variegated Gems). In that pavilion, while the queen <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s> leaned upon the middle branch of the wish-fulfilling tree, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s>, was born. At the time of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s birth, a nurse named <s>Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā</s> (Radiance of Stainless Arising) came forward and attended. As soon as the <s>bodhisattva</s> was born, the World-Lords bathed him with supremely fragrant water-vessels overflowing with showers of various fragrant and lovely divine flowers, worshipped him with inconceivable and innumerable supreme offerings, and placed him in the arms of the nurse <s>Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā</s>. The very moment the <s>bodhisattva</s> was received by that nurse in both hands and on her lap, that nurse, seized by a great surge of joy and delight, attained a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Samantacakṣurviṣaya</s> (Domain of Universal Vision), upon attaining which <s>samādhi</s>

body.text:
sahapratilābhāttasmāddaśasu dikṣu nānālokadhātusthitā aprameyāstathāgatāścakṣuṣa ābhāsamagaman / eṣa ca aprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśano
bodhisattvavimokṣo 'vakrāntaḥ susūkṣmaḥ tadyathāpi nāma taddivasāvakrānte mātuḥ kukṣau garbhavijñānam, yasya vimokṣasya pratilambhādanayā sarvatathāgatajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanamahāpraṇidhirabhinirhṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: with its very attainment, innumerable <s>Tathāgatas</s> abiding in various world-realms in the ten directions became visible to her eye. And this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation — the display of <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles initiating all immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> — entered subtly, just as on that very day the embryonic consciousness entered the mother's womb. Through the attainment of this liberation, the great vow of displaying the birth-miracles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> was brought forth by this method. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā nāma bodhisattvadhātryabhūt? na khalu punastvayā evaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā nāma bodhisattvadhātryabhūvam / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyāni tena kālena tena samayena viṃśatistrīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / imāni tāni viṃśatidevatāniyutaśatasahasrāṇi, yānīha lumbinīvane prativasanti mama parivārāḥ / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena supraharṣitaprabheśvarā nāma devyabhūdīśvaraguṇāparājitadhvajasya kumārasya janetrī? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / iyaṃ sā māyādevī tena kālena tena samayena supraharṣitaprabheśvarā nāma devyabhūt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ratnārcinetraprabho nāma rājā abhūt / na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ayaṃ sa rājā śuddhodanaḥ tena kālena tena samayen ratnārcinetraprabho nāma rājā abhūt / sā khalvahaṃ kulaputra tata upādāya sarvacittakṣaṇeṣvavirahitā abhūvaṃ bhagavato vairocanasya bodhisattvajanmavikurvitasāgarāvataraṇatayā sattvanayavṛṣabhitāvikurvitasāgarāvataraṇatayā //
body.translated_text: What do you think, O son of good family — was that nurse named <s>Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā</s> at that time and on that occasion someone else? You should certainly not regard it thus. I myself was the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s nurse named <s>Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā</s> at that time and on that occasion. What do you think, O son of good family — were those twenty <s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of women at that time and on that occasion others? You should certainly not regard it thus. These are those very twenty <s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of goddesses who dwell here in <s>Lumbinī</s> grove as my retinue. What do you think, O son of good family — was the queen named <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s>, the mother of the prince <s>Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja</s>, at that time and on that occasion someone else? You should certainly not regard it thus. This very <s>Māyādevī</s> was at that time and on that occasion the queen named <s>Suharṣitaprabheśvarā</s>. What do you think, O son of good family — was the king named <s>Ratnārcinetraprabha</s> at that time and on that occasion someone else? You should certainly not regard it thus. This very King <s>Śuddhodana</s> was at that time and on that occasion the king named <s>Ratnārcinetraprabha</s>. From that time on, O son of good family, I have never been without this at any mind-moment, through descending into the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, and through descending into the ocean of transformations for the conduct of bringing about the rain of beings. //

body.text: yathā cāhaṃ kulaputra asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau bhagavato vairocanasya mahāpraṇidhānasamudrasāgarasaṃbhavānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sarvacittakṣaṇeṣu sarvaparamāṇurajaḥpraveśasamavasṛtena jñānacakṣuṣā sarvaparamāṇurajaḥsu kṣetrasamudrānavatarāmi, teṣu ca kṣetreṣu tathāgatotpādasāgarānavatarāmi / yathā teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ bodhisattvajanmavikurvitamahāsamudrānavatarāmi, tathā daśasu dikṣu anantamadhyānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sarvacittakṣaṇeṣu bodhisattvajanmavikurvitasāgarānavatarāmi / yathā ca asyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvaparamāṇurajaḥprasaraparaṃparāvatāreṇa samyaksaṃbuddhabodhisattvajanmābhimukhībhāvagatān buddhaguṇānavatarāmi, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥprasarāntargatān kṣetrasāgarānavatarāmi / teṣu ca vipulān buddhasamudrānavatarāmi / tāṃśca buddhān bhagavato bodhisattvabhūtajanmavikurvitasaṃmukhībhāvagatān paśyāmi / tathāgatabhūtānapi pūjayāmi / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇomi, dharmasya ca anudharmaṃ pratipadye //
body.translated_text: And just as I, O son of good family, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, with the eye of knowledge that converges with all atoms at every mind-moment for all <s>Tathāgatas</s> arisen from the ocean-sea of great vows of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, descend into oceans of fields in all atoms, and in those fields descend into the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s>-arisings — just as I descend into the great ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so too in the ten directions, at every mind-moment, I descend into the ocean of <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles of infinite and middleless <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And just as in this triple-thousand great-thousand world-realm, through descending into the succession of all atoms, I witness the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of those who face the birth of the Perfectly Awakened <s>bodhisattva</s>, so too in the ten directions I descend into field-oceans contained within the succession of atoms of unspeakable <s>koṭi</s> <s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And in those I descend into vast <s>Buddha</s>-oceans. And I behold those <s>Buddhas</s> who face the <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. I also worship those who have become <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And I listen to the <s>Dharma</s>-teachings of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and I practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrīrlumbinīvanadevatā evamevāprameyasarvakalpasarvāvaraṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanabodhisattvavimokṣaṃ paridīpayamānā buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove goddess <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, while illuminating the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation that displays <s>bodhisattva</s> birth-miracles initiating all immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, surveying the ten directions through the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, at that moment spoke these verses:

body.text: buddhaputra śṛṇu mahya bhāṣitaṃ yasmi pṛcchasi janitva gauravam /
body.translated_text: O son of the <s>Buddha</s>, hear my speech regarding that about which you ask, having generated reverence;

body.text: śānta durdṛśu jināna gocaro hetukāraṇanayairnidarśitaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: peaceful, hard to see, the domain of the <s>Jinas</s>, demonstrated through the methods of causes and conditions. // 1 //

children.translated_text: I remember inconceivable former <s>kalpas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of <s>koṭis</s> of fields,

children.text: kalpa ādiriva ananta nāyako yatrāśītinayutā jinānabhūt // 2 //
children.translated_text: where the <s>kalpa</s> was like a beginningless, infinite <s>Nāyaka</s> (Leader), in which eighty <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Jinas</s> arose. // 2 //
At that time, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Īśvarājitaguṇadhvaja</s> (Banner of Lordly Conquered Qualities) was the first among them,

children.text: jānamāna maya draṣṭu nāyakaḥ svarṇapuṣpaprabhave vanottame // 3 //
children.translated_text: and I, seeing the birth of that <s>Nāyaka</s>, was in the finest park called <s>Suvarṇapuṣpaprabhava</s> (Arising of Golden Flowers). // 3 //

children.text: nāmato vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā tasya āsi ahu dhātri paṇḍitā /
children.translated_text: By the name <s>Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā</s>, I was his wise nurse,

children.text: lokapāla mama aṃsi taṃ sthapī jātamātra kanakottamaprabham // 4 //
children.translated_text: and the World-Protectors placed him in my arms — the newborn one, radiant as the finest gold. // 4 //

children.text: aṃsi taṃ grahiya agrapudgalaṃ mūrdhnimasya na prabhomi prekṣitum /
children.translated_text: Having received him in my arms, that foremost being, I could not gaze upon the crown of his head;

children.text: * * * * taṃ acintiyaṃ prekṣamāṇa na ca antu paśyami // 5 //
children.translated_text: * * * * that inconceivable one — gazing upon him, I could not see his limit. // 5 //

children.text: lakṣaṇebhi pratimaṇḍitaṃ śubhaṃ kāyamasya vimalaṃ sudarśanam /
children.translated_text: His body, adorned with the marks, auspicious, stainless, beautiful to behold,

children.text: dṛṣṭa me ratanabimbasādṛśaṃ prītivega atulā vivardhitāḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: appeared to me like an image of jewels — surges of incomparable joy increased. // 6 //

children.text: cintayitva guṇa tasya me 'mitān puṇyasāgara ameya vardhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Reflecting upon his immeasurable qualities, oceans of merit were increased;

children.text: dṛṣṭva tasya ca vikurvitodadhīn bodhicittavipulaṃ mi saṃbhutam // 7 //
children.translated_text: and having witnessed his ocean of transformations, vast <s>bodhicitta</s> (aspiration for awakening) arose in me. // 7 //
Having aspired toward the oceans of <s>Jina</s>-qualities, my ocean of vows was increased;
all field-successions were purified, all paths of evil destinies were turned back. // 8 //

body.text: pūjanāya sugatānacintiyān sarvakṣetraprasareṣvanāgatān /
body.translated_text: For worshipping the inconceivable <s>Sugatas</s> who have come through all field-successions,

body.text: sattvaduḥkhitavimocanāya ca proditaḥ praṇidhisāgaro mama // 9 //
body.translated_text: and for liberating suffering beings — my ocean of vows has arisen. // 9 //

children.text: śrutva dharmamatha tasya tāyino labdhimaṃ varavimokṣamaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of that Protector, I obtained this excellent jewel of liberation;
to purify awakening, I have wandered for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to <s>koṭis</s> of atoms of fields, // 10 //

children.text: yeṣu yāntakupapanna nāyakā te aśeṣa mayi sarvi pūjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: and in whichever <s>Nāyakas</s> (Leaders) arose therein, all of them without exception have been worshipped by me.

children.text: śāsanaṃ ca maya teṣu dhāritaṃ śodhanā imu vimokṣasāgaram // 11 //
children.translated_text: And I upheld the teaching among them, purifying this ocean of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). // 11 //
Equal to the atoms of koṭis of buddha-fields were the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered Ones) of the past,
I upheld the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) of those [Buddhas] and cultivated the excellent <s>vimokṣamaṇḍala</s> (sphere of liberation). // 12 //

children.text: buddhakṣetri raja yāvato iho tān rajāgraprasarābdhi paśyatī /
children.translated_text: As many atoms as there are in buddha-fields here, she beholds those oceans of foremost expanses of atoms,

children.text: ekameki raji kṣetrasāgarān pūrva śodhita jinena paśyatī // 13 //
children.translated_text: In each single atom she beholds oceans of fields formerly purified by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). // 13 //

children.text: teṣu kṣetraprasareṣu nāyakān jāyato vanavareṣu paśyami /
children.translated_text: In those expanses of fields I behold the Leaders being born in the finest groves,
In a single moment of thought, inconceivable, displaying vast miraculous transformations. // 14 //

children.text: paśyami kvaci ca kṣetri nāyakān prārthayanta varabodhimuttamām /
children.translated_text: Somewhere I behold in fields the Leaders aspiring to the supreme and excellent <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening),
Abiding in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven [...] with inconceivable koṭi-nayutas of fields. // 15 //
Being born with vast miraculous transformations, I behold them in hundreds of oceans of fields,
Accompanied by an excellent assembly of women, the Leaders teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. // 16 //
Equal to the atoms of koṭis of fields, in a single moment of thought, O hero, I behold them,
Displaying to the world in manifold ways, in a single instant, peaceful <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). // 17 //

children.text: janma yātuka jināna paśyami prekṣamāṇa raji kṣetrasāgarān /
children.translated_text: I behold the births the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) have undergone, gazing upon oceans of fields of atoms,

children.text: janmi janmi bahukāyakoṭibhiḥ pūji teṣa karuṇāmupāgami // 18 //
children.translated_text: In birth after birth, with many koṭis of bodies, I worshipped them and approached their compassion. // 18 //
Through inconceivable methods of oceans of fields, inexhaustible, those who have gone forth in courses of destiny,

children.text: teṣu sarvajagadāmukhā ahaṃ dharmamegha vipulān pravarṣami // 19 //
children.translated_text: Among them all, as leader of all beings, I shower vast clouds of <s>Dharma</s>. // 19 //
This inconceivable [liberation] I know, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, the excellent sphere of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation),

children.text: kalpakoṭinayutairacintiyairyaṃ na śakya ayu sarva darśitum // 20 //
children.translated_text: Which cannot be fully shown even in inconceivable koṭi-nayutas of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). // 20 //

body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra aprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe sarvakalpaprasthānagarbhasaṃbhūtacittānāṃ sarvadharmanayanidhyaptijātinidarśakānāṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpraṇidhisaṃbhūtāśayānāṃ sarvabuddhadharmābhisaṃbodhipraṇidhiparamāṇāṃ sarvakulagotropapattigatisaṃdarśanapratibhāsakalpānāṃ sarvatathāgatapādamūlapadmagarbhopapattīnāṃ sarvajagatparipākakālābhijñānāṃ sarvavinayābhimukhajanmopapattivikurvitasaṃdarśakānāṃ sarvakṣetraprasaravikurvitameghasaṃdarśakānāṃ sarvajagadgatijātikulapratibhāsaprāptānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: This, O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva-vimokṣa</s> (bodhisattva liberation) called 'Display of the Miraculous Transformations of Bodhisattva Births Sustained by All Objects across Immeasurable Kalpas' that I know. How could I know the conduct or speak of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> whose minds arise from the womb of all <s>kalpa</s>-courses in every moment of thought, who demonstrate births through penetration of all <s>dharma</s>-methods, whose aspirations arise from the worship and vows directed toward all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whose vows aim at the awakening to all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, whose <s>kalpas</s> manifest the display of births in all families and lineages, who are born in the lotus-wombs at the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who possess superknowledge of the time for ripening all beings, who display miraculous birth-manifestations directed toward the discipline of all, who display clouds of miraculous transformations across all field-expanses, and who have attained the reflection of the births, destinies, and families of all beings?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva kapilavastuni mahānagare gopā nāma śākyakanyā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvaparipākāya saṃsāre saṃsaritavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, O son of good family! Here in this very <s>Kapilavastu</s>, the great city, there dwells a <s>Śākya</s> maiden named <s>Gopā</s>. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the ripening of <s>bodhisattvas</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyo lumbinīvanadevatāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyaṃ lumbinīvanadevatāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyo lumbinīvanadevatāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 40 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, bowing his head at the feet of <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s>, the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove deity, circumambulating <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove deity many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove deity. // 40 //

body.text: 43 gopā /

atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sutejomaṇḍalaratiśriyo lumbinīvanadevatāyā antikādapakramya yena kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkramya etamevāprameyakalpasarvārambaṇabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ bhāvayan avataran vipulīkurvan anutiṣṭhan uttāpayan parijayan paricintayan pravicinvan anupūrveṇa yena dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabho bodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādastenopasaṃkrāmat / tasyopasaṃkramaṇasya aśokaśrīrnāma bodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādadevatā daśabhirgṛhadevatāsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ pratyudgamya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamevamāha - svāgataṃ te mahāpuruṣa mahāprajñājñānavikrāmin acintyabodhisattvavimokṣabhāvanādhyālambanapraṇidhicittavipuladharmavimānagocaracārin dharmanagarābhimukha anantabodhisattvopāyanayāvatāraṇāpratiprasrabdhatathāgataguṇasāgarāvabhāsapratilabdha sarvajagadvinayapratibhāsapratibhānajñānābhimukhasarvasattvacaryājñānakāyamantrānuvartana caryābhimukhacitta sarvajagadvedanāprītisamudravegavivardhanapraṇidhāna sarvatathāgatadharmaprativedhamārgapratipanna / yathā tvāṃ paśyāmi animiṣanetragambhīracaryeryāpathaviśuddhagocaram, nacireṇa tvamanuttaratathāgatakāyavākcittālaṃkāraviśuddhiṃ pratilabdho lakṣaṇānuvyañjanapratimaṇḍitena kāyena daśabalajñānālokālaṃkṛtena cittena lokaṃ vicariṣyasi / yādṛśīṃ ca te dṛḍhavīryaparākramatāṃ paśyāmi, nacireṇa tvaṃ sarvatryadhvatathāgatasaṃmukhībhāvadarśanasamaṅgī sarvatathāgatadharmameghān saṃpratīcchan sarvabodhisattvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattiśāntadharmavimānaratimanubhavan gambhīraṃ buddhavimokṣamanupravekṣyasi / tathā hi tvaṃ kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇadarśanaparyupāsanānuśāsanīḥ saṃpratīcchaṃstadguṇapratinayeṣu prayujyamāno na parikhidyase, na vinivartase, na paritapasi / na ca te kaścidantarāyo vā āvaraṇaṃ vā nivaraṇaṃ vā prasahate, mārā vā mārakāyikā vā devatāḥ / tena acirādeva tvaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ prītikaro bhaviṣyasi //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, departing from the presence of <s>Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī</s> the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove deity, approached the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, contemplating, entering into, expanding, practicing, developing, mastering, reflecting upon, and investigating this very <s>bodhisattva-vimokṣa</s> called 'Display of the Miraculous Transformations of Bodhisattva Births Sustained by All Objects across Immeasurable Kalpas.' Gradually he approached the <s>Bodhisattvasaṃgīti</s> (Bodhisattva Assembly) palace called <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabha</s> (Radiance of the Reflection of the Dharma-realm). As he approached, a <s>bodhisattvasaṃgīti</s> palace deity named <s>Aśokaśrī</s>, together with ten thousand household deities, came forth to meet him and addressed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son thus: 'Welcome, O great being, you who stride with great wisdom-knowledge, whose range is the vast dharma-palace sustained by the vow of cultivating inconceivable <s>bodhisattva-vimokṣas</s> (liberations), who face the city of <s>Dharma</s>, who have attained the radiance of the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities through unrelenting entry into infinite <s>bodhisattva</s> methods, whose body of knowledge follows the <s>mantras</s> of the conduct-knowledge of all beings directed toward the reflection of the disciplines of all beings, whose mind faces practice, whose vow increases the ocean-force of joy and feeling of all beings, who have entered the path of penetrating the <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. As I behold you, one whose range is the pure conduct of unwinking eyes and profound deportment, before long you, having attained the purity of the unsurpassed ornament of the body, speech, and mind of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, will wander through the world with a body adorned with the marks and secondary characteristics and a mind illuminated by the light of the knowledge of the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten Powers). And seeing your firm heroic valor, before long you will attain the direct vision of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, receive the clouds of <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, enjoy the delight of the peaceful dharma-palace of the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and enter the profound <s>Buddha-vimokṣa</s> (Buddha liberation). For indeed, you who approach, behold, attend upon, and receive the instructions of spiritual friends, and who apply yourself to following their qualities, do not become weary, do not turn back, do not become distressed. And neither <s>Māra</s> nor the deities of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue can overcome you with obstacles, hindrances, or obstructions. Therefore, before long, you will become the source of joy for all beings.'

body.text: evamukte sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'śokaśriyaṃ bodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādadevatāmetadavocat - tathāstu devate yathā vadasi / ahaṃ khalu devate sarvasattvakleśasaṃtāpavyupaśamena paramāṃ prītiṃ vindāmi / sarvasattvaviṣayakarmavipākavinivartanena sarvasattvasukhasaṃbhavena sarvasattvānavadyakarmapratipattyā paramāṃ prītiṃ vindāmi / yadā ca devate sattvā vividhaviṣayakarmakleśaprayogākṣiptacittā durgatiṣu prapatanti sugatiṣu vā, vividhāni kāyikacaitasikāni duḥkhadaurmanasyāni pratyanubhavanti, durmanasastasmin samaye bodhisattvā bhavanti paramadurmanasaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma devate puruṣasyaikāntatṛṣṇācaritasya ekaputrako bhavet priyo manāpaḥ / sa tasyāṅgapratyaṅgeṣu cchidyamāneṣu ekāntatṛṣṇācaritatvāt paramadurmanāḥ syādanāttamanaskaḥ, evameva devate bodhisattvo bodhisattvacārikāṃ caran sattvān karmakleśavaśena tisṛṣu durgatiṣu patitān dṛṣṭvā durmanā bhavati paramadurmanāḥ / yasmin vā punaḥ samaye sattvāḥ kāyavāṅbhanaḥsucaritasamādanahetoḥ kāyasya bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante, devamanuṣyagatiṣu ca kāyikacaitasikāni sukhāni pratyanubhavanti, paramasukhī tasmin samaye bodhisattvo bhavati sumanā āttamanaskaḥ pramuditaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son said to <s>Aśokaśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattvasaṃgīti</s> palace deity: 'May it be so, O deity, as you say! I indeed, O deity, find supreme joy in the pacification of the afflictions of all beings, in turning all beings away from the ripening of actions in the sense-domains, in the arising of happiness for all beings, and in the practice of blameless actions by all beings. And when, O deity, beings whose minds are driven by the exertions of various sense-domain actions and afflictions fall into the evil destinies or [even] into the good destinies, and experience various bodily and mental sufferings and displeasures, at that time <s>bodhisattvas</s> become distressed, supremely distressed. Just as, O deity, if a man of utterly devoted affection had an only son, dear and beloved, and if that son's limbs were being cut apart, due to his utterly devoted affection he would become supremely distressed and disheartened -- even so, O deity, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> career, seeing beings fallen into the three evil destinies through the power of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), becomes distressed, supremely distressed. And again, when beings, through the undertaking of good conduct of body, speech, and mind, upon the dissolution of the body are reborn in the good destiny, in the heavenly world among the gods, and experience bodily and mental happiness in the destinies of gods and humans, at that time the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes supremely happy, glad, uplifted, and joyful.

body.text:
prītisaumanasyajātaḥ / na khalu punardevate bodhisattvā ātmārthāya sarvajñatāmabhiprārthayante / na vicitrasaṃsāraratisukhaprabhavanārthaṃ na kāmadhātuparyāpannaṃ vividharativyūhaprārthanayā saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsavaśena na saṃyojanabandhanānuśayaparyavasthānavaśagatāḥ / na tṛṣṇādṛṣṭivaśagatāḥ, na vividhasattvasaṃsargaratisaṃjñāvinibaddhacetasaḥ, na dhyānaratisukhāsvādaparigṛddhāḥ, na vividhāvaraṇāvṛtāḥ saṃsāragatiṣu parivartante / api tu khalu punardevate bodhisattvā bhavasamudragatānāmaparimitaduḥkhaprapīḍitānāṃ sattvānāmantike mahākaruṇāṃ saṃjanayitvā sarvajagatsaṃgrahamahāpraṇidhimabhinirharanti / te mahākaruṇāpraṇidhyabhinirhārabalavegena sattvaparipākavinayaprayuktāḥ saṃsāre bodhisattvacaryāṃ carantaḥ saṃdṛśyante / te sarvasattvanāṃ sarvāvaraṇasarvajñatājñānaṃ paryeṣamāṇāḥ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānapraṇidhimabhinirharanti / te tathāgatapūjopasthānapraṇidhivaśairna parikhidyante bodhisattvacaryāyām / te bodhisattvacaryāṃ carantaḥ saṃkliṣṭāni kṣetrāṇi saṃpaśyantaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanapraṇidhimabhinirharanti
saṃkliṣṭān kṣetrasāgarān pariśodhayamānāḥ sarvasattvānāmāyatananānātvaṃ saṃpaśyamānāḥ / anānātvānuttaradharmakāyapariśuddhaye praṇidhimabhinirharanti saṃkliṣṭakāyavākcittatāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃpaśyamānāḥ / sarvasattvakāyavākcittālaṃkārapariśuddhaye praṇidhimabhinirharanti / vikalāyatanānapariśuddhacetasaḥ sarvān saṃpaśyamānāḥ sarvasattvacittacaritāni pariśodhayamānā bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranto na parikhidyante / evaṃ hi devate bodhisattvā anantamadhyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranto 'parikhinnacittāḥ / evaṃ caranto 'laṃkārabhūtā bhavanti sadevakasya lokasya devamanuṣyasaṃpattisaṃjananatayā / mātāpitṛbhūtā bhavanti bodhisattvotpādapratiṣṭhāpanatayā / dhātrībhūtā bhavanti bodhisattvamārgāvataraṇatayā / nityānubaddhasahajadevatā bhavanti durgatiprapātabhayārakṣaṇatayā / mahādāśabhūtā bhavanti saṃsārasamudrottāraṇatayā / śaraṇabhūtā bhavanti sarvamārakleśabhayavinivartanatayā / parāyaṇabhūtā bhavanti antaparamaśītibhāvopanayanatayā / tīrthabhūtā bhavanti sarvabuddhasamudrāvataraṇayā / saṃgrāhakabhūtā bhavanti dharmaratnadvīpopanayanatayā / puṣpabhūtā bhavanti sarvabuddhaguṇasaṃpuṣpitacittatayā / alaṃkārabhūtā bhavanti vipulapuṇyajñānaprabhāpramuñcanatayā / paramaprītikarā bhavanti samantaprāsādikatayā / abhigamanīyā bhavanti anavadyakarmapratipattyā / samantabhadrā bhavanti sarvākāravarāṅgasuparipūrṇakāyatayā / asecanakarūpā bhavanti apratikūladarśanatayā / avabhāsakarā bhavanti jñānaraśmipramuñcanatayā / ālokakarā bhavanti dharmapradīpadhāraṇatayā / pradyotakarā bhavanti bodhyāśayapariśodhanatayā / senāpatibhūtā bhavanti mārakarmavinivartanatayā / sūryabhūtā bhavanti prajñāraśmijālaprabhāpramuñcanatayā / candrabhūtā bhavanti gaganabuddhicandrodāgamanatayā / meghabhūtā bhavanti sarvajaganmahādharmameghābhipravarṣaṇatayā / evaṃ khalu devate pratipadyamānā bodhisattvāḥ priyā bhavanti sarvasattvānām //
