body.translated_text:
filled with joy and gladness. Indeed, O goddess, <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not seek <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) for their own sake. Not for the sake of producing the pleasure and happiness of variegated <s>saṃsāra</s>, not through the desire for various arrays of pleasure belonging to the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), not under the power of the perversion of perception, thought, and view, not fallen under the power of fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, and entanglements. Not fallen under the power of craving and views, not with minds bound by the perception of delight in association with various beings, not greedy for the taste of the pleasure of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), not covered by various obstructions do they revolve in the courses of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Rather, O goddess, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having generated great compassion toward beings who have entered the ocean of existence and are afflicted by immeasurable suffering, bring forth the great vow to embrace all the world. By the force and momentum of bringing forth that great compassion-vow, they are seen practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct in <s>saṃsāra</s>, engaged in the ripening and training of beings. Seeking the <s>sarvajñatā</s>-knowledge that removes all obstructions for all beings, they bring forth the vow of worship and attendance upon all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Through the power of that vow of worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they do not grow weary in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. Practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct and seeing the defiled fields, they bring forth the vow to purify all <s>Buddha-fields</s>.
Purifying the oceans of defiled fields and perceiving the diversity of the sense-faculties of all beings, they bring forth the vow for the purification of the unsurpassed <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) which is without diversity. Seeing the defilement of body, speech, and mind of beings, they bring forth the vow for the purification and adornment of the body, speech, and mind of all beings. Seeing all those with impaired faculties and impure minds, purifying the mental conduct and dispositions of all beings, they practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct without growing weary. Thus indeed, O goddess, <s>bodhisattvas</s> practice the endless and boundless <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct with unwearied minds. Practicing thus, they become ornaments of the world together with its gods, by generating the prosperity of gods and humans. They become like parents, by establishing the arising of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-aspiration. They become like nurses, by causing entry into the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path. They become ever-attendant innate deities, by protecting from the fear of falling into evil destinies. They become great helmsmen, by ferrying across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. They become refuges, by turning back the fear of all <s>Māra</s>s and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). They become final resorts, by leading to the state of the ultimate and supreme cool. They become fords, by enabling entry into the ocean of all <s>Buddhas</s>. They become gatherers, by leading to the island of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>. They become flowers, by having minds blossoming with all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. They become ornaments, by releasing the radiance of vast merit and wisdom. They become supremely delightful, by being universally pleasing. They become approachable, by practicing blameless actions. They become universally auspicious, by having bodies perfectly endowed with all excellent limbs. They become beautiful in form, by being not unpleasant to behold. They become illuminators, by releasing rays of wisdom. They become light-bringers, by holding the lamp of <s>Dharma</s>. They become beacons, by purifying the disposition toward awakening. They become generals, by turning back the works of <s>Māra</s>. They become suns, by releasing the radiance of the net of rays of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). They become moons, by the rising of the moon of space-like intelligence. They become clouds, by raining the great <s>Dharma</s>-cloud upon the entire world. Thus indeed, O goddess, <s>bodhisattvas</s> who practice in this way become dear to all beings.

body.text: atha khalu aśokaśrīrbodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādadevatā sārdhaṃ tairdaśabhiḥ gṛhadevatāsahasraiḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ divyasamatikrāntaiḥ manomayaiḥ puṣpamālyagandhacūrṇavilepanaratnābharaṇavarṣaiḥ pravṛṣya anuparivārya bodhisattvabhavanaṃ praviśantamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Aśokaśrī</s>, the deity of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly palace, together with those ten thousand household deities, having showered <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son with rains of divine and surpassingly exquisite mind-created flowers, garlands, incense, powders, unguents, and jeweled ornaments, and having surrounded him, praised him with these verses as he entered the <s>bodhisattva</s>-abode:

children.translated_text: The <s>Jinas</s> arise in the world, sometimes, as suns of wisdom,
having generated the mind toward <s>saṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening) out of compassion for all beings. // 1 //
Through myriads of <s>kalpas</s> their sight is difficult to obtain,
you are a great sun of wisdom for the world blinded by ignorance. // 2 //
Having seen the world perverted, enveloped in the darkness of ignorance,
generating great compassion, you have set forth toward the state of the Self-arisen. // 3 //
With purified intention, you are striving for <s>Buddha</s>-awakening,
you serve the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend), without regard for body or life. // 4 //

children.text: na niśrayaste loke 'sminna niketo na saṃstavaḥ /
children.translated_text: You have no reliance in this world, no dwelling, no intimacy,
without attachment, unentangled, free from clinging, with a mind like space. // 5 //
You practice the supreme conduct of awakening, resplendent with the circle of merit,
releasing rays of wisdom upon a world of rising and setting. // 6 //
You do not depart from the world, yet you are not stained by worldly conditions,
you move unattached in the world, like the wind in the sky. // 7 //
Like fire blazing in the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, ever active,
with fire-like vigor you practice the conduct of awakening. // 8 //
Lion-like, O great hero, with firm vigor and valor,
endowed with the power of wisdom, you move undefeated. // 9 //
In this ocean of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), whatever oceans of method there are,
through serving the true friend, O hero, you shall enter them all. // 10 //

body.text: atha khalvaśokaśrīrbodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādadevatā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya gacchantaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubadhnāti sma dharmakāmatayā / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabhabodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādamupasaṃkramya anupraviśya samantādanuvilokayāmāsa gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyā darśanakāmaḥ / so 'paśyadgopāṃ śākyakanyāṃ dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabhasya bodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādasya madhye sarvabodhisattvasya gṛhāvasanapratibhāsamaṇipadmagarbhāsananiṣaṇṇāṃ strīṇāṃ caturaśītyā sahasraiḥ parivṛtāṃ sarvāsāṃ pārthivakulasaṃbhavānāṃ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāsabhāgakuśalamūlānāṃ pūrvadānasaṃgrahasaṃgṛhītānāṃ ślakṣṇamadhuravacanasamudācārāṇāṃ sarvajñatārthābhimukhasukhasaṃgṛhītānāṃ buddhabodhisattvasamudāgamasamānārthatayā susaṃgṛhītānāṃ mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamaputradāraparigrahasusaṃparigṛhītānāṃ mahāmaitryupetasvadārānuvartanapariśodhitānāṃ pūrvabodhisattvācintyopāyakauśalyapariparipācitānām / sarvāṇi ca tāni caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇyavaivartikānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bodhisattvapāramitānayāvatīrṇāni sarvabodhisattvaśikṣāsu aparapraṇeyāni sarvagrahavigatacitāni sarvasaṃsārarativiratamānasāni asaṅgadharmadhātunayapariśuddhāni sarvajñatābhimukhacittavegāni
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Aśokaśrī</s>, the deity of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly palace, having praised <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son with these verses, followed after him from behind out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>. Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly palace called <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabhā</s> (Radiance of the Reflection of the Dharma-realm), entered it, and looked around in all directions, wishing to see <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden. He saw <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden seated in the middle of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly palace of <s>Dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabhā</s>, upon a jeweled lotus throne reflecting the householder-life of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, surrounded by eighty-four thousand women — all born of royal families, possessing roots of merit concordant with previous <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, gathered through previous acts of giving and generosity, of smooth and sweet speech in their conduct, well-gathered by happiness directed toward the goal of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), well-gathered through the common purpose of the attainment of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, well-embraced in the care of sons and spouses preceded by great compassion, purified in the following of their own spouses endowed with great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), matured by the inconceivable skillful means of former <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And all those eighty-four thousand women were irreversible from supreme perfect awakening, had entered the method of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitās</s>, were not to be led by others in all <s>bodhisattva</s>-trainings, their minds free from all grasping, their minds turned away from the pleasures of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, purified in the method of the unattached <s>dharmadhātu</s>, with mental momentum directed toward <s>sarvajñatā</s>,

body.text: sarvanivaraṇāvaraṇajālavigatāni sarvāṅgapathasamatikrāntāni dharmakāyasunirmitavicārāṇi sarvalokaparipākavinayābhimukhāni vipulapuṇyasamudrasaṃbhūtacittāni samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaniryātāni vipulabodhisattvabalavegasaṃvardhitāni jñānasūryamaṇḍalacittapradīpāni //
body.translated_text: free from the net of all obstructions and hindrances, having transcended all paths of the limbs, their deliberations well-fashioned by the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), directed toward the ripening and training of all worlds, their minds arisen from the ocean of vast merit, devoted to the vow-conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, nourished by the vast force and power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, their minds being lamps of the solar disk of wisdom.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena gopā śākyakanyā tenopasaṃkramya gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyāḥ kramatalayoḥ sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya utthāya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvāḥ saṃsāre saṃsaranti, saṃsāradoṣaiśca na lipyante / sarvadharmasamatāsvabhāvaṃ cāvabudhyante / śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmau na ca pratiṣṭhante / buddhadharmāvabhāsapratilabdhāśca bhavanti / bodhisattvacaryāṃ na ca vyavacchindanti / bodhisattvabhūmau ca pratiṣṭhitā bhavanti / sarvatathāgataviṣayaṃ ca saṃdarśayanti / sarvalokagatisamatikrāntāśca bhavanti / sarvalokagatiṣu copavicaranti / dharmakāyapariniṣpannāśca bhavanti / anantavarṇāṃśca rūpakāyānabhinirharanti / alakṣaṇadharmakāyaparāyaṇāśca bhavanti / sarvajagadvarṇasaṃsthānāṃśca kāyānādarśayanti / anabhilāpyāṃśca sarvadharmānavaranti / sarvavākpathaniruktyudāhāraiśca sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti / niḥsattvāṃśca sarvadharmān prajānanti / sattvadhātuvinayaprayogācca na vinivartante / anutpādānirodhāṃśca sarvadharmānavataranti / sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānaprayogācca na vinivartante / akarmavipākāṃśca sarvadharmānavataranti kuśalakarmābhisaṃskāraprayogācca na vinivartante //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, prostrated with his whole body at the soles of her feet, rose, stood before her with palms joined, and spoke thus: O noble one, I have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Yet I do not know how <s>bodhisattvas</s> transmigrate in <s>saṃsāra</s> yet are not stained by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>; how they awaken to the inherent nature of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; how they do not abide on the level of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones); how they obtain the illumination of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities; how they do not interrupt the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct; how they abide on the <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages; how they reveal the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; how they have transcended all worldly destinies yet move about in all worldly destinies; how they have perfected the <s>dharmakāya</s> yet manifest endless and varied form-bodies; how their final resort is the <s>dharmakāya</s> without characteristics yet they display bodies of every color and shape in all the world; how they comprehend all <s>dharmas</s> as inexpressible yet teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through all vocal paths, analyses, and explanations; how they know all <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of beings yet do not turn away from the effort to train the realm of beings; how they penetrate all <s>dharmas</s> as without arising and cessation yet do not turn away from the effort of worship and attendance upon all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; how they penetrate all <s>dharmas</s> as without karmic result yet do not turn away from the effort of accumulating wholesome actions.

body.text: evamukte gopā śākyakanyā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvaṃ bodhisattvānāmimāmevaṃrūpāṃ caryāṃ dharmatāṃ paripraṣṭavyāṃ manyase, yathāpi tatsamantabhadrapraṇidhānacaryābhimukhasya ayaṃ praśnodāhāraḥ / tena hi kulaputra śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye buddhānubhāvena / daśabhiḥ kulaputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā imāmevaṃrūpāmindrajālatalopamāṃ samantajñānaprabhāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrayanti / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta udārakalyāṇamitrasaṃniśrayeṇa vipulādhimuktipratilābhena udārakalyāṇāśayaviśuddhyā vipulapuṇyajñānasamudropastabdhacittatayā buddhotpattisaṃbhavamahādharmanirdeśaśravaṇapratilābhena tryadhvatathāgatādhimukticetanāsaṃvāsena sarvabodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalasamatānugamena sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānapratilābhena prakṛtimahākaruṇādhyāśayaviśuddhyā sarvasaṃsāracakropacchedacittabalādhānapratilābhena / ebhiḥ kulaputra daśabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā imāmevaṃrūpāmindrajālatalopamāṃ samantajñānaprabhāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrayanti //
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you consider this form of conduct and <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> to be worth inquiring about — such indeed is the statement of questions for one directed toward the conduct of the vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. Therefore, son of good family, listen well and attend carefully, I shall speak by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>. Son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with ten qualities fulfill this form of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — the radiance of universal wisdom, resembling a net of illusions. Which ten? Namely: through reliance on exalted spiritual friends, through the attainment of vast aspiration, through the purification of exalted and wholesome intention, through having minds supported by the ocean of vast merit and wisdom, through the attainment of hearing the great <s>Dharma</s>-teaching arising from the birth of <s>Buddhas</s>, through dwelling in the aspiration-volition toward the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, through following the equality of the circle of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, through the attainment of the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, through the purification of the disposition of innate great compassion, and through the attainment of the power and firmness of mind that cuts through the wheel of all <s>saṃsāra</s>. Son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with these ten qualities fulfill this form of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — the radiance of universal wisdom, resembling a net of illusions.

body.text: tatra kulaputra avivartyavīryā bodhisattvā etān dharmān pratilabhya akṣayākārābhinirhāreṇa bhāvayanto bahulīkurvantaḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇyārāgya daśabhirākārairabhirādhayanti / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta kāyajīvitānapekṣatayā saṃsāropakaraṇānarthikatayā sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatānugamena sarvajñatāpraṇidhānāvivartyatayā sarvadharmadhātunayavyavalokanatayā sarvabhavasamudroccalitamānasatayā anālayadharmagaganapraviṣṭānālayatayā sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānānāvaraṇatayā sarvakṣetrasāgaraprasaraṇatayā
anāvaraṇabodhisattvajñānamaṇḍalasuparyavadāpitatayā / ebhiḥ kulaputra daśabhirākārairbodhisattvāḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇyārāgayitvā abhirādhayanti //
atha khalu gopā śākyakanyā etamevārthanayaṃ saṃdarśayamānā buddhādhiṣṭhānena daśa diśo vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -

children.text: adhimukti yeṣa vipulā gaganaprakāśā yasyāṃ samosarati sarvatriyadhvalokaḥ /
kṣetrāśca sattva tatha dharma tathaiva buddhāsteṣāmiyaṃ cariya jñānaprabhaṃkarāṇām // 12 //
yeṣāśayo gaganakalpa anantamadhyaḥ saṃkleśanirmalatayā paramaṃ viśuddhaḥ /
te puṇyasāgaraśarīraviśuddhagarbhā loke caranti na ca lokamalena liptāḥ // 14 //
sarvasvarāṅgarutaghoṣanayairjinānāṃ ye dharmagarjita śṛṇonta na yāni tṛptim /
ye te daśaddiśi tathāgata aprameyān sarvatra cittakṣaṇi otari anyamanyān /
paśyanti ye pariṣado vipulā jinānāṃ teṣāṃ samādhinayasāgaramotaranti /

body.text: ye 'dhiṣṭhitā daśasu dikṣu jinairaśeṣaiḥ / kalpāṃścarantyanaparāntasamantabhadrāḥ /

children.text: ye te mahākaruṇamaṇḍalajñānasūryā dṛṣṭvā jagadvyasanaprāptamudenti dhīrāḥ /
dharmābhayā jagati moha vidhūya teṣāmiyaṃ cari divākarasādṛśānām // 19 //
dṛṣṭvā prajāṃ bhavagatau parivartamānāṃ saṃsārasrotapravilomasthitāḥ sumedhāḥ /
te 'tra śikṣita nayehi anantamadhyān kāyān yathāśaya jagatyupadarśayitvā /
pratibhāsabimbasadṛśairapi taiḥ svakāyaiḥ paripācayanti janatāṃ bhavasāgareṣu // 21 //
maitrīnayaiḥ suvipulairjanatāṃ spharitvā nānādhimuktiṣu janeṣu cariṃ vidarśya /
dharmaṃ yathāśaya jagatyabhivarṣamāṇā bodhāya sattvanayutān vinayanti dhīrāḥ // 22 //

body.text: atha khalu gopā śākyakanyā imā gāthā bhāṣitvā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ahaṃ khalu kulaputra sarvabodhisattvasamādhisāgaranayavyavalokanaviṣayasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sudhana āha - ka etasya ārye sarvabodhisattvasamādhisāgaranayavyavalokanaviṣayasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ? āha - etamahaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ samāpannā iha lokadhātāvanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpānavatarāmi / teṣu ye sattvāḥ sarvagatiparyāpannāḥ, tān prajānāmi / yāvanti ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ cyutyupapattimukhāni, tāni prajānāmi / yāvantyabhinirvṛttimukhāni, yāvatyaḥ karmābhisaṃskārasamāpattayaḥ, yāvatyaḥ karmavipākavicitratāḥ, tā api prajānāmi / kuśalamapyeṣāṃ karmasamādānaṃ prajānāmi / akuśalamapi nairyāṇikamapi anairyāṇikamapi niyatamapi aniyatamapi mithyātvaniyatamapi sānuśayamapi niranuśayamapi kuśalamūlasaṃpannamapi kuśalamūlavipannamapi kuśalamūlaparigṛhītamapi
akuśalamūlaparigṛhītamapi kuśalākuśalaparigṛhītamapi samudānītakuśalamūlamapi asamudānītapāpadharmamapi eṣāṃ karmasamādānaṃ prajānāmi //

teṣu ca anabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu ye buddhā bhagavantaṃ utpannāḥ, teṣāṃ nāmasamudrānavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ prathamacittotpādasamudrānapi prajānāmi / sarvajñatāprasthānanayasamudrānapi prajānāmi / sarvapraṇidhisāgarābhinirhārānapi prajānāmi / pūrvabuddhotpādaprasthānasamudrānapi prajānāmi / pūrvabuddhapūjopasthānaprayogasamudrānapi prajānāmi / pūrvabodhisattvacaryāparipūrisamudrānapi prajānāmi / niryāṇavyūhasamudrānapi prajānāmi / teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sattvaparipākavinayasamudrānapi prajānāmi / abhisaṃbodhisamudrānapi prajānāmi / dharmacakrapravartanavṛṣabhitāvikurvitānyapi prajānāmi / sarvabuddhavikurvitasamudrānapi prajānāmi / teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parṣanmaṇḍalavibhaktīrapi prajānāmi / teṣu ca parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu ye śrāvakāsteṣāṃ niryāṇanayamapi prajānāmi / pūrvakuśalamūlānyapi prajānāmi / mārgabhāvanānānātvamapi prajānāmi / jñānapratilābhasaṃpadviśuddhaprabhedamapi prajānāmi / ye ca taistathāgataiḥ sattvāḥ pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāstānapi prajānāmi / yāni ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ pūrvakuśalamūlāni tānyapi prajānāmi / ye ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ pratyekabodhyadhigamāstānapi prajānāmi / yāni ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ śāntavihāravikurvitavimokṣamukhāni tānyapi prajānāmi / yāni ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vividhavikurvitāni tānyapi prajānāmi / yaśca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ sattvaparipākastamapi prajānāmi / yā ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ dharmadeśanā, tāmapi prajānāmi / yāni ca teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāmanantasamādhivihāravividhavimokṣakrīḍitāni tānyapi prajānāmi / yacca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parinirvāṇaṃ tadapi prajānāmi / ye ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrāstānapi prajānāmi / teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ prathamakuśalamūlāvaropaṇānyapi prajānāmi / prathamacittotpādapraṇidhānānyapi prajānāmi / praṇidhānavimātratāmapi sarvabodhisattvacaryāniryāṇavyūhābhinirhāravimātratāmapi prajānāmi
/ pāramitāmārgāṅgasaṃbhāraviśuddhivimātratāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvamārgapratipattivyūhavimātratāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇasaṃbhāravimātratāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavegavimātratāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmisaṃkramasamādhimaṇḍalavimātratāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavikurvitānyapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavihārānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmipratiṣṭhānānyapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmibhāvanāvicārānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmipariśodhananayānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmisaṃvāsānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūminimittānyapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmivaśitāmapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇajñānamapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvasaṃgrahajñānamapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvaparipākajñānamapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvavyavasthānasaṃvāsamapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvacaryāmaṇḍalavistārānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvacaryāvikurvitānyapi

prajānāmi / bodhisattvasamādhisāgarānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvavimokṣanayasamudrānapi prajānāmi / teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ nānāsamādhisamudrapratilābhānapi prajānāmi / sarvajñatāvabhāsanapratilābhānapi prajānāmi / sarvajñatāvidyudālokameghānapi prajānāmi / bodhisattvakṣāntipratilābhanayānapi prajānāmi / sarvajñatāvagāhanavikramānapi prajānāmi / teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kṣetrasamudrānugamānapi prajānāmi / dharmasamudranayāvatārānapi prajānāmi / sarvasamudralakṣaṇanānātvamapi prajānāmi / sarvabodhisattvavihāranayavikurvitānyapi prajānāmi / nānāpraṇidhānanayasamudrānapi prajānāmi / vividhavikurvitasamudravimātratāmapi
prajānāmi //

yathā ca ahaṃ kulaputra asyāṃ lokadhātau atītavartamānān kalpasamudrān nānāvidhānavatarāmi, evamaparāntaparaṃparāvyavacchinnānanāgatān kalpasamudrān prajānāmi / yathā ca sahāyāṃ lokadhātau prajānāmi, tathā sahālokadhātusamavasaraṇāsu sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāsu prajānāmi / yathā ca sahālokadhātusamavasaraṇāsu sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāsu prajānāmi, evaṃ sahālokadhātuparamāṇurajontargatāsvapi sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāsu prajānāmi / yathā ca sahālokadhātuparamāṇurajontargatāsu sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāsu prajānāmi, evaṃ sahālokadhātudaśadigānantaryasthitāsvapi lokadhātuṣu prajānāmi / yathā ca sahālokadhātudaśadigānantaryasthitāsu sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi, evaṃ sahālokadhātudaśadigānantaryaparaṃparāsthitāsvapi sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi / yathā ca sahālokadhātudaśadigānantaryaparaṃparāsthitāsu sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi, evaṃ samantadikprabhāsavairocanalokadhātuvaṃśaparyāpannāsvapi sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi / yathā samantadikprabhāsavairocanalokadhātuvaṃśaparyāpannāsvapi lokadhātuṣu prajānāmi, evaṃ samantadikprabhāsavairocanalokadhātuvaṃśadigānantaryaparaṃparāsthitāsu sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi / yathā cāsya samantadikprabhāsavairocanasya lokadhātuvaṃśasya daśadigānantaryaparaṃparāvasthitāsu sarvalokadhātuṣu prajānāmi, evamiha sarvāvati kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāreṣu lokadhātusumeruṣu lokadhātusamudrāntargateṣu lokadhātuprasareṣu prajānāmi / evaṃ lokadhātunayeṣu lokadhātucakreṣu lokadhātumaṇḍaleṣu lokadhātuvibhāgeṣu lokadhātunadīṣu lokadhātvāvarteṣu lokadhātuparivarteṣu lokadhātusumeruṣu lokadhātusamudgateṣu lokadhātupadmeṣu lokadhātuvṛkṣeṣu lokadhātukhārakeṣu lokadhātusaṃjñāgateṣvapi prajānāmi //
body.translated_text: And just as I, son of good family, descend into the past and present oceans of <s>kalpas</s> of various kinds in this world-realm, so also I know the future oceans of <s>kalpas</s> uninterrupted in their successive continuity to the ultimate end. And just as I know in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, so I know in all the successions of world-realms converging in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. And just as I know in all the successions of world-realms converging in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, so I know also in all the successions of world-realms contained within the atoms of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. And just as I know in the successions of world-realms contained within the atoms of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, so I know also in the world-realms situated in the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. And just as I know in all the world-realms situated in the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, so I know also in all the world-realms situated in the successive continuity of the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. And just as I know in the world-realms situated in the successive continuity of the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, so I know also in all the world-realms comprised within the <s>Samantadikprabhāsavairocana</s> (Universal Directional Radiance of <s>Vairocana</s>) world-realm lineage. And just as I know in the world-realms comprised within the <s>Samantadikprabhāsavairocana</s> world-realm lineage, so I know in all the world-realms situated in the successive continuity of the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Samantadikprabhāsavairocana</s> world-realm lineage. And just as I know in all the world-realms situated in the successive continuity of the unbroken ten directions of the <s>Samantadikprabhāsavairocana</s> world-realm lineage, so I know in the expanses of world-realms contained within the oceans of world-realms, the <s>Sumerus</s> of world-realms, in all the <s>Sarvāvati Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra</s> (All-Possessing Ornament of the Array of the Lotus-Surface-Womb). Likewise I know in the methods of world-realms, wheels of world-realms, maṇḍalas of world-realms, divisions of world-realms, rivers of world-realms, vortices of world-realms, revolutions of world-realms, <s>Sumerus</s> of world-realms, emergences of world-realms, lotuses of world-realms, trees of world-realms, crucibles of world-realms, and even in those designated by the names of world-realms. //

body.text: yathā ca asmin kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāre lokadhātusamudre prajānāmi, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu anantaparyanteṣu dharmadhātuparameṣu ākāśadhātuparyavasāneṣu sarvalokadhātusamudreṣu vairocanasya pūrvapraṇidhānasāgarān prajānāmi avatarāmi anusmarāmi / pūrvayogasamudrānapyavatarāmi / pūrvasamudrāgamanasāgarānapyavatarāmi / anantamadhyakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsamapyavatarāmi / kṣetrapariśuddhinayānapyavatarāmi / sattvaparipākopāyanayānapyavatarāmi / pūrvatathāgatārāgaṇopasaṃkramaṇavikurvitānapyavatarāmi / pūrvatathāgatapūjopasthānaprayoganayānapyavatarāmi / pūrvatathāgatadharmadeśanāsaṃpratīcchananayānapyavatarāmi /
body.translated_text: And just as I know in this <s>Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra</s> ocean of world-realms, so in the ten directions, in all the world-realm oceans that are infinite and boundless, that are the ultimate of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, that reach the boundary of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space-element) — I know, descend into, and recall the oceans of former vows of <s>Vairocana</s>. I descend into [his] former methods of practice,

body.text:
pūrvabodhisattvasamādhipratilābhanayānapyavatarāmi / pariṣkāravaśitāpratilābhanayānapyavatarāmi / pūrvatathāgataguṇasamudrapratipattinayānapyavatarāmi / dānapāramitānayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / bodhisattvaśīlavratamaṇḍalapariśuddhyabhinirharaṇanayānapyavatarāmi / bodhisattvakṣāntipratilābhanayānapyavatarāmi / bodhisattvavīryavegasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sarvadhyānāṅgapariniṣpattinayasāgarānapyavatarāmi / prajñāmaṇḍalapariśuddhinayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sarvalokopapattikāyapratibhāsasaṃdarśanopāyanayānapyavatarāmi / samantabhadracaryāpraṇidhānamaṇḍalapariśuddhinayānapyavatarāmi / sarvakṣetrasāgaraspharaṇatāmapyavatarāmi / sarvakṣetrapariśuddhinayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sarvatathāgatajñānāvabhāsasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sarvabuddhabodhyākramaṇavikurvitasāgarānapyavatarāmi / sarvatathāgatajñānāvabhāsapratilābhanayānapyavatarāmi / sarvajñātādhigamāvatāranayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / abhisaṃbodhivikurvitasamudrānapyavatarāmi / dharmacakrapravartanavṛṣabhitāvikrīḍitanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / nānāparṣanmaṇḍalasamudrānapyavatarāmi / teṣu ca sarvaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu sarvabodhisattvānāṃ pūrvakuśalasamudrānapyavatarāmi / prathamapraṇidhānanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sattvaparipākavinayopāyanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / ye ca bhagavatā purvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sattvasamudrāḥ paripācitāstānapyavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ praticittakṣaṇaṃ kuśalamūlavivardhanopāyanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / samādhipratilābhanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / dhāraṇīmukhasamudrapratilābhanayasāgarānapyavatarāmi / pratibhānajñānamaṇḍalaviśuddhinayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / sarvabodhisattvabhūmyākramaṇavikurvitanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi
/ caryājālābhinirhāranayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / anupūrvasamudrānapyavatarāmi / anupūrvasamudāgamadikpraveśajñānanayasamudrānapyavatarāmi / teṣāṃ ca sarvendriyabalabodhyaṅgadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattivikurvitasamudrānapyavatarāmi //
body.translated_text: and I descend into the methods of attaining former <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>. I descend into the methods of attaining mastery of requisites. I descend into the methods of practicing the ocean of qualities of former <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I descend into the oceans of methods of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity). I descend into the methods of accomplishing the purification of the maṇḍala of <s>bodhisattva</s> moral conduct and observances. I descend into the methods of attaining <s>bodhisattva</s> patience. I descend into the oceans of the force of <s>bodhisattva</s> energy. I descend into the oceans of methods of perfecting all limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). I descend into the oceans of methods of purifying the maṇḍala of wisdom. I descend into the methods of displaying reflections of bodies of rebirth in all worlds through skillful means. I descend into the methods of purifying the maṇḍala of the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. I descend into the pervading of all field-oceans. I descend into the oceans of methods of purifying all fields. I descend into the oceans of illumination of the knowledge of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I descend into the oceans of transformations of ascending to the awakening of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I descend into the methods of attaining the illumination of the knowledge of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I descend into the oceans of methods of entry into the attainment of omniscience. I descend into the oceans of transformations of awakening. I descend into the oceans of methods of the sport of the bull-like turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>. I descend into the oceans of various assembly-maṇḍalas. And in all those assembly-maṇḍalas, I descend into the oceans of former wholesome [roots] of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. I descend into the oceans of methods of first vows. I descend into the oceans of methods of skillful means for the ripening and discipline of beings. And whatever oceans of beings were ripened by the <s>Bhagavān</s> while formerly practicing <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — I descend into those too. I descend into the oceans of methods of skillful means for augmenting roots of merit of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> at every mind-moment. I descend into the oceans of methods of attaining <s>samādhis</s>. I descend into the oceans of methods of attaining the ocean of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways. I descend into the oceans of methods of purifying the maṇḍala of the knowledge of eloquence. I descend into the oceans of methods of the transformations of ascending the stages of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. I descend into the oceans of methods of accomplishing the net of conduct. I descend into the oceans of succession. I descend into the oceans of methods of the knowledge of entering the directions through successive attainment. I descend into the oceans of transformations of all the faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments of those [<s>bodhisattvas</s>]. //

body.text: yathā ca bhagavato vairocanasya sarvasmin dharmadhātau bodhisattvacaritasamudrānapyavatarāmi prajānāmi abhinirharāmi, evaṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ daśasu dikṣu dharmadhātuparameṣvākāśadhātuparyavasāneṣu sarvalokadhātusamudreṣvasaṃbhinnasarvabodhisattvacaritasamudrānapyavatarāmi prajānāmi abhinirharāmi / evaṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ daśasu dikṣu dharmadhātuparameṣvākāśadhātuparyavasāneṣu sarvalokadhātusamudreṣvasaṃbhinnasarvabodhisattvacaritapraveśamanantamāyājālapraveśamanantadharmadhātuspharaṇamanantamukhanirdeśamaparyantakalpādhiṣṭhānapraveśanirdeśamavatarāmi prajānāmi abhinirharāmi / tatkasya heto? eṣa hi kulaputra asya sarvabodhisattvasamādhinayasāgaravyavalokanaviṣayasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya viṣayaḥ, yadetaṃ samāpannā sarvasattvacittacaritanayān prajānāmi / sarvasattvakuśalasaṃcayān prajānāmi / sarvasattvasaṃkleśavyavadānanayān prajānāmi / sarvasattvakarmanānātvaṃ prajānāmi / sarvaśrāvakasamādhidvārāṇi prajānāmi / sarvaśrāvakasamādhibhūmiṃ prajānāmi / sarvapratyekabuddhaśāntavimokṣavikurvitamavatarāmi / sarvabodhisattvasamādhisamudranayān prajānāmi / sarvabodhisattvavimokṣanayasāgarāvatāraṃ prajānāmi / sarvatathāgatavimokṣanayasāgarāvatāramapi prajānāmi //
body.translated_text: And just as I descend into, know, and bring forth the oceans of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, so also I descend into, know, and bring forth the undivided oceans of conduct of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in all the oceans of world-realms in the ten directions, reaching the ultimate of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, to the boundary of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s>. I descend into, know, and bring forth the entry into the undivided conduct of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — the entry into the infinite net of illusion, the infinite pervading of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the infinite gateway-exposition, the exposition of entry into the empowerment of limitless <s>kalpas</s>. And why? For this, son of good family, is the domain of this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation whose domain is the observation of the ocean of methods of the <s>samādhis</s> of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — namely, that having entered this [liberation], I know the methods of the mind-conduct of all beings. I know the accumulations of merit of all beings. I know the methods of defilement and purification of all beings. I know the diversity of <s>karma</s> of all beings. I know the gateways of the <s>samādhis</s> of all <s>śrāvakas</s>. I know the ground of the <s>samādhis</s> of all <s>śrāvakas</s>. I descend into the transformations of the peaceful liberations of all <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. I know the methods of the oceans of <s>samādhis</s> of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. I know the entry into the oceans of methods of the liberations of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. I also know the entry into the oceans of methods of the liberations of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako gopāṃ śākyakanyāmetadavocat - kiyaccirapratilabdhastvayāyamārye bodhisattvasamādhinayasāgaravyavalokanaviṣayo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ? āha - bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani buddhakṣetraśataparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa abhayaṃkarā nāma lokadhāturabhūt / tasyāṃ khalu lokadhātau gatipravaro nāma kalpo 'bhūt / tasyāḥ khalu punarlokadhātormadhye kṣemāvatī nāma cāturdvīpikā abhūt / tasyāṃ khalu cāturdvīpikāyāṃ madhye jambudvīpasya drumameruśrīrnāma rājadhānyabhūccaturaśīternagarakoṭīsahasrāṇāṃ pramukhā / sā khalu punardrumameruśrī rājadhānī / tāni caturaśītinagarakoṭīsahasrāṇi pratyekaṃ nīlavaiḍūryabhūmibhāgasaṃsthāpitāni saptaratnamayaprākāraparikṣiptāni vicitravarṇaprabhājālaśubhagandhaśakaṭacakrapramāṇotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannakanakavālikāsaṃstṛtatalagandhodakaparipūrṇasaptaparikhāparikṣiptāni ratnamayasaptavedikājālasaptatālapaṅktiparivṛtāni saptaratnamayavṛkṣamālāparikṣiptāni upari meghajālasaṃchāditāni ratnāṣṭāpadasuvibhaktavicitraratnabhaktivirājitabhūmibhāgāni siddhagaṇavicaritāni abhijātapakṣisaṃghamanojñarutaravitanirghoṣanikūjitāni udyānakoṭīśatasahasropaśobhitāni ṛddhisphītāni pramuditanaranārīgaṇaśatasahasrākīrṇāni śubhābhilaṣaṇīyamāruteritānuparatapuṣpavṛṣṭisahasrābhipravṛṣṭāni pārthivendraśatasahasrādhyuṣitāni / teṣāṃ khalu punarmahānagarāṇāṃ sarvaratnavṛkṣahemajālālaṃkārādibhyo vātasaṃghaṭṭitebhyo bahutūryanirghoṣasamarutaniścaritebhyo 'yamevaṃrūpa ānandaśabdo niścarati sma - snāta, pibata, khādata, dharmaṃ carata, bodhicittamutpādayata, avinivartanīyabhūmivaśitāmadhigacchata / bhadramastu vaḥ / iti //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son spoke thus to <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden: 'How long ago, noble lady, did you obtain this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation whose domain is the observation of the ocean of methods of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>?' She replied: 'Once upon a time, son of good family, in the past, beyond a number of <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of a hundred <s>Buddha</s>-fields, there was a world-realm called <s>Abhayaṃkarā</s> (Fear-Removing). In that world-realm there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Gatipravara</s> (Best of Courses). In the center of that world-realm there was a four-continent system called <s>Kṣemāvatī</s> (Abounding in Security). In the center of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in that four-continent system, there was a royal capital called <s>Drumameruśrī</s> (Glory of the Tree-Meru), foremost among eighty-four thousand <s>koṭis</s> of cities. That royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s>, and those eighty-four thousand <s>koṭis</s> of cities, were each established upon ground-surfaces of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), enclosed by ramparts of the seven jewels, surrounded by seven moats filled with fragrant water, with ground strewn with golden sand, covered with lotuses — <s>utpalas</s>, <s>padmas</s>, <s>kumudas</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> — of variegated colors, radiance, fragrances, and the size of chariot-wheels, surrounded by seven railings of the seven jewels, enclosed by rows of seven palm-trees made of the seven jewels, enclosed by garlands of trees made of the seven jewels, covered above by nets of clouds, with ground-surfaces well-differentiated with jewel-checkerboard patterns and adorned with variegated jewel-designs, frequented by hosts of <s>siddhas</s> (accomplished ones), resounding with the delightful songs, cries, and calls of flocks of noble birds, embellished with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of parks, prosperous and flourishing, thronged with hundreds of thousands of joyful crowds of men and women, showered with thousands of unceasing flower-rains stirred by auspicious and pleasing winds, inhabited by hundreds of thousands of princes. And from the golden net-ornaments and all-jewel-trees of those great cities, stirred by the wind, the sounds of many musical instruments were released, and from them this kind of joyful sound issued forth: 'Bathe! Drink! Eat! Practice the <s>Dharma</s>! Generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening)! Attain the mastery of the irreversible stage! May it be well with you!' //

body.text: tasyāṃ khalu drumameruśriyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ dhanapatirnāma rājā abhūt maṇḍalikaḥ / tasya caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇyantaḥpuramabhūt / pañca ca amātyaśatānyabhūvan / rājñaḥ khalu punardhanapateḥ pañca putraśatānyabhūvan sarveṣāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānāṃ prāsādikānāṃ darśanīyānāṃ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatānāṃ / rājñaḥ khalu punardhanapateḥ padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā nāma agramahiṣī abhūt teṣāṃ caturaśīteḥ strīsahasrāṇāṃ pramukhā / tasyāṃ tejodhipatirnāma putro 'bhūdabhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtakāyaḥ / tasyemāni dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānyabhūvan / yaduta - supratiṣṭhitapāṇipādaḥ tejodhipatirājakumāro 'bhūt / samaṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ pādatalāvutkṣipati, samaṃ nikṣipati, nikṣipaṃśca sarvāvatpādatalābhyāṃ samaṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ saṃspṛśati / pādatalayoścāsya cakrāṇi jātāni sahasrārāṇi sanābhīni sanemikāni sarvākāraparipūrṇāni surucirāṇi darśanīyāni / ucchaṅkhapādatā cāsya abhinirvṛttābhūt, suvyaktaparamopaśobhitā upari pādacchavikusumagarbhātirekaprabhāsvarā / ubhe cāsya hastapādatale jālinī abhūtāṃ vicitrasuvibhaktācchidrāparisrāviṇī, tadyathā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya haṃsarājasya / āyatapādapārṣṇitā asyābhinirvṛttābhūtpariśuddhā prabhāsvarā sarvaratnavarṇāvabhāsapramuktā / dīrghā asyāṅgulayo 'bhūvan vṛttāḥ samāyatasaṃdhayaḥ / sa tāḥ samaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa, samuddharati sma / mṛdūni cāsya
body.translated_text: In that royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s>, there was a king named <s>Dhanapati</s>, a provincial ruler. His inner palace had eighty-four thousand women. He had five hundred ministers. King <s>Dhanapati</s> had five hundred sons, all of them heroes, valiant, of excellent bodily form, crushers of enemy armies, handsome, pleasing to behold, endowed with the fullness of supremely auspicious complexion. King <s>Dhanapati</s>'s chief queen was named <s>Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā</s>, foremost among those eighty-four thousand women. By her was born a son named <s>Tejodhipati</s>, beautiful, handsome, pleasing to behold, his body adorned with the thirty-two <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>s (marks of a great person). These were his thirty-two <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>s (marks of a great person), namely: Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> had well-established hands and feet. He placed his soles evenly upon the great earth, set them down evenly, and when setting them down, touched the great earth evenly with the entire surface of both soles. On his soles, wheels had arisen — with a thousand spokes, with hubs and rims, complete in all aspects, resplendent and beautiful to behold. He had high-arched feet, supremely well-defined and adorned, radiant above with a luster surpassing the beauty of foot-skin blossoms. Both his palms and soles were webbed, variegated, well-proportioned, without gaps or openings, like those of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, king of the <s>haṃsa</s>-geese. He had long, extended heels, pure, radiant, emitting the luster of the colors of all jewels. His fingers were long, rounded, with evenly extended joints. He placed them evenly on the earth and lifted them up. And his

body.text:
hastapādatalānyabhūvan kācilindikātirekasukhasaṃsparśāni / sa tairyān spṛśati striyaṃ vā puruṣaṃ vā dārakaṃ vā dārikāṃ vā, sarve te prītimanaso 'bhūvan paramasukhasaumanasyasamarpitāḥ / eṇeyajaṅghatā cāsya abhinirvṛttābhūt / tasya jaṅghe anupurvasamudgate abhūtāṃ racite vṛtte sujāte eṇeyasyeva mṛgarajñaḥ / nainaṃ kaścitsamartho 'nujavitumanaprāptuṃ vā, na ca vrajan klamamāpadyate sma / saptotsadaḥ khalu punaḥ sa tejodhipatirājakumāro 'bhūt / tasya dvayoḥ pādayordvāvutsadau jātāvabhūtāṃ vṛttau sujātau suparipūrṇāvadṛśyasaṃdhī suracitau darśanīyau, dvau hastayordvāvaṃsakūṭayoḥ pṛṣṭhato grīvāyāmekaḥ / kośagatabastiguhyatā cāsya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇamabhinirvṛttamabhūt / suguptamasya kośabastiguhyamabhūnnimagnaṃ saṃchāditam, tadyathā hastyājāneyasya vā aśvājāneyasya vā / nāsya kaścitstrī vā puruṣo vā dārako vā dārikā vā vṛddho vā madhyo vā daharo vā gururvā gurusthānīyo vā nirvasanasyāpyapaśyadanyatra svaparibhogena naimittikena vā kāmopacitena / siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaḥ khalu punaḥ sa tejodhipatirājakumāro 'bhūt / anupūrvodgataśarīra upavistīrṇavṛtorasko 'bhijātamṛgarājātirekasusaṃsthitasamucchrayaḥ / citāntarāṃsaḥ
khalu punarabhavat sūpacitaśarīraḥ suvibhaktasamucchrayaḥ sarvakāyasamabhāgapratiṣṭhitaḥ anūnagātraḥ anunnatagātro 'pariṇatagātro maṇiphalakavisṛṣṭātirekadyutigātraḥ / saṃvṛttaskandhaḥ khalu punarabhavat / vṛttāvasya skandhāvabhūtāṃ pīnau śubhau suparipuṣṭau / pralambabāhutāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhavat / so 'navanamanenobhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ jānumaṇḍale parimārjati, parāmṛśati samabhāgasthitena śarīreṇa / vṛhadṛjugātramahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhavat sarvāvaropetaparamāṇusamagātraḥ praśamagātro gurugātraḥ prasannagātraḥ prahlādagātraḥ / kambugrīvatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhavat adīnakaṇṭhaśca / tasya yāvatyo grīvāsāmantakena mukhasāmantakena ca rasaharaṇyaḥ, tāḥ sarvāḥ samā abhūvan samantāḥ suparipūrṇāḥ / siṃhahanutāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhavat, suniṣpīḍitahanuḥ suparipūrṇamukhamaṇḍalaḥ sujātapariśuddhamukhamaṇḍalaḥ svāyatamukhadvāro 'pavivaraḥ / samacatvāriṃśaddantatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhūt anūnadaśanaḥ / tasya kiṃcidbhaktaparibhogeṣu ekavāramapi mukhabhaktaṃ parivartamānamasaṃbhinnamabhyavahāramagamat antaśa ekodanabindurapi / aviralāviṣamadantatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punarabhavat / aviralā aviṣamā asya dantā abhūvan acchidrasaṃdhayaḥ samāṃ suvibhaktāḥ, yairasyāhāraṃ paribhuñjānasya nābhūtsaṅgo vā parisaṅgoparudvaṅgo(?) vā upakledo vā abhiṣyando vā paryavanāho vā atisarjanaṃ vā / samadantatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ khalu punarabhavat samadanto nonadanto nādhikadanto nonnatadanto na saṃnatadanto na saṃbhinnadantaḥ samantamadhyadanto 'nutsannadanto avinirbhinnadantaḥ / suśukladaṃṣṭraśca kumāro 'bhūt nirupakleśadaṣṭraḥ suprasannadaṃṣṭraḥ supariśuddhadaṃṣṭraḥ susaṃsthitavicitradaṃṣṭraḥ / suprabhūtajihvatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ khalu punarabhavat /
body.translated_text: palms and soles were soft, surpassing the touch-pleasure of <s>kācilindika</s> silk. Whomever he touched with them — whether woman or man, boy or girl — all became joyful in mind, filled with supreme happiness and delight. He had antelope-like calves. His calves were gradually tapering, well-formed, rounded, well-proportioned, like those of an <s>eṇeya</s> antelope-king. No one was able to outrun or overtake him, nor did he become fatigued while walking. Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> had seven prominences. On his two feet two prominences had arisen, rounded, well-formed, perfectly full, with invisible joints, well-shaped and beautiful to behold; two on his hands, two on his shoulder-crests, and one on the back of his neck. The <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> (mark of a great person) of his male organ being sheathed and concealed had manifested. His male organ was well-hidden, retracted, and covered, like that of a thoroughbred elephant or a thoroughbred horse. No woman, man, boy, girl, elder, middle-aged person, youth, teacher, or one in a teacher's position could see it even when he was unclothed, except through his own enjoyment or on a specific occasion of desire. Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> had the fore-body of a lion. His body rose gradually, his chest was broad and rounded, his stature surpassed that of a noble king of beasts in its well-proportioned and lofty bearing. He had broad shoulders, a well-developed body, a well-proportioned and lofty frame, established in equal proportion throughout all limbs — with no limb deficient, no limb protruding, no limb crooked — his limbs surpassing the luster of a jewel surface in radiance. He had well-rounded shoulders; his shoulders were rounded, full, auspicious, and well-nourished. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of arms reaching to the knees. Without bending, with both hands he could stroke and touch his kneecaps while standing with his body upright. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of a large, straight body — a body endowed with all features, with limbs as smooth as atoms, a body of tranquility, a body of gravity, a body of serenity, a body of delight. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of a conch-shaped neck, and his voice was unwavering. All the taste-carrying channels around his neck and around his mouth were even, uniform, and perfectly full. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of lion-jaws, with well-compressed jaws, a perfectly full facial circle, a well-formed and pure facial circle, with well-proportioned mouth-openings and no gaps. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of forty even teeth, with no teeth missing. In his consumption of food, not even once did a morsel turning in his mouth go down unchewed — not even a single grain of rice. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of teeth without gaps or unevenness. His teeth were without gaps, without unevenness, with seamless joints, even and well-proportioned — so that when he ate, there was no obstruction, no adhesion, no friction, no moisture, no congestion, no blockage, and no excess discharge. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of even teeth: his teeth were even — not too few, not too many, not protruding, not receding, not broken, centered in the middle, not sunken, not split apart. The prince had brilliantly white canine teeth — unblemished canines, serene canines, perfectly pure canines, well-formed and variegated canines. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of an ample tongue.

body.text:
prabhūtā cāsya jihvā abhūt tanvī mṛdvī sukumārā karmaṇyā kamanīyā laghuparivartinī mukhamaṇḍalasaṃchādanī tathyapathyārthavyañjanapadaniruktyadhiṣṭhānasaṃprayuktā / brahmasvaraśca sa kumāro 'bhūdabhirucirasvaraḥ sarvatūryanirnādagītavādyaghoṣamanojñarutaravitālāpasaṃlāpavākkarmapravyāhāraḥ / vākpathābhiratisaṃjananīṃ sarvalokābhinandinīṃ vācamudīrayati sma / brahmātirekeṇa svareṇa ca parṣanmaṇḍalamatikrāmati, sarvaṃ ca anuravati / abhinīlanetraśca sa kumāro 'bhūdacchanetraḥ pariśuddhanetraḥ prabhāsvaranetraḥ viprasannanetro 'bhirūpanetro
darśanīyanetraḥ suruciranetraḥ prahasitanetraḥ / gopakṣmo sa kumāro 'bhūtpadmarāgasuviśuddhacakṣurāyatanaḥ samanetraraṅgaḥ samasadṛśanetraraṅgaḥ sujātanetraraṅgaḥ āyatanetraraṅgaḥ paripūrṇanetraraṅgaḥ supratiṣṭhitanetraraṅgaḥ / bhruvontare cāsya ūrṇā jātābhūnmṛdvī karmaṇyā sukumārākulasaṃsparśā svacchā śuddhā prabhāsvarā himaguḍikātuṣāravarṇā suśuklaraśmimaṇḍalaprabhāvabhāsā / murdhni ca asyoṣṇīṣamabhinirvṛttamabhūt sujātaṃ samantaparimaṇḍalaṃ madhyābhinyastakeśālaṃkāraṃ koṭīśatasahasrapatraratnapadmasaṃdarśitaṃ samantātsamabhāgapratiṣṭhitamaparimitamahārdhyatāpradhānamadhyam / sūkṣmacchaviśca sa kumāro 'bhūt / nāsya kāye rajo vā malo vā kledo vā jālaṃ vā valī vā śaithilyaṃ vā bhaṅgo vā prasaraṇaṃ vā visaraṇaṃ vā asamaṃ vā asthiṣata / suvarṇavarṇacchaviśca sa kumāro 'bhūjjāmbūnadahemanirbhāsaḥ samantavyāmaprabhaḥ kāñcanaikajvālāprabhāmaṇḍalopaśobhitaḥ sarvaromakūpapramuktagandharaśmivitimiraprabhāsvaraśarīrālaṃkāraḥ / ekaikaromā ca sa kumāro 'bhūt / ekaikaromasya ekaikasmin romakūpe roma jātamabhūnnīlavaiḍūryavarṇapradakṣiṇāvartakuṇḍalajātaṃ suparisaṃcitaṃ suniviṣṭaṃ supratiṣṭhitam / ūrdhvāṅgaromā ca sa kumāro 'bhūdavinivartanīyaromā apratyudāvartanīyaromā asaṃsṛṣṭaromā / indranīlavarṇakeśatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ / sa kumāro 'bhūt / tasya nīlāḥ keśā abhūvan vairocanamaṇiratnanīlavarṇanirbhāsāḥ snigdhā mṛdavaḥ sukuñcitāḥ pradakṣiṇāvartakuṇḍalinaḥ sujātamūlā anuddhatāḥ niṣpīḍitā asaṃlulitāḥ samasadṛśasthānasaṃsthitāḥ / nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatāmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇapratilabdhaḥ sa khalu punaḥ tejodhipatī rājakumāro 'bhūt samantabhadraparimaṇḍalaḥ samantabhadraḥ samantaprāsādikaḥ / sa purato 'pyatṛptikaracārudarśano 'bhūt / pṛṣṭhato 'pi dakṣiṇato 'pi vāmato 'pi gacchannapi tiṣṭhannapi niṣaṇṇo 'pi bhāṣamāṇo 'pi tūṣṇībhūto 'pi atṛptikaramanāpacārudarśano 'bhut / ebhiḥ kulaputra dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtakāyaḥ sa tejodhipatī rājakumāro 'bhūt sarvasattvāpratikūladarśanaḥ sarvābhiprāyaparipūrikadarśanaḥ sarvasattvaratikaradarśanaḥ //
body.translated_text: His tongue was ample, thin, soft, delicate, pliant, beautiful, turning lightly, covering the entire facial circle, connected with the establishment of true, beneficial, meaningful syllables, words, and etymological explanations. The prince had a <s>Brahma</s>-voice, a supremely beautiful voice. All his verbal activities — speaking, conversing, and uttering words — were as delightful as the sounds of all musical instruments, songs, music, and melodious calls. He uttered speech that generated delight in the way of words and that gladdened all the world. With a voice surpassing that of <s>Brahmā</s>, he pervaded the entire assembly-circle, and everything resonated in response. The prince had deep blue eyes — clear eyes, pure eyes, radiant eyes, serene eyes, beautiful eyes, pleasing eyes, resplendent eyes, smiling eyes. The prince had eyelashes like those of a cow, with eye-sockets well-purified like <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby) gems, with even eye-sockets, symmetrical eye-sockets, well-formed eye-sockets, elongated eye-sockets, full eye-sockets, well-established eye-sockets. Between his brows, an <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair) had arisen — soft, pliant, delicate, gentle to the touch, clear, pure, radiant, white as a ball of snow or frost, shining with the radiance of a circle of brilliantly white rays. On his crown, an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) had manifested — well-formed, evenly rounded on all sides, with a hair-ornament set in the center, displayed upon a jewel-lotus of a hundred <s>koṭī</s>-thousand petals, established in equal proportion on all sides, with its center distinguished by immeasurable great magnificence. The prince had fine skin. On his body there was no dust, no impurity, no moisture, no web-like marks, no wrinkles, no laxity, no cracks, no spreading, no scattering, no unevenness, and no protrusion of bones. The prince had skin the color of gold, with the radiance of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, with a <s>vyāma</s>-aura extending evenly on all sides, adorned by a halo of golden flame-radiance, his body ornamented with fragrant rays emitted from every hair-pore that dispelled all darkness and shone brilliantly. The prince had one hair per pore. In each single hair-pore, a single hair had grown — dark blue like <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) in color, turning clockwise in curls, well-gathered, well-set, well-established. The prince had upward-growing body-hair — hair that did not turn back, hair that did not curl in reverse, hair that was not tangled. He had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of <s>Indranīla</s>-colored (sapphire-colored) head-hair. The prince's head-hair was dark blue, shining with the radiance of the blue color of <s>Vairocana-maṇi</s> jewels, smooth, soft, finely curled, turning clockwise in ringlets, well-rooted, not raised up, close-lying, undisturbed, situated in even and symmetrical positions. Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> had attained the <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s> of a <s>nyagrodha</s>-proportioned (banyan-tree-proportioned) body — evenly proportioned on all sides like <s>Samantabhadra</s>, auspicious on all sides, pleasing on all sides. He was beautiful and delightful to behold unsatiatingly from the front, from behind, from the right, from the left — whether walking, standing, seated, speaking, or silent — beautiful, agreeable, and delightful to behold without satiation. Son of good family, adorned with these thirty-two <s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>s (marks of a great person), Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> was pleasing to the sight of all beings, fulfilling the wishes of all, and delightful to all beings. //

body.text: sa khalu kulaputra tejodhipatī rājakumāro 'pareṇa samayena pitrābhyanujñāto drumameruśriyo rājadhānyā gandhāṅkuraprabhameghaṃ nāmodyānam, tatra bhūmidarśanāya abhiniryayau viṃśatyā kanyāsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ mahatā puṇyatejautaḥśrīsaubhāgyavikurvitavyūhena naranārīgaṇaiḥ samantādabhinandyamāno jāmbūnadasuvarṇarathamāruhya mahāvajraratnacatuścakraṃ nārāyaṇavajramayadṛḍhākṣayākṣamuttamacandanasupariniṣṭhitapratiṣṭhiteṣaṃ sarvagandhamaṇirājasuvibhaktapañjaraṃ sarvaratnapuṣpasuvicitropaśobhitavyūhaṃ sarvaratnajālasaṃchāditavyūhaṃ
body.translated_text: Son of good family, at another time Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, having received permission from his father, set out from the royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s> to the park named <s>Gandhāṅkuraprabhamegha</s> (Cloud of Radiance of Fragrant Sprouts) for a survey of the land, together with twenty thousand maidens, with a great display of meritorious splendor, inner glory, and fortune-transformations, acclaimed on all sides by throngs of men and women. He mounted a chariot of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold with four wheels of great <s>vajra</s>-jewels, with axles and axle-pins of indestructible <s>Nārāyaṇa-vajra</s> made firm and well-finished of the finest sandalwood, with a cage well-constructed of all fragrance-<s>maṇi</s>-kings, beautifully adorned with arrays of flowers of all jewels, covered by an array of nets of all jewels,

body.text: mahāmaṇiratnarājavyūhagarbhamadhyapratiṣṭhāpitasiṃhāsanaṃ pañcakanyāśataratnasūtradāmaparigṛhītaṃ gaganāsaktavāyusamajavājāneyāśvasahasrayuktam anupūrvapariṇatacārudarśanena śvetavaidūryamaṇirājamayacchadanena vimalāpramāṇaprabheṇa acintyādbhutasarvaratnaviracanābhaktivinyāsacitrasarvākāravyūhopaśobhitena nīlavaidūryamaṇirājodviddhadaṇḍena mahatā ratnacchatreṇa dhriyatā bahuprāṇiśatasahasraparivṛtadivyamadhuramanojñanirdhoṣaistūryaśatasahasraiḥ pravādyamānaiḥ mahadbhiḥ puṣpameghairabhipravarṣadbhiḥ surabhidivyagandhadhūpaghaṭikāniyutaśatasahasraiḥ pradhūpyamānaiḥ / tasya tathā vrajato 'ṣṭavartmā mārgaḥ samavasthiṣata nimnonnatavigato 'pagataśarkarakaṭhallotsado jātarūparajatasarvaratnarājadhātusaṃcitabhūmitalapratiṣṭhānaḥ suvarṇavālikāsaṃstīrṇo vicitraratnapuṣpābhikīrṇaḥ ubhayato ratnavṛkṣapaṅktisamalaṃkṛtavicitraratnavedikāparivṛtaḥ / upari ratnakiṅkiṇījālasaṃchanno vividharatnavitatapratimaṇḍito 'nekaratnadhvajapatākāpaṭṭaśatasahasrābhipralambitopaśobhitavyūhaḥ ubhayato nānāratnavyomakapaṅktiviracitavyūhaḥ //
body.translated_text: a lion-throne established in the midst of a womb of great jewel-king arrays, held by jewel-thread garlands of five hundred maidens, yoked with a thousand excellent thoroughbred horses swift as the wind attached to the sky, with a canopy made of white <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel-king of gradually refined and beautiful appearance, of stainless and immeasurable radiance, adorned with wondrous arrays of all kinds beautifully arranged with inconceivable varieties of all jewels, held by a great jewel parasol with a staff set with dark <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel-king, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of beings, with hundreds of thousands of divine, sweet, delightful, and resonant musical instruments being played, showering great clouds of flowers, perfumed by tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of censers of fragrant divine incense. As he thus traveled, an eightfold path was established, free from unevenness, devoid of gravel, stones, and mounds, its ground-surface layered with gold, silver, and all jewel-king ores, strewn with golden sand, scattered with various jewel-flowers, adorned on both sides with rows of jewel trees and enclosed by various jewel railings. Above it was covered with nets of jewel bells, decorated with various spread jewels, adorned with arrays of hundreds of thousands of hanging jewel banners, flags, and silk pennants, and arrayed on both sides with rows of various jewel canopy-frames.

body.text: tatra keṣucidratnavyomakeṣu vividharatnaparipūrṇāni ratnabhājanāni sthāpitānyabhūvan yācanakasaṃghapratipādanakārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu sarvaratnābharaṇavidhayaḥ sthāpitā alaṃkārārthināṃ yācakānāmalaṃkaraṇārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu cintāmaṇiratnāni sthāpitāni sarvasattvānāṃ sarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu sarvākāravividhānnapānarasaparipūrṇāni bhojanāni sthāpitāni, yasya yenārthaḥ tasya taṃ pratipādanārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu sarvākāraparamasvādumanojñavarṇagandharasasparśāḥ divyabhaktavidhayaḥ sthāpitāḥ / keṣucidvyomakeṣu vicitrarasāsvādādivyasarvaphalavidhayaḥ sthāpitāḥ / keṣucidvyomakeṣu vividhojjvalavicitraraṅgaraktāni nānācitrabhaktivinyāsavirājitāni paramamahārhāṇi sūkṣmāṇi sukumārakāntavarṇāni divyavastrakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi sthāpitāni vastrārthināṃ yathābhiprāyaparibhogārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu sarvākāravividhadivyamanojñavarṇagandhāḥ sarvagandhavidhayaḥ sthāpitā abhuvan vilepanārthināṃ yathābhiprāyaparibhogārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu sarvopakaraṇarāśayaḥ sthāpitā abhūvan sattvānāṃ yathāśayābhiprāyaparibhogārtham / keṣucidvyomakeṣu nāryo 'bhirūpāḥ prāsādikā darśanīyā vividhacārurūpaveśā vicitramanojñavastrasaṃdhitāḥ sarvābharaṇasvalaṃkṛtā vividhavilepanabhaktivinyāsapratimaṇḍitopaśobhitaśarīrāḥ sarvastrīśilpamāyākalāvidhijñāḥ sthāpitā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: In some of those jewel canopy-frames, jewel vessels filled with various jewels had been placed for the purpose of giving to assemblies of supplicants. In some canopy-frames, all varieties of jewel ornaments had been placed for adorning those supplicants who desired adornment. In some canopy-frames, <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) jewels had been placed for fulfilling all wishes of all beings. In some canopy-frames, foods filled with all varieties of food, drink, and flavors had been placed, for providing to each whatever they needed. In some canopy-frames, divine food preparations of supremely delicious, delightful color, fragrance, taste, and touch of all kinds had been placed. In some canopy-frames, various divine fruit preparations of wondrous and brilliant flavors had been placed. In some canopy-frames, tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of divine garments -- luminous, variously dyed in brilliant colors, adorned with diverse beautiful patterns, supremely valuable, fine, soft, and of lovely hue -- had been placed for the use of those desiring garments according to their wishes. In some canopy-frames, all varieties of divine, delightful fragrances of all colors and scents had been placed for the use of those desiring unguents according to their wishes. In some canopy-frames, heaps of all requisites had been placed for the use of beings according to their dispositions and wishes. In some canopy-frames, beautiful, graceful, lovely women of various charming forms and appearances had been placed, clothed in various delightful garments, well-adorned with all ornaments, their bodies beautified with various applied cosmetic patterns, skilled in all feminine arts, crafts, and enchantments.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasyāmeva drumameruśriyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ sudarśanā nāma agragaṇikābhūdrājaparibhogyā / tasyāḥ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīrnāma dārikābhūdabhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā nātidīrghā nātihrasvā nātisthūlā nātikṛśā nātigaurā nātiśyāmā abhinīlanetrā abhinīlakeśī abhirāmavaktrā brahmasvarā madhurapriyavādinī prājñā sarvakalāvidhijñā sarvaśāstrakovidā dakṣā analasā sagauravā saprasādā maitracittā apratighātabahulā atṛptikaramanāpadarśanā mandarāgadoṣamohā hryapatrāpyasaṃpannā mārdavā ṛjvī aśāṭyā amāyā
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in that very royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s>, there was a chief courtesan named <s>Sudarśanā</s>, enjoyed by the king. She had a daughter named <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>, who was beautiful, graceful, lovely, neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too thin, neither too fair nor too dark, with deep blue eyes and deep blue hair, with a charming face, with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, speaking sweetly and pleasingly, wise, skilled in all arts and crafts, learned in all sciences, dexterous, energetic, dignified, serene, benevolent of mind, abundant in non-obstruction, of insatiably lovely appearance, with diminished passion, hatred, and delusion, endowed with modesty and shame, gentle, honest, without deceit, without guile,

body.text: vinītā / sā mātrā sārdhamanekakanyāparivṛtā ratnarathābhirūḍhā drumameruśriyo rājadhānyā niṣkramya tejodhipate rājakumārasya purataḥ tejodhipatiṃ rājakumāraṃ parimārgayamāṇā rājājñāniyogādgacchantī tejodhipatiṃ rājakumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā tīvraṃ rāgacittamutpādayāmāsa / sā tejodhipate rājakumārasyāntike 'dhimātraṃ saṃjātasnehānubaddhā asvatantracittā mātaraṃ sudarśanāmetadavocat - yatkhalu amba jānīyāḥ - sacenmāṃ tejodhipate rājakumārasya na dāsyasi, maraṇaṃ vopagamiṣyāmi maraṇamātrakaṃ vā duḥkham / sā prāha - maivaṃ dārike cetanāmutpādaya / eṣa hi kumāraścakravartilakṣaṇasamanvāgataḥ / sthānametadvidyate - yadeṣa piturdhanapateratyayāccakravartirājyamadhyāvasiṣyati / sa rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī / tato 'sya strīratnaṃ prādurbhaviṣyati vaihāyasaṃgamam / api tu khalu punardārike gaṇikā vayaṃ sarvalokaratikarāḥ / na vayamekasattvaṃ pratiniyamena yāvajjīvamupatiṣṭhāmahe / vayaṃ hi rājño dhanapaterājñayā tejodhipateḥ kumārasyopasthānāya niryātāḥ / maināṃ cetanāṃ dṛḍhīkuruṣva / durlabhametatsthānam //
body.translated_text: well-disciplined. She, together with her mother and surrounded by many maidens, mounted upon a jewel chariot and departed from the royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s>. Searching for the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> before him, going by the king's command, upon seeing the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, she gave rise to an intense mind of passion. She, having become exceedingly attached with affection toward the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, her mind no longer her own, said to her mother <s>Sudarśanā</s>: 'Know this, dear mother -- if you do not give me to the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, I will either die or suffer pain equal to death.' She replied: 'Do not give rise to such an intention, my daughter! For this prince possesses the marks of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). It is possible that upon the passing of his father <s>Dhanapati</s>, he will assume the sovereignty of a <s>Cakravartin</s>. He will become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>. Then there will appear for him a jewel-woman who traverses the sky. Moreover, my daughter, we are courtesans who bring delight to all the world. We do not attend upon a single being exclusively for life. We have been sent forth by the command of King <s>Dhanapati</s> for the attendance upon the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>. Do not make this intention firm. Such a station is difficult to attain.'

body.text: tena ceha samayena sūryagātrapravaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān / tasya khalu punargandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhameghasyodyānasyāntare dharmameghodgataprabhāso nāma bodhimaṇḍo 'bhūt / tatra sa bhagavān sūryagātrapravarastathāgataḥ prathamasaptāhābhisaṃbuddho vyāhārṣīt / sa tayā dārikayā rathābhirūḍhayaiva pracalāyamānayā svapnāntare dṛṣṭaḥ / prativibuddhāyāśca purāṇajñātisālohitayā devatayā ārocitam - eṣa dārike sūryagātrapravarastathāgato dharmameghodgataprabhāse bodhimaṇḍe viharati prathamasaptāhābhisaṃbuddho bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛto devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragadevendrabrahmābhāsvarākaniṣṭhadevagaṇapuraskṛtaḥ / tatraiva ca sarvāḥ pṛthvīdevatāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ / ākāśadevatā abdevatā jvalanadevatā vāyudevatāḥ sāgaradevatāḥ nadīdevatā parvatadevatā rātridevatā aruṇodgatadevatā vanadevatā vṛkṣadevatā auṣadhidevatāḥ sasyadevatā nagaradevatāḥ padagāminīdevatā bodhimaṇḍadevatāḥ śarīraraśmidevatāḥ sattvanikāyadevatā gaganadevatā sarvadigdevatāśca saṃnipatitāḥ tasya bhagavataḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasya darśanāyeti //
body.translated_text: And at that time, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> appeared in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Within the park called <s>Gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhāmegha</s>, there was a <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) named <s>Dharmameghodgataprabhāsa</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, newly awakened in the first week, gave his discourse. He was seen by that maiden while she was dozing in her chariot, in a dream. And when she awoke, a deity who had been a former kinsman informed her: 'O maiden, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> dwells at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> <s>Dharmameghodgataprabhāsa</s>, newly awakened in the first week, surrounded by a multitude of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, attended by hosts of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>Indras</s> among gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods. And there all the earth deities have assembled -- sky deities, water deities, fire deities, wind deities, ocean deities, river deities, mountain deities, night deities, dawn deities, forest deities, tree deities, herb deities, grain deities, city deities, walking deities, <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> deities, body-radiance deities, being-assembly deities, space deities, and deities of all directions have assembled for the sight of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>.'

body.text: sā tena tathāgatadarśanena tathāgataguṇaśravaṇena ca viśāradā bhūtvā avakāśapratilabdhā tejodhipate rājakumārasya puratastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: She, having become confident through that vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and hearing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities, having gained an opportunity, spoke these verses before the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> at that time:

children.text: rūpavareṇahu loki viśiṣṭā viśruta sarvadiśāsu guṇebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: I am distinguished in the world by excellent beauty, renowned in all directions for my qualities,
In the power of wisdom none is my equal, skilled in all arts, delights, enchantments, and crafts. // 1 //

children.text: prāṇaśatā bahu naikasahasrā ye mama prekṣiṣu rāgavaśena /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of living beings, indeed many thousands, who gaze upon me under the sway of passion --

children.text: nāpi ca rajyati mahya kumārā kasyacidantiki mānasu loke // 2 //
children.translated_text: Yet my mind, O prince, is not attached to anyone in the world. // 2 //

children.text: no ca mama pratihanyati cittaṃ nāpyanunīyati kutraci sattve /
children.translated_text: My mind is neither repelled nor is it won over by any being,

children.text: nāpi ca me kvaci vairu na doṣaḥ sarvahite 'bhirataṃ mama cittam // 3 //
children.translated_text: Nor do I have enmity or fault toward anyone; my mind delights in the welfare of all. // 3 //

children.text: yada mi tvamapi dṛṣṭa kumāro rūpabalapravaro guṇadhārī /
children.translated_text: But when I beheld you, O prince, supreme in beauty and strength, bearer of virtues,

children.text: tada indriya prīṇita sarve prīta mamo vipulā upajātā // 4 //
children.translated_text: Then all my senses were gladdened, and vast joy arose in me. // 4 //
Pure as the radiance of jewel-gold, with deep blue and beautifully curling hair --

children.text: subhrulalāṭa sunāsā eṣa nivedayamī tava ātmā // 5 //
children.translated_text: With lovely brow, forehead, and fine nose, I offer myself to you. // 5 //
Bearer of excellent marks, resplendent, with a form like a golden mountain --

children.text: purato na virājami tubhyaṃ śyāmakṛtā maṣivigrahatulyā // 6 //
children.translated_text: Before you I do not shine, rendered dark, like a body of ink. // 6 //
With deep blue, large, wide eyes, with a lion's jaw (?), full and fair-faced --

children.text: na ca te pratihanyati vācyaṃ agraruta pratigṛhṇami mahyam // 7 //
children.translated_text: Your speech does not falter; I accept for myself your supreme voice. // 7 //

children.text: vadane tava jihva prabhūtā tāmratanū vipulā ratanābhā /
children.translated_text: In your mouth, your tongue is ample, copper-hued, broad, with the luster of jewels,
With the excellent voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, beautifully resonant -- you delight the world as you speak. // 8 //

body.text: vadane sahitāstava dantā śaṅkhanibhā vimalā suvibhaktā /
body.translated_text: In your mouth, your teeth are even, conch-white, stainless, well-proportioned,

body.text: smitu yehi vidarśayamānaḥ toṣayase janatāṃ naravīra // 9 //
body.translated_text: And displaying a smile with them, you delight the people, O hero among men. // 9 //

children.text: tava lakṣaṇaśobhana kāyastriṃśa duveva prabhāsura śuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your body adorned with beautiful marks, thirty-two, radiant and pure,

children.text: samalaṃkṛtu yehi surūpaḥ cakradharo bhavitāsi narendrā // 10 //
children.translated_text: Beautifully adorned with these, you shall become a wheel-bearing lord of men. // 10 //

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputraḥ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyaṃ dārikāmetadavocat - kasya tvaṃ dārike, ko vā tavārakṣakaḥ? na mama dārike kalpate paraparigṛhīteṣu dāreṣu mamatāṃ kartum / tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> said to the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>: 'Whose are you, maiden? Who is your protector? It is not proper for me, maiden, to show possessiveness toward wives belonging to another.' At that time he spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: O <s>Sudarśanā</s>, endowed with beauty and virtues, well-marked, with a body purified by merit,

children.text: pṛcchāmi te brūhi mamaitamarthaṃ parigrahastvaṃ varagātri kasya // 11 //
children.translated_text: I ask you -- tell me this matter: whose possession are you, O fair-bodied one? // 11 //

children.text: mātā pitā vā tava kaccidasti bhartāpi vā svāmi parigraho vā /
children.translated_text: Do you have a mother or father, or indeed a husband, a master, or an owner,

children.text: sattvo 'pi cānyaḥ khalu yena saṃjñā kṛtā mameti tvayi saumyarūpe // 12 //
children.translated_text: Or yet another being who has conceived the notion 'she is mine' regarding you, O gentle-formed one? // 12 //

children.text: kaccinna hiṃsābhirataṃ manaste harasyadattaṃ khalu mā pareṣām /
children.translated_text: Is your mind not inclined to harm? Do you not take what is not given from others?

children.text: mā kāmamithyācaraṇe ratiste mā vā mṛṣādya prasṛtaṃ manaste // 13 //
children.translated_text: May you not delight in sexual misconduct! May your mind not be inclined to falsehood! // 13 //

children.text: mā mitrabhedaprasṛtā matiste mā marmabhedīni vacāṃsi vakṣi /
children.translated_text: May your intent not be inclined to dividing friends! May you not speak words that pierce the vital points!

children.text: mā te 'parakṣeṣu dhaneṣvabhidhyā vyāpādacittaṃ janatāsu cāpi // 14 //
children.translated_text: May you not covet the wealth and property of others, nor harbor a mind of malice toward people! // 14 //

children.text: mā dṛṣṭikāntārapathi sthitāsi mā karmavaṃśoddhuracetanā vā /
children.translated_text: May you not stand on the wilderness path of wrong views! May you not have intentions reckless in the lineage of karma!

children.text: māyāvinī śāṭhyavaśānugā vā mā bādhase tvaṃ viṣameṇa lokam // 15 //
children.translated_text: May you not be deceitful or subject to guile! May you not oppress the world with crookedness! // 15 //

body.text: mātāpitājñātisuhṛdgurūṇāṃ kaccitpriyatvaṃ tava gauravaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Do you have affection and respect for your mother, father, kinsmen, friends, and teachers?

body.text: daridrabhūteṣu ca saṃgrahāya kaccitpradātuṃ prasṛtaṃ manaste // 16 //
body.translated_text: Is your mind inclined to give for the care of those who are destitute? // 16 //

children.text: premāsti kalyāṇasuhṛtsvatho vā dharmeṇa kāle ca vadanti ye tvām /
children.translated_text: Do you have love for virtuous friends and well-wishers who speak to you with <s>Dharma</s> and at the right time,

children.text: kāyasya cittasya ca kalyatāṃ te karmaṇyatāṃ vā janayanti samyak // 17 //
children.translated_text: Who rightly bring about the fitness and readiness of your body and mind? // 17 //

children.text: buddheṣu te gauravamasti kaccit premāpi vā buddhasuteṣu tīvram /
children.translated_text: Do you have reverence for the <s>Buddhas</s>? Do you have intense love for the sons of the <s>Buddhas</s>?
Do you understand that supreme <s>Dharma</s> from which the children of the <s>Sugatas</s> are born? // 18 //

children.text: kaccitpare tiṣṭhasi dharmavaṃśe na cāpyadharmaṃ carituṃ matiste /
children.translated_text: Do you stand in the highest lineage of <s>Dharma</s>? Is your mind not inclined to practice <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness)?

children.text: anantavarṇe ca guṇārṇave te kaccitparaṃ prema ca gauravaṃ ca // 19 //
children.translated_text: Do you have supreme love and reverence for the ocean of infinite and praiseworthy qualities? // 19 //
Is your mind benevolent toward people who are destitute and without a guide?

children.text: āpāyike karmaṇi ca pravṛttā kaccidbhṛśārtā karuṇāyase tvam // 20 //
children.translated_text: When beings are engaged in actions leading to the lower realms, do you feel compassion, being deeply pained? // 20 //

children.text: pareṣu saṃpattimudīkṣya cāgrāṃ kaccitparāṃ tuṣṭimupaiṣi ca tvam /
children.translated_text: And beholding the supreme fortune of others, do you attain supreme contentment?
Do you, by the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), generate equanimity toward people who are not free from <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions)? // 21 //
Seeing the multitude asleep in ignorance, do you firmly aspire to supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?

children.text: kalpānanantān caramāṇa caryāṃ kaccinna te prārthanayāsti khedaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: Practicing the conduct through endless <s>kalpa</s>s, do you not grow weary of your aspiration? // 22 //

body.text: atha khalu sudarśanā agragaṇikā sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyo dārikāyā mātā tejodhipatiṃ rājakumārametadavocat - mamaiṣā kumāra dārikā upapādukā padmagarbhasaṃbhūtā nābhiniṣkrāntapūrvā gṛhāt / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudarśanā</s>, the chief courtesan, the mother of the girl <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>, spoke thus to Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>: "This girl of mine, O prince, is a spontaneously born being, arisen from the interior of a lotus; she has never before come forth from a house." And at that time she spoke these verses:

children.text: māṃ bhāṣamāṇāṃ śṛṇu rājaputra yaddārikā te paripṛcchateyam /
children.translated_text: Hear me as I speak, O prince — regarding this girl about whom you inquire,

children.text: vakṣye 'nupūrvyā tava dārikeyaṃ jātā yathā saumya vivardhitā ca // 23 //
children.translated_text: I shall tell you in due order, O gentle one, how this girl was born and how she was raised. // 23 //

children.text: niśākṣaye yatra bhavān prasūtaḥ tatraiva jātā mama dārikeyam /
children.translated_text: At the end of the night, at the very place where you were born, this girl of mine was born,
Spontaneously arisen in a stainless lotus-womb, with all limbs complete and wide beautiful eyes. // 24 //
In springtime, the finest of seasons, when crops and herbs were sprouting forth,

children.text: sālaprabhodyānavare madīye ciraṃ mayā tatra vinirgatāham // 25 //
children.translated_text: I went out for a long time to my excellent garden of blossoming <s>sāla</s> trees. // 25 //
Among trees with branches spread open revealing colorful buds, amid fully blossomed trees dark as dense clouds,
In a grove resounding with various birds amid the thickets of trees, I delight, joyful and free from sorrow. // 26 //
I was accompanied by eight hundred maidens, beautifully adorned and captivating,

children.text: vicitraratnāmbaradhāriṇībhiḥ gīte ca vādye ca suśikṣitābhiḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: Wearing garments of various jewels, well-trained in song and instrumental music. // 27 //
I was seated at the bank of a pond adorned with fragrant lotuses bearing colorful banners,
In a place on the ground strewn with flowers, filled with a retinue of well-trained women. // 28 //
Then in the midst of the water there appeared a thousand-petaled lotus of supreme jewels,
