With a stalk of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), petals of <s>maṇi</s>-jewel kings, and a pistil of pure <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold. // 29 //
Rich with supremely fragrant, jewel-colored filaments, with a great radiance arisen as if the banner of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,

children.text: āsaṃstadā saṃśayitā janaughā rātryāṃ kimabhyudgata eṣa sūryaḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: The crowds of people were then filled with doubt: "Has the sun risen during the night?" // 30 //
From that great lord of lotuses, at the end of night, as if awakened by the rays of the sun,
A radiance was released and a sweet sound — these were the prior omens of her birth. // 31 //
This jewel among women appeared in the human world, through the purity of supreme moral conduct;

children.text: na karmaṇo hyasti kṛtasya nāśaḥ pūrve sucīrṇasya vipāka eṣaḥ // 32 //
children.translated_text: For there is no destruction of <s>karma</s> once performed — this is the ripening of what was well-practiced in former lives. // 32 //
With beautiful dark hair, eyes blue as <s>utpala</s> lotuses, with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, of pure golden complexion,
Adorned with garlands and ornaments, beautifully dressed, born from a lotus — like <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) herself in her stainless radiance. // 33 //
With pure limbs, a body of balanced proportions, with fully developed limbs and a well-formed figure,
She shines like a golden image polished with jewels, illuminating all directions. // 34 //
A fragrance of the finest sandalwood, born of her lineage, wafts from her, pervading all directions,

children.text: rutaṃ ca divyaṃ madhuraṃ ruvatyā gandho mukhādvāti yathotpalasya // 35 //
children.translated_text: And when she speaks, a divine sweet sound issues forth, and from her mouth a fragrance wafts like that of a blue lotus. // 35 //

children.text: smitaṃ yadaiṣā prakaroti caiva divyaṃ tadā tūryaravaṃ virauti /
children.translated_text: And whenever she smiles, a divine sound of musical instruments resounds;

children.text: strīratnametatkhalu jātu loke na prākṛtānāṃ vaśamabhyupaiti // 36 //
children.translated_text: This jewel among women in this world never comes under the power of ordinary men. // 36 //

children.text: manuṣyaloke na hi vidyate 'sau bhartā hi yo 'syāstvadṛte paraḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: In the human world there exists no husband who could be hers other than you;
You whose beautiful form is adorned with auspicious marks — therefore accept this maiden. // 37 //

children.text: hrasvā na ceyaṃ hi na cātidīrghā sthūlā na caiṣā na kṛśātimātram /
children.translated_text: She is neither too short nor too tall, neither stout nor excessively thin,
With a slender waist and full breasts — she is suited to you, O one of blameless limbs. // 38 //

body.text: saṃkhyālipijñānanaye tathaiva mudrāvidhau śāstranayeṣvabhijñā /
body.translated_text: Skilled in arithmetic, writing, systems of knowledge, likewise in the methods of <s>mudrā</s>s (seals/gestures), and proficient in the principles of the <s>śāstra</s>s,

body.text: śilpāni yāvanti ca sarvaloke pāraṃgateyaṃ nikhileṣu teṣu // 39 //
body.translated_text: Of whatever arts exist in the entire world, she has reached perfection in all of them. // 39 //

children.text: iṣvastravijñāna paraṃ vidhijñā sattvāna yuktau suviniścitā ca /
children.translated_text: Supremely skilled in the science of archery and weapons, well-versed in the governance of beings,

children.text: ākarṣaṇe śatrumanaḥprasāde sarvatra pāraṃ paramaṃ gateyam // 40 //
children.translated_text: In attraction and in pacifying the minds of enemies — in all these she has reached the highest perfection. // 40 //
With all her limbs of pure, supreme jewels, adorned with circles of radiance from released pearls,
Well-adorned by her own merits accumulated in former lives — this attendant is suited to you. // 41 //

children.text: ye vyādhayaḥ kecana jīvaloke teṣāṃ samutthānanaye vidhijñā /
children.translated_text: Whatever diseases exist in the world of the living, she is skilled in the methods of their arising,
And in the complete pacification of all of them, and in the proper examination of medicines. // 42 //

children.text: jambudhvaje ye 'pi ca sarvamantraniruktibhedā nikhilā janānām /
children.translated_text: And whatever distinctions of all <s>mantra</s>s (sacred formulas) and <s>nirukti</s>s (etymologies) exist among people in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,

children.text: sarvatra lokavyavahārasaṃghau citre gateyaṃ paramāṃ gatiṃ ca // 43 //
children.translated_text: In all worldly transactions and assemblies, and in the art of painting, she has attained the highest mastery. // 43 //

children.text: svarāṅganirhāranayāśca ye 'pi teṣāṃ prabhedeṣu naye praviṣṭā /
children.translated_text: And whatever methods of vocal music and instrumental playing exist, she has entered into their various principles,

children.text: gītāni nṛtyāni ca yāni loke teṣvapyaśeṣeṣu paraṃ vidhijñā // 44 //
children.translated_text: And whatever songs and dances exist in the world — in all of them without exception she is supremely skilled. // 44 //

children.text: tūryeṣu vādyeṣu ratiprayoge hāsye ca lāsye ca gatiṃ gateyam /
children.translated_text: In musical instruments, in playing, in the arts of love, in jest and dance, she has attained mastery;
She is skilled in discerning men who are attracted and those who are not, whether men are conciliated or filled with hostility. // 45 //

children.text: strīṇāṃ rutānīha ca yāni loke viśeṣatastānyakhilānyavaiti /
children.translated_text: And whatever modes of speech women use in the world, she knows all of them in their particularity,

children.text: ye cāprameyā vanitājanasya doṣā na teṣāṃ nikhilena santi // 46 //
children.translated_text: And the immeasurable faults that belong to womankind — none of these are present in her at all. // 46 //

body.text: nirīkṣite cārdhanirīkṣite ca aṅgapradāne 'ṅgavidarśane ca /
body.translated_text: In the full glance and the half-glance, in offering her limbs and in displaying her form,

body.text: niṣṭhāṃ gatā sarvakalāsu caiva manorathānāṃ paripūraṇī te // 47 //
body.translated_text: She has reached perfection in all the arts — she is the fulfiller of your desires. // 47 //

children.text: amatsarā ceyamanīrṣukā ca na kāmalolā na pānagṛddhā /
children.translated_text: She is free from jealousy and free from envy, neither fickle in passion nor greedy for drink,
Possessed of safety, rectitude, gentleness, and heroism, free from anger, never harsh, and deeply wise. // 48 //
Diligent in effort, never speaking contrary words, always following the wishes of her elders,
Respectful and ever seeking your welfare — she is fit for you in the practice of good conduct. // 49 //

children.text: jīrṇeṣu vṛddheṣu ca rogavatsu daridrabhūteṣu suduḥkhiteṣu /
children.translated_text: Toward the aged, the elderly, the diseased, those fallen into poverty, those greatly afflicted,
Those deprived of sight and those without refuge — she unceasingly generates a cloud of compassion. // 50 //
She is always delighted in thinking of the welfare of others, and never considers her own benefit;

children.text: sarvasya lokasya hitaiṣiṇī ca svalaṃkṛtā cittaguṇairudāraiḥ // 51 //
children.translated_text: She wishes for the welfare of the entire world, well-adorned with noble qualities of mind. // 51 //

children.text: nityāpramattā smṛtisaṃprajanye sthitā niṣaṇṇā śayitā vrajantī /
children.translated_text: Ever vigilant in <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension), whether standing, sitting, lying down, or walking,

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ prabhāṣatyapi ca smṛtaiva lokasya caivābhimatā sadaiṣā // 52 //
children.translated_text: Whether silent or speaking — she is ever mindful, and she is always beloved of the world. // 52 //

children.text: samantataḥ puṇyavatī vibhāti sadaiva ca premakarī janānām /
children.translated_text: She shines with merit on all sides, and is always a source of love for people;

children.text: etāmudīkṣanna hi tṛptimeti loke na cāsyāḥ kvacidasti saktiḥ // 53 //
children.translated_text: One who gazes upon her never reaches satiety, yet she herself has no attachment anywhere in the world. // 53 //
She is respectful toward <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s (spiritual friends), always eager for your sight,
Far-seeing and of unblemished conduct, with a mind pure and steadfast like <s>Sumeru</s>. // 54 //

body.text: sadā svapuṇyaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaiṣā na vidyate 'syāḥ kvacidapyamitram /
body.translated_text: She is always adorned by her own merits; nowhere does she have any enemy;

body.text: jñāne na cāsyāḥ sadṛśāsti yoṣideṣānurūpā tava rājaputra // 55 //
body.translated_text: And in knowledge there is no woman equal to her — she is suited to you, O prince. // 55 //

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputro gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhameghamudyānaṃ praviśya sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyo dārikāyā māturagragaṇikāyāḥ sudarśanāyāḥ samakṣaṃ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyaṃ dārikāmetadavocat - ahaṃ khalu dārike anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitaḥ / tena mayā aparimāṇāḥ sarvajñatāsaṃbhārāḥ samudānayitavyāḥ / anantamadhyān kalpān bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sarvapāramitāḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ / aparāntakoṭīgatān kalpāṃstathāgatāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ / sarvabuddhaśāsanāni saṃdhārayitavyāni / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi pariśodhayitavyāni / sarvatathāgatavaṃśā na vyavacchettavyāḥ / sarvasattvavaṃśāḥ paripācayitavyāḥ / sarvasattvasaṃsāraduḥkhāni vinivartayitavyāni / atyantasukhe sattvāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / sarvasattvānāṃ jñānacakṣuḥ pariśodhayitavyam / sarvabuddhabodhisattvasamudāgame prayoktavyam / sarvabodhisattvasamatāyāṃ sthātavyam / sarvabodhisattvabhūmayo niṣpādayitavyāḥ / sarvasattvadhātuḥ pariśodhayitavyaḥ sarvasattvadāridryavyavacchedāya sarvasvaparityāginā bhavitavyam / aparāntakoṭīgatān kalpān dānapāramitāyāṃ caratā annapānadānena sattvāḥ saṃtarpayitavyāḥ / sarvopakaraṇavastuparityāgena sarvayācanakasaṃghaḥ saṃtarpayitavyaḥ / tena mayā sarvasvaparityāgitāyāṃ pratipadyamānena nāsti tadādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ vā vastu yanna parityaktavyam / tena mayā putraduhitṛbhāryā dātavyāḥ / cakṣuḥśirohastapādasarvāṅgapratyaṅgāni parityaktavyāni / sā tvaṃ mama tadā pareṣu pratipadyamānā dānāntarāyaṃ kariṣyasi / priyeṣu putreṣu parityajyamāneṣvanāttamanā bhaviṣyasi / bahu kāyikacaitasikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyasi / mama sarvasvaparityāgacitte pratyupasthite mātsaryacittamutpādayiṣyasi / mamāṅgapratyaṅgāni cchittvā yācanakebhyaḥ parityajyamānasya duḥkhitā durmanasvinī bhaviṣyasi / bhaviṣyati ca sa kālo yadahaṃ tvāṃ parityajya tathāgataśāsane pravrajiṣyāmi / sā tvaṃ tasmin samaye 'nāttamanā bhaviṣyasi //
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, having entered the <s>Gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhamegha</s> garden, spoke thus to the girl <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> in the presence of her mother, the chief courtesan <s>Sudarśanā</s>: "I, O maiden, have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore I must accumulate immeasurable provisions for omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). Practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct through endless <s>kalpa</s>s, I must perfect all the <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections). Through <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the ultimate limit, I must worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>s. I must uphold the teachings of all <s>Buddha</s>s. I must purify all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. The lineages of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s must not be cut off. The lineages of all beings must be brought to maturation. The sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s> of all beings must be turned away. Beings must be established in ultimate happiness. The eye of knowledge of all beings must be purified. I must strive for the attainment of all <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. I must stand in the equality of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. All the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>s) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must be accomplished. The entire realm of beings must be purified. To cut off the poverty of all beings, I must become one who relinquishes everything. Through <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the ultimate limit, while practicing the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), I must satisfy beings through the gift of food and drink. Through the relinquishment of all requisites and possessions, the entire assembly of supplicants must be satisfied. As I undertake the relinquishing of everything, there is no internal or external thing that should not be given away. I must give away sons, daughters, and wives. Eyes, head, hands, feet, and all major and minor limbs must be relinquished. And you, when I am giving these to others, will create obstacles to my giving. When beloved sons are being given away, you will be displeased. You will experience much physical and mental suffering. When my mind is set upon relinquishing everything, you will generate a mind of jealous possessiveness. When my limbs and minor limbs are being cut off and given to supplicants, you will be grieved and dejected. And there will come a time when I shall abandon you and go forth into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching. At that time you will be displeased."

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputraḥ tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyaṃ dārikāṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> at that time addressed the girl <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: The great oceans of provisions for awakening (<s>saṃbodhi-saṃbhāra</s>) must be filled by me, immeasurable as they are,

children.text: yataḥ kṛpāṃ sarvajagatsu kṛtvā saṃprasthito 'haṃ sucirāya bodhau // 56 //
children.translated_text: For having generated compassion toward all worlds, I have set forth toward <s>bodhi</s> for a very long time. // 56 //
Through oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, truly endless and immeasurable as space, the <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow) must be purified;
On the stages of the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, through infinite <s>kalpa</s>s, preparatory work must be done. // 57 //

children.text: tryadhvasthitānāṃ ca mayā jinānāṃ saṃśikṣitā pāramitāpatheṣu /
children.translated_text: I have trained under the <s>Jina</s>s (Victors) abiding in the three times on the paths of the <s>pāramitā</s>s;
The supreme path of awakening must be purified through the great method of unsurpassed knowledge. // 58 //

children.text: kṣetrāṇi sarvāṇyapi sarvadikṣu kliṣṭāni śodhyāni mayākhilāni /
children.translated_text: All fields in all directions, defiled as they are, must be entirely purified by me;

children.text: sarvākṣaṇā durgatayaśca sarvā vyāvartanīyāḥ khalu sarvaloke // 59 //
children.translated_text: All unfavorable conditions and all states of misfortune must indeed be turned away in every world. // 59 //

children.text: sarve ca sattvā nikhilā viśodhyāḥ kleśāvṛtā mohatamondhabhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: And all beings without exception must be purified — those covered by <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions), blinded by the darkness of delusion;
Having matured them through various skillful means (<s>upāya</s>s), they must be established on the path of omniscience. // 60 //

children.text: bhūmīrasaṅgāśca mayā viśodhyā kalpārṇavāścaiva jināḥ prapūjyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The unattached stages (<s>bhūmi</s>s) must be purified by me, and the <s>Jina</s>s must be worshipped through oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s;

children.text: maitrīṃ ca saṃjanya jagatyaśeṣe deyāni dānānyakhilāni loke // 61 //
children.translated_text: Having generated <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward the entire world, all gifts must be given in the world. // 61 //
Seeing the supplicants who have come, as one always delighting in giving everything,

children.text: mā līnadīnā kṛpaṇā tadānīṃ bhūyā mama tvaṃ visabhāgacittā // 62 //
children.translated_text: Do not then become timid, dejected, or wretched, nor be of a mind contrary to mine. // 62 //

children.text: śirorthino me 'rthamudīkṣya dhīmān caryāmudārā ca ratastadānīm /
children.translated_text: Seeing the wise purpose of those who seek my head, and delighting then in the noble conduct,
You will be scorched by intense suffering — hearing this matter, attain steadfastness. // 63 //

children.text: tvaṃ daurmanasyaṃ mama hastapādacchedān pradāsyāmyāpi yācakānām /
children.translated_text: You will feel despair when my hands and feet are cut off; I shall give them to the supplicants;
Weak and pained in form, you will speak harsh words — hearing this matter, reflect carefully. // 64 //

children.text: priyāṇi vastūni tathaiva putrān dāsyāmi ca tvāmahamarthinaḥ san /
children.translated_text: I shall give away beloved possessions and likewise sons, and I shall give you as well, being a seeker of the goal;

children.text: śrutvaitamarthaṃ yadi te na sādaḥ sarvaṃ tathaivāstu yathā taveṣṭam // 65 //
children.translated_text: If, hearing this matter, you feel no distress, then let everything be just as you wish. // 65 //

body.text: evamukte sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīrdārikā tejodhipatiṃ rājaputrametadavocat - tathā bhavatu kumāra yathā vadasi / ahaṃ te yathākāmaṃ karaṇīyā yathecchāparibhogyā yenakāmaṃgamā sarvatrātyantānugāminī nityānubaddhā sarvakāryotsukā āśayānukūlopacārā samyakparākramā aviṣamapratipattiprayogopacārā bhaviṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> spoke thus to prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>: 'So be it, O prince, as you say. I shall be at your disposal as you wish, to be enjoyed as you desire, going wherever you wish, following you everywhere and always, ever devoted, eager in all tasks, with conduct agreeable to your intentions, of right exertion, with conduct and practice that is even and impartial.'

body.text: atha khalu sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīrdārikā tejodhipatiṃ rājaputraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> addressed prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> in verses:

children.text: kāyo hi yanme narakāgnināyaṃ saṃtāpyamāno vilayaṃ prayāyāt /
children.translated_text: Even if this body of mine were to be consumed, tormented by the fires of hell, and perish,
even through oceans of births I would endure — a companion in your practice, your attendant. // 66 //
Even in infinite births, born again and again, if my body were to be cut apart exceedingly,

children.text: tadutsahe 'haṃ sthiradhīracittā bhartā bhava tvaṃ mama sādhurūpa // 67 //
children.translated_text: that I would endure with firm and steadfast mind — be my husband, O one of beautiful form. // 67 //
Even through endless <s>kalpa</s>s, even if the <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains were to crush my head to powder,

children.text: āklāntacittāpi tadutsahe 'haṃ svāmī bhava tvaṃ mama sādhvacintya // 68 //
children.translated_text: that too I would endure with unwearied mind — be my lord, O one of marvelous beauty. // 68 //

children.text: jātyantarāṇyapyamitāni ca tvaṃ chittvāṅgamātmāni parasya dehi /
children.translated_text: Even through immeasurable lifetimes, cut your own limbs and give them to others,

children.text: cetovaśitvaṃ mayi saṃniveśya dṛḍhaṃ pratiṣṭhāpaya māṃ svadharme // 69 //
children.translated_text: and establishing mastery of mind in me, firmly establish me in your own <s>dharma</s>. // 69 //
I surrender this body to you completely, O son of a god among men;

children.text: caryāṃ caran kalpamahāsamudrān prayaccha māmarthijanāya hṛṣṭām // 70 //
children.translated_text: practicing your conduct through the great oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, give me joyfully to those who seek their purpose. // 70 //
You who have set forth toward the supreme and highest awakening, generating infinite compassion toward beings,
for the sake of embracing the ocean of all beings without remainder, accept me also, out of compassion. // 71 //

body.text: na bhogahetorna dhanasya hetorna kāmacaryāratisaṃbhavārtham /
body.translated_text: Not for the sake of enjoyment, not for the sake of wealth, not for the purpose of the pleasure of sensual conduct,

body.text: icchāmyahaṃ svāminamagrasattvaṃ sabhāgacaryācaraṇāya tu tvām // 72 //
body.translated_text: do I desire you as my lord, O foremost of beings, but for the practice of conduct in common. // 72 //

children.text: śuddhābhinīlekṣaṇa maitracittā yathekṣase tvaṃ khalu sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: O one of pure, deep-blue eyes and mind of loving-kindness, as you look upon the entire world,

children.text: āraktacittaḥ karuṇāyamāno niḥsaṃśayaṃ tvaṃ bhavitā munīndraḥ // 73 //
children.translated_text: with a mind full of affection, full of compassion — without doubt you shall become the lord of sages. // 73 //

children.text: yathā kramātprakramato mahī te ratnojjvalā tiṣṭhati nirmaleyam /
children.translated_text: As the earth, blazing with gems, stands stainless wherever you step forth,

children.text: sallakṣaṇālaṃkṛta cakravartī niḥsaṃśayaṃ tvaṃ bhavitā nṛloke // 74 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the marks of excellence, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) — without doubt you shall become one in the world of men. // 74 //
In a dream at night I saw, at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> of radiant good <s>dharma</s>-clouds,
at the root of the king of trees, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) seated, attended by many sons of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 75 //
That foremost lord of <s>Jina</s>s, with a body like the sun, like a great mountain of refined <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold,

children.text: svapnāntare murdhnyakarotsa me 'dya pāṇiṃ prabuddhā muditā tato 'ham // 76 //
children.translated_text: in that dream he placed his hand upon my head — and upon awakening, I was filled with joy. // 76 //
A deity of mine named <s>Ratiprabhā</s>, of pure body, an ancient guardian spirit of my bloodline,
announced: 'This <s>Tathāgata</s> dwells at this noble <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>.' // 77 //

children.text: abhūtpurā me khalu cetanaivamīkṣeya tejodhipatiṃ kumāram /
children.translated_text: There arose in me formerly this very thought: 'May I see prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>.'

children.text: ārocitaṃ devatayā kumāraṃ tvaṃ drakṣyasītyadya niśāntare me // 78 //
children.translated_text: The deity announced to me in the middle of the night: 'You shall see the prince today.' // 78 //

children.text: svapnāntare me sugato 'dya dṛṣṭaḥ tvaṃ caiva dṛṣṭaḥ pariśuddhasattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: In my dream today I saw the <s>Sugata</s>, and you too I have seen, O one of pure being;
together with you, my heart's wish fulfilled, I shall worship that lord of sages today. // 79 //

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputraḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā buddhadarśanāvakāśapratilabdho mahāprītiprasādavegasaṃjātaḥ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyaṃ dārikāṃ
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, having heard the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, having obtained the opportunity to see the <s>Buddha</s>, filled with a great surge of joy and faith, [showered] the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>

body.text: pañcabhirmaṇiratnaśatairabhyavakīrya śrīgarbhaprabhāsaṃ nāma cūḍāmaṇiratnamasyāḥ prādāt / agnivarṇena caināṃ mahāmaṇiratnacitreṇa vastraratnenācchādayāmāsa / saivaṃ satkṛtā na hṛpyati notpluvati na carati vā pramādaṃ vāgamat anyatra kṛtāñjalipuṭā animiṣanayanā tejodhipateḥ kumārasya vadanaṃ prekṣamāṇā sthitābhūt //
body.translated_text: with five hundred gem-jewels and gave her a crest-jewel called <s>Śrīgarbhaprabhāsa</s>. And he covered her with a jewel-cloth adorned with a great gem-jewel of fire-color. Thus honored, she was neither elated nor agitated nor careless nor heedless, but stood with palms joined together, with unblinking eyes, gazing at the face of prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudarśanā agragaṇikā tejodhipatiṃ rājakumāraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the chief courtesan <s>Sudarśanā</s> addressed prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> in verses:

children.text: dadyāmimāṃ te khalu dārikāṃ hamityevamāsīnmama dirgharātram /
children.translated_text: 'I would give you this maiden' — thus was my wish for a long time;

children.text: seyaṃ pradattā tava cārurūpā svalaṃkṛtā puṇyaguṇairupetā // 80 //
children.translated_text: she is now given to you, this beautiful one, well-adorned, endowed with qualities of merit. // 80 //

children.text: manuṣyaloke sadṛśī na kanyā saṃvidyate 'syāḥ kvaciduttamā yā /
children.translated_text: In the human world, no maiden equal to her is found anywhere, none superior;

children.text: śīlena buddhyātha guṇaistathānyaiḥ strīṇāṃ vareyaṃ svalu sarvaloke // 81 //
children.translated_text: in virtue, wisdom, and other qualities, she is the most excellent among women in all the world. // 81 //

children.text: padmodbhaveyaṃ na hi jātivādaḥ saṃdūṣaṇāmarhati nirmalatvāt /
children.translated_text: She is lotus-born — no reproach of birth can apply to her, on account of her purity;
her mind untouched by any fault whatsoever, she has become a companion in your practice. // 82 //
Her limbs, supremely soft, bring the happiness of the most excellent touch;
those who are sick and afflicted, by her touch, attain freedom from disease in that very instant. // 83 //

children.text: yo 'syāḥ śubho vāti hi gātragandho varāṃstadanyānabhibhūya gandhān /
children.translated_text: The beautiful fragrance that wafts from her body, surpassing all other fine fragrances —
upon smelling that fragrance, all people become established in pure moral conduct. // 84 //

children.text: asyā hi kāyaḥ kanakaprakāśo virocate nirmalapadmagarbhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Her body, radiant as gold, shines like a stainless lotus-womb;

children.text: kruddhā yamudvīkṣya hi maitracittā bhavanti sarve nikhilena sattvāḥ // 85 //
children.translated_text: even those who are angered, upon beholding her, become entirely endowed with minds of loving-kindness. // 85 //

body.text: snigdhaṃ vaco 'syā madhuraṃ manojñaṃ kāntaṃ janānāṃ śravaṇābhirāmam /
body.translated_text: Her speech is gentle, sweet, pleasing, beloved of people, delightful to the ears;

body.text: śrutvaiva yaddoṣatamovighāti karmāśubhaṃ nābhilaṣanti kartum // 86 //
body.translated_text: upon hearing it, which destroys the darkness of faults, they do not wish to perform unwholesome <s>karma</s>. // 86 //

children.text: śuddhāśayā nirmalamānaseyaṃ sarvatra śāṭhyaṃ na hi vidyate 'syāḥ /
children.translated_text: Her intentions are pure, her mind stainless; no deceit whatsoever is found in her;

children.text: yadbhāṣate cetasi tattathaiva yato jagattoṣayati svareṇa // 87 //
children.translated_text: what she speaks is exactly so in her mind, and therefore she delights the world with her voice. // 87 //

children.text: na māyayā mohayate ca sattvān vilobhayatyeva ca nārthahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: She does not deceive beings with illusion, nor does she seduce them for the sake of gain;
this one is modest and restrained in mind, always respectful toward elders and juniors. // 88 //

children.text: na jātigotreṇa na rūpamattā tathaiva neyaṃ parivāramattā /
children.translated_text: She is not intoxicated by birth or family, nor by beauty, nor likewise by retinue;

children.text: madena mānena ca viprayuktā namrā jineṣu praṇatā sadaiva // 89 //
children.translated_text: free from the intoxication of pride and arrogance, she is ever humble and bowed before the <s>Jina</s>s. // 89 //

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputraḥ saparivārayā sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyā dārikayā viṃśatyā kanyāsahasraiḥ parivāreṇa ca sārdhaṃ tato gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhameghādudyānānniṣkramya yena dharmodgataprabhāso bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bhagavān sūryagātrapravaraḥ tathāgataḥ, tenopasaṃkrānto 'bhūt bhagavataḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasya darśanāya vandanāya pūjanāya paryupāsanāya / sa yāvadyānasya bhūmistāvadyānena gatvā yānādavatīrya padbhyāmeva bhagavataḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkrāman adrākṣīttejodhipatī rājaputro bhagavantaṃ sūryagātrapravaraṃ tathāgatarmahantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dūrata eva prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ guptendriyaṃ nāgamiva sudāntaṃ hṛdamivācchaṃ anāvilaṃ viprasannam / dṛṣṭvā cāsya cittamabhiprasannam / prasannacitto buddhadarśanamahāprītiprasādavegān saṃvardhayāmāsa / mahāprītivegaprasādaprāmodyaparisphuṭena cittena taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya sārdhaṃ sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīdārikāpramukhena sarvaparivāreṇa pañcabhirmahāmaṇiratnapadmaśatasahasraiḥ taṃ bhagavantamabhicchādayāmāsa / pañca ca vihāraśātāni sarvagandhamaṇiratnamayāni sarvamaṇiratnarājavicitrāṇi tasya bhagavataḥ kārayāmāsa / ekaikaṃ ca vihāraṃ pañcabhirmahāmaṇiratnarājaśatasahasraiḥ pratimaṇḍayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, together with the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> and her retinue, along with twenty thousand maidens and his retinue, departed from the garden called <s>Gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhāmegha</s> and approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Dharmodgataprabhāsa</s>, where the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> was, for the purpose of seeing, honoring, worshipping, and attending upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>. Having gone by chariot as far as was fitting for a chariot, he descended from the chariot and approached on foot the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>. Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> beheld from afar the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, the great, perfectly and fully awakened one — inspiring, beautiful to behold, with senses calmed, with mind calmed, with senses guarded, like a well-tamed elephant, like a clear and limpid lake, serene. And upon seeing him, his mind was filled with faith. With a mind filled with faith, he increased the great surges of joy and faith in seeing the <s>Buddha</s>. With a mind overflowing with the great surge of joy, faith, and delight, he circumambulated that <s>Bhagavān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, bowed his head at the feet of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, and together with the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> and his entire retinue, covered that <s>Bhagavān</s> with five hundred thousand great gem-jewel lotuses. And he had five hundred <s>vihāra</s>s (monasteries) built for that <s>Bhagavān</s>, made entirely of fragrant gem-jewels, variegated with all gem-jewel kings. And he adorned each <s>vihāra</s> with five hundred thousand great gem-jewel kings.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra sa bhagavān sūryagātrapravarastathāgataḥ tejodhipate rājakumārasya adhyāśayaṃ viditvā samantanetradvārapradīpaṃ nāma sūtrāntaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa / sa taṃ śrutvā sarvadharmanayeṣu daśa samādhimukhasamudrān pratyalabhata / yaduta - sarvatathāgatapraṇidhānasāgarasaṃbhavāvabhāsaṃ nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / tryadhvāvabhāsagarbhaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ
body.translated_text: Then, son of good family, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, knowing the deep intention of prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, illuminated a <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourse) called <s>Samantanetradvārapradīpa</s> ('Lamp of the Gateway of the Universal Eye'). Upon hearing it, he attained ten oceans of <s>samādhi</s>-gateways in all the methods of <s>dharma</s>. Namely — he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Radiance Born from the Ocean of the Vows of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Womb of the Radiance of the Three Times.'

body.text: pratyalabhata / sarvabuddhamaṇḍalābhimukhaniryāṇaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvasattvapravarāvabhāsapraveśaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvalokasamudayajñānāvabhāsapratipannaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvasattvendriyasamudrāvabhāsapradīpaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvajagatparitrāṇajñānameghaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvasattvajagatparipākavinayābhimukhapradīpaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣavijñapanaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalapariśuddhipraṇidhimeghaṃ ca nāma samādhimukhaṃ pratyalabhata / imāni daśa samādhimukhāni pramukhaṃ kṛtvā sarvadharmanayeṣu daśasamādhimukhasamudrān pratyalabhata / sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīśca dārikā duryodhanajñānasāgaragarbhaṃ ca nāma cittanidhyaptiṃ pratyalabhata, avaivartikā cābhūdanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Going Forth Toward All <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Maṇḍala</s>s.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Entry into the Radiance of the Most Excellent of All Beings.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Attainment of the Radiance of the Knowledge of the Arising of All Worlds.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Lamp of the Radiance of the Ocean of the Faculties of All Beings.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Cloud of Knowledge for the Protection of All the World.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Lamp Directed Toward the Ripening and Discipline of All Beings of the World.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Making Known the Sound of the Turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' And he attained the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway called 'Cloud of the Vow of the Purification of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of <s>Samantabhadra</s>-Conduct.' Having attained these ten <s>samādhi</s>-gateways as the foremost, he attained ten oceans of <s>samādhi</s>-gateways in all the methods of <s>dharma</s>. And the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> attained a mental concentration called 'Womb of the Ocean of Invincible Knowledge,' and she became irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: atha khalu tejodhipatī rājaputraḥ bhagavataḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya taṃ bhagavantamanekatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyā dārikayā sarvaparivāreṇa ca sārdhaṃ tasya bhagavato 'ntikātprākrāmat / sa yena drumameruśrī rājadhānī, yena ca pitā rājā dhanapatistenopajagāma / upetya piturdhanapate rājñaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya etamarthamārocayāmāsa - yatkhalu deva jānīyāḥ - sūryagātrapravaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān / ihaiva tava vijite dharmameghodgataprabhāse bodhimaṇḍe viharatyacirābhisaṃbuddhaḥ / atha khalu rājā dhanapatistejodhipatiṃ kumārametadavocat - kena te kumāra ayamarthaṃ ārocito devena vā manuṣyeṇa vā? sa prāha - sucalitaratiprabhāsaśriyā dārikayeti //
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> and having circumambulated that <s>Bhagavān</s> many tens of thousands of times, together with the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> and his entire retinue, departed from the presence of that <s>Bhagavān</s>. He went to the royal capital <s>Drumameruśrī</s>, to his father, King <s>Dhanapati</s>. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of his father King <s>Dhanapati</s> and announced this matter: 'May the lord know this — a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly and fully awakened one, has appeared in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwells right here in your domain, at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> <s>Dharmameghodgataprabhāsa</s>, having recently attained full awakening.' Then King <s>Dhanapati</s> spoke thus to prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>: 'By whom, O prince, was this matter announced to you — by a god or by a human?' He replied: 'By the maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu rājā dhanapatirbuddhotpādaśravaṇena mahānidhānapratilābhasaṃjñī sudurlabhabuddharatnaparilābhasaṃjñī tathāgatadarśane sarvadurgatiprapātabhayavinivartanasaṃjñī sarvakleśavyādhipraśamanamahāvaidyarājapratilābhasaṃjñī sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhaparimocakasaṃjñī atyantayogakṣemapratiṣṭhāpakasaṃjñī vitimirajñānālokadarśakasaṃjñī avidyāndhakāravidhvaṃsanamaholkāprādurbhāvasaṃjñī anāyakasya lokasya dharmanayavināyakapratilābhasaṃjñī apariṇāyakasya sarvajñatāyānapariṇāyakasamutpādasaṃjñī mahāprītiprasādaprāmodyapratilabdho buddhotpādaṃ śrutvā kṣatriyabrāhmaṇanaigamajanapadāmātyapurohitakumārakoṭṭarājāno dauvārikapārṣadyāṃśca saṃnipātya buddhotpādanandaśabdāvedinastejodhipateḥ kumārasya tadrājyaṃ dharmācchādaṃ prādāt / sa taṃ kumāraṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ prāṇisahasrairyena bhagavān sūryagātrapravarastathāgatastenopajagāma / upetya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tasya bhagavataḥ purastānnyaṣīdat sārdhaṃ svakena parivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanapati</s>, upon hearing of the arising of the <s>Buddha</s>, conceived the perception of obtaining a great treasure, the perception of obtaining the extremely rare <s>Buddha</s>-jewel, the perception that in seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> the fear of falling into all bad destinies is turned back, the perception of obtaining a great king of physicians who pacifies the disease of all afflictions, the perception of one who liberates from the suffering of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, the perception of one who establishes [beings] in absolute safety, the perception of seeing the light of knowledge free from darkness, the perception of the appearance of a great torch that dispels the darkness of ignorance, the perception of obtaining a guide of the method of <s>dharma</s> for the leaderless world, the perception of the arising of a conductor to the vehicle of omniscience for a world without a conductor. Having obtained great delight, serenity, and joy upon hearing of the arising of the <s>Buddha</s>, he summoned the <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, guild-leaders, provincial folk, ministers, priests, princes, and vassal kings, along with the doorkeepers and retinue, and — making the sound of the joy of the arising of the <s>Buddha</s> known — bestowed that kingdom as a <s>dharma</s>-canopy upon the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>. Having consecrated that prince in the kingdom, together with ten thousand living beings, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated that <s>Bhagavān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before that <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his retinue. //

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra sa bhagavān sūryagātrapravarastathāgato dhanapatiṃ rājānaṃ sarvāvacca parṣanmaṇḍalamavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāmūrṇākośātsarvajagaccittapradīpaṃ nāma raśmiṃ prāmuñcat / sā daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātūnavabhāsya sarvalokendrānabhimukhaṃ parisaṃsthāpya acintyāni buddhavikurvitāni
body.translated_text: Then, son of good family, that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, having surveyed King <s>Dhanapati</s> and the entire assembly, at that moment released from the tuft between his brows (<s>ūrṇākośa</s>) a ray called 'Lamp of the Mind of All Beings.' That ray, having illuminated all world-realms in the ten directions and having arranged all the lords of the world face-to-face, displaying inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-transformations,

body.text: saṃdarśya buddhavainayikānāṃ sattvānāmāśayān viśodhya tasyāṃ velāyāmacintyena buddhādhipateyena sarvalokābhyudgatena buddhakāyena sarvasvarāṅgasāgarasaṃprayuktena buddhaghoṣeṇa sarvadharmavitimirārthapradīpaṃ nāma dhāraṇīmukhaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamadhāraṇīmukhaparivāram / atha rājño dhanapatestaddhāraṇīmukhaṃ śrutvā sarvadharmeṣu mahān dharmāvabhāsaḥ prādurabhūt / tasyāṃ ca parṣadi jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmavitimirārthapradīpāyā dhāraṇyāḥ pratilambho 'bhūt / ṣaṣṭeśca prāṇiniyutānāmanupādāya āsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni / daśānāṃ ca prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham / aparimāṇānāmanutpannapūrvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpannam / daśasu dikṣu acintyabuddhavikurvitasaṃdarśanenānantamadhyaḥ sattvadhāturvinayamagamāt tribhiryānaiḥ //
body.translated_text: having purified the intentions of beings to be disciplined by the <s>Buddha</s>, at that moment, with an inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-sovereignty, with a <s>Buddha</s>-body surpassing all worlds, with a <s>Buddha</s>-voice conjoined with the ocean of all sounds, limbs, and cries, he expounded the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gate called 'Lamp of the Meaning that Dispels the Darkness of All <s>Dharma</s>s,' together with its retinue of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Then, upon hearing that <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gate, a great illumination of <s>Dharma</s> arose for King <s>Dhanapati</s> in all <s>dharma</s>s. And in that assembly, <s>bodhisattva</s>s equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> attained that <s>dhāraṇī</s> 'Lamp of the Meaning that Dispels the Darkness of All <s>Dharma</s>s.' And sixty <s>niyuta</s>s of living beings had their minds liberated from the defilements without further clinging. And ten thousand living beings attained the purified <s>dharma</s>-eye, stainless and free from impurity, regarding <s>dharma</s>s. And immeasurable beings generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening that had never before arisen. And by the display of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-transformations in the ten directions, an infinite and middleless realm of beings was brought to discipline through the three vehicles. //

body.text: rājñaśca dhanapatermahādharmāvabhāsapratilabdhasya etadabhavat - na śakyamagāramadhyāvasatā imā evaṃrūpā dharmā adhimoktum, evaṃrūpaṃ ca jñānaṃ niṣpādayitum / yannvahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike pravrājayeyam / atha khalu rājā dhanapatistaṃ bhagavantametadavocat - labheyāhaṃ bhagavato 'ntike pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam / āha - yasyedānīṃ mahārāja kālaṃ manyase //
body.translated_text: And King <s>Dhanapati</s>, having obtained the great illumination of <s>Dharma</s>, thought thus: 'It is not possible for one dwelling in a household to devote oneself to <s>dharma</s>s of such a nature, or to accomplish such knowledge. I should go forth into homelessness in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then King <s>Dhanapati</s> spoke to that <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May I obtain, in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the going-forth, the ordination, and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>.' He replied: 'Now is the time, great king, if you think fit.' //

body.text: atha khalu rājā dhanapatiḥ sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasyāntike prāvrajat sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ / tena acireṇa pravrajitena sarvadharmavitimirārthapradīpaṃ dhāraṇīmukhaṃ saparivāraṃ niṣpāditaṃ bhāvitam, tāvantyeva ca samādhimukhāni pratilabdhāni / daśa ca bodhisattvābhijñāḥ pratilabdhā / anantamadhyaṃ ca pratisaṃvinnayasāgarāmavatīrṇaḥ / asaṅgagocarā ca nāma kāyapariśuddhiḥ daśadiktathāgatopasaṃkramaṇeṣu pratilabdhā / sa tasya bhagavato dharmacakraṃ pratīcchitavān saṃdhāritavān, kathāpuruṣatvaṃ ca kārayāmāsa / mahādharmabhāṇakatvaṃ ca akarot / śāsanaparigrahaṃ cākārṣīt / abhijñāpratilābhabalena ca sarvāvatīṃ lokadhātuṃ spharitvā yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāyaṃ saṃdarśya etaṃ buddhotpādaṃ prabhāvayan tāṃ sarvatathāgatasamudayadharmatāmabhidyotayan tāṃ pūrvayogasaṃpadaṃ saṃprakāśayan taṃ buddhavikurvitaprabhāvaṃ saṃvarṇayamānaḥ śāsanaparigrahamakārṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanapati</s> went forth into homelessness in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, together with ten thousand living beings. Having gone forth, in a short time he accomplished and cultivated the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gate 'Lamp of the Meaning that Dispels the Darkness of All <s>Dharma</s>s' together with its retinue, and attained an equal number of <s>samādhi</s>-gates. And he attained the ten <s>bodhisattva</s>-superknowledges. And he descended into the infinite and middleless ocean of the method of analytical knowledge. And he attained a body-purification called 'unobstructed range' for approaching <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the ten directions. He received and upheld the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, and served as the one who carries on the discourse. He performed the role of a great <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. He took charge of the teaching. And by the power of attaining the superknowledges, having pervaded the entire world-realm, displaying bodies according to the dispositions of beings, proclaiming that arising of the <s>Buddha</s>, illuminating that <s>dharmatā</s> of the arising of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, expounding that fulfillment of former practice, praising that power and glory of <s>Buddha</s>-transformation — he took charge of the teaching. //

body.text: tejodhipatinā ca rājaputreṇa tatraiva divase pūrṇāyāṃ pūrṇamāsyāṃ sapta ratnāni pratilabdhāni / tasyopariprāsādatalagatasya strīgaṇaparivṛtasya purastādapratihatavegaṃ nāma śatasahasrāraṃ sarvaratnasamalaṃkṛtaṃ divyaṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayaṃ samantaprabhaṃ sarvākāravaropetaṃ mahācakraratnaṃ prādurabhūt / vajraratnagiritejaśca nāma mahāhastiratnaṃ prādurabhūt / nīlagiryanilavegaṃ ca nāma aśvaratnaṃ prādurabhavat / ādityagarbhaprabhamegharājaṃ ca nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ prādurabhavat / sā ca sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī dārikā strīratnaṃ prādurabhavat / prabhūtaghanaskandhaṃ ca nāma gṛhapatiratnaṃ prādurabhavat / vimalanetraṃ ca nāma pariṇāyakaratnaṃ saptamaṃ prādurabhavat / sa saptaratnasamanvāgato rājābhavaccakravartī caturdvīpeśvaro dhārmiko dharmarājo vijitāvī janapadasthāmavīryaprāptaḥ / pūrṇaṃ khalu punarasya sahasraṃ putrāṇāmabhūcchūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām / sa
body.translated_text: And on that very day, on the full-moon day, the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s> obtained the seven treasures. As he was on the upper terrace of his palace, surrounded by a retinue of women, there appeared before him the great wheel-treasure (<s>cakraratna</s>) called <s>Apratihatavega</s> (Irresistible Force) — with a hundred thousand spokes, adorned with all gems, divine, made of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, radiating in all directions, endowed with all excellent qualities. And a great elephant-treasure called <s>Vajraratnagiritejas</s> appeared. And a horse-treasure called <s>Nīlagiryanilavegas</s> appeared. And a great gem-treasure called <s>Ādityagarbhaprabhāmegharāja</s> appeared. And that maiden <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> appeared as the woman-treasure. And a householder-treasure called <s>Prabhūtaghanaskandha</s> appeared. And a general-treasure called <s>Vimalanetra</s> appeared as the seventh. Endowed with the seven treasures, he became a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), lord of four continents, righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, victorious, having attained the strength and might of the provinces. He had a full thousand sons — heroes, champions, of fine limbs and form, crushers of enemy armies. He

body.text: imāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ sasāgaragiriparyantāmakhilāmakaṇṭakāmanītikāmanupadravāmṛddhāṃ sphītāṃ kṣemāṃ subhikṣāṃ ramaṇīyāmākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṃ dharmeṇābhinirjitya adhyāvasati sma //
body.translated_text: having conquered by <s>dharma</s> this entire great earth, bounded by oceans and mountains, whole, without thorns, without calamities, without afflictions, prosperous, flourishing, safe, well-provisioned, delightful, filled with many people and humans — he ruled over it. //

body.text: sa tasmin jambudvīpe caturaśītirājadhānīsahasreṣu ekaikasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ pañca vihāraśatāni kārayāmāsa sarvākāravaropetāni sarvopabhogaparibhogopacārasaṃpannāni sarvodyānaprāsādacaṃkramaniryāṇasukhaparibhogyavanarājīvibhūṣitāni / ekaikasmiṃśca vihāre tathāgatacaityaṃ kārayāmāsa vipulodviddhamatyantarānekākāraratnavyūhaṃ sarvamaṇiratnarājavicitram / sarvāsu ca tāsu rājadhānīṣu taṃ bhagavantaṃ sūryagātrapravaraṃ tathāgataṃ saparivāramupanimantrayāmāsa nagarapraveśāya / sarvāsu rājadhānīṣu taṃ tathāgataṃ sarvākārayā acintyayā tathāgatapūjayā pūjayan praveśayāmāsa / sa buddhanagarapraveśaprātihāryavikurvitena apramāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlāni saṃjanayamāsa / tatrāprasannacittāḥ sattvāḥ prasādaṃ pratyalabhanta / prasannacittāḥ sattvā buddhadarśanaprītivegān vivardhayāmāsuḥ / prītivegavivardhitāḥ sattvā bodhyāśayaviśuddhiṃ pratyalabhanta / bodhyāśayaviśuddhāḥ sattvāḥ mahākaruṇācetanāmutpādayāmāsuḥ / sattvahitapratipannāḥ sattvāḥ sarvabuddhadharmaparyeṣṭyabhiyuktā abhūvan / buddhadharmanayavidhijñāḥ sattvāḥ sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyaptaye cittamabhinirṇāmayāmāsuḥ / dharmasamatāvatīrṇāḥ sattvāḥ tryadhvasamatāvatārāya cittamabhinirṇāmayāmāsuḥ / tryadhvajñānāvabhāsapratilabdhāḥ sattvāḥ sarvabuddhaparaṃparāvijñaptaye jñānālokamavakrāmati sma / vicitratathāgatavijñaptyavakrāntāḥ sattvāḥ sarvajagatsaṃgrahāya cittamabhinirṇāmayāmāsuḥ / sarvajagatsaṃgrahaprayuktāḥ sattvā bodhisattvamārgaviśuddhaye praṇidhānamutpādayāmāsuḥ / mārgasamatāvatīrṇāḥ sattvāḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrābhinirhārāya jñānālokamutpādayāmāsuḥ / dharmasāgaravinayābhimukhā sattvāḥ sarvakṣetrajālasvakāyaspharaṇatāyai cittamabhinirṇāmayāmāsuḥ / kṣetrasamatāvatīrṇāḥ sattvāḥ sarvasattvendriyasamudraparijñāyai praṇidhānamakārṣuḥ / sarvajagadindriyayathādhimuktivicāraprayuktāḥ sattvāḥ sarvajñatādhigamāya adhyāśayaṃ viśodhayāmāsuḥ / ityevaṃrūpāṇāṃ sattvānāmimāmevaṃrūpārthasiddhiṃ saṃpraveśya tejodhipatī rājā sarvāsu rājadhānīṣu taṃ sūryagātrapravaraṃ tathāgataṃ praveśayāmāsa acintyena buddhavikurvitaprātihāryasaṃdarśanena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ paripākavinayāya //
body.translated_text: In that <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in eighty-four thousand royal capitals, in each and every royal capital, he had five hundred monasteries built — endowed with all excellent qualities, furnished with all provisions for use and enjoyment, adorned with rows of forest-trees delightful for the enjoyment of all gardens, palaces, and walkways. In each and every monastery he had a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine built — vast and lofty, of manifold and diverse gem-arrays, variegated with all gem-jewel kings. And in all those royal capitals, he invited that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> together with his retinue to enter the cities. In all the royal capitals, he ushered in that <s>Tathāgata</s> with all manner of inconceivable <s>Tathāgata</s>-worship. And through the miraculous transformation-display of the <s>Buddha</s>'s entering the cities, he caused wholesome roots to arise in immeasurable beings. Therein, beings of unbelieving mind attained faith. Beings of faithful mind increased the momentum of delight in seeing the <s>Buddha</s>. Beings whose momentum of delight was increased attained purification of the intention for awakening. Beings whose intention for awakening was purified generated the thought of great compassion. Beings who had set out for the benefit of beings became devoted to the search for all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. Beings who knew the method of the manner of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s turned their minds toward the contemplation of the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s. Beings who had entered the equality of <s>dharma</s>s turned their minds toward entry into the equality of the three times. Beings who had attained the illumination of the knowledge of the three times entered the light of knowledge for making known the succession of all <s>Buddha</s>s. Beings who had entered the making known of variegated <s>Tathāgata</s>s turned their minds toward the gathering of the entire world. Beings engaged in gathering the entire world generated the vow for the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path. Beings who had entered the equality of the path generated the light of knowledge for the accomplishment of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Beings facing the ocean of <s>dharma</s>-discipline turned their minds toward pervading all nets of fields with their own bodies. Beings who had entered the equality of fields made the vow for the thorough knowledge of the ocean of the faculties of all beings. Beings engaged in investigating the aspirations and faculties of all beings purified their deep intention for the attainment of omniscience. Thus, having caused beings of such natures to enter the accomplishment of purposes of such kinds, King <s>Tejodhipati</s> ushered in the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> into all the royal capitals — through the inconceivable display of <s>Buddha</s>-transformation miracles, for the ripening and discipline of those beings. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena tejodhipatirnāma rājaputro 'bhūt? na khalu punastvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam / ayaṃ sa bhagavān śākyamunistathāgatastena kālena tena samayena tejodhipatirnāma rājaputro 'bhūt, yena taccakravartirājyaṃ pratilabdham, sa ca sūryagātrapravaro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena dhanapatirnāma rājā abhūt tejodhipateḥ kumārasya pitā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ratnakusumaprabho nāma tathāgatastena kālena tena samayena dhanapatirnāma rājā abhūt, ya etarhi pūrvasyāṃ diśi lokadhātau sāgaraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātusamudrāṇāṃ pareṇa dharmadhātugaganapratibhāsameghanāmni lokadhātusamudre tryadhvapratibhāsamaṇirājasaṃbhavakulamadhyame lokadhātuvaṃśe buddhaprabhāmaṇḍalaśrīpradīpāyāṃ lokadhātau sucandrakāyapratibhāsadhvaje bodhimaṇḍe
body.translated_text: What do you think, son of good family — was that prince named <s>Tejodhipati</s> someone else at that time, in that era? You should not view it thus. This <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> was at that time, in that era, the prince named <s>Tejodhipati</s>, by whom that <s>Cakravartin</s> kingdom was obtained and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s> was honored. And what do you think, son of good family — was that King named <s>Dhanapati</s>, the father of the prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, someone else at that time? You should not view it thus. The <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnakusumaprabha</s> was at that time, in that era, the King named <s>Dhanapati</s> — who now, in the eastern direction, beyond oceans of world-realms equal to the atoms of oceans, in the ocean of world-realms called <s>Dharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamegha</s>, in the middle succession of world-realms called <s>Tryadhvapratibhāsamaṇirājasaṃbhavakula</s>, in the world-realm called <s>Buddhaprabhāmaṇḍalaśrīpradīpa</s>, at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> called <s>Sucandrakāyapratibhāsadhvaja</s>,

body.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'nabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamabodhisattvaparivṛto dharmaṃ deśayati / tena ca bhagavatā ratnakusumaprabheṇa tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sarvadharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamegho lokadhātusamudraḥ pariśodhitaḥ / yāvantaśca tasmin lokadhātusamudre tathāgatā utpannāśca utpadyante ca utpatsyante ca, te sarve ca bhagavatā ratnakusumaprabheṇa tathāgatena pūrvabodhisattvacaryāścaratā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācitāḥ //
body.translated_text: has attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, and surrounded by <s>bodhisattva</s>s equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, is teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And by that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnakusumaprabha</s>, while formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, the ocean of world-realms <s>Sarvadharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamegha</s> was purified. And as many <s>Tathāgata</s>s as have arisen, are arising, and will arise in that ocean of world-realms — all of them were ripened by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnakusumaprabha</s> while he was formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, for unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā nāma rājabhāryā abhūt tejodhipateḥ kumārasya mātā caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇāṃ pramukhānām? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / eṣā sā kulaputra māyādevī bhagavato mātā bodhisattvajananī samantāvabhāsānāvaraṇavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā asaṃkhyeyasarvatathāgatasamudrāgamapratyakṣā sarvabodhisattvajanmasaṃdarśanavidhijñā tena kālena tena samayena padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā nāma rājño dhanateragramahiṣyabhūt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena sudarśanā nāma agragaṇikā abhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / eṣā sā sunetrā nāma daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya bhāryā mama mātā tena kālena tena samayena sudarśanā nāma agragaṇikābhūt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīrnāma gaṇikādārikābhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrīrgaṇikādārikā abhūt / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena tejodhipate rājñaḥ parivāro 'bhūt? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ime te bodhisattvāḥ sarve samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaparipūryāṃ bhagavatā pratiṣṭhāpitā asminneva parṣanmaṇḍale saṃniṣaṇṇāsarvalokadhātupratibhāsaprāptena kāyena sarvabodhisattvasamādhivihārasaṃbhinnena cittena sarvatathāgataḥ saṃmukhabhāvavadanavijñaptena cakṣuṣā sarvatathāgatagaganasvarāṅgameghacakranigarjitanirghoṣavijñaptena śrotreṇa sarvadharmavihāravaśavartinā āśvāsapraśvāsena sarvabuddhakṣetrānucalitena nirghoṣeṇa sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalopasaṃkramaṇāpratiprasrabdhena bodhisattvakāyena bodhisattvayathāśayābhimukhena paripākavinayānukūlena ātmabhāvābhinirhāreṇa aśeṣasarvadigjālaprasṛtena nānāgatasarvakalpāvyavacchinnena samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaparipūrisamudāgamena samanvāgatā bhagavataḥ parṣanmaṇḍale saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ / sa khalu kulaputra sūryagātrapravarastathāgatastejodhipatinā cakravartinā ca mayā ca yāvajjīvamupasthito 'bhūt cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: What do you think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the king's wife named <s>Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā</s>, the mother of Prince <s>Tejodhipati</s>, foremost among eighty-four thousand women, someone else? It should not be seen thus. This, son of good family, is <s>Māyādevī</s>, the mother of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the one who gives birth to <s>bodhisattvas</s>, established in the liberation <s>Samantāvabhāsānāvaraṇa</s> (Unobstructed Universal Illumination), one with direct knowledge of innumerable oceans of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, one who knows the methods of displaying the births of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — she was at that time the chief queen named <s>Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā</s> of King <s>Dhanateragra</s>. What do you think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the chief courtesan named <s>Sudarśanā</s> someone else? It should not be seen thus. She was <s>Sunetrā</s>, the wife of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, my mother — she was at that time the chief courtesan named <s>Sudarśanā</s>. What do you think, son of good family — was the one who at that time was the courtesan-maiden named <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s> someone else? It should not be seen thus. I myself was at that time the courtesan-maiden named <s>Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī</s>. What do you think, son of good family — was the retinue of King <s>Tejodhipati</s> at that time someone else? It should not be seen thus. These <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the fulfillment of the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, are seated right here in this very assembly-<s>maṇḍala</s> — endowed with bodies that have attained reflection in all world-realms, with minds entered into the <s>samādhi</s>-abiding of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, with eyes cognized by the face-to-face presence and speech of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with ears cognized by the thundering proclamation of the sky-voice-limb-cloud-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with breathing that commands all <s>dharma</s>-abodes, with sound that does not waver from all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, with a <s>bodhisattva</s>-body unrelaxed in approaching the assembly-<s>maṇḍalas</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with an accomplishment of self-manifestation that faces <s>bodhisattvas</s> according to their dispositions and is favorable to ripening and discipline, extended through the net of all directions without remainder, uninterrupted through all <s>kalpas</s> of the future, endowed with the accomplishment of fulfilling the practice and vow of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> — they are seated in the assembly-<s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. That <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, son of good family, was attended by me as a king's wife, together with the <s>cakravartin</s> <s>Tejodhipati</s>, for his entire life, with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick as provisions. //

body.text: tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputra sūryagātrapravarasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasyānantaraṃ tasyāmeva lokadhātau prasannagātro nāma tathāgato loka udapādi / so 'pyasmābhirārāgitaḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sarvagātrajñānapratibhāsacandro nāma tathāgato loka udapādi / so 'pyasmābhirdevendrabhūtairārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jāmbūnadatejorājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ lakṣaṇabhūṣitagātro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vicitraraśmijvalanacandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ suvilokitajñānaketurnāma tathāgata
body.translated_text: After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sūryagātrapravara</s>, son of good family, in that very world-realm, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prasannagātra</s> (Of Pleasant Body) arose in the world. He too was pleased, honored, venerated, respected, and worshipped by us. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvagātrajñānapratibhāsacandra</s> (Moon of the Reflection of the Knowledge of All Bodies) arose in the world. He too was pleased by us when we were lords of <s>devas</s>. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jāmbūnadatejorāja</s> (King of the Splendor of Jāmbūnada Gold) was pleased. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Lakṣaṇabhūṣitagātra</s> (Body Adorned with Marks) was pleased. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vicitraraśmijvalanacandra</s> (Moon Blazing with Variegated Rays) was pleased. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Suvilokitajñānaketu</s> (Banner of Well-Surveyed Knowledge)

body.text:
ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vipulamahājñānaraśmirājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ nārāyaṇavajravīryo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaramaparājitajñānasthāmo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantavilokitajñāno nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vimalaśrīmegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitaprabho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānaraśmijvalanacūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ guṇaraśmidhvajonāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānabhāskaratejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnapadmapraphullitagātro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ puṇyapradīpadhvajo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānaraśmimeghaprabho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantavairocanacandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ābharaṇacchatranirghoṣo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantajñānālokavikramasiṃho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmadhātuviṣayamaticandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sattvagaganacittapratibhāsabimbo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ praśamagandhasunābho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantānuravitaśāntanirghoṣo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ sudṛḍhajñānaraśmijālabimbaskandho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ amṛtaparvataprabhātejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmasāgaranigarjitaghoṣo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ buddhagaganaprabhāsacūḍo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ raśmicandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ raśmicandrorṇamegho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ suparipūrṇajñānamukhaktro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ suviśuddhajñānakusumāvabhāso nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnārciḥparvataśrītejorājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vipulaguṇajyotiḥprabho nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samādhimervabhyudgatajñāno nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnacandradhvajo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaramarcirmaṇḍalagātro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ ratnāgraprabhatejo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ samantajñānacaryāvilambo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ arciḥsamudramukhavegapradīpo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmavimānanirghoṣarājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaramasadṛśaguṇakīrtidhvajo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ pralambabāhurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ pūrvapraṇidhinirmāṇacandro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaramākāśajñānārthapradīpo
nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmodgatanabheśvaro nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ vairocanaśrīgarbharājo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmanārāyaṇaketurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ jñānaketurnāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / tasyānantaraṃ dharmasāgarapadmo nāma tathāgata ārāgitaḥ / iti hi kulaputra etāṃstathāgatān pramukhān kṛtvā tasyāṃ lokadhātau ṣaṣṭibuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyutpannāni
body.translated_text: was pleased. After him, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vipulamahājñānaraśmirāja</s> (King of Rays of Vast Great Knowledge) was pleased. After him, <s>Nārāyaṇavajravīrya</s> (Of Nārāyaṇa-Vajra Vigor). After him, <s>Aparājitajñānasthāma</s> (Of Unconquered Knowledge-Power). After him, <s>Samantavilokitajñāna</s> (Universal-Surveying Knowledge). After him, <s>Vimalaśrīmegha</s> (Cloud of Stainless Glory). After him, <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitaprabha</s> (Radiance of Lion's Stretch). After him, <s>Jñānaraśmijvalanacūḍa</s> (Crest Blazing with Knowledge-Rays). After him, <s>Guṇaraśmidhvaja</s> (Banner of Quality-Rays). After him, <s>Jñānabhāskarateja</s> (Splendor of the Sun of Knowledge). After him, <s>Ratnapadmapraphullitagātra</s> (Body Blossoming with Jewel-Lotuses). After him, <s>Puṇyapradīpadhvaja</s> (Banner of the Lamp of Merit). After him, <s>Jñānaraśmimeghaprabha</s> (Radiance of the Cloud of Knowledge-Rays). After him, <s>Samantavairocanacandra</s> (Moon of Universal Vairocana). After him, <s>Ābharaṇacchatranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Ornament-Parasol). After him, <s>Samantajñānālokavikramasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Advance of Universal Knowledge-Light). After him, <s>Dharmadhātuviṣayamaticandra</s> (Moon of the Mind of the Domain of the Dharmadhātu). After him, <s>Sattvagaganacittapratibhāsabimba</s> (Image of the Reflection of the Mind-Sky of Beings). After him, <s>Praśamagandhasunābha</s> (Of Fragrant Tranquility and Beautiful Navel). After him, <s>Samantānuravitaśāntanirghoṣa</s> (Sound of Universal Peaceful Resonance). After him, <s>Sudṛḍhajñānaraśmijālabimbaskandha</s> (Mass of the Image of the Net of Firm Knowledge-Rays). After him, <s>Amṛtaparvataprabhāteja</s> (Splendor of the Radiance of the Immortal Mountain). After him, <s>Dharmasāgaranigarjitaghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Roaring of the Dharma-Ocean). After him, <s>Buddhagaganaprabhāsacūḍa</s> (Crest of the Illumination of the Buddha-Sky). After him, <s>Raśmicandra</s> (Ray-Moon). After him, <s>Raśmicandrorṇamegha</s> (Cloud of the Ūrṇā of the Ray-Moon). After him, <s>Suparipūrṇajñānamukhaktra</s> (Of the Well-Fulfilled Face of Knowledge). After him, <s>Suviśuddhajñānakusumāvabhāsa</s> (Illumination of the Flower of Well-Purified Knowledge). After him, <s>Ratnārciḥparvataśrītejorāja</s> (King of the Splendor of the Glory of the Mountain of Jewel-Flame). After him, <s>Vipulaguṇajyotiḥprabha</s> (Radiance of the Light of Vast Qualities). After him, <s>Samādhimervabhyudgatajñāna</s> (Knowledge Arisen above the Sumeru of Samādhi). After him, <s>Ratnacandradhvaja</s> (Banner of the Jewel-Moon). After him, <s>Arcirmaṇḍalagātra</s> (Body of the Flame-Maṇḍala). After him, <s>Ratnāgraprabhateja</s> (Splendor of the Radiance of the Foremost Jewel). After him, <s>Samantajñānacaryāvilamba</s> (Pendant of the Conduct of Universal Knowledge). After him, <s>Arciḥsamudramukhavegapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Swift Gateway of the Ocean of Flame). After him, <s>Dharmavimānanirghoṣarāja</s> (King of the Sound of the Dharma-Palace). After him, <s>Asadṛśaguṇakīrtidhvaja</s> (Banner of the Fame of Incomparable Qualities). After him, <s>Pralambabāhu</s> (Of Pendulous Arms). After him, <s>Pūrvapraṇidhinirmāṇacandra</s> (Moon of the Emanation of Former Vows). After him, <s>Ākāśajñānārthapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Purpose of Space-Knowledge). After him, <s>Dharmodgatanabheśvara</s> (Lord of the Navel of the Arising of Dharma). After him, <s>Vairocanāśrīgarbharāja</s> (King of the Womb of the Glory of Vairocana). After him, <s>Dharmanārāyaṇaketu</s> (Banner of the Nārāyaṇa of Dharma). After him, <s>Jñānaketu</s> (Banner of Knowledge). After him, <s>Dharmasāgarapadma</s> (Lotus of the Dharma-Ocean). Thus, son of good family, headed by these <s>Tathāgatas</s>, sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> arose in that world-realm

body.text: abhūvan, yānyasmābhirārāgitāni satkṛtāni gurukṛtāni mānitāni pūjitāni cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: — all of whom were pleased, honored, venerated, respected, and worshipped by us with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick as provisions. //

body.text: teṣāṃ khalu kulaputra ṣaṣṭerbuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ sarvapaścimo vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavatejo nāma tathāgata utpanno 'bhūt / tasya bhagavato nagare praviṣṭasya mayā rājabhāryābhūtayā sārdhaṃ svāminā sarvākārapūjāmukhaṃ prayuktayā tathāgatapūjayā pūjāṃ kṛtvā sarvatathāgatotpattisaṃbhavapradīpo nāma tathāgatadharmaparyāyastasya bhagavato 'ntikāt śrutaḥ, yasya sahaśravaṇānmayā jñānacakṣuḥ pratilabdham / eṣa ca sarvabodhisattvasamādhinayasāgaravyavalokanaviṣayo bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Of those sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, son of good family, the very last was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavateja</s> (Splendor of the Arising from the Resolute Faith in the Vast Dharma) who arose. When that <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered the city, I, having been a king's wife, together with my husband, with worship of all forms employed, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> with worship, heard from that <s>Bhagavān</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) called <s>Sarvatathāgatotpattisaṃbhavapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Arising and Manifestation of All Tathāgatas). Upon hearing it, I attained the eye of knowledge. And this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation, whose domain is the survey of the ocean of methods of <s>samādhi</s> of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, was attained. //

body.text: sā khalvahaṃ kulaputra etaṃ vimokṣaṃ bhāvayamānā buddhakṣetraśataparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpānāgatān bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇā / teṣu ca me buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu anantamadhyāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / kvacit kalpe kalpastho 'pi ekatathāgata ārāgitaḥ / kvacit kalpe dvau tathāgatāvārāgitau / kvacit kalpe yāvadanabhilāpyāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / kvacit kalpe buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / na ca me jātu bodhisattvasya kāyo jñātaḥ - kiṃpramāṇaḥ kīdṛksaṃsthānaḥ kīdṛgvarṇaḥ / na kāyakarma jñātaṃ na vākkarma na manaskarma jñātaṃ na jñānadarśanaṃ na jñānagocaraṃ na jñānasamādhiviṣayo jñātaḥ / ye khalu punaḥ kulaputra sattvā bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ carantaṃ dṛṣṭvā bodhisattvasyāntike 'nunayacittamutpādayāmāsuḥ, nānāsaṃketairnānāsaṃvāsaiśca prasādaṃ janayāmāsuḥ, sarve te bodhisattvena laukikalokottarairvividhairupāyaiḥ saṃgṛhītā bodhisattvasya parivārā bhavanti sma / te bodhisattvasya bodhisattvacaryāṃ carataḥ parivārasaṃvāse na avaivartikā bhavanti sma anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, while cultivating this liberation, have practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct together with the <s>bodhisattva</s> through future <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of a hundred <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And during those <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, boundless and middleway-less <s>Tathāgatas</s> have been pleased by me. In some <s>kalpas</s>, even one <s>Tathāgata</s> dwelling for the entire <s>kalpa</s> was pleased. In some <s>kalpas</s>, two <s>Tathāgatas</s> were pleased. In some <s>kalpas</s>, up to inexpressibly many <s>Tathāgatas</s> were pleased. In some <s>kalpas</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields were pleased. And yet I have never known the body of the <s>bodhisattva</s> — of what measure, of what configuration, of what color. I have not known his bodily action, nor his verbal action, nor his mental action, nor his knowledge-vision, nor his knowledge-domain, nor the domain of his knowledge-<s>samādhi</s>. But whatever beings, son of good family, having seen the <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-pilgrimage, generated a mind of affection toward the <s>bodhisattva</s> through various signs and various dwellings-together, and generated faith — all of them were gathered by the <s>bodhisattva</s> through various worldly and supramundane skillful means and became the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s retinue. And in the retinue-dwelling of the <s>bodhisattva</s> while he practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, they became irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: sāhaṃ kulaputra vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavatejastathāgatasya sahadarśanādimaṃ sarvabodhisattvasamādhisāgaravyavalokanaviṣayaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratilabhya bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ buddhakṣetraśataparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpānāgatā etaṃ vimokṣaṃ saṃbhāvayamānā / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu tathāgatā utpannāḥ, sarve te mayā tathāgatā ārāgitāḥ pūjitā upasthitāḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā śrutā, śrutvā udgṛhītā saṃdhāritā / sarveṣāṃ ca mayā teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantikādeṣa vimokṣaḥ pratilabdho nānānayairvā nānāsūtrāntanayanirghoṣairnānāvimokṣaśarīrairnānāvimokṣadvārairnānāvimokṣavicārairnānādhvajapraveśaiḥ nānābuddhakṣetrasāgarāvatāraiḥ nānābuddhadarśanasamudravijñaptibhiḥ nānātathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāvatāraiḥ nānābodhisattvapraṇidhānasāgaranayapathaiḥ nānābodhisattvacaryāprasaraiḥ nānābodhisattvacaryābhinirhāraiḥ nānābodhisattvaprasaraiḥ / na ca bodhisattvasya samantabhadravimokṣanayamavatarāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? ākāśatalapraveśāpramāṇā hi kulaputra samantabhadrāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vimokṣanayāḥ sarvasattvasaṃjñāgatatalāpramāṇāḥ tryadhvaparivartasāgaratalāpramāṇā
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, upon first seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavateja</s>, attained this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation whose domain is the contemplation of the ocean of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>s, and together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, I have come through <s>kalpa</s>s equal in number to the atoms of a hundred <s>Buddha</s>-fields, cultivating this liberation. And whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s arose in those <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s were honored, worshipped, and attended by me. And the <s>Dharma</s>-teachings of all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s were heard by me, and having heard them, I grasped and retained them. And from all those Blessed <s>Buddha</s>s, this liberation was attained by me through various methods, through various sounds of approaches to <s>sūtrānta</s>s, through various bodies of liberation, through various doors of liberation, through various deliberations on liberation, through various entries into banner-ways, through various descents into oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, through various perceptions of seeing oceans of <s>Buddha</s>s, through various entries into the assembly-circles of <s>Tathāgata</s>s, through various paths of methods of oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s> vows, through various extents of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, through various accomplishments of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, through various extents of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. Yet I do not penetrate the method of <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s liberation. For what reason? Because, son of good family, the methods of liberation of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>s are as immeasurable as entry into the expanse of space, as immeasurable as the expanse of all designations of beings,

body.text: diksamudratalāpramāṇā dharmadhātunayasāgaratalāpramāṇāḥ / tathāgataviṣayasamaśarīrā hi kulaputra samantabhadrāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vimokṣanayāḥ //
body.translated_text: as immeasurable as the expanse of the ocean of the revolutions of the three times, as immeasurable as the expanse of the oceans of directions, as immeasurable as the expanse of the ocean of methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. For, son of good family, the methods of liberation of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>s have a body equal to the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: sā ahaṃ kulaputra buddhakṣetraparmāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān bodhisattvaśarīraṃ prekṣamāṇā atṛptaiva darśanena / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra ekāntarāgacaritayoḥ strīpuruṣayoranyonyasamāgame saṃketakṛtayorapramāṇā ayoniśomanasikāraprabhavāḥ śubhasaṃjñāvitarkasaṃmohasaṃbhavāścittotpādā utpadyante, evameva kulaputra mama bodhisattvasya śarīraṃ prekṣamāṇāyā ekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyāpramāṇanirdeśā lokadhātuvaṃśaprasarā nānāpratiṣṭhānā nānāsaṃdhivyūhā nānāsaṃsthānā nānāparvatavyūhā nānāpṛthivītalavyūhanirdeśā nānāgaganameghasaṃchannālaṃkārā nānākalpanāmasaṃkhyānirdeśā nānābuddhotpādatathāgatavaṃśaprabhavā nānābodhimaṇḍālaṃkārā nānātathāgatadharmacakrapravartanavikurvitā nānātathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhā nānāsūtrāntanayanirdeśanirghoṣā nānāyānanayanirhāraprabhavā nānāpariśuddhaprabhālokāvabhāsā adṛṣṭapūrvanimittāḥ praticittakṣaṇaṃ cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / ekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyā buddhasamudrāścakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / nānābodhimaṇḍālaṃkārā nānādharmacakrapravartanavikurvitā nānāsūtrāntanirghoṣavikurvitāḥ apratisrabdhayogena praticittakṣaṇaṃ cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / ekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyāḥ sattvasamudrā nānābhavanārāmaparvatavimānanadīsamudranilayā nānārūpakāyā nānāparibhogaviṣayā nānācārayogacāraprayogā nānendriyapariniṣpattisaṃsthānāḥ praticittakṣaṇaṃ cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / ekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyāstryadhvasāgarapraveśanayā avabhāsamāgacchanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvapraṇidhānasamudrā viśudhyante / anantamadhyā bodhisattvabhūmicaryāvimātratāsamudrā ābhāsamāgacchanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvapāramitānayasāgarapariśuddhayo 'vabhāsamāgacchanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvapūrvayogasamudrā ābhāsamāgacchanti / anantamadhyā buddhakṣetrapariśodhananayasamudrā ābhāsamāgacchanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvamahāmaitrīnayasamudrāḥ sarvasattvamahāmaitrīnayasamudrāḥ sarvasattvaparipākavinayaparākramaprayogasāgarā avakrāmanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvamahākaruṇāmeghanayasāgarāḥ saṃbhavanti / anantamadhyā bodhisattvamahāprītivegasāgarā vivardhante / praticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyāḥ sarvasattvasaṃgrahaprayogasāgarā niṣpadyante //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, throughout <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, gazing upon the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, remain unsatiated even by that sight. Just as, for example,

body.text: sā ahaṃ kulaputra teṣu buddhakṣetraśataparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu bodhisattvasya ekaikasmādromavivarātpraticittakṣaṇamanantamadhyān dharmanayasāgarānavataramāṇā paryantaṃ nādhigacchāmi / na ca avatīrṇapūrvamavatarāmi / na pratilabdhapūrvaṃ pratilabhe yāvadantaḥpuramadhyagatasyāpyahaṃ kulaputra sarvārthasiddhasya strīgaṇaparivṛtasya nānāvimokṣanayasāgarāvatāraiḥ / ekaikasmādromavivarādanantamadhyāṃstryadhvanayasāgarānavatārāmi dharmadhātvavatāranayasamudrāvatāreṇa //
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, in those <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of a hundred <s>Buddha</s>-fields, from each single pore of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, at every moment of thought, see <s>Tathāgata</s>s arising with their various miraculous displays, assemblies, and <s>Dharma</s>-teachings — and those too I am unable to fully fathom.
