body.text: etamahaṃ kulaputra sarvabodhisattvasamādhisāgaravyavalokanaviṣayaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi, samāpadye / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmanantamadhyopāyanayasāgaraprasṛtānāṃ sarvasattvasamasadṛśasaṃsthānasaṃsthitakāyavijñaptisaṃdarśakānāṃ sarvajagadāśayānukūlacaryāsaṃdarśakānām
body.translated_text: I, son of good family, know and enter into this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation whose domain is the contemplation of the ocean of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>s. But how could I know or describe

body.text: anantamadhyavarṇanirmitameghasamudrasarvaromamukhapramuñcakānāṃ sarvaśarīradharmatāsvabhāvaprakṛtipariśuddhānāmākāśalakṣaṇajagatprakṛtyavabodhanirvikalpānāṃ sarvatrānugatabuddhiviniścayatathāgatasamavikurvitaparamāṇām anantamadhyavimokṣaviṣayavikurvitaniryātānāṃ vipuladharmadhātucittotpādapraveśavihāravaśavartināṃ samantamukhasarvadharmabhūmivimokṣasāgaravikrīḍitānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum, nikhilān vā guṇanidhīn saṃdarśayitum //
body.translated_text: the practice of those whose bodies are utterly pure by the inherent nature of the <s>dharmatā</s> of all bodies, who release from every hair-opening oceans of limitless, boundless emanation-clouds of manifold hues, who are as immeasurable as the expanse of space?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ihaiva bhagavato vairocanasya pādamūle vividharatnavyūhamahāmaṇirājapadmagarbhāsananiṣaṇṇā bodhisattvajanetrī māyā nāma devī / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvā bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranto 'nupaliptā bhavanti sarvalokadharmamalaiḥ / apratiprasrabdhā bhavanti tathāgatapūjāprayogeṣu / avaivartikā bhavanti sarvabodhisattvakarmāntebhyaḥ / sarvāvaraṇavigatā bhavanti bodhisattvavimokṣāvatāreṣu / aparapratyayā bhavanti sarvabodhisattvavihāreṣu / saṃmukhībhāvagatā bhavanti sarvatathāgatānām / na vivartante sarvasattvasaṃgrahaprayogebhyaḥ, na nivartante 'parāntakoṭīgatakalpasarvabodhisattvacaryāsaṃvāsebhyaḥ / na pratyudāvartante mahāyānapraṇidhānāt / na saṃsīdanti jagatkuśalamūlasaṃdhāraṇavivardhanatayā //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here at the feet of Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> sits upon a seat of a great <s>maṇi</s>-king lotus of arrays of various jewels —

body.text: atha khalu gopā śākyakanyā etameva vimokṣamukhanayaṃ saṃdarśayantī buddhādhiṣṭhānena tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, displaying this very gate of the method of liberation, by the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, at that time spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Those beings who see the supreme being engaged in the practice of the conduct of <s>saṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening),

children.text: prasannacittāḥ pratighātino vā vrajanti te saṃgrahamasya sarve // 90 //
children.translated_text: whether with minds of faith or of hostility — they all come under his gathering. // 90 //

children.text: yāvanti hi kṣetraśate rajāṃsi smarāmi kalpāniha tāvato 'ham /
children.translated_text: However many atoms there are in hundreds of fields, I remember that many <s>kalpa</s>s here;
the world-realm was <s>Meruprabhā</s>, supreme among worlds, and beyond that, in a <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Vyūha</s>. // 91 //
In that <s>kalpa</s>, twenty-six <s>koṭī-ayuta</s>-thousands of Sages arose;
the last among them was the lord of Sages named <s>Dharmadhvaja</s>, a lamp of the world. // 92 //
At that time there was a king named <s>Śrīteja</s>; when that lord of Sages had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
in this <s>Jambudhvaja</s>, having vanquished enemy forces, he became the supreme lord with unimpeded authority. // 93 //

children.text: śūrāṇi vīrāṇyatha rūpavanti pañcābhavan putraśatāni tasya /
children.translated_text: He had five hundred sons, heroic, valiant, and handsome,
with bodies complete in all limbs and purified, adorned with unsurpassed splendor. // 94 //

children.text: rājā saputraḥ sugate prasannaḥ pūjāmakārṣīdvipulāṃ jinasya /
children.translated_text: The king, together with his sons, having faith in the <s>Sugata</s>, made vast offerings to the <s>Jina</s>,
and he always upheld the true <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, unshakable. // 95 //
That king had a prince named <s>Suraśmi</s>, of purified nature,
beautiful to behold, of pleasing form, with limbs adorned by the thirty excellent marks. // 96 //

children.text: rājyaṃ parityajya nṛṇāṃ sa pañcakoṭīvṛtaḥ pravrajitastadānīm /
children.translated_text: Renouncing the kingdom of men, he went forth at that time, accompanied by five <s>koṭī</s>s of followers;

children.text: sa pravrajitvā dṛḍhavīryayuktaḥ saṃdhārayāmāsa jinasya dharmam // 97 //
children.translated_text: having gone forth, endowed with firm vigor, he upheld the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s>. // 97 //
There was a city called <s>Drumāvatī</s>, surrounded by thousands of <s>koṭī</s>s of excellent cities;
there was a grove with variegated branches, of tranquil sounds and unsurpassed splendor. // 98 //
There <s>Suraśmi</s> dwelt, confident, purified in wisdom and eloquence;
he illuminated the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s> for the purification of the multitude of afflicted beings. // 99 //

children.text: piṇḍāya dhīmān sa puraṃ viveśa prāsādikeryāpathaśāntaveṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one entered the city for alms, with graceful deportment and tranquil appearance,
with eyes not cast upward, mindful, clearly comprehending, of profound conduct, steady and deliberate in gait. // 100 //
There was an eminent householder named <s>Nandīdhvaja</s>, foremost among citizens at that time, of widely proclaimed fame;

children.text: tasyāhamāsaṃ duhitā manāpā bhānuprabhā nāma sucārurūpā // 101 //
children.translated_text: I was his beloved daughter, named <s>Bhānuprabhā</s>, of very beautiful form. // 101 //
At the door of the northern mansion, <s>Suraśmi</s> with his retinue was seen by me;
his form was graceful, with limbs adorned by the marks — there arose in me a very great faith. // 102 //

children.text: yadā gṛhadvāragato mamābhūt pātre pradatto 'sya maṇistadā me /
children.translated_text: When he arrived at the door of my house, I placed a jewel in his bowl;
and having removed all my ornaments, led by a mind of loving-kindness, I gave them to him. // 103 //
Having made an offering with a passionate mind to <s>Suraśmiketu</s>, the son of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: ardhatṛtīyāni śatāni nāgāṃ kalpottamāyāṃ khalu jātvapāyān // 104 //
children.translated_text: for two and a half hundred <s>kalpa</s>s in supreme <s>kalpa</s>s, I was never born in lower realms. // 104 //

children.text: deveṣu devendrakuleṣu jātā narendraputrī manujeṣu cāham /
children.translated_text: I was born among <s>Deva</s>s, in the families of lords of <s>Deva</s>s, and among humans as the daughter of a king;
with infinite beauty and stature, everywhere my very sight became a gift. // 105 //
When two and a half hundred <s>kalpa</s>s had passed, I was born as the daughter
of a renowned courtesan named <s>Sudarśanā</s>, among fearless ones, and was called <s>Saṃcālitā</s> at that time. // 106 //
Then, having seen Prince <s>Tejādhipati</s>, I made offerings to him with joy;

children.text: ātmānamasyaiva nivedayitvā bhūtāsmi vaśyā khalu tasya bhāryā // 107 //
children.translated_text: having offered myself to him, I became his obedient wife. // 107 //

children.text: saṃpūjitastena mayā sahābhūt sa sūryagātrapravaro maharṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: Together with me who worshipped him, he was <s>Sūryagātra</s>, the supreme great sage;

children.text: prasannayā caiva tamīkṣya buddhamutpāditaṃ me varabodhicittam // 108 //
children.translated_text: and having beheld that <s>Buddha</s> with faith, the excellent <s>bodhicitta</s> (aspiration for awakening) was generated in me. // 108 //

body.text: pūrṇā jinānāṃ khalu ṣaṣṭikoṭyastatraiva kalpe susamutthitānām /
body.translated_text: Full sixty <s>koṭī</s>s of <s>Jina</s>s arose in that very <s>kalpa</s>;

body.text: babhūva teṣāṃ caramo jinānāṃ buddhastadānīmadhimuktitejāḥ // 109 //
body.translated_text: The last of those <s>Jinas</s> was the <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Adhimuktitejas</s> (Splendor of Resolute Faith) at that time. // 109 //

children.translated_text: Under him, my <s>dharma</s>-eye was purified, and the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> was awakened by me.
Improper and extreme conceptual elaboration was pacified; having attained illumination, I became [free from] existence from that time forth. // 110 //
From that time onward, I behold the ground of <s>samādhi</s> of the sons born from the breast of the <s>Jina</s>,
and in a single mind-moment, I point out in all directions the oceans of fields that transcend thought. // 111 //
I see in all directions variously purified fields, infinite and wonderful;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā manasteṣu na sajjate me kliṣṭeṣu naiva pratihanyate ca // 112 //
children.translated_text: having seen them, my mind does not cling to them, nor does it falter even in those that are defiled. // 112 //

children.text: kṣetreṣu teṣveva ca bodhimaṇḍe paśyāmi buddhān nikhileṣvaśeṣān /
children.translated_text: In those very fields, at the seats of awakening, I see all the <s>Buddhas</s> without exception,
and their infinite oceans of radiance I behold with a single mind. // 113 //
Likewise, in a single mind-moment I descend into their oceans of assemblies, unattached,
and I know all their <s>samādhis</s> completely, and all their immeasurable liberations. // 114 //

children.text: caryāṃ ca teṣāṃ vipulāṃ dharemi bhūmīnayāṃścāvatarāmyaśeṣān /
children.translated_text: I bear their vast conduct, and I descend into all the methods of the stages;
and at every moment I descend into innumerable great oceans of vows, infinite [in number]. // 115 //

children.text: saṃprekṣatī satpuruṣasya kāyaṃ kalpānanantāṃścaratī ca caryām /
children.translated_text: Gazing upon the body of the noble being, I practice the conduct for infinite <s>kalpas</s>;
of the magical displays from each single hair-pore of his, I never reach the end. // 116 //
In a single hair-pore, I behold oceans of fields beyond counting,
with great floods of wind-aggregates and skandha-fires, and earth-bodies filled with flame. // 117 //
Of various forms with different foundations and conceptual appearances, with entries into the methods of variegated configurations,
various in their divisions of elements and bodies, with forms of infinite and middleless [extent]. // 118 //
In immeasurable, inexhaustible oceans of fields, I behold the separate elements individually,

children.text: dharmābhidhānairjanatāṃ vinītāṃ teṣveva paśyāmi jinān prayuktān // 119 //
children.translated_text: and in those very [fields] I see <s>Jinas</s> engaged in disciplining beings through the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>. // 119 //

children.text: na kāyakarmāsya mayāvabuddhaṃ na vāgna cittaṃ na tayośca karma /
children.translated_text: His bodily activity has not been comprehended by me, nor his verbal, nor his mental, nor the activity of those two [combined];

children.text: ṛddhirna naivāsya pṛthagvikurvā kalpāṃścarantyā vipulāṃ sucaryām // 120 //
children.translated_text: neither his supernatural power, nor his individual magical displays — though I practice the vast, excellent conduct for [countless] <s>kalpas</s>. // 120 //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya gopāṃ śākyakanyāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyā antikāt prakrāntaḥ // 41 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of <s>Gopā</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, circumambulated <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden. // 41 //

body.text: 44 Māyā /
body.translated_text: 44. <s>Māyā</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya māyāyā devyāḥ sakāśaṃ gamanābhimukhasya buddhagocaravicārajñānapratipannasya etadabhavat - kenopāyena mayā śakyaṃ sarvalokoccalitaṣaḍāyatanānāmapratiṣṭhitānāṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ sarvasaṅgasamatikrāntakāyānāmasaṅgagatigāminīpratipadāpratipannānāṃ dharmakāyasuviśuddhānāṃ kāyakarmamāyāsunirmitaśarīrāṇāṃ jñānamāyāgatalokavicārāṇāṃ praṇidhirūpakāyānāṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānamanomayaśarīrāṇāmanutpannāniruddhakāyānāmasatyāmṛṣakāyānāmasaṃkrāntavinaṣṭakāyānāmasaṃbhavāvibhavakāyānām alakṣaṇaikalakṣaṇakāyānām / advayasaṃṅgavinirmuktakāyānām, anālayanilayakāyānām, anakṣatakāyānāṃ pratibhāsasamanirvikalpakāyānāṃ svapnasamavicārakāyānām, ādarśamaṇḍalasamasadṛśākrāntakāyānāṃ diksamapraśāntapratiṣṭhakāyānāṃ sarvadikspharaṇanirmāṇakāyānāṃ tryadhvāsaṃbhinnakāyānāmaśarīracittanirvikalpakāyānāṃ sarvalokacakṣuṣpathasamatikrāntakāyānāṃ samantabhadracakṣuḥprasaravijñeyavinayakāyānām asaṅgagaganagocarāṇāṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ darśanamārāgayituṃ saṃmukhībhāvatāmanuprāptuṃ samavadhānaṃ cāptuṃ nimittaṃ codgrahītuṃ ghoṣamaṇḍalaṃ vā vijñātuṃ mantravyavacārān vā ājñātumanuśāsanīṃ codgrahītum //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, proceeding toward the presence of Queen <s>Māyā</s>, having entered the knowledge that investigates the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, thought thus: 'By what means might I be able to see, to come face to face with, to meet, to grasp the mark, to know the sound-maṇḍala, to learn the <s>mantra</s>-practices, and to receive the instruction of spiritual friends — those whose six sense-bases have risen above all worldly [attachments], who are without fixed abode, whose bodies have transcended all attachment, who have entered the path of conduct leading to the unattached state, whose <s>dharmakāya</s> is well-purified, whose bodily activity is a body magically created like an illusion, who investigate the world through the <s>māyā</s> of knowledge, whose visible bodies are [manifestations of] their vows, whose mind-made bodies are empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, whose bodies are unborn and unceasing, whose bodies are neither true nor false, whose bodies are neither transferring nor perishing, whose bodies are neither arising nor ceasing to exist, whose bodies are of a single mark that is without marks, whose bodies are freed from the bondage of duality, whose bodies dwell in non-dwelling, whose bodies are indestructible, whose bodies are without conceptual elaboration like reflections, whose bodies investigate like dreams, whose bodies enter like mirror-surfaces, whose bodies are established in peace like the directions, whose emanation-bodies pervade all directions, whose bodies are undivided across the three times, whose bodies are without conceptual elaboration regarding body or mind, whose bodies have transcended the path of the eyes of all the world, whose bodies for disciplining [beings] are knowable through the range of the eye of <s>Samantabhadra</s> — spiritual friends of unattached, sky-like domain?' //

body.text: tamevaṃ cintāmanasikāraprayuktaṃ ratnanetrā nāma nagaradevatā gaganadevatāgaṇaparivṛtā gaganatalagatamātmānamupadarśya nānāvibhūṣaṇavibhūṣitaśarīrā anekākāravarṇadivyakusumapuṭaparigṛhītā saṃmukhamabhyavakīramāṇā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - cittanagaraparipālanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvasaṃsāraviṣayaratyasaṃvasanatayā / cittanagarālaṃkāraprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ daśatathāgatabalādhyānalambanatayā / cittanagarapariśodhanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyamīrṣyāmātsaryaśāṭhyāpanayanatayā / cittanagarasaṃtāpapraśamābhiyuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvadharmanidhyaptyā / cittanagaravivardhanābhiyuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvajñatāsaṃbhāramahāvīryavegavivardhanatayā / cittanagarabhavanakośavyūhārakṣāprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvasamādhisamāpattidhyānavimokṣavipuladharmavinayamānavihāravaśavartitayā / cittanagarāvabhāsaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasamudayasamantabhūmiprajñāpāramitāpratilambhapratīcchanatayā / cittanagaropastambhaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgatasaṃbhavopāyamārgasvacittanagarasamavasaraṇatayā / cittanagaradṛḍhaprākārābhinirhāraprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānābhinirhāracittaviśuddhaye / cittanagaraduryodhanadurāsadatābhinirhāraprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvakleśamārakāyikapāpamitramāracakrānavamṛdyatayā / cittanagarāvabhāsanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvasattvatathāgatajñānāvabhāsapratipadyamānatayā / cittanagarābhiniṣyandanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanatayā / cittanagaropastambhanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgatapuṇyasamudrasvacittāśayasaṃpratīcchanatayā / cittanagarapravistaraṇaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ mahāmaitrīsarvajagatpharaṇatayā / cittanagarasaṃpraticchādanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ vipuladharmacchatrasarvākuśaladharmapratipakṣābhinirharaṇatayā /
body.translated_text: To him, thus engaged in thought and mental attention, a city-deity named <s>Ratnanetrā</s> (Jewel-Eyed), surrounded by a host of sky-deities, appeared in her own form in the sky, with a body adorned with various ornaments, holding divine flower-pouches of manifold colors and forms, scattering them before <s>Sudhana</s>, and spoke to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> thus: 'You should, son of good family, be engaged in guarding the city of the mind, through not dwelling in the pleasures of all <s>saṃsāric</s> domains. You should be engaged in adorning the city of the mind, through relying on the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You should be engaged in purifying the city of the mind, through removing envy, miserliness, and deceit. You should be engaged in pacifying the burning of the city of the mind, through contemplating all <s>dharmas</s>. You should be engaged in expanding the city of the mind, through increasing the great force of vigor in accumulating the equipment for omniscience. You should be engaged in protecting the treasure-houses of the city of the mind, through mastery over all <s>samādhis</s>, attainments, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, vast <s>Dharma</s>-disciplines, and mental states. You should be engaged in illuminating the city of the mind, through receiving the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the universal-ground convergence of the assembly-maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. You should be engaged in supporting the city of the mind, through the convergence of the path of the method of the arising of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the city of one's own mind. You should be engaged in constructing firm ramparts for the city of the mind, for the purification of the mind through the accomplishment of the vow of the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. You should be engaged in making the city of the mind difficult to attack and unapproachable, through not being crushed by the hosts of all defilements, of <s>Māra</s>, of the bodily [<s>Māra</s>], and of evil-friend <s>Māra</s>. You should be engaged in illuminating the city of the mind, through approaching the illumination of all beings with the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You should be engaged in making the city of the mind overflow, through receiving the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. You should be engaged in supporting the city of the mind, through receiving the ocean of merit of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the disposition of one's own mind. You should be engaged in extending the city of the mind, through pervading all beings with great loving-kindness. You should be engaged in sheltering the city of the mind, through accomplishing the vast <s>Dharma</s>-parasol as the antidote to all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
cittanagarapratisyandanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ vipulamahākaruṇāsarvajagadanukampanatayā / cittanagaradvāravivaraṇaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyamādhyātmikavāhyavastusarvajagatsaṃprāpaṇatayā / cittanagaraviśodhanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvasaṃsāraviṣayaratiparāṅbhukhatayā / cittanagaradṛḍhasthāmābhinirhāraprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvākuśaladharmasvasaṃtatyasaṃbhavanatayā / cittanagaravīryaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvajñatāsaṃbhārasamārjanavīryābhinirvartanatayā
/ cittanagaraprabhāsanaprayuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatryadhvatathāgatamaṇḍalasmṛtyavabhāsanatayā / cittanagaravicayavidhijñena te kulaputra sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasūtrāntavividhadharmadvārapravicayaśrutābhijñatayā / cittanagaraniyāmavidhijñena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvajagadabhimukhasarvajñatādvāramārgavividhasaṃdarśanatayā / cittanagarādhiṣṭhānavidhijñena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatryadhvatathāgatapraṇidhānanirhāraviśuddhaye / cittanagarasaṃbhārabalavivardhanavidhijñena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvadharmadhātuvipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāravivardhanatayā / cittanagarasamantaprabhāsapramuñcanavidhijñena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvasattvacittāśayendriyādhimuktisaṃkleśavyavadānajñānābhijñatayā / cittanagaravaśavartanavidhijñena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvadharmadhātunayasamavasaraṇatayā / cittanagaraprabhāsvarābhiyuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgatasmṛtyavabhāsanatayā / cittanagarasvabhāvaparijñābhiyuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyamaśarīrasarvadharmanayapratividhyanatayā / cittanagaramāyopamapratyavekṣaṇābhiyuktena te kulaputra bhavitavyaṃ sarvajñatādharmanagaragamanatayā / evaṃ cittanagarapariśuddhyabhiyuktena te kulaputra bodhisattvena śakyaṃ sarvakuśalasamārjanamanuprāptum / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bodhisattvasya evaṃ cittanagarapariśuddhasya sarvāvaraṇāni purato na saṃtiṣṭhante buddhadarśanāvaraṇaṃ vā dharmaśravaṇāvaraṇaṃ vā tathāgatapūjopasthānāvaraṇaṃ vā sattvasaṃgrahaprayogāvaraṇaṃ vā buddhakṣetrapariśuddhyāvaraṇaṃ vā / sarvāvaraṇavigatena hi kulaputra cittādhyāśayena kalyāṇamitraparyeṣṭyabhiyuktasya bodhisattvasya alpakṛcchreṇa kalyāṇamitrāṇyābhāsamāgacchanti / kalyāṇamitrādhīnā ca kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajñatā //
body.translated_text: You should be engaged in making the city of the mind flow forth, through compassionating all beings with vast great compassion. You should be engaged in opening the gates of the city of the mind, through providing all beings with both inner and outer goods. You should be engaged in purifying the city of the mind, through turning away from delight in all <s>saṃsāric</s> domains. You should be engaged in producing firm strength in the city of the mind, through non-arising of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> in one's own continuum. You should be engaged in the vigor of the city of the mind, through producing the vigor of sweeping together the equipment for omniscience. You should be engaged in illuminating the city of the mind, through illuminating the memory of the maṇḍalas of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times. You should be skilled in the method of investigating the city of the mind, through knowledgeable expertise in the investigation of the various <s>Dharma</s>-gateways of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel <s>sūtrāntas</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. You should be skilled in the method of the definite course of the city of the mind, through variously demonstrating to all beings the path of the gateway to omniscience. You should be skilled in the method of empowering the city of the mind, for the purification of the accomplishment of the vows of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times. You should be skilled in the method of increasing the power of the provisions of the city of the mind, through increasing the vast provisions of merit and knowledge throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. You should be skilled in the method of releasing universal radiance from the city of the mind, through knowledgeable expertise in the mental dispositions, faculties, resolute faiths, defilements, and purifications of all beings. You should be skilled in the method of mastering the city of the mind, through convergence with the methods of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. You should be engaged in the luminosity of the city of the mind, through illuminating the memory of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. You should be engaged in the thorough knowledge of the intrinsic nature of the city of the mind, through penetrating the method of all <s>dharmas</s> which are without body. You should be engaged in contemplating the city of the mind as illusion-like, through going to the city of the <s>Dharma</s> of omniscience. Thus, son of good family, by a <s>bodhisattva</s> engaged in the purification of the city of the mind, it is possible to attain the sweeping together of all that is wholesome. For what reason? Because for the <s>bodhisattva</s> whose city of the mind is thus purified, no obstructions stand before him — neither the obstruction to seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, nor the obstruction to hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, nor the obstruction to worshipping and attending the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor the obstruction to the practice of gathering beings, nor the obstruction to the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field. For, son of good family, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> whose mental disposition is free from all obstructions and who is engaged in seeking spiritual friends, spiritual friends come into view with little difficulty. And omniscience, son of good family, is dependent on spiritual friends for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: tatra dharmapadmaśrīkuśalā śarīrakāyikadevatā hrīśrīmañjariprabhāvā aparimāṇadevatāgaṇaparivṛtā māyāyā devyā varṇamudīrayamāṇā bodhimaṇḍānniṣkramya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasyābhimukhaṃ gaganatale sthitvā svakasvakebhyo 'nekaratnavarṇāni raśmijālāni anekagandhadhūpavimalārcirvarṇāni cittāśayaprasādanavarṇāni cittaprītivegavivardhanavarṇāni kāyaparidāhaprahlādanavarṇāni kāyapariśuddhisaṃdarśanavarṇāni asaṅgakāyavikramasaṃbhavaviṣayāṇi raśmijālāni prāmuñcat / tāni vipulāni kṣetrāṇyavabhāsya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya sarvatrānugataṃ samantābhimukhaṃ sarvatathāgatakāyaṃ saṃdarśayitvā sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhasaṃdhau nipatanti sma / tāni mūrdhānamupādāya sarvaromakūpeṣvanupraviśya anuprasaranti sma / samanantaraspṛṣṭaśca sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastābhirdevatāraśmibhiḥ, atha tāvadeva virajaḥprabhāsaṃ nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yat sarvatamondhakāreṇa sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati / vitimiraṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena sattvasvabhāvamavatarati /
body.translated_text: There, the body-deity <s>Dharmapadmaśrīkuśalā</s>, of the power of <s>Hrīśrīmañjariprabhā</s>, surrounded by an immeasurable host of deities, praising Queen <s>Māyā</s>, emerging from the seat of awakening and standing in the sky face to face with the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, released from their respective [bodies] nets of rays of many jewel-colors, nets of rays of variegated colors of stainless flames of incense and fragrance, colors that purify the disposition of the mind, colors that increase the force of mental joy, colors that refresh the burning of the body, colors that demonstrate the purification of the body, [rays] whose domain produces the arising of the prowess of the unattached body. Those [rays], having illuminated vast fields, having shown to the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> the body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> that follows everywhere and faces all directions, having circumambulated the entire world, fell upon the crown of the head of the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>. Having fallen upon the crown, they entered and pervaded all the hair-pores. And the moment the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> was touched by those deity-rays, he immediately attained the eye called '<s>Virajaḥprabhāsa</s>' (Stainless Radiance Illumination), which does not coexist with any darkness or gloom. And he attained the eye called '<s>Vitimira</s>' (Free from Obscurity), by which one penetrates the intrinsic nature of beings.

body.text:
virajaḥpatiṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena ca sarvadharmasvabhāvamaṇḍalaṃ vyavalokayati / viśuddhagatiṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena sarvakṣetraprakṛtiṃ vyavalokayati / vairocanaprabhaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena tathāgatadharmaśarīraṃ vyavalokayati / viśuddhagatiṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yenācintyāṃ tathāgatarūpakāyapariniṣpattiṃ vyavalokayati / samantaprabhaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yenācintyāṃ tathāgatarūpakāyapariniṣpattibhaktiṃ vyavalokayati / asaṅgaprabhaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena sarvakṣetrasāgaraprasaralokadhātusaṃbhavavibhaktiṃ vyavalokayati / samantāvabhāsaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena sarvatathāgatadharmeṣu sūtrāntanayanirhāradiśaṃ vyavalokayati / samantaviṣayaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yenānantamadhyabuddhavikurvitasattvavinayādhiṣṭhānaṃ vyavalokayati / samantadarśaṃ ca nāma cakṣuḥ pratilebhe, yena sarvakṣetrasamutpattiprasṛtaṃ
buddhotpādaṃ vyavalokayati //
body.translated_text: He attained the eye called <s>Virajaḥpati</s> (Lord of the Dustless), by which he perceives the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s. He attained the eye called <s>Viśuddhagati</s> (Pure Course), by which he perceives the nature of all fields. He attained the eye called <s>Vairocanaprabha</s> (Radiance of Vairocana), by which he perceives the <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He attained the eye called <s>Viśuddhagati</s> (Pure Course), by which he perceives the inconceivable perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s> (form-body). He attained the eye called <s>Samantaprabha</s> (Universal Radiance), by which he perceives the inconceivable manifestation of the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s>. He attained the eye called <s>Asaṅgaprabha</s> (Unobstructed Radiance), by which he perceives the differentiation of the arising of world-realms spread across the ocean of all fields. He attained the eye called <s>Samantāvabhāsa</s> (Universal Illumination), by which he perceives the direction of the exposition of the <s>sūtrānta</s>-method in all <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. He attained the eye called <s>Samantaviṣaya</s> (Universal Domain), by which he perceives the empowerment for the discipline of beings through the magical transformations of <s>Buddha</s>s without beginning or end. He attained the eye called <s>Samantadarśa</s> (Universal Vision), by which he perceives the arising of <s>Buddha</s>s extending throughout the origination of all fields.

body.text:
atha khalu sunetro nāma rākṣasendro bodhisattvasaṃgītiprāsādadvārapālo daśānāṃ rākṣasasahasrāṇāṃ pramukhaḥ sabhāryaḥ saputraḥ sasvajanaparivāraḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakaṃ nānāvarṇamanojñagandhaiḥ kusumairabhyavakīrya evamāha - daśabhiḥ kulaputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattva āsanno bhavati sarvakalyāṇamitrāṇām / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta māyāśāṭhyāpagatena supariśuddhenāśayena, sarvajagatparigrahāsaṃbhinnayā mahākaruṇayā, sarvasattvaniḥsattvasvabhāvanidhyaptyā pratyavekṣayā, sarvajñatāgamanāvaivartyenādhyāśayabalena, tathāgatamaṇḍalābhimukhenādhimuktibalena, sarvadharmasvabhāvavimalaviśuddhena cakṣuṣā, sarvasattvamaṇḍalāsaṃbhinnayā mahāmaitryā, sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇena jñānālokena, sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhapratipakṣacchatrabhūtena mahādharmameghena, sarvadharmadhātuśrotrasamantaprasṛtena kalyāṇamitragamanābhimukhena jñānacakṣuṣā / ebhiḥ kulaputra daśabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattva āsanno bhavati sarvakalyāṇamitrāṇām / daśabhiśca samādhinidhyaptimukhairvyavalokayan bodhisattvaḥ saṃmukhībhāvaṃ pratilabhate sarvakalyāṇamitrāṇām / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta dharmagaganavirajovicāramaṇḍalena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvadiksamudrābhimukhacakṣuṣā ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvārambaṇāvikalpāvicāreṇa ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvadiktathāgatameghasaṃbhavena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvajñajñānapuṇyasamudropacayagarbheṇa ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvacittotpādāvirahitakalyāṇamitrasaṃbhavāsannena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvatathāgataguṇakalyāṇamitrasukhasaṃbhavena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvakalyāṇamitrātyantāvipravāsena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvakalyāṇamitrasamatāsadāsamantopasaṃkramaṇaprayogena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena, sarvakalyāṇamitropāyacariteṣvaklāntaprayogena ca samādhinidhyaptimukhena / ebhiḥ kulaputra daśabhiḥ samādhinidhyaptimukhaiḥ
samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ saṃmukhībhāvaṃ pratilabhate sarvakalyāṇamitrāṇām / sarvatathāgatadharmacakrakalyāṇamitramukhanirghoṣaṃ ca nāma samādhivimokṣaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>rākṣasa</s>-lord named <s>Sunetra</s>, the gatekeeper of the palace of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly, foremost among ten thousand <s>rākṣasa</s>s, together with his wife, son, and retinue of kinsmen, having showered the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> with flowers of various colors and delightful fragrances, spoke thus: "Son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with ten <s>dharma</s>s becomes close to all spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s). Which ten? Namely: with a perfectly pure intention free from deceit and fraud; with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) that embraces all beings without division; with discernment that examines the selfless own-nature of all beings; with the power of an aspiration that is irreversible in attaining omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>); with the power of faith directed toward the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s; with an eye that is stainlessly pure regarding the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s; with great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) that is undivided toward the assembly of all beings; with the light of knowledge that scatters all obstructions; with the great cloud of <s>Dharma</s> that serves as an antidote to the suffering of all <s>saṃsāra</s>; and with the wisdom-eye that extends everywhere through the ear of the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) and is directed toward approaching spiritual friends. Son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with these ten <s>dharma</s>s becomes close to all spiritual friends. And by observing through ten gateways of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> comes face to face with all spiritual friends. Which ten? Namely: through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is the <s>maṇḍala</s> of investigation free from defilement in the sky of <s>Dharma</s>; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is the eye facing the ocean of all directions; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is free from conceptual discrimination regarding all objects; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is the arising of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-cloud in all directions; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is the womb of the accumulation of the ocean of merit and omniscient knowledge; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is close to the arising of spiritual friends without ever lacking the generation of mind; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment that is the arising of the happiness of spiritual friends endowed with the qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment of ultimate inseparability from all spiritual friends; through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment of the practice of constantly and universally approaching all spiritual friends with equanimity; and through the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment of unwearying practice in the skillful conduct of all spiritual friends. Son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with these ten gateways of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment comes face to face with all spiritual friends. And he attains the <s>samādhi</s>-liberation called <s>Sarvatathāgatadharmacakrakalyāṇamitramukhanirghoṣa</s> (Sound Issuing from the Mouths of Spiritual Friends Who Are the Dharma-Wheel of All Tathāgatas),

body.text: pratilabhate, yatra pratipadyamāno bodhisattvo 'saṃbhinnāṃ sarvabuddhasamatāmavatarati, asaṃbhinnāni ca sarvatrānugatāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi pratilabhate //
body.translated_text: which, upon entering, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters into the undivided equality of all <s>Buddha</s>s, and attains spiritual friends who follow everywhere without division.

body.text: evamukte sunetreṇa rākṣasendreṇa sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako gaganatalamavalokya evamāha - sādhu sādhu ārya, anukampako 'smākamanugrahapravṛttaḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ darśayitā / tatsādhvamasmākaṃ samyagupāyamukhamupadiśan kathaṃ parikramāti? katamāṃ diśamabhimukhaṃ nirjavāmi? kasminnadhiṣṭhāne parimārgayāmi? katamadārambaṇamupanidhyāyāmi kalyāṇamitradarśanāya? āha - tena hi kulaputra samantadikpraṇipatitena śarīreṇa sarvārambaṇena kalyāṇamitrasmṛtyupanibaddhenāśayena samantanirjavena samādhyanugamena svapnopamena cittajavena pratibhāsopamena manaḥśarīravicāragamanena kalyāṇamitrasakāśamupasaṃkramitavyam //
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, gazing up at the sky, spoke thus to the <s>rākṣasa</s>-lord <s>Sunetra</s>: "Excellent, excellent, noble one! You are compassionate, engaged in benefiting us, one who shows us spiritual friends. Then please teach us properly the gateway of skillful means: how should I proceed? In which direction should I set forth? In which place should I search? What object should I contemplate for the vision of spiritual friends?" He replied: "Then, son of good family, with a body prostrated in all directions, with an intention bound to the recollection of spiritual friends regarding all objects, with a <s>samādhi</s>-practice of setting forth in all directions, with the swiftness of mind like a dream, with the movement of the mental body like a reflection, you should approach the spiritual friend."

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yathānuśiṣṭaḥ sunetreṇa rākṣasendreṇa pratipadyamāno 'drākṣītpurato dharaṇitalānmahāratnapadmasamudgataṃ sarvavajraśarīradaṇḍaṃ sarvajagatsāgaramaṇirājagarbhaṃ sarvamaṇirājapatrapaṅktivairocanamaṇirājakarkaṭikāṃ sarvaratnavarṇagandhamaṇirājakesaramasaṃkhyeyaratnajālasaṃchāditam / tasyāṃ ca mahāratnarājapadmakarkaṭikāyāṃ dharmadhātudiksamavasaraṇagarbhaṃ nāma kūṭāgāramapaśyaccitraṃ darśanīyaṃ vajravairocanadharaṇitalasaṃsthānaṃ sarvamaṇirājamayaparipūrṇastambhasahasropaśobhitaṃ sarvaratnasaṃghaṭṭitāyāmaṃ jāmbūnadavimalakanakadivyavinyastapaṭṭamasaṃkhyeyanānāmuktāhārajālopanibaddhaṃ maṇiratnarājavicitrabhaktivinyāsaṃ jambūdhvajamaṇiratnasamantavyūhamasaṃkhyeyaratnavedikāparivṛtaṃ samantadigmaṇirājasopānasuvibhaktam / tasya kūṭāgārasya madhye cintārājamaṇiratnapadmagarbhamāsanamadrākṣīt sarvalokendrasaṃsthānamaṇivigrahabimbapratiṣṭhitaṃ sarvamaṇiratnavigrahavarṇamindradhvajapradyotasaṃsthānaṃ vajramaṇicakrabhūmitalapratiṣṭhitaṃ nānāmaṇirājapaṅktivyūhamanekaratnavedikāparivṛtaṃ jyotirdhvajamaṇirājasupratyarpitaṃ nānāratnavyūhopaśobhitaṃ divyātikrāntamaṇirājavastrasuprajñaptamanekavarṇavicitravastraratnasusaṃskṛtaṃ sarvaratnavastravitānavitatagaganālaṃkāraṃ sarvaratnajālasaṃchāditaṃ samantadiksuvibhaktavajradhvajanirghoṣaṃ sarvaratnapaṭṭadhvajasusamīritavidyotitaṃ sarvagandhamaṇirājadhvajavinyastasamatālaṃkāraṃ sarvapuṣpadhūpavicitrakusumaughasaṃpravarṣaṇaṃ sarvaratnakiṅkiṇīdhvajasusamīritaśravaṇamanaḥsukhamadhuranirghoṣaṃ nānāratnabhavanamukhadvāraprayuktaṃ nānāratnamaṇivigrahamukhānekavarṇagandhodakapravṛddhavairocanamaṇirājavigrahagajendramukhapadmajālaprayuktaṃ nānāvajrasiṃhamukhānantavarṇadhūpameghaprayuktaṃ brahmasaṃsthānavairocanamaṇirājamukhamahāmaitrīnayabrahmaghoṣanirnādapramuktaṃ nānāratnarajatamukhaśuklapakṣoddyotanamadhuranirnādarutavarṇaṃ tryadhvabuddhanāmakanakaghaṇṭāmālāmadhurarutapramuktanirghoṣaṃ sarvabuddhadharmacakramahāmaṇirājaghaṇṭāmālāmanojñarutaravaṇaṃ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhinānāvajraghaṇṭāniścaritanirghoṣaṃ candradhvajamaṇirājapaṅktisarvabuddhapratibhāsanicitanāmanirnādavijñapanaṃ śuddhagarbhamaṇirājapaṅkti sarvatryadhvatathāgatajanmaparaṃparāpratibhāsavijñapanamādityagarbhamaṇirājapaṅkti sarvavikurvitapratipattyākāśadhātuparamadaśadiksarvabuddhakṣetravidhipatharaśmisaṃdarśanam avabhāsadhvajamaṇirājapaṅkti
body.translated_text: Then the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, practicing as instructed by the <s>rākṣasa</s>-lord <s>Sunetra</s>, saw before him, rising from the surface of the earth, a great jewel-lotus bearing a staff made entirely of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), with a womb of <s>maṇi</s>-king jewels encompassing the ocean of all beings, with a row of petals of all <s>maṇi</s>-kings and a pistil of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-king, with stamens of all jewel-colored fragrant <s>maṇi</s>-kings, covered by an innumerable net of jewels. And upon the pistil of that great jewel-king lotus, he saw a pavilion called <s>Dharmadhātudiksamavasaraṇagarbha</s> (Womb of the Descent from the Directions of the Dharma-Realm) — wondrous and beautiful to behold, standing upon a ground of <s>vajra</s>-<s>Vairocana</s>, adorned with a thousand pillars made entirely of all <s>maṇi</s>-kings, with dimensions formed of the joining of all jewels, of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> pure gold with divinely arranged panels bound with innumerable nets of various pearl-garlands, with artfully arranged designs of <s>maṇi</s>-jewel kings, with a universal array of <s>Jambūdhvaja</s> <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, surrounded by innumerable jeweled railings, well-divided with <s>maṇi</s>-king staircases in all directions. In the center of that pavilion, he saw a throne upon a <s>Cintāmaṇirājaratnapadmagarbha</s> (Womb of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel-King Lotus), established upon images of <s>maṇi</s>-forms resembling all lords of the world, with the color of all <s>maṇi</s>-jewel forms like the radiance of <s>Indra</s>'s banner, standing upon a ground of <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇi</s>-wheels, with an array of rows of various <s>maṇi</s>-kings surrounded by many jeweled railings, well-established with <s>Jyotirdhvaja</s> (Light-Banner) <s>maṇi</s>-kings, adorned with arrays of various jewels, beautifully prepared with divine surpassing <s>maṇi</s>-king garments and well-fashioned with jeweled fabrics of many colors, with a canopy of all jewel-garments spread across the sky as ornament, covered with nets of all jewels, with the sound of <s>vajra</s>-banners well-arranged in all directions, illuminated by well-waving banners of all jeweled panels, with ornaments of evenly arranged banners of all fragrant <s>maṇi</s>-kings, raining forth showers of all flowers, incense, and diverse blossoms, with the sweet and pleasant sound of all jeweled bell-banners gently stirred, fitted with doorways of various jeweled edifice-mouths, fitted with lotus-net elephant-lord forms of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-king enlarged by incense-water of various colors issuing from the mouths of various jewel-<s>maṇi</s> forms, fitted with clouds of incense of infinite colors issuing from the mouths of various <s>vajra</s>-lions, issuing forth the <s>Brahma</s>-voice of the method of great loving-kindness from the mouths of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-kings in <s>Brahma</s>-form, with sweet and resonant tones issuing from the mouths of various jewel-silver illuminating the bright half of the moon, issuing forth the sweet sound of golden bell-garlands proclaiming the names of the <s>Buddha</s>s of the three times, resounding with the delightful sounds of great <s>maṇi</s>-king bell-garlands of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Buddha</s>s, issuing forth sounds from various <s>vajra</s>-bells of the vows of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, announcing through sounds the names reflected in rows of <s>Candradhvaja</s> (Moon-Banner) <s>maṇi</s>-kings of all <s>Buddha</s>s, announcing through reflections of the succession of births of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the three times in rows of <s>Śuddhagarbha</s> (Pure Womb) <s>maṇi</s>-kings, displaying through rays the paths and methods of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions throughout the supreme expanse of space of the practice of all magical transformations in rows of <s>Ādityagarbha</s> (Sun Womb) <s>maṇi</s>-kings, in rows of <s>Avabhāsadhvaja</s> (Illumination Banner) <s>maṇi</s>-kings

body.text: sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalāvabhāsapramuñcanavairocanamaṇirājapaṅkti sarvajagadindrasadṛśanirmāṇameghatathāgatapūjopasthānapramuñcanaṃ cintāmaṇirājapaṅkti samantabhadrabodhisattvavikurvitapratikṣaṇasarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaṃ merudhvajamaṇirājapaṅkti sarvadevendrabhavanameghāpsarorutanigarjitanirghoṣaṃ sarvārambaṇatathāgatastutimeghapramuñcanācintyaguṇavarṇanirdeśaṃ ca tadāsanamadrākṣīt acintyaratnavyūhāsanaparivāram //
body.translated_text: releasing the illumination of the radiance-<s>maṇḍala</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, in rows of <s>Vairocana</s> <s>maṇi</s>-kings releasing clouds of magical emanations resembling the lords of all worlds for the worship and attendance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, in rows of <s>Cintāmaṇirāja</s> (Wish-Fulfilling Jewel King) spreading throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every moment the magical transformations of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in rows of <s>Merudhvaja</s> (Meru-Banner) <s>maṇi</s>-kings resounding with the thundering sounds of <s>Apsaras</s>-music in the cloud-palaces of all lords of <s>Deva</s>s, releasing clouds of praise of <s>Tathāgata</s>s regarding all objects and proclaiming the exposition of inconceivable qualities — that throne he saw, surrounded by a retinue of thrones with an inconceivable array of jewels.

body.text:
tasmiṃścāsane māyādevīṃ niṣaṇṇāmadrākṣīt trailokyasamatikrāntena rūpeṇa, sarvalokābhimukhena sarvabhavagatyudgatena rūpeṇa, yathāśayajagadvijñaptena sarvalokānupaliptena rūpeṇa, vipulapuṇyasaṃbhūtena sarvajagatsadṛśena rūpeṇa, sarvasattvasukhopadarśanena sarvajagatparipākavinayānukūlena rūpeṇa, sarvasattvābhimukhapralambitena sarvakālagaganajagadvijñaptyasaṃbhinnena rūpeṇa, sarvajaganniṣṭhāvijñaptyādhiṣṭhānena agatikena rūpeṇa, sarvalokagatikena rūpeṇa, sarvalokagatiniruddhena anāgatikena rūpeṇa, sarvajagadasaṃbhūtena anutpannena rūpeṇa, anutpattisamadharmaniratena aniruddhena rūpeṇa, sarvalokavyavahāraparameṇa asatyena rūpeṇa, yathāvatpratilabdhena amṛṣeṇa rūpeṇa, yathālokavijñaptena akrāntena rūpeṇa, cyutyupapattivinivṛtena avinaṣṭena rūpeṇa, dharmadhātuprakṛtyavināśena alakṣaṇena rūpeṇa, tryadhvavākpathaparameṇa ekalakṣaṇena rūpeṇa, alakṣaṇasulakṣaṇaniryātena pratibhāsakalpena rūpeṇa, sarvajagaccittayathāśayavijñaptena māyākalpena rūpeṇa, jñānamāyāpariniṣpannena marīcikalpena rūpeṇa, pratikṣaṇajagatsaṃjñādhiṣṭhānaparameṇa cchāyopamena rūpeṇa, praṇidhānasarvajagadanubaddhena svapnopamena rūpeṇa, yathāśayajagadvijñaptyasaṃbhinnena sarvadharmadhātuparameṇa rūpeṇa, ākāśadhātuprakṛtipariśuddhena mahākaruṇāniryātena rūpeṇa, sattvavaṃśaparipālanaprayuktena asaṅgamukhaniryātena rūpeṇa, pratikṣaṇadharmadhātuspharaṇena anantamadhyena rūpeṇa, anāvilasarvajaganniśritena apramāṇena rūpeṇa, sarvavākpathasamatikrāntena supratiṣṭhitena rūpeṇa, sarvajagadvinayādhiṣṭhānanirvṛttena anadhiṣṭhitena rūpeṇa, adhiṣṭhānajagatkāyaprayuktena asaṃvṛtena rūpeṇa, praṇidhānamāyāpariniṣpannena anabhibhūtena rūpeṇa, sarvalokābhyudgatena ayathāvatena rūpeṇa, śamathālokavijñaptena asaṃbhavena rūpeṇa, yathākarmajagadanubaddhena cintāmaṇirājakalpena rūpeṇa, yathāśayasarvasattvābhiprāyaparipūrṇapraṇidhiparipūrṇena avikalpena rūpeṇa, sarvajagatparikalpopasthitena adhikalpena rūpeṇa, sarvajagadvijñaptyakalpena
adhiṣṭhānena rūpeṇa, saṃsārāvinivṛttiparameṇa viśuddhena rūpeṇa tathatāsamanirvikalpena / ityevaṃprakāreṇa rūpeṇa sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako māyādevīmadrākṣīdarūpeṇa rūpapratibhāsena avedanena rūpeṇa lokaduḥkhavedanāpraśāntiparameṇa, sarvasattvasaṃjñāgatoccālitena rūpeṇa parasattvasaṃjñāgatavijñaptena, anabhisaṃskāradharmatāniryātena rūpeṇa māyāgatakarmavinivṛttena, vijñānaviṣayasamatikrāntena rūpeṇa bodhisattvapraṇidhijñānasaṃbhavena, asvabhāvena rūpeṇa sarvajagadvākpathaparameṇa śarīreṇa, saṃsāre saṃtāpaniruddhena rūpeṇa dharmakāyaparamaśītībhāvopagatena yathāśayajagadrūpakāyasaṃdarśanīṃ sattvāśayavaśena sarvajagatsadṛśaṃ sarvajagadrūpakāyātirekaṃ rūpakāyaṃ saṃdarśayamānām /
body.translated_text: And on that throne he saw <s>Māyādevī</s> seated — with a form that transcended the three worlds, with a form facing all worlds and risen above all states of existence, with a form manifesting to the world according to their dispositions yet unstained by any world, with a form born of vast merit and resembling all the world, with a form displaying happiness to all beings and conducive to the maturation and discipline of all the world, with a form extending toward all beings yet unbroken by the manifestation of the world across all times and space, with a form that was the basis of manifestation for the ultimate destiny of all the world yet without destination, with a form traversing all world-destinations, with a form in which all world-destinations had ceased yet was without coming, with a form unproduced in all the world and unarisen, with a form delighting in the doctrine of equality with non-arising yet unceased, with a form supreme in the conventions of all worlds yet unreal, with a form obtained just as it truly is yet not false, with a form manifested according to the world yet unencroached upon, with a form free from death and rebirth yet unperished, with a form imperishable by the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) yet without characteristics, with a form supreme in the paths of speech across the three times yet of a single characteristic, with a form issuing from the well-characterized characteristicless, like a reflection, with a form manifested to the minds and dispositions of all the world, like an illusion, with a form perfectly accomplished through the illusion of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), like a mirage, with a form supreme in sustaining the perceptions of the world at every moment, like a shadow, with a form following all the world through <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vow), like a dream, with a form unbroken by manifestation to the world according to their dispositions yet supreme in the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, with a form pure by the nature of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space-element) yet issuing from great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), with a form devoted to protecting the lineage of beings yet issuing from the door of non-attachment, with a form pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> at every moment yet without end or middle, with a form relied upon by all the world without turbidity yet immeasurable, with a form completely transcending all paths of speech yet well-established, with a form accomplished through the sustaining power of disciplining all the world yet unsustained, with a form engaged in embodying the world through sustaining power yet unconcealed, with a form perfectly accomplished through the illusion of <s>praṇidhāna</s> yet unconquered, with a form risen above all worlds yet not as it truly is, with a form manifested through the light of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) yet without origination, with a form following the world according to their <s>karma</s>, like a wish-fulfilling <s>cintāmaṇi</s>-king, with a form fulfilling the intentions of all beings according to their dispositions through fulfilled vows yet free from conceptual construction, with a form present through the imaginations of all the world yet beyond imagination, with a form that was a sustaining power unconditioned by the manifestation of all the world, with a form supreme in non-cessation from <s>saṃsāra</s> yet purified and free from conceptual construction like <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). With a form of such a nature did <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son see <s>Māyādevī</s> — with a formless form-appearance, with a form without feeling yet supreme in pacifying the suffering-feelings of the world, with a form that had transcended the perception-category of all beings yet manifested through the perception-category of other beings, with a form issuing from the nature of the unconditioned yet free from actions belonging to illusion, with a form completely transcending the domain of consciousness yet born from the wisdom of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vows, with a form without own-nature yet with a body supreme in all the world's paths of speech, with a form in which the burning of <s>saṃsāra</s> had ceased yet endowed with the supreme coolness of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) — displaying a form-body manifestation to the world according to their dispositions, showing a form-body that conformed to all the world through the power of beings' dispositions yet surpassed the form-bodies of all the world.

body.text: tatra kecitsattvā mārakanyārūpeṇa mārakanyātirekarūpāṃ māyādevīmadrākṣuḥ / kecitsattvā vaśavartyapsarotirekarūpāṃ kecitsunirmitāpsarotirekarūpāṃ kecitsaṃtuṣitāpsarotirekarūpāṃ kecitsuyāmāpsarotirekarūpāṃ kecitrtrāyastriṃśāpsarotirekarūpāṃ keciccāturmahārājikāpsarotirekarūpāṃ kecitkumbhāṇḍendrakanyātirekarūpāṃ kecinmahoragendrakanyātirekarūpāṃ / kecitsattvā manuṣyendrakanyātirekarūpāṃ māyādevīmapaśyan //
body.translated_text: There, certain beings saw <s>Māyādevī</s> in the form of a <s>Māra</s>-maiden yet surpassing the form of <s>Māra</s>-maidens; certain beings saw her surpassing the form of <s>Vaśavartī</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Sunirmita</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Suyāma</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> <s>Apsaras</s>es, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>-lord maidens, certain ones surpassing the form of <s>Mahoraga</s>-lord maidens; certain beings saw <s>Māyādevī</s> surpassing the form of human-lord maidens. //

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sarvajagadrūpasaṃjñāpagataḥ parasattvāśayānavataran sarvasattvacittāśayagateṣu māyādevīmapaśyat sarvajagadupajīvyapuṇyāṃ sarvajñatāpuṇyopacitaśarīrāmasaṃbhinnadānapāramitāprayogāṃ sarvajagatsamatāpratipannāṃ mahākaruṇāgoṣṭhasarvasattvasamavasaraṇāṃ sarvatathāgataguṇapratipattiniryātāṃ sarvakṣāntinayasāgarāvatīrṇāṃ sarvajñatāvīryavegavivardhitacetanāṃ sarvadharmamaṇḍalapariśuddhyavivartyavīryāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyaptiniryātāṃ sarvadhyānāṅganayaniṣpatticittāmasaṃbhinnadhyānāṅgaviṣayāsādhāraṇatathāgatadhyānamaṇḍalāvabhāsapratilabdhāṃ sarvasattvakleśasāgarocchoṣaṇaniścayanānānidhyaptiparamāṃ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravicayavidhijñāṃ sarvadharmanayasamudravyavacāraṇaprajñāṃ sarvatathāgatādarśanāvitṛptāṃ tryadhvatathāgataparaṃparāvyavalokanāpratiprasrabdhāṃ sarvabuddhadarśanadvārābhimukhāṃ sarvatathāgatasamudāgamamārgapariśuddhivimātratāvidhijñāṃ sarvatathāgatagaganagocarāṃ sarvasattvasaṃgrahopāyavidhijñāmanantamadhyayathāśayajagatparipākavinayapratibhāsaprāptāṃ sarvabuddhakāyaviśuddhivimātratāvatīrṇāṃ sarvakṣetrasāgarapariśuddhipraṇidhānasamanvāgatāṃ sarvasattvadhātuvinayādhiṣṭhānaparyavasānapraṇidhānapariśuddhāṃ sarvatathāgataviṣayapūjāspharaṇacittāṃ sarvabodhisattvavikurvitavīryaniryātāmanuttaradharmakāyapariśuddhāmanantarūpakāyasaṃdarśanīṃ sarvamārabalapramardanīṃ vipulakuśalamūlabalopapannāṃ dharmabalasaṃjātabuddhibuddhabalāvabhāsapratilabdhāṃ sarvabodhisattvaśitābalapariniṣpannāṃ sarvajñatāvegabalasaṃjātāṃ sarvatathāgatajñānavidyudavabhāsitaprajñāmanantamadhyasattvacittasamudravicaraṇajñānāṃ vipulajagadāśayāvatīrṇāṃ parasattvendriyavimātratājñānanayavidhijñāmanantasattvādhimuktivimātratājñānakauśalyānugatāṃ daśadigapramāṇakṣetrasamudrakāyaspharaṇāṃ sarvalokadhātuvimātratājñānanayavidhijñāṃ sarvakṣetrasaṃbhedavidhijñānanayakauśalyānugatāṃ sarvadiksāgaraprasṛtajñānadarśanāṃ sarvādhvasāgarānuprasṛtabuddhiṃ sarvabuddhasāgarābhimukhapraṇipatitakāyāṃ sarvabuddhadharmameghasamudrasaṃpratīcchanābhimukhacittāṃ sarvatathāgataguṇapratipūraṇapratipattiniryāṇaprayuktāṃ sarvabodhisaṃbhārasaṃbhavānuprasṛtabuddhiṃ sarvabodhisattvaprasthānavicāravikrāntāṃ sarvabodhicittotpādāṅgapariniṣpannāṃ sarvasattvaparipālanaprayuktāṃ sarvabuddhavarṇameghālokaprabhāvanāṃ sarvabodhisattvajinajanetrīpraṇidhānaniryātām / etatpramukhairjambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamairdarśananayaiḥ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako
māyādevīmapaśyat / sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā yatpramāṇā māyādevī tatpramāṇaṃ svakāyamadhiṣṭhāya samantadigabhimukhāṃ māyādevīṃ sarvatrānugatena kāyena praṇipatitaḥ / tasya praṇipatamānasya anantamadhyāni samādhimukhāni avakrāntāni / sa tāni samādhimukhāni vyavalokya animittīkṛtvā prabhāvayitvā sārīkṛtvā anusmṛtya spharitvā prasaritvā avalokayitvā vipulīkṛtvā abhinirhṛtya mudrayitvā tebhyaḥ samādhimukhebhyo vyutthāya
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having gone beyond the perception of the forms of all the world, penetrating the dispositions of other beings, saw <s>Māyādevī</s> within the mental dispositions of all beings — endowed with merit sustaining all the world, with a body accumulated through merit directed toward <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), with unbroken practice of <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), established in equality toward all the world, a gathering-place for all beings in the assembly-hall of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), issuing from the practice of the qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having descended into the ocean of all modes of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), with aspiration increased by the force of vigor toward <s>sarvajñatā</s>, with irreversible vigor in the purification of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of all <s>dharma</s>s, issuing from penetrative insight into the own-nature of all <s>dharma</s>s, with a mind accomplished in the methods of all <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) limbs and having attained the illumination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s extraordinary meditation-<s>maṇḍala</s> unbroken in the domain of <s>dhyāna</s>-limbs, supreme in various penetrative insights determining the drying up of the ocean of <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions) of all beings, skilled in the methods of investigating the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, possessed of the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that traverses the ocean of all <s>Dharma</s>-approaches, insatiable in seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, unrelenting in contemplating the succession of <s>Tathāgata</s>s across the three times, facing the doors of seeing all <s>Buddha</s>s, skilled in the methods and variety of purifying the path of attainment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, ranging in the sky-domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, skilled in the methods of means for gathering all beings, having attained a reflection of maturing and disciplining the world according to their dispositions without end or middle, having descended into the variety of purifying the bodies of all <s>Buddha</s>s, endowed with vows for purifying all fields of <s>Buddha</s>-lands, purified in vows culminating in the sustaining power of disciplining all the realm of beings, with a mind pervading the worship of the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, issuing from the vigor of miraculous transformation of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, purified in the unsurpassed <s>dharmakāya</s>, displaying infinite form-bodies, crushing the forces of all <s>Māra</s>s, endowed with the power of vast roots of merit, having attained the illumination of <s>Buddha</s>-power through the intelligence born of the power of <s>Dharma</s>, perfected in the power of firmness of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, born from the force of vigor toward <s>sarvajñatā</s>, possessed of <s>prajñā</s> illuminated by the lightning of wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, possessed of knowledge traversing the ocean of minds of beings without end or middle, having descended into the vast dispositions of the world, skilled in the methods and variety of knowledge of the faculties of other beings, endowed with the skill of knowledge of the immeasurable variety of convictions of beings, with a body pervading oceans of fields in the ten directions without measure, skilled in the methods and variety of knowledge of all world-realms, endowed with the skill of knowledge-methods for the synthesis of all fields, with knowledge-vision extended into oceans of all directions, with intelligence extending into oceans of all time-periods, with a body bowed in homage facing the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>s, with a mind facing to receive the ocean-clouds of the <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, devoted to the practice of fulfilling the qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with intelligence extending into the arising of all requisites of awakening, striding forth in the investigation of the career of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, perfected in the limbs of the arising of all <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), devoted to protecting all beings, illuminating the radiance of clouds of praise of all <s>Buddha</s>s, issuing from the vows of the mother of Victors among all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. Through these foremost modes of seeing, equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, did <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son see <s>Māyādevī</s>. Having seen her, he sustained his own body to the same measure as <s>Māyādevī</s>'s measure, and with a body following everywhere, facing all directions, he bowed down to <s>Māyādevī</s>. As he bowed down, he entered into immeasurable, infinite <s>samādhi</s>-gateways. Having surveyed those <s>samādhi</s>-gateways, having made them signless, having empowered them, having made them essential, having recollected them, having pervaded them, having extended them, having contemplated them, having expanded them, having brought them forth, having sealed them, he arose from those <s>samādhi</s>-gateways,

body.text: māyādevīṃ saparivārāṃ sabhavanāsanāṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - ahamārye mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya kalyāṇamitraparyupāsanena samādāpitam / so 'haṃ kalyāṇamitraṃ paryupāsamāno 'nupūrveṇa yāvattava sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ pariniṣpanno bhavati sarvajñatāyām / sā avocat - ahaṃ kulaputra mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatavyūhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sāhaṃ kulaputra anena vimokṣeṇa samanvāgatā yāvanti iha lokadhātusamudre bhagavato vairocanasya sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvajambudvīpeṣu caramabhavikabodhisattvajanmavikurvitāni pravartante, sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ caramabhavikānāṃ bodhisattvānāmahaṃ jananī / sarve te bodhisattvā mama kukṣau saṃbhavanti / mama dakṣiṇātpārśvānniṣkramanti / ihaiva tāvadahaṃ kulaputra bhāgavatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ kapilavastuni mahānagare rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya kulabaddhakalpena siddhārthaṃ bodhisattvaṃ janitravatī mahatācintyena bodhisattvajanmavikurvitena //
body.translated_text: circumambulated <s>Māyādevī</s> together with her retinue and throne-palace, stood before her with palms joined, and spoke thus: "O Noble Lady, I have had the mind of awakening toward supreme perfect <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (complete enlightenment) aroused by the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and was encouraged in the attendance upon spiritual friends. Thus attending upon spiritual friends, I have gradually come into your presence. May the Noble Lady please tell me — how does a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, training in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, become perfected in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)?" She replied: "Son of good family, I have attained the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) called 'Array Arising from the Illusion of the Wisdom of Great Vows.' Son of good family, endowed with this <s>vimokṣa</s>, in however many oceans of world-realms of the Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, in all their world-realms, in all their <s>Jambudvīpa</s>s, wherever the birth-transformations of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s in their final existence take place — of all those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s in their final existence, I am the mother. All those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s take birth in my womb. They emerge from my right side. Here indeed, son of good family, in this blessed four-continent world-system, in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, being established as the wife of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, I gave birth to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Siddhārtha</s> through the great and inconceivable birth-transformation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: sā khalvahaṃ kulaputra tadā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhagatā bhavāmi / atha bodhisattvasya tuṣitabhavanāccyavanakālasamaye pratyupasthite sarvaromamukhebhya ekaikasmādromamukhādanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ sarvabodhisattvajananīguṇanayavyūhāḥ sarvatathāgatajananīguṇamaṇḍalaprabhavaprabhāsā nāma raśmayo niścaritvā sarvāvantaṃ lokadhātumavabhāsya mama śarīre nipatya mūrdhānamupādāya sarvaromakūpeṣvanuprāviśan / samanantarapraviṣṭābhiśca kulaputra tābhirbodhisattvaraśmibhiranekanāmadheyābhirnānābodhisattvajananīvikurvitavyūhapramuñcanībhiḥ, atha tāvadeva mama kāye bodhisattvaraśmimukhamaṇḍalābhivijñaptāḥ sarvabodhisattvajanmavikurvitanayavyūhāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma antargatena parivāreṇa / samanantarapraviṣṭābhiśca kulaputra mama kāye tābhirbodhisattvaraśmibhiḥ, atha tāvadeva yeṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tāni bodhisattvaraśmimukhamaṇḍalāni vijñaptāni janmanayavikurvitāni pravartante, sarve te mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamagaman, yaduta bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatā buddhasiṃhāsananiṣaṇṇā bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalaparivṛtā lokendrābhipūjitā dharmacakraṃ pravartayamānāḥ / ye ca taistathāgataiḥ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāṃ caradbhistathāgatā ārāgitāḥ, te 'pi sarve mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamagaman / prathamacittotpādajanmavikurvitāḥ sābhisaṃbodhidharmacakrapravartanaparinirvāṇavikurvitāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraviśuddhavyūhāḥ, yāni ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ nirmāṇamaṇḍalāni praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti, tānyapi sarvāṇi mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsamagaman / tasyā mama kulaputra kāye tābhirbodhisattvaraśmibhiranupraviṣṭābhiḥ sarvajagadabhyudgataḥ kāyaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt, ākāśadhātuvipulaśca kukṣiḥ, na ca manuṣyāśrayapramāṇādatikrāntaḥ / yāvantaśca daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvagarbhāvāsabhavanavyūhāḥ, te sarve mama kāye 'ntargatā anupraviṣṭāḥ sarve saṃdṛśyante //
body.translated_text: At that time, O son of good family, I was dwelling in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Then, when the time of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s descent from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven was at hand, from every single hair-pore there issued forth rays called 'Radiance Arising from the Qualities-Maṇḍala of the Mothers of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, embodying the arrays of qualities and methods of the mothers of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. Having illuminated the entire world-realm, they descended upon my body and, beginning from the crown of my head, entered into all my hair-pores. As soon as those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-rays of many names, releasing diverse arrays of the miraculous transformations of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-mothers, entered my body, O son of good family, all the arrays of methods and miraculous birth-transformations of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, made known through the maṇḍalas of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-ray-openings, became visible within, together with their retinues. As soon as those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-rays entered my body, O son of good family, all those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s whose birth-method-transformations proceeded through those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-ray-maṇḍala-openings came into the range of my vision — seated upon lion-thrones at the supreme site of enlightenment, surrounded by assemblies of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, worshipped by lords of the world, turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma). And all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s who had been pleased by those <s>Tathāgata</s>s while they were practicing the prior <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — they too all came into the range of my vision. The miraculous transformations from the first arising of the mind of enlightenment through birth, up to the miraculous transformations of full enlightenment, turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, and <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, all the pure arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and the emanation-maṇḍalas of those <s>Tathāgata</s>s that pervade the entire <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) at every mind-moment — all these too came into the range of my vision. When those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-rays had entered my body, O son of good family, my body stood surpassing the entire world, and my womb became as vast as the realm of space, yet it did not exceed the measure of a human form. And all the arrays of <s>Bodhisattva</s> womb-dwelling palaces in the ten directions — all of them entered within my body and were fully visible.

body.text: samanantaraprādurbhūtasya ca mama kulaputra kāye bodhisattvagarbhāvāsabhavanavyūhaparibhogasya, atha tāvadeva bodhisattvaḥ sārdhaṃ daśabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbodhisattvairekapraṇidhānaiḥ sabhāgacaritairekakuśalamūlair
body.translated_text: As soon as the enjoyment of the array of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-dwelling palace manifested in my body, O son of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, together with <s>Bodhisattva</s>s equal in number to the atoms of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields, of common conduct, sharing one aspiration, sharing one root of merit,

body.text: ekavyūhairekavimokṣavihāribhirekajñānabhūmisaṃvāsibhirekavikurvitaniryātairekapraṇidhānasamudāgatairekacaryāniryātairdharmakāyapariśuddhairanantamadhyarūpakāyādhiṣṭhānaiḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhivikurvitaniryātairnāgendragarbhamaṇikūṭāgāragataiḥ sāgaranāgarājapūrvaṃgamairaśītyā nāgendrasahasraiḥ sarvalokendrasahasraiścābhipūjyamāno mahatā bodhisattvavikurvitena sarvatuṣitabhavanacyutisaṃdarśanena ekaikasmāttuṣitabhavanāt sarvalokadhātuprasṛtacāturdvīpopapattipratilābhasaṃdarśanena acintyasattvaparipākopāyakauśalyānugatena pramattasarvasattvasaṃcodanena sarvābhiniveśoccālanena mahāraśmijālapramuñcanena sarvalokāndhakāravidhamanena sarvāpāyaduḥkhavyupaśamanena sarvanirayagatinivartanena sarvasattvapūrvakarmasaṃcodanena sarvasattvadhātuparitrāyaṇena sarvasattvābhimukhakāyasaṃdarśanena tuṣitabhavanāccyutvā sārdhaṃ saparivāreṇa mama kukṣau prāviśat //
body.translated_text: sharing one array, abiding in one <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), dwelling on one stage of knowledge, proceeding through one miraculous transformation, arisen from one aspiration, proceeding through one practice, pure in <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body), endowed with boundless and infinite <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form-body) empowerments, proceeding through the miraculous transformations of the aspirations of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conduct, dwelling in gem-pinnacled palaces within <s>Nāgendra</s>-wombs, preceded by <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s> (Dragon King), worshipped by eighty thousand <s>Nāgendra</s>s (sovereign serpent kings) and all the lords of the world — with a great <s>Bodhisattva</s> miraculous display showing the descent from all <s>Tuṣita</s> heavens, showing from each <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven the attainment of birth in the four-continent realms pervading all world-realms, accompanied by inconceivable skillful means for maturing beings, rousing all heedless beings, uprooting all attachments, releasing a great net of rays, dispelling the darkness of all worlds, extinguishing the suffering of all lower realms, turning back all beings from the paths of hell, awakening all beings to their past <s>karma</s>, protecting all realms of beings, showing a body facing all beings — having descended from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, entered my womb together with his retinue.

body.text: te sarve mama kukṣau trisāhasralokadhātuvipulena yāvadanabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuvipulena ākramavikrameṇa anuvicaranti sma / sarvāṇi ca daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāni praticittakṣaṇamanabhilāpyāni mama kukṣau samavasaranti sma bodhisattvagarbhāvāsavikurvitaṃ draṣṭum / catvāraśca mahārājāḥ śakrasuyāmasaṃtuṣitasunirmitavaśavartinaśca devendrāḥ brahmendrāśca garbhāvāsopagatabodhisattvamupasaṃkrāmanti sma darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya sāṃkathyānubhāvanāya / na cāyaṃ mama kukṣistāvanti parṣanmaṇḍalāni pratīcchan vipulībhavati / na cāsmānmanuṣyāśrayādayaṃ mama kāyo viśiṣṭataraḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / tāni ca tāvanti parṣanmaṇḍalāni saṃpratīcchati / sarve ca te devamanuṣyā nānābodhisattvaparibhogapariśuddhivyūhānapaśyan / tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi tadasyaiva mahāpraṇidhānamāyāgatasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya subhāṣitatvāt //
body.translated_text: They all moved about within my womb with a stride and range as vast as a <s>trisāhasra</s>-great-thousand world-realm, and even as vast as world-realms equal in number to the atoms of inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And at every mind-moment, inexpressible assemblies of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s throughout all world-realm expanses in the ten directions converged within my womb to behold the miraculous display of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-dwelling. The four great kings, <s>Śakra</s>, the <s>Deva</s> lords of <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, and <s>Vaśavartin</s>, and the <s>Brahmendra</s>s (lords of <s>Brahmā</s>) all approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who had entered the womb, for seeing, for paying homage, for attending upon, for hearing the Dharma, and for conversing. Yet my womb, receiving so many assemblies, did not become enlarged; nor did my body stand forth as exceeding this human form; and yet it received all those assemblies. And all those <s>Deva</s>s and humans beheld the diverse pure arrays of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s enjoyments. Why is this? Because this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), born of the great aspiration and <s>māyā</s> (illusion), is well proclaimed.

body.text: yathā cāhaṃ kulaputra asyāṃ bhāgavatyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ jambudvīpe bodhisattvaṃ kukṣiṇā saṃpratīcchāmi, evaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvacāturdvīpikājambudvīpeṣu saṃpratīcchāmi anena ca vikurvitavyūhena / na cāyaṃ mama kāyo dvayībhavati nādvayībhavati, na caikatve saṃtiṣṭhate na bahutve, yathāpi nāma tadasyaiva mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya subhāṣitatvāt / yathā cāhaṃ kulaputra asya bhagavato vairocanasya mātā abhūvam, tathā pūrvakāṇāmapi tathāgatānāmanantamadhyānāṃ mātā abhūvam / yatra bodhisattvo loka upapāduka upāpadyata padmagarbhe, tatrāhaṃ nalinīdevatā bhūtvā bodhisattvaṃ saṃpratīcchāmi / lokaśca māṃ bodhisattvajananīti saṃjānāti / yatrotsaṅge prādurbabhūva, tatrāhamasya jananyabhūvam / yatra buddhakṣetre prādurbhavati, tatrāhaṃ bodhimaṇḍadevatā bhavāmi / iti hi kulaputra yāvadbhirupāyamukhaiścaramabhavikā bodhisattvā loka upapattiṃ saṃdarśayanti, tāvadbhirupāyamukhairahaṃ bodhisattvajananī bhavāmi //
body.translated_text: Just as I, O son of good family, receive the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in my womb here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> of this blessed four-continent world, so too do I receive him in all the <s>Jambudvīpa</s>s of all four-continent worlds throughout the <s>trisāhasra</s>-great-thousand world-realm, by means of this miraculous display. Yet my body does not become dual nor does it remain non-dual; it does not abide in oneness nor in multiplicity — because this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), born of the knowledge of the great aspiration and <s>māyā</s> (illusion), is well proclaimed. Just as I, O son of good family, was the mother of this Blessed <s>Vairocana</s>, so too was I the mother of <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the past, infinite and without middle. Where the <s>Bodhisattva</s> appears in the world as one born miraculously within a lotus-womb, there I become the deity of the lotus pond and receive the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and the world knows me as the mother of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Where he manifested upon a lap, there I was his mother. In whatever <s>Buddha</s>-field he appears, there I am the deity of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of enlightenment). Thus, O son of good family, by however many skillful means <s>Bodhisattva</s>s in their final existence display their birth in the world, by that many skillful means am I the mother of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: yathā ahaṃ kulaputra iha lokadhātau asya bhagavataḥ sarvabodhisattvajanmavikurvitasaṃdarśaneṣu janetryabhūvam, tathā bhagavataḥ krakucchandasyāpi tathāgatasya, kanakamuneḥ, kāśyapasya tathāgatasya
body.translated_text: Just as I, O son of good family, was the mother for the display of all the birth-transformations of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s of this Blessed One in this world-realm, so too was I the mother of the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, of <s>Kanakamuni</s>, of <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

body.text:
janetryabhūvam / tathā sarveṣāṃ bhadrakalpikānāmanāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ janetrī bhaviṣyāmi / tadyathā maitreyasya bodhisattvasya tuṣitabhavanagatasya cyutisaṃdarśanakāle pravṛtte sarvabodhisattvopapattisaṃbhavagarbhasaṃvāsavikurvitasaṃdarśanaprabhāsāyāṃ raśmyāmutsṛṣṭāyāṃ prabhāsiteṣu sarvadharmadhātunayataleṣu yāvanti mama dharmadhātunayatalāni cakṣuṣo 'vabhāsamāgamiṣyanti, yeṣu maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena manuṣyaloke manuṣyendrakuleṣu janmopapattisaṃdarśanena sattvā vinayitavyāḥ, teṣvahaṃ sarvatra bodhisattvajananī bhaviṣyāmi / yathā ca maitreyasya bodhisattvasya, tathā siṃhasya yo maitreyasyānantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, tathā pradyotasya ketoḥ sunetrasya kusumasya kusumaśriyaḥ tiṣyasya puṣyasya sumanaso vajrasya virajasaḥ candrolkādhāriṇo yaśaso vajraśuddhasya ekārthadarśino sitāṅgasya pāraṃgatasya ratnārciḥparvatasya maholkādhāriṇaḥ padmottarasya vighuṣṭaśabdasya aparimitaguṇadharmasya dīpaśriyo vibhūṣitāṅgasya suprayāṇasya maitraśriyo nirmitasyāniketasya jvalitatejaso 'nantaghoṣasya aninemasya aninetrasya vimativikiraṇasya pariśuddhasya suviśālābhasya yaśaḥśuddhoditasya meghaśriyo vicitrabhūtasya sarvaratnavicitravarṇamaṇikuṇḍalasya sāgaramateḥ śubharatnasya anihatamallasya paripūrṇamanorathasya maheśvarasya indraśriyo 'gniśriyaḥ candanameghasya sitaviśālākṣasya śreṣṭhamatervibhāvitamateravaropaṇarājasyottāpanarājamatervibhūṣitasya vibhūteḥ keśaranandina īśvaradevasya īśvarasya uṣṇīṣaśriyo vajrajñānaparvatasya śrīgarbhasya kanakajālakāyavibhūṣitasya suvibhaktasya īśvaradevasya mahendradevasya anilaśriyo viśuddhanandino 'rciṣmato varuṇaśriyo viśuddhamateragrayānasya nihitaguṇoditasya ariguptasya vākyanudasya vaśībhūtasya guṇatejasya vairocanaketorvibhavagandhasya vibhāvanagandhasya vibhaktāṅgasya suviśākhasya sarvagandhārcimukhasya vajramaṇivicitrasya prahasitanetrasya nihatarāgarajasaḥ pravṛddhakāyarājasya vāsudevasya udāradevasya nirodhanimnasya vibuddherdhūtarajasaḥ arcirmahendrasya upaśamavato

body.translated_text: and I was their mother. Likewise, I shall be the mother of all the future <s>Tathāgata</s>s of this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon). That is to say, when the time of displaying the descent of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven has come, when the ray called 'Radiance Displaying the Miraculous Transformations of All <s>Bodhisattva</s>s' Birth, Arising, Womb-Dwelling' has been released and all the planes of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-method have been illuminated — as many planes of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-method as shall come into the range of my vision, in which <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> is to discipline beings by displaying birth and arising in the human world among royal families — in all those places I shall be the mother of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And just as for <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, so too for <s>Siṃha</s>, who shall attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment immediately after <s>Maitreya</s>, and likewise for <s>Pradyota</s>,
