aparājitameroranilayajñānasya anantāsanasya ayudhiṣṭhirasya caryāgatasya uttaradattasya atyantacandramaso 'nugrahacandrasya acalaskandhasya agrasānumateranugrahamaterabhyuddharasya arcitanamasyānupagamanāmno nihatatejaso viśvavarṇasya animittaprajñasya acaladevasya acintyaśriyo vimokṣacandrasya anuttararājasya candraskandhārcitabrahmaṇo 'kampyanetrasya anunayagātrasya abhyudgatakarmaṇo 'nudharmamateranuttaraśriyo brahmadevasya acintyaguṇānuttaradharmagocarasya aparyantabhadrasya anurūpasvarasya abhyuccadevasya bodhisattvasya / iti hi kulaputra etān maitreyapramukhānanāgatāṃstathāgatān pramukhān kṛtvā sarveṣāṃ bhadrakalpikānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmahameva jananī bhaviṣyāmi asyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau / yathā ca iha lokadhātau, tathā daśasu dikṣu aparimāṇeṣu lokadhātuṣu anantamadhyān dharmadhātunayānavataramāṇā yathā ca maitreyasya tathāgatasya anabhilāpyairguṇaviśeṣairjananī bhaviṣyāmi, evamanabhilāpyaguṇaviśeṣaiḥ siṃhasya evaṃ yāvadrocamasya tathāgatasya jananī bhaviṣyāmi / yathā ca bhadrakalpikānāṃ tathāgatānām, evamasmin sarvāvati kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāre lokadhātusamudre sarvalokadhātuvaṃśeṣu sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvajambudvīpeṣvaparāntakoṭīgatān kalpān samantabhadrāyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caramāṇā sarvakalpeṣu sarvasattvaparipākavinayamadhiṣṭhāya sarveṣāmanāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ bodhisattvabhūtānāṃ
jananī bhaviṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: of <s>Aparājitameroranilayanajñāna</s> (Wisdom of the Abode at the Summit of Invincible Meru), of <s>Anantāsana</s> (Infinite Seat), of <s>Ayudhiṣṭhira</s> (Firm in Weapons), of <s>Caryāgata</s> (Gone in Practice), of <s>Uttaradatta</s> (Given by the Supreme), of <s>Atyantacandramās</s> (Eternal Moon), of <s>Anugrahacandra</s> (Moon of Grace), of <s>Acalaskandha</s> (Immovable Aggregate), of <s>Agrasānumati-Anugahamati-Abhyuddhara</s> (Foremost Consent-Gracious Wisdom-Uplifting), of <s>Arcitanamasyānupagama</s> (Approach of Worshipped Homage), of <s>Nihatatejas</s> (Struck Radiance), of <s>Viśvavarṇa</s> (Universal Color), of <s>Animittaprajñā</s> (Signless Wisdom), of <s>Acaladeva</s> (Immovable God), of <s>Acintyaśrī</s> (Inconceivable Glory), of <s>Vimokṣacandra</s> (Moon of Liberation), of <s>Anuttararāja</s> (Unsurpassed King), of <s>Candraskandhārcitabrahman</s> (Brahmā Honored by Moon-Aggregates), of <s>Akampyanetra</s> (Unshakable Eye), of <s>Anunayagātra</s> (Body of Conciliation), of <s>Abhyudgatakarman</s> (Arisen Action), of <s>Anudharmamatyanuttaraśrī</s> (Unsurpassed Glory of Conforming Wisdom), of <s>Brahmadeva</s>, of <s>Acintyaguṇānuttaradharmagocara</s> (Domain of the Unsurpassed Dharma of Inconceivable Qualities), of <s>Aparyantabhadra</s> (Boundless Virtue), of <s>Anurūpasvara</s> (Fitting Sound), of <s>Abhyuccadeva</s> (Exalted God) — [these are] the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Thus indeed, son of good family, beginning with <s>Maitreya</s> as foremost among these future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I shall be the mother of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Auspicious Aeon) in this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (three-thousand great-thousand) world-realm. And just as in this world-realm, so in the immeasurable world-realms in the ten directions, descending into the infinite and boundless methods of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — and just as I shall be the mother of <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with inexpressible distinctions of qualities, so with inexpressible distinctions of qualities I shall be the mother of <s>Siṃha</s> (Lion), and likewise up to <s>Rocamasa</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. And just as for the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, so in this entire <s>Sarvāvati Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra</s> (All-Possessing Ornament of the Lotus-Surface-Womb Array) ocean of world-realms, in all the lineages of world-realms, in all the expanses of world-realms, in all world-realms, in all <s>Jambudvīpas</s>, for <s>kalpas</s> reaching the ultimate end, practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, having resolved to ripen and discipline all beings in all <s>kalpas</s>, I shall be the mother of all future <s>Tathāgatas</s> while they are still <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: evamukte sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako māyādevīmetadavocat - kiyaccirapratilabdhastvayā ayamārye mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatavyūho bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ? āha - bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani acintyānāṃ cittaviṣayasamatikrāntānāmabhijātabodhisattvacakṣuṣpathavijñaptānāṃ vijñānagaṇanāsamatikrāntānāṃ pareṇa śubhaprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūt / tasmin khalu punaḥ śubhaprabhe kalpe merūdgataśrīrnāma lokadhāturabhūdviśuddhasaṃkliṣṭānekaratnamayī sacakravālasumerusāgarā pañcagatipracārā citrā darśanīyā / tasyāṃ khalu merūdgataśriyāṃ lokadhātau daśa cāturdvīpikakoṭīśatānyabhūvan / teṣāṃ khalu daśānāṃ cāturdvīpikakoṭīśatānāṃ madhye siṃhadhvajāgratejo nāma madhyamā cāturdvīpikābhūt, yasyāmaśītirājadhānīkoṭīśatānyabhūvan / teṣāṃ khalu aśītīnāṃ rājadhānīkotīśatānāṃ madhye dhvajāgravatī nāma madhyamarājadhānyabhūt / tasyāṃ mahātejaḥparākramo nāma rājā abhūccakravartī / tasyāṃ khalu punardhvajāgravatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ citramañjariprabhāso nāma bodhimaṇḍo 'bhūt / tatra netraśrīrnāma bodhimaṇḍadevatā abhūt / tasmin khalu punaścitramañjariprabhāse bodhimaṇḍe vimaladhvajo nāma bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt sarvajñatādharmādhigamāya / tasya sarvajñatādharmādhigamāntarāyāya suvarṇaprabho nāma māro mahāsainyaparivāro 'ntardhitakāya upakrānto 'bhūt / sa ca mahātejaḥparākramaścakravartī bodhisattvavaśitāpratilabdho 'bhūt maharddhivikurvitaniryātaḥ / sa tato mahāsainyādvipulataramugrataraṃ ca mahāntaṃ balakāyamabhinirmāya taṃ bodhimaṇḍaṃ samantādanuparivārayāmāsa mārasainyaparājayāya / tena hi mahatī mārasenā
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son said this to <s>Māyādevī</s>: 'How long ago, noble lady, did you obtain this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called the <s>Mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatavyūha</s> (Array of Illusion-Attainment through the Wisdom of the Great Vow)?' She replied: 'Once upon a time, son of good family, in the past, beyond inconceivable [<s>kalpas</s>], beyond the domain of thought, made known to the eyes of noble <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, beyond the calculation of consciousness, there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Śubhaprabha</s> (Auspicious Radiance). In that <s>Śubhaprabha</s> <s>kalpa</s> there was a world-realm called <s>Merūdgataśrī</s> (Glory Arisen from Meru), purified and defiled, made of many jewels, with <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains, <s>Sumeru</s>, and oceans, with the five courses of rebirth, variegated and beautiful to behold. In that world-realm <s>Merūdgataśrī</s>, there were ten hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of four-continent systems. In the center of those ten hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of four-continent systems, there was a central four-continent system called <s>Siṃhadhvajāgrateja</s> (Radiance of the Lion-Banner's Summit), in which there were eighty hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of royal capitals. In the center of those eighty hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of royal capitals, there was a central royal capital called <s>Dhvajāgravatī</s> (Possessing the Summit of Banners). In it there was a king named <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s> (Of Great Radiant Valor), a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign). In that royal capital <s>Dhvajāgravatī</s>, there was a <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) called <s>Citramañjariprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of Colorful Clusters). There, there was a deity of the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> named <s>Netraśrī</s> (Glory of the Eye). At that <s>Citramañjariprabhāsa</s> <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vimaladhvaja</s> (Stainless Banner) was seated for the attainment of the <s>dharmas</s> of omniscience. To create an obstacle to his attainment of the <s>dharmas</s> of omniscience, a <s>Māra</s> named <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s> (Golden Radiance), surrounded by a great army, approached with hidden body. And that <s>Cakravartin</s> <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s> had obtained the <s>Bodhisattva</s> masteries and had issued forth with great miraculous powers. Having emanated from that great army a force even more vast and more fierce, he surrounded the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> on all sides for the defeat of <s>Māra</s>'s army. By that, the great army of <s>Māra</s>

body.text: vikīrṇā / tena ca bhagavatā vimaladhvajena tathāgatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā / atha khalu netraśrībodhimaṇḍadevatā mahātejaḥparākramasya cakravartino 'ntike putrasaṃjñāmutpādya tasya tathāgatasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya praṇidhānamakārṣīt - yatra yatrāhaṃ bhagavan utpadyeyam, tatra tatraiṣa me mahātejaḥparākramaścakravartī putro bhavet / yadā caiṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta, tadāpyahametasya jananī bhaveyam / saivaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā tasminneva citramañjariprabhāse bodhimaṇḍe tasminneva śubhaprabhe kalpe daśa nayutāni tathāgatānāmārāgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: was scattered. And by that Blessed One <s>Vimaladhvaja</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) was fully realized. Then indeed the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> deity <s>Netraśrī</s>, having generated the perception of sonship toward the <s>Cakravartin</s> <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s>, prostrated at the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s> and made this vow: 'Wherever I may be born, O Blessed One, may this <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s> <s>Cakravartin</s> be my son. And when he attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening, may I also be his mother.' Having made this vow, at that very <s>Citramañjariprabhāsa</s> <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, in that very <s>Śubhaprabha</s> <s>kalpa</s>, she served ten <s>nayutas</s> (myriads) of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena netraśrīrnāma bodhimaṇḍadevatā abhūt? na khalu punaste kulaputra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sā tena kālena tena samayena netraśrīrnāma bodhimaṇḍadevatā abhūvam / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena mahātejaḥparākramo nāma cakravartyabhūdbodhisattvavaśitāpratilabdho maharddhikavikurvitaniryāto yena sā mahatī mārasenā vikīrṇā? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ayaṃ sa bhagavān vairocanastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ tena kālena tena samayena mahātejaḥparākramo nāma rājā cakravartyabhūt / sā ahaṃ kulaputra tata upādāya yatratatropapannāḥ, sarvatra eṣa mama putratvamupāgataḥ sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran sarvagatimukheṣu sarvopapattimukheṣu sarvakuśalamūlamukheṣu sarvabodhisattvacaryāvicāraparākrameṣu sarvajātakanayeṣu sarvadevendrajanmasu sarvalokendragateṣu sarveśvarabhūmiṣu sarvagatiprabhāgeṣu / yatra yatropapadyate sattvaparipākahetoḥ, sarvatra ahamevāsya jananyabhūvam / carame ca bhave 'sya ahameva sarvatrānugatā jananyabhūvam / sarvabodhisattvajanmamukheṣu kṣaṇe kṣaṇe yāvanti bodhisattvajanmavikurvitānyādarśayāmāsa, sarvatrāhamevāsya mātā abhūvam / atītānāmapi tathāgatānām, anantamadhyānāmaparimāṇānāmahaṃ jananyabhūvam / pratyutpannānāmapi daśasu dikṣu anantamadhyānāmaparimāṇānāṃ tathāgatānāmahameva jananītvaṃ pratyanubhavāmi / yāvatāṃ ca tathāgatānāmahaṃ carame bhave bodhisattvamātā abhūvam, sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ nābhimaṇḍalebhyo raśmayo niścaritvā mahākāyamāsanaṃ cāvabhāsayāmāsuḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatavyūhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ mahākaruṇāgarbhāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajñatāparipākavinayāparitṛptakukṣīṇāṃ sarvatathāgatavikurvitaromamukhaniryātanidarśanavaśavartinā caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: What do you think, son of good family — was that <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> deity named <s>Netraśrī</s> at that time, in that era, someone else? You should certainly not regard it so, son of good family. I myself was at that time, in that era, the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> deity named <s>Netraśrī</s>. What do you think, son of good family — was that <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s> at that time, in that era, who had obtained the <s>Bodhisattva</s> masteries, who had issued forth with great miraculous powers, by whom that great army of <s>Māra</s> was scattered — someone else? It should certainly not be regarded so. The Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One — he was at that time, in that era, the <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Mahātejaḥparākrama</s>. I, son of good family, from that time onward, wherever we were reborn, everywhere he came to be my son — practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in all gateways of rebirth, in all gateways of modes of birth, in all gateways of wholesome roots, in all valorous exertions of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, in all methods of <s>Jātaka</s> (birth-story) tales, in all births as lords of <s>Devas</s>, in all stations of lords of worlds, in all sovereign grounds, in all portions of the courses of rebirth. Wherever he was born for the sake of ripening beings, everywhere I was his mother. And in his final existence, I was indeed his mother following him everywhere. In all the gateways of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-births, at every moment, however many miraculous displays of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-birth he manifested, in all of them I was his mother. I was also the mother of past <s>Tathāgatas</s>, infinite and boundless, immeasurable. I also experience being the mother of the present <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, infinite and boundless, immeasurable. And of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> of whom I was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-mother in the final existence, from the navel-maṇḍalas of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, rays of light issued forth and illuminated my great body and seat. This, son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Mahāpraṇidhānajñānamāyāgatavyūha</s> (Array of Illusion-Attainment through the Wisdom of the Great Vow) that I know. How could I know the conduct, or speak the qualities of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are wombs of great compassion, whose bellies are never satiated in the ripening and discipline leading to omniscience, who are under the sway of the displays issuing forth from every hair-opening through the miraculous transformations of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva tridaśendrabhavane surendrābhā nāma devakanyā smṛtimato devaputrasya duhitā / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipatavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in the palace of <s>Tridaśendra</s> (Lord of the Thirty-Three), there is a divine maiden named <s>Surendrābhā</s> (Radiance of the Lord of Gods), the daughter of the god-son <s>Smṛtimat</s> (Possessing Mindfulness). Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako māyāyā devyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya māyādevīmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya māyādevyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 42 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having bowed his head at the feet of <s>Māyādevī</s>, having circumambulated <s>Māyādevī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing at her again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Māyādevī</s>. // 42 //

body.text: 45 Surendrābhā /
body.translated_text: [45] <s>Surendrābhā</s>

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena tridaśendrabhavanaṃ yena ca surendrābhā devakanyā smṛtimato devaputrasya duhitā, tenopajagāma / upetya surendrābhāyā devakanyāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya surendrābhāṃ devakanyāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya surendrābhāyā devakanyāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitva evamāha - mayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadasva me devate kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the palace of <s>Tridaśendra</s> (Lord of the Thirty-Three) where the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s>, the daughter of the god-son <s>Smṛtimat</s>, was. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s>, circumambulated the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s> with palms joined, spoke thus: 'I, noble lady, have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Yet I do not know — how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice? And I have heard that the noble lady gives instruction and exhortation to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Please tell me, O goddess, how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text:
evamukte surendrābhā nāma devakanyā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgasmṛtiviśuddhavyūhasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhinī / sā ahaṃ kulaputra abhijānāmi - utpalako nāma kalpo 'bhūt / tatra me gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / abhiniṣkrāmatāṃ caiṣāmārakṣā kṛtā, pūjā kṛtā, ārāmāśca kṛtāḥ paribhogāya / yaśca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvabhūtairmātuḥ kukṣigatairjāyamānaiḥ sapta padāni prakrāmadbhirmahāsiṃhanādaṃ nadadbhiḥ kumārabhūmisthitairantaḥpuramadhyagatairvā abhiniṣkrāmadbhirvā bodhimabhisaṃbudhyamānairvā dharmacakraṃ pravartayamānaiḥ sarvabuddhavikurvitaṃ vā saṃdarśayadbhiḥ sattvaparipākavinayaḥ kṛtaḥ, tatsarvaṃ prathamacittotpādāya yāvatsaddharmaparyantaniṣṭhaṃ prajānāmi smarāmi anusmarāmi dhārayāmi saṃdhārayāmi upadhārayāmi anusarāmi / subhūtirnāma kalpo 'bhūt / tatra me daśa gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / subhago nāma kalpo 'bhūttatra me buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / anilambho nāma kalpo 'bhūt, tatra me caturaśītirbuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyārāgitāni / suprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūt tatra me jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / atulaprabho nāma kalpo 'bhūt, tatra me viṃśatigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / uttaptaśrīrnāma kalpobhūt, tatra me gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / sūryodayo nāma kalpo 'bhūt, tatra me 'śītigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / jayaṃgamo nāma kalpo 'bhūt, tatra me ṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / sucandro nāma kalpo 'bhūt, tatra me saptatirgaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ārāgitāḥ / iti hi kulaputra anenopāyena gaṅgānadīvālukāsamān kalpānanusmarāmi, yadahaṃ satatasamitamavirahitābhūvaṃ tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantikādayamasaṅgasmṛtiviśuddhavyūho bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ śrutaḥ / śrutvā ca ārāgitaḥ yathoktaṃ ca pratipannaḥ / evaṃ cāhaṃ vimokṣaṃ satatasamitamanupraviṣṭā yacca teṣāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya yāvatsaddharmasthitiparyantaniṣṭhaṃ buddhavikurvitaṃ tatsarvamanena asaṅgasmṛtiviśuddhavyūhena bodhisattvavimokṣeṇānusmarāmi dhārayāmi saṃdhārayāmi upadhārayāmi
anusmarāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vigatatamondhakārāṇāṃ saṃsārarātriprabhāvitānāṃ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the divine maiden named <s>Surendrābhā</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'I, son of good family, am the recipient of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Asaṅgasmṛtiviśuddhavyūha</s> (Array of the Purification of Unattached Mindfulness). I, son of good family, recall: there was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Utpalaka</s> (Lotus). Therein <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were propitiated by me. I provided protection as they went forth, performed worship, and made pleasure-grounds for their use. And whatever disciplining and ripening of beings was accomplished by those <s>Bhagavān Buddhas</s>, when as <s>bodhisattvas</s> they were in the mother's womb, being born, taking seven steps, uttering the great lion's roar, dwelling on the youth-stage, dwelling in the inner palace, going forth, awakening to <s>Bodhi</s>, turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, or displaying all <s>Buddha</s>-transformations — all that, from the first generation of the mind up to the end of the true <s>Dharma</s>, I know, recall, recollect, retain, uphold, preserve, and follow. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Subhūti</s> (Well-Being); therein ten Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Subhaga</s> (Fortunate); therein <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of a <s>Buddha</s>-field were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Anilambha</s> (Unsupported); therein eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Suprabha</s> (Beautiful Radiance); therein <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Atulaprabha</s> (Incomparable Radiance); therein twenty Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Uttaptaśrī</s> (Heated Glory); therein Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Sūryodaya</s> (Sunrise); therein eighty Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Jayaṃgama</s> (Victorious Going); therein sixty Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. There was a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Sucandra</s> (Beautiful Moon); therein seventy Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>Tathāgatas</s> were propitiated by me. Thus, son of good family, by this method I recall Gaṅgā-sand-number <s>kalpas</s>, during which I was constantly and continuously never separated from <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. In the presence of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, this <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the Array of the Purification of Unattached Mindfulness was heard by me. Having heard it, it was cultivated, and practiced as taught. Thus I continually practice this liberation.

body.text: vigatanivaraṇānāmanidrāgamānāṃ vigatastyānamiddhānāṃ prasrabdhakāyasaṃskārāṇāṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvānubodhasuviśuddhānāṃ daśabalaviśuddhibodhayitṝṇāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: — those whose hindrances are removed, who are free from drowsiness, whose sloth and torpor have departed, whose bodily formations are tranquil, who are well-purified in the awakening to the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, who awaken others to the purification of the ten powers — to know their conduct or speak of their qualities? //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, kapilavastuni mahānagare viśvāmitro nāma dārakācāryaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. In the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> there dwells a boys' teacher named <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'cintyakuśalamūlavegasaṃvardhitaḥ surendrābhāyā devakanyāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya surendrābhāṃ devakanyāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya surendrābhāyā devakanyāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 43 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son — delighted, elated, overjoyed, born of gladness and mental happiness, nourished by the force of inconceivable roots of merit — bowed his head at the feet of the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s>, circumambulated the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing upon her again and again, departed from the presence of the divine maiden <s>Surendrābhā</s>. // 45 //

body.text: 46 Viśvāmitraḥ /
body.translated_text: 46. <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako tridaśendrabhavanādavatīrya anupūrveṇa yena kapilavastuni mahānagare viśvāmitro dārakācāryastenopajagāma / upetya viśvāmitrasya dārakācāryasya pādau śirasābhivandya viśvāmitraṃ dārakācāryamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya viśvāmitrasya dārakācāryasya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / evamukte viśvāmitro dārakācāryaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - ayaṃ kulaputra śilpābhijño nāma śreṣṭhidārako bodhisattvāllipijñānaṃ śikṣitaḥ / etamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha / eṣa te nirdekṣyati yathā bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, yathā pratipattavyam // 44 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having descended from the palace of the lord of the <s>Tridaśas</s> (Thirty [gods]), gradually approached <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the boys' teacher in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the boys' teacher, circumambulated <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the boys' teacher many hundreds of thousands of times, stood before <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the boys' teacher with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble one gives admonition and instruction to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the noble one tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' Thus addressed, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the boys' teacher spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'This, son of good family, is a merchant's son named <s>Śilpābhijña</s> (Skilled in Crafts), who has learned the knowledge of writing from the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Approach him and ask. He will explain to you how to train and practice in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct.' // 44 //

body.text: 47 śilpābhijñaḥ /
body.translated_text: 47. <s>Śilpābhijña</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena śilpābhijño śreṣṭhidārakastenopasaṃkramya śilpābhijñasya śreṣṭhidārakasya pādau śirasābhivandya śilpābhijñasya śreṣṭhidārakasya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the merchant's son <s>Śilpābhijña</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the merchant's son <s>Śilpābhijña</s>, stood before the merchant's son <s>Śilpābhijña</s> with palms joined, and spoke thus: 'Noble one, I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But I do not know how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble one gives admonition and instruction to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. May the noble one tell me: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra śilpābhijñāvato bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / tasya me kulaputra mātṛkāṃ vācayamānasya akāramakṣaraṃ parikīrtayato bodhisattvānubhāvena asaṃbhinnaviṣayaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / rakāraṃ parikīrtayato 'nantatalasaṃbhedaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / pakāraṃ parikīrtayato dharmadhātutalasaṃbhedaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / cakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ samantacakravibhakticchedanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / nakāraṃ parikīrtayato 'nilayapratilabdhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / lakāraṃ parikīrtayato vigatānālayavimalaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / dakāraṃ parikīrtayato 'vaivartyaprayogaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / bakāraṃ parikīrtayato vajramaṇḍalaṃ nāma prajñāpārabhitāmukhamavakrāntam / ḍakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ samantacakraṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / sakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sāgaragarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / vakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ samantavirūḍhaviṭhapanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / takāraṃ parikīrtayato jyotirmaṇḍalaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / yakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ saṃbhedakūṭaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ṣṭakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ samantadāhapraśamanaprabhāsaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / kakāraṃ parikīrtayato 'saṃbhinnameghaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ṣakāraṃ parikīrtayato abhimukhapravarṣaṇapralambaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / makāraṃ parikīrtayato mahāvegavicitravegaśikharaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / gakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ samantatalaviṭhapanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / thakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ tathatāsaṃbhedagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / jakāraṃ parikīrtayato jagatsaṃsāraviśuddhivigāhanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / svakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvabuddhasmṛtivyūhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / dhakāraṃ parikīrtayato dharmamaṇḍalavicāravicayaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / śakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvabuddhānuśāsanīcakrarocaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / khakāraṃ parikīrtayato 'bhisaṃskārahetubhūmijñānagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / kṣakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ karmaniśāntasāgarakośavicayaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / stakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvakleśavikiraṇaviśuddhiprabhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ñakāraṃ parikīrtayato lokasaṃbhavavijñaptimukhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / thakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ saṃsārapraticakrajñānamaṇḍalaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmuikhamavakrāntam / bhakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvabhavanamaṇḍalavijñaptivyūhaṃ
body.translated_text: He replied: 'I, son of good family, am the recipient of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Śilpābhijñāvat</s> (Possessed of Knowledge of Crafts). As I, son of good family, recite the syllabary — when I pronounce the syllable <s>a</s>, by the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Asaṃbhinnaviṣaya</s> (Undivided Domain) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ra</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Anantatalasaṃbheda</s> (Penetration of the Infinite Surface) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>pa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Dharmadhātutalasaṃbheda</s> (Penetration of the Surface of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ca</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantacakravibhakticchedana</s> (Cutting the Division of the Universal Wheel) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>na</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Anilayapratilabdha</s> (Attained through Non-Abiding) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>la</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Vigatānālayavimala</s> (Stainless and Free from Abode-Attachment) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>da</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Avaivartyaprayoga</s> (Irreversible Application) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ba</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Vajramaṇḍala</s> (Vajra-Maṇḍala) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ḍa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantacakra</s> (Universal Wheel) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>sa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sāgaragarbha</s> (Ocean-Womb) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>va</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantavirūḍhaviṭhapana</s> (Establishment of Universal Growth) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ta</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Jyotirmaṇḍala</s> (Light-Maṇḍala) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ya</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Saṃbhedakūṭa</s> (Peak of Penetration) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ṣṭa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantadāhapraśamanaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of Pacifying Universal Burning) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ka</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Asaṃbhinnamegha</s> (Undivided Cloud) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ṣa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Abhimukhapravarṣaṇapralamba</s> (Suspended Raining Facing Forward) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ma</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Mahāvegavicitravegaśikhara</s> (Peak of Great Velocity and Variegated Velocity) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ga</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Samantatalaviṭhapana</s> (Establishment of the Universal Surface) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>tha</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Tathatāsaṃbhedagarbha</s> (Womb of Penetrating Suchness) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ja</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Jagatsaṃsāraviśuddhivigāhana</s> (Plunging into the Purification of Worldly <s>Saṃsāra</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>sva</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvabuddhasmṛtivyūha</s> (Array of the Recollection of All <s>Buddhas</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>dha</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Dharmamaṇḍalavicāravicaya</s> (Investigation of the Examination of the <s>Dharma</s>-Maṇḍala) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>śa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvabuddhānuśāsanīcakraroca</s> (Radiance of the Wheel of All <s>Buddha</s>-Instructions) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>kha</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Abhisaṃskārahetubhūmijñānagarbha</s> (Womb of the Knowledge of the Ground of the Causes of Formations) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>kṣa</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Karmaniśāntasāgarakośavicaya</s> (Investigation of the Treasury of the Ocean of Pacified <s>Karma</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>sta</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvakleśavikiraṇaviśuddhiprabha</s> (Radiance of Purification Scattering All <s>Kleśas</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>ña</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Lokasaṃbhavavijñaptimukha</s> (Gateway of the Cognition of World-Arising) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>tha</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Saṃsārapraticakrajñānamaṇḍala</s> (Maṇḍala of the Knowledge of the Counter-Wheel of <s>Saṃsāra</s>) is entered. When I pronounce the syllable <s>bha</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-gateway called <s>Sarvabhavanamaṇḍalavijñaptivyūha</s> (Array of the Cognition of the Maṇḍala of All Dwellings)

body.text:
nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / chakāraṃ parikīrtayata upacayagarbhaprayogaṃ cāritracchatramaṇḍalabhedaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / smakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ
savarbuddhadaśarnadigabhimukhāvartaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / hvakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvasattvābhavyāvalokanabalasaṃjātagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / tsakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvaguṇasāgarapratipattyavatāravigāhanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ghakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvadharmameghasaṃdhāraṇadṛḍhasāgaragarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ṭhakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvabuddhapraṇidhānadigabhimukhagamanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ṇakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ cakrākṣarākārakoṭivacanaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / phakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvasattvaparipākakoṭīgatamaṇḍalaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / skakāraṃ parikīrtayato bhūmigarbhāsaṅgapratisaṃvitprabhācakraspharaṇaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / syakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sarvabuddhadharmanirdeśaviṣayaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ścakāraṃ parikīrtayataḥ sattvagaganadharmaghananigarjitanirnādaspharaṇaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ṭakāraṃ parikirtayataḥ sattvārthanairātmyakāryātyantapariniṣṭhāpradīpaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam / ḍhakāraṃ parikīrtayato dharmacakrasaṃbhedagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitāmukhamavakrāntam //
body.translated_text: Upon pronouncing the syllable 'cha,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Penetration into the Womb of Accumulation through the Breaking of the Canopy-Circle of Conduct.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'sma,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Turning Toward All Directions of the Vision of All <s>Buddha</s>s.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'hva,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Womb Born from the Power of Beholding All Beings as Without Separate Existence.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'tsa,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Plunging into the Descent of Practice in the Ocean of All Qualities.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'gha,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Firm Ocean-Womb of Upholding All <s>Dharma</s>-Clouds.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'ṭha,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Going Toward All Directions of All <s>Buddha</s>-Vows.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'ṇa,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Utterance of the Limit of the Form of the Syllable-Wheel.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'pha,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Circle Reaching the Limit of the Ripening of All Beings.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'ska,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Spreading of the Radiance-Wheel of Unattached Analytical Knowledge of the Womb of the Stages.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'sya,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Domain of the Exposition of All <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'śca,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Spreading of the Thundering Sound of Dense <s>Dharma</s>-Clouds in the Sky of Beings.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'ṭa,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Lamp of the Ultimate Accomplishment of the Selfless Purpose of Beings.' Upon pronouncing the syllable 'ḍha,' one enters the gate of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'Womb of the Differentiation of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma).' //

body.text: iti hi kulaputra mama mātṛkāṃ vācayata etāni dvācatvāriṃśat prajñāpāramitāmukhapramukhānyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni prajñāpāramitāmukhānyāvakrāntāni / etasya ahaṃ kulaputra śilpābhijñāvato bodhisattvavimokṣasya lābhī / etamahaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ sarvalaukikalokottaraśilpasthānapāramitāprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān va vaktum? yathā sarvaśilpasthānapraveśeṣu sarvalipisaṃkhyāgaṇanānikṣepapraveśeṣu sarvamantrauṣadhividhijñānaprayogaprativedheṣu sarvabhūtagrahajyotiṣāpasmārakākhordavetālapratiṣṭhāneṣu sattvadhātucikitsābhaiṣajyasaṃyogajñāneṣu dhātutantrasaṃyogaprayogeṣu suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālalohitakamusāragalvakeśaraśrīgarbhāśmagarbhasarvaratnasaṃbhavotpattigotrākaramūlyajñāneṣu udyānatapovanagrāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānyabhinirhāreṣu mṛgacakrāṅkavidyāsarvalakṣaṇanimittabhūmicāladigdāholkāpātakṣemākṣemasubhikṣadurbhikṣasarvalaukikāvartanivartapraveśeṣu sarvalokottaradharmavibhaktisūcanādinirdeśapraveśatattvānugamajñāneṣu nāstyāvaraṇaṃ vā vimarśo vā vimatirvā saṃdeho vā saṃśayo vā saṃmoho vā dhaṃdhāyitatvaṃ vā vyābādhikaṃ vā avasādanaṃ vā ajñānaṃ vā anabhisamayo vā //
body.translated_text: Thus, son of good family, when reciting my syllabary, these forty-two gates of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, foremost among immeasurable and innumerable gates of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, are entered. I, son of good family, have attained this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation of one skilled in the arts (<s>śilpābhijña</s>). This I know. But how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who have attained perfection in all worldly and supramundane arts and sciences? For in all entries into the arts, in all entries into writing, calculation, enumeration, and analysis, in all penetrations of the knowledge and application of <s>mantra</s>s, medicines, and procedures, in all establishments concerning <s>bhūta</s>s (spirits), <s>graha</s>s (seizers), astrology, epilepsy, <s>kākhorda</s>s, and <s>vetāla</s>s, in the knowledge of treating beings' constitutions with medicinal combinations, in the application of alchemical and <s>tantra</s> combinations, in the knowledge of the origin, source, mine, and value of gold, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, rubies, <s>musāragalva</s>, cow-bezoard, <s>śrīgarbha</s>, and all precious stones, in the construction of gardens, ascetic groves, villages, cities, towns, countries, and royal capitals, in all entries into the worldly sciences of animal-tracking, markings, all signs and omens, earthquakes, portents, meteor-falls, prosperity and adversity, abundance and famine — in all entries into the discernment, indication, and exposition of all supramundane <s>dharma</s>s and the knowledge of penetrating their reality — there is no obstruction, no hesitation, no doubt, no uncertainty, no suspicion, no confusion, no wavering, no impediment, no depression, no ignorance, no failure of comprehension. //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva magadhaviṣaye kevalake janapade vartanake nagare bhadrottamā nāmopāsikā prativasati / tāmupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in the land of <s>Magadha</s>, in the district of <s>Kevalaka</s>, in the city of <s>Vartanaka</s>, there dwells a lay-woman named <s>Bhadrottamā</s>. Approach her and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ śilpābhijñasya śreṣṭhidārakasya pādau śirasābhivandya śilpābhijñaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya śilpābhijñasya śreṣṭhidārakasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 45 //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the merchant's son <s>Śilpābhijña</s>, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the merchant's son <s>Śilpābhijña</s>. // 45 //

body.text: 48 Bhadrottamā /
body.translated_text: 48. <s>Bhadrottamā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena kevalake janapade vartanakaṃ nagaram, yena ca bhadrottamopāsikā, tenopajagāma / upetya bhadrottamāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhadrottamāmupāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhadrottamāyā upāsikāyāḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārye anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryā bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryā - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son went to the city of <s>Vartanaka</s> in the district of <s>Kevalaka</s>, to the lay-woman <s>Bhadrottamā</s>. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the lay-woman <s>Bhadrottamā</s>, circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before the lay-woman <s>Bhadrottamā</s> with palms joined, spoke thus: 'Noble lady, I have generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble lady gives instruction and counsel to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble lady tell me: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: sā avocat - ahaṃ kulaputra anālayamaṇḍalaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ jānāmi deśayāmi / adhiṣṭhānaśca me samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ / na tatra samādhau kasyaciddharmasyādhiṣṭhānam / tatra sarvajñatācakṣuḥ pravartate 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvajñatāśrotram / adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvajñatāghrāṇam, adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvajñatājihvā, adhiṣṭhānaḥ sarvajñatākāyaḥ, adhiṣṭhānaṃ tatra sarvajñatāmanaḥ pravartate, adhiṣṭhānā sarvajñatormiḥ, adhiṣṭhānā sarvajñatāvidyut, adhiṣṭhānāḥ sarvajñatāvegāḥ pravartante jagadrocanāmaṇḍalāḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra, anālayamaṇḍalaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamasaṅgabodhisattvacaryā sakalā jñātum?
body.translated_text: She replied: 'I, son of good family, know and teach a <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called <s>Anālayamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of Non-Attachment). And I have attained a <s>samādhi</s> of empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>). In that <s>samādhi</s>, there is no basis for any <s>dharma</s>. Therein operates the eye of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) as empowerment, the ear of omniscience as empowerment, the nose of omniscience as empowerment, the tongue of omniscience as empowerment, the body of omniscience as empowerment, the mind of omniscience operates therein as empowerment, the wave of omniscience as empowerment, the lightning of omniscience as empowerment, the surges of omniscience operate therein as circles illuminating the world. I, son of good family, know this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called <s>Anālayamaṇḍala</s>. But how could I know the entire conduct of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s of unattached practice?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra dakṣiṇāpathe / tatra bharukacchaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra muktāsāro nāma hairaṇyakaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, to the southern region. There is a city called <s>Bharukaccha</s>. There dwells a banker named <s>Muktāsāra</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bhadrottamāyā upāsikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhadrottamāmupāsikāmanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya bhadrottamāyā upāsikāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 46 //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the lay-woman <s>Bhadrottamā</s>, circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon her again and again, and departed from the presence of the lay-woman <s>Bhadrottamā</s>. // 46 //

body.text: 49 Muktāsāraḥ /
body.translated_text: 49. <s>Muktāsāra</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa dakṣiṇāpathaṃ gatvā yena bharukacche nagare muktāsāro hairaṇyakaḥ, tenopasaṃkramya muktāsārahairaṇyakasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, traveling gradually to the southern region, went to the banker <s>Muktāsāra</s> in the city of <s>Bharukaccha</s>. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the banker <s>Muktāsāra</s>, and standing before him with palms joined, spoke thus: 'Noble sir, I have generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble sir gives instruction and counsel to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble sir tell me: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgasmṛtivyūhaṃ nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / apratiprasrabdhā ca me daśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu dharmaparyeṣṭiḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra asaṅgasmṛtivyūhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi, prajānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ bodhisattvānāmacchambhitasiṃhanādanādināṃ mahāpuṇyajñānapratiṣṭhitānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: He replied: 'I, son of good family, know a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Asaṅgasmṛtivyūha</s> (Array of Unattached Mindfulness). And my quest for the <s>Dharma</s> at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the ten directions is unrelenting. I, son of good family, know this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Asaṅgasmṛtivyūha</s>. But how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who roar the fearless lion's roar and are established in great merit and knowledge?' //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva bharukacche nagare sucandro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati / tadavabhāsitamasya gṛham / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family, right here in the city of <s>Bharukaccha</s> there dwells a householder named <s>Sucandra</s>. His house is illuminated by that [light]. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako muktāsārasya hairaṇyakasya pādau śirasābhivandya muktāsāraṃ hairaṇyakamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya muktāsārasya hairaṇyakasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 47 //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the banker <s>Muktāsāra</s>, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the banker <s>Muktāsāra</s>. // 47 //

body.text: 50 Sucandraḥ /
body.translated_text: 50. <s>Sucandra</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako yena sucandro gṛhapatiḥ, tenopasaṃkramya sucandrasya gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātītī / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son approached the householder <s>Sucandra</s>. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, and standing before him with palms joined, spoke thus: 'Noble sir, I have generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble sir gives instruction and counsel to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble sir tell me: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: āha - mayā kulaputra vimalajñānaprabho nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ / etamahaṃ kulaputra vimalajñānaprabhaṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyamapramāṇavimokṣapratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: He replied: 'I, son of good family, have attained a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vimalajñānaprabha</s> (Radiance of Stainless Knowledge). I, son of good family, know this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Vimalajñānaprabha</s>. But how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who have attained immeasurable liberations?' //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, idamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe rorukaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra ajitaseno nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in the southern region there is a city called <s>Roruka</s>. There dwells a householder named <s>Ajitasena</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ sucandrasya gṛhapateḥ pādua śirasābhivandya sucandraṃ gṛhapatimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya sucandrasya gṛhapaterantikātprakrāntaḥ // 48 //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son bowed his head at the feet of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him again and again, and departed from the presence of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>. // 48 //

body.text: 51 Ajitasenaḥ /
body.translated_text: 51. <s>Ajitasena</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa rorukaṃ nagaraṃ gatvā yena ajitaseno nāma gṛhapatistenopasaṃkramya ajitasenasya gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadātīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, traveling gradually to the city of <s>Roruka</s>, approached the householder <s>Ajitasena</s>. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the householder <s>Ajitasena</s>, and standing before him with palms joined, spoke thus: 'Noble sir, I have generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). But I do not know how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, or how one should practice. I have heard that the noble sir gives instruction and counsel to <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. May the noble sir tell me: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: āha - mayā kulaputra akṣayalakṣaṇo nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yasya sahapratilambhādakṣayabuddhadarśananidhānapratilābho bhavati //
body.translated_text: He replied: 'I, son of good family, have attained a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Akṣayalakṣaṇa</s> (Inexhaustible Characteristic), upon attaining which one gains the inexhaustible treasury of seeing <s>Buddha</s>s.' //

body.text: gaccha kulaputra iyamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe dharmagrāme śivarāgro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in the southern region, in <s>Dharmagrāma</s>, there dwells a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śivarāgra</s>. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct? How should one practice?' //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'jitasenasya gṛhapateḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ajitasenaṃ gṛhapatimanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya ajitasenasya gṛhapaterantikātprakrāntaḥ // 49 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having bowed his head at the feet of the householder <s>Ajitasena</s>, circumambulated the householder <s>Ajitasena</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of the householder <s>Ajitasena</s>. // 49 //

body.text: 52 śivarāgraḥ /
body.translated_text: 52. <s>Śivarāgra</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa dharmagrāmaṃ gatvā yena śivarāgro brāhmaṇaḥ, tenopasaṃkramya śivarāgrasya brāhmaṇasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā ārya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryo bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ dadādīti / tadvadatu me āryaḥ - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, traveling gradually, went to <s>Dharmagrāma</s> and approached <s>Śivarāgra</s> the brahmin. Having bowed his head at the feet of <s>Śivarāgra</s> the brahmin and standing before him with palms joined, he spoke thus: O noble one, I have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Yet I do not know — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice? And I have heard that the noble one gives instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, may the noble one tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice?

body.text: so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra satyādhiṣṭhānena carāmi / yena satyena satyavacanena tryadhvasu na kaścidbodhisattvo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhervivṛttaḥ, na vivartate, na vivartiṣyati, tena satyavacanādhiṣṭhānena idaṃ ca me kāryaṃ smṛdhyatviti / tanme yathābhiprāyaṃ sarvaṃ samṛdhyati / etenāhaṃ kulaputra satyavacanādhiṣṭhānena sarvakāryāṇi sādhayāmi / etamahaṃ kulaputra satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ mayā śakyaṃ satyānuparivartanī vākpratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: He replied: I, son of good family, abide by the foundation of truth. By this truth, by this true speech — that in the three times no <s>bodhisattva</s> has ever turned back from supreme perfect awakening, nor turns back, nor shall turn back — by the foundation of that true speech, 'may this undertaking of mine succeed!' And thus all things succeed for me according to my intention. By this foundation of true speech, son of good family, I accomplish all undertakings. This foundation of truth, son of good family, is what I know. How could I be capable of knowing the conduct or speaking of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained speech that follows truth?

body.text: gaccha kulaputra, iyamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe sumanāmukhaṃ nāma nagaram / tatra śrīsaṃbhavo nāma dārakaḥ prativasati, śrīmatiśca nāma dārikā / tāvupasaṃkramya paripṛccha kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Go, son of good family. Right here in the southern region there is a city called <s>Sumanāmukha</s>. There dwells a boy named <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and a girl named <s>Śrīmatī</s>. Approach them and ask — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahādharmagauravamutpādya śivarāgrasya brāhmaṇasya pādau śirasābhivandya śivarāgraṃ brāhmaṇamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥpunaravalokya śivarāgrasya brāhmaṇasyāntikātprakrāntaḥ // 50 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having generated great reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Śivarāgra</s> the brahmin, circumambulated <s>Śivarāgra</s> the brahmin many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of <s>Śivarāgra</s> the brahmin. // 50 //

body.text: 53 śrīsaṃbhavaḥ śrīmatiśca /
body.translated_text: 53. <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and <s>Śrīmatī</s>. /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nupūrveṇa sumanāmukhanagaraṃ gatvā yena śrīsaṃbhavo dārakaḥ śrīmatiśca dārikā / tāvupakramya tayoḥ pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvā evamāha - mayā āryau anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / na ca jānāmi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam / śrutaṃ ca me āryau bodhisattvānāmavavādānuśāsanīṃ datta iti / tadvadatāṃ me āryau - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, traveling gradually, went to the city of <s>Sumanāmukha</s> and approached the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s>. Having bowed his head at the feet of those two and standing before them with palms joined, he spoke thus: O noble ones, I have generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Yet I do not know — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice? And I have heard that the noble ones give instruction and admonition to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, may the noble ones tell me — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice?

body.text: atha khalu śrīsaṃbhavo dārakaḥ śrīmatiśca dārikā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocatām - iha āvābhyāṃ kulaputra māyāgato nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ pratilabdhaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ / tāvāvāṃ kulaputra anena vimokṣeṇa samanvāgatau māyāgataṃ sarvalokaṃ paśyāvo hetupratyayamāyāsaṃbhūtam / māyāgatān sarvasattvān vijānīvaḥ / karmakleśamāyājñānena māyāgataṃ sarvajagatpaśyāvaḥ / avidyābhavatṛṣṇāmāyāsaṃbhavān māyāgatān sarvadharmān paśyāvaḥ / anyonyapratyayamāyānirvṛttaṃ māyāgataṃ sarvatraidhātukaṃ paśyāvaḥ abhinirhṛtamacintyaviṣayamāyābodhiviparyāsamāyāsaṃbhūtam / māyāgatān sarvasattvān cyutyupapattijātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsān paśyāvaḥ / asadbhūtasaṃkalpamāyājanitāni māyājanitāni sarvakṣetrāṇi paśyāvaḥ / saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsamāyābhāvadravyasaṃjñāsaṃmohaprabhavān māyāgatān sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhān paśyāvaḥ / jñānaprahāṇamāyāsaṃkalpajanitāṃ māyāgatāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānasattvaparipākavinayaparaṃparāṃ prajānīvaḥ / māyānirhārābhinirvṛttanirmitacaryāvinayamāyāsvabhāvān māyāgataṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvamaṇḍalaṃ paśyāvaḥ praṇidhānajñānamāyābhinirhṛtamacintyaviṣayamāyāsvabhāvam / etamāvāṃ kulaputra māyāgataṃ bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ prajānīvaḥ / kimāvābhyāṃ śakyamanantakarmamāyāviṭhapajālānugatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāṃ jñātuṃ guṇān vā vaktum //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s> spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: Here, son of good family, we two have attained and directly realized the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Māyāgata</s> (Arrived through Illusion). Endowed with this liberation, we two see the entire world as arrived through illusion, arisen from the illusion of causes and conditions. We understand all beings as arrived through illusion. Through the illusion-knowledge of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), we see the entire world as arrived through illusion. We see all <s>dharmas</s> as arrived through illusion, arisen from the illusion of ignorance, existence, and craving. We see the entire triple world as arrived through illusion, produced by the illusion of mutual conditions — manifested in an inconceivable domain, arisen from the illusion of the perversion of illusion-awakening. We see all beings as arrived through illusion, with their death and rebirth, birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. We see all fields as arrived through illusion, generated by the illusion of unreal conceptual constructions. We see all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) as arrived through illusion, arisen from the illusion of the perversion of perception, thought, and view, and the delusion of the notion of substance in non-being. We understand the entire succession of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, vows, and ripening and training of beings as arrived through illusion, generated by the illusion-conceptualization of wisdom and abandonment. We see the entire maṇḍala of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> as arrived through illusion, of illusion-nature, manifested through the creation-conduct of illusion-manifestation, of an inconceivable domain, brought forth through the illusion of vow-knowledge, of illusion-nature. This <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>Māyāgata</s> (Arrived through Illusion) is what we two know, son of good family. How could we be capable of knowing the conduct or speaking of the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who follow the net of magical displays of infinite <s>karma</s>-illusion?

body.text: atha khalu śrīsaṃbhavo dārakaḥ śrīmatiśca dārikā sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamacintyena kuśalamūlavegena abhiṣyandayitvā svaṃ ca vimokṣaviṣayaṃ śrāvya etadavocatām - gaccha kulaputra, ayamihaiva dakṣiṇāpathe samudrakaccho nāma digmukhapratyuddeśaḥ / tatra mahāvyūhaṃ nāmodyānam / tatra vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbho nāma mahākūṭāgāro bodhisattvakuśalamūlavipākābhinirvṛto bodhisattvacetanāmanasikārasaṃbhūto bodhisattvapraṇidhānasamudgato bodhisattvavaśitāsamutthito bodhisattvābhijñānabalābhinirmito bodhisattvopāyakauśalyasaṃbhūto bodhisattvapuṇyajñānabalapariniṣpanno bodhisattvamahākaruṇāsattvavinayasaṃdarśano bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānavyūhopacito bodhisattvācintyavimokṣavihārālaṃkāraḥ / tatra maitreyo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prativasati janmabhūmikānāṃ manuṣyāṇāmanugrahāya / mātāpitṛjñātisaṃbandhināṃ paripākāya / tatropapannānāṃ sabhāgacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ mahāyānadṛḍhīkaraṇāya / tadanyeṣāmapi sattvānāṃ yathābhūmiṣu kuśalamūlaparipācanāya / svasya ca vimokṣanayāvatārasya saṃdarśanāya /
body.translated_text: Then indeed the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s>, having saturated <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son with the inconceivable momentum of their roots of merit, and having told him of their own liberation-domain, spoke thus: Go, son of good family. Right here in the southern region there is a district called <s>Samudrakaccha</s> (Ocean Shore). There is a garden called <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array). In it is a great pavilion called <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> (Womb of the Array and Ornament of <s>Vairocana</s>) — produced by the ripening of the roots of merit of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, arisen from the volition and mental attention of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, generated from the vows of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, arisen from the mastery of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, magically created by the power of the supernatural knowledge of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, arisen from the skillful means of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, perfected by the power of the merit and wisdom of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, displaying the training of beings through the great compassion of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, enriched with the array of the empowerment of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, adorned with the dwelling in the inconceivable liberation of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. There the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) named <s>Maitreya</s> dwells — for the benefit of humans on the stage of birth, for the ripening of parents, relatives, and kinsmen, for the strengthening of beings of similar conduct born there in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, for the ripening of roots of merit of other beings also in their respective stages, and for the demonstration of his own method of entry into liberation.

body.text:
sarvatrānugatāṃ ca bodhisattvopapattivaśitāṃ prabhāvayan sarvasattvajanmasaṃdarśanābhimukhatayā ca sattvaparipākāriñcanatāyai / sarvajagatparigrahajugupsanatayā ca bodhisattvamahākaruṇābalodbhāvanāya / sarvaniketasthānoccalitaṃ ca bodhisattvavihāramavabodhanāya / aniketaparamaṃ ca sarvabhavopattisaṃvāsasaṃdarśanāya / tamupasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryā paripraṣṭavyā, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvamārgaḥ pariśodhayitavyaḥ, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvaśikṣāsu pratipattavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhicittaṃ pratiśodhayitavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvapraṇidhānamabhinirhartavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvasaṃbhārāḥ samutthāpayitavyāḥ, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvabhūmaya ākramitavyāḥ, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvapāramitāḥ paripūrayitavyāḥ, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvakṣāntayo 'vataritavyāḥ, kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvapratipattiguṇeṣu sthātavyam, kathaṃ bodhisattvena kalyāṇamitrāṇi
paryupāsitavyāni / tatkasya hetoḥ? sa hi kulaputra maitreyo bodhisattvo 'vatīrṇaḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsu gatiṃgataḥ / sarvabodhisattvacittāśayeṣu so 'nupraviṣṭaḥ / sarvasattvacaryāsu so 'bhimukhaḥ sarvasattvaparipākavinayeṣu / tena paripūritāḥ sarvapāramitāḥ / supratiṣṭhitāḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmiṣu / tena pratilabdhāḥ sarvabodhisattvakṣāntayaḥ / so 'vakrānto bodhisattvaniyāmam / tena pratīṣṭāni sarvavyākaraṇāni / sa vikrīḍitaḥ sarvabodhisattvavimokṣeṣu / tena saṃdhāritāni sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānāni / so 'bhiṣiktaḥ sarvatathāgataiḥ sarvajñajñānaviṣayābhiṣekeṇa / sa te kulaputra kalyāṇamitro 'bhiṣyandayiṣyati sarvakuśalamūlāni vivardhayiṣyati / bodhicittotpādaṃ dṛḍhīkariṣyati / adhyāśayadhātumuttāpayiṣyati / sarvakuśalamūlāni vivardhayiṣyati / bodhisattvendriyavegān saṃdarśayiṣyati / anāvaraṇadharmadiśaṃ praveśayiṣyati / samantabhadrabhūmyanugame niveśayiṣyati / sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānaniryāṇamukheṣu saṃvarṇayiṣyati / sarvabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānaguṇapariniṣpattimākhyāsyati samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāśravaṇaparyāyadvāram / na ca te kulaputra ekakuśalamūlatanmayena bhavitavyaṃ naikadharmamukhālokāvabhāsaparameṇa naikacaryāparisaṃtuṣṭena naikapraṇidhānābhinirhāraparameṇa naikavyākaraṇena, na niṣṭhāpratiprasrabdhena, na trikṣāntyavatāraparamasaṃjñinā, na ṣaṭpāramitāparipūriprasrabdhena, na daśabhūmipratilābhaniṣṭhāgatena, na prāmāṇikabuddhakṣetraparigrahapariśuddhipraṇidhānena, na pramāṇīkṛtakalyāṇamitrārāgaṇaparyupāsanasaṃtuṣṭena bhavitavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? apramāṇāni hi kulaputra bodhisattvena kuśalamūlāni samudānetavyāni / apramāṇā bodhisattvasaṃbhārā utthāpayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā bodhicittahetavaḥ samārjayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā nayāḥ śikṣitavyāḥ / apramāṇāḥ sattvadhātuḥ parinirvāpayitavyaḥ
/ apramāṇā sattvāśayadhāturanupraveṣṭavyā / apramāṇāni sattvendriyāṇi parijñātavyāni / apramāṇā sattvavimuktiranuvartayitavyā / apramāṇāḥ sattvadhātucaryā anubodhyavyāḥ / apramāṇasattvavinayaḥ kartavyaḥ / apramāṇāḥ kleśānuśayāḥ samuddhāṭayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni karmāvaraṇāni pariśodhayitavyāni / apramāṇāni dṛṣṭigatāni
body.translated_text:
Manifesting the mastery of <s>bodhisattva</s>-birth that follows everywhere, for the sake of unstinting ripening of beings by facing toward the display of the birth of all beings; for the cultivation of the great compassion-power of the <s>bodhisattva</s> through revulsion at the clinging to the entire world; for the realization of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-dwelling that has departed from all fixed abodes; and for the demonstration of dwelling in birth in all existences, which is supremely without fixed abode. Approach him and ask — how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> inquire about <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> purify the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> practice in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-trainings, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> purify the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> bring forth the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vow, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> produce the <s>bodhisattva</s>-provisions, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> ascend the <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> fulfill the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>pāramitās</s>, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> enter the <s>bodhisattva</s>-patiences, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> abide in the qualities of <s>bodhisattva</s>-practice, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> attend upon
spiritual friends? For what reason? Because, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> has descended into all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts and reached their destination. He has entered into the mental dispositions of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. He faces toward the conduct of all beings for their ripening and training. He has fulfilled all <s>pāramitās</s>. He is well-established on all <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages. He has attained all <s>bodhisattva</s>-patiences. He has entered the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. He has received all predictions. He has sported in all <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberations. He has upheld the empowerment of all <s>Buddhas</s>. He has been consecrated by all <s>Tathāgatas</s> with the consecration of the domain of omniscient wisdom. He, son of good family, as your spiritual friend, shall saturate all your roots of merit and cause them to grow. He shall strengthen your generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>. He shall kindle the element of your aspiration. He shall cause all roots of merit to grow. He shall reveal the force of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-faculties. He shall cause you to enter the direction of unobstructed <s>Dharma</s>. He shall establish you in following the ground of <s>Samantabhadra</s>. He shall praise the gateway-mouths of the fruition of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows. He shall declare the accomplishment of the qualities of the vow-conduct of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — the gateway-chapter for hearing the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. But you, son of good family, must not be one who is absorbed in a single root of merit, nor one whose supreme [attainment] is the illumination of a single <s>Dharma</s>-door, nor one content with a single practice, nor one whose supreme [attainment] is the bringing forth of a single vow, nor one [satisfied] with a single prediction, nor one who relaxes at the culmination, nor one who considers the entry into the three patiences as the supreme, nor one who relaxes at the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, nor one who considers himself as having reached the culmination at the attainment of the ten stages, nor one whose vow for purification involves the embrace of a limited <s>Buddha</s>-field, nor one content with attending upon a limited number of spiritual friends. For what reason? Because immeasurable are the roots of merit to be gathered by a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Immeasurable are the <s>bodhisattva</s>-provisions to be produced. Immeasurable are the causes of <s>bodhicitta</s> to be assembled. Immeasurable are the methods to be trained in. Immeasurable is the realm of beings to be led to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Immeasurable are the elements of the dispositions of beings to be entered into. Immeasurable are the faculties of beings to be fully known. Immeasurable is the liberation of beings to be followed. nivartayitavyāni / apramāṇāścittasaṃkleśā apanayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāścittaviśuddhaya utpādayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā duḥkhaśalyāḥ samuddhārayitavyāḥ / apramāṇaḥ sattvatṛṣṇārṇavaḥ samucchoṣitavyaḥ / apramāṇamavidyāndhakāraṃ vidhamitavyam / apramāṇāḥ parvatāḥ prapātayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni saṃsārabandhanāni nirhārayitavyāni / apramāṇo janmasamudraḥ śoṣayitavyaḥ / apramāṇo bhavaughastaritavyāḥ / apramāṇāḥ sattvāḥ kāmapaṅkasaktā abhyuddhartavyāḥ / apramāṇāstraidhātukapuraniruddhāḥ sattvā niṣkrāmayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāḥ sattvā āryamārge pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā rāgadveṣamohāḥ praśamayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā mārapāśāḥ samatikramayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni mārakarmāṇi vinivartayitavyāni / apramāṇo bodhisattvādhyāśayadhātuḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā bodhisattvaprayogā vivardhayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni bodhisattvendriyāṇi saṃjanayitavyāni / apramāṇā bodhisattvādhimuktayo viśodhayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā bodhisattvasamatā avatārayitavyāḥ / apramāṇo bodhisattvacaryāviśeṣo 'nusartavyaḥ / apramāṇā bodhisattvaguṇāḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā bodhisattvacāritracaryāḥ pratipūrayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni lokacāritrāṇyanuvartayitavyāni / apramāṇā lokānuvartanāḥ saṃdarśayitavyāḥ / apramāṇaṃ śraddhābalaṃ saṃjanayitavyām / apramāṇaṃ vīryabalamupastambhayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ smṛtibalaṃ pariśodhayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ samādhibalaṃ pariśodhayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ prajñābalamutpādayitavyam / apramāṇamadhimuktibalaṃ dṛḍhīkartavyam / apramāṇaṃ puṇyabalaṃ samupārjayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ jñānabalaṃ vivardhayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ bodhisattvabalaṃ samutthāpayitavyam / apramāṇaṃ buddhabalaṃ paripūrayitavyam / apramāṇāni dharmamukhāni pravicetavyāni / apramāṇā dharmadiśaḥ praveṣṭavyāḥ / apramāṇāni dharmadvārāṇi pariśodhayitavyāni / apramāṇā dharmālokāḥ saṃjanayitavyāḥ / apramāṇo dharmāvabhāsaḥ kartavyaḥ / apramāṇā indriyavaṃśā avabhāsayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāḥ kleśavyādhayaḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ
/ apramāṇāni dharmabhaiṣajyāni samudānetavyāni / apramāṇaḥ kleśavyādhyāturaḥ sattvadhātuḥ cikitsitavyaḥ / apramāṇā amṛtasaṃbhārāḥ samudānetavyāḥ / apramāṇāni buddhakṣetrāṇyākramitavyāni / apramāṇāstathāgatāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ / apramāṇāni bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalānyavagāhayitavyāni / apramāṇāni tathāgataśāsanāni saṃdhārayitavyāni / apramāṇāni sattvadrohiṇyāni soḍhavyāni / apramāṇā akṣaṇāpāyapathāḥ samucchettavyāḥ / apramāṇāni sattvasukhānyupasaṃhartavyāni / apramāṇāḥ sattvasaṃgrahāḥ kartavyāḥ / apramāṇāni dhāraṇīmukhāni pariśodhayitavyāni / apramāṇāni praṇidhānamukhānyabhinirhartavyāni / apramāṇāni mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇābalāni paribhāvayitavyāni / apramāṇāni dharmaparyeṣṭyabhiyogāni na pratiprasrambhayitavyāni / apramāṇāni nidhyaptibalānyanusartavyāni / apramāṇā abhijñābhinirhārā utpādayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā vidyājñānālokā viśodhayitavyāḥ / apramāṇā sattvagatiranugantavyā / apramāṇā bhavotpattiḥ
