parigrahītavyāḥ / apramāṇā kāyavibhaktiḥ saṃdarśayitavyā / apramāṇā mantravibhaktiḥ parijñātavyā / apramāṇāḥ sattvacittavimātratā anupraveṣṭavyāḥ / vistīrṇo bodhisattvagocaro 'nupraveṣṭavyaḥ / vipulaṃ bodhisattvabhavanamanuvicaritavyam / gambhīro bodhisattvavihāro vyavalokayitavyaḥ / duranubodho bodhisattvaviṣayo 'nuboddhavyaḥ / durgamā bodhisattvagatirgantavyā / durāsadā bodhisattvavegāḥ saṃdhārayitavyāḥ / duravakrāmo bodhisattvaniyāmo 'vakramitavyaḥ / vicitrā bodhisattvacaryā anuboddhavyā / sarvatrānugataṃ bodhisattvavikurvaṇaṃ saṃdarśayitavyam / abhisaṃbhinnā bodhisattvena dharmameghāḥ saṃpratyeṣṭavyāḥ / anantamadhyaṃ bodhisattvacaryājālaṃ pravistaritavyam / aparyantā bodhisattvena pāramitāḥ paripūrayitavyāḥ / aprameyāṇi bodhisattvena vyākaraṇāni saṃpratyeṣṭavyāni / asaṃkhyeyāni bodhisattvena kṣāntimukhānyavatartavyāni / asaṃkhyeyā bodhisattvena bhūmayaḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ / asamantāni bodhisattvena dharmamukhāni paryavadāpayitavyāni / anabhilāpyāni bodhisattvena buddhakṣetrāṇi pariśodhayitavyāni / aparyantān bodhisattvena kalpān saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddhavyaḥ / amāpyā bodhisattvena tathāgatāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ
/ acintyā bodhisattvena praṇidhānābhinirhārā abhinirhartavyāḥ / saṃkṣiptena kulaputra sarvasattvasamoktā bodhisattvānāṃ caryā sattvaparipācanatayā / sarvakalpasamoktā sarvakalpasaṃvasanatayā / sarvopapattisamoktā sarvatrajanmasaṃdarśanena / sarvādhvasamoktā tryadhvajñānānubodhāya / sarvadharmasamoktā tatpratipattyā / sarvakṣetrasamoktā tatpariśodhanena / sarvapraṇidhānasamoktā tatparipūraṇatayā / sarvabuddhasamoktā tatpūjābhinirhāreṇa / sarvabodhisattvasamoktā tatpraṇidhānaikatvena / sarvakalyāṇamitrasamoktā bodhisattvānāṃ caryā tadārāgaṇatayā //
body.translated_text: must be embraced. Immeasurable differentiations of body must be demonstrated. Immeasurable differentiations of <s>mantras</s> must be fully known. The immeasurable varieties of the minds of beings must be penetrated. The vast domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be entered. The vast dwelling of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be explored. The profound abiding of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be examined. The hard-to-comprehend domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be comprehended. The hard-to-reach course of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be traversed. The hard-to-approach forces of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be upheld. The hard-to-enter fixed course of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be entered. The variegated conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be comprehended. The universally-following magical display of the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be demonstrated. The undivided <s>Dharma</s>-clouds must be received by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. The net of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, infinite and without middle, must be spread forth. The boundless <s>pāramitās</s> must be fulfilled by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Immeasurable prophecies must be received by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Innumerable gateways of patience must be entered by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Innumerable stages must be purified by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Unlimited <s>Dharma</s>-gateways must be perfected by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields must be purified by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. For boundless <s>kalpas</s>, the armor must be donned by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s> must be worshipped by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Inconceivable accomplishments of vows must be accomplished by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. In brief, son of good family, the conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is co-extensive with all beings, for the purpose of ripening beings; co-extensive with all <s>kalpas</s>, through dwelling in all <s>kalpas</s>; co-extensive with all births, through demonstrating birth everywhere; co-extensive with all times, for the awakening to the knowledge of the three times; co-extensive with all <s>dharmas</s>, through the practice of them; co-extensive with all fields, through their purification; co-extensive with all vows, through their fulfillment; co-extensive with all <s>Buddhas</s>, through accomplishing their worship; co-extensive with all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, through oneness with their vows; co-extensive with all spiritual friends — the conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is [thus co-extensive] through pleasing them. //

body.text: tasmāttarhi kulaputra na te parikheda utpādayitavyaḥ kalyāṇamitraparimārgaṇāsu / na paritṛptirutpādayitavyā kalyāṇamitrasaṃdarśaneṣu / na parituṣṭirāpattavyā kalyāṇamitraparipṛcchāsu / nāśayo vinivartayitavyaḥ kalyāṇamitrasaṃsargeṣu / na prayogaḥ pratiprasrambhayitavyaḥ kalyāṇamitragauravopasthāneṣu / na vilomagrāhiṇā bhavitavyaṃ kalyāṇamitrāvavādānuśāsanīṣu / na saṃśaya utpādayitavyaḥ kalyāṇamitraguṇapratilābheṣu / na vicikitsā karaṇīyā kalyāṇamitraniryāṇamukhasaṃdarśaneṣu / na doṣotpādanaṃ karaṇīyaṃ kalyāṇamitropāyasaṃdhilokānuvartanapraticāreṣu / na kāyacittavinivartanaṃ karaṇīyaṃ kalyāṇamitraprasādavivardhaneṣu / tatkasya hetoḥ? kalyāṇamitrādhīnāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāḥśravāḥ / kalyāṇamitraprabhavāḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇapariniṣpattayaḥ / kalyāṇamitraprabhavāṇi sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānasrotāṃsi / kalyāṇamitrajanitāni sarvabodhisattvakuśalamūlāni / kalyāṇamitrotthāpitāḥ sarvabodhisattvasaṃbhārāḥ / kalyāṇamitraniryātāḥ sarvabodhisattvadharmamukhālokāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃbhūtāḥ sarvabodhiniryāṇamukhaviśuddhayaḥ / kalyāṇamitrapratibaddhāḥ sarvabodhisattvaśikṣāpratipattayaḥ / kalyāṇamitrapratiṣṭhitāḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇadharmāḥ / kalyāṇamitramūlāḥ sarvabodhisattvādhyāśayapariśuddhayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, son of good family, you should not generate weariness in seeking spiritual friends. You should not generate satisfaction in seeing spiritual friends. You should not reach contentment in questioning spiritual friends. You should not turn your intention away from association with spiritual friends. You should not relax your effort in reverently attending spiritual friends. You should not become one who grasps in opposition to the counsel and instruction of spiritual friends. You should not generate doubt regarding the attainment of the qualities of spiritual friends. You should not harbor uncertainty regarding the demonstrations of the gateways of going forth by spiritual friends. You should not produce fault-finding regarding the expedient means, hidden intentions, and worldly adaptations of spiritual friends. You should not turn away in body or mind from increasing devotion to spiritual friends. For what reason? Because all streams of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct are dependent on spiritual friends, son of good family. All perfections of <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities arise from spiritual friends. All streams of <s>bodhisattva</s> vows arise from spiritual friends. All roots of merit of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are generated by spiritual friends. All provisions of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are raised up by spiritual friends. All lights of the <s>Dharma</s>-gateways of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are bestowed by spiritual friends. All purifications of the gateways of going forth to awakening arise from spiritual friends. All practices of the training of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are bound to spiritual friends. All qualities and <s>dharmas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are established in spiritual friends. All purifications of the resolute intention of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are rooted in spiritual friends.

kalyāṇamitrasaṃjātā sarvabodhisattvacittotpādadṛḍhatā / kalyāṇamitranetrikāḥ sarvabodhisattvasamudradhāraṇīpratībhānamukhālokāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃdhāritāḥ sarvabodhisattvaviśuddhimukhakośāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃjanitāḥ sarvabodhisattvajñānālokāḥ / kalyāṇamitrahastagatā sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānavaiśeṣikatā / kalyāṇamitrapradhāna ekotībhāvaḥ / kalyāṇamitragotrāḥ sarvabodhisattvasamudāgamavaiśeṣikaśraddhāḥ / kalyāṇamitrakośagatāni
sarvabodhisattvaguhyasthānāni / kalyāṇamitrākarāḥ sarvabodhisattvadharmākarāḥ / kalyāṇamitravivardhitāḥ sarvabodhisattvendriyavegāṅkurāḥ / kalyāṇamitravivardhitāḥ sarvabodhisattvajñānasāgarāḥ / kalyāṇamitrapratipālitāḥ sarvabodhisattvanidhānakośāḥ / kalyāṇamitrarakṣitāḥ sarvabodhisattvapuṇyopacayāḥ / kalyāṇamitrajanitāḥ sarvabodhisattvajanmaviśuddhayaḥ / kalyāṇamitramukhāgatāḥ sarvabodhisattvadharmameghāḥ / kalyāṇamitrakoṣṭhagatāḥ sarvabodhisattvaniryāṇapathapraveśāḥ / kalyāṇamitrārādhanapratilabdhā sarvabuddhabodhiḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃgṛhītāḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāḥ / kalyāṇamitroddyotitāḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇodbhāvanāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃdarśitāḥ sarvabodhisattvadiganugamāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃvarṇitā sarvabodhisattvacittādhyāśayamahātmatā / kalyāṇamitrasaṃbhūtaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāmaitrībalam / kalyāṇamitrasaṃjanitaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇābalam / kalyāṇamitrasaṃgṛhītāni sarvabodhisattvādhipatyāni / kalyāṇamitrasaṃjanitāni sarvabodhyaṅgāni / kalyāṇamitrasaṃbhavāḥ sarvabodhisattvahitopasaṃhārāḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃdhāritāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvā na patanti durgatiṣu / kalyāṇamitraparigṛhītā bodhisattvā na nivartante mahāyānāt / kalyāṇamitrasamanvāhṛtā bodhisattvā nātikrāmanti bodhisattvaśikṣām / kalyāṇamitrasvārakṣitā bodhisattvā na gacchanti pāpamitravaśam / kalyāṇamitraparipālitā bodhisattvā na parihīyante bodhisattvadharmebhyaḥ / kalyāṇamitrasaṃgṛhītā bodhisattvā atikrāmanti pṛthagjanabhūmim / kalyāṇamitrānuśikṣitā bodhisattvā nāvakrāmanti śrāvakapratyekabuddhanipātam / kalyāṇamitrapraticchannā bodhisattvā abhyudgatā bhavanti lokāt / kalyāṇamitrasaṃvardhitā bodhisattvā anupaliptā bhavanti
lokadharmaiḥ / kalyāṇamitraparyupāsitā bodhisattvā asaṃpramoṣacāriṇo bhavanti sarvacaryāsu / kalyāṇamitrotthāpitā bodhisattvā na nivartante sarvārambhebhyaḥ / kalyāṇamitraparigṛhītā bodhisattvā durdharṣā bhavanti karmakleśaiḥ / kalyāṇamitrabalopastabdhā bodhisattvā anavamardyā bhavanti sarvamāraiḥ / kalyāṇamitropaniśrayavihāriṇo bodhisattvā vivardhante sarvabodhyaṅgaiḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? viśodhakāni kulaputra kalyāṇamitrāṇyāvaraṇīyānāṃ vinivartakāni / kalyāṇamitrāṇyapāyebhyaḥ saṃbodhanāni / kalyāṇamitrāṇyakaraṇīyānāṃ saṃnivārakāni pramādasthānebhyaḥ / vidhamitāro 'vidyāndhakārasya / nirdārayitāro dṛṣṭibandhanānām / niṣkrāmayitāraḥ saṃsārāt / utkhāṭayitāro lokaniketāt / nirmocayitāro mārapaśebhyaḥ / samābṛṃhayitāro duḥśalyānām / parimocayitāraḥ ajñānagahanāt / samatikrāmayitāro dṛṣṭikāntārāt / uttārayitāro bhavaughebhyaḥ / uddhartāraḥ kāmapaṅkāt / vinivartayitāraḥ
body.translated_text: Born from <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s (spiritual friends) is the firmness of the arising of the mind of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Led by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the lights of the gateways of eloquence and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) of the ocean of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Upheld by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the treasuries of the gateways of purification of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Generated by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the lights of knowledge of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. In the hands of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s lies the distinction of the vows of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. The <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> is foremost in bringing about single-pointed concentration. Of the lineage of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s is the distinctive faith in the attainments of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Held within the treasury of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are all the secret abodes of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the mines of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s> mines. Nurtured by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the sprouts of the momentum of the faculties of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Increased by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the oceans of knowledge of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Guarded by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the treasure-stores of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Protected by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the accumulations of merit of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Generated by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the purities of birth of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Proceeding from the mouth of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the <s>dharma</s>-clouds of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Held within the granaries of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the entries to the paths of going-forth of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Through the worship of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s is all <s>Buddha</s>-awakening attained. Gathered by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts. Illuminated by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the manifestations of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities. Shown by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are the followings of the directions of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Praised by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s is the greatness of the deep intention of the minds of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Born from <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s is the power of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Generated by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s is the power of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Gathered by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are all the sovereignties of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Generated by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are all the limbs of awakening. Born from <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are all the beneficial accomplishments of <s>bodhisattva</s>s. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s upheld by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s, O <s>kulaputra</s>, do not fall into bad destinies. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s embraced by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not turn back from the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s cared for by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not transgress the <s>bodhisattva</s>-training. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s well-guarded by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not fall under the power of evil friends. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s watched over by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not decline from the <s>dharma</s>s of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s gathered by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s transcend the stage of ordinary beings. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s trained by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not descend into the fall of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s sheltered by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s become elevated above the world. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s nourished by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s become unstained by worldly <s>dharma</s>s. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s attended upon by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s conduct themselves without negligence in all practices. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s raised up by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s do not turn back from all undertakings. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s embraced by <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s become invulnerable to <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements). <s>Bodhisattva</s>s supported by the power of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s become unconquerable by all <s>Māra</s>s. <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who dwell in reliance upon <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s grow in all the limbs of awakening. Why is that? Because <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s, O <s>kulaputra</s>, are purifiers, turning one away from obstructions. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are awakeners from the bad destinies. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are restrainers from heedless places regarding what should not be done. They are dispellers of the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). They are breakers of the bonds of wrong views. They are those who lead out of <s>saṃsāra</s>. They are uprooters from the dwellings of the world. They are liberators from the snares of <s>Māra</s>. They are healers of those pierced by thorns. They are deliverers from the jungle of ignorance. They are those who carry across the wilderness of wrong views. They are rescuers from the floods of existence. They are those who lift out of the mire of sensual desire. They are those who turn back from

body.text: kumārgāt / saṃdarśayitāro bodhisattvamārgasya / niyojayitāro bodhisattvasamādānena / pratiṣṭhāpayitāraḥ pratipattiṣu / praṇetāraḥ sarvajñatāgamanadiśam / viśodhayitāraḥ prajñācakṣuṣaḥ / vivardhayitāro bodhicittasya / saṃjanayitāro mahākaruṇāyāḥ / ākhyātāraḥ caryāyāḥ / avavāditāraḥ pāramitāsu / pratiyāpayitāraḥ bhūmiṣu / vibhajitāraḥ kṣāntīnām / saṃbhāvayitāraḥ sarvakuśalamūlānām / utthāpayitāraḥ sarvasaṃbhārāṇām / dātāraḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇānām / saṃprāpayitāraḥ sarvabuddhapādamūleṣu / saṃdarśayitāraḥ sarvaguṇeṣu / samādāpayitāraḥ artheṣu / samuttejayitāraḥ pratipattiṣu / nidarśayitāro niryāṇamukhānām / ārakṣitāraḥ praṇāśapathebhyaḥ / avabhāsayitāro dharmālokamukhānām / abhipravarṣayitāro dharmaśravaṇameghānām / nāśayitāraḥ sarvakleśānām / vinivartayitāraḥ sarvadṛṣṭikṛtānām / niveśayitāraḥ sarvabuddhadharmeṣu //
body.translated_text: the wrong path. They are revealers of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-path. They are those who engage with the undertaking of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. They are those who establish in practices. They are guides toward the direction of reaching <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). They are purifiers of the eye of wisdom. They are nurturers of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). They are generators of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). They are proclaimers of the conduct. They are instructors in the <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections). They are those who advance on the stages. They are those who distinguish the <s>kṣānti</s>s (patiences). They are those who honor all roots of wholesome merit. They are those who raise up all the accumulations. They are bestowers of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities. They are those who bring one to the feet of all <s>Buddha</s>s. They are revealers of all qualities. They are those who inspire with purposes. They are those who encourage in practices. They are those who show the gateways of going-forth. They are protectors from the paths of destruction. They are illuminators of the gateways of the light of <s>dharma</s>. They are those who rain down clouds of <s>dharma</s>-hearing. They are destroyers of all <s>kleśa</s>s. They are those who turn back what is produced by wrong views. They are those who establish in all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: api ca kulaputra mātṛbhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi buddhakuleṣu janayitrīṇi / pitṛbhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi vipulahitopasaṃharaṇatayā / dhātrībhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvapāpārakṣaṇatayā / ācāryabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi bodhisattvaśikṣānubodhanatayā / daiśikabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi pāramitāmārgāvataraṇatayā / vaidyabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi kleśavyādhiparimocanatayā / himavatparvatabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi jñānauṣadhivivardhanatayā / śūrabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvabhayārakṣaṇatayā / dāśabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi saṃbhāramahaughottaraṇatayā / karṇadhārabhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi sarvajñajñānaratnadvīpasaṃprāpaṇatayā //
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like mothers, giving birth in <s>Buddha</s>-families. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like fathers, by bringing about vast benefit. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like nurses, by protecting from all evil. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like teachers, by awakening to the <s>bodhisattva</s>-training. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like guides, by leading into the path of the <s>pāramitā</s>s. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like physicians, by liberating from the disease of the <s>kleśa</s>s. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like the <s>Himālaya</s> mountains, by increasing the herbs of knowledge. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like heroes, by protecting from all fears. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like ferrymen, by carrying across the great flood of the accumulations. <s>Kalyāṇamitra</s>s are like helmsmen, by bringing one to the jewel-island of omniscient knowledge.

body.text: tasmāttarhi kulaputra evaṃ manasikārāt pratiprasrabdhena kalyāṇamitrāṇyupasaṃkramitavyāni pṛthivīsamacittena sarvabhāravahanāpariṇamanatayā / vajrasamacittenābhedyāśayatayā / cakravālasamacittena sarvaduḥkhāsaṃpravedhanatayā / samacittena yatheṣṭājñākaraṇatayā / śiṣyasamacittena sarvājñāvilomanatayā / lokadāsasamacittena sarvakarmasamādānāvijugupsanatayā / dhātrīsamacittena sarvakleśāparitamanatayā / bhṛtyasamacittena kiṃkaraṇīpradakṣiṇagrāhatayā / rajopaharaṇasamacittena mānātimānavivarjanatayā / pūrṇacandrasamacittena kālākālānāmāvamanatayā / ājāneyāśvasamacittena sarvakhaṭukatāvivarjanatayā / yānasamacittena gurubhāravahanatayā / nāgasamacittena dāntājāneyacittatayā / śailasamacittena acalākampyatayā / śvasamacittena akrodhanatayā / caṇḍālakumārakasamacittena nirmānanirahaṃkāratayā / chinnaviṣāṇarṣabhasamacittena sarvadarpavigatena / antevāsisamacittenānatimānatayā / nausamacittena gamanāgamanāparikhinnatayā / setusaṃkramacittena kalyāṇamitrājñottaraṇatayā / suputrasamacittena kalyāṇamitramukhodīkṣaṇatayā / rājakumārasamacittena dharmarājājñāprativahanatayā //
body.translated_text: Therefore, son of good family, with such mental attention and with a relaxed mind, one should approach <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s: with a mind equal to the earth, through not wearying of bearing all burdens; with a mind equal to <s>vajra</s>, through having an unbreakable intention; with a mind equal to <s>Cakravāla</s>, through being unshaken by all suffering; with an equal mind, through carrying out commands as desired; with a mind equal to a pupil, through not opposing any instruction; with a mind equal to a servant of the world, through not being repelled by any task undertaken; with a mind equal to a nurse, through not being distressed by all defilements; with a mind equal to a hired servant, through readiness to do whatever is needed; with a mind equal to a dust-remover, through abandoning pride and conceit; with a mind equal to the full moon, through illuminating both timely and untimely occasions; with a mind equal to a thoroughbred horse, through abandoning all harshness; with a mind equal to a vehicle, through bearing heavy loads; with a mind equal to an elephant, through having a tamed and noble mind; with a mind equal to a mountain, through being immovable and unshakable; with a mind equal to a dog, through being free from anger; with a mind equal to a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> youth, through being free from pride and self-conceit; with a mind equal to a bull with broken horns, through being free from all arrogance; with a mind equal to a resident pupil, through being free from excessive pride; with a mind equal to a ship, through being unwearied in coming and going; with a mind equal to a bridge, through carrying out the commands of the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>; with a mind equal to a good son, through looking to the face of the <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>; with a mind equal to a prince, through bearing the commands of the <s>Dharma</s>-king.

body.translated_text: And you should generate, son of good family, the perception of yourself as one who is sick, of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s as physicians, of their instructions as medicine, and of practice as the cure of disease. And you should generate, son of good family, the perception of yourself as a traveler, of <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s as guides, of their instructions as the path, and of practice as

body.text:
kṣetradiggamanasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra pāragasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu nāvikasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu tīrthasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu nausaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra karṣakasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu bhujagendrasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu varṣasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu śasyaniṣpattisaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra daridrasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu vaiśravaṇasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu dhanasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu dāridryāpanayanasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra antevāsikasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣvācāryasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu śilpasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣvadhigamanasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra abhīrusaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu śūrasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu praharaṇasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu śatrunirghātanasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra vaṇiksaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu karṇadhārasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu ratnasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu ratnagrahaṇasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra satputrasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu mātāpitṛsaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu kulavṛttisaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu vṛttyavipraṇāśasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / ātmani ca te kulaputra rājakumārasaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu dharmarājāgrāmātyasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu rājaśikṣā, pratipattiṣu jñānarājamakuṭālaṃkāradharmapaṭṭaśirobandhanadharmarājanagaravyavalokanasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / evaṃ cittasaṃjñāmanasikāraparibhāvitena kulaputra kalyāṇamitrāṇyupasaṃkramitavyāni
/ tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ kalyāṇamitrādhyāśayapariśuddhā hi kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ kalyāṇamitrājñāsu pratipadyamānā vivardhante sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ himavatsaṃniśritā iva tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ / bhājanībhavanti sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ mahāsāgara iva jalasya / ākarībhavanti sarvaguṇānāṃ mahāsamudra iva ratnānām / uttāpayanti bodhicittaṃ suvarṇamivāgnisaṃtāpe / abhyudgatā bhavanti lokāt, sumeruriva sāgarāt / anupaliptā bhavanti lokadharmaiḥ, padmamiva jalen / saṃvasanti sarvaduścaritaiḥ, mahāsāgara iva pūtikuṇapena / vivardhante śukladharmaiḥ, candra iva śuklapakṣe / avabhāsayanti dharmadhātuṃ sūrya iva jambudvīpam / pravardhayanti bodhisattvapraṇidhānaśarīrāṇi kumārakā iva mātṛpitṛniśritāḥ / saṃkṣiptena kulaputra kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanīṣu pratipannā bodhisattvā daśānabhilāpyaguṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pratigṛhṇanti / daśādhyāśayakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pariśodhayanti / daśa bodhisattvendriyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi vivardhayanti / daśādhiṣṭhānakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi viśodhayanti / caraṇīyadharmāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi pariśodhayanti / daśa mārāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi samatikrāmanti / daśa dharmamukhadvārāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti / daśasaṃbhāraviśuddhimukhāsaṃkhyeyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi paripūrayanti / daśa caryāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi paripūrayanti / daśa caryāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi paryavadāpayanti / daśa mahāpraṇidhānāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyabhinirharanti / saṃkṣiptena kulaputra sarvabodhisattvacaryāḥ sarvabodhisattvapāramitāḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmayaḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhimukhāni sarvabodhisattvābhijñājñānavikurvitāni sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratibhānālokāḥ,
body.translated_text: you should generate the perception of going to the direction of the field. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of one who has reached the far shore; in spiritual friends, the perception of a boatman; in their admonitions, the perception of a crossing; in their practices, the perception of a boat. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a farmer; in spiritual friends, the perception of a serpent-king; in their admonitions, the perception of rain; in their practices, the perception of the ripening of crops. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a poor man; in spiritual friends, the perception of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (god of wealth); in their admonitions, the perception of wealth; in their practices, the perception of the removal of poverty. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a student; in spiritual friends, the perception of a teacher; in their admonitions, the perception of an art; in their practices, the perception of attainment. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of one without fear; in spiritual friends, the perception of a hero; in their admonitions, the perception of a weapon; in their practices, the perception of the destruction of enemies. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a merchant; in spiritual friends, the perception of a helmsman; in their admonitions, the perception of gems; in their practices, the perception of gathering gems. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a good son; in spiritual friends, the perception of father and mother; in their admonitions, the perception of the family tradition; in their practices, the perception of the non-loss of that tradition. And you, son of good family, should generate in yourself the perception of a prince; in spiritual friends, the perception of the chief minister of the <s>Dharma</s>-king; in their admonitions, the perception of royal training; in their practices, the perception of seeing the city of the <s>Dharma</s>-king through the crown-ornament of the knowledge-king and the binding of the <s>dharma</s>-diadem upon the head. Thus, son of good family, cultivated with such mind, perception, and mental attention, one should approach spiritual friends. And why? Because, son of good family, <s>bodhisattva</s>s whose deep intention is purified by spiritual friends, practicing the instructions of spiritual friends, grow through all wholesome roots — like grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees dependent on <s>Himavat</s>. They become vessels of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — like the great ocean for water. They become mines of all qualities — like the great ocean for gems. They refine <s>bodhicitta</s> — like gold in the heat of fire. They rise above the world — like <s>Sumeru</s> above the ocean. They are unstained by worldly <s>dharma</s>s — like a lotus by water. They dwell with all evil conduct — like the great ocean with a putrid corpse. They grow through white <s>dharma</s>s — like the moon in the bright fortnight. They illuminate the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — like the sun illuminates <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. They increase the bodies of <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows — like boys dependent on father and mother. In brief, son of good family, <s>bodhisattva</s>s practicing the admonitions of spiritual friends receive ten inexpressible <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of qualities. They purify ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of deep intentions. They increase ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattva</s>-faculties. They purify ten <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of foundations. They purify innumerable hundred-thousands of the <s>dharma</s>s to be practiced. They surpass ten innumerable hundred-thousands of <s>Māra</s>s. They dwell in ten innumerable hundred-thousands of <s>dharma</s>-gate doors. They fulfill ten innumerable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of the gates of purification of provisions. They fulfill ten innumerable hundred-thousands of conducts. They bring to completion ten innumerable hundred-thousands of conducts. They accomplish ten innumerable hundred-thousands of great vows. In brief, son of good family, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>pāramitā</s>s, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-stages, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-gates, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-superknowledge-knowledge-transformations, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>-eloquence-lights,

sarvabodhisattvapariṇamanājñānābhijñāpramāṇatāḥ, sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānābhinirhārāḥ, sarvabuddhadharmapratilambhapariniṣpattayaḥ

body.translated_text: all <s>bodhisattva</s>-immeasurabilities of the superknowledge of the knowledge of dedication, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-accomplishments of vows, all perfections of the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — are dependent on spiritual friends, rooted in spiritual friends, originating from spiritual friends, born from spiritual friends, having spiritual friends as their door, produced by spiritual friends, nurtured by spiritual friends, established by spiritual friends, caused by spiritual friends, and arising from spiritual friends. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ imāmevaṃrūpāṃ kalyāṇamitrāguṇavarṇānuśāsanīṃ bodhisattvacaryāpramāṇatāṃ buddhadharmavistīrṇatāṃ ca śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ śrīsaṃbhavasya dārakasya śrīmatyāśca dārikāyāḥ pādau śirasābhivandya śrīsaṃbhavaṃ dārakaṃ śrīmatīṃ dārikāṃ ca anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya śrīsaṃbhavasya dārakasya śrīmatyāśca dārikāyā antikātprakrāntaḥ // 51 // // 52 //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, having heard this kind of admonition praising the qualities of spiritual friends, the immeasurability of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, and the vastness of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with delight and gladness — bowed his head at the feet of the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s>, circumambulated the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, looked back at them again and again, and departed from the presence of the boy <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> and the girl <s>Śrīmatī</s>. // 51 // // 52 //

body.text: 54 Maitreyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 54 <s>Maitreya</s> /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ kalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyabhiṣyanditacitto yena samudrakaccho janapadastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ tāmeva bodhisattvacaryānuśāsanīmanuvicintayan, samyakcaryāniḥsamarthapūrvāntakoṭīgatakāyapraṇāmasamanvāhāreṇa kāyabalaṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ, pūrvāntakoṭīgatakāyacittapariśuddhiniṣkāraṇasaṃsārikacittapracārasamanvāhāreṇa cittamanasikāraṃ gṛhṇan, pūrvāntakoṭyasatkarmalaukikakāryaprayuktaḥ niṣprayojanapariṣyandasamanvāhāreṇa pratyutpannaprayojanamahāsāmarthyaṃ vicintayan, pūrvāntabhūtaparikalpasamutthitavitathasaṃkalpasaṃdarśitamanasikārasamanvāhāreṇa sarvabodhisattvacaryāsamyaksaṃkalpābhisaṃskārabalaṃ samutthāpayan, atītātmabhāvātmārthaprayogārambhaviṣamatāsamanvāhāreṇa sarvasattvārthārambhavaiśeṣikatayā adhyāśayabalaṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ, atītakāyaparyeṣṭisamudācārasvādatāsamanvāhāreṇa sarvabuddhadharmāpratilambhaprayogamahāśvāsapratilambhena indriyavegān vivardhayamānaḥ, atītādhvaviparyāsasaṃprayuktamithyāmayayogaprayogasamanvāhāreṇa pratyutpannādhvasamyaksaṃdarśanāviparyāsasaṃprayuktena bodhisattvapraṇidhānena saṃtatiṃ pariśodhayan, pūrvāntagatavīryārambhakāryāpariniṣpannasamanvāhāreṇa pratyutpannasarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamapratyupasthānena mahāvīryārambhavikrameṇa kāyacittasaṃpragrahaṃ janayan, pūrvāntakoṭīpañcagatyapāyanikṣiptātmabhāvanirupaṇākhyanirupajīvyasamucchrāyamaparāntakoṭīgatakalpaparigrahaprayuktasya samanvāhāreṇa sarvabuddhadharmotthāpakasarvajagadupajīvyasarvakalyāṇasamarthātmabhāvaparigraheṇa vipulaprītiprāmodyavegān vivardhayamānaḥ pratyutpannajanmābhinivṛttaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokakarabhūtaṃ saṃyogaviyoganidhānabhūtaṃ samucchrayamaparāntakoṭīgatakalpabodhisattvacaryācaraṇaprayuktasya sattvaparipācanabuddhadharmaparigrahaprayuktasya tathāgatadarśanasarvakṣetrānucaraṇasarvadharmabhāṇakopasthānasarvatathāgataśāsanasaṃdhāraṇaprayuktasyasarvadharmaparyeṣṭisahāyabhūtasya sarvakalyāṇamitradarśanasarvabuddhadharmasamudānayanaprayuktasya bodhisattvapraṇidhānaśarīrasya hetupratyayabhūtamavalokya acintyakuśalamūlendriyavegān vivardhayamānaḥ / evaṃcittaḥ evaṃmanasikāraḥ evaṃyoniśaḥprayuktaḥ sarvabodhisattvaprasādasamāropitayā śraddhayā sarvabodhisattvāśayasamāropitena premṇā sarvabodhisattvāśayasamāropitena gauraveṇa sarvabodhisattvendriyaprasādasamāropitena citrīkāreṇa sarvabodhisattvaśāstryadhimuktisamutthitairindriyaprasādavegaiḥ sarvabodhisattvagauravaniryātena cittaprasādena sarvabodhisattvaśraddhāsamutthitaiḥ kuśalamūlasaṃbhāraiḥ, sarvabodhisattvābhisaṃskārasamutthitābhiḥ
pūjāvimātratābhiḥ, sarvabodhisattvasamairāśrayaiḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭaiḥ sarvajagaccharīrasaṃbhavābhiścakṣurvimātratāvalokanatābhiḥ, sarvajagatsaṃjñājagatsamāropitābhiḥ sarvabodhisattvasvarāṅgaviśuddhisamutthitavarṇodāhāravyūhābhinirhāraiḥ, pūrvāntapratyutpannakoṭīgatasarvabodhisattvādhiṣṭhānaparipūrṇena tathāgatavihārābhimukhībhāvagatena saṃjñāgatena sarvatrānugatena tathāgatabodhisattvavikurvaṇāsaṃbodhena ekavālapathāvyatiriktena sarvabuddhabodhisattvakāyaspharaṇānugatena sarvabodhisattvacakṣuṣpathapariśuddhisamāropitābhijñājñānālokavijñaptibhiḥ, sarvadigjālasaṃbhedānugatena manaāyatanena dharmadhātutalabhedaspharaṇena praṇidhyabhinirhārabalena ākāśadhātuparamaparyavasānena sarvatrānugatena tryadhvāsaṃbhinnena
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, his mind overflowing with the admonition of the spiritual friend, proceeded to the province of <s>Samudrakaccha</s>, contemplating that very admonition of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — strengthening the power of his body by the recollection of bodily prostration throughout <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit of the past directed toward right conduct; grasping the mental attention of his mind by the recollection of the purity of body and mind throughout the furthest limit of the past, free from causeless saṃsāric mental activity; contemplating the great capability of the present purpose by the recollection of having been engaged in useless worldly tasks with fruitless results throughout the furthest limit of the past; arousing the power of right intention and mental formation of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct by the recollection of the mental attention displayed by false intentions arising from the imagined constructions of the past; strengthening the power of deep intention by the recollection of the unevenness of undertaking selfish purposes in past states of being, through the excellence of undertaking the purpose of all beings; increasing the momentum of faculties by the recollection of the former relishing of bodily pursuits in past times, through the attainment of great relief in the effort to attain all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; purifying the continuum by the recollection of engagement in wrong, deceitful, and illusory practices conjoined with the perversions of the past, through the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vow conjoined with right seeing and non-perversion in the present; generating the restraint of body and mind by the recollection of the non-accomplishment of tasks through the exertion of vigor in past times, through the great stride of vigor for the present accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; increasing the vast momentum of delight and joy by the recollection of the bodies cast into the five destinies of bad rebirths throughout the furthest limit of the past — bodies without repute, worthless, without sustenance — through the present embrace of bodies that are the producers of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, the sustenance of the entire world, capable of all goodness, for <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit; increasing the inconceivable momentum of the faculties of wholesome roots by surveying the present birth — turned away from saṃsāric attachment, the basis of old age, sickness, death, and sorrow, the repository of union and separation — as the cause and condition for the body of <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows engaged in practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct for <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit, engaged in ripening beings and embracing <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, engaged in seeing <s>Tathāgata</s>s and following through all fields, engaged in attending all <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, upholding the teaching of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, a companion in the search for all <s>dharma</s>s, engaged in seeing all spiritual friends and assembling all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. With such a mind, such mental attention, thus properly engaged — with faith mounted upon the serenity of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with affection mounted upon the intention of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with reverence mounted upon the intention of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with wonder mounted upon the serenity of the faculties of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the momentum of the serenity of faculties arising from the devotion to the teaching of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the mental serenity produced by the reverence for all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the provisions of wholesome roots arising from the faith of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the immeasurabilities of worship arising from the mental formations of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the supports equal to all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with palms joined, with the immeasurabilities of the sight of the eye arising from the body of the entire world, with the proclamations of descriptions of qualities arising from the purity of the sounds and limbs of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s mounted upon the perception of the entire world — with the comprehension of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s abode-facing state, the perception permeating everything, the unconfused awareness of the transformations of <s>Tathāgata</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s, following the pervading of the bodies of all <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s without deviating from a single hair-path, with the light of superknowledge-knowledge mounted upon the purification of the eye-path of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with the mental base following the penetration of the net of all directions, with the power of the accomplishment of vows pervading the ground of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> without division, following everywhere unto the ultimate limit of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s>, undivided from the three times,

body.text:
apratiprasrabdhena sarvadharmāvatāramukhena sarvakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyavabhāsadikprasṛtena śraddhādhimuktipraveśabalena / iti hi sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ evaṃ gauravacitrīkārapūjāstavapraṇipātodīkṣamāṇādhiṣṭhānapraṇidhānasaṃjñānugatamānasaḥ evamapramāṇajñānagocarabhūmiprasṛtena jñānacakṣuṣā vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya purastāddvāramūle sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatitaḥ / sa imamevaṃrūpamabhinirhāraprayogaṃ muhūrtaṃ vicārya adhimuktiśraddhāsamutthitena adhyāśayapraṇidhyabhinirhārabalena apratiprasrabdhamātmānamadhyatiṣṭhat sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu, evaṃ sarvabodhisaṃmukhībhāveṣu sarvakalyāṇamitrabhavaneṣu sarvatathāgatacaityeṣu sarvatathāgatavigraheṣu sarvabodhisattveṣu sarvabuddhāvāseṣu sarvadharmaratnasthāneṣu sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāśrayacaityasaṃmukhībhāveṣu sarvāryagaṇadakṣiṇīyagurumātāpitṛparyanteṣu apratiprasrabdhamātmānamadhyatiṣṭhat sarvajagatkāyasaṃmukhībhāveṣu sarvatrānugatena jñānaśarīrāsaṃbhedanayapraveśānugatena saṃjñādhiṣṭhānajñānamanasikāreṇa / yathā ca vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya purastāt, evaṃ pūrvaparikīrtiteṣu sarvārambaṇeṣu sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaṃ praṇipātamadhyatiṣṭhat / evamaparāntakoṭīgatān kalpānapratiprasrabdhamadhiṣṭhāya ākāśadhātuparyantapramāṇasamatayā dharmadhātvanāvaraṇasamatayā sarvatrānugatabhūtakoṭīsamatayā tathāgatāvikalpasamatayā chāyāgatajñānasaṃjñāspharaṇatayā svapnasamavicārasamatayā pratibhāsasamasarvalokajagadvijñaptisamatayā pratiśrutkāsamahetupratyayasamutthānasamatayā anutpādasamatayā saṃbhavavibhavasamatayā abhāvasamapratyayapratītyāvartanasamatayā yathākarmasamutthitaṃ vipākamadhimucyamāno yathāhetusamutthitaṃ phalamadhimucyamāno yathopacayasamutthitāṃ sarvakriyāmadhimucyamānaḥ śraddhāsamutthitaṃ sarvatathāgatotpādamadhimucyamāno yathādhimuktisamutthitāni
sarvabuddhapūjānirmāṇānyadhimucyamāno gauravasamutthitāni sarvatathāgatanirmāṇānyadhimucyamānaḥ kuśalamūlopacayasamutthitāṃ sarvabuddhadharmatāmadhimucyamānaḥ prajñopāyasamutthitān sarvamanomayavyūhopacayānadhimucyamānaḥ praṇidhisamutthitān sarvabuddhadharmānadhimucyamānaḥ pariṇāmanāsamutthitān sarvabodhisattvacaryāsarvajñatāviṣayadharmadhātuviṭhapanaspharaṇālaṃkāravyūhānadhimucyamānaḥ ucchedasaṃjñāvigatena pariṇāmanājñānena śāśvatasaṃjñāvibhūtena anutpādajñānena hetukriyādṛṣṭivigatena samyakkriyādṛṣṭivigatena samakriyādṛṣṭivigatena samakriyāvatārahetūpacayajñānena, viparyāsadṛṣṭivigatena aparapratyayajñānena, ātmaparasaṃjñādṛṣṭivigatena pratītyāvatārajñānena, antagrāhadṛṣṭivigatena anantamadhyadharmadhātupraveśajñānena, saṃkrāntidṛṣṭivigatena pratiṣṭhāsamatābhinirvṛttijñānena bhavavibhavadṛṣṭivigatena anutpādanirodhajñānena, sarvadṛṣṭivigatena śūnyatānutpādajñānena, anaiśvaryadharmatāpratibaddhena praṇidhyabhinirhārajñānabalena sarvanimittasaṃjñāpanītena animittakoṭīmukhajñānena bījāṅkuravināśadharmatayā mudrāpratimudrāsamutthānasamadharmatayā pratibimbadarśanasamadharmatayā pratiśrutkāsamarutaghoṣavijñaptidharmatayā svapnasamavicāravijñaptidharmatayā pratibhāsadarśanasamadharmatayā māyāgatasamakarmasamutthānadharmatayā cittārūpilokotthāpanadharmatayā yathāpratyayahetūpacayaphaladharmatayā, yathākarmopacayavipākasamadharmatayā upāyakauśalyaviṭhapanadharmatayā dharmādharmasamatisamatābhiṣyanditadharmatayā / evaṃ jñānapraveśābhinirhṛtena saṃjñāmanasikāreṇa sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako
body.translated_text: with unrelenting power of entry into faith and aspiration (<s>śraddhādhimukti</s>), through the gateway of entry into all <s>dharma</s>s, extended in the direction illuminated by the instructions of all spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>s). Thus <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, with a mind pervaded by the perception of resolution and vow through reverence, wonder, worship, praise, and prostration, with the eye of knowledge extended to the ground of immeasurable fields of knowledge, prostrated with his entire body at the base of the entrance before the great pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> (Womb of the Array and Ornament of Vairocana). Having reflected for a moment on this manner of practice and application, through the power of the application of aspiration and vow arisen from conviction and faith, he sustained himself unrelentingly at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, likewise in the presence of all awakenings, in the abodes of all spiritual friends, at all <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines, before all <s>Tathāgata</s> images, before all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, in all <s>Buddha</s>-abodes, in all places of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, in the presence of all shrines and refuges of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, and extending to all assemblies of Noble Ones, those worthy of offerings, teachers, mothers, and fathers — he sustained himself unrelentingly in the presence of the bodies of all beings in the world, through an attention of perception, sustaining power, and knowledge that followed the method of entry into the non-differentiation of the knowledge-body pervading everywhere. And just as before the great pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s>, so too in all the previously described objects of support, he sustained prostration pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). Thus, having sustained himself unrelentingly through <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the ultimate limit — through the equality of measure coextensive with the realm of space, through the equality of non-obstruction of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, through the equality of the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭī</s>) pervading everywhere, through the equality of non-conceptualization of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, through the pervading of knowledge-perception arrived like a shadow, through the equality of investigation like a dream, through the equality of cognition of all worlds and beings like a reflection, through the equality of arising from causes and conditions like an echo, through the equality of non-arising, through the equality of existence and non-existence, through the equality of turning through dependent origination equal to non-being — resolving upon the ripening arisen according to <s>karma</s>, resolving upon the fruit arisen according to cause, resolving upon all action arisen according to accumulation, resolving upon the arising of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s arisen from faith, resolving upon all manifestations of <s>Buddha</s>-worship arisen from aspiration, resolving upon all manifestations of <s>Tathāgata</s>s arisen from reverence, resolving upon the nature of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities arisen from the accumulation of roots of merit, resolving upon all accumulations of mind-made arrays arisen from wisdom and skillful means (<s>prajñopāya</s>), resolving upon all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities arisen from vows (<s>praṇidhi</s>), resolving upon the ornament-arrays pervading and establishing the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the domain of omniscience within the conduct of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s arisen from dedication of merit (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>) — with the knowledge of dedication free from the perception of annihilation, with the knowledge of non-arising free from the perception of eternalism, with the knowledge of the accumulation of causes entering into balanced action free from the view of action based on causality, free from the view of correct action, free from the view of equal action, with the knowledge independent of others free from the view of inversion, with the knowledge of entry into dependent origination free from the perception and view of self and other, with the knowledge of entry into the endless and middleless <s>dharmadhātu</s> free from the view grasping at extremes, with the knowledge of accomplishment through the equality of establishment free from the view of transmigration, with the knowledge of non-arising and cessation free from the view of existence and non-existence, with the knowledge of emptiness and non-arising free from all views — with the power of the knowledge of vow-accomplishment unbound by the nature of non-mastery, with the knowledge of the gateway to the limit of the signless from which all perceptions of signs have been removed, through the nature of the destruction of seed and sprout, through the equal nature of arising from seal and counter-seal, through the equal nature of seeing a reflection, through the nature of cognition of sounds and utterances like an echo, through the nature of cognition of investigation like a dream, through the equal nature of seeing a reflection, through the nature of arising of action equal to that produced by illusion, through the nature of raising up the formless world by mind, through the nature of fruit from the accumulation of causes and conditions, through the equal nature of ripening from the accumulation of <s>karma</s>, through the nature of establishment through skillful means, through the nature flowing from the equality of equal <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s> — thus, with perception and attention brought forth through the entry into knowledge, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son

body.text:
vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya purastāt praṇipātitaḥ / suciramatinamayya acintyakuśalamūlavegābhiṣyanditasaṃtānaḥ prahlāditakāyacittaḥ tataḥ kūṭāgāradvāramūlādutthāya muhūrtamanimiṣābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhaṃ mahākūṭāgāraṃ saṃprekṣya kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'nekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya evaṃsaṃjñāmanasikārasaṃpreṣitacitto vācamabhāṣata - ayaṃ sa śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavihāravihāriṇāmāvāsaḥ / ayaṃ sa sarvadharmāvikalpavihāravihāriṇāmāvāsaḥ / dharmadhātvasaṃbhedavihāravihāriṇāṃ sattvadhāttvanupalambhavihāravihāriṇāṃ
sarvadharmānutpādavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvalokāniketavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvajagadālayānilayavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvāvasiñcitavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvāpāśrayāniśritavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvasamucchrayāniśritavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvakleśasaṃjñāgatavidhūtavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvadharmāsvabhāvavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvakalpavikalpāvikalpavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvasaṃjñācittamanoviviktavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvasaṃjñānāyūhaniryūhavihāravihāriṇāṃ gambhīraprajñāpāramitāpraveśavihāravihāriṇāṃ samantamukhadharmadhātuspharaṇopāyavihāravihāriṇāṃ samantakleśaśāntopāyavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvadṛṣṭitṛṣṇāmānaprahīṇaprajñottaravihāriṇāṃ sarvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāvidyotpādavikrīḍitavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvabodhisattvasamādhigocarabhāvanāvihāravihāriṇāmayaṃ sarvabuddhapādamūlopaniśritavihāravihāriṇāmāvāsaḥ / ye te ekakalpasarvakalpasarvakalpaikakalpānupraveśavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te ekakṣetrasarvakṣetraikakṣetrāsaṃbhedavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te ekadharmasarvadharmasarvadharmaikadharmāvirodhavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te ekasattvasarvasattvaikasattvānānātvavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te ekabuddhasarvabuddhasarvabuddhaikabuddhādvayavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvārthaikakṣaṇapraveśavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvakṣetraikacittotpādagamanavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvasattvabhavanapratibhāsavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvalokahitasukhacittavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvasvādhīnapratilambhavihāravihāriṇaḥ, teṣāmayaṃ vihāraḥ / ye te lokaniketoccalitāśca sarvajagadbhavaneṣu saṃdṛśyante sarvasattvaparipācanāya
/ ye te sarvakṣetrāniśritāśca sarvakṣetreṣu ca anuvicaranti tathāgatapūjākarmaṇe / ye te sarvakṣetrāṇi ca anuvicaranti sarvabuddhakṣetravyūhaparigrahaṇatāyai, na ca sthānādvicaranti / ye te sarvatathāgatapādamūlagatāśca buddhasaṃjñābhiniveśavigatāśca / ye te sarvakalyāṇamitropaniśrayavihāravihāriṇaśca, na caiṣāṃ sarvajagati samasamo 'sti jñānena / ye te sarvamārabhavanavihāravihāriṇaśca kāmaguṇarativiprayuktāśca / ye te sarvasaṃjñāgatapraveśavihāravihāriṇaśca sarvasaṃjñāgatavidhūtamānasāśca / ye te sarvajagaccharīrānugatakāyāśca na cātmasattvadvayavihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvalokadhātvantargatakāyā na ca dharmadhātusaṃbhedavihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvānāgatakalpasaṃvāsapraṇidhānāśca, na ca dīrghahrasvakalpasaṃjñāgatavihāravihāriṇaḥ / ye te ekavālapathāśca na calanti, sarvalokadhātuṣu ca saṃdṛśyante, teṣāmayaṃ dūrāsadadharmadiganupraveśavihāravihāriṇāṃ durājñeyavihāravihāriṇāṃ gambhīravihāravihāriṇām advayavihāravihāriṇām alakṣaṇavihāravihāriṇāṃ niḥpratipakṣavihāravihāriṇām anupalambhavihāravihāriṇāṃ
body.translated_text: prostrated before the great pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s>. Having bowed for a very long time, his continuum flooded by the force of inconceivable roots of merit, with body and mind gladdened, he then rose from the base of the entrance to the pinnacled mansion and, gazing for a moment with unblinking eyes at the great pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s>, with palms joined together, having circumambulated it many hundreds of thousands of times, with a mind dispatched by such perception and attention, he uttered these words: "This is the abode of those who dwell in the meditation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatā-animitta-apraṇihita</s>). This is the abode of those who dwell in the meditation of non-conceptualization of all <s>dharma</s>s. Of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-differentiation of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-apprehension of the realm of beings, of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-arising of all <s>dharma</s>s, of those who dwell in the meditation of homelessness in all worlds, of those who dwell in the meditation of non-attachment to the dwellings of all beings, of those who dwell in the meditation of being entirely unanointed, of those who dwell in the meditation of being unsupported by any refuge, of those who dwell in the meditation of being unsupported by any elevation, of those who dwell in the meditation of having dispelled all perceptions associated with <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions), of those who dwell in the meditation of the essencelessness of all <s>dharma</s>s, of those who dwell in the meditation of non-conceptualization beyond all <s>kalpa</s>-conceptualizations, of those who dwell in the meditation of seclusion from all perception, thought, and mind, of those who dwell in the meditation of the gathering and dispersing of all perceptions, of those who dwell in the meditation of entry into the profound perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), of those who dwell in the meditation of the skillful means of pervading the <s>dharmadhātu</s> through the universal gateway, of those who dwell in the meditation of the skillful means of universal pacification of <s>kleśa</s>s, of those who dwell in the meditation of supreme wisdom having abandoned all views, craving, and pride, of those who dwell in the meditation of sporting with the production of all <s>dhyāna</s>s (meditations), liberations, <s>samādhi</s>s (concentrations), attainments, and <s>abhijñā</s>s (superknowledges), of those who dwell in the meditation of cultivation of the domain of the <s>samādhi</s> of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s — this is the abode of those who dwell in the meditation of reliance at the feet of all <s>Buddha</s>s. Of those who dwell in the meditation of the mutual entry of one <s>kalpa</s> into all <s>kalpa</s>s and all <s>kalpa</s>s into one <s>kalpa</s>; of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-differentiation of one field into all fields and one field; of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-contradiction of one <s>dharma</s> with all <s>dharma</s>s and all <s>dharma</s>s with one <s>dharma</s>; of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-duality of one being and all beings and one being; of those who dwell in the meditation of the non-duality of one <s>Buddha</s> and all <s>Buddha</s>s and all <s>Buddha</s>s and one <s>Buddha</s>; of those who dwell in the meditation of entry into all purposes in a single instant; of those who dwell in the meditation of going to all fields with a single arising of mind; of those who dwell in the meditation of appearing as reflections in the dwellings of all beings; of those who dwell in the meditation of minds for the benefit and happiness of all worlds; of those who dwell in the meditation of attaining complete mastery over all — this is their abode. Those who have moved beyond worldly habitation yet appear in the dwellings of all beings for the maturation of all beings; those who are unsupported in any field yet roam through all fields for the work of worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>s; those who roam through all fields for the embrace of the array of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, yet do not move from their place; those who have gone to the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s yet are free from the attachment of <s>Buddha</s>-perception; those who dwell in reliance on all spiritual friends, yet in all the world there is none equal to them in knowledge; those who dwell in the meditation of all <s>Māra</s>-realms yet are separated from attachment to sensual pleasures; those who dwell in the meditation of entry into all perceptions yet have minds that have dispelled all perceptions; those whose bodies follow the bodies of all beings yet do not dwell in the duality of self and being; those whose bodies have entered into all world-realms yet do not dwell in the differentiation of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; those whose vows are to dwell together through all future <s>kalpa</s>s yet do not dwell in the perception of long or short <s>kalpa</s>s; those who do not move from a single hair-tip yet appear in all world-realms — this is the abode of those who dwell in the meditation of entry into the direction of the <s>dharma</s> difficult to approach, of those who dwell in meditation difficult to comprehend, of those who dwell in profound meditation, of those who dwell in non-dual meditation, of those who dwell in the meditation of the characteristicless, of those who dwell in meditation without opposition, of those who dwell in the meditation of non-apprehension

body.text:
niṣprapañcavihāravihāriṇāṃ mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāvihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaduravagāhavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvamāraviṣayasamatikrāntavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvalokaviṣayānupaliptavihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvabodhisattvapāramitāvihāravihāriṇāṃ sarvabuddhavihārānukūlavihāravihāriṇāmayaṃ vihāraḥ / ye te sarvanimittāpagatavihāriṇaśca, na ca śrāvakaniyāmamavakrāmanti / ye te sarvadharmānutpādavihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca anutpādadharmatāyāṃ patanti / ye te 'śubhāvihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca rāgavirāgadharmatāṃ sākṣātkurvanti, na ca rāgadharmaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvasanti / ye te maitrīvihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca doṣamalopagatacittāḥ / pratītyasamutpādavihāravihāriṇaśca
atyantāsaṃmūḍhāśca sarvadharmeṣu / ye te caturdhyānavihāriṇaśca, na ca dhyānavaśenopapadyante / ye te caturapramāṇavihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca rūpadhātugatiṃ gacchanti sarvasattvaparipācanārtham / ye te caturārūpyasamāpattivihāravihāriṇaśca, na cārūpyadhātugatiṃ gacchanti mahākaruṇāparigṛhītatvāt / ye te śamathavipaśyanāvihāravihāriṇaśca, na cātmanā vidyāvimuktiṃ sākṣātkurvanti sarvasattvaparipākāya / ye te mahopekṣāvihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca sattvadhātuṃ parityajanti / ye te śūnyatāvihāravihāriṇaśca, na ca dṛṣṭigatasaṃniśritāḥ / ye te ānimittagocarāśca nimittacaritasattvanayābhimuktāśca / ye te sarvapraṇidhānavigatāśca bodhisattvapraṇidhānavyavacchinnāśca / ye te sarvakarmakleśavaśavartinaśca, sattvaparipākāya ca karmakleśavaśānugāḥ saṃdṛśyante / ye te cyutyupapattiparijñātāvinaśca, janmacyutimaraṇaṃ ca saṃdarśayanti / ye te sarvagativyativṛttāśca, sarvagatiṣu ca gacchanti sarvavinayavaśena / ye te maitrīvihāriṇaśca, na kvacidanunayavihāriṇaḥ / ye te karuṇāvihāriṇaśca, na kvacidanusaṃśayadarśanavihāriṇaḥ / ye te muditāvihāriṇaśca nityodvignāśca duḥkhitasarvavyavalokanatayā / ye te upekṣāvihāriṇaśca parakāryeṣu / ye te navānupūrvavihārasamāpattivihāriṇaśca, na kāmadhātūpapattivijugupsakāḥ / ye te sarvopapattyaniśritavihāriṇaśca, na ca bhūtakoṭīsākṣātkaraṇavihāriṇaḥ / ye te trivimokṣavihāriṇaśca, na ca śrāvakavimuktisparśavihāriṇaḥ / ye te caturāryasatyavyavalokanavihāriṇaśca, na ca phalasākṣātkaraṇavihāriṇaḥ / ye te gambhīrapratītyasamutpādavyupaparīkṣaṇavihāriṇaśca, na cātyantanipatanavihāriṇaḥ / ye te āryāṣṭāṅgamārgabhāvanāvihāriṇaśca, na cātyantaniryāṇavihāriṇaḥ / ye te pṛthagjanabhūmisamatikrāntavihāriṇaśca, na ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipatanavihāriṇaḥ / ye te pañcopādānaskandhaparijñānavihāriṇaśca,
na cātyantaskandhanirodhavihāriṇaḥ / ye te caturmārapathasamatikrāntavihāriṇaśca, na ca mārakalpanavihāriṇaḥ / ye te ṣaḍāyatanasamatikrāntavihāriṇaśca, na cātyantānabhinirvṛttivihāriṇaḥ / ye te tathatāvihāriṇaśca, na ca bhūtakoṭyāyatanavihāriṇaḥ / ye te sarvayānaniryāṇasaṃdarśanavihāriṇaśca, na ca mahāyānacyavanavihāriṇaḥ teṣāmayaṃ sarvaguṇavihāriṇāṃ vihāraḥ //
body.translated_text: of those who dwell in the dwelling free from proliferation, who dwell in the dwelling of great loving-kindness and great compassion, who dwell in the dwelling unfathomable to all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, who dwell in the dwelling that has completely transcended the domain of all <s>Māras</s>, who dwell in the dwelling unstained by the domain of all worlds, who dwell in the dwelling of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>pāramitās</s>, who dwell in the dwelling favorable to the dwelling of all <s>Buddhas</s> — this is the dwelling. Those who dwell free from all signs, yet do not descend into the fixed course of the <s>śrāvaka</s>; those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, yet do not fall into the nature of non-arising; those who dwell in the dwelling of the impure, yet do not directly realize the nature of the fading of passion, nor do they cohabit with the qualities of passion; those who dwell in the dwelling of loving-kindness, yet whose minds have not departed from the stain of hatred; those who dwell in the dwelling of dependent origination, yet are utterly unconfused regarding all <s>dharmas</s>; those who dwell in the four <s>dhyānas</s>, yet are not reborn by the power of <s>dhyāna</s>; those who dwell in the dwelling of the four immeasurables, yet do not go to rebirth in the realm of form, for the purpose of ripening all beings; those who dwell in the dwelling of the four formless attainments, yet do not go to rebirth in the formless realm, because they are embraced by great compassion; those who dwell in the dwelling of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), yet do not themselves directly realize liberation through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), for the ripening of all beings; those who dwell in the dwelling of great equanimity, yet do not abandon the realm of beings; those who dwell in the dwelling of emptiness, yet are not attached to views; those whose domain is the signless, yet who are inclined to the method of beings whose conduct involves signs; those who have departed from all vows, yet whose <s>bodhisattva</s>-vows are uninterrupted; those who are free from the power of all <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), yet appear to follow the power of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> for the ripening of beings; those who have fully understood death and rebirth, yet display birth, death, and dying; those who have transcended all destinies, yet go to all destinies through the power of all forms of discipline; those who dwell in loving-kindness, yet nowhere dwell in attachment; those who dwell in compassion, yet nowhere dwell in the perception of doubt; those who dwell in sympathetic joy, yet are constantly alarmed by the perception of all who are suffering; those who dwell in equanimity regarding others' affairs; those who dwell in the attainment of the nine successive dwellings, yet are not disgusted with rebirth in the desire-realm; those who dwell free from reliance on all rebirths, yet do not dwell in the direct realization of the limit of reality; those who dwell in the three liberations, yet do not dwell in contact with <s>śrāvaka</s>-liberation; those who dwell in the contemplation of the four noble truths, yet do not dwell in the direct realization of their fruits; those who dwell in the investigation of profound dependent origination, yet do not dwell in ultimate falling; those who dwell in the cultivation of the noble eightfold path, yet do not dwell in ultimate escape; those who dwell having transcended the stage of ordinary beings, yet do not dwell in falling to the stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; those who dwell in the full knowledge of the five aggregates of clinging, yet do not dwell in the ultimate cessation of the aggregates; those who dwell having transcended the path of the four <s>Māras</s>, yet do not dwell in the fabrication of <s>Māra</s>; those who dwell having transcended the six sense-bases, yet do not dwell in ultimate non-production; those who dwell in suchness, yet do not dwell in the realm of the limit of reality; those who dwell in displaying the escape through all vehicles, yet do not dwell in falling from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — this is the dwelling of those who dwell in all these qualities. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, at that moment, spoke these verses:

body.text: iha so mahākaruṇa lābhi viśuddhabuddhirmaitreya maitraśiri lokahitābhiyuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here that one of great compassion has gained, of purified wisdom, <s>Maitreya</s> of auspicious glory, devoted to the benefit of the world,

body.text: abhiṣekabhūmisthita jyeṣṭhasuto jinānāṃ viharāti buddhaviṣayaṃ anucintayantaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: established on the stage of consecration, the eldest son of the <s>Jinas</s>, he dwells contemplating the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 1 //

children.text: sarveṣa yo jinasutāna mahāyaśānāṃ mahājñānagocara vimokṣapratiṣṭhitānām /
children.translated_text: Of all the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, those of great renown, established in the liberation of the domain of great knowledge,

children.text: ye dharmadhātu vicaranti asajjamānā āvāsu teṣamayamapratipudgalānām // 2 //
children.translated_text: who wander through the <s>dharmadhātu</s> unattached — this is the dwelling of those incomparable ones. // 2 //
Of those arisen in taming, generosity, moral conduct, patience, vigor, and strength, who through <s>dhyānas</s> and superknowledges have gone to the far shore of powers,
of those established in wisdom, skillful means, vow, and strength, who have gone to the far shore of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>pāramitās</s> — this is the dwelling. // 3 //
This is the dwelling of those of unattached mind, of vast aspiration, who delight in the domain of space, who are unsupported,
who pervade the three times without obstruction — this is the dwelling of those who have illuminated all states of existence. // 4 //
Those who have entered the method of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, who investigate the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> which is of the nature of space,

children.text: na karonti niśrayu kvacidgagane va pakṣī teṣāṃ vihāru ayu jñānaviśāradānām // 5 //
children.translated_text: who do not make reliance anywhere, like birds in the sky — this is the dwelling of those wise in knowledge. // 5 //

children.text: ye rāgadoṣamatha mohasvabhāva jñātvā saṃkalpahetujanitāṃ vitathapravṛttim /
children.translated_text: Those who, having known the nature of passion, hatred, and delusion — the false operation generated by the cause of conceptualization —

children.text: nirvikalpayanti ca virāgamayīha teṣāṃ śāntapraśāntyumagatānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: make it free from conceptualization and free from passion — this is the dwelling of those who have attained peace and supreme tranquility. // 6 //
Those who, examining the liberation-gateways, truths, methods, meanings, paths, aggregates, elements, sense-bases, beings, and dependent origination,

children.text: praparīkṣamāṇa na patanti vidū praśāntiprajñāupāyakuśalānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: do not fall into [mere] tranquility, the wise ones skilled in wisdom and means — this is the dwelling. // 7 //

children.text: ye te anāvaraṇajñānadiśaṃ praviṣṭā jinakṣetra sattvaparikalpavikalpaśāntā /
children.translated_text: Those who have entered the direction of unobstructed knowledge, whose conceptual fabrication of beings and <s>Buddha</s>-fields is pacified,

children.text: bhāvasvabhāvarahitā na vimṛṣanti dharmān āvāsu teṣamaya śāntiparāyaṇānām // 8 //
children.translated_text: who are devoid of the inherent nature of existence and do not conceptualize <s>dharmas</s> — this is the dwelling of those whose ultimate goal is peace. // 8 //

body.text: ye te asaṅgacaritā ima dharmadhātuṃ vicaranti bhāvavigatā khagavāyubhūtāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those of unattached conduct who wander through this <s>dharmadhātu</s>, devoid of [attachment to] existence, like birds or wind,

body.text: sarvaṃ niketavigatā aniketacārī teṣāmaniśritamatīnamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 9 //
body.translated_text: all free from any abode, wanderers without a home — this is the dwelling of those of unsupported mind. // 9 //

children.text: ye dṛṣṭidurgatigatāṃ janatāmakhinnāṃ duḥkhāntarāṃ kaṭuka vedana vedayantīm /
children.translated_text: Those who, seeing beings gone to the bad destinies of wrong views, unwearied, experiencing bitter painful sensations in the midst of suffering,

children.text: maitraprabhāya śamayanti apāya sarvān āvāsu teṣamaya maitrakṛpāśayānām // 10 //
children.translated_text: pacify all bad destinies with the radiance of loving-kindness — this is the dwelling of those whose disposition is loving-kindness and compassion. // 10 //
Seeing the world gone into the straits of <s>saṃsāra</s>, gone astray from the noble path, like a blind caravan bereft of a guide,

children.text: ye prekṣya lokamiha mokṣapathe praṇenti sārthātivāhasadṛśānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: those who lead [the world] here to the path of liberation — this is the dwelling of those like caravan leaders. // 11 //
Those who, having seen the world brought under the power of birth, grief, old age, and death, bound by the fetters and bonds of <s>Namucī</s>'s (Māra's) hosts,
liberate and bring them to the direction of fearlessness and security — this is the dwelling of those heroes, hard to conquer. // 12 //
Those who, having surveyed these people afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), bring forth the great medicines of the nectar of knowledge,

children.text: parimocayanti vipulāṃ karuṇāṃ janitvā mahavaidyarājadṛśānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: and liberate them having generated vast compassion — this is the dwelling of those like great physician-kings. // 13 //

children.text: ye te niśāmya janatāṃ dukhitāmatrāṇāṃ śokākare patita mṛtyusamudragāmi /
children.translated_text: Those who, having perceived the suffering, unprotected people fallen into floods of grief, headed for the ocean of death,

children.text: tārenti kṛva mahatīṃ śubhadharmanāvaṃ teṣāṃ vihāramaya dāśasutopamānām // 14 //
children.translated_text: ferry them across having fashioned a great ship of the good <s>Dharma</s> — this is the dwelling of those like sons of ferrymen. // 14 //
Those who, having perceived people wandering in the ocean of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), beings of pure aspiration for the jewel of the mind of omniscience,
lift them up having plunged into the ocean of existence — this is the dwelling of those like sons of fishermen. // 15 //
Those who, having gone to the abode of vows, with the vision of compassion and loving-kindness, having surveyed all the dwellings of beings,
lift up the people dwelling in the ocean of existence — this is the dwelling of those like young <s>Garuḍa</s>-kings. // 16 //
Those who, like the moon and sun in the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, wander having attained the reflection in the dwellings of beings,
with the rays of knowledge from the <s>maṇḍala</s> of vows — this is the dwelling of those who illuminate the world. // 17 //
Those steadfast ones who, for the ripening of even a single being, remain for myriads of <s>kalpas</s> to the end of the future,

children.text: yatha eki sattvi tatha sarvajagatyaśeṣam āvāsu teṣamaya lokaparāyaṇānām // 18 //
children.translated_text: and as with one being, so with all the world without remainder — this is the dwelling of those whose ultimate concern is the world. // 18 //

children.text: ye ekakṣetraprasare aparāntakalpān vicaranti cārika jagārthamakhinnavīryāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, in the expanse of a single field, wander on pilgrimage for <s>kalpas</s> to the end of the future, for the world's benefit, with unwearied vigor,

children.text: yatha ekakṣetri tatha sarvadaśaddiśāsu āvāsu teṣamaya vajradṛḍhāśayānām // 19 //
children.translated_text: and as in one field, so in all the ten directions — this is the dwelling of those of vajra-firm aspiration. // 19 //

children.text: ye dharmamegha sugatāna daśaddiśāsu ekāsane sthita pibanti asaṃpramūḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, seated on a single seat, drink the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of the <s>Sugatas</s> in the ten directions, unconfused,
with minds unsatiated for myriads of <s>kalpas</s> of the future — this is the dwelling, equal to the ocean of wisdom. // 20 //

children.text: ye kṣetrasāgara vrajanti anābhilāpyān praviśanti co pariṣasāgara nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: Those who enter inexpressible oceans of fields and enter the oceans of assemblies of the leaders,

children.text: ye pūjasāgara vicitra jine karonti teṣāmasaṅgacaraṇānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: who make variegated oceans of offerings to the <s>Jinas</s> — this is the dwelling of those of unattached conduct. // 21 //
Those steadfast ones who, having entered from the midst of the boundless ocean of the noble ones, plunge into the ocean of vows,

children.text: bahukalpasāgara caranti jagaddhitārthā teṣāṃ vihāru ayu sarvaguṇākarāṇām // 22 //
children.translated_text: and practice for many oceans of <s>kalpas</s> for the world's benefit — this is the dwelling of those who are mines of all qualities. // 22 //

children.text: ye eki vālapathi uttaramāna kṣetrāt buddhāṃśca sattva tatha kalpa anantamadhyān /
children.translated_text: Those who, on the tip of a single hair, transcend from the field and enter <s>Buddhas</s>, beings, and <s>kalpas</s> boundless and without middle,

children.text: praviśanti enta na punā ca upenti sīmāṃ teṣāmasaṅganayanānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: enter there yet do not reach any boundary — this is the dwelling of those of unobstructed eyes. // 23 //

children.text: ye ekacittakṣaṇi kalpamahāsamudrān praviśanti kṣetra tatha buddhajagatpracārān /
children.translated_text: Those who, in a single mind-moment, enter great oceans of <s>kalpas</s> and enter fields and the courses of <s>Buddhas</s> and the world —
this is the dwelling of those established in unobstructed knowledge and mind, arisen in the <s>pāramitās</s> of qualities. // 24 //

children.text: ye sarvakṣetraparamāṇurajān gaṇitvā bindupramāṇa tulayitva jalaugha sarvam /
children.translated_text: Those who, having counted all the atom-particles of all fields and having measured all the water-masses drop by drop,
bring forth vows of that measure — this is the dwelling of those who have attained unattachment. // 25 //
They bring forth entries into the gateways of vows, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>s, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, and gateways of vows,

children.text: abhinirharanti vicaranti anantakalpān iha te praviṣṭa sugatāna sutāḥ smṛtīmāḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: and wander for endless <s>kalpas</s> — these sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>, possessed of mindfulness, have entered here. // 26 //

children.text: iha te sthitā jinasutā vividhā vicitrā abhinirharanti bahuśāstrakathārthayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Stationed here, the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, diverse and variegated, bring forth many teachings and discourses endowed with meaning,

children.text: saukhyāvahāni jagatāmiha śilpasthānānyanucintayanta viharanti satāṃ vihāraḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: and contemplating the crafts and sciences that bring happiness to the world, they dwell — this is the dwelling of the noble ones. // 27 //

children.text: iha te sthitā mahaabhijñaupāyajñāne yāvanta sattvagatibheda daśaddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Stationed here in great superknowledge, skillful means, and knowledge, they display the differentiations of birth and death everywhere among all the varieties of beings' destinies in the ten directions,

children.text: sarvatra janmacyutibheda vidarśayanti māyāgate sthita vimokṣa asaṅgacaryāḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: established in the liberation of one arrived through illusion, of unattached conduct. // 28 //

children.text: iha te sthitā prathamacittasamudbhavādyāṃ darśenti dharmacaryāṃ vasudharmaniṣṭhām /
children.translated_text: Stationed here, they display the <s>Dharma</s>-conduct from the first arising of the mind to the ultimate foundation of the excellent <s>Dharma</s>,
filling the <s>dharmadhātu</s> with dense emanations — thus they display hundreds of magical transformations. // 29 //

children.text: ye ekacittaprasareṇa vibuddha bodhiṃ praviśanti jñānamatikarma anantamadhyā /
children.translated_text: Those who, in a single mind-moment, are awakened to awakening and enter knowledge and action boundless and without middle,

children.text: saṃmohaketvavraji loku ya cintayāna evaṃ durāsadagatānamayaṃ vihāraḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: while the world, thinking about them, does not reach the banner of bewilderment — this is the dwelling of those who have attained the hard-to-reach. // 30 //
This is the dwelling of those of unattached mind, of conduct in the unobstructed <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
whose domain is without support — the dwelling of those of stainless aspiration and mind. // 31 //
Those of unattached conduct, who dwell without a home in all fields,
who dwell in the dwelling of non-dual knowledge — this is the dwelling of those incomparable ones. // 32 //
These who are equal to the nature of space, who dwell in <s>dharmas</s> that are without abode, peaceful,
whose domain is the sky — this is the dwelling of those who are free from dust. // 33 //

children.text: iha te kṛpāśayamatī sthitvā jagadīkṣya duḥkhaśokahatam /
children.translated_text: Here those of compassionate aspiration and mind, having stood and seen the world afflicted by suffering and grief,
devoted to contemplation of the world's benefit, dwell — those who have gained great compassion. // 34 //
Here those without interval are seen in all the dwellings of beings,
liberated from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> by the <s>samādhi</s> of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the moon and sun. // 35 //

children.text: iha te sthitā jinasutāḥ sarvajinānāṃ ca pādamūleṣu /
children.translated_text: Here these sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) stand, and at the feet of all the <s>Jinas</s>,
they are seen in all <s>kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), passing through endless <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). (36)
Here they, with emanations equal to world-eggs in measure, equal to the abodes of all sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,
pervade all directions without remainder with clouds of magical transformations. (37)

children.text: iha te praviṣṭa śūrāḥ sarvaṃ jinagocaraṃ tulayamānā /
children.translated_text: Here these heroes have entered, fathoming the entire domain of the <s>Jinas</s>,
they abide for myriads of <s>kalpas</s> and yet do not reach satiation. (38)
Here they, with myriads of <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions), inexpressible, at every moment through wisdom,
reveal the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, according to their entry into <s>samādhi</s>. (39)
Here they, seizing upon a single moment, enter <s>kalpas</s>, <s>kṣetras</s>, and <s>Buddha</s>-names,
possessing vast wisdom, they exhaust immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>. (40)
Here they, standing as immeasurable ones, enter <s>kalpas</s> with a single thought,
free from the notion of conceptual construction, through a thought gone into the power of perception of beings. (41)
Here they, established in the mansion of <s>samādhi</s>, see the three times,
having attained koṭis in a single moment, wandering in the mansion of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). (42)
