body.translated_text: it becomes clear water, by being unturbid; it becomes an ornament of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, by rendering crooked the accumulation of roots of merit within the conditioned realm; it becomes the great king of mountains, by not falling from the three worlds; it becomes a protector, by not abandoning those who have taken refuge; it becomes a purpose, by conveying meaning; it becomes the mind, by satisfying the heart; it becomes a sacrificial implement, by nourishing the entire world; it becomes intelligence, by being the foremost and supreme among the minds of all the world; it becomes a treasury, by receiving all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; it becomes a summary, by gathering the conduct and vows of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; it becomes a guardian, by protecting the entire world; it becomes a defender, by turning back all evil; it becomes a net of <s>Indra</s>, by attracting the <s>asuras</s> of <s>kleśas</s>; it becomes the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>, by drawing in those to be trained; it becomes <s>Indra</s>'s fire, by burning all habitual imprints, latent tendencies, and <s>kleśas</s>; it becomes a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), for the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Thus indeed, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is endowed with these and other immeasurable distinctive qualities. In brief, son of good family, as many as are all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, just so many are the qualities of <s>bodhicitta</s> and the benefits of <s>bodhicitta</s> to be understood. For what reason? Because from this arises the entire maṇḍala of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. From this proceed the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present. Therefore, son of good family, one who has generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening is endowed with immeasurable qualities, being well-gathered by the disposition of the mind toward <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra, astyabhayā nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā pañca bhayāni na bhavanti / tadyathā - agninā na dahyate, viṣasya na ākramati, śastreṇa na kṣaṇyate, udakena nohyate, dhūmena na mriyate / evameva kulaputra sarvajñatācittauṣadhiparigṛhīto bodhisattvo rāgāgninā na dahyate, viṣayaviṣamasya nākramati, kleśaśastreṇa na kṣaṇyate, bhavaughena nohyate, saṃkalpadhūmena na mriyate / tadyathā kulaputra astyanirmuktā nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā gṛhītayā sarvaparopakramabhayāni na bhavanti / evameva bodhicittajñānauṣadhiparigṛhītasya bodhisattvasya sarvasaṃsāropakramabhayāni na bhavanti / tadyathā kulaputra, asti maghī nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā gṛhītayā gandhenaiva sarvāśīviṣāḥ palāyante / evameva bodhicittagandhenaiva sarvakleśāśīviṣāḥ palāyante / tadyathā kulaputra aparājitabhaiṣajyagṛhītaḥ puruṣo 'jayo bhavati sarvaśatrumaṇḍalena, evameva sarvajñatācittāparājitabhaiṣajyagṛhīto bodhisattvo durgharṣo bhavati sarvamārapratyarthikamaṇḍalena / tadyathā kulaputra asti vigamo nāma bhaiṣajyam / tena sarvaśalyāḥ patanti / evameva bodhicittavigamabhaiṣajyaparigṛhītasya bodhisattvasya sarvarāgadoṣamohadṛṣṭiśalyāḥ patanti /
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Abhayā</s> (Fearlessness). Through it, five fears do not arise. Namely: one is not burned by fire, poison does not take hold, one is not cut by weapons, one is not carried away by water, one does not die from smoke. Just so, son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses the medicine of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) is not burned by the fire of passion, is not afflicted by the poison of sense-objects, is not cut by the weapon of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is not carried away by the flood of existence, and does not die from the smoke of conceptual thinking. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Anirmuktā</s> (Never-released). When it is held, all fears from others' attacks do not arise. Just so, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses the medicine of the wisdom of <s>bodhicitta</s>, all fears from the attacks of <s>saṃsāra</s> do not arise. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Maghī</s>. When it is held, by its very fragrance all venomous serpents flee. Just so, by the very fragrance of <s>bodhicitta</s>, all the venomous serpents of <s>kleśas</s> flee. Just as, son of good family, a person who has taken the medicine <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquerable) becomes invincible to the entire host of enemies, just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has taken the unconquerable medicine of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> becomes unassailable by the entire host of <s>Māra</s> and his adversaries. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Vigama</s> (Removal) — through it, all thorns fall out. Just so, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses the medicine <s>Vigama</s> of <s>bodhicitta</s>, all the thorns of passion, hatred, delusion, and wrong views fall out.

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra asti sudarśano nāma mahābhaiṣajyarājaḥ / tadgṛhītaḥ sarvavyādhīnnirghātayati / evameva bodhicittasudarśanamahābhaiṣajyarājagṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ sarvakleśājñānavyādhīnnirghātayati / tadyathā kulaputra asti saṃtāno nāma mahābhaiṣajyavṛkṣaḥ / tasya sahanipātitā tvak sarvavraṇān saṃrohayati, yathotpāṭitāsya tvak saṃbhavati / evameva bodhisattvabījasaṃbhūtaḥ sarvajñatāsaṃtānavṛkṣaḥ sahadarśanena śrāddhānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ karmakleśavraṇān saṃrohayati / sa ca sarvajñatāvṛkṣaḥ sarvalokena akṣato 'nupahataḥ / tadyathā kulaputra astyanirvṛttamūlā nāma mahābhaiṣajyajātiḥ, yasyāḥ prabhāvena sarvajambudvīpakā
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, there is a great medicine-king called <s>Sudarśana</s> (Beautiful to Behold). One who holds it destroys all diseases. Just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who holds the great medicine-king <s>Sudarśana</s> of <s>bodhicitta</s> destroys all the diseases of <s>kleśas</s> and ignorance. Just as, son of good family, there is a great medicinal tree called <s>Saṃtāna</s> (Continuity). Its bark, the moment it is applied, heals all wounds, and when its bark is stripped off, it grows again. Just so, the tree of the continuity of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), born from the seed of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, at the very sight of it heals the wounds of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> in faithful sons of good family. And that tree of <s>sarvajñatā</s> remains unharmed and undamaged by the entire world. Just as, son of good family, there is a great medicinal species called <s>Anirvṛttamūlā</s> (Unfailing Root), by whose power all the inhabitants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>

body.text:
vṛkṣā sarvā vivardhante, evameva bodhicittanirvṛttamūlamahābhaiṣajyaprabhāvena sarvaśaikṣāśaikṣapratyekabuddhabodhisattvadharmataravo vivardhante / tadyathā kulaputra asti ratilambhā nāmauṣadhiḥ / sā yasya śarīragatā bhavati, tasya kāyacittakalyatā jāyate / evameva sarvajñatācittotpādaratilambhauṣadhiḥ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ kāyacittakalyatāṃ saṃjanayati / tadyathā kulaputra asti smṛtilabdhā nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā cittasmṛtirviśudhyati / evameva sarvajñatācittotpādasmṛtilambhauṣadhirbodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhadharmānāvaraṇasmṛtiviśuddhaye saṃvartate / tadyathā kulaputra asti mahāpadmā nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā kalpamāyuḥpramāṇaṃ bhavati / evameva bodhicittamahādharmauṣadhiprasito bodhisattvo 'saṃkhyeyakalpāyurvaśitāprāpto bhavati / tadyathā kulaputra asti adṛśyā nāmauṣadhiḥ / tayā gṛhītayā sarvamanuṣyāmanuṣyairna dṛśyate / evameva bodhicittādṛśyamahauṣadhigṛhīto vyavakīrṇavihārī bodhisattvaḥ sarvamāraviṣaye na dṛśyate / tadyathā kulaputra asti sarvamaṇiratnasamuccayaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnarājaṃ mahāsamudre / tasya anyalokadhātvasaṃkrāntasya asthānamanavakāśo yanmahāsamudrasya sarvakalpoddāhāgninā śakyaṃ tālamātramapi pariśoṣayitum / evameva sarvajñatācittotpādasarvamaṇiratnasamuccayamahāmaṇiratnarājādhyāśayasaṃtānagatānāṃ bodhisattvānāmasthānamanavakāśo yadekakuśalamapi sarvajñatāpariṇāmitaṃ praṇaśyet nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / utsṛṣṭe ca punaḥ sarvajñatācittotpāde sarvakuśalamūlānyupaśuṣyanti / tadyathā asti sarvaprabhāsasamuccayaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnam / tena kaṇṭhāvasaktena sarvamaṇiratnālaṃkārā jihmībhavanti / evameva bodhisattvasarvaprabhāsasamuccayamahāmaṇiratnāśayālaṃkārāvabaddho bodhisattvaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhacittotpādaratnālaṃkārānabhibhavati / tadyathā kulaputra
asti udakaprasādakaṃ mahāmaṇiratnam / tadvāriprakṣiptaṃ sarvakardamakāluṣyaṃ prasādayati / evameva bodhicittodakaprasādakamahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvakleśakardamakāluṣyaṃ prasādayati / tadyathā kulaputra udakasaṃvāsamaṇiratnāvabaddhaḥ kaivarta udake na mriyate, evameva sarvajñatācittodakasaṃvāsamaṇiratnagṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃsārasāgare na mriyate / tadyathā kulaputra asti nāgamaṇivarmamahāratnam / tena sahagate kaivartādayo jalajīvinaḥ sarvanāgabhavanāni praviśanto 'dhṛṣyā bhavanti sarvanāgoragaiḥ / evameva sarvajñatācittotpādajñānanāgamaṇidharmadhārī bodhisattvaḥ sarvakāmadhātubhavanāni praviśanna kṣaṇyate / tadyathā kulaputra śakrābhilagnamaṇiratnāvabaddhaḥ śakro devarājo sarvadevagaṇānabhibhavati, evameva sarvajñatācittaśakrābhilagnamahāmaṇiratnarājapraṇidhimakuṭāvabaddho bodhisattvaḥ sarvatraidhātukamabhibhavati / tadyathā kulaputra cintārājamahāmaṇiratnagṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvadāridryānna bibheti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādacintārājamahāmaṇiratnagṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ sarvopakaraṇajīvikābhayebhyo na bibheti / tadyathā kulaputra sūryakāntamaṇiratnaṃ sūryadarśitamagniṃ pramuñcati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādasūryakāntamaṇiratnaṃ prajñāratnaraśmisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ jñānāgniṃ pramuñcati / tadyathā kulaputra candrakāntaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ candrābhayā spṛṣṭamudakadhārāṃ pramuñcati, evameva bodhicittotpādacandrakāntamahāmaṇiratnaṃ kuśalamūlapariṇāmanācandraprabhāspṛṣṭaṃ sarvakuśalamūlapraṇidhitoyadhārāḥ
body.translated_text: all trees grow, just so, by the power of the great medicine whose root is the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, all <s>dharma</s>-trees of <s>śaikṣas</s> (trainees), <s>aśaikṣas</s> (those beyond training), <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s> flourish. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Ratilambhā</s> (Obtainer of Delight), and when it enters someone's body, well-being of body and mind arises — just so, the medicine of generating the mind of omniscience, <s>Ratilambhā</s>, generates well-being of body and mind for all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Smṛtilabdhā</s> (Obtainer of Mindfulness), by which mental mindfulness is purified — just so, the medicine of generating the mind of omniscience, <s>Smṛtilabdhā</s>, conduces to the purification of unobstructed mindfulness of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Mahāpadmā</s> (Great Lotus), by which one's lifespan becomes a <s>kalpa</s> in measure — just so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to the great <s>Dharma</s>-medicine of <s>bodhicitta</s> attains mastery over a lifespan of innumerable <s>kalpas</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a medicine called <s>Adṛśyā</s> (Invisible), by which the one who grasps it is not seen by any human or non-human beings — just so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has grasped the great medicine <s>Adṛśyā</s> of <s>bodhicitta</s>, though dwelling in ordinary life, is not seen in the entire domain of <s>Māra</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a great jewel-king called <s>Sarvamaṇiratnasamuccaya</s> (Collection of All Jewels) in the great ocean, and so long as it has not been transferred to another world-realm, there is no possibility or occasion for the fire of the conflagration of all <s>kalpas</s> to dry up even a palm-measure of the great ocean — just so, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> in whose mental continuum abides the great jewel-king of the resolute intention of the <s>Sarvamaṇiratnasamuccaya</s> of generating the mind of omniscience, there is no possibility that even a single root of merit dedicated to omniscience could perish — this situation does not exist. But if the generation of the mind of omniscience is abandoned, all roots of merit dry up. Just as there is a great jewel called <s>Sarvaprabhāsasamuccaya</s> (Collection of All Radiances), and when hung around the neck, all ornaments of other jewels become dim — just so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> adorned with the ornament of the resolute intention of the great jewel <s>Sarvaprabhāsasamuccaya</s> of <s>bodhicitta</s> outshines the jewel-ornaments of the mind-generation of all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a great jewel that purifies water, and when thrown into water, it clarifies all mud and turbidity — just so, the great water-purifying jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s> clarifies all the mud and turbidity of defilements. Just as, son of good family, a fisherman bound with the water-dwelling jewel does not die in water — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has grasped the water-dwelling jewel of the mind of omniscience does not die in the entire ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a great jewel called the <s>nāga</s>-jewel-armor, and fishermen and other water-dwellers who possess it, entering all <s>Nāga</s>-palaces, become invulnerable to all <s>Nāga</s>-serpents — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who bears the <s>Dharma</s> of the knowledge-<s>nāga</s>-jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, entering all the realms of the desire-world, is not injured. Just as, son of good family, <s>Śakra</s>, the king of gods, bound with the <s>Śakrābhilagna</s> (Śakra-adhering) jewel, outshines all the hosts of gods — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose crown of vows is bound with the great jewel-king <s>Śakrābhilagna</s> of the mind of omniscience outshines all the three realms. Just as, son of good family, a person who has grasped the wish-fulfilling great jewel <s>Cintārāja</s> does not fear any poverty — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has grasped the great wish-fulfilling jewel <s>Cintārāja</s> of generating the mind of omniscience does not fear any danger regarding requisites or livelihood. Just as, son of good family, the sun-stone jewel, when shown to the sun, releases fire — just so, the sun-stone jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, when touched by the rays of the jewel of wisdom, releases the fire of knowledge. Just as, son of good family, the great moonstone jewel, when touched by moonlight, releases streams of water — just so, the great moonstone jewel of generating <s>bodhicitta</s>, when touched by the moonlight of the dedication of roots of merit, releases streams of water of vows of all roots of merit

body.text:
pramuñcati / tadyathā kulaputra cintārājamaṇimakuṭāvabaddhānāṃ mahānāgarājānāṃ nāsti paropakramabhayam, evameva bodhicittamahākaruṇācintārājamaṇimakuṭāvabaddhānāṃ nāsti durgatyapāyopasaṃkramabhayam / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra jagadvyūhagarbhaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvasattvābhiprāyaparipūraṇatayā na kadācitkṣayamupaiti, evameva bodhisattvacittotpādasarvajagadvyūhagarbhamahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvasattvābhiprāyabodhipraṇidhiparipūraṇatayā na kadācitkṣayamupaiti / tadyathā kulaputra rājñaścakravartino mahāmaṇiratnaḥ sa tamondhakāravidhamaṃ gacchati, antaḥpuramadhyagataṃ ca prabhāsayati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādacakravartimahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvamavidyāndhakāravidhamaṃ sattvagatiṣu gacchati, kāmadhātusthitaṃ
ca mahājñānālokamavamuñcati / tadyathā kulaputra ye indranīlamahāmaṇiratnābhayā spṛśyante, sarve te indranīlamahāmaṇiratnavarṇā bhavanti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādendranīlamahāmaṇiratnaṃ yeṣu vicāryate preṣyate, yāni ca kuśalamūlāni sarvajñatācittotpādena pariṇamyante, tāni sarvāṇi sarvajñatāmahāmaṇiratnavarṇāni bhavanti / tadyathā kulaputra vaiḍūryamaṇiratnaṃ varṣaśatasahasramapi amedhyamadhyagataṃ tiṣṭhat sarvadaurgandhyena sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādātyantavimalaviśuddhaprabhamaṇiratnaṃ sarvapṛthagjanaśaikṣāśaikṣapratyekabuddhaguṇaratnākarānabhibhavati / tadyathā kulaputra ekamāgneyaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvatamondhakāraṃ vidhamati, evameva ekasarvajñatācittotpādāgneyamahāmaṇiratnaṃ vipaśyanāsaṃprayuktaṃ yoniśo manasikārataḥ sarvamajñānatamondhakāraṃ vidhamati / tadyathā kulaputra mahāsamudre potāropitamanardhyeyamaṇiratnaṃ vaṇigghastagataṃ nagarapratiṣṭhāni kācamaṇiśatasahasrāṇyabhibhavati varṇataśca āyataśca, evameva saṃsāramahāsamudragatamapi sarvajñatācittotpādānarghamahāmaṇiratnaṃ praṇidhipotāropitaṃ prathamacittotpādikabodhisattvādhyāśayasaṃtānagatamaprāptameva sarvajñatānagaraṃ vimuktinagaraṃ praviṣṭān sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakācamaṇikānabhibhavati / tadyathāsti vaśirājaṃ nāma maṇiratnaṃ yajjambudvīpagatameva catvāriṃśadyojanasahasrasthitānāṃ candrasūryamaṇḍalānāṃ bhavanavimānapratibhāsavyūhān saṃdarśayati, evameva sarvaguṇapariśodhitaṃ sarvajñatācittotpādavaśirājamaṇiratnaṃ saṃsāragatameva dharmadhātugaganagocarāṇāṃ tathāgatamahājñānasūryacandramasāṃ sarvabuddhaviṣayamaṇḍalapratibhāsavyūhān saṃdarśayati / tadyathā kulaputra yāvaccandrasūryamaṇḍalāni prabhayāvabhāsayanti, atrāntare ye keciddhanadhānyaratnajātarūparajatapuṣpagandhamālyavastraparibhogāḥ, sarve te vaśirājamaṇiratnasya mūlyaṃ na kṣamante, evameva yāvat tryadhvasu sarvajñajñānaṃ dharmadhātuviṣayamavabhāsayati, atrāntare yāni kāniciddevamanuṣyasarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalāni sāsravāṇyanāsravāṇi vā, sarvāṇi tāni bodhicittotpādavaśirājamahāmaṇiratnasya mūlyaṃ na kṣamante / tadyathā kulaputra asti sāgaravyūhagarbhaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ yatsarvamahāsāgaravyūhān saṃdarśayati,
evameva bodhicittotpādasāgaravyūhagarbhamahāmaṇiratnaṃ sarvajñajñānaviṣayasāgaravyūhaṃ saṃdarśayati / tadyathā kulaputra cintārājamaṇiratnaṃ sthāpayitvā nāsti kiṃcitprativiśiṣṭataraṃ divyena jāmbūnadasuvarṇena, evameva sarvajñajñānacintārājamahāmaṇiratnaṃ
body.translated_text: . Just as, son of good family, great <s>Nāgarājas</s> whose crowns are bound with the wish-fulfilling jewel <s>Cintārāja</s> have no fear of attack from others — just so, those whose crowns are bound with the wish-fulfilling jewel <s>Cintārāja</s> of the great compassion of <s>bodhicitta</s> have no fear of approaching bad destinies or lower realms. Just as, son of good family, the great jewel called <s>Jagadvyūhagarbha</s> (Womb of the Array of the World), through fulfilling the wishes of all beings, never reaches exhaustion — just so, the great jewel <s>Jagadvyūhagarbha</s> of generating <s>bodhicitta</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, through fulfilling the wishes and vows of awakening of all beings, never reaches exhaustion. Just as, son of good family, the great jewel of a <s>cakravartin</s> king dispels darkness and gloom and illuminates the inner chambers — just so, the <s>cakravartin</s> great jewel of generating the mind of omniscience goes among the courses of beings dispelling all darkness of ignorance, and while abiding in the desire-realm, it releases the great light of knowledge. Just as, son of good family, whatever is touched by the radiance of the great indranīla (sapphire) jewel, all become the color of the great indranīla jewel — just so, the indranīla great jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, in whatever [domains] it is applied and directed, and whatever roots of merit are dedicated through the generation of the mind of omniscience, all of them become the color of the great jewel of omniscience. Just as, son of good family, the <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl) jewel, even if it remains in filth for a hundred thousand years, does not coexist with any bad odor — just so, the absolutely stainless, pure, radiant jewel of generating the mind of omniscience outshines the jewel-mines of the qualities of all ordinary beings, <s>śaikṣas</s>, <s>aśaikṣas</s>, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as, son of good family, a single great fiery jewel called <s>Āgneya</s> dispels all darkness and gloom — just so, the single fiery great jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, conjoined with <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), through wise attention, dispels all darkness of ignorance. Just as, son of good family, a priceless jewel mounted on a ship in the great ocean, when it comes into the hands of a merchant and reaches a city, outshines hundreds of thousands of glass beads in both color and size — just so, the priceless great jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, even while in the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, mounted on the ship of vows, abiding in the mental continuum of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has first generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, even without having yet reached the city of omniscience, outshines all the glass beads of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> who have already entered the city of liberation. Just as there is a jewel called <s>Vaśirāja</s> (King of Mastery) which, though situated on <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, displays the reflected arrays of the palaces and mansions of the discs of the moon and sun situated forty thousand <s>yojanas</s> away — just so, the <s>Vaśirāja</s> jewel of generating the mind of omniscience, fully purified in all qualities, while situated in <s>saṃsāra</s>, displays the reflected arrays of the maṇḍalas of all <s>Buddha</s>-domains of the great knowledge-sun and -moon of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> whose domain is the sky of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Just as, son of good family, as far as the discs of the sun and moon illuminate with their radiance — within that range, whatever wealth, grain, jewels, gold, silver, flowers, fragrances, garlands, garments, and possessions exist, none of them equal the price of the <s>Vaśirāja</s> jewel — just so, as far as the omniscient knowledge in the three times illuminates the domain of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, within that range, whatever wholesome [deeds] of gods, humans, and all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, whether with or without outflows, none of them equal the price of the great <s>Vaśirāja</s> jewel of generating <s>bodhicitta</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a great jewel called <s>Sāgaravyūhagarbha</s> (Womb of the Array of the Ocean) which displays all the arrays of the great ocean — just so, the great jewel <s>Sāgaravyūhagarbha</s> of generating <s>bodhicitta</s> displays the array of the ocean of the domain of omniscient knowledge. Just as, son of good family, setting aside the wish-fulfilling jewel <s>Cintārāja</s>, nothing is more excellent than divine <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold — just so, setting aside the great wish-fulfilling jewel <s>Cintārāja</s> of omniscient knowledge

body.text: sthāpayitvā nāsti kiṃcitprativiśiṣṭataraṃ bodhicittotpādadivyajāmbūnadasuvarṇena / tadyathā kulaputra nāgamaṇḍalasiddha āhituṇḍikaḥ sarvanāgoragān vaśe sthāpayati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādapratipattināgamaṇḍalasiddho bodhisattvāhituṇḍikaḥ sarvakleśanāgoragān vaśe sthāpayati / tadyathā kulaputra praharaṇagṛhītaḥ śūro durgharṣo bhavati śatrumaṇḍalena, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādapraharaṇagṛhīto bodhisattvo durgharṣo bhavati sarvakleśaśatrumaṇḍalena /
body.translated_text: , nothing is more excellent than the divine <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold of generating <s>bodhicitta</s>. Just as, son of good family, a snake-charmer who has mastered the <s>nāga</s>-maṇḍala brings all <s>nāga</s>-serpents under his control — just so, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-snake-charmer who has mastered the <s>nāga</s>-maṇḍala of the practice of generating the mind of omniscience brings all the <s>nāga</s>-serpents of defilements under his control. Just as, son of good family, a hero who has grasped a weapon becomes unapproachable by the host of enemies — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has grasped the weapon of generating the mind of omniscience becomes unapproachable by the entire host of defilement-enemies. //

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra divyoragasāracandanasya ekacūrṇadhāraṇaṃ sāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ gandhena spharati, karṣapramāṇaṃ sarvatrisāhasre lokadhāturatnaparipūrṇena mūlyaṃ na kṣamate, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādadivyoragasāracandanasyaikādhyāśayadhātuḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ guṇagandhena spharati, sarvaśaikṣāśaikṣapratyekabuddhacittāni cābhibhavati / tadyathā kulaputra himavaccandanaṃ nāma mahācandanaratnaṃ sarvadāhaṃ praśamayati, sarvaṃ cāśrayaṃ śītalīkaroti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādahimavaccandanaratnaṃ sarvakleśasaṃkalparāgadoṣamohadāhaṃ praśamayati, jñānāśrayaṃ ca prahlādayati / tadyathā kulaputra ye sumeruṃ parvatarājamupasaṃkrāmanti, sarve te ekavarṇā bhavanti yaduta suvarṇavarṇāḥ, evameva ye sarvajñatācittotpādasamān bodhisattvānupasaṃkrāmanti, sarve te ekavarṇā bhavanti yaduta sarvajñatāvarṇāḥ / tadyathā kulaputra yaḥ pāriyātrakasya kovidārasya cchavigandhaḥ pravāti, sa sarvajambudvīpe sarvavārṣikājātisumanādīnāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ na saṃvidyate, evameva yo bodhisattvasya sarvajñatācittotpādabījapraṇidhivṛkṣaguṇajñānatvaco gandhaḥ pravāti, sa sarvapratyavarakuśalamūlānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavārṣikājātisumanānāmanāsravaśīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanānāṃ na saṃvidyate / tadyathā kulaputra pāriyātrakasya kovidārasya śuṅgībhūtasya veditavyaṃ bahūnāṃ puṣpaśatasahasrāṇāmāyadvāraṃ bhaviṣyatīti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādapāriyātrakavṛkṣasya kuśalamūlaśuṅgībhūtasya veditavyamasaṃkhyeyānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ sāsravanāsravabodhikusumāyadvāraṃ bhaviṣyatīti / tadyathā kulaputra yaḥ ekadivasaparibhāvitasya pāriyātrakusumairvastrasya tailasya vā gandhaḥ pravāti, sa divasatasahasraparibhāvitasya campakavārṣikāsumanābhivastrasya vā tailasya vā na saṃvidyate /
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, a single particle of the divine <s>uragasāra</s>-sandalwood pervades a thousandfold world-realm with its fragrance, and even a <s>karṣa</s>-weight of it cannot be valued by the entire trichiliocosm filled with jewels — just so, a single element of deep intention of the divine <s>uragasāra</s>-sandalwood of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) pervades the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with the fragrance of its qualities, and surpasses the minds of all <s>śaikṣa</s>s (learners), <s>aśaikṣa</s>s (those beyond learning), and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, the great sandalwood jewel called <s>Himavat</s>-sandalwood quenches all burning and makes every place cool — just so, the <s>Himavat</s>-sandalwood jewel of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> quenches the burning of all <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements), conceptual thought, desire, hatred, and delusion, and refreshes the basis of knowledge. Just as, son of good family, all who approach <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, become of one color — namely, the color of gold — just so, all who approach <s>bodhisattva</s>s who are like the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> become of one color — namely, the color of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Just as, son of good family, the fragrance of the bark of the <s>Pāriyātraka</s> <s>Kovidāra</s> tree, when it wafts forth, is not to be found among all the flower-species in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — the <s>Vārṣikā</s>, <s>Jāti</s>, <s>Sumanā</s>, and other flowers — just so, the fragrance of the bark of knowledge and qualities of the tree of the vow-seed of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, when it wafts forth, is not to be found among all inferior roots of wholesome merit, among the outflow-free moral conduct, <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, liberation, liberation-knowledge, and vision of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s — the <s>Vārṣikā</s>, <s>Jāti</s>, and <s>Sumanā</s> flowers. Just as, son of good family, when the <s>Pāriyātraka</s> <s>Kovidāra</s> tree has budded, it should be known that it will become the gateway for hundreds of thousands of flowers — just so, when the <s>Pāriyātraka</s> tree of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> has put forth the bud of roots of wholesome merit, it should be known that it will become the gateway for the awakening-flowers — both with and without outflows — of innumerable gods and humans. Just as, son of good family, the fragrance of a cloth or oil permeated for a single day with <s>Pāriyātraka</s> flowers is not to be found in a cloth or oil permeated for a hundred thousand days with <s>Campaka</s>, <s>Vārṣikā</s>, and <s>Sumanā</s> flowers,

body.text: evameva ya ekajanmaparibhāvitasya sarvajñatācittasaṃtānasya bodhisattvaguṇajñānagandho daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhapādamūleṣu pravāti, sa kalpaśatasahasraparibhāvitānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhacittānāmanāsravakuśaladharmajñānagandho na saṃvidyate / tadyathā kulaputra asti nālīkerī nāma vṛkṣajātiḥ udyatake samudre saṃbhūtā / sā mūlata upādāya yāvatpuṣpaphalaparyantātsarvakālaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ na kadācinnopajīvyā bhavati / evameva mahākaruṇāpraṇidhimūlasaṃjāto bodhisattvasya prathamasarvajñatācittotpādo yāvatsaddharmasthitiparyavasānāt sadevakasya lokasya na kadācinnopajīvyo bhavati / tadyathā kulaputra asti hāṭakaprabhāsaṃ nāma rasajātam / tasya ekapalaṃ lohapalasahasraṃ svarṇīkaroti / na ca tadrasapalaṃ śakyaṃ tena lohapalasahasreṇa paryādātuṃ na lohīkartum / evameva ekasarvajñatācittotpādarasadhātuḥ kuśalamūlapariṇāmanājñānasaṃgṛhītaḥ sarvakarmakleśāvaraṇalohāni
body.translated_text: just so, the fragrance of the qualities and knowledge of a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose continuum of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> has been permeated for a single birth, wafting forth at the feet of all <s>Buddha</s>s in the ten directions, is not to be found in the fragrance of the outflow-free knowledge of wholesome <s>dharma</s>s of the minds of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s permeated for a hundred thousand <s>kalpa</s>s. Just as, son of good family, there is a species of tree called <s>Nālikerī</s> (coconut palm), growing in the ocean called <s>Udyataka</s>; from its root up to the end of its flowers and fruits, at all times it is never without sustenance for all beings — just so, the first arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, born from the root of the vow of great compassion, is never without sustenance for the world with its gods, from beginning to the end of the duration of the true <s>dharma</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is a chemical substance called <s>Hāṭakaprabhāsa</s>; a single <s>pala</s>-weight of it turns a thousand <s>pala</s>-weights of iron into gold, yet that single <s>pala</s> of the substance cannot be consumed or turned into iron by those thousand <s>pala</s>s of iron — just so, a single element of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, gathered by the knowledge of the dedication of roots of wholesome merit, consumes all the iron of obstructions of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>s and

body.text:
paryādāya sarvadharmān sarvajñatāvarṇān karoti / na ca sarvajñatācittotpādarasadhātuḥ śakyaṃ sarvakarmakleśalohaiḥ saṃkleśayituṃ paryādātuṃ vā / tadyathā kulaputra kiyatparītto 'pyagniryāvadupādānaṃ labhate tāvatīṃ jvālāṃ pramuñcati, evameva kiyatparītto 'pi sarvajñatācittotpādāgnirārambaṇavyavakīrṇatayā yāvat saṃbhāropādānaṃ labhate, tāvadvivardhate jñānārciḥpramocanatayā / tadyathā kulaputra ekasmātpradīpādanekāni pradīpakoṭīśatasahasrāṇyādīpyante, akṣaya eva pradīpo bhavatyaparyādattaḥ sarvapradīpaniryāṇaiḥ evameva ekasmātsarvajñatācittotpādapradīpādatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvajñatācittotpādapradīpānāṃ dīpyamānānāmakṣaya eva sa ekaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādapradīpo 'vabhāti aparyādattaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādapradīpaniryāṇaiḥ / tadyathā kulaputra ekaḥ pradīpo yādṛśe gṛhe vātāyane vā praveśyate, sahapraveśito varṣasahasrasaṃcitamapi tamondhakāraṃ vidhamati avabhāsaṃ ca karoti, evameva ekasarvajñatācittotpādapradīpo yādṛśe sattvāśayagṛhagahane 'vidyātamondhakārānugate praveśyate, sa sahapraveśito 'nabhilāpyakalpaśatasahasrasaṃcitamapi kleśāvaraṇatamondhakāraṃ vidhamati, jñānālokaṃ ca saṃjanayati / tadyathā kulaputra yādṛśī pradīpavartirbhavati tādṛśaṃ pradīpo 'vabhāsaṃ karoti, yāvāṃśca snehasaṃcayo bhavati tāvaddīpyate / evameva yasya bodhisattvasya yādṛśī praṇidhānavartiviśeṣatā bhavati, tādṛśaṃ sarvajñatācittotpādapradīpo dharmadhātvavabhāsaṃ karoti / yāvacca mahākaruṇācaryāsnehasaṃcayo bhavati, tāvatsattvavinayakṣetraviśuddhibuddhakāryaprabhāvanā bhavati / tadyathā kulaputra divyajāmbūnadasuvarṇālaṃkāro vaśavartino devarājasya mūrdhnāvabaddho 'saṃhāryo bhavati sarvakāmāvacarairdevaputraiḥ,
evameva pratipattiguṇapratiṣṭhitaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādadivyajāmbūnadasuvarṇālaṃkāro 'vinivartanīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāpraṇidhānamūrdhnāvabaddho 'saṃhāryo bhavati sarvabālapṛthagjanaśaikṣāśaikṣapratyekabuddhaiḥ / tadyathā kulaputra siṃhasya mṛgarājasya nādena acirajātāḥ siṃhapotāḥ puṣyanti, sarvamṛgāśca vilayaṃ gacchanti, evameva tathāgatapuruṣasiṃhasya bodhicittasaṃvarṇanasarvajñatānādena prayuktena sarvādikarmikabodhisattvasiṃhapotāḥ puṣyanti buddhadharmaiḥ, sarvopalambhasaṃniśritāśca sattvā vilayaṃ gacchanti / tadyathā kulaputra siṃhasnāyukṛtavīṇātantrīśabdena sarvavīṇātantryaḥ saṃchidyante, evameva pāramitāśarīratathāgatasiṃhabodhicittotpādasnāyutantrīguṇavarṇaśabdena sarvakāmaguṇarativīṇātantryaḥ saṃchidyante, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhacaryāguṇakathāśca saṃnirūdhyante / tadyathā kulaputra gomahiṣyajākṣīrapūrṇamahāsamudre ekasiṃhadugdhabinduprakṣepeṇa sarvakṣīrāṇyapakrāmanti, na saṃdhayati, evameva kalpaśatasahasrasaṃcitaḥ karmakleśakṣīramahāsamudraḥ tathāgatamahāpuruṣasiṃhasarvajñatācittotpādadugdhaikabinduprakṣepeṇa sarvo 'navaśeṣaḥ kṣayaṃ gacchanti, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavimuktayaśca na saṃtiṣṭhante, na saṃvasati / tadyathā kulaputra aṇḍakośādanirgatasya kalaviṅkapotasya yo nādabalaviśeṣaḥ sarvabalavegasaṃpannānāṃ himavannivāsināṃ sarvapakṣigaṇānāṃ na saṃvidyate, evameva yaḥ saṃsārāṇḍakośagatasyādikarmikabodhisattvakalaviṅkapotasya mahākaruṇābodhicittanādabalaviśeṣaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ na saṃvidyate / tadyathā kulaputra yo 'cirajātasya mahāgaruḍendrapotasya pakṣavātabalaparākramo nayanapariśuddhiguṇaśca,
body.translated_text: makes all <s>dharma</s>s the color of <s>sarvajñatā</s>; yet the element of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> cannot be defiled or consumed by all the iron of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>s. Just as, son of good family, however small a fire may be, it sends forth as much flame as the fuel it obtains — just so, however small the fire of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> may be, because it is scattered among objects, it grows in proportion to the fuel of accumulations it obtains, by sending forth the flames of knowledge. Just as, son of good family, from a single lamp innumerable tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of lamps are lit, and yet that lamp remains inexhaustible, not consumed by all the emanations of lamps — just so, from the single lamp of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, the lamps of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the past, future, and present are lit, and yet that single lamp of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> shines inexhaustibly, not consumed by all the emanations of the lamps of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Just as, son of good family, when a single lamp is brought into any house or window, the moment it is brought in, it dispels even the darkness accumulated over a thousand years and produces light — just so, when the single lamp of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> is brought into the dense dwelling of the deep dispositions of any being, enveloped in the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the moment it is brought in, it dispels even the darkness of the obstructions of <s>kleśa</s>s accumulated over inexpressible hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpa</s>s, and produces the light of knowledge. Just as, son of good family, as is the wick of a lamp, so is the light the lamp produces, and as much as the store of oil, so long does it burn — just so, as is the distinctive quality of the wick of vows of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, so does the lamp of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> produce illumination of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; and as much as the store of the oil of the conduct of great compassion, so much is the manifestation of the <s>Buddha</s>-work of the purification of fields for the discipline of beings. Just as, son of good family, the divine <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold ornament fastened to the crown of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> lord of gods cannot be taken away by all the <s>devaputra</s>s of the desire-realm — just so, the divine <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold ornament of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, established in the qualities of practice, fastened to the crown of the great vow of irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s>s, cannot be taken away by all foolish ordinary beings, <s>śaikṣa</s>s, <s>aśaikṣa</s>s, and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, by the roar of the lion, the king of beasts, newborn lion cubs grow, and all other animals flee — just so, by the sound of <s>sarvajñatā</s> employed in praising the awakening-mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the lion among men, all beginner-<s>bodhisattva</s> lion cubs grow in the <s>dharma</s>s of a <s>Buddha</s>, and all beings who rely on apprehension flee. Just as, son of good family, by the sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> string made from lion sinew, all other <s>vīṇā</s> strings are severed — just so, by the sound of the praise of the qualities of the sinew-string of the arising of the awakening-mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lion with a body of <s>pāramitā</s>s, all the strings of the <s>vīṇā</s> of delight in sense-pleasures are severed, and all narratives of the qualities of the conduct of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s are silenced. Just as, son of good family, by dropping a single drop of lion's milk into a great ocean full of the milk of cows, buffaloes, and goats, all the milks recede and do not coagulate — just so, by dropping a single drop of the milk of the arising of the mind of <s>sarvajñatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the great lion among men, into the great ocean of the milk of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>s accumulated over a hundred thousand <s>kalpa</s>s, all of it without remainder goes to destruction, and the liberations of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s do not remain, do not coexist. Just as, son of good family, the distinctive power of the call of a <s>Kalaviṅka</s> chick that has not yet emerged from the eggshell is not to be found among all the flocks of birds dwelling on the <s>Himālaya</s>s, endowed with all the strength and power — just so, the distinctive power of the call of the awakening-mind of great compassion of the beginner-<s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Kalaviṅka</s> chick dwelling within the eggshell of <s>saṃsāra</s> is not to be found among all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, the strength of the wing-wind and the quality of the purity of vision of a newly-born chick of the great <s>Garuḍa</s>-king

body.text:
sa sarvaśarīrapravṛddhānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ na saṃvidyate, evameva yaḥ prathamacittotpādikasya tathāgatamahāgaruḍendrasya kulagotrasaṃbhavasya bodhisattvamahāgaruḍendrapotasya sarvajñatācittotpādabalaparākramo mahākaruṇādhyāśayanayanapariśuddhiguṇaśca, sa kalpaśatasahasraniryātānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ na saṃvidyate / tadyathā kulaputra mahāpuruṣahastagato nārācaḥ kiyaddṛḍhamapi varma nirbhinatti, evameva dṛḍhavīryabodhisattvahastagataḥ sarvajñatācittotpādanārācaḥ sarvadṛṣṭyanuśayavarmāṇi nirbhinatti / tadyathā kulaputra
krodhāviṣṭasya mahānagnasya yāvallalāṭe piṭakāstiṣṭhanti, tāvadaghṛṣyo bhavati sarvajambudvīpakairmanuṣyaiḥ, evameva mahāmaitrīmahākarūṇāviṣṭasya bodhisattvamahānagnasya yāvadadhyāśayavadane sarvajñatācittotpādapiṭakā na vigacchanti, tāvadaghṛṣyo bhavati sarvalokadhātuparyāpannaiḥ sarvamāraiḥ sarvakarmabhiśca / tadyathā kulaputra yaḥ śikṣitasyeṣvastrāntevāsina iṣvastrajñāne kṛtābhyāsasya śilpasthānayogabalaviśeṣaḥ, sa sarvaśikṣitasya iṣvastrācāryasya na saṃvidyate, evameva yaḥ sarvādikarmikasya sarvajñatābhūmyā kṛtābhyāsasya bodhisattvājāneyasya praṇidhijñānādhimukticaryābalaviśeṣaḥ, so 'nutpāditabodhicittānāṃ sarvaśaikṣāśaikṣapratyekabuddhānāṃ ca na saṃvidyate / tadyathā kulaputra iṣvastraṃ śikṣamāṇasya prathamaḥ padabandhayogyābhyāsaḥ pūrvaṃgamo bhavati sarveṣvastrajñānasya, evameva bodhisattvasya sarvajñabhūmau śikṣamāṇasya prathamaṃ sarvajñatācittādhyāśayasaṃprasthānaṃ pūrvagamaṃ bhavati sarvabuddhadharmādhigamāya / tadyathā kulaputra māyākārasya māyāgataviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayamānasya prathamamantrapadasiddhyabhinirhārameva manasikurvāṇasya sarvakriyāsiddhirbhavati, evameva bodhisattvasya sarvabuddhabodhisattvaviṣayavikurvāḥ saṃdarśayataḥ prathamacittotpādapraṇidhānābhinirhāra evotthāpako bhavati sarvabuddhabodhisattvaviṣayasya / tadyathā kulaputra sarvamāyāvidyāmantrāścārūpiṇo 'nidarśanāḥ sarvamāyānirmāṇarūpagatāni saṃdarśayanti cittotpādena, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādaścārūpyānidarśanaḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ viṭhapayati sarvaguṇālaṃkāravyūhaiścittotpādavaśitāmātreṇa / tadyathā kulaputra mārjārasya sahadṛṣṭavicāramātreṇa sarvamūṣikā vilayamāpadyante, evameva bodhisattvasya sarvajñatācittotpādādhyāśayaprayogavicāramātreṇa sarvakarmakleśā vilayamāpadyante / tadyathā kulaputra jāmbūnadasuvarṇālaṃkāra ābaddhaḥ sarvābharaṇāni jihmīkaroti, evameva bodhicittajāmbūnadasuvarṇālaṃkārādhyāśayāvabaddho bodhisattvaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaguṇālaṃkārānabhibhavati jihmīkaroti / tadyathā kulaputra ayaskāntarājasya kiyatparītto 'pi dhātuḥ sarvadṛḍhamāyasaṃ bandhanaṃ sphoṭayati, evameva kiyatparītto 'pyadhyāśayotpāditaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādadhātuḥ
sarvadṛṣṭikṛtāvidyātṛṣṇābandhanāni sphoṭayati / tadyathā kulaputra yatra yatraiva ayaskāntadhāturvicāryate, tatra tatraiva sarvāṇītarāṇyayāṃsi palāyante, na tiṣṭhante na saṃdadhati / evameva yatra yatraiva sarvajñatācittotpādadhāturvicāryate kārmeṣu vā kleśeṣu vā śrāvakapratyekabuddhavimuktau vā, tatastata eva karmakleśāḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavimuktayaśca palāyante na tiṣṭhanti, na saṃdadhati / tadyathā kulaputra makaraviddhāśritaḥ kaivartaḥ sarvodakaprāṇibhayavinirvṛto bhavatyanupaghātaśarīro makaramukhagato 'pi, evameva adhyāśayabodhicittaviddhāśrito
body.translated_text: that [power] which exists in all full-grown birds of other kinds does not exist [in the chick]. Just so, the power and prowess of the arising of the mind of omniscience and the quality of the purity of the eye of deep intention of great compassion that belong to a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is a great <s>Garuḍa</s>-chick, born of the family and lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s> great <s>Garuḍa</s>-lord, one who has just generated the first aspiration — that does not exist in all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s who have gone forth for a hundred thousand <s>kalpa</s>s. Just as, son of good family, an iron arrow grasped by a great man pierces through even the most solid armor, just so the arrow of the arising of the mind of omniscience grasped by a <s>bodhisattva</s> of firm vigor pierces through all the armors of latent views. Just as, son of good family, as long as the boils remain on the forehead of a great naked ascetic possessed by wrath, he is invincible to all humans in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — just so, as long as the boils of the arising of the mind of omniscience do not depart from the face of the deep intention of the <s>bodhisattva</s> great naked ascetic possessed by great loving-kindness and great compassion, he is invincible to all <s>Māra</s>s and all <s>karma</s>s included in all world-realms. Just as, son of good family, the excellence of power in the art and application of skill that belongs to a trained student of archery who has practiced in the knowledge of archery does not exist in the fully trained archery teacher — just so, the excellence of power in the conduct of aspiration, knowledge, and devotion of a noble <s>bodhisattva</s> who is a beginner practiced on the stage of omniscience does not exist in all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s, trainees, non-trainees, and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s who have not generated <s>bodhicitta</s>. Just as, son of good family, for one training in archery, the first practice of the proper stance is the precursor of all knowledge of weapons — just so, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> training on the stage of omniscience, the first setting-forth with the deep intention of the mind of omniscience is the precursor for the attainment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. Just as, son of good family, for a magician displaying a domain produced by magic, the accomplishment of all actions comes merely from attending to the first accomplishment of the mantra-formula — just so, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> displaying the transformations of the domain of all <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s, the accomplishment of the first aspiration at the arising of the mind is the very producer of the entire domain of all <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Just as, son of good family, all magical knowledge-mantras are formless and invisible, yet by a mere act of mind they display all forms produced by magical creation — just so, the arising of the mind of omniscience is formless and invisible, yet by the mere mastery of the arising of mind it fills the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> with all arrays of ornaments of qualities. Just as, son of good family, merely by the cat's glance of investigation, all mice run away — just so, merely by the investigation of the effort of deep intention in the arising of the mind of omniscience of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, all <s>karma</s>s and afflictions run away. Just as, son of good family, an ornament of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, when worn, outshines all other ornaments — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> bound with the ornament of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold of the deep intention of <s>bodhicitta</s> overpowers and outshines all the ornaments of qualities of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, even a small quantity of the loadstone king shatters all firm iron bonds — just so, even a small [quantity] of the element of the arising of the mind of omniscience, generated by deep intention, shatters all the bonds of views, constructed ignorance, and craving. Just as, son of good family, wherever the loadstone element moves, all other iron objects flee and do not remain or adhere — just so, wherever the element of the arising of the mind of omniscience moves — whether among <s>karma</s>s, or afflictions, or the liberation of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s — from there all <s>karma</s>s and afflictions and all liberations of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s flee, do not remain, and do not adhere. body.text: bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃsārakarmakleśabhayavinivṛtto bhavati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhābhisamayāntaraprāptyanughātyo bhūtakoṭīsākṣātkriyāpraṇāśapathāpatanatayā / tadyathā kulaputra amṛtapānapītaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaparopakramairna mriyate, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādāmṛtapānapīto bodhisattvaḥ sarvaśrāvakabhūmiṣu na mriyate, na coparamati bodhisattvamahākaruṇāpraṇidhānāt / tadyathā kulaputra añjanasiddhaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvamanuṣyabhavaneṣu cānuvicarati na ca sarvamanuṣyairdṛśyate, evameva bodhicittotpādaprajñāpraṇidhyupastabdho bodhisattvaḥ sarvamāraviṣayeṣu cānuvicarati, sarvamāraiśca na dṛśyate / tadyathā kulaputra mahārājasaṃniśritaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaprākṛtajanāt na bibheti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādamahādharmarājasaṃniśrito bodhisattvaḥ sarvāvaraṇanivaraṇadurgatibhyo na bibheti / tadyathā kulaputra parvatagṛheṣu sarvabhūmyantargatapānīyabhayānnāstyagnibhayam, evameva bodhicittakuśalamūlābhiṣyanditasaṃtānasya bodhisattvasya nāsti śrāvakapratyekabuddhavimuktijñānāgnibhayam / tadyathā kulaputra śūrasaṃniśritaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaśatrubhyo na bibheti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādaśūrasaṃniśrito bodhisattvaḥ sarvaduścaritaśatrubhyo na bibheti /
body.translated_text: <s>bodhisattva</s> who has seized the deep intention of <s>bodhicitta</s> is freed from fear of all <s>karma</s>s and afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is not harmed by the attainment of realization of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, because he does not fall onto the path of destruction through the direct realization of the limit of reality. Just as, son of good family, a man who has drunk the elixir of immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) does not die through any attack by others — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has drunk the elixir of the arising of the mind of omniscience does not die on any of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stages, and does not cease from the vow of <s>bodhisattva</s> great compassion. Just as, son of good family, a man who has attained the accomplishment of a magical ointment wanders through all human dwellings and is not seen by any humans — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> supported by the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, wisdom, and vow wanders through all domains of <s>Māra</s> and is not seen by any <s>Māra</s>s. Just as, son of good family, a man who relies on a great king does not fear any common people — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who relies on the great <s>Dharma</s>-king of the arising of the mind of omniscience does not fear any obscurations, hindrances, or bad destinies. Just as, son of good family, in mountain dwellings there is no fear of fire because all the water is underground — just so, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose continuum is overflowed by the wholesome roots of <s>bodhicitta</s>, there is no fear of the fire of the knowledge of the liberation of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, a man who relies on a hero does not fear any enemies — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who relies on the hero of the arising of the mind of omniscience does not fear any enemies of evil conduct.

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra vajrapraharaṇagṛhītaḥ śakro devendraḥ sarvāsuragaṇaṃ pramardayati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādadṛḍhādhyāśayavajrapraharaṇagṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ sarvamāraparapravādyasuragaṇaṃ pramardayati / tadyathā kulaputra rasāyanopayuktaḥ puruṣo dīrghamāyuḥ pālayati na ca durbalībhavati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādarasāyanasaṃbhāraprayukto bodhisattvo 'saṃkhyeyān kalpān saṃsāre saṃsaranna parikhidyate, na ca saṃsāradoṣairlipyate / tadyathā kulaputra sarvabhaiṣajyarasasaṃprayogeṣu pānīyaṃ pūrvaṃgamaṃ na kvacidduṣyati, evameva sarvabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānasaṃbhārayogeṣu sarvajñatācittotpādaḥ pūrvaṃgamo bhavati, na kvacidduṣyati / tadyathā kulaputra puruṣasya sarvakāryeṣu jīvitendriyaṃ pūrvaṃgamam, evameva bodhisattvasya sarvabuddhadharmādāneṣu bodhicittaṃ pūrvaṃgamam / tadyathā kulaputra jīvitendriyavimuktaḥ puruṣo nirupajīvyo bhavati mātāpitṛjñātivargasya sarvakarmāsamarthatvāt, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādaviyukto bodhisattvaḥ sarvajñatāguṇanirupajīvyo bhavati sarvasattvānāṃ buddhajñānapratilambhāsamarthatvāt / tadyathā kulaputra mahāsamudraḥ sarvaviṣairadūṣyo bhavati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādamahāsamudro 'dūṣyo bhavati sarvakarmakleśaśrāvakapratyekabuddhacittotpādaviṣaiḥ / tadyathā kulaputra sūryamaṇḍalamaparyantaḥ sarvatārāvabhāsaiḥ, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādasūryamaṇḍalamaparyāpannaṃ bhavati, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatārānāsravaguṇānabhibhavati / tadyathā kulaputra acirajāto rājaputro mūrdhaprāptān sarvavṛddhāmātyānabhibhavati kulābhijātyādhipatyena, evameva acirotpāditabodhicittastathāgatadharmarājakulapratyājāta ādikarmiko bodhisattvaściracaritabrahmacaryān vṛddhaśrāvakānabhibhavati bodhicittamahākaruṇādhipatyena / tadyathā kulaputra kiyadvṛddhenāpyamātyena kiyadbālasyāpi rājakumārasya praṇipatitavyam, na ca rājaputreṇa vṛddhāmātyasya gauravaṃ na karaṇīyam, evameva kiyadvṛddhairapi ciracaritabrahmacaryaiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhairādikarmikasya bodhisattvasya avanamitavyam, na ca bodhisattvena pratyekabuddheṣu gauravaṃ na karaṇīyam / tadyathā kulaputra
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of gods, grasping the <s>vajra</s>-weapon, crushes all hosts of <s>Asura</s>s — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> grasping the <s>vajra</s>-weapon of firm deep intention in the arising of the mind of omniscience crushes all hosts of <s>Māra</s>s and proponents of rival doctrines. Just as, son of good family, a man who has consumed the elixir of rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) preserves a long life and does not become weak — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> engaged in the provisions of the elixir of the arising of the mind of omniscience transmigrates in <s>saṃsāra</s> for innumerable <s>kalpa</s>s without becoming wearied and is not stained by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Just as, son of good family, in all compounds of medicinal essences, water is the precursor and never spoils — just so, in all undertakings of the provisions and vows of <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, the arising of the mind of omniscience is the precursor and never spoils. Just as, son of good family, the life-faculty is the precursor for a man in all his activities — just so, <s>bodhicitta</s> is the precursor for a <s>bodhisattva</s> in receiving all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. Just as, son of good family, a man separated from the life-faculty is of no sustenance to his parents and relatives, being incapable of all activities — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> separated from the arising of the mind of omniscience is of no sustenance for the qualities of omniscience for all beings, being incapable of attaining <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. Just as, son of good family, the great ocean is not spoiled by any poisons — just so, the great ocean of the arising of the mind of omniscience is not spoiled by the poisons of all <s>karma</s>s, afflictions, and the mental arisings of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. Just as, son of good family, the maṇḍala of the sun is not encompassed by all the lights of the stars — just so, the sun-maṇḍala of the arising of the mind of omniscience is not encompassed by the undefiled qualities of all the stars of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s — it overpowers them. Just as, son of good family, a newly-born prince overpowers all aged ministers who have attained the highest rank, by the sovereignty of his noble birth — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is a beginner, newly born in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharma</s>-king, who has recently generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, overpowers aged <s>Śrāvaka</s>s who have long practiced the holy life, by the sovereignty of <s>bodhicitta</s> and great compassion. Just as, son of good family, an aged minister, however old, must bow before even a young prince, and yet the prince should not fail to show reverence to the aged minister — just so, even aged <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s who have long practiced the holy life must bow before a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>, and yet the <s>bodhisattva</s> should not fail to show reverence to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s.
