sarvāparibhūto rājaputro 'virahito rājalakṣaṇena sarvāgratāprāptairapi rājāmātyairna samo jātyadhyakṣatvāt, evameva kiyatkarmakleśopādānaparibhūta ādikarmiko bodhisattvaḥ
sarvajñatācittotpādalakṣaṇenāvirahitaḥ sarvāgraprāptairapi sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairna samo buddhakulādhipatyādhyakṣatvāt / tadyathā kulaputra pariśuddhamaṇiratnaṃ cakṣustimiradoṣeṇāpariśuddhamityābhāsamāgacchati, evameva prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ sarvajñatācittotpādaratnaṃ sattvā aśraddhānayanājñānatimiradoṣeṇāpariśuddhamiti saṃjānanti / tadyathā kulaputra sarvavidyauṣadhisaṃgrahasaṃprayukto bhaiṣajyavigraho darśanasparśanasaṃvāsanaiḥ sattvānāṃ vyādhīn śamayati, evameva sarvakuśalamūlopacayaprajñopāyavidyauṣadhisaṃgṛhītaṃ bodhicittasaṃprayuktaṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhijñānaśarīraṃ śravaṇadarśanasaṃvāsanānusmṛtiprayogena sattvānāṃ kleśavyādhīn praśamati / tadyathā kulaputra haṃsalakṣaṇaṃ vastraṃ sarvakardamadoṣairna kliśyate, evameva bodhicittotpādahaṃsalakṣaṇavastraṃ saṃsārakleśakardamadoṣairna kliśyate / tadyathā kulaputra mūrdhaśalyasaṃgṛhīto dāruvigraho na vikīryate, sarvakriyāścānubhavati, evameva bodhicittotpādapraṇidhimūrdhaśalyasaṃgṛhītaṃ sarvajñatāpraṇidhijñānaśarīraṃ bodhisattvakriyāsamarthaṃ bhavati, na ca vikīryate sarvajñatāpraṇidhiśarīratvāt / tadyathā kulaputra śalyavimuktaṃ yantramakāryasamarthaṃ bhavati tānyeva dārupratyaṅgāni, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādādhyāśayaviyukto bodhisattvo buddhadharmapariniṣpādanāsamartho bhavati, evaṃ ca te bodhyaṅgasaṃbhārāḥ / tadyathā kulaputra rājñaścakravartino hastigarbhaṃ nāma kālāgaruratnam /
body.translated_text: a prince who is not despised by anyone, not separated from the marks of royalty, is not equal even to ministers who have attained the highest rank, because of his sovereignty of noble birth — just so, a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>, however much despised through the appropriation of <s>karma</s> and afflictions, is not separated from the mark of the arising of the mind of omniscience and is not equal even to all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s who have attained the highest [rank], because of the sovereignty of the supremacy of the <s>Buddha</s>-family. Just as, son of good family, a pure gem-jewel appears to be impure through the defect of the dimness of [defective] eyesight — just so, beings perceive the gem of the arising of the mind of omniscience, which is pure by nature, to be impure through the defect of the dimness of faithless eyes and ignorance. Just as, son of good family, a medicinal body compounded with all knowledge-herbs and medicines pacifies the diseases of beings through seeing, touching, and being near — just so, the body of <s>bodhisattva</s>-vow-knowledge, conjoined with <s>bodhicitta</s> and gathered together with the medicine-herbs of the knowledge of wisdom and skillful means accumulated from all wholesome roots, pacifies the diseases of afflictions of beings through hearing, seeing, being near, and the application of recollection. Just as, son of good family, a cloth bearing the mark of a <s>haṃsa</s> (goose) is not soiled by any stains of mud — just so, the cloth bearing the mark of a <s>haṃsa</s> of the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> is not soiled by the stains of the mud of <s>saṃsāra</s> and afflictions. Just as, son of good family, a wooden body held together by a head-pin is not scattered and performs all functions — just so, the body of the knowledge of the vow of omniscience held together by the head-pin of the vow of the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s> is capable of <s>bodhisattva</s> activities and is not scattered, because it is the body of the vow of omniscience. Just as, son of good family, the same wooden limbs, when separated from the pin, are incapable of any function — just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> separated from the deep intention of the arising of the mind of omniscience is incapable of accomplishing <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — and such too are the limbs of the provisions of awakening. Just as, son of good family, a <s>Cakravartin</s> king has a <s>kālāgaru</s> (aloe-wood) gem called <s>Hastigarbha</s> (Elephant-Womb) —

body.text: tena saha dhūpitamātraḥ sarvarājñaścaturaṅgabalakāyo vihāyase tiṣṭhati / evameva sarvajñatācittotpādāgarudhūpitāni bodhisattvasya kuśalamūlāni sarvatraidhātukavyativṛttāni bhavanti asaṃskṛtasarvatathāgatajñānagaganagocaraparyavasānāni / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ netarādratnākarādutpadyate 'nyatra vajrākarātsuvarṇākarādvā, evameva vajropamaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādaḥ / sa netarātsattvāśayakuśalamūlaratnākarādutpadyate 'nyatra sattvaparitrāṇamahākaruṇāvajrākarāt sarvajñajñānādhyālambanamahāsuvarṇākarādvā / tadyathā kulaputra astyamūlā nāma vṛkṣajātiḥ / tasya mūlapratiṣṭhānaṃ nopalabhyate sarvaśākhāpatrapalāśasaṃkusumitā ca vṛkṣeṣu jālībhūtā ca saṃdṛśyate, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādasya mūlapratiṣṭhānaṃ nopalabhyate, sarvapuṇyajñānābhijñāsaṃkusumitaścasa sarvalokopapattiṣu mahāpraṇidhānajālībhūtaḥ saṃdṛśyate / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ netare bhājane tiṣṭhacchobhate, nāpi cchidraśuṣirabhājanena śakyaṃ saṃdhārayitumanyatra acchidrabhāja 'nena, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādavajraṃ na hīnādhimuktikeṣu sattvabhājaneṣu matsariṣu duḥśīleṣu vyāpannacitteṣu kusīdeṣu muṣitasmṛtiṣu duḥprajñeṣu śobhate, nādhyāśayavipannacalācalabuddhisarvabhājanena śakyaṃ saṃdhārayitumanyatra bodhisattvādhyāśayaratnabhājanena / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ sarvaratnāni nirvidhyāti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādavajraṃ sarvadharmaratnāni nirvidhyati / tadyathā vajraṃ sarvaśailāni bhinatti, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādavajraṃ sarvadṛṣṭigataśailāni bhinatti / tadyathā kulaputra bhinnamapi vajraratnaṃ sarvaratnaprativiśiṣṭaṃ suvarṇālaṃkāramabhibhavati, evameva āśayavipattibhinnamapi sarvajñatācittotpādavajraratnaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaguṇasuvarṇālaṃkārānabhibhavati /
body.translated_text: One who is merely fumigated with that incense, together with the entire fourfold army of every king, stands suspended in the sky. Just so, the roots of merit of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> that are fumigated with the incense of the arising of the mind of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā-cittotpāda</s>) transcend the entire triple world and culminate in the domain of the unconditioned sky of the knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> (diamond) does not arise from any other jewel-mine but only from a <s>vajra</s>-mine or a gold-mine, just so the <s>vajra</s>-like arising of the mind of omniscience does not arise from any other jewel-mine of the dispositions and roots of merit of beings, but only from the <s>vajra</s>-mine of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) for the protection of beings or from the great gold-mine that has omniscient knowledge as its support. Just as, son of good family, there is a species of tree called 'rootless' — its root-foundation is not to be found, yet it appears fully branched with leaves, foliage, and blossoms, forming a network among the trees — just so the root-foundation of the arising of the mind of omniscience is not to be found, yet it appears blossoming with all merit, knowledge, and <s>abhijñā</s>s (superknowledges), forming a great network of vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) in all births in the world. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> does not shine in any other vessel nor can it be held by a cracked or hollow vessel but only by an uncracked vessel, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of omniscience does not shine in beings who are vessels of inferior aspiration — in those who are miserly, of poor morality, of corrupt minds, lazy, of confused mindfulness, or of poor wisdom — nor can it be held by any vessel of corrupted aspiration and wavering intellect, but only by the jewel-vessel of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> pierces through all jewels, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of omniscience pierces through all jewels of <s>dharma</s>. Just as a <s>vajra</s> shatters all mountains, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of omniscience shatters all mountains of wrong views. Just as, son of good family, even a broken <s>vajra</s>-jewel surpasses all other jewels and overcomes golden ornaments, just so even the <s>vajra</s>-jewel of the arising of the mind of omniscience that is broken by the corruption of aspiration overcomes the golden ornaments of the qualities of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s.

body.text:
tadyathā kulaputra bhinnamapi vajraratnaṃ sarvadāridryaṃ vinivartayati, evameva pratibhinnamapi sarvajñatācittotpādavajraratnaṃ sarvasaṃsāradāridryaṃ vinivartayati / tadyathā kulaputra kiyatparītto 'pi vajradhātuḥ sarvamaṇipāṣāṇabhedalakṣaṇaḥ, evameva kiyatparīttārambaṇaprasṛto 'pi sarvajñatācittotpādavajradhātuḥ sarvājñānabhedalakṣaṇaḥ / tadyathā kulaputra vajraratnaṃ na prākṛtajanahastagataṃ bhavati, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādavajraratnaṃ
na prākṛtādhyāśayānāmitvarakuśalamūlānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ hastagataṃ bhavati / tadyathā kulaputra ratnaparīkṣānabhijñaḥ puruṣo vajramaṇiratnaguṇānajānan nāsya guṇaviśeṣamanubhavati, evameva duṣprajñajātīyaḥ puruṣapudgalo bodhisattvacittamahāprajñāvajraratnaguṇānabhijño nāsya guṇaviśeṣamanubhavati / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ na śakyaṃ jarayitum, evameva sarvajñatāhetubhūtaṃ bodhicittotpādavajraṃ na śakyaṃ jarayitum / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ mahāpraharaṇaṃ na śakyaṃ mahānagnenāpi saṃdhārayitumanyatra mahānārāyaṇasthāmabalavegena, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādamahāvajrapraharaṇaṃ na śakyaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhamahānagnairapi saṃdhārayitumanyatra sarvajñatāhetubalopastabdhāpramāṇakuśalamūlamahānārāyaṇasthāmaprativiśiṣṭairmahāvabhāsaprāptairmahābodhisattvaiḥ / tadyathā kulaputra yatra sarvapraharaṇāni na prasahante tatra vajraṃ prasahate, na pratihanyate, evameva yatra sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhapraṇidhijñānapraharaṇāni na prasahante sattvaparipākavinaye vā tryadhvakalpacaryāduḥkhasaṃvāse vā, tatra sarvajñatācittotpādamahāvajrapraharaṇagṛhīto bodhisattvo 'parikhinnamānasaḥ prasahate, na pratihanyate / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ na śakyaṃ kenacitpṛthivī pradeśena saṃdhārayitumanyatra vajratalena, evameva sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairbodhisattvaniryāṇapraṇidhānasaṃbhāravajraṃ na śakyaṃ saṃdhārayitumanyatrādhyāśayabodhicittotpādavajradṛḍhapṛthivītalena / tadyathā kulaputra dṛḍhavajratalācchidrabhājanatvānmahāsamudre pānīyaṃ na visarati, evameva bodhisattvavajrācchidradṛḍhatalapariṇāmanāpratiṣṭhitāni bodhisattvasya kuśalamūlāni na kṣīyante sarvabhavopapattiṣu / tadyathā kulaputra vajratalapratiṣṭhitā mahāpṛthivī na vidīryate na saṃsīdati, evameva bodhicittotpādavajradṛḍhatalapratiṣṭhitāni bodhisattvapraṇidhānāni sarvatraidhātuke na vidīryante na saṃsīdanti / tadyathā kulaputra vajramudakena na klidyate, evameva bodhicittotpādavajraṃ sarvakarmakleśodakena sarvakarmasaṃvāsairna klidyate na svidyate / tadyathā kulaputra vajraṃ sarvāgnidāhairna dahyate na saṃtapyate, evameva sarvajñatācittotpādavajraṃ sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhāgnidāhairna dahyate, sarvakleśāgnitāpairna saṃtapyate / tadyathā kulaputra tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bodhimaṇḍe
niṣīdatāṃ māraṃ yodhayatāṃ sarvajñatābhisaṃbuddhamānānāṃ nānyena pṛthivīpradeśena śakyamāsanaṃ saṃdhārayitumanyatra trisāhasramahāsāhasravajranābhidharaṇitalena, evameva bodhisattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidadhatāṃ caryāṃ caratāṃ pāramitāḥ paripūrayatāṃ kṣāntimavakrāmatāṃ bhūmiṃ pratilabhamānānāṃ kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayatāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ saṃpratīcchatāṃ sarvabodhisattvamārgasaṃbhāramupastambhayatāṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ mahādharmameghān saṃdhārayatāṃ te mahākuśalamūlabalādhānavegā nānyena cittena śakyāḥ saṃdhārayitumanyatra sarvapraṇidhānajñānavajradṛḍhanābhinā sarvajñatācittotpādena / iti hi
body.translated_text: Just as, son of good family, even a broken <s>vajra</s>-jewel turns away all poverty, just so even a shattered <s>vajra</s>-jewel of the arising of the mind of omniscience turns away the poverty of all <s>saṃsāra</s>. Just as, son of good family, however small a <s>vajra</s>-element may be, it has the characteristic of breaking all <s>maṇi</s>-gems and stones, just so however small the scope of the <s>vajra</s>-element of the arising of the mind of omniscience, it has the characteristic of breaking all ignorance. Just as, son of good family, the <s>vajra</s>-jewel does not come into the hands of ordinary people, just so the <s>vajra</s>-jewel of the arising of the mind of omniscience does not come into the hands of gods and humans of ordinary aspiration and inferior roots of merit. Just as, son of good family, a person unskilled in the examination of jewels, not knowing the qualities of a <s>vajra-maṇi</s>-jewel, does not experience its special qualities, just so a person of poor wisdom, not knowing the qualities of the great wisdom-<s>vajra</s>-jewel of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind, does not experience its special qualities. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> cannot be worn down, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicittotpāda</s>), which is the cause of omniscience, cannot be worn down. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> as a great weapon cannot be held even by a great <s>Nāga</s> but only by one possessing the might, strength, and force of a great <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, just so the great <s>vajra</s>-weapon of the arising of the mind of omniscience cannot be held even by the great <s>Nāga</s>s of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, but only by great <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who have attained great illumination, possessing supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-might sustained by immeasurable roots of merit upheld by the power of the causes of omniscience. Just as, son of good family, where all other weapons fail, the <s>vajra</s> prevails and is not repelled, just so where all the weapons of the vows and knowledge of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s fail — whether in the discipline and maturation of beings or in dwelling together with the suffering of conduct through <s>kalpa</s>s of the three times — there the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has grasped the great <s>vajra</s>-weapon of the arising of the mind of omniscience, with unwearied mind, prevails and is not repelled. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> cannot be held by any spot of ground except upon a <s>vajra</s>-surface, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the provisions for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s career-vows cannot be held by all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s except upon the firm ground-surface of the <s>vajra</s> of the aspiration and arising of the mind of awakening. Just as, son of good family, because of the uncracked vessel-nature of a firm <s>vajra</s>-surface, water in the great ocean does not leak away, just so the roots of merit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established upon the uncracked firm surface of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> dedication of merit are not exhausted in all births in existence. Just as, son of good family, the great earth established upon a <s>vajra</s>-surface does not disintegrate or collapse, just so the vows of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established upon the firm <s>vajra</s>-surface of the arising of the mind of awakening do not disintegrate or collapse in the entire triple world. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> is not moistened by water, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of awakening is not moistened or wetted by the waters of all <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions) or by all associations with <s>karma</s>. Just as, son of good family, a <s>vajra</s> is not burned or heated by all conflagrations, just so the <s>vajra</s> of the arising of the mind of omniscience is not burned by the conflagrations of suffering in all <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor heated by the fires of all <s>kleśa</s>s. Just as, son of good family, when <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>s sit at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), conquering <s>Māra</s>, attaining omniscience, their seat cannot be supported by any other spot of ground except by the <s>vajra</s>-navel ground-surface of the great trichiliocosm, just so when <s>Bodhisattva</s>s make their vows toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, practice the conduct, fulfill the <s>pāramitā</s>s, advance in patience, attain the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>s), dedicate roots of merit, receive <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecy), and support the provisions of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> paths, and uphold the great <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — those great forces of the empowerment of roots of merit cannot be supported by any other mind except by the arising of the mind of omniscience, whose navel is the firm <s>vajra</s> of the knowledge of all vows. Thus indeed

body.text: kulaputra ebhiśca anyaiśca apramāṇairyāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyairguṇaviśeṣaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarvajñatācittotpādaḥ / te 'pi sattvā evaṃguṇadharmasamanvāgatā bhūtāśca bhaviṣyanti ca, yairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni / tasmāttarhi kulaputra sulabdhāste lābhāḥ, yastvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya bodhisattvacaryāṃ parimārgasi eṣāṃ guṇānāṃ pratilābhāya //
body.translated_text: son of good family, the arising of the mind of omniscience is endowed with these and other immeasurable, indeed inexpressibly inexpressible, special qualities. And those beings who have aroused their minds toward unsurpassed perfect awakening are and will be endowed with such qualities and attributes. Therefore, son of good family, well-gained are your gains, that you, having aroused the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, seek the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct for the attainment of these qualities.

body.text: api ca kulaputra yadvadasi - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti / gaccha kulaputra, asya vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya abhyantaraṃ praviśya vyavalokaya / atra jñāsyasi yathā bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, śikṣamāṇasya ca yādṛśī guṇapariniṣpattirbhavati //
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, as to what you say — 'How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how should one practice?' — go, son of good family, enter the interior of this great pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> and observe. There you will understand how one should train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, and what accomplishment of qualities arises for one who trains.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā evamāha - vivṛṇu ārya asya kūṭāgārasya dvāram / pravekṣyāmi / atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya kūṭāgārasya dvāramūlamupasaṃkramya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā acchaṭāśabdamakārṣīt / tasya dvāraṃ vivṛtamabhūt / sa āha - praviśa kulaputra etatkūṭāgāram / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ paramāścaryaprāptastatkūṭāgāraṃ prāviśat / tasya samanantarapraviṣṭasya taddvāraṃ saṃvṛtamabhūt / so 'drākṣīt taṃ kūṭāgāraṃ vipulavistīrṇaṃ bahuyojanaśatasahasravistīrṇaṃ gaganatalāpramāṇaṃ samantādākāśadhātuvipulam asaṃkhyeyacchatradhvajapatākālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnālaṃkāram / asaṃkhyeyamuktāhārapralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnahārapralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyalohitamuktāhārapralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasiṃhamuktāhārapralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasiṃhadhvajālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyacandrārdhacandrālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyavicitrapaṭṭadāmābhipralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyavividhapaṭṭapaṭṭālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyamaṇijālaprabhālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyahemajālālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnapaṭṭālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnasuvarṇasūtrapratyuptālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaghaṇṭāmadhuranirghoṣālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnakiṅkiṇījālasamīritamanojñaśabdālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyadivyapuṣpaughābhipravarṣaṇālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyadivyamālyadāmābhipralambitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyagandhaghaṭikānirdhūpitopacārālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasuvarṇacūrṇasaṃpravarṣaṇālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaharmyajālālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyagavākṣālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyatoraṇālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaniryūhālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyādarśamaṇḍalaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratneṣṭakānicitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnabhittyalaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasthūṇālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnavastrameghālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnavṛkṣālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnavedikālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnapathālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnacchadanasarvavyūhālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyabhūmitalapratiṣṭhānavicitravyūhālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnanicitaprāsādālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnāsanālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyamaṇikanyālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnapaṭṭasaṃstṛtacaṃkramālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyajāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇakadalīstambhasuvibhaktālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasarvaratnavigrahālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyabodhisattvātmabhāvālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyapakṣigaṇavicitramanojñarutānuravitālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnapadmālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnayaṣṭisaṃdhāraṇālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyapuṣkariṇyalaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyapuṇḍarīkālaṃkāram
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and said thus: 'Open, O Noble One, the door of this pinnacled mansion. I shall enter.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> approached the entrance of the pinnacled mansion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> and snapped his fingers with his right hand. Its door opened. He said: 'Enter, son of good family, this pinnacled mansion.' Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having attained the utmost wonder, entered that pinnacled mansion. No sooner had he entered than the door closed behind him. He beheld that pinnacled mansion — vast and extensive, extending over many hundreds of thousands of <s>yojana</s>s, immeasurable as the surface of the sky, as vast as the realm of space on every side — with ornaments of innumerable parasols, banners, and pennants; with ornaments of innumerable jewels; with ornaments of innumerable hanging pearl necklaces; with ornaments of innumerable hanging jewel garlands; with ornaments of innumerable hanging red-pearl necklaces; with ornaments of innumerable hanging lion-pearl necklaces; with ornaments of innumerable lion-banners; with ornaments of innumerable moons and half-moons; with ornaments of innumerable variegated silken garlands hanging down; with ornaments of innumerable various silk cloths and fabrics; with ornaments of innumerable radiant <s>maṇi</s>-jewel nets; with ornaments of innumerable golden nets; with ornaments of innumerable jewel-silk cloths; with ornaments of innumerable jewel and gold threads set with gems; with ornaments of innumerable sweet-sounding bells; with ornaments of innumerable delightful sounds stirred by nets of jewel-bells; with ornaments of innumerable showers of floods of divine flowers; with ornaments of innumerable hanging divine garland-chains; with ornaments of innumerable offerings of incense wafting from fragrance-pots; with ornaments of innumerable showers of gold dust; with ornaments of innumerable nets of upper chambers; with ornaments of innumerable latticed windows; with ornaments of innumerable arched gateways; with ornaments of innumerable projecting balconies; with ornaments of innumerable mirror-circles; with ornaments of innumerable pavements of jewel bricks; with ornaments of innumerable jewel walls; with ornaments of innumerable pillars; with ornaments of innumerable clouds of jewel fabrics; with ornaments of innumerable jewel trees; with ornaments of innumerable jewel railings; with ornaments of innumerable jewel pathways; with ornaments of innumerable arrays of jewel canopies in every arrangement; with ornaments of innumerable variegated arrays established on the ground-surface; with ornaments of innumerable palaces built of piled jewels; with ornaments of innumerable jewel seats; with ornaments of innumerable <s>maṇi</s>-jewel maidens; with ornaments of innumerable promenades spread with jewel cloths; with ornaments of innumerable well-formed plantain pillars of the color of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold; with ornaments of innumerable images of all jewels; with ornaments of innumerable forms of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s; with ornaments of innumerable flocks of birds singing various delightful sounds; with ornaments of innumerable jewel lotuses; with ornaments of innumerable jewel staffs held aloft; with ornaments of innumerable lotus ponds; with ornaments of innumerable white lotuses

body.text: asaṃkhyeyaratnasopānālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaratnavāmakaviracanālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyavicitraratnanicitabhūmyalaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyamahāmaṇiratnaprabhāpramuktālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyasarvaratnavyūhālaṃkāram asaṃkhyeyaguṇavarṇasamuditālaṃkāram / tasya ca mahākūṭāgārasya abhyantare tadanyāni kūṭāgāraśatasahasrāṇyevaṃrūpavyūhālaṃkṛtānyevāpaśyat asaṃkhyeyaratnacchatradhvajapatākālaṃkārāṇi yāvadasaṃkhyeyaguṇavarṇasamuditālaṃkārāṇi ca / tāni kūṭāgārāṇi vipulavistīrṇānyapramāṇākāśakośabhūtānyapaśyat samantāt suvibhaktāni / te cāsya kūṭāgāravyūhā anyonyāsaṃbhinnā anyonyāmaitrībhūtā anyonyāsaṃkīrṇāḥ pratibhāsayogena ābhāsamagaman ekasminnārambaṇe / yathā ca ekasminnārambaṇe, tathā śeṣasarvārambaṇeṣu //
body.translated_text: ornaments of innumerable jewel staircases, ornaments of innumerable jewel spiral designs, ornaments of innumerable ground-surfaces inlaid with various jewels, ornaments of innumerable radiances emitted from great jewel-king gems, ornaments of innumerable arrays of all jewels, ornaments resounding with innumerable qualities and praises. And within that great tower-pavilion, he beheld yet other hundreds of thousands of tower-pavilions adorned with such arrays, with ornaments of innumerable jewel parasols, banners, and flags, up to ornaments resounding with innumerable qualities and praises. He beheld those tower-pavilions as vast and extensive, constituting immeasurable spaces of sky, well-arranged on all sides. And those arrays of tower-pavilions were unmingled with one another, non-obstructing of one another, unsullied by one another, yet through the conjunction of reflections they came to be reflected in a single object. And just as in one object, so also in all remaining objects.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya idamevaṃrūpamacintyaviṣayavikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā atulaprītivegavivardhitena mahāharṣaprāmodyena abhiṣyanditakāyacittaḥ sarvasaṃjñāgatavidhūtamānasaḥ sarvāvaraṇavivartitacittaḥ sarvamohavigato 'saṃpramoṣadivyanayanaḥ sarvaśabdāsaṅgasmṛtivijñaptiśrotraḥ sarvamanasikāravikṣepavigato 'nāvaraṇavimokṣanayanānusaraṇabuddhiḥ sarvadiksrotobhimukhena kāyapraśamena sarvārambaṇānāvaraṇasaṃpreṣitacakṣuḥ sarvatrānugatena abhinirhārabalena sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having beheld this inconceivable miraculous display of the domain of the great tower-pavilion <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s>, his body and mind overflowing with great joy and delight heightened by an incomparable surge of bliss, his mind freed from all conceptual categorizations, his mind turned away from all obstructions, all delusion departed, with divine eyes of unfailing method, with ears of mindfulness-cognition unattached to all sounds, freed from all distraction of mental attention, with intelligence that follows the sight of unobstructed liberation, with bodily tranquility facing the streams of all directions, with eyes dispatched unobstructedly toward all objects, with the power of accomplishment following everywhere -- he prostrated with his entire body.

body.text: samanantarapraṇipatitamātraśca sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako maitreyasya bodhisattvasya adhiṣṭhānabalena sarveṣu teṣu kūṭāgāreṣvabhyantarapraviṣṭamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma / teṣu ca sarvakūṭāgāreṣu vividhavaimātryagatānyacintyaviṣayavikurvitānyadrākṣīt / kvacitkūṭāgāre yatra maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena prathamaṃ praṇidhānacittamutpāditamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yannāmagotropapannena yena kuśalamūlena yayā samādāpanayā yena kalyāṇamitrasaṃcodanena yadāyuḥpramāṇena yannāmake kalpe yatratathāgate yadvyūhe yādṛśyāṃ parṣadi yādṛśena praṇidhānaviśeṣābhinirhāreṇa, tatsarvamadrākṣīt, saṃjānīte anusarati / yāvacca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasya ca tathāgatasya tena samayenāyuḥpramāṇamabhūt, tāvatkāle tasya tathāgatasya pādamulagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma / tāṃ ca sarvāṃ kriyāmapaśyat //
body.translated_text: And the very moment <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son prostrated, through the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>'s spiritual sustaining, he perceived himself as having entered within all those tower-pavilions. And in all those tower-pavilions he beheld inconceivable miraculous displays of various kinds. In one tower-pavilion he beheld where the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> had first generated the mind of aspiration toward unsurpassed perfect awakening -- under what name and lineage, through what root of merit, through what exhortation, through what urging of a spiritual friend, during what lifespan, in what <s>kalpa</s>, under what <s>Tathāgata</s>, in what array, in what kind of assembly, and through what special accomplishment of vows -- all this he beheld, recognized, and followed. And for as long as the lifespan of those beings and that <s>Tathāgata</s> was at that time, for that entire duration he perceived himself as present at the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s>. And he beheld all that activity.

body.text: kvacitkūṭāgāre yatra maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena prathamo maitrasamādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ, yata upādāya asya maitreya iti saṃjñodapādi tadadrākṣīt / kvacidyatra caryāḥ cīrṇāḥ, kvacidyatra pāramitāḥ paripūritāḥ, kvacidyatra kṣāntiravatīrṇā, kvacidyatra bhūmiravakrāntā, kvacidyatra buddhakṣetravyūhāḥ parigṛhītāḥ, kvacidyatra tathāgataśāsanaṃ saṃdhāritam, kvacidyatra anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā, kvacidyatra vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yathā vyākṛto yena vyākṛto yāvaccireṇa ca vyākṛtastatsarvamadrākṣīt / sa kvacitkūṭāgāre maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ cakravartirājabhūtaṃ sattvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayamānamapaśyat / kvacillokapālabhūtaṃ sarvalokahitasukhaṃ sattvānāmupasaṃharamāṇam, kvacicchakrabhūtaṃ kāmaguṇaratiṃ sattvānāṃ vinivartayamānam, kvacidbrahmabhūtaṃ dhyānāpramāṇaratiṃ sattvānāṃ saṃvarṇayamānam, kvacitsuyāmadevādhipatibhūtamapramāṇaguṇān sattvānāṃ saṃvarṇayamānam, kvacit saṃtuṣitadeveśvarabhūtamekajātipratibaddhabodhisattvaguṇānudbhāvayamānam,
body.translated_text: In one tower-pavilion he beheld where the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> had first attained the <s>maitrasamādhi</s> (concentration of loving-kindness), from which arose the designation '<s>Maitreya</s>' for him. Somewhere he saw where practices had been carried out, somewhere where <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) had been fulfilled, somewhere where <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) had been entered, somewhere where <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) had been traversed, somewhere where buddha-field arrays had been undertaken, somewhere where the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching had been upheld, somewhere where patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> had been attained, somewhere where he had received a prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening -- how predicted, by whom predicted, and how long until predicted -- all this he beheld. In one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> as a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), establishing beings in the ten wholesome courses of action. Somewhere as a world-protector, gathering the welfare and happiness of all the world for beings; somewhere as <s>Śakra</s>, turning beings away from delight in sensual pleasures; somewhere as <s>Brahmā</s>, praising to beings the delight of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the immeasurables; somewhere as lord of the <s>Suyāma</s> gods, praising immeasurable qualities to beings; somewhere as sovereign of the <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (Tuṣita) gods, proclaiming the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound by one more birth,

body.text:
kvacitsunirmitadevarājabhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvanirmāṇavyūhaṃ devaparṣadi saṃdarśayamānam, kvacidvaśavartidevarājabhūtaṃ sarvadharmavaśavartitāṃ devānāṃ saṃprakāśayamānam, kvacinmāratvaṃ kārayamāṇam, sarvasaṃpattyanityatāṃ devānāṃ deśayamānam, kvacidasurendrabhavanopapannaṃ sarvamānamadadarpaprahāṇāya mahājñānasāgaravigāhanāya dharmajñānasāgaravigāhanāya dharmajñānamāyāpratilambhāya asuraparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayamānamapaśyat / kvacitkūṭāgāre yamalokamadrākṣīt / tatra maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ prabhayā mahānarakānavabhāsya narakopapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvanirayaduḥkhaṃ praśamayamānamadrākṣīt / kvacitkūṭāgāre pretabhavanamadrākṣīt / tatra maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ pretabhavanopapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ vipulamannapānamupasaṃhṛtya kṣutpipāsāṃ praśamayamānamadrākṣīt / kvacitkūṭāgāre tiryagyonau vividhopapatyāyatanavimātratayā tiryagyonigatān sattvān vinayantamadrākṣīt / kvacitkūṭāgāre mahārājikadevaparṣadi lokapālānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānamapaśyat / kacicchakradevarājaparṣadi kvacitsuyāmadevarājaparṣadi kvacitsaṃtuṣitadevarājaparṣadi kvacitsunirmitadevarājaparṣadi kvacidvaśavartidevarājaparṣadi kvacitkūṭāgāre brahmendraparṣadi maitreyaṃ bodhisattva mahābrahmabhūtaṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānapaśyat / kvacinnāgamahoragaparṣadi kvacidyakṣarākṣasaparṣadi kvacidgandharvakinnaraparṣadi
kvacidasuradānavendraparṣadi kvacinmahoragendraparṣadi kvacinmanuṣyendraparṣadi kvacitkūṭāgāre devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaparṣadi maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānamapaśyat / kvacicchrāvakaparṣadi kvacitpratyekabuddhaparṣadi kvacidbodhisattvaparṣadi kvacitkūṭāgāre prathamacittotpādikānāmādikarmikāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānamapaśyat / kvaciccaryāpratipannānāṃ kvacitkṣāntipratilabdhānāmavinivartanīyānāṃ kvacidekajātipratibaddhānāmabhiṣekaprāptānāṃ kvacitkūṭāgāre prathamabhūmisthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bhūmivaiśeṣikatāṃ saṃvarṇayamānamapaśyat / kvacidyāvaddaśabhūmisthitairbodhisattvaiḥ saha maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sarvabhūmivaiśeṣikatāṃ saṃgāyantamapaśyat / kvacitsarvapāramitāparipūraye 'pramāṇatāṃ kvacitsarvaśikṣābhimukhāvatārasamatāṃ kvacitsamādhimukhapraveśavistīrṇatāṃ kvacidvimokṣanayagambhīratāṃ kvacicchāntadhyānasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāviṣayaspharaṇatāṃ kvacidbodhisattvacaryāvinayopāyamukhapraveśatāṃ kvacitpraṇidhānābhinirhāravistīrṇatāṃ kvacitkūṭāgāre maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ caṃkramābhiyuktaṃ sabhāgacaritairbodhisattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ lokahitakriyārthaṃ vividhaśilpaśānaśāstraviśeṣāṃ sarvasattvahitasukhādhānopasaṃhitatāṃ saṃgāyamānamapaśyat / kvacidekajātipratibaddhairbodhisattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvabuddhajñānābhiṣekamukhaṃ saṃgāyantamapaśyat / kvacitkūṭāgāre maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ caṃkramābhiyuktaṃ varṣaśatasahasrairanikṣiptadhuramapaśyat / kvaciduddeśasvādhyāyaprayuktaṃ kvaciddharmamukhapratyavekṣaṇaprayuktaṃ kvaciddharmasaṃgāyanaprayuktaṃ kvaciddharmalekhanaprayuktaṃ kvacinmaitrīsamādhisamāpannaṃ kvacitsarvadhyānāpramāṇāni samāpannaṃ kvacisarvakṛtsnāyatanavimokṣasamāpannaṃ kvacitkūṭāgāre bodhisattvābhijñābhinirhāraprayogasamādhisamāpannaṃ maitreyaṃ bodhisattvamapaśyat //
body.translated_text: somewhere as king of the <s>Sunirmita</s> gods, displaying to the divine assembly all the arrays of <s>bodhisattva</s> miraculous emanations; somewhere as king of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods, illuminating for the gods the mastery over all <s>dharmas</s>; somewhere performing the role of <s>Māra</s>, teaching the gods the impermanence of all attainments; somewhere born in the palace of the lord of <s>asuras</s>, he beheld him teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>asura</s> assembly for the abandonment of all pride, arrogance, and haughtiness, for plunging into the great ocean of knowledge, for plunging into the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge, and for attaining the mastery of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge. In one tower-pavilion he beheld the realm of <s>Yama</s>. There he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> illuminating the great hells with his radiance, pacifying all the suffering of the hells for beings reborn there. In one tower-pavilion he beheld the abode of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts). There he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> providing abundant food and drink to beings reborn in the <s>preta</s> realm, pacifying their hunger and thirst. In one tower-pavilion he beheld him disciplining beings reborn in the animal realm through various kinds of birth-places in the animal world. In one tower-pavilion he beheld him teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the world-protectors in the assembly of the <s>Mahārājika</s> gods. Somewhere in the assembly of the god-king <s>Śakra</s>, somewhere in the assembly of the god-king <s>Suyāma</s>, somewhere in the assembly of the god-king <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, somewhere in the assembly of the god-king <s>Sunirmita</s>, somewhere in the assembly of the god-king <s>Vaśavartin</s>, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> in the form of <s>Mahābrahmā</s> teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in the assembly of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>. Somewhere in the assembly of <s>nāgas</s> and <s>mahoragas</s>, somewhere in the assembly of <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, somewhere in the assembly of <s>gandharvas</s> and <s>kinnaras</s>, somewhere in the assembly of <s>asura</s> and <s>dānava</s> lords, somewhere in the assembly of <s>mahoraga</s> lords, somewhere in the assembly of human lords, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in assemblies of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans. Somewhere in the assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s>, somewhere in the assembly of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, somewhere in the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had just generated the initial aspiration, beginners. Somewhere to those engaged in practice, somewhere to those who had attained patience and become irreversible, somewhere to those bound by one more birth who had attained consecration, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld him praising the distinctive features of the stages to <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). Somewhere he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> established up to the tenth <s>bhūmi</s>, singing together of the distinctive features of all the stages. Somewhere the immeasurability of fulfilling all <s>pāramitās</s>, somewhere the equality of entering all trainings, somewhere the extensiveness of entering the gates of <s>samādhi</s>, somewhere the profundity of the methods of liberation, somewhere the pervasion of the domains of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>samāpatti</s>, and <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), somewhere the entry into the gates of skillful means of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct and discipline, somewhere the extensiveness of the accomplishment of vows, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> engaged in walking meditation, together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> of similar practice, singing together about the various special crafts, knowledge, and sciences for the benefit of the world, all directed toward providing welfare and happiness for all beings. Somewhere he beheld him together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound by one more birth, singing together about the gate of consecration into the knowledge of all <s>Buddhas</s>. In one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> engaged in walking meditation for hundreds of thousands of years without setting down his burden. Somewhere engaged in recitation and study, somewhere engaged in examining the gates of <s>Dharma</s>, somewhere engaged in chanting the <s>Dharma</s>, somewhere engaged in writing the <s>Dharma</s>, somewhere absorbed in the <s>maitrī-samādhi</s> (loving-kindness concentration), somewhere absorbed in all <s>dhyānas</s> and immeasurables, somewhere absorbed in all totality-bases and liberations, and in one tower-pavilion he beheld the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> absorbed in the <s>samādhi</s> of the practice of accomplishing <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledges.

body.text: kvacitkūṭāgāre nirmāṇavatīṃ bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpannān bodhisattvānapaśyat / teṣāṃ ca sarvaśarīraromamukhebhyaḥ sarvanirmāṇameghānniścarato 'paśyat / keṣāṃcitsarvaromamukhebhyo devanikāyameghānniścarato 'paśyat / keṣāṃcinnāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālacakravartimeghān keṣāṃcitkoṭṭarājameghān keṣāṃcidrājakumārameghān keṣāṃcicchreṣṭhyamātyagṛhapatimeghān keṣāṃcicchrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvameghān keṣāṃcittathāgatakāyameghān keṣāṃcitsarvaśarīraromamukhebhyo 'pramāṇān sarvasattvanirmāṇameghānniścarato 'paśyat / keṣāṃcitsarvaromamukhebhyo vividhāni dharmamukhāni niścaramāṇānyaśrauṣīt - yaduta bodhisattvaguṇavarṇamukhāni dānapāramitāmukhāni śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyapraṇidhānabalajñānapāramitāmukhāni saṃgrahavastudhyānāpramāṇasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāvidyādhāraṇīpratibhānasatyapratisaṃvicchamathavipaśyanāvimokṣamukhapratītyasamutpādapratiśaraṇadharmoddānasmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgaśrāvakayānakathāpratyekabuddhayānakathāmahāyānakathābhūmikṣānticaryāpraṇidhānamukhāni evaṃ sarvadharmamukhapraveśaśabdānniścarato 'śrauṣīt / kvacitkūṭāgāre tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalasaṃnipātānadrākṣīt / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāṃ nānāvimātratāṃ janmakulavimātratāṃ kāyavyūhāpramāṇavimātratāmāyurvimātratāṃ kṣetravimātratāṃ kalpavimātratāṃ dharmadeśanāvimātratāṃ nirmāṇamukhavimātratāṃ saddharmasthitivimātratāṃ yāvadaśeṣasarvākāraparṣanmaṇḍalavimātratāmadrākṣīt //
body.translated_text: In one tower-pavilion he beheld <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had entered the <s>bodhisattva-samādhi</s> called <s>Nirmāṇavatī</s> (Possessing Emanations). And from all the pores of their bodies he beheld clouds of all emanations issuing forth. From the pores of some he beheld clouds of assemblies of gods issuing forth. From some, clouds of <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, and <s>cakravartins</s>; from some, clouds of tributary kings; from some, clouds of princes; from some, clouds of merchants, ministers, and householders; from some, clouds of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s>; from some, clouds of <s>Tathāgata</s> bodies; and from the pores of some he beheld immeasurable clouds of emanations of all beings issuing forth. From the pores of some he heard various gates of <s>Dharma</s> issuing forth -- namely, gates praising <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities, gates of the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), gates of the <s>pāramitās</s> of <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows), <s>bala</s> (powers), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); gates of the means of attraction, <s>dhyāna</s>, immeasurables, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>samāpatti</s>, <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), <s>vidyā</s> (sciences), <s>dhāraṇī</s>, eloquence, truths, analytical knowledges, <s>śamatha</s> (calm), <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), liberation-gates, dependent origination, refuges, <s>dharma</s>-summaries, foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, path-factors; and gates of <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle discourses, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle discourses, <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourses, stages, patience, practice, and vows -- thus he heard the sounds of entry into all gates of <s>Dharma</s> issuing forth. In one tower-pavilion he beheld assemblies of <s>Tathāgata</s> congregations. And he beheld the various differences among those <s>Tathāgatas</s> -- differences of birth and lineage, immeasurable differences of bodily arrays, differences of lifespan, differences of fields, differences of <s>kalpas</s>, differences of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, differences of gates of emanation, differences in the duration of the true <s>Dharma</s>, up to differences in all aspects of their assemblies without remainder.

body.text: madhye ca vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhasya mahākūṭāgārasya ekamudārataraṃ vistīrṇataraṃ ca tadanyasarvakūṭāgārāśeṣasarvavyūhātiriktataravyūhasamalaṃkṛtaṃ kūṭāgāramadrākṣīt / sa tasya kūṭāgārasyābhyantare trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumadrākṣīt / tasmiṃśca trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau koṭīśataṃ cāturdvīpikānāṃ koṭīśataṃ jambudvīpakānāṃ koṭīśataṃ tuṣitabhavanānāmadrākṣīt / sa tatra jambudvīpeṣu maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ padmagarbhagataṃ jāyamānamapaśyat / śakrabrahmābhyāṃ pratīkṣyamāṇaṃ saptapadāni prakrāntaṃ daśa diśo vyavalokayamānaṃ mahāsiṃhanādaṃ nadantaṃ sarvakumārabhūmiṃ saṃdarśayamānaṃ antaḥpuramadhye gatamudyānabhūmiṃ niṣkrāntaṃ sarvajñatābhimukhamabhiniṣkramya pravrajantaṃ duṣkaracaryāṃ saṃdarśayantamāhāraṃ paribhuñjānaṃ bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkrāntaṃ māraṃ dharṣayamāṇaṃ bodhiṃ vibudhyamānaṃ bodhivṛkṣamanimiṣaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaṃ mahābrahmaṇādhyeṣyamāṇaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayamānaṃ devabhavaneṣu praviśantamadrākṣīt / nānābhisaṃbodhidharmacakrapravartanaviṣayasaṃdarśanavimātratābhirnānākalpanāmapravartanavimātratābhirnānāyuḥpramāṇavimātratābhirnānāparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhavimātratābhirnānākṣetraviśuddhinayasaṃdarśanavimātratābhiḥ nānācaryāpraṇidhānaprabhāvanāvimātratābhiḥ nānādharmadeśanāvyavasthānasarvaparipācanopāyavimātratābhiḥ nānādhātuvibhaṅgaśāsanasthityadhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśana vimātratābhiḥ / sarvatra ca tatra sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ pādamūlagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma //
body.translated_text: And in the center of the great tower <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> (Womb of the Ornamental Array of Vairocana), he saw one tower that was more exalted and more vast, adorned with arrays surpassing all the arrays of all the other towers combined. Inside that tower he saw a <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (three-thousand great-thousand) world-realm. And in that three-thousand great-thousand world-realm he saw a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of four-continent systems, a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Jambudvīpas</s>, and a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tuṣita</s> heavens. There, in those <s>Jambudvīpas</s>, he saw <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> being born, emerging from a lotus-womb, being received by <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, taking seven steps, surveying the ten directions, roaring the great lion's roar, displaying all the stages of princehood, dwelling in the inner palace, going forth to the pleasure grounds, going forth facing omniscience and taking ordination, displaying the practice of austerities, partaking of food, approaching the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), vanquishing <s>Māra</s>, awakening to enlightenment, gazing at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree without blinking, being requested by <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), and entering the heavenly abodes — with diverse variations in displaying the domains of awakening and turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, with diverse variations in the names of <s>kalpas</s>, with diverse variations in lifespans, with diverse variations in the arrays of assembly-circles, with diverse variations in displaying the methods of field-purification, with diverse variations in manifesting conduct and vows, with diverse variations in the means of establishing <s>Dharma</s>-teachings for ripening all, and with diverse variations in displaying the teaching, establishment, and empowerment of the analysis of <s>dhātus</s> (elements). And everywhere therein, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son recognized himself as present at the feet [of those Buddhas]. //

body.text: sa sarvaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu sarvakriyāsaṃdarśaneṣu sarvāyuḥpramāṇavimātratāsu asaṃpramuṣitena smṛtyadhiṣṭhānajñānena sarvasaṃjñāgatavyavasitāyāṃ jñānabhūmau sthito yāvanti teṣu sarvakūṭāgāreṣu
body.translated_text: Standing on the ground of knowledge established through all perceptions, with unfailing knowledge of the empowerment of mindfulness, in all those assembly-circles, in all those displays of activities, in all those diverse lifespans — in however many of all those towers

body.text:
ghaṇṭākiṅkiṇījālatūryasaṃgītiprabhṛtīnyārambaṇāni sattvebhyastebhyo 'cintyameghanigarjitanirghoṣaśabdaṃ niścarantamaśrauṣīt / kvacidbodhicittavimātratāṃ kvacitpāramitācaryāpraṇidhānavimātratāṃ kvacidbhūmyapramāṇavimātratāṃ kvacidabhijñācintyavikurvitavimātratāṃ kvacittathāgatapūjāvimātryavimātratāṃ kvacidbuddhakṣetravyūhavimātratāṃ kvacidapramāṇatathāgatadharmameghavimātratām evaṃ sarvadharmanirghoṣān yathāpūrvaparikīrtitānaśrauṣīt / kvacitsarvajñatāprasthānaśabdamaśrauṣīt - amuṣmin lokadhātāvamuko nāma bodhisattvo bodhicittamutpādayati amukaṃ dharmamukhaṃ śrutvā amukena kalyāṇamitreṇa samādāpito 'mukasya tathāgatasya pādamūle evaṃnāmni kalpe īdṛśe buddhakṣetre īdṛkparṣanmadhyagate īdṛśaṃ kuśalamūlamūlamavaropya īdṛśāṃstathāgataguṇān śrutvā īdṛśenādhyāśayena īdṛśyā praṇidhānavimātratayā / iyataḥ kalpān bodhisattvacaryāṃ caritvā iyadbhiḥ kalpairanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / īdṛgnāmadheyaḥ īdṛśena āyuḥpramāṇena īdṛśyā buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāsaṃpadā / īdṛśena praṇidhānaviśeṣeṇa īdṛśena sattvavinayena īdṛśena śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvasaṃnipātena / tasya parinirvṛtasya iyataḥ kalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati, iyān samartho bhaviṣyati / kvacinnirghoṣamaśrauṣīt - amuṣmiṃllokadhātāvamuko nāma bodhisattvo dānapāramitāyāṃ carannīdṛśāni duṣkaraparityāgaśatāni karoti / amuko bodhisattvaḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati, kṣāntiṃ bhāvayati, vīryamālabhate, dhyānāni samāpadyate prajñāvicayaprayuktaḥ / amuko bodhisattvaḥ saddharmaparyeṣṭiheto rājaparityāgaṃ karoti, ratnaparityāgaṃ putraparityāgaṃ bhāryāparityāgaṃ hastapādanayanottamāṅgaparityāgaṃ karoti, agniprapatanaṃ karoti / amuko nāma bodhisattvaḥ tathāgataśāsanamabhyudgato dharmabhāṇakatvaṃ karoti, dharmadānaṃ dadāti, dharmayajñaṃ yajati, dharmadhvajamucchrayati, dharmabherīṃ parāhanti, dharmaśaṅkhamāpūrayati, dharmavarṣaṃ pravarṣati, tathāgataśāsanaṃ dhārayati, tathāgatacaityānyalaṃkaroti,
tathāgatavigrahān kārayati, sattvasukhopadhānamupasaṃharati, saddharmakośamārakṣati / kvacinnirghoṣamaśrauṣīt - amuṣmiṃllokadhātāvamuko nāma tathāgata etarhi tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati, dharmaṃ ca deśayati evaṃnāmnābhiṣekeṇa īdṛśyāṃ parṣadi īdṛśe buddhakṣetre īdṛśe kalpe īdṛśenāyuḥpramāṇena īdṛśyā dharmadeśanayā īdṛśena sattvavinayena īdṛkpraṇidhyabhisaṃbodhena / evamekaikasmād ghaṇṭākiṅkiṇījālatūryādikādārambaṇādapramāṇadharmamukhavimātratānirghoṣānaśrauṣīt / sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ nirghoṣāṇāṃ śraveṇa sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako vipulaprītivegābhiṣyandita cittastāni dharmamukhāni śṛṇoti / kvaciddhāraṇīmukhāni pratyalabhata, kvacitpraṇidhānamukhāni, kvacitkṣāntimukhāni, kvaciccaryāmukhāni, kvacitpraṇidhānamukhāni, kvacitpāramitāmukhāni, kvacidabhijñāmukhāni, kvacidvidyājñānālokamukhāni, kvacidvimokṣamukhāni, kvacitsamādhipraveśamukhāni pratyalabhata //
body.translated_text: he heard the sound of inconceivable cloud-thunder reverberating from the nets of bells, small bells, musical instruments, and songs that served as supports for those beings. Somewhere he heard diverse aspects of <s>bodhicitta</s>, somewhere diverse aspects of the practices, conduct, and vows of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), somewhere diverse immeasurable aspects of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), somewhere diverse aspects of inconceivable miraculous transformations of <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledges), somewhere diverse aspects of worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, somewhere diverse aspects of <s>Buddha</s>-field arrays, somewhere diverse immeasurable aspects of the <s>Dharma</s>-clouds of <s>Tathāgatas</s> — thus he heard all the <s>Dharma</s>-sounds as previously proclaimed. Somewhere he heard the sound of setting forth toward omniscience: 'In such-and-such a world-realm, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such a name generates <s>bodhicitta</s>, having heard such-and-such a <s>Dharma</s>-gateway, urged on by such-and-such a spiritual friend, at the feet of such-and-such a <s>Tathāgata</s>, in such-and-such a named <s>kalpa</s>, in such-and-such a <s>Buddha</s>-field, in the midst of such-and-such an assembly, having planted such-and-such wholesome roots, having heard such-and-such qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with such-and-such an aspiration, with such-and-such a diverse extent of vows. Having practiced <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct for so many <s>kalpas</s>, he will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening after so many <s>kalpas</s> — with such-and-such a name, with such-and-such a lifespan, with such-and-such a splendor of <s>Buddha</s>-field quality-arrays, with such-and-such a distinctive vow, with such-and-such a discipline of beings, with such-and-such an assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. After his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for so many <s>kalpas</s> and will be so powerful.' Somewhere he heard the sound: 'In such-and-such a world-realm, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such a name, practicing the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), performs hundreds of difficult renunciations. Such-and-such a <s>Bodhisattva</s> guards moral conduct, cultivates patience, undertakes energy, enters <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and is engaged in the investigation of wisdom. Such-and-such a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of seeking the true <s>Dharma</s>, renounces kingship, renounces treasures, renounces sons, renounces wives, renounces hands, feet, eyes, and head, and casts himself into fire. Such-and-such a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, exalting the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, acts as a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, performs the <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice, raises the <s>Dharma</s>-banner, beats the <s>Dharma</s>-drum, fills the <s>Dharma</s>-conch, rains the <s>Dharma</s>-rain, upholds the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, adorns the <s>caityas</s> (shrines) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, commissions images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, brings about the happiness of beings, and guards the treasury of the true <s>Dharma</s>.' Somewhere he heard the sound: 'In such-and-such a world-realm, such-and-such a <s>Tathāgata</s> presently lives, endures, and maintains himself, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> — with such-and-such a consecration-name, in such-and-such an assembly, in such-and-such a <s>Buddha</s>-field, in such-and-such a <s>kalpa</s>, with such-and-such a lifespan, with such-and-such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, with such-and-such a discipline of beings, with such-and-such an awakening through vows.' Thus from each and every bell, small bell, net of musical instruments, and similar support, he heard the sounds of immeasurable diverse <s>Dharma</s>-gateways. And upon hearing all those sounds, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, his mind flooded with a surge of abundant joy, listened to those <s>Dharma</s>-gateways. In some he attained <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, in some vow-gateways, in some patience-gateways, in some conduct-gateways, in some aspiration-gateways, in some <s>pāramitā</s>-gateways, in some <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge)-gateways, in some gateways of the light of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge)-wisdom, in some liberation-gateways, and in some gateways of entry into <s>samādhi</s>. //

body.text: tebhyaśca ādarśamaṇḍalebhyo 'parimāṇapratibhāsavyūhavijñaptimapaśyat / kvacittathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidbodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacicchrāvakaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitpratyekabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacittathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ
body.translated_text: And from those mirror-maṇḍalas he saw immeasurable arrays of reflections. Somewhere he saw the reflected display of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly-circles, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Śrāvaka</s> assembly-circles, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> assembly-circles, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles,

body.text:
kvacitsaṃkliṣṭakṣetrapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidviśuddhakṣetrapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitsaṃkleṣṭaviśuddhakṣetrapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitsarvabuddhaikalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidbuddhalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitparīttalokadhātupravibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacinmahadgatalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitsūkṣmalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidudāralokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidindrajālapraveśalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidvyatyastalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidadhamūrdhvaṃlokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacitsamadharaṇītalapraveśalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacinnarakatiryakpretāvabhāsalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvaciddevamanuṣyākīrṇalokadhātupratibhāsavijñaptimadrākṣīt / teṣu ca caṃkrameṣu niṣadya svāsaneṣu ca asaṃkhyeyān bodhisattvān nānākāryaprayuktānapaśyat / kāṃściccaṃkramyamāṇān kāṃścidvyāyacchataḥ kāṃścidvipaśyataḥ kāṃścinmahākaruṇayā spharamāṇān kāṃścidvividhān śāstranayān lokārthasaṃprayuktānabhinirharamāṇān kāṃściduddiśataḥ kāṃścitsvādhyāyamānān kāṃścillikhitaḥ kāṃścitparipraśnayataḥ kāṃścitrtriskandhadeśanāpariṇamanābhiyuktān kāṃścitpraṇidhānānyabhinirharamāṇān
//
body.translated_text: somewhere the reflected display of defiled fields, somewhere the reflected display of purified fields, somewhere the reflected display of both defiled and purified fields, somewhere the reflected display of a single world-realm of all <s>Buddhas</s>, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Buddha</s> world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of small world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of great world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of subtle world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of exalted world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of world-realms entering <s>Indra</s>'s net of illusion, somewhere the reflected display of inverted world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of upside-down world-realms, somewhere the reflected display of world-realms entering the same ground-surface, somewhere the reflected display of world-realms illuminated by hells, animal realms, and <s>preta</s> realms, and somewhere he saw the reflected display of world-realms filled with <s>devas</s> and humans. In those walkways and upon their own seats, he saw innumerable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> engaged in various activities — some walking, some stretching, some practicing <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight meditation), some pervading [all] with great compassion, some bringing forth various <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) methods connected with the welfare of the world, some instructing, some reciting, some writing, some questioning, some engaged in the <s>triskandha</s> (three-heap) confession and dedication, and some accomplishing vows. //

body.text: tebhyaśca stambhebhyaḥ sarvamaṇirājaprabhājālāni niścaranti vyapaśyat / kvacinnīlavarṇāni kvacitpītavarṇāni kvacillohitavarṇāni kvacidavadātavarṇāni kvacitsphaṭikavarṇāni kvacittapanīyavarṇāni kvacidindranīlavarṇāni kvacidindrāyudhavarṇāni kvacijjāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇāni kvacitsarvaprabhāsavarṇāni kāyacittaprītisaṃjananaparamanayanābhirāmāṇi / tāṃśca jāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇakadalīstambhān sarvaratnavigrahāṃśca puṣpameghāvalambitāpāṇīnadrākṣīt / mālyadāmapāṇīn chatradhvajapatākāpāṇīn gandhadhūpavilepanapāṇīn vividharatnavicitrasuvarṇasūtrapāṇīn vividhamuktāhārapāṇīn nānāratnahārapāṇīn sarvavyūhaparigṛhītapāṇīn / kāṃścidavanatacūḍāmaṇimakuṭān animiṣanayanān kṛtāñjalipuṭān namasyato 'paśyat / tebhyaśca muktāhārebhyaḥ sarvagandhaparibhāvitāṣṭāṅgopetasūkṣmajaladharān prasravamāṇānapaśyat / tebhyaśca vaiḍūryamaṇihārajālebhyo dīrghapaṅktīn kṣarantīnapaśyat / tāni ca ratnacchatrāṇi sarvālaṃkāravyūhopaśobhitānyapaśyat / tāṃ ca ratnaghaṇṭākiṅkiṇījālapaṭṭadāmakalāpamaṇiśalākāvicitramaṇiratnakośasamalaṃkṛtagarbhāmapaśyat / tābhyaśca puṣkiriṇībhyo 'saṃkhyeyāni ratnapadmotpalakumudapuṇḍarīkānyabhyudgatānyapaśyat / kānicidvitastipramāṇamātrāṇi kānicidvyāmapramāṇamātrāṇi kānicicchakaṭacakrapramāṇamātrāṇi / teṣu ca nānārūpān vyūhānapaśyat / yaduta strīrūpān puruṣarūpān dārakarūpān dārikārūpān śakrarūpān brahmarūpān lokapālarūpān devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragarūpān śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvarūpān sarvajagadrūpasaṃsthānaśarīrān vicitranānāvarṇān kṛtāñjalipuṭānavanatakāyānnamasyato 'paśyat / dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtakāyāṃśca tathāgatavigrahān paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: And from those pillars he saw issuing forth nets of radiance of all jewel-kings — somewhere blue-colored, somewhere yellow-colored, somewhere red-colored, somewhere white-colored, somewhere crystal-colored, somewhere gold-colored, somewhere indranīla (sapphire)-colored, somewhere rainbow-colored, somewhere the color of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, and somewhere the color of all radiances — supremely pleasing to the eyes, generating delight of body and mind. And he saw those pillars of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, like plantain trunks, and those jewel-figures, with hands holding clouds of flowers, with hands holding garlands and wreaths, with hands holding parasols, banners, and pennants, with hands holding fragrances, incense, and unguents, with hands holding variegated golden threads adorned with various jewels, with hands holding various pearl necklaces, with hands holding necklaces of various jewels, with hands holding all ornamental arrays — some with bowed diadems, jewel-crowns, and unblinking eyes, with palms joined in homage, he saw them paying reverence. And from those pearl necklaces he saw flowing forth fine streams of water endowed with the eight qualities, perfumed with all fragrances. And from those nets of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> jewel garlands he saw long rows streaming forth. And he saw those jewel parasols adorned with the splendor of all ornamental arrays. And he saw that interior adorned with nets of jewel bells and small bells, silk-ribbon garlands, clusters of gem rods, and variegated jewel-gem caskets. And from those pools he saw innumerable jewel lotuses — <s>utpalas</s>, <s>kumudas</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> — rising up; some a hand-span in size, some a fathom in size, some the size of a chariot wheel. And in them he saw various forms of arrays — namely, forms of women, forms of men, forms of boys, forms of girls, forms of <s>Śakra</s>, forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, forms of world-guardians, forms of <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, forms of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with bodies in the shapes and forms of all beings, of variegated diverse colors, with palms joined and bodies bowed — he saw them paying reverence. And he saw <s>Tathāgata</s> figures adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, seated cross-legged. //

body.text: yā ca sā vaiḍūryatalāṣṭāpadamahāpṛthivī, tatra ekaikato 'ṣṭāpadādacintyāḥ pratibhāsavijñaptīrapaśyat / kvacitkṣetrapratibhāsavijñaptiṃ kvacidbuddhapratibhāsavijñaptim / yāvantaśca teṣu
body.translated_text: And on that great ground-surface of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> squares like a chessboard, from each and every square he saw inconceivable reflected displays — somewhere the reflected display of fields, somewhere the reflected display of <s>Buddhas</s>. And however many in those

body.text: kūṭāgāreṣvalaṃkāravyūhāḥ, tān sarvānekaikasminnaṣṭāpade pratibhāsaprāptānapaśyat / teṣāṃ ca ratnavṛkṣāṇāṃ sarvatra puṣpaphalakośebhyo nānāsaṃsthānavicitrasuvarṇarūpārdhakāyānapaśyat / kvacidbuddhārdhakāyān kvacidbodhisattvārdhakāyān kvaciddevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragārdhakāyān kvacicchakrabrahmalokapālārdhakāyān kvaciccakravartimanuṣyendrārdhakāyān kvacidrājakumāraśreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyastrīpuruṣadārakadārikābhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikārdhakāyān kāṃścitpuṣpadāmāvalambitapāṇīn kāṃścidratnahārābhipralambitapāṇīn kāṃścitsarvavyūhaparigṛhītapāṇīn kāṃścidavanatakāyān kṛtāñjalipuṭānanimiṣanayanān namasyataḥ kāṃścidabhiṣṭuvataḥ kāṃścitsamāpannān kāṃścitsuvarṇavarṇāvabhāsān kāṃścidrūpyavarṇāvabhāsān kāṃścittuṣārasukumāravarṇāvabhāsān kāṃścidindranīlamaṇivarṇāvabhāsān kāṃścidvirocanamaṇiratnāvabhāsān kāṃścitsarvaratnavarṇāvabhāsān kāṃściccampakapuṣpavarṇāvabhāsān kāṃścitprabhākāyāvabhāsān kāṃścillakṣaṇavicitrātmabhāvānapaśyat / tebhyaśca ardhacandrebhyo 'saṃkhyeyāṃścandrasūryagrahanatārāpratibhāsān niścarya daśadiśo 'vabhāsayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: ornamental arrays in the pavilions — all these he saw reflected in each single tile-square. And from the flower-and-fruit clusters of those jewel-trees everywhere, he saw half-bodies of variegated golden form in diverse configurations: somewhere half-bodies of <s>Buddhas</s>, somewhere half-bodies of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, somewhere half-bodies of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, somewhere half-bodies of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and world-protectors, somewhere half-bodies of <s>cakravartins</s> and lords of men, somewhere half-bodies of princes, merchants, householders, ministers, women, men, boys, girls, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — some with hands holding garlands of flowers, some with hands dangling jewel-necklaces, some with hands holding all kinds of ornaments, some with bodies bowed, palms joined, eyes unblinking, paying homage, some offering praises, some absorbed in meditation, some with the radiance of golden hue, some with the radiance of silver hue, some with the radiance of the delicate color of frost, some with the radiance of the color of <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gems, some with the radiance of <s>Virocana</s> jewel-gems, some with the radiance of the color of all jewels, some with the radiance of the color of <s>campaka</s> flowers, some with radiant luminous bodies, some he saw with forms variously adorned with marks. And from those half-moons, innumerable reflections of moons, suns, planets, and stars emerged, illuminating the ten directions.

body.text: tāśca prāsādavimānakūṭāgārabhittīḥ sarvaratnāṣṭāpadavicitrā apaśyat / teṣu ca sarvaratnāṣṭāpadeṣu maitreyasya bodhisattvasya sarvabodhisattvacaryākramamapaśyat yathā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvāścaryāmacaran / kvacidaṣṭāpade maitreyasya bodhisattvasya śiraḥpradānamapaśyat / kvacinnetrapradānaṃ kvacidvastrapradānaṃ kvaciccūḍāmaṇiratnapradānaṃ kvacitsaddharmacūḍāmaṇipradānaṃ kvaciddantapradānaṃ kvacijjihvāpradānaṃ kacitkarṇanāsāpradānaṃ kvaciddhṛdayapradānaṃ kvacinmajjamāṃsapradānaṃ kvacidrudhirapradānaṃ kvacicchavicarmapradānaṃ kvacinmāṃsanakhapradānaṃ kvacitsajālāṅgulipradānaṃ kvacitsarvaśarīrapradānaṃ kvacitputraduhitṛbhāryāpradānaṃ kvacidratnarāśipradānaṃ kvacidgrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīpradānaṃ kvacijjambudvīpapradānaṃ kvaciccaturdvīpapradānaṃ kvacitsarvarājyaiśvaryapradānaṃ kvacidbhadrarājāsanapradānaṃ kvaciddāsadāsīpradānaṃ kvacidantaḥpurapradānaṃ kvacidudyānatapovanapradānaṃ kvacicchatradhvajapatākāpradānaṃ kvacitpuṣpamālyagandhānulepanapradānaṃ kvacid glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapradānaṃ kvacitsarvānnapānavidhipradānaṃ kvacitsarvopakaraṇapradānaṃ kvacitsarvopāśrayapradānaṃ kvacidratnakāṃsyapātrīpradānaṃ kvacidvararathapradānaṃ kvacidbandhanāgāragatān vimokṣayantaṃ kvacidvadhyān nirmokṣayantaṃ kvacidbālāṃścikitsamānaṃ kvacitpranaṣṭamārgāṇāṃ mārgamupadarśayantaṃ kvaciddāśabhūtaṃ nadīpathe nāvaṃ vāhayamānaṃ kvacidbālāhāśvarājabhūtaṃ mahāsamudre rākṣasīdvīpagatān sattvān paritrāyamāṇaṃ kvacinmaharṣibhūtaṃ śāstrāṇyabhinirharamāṇaṃ kvaciccakravartibhūtaṃ daśakuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānaṃ kvacidvaidyabhūtamāturāṇāṃ cikitsāṃ prayojayamānaṃ kvacinmātāpitaramupatiṣṭhantaṃ kvacitkalyāṇamitrāṇi śuśrūṣantaṃ kvacicchrāvakavarṇarūpeṇa sattvavinayena prayuktaṃ kvacitpratyekabuddhavarṇarūpeṇa kvacidbodhisattvavarṇarūpeṇa kvacidbuddhavarṇarūpeṇa kvacitsattvavinayaprayuktaṃ kvacitsattvajātakaviśeṣairupapattiṃ saṃdarśya sattvān paripācayamānaṃ kvaciddharmabhāṇakarūpeṇa tathāgataśāsanopagatamuddiśantaṃ svādhyāyamānaṃ yoniśomīmāṃsāprayuktaṃ tathāgatacaityānyalaṃkurvāṇaṃ tathāgatavigrahān
body.translated_text: And he saw the walls of those palaces, aerial mansions, and pavilions inlaid with tile-squares of all jewels. And in each of those jeweled tile-squares, he saw the entire sequence of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of <s>Maitreya</s> — how formerly as a <s>bodhisattva</s> he practiced his conduct. In one tile-square he saw <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s gift of his head; in another, the gift of his eyes; in another, the gift of clothing; in another, the gift of his crest-jewel; in another, the gift of the jewel of the true <s>Dharma</s>; in another, the gift of his teeth; in another, the gift of his tongue; in another, the gift of his ears and nose; in another, the gift of his heart; in another, the gift of his marrow and flesh; in another, the gift of his blood; in another, the gift of his skin and hide; in another, the gift of his flesh and nails; in another, the gift of his webbed fingers; in another, the gift of his entire body; in another, the gift of his sons, daughters, and wife; in another, the gift of heaps of jewels; in another, the gift of villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and capital cities; in another, the gift of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; in another, the gift of the four continents; in another, the gift of all royal sovereignty; in another, the gift of the auspicious royal throne; in another, the gift of male and female servants; in another, the gift of the inner palace; in another, the gift of gardens and ascetic groves; in another, the gift of parasols, banners, and flags; in another, the gift of flowers, garlands, incense, and unguents; in another, the gift of medicine for the sick; in another, the gift of all kinds of food and drink; in another, the gift of all requisites; in another, the gift of all shelters; in another, the gift of jeweled bronze vessels; in another, the gift of excellent chariots; in another, liberating those confined in prison; in another, rescuing those condemned to death; in another, tending the sick; in another, showing the path to those who had lost their way; in another, as a helmsman steering a boat on the river; in another, as the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>, rescuing beings stranded on the island of <s>rākṣasīs</s> in the great ocean; in another, as a great sage, composing treatises; in another, as a <s>cakravartin</s>, establishing beings in the ten wholesome courses of action; in another, as a physician, applying treatment to the ill; in another, attending upon his parents; in another, serving spiritual friends; in another, engaged in the training of beings in the appearance and form of a <s>śrāvaka</s>; in another, in the appearance and form of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>; in another, in the appearance and form of a <s>bodhisattva</s>; in another, in the appearance and form of a <s>Buddha</s>; in another, engaged in the training of beings; in another, displaying birth through special <s>jātaka</s> stories of beings, ripening them; in another, in the form of a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, teaching those who had entered the doctrine of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, reciting, engaged in proper investigation, adorning <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines, making images of <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

body.text:
kārayamāṇaṃ buddhapūjāyāṃ sattvān samādāpayamānaṃ gandhānulepanapradānaṃ sugandhatailābhyañjanapuṣpamālyāropaṇādisarvākārabuddhapūjāprayuktaṃ daśasu kuśalamūleṣu karmapatheṣu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayamānaṃ pañcasu śikṣāpadeṣu aṣṭāṅgapoṣadheṣu buddhadharmasaṃghaśaraṇagamaneṣu pravrajyāyāṃ dharmaśravaṇe uddeśasvādhyāyayoniśomanasikāreṣu sattvānniyojayamānaṃ dharmasāṃkathyāya siṃhāsanasaṃniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhabodhiṃvivṛṇvantam / iti hi yāvanmaitreyo bodhisattvo
'saṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu cīrṇacaritaḥ, tatsarvaṃ sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastata ekaikasmādaṣṭāpadādaparāparairākārairadrākṣīt / sa kvacitkūṭāgāre yāvanti maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena kalyāṇamitrāṇi paryupāsitāni teṣāṃ vikurvitavyūhānadrākṣīt / sarveṣu ca teṣu kalyāṇamitreṣu upasaṃkrāntamābhāṣyamāṇamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma - ehi sudhana svāgatam / māsi klāntaḥ / paśyemāṃ bodhisattvācintyatām //
body.translated_text: encouraging beings in the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, engaged in all forms of <s>Buddha</s>-worship such as offering incense, unguents, fragrant oils, anointing, adorning with flowers and garlands; establishing beings in the ten wholesome courses of action; directing beings to the five training-precepts, the eight-limbed <s>poṣadha</s> observances, taking refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, going forth into the renunciant life, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, recitation, study, and proper mental attention; seated upon the lion-throne for <s>Dharma</s>-discussion, revealing <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. Thus indeed, all that <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> had practiced in the six <s>pāramitās</s> over innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — all of that <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw from each single tile-square in various aspects. And in one pavilion, he saw the miraculous display-arrays of all the spiritual friends whom <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> had attended upon. And he recognized himself as having approached each of those spiritual friends and being addressed by them: 'Come, <s>Sudhana</s>, welcome! Are you not weary? Behold this inconceivable [nature] of the <s>bodhisattva</s>!'

body.text: iti hi sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastata ekaikasmātkūṭāgārādekaikasmādārambaṇādimāni ca anyāni ca avicintyavyūhaviṣayavikurvitānyadrākṣīt / asaṃpramuṣitena smṛtibalādhānena samantadigvyavacāritayā cakṣuḥpariśuddhyā anāvaraṇena vipaśyanākauśalyajñānena bodhisattvajñānādhiṣṭhānavaśitāpratilambhena bodhisattvasaṃjñāgataprasṛtāyāṃ jñānabhūmau sthitaḥ, tatsarvamanantavyūhaviṣayavikurvitamadrākṣīt / tadyathā puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragato vividhān rūpārambaṇaviśeṣān paśyet yaduta gṛhavimānaramaṇīyāni vā grāmanagaranigamajanapadaramaṇīyāni vā vastrānnapānaparibhogaramaṇīyāni vā gītavādyatūryasaṃgītivividharatikrīḍāramaṇīyāni vā paśyet / udyānārāmatapovanaramaṇīyāni vā vṛkṣanadīpuṣkiriṇīparvataramaṇīyāni vā mātāpitṛmitrajñātisālohitasamavadhānagataṃ vā ātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / mahāsamudraṃ vā paśyet sumeruṃ vā parvatarājānaṃ sarvadevabhavanāni vā jambudvīpaṃ vā, anenakayojanaśatasthitaṃ vā ātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / tacca gṛhaṃ vā avacarakaṃ vā vipulaṃ paśyet / sarvaguṇālaṃkārasamavasṛtaṃ divasameva saṃjānīte / na rātridīrghaṃ ca saṃjānīte na hrasvam, na svapna iti saṃjānīte / sukhopasthānaṃ cātmanaḥ paśyet / sa prasrabdhakāyasaṃskāro vigatastyānamiddhaḥ sarvaratyapakarṣito vipulaprītisukhasaṃvedī dīrghaṃ ca vipulaṃ ca saṃjānīte / divasaṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā ardhamāsaṃ vā saṃvatsaraṃ vā varṣaśataṃ vā tato vā uttari saṃjānīte / prativibuddhaśca tatsarvamanusmaret / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānena sarvatraidhātukasvapnasamavasaraṇajñānena parīttasaṃjñāgataniruddhacetā vipulamahadgatānāvaraṇabodhisattvasaṃjñāgatavihārī bodhisattvaviṣayānugato 'cintyabodhisattvanayapraveśānusṛtabuddhistatsarvavyūhavikurvitamapaśyat saṃjānīte 'nubhavati vicārayati nimittīkaroti ālakṣayati, tatra ca sthitamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / tadyathā glānaḥ puruṣaścarame cittotpāde vartamāna upapatyānantaryacitte pratyupasthite karmabhave āmukhībhūte yathākṛtakarmopacayavipākena aśubhakarmapratyayena narakaṃ vā paśyet, tiryagyoniṃ vā pretaviṣayaṃ vā yamapuruṣān vā dṛḍhapraharaṇagṛhītān ruṣitānākrośato ruditākrośitaśabdaṃ ca nārakāṇāṃ śruṇuyāt / tāṃ ca kṣāranadīṃ paśyet, tāṃśca kṣuradhārāparvatān, tāṃ ca kūṭāśālmalīm, tacca asipatravanaṃ paśyet / tāṃśca mahānarakānādīptān
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, from each single pavilion and each single object of meditation, saw these and other inconceivable miraculous displays of the domain of arrays. With unforgotten power of mindfulness, with the purity of vision extending in all directions, with unobstructed knowledge of the skill of insight, through the attainment of the mastery of the empowerment of <s>bodhisattva</s>-wisdom, established on the ground of wisdom that extends through the perceptual domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, he saw all those endless miraculous displays of the domain of arrays, recognized them, experienced them, reflected upon them, grasped their signs, and observed them — and he recognized himself as standing within them. Just as a sleeping person, having entered a dream, might see various special forms and objects — delightful dwellings and aerial mansions, delightful villages, cities, towns, and districts, delightful clothing, food, drink, and enjoyments, delightful songs, music, instruments, concerts, and various pleasures and amusements; or might see delightful gardens, parks, and ascetic groves, delightful trees, rivers, lotus-ponds, and mountains; or might recognize himself as present at a gathering of parents, friends, relatives, and kinsmen; or might see the great ocean, or <s>Sumeru</s> the king of mountains, or all the divine abodes, or <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, or might recognize himself as situated at a distance of many hundreds of <s>yojanas</s>; and might see that dwelling or its environs as vast, might perceive it all as daytime, might not perceive the night as long or short, might not recognize it as a dream, and might see the arising of happiness for himself — he, with bodily formations relaxed, with torpor and drowsiness gone, drawn away from all pleasures, experiencing vast joy and happiness, perceives it as long and vast, perceives it as a day, or a week, or a fortnight, or a year, or a hundred years, or even more; and upon awakening, he would remember all of it. Just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, through the empowerment of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, through the knowledge of entering into the dream-convergence of all three realms, with his consciousness based on limited perception having ceased, dwelling in the perceptual domain of the vast, exalted, unobstructed <s>bodhisattva</s>, following the domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, with his intelligence conforming to entry into the inconceivable method of the <s>bodhisattva</s> — he saw, recognized, experienced, reflected upon, grasped the signs of, and observed all those miraculous displays of the domain of arrays. And he recognized himself as standing within them. Just as a sick person, at the moment of his final arising of consciousness, when the consciousness of the next birth is at hand, when <s>karma</s>-existence has come to the fore — by the ripening of accumulated deeds and through the condition of unwholesome <s>karma</s>, he might see hell-realms, or animal births, or the realm of hungry ghosts, or the men of <s>Yama</s> seizing firm instruments of punishment, enraged and shouting, and might hear the sounds of crying and shrieking of hell-beings; and he might see that caustic river, and those razor-edged mountains, and that thorny <s>śālmalī</s> tree, and that forest of sword-leaves; and he might see those great hells, blazing,
