paśyedanubhavet / śubhakarmopacayena vā devabhavanaṃ paśyet / devaparṣadapsarogaṇaṃ sarvavyūhālaṃkārāṃśca paśyet, udyānavimānanadīpuṣkariṇīratnaparvatakalpavṛkṣaparibhogān vā paśyedanubhavet, tadāyuḥkālaṃ ca saṃjānīyāt - itaścyutastatra vopapanno 'nantarhita eva karmaviṣayācintyatayā etāṃ kriyāṃ paśyet saṃjānīta anubhavet / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bodhisattvakarmaviṣayācintyatayā tatsarvavyūhavikurvitamadrākṣīt / tadyathā bhūtagrahāviṣṭaḥ puruṣo vividhāni rupagatāni paśyati / yacca paripṛcchate, tadvyākaroti / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bodhisattvajñānādhiṣṭhānabalena tān sarvavyūhānadrākṣīt / tadyathā nāgabhavanapraviṣṭaḥ puruṣo nāgasaṃjñāgatapraveśena divasaṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā ardhamāsaṃ vā māsaṃ vā saṃvatsaraṃ vā varṣaśataṃ vā saṃjñāmātraṃ saṃjānīte, nāgasaṃjñāgatotsṛṣṭo manuṣyasaṃjñāgatena muhūrtamātraṃ paśyet / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako bodhisattvasaṃjñāgatānusmṛtabuddhistanmaitreyasya bodhisattvasya adhiṣṭhānavaśena tanmuhūrtaṃ bahūni kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃjānīte sma / tadyathāsti sarvajagadvaravyūhagarbhaṃ nāma mahābrahmaṇo vimānam / tatra sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturābhāsamāgacchati pratibhāsayogena sarvārambaṇāmiśrībhūtaḥ / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tān sarvān vyūhānanyonyāsaṃkīrṇān sarvārambaṇeṣu pratibhāsaprāptaḥ tadyathā kṛtsnāyatanasamāpattivihārī bhikṣureko 'dvitīyaḥ śayane vā caṃkrame vā niṣadyāyāṃ vā utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā yathākṛtsnasamāpattiviṣayāvatāreṇa sarvalokaṃ saṃjānīte paśyatyanubhavati dhyāyiviśeṣācintyatāyai / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tān sarvān vyūhān yathāviṣayāvatāreṇa paśyati saṃjānīte / tadyathā gandharvanagarāṇāṃ sarvavyūhālaṃkārā gaganatale saṃdṛśyante, na ca kasyacidāvaraṇatvāya kalpante / tadyathā yakṣavimānapraviṣṭāni manuṣyavimānāni yakṣavimānāntargatānyanyonyāsaṃbhinnāni yathākāmaviṣayapariśuddhyā saṃdṛśyante / tadyathā mahāsamudre sarvasya trisāhasramahāsāhasrasya lokadhātoḥ pratibhāsasamudrāḥ saṃdṛśyante / tadyathā māyākāro mantravidyauṣadhibalādhiṣṭhānena sarvarūpagatāni sarvakriyāśca saṃpaśyati / evameva sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako maitreyasya bodhisattvasyādhiṣṭhānajñānamāyācintyapradeśena tāni sarvavyūhavikurvitānyadrākṣīt dharmajñānamāyābalābhinirhṛtena bodhisattvavaśitādhiṣṭhānajñānamāyāgatena //
body.translated_text: blazing with many flames, and would see those iron cauldrons, and those punishments being inflicted, and would perceive those sensations being experienced; and would see and experience those hellish sufferings of burning by fire. Or, through the accumulation of meritorious <s>karma</s>, one would see a celestial mansion, and would see the assemblies of <s>devas</s> and hosts of <s>apsarases</s> and all their arrays and ornaments, and would see and experience the enjoyments of gardens, palaces, rivers, lotus-ponds, jewel-mountains, wish-fulfilling trees, and would perceive the duration of that lifespan — having passed away from here and been reborn there, without any interval, by the inconceivability of the domain of <s>karma</s>, one would see, perceive, and experience this activity. Just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, through the inconceivability of the domain of <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>karma</s>, saw all those array-transformations. Just as a person possessed by a <s>bhūtagraha</s> (spirit-seizure) sees various forms and appearances, and whatever is asked of him, he declares — just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, by the power of the empowerment of <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge, saw all those arrays. Just as a person who has entered a <s>Nāga</s>-palace, through the entry into <s>Nāga</s>-perception, perceives it as merely a perception lasting a day, or a week, or a half-month, or a month, or a year, or a hundred years; but released from <s>Nāga</s>-perception and returned to human perception, one would see it as merely a moment — just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, his mind recalled through <s>bodhisattva</s>-perception, by the power of the empowerment of that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, perceived many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> in that moment. Just as there is a palace of <s>Mahābrahmā</s> called <s>Sarvajagadvaravyūhagarbha</s> (Womb of the Array of the Best of All Worlds), in which the reflection of the entire trichiliocosm (billion-world-realm) arrives through the conjunction of reflections, unmixed with all objects — just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son arrived at the reflection in all objects of all those arrays, unmixed with one another. Just as a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) dwelling in the attainment of the <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s> (totality-base) <s>samāpatti</s>, alone and without a second, whether lying down, walking, sitting, standing up, or seated, perceives, sees, and experiences the entire world according to his entry into the domain of the totality-attainment, through the inconceivability of the meditator's distinction — just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son saw and perceived all those arrays according to his entry into their domain. Just as the array-ornaments of <s>gandharva</s>-cities are seen on the surface of the sky, yet do not serve as an obstruction to anything — just as human palaces that have entered <s>yakṣa</s>-palaces are seen within the <s>yakṣa</s>-palaces, unmixed with one another, through the purity of their respective domains of enjoyment — just as in the great ocean, oceans of reflections of the entire trichiliocosm are seen — just as a <s>māyākāra</s> (magician), through the power of the empowerment of <s>mantras</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, and herbs, sees all forms and all activities — just so, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, through the inconceivable domain of the empowerment-knowledge-illusion of <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, saw all those array-transformations, brought forth by the power of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge-illusion, arrived through the <s>bodhisattva</s>-mastery-empowerment-knowledge-illusion. //

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvastatkūṭāgāraṃ praviśya tadadhiṣṭhānamavasṛjya sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakamacchaṭāśabdaṃ kṛtvā etadavocata - uttiṣṭha kulaputra / eṣā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / aviṣṭhapanapratyupasthānalakṣaṇāḥ kulaputra sarvadharmā bodhisattvajñānādhiṣṭhitāḥ / evaṃ svabhāvāpariniṣpannā māyāsvapnapratibhāsopamāḥ / atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ tenācchaṭāśabdena tataḥ samādhervyutthitaḥ / taṃ maitreyo bodhisattva āha - dṛṣṭā te kulaputra bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānavikurvāḥ? dṛṣṭāste bodhisattvasaṃbhārabalaniṣyandāḥ? dṛṣṭā te bodhisattvapraṇidhijñānaviṭhapanā? dṛṣṭāste bodhisattvacaryāsamudāgamāḥ? śrutaṃ te bodhisattvaniryāṇamukham? dṛṣṭā te buddhakṣetravyūhāpramāṇatā? dṛṣṭā
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having entered that pavilion and released that empowerment, snapped his fingers and spoke thus to <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son: 'Rise, son of good family! Such is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. All <s>dharmas</s>, son of good family, are characterized by non-abiding and presence, empowered by <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge. Thus is their nature — unaccomplished in inherent existence, like illusion, dreams, and reflections.' Then indeed <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son arose from that <s>samādhi</s> through that snapping of fingers. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said to him: 'Did you see, son of good family, the magical transformations of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s empowerment? Did you see the fruits arising from the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s accumulations? Did you see the establishment of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vow-knowledge? Did you see the accomplishments of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct? Did you hear the gateway of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s going forth? Did you see the immeasurability of <s>Buddha</s>-field arrays? Did you see

body.text:
te tathāgatapraṇidhivaiśāradyavaiśeṣikatā? anugatā te bodhisattvavimokṣācintyatā? anubhūtaṃ te bodhisattvasamādhiprītimukham? sudhana āha - dṛṣṭamārya kalyāṇamitrādhiṣṭhānena kalyāṇamitraprabhāveṇa / api tu khalu ārya ko nāmaiṣa vimokṣaḥ? maitreya āha - sarvatryadhvārambaṇajñānapraveśāsaṃmoṣasmṛtivyūhagarbho nāma kulaputra eṣa vimokṣaḥ / īdṛśānāṃ ca kulaputra vimokṣāṇāmanabhilāpyānabhilāpyānāmekajātipratibaddho bodhisattvo lābhī / sudhana āha - kva asau ārya vyūho gataḥ? maitreyo bodhisattva āha - yata evāgataḥ / sudhana āha - kuta āgataḥ? maitreyo bodhisattva āha - bodhisattvajñānādhiṣṭhānābhinirhārādāgataḥ / tatraivādhiṣṭhānena tiṣṭhati / na kvacidgato nāgato na rāśībhūto na saṃcayabhūto na kūṭastho na bhāvastho na bhāvasthito na deśastho na pradeśasthaḥ / tadyathā kulaputra nāgānāṃ meghajālaṃ na kāyena cittena abhyantarībhūtaṃ na saṃcayasthitaṃ na saṃdṛśyate / nāgacetanāvaśena apramāṇā vārighārāḥ pramuñcati nāgaviṣayācintyatayā / evameva kulaputra te vyūhā nādhyātmagatā na bahirdhāgatā na ca na saṃdṛśyante, bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānavaśena, tava ca subhājanatayā / tadyathā kulaputra māyākārasya sarvamāyāgataviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayamānasya māyā na kutaścidāgacchanti na vigacchanti na kvacitsaṃkrāntim, saṃdṛśyate ca mantrauṣadhibalena / evameva kulaputrate vyūhā na kvacidgatā na kutaścidāgatā na kvacidrāśībhūtāḥ / saṃdṛśyante ca acintyabodhisattvajñānamāyāsuśikṣitvāt pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānajñānavaśitayā / sudhana āhaṃ-kiyaddūrādārya āgacchasi? āha - anāgatagatiṃgataḥ / kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ gatiḥ acalanāsthānagatiḥ / anālayāniketagatiḥ / acyutyupapattigatiḥ / asthānasaṃkrāntigatiḥ / acalanānutthānagatiḥ
/ anavekṣāniketagatiḥ / akarmavipākagatiḥ / anutpādānirodhagatiḥ / anucchedāśāśvatagatiḥ / api tu kulaputra mahākaruṇāgatirbodhisattvānāṃ vineyasattvāvekṣaṇatayā, mahāmaitrīgatirbodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhitasattvaparitrāṇatayā, śīlagatirbodhisattvānāṃ yathāśayopapattitayā, praṇidhānagatirbodhisattvānāṃ pūrvādhiṣṭhānena, abhijñāgatirbodhisattvānāṃ sarvasukhasaṃdarśanatayā, anabhisaṃskāragatirbodhisattvānāṃ sarvatathāgatapādamūlānuccalanatayā, anāyūhaviyūhagatirbodhisattvānāṃ kāyacittāsaṃpravaṇatayā, prajñopāyagatirbodhisattvānāṃ sattvānuvartanatayā, nirmāṇasaṃdarśanagatirbodhisattvānāṃ pratibhāsapratibimbanirmitaśarīrasamatayā //
body.translated_text: the distinction of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s vow-confidence? Did you follow the inconceivability of <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation? Did you experience the gateway of the joy of <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>?' <s>Sudhana</s> replied: 'I have seen, Noble One, through the empowerment of the spiritual friend, through the power of the spiritual friend.' 'But, Noble One, what is the name of this liberation?' <s>Maitreya</s> replied: 'This liberation, son of good family, is called <s>Sarvatryadhvārambaṇajñānapraveśāsaṃmoṣasmṛtivyūhagarbha</s> (Womb of the Array of Unfailing Mindfulness of the Entry into Knowledge Whose Object Is All Three Times). And a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is one-birth-bound, son of good family, obtains inexpressibly many inexpressible liberations such as this.' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'Where, Noble One, has that array gone?' The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> replied: 'To the very place whence it came.' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'Whence did it come?' The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> replied: 'It came from the production of the empowerment of <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge. It abides right there through that very empowerment. It has gone nowhere, has not come, has not become a heap, has not become an accumulation, is not fixed in position, is not abiding in existence, is not established in existence, is not established in place, is not established in location. Just as, son of good family, the cloud-net of the <s>Nāgas</s> has not become interior to their body or mind, does not remain as an accumulation, and is not visible — yet by the volition of the <s>Nāgas</s>, it releases immeasurable rain-showers, through the inconceivability of the domain of the <s>Nāgas</s> — just so, son of good family, those arrays have neither gone inside nor come from outside, and yet they are visible, through the power of <s>bodhisattva</s>-empowerment and through your own receptivity. Just as, son of good family, when a magician displays all the domains of magical creation, the illusions do not come from anywhere nor go anywhere nor undergo any transition, yet they are visible through the power of <s>mantras</s> and herbs — just so, son of good family, those arrays have gone nowhere, have not come from anywhere, have not become a heap anywhere; yet they are visible through being well-trained in the inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge-illusion and through the mastery of former vow-empowerment-knowledge.' <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'From how far away, Noble One, do you come?' He replied: 'One whose course is the future. Son of good family, the course of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is a course that is motionless and without abiding; a course without attachment and without a home; a course without death and rebirth; a course of transition without a place; a course of motionlessness and non-arising; a course without a backward look and without a home; a course without <s>karma</s>-ripening; a course of non-arising and non-cessation; a course of neither annihilation nor eternalism. But indeed, son of good family, the course of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is the course of great compassion, through surveying beings to be trained; the course of great loving-kindness, through rescuing beings in suffering; the course of moral conduct, through rebirth according to their dispositions; the course of vows, through former empowerment; the course of superknowledge, through displaying all happiness; the course of non-fabrication, through not moving from the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; the course of non-effort and non-withdrawal, through the non-inclination of body and mind; the course of wisdom and skillful means, through following beings; the course of displaying emanations, through equality with bodies of reflections, images, and emanations. //

body.text: api ca kulaputra yadvadasi - kiyaddūrāttvamāgacchasīti / ahamasmin kulaputra āgacchāmi janmabhūmermāladebhyo janapadebhyaḥ kuṭigrāmakāt / tatra gopālako nāma śreṣṭhī / taṃ buddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpya janmabhūmakānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ yathābhājanatayā dharmaṃ deśayitvā mātāpitṛjñātisaṃbandhinaśca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn mahāyāne samādāpya / sudhana āha - katamā ārya bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ? āha - daśemāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmayaḥ / katamā daśa? yaduta bodhicittotpādo bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ / bodhisattvakulajanaka adhyāśayo bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ / kalyāṇamitrakule janayitāḥ.......bhūmipratiṣṭhānaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ / pāramitākule janakaṃ........ praṇidhānābhinirhāro bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ / anutpattikadharmakṣāntikule
body.translated_text: Moreover, son of good family, when you say 'From how far away do you come?' — I, son of good family, come from the birth-ground, from the <s>Mālada</s> districts, from the village of <s>Kuṭigrāmaka</s>. There is a merchant named <s>Gopālaka</s>. Having established him in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and having taught the <s>Dharma</s> according to the receptivity of the humans of the birth-ground, and having induced my mother, father, relatives, and kinsmen, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, to take up the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — [I have come here.] <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'What, Noble One, are the birth-grounds of <s>bodhisattvas</s>?' He replied: 'These, son of good family, are the ten birth-grounds of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. What are the ten? Namely: the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) is the birth-ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; the resolute intention that generates the <s>bodhisattva</s>-family is the birth-ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; giving birth in the family of spiritual friends......the establishment on the stages is the birth-ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; giving birth in the family of <s>pāramitās</s>........ the production of vows is the birth-ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; giving birth in the family of the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>

body.text: janakau....... / sarvadharmapratipattiḥ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ janmabhūmiḥ / atītānāgatapratyutpannasarvatathāgatakule janayitrī janmabhūmiḥ / imāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ daśa janmabhūmayaḥ //
body.translated_text: ........ The practice of all <s>dharmas</s>, son of good family, is the birth-ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Giving birth in the family of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present is the birth-ground. These, son of good family, are the ten birth-grounds of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: prajñāpāramitā kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ mātā, upāyakauśalyaṃ pitā, dānapāramitā stanyam, śīlapāramitā dhātrī, kṣāntīpāramitā bhūṣaṇālaṃkāraḥ, vīryapāramitā saṃvardhikā, dhyānapāramitā caryāviśuddhiḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇi śikṣācaryaḥ, sarvabodhyaṅgāni sahāyāḥ, sarvabodhisattvā bhrātaraḥ bodhicittaṃ kulam, pratipattiḥ kuladharmāḥ, bhūmyavasthānaṃ kṣāntipratilambhaḥ, kulābhijātiḥ praṇidhānābhinirhāraḥ, kulavidyālābhaḥ, caryāviśuddhiḥ, kuladharmānuvartanatā mahāyānasamādāpanā, kulavaṃśāvyavacchedaḥ abhiṣekaikajātipratibaddhatā, dharmarājeṣu putratvam, sarvatathāgatasamudāgamaḥ kulavaṃśapariśuddhiḥ / evaṃ hi kulaputra bodhisattvo 'tikrānto bhavati bālapṛthagjanabhūmim / avakrānto bhavati bodhisattvaniyāmam / saṃbhūto bhavati tathāgatakūle / pratiṣṭhito bhavati tathāgatavaṃśe / avyavacchedāya pratipanno bhavati triratnavaṃśasya / paripālanābhiyukto bhavati bodhisattvakulasya / pariśuddho bhavati jātigotreṇa / anupakruṣṭo bhavati varṇajātyoḥ / anavadyo bhavati sarvajātaḥ / adoṣaḥ sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyām / kulīno bhavati uttamabuddhakulasaṃbhūto mahāpraṇidhigarbhaśarīraḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), son of good family, is the mother of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; skillful means is the father; the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving) is the breast-milk; the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Moral Conduct) is the nurse; the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) is the adornment; the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor) is the nurturer; the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation) is the purification of conduct; spiritual friends are the teachers of training; all the limbs of awakening are the companions; all <s>bodhisattvas</s> are the brothers; <s>bodhicitta</s> is the family; practice is the family <s>dharma</s>; establishment on the stages is the attainment of patience; noble birth is the production of vows; the acquisition of family knowledge; the purification of conduct; the following of the family <s>dharma</s> is the taking up of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; the non-interruption of the family lineage is the being bound to a single birth at consecration; sonship to the <s>Dharma</s>-kings; the accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> is the purification of the family lineage. Thus indeed, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> has transcended the stage of foolish ordinary beings; has descended into the fixed course of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; has been born into the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; is established in the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; has entered upon the path for the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels; is devoted to the protection of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-family; is well-purified in birth and lineage; is unimpeached in color and caste; is blameless in all his births; is faultless in the world with its <s>devas</s>, <s>Māras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and among the progeny of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; is of noble birth, born into the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-family, with a body that is the womb of great vows. //

body.text: evaṃ kulajātisamṛddhāśca kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ pratibhāsāyatanasarvadharmaparijñātatvānna vijugupsante sarvalokopapattiṣu / nirmitopamasarvabhavopapattiparijñātatvānna saṃkliśyante sarvabhavagatyupapattisaṃvāseṣu / nirātmasarvabuddhatvānna parikhidyante sarvasattvaparipākavinayeṣu / mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāśarīratvānna śrāmyanti sarvasattvānugraheṣu / svapnopamasaṃsārādhimuktatvānna paritrasanti sarvakalpasaṃvāseṣu / māyāmayaṃ ca skandhaparijñātatvānna krāmyanti sarvajanmacyutimaraṇasaṃdarśanena / dharmadhātuprakṛtikatvāyatanamucitvānna kṣaṇyante sarvaviṣayeṣu / marīcyupamasarvasaṃjñāgatasubhāvitatvānna muhyanti sarvasaṃsāragatiṣu / māyopamasarvadharmavikrīḍitatvādanupaliptā bhavanti sarvamāraviṣayaiḥ / sarvakāyaprabhāvitatvādavañcanīyā bhavanti sarvakleśaiḥ / upapattivaśitālabdhatvādgatiṃgatā bhavanti sarvagatiṣu / so 'haṃ kulaputra sarvalokadhātūpapattyantargatena kāyena sarvajagadrūpasamairbalaviśeṣaiḥ sarvasattvopamairniruktisaṃbhedaiḥ sarvajagadupamābhirnāmadheyavimātratābhiḥ sarvasattvādhimuktisamairīryāpathaiḥ, sarvajagadvinayapramāṇairlokānuvartanaiḥ, sarvaviśuddhisamairjanmakulopapattisaṃdarśanaiḥ, kriyāvatāramukhaiḥ sarvasattvasaṃjñānupraveśaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhinirmāṇasamairātmabhāvasaṃdarśanaprabhāvanaiḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā pūrvasabhāgacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ pranaṣṭabodhicittānāṃ paripācanārthaṃ jambudvīpe ca janmopapattisaṃdarśanārthamiha dakṣiṇāpathe māladeṣu janapadeṣu kūṭāgrāmake brāhmaṇakuleṣūpapannānāṃ mātṛpitṛjñātisaṃbandhināṃ vinayārthaṃ brāhmaṇakulajātiviśeṣeṇa caiṣāṃ jātyabhimānikānirabhimānatāyai tathāgatakule saṃjananārthamihopapannaḥ / so 'haṃ kulaputra iha dakṣiṇāpathe anenopāyena yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ yathāvineyānāṃ paripākavinayaṃ kurvan ihaiva vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbhe kūṭāgāre
body.translated_text: Thus, son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with noble birth and lineage — because they have fully understood all <s>dharmas</s> as the domain of reflections — do not feel revulsion toward births in all worlds. Because they have fully understood all births in existence as resembling magical creations — they are not defiled by dwelling in the births of all existences and courses. Because all <s>Buddha</s>-nature is selfless — they do not become weary in the ripening and disciplining of all beings. Because their bodies are great loving-kindness and great compassion — they do not grow fatigued in favoring all beings. Because they have resolute faith in <s>saṃsāra</s> as dreamlike — they do not tremble at dwelling in all <s>kalpas</s>. Because they have fully understood the aggregates as illusion-like — they are not dismayed by the display of birth, death, and passing in all lifetimes. Because they have freed the sense-bases of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — they are not harmed in any domain of objects. Because they have well-cultivated all perceptions as mirage-like — they are not deluded in all the courses of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Because they sport with all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion-like — they remain untainted by all the domains of <s>Māra</s>. Because they have made all bodies their domain — they cannot be deceived by any defilements. Because they have attained mastery over rebirth — they have reached their destination in all courses. I, son of good family, with a body that encompasses birth in all world-realms, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> — with distinctions of power equal to the forms of all beings, with differentiations of language equal to the analogies of all beings, with varieties of names equal to the analogies of all beings, with deportments equal to the resolute faiths of all beings, with worldly adaptations proportioned to the disciplining of all beings, with demonstrations of births in families and lineages equal to all purifications, with entries into action that penetrate the perceptions of all beings, with manifestations of personal existence equal to the emanations of the vows of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — for the purpose of ripening beings of former similar conduct whose <s>bodhicitta</s> has been lost, and for the purpose of demonstrating birth in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and for the purpose of disciplining those born in <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families in <s>Kūṭāgrāmaka</s> in the <s>Māla</s> districts of the southern region — mothers, fathers, relatives, and kinsmen — and for the purpose of removing the pride of birth through the distinction of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> family-birth for those who are proud of their birth, and for the purpose of generating [them] in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — I have taken birth here. I, son of good family, by this method, here in the southern region, ripening and disciplining beings according to their dispositions and [suitability for] disciplining, dwell here in this very aerial palace called <s>Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha</s> (Womb of the Ornamental Array of Vairocana)

body.text:
prativasāmi / itaścāhaṃ cyutaḥ tuṣitabhavane upapattiṃ saṃdarśayiṣyāmi yathāśaye sattvānuvartanatāyai, tuṣitakāyikānāṃ ca sabhāgacaritānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ paripākāya,
sarvakāmadhātusamatikrāntānāṃ bodhisattvapuṇyajñānanirmāṇavyūhasaṃdarśanatāyai, kāmaratitṛṣṇāvinivartanatāyai, sarvasaṃsārānityatvaparidīpanatāyai, vipattiparyavasānasarvadevopapattisaṃdarśanatāyai, cyavanākāraṃ nāma mahājñānadharmamukhamekajātibaddhairbodhisattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgāyanāya, sahaparipācitānāṃ ca tatropapattisaṃgrahaṇatāyai, śākyamunisaṃpreṣitānāṃ ca vineyakalānāṃ prabodhanatāyai / kāle paripūrṇābhiprāyasarvajñatāmadhigamiṣyāmi / bodhiprāptaṃ ca māṃ kulaputra tvaṃ punarapi drakṣyasi sārdhaṃ mañjuśriyā kalyāṇamitreṇa //
body.translated_text: . And departing from here, I shall demonstrate birth in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, for the purpose of conforming to beings according to their dispositions, and for the ripening of <s>Tuṣita</s>-dwelling <s>devaputras</s> of similar conduct, and for the demonstration of the arrays of <s>bodhisattva</s> merit-and-knowledge emanations that transcend the entire desire-realm, and for turning [beings] away from the thirst and attachment to sensual pleasures, and for illuminating the impermanence of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, and for demonstrating that all divine births end in downfall, and for reciting together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound to one more birth the great knowledge <s>dharma</s>-gateway called 'The Mode of Passing Away' (<s>Cyavanākāra</s>), and for gathering those who have been ripened together into that rebirth, and for awakening those sent by <s>Śākyamuni</s> who are parts [of beings] to be disciplined. In due time, with my intentions fulfilled, I shall attain omniscience. And when I have attained awakening, son of good family, you will see me again, together with your spiritual friend <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. //

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra - gaccha tvaṃ tameva mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam / upasaṃkramya paripṛccha - kathaṃ bodhisattvena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathaṃ samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍalamavataritavyam, kathamabhinirhartavyam, kathaṃ praṇidhātavyam, kathaṃ vipulīkartavyam, kathamanusartavyam, kathaṃ paryadātavyam, kathaṃ praveṣṭavyam, kathaṃ paripūrayitavyam, sa te kulaputra kalyāṇamitra saṃdarśayiṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? sa kulaputra bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ praṇidhānaviśeṣaḥ saṃvidyate yo mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya / vistīrṇaḥ kulaputra mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya caryānihāraṃ / apramāṇo mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya praṇidhānābhinirhāraḥ apratiprasrabdho mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya sarvabodhisattvaguṇaviśeṣābhinirhāraḥ / mātā mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇām / avavādako mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇām / udyukto mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sarvasattvadhātuparipākavinayāya / vistīrṇanāmacakro mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto daśadiksarvalokadhātuṣu / kathāpuruṣo mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto 'nabhilāpyeṣu tathāgataparṣanmaḍaleṣu / saṃvarṇito mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sarvatathāgataiḥ / gambhīradharmajñānavihārī mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sarvadharmayathārthadarśī / durāgatagocaro mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sarvavimokṣanayeṣu / avatīrṇaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāyām / sa te kulaputra kalyāṇamitrājanakaḥ, tathāgatakule saṃvardhakaḥ, sarvakuśalamūlānutthāpakaḥ, bodhisaṃbhārāṇāṃ darśakaḥ, bhūtakalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ samādāpakaḥ sarvaguṇeṣu avatārakaḥ, mahāpraṇidhānajāle pratiṣṭhāpakaḥ, sarvapraṇidhānābhinirhāreṣu śrāvayitā, sarvabodhisattvaguhyānāṃ saṃdarśakaḥ, sarvabodhisattvacintyatāyāḥ, sabhāgacaritaḥ pūrvajanmasaṃvāseṣu / tasmāttarhi tvaṃ kulaputra mañjuśrīpādamūlagataḥ eva mā parīttamanamutpādaya, mā parikhedaṃ janaya sarvaguṇānuśāsanīpratilambheṣu / tatkasya hetoḥ? yāvanti tvayā sudhana kalyāṇamitrāṇi dṛṣṭāni, yāvanti caryāmukhāni śrutāni, yāvanto vimokṣanayā avatīrṇāḥ, yāvantaḥ praṇidhānaviśeṣā avagāḍhāḥ, sarvaṃ mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasyānubhāvo 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ ca draṣṭavyam / sa ca mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ paramapāramitāprāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: But furthermore, son of good family — go to that very <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince. Approach him and ask: 'How should a <s>bodhisattva</s> train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct? How should he practice? How should he enter the maṇḍala of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s>? How should he accomplish it? How should he make vows? How should he expand it? How should he follow it? How should he perfect it? How should he enter it? How should he fulfill it?' He, son of good family, will show you the spiritual friend. For what reason? Son of good family, the vow-distinction of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is found among hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Vast, son of good family, is the accomplishment of the conduct of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince. Immeasurable is the accomplishment of the vows of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince. Unrelaxed is the accomplishment of the distinction of all <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities by <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is the mother of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is the counselor of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is devoted to the ripening and disciplining of the entire realm of beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince has a vast wheel of renown in all the world-realms of the ten directions. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is the speaker in inexpressible assembly-maṇḍalas of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince is praised by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince dwells in the abiding of deep <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge, seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince has a domain difficult to reach in all the methods of liberation. He has descended into the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. He, son of good family, is the generator of your spiritual friends, the nourisher in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the raiser of all roots of merit, the shower of the provisions for awakening, the instigator toward genuine spiritual friends, the one who leads into all qualities, the establisher in the net of great vows, the proclaimer of all accomplishments of vows, the revealer of all the secrets of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the one of similar conduct in former-life associations with the inconceivable nature of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, son of good family, having gone to the feet of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do not generate a narrow mind, do not generate weariness in the attainment of instruction in all qualities. For what reason? However many spiritual friends you have seen, <s>Sudhana</s>, however many gateways of conduct you have heard, however many methods of liberation you have entered, however many distinctions of vows you have plunged into — all of that should be seen as the power and empowerment of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince. And <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince has attained the ultimate <s>pāramitā</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako maitreyasya bodhisattvasya pādau śirāsābhivandya maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punaḥ punaravalokya maitreyasya bodhisattvasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 52 //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, circumambulated the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, and gazing upon him again and again, departed from the presence of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>. // 52 //

body.text: 55 Mañjuśrīḥ /
body.translated_text: 55. <s>Mañjuśrī</s> /

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako daśottaraṃ nagaraśatamaṭitvā sumanāmukhadikpratyuddeśaṃ gatvā atiṣṭhat mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ cintayan anuvilokayan mañjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya darśanamabhilaṣan prārthayamānaḥ samavadhānamākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ / atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto daśottarādyojanaśatātpāṇiṃ prasārya sumanāmukhanagarasthitasyaiva sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpya evamāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra na śakyaṃ śraddhendriyavirahitaiḥ khinnacittaiḥ līnacittairanabhyastaprayogaiḥ pratyudāvartyavīryairitvaraguṇasaṃtuṣṭairekakuśalamūlatanmayaiścaryāpraṇidhānābhinirhārākuśalaiḥ kalyāṇamitrāparigṛṣṭītairbuddhāsamanvāhṛtairiyaṃ dharmatā jñātum, eṣa nayaḥ eṣa gocaraḥ eṣa vihāro jñātuṃ vā avagāhayituṃ vā avatarituṃ vā adhimoktuṃ vā kalpayituṃ vā pratyavagantuṃ vā pratilabdhuṃ vā iti //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, having traversed more than a hundred cities, arrived at the region called <s>Sumanāmukha</s> and stood there, contemplating <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, gazing toward him, longing for the sight of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, desiring, hoping for a meeting. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, from more than a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away, extended his hand and placed it upon the head of the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>, still standing in the city of <s>Sumanāmukha</s>, and spoke thus: 'Well done, well done, son of good family! It is not possible for those devoid of the faculty of faith, with weary minds, with sunken minds, with unpracticed effort, with retreating vigor, with those content with paltry qualities, with those absorbed in a single root of merit, with those unskilled in the accomplishment of the vows of conduct, with those not embraced by spiritual friends, with those not kept in mind by the <s>Buddhas</s> — for them to know this nature of <s>dharmas</s>, to know this method, this domain, this abiding, or to plunge into it, or to enter it, or to have resolute faith in it, or to reflect upon it, or to comprehend it, or to attain it.' //

body.text: sa taṃ dharmakathayā saṃdarśayitvā samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣayitvā asaṃkhyeyadharmamukhasamanvāgataṃ kṛtvā anantajñānamahāvabhāsaprāptaṃ kṛtvā aparyantabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratibhānasamādhyabhijñajñānaveśāviṣṭaṃ kṛtvā samantabhadracaryāmaṇḍale 'vatārayitvā svadeśe ca pratiṣṭhāpya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ // 53 //
body.translated_text: He, having instructed him, established him, encouraged him, and delighted him with the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, having endowed him with innumerable <s>Dharma</s>-gateways, having caused him to attain the great illumination of infinite knowledge, having caused him to be entered by the knowledge of boundless <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>, eloquence, <s>samādhi</s>, superknowledge, and wisdom, having caused him to enter the maṇḍala of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, and having established him in his own domain — departed from the presence of the merchant's son <s>Sudhana</s>. // 53 //

body.text: 56 Samantabhadracaryāpraṇidhānam /
body.translated_text: 56. The Vow of the Conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> (<s>Samantabhadracaryāpraṇidhāna</s>) /

body.text:
atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamakalyāṇamitraparyupāsitaḥ sarvajñatāsaṃbhāropacitacetāḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrāvavādānuśāsanīṣu pradakṣiṇagrāhitayā pratipannaḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrāśayasamatāprasṛtaḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrārāgaṇāvirāgaṇabuddhiḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrāvavādānuśāsanīnayasamudrānugataḥ mahākaruṇāśayasāgarasaṃbhūtagarbho mahāmaitrīnayameghasarvajagadvirocanaḥ mahāprītivegasaṃvardhitaśarīraḥ vipulabodhisattvavimokṣapraśāntavihārī samantasukhaprasṛtatyāgacakṣuḥ sarvatathāgataguṇasamudrapratipattisuparipūrṇaḥ sarvatathāgatādhimuktipathaprasṛtaḥ sarvajñatāsaṃbhāravīryavegavivardhitaḥ sarvabodhisattvacittāśayasupariṇāmitabuddhiḥ sarvatryadhvatathāgataparaṃparāvatīrṇaḥ sarvabuddhadharmanayasāgarānubuddhaḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakranayasāgarānugataḥ sarvalokopapattipratibhāsasaṃdarśanagocaraḥ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānanayasāgarāvatīrṇaḥ sarvakalpabodhisattvacaryāsaṃprasthitaḥ sarvajñatāviṣayāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ sarvabodhisattvendriyavivardhitaḥ sarvajñatāmārgāvabhāsapratilabdhaḥ sarvadigvitimirālokaprāptaḥ sarvadharmadhātunayaprasṛtabuddhiḥ sarvakṣetranayāvabhāsasaṃjātaḥ sarvasattvaprasārārthakriyāpratisrotonugataḥ sarvāvaraṇaprapātaparvatavikiraṇo 'nāvaraṇadharmatānugataḥ samantatalabhūmidharmadhātugarbhabodhisattvavimokṣapraśāntavihārī sarvatathāgatagocaramanveṣamāṇaḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitaḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya gocaraṃ vicārayamāṇaḥ sthito 'bhūt / samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā bodhicaryāṃ śrutvā praṇidhānaviśeṣaṃ ca śrutvā saṃbhārasaṃbhavaprasthānapratiṣṭhitaviśeṣaṃ ca śrutvā abhinirhāraniryāṇapathaviśeṣaṃ ca śrutvā samantabhadrabhūmyācāravicāraṃ ca śrutvā bhūmisaṃbhāraṃ ca śrutvā lambhaviśeṣaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmipratilambhavegaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmyākramaṇaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmipratiṣṭhānaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmiparākramavikramaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmigauravaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmyadhiṣṭhānaṃ ca śrutvā bhūmisaṃvāsaṃ ca śrutvā samantabhadrabodhisattvadarśanaparitṛṣitastasminneva vajrasāgaragarbhabodhimaṇḍe tathāgatasiṃhāsanābhimukhaḥ sarvaratnagarbhapadmāsananiṣaṇṇaḥ ākāśadhātuvipulena cittena sarvābhiniveśoccalitena, subhāvitayā sarvakṣetrasaṃjñayā, sarvasaṅgasamatikrāntena cittena, sarvadharmānāvaraṇagocareṇa apratihatena cittena, sarvadiksamudraspharaṇena anāvaraṇena cittena, sarvajñatāviṣayākramaṇena śuddhena cittena, bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāravipaśyanāpariśuddhena
suvibhaktena cittena, sarvabuddhadharmasamudrāvatīrṇena vipulena cittena, sarvasattvadhātuparipākavinayaspharaṇena mahadgatena cittena, sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanena aparimāṇena cittena, sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsaprāptena sarvakalpasaṃvāsāparyādattena anantena cittena sarvatathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmaparyavasānena / evaṃ cittamanasikāraprayuktasya khalu punaḥ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya pūrvakuśalamūlābhiṣyanditasarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena ca samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya pūrvakuśalamūlasabhāgatayā samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya darśanāya daśa pūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan / katamāni daśa? yaduta sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son — who had attended spiritual friends equal in number to the atoms of the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-realm; whose mind was enriched by the provisions of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience); who had practiced with skill in all the admonitions and instructions of spiritual friends; who had extended himself in the equality of aspiration of all spiritual friends; whose intellect was free from attachment and aversion toward all spiritual friends; who had followed the ocean of methods of admonition and instruction of all spiritual friends; whose womb was born from the ocean of the disposition of great compassion; who illuminated all the world with clouds of the method of great loving-kindness; whose body was nourished by the force of great joy; who dwelt in the tranquil abiding of vast <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation; whose eye of renunciation extended to universal happiness; who was perfectly accomplished in the practice of the ocean of qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; who had set forth on the path of the <s>adhimukti</s> (resolute faith) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; who was increased by the force of vigor in the provisions of omniscience; whose intellect was well-transformed by the mental dispositions of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s; who had descended into the succession of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s of the three times; who had awakened to the ocean of the methods of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s; who had followed the ocean of methods of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; whose domain was the display of the reflected images of all births in the world; who had descended into the ocean of methods of the vows of all <s>Bodhisattva</s>s; who had set forth upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct through all <s>kalpa</s>s; who had attained the illumination of the domain of omniscience; whose <s>Bodhisattva</s>-faculties were fully developed; who had attained the illumination of the path of omniscience; who had attained light free from darkness in all directions; whose intellect was extended into the methods of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>s; in whom was born the illumination of methods of all fields; who followed the counter-current for the benefit and welfare of all beings; who scattered the mountains and precipices of all obscurations, following the nature of non-obstruction; who dwelt in the tranquil abiding of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-liberation of the womb of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the universal ground-stage; who sought the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; who was empowered by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — stood contemplating the domain of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. Having heard the name of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, having heard of his <s>Bodhi</s>-conduct, having heard of the distinction of his vows, having heard of the distinction of his establishment in setting forth through the arising of provisions, having heard of the distinction of the path of accomplishment and deliverance, having heard of the exploration of <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s stage-conduct, having heard of his stage-provisions, having heard of the distinction of his attainments, having heard of the force of his stage-attainment, having heard of his stage-ascent, having heard of his stage-establishment, having heard of the exertion and might of his stages, having heard of the gravity of his stages, having heard of his stage-empowerment, having heard of his stage-abiding — thirsting for the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, right there at the <s>Vajrasāgaragarbha Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, facing the lion-throne of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, seated upon a lotus-seat of all jewel-womb, with a mind vast as the expanse of space, free from all attachment, with the perception of all fields well-cultivated, with a mind that had transcended all clinging, with a mind unobstructed in the domain of non-obstruction of all <s>dharma</s>s, with a mind pervading the oceans of all directions without obstruction, with a mind purified by ascending into the domain of omniscience, with a mind purified by the <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) that is the contemplation of the ornament of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and well-discerning, with a vast mind that had descended into the ocean of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, with a far-reaching mind pervading the ripening and discipline of the entire realm of beings, with an immeasurable mind purifying all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, with an infinite mind that had attained the reflected images of all <s>Buddha</s>-assembly-circles and was inexhaustible in abiding through all <s>kalpa</s>s, terminating in the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — as <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son thus applied his mind and mental attention, by the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the outflow of his former roots of wholesome merit, and by the affinity with the former roots of wholesome merit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, ten portents appeared for the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. What are the ten? Namely, all <s>Buddha</s>-fields

body.text: viśudhyanti sma sarvatathāgatabodhimaṇḍālaṃkāraviśuddhyā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvākṣaṇāpāyadurgatipathavinivṛttatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma dharmanalinīvyūhabuddhakṣetraviśuddhyā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvasattvakāyacittaprahlādanaprāptatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvaratnamayasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvasattvadhātulakṣaṇānuvyañjanapratimaṇḍitasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvasattvadhātulakṣaṇānuvyañjanapratimaṇḍitasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvavyūhālaṃkārameghasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvasattvadhātvanyonyamaitrahitacittāvyāpannacittasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāravyūhasaṃsthānatayā / sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi viśudhyanti sma sarvasattvabuddhānusmṛtimanasikāraprayuktasaṃsthānatayā / imāni daśa pūrvanimittāni prādurabhavan samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya darśanāya //
body.translated_text: became purified by the purification of the ornament of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by the cessation of all untimely births, bad destinies, and evil paths. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field arrayed as a lotus-pond of <s>Dharma</s>. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by having attained the refreshment of the bodies and minds of all beings. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by being entirely composed of all jewels. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by being configured in the form adorned with the marks and minor characteristics of the realm of all beings. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by being configured in the form adorned with the marks and minor characteristics of the realm of all beings. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by being configured as clouds of all array-ornaments. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by the configuration in which all beings in the realm had minds of mutual loving-kindness and benevolence, with unimpaired minds. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by the configuration of the ornament-array of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. All <s>Buddha</s>-fields became purified by the configuration in which all beings were engaged in the mental attention of recollecting the <s>Buddha</s>. These are the ten portents that appeared for the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great being. //

body.text: apare daśa mahāvabhāsāḥ prādurabhavan samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya darśanapūrvanimittam / katame daśa? yaduta sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsu ekaikasmin paramāṇurajasi sarvatathāgatajālāni vidyotayanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvabuddhaprabhāmaṇḍalameghā niścarya anekavarṇā nānāvarṇā anekaśatasahasravarṇāḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvaratnameghāḥ sarvatathāgatapratibhāsavijñapanānniścaritvā sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvatathāgatārciścakramaṇḍalameghā niścaritvā sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvagandhapuṣpamālyavilepanadhūpameghā niścaritvā samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya sarvaguṇadharmasamudrameghānnigarjamāṇā daśadiksarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvacandrasūryajyotirmeghā niścaritvā samantabhadrabodhisattvaprabhāṃ pramuñcamānāḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvasattvakāyasaṃsthānapradīpameghā niścaritvā buddharaśmivatprabhāsamānāḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvatathāgatakāyapratibhāsamaṇiratnavigrahameghā niścaritvā daśasu dikṣu sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvatathāgatakāyasaṃsthānaraśmivigrahameghā niścaritvā sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānapraṇidhānameghānabhipravarṣamāṇāḥ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajobhya ekaikasmātparamāṇurajasaḥ sarvarūpagatavarṇāvabhāsā bodhisattvakāyapratibhāsameghasamudrāḥ sarvasattvanirmāṇakāryaprayogāḥ sarvasattvasarvābhiprāyaparipūriniṣpādanā niścaritvā sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharanti sma / ime daśa mahāvabhāsāḥ prādurabhūvan samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya darśanapūrvanimittam //
body.translated_text: Moreover, ten great illuminations appeared as portents heralding the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great being. What are the ten? Namely, in the atoms of all world-realms, in each single atom, the nets of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s shone forth. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of radiance-circles of all <s>Buddha</s>s issued forth — of many colors, of diverse colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors — and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of all jewels issued forth as manifestations of the reflected images of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of radiant flame-wheel-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of all fragrances, flowers, garlands, unguents, and incense issued forth, thundering with clouds of the oceans of all quality-<s>dharma</s>s of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, and pervaded the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in all ten directions. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of all moon, sun, and stellar lights issued forth, releasing the radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of lamps in the form of the bodies of all beings issued forth, blazing with radiance like <s>Buddha</s>-rays, and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of jewel-gem bodies reflecting the body-images of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> in the ten directions. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, clouds of ray-bodies in the form of the bodies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth, raining down clouds of empowerment and vows of all <s>Buddha</s>s, and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. From the atoms of all world-realms, from each single atom, illuminations of color and form of all kinds, ocean-clouds of reflected images of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-bodies, engaged in the task of creating emanations for all beings, accomplishing and fulfilling all wishes and intentions of all beings, issued forth and pervaded the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. These are the ten great illuminations that appeared as portents heralding the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidāraka imān daśa pūrvanimittāvabhāsān dṛṣṭvā samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya darśanāvakāśapratilabdhaḥ svakuśalamūlabalopastabdhaḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasarvabuddhadharmāvabhāsasaṃjātaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvapraṇidhānāviṣṭaḥ sarvatathāgatagocarābhimukhaḥ udārabodhisattvagocaraniścayabalādhānaprāptaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvadarśanasarvajñatāprabhālābhasaṃjñī samantabhadrabodhisattvadarśanābhimukhendriyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, having seen these ten portent-illuminations, having attained the opportunity for the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, supported by the power of his own roots of wholesome merit, having arisen through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the illumination of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, penetrated by the vows of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, facing the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having attained the sustaining power of certainty in the exalted <s>Bodhisattva</s>-domain, perceiving the attainment of the radiance of omniscience through seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, with faculties directed toward the vision of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>,

body.text:
samantabhadrabodhisattvadarśanamahāvīryavegaprāptaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvaparigaveṣamāṇāvivartyavīryaprayogaḥ sarvadigabhimukhenendriyacakreṇa samantabhadracakṣurviṣayāvakramaṇena bodhisattvaśarīreṇa sarvatathāgatārambaṇasaṃpreṣitena anavaśeṣabuddhapādamūlagatasamantabhadrabodhisattvānubaddhena cittena samantabhadrabodhisattvārambaṇaparigaveṣaṇāvipravasitenāśayena sarvārambaṇeṣu samantabhadrabodhisattvadarśanasaṃjñāgatagarbhaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvapathaprasṛtena jñānacakṣuṣā ākāśadhātuvipulenāśayena mahākaruṇāvajrasusaṃgṛhītenādhyāśayena aparāntakoṭīgatakalpādhiṣṭhānena samantabhadrabodhisattvānubandhanapraṇidhānena samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāsamatānugatayā kramavikramaviśuddhyā sarvatathāgataviṣayasaṃvasanena samantabhadrabodhisattvabhūmipratiṣṭhānajñānavihāreṇa samanvāgato 'drākṣīt samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvaṃ bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya purato mahāratnapadmagarbhe siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasamudragataṃ bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaṃ bodhisattvasaṃghapuraskṛtaṃ sarvaparṣamaṇḍalānusṛtābhyudgatakāyaṃ sarvalokānabhibhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvānuvyavalokitamaparyantajñānaviṣayamasaṃhāryagocaramacintyaviṣayaṃ tryadhvasamatānugataṃ sarvatathāgatasamatānuprāptam / sa tasya sarvaromavivarebhyaḥ ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamān raśmimeghānniścaritvā dharmadhātuparamākāśadhātuparyavasānān sarvalokadhātūnavabhāsya sattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ praśamayamānānapaśyat / sa tasya kāyāt sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān prabhāmaṇḍalameghānniścaritvā nānāvarṇān sarvabodhisattvānudāraprītiprāmodyavegān vivardhayamānānapaśyat / mūrdhatoṃ 'sakūṭābhyāṃ sarvaromavivarebhyaśca nānāvarṇān gandhārcimeghānniścārya sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni spharitvā abhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvapuṣpameghānniścārya sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni spharitvā abhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvagandhavṛkṣameghānniścārya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ gandhavṛkṣameghālaṃkārāṃlaṃkṛtaṃ kṛtvā akṣayagandhacūrṇavilepanakośaprayuktān sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni spharitvā abhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvavastrameghānniścārya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ saṃchādya alaṃkurvāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvapaṭṭadāmameghān sarvabhāraṇameghān sarvamuktāhārameghāṃścintāmaṇiratnameghānniścārya
sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni spharitvā abhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat sarvasattvānāṃ sarvābhiprāyapariniṣpattaye / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān ratnadrumameghānniścārya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā visphuṭaratnadrumameghālaṃkārālaṃkṛtaṃ kṛtvā sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalāni mahāratnavarṣairabhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān rūpadhātudevanikāyameghānniścārya bodhisattvaṃ saṃvarṇayataḥ sarvalokadhātuṃ spharamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvabrahmagatiparyāpannadevanikāyanirmitameghānniścārya abhisaṃbuddhān
body.translated_text: Having attained the great surge of vigor for the vision of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, exerting irreversible vigor in searching for <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the wheel of his faculties facing all directions, with a <s>bodhisattva</s>-body entering the domain of <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s vision, with a mind dispatched toward all <s>Tathāgata</s>s as its object and following <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has gone to the feet of all <s>Buddha</s>s without remainder, with an intention that never departed from the search for <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> as its object, with a womb containing the perception of seeing <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> in all objects, with the eye of knowledge proceeding on the path of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an intention vast as the expanse of space, with a deep intention well-gathered by the <s>vajra</s> of great compassion, with an empowerment of <s>kalpa</s>s extending to the furthest limit and a vow of following <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the purity of steps and strides following the equality of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conduct, dwelling in the experience of the domain of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and in the knowledge of being established on the stage of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> — thus endowed, he beheld <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated on a lion-throne within a great jewel-lotus womb before the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one — having entered the ocean of the assembly-circles of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, surrounded by a multitude of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, attended by the community of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, with a body risen above all the assembly-circles, unconquered by all the worlds, looked upon by all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, of unlimited domain of knowledge, of indestructible range, of inconceivable domain, following the equality of the three times, having attained the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He saw from every pore of his body, from each and every pore, clouds of rays equal to the atoms of all world-realms issuing forth, extending to the limit of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and the expanse of space, illuminating all world-realms and pacifying the suffering of beings. He saw from his body clouds of radiance-circles equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, of various colors, increasing the surges of noble joy and delight of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s. He saw from his crown, from his two summit-protuberances, and from all his pores, clouds of fragrance-flames of various colors issuing forth, pervading all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, raining down upon them. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of all flowers equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, raining down upon them. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of all fragrant trees equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading and adorning the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space with the ornament of fragrant tree-clouds, furnished with inexhaustible repositories of fragrant powders and unguents, pervading all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, raining down upon them. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of all garments issuing forth, covering and adorning the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of silk banners, clouds of all ornaments, clouds of pearl-necklaces, and clouds of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gem-jewels equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, raining down for the fulfillment of all the wishes of all beings. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of jewel-trees equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, adorning it with the ornament of blossoming jewel-tree clouds, raining great jewel-rains upon all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of hosts of gods of the form-realm equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, praising the <s>bodhisattva</s> and pervading all world-realms. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of emanated hosts of gods belonging to the <s>Brahma</s>-destinies issuing forth, requesting the fully awakened

tathāgatān dharmacakrapravartanāyādhyeṣamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvakāmadhātudevendrakāyameghānniścarya sarvatathāgatadharmacakrāṇi saṃpratīcchamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān tryadhvaparyāpannasarvabuddhakṣetrameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā alayanānāmatrāṇānāmapratiśaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ layanatrāṇapratiśaraṇabhūtānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt praticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvabuddhotpādabodhisattvaparṣanmaḍalaparipūrṇapariśuddhakṣetrameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā udārādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ viśuddhaye vartamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātpraticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān viśuddhasaṃkliṣṭakṣetrameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā saṃkliṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ viśuddhaye saṃvartamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātpraticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān saṃkliṣṭacittaviśuddhakṣetrameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā ekāntasaṃkliṣṭānāṃ viśuddhaye saṃvartamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātpraticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvabodhisattvakāyameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā sarvasattvacaryāmanuvartamānānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sarvasattvānāṃ paripācayamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātpraticittakṣaṇaṃ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamān bodhisattvakāyameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā sarvasattvakuśalamūlavivardhanatāyai sarvabuddhanāmānyudīrayamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān bodhisattvakāyameghānniścarya ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadharmadhātuṃ spharitvā sarvabuddhakṣetraprasareṣu prathamacittotpādamupādāya sarvabodhisattvānāṃ sarvakuśalamūlābhinirhāramupasaṃharamāṇānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān bodhisattvameghānniścaritvā
sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ekaikasmin buddhakṣetre samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāviśuddhaye sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānasāgarānabhidyotayamānānapaśyat / sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarāt sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvasattvābhiprāyaparipūraṇān sarvajñatāsamudāgamaprītivegavivardhanān samantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāmeghānniścarya abhipravarṣamāṇānapaśyat / sa tasya sarvaromavivarebhya ekaikasmādromavivarātsarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān sarvabuddhakṣetrābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanān sarvajñatāsamudāgamamahādharmavegavivardhanānabhisaṃbodhimeghānniścaramāṇānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: <s>Tathāgata</s>s to turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma). He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of the bodies of <s>Indra</s>s of the desire-realm issuing forth, receiving the <s>Dharmacakra</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields encompassed by the three times equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, becoming a resting-place, a protection, and a refuge for beings who are without rest, without protection, and without refuge. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of pure fields filled with assemblies of <s>bodhisattva</s>s and arisings of all <s>Buddha</s>s equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, operating for the purification of beings of noble inclination. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of fields both pure and defiled equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, operating for the purification of defiled beings. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of fields with defiled minds yet pure equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, operating for the purification of beings who are utterly defiled. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of bodies of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, following the conduct of all beings, ripening all beings toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, at each mind-moment, clouds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies equal to the atoms of all world-realms issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, uttering the names of all <s>Buddha</s>s for the increase of all the roots of wholesome merit of all beings. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-bodies equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth, pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> extending to the limit of the expanse of space, illuminating in each and every <s>Buddha</s>-field all the oceans of the vows of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s for the purification of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth and raining down — fulfilling the wishes of all beings, increasing the surges of joy in the attainment of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. He saw from every pore, from each and every pore, clouds of awakening equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields issuing forth — displaying the full awakening in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, increasing the great momentum of <s>dharma</s> in the attainment of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya idamṛddhiviṣayavikurvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaḥ tuṣṭaḥ udagraḥ āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhūyasyā mātrayā samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya kāyamupanidhyāyan adrākṣīt samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya ekaikasmādaṅgādekaikāṅgavibhaktitaḥ ekaikasmāccharīrāvayavāt ekaikasyāḥ śarīrāvayavavibhakteḥ ekaikasmādaṅgapradeśāt
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, having seen this miraculous display of the domain of power of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was delighted, satisfied, elated, joyful, rejoicing, filled with happiness and gladness. With even greater intensity, contemplating the body of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he beheld from each limb of <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from each division of each limb, from each member of the body, from each division of each member, from each part of each limb,
