ekaikato 'ṅgapradeśavibhaktitaḥ ekaikasmāddehāt ekaikasmāddehavibhaktitaḥ ekaikasmādromavivarāt ekaikasmādromavibhakterimaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ savāyuskandhaṃ sapṛthivīskandhaṃ satejaḥskandhaṃ sasāgaraṃ sadvīpaṃ sanadīkaṃ saratnaparvataṃ sasumeruṃ sacakravālaṃ sagrāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhāniṃ savanaṃ sabhavanaṃ sajanakāyaṃ sanarakalokaṃ satiryagyonilokaṃ sayamalokaṃ sāsuralokaṃ sanāgalokaṃ sagaruḍalokaṃ samanujalokaṃ sadevalokaṃ sabrahmalokaṃ sakāmadhātuviṣayaṃ sārūpyadhātuviṣayaṃ sādhiṣṭhānaṃ sapratiṣṭhānaṃ sasaṃsthānaṃ sameghaṃ savidyutaṃ sajyotiṣaṃ sarātriṃdivasārdhamāsaṃ samāsartuṃ sasaṃvatsaraṃ sāntarakalpaṃ sakalpam / yathā cemaṃ lokadhātum, evaṃ pūrvasyāṃ diśi sarvalokadhātūnadrākṣīt / yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi, evaṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarasyāmuttarapūrvāyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ paścimottarāyāmadhaḥ ūrdhvaṃ samantātsarvadigvidikṣu sarvalokadhātūnadrākṣīt pratibhāsayogena sarvabuddhotpādān sabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalān sasattvān, yāśceha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau pūrvāntakoṭīgatāḥ sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāḥ tā api sarvāḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya ekasmānmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇādadrākṣīt sarvabuddhotpādāḥ sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāḥ sasattvāḥ sabhavanāḥ sarātriṃdivāḥ sakalpāḥ / evamaparāntakoṭīgatānapi sarvabuddhakṣetraprasarānadrākṣīt / yathā ceha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau pūrvāntāparāntakoṭīgatāḥ sarvalokadhātuparaṃparā adrākṣīt, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu pūrvāntāparāntakoṭīgatāḥ sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya kāyādekaikasmānmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇādekaikasmādromavivarādadrākṣīt suvibhaktā anyonyāsaṃbhinnāḥ / yathā ca samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvaṃ bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya purato mahāratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇamadrākṣīt etadvikrīḍitaṃ saṃdarśayamānam, evaṃ pūrvasyāṃ diśi bhagavato bhadraśriyastathāgatasya padmaśriyāṃ lokadhātāvetadeva vikrīḍitaṃ saṃdarśayamānamadrākṣīt / yathā ca pūrvasyāṃ diśi, evaṃ samantātsarvadigvidikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇametadeva
vikrīḍitaṃ saṃdarśayamānamadrākṣīt / yathā ca daśasu dikṣu, evaṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu tathāgatapādamūleṣu mahāratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇametadeva vikrīḍitaṃ saṃdarśayamānamadrākṣīt / evaṃ samantāddaśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu ekaikasmin paramāṇurajasi dharmadhātuvipuleṣu buddhadharmaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvamadrākṣīt / ekaikataśca asyātmabhāvātryadhvaprāptāni sarvārambaṇāni abhivijñapyamānāni apaśyatpratibhāsayogena, sarvakṣetrāṇyapi sarvasattvānapi sarvabuddhotpādānapi sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalānyabhivijñapyamānānapaśyat pratibhāsayogena / sarvasattvarutāni ca sarvabuddhāghoṣāṃśca sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravartanāni ca sarvānuśāsanyādeśanaprātihāryāṇi ca sarvabodhisattvasamudāgamāṃśca sarvabuddhavikrīḍitāni cāśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: from each and every division of limb and body-part, from each body, from each division of the body, from each pore-opening, from each division of the hair-pores — he saw this three-thousand-fold great thousand world-realm, with its mass of wind, mass of earth, mass of fire, with its oceans, continents, rivers, gem-mountains, <s>Sumeru</s>s, <s>Cakravāla</s>s, with its villages, cities, towns, provinces, and royal capitals, with its forests, dwellings, and masses of beings, with its hell-worlds, animal-worlds, <s>Yama</s>-worlds, <s>Asura</s>-worlds, <s>Nāga</s>-worlds, <s>Garuḍa</s>-worlds, human worlds, divine worlds, <s>Brahmā</s>-worlds, with the domain of the desire-realm, with the domain of the formless-realm, with its foundations, supports, and configurations, with its clouds, lightning, and luminaries, with its nights, days, and half-months, with its months, seasons, and years, with its intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s and <s>kalpa</s>s. And just as he saw this world-realm, so he saw all world-realms in the eastern direction. And just as in the eastern direction, so in the south, west, north, northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest, below, above — in all directions and intermediate directions everywhere, he saw all world-realms through the yoga of reflection — all arisings of <s>Buddha</s>s with their <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly-maṇḍalas and beings. And whatever successions of all world-realms in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm extending to the furthest limit of the past — all those too he saw from a single great-man mark of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, all arisings of <s>Buddha</s>s, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly-maṇḍalas, with beings, with dwellings, with nights and days, with <s>kalpa</s>s. Likewise he saw all extents of <s>Buddha</s>-fields extending to the furthest limit of the future. And just as he saw in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm all successions of world-realms extending to the furthest limit of the past and future, so too in all world-realms in the ten directions — all successions of world-realms extending to the furthest limit of the past and future — he saw them from the body of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, from each great-man mark, from each pore-opening, well-distinguished and mutually unconfused. And just as he saw <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> seated on the great gem-lotus-womb lion-throne before the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, displaying this sport — so in the eastern direction, before the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhadraśrī</s> in the world-realm <s>Padmaśrī</s>, he saw him displaying this very same sport. And just as in the eastern direction, so everywhere in all directions and intermediate directions, in all world-realms, at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he saw <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> seated on a great gem-lotus-womb lion-throne, displaying this very same sport. And just as in the ten directions, so in all world-realms, at the feet of <s>Tathāgata</s>s, seated on a great gem-lotus-womb lion-throne, displaying this very same sport he saw him. Thus everywhere in all directions and intermediate directions, in all world-realms contained within the atoms of all world-realms too, in all world-realms at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he saw <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>. And from each body of his, he saw all objects of the three times being made known through the yoga of reflection — all fields, all beings, all arisings of <s>Buddha</s>s, all <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly-maṇḍalas being made known through the yoga of reflection. And he heard all the sounds of all beings, all <s>Buddha</s>-voices, all turnings of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, all miracles of admonition and instruction, all accomplishments of all <s>bodhisattva</s>s, and all sports of all <s>Buddha</s>s. //

body.text: sa tadacintyaṃ samantabhadramahābodhisattvavikrīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca daśa jñānapāramitāvihārān pratyalabhata / katamān daśa? yaduta ekacittakṣaṇe sarvabuddhakṣetrakāyaspharaṇajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvatathāgatapādamūlopasaṃkramaṇāsaṃbhinnajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata /
body.translated_text: Having seen and heard that inconceivable sport of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, he attained ten abodes of the perfection of knowledge. What are the ten? Namely: he attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-fields with his body in a single mind-moment. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of approaching the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s without interruption.

body.text:
sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvatathāgatebhya ekaikasmāttathāgatātsarvabuddhadharmapraśnaparipṛcchāsaṃpratīcchanajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvatathāgatadharmacakrapravartananidhyaptijñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / acintyabuddhavikurvitajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvadharmākṣayapratisaṃvidaparāntakoṭīgatakalpādhiṣṭhānaikadharmapadanirdeśajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvadharmamudrāpratyakṣajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvadharmadhātunayasāgarajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / sarvasattvasaṃjñāgatasaṃvasanajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / ekakṣaṇasamantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpratyakṣajñānapāramitāvihāraṃ pratyalabhata / tasyaivaṃ jñānapāramitāvihārasamanvāgatasya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya samantabhadrao bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / samanantarapratiṣṭhāpitaśca sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya samantabhadreṇa bodhisattvena mūrdhni pāṇiḥ, atha tāvadevāsya sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni samādhimukhānyavakrāntāni / ekaikena ca samādhinā sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃllokadhātumudrānavatīrṇo 'bhūt / adṛṣṭapūrvā sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāścāsya sarvajñatāsaṃbhārā upacayamagaman / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāścāsya sarvajñatādharmasaṃbhavāḥ prādurabhavan / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiśca sarvajñatāmahāprasthānairamyutthitaḥ / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca praṇidhānasāgarānavatīrṇaḥ / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiśca sarvajñatāniryāṇapathairniryātaḥ / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāsu ca bodhisattvacaryāsu prasṛtaḥ / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiśca sarvajñatāvegairvivardhitaḥ / sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiśca sarvabuddhajñānāvabhāsaiḥ prabhāvabhāsitaḥ / yathā ceha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau bhagavato vairocanasya pādamūlagataḥ samantabhadro bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya sudhanasya murdhni pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa, tathā sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu niṣaṇṇaḥ samantabhadro bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / evaṃ samantāt sarvadigvidikṣu sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajontargateṣvapi sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatapādamūleṣu niṣaṇṇaḥ samantabhadro bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / yathā bhagavato vairocanasya pādamūlagatena samantabhadreṇa bodhisattvena pāṇinā spṛṣṭasya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya
dharmamukhānyavakrāntāni, evaṃ sarvasamantabhadrātmabhāvaprasṛtaiḥ pāṇimeghaiḥ spṛṣṭasya sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya dharmamukhānyavakrāntānyabhūvan nānānayaiḥ //
body.translated_text: He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of worshipping and attending all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of asking questions about all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s and receiving answers from each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of contemplating the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-transformation. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of teaching a single <s>dharma</s>-word through the foundation of <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the furthest limit of the inexhaustible analytical knowledge of all <s>dharma</s>s. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of directly perceiving the seal of all <s>dharma</s>s. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of the ocean of the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> of all <s>dharma</s>s. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of dwelling together with all beings in accordance with their perceptions. He attained the abode of the perfection of knowledge of directly perceiving the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> in a single moment. Then, for <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, endowed with these abodes of the perfection of knowledge, <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> extended his right hand and placed it on his head. As soon as the hand of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> was placed on the head of <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, <s>samādhi</s>-gates equal in number to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields were entered by him. And through each <s>samādhi</s> he descended into the seals of world-realms equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And provisions for omniscience equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, never seen before, accumulated for him. And arisings of <s>dharma</s>s of omniscience equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared for him. And he was roused by great settings-forth toward omniscience equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he descended into oceans of vows equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he went forth on paths of the departure for omniscience equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he was extended in <s>bodhisattva</s>-conducts equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he was increased by surges of omniscience equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he was illuminated by illuminations of the knowledge of all <s>Buddha</s>s equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And just as here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, seated at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, extended his right hand and placed it on the head of <s>Sudhana</s> — so too in all world-realms, at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> seated there extended his right hand and placed it on the head of <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son. Likewise everywhere in all directions and intermediate directions, in all world-realms contained within the atoms of all world-realms too, at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> seated there extended his right hand and placed it on the head of <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son. And just as <s>dharma</s>-gates were entered by <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, when touched by the hand of <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s> at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s> — so too <s>dharma</s>-gates were entered by <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, when touched by the clouds of hands extended from all the bodies of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, through various methods. //

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sudhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat - dṛṣṭaṃ te kulaputra mama vikurvitam? āha - dṛṣṭamārya / api tu tathāgataḥ prajānan prajānīyāttāvadacintyamidaṃ vikurvitam / so 'vocat - ahaṃ kulaputra anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān vicaritaḥ sarvajñatācittamabhilaṣamāṇaḥ / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā ārāgitā bodhicittaṃ pariśodhayatā / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe sarvatyāgasamāyuktāḥ sarvalokavighuṣṭā mahāyajñā yaṣṭāḥ / sarvasattvapratipādanā sarvajñatāpuṇyasaṃbhāratā / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstyāgā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Samantabhadra Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, spoke to <s>Sudhana</s>, the merchant's son, thus: 'Have you seen, son of good family, my transformation?' He replied: 'I have seen it, Noble One. But only the <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing with his knowledge, could [fully] know how inconceivable this transformation is.' He said: 'I, son of good family, have wandered for <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, aspiring to the mind of omniscience. And in each great <s>kalpa</s>, I have honored <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields while purifying <s>bodhicitta</s>. And in each great <s>kalpa</s>, I have performed great sacrifices renowned throughout the entire world, endowed with the relinquishment of everything — the provision of merit for omniscience through providing for all beings. And in each great <s>kalpa</s>, relinquishments equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields,

body.text: mahātyāgāḥ kṛtāḥ, atyarthatyāgāḥ kṛtāḥ sarvajñatādharmānabhiprārthayatā / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyānatmabhāvāḥ parityaktāḥ, mahārājyāni ca parityaktāni, grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānyaḥ parityaktāḥ, priyamanāpā dustyajāḥ parivārasaṃghāḥ parityaktāḥ, putraduhitṛbhāryāḥ parityaktāḥ / svaśarīramāṃsāni parityaktāni, svakāyebhyo rudhiraṃ yācanakebhyaḥ parityaktam, asthimajjāḥ parityaktāḥ / aṅgapratyaṅgāni parityaktāni / karṇanāsāḥ parityaktāḥ / cakṣūṃṣi parityaktāni / svamukhebhyo jihvendriyāṇi parityaktāni buddhajñānāvekṣayā kāyajīvitanirapekṣeṇa / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni svaśirāṃsi parityaktāni svakāyebhyaḥ sarvalokābhyudgatamanuttarasarvajñatāśīrṣamabhiprārthayatā / yathā ca ekaikasmin mahākalpe, tathā anabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu mahākalpasāgareṣu / ekaikasmiṃśca mahākalpe 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatāḥ parameśvarabhūtena satkṛtā gurukṛtā mānitāḥ pūjitāḥ, cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ pratipāditāḥ / teṣāṃ ca asmiṃstathāgatānāṃ śāsane pravrajitā sarvabuddhānuśāsanīṣu pratipannaḥ śāsanaṃ ca me teṣāṃ saṃdhāritam //
body.translated_text: great relinquishments were made — surpassing relinquishments were made by one aspiring to the <s>dharma</s>s of omniscience. In each great <s>kalpa</s>, inexpressible-inexpressible bodies were abandoned, great kingdoms were abandoned, villages, cities, towns, provinces, kingdoms, and royal capitals were abandoned, dear and beloved retinues difficult to relinquish were abandoned, sons, daughters, and wives were abandoned. The flesh of one's own body was abandoned, blood from one's own body was abandoned to supplicants, bones and marrow were abandoned. Limbs and minor limbs were abandoned. Ears and nose were abandoned. Eyes were abandoned. Tongues were abandoned from one's own mouths — with the vision of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, heedless of body and life. And in each great <s>kalpa</s>, one's own heads, equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, were abandoned from one's own bodies — aspiring to the unsurpassed summit of omniscience that surpasses all worlds. And just as in each great <s>kalpa</s>, so in great oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And in each great <s>kalpa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressible-inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields were honored, venerated, respected, and worshipped as one who was the supreme lord — provided with robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicine and requisites for the sick. And I went forth in the teachings of those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, practiced all <s>Buddha</s>-instructions, and upheld their teachings. //

body.text: nābhijānāmi kulaputra tāvadbhiḥ kalpasamudrerekacittotpādamapi tathāgaśāsane vilopamutpādayituṃ nābhijānāmi / tāvadbhiḥ kalpasamudrairekacittotpādamapi pratighasahagatamutpādayitumātmagrahacittaṃ vā ātmagrahaparigrahacittaṃ vā ātmaparanānātvacittaṃ vā bodhimārgavipravāsacittaṃ vā saṃsārasaṃvāsaparikhedacittaṃ vā avalīnacittaṃ vā āvaraṇasaṃmohacittaṃ vā utpādayitumanyatra aparājitajñānaduryodhanagarbhabodhicittāt sarvajñatāsaṃbhāreṣu / iti hi kulaputra sarvakalpasāgarāḥ kṣayaṃ vrajeyuḥ tānnirdiśato ye mama pūrvayogasaṃbuddhakṣetrapariśuddhiprayogāḥ, ye mama mahākaruṇāpratilabdhacittasya sarvaparitrāṇaparipācanapariśodhanaprayogāḥ / evaṃ ye buddhapūjopasthānaprayogāḥ, ye saddharmaparyeṣṭihetorguruśuśrūṣāprayogāḥ, ye saddharmaparigrahahetorātmabhāvaparityāgaprayogāḥ, ye saddharmārakṣaṇanidānāḥ svajīvitaparityāgaprayogāḥ, tāvadbhyo me kulaputra dharmasamudrebhyo na kiṃcidekapadavyañjanamapi yanna cakravartirājyaparityāgena krītam, yannāsti sarvāstiparityāgena krītaṃ sarvasattvaparitrāṇaprayuktena svasaṃtaticittanidhyaptiprayuktena abhimukhaparadharmasaṃprāpaṇaprayuktena sarvalaukikajñānālokaprabhāvanāprayuktena sarvalokottarajñānaprabhāvanāprayuktena sarvasattvasaṃsārasukhasaṃjananaprayuktena sarvatathāgataguṇasaṃvarṇanaguṇaprayuktena / evamanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ kalpasāgarāḥ kṣayaṃ vrajeyurmama svapūrvayogasaṃpadaṃ nirdiśataḥ //
body.translated_text: I do not recall, son of good family, in so many oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, generating even a single arising of mind that would constitute a violation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching. I do not recall generating in so many oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s even a single arising of mind accompanied by hostility, or a mind grasping at self, or a mind clinging to the possession of self-grasping, or a mind conceiving the difference between self and other, or a mind estranged from the path of awakening, or a mind wearied by dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s>, or a mind of timidity, or a mind deluded by obstructions — except for the <s>bodhicitta</s> that is the womb of unconquerable knowledge and invincible warriors, directed toward the provisions of omniscience. Indeed, son of good family, all oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s would come to exhaustion while describing my former practices of purifying <s>Buddha</s>-fields through the union of former yoga, my practices of complete protection, maturation, and purification of all beings with a mind attained through great compassion. Likewise the practices of worshipping and attending upon the <s>Buddha</s>s, the practices of serving teachers for the sake of seeking the true <s>Dharma</s>, the practices of relinquishing one's own being for the sake of upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>, the practices of giving up one's own life for the purpose of protecting the true <s>Dharma</s> — from so many oceans of <s>Dharma</s> of mine, son of good family, there is not even a single word or syllable that was not purchased by the relinquishment of universal sovereignty, that was not purchased by the relinquishment of all possessions — while being engaged in the protection of all beings, while being engaged in the contemplation of one's own mind-stream, while being engaged in directly bringing others to the <s>Dharma</s>, while being engaged in manifesting the light of all worldly knowledge, while being engaged in manifesting all supramundane knowledge, while being engaged in generating happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> for all beings, while being engaged in the quality of praising the qualities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Thus, oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields would come to exhaustion while describing the attainment of my own former practice.

body.text: tena mayā kulaputra anena evaṃrūpeṇa saṃbhārabalena mūlahetūpacayabalena udārādhimuktibalena guṇapratipattibalena sarvadharmayathāvannidhyaptibalena prajñācakṣurbalena tathāgatādhiṣṭhānabalena mahāpraṇidhānabalena mahākaruṇābalena supariśodhitābhijñābalena kalyāṇamitraparigrahabalena atyantapariśuddho dharmakāyaḥ pratilabdhaḥ sarvatryadhvāsaṃbhinnaḥ / anuttaraśca rūpakāyaḥ pariśodhitaḥ
body.translated_text: By me, son of good family, through the power of such provisions, through the power of accumulating root causes, through the power of noble aspiration, through the power of the practice of qualities, through the power of contemplating all <s>dharma</s>s as they truly are, through the power of the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment, through the power of great vows, through the power of great compassion, through the power of well-purified <s>abhijñā</s>s (superknowledges), through the power of reliance on spiritual friends — the utterly purified <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) has been attained, undifferentiated throughout the three times. And the unsurpassed <s>rūpakāya</s> (form-body) has been purified

body.text:
sarvalokābhudgataḥ sarvajagadyathāśayavijñapanaḥ sarvatrānugataḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraprasṛtaḥ samantapratiṣṭhānaḥ sarvataḥ sarvavikurvitasaṃdarśanaḥ sarvajagadabhilakṣaṇīyaḥ / prekṣasva kulaputra imāmātmabhāvapratilābhasaṃpadamanantakalpasāgarasaṃbhūtāṃ bahukalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasradurlabhaprādurbhāvāṃ durlabhasaṃdarśanām / nāhaṃ kulaputra anavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ śravaṇapathamapyāgacchāmi prāgeva darśanam / santi kulaputra sattvāḥ, ye mama nāmadheyaśravaṇamātreṇa avaivartikā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / santi darśanamātreṇa, santi sparśanamātreṇa, santyanuvrajanamātreṇa, santyanubandhanamātreṇa, santi svapnadarśanena, santi svapne nāmadheyaśravaṇena avaivartikā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / kecitsattvā māmekarātriṃdivasamanusmaramāṇāḥ paripākaṃ gacchanti / kecidardhamāsaṃ kecinmāsaṃ kecidvarṣaṃ kecidvarṣaśataṃ kecitkalpaṃ kecitkalpaśataṃ kecidyāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān māmanusmaramāṇāḥ paripākaṃ gacchanti / kecidekajātyā paripākaṃ gacchanti māmanusmaramāṇāḥ / kecijjātiśatena, kecidyāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairjātiparivartaiḥ / kecitsattvā mama prabhādarśanena paripākaṃ gacchanti / kecidraśmipramokṣasaṃdarśanena, kecitkṣetraprakampanena, kecidrūpakāyasaṃdarśanena, kecitsaṃpraharṣaṇena paripākaṃ gacchanti / iti hi kulaputra buddhākṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairupāyaiḥ sattvā avaivartikā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye khalu punaḥ kulaputra sattvā mama buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ śṛṇvanti, te pariśuddheṣu buddhākṣetreṣūpapadyante / ye mamātmabhāvapariśuddhiṃ paśyanti, te mamātmabhāve upapadyante / paśya kulaputra imāṃ mamātmabhāvapariśuddhim
//
body.translated_text: surpassing all worlds, making known to all beings according to their dispositions, pervading everywhere, extending through all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, established universally, displaying all miraculous transformations in every direction, worthy of being beheld by all beings. Behold, son of good family, this attainment of embodiment, arisen through infinite oceans of <s>kalpa</s>s, of rare appearance through many <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>kalpa</s>s, rarely seen. I, son of good family, do not even come within the range of hearing for beings who have not planted roots of merit, much less within the range of sight. There are beings, son of good family, who by merely hearing my name become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in unsurpassed perfect awakening. Some by merely seeing, some by merely touching, some by merely following, some by merely accompanying, some through seeing in a dream, some through hearing my name in a dream become irreversible in unsurpassed perfect awakening. Certain beings, recollecting me for a single day and night, reach maturation. Some for a half-month, some for a month, some for a year, some for a hundred years, some for a <s>kalpa</s>, some for a hundred <s>kalpa</s>s, some for as many <s>kalpa</s>s as atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, recollecting me, reach maturation. Some reach maturation recollecting me through a single birth. Some through a hundred births, some through as many cycles of birth as atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Certain beings reach maturation by seeing my radiance. Some by witnessing the release of rays, some by the trembling of the field, some by seeing my form-body, some through exhortation reach maturation. Thus indeed, son of good family, by means as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, beings become irreversible in unsurpassed perfect awakening. Moreover, son of good family, those beings who hear of the purification of my <s>Buddha</s>-field are reborn in purified <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Those who behold the purification of my embodiment are reborn in my embodiment. Behold, son of good family, this purification of my embodiment.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya kāyamupanidhyāyannadrākṣīt ekaikasmin romavivare 'nabhilāpyabuddhakṣetrasāgarān buddhotpādaparipūrṇān / ekaikasmiṃśca buddhakṣetrasāgare tathāgatān bodhisattvaparṣatsāgaraparivṛtānadrākṣīt / sarvāṃśca tān kṣetrasāgarān nānāpratiṣṭhānān nānāsaṃsthānān nānāvyūhān nānācakravālān nānāmeghagaganasaṃchannān nānābuddhotpādān nānādharmacakranirghoṣānapaśyat / yathā ca ekaikasmin romavivare, tathā anavaśeṣataḥ sarvaromavivareṣu sarvalakṣaṇeṣu sarvānuvyañjaneṣu sarvāṅgapratyaṅgeṣu / ekaikasmiṃśca kṣetrasāgarān sarvabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhakāyanirmitameghānnirgamya daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātūn spharitvā anuttarāyāṃ samyakaṃbodhau sattvān paripācayamānānapaśyat //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, contemplating the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, beheld in each single hair-opening inexpressible oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-fields filled with arisings of <s>Buddha</s>s. And in each ocean of <s>Buddha</s>-fields he beheld <s>Tathāgata</s>s surrounded by oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s> assemblies. And he saw all those oceans of fields with various foundations, various configurations, various arrays, various <s>Cakravāla</s> mountain-ranges, various sky-canopies of clouds, various arisings of <s>Buddha</s>s, and various sounds of the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. And just as in each single hair-opening, so too without remainder in all hair-openings, in all major marks, in all minor characteristics, in all major and minor limbs. And from each ocean of fields, he beheld clouds of <s>Buddha</s>-body emanations, equal to the atoms of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, emerging and pervading all world-realms in the ten directions, maturing beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: atha khalu sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvāvavādānuśāsanyanuśiṣṭaḥ samantabhadrabodhisattvakāyāntargateṣu sarvalokadhātuṣvavatīrya sattvān paripācayāmāsa / ye ca khalu punaḥ sudhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamakalyāṇamitropasaṃkramadarśanaparyupāsanajñānālokakuśalamūlopacayāḥ, te samantabhadrabodhisattvasahadarśanena kuśalamūlopacayasya śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopayānti, sahasratamīmapi śatasahasratamīmapi koṭīśatasahasratamīmapi / saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi upamāmapi upanisāmapi na kṣamante saprathamacittotpādāya yāvatsamantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya darśanam / asminnantare yāvatīrbuddhakṣetrasāgaraparaṃparā avatīrṇastato 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaguṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, instructed and guided by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s admonitions and teachings, descended into all the world-realms contained within the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> and matured beings. Now, the accumulation of roots of merit from the illumination of knowledge through approaching, seeing, and attending upon spiritual friends equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields that <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son had acquired — these, upon seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, did not amount even to a hundredth part of that accumulation of roots of merit, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a <s>koṭī</s>-hundred-thousandth. They were not adequate for any calculation, any fraction, any enumeration, any comparison, or any proportion, from the first arising of the mind up to the seeing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. In this interval, however many successions of oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-fields he had descended into, from those, qualities equal to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields

body.text:
samantabhadrabodhisattvasyaikasmin romavivare buddhakṣetrasāgaraparaṃparāḥ praticittakṣaṇamavataranti sma / yathā caikasmin romavivare, tathaiva sarvaromavivareṣu praticittakṣaṇamanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamalokadhātuṃ pareṇa aparāntakoṭīgatakalpādhiṣṭhānalokadhātuṃ pareṇa vikrameṇa paryantaṃ nopajagāma / kṣetrasāgaraparaṃparāṇāṃ kṣetrasāgaragarbhāṇāṃ kṣetrasāgarasaṃbhedānāṃ kṣetrasāgarasamavasaraṇānāmanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetrasāgarasaṃbhavānāṃ kṣetrasāgaravibhavānāṃ kṣetrasāgaravyūhānāṃ buddhotpādasāgaragarbhāṇāṃ buddhotpādasāgarasamavasaraṇānāṃ buddhotpādasāgarasaṃbhavānāṃ buddhotpādasāgaravibhavānāṃ bodhisattvasāgaraparṣanmaṇḍalasāgarāṇāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasāgaraparaṃparāṇāṃ bodhisattvaparṣamaṇḍalasāgaragarbhāṇāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasāgarasaṃbhedānāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasāgarasamavasaraṇānāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasāgarasaṃbhavānāṃ bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalasāgaravibhavānāṃ sattvadhātupraveśānāṃ sattvendriyapratikṣaṇajñānapraveśānāṃ sattveindriyajñānaprativedhānāṃ sattvaparipākavinayānāṃ gambhīrabodhisattvavikurvitavihārāṇāṃ bodhisattvabhūmyavakramaṇavikramasāgarāṇāṃ paryantaṃ nopajagāma / sa kvacitkṣetre kalpaṃ vicarati sma / sa kvacitkṣetre yāvadanabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān vicarati sma / tataśca kṣetrānna calati sma / cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe ca anantamadhyān kṣetrasāgarānavatarati sma, sattvāṃśca paripācayati sma anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / so 'nupūrveṇa yāvatsamantabhadrabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānasāgarasamatāmanuprāptaḥ sarvatathāgatasamatāṃ sarvakṣetrakāyapāraṇasamatāṃ caryāparipūraṇasamatāmabhisaṃbodhivikurvitasaṃdarśanapāraṇasamatāṃ dharmacakrapravartanasamatāṃ pratisaṃvidviśuddhisamatāṃ ghoṣodāhārasamatāṃ sarvasvarāṅgasāgarasaṃprayogasamatāṃ balavaiśāradyasamatāṃ
buddhavihārasamatāṃ mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāsamatāmacintyabodhisattvavimokṣavikurvitasamatāmanuprāptaḥ iti //
body.translated_text: were entering into a single hair-opening of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> as successions of oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-fields at each moment of mind. And just as in a single hair-opening, so too in all hair-openings, at each moment of mind, world-realms equal to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields — and beyond those, world-realms sustained through <s>kalpa</s>s reaching to the ultimate limit — and beyond those, by further exertion, he reached no end. Of the successions of oceans of fields, of the womb-oceans of fields, of the merging of oceans of fields, of the assemblages of oceans of fields, of those arising from inexpressibly inexpressible oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-field oceans, of the varieties of oceans of fields, of the arrays of oceans of fields, of the womb-oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, of the assemblages of oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, of those arising from oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, of the varieties of oceans of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, of the oceans of maṇḍala-assemblies of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly-oceans, of the successions of oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of the womb-oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of the mergings of oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of the assemblages of oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of those arising from oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of the varieties of oceans of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly maṇḍalas, of entries into the realm of beings, of entries into the knowledge of the faculties of beings at each moment, of penetrations of the knowledge of beings' faculties, of the maturation and discipline of beings, of the profound miraculous transformative abodes of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, of the oceans of exertion in advancing through the stages of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s — he reached no end. In some fields he wandered for a <s>kalpa</s>. In some fields he wandered for as many <s>kalpa</s>s as atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And he did not move from those fields. And at each moment of mind he descended into endless oceans of fields and matured beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening. Gradually he attained the equality of the ocean of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s conduct-vows — the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the equality of traversing all bodies of fields, the equality of fulfilling conduct, the equality of traversing the display of miraculous transformations of complete awakening, the equality of turning the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, the equality of purification of the analytical knowledges, the equality of utterance of sound, the equality of the engagement with the ocean of all vocal expressions, the equality of powers and fearlessnesses, the equality of the <s>Buddha</s>'s meditation, the equality of great loving-kindness and great compassion, the equality of the miraculous transformations of the inconceivable <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberations.

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ evameva lokadhātuparaṃparānabhilāpyānabhilāpyabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān kalpaprasarānabhidyotayamāno bhūyasyā mātrayā gāthābhigītena praṇidhānamakārṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, illuminating in this very manner successions of world-realms through <s>kalpa</s>s and extensions of <s>kalpa</s>s equal to the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>Buddha</s>-fields, to an even greater extent made a vow through verses sung:

children.text: yāvata keci daśaddiśi loke sarvatriyadhvagatā narasiṃhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever lion-among-men there are in the worlds of the ten directions, all those who have gone in the three times,

children.text: tānahu vandami sarvi aśeṣān kāyatu vāca manena prasannaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: To all of them without exception I pay homage, with body, speech, and mind, with a joyful heart. // 1 //
With bodies as numerous as the atoms of all fields, I make prostrations to all the <s>Jina</s>s (Victors),
With a mind directed toward all <s>Jina</s>s, through the power of the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Good Conduct) vow. // 2 //

body.text: ekarajāgri rajopamabuddhā buddhasutāna niṣaṇṇaku madhye /
body.translated_text: Upon a single atom, <s>Buddha</s>s as numerous as atoms, seated in the midst of sons of the <s>Buddha</s>,

body.text: evamaśeṣata dharmatadhātuṃ sarvādhimucyami pūrṇa jinebhiḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus I am convinced that the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is completely filled with <s>Jina</s>s. // 3 //

children.translated_text: And to them, with inexhaustible oceans of praise, with the sounds of oceans of all vocal expressions,

children.text: sarvajināna guṇān bhaṇamānastān sugatān stavamī ahu sarvān // 4 //
children.translated_text: Proclaiming the qualities of all <s>Jina</s>s, I praise all those <s>Sugata</s>s (Well-Gone Ones). // 4 //
With the finest flowers and the finest garlands, with the finest music, ointments, and parasols,

children.text: dīpavarebhi ca dhūpavarebhiḥ pūjana teṣa jināna karomi // 5 //
children.translated_text: With the finest lamps and the finest incense, I make offerings to those <s>Jina</s>s. // 5 //
With the finest garments and the finest fragrances, with packets of powder equal to <s>Meru</s>,
With the finest of all distinguished arrays, I make offerings to those <s>Jina</s>s. // 6 //

children.text: yā ca anuttara pūja udārā tānadhimucyami sarvajinānām /
children.translated_text: And whatever unsurpassed and noble offerings there are, to all the <s>Jina</s>s I resolve upon them;
Through the power of aspiration in the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Good Conduct), I pay homage and make offerings to all the <s>Jina</s>s. // 7 //

children.text: yacca kṛtaṃ mayi pāpu bhaveyyā rāgatu dveṣatu mohavaśena /
children.translated_text: Whatever evil I may have done, through the power of passion, hatred, and delusion,

children.text: kāyatu vāca manena tathaiva taṃ pratideśayamī ahu sarvam // 8 //
children.translated_text: By body, speech, and mind alike — all of that I confess entirely. // 8 //

children.text: yacca daśaddiśi puṇya jagasya śaikṣa aśaikṣapratyekajinānām /
children.translated_text: And whatever merit there is in the ten directions of the world, of learners, non-learners, and solitary <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: buddhasutānatha sarvajinānāṃ taṃ anumodayamī ahu sarvam // 9 //
children.translated_text: And of the sons of the <s>Buddhas</s> and of all the <s>Jinas</s> -- I rejoice in all of it. // 9 //

children.text: ye ca daśaddiśi lokapradīpā bodhivibuddha asaṅgataprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are lamps of the world in the ten directions, who have awakened to <s>Bodhi</s> and attained non-attachment,

children.text: tānahu sarvi adhyeṣami nāthāṃ cakru anuttaru vartanatāyai // 10 //
children.translated_text: All those protectors I entreat to turn the unsurpassed wheel. // 10 //

body.text: ye 'pi ca nirvṛti darśitukāmāstānabhiyācami prāñjalibhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: And those who wish to display <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) -- them I beseech with palms joined:

body.text: kṣetrarajopamakalpa sthihantu sarvajagasya hitāya sukhāya // 11 //
body.translated_text: May they remain for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of the fields, for the benefit and happiness of all beings! // 11 //

children.translated_text: Through worship, offering, and teaching, through rejoicing, entreating, and beseeching,

children.text: yacca śubhaṃ mayi saṃcitu kiṃcidbodhayi nāmayamī ahu sarvam // 12 //
children.translated_text: Whatever small merit has been accumulated by me -- all of it I dedicate to awakening. // 12 //

children.text: pūjita bhontu atītaka buddhā ye ca ghriyanti daśaddiśi loke /
children.translated_text: May the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past be worshipped, and those who abide in the worlds of the ten directions,

children.text: ye ca anāgata te laghu bhontu pūrṇamanoratha bodhivibuddhāḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: And may those of the future swiftly fulfill their aspirations and awaken to <s>Bodhi</s>! // 13 //

children.text: yāvat keci daśaddiśi kṣetrāste pariśuddha bhavantu udārāḥ /
children.translated_text: As many fields as there are in the ten directions, may they all become purified and magnificent,
Filled with <s>Jinas</s> seated beneath the lords of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees and with sons of the <s>Buddhas</s>! // 14 //

children.text: yāvat keci daśaddiśi sattvāste sukhitāḥ sada bhontu arogāḥ /
children.translated_text: As many beings as there are in the ten directions, may they always be happy and free from illness,

children.text: sarvajagasya ca dharmiku artho bhontu pradakṣiṇu ṛdhyatu āśā // 15 //
children.translated_text: May the righteous purpose of all the world be fulfilled, and may their hopes prosper! // 15 //

children.text: bodhicariṃ ca ahaṃ caramāṇo bhavi jātismaru sarvagatīṣu /
children.translated_text: And as I practice the career of awakening, may I remember my past births in all destinies,

children.text: sarvasu janmasu cyutyupapattī pravrajito ahu nityu bhaveyyā // 16 //
children.translated_text: In all births, in death and rebirth, may I always be one who has gone forth as a renunciant! // 16 //
Training in the ways of all the <s>Jinas</s>, fulfilling the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Conduct of the Auspicious),
May I practice the conduct of morality, stainless and pure, always unbroken and unimpaired! // 17 //
In the languages of gods and <s>nāgas</s>, of <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and humans,

children.text: yāni ca sarvarutāni jagasya sarvaruteṣvahu deśayi dharmam // 18 //
children.translated_text: And in whatever languages of all beings there are -- in all languages may I teach the <s>Dharma</s>! // 18 //

body.text: ye khalu pāramitāsvabhiyukto bodhiyi cittu ma jātu vimuhyet /
body.translated_text: May the one who is devoted to the <s>pāramitās</s> never let the mind be confused about awakening,

body.text: ye 'pi ca pāpaka āvaraṇīyāsteṣu parikṣayu bhotu aśeṣam // 19 //
body.translated_text: And may there be complete exhaustion of whatever evil obstructions there are! // 19 //

children.text: karmatu kleśatu mārapathāto lokagatīṣu vimuktu careyam /
children.translated_text: Liberated from <s>karma</s>, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and the path of <s>Māra</s>, may I practice in the destinies of the world,

children.text: padma yathā salilena aliptaḥ sūrya śaśī gaganeva asaktaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: Like a lotus unstained by water, like the sun and moon unattached in the sky! // 20 //

children.text: sarvi apāyadukhāṃ praśamanto sarvajagat sukhi sthāpayamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pacifying all the sufferings of the evil destinies, establishing all beings in happiness,

children.text: sarvajagasya hitāya careyaṃ yāvata kṣetrapathā diśatāsu // 21 //
children.translated_text: May I practice for the benefit of all beings, in as many field-regions as there are in the directions! // 21 //
Conforming to the conduct of beings, fulfilling the career of awakening,

children.text: bhadracariṃ ca prabhāvayamānaḥ sarvi anāgatakalpa careyam // 22 //
children.translated_text: And illuminating the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Conduct of the Auspicious), may I practice through all future <s>kalpas</s>! // 22 //

children.text: ye ca sabhāgata mama caryāye tebhi samāgamu nityu bhaveyyā /
children.translated_text: Those whose conduct is similar to mine, may I always meet with them,

children.text: kāyatu vācatu cetanato vā ekacari praṇidhāna careyam // 23 //
children.translated_text: And in body, speech, and thought may I practice a single conduct and vow! // 23 //

children.text: ye 'pi ca mitrā mama hitakāmā bhadracarīya nidarśayitāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And those friends who desire my benefit, who show the <s>Bhadracarī</s>,

children.text: tebhi samāgamu nityu bhaveyyā tāṃśca ahaṃ na virāgayi jātu // 24 //
children.translated_text: May I always meet with them, and may I never become disenchanted with them! // 24 //

children.text: saṃmukha nityamahaṃ jina paśye buddhasutebhi parīvṛtu nāthān /
children.translated_text: May I always behold the <s>Jinas</s> face to face, the protectors surrounded by sons of the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: teṣu ca pūja kareya udārāṃ sarvi anāgatakalpamakhinnaḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: And may I make magnificent offerings to them, unwearied through all future <s>kalpas</s>! // 25 //
Upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, illuminating the career of awakening,

children.text: bhadracariṃ ca viśodhayamānaḥ sarvi anāgatakalpa careyam // 26 //
children.translated_text: And purifying the <s>Bhadracarī</s>, may I practice through all future <s>kalpas</s>! // 26 //

children.text: sarvabhaveṣu ca saṃsaramāṇaḥ puṇyatu jñānatu akṣayaprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: And wandering through all states of existence, having attained inexhaustibility through merit and knowledge,
Through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), may I become an inexhaustible treasury of all qualities in every existence! // 27 //

children.text: ekarajāgri rajopamakṣetrā tatra ca kṣetri acintiya buddhān /
children.translated_text: In a single atom-tip, fields equal in number to atoms, and in those fields, inconceivable <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: buddhasutāna niṣaṇṇaku madhye paśyiya bodhicariṃ caramāṇaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: Seated amidst sons of the <s>Buddhas</s> -- may I behold them while practicing the career of awakening! // 28 //
Thus in all directions without remainder, in the pathways of even a single hair, <s>Buddhas</s> measured by the three times,
Oceans of <s>Buddhas</s> and oceans of fields -- may I enter and practice through oceans of <s>kalpas</s>! // 29 //
From the ocean-sounds of a single voice's features, the purity of the voice-features of all <s>Jinas</s>,
The tones of all <s>Jinas</s> according to the aspirations of beings -- may I always enter the eloquence of the <s>Buddhas</s>! // 30 //
In those inexhaustible sounds and utterances of all <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times,
As they turn the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>-method, may I enter through the power of wisdom! // 31 //

children.text: ekakṣaṇena anāgata sarvān kalpapraveśa ahaṃ praviśeyam /
children.translated_text: In a single instant, may I enter all future <s>kalpas</s> and their approaches,

children.text: ye 'pi ca kalpa triyadhvapramāṇāstān kṣaṇakoṭipraviṣṭa careyam // 32 //
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>kalpas</s> measured by the three times there are, may I practice having entered them in a koṭi of instants! // 32 //

children.text: ye ca triyadhvagatā narasiṃhāstānahu paśyiya ekakṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: Those lion-among-men gone through the three times -- may I behold them all in a single instant,

children.text: teṣu ca gocarimotari nityaṃ māyagatena vimokṣabalena // 33 //
children.translated_text: And may I always enter their domain through the power of liberation operating like an illusion! // 33 //

body.text: ye ca triyadhvasukṣetraviyūhāstānabhinirhari ekarajāgre /
body.translated_text: Whatever arrays of excellent fields of the three times there are, may I produce them on a single atom-tip,

body.text: evamaśeṣata sarvadiśāsu otari kṣetraviyūha jinānām // 34 //
body.translated_text: And thus in all directions without remainder may I enter the field-arrays of the <s>Jinas</s>! // 34 //

children.text: ye ca ānāgata lokapradīpāsteṣu vibudhyana cakrapravṛttim /
children.translated_text: Those future lamps of the world -- their awakening, their turning of the wheel,

children.text: nirvṛtidarśananiṣṭha praśāntiṃ sarvi ahaṃ upasaṃkrami nāthān // 35 //
children.translated_text: Their displaying the culmination of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) and peace -- may I approach all those protectors! // 35 //
Through the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), universally swift; through the power of knowledge, universally facing;
Through the power of conduct, universally virtuous; through the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), universally pervading; // 36 //
Through the power of merit, universally auspicious; through the power of knowledge, going unobstructed;
Through the powers of <s>prajñā</s>, <s>upāya</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>, may I accumulate the power of <s>Bodhi</s>! // 37 //
Purifying the power of <s>karma</s>, crushing the power of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
Rendering the power of <s>Māra</s> powerless -- may I fulfill all the powers of the <s>Bhadracarī</s>! // 38 //
Purifying oceans of fields, liberating oceans of beings,
Discerning oceans of <s>Dharma</s>, plunging into oceans of knowledge, // 39 //
Purifying oceans of conduct, fulfilling oceans of vows,
Worshipping oceans of <s>Buddhas</s> -- may I practice unwearied through oceans of <s>kalpas</s>! // 40 //
Whatever special vows of the career of awakening there are of the <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times,

children.text: tānahu pūrayi sarvi aśeṣān bhadracarīya vibudhyiya bodhim // 41 //
children.translated_text: May I fulfill them all without remainder, and through the <s>Bhadracarī</s> may I awaken to <s>Bodhi</s>! // 41 //

children.text: jyeṣṭhaku yaḥ sutu sarvajinānāṃ yasya ca nāma samantatabhadraḥ /
children.translated_text: The eldest son of all the <s>Jinas</s>, whose name is <s>Samantabhadra</s>,

children.text: tasya vidusya sabhāgacarīye nāmayamī kuśalaṃ imu sarvam // 42 //
children.translated_text: To the practice equal to that wise one's, I dedicate all this merit. // 42 //
The purity of body, speech, and mind, the purity of conduct, and the purity of fields --

children.text: yādṛśa nāmana bhadra vidusya tādṛśa bhotu samaṃ mama tena // 43 //
children.translated_text: May mine be equal to those of the wise <s>Bhadra</s> (<s>Samantabhadra</s>), in every way the same! // 43 //
For the sake of the universally auspicious <s>Bhadracarī</s>, may I practice the vow of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>,

children.text: sarvi anāgata kalpamakhinnaḥ pūrayi tāṃ kriya sarvi aśeṣām // 44 //
children.translated_text: Unwearied through all future <s>kalpas</s>, may I fulfill all those activities without remainder! // 44 //

children.text: no ca pramāṇu bhaveyya carīye no ca pramāṇu bhaveyya guṇānām /
children.translated_text: May there be no measure to my conduct, may there be no measure to my qualities,

children.text: apramāṇa cariyāya sthihitvā jānami sarvi vikurvitu teṣām // 45 //
children.translated_text: Standing firm in immeasurable conduct, may I know all their miraculous transformations! // 45 //

children.text: yāvata niṣṭha nabhasya bhaveyyā sattva aśeṣata niṣṭha tathaiva /
children.translated_text: As long as space endures, and as long as beings endure without remainder,

children.text: karmatu kleśatu yāvata niṣṭhā tāvataniṣṭha mama praṇidhānam // 46 //
children.translated_text: And as long as <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> endure -- so long may my vow endure without end! // 46 //

children.text: ye ca daśaddiśi kṣetra anantā rathaalaṃkṛtu dadyu jinānām /
children.translated_text: Whoever in the ten directions might adorn fields with jewels and offer them to the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: divya ca mānuṣa saukhyaviśiṣṭāṃ kṣetrarajopama kalpa dadeyam // 47 //
children.translated_text: And might give divine and human happiness supreme for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of the fields, // 47 //
Yet whoever, having heard this king of dedications, should generate faith even once,
Aspiring to the excellent awakening -- that merit would be supreme and most distinguished. // 48 //

children.text: varjita tena bhavanti apāyā varjita tena bhavanti kumitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: By that one, the evil destinies are abandoned; by that one, bad companions are abandoned,

children.text: kṣipru sa paśyati taṃ amitābhaṃ yasyimu bhadracaripraṇidhānam // 49 //
children.translated_text: Swiftly does that one behold <s>Amitābha</s>, the one who holds this vow of the <s>Bhadracarī</s>. // 49 //

children.text: lābha sulabdha sujīvitu teṣāṃ svāgata te imu mānuṣa janma /
children.translated_text: Well-gained is their gain, well-lived their life; welcome is this human birth for them,

children.text: yādṛśa so hi samantatabhadraste 'pi tathā nacireṇa bhavanti // 50 //
children.translated_text: And just as <s>Samantabhadra</s> is, so too they shall swiftly become! // 50 //

children.text: pāpaka pañca anantariyāṇi yena ajñānavaśena kṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Whatever evil deeds of the five heinous acts have been committed through the power of ignorance,

children.text: so imu bhadracariṃ bhaṇamānaḥ kṣipru parikṣayu neti aśeṣam // 51 //
children.translated_text: That one, reciting this <s>Bhadracarī</s>, swiftly brings them to complete exhaustion. // 51 //

children.text: jñānatu rūpatu lakṣaṇataśca varṇatu gotratu bhotirupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with knowledge, form, marks, complexion, and lineage,
Invincible by hosts of heretics and <s>Māra</s>, worshipped in all the three worlds! // 52 //

children.text: kṣipru sa gacchati bodhidrumendraṃ gatva niṣīdati sattvahitāya /
children.translated_text: Swiftly does one go to the lord of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, and having gone, one sits for the benefit of beings,

children.text: budhyati bodhi pravartayi cakraṃ dharṣati māru sasainyaku sarvam // 53 //
children.translated_text: Awakens to <s>Bodhi</s>, turns the wheel, and defeats <s>Māra</s> with all his forces. // 53 //

children.text: yo imu bhadracaripraṇidhānaṃ dhārayi vācayi deśayito vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever upholds, recites, or teaches this vow of the <s>Bhadracarī</s>,

children.text: buddha vijānati yo 'tra vipāko bodhi viśiṣṭa ma kāṅkṣa janetha // 54 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> knows what the result is -- have no doubt about the supreme awakening! // 54 //

children.text: mañjuśirī yatha jānati śūraḥ so ca samantatabhadra tathaiva /
children.translated_text: As the hero <s>Mañjuśrī</s> knows, and as <s>Samantabhadra</s> likewise,

children.text: teṣu ahaṃ anuśikṣayamāṇo nāmayamī kuśalaṃ imu sarvam // 55 //
children.translated_text: Training after them, I dedicate all this merit. // 55 //
By the dedication praised as supreme by all the <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times,

children.text: tāya ahaṃ kuśalaṃ imu sarvaṃ nāmayamī varabhadracarīye // 56 //
children.translated_text: By that I dedicate all this merit to the excellent <s>Bhadracarī</s>. // 56 //

children.text: kālakriyāṃ ca ahaṃ karamāṇo āvaraṇān vinivartiya sarvān /
children.translated_text: And when I am making the time of death, removing all obstructions,

children.text: saṃmukha paśyiya taṃ amitābhaṃ taṃ ca sukhāvatikṣetra vrajeyam // 57 //
children.translated_text: May I behold <s>Amitābha</s> face to face and may I go to the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> field! // 57 //

children.text: tatra gatasya imi praṇidhānā āmukhi sarvi bhaveyyu samagrā /
children.translated_text: Having gone there, may all these vows come together and be fulfilled before me,

children.text: tāṃśca ahaṃ paripūrya aśeṣān sattvahitaṃ kari yāvata loke // 58 //
children.translated_text: And having fulfilled them all without remainder, may I work for the benefit of beings as long as the world endures! // 58 //

children.text: tahi jinamaṇḍali śobhani ramye padmavare rucire upapannaḥ /
children.translated_text: Born in that beautiful and delightful assembly of the <s>Jina</s>, upon a supreme and radiant lotus,

children.text: vyākaraṇaṃ ahu tatra labheyyā saṃmukhato abhitābhajinasya // 59 //
children.translated_text: May I there receive a prediction face to face from the <s>Jina</s> <s>Amitābha</s>! // 59 //
Having received that prediction there, with many hundreds of koṭis of emanations,

children.text: sattvahitāni bahūnyahu kuryāṃ dikṣu daśasvapi buddhibalena // 60 //
children.translated_text: May I accomplish many benefits for beings in the ten directions through the power of wisdom! // 60 //

children.text: bhadracaripraṇidhāna paṭhitvā yatkuśalaṃ mayi saṃcitu kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: Having recited the vow of the <s>Bhadracarī</s>, whatever small merit has been accumulated by me,

children.text: ekakṣaṇena samṛdhyatu sarvaṃ tena jagasya śubhaṃ praṇidhānam // 61 //
children.translated_text: May it all be fulfilled in a single instant -- that auspicious vow for the world! // 61 //
The merit obtained through the dedication of the <s>Bhadracarī</s>, infinite and supremely distinguished,
By that may the world, sunk in the flood of calamity, go to the excellent city of <s>Amitābha</s>! // 62 //
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, uplifted in mind.

children.text: sudhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaste ca bodhisattvā āryamañjuśrīpūrvaṃgamāḥ, te ca bhikṣavaḥ āryamañjuśrīparipācitāḥ, te ca āryamaitreyapūrvaṃgamāḥ sarvabhadrakalpikā bodhisattvāḥ, te cāryasamantabhadrabodhisattvapramukhā yauvarājyābhiṣiktāḥ paramāṇurajaḥsamā mahābodhisattvā nānālokadhātusaṃnipatitāḥ, te cāryaśāriputramaudgalyāyanapramukhā mahāśrāvakāḥ, sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat, sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavataḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
children.translated_text: <s>Sudhana</s> the merchant's son, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> led by the noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and those monks matured by the noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the Auspicious <s>Kalpa</s> led by the noble <s>Maitreya</s>, and the noble <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>...

body.text: āryagaṇḍavyūhānmahādharmaparyāyādyathālabdhaḥ sudhanakalyāṇamitraparyupāsanacaryaikadeśaḥ āryagaṇḍavyūho mahāyānasūtraratnarājaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s>, the great <s>Dharma</s> discourse, as obtained: a portion of <s>Sudhana</s>'s practice of attending upon spiritual friends. The noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras, is complete.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tethāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes -- the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodho evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: And also their cessation -- thus has the Great Renunciant taught.

body.text: sahasrāṇi dvādaśa //
body.translated_text: Twelve thousand [verses].
